releases.name: v2.1.304
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added a transcript line when a plugin that runs first skips one of your mod's hooks, naming the event and the plugin
- Added `decider: "person"` to a mod's `tool.check` answer: only the permission dialog or a host's callback can approve the ask, and it is refused with the mod's reason where nobody can be asked
- Added `e.isReadOnly` to a mod's `tool.check` event, set when the tool call is read-only
- Added `/auto-mode-setup`: a guided setup that reads your project and recent sessions to teach auto mode about your environment, now also available on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, Claude apps gateway and telemetry-disabled sessions
- Added `/claude-api managed-agents-secure`, which compares a Managed Agents agent's settings with Anthropic's published security guide, without changing anything
- Added the names of the tools called earlier to the compaction summary in the transcript view (Ctrl+O)
- Added a warning on Pro and Max plans when resuming an inactive conversation would use a noticeable share of your 5-hour usage limit: resume anyway, or start a new conversation and Claude can look up the previous one if you refer to it
- Fixed the organization policy not refreshing until the hourly check after approving an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` at startup or switching "Use custom API key" in `/config`
- Fixed sandboxed commands failing to start on Linux when a `sandbox.filesystem.denyRead` glob contains brackets that are not a character class, such as a `[user-id]` route folder
- Fixed `rm -r` of a mounted drive or a folder at its top level (`/Volumes`, `/media`, WSL's `/mnt/c`) not getting the safety prompt that `rm -rf /Applications` gets
- Fixed `CLAUDE_CODE_TRANSCRIPT_LOCAL_GC` dropping messages from the saved transcript when the disk filled up while the file was being trimmed
- Fixed a plugin keeping a headless run going past `--max-turns`, Stop, or ended input by spawning subagents or re-running a finished one
- Fixed a failed mod reload removing the tools and commands of the version that stays loaded, and its messages being wrong or silent about whether the previous version is still loaded
- Fixed a click on a mod's button being lost when buttons with the same label and no `key` were redrawn unchanged
- Fixed mod sharing in the built-in `plugin-authoring` skill stopping at the secret scan on machines with managed settings and on Team and Enterprise plans
- Fixed scheduled Cowork cloud sessions waiting five minutes again for each subagent whose WebFetch needed a URL approval that nobody was there to give
- Fixed Write results and rejected edits showing a file outside the working directory as `../../…`; they now show `~/…` or the full path
- Fixed a claude.ai Directory plugin's skills not running as commands when picked from the "/" menu in Cowork cloud sessions
- Fixed Remote Control permanently withholding a desktop conversation's history when a different account was signed in to the terminal
- Fixed Remote Control failing to start from Claude Desktop when DISABLE_TELEMETRY or DO_NOT_TRACK is set on a paid plan
- Fixed model switches, messages and interrupts waiting behind a context usage check in SDK and desktop sessions
- Fixed `context_management: Extra inputs are not permitted` errors behind LLM gateways; Claude Code now resends the request without that field
- Fixed OpenTelemetry settings delivered through server-managed settings being ignored for the whole session after signing in during first-run setup or the first start after /logout
- Fixed unsandboxed Bash commands in Claude Desktop Code tab sessions on macOS and Linux not seeing environment variables exported in shell startup files such as ~/.zshrc
- Fixed the Consumer Terms notice being skipped for a day or longer after a server error
- Fixed `/privacy-settings` offering choices that may not apply to you after a network or server error
- Fixed a "Context limit reached" or "Prompt is too long" error after stopping a turn while Claude Code was compacting a conversation the API had rejected as too long
- Fixed subagents sometimes forgetting their most recent work when they were messaged or resumed right after finishing
- Fixed `claude --help` text for `--tools`, `--resume`, `--debug`, `--json-schema`, `--disable-slash-commands`, `--system-prompt-snapshot` and `claude update` to match actual behavior
- Fixed `claude --worktree` removing the worktree and its branch without asking at exit when HEAD was detached or on another branch, which could lose commits
- Fixed resumed and cloud sessions sending Claude the whole skill list again each time plugins reloaded at startup
- Fixed an interrupt not ending a Read that waits on an idle pipe or device named like an image
- Fixed `/effort status`, `/effort ultracode` and the prompt's effort indicator showing a guessed effort level when `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` is `auto` or `unset` and no level is sent
- Fixed a PreToolUse hook's deny reason being replaced by a timeout error when an Agent SDK callback hook on the same tool call timed out
- Fixed Bash and PowerShell deleting a large command's output file when it could not be copied to the session's tool-results folder, unless the disk is full
- Fixed notes typed into a multiple-choice question with previews being cut off with "…" in terminals under about 100 columns, hiding what was typed (anthropics/claude-code#82768)
- Fixed self-paced `/loop` wakeups scheduled at the 1-hour maximum firing just after the 1-hour prompt cache expired, so those wakeups no longer re-read the conversation uncached
- Fixed agent teams: approving a shutdown request from the main session no longer exits the whole CLI
- Fixed a skill's `once` hook also removing another skill's identical hook after it ran
- Fixed transcript mode's `{` and `}` landing the prompt on an inconsistent row, or off screen, instead of the transcript's first row
- Fixed `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=200k` silently setting a 100K window: the variable now accepts `k` and `M` suffixes like `--autocompact`, and warns when a value is out of range or ignored
- Fixed Ctrl+C in the agents view clearing a text selection without copying it when pressed before the mouse button was released
- Improved `/usage` to say when a rate limit on usage data ends instead of "try again in a moment"
- Improved the lines shown when a mod written in the session loads, reloads or fails to load
- Improved artifacts with several views: when you ask for links to them, Claude now writes out each view's link and explains that the address bar stays the same as you switch views
- Improved cloud sessions: a new conversation's first turn no longer waits for the local (stdio) MCP servers of plugins synced from claude.ai, unless a server sets `alwaysLoad: true`
- Improved how a remote session recovers its status when the server refuses a status update that carried other session data
- Improved session file size in auto mode: the safety classifier's context is no longer stored with every request
- Improved the `claude -p` invalid-settings warning: a file that did not load lists only what stopped it, and long lists are capped per file
- Improved resume of large compacted sessions in SDK and headless mode: the first request after resuming is sent sooner
- Improved responsiveness and throughput when many subagents are running at the same time
- Improved memory use when sending requests in long or resumed conversations
- Self-hosted runner: Improved the error shown when the git host answers "not found" for a session's repository: it now names the repository and whom to ask
- Windows: Improved git command start-up with a standard Git for Windows install by running its git.exe directly instead of through its cmd launcher
- Changed mods' `settings.read` hooks to receive each settings layer and rewrite the merged settings, so a managed mod can make an organization's setting a ceiling, including the `cleanupPeriodDays` the retention sweep uses
- Changed the `/artifacts` delete confirmation to show numbered choices: 1 or Enter keeps the artifact, 2 deletes it, and y, n and Esc still work
- Changed the question that turns on the mods Claude writes in a session to plain text with no link or session id; it stays up when a new turn starts, and Claude tells you what loaded when you turn them on
- Changed tool search to be on by default behind a custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`; a 400 or 422 from the gateway is retried without it
- Changed compaction to send Claude the skill list again afterwards; `/reload-skills` now sends only new or changed skills
- Changed skill hooks: the skills of one source (a repo, your own folder, or a plugin) can register at most 1,024 hooks and 16,384 matcher characters per session
- Changed skills under a policy that allows hooks from plugins only: a skill used in the main conversation whose hooks are kept out no longer gets its `allowed-tools`
- Updated the /claude-api skill to use the `ant` CLI on Claude Platform on AWS instead of falling back to the SDK or curl
- Removed the notes from `claude plugin validate` that predicted where a mod's hooks would run
- Removed the "(research preview)" label from the `/fast` dialog title on Opus 5.5
- [VSCode] Added mod drawing in the chat panel for sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry, behind an LLM gateway, or with telemetry turned off
- [VSCode] Fixed one cause of sessions failing to start with "Subprocess initialization did not complete within 60000ms": time a SessionStart command hook spends running no longer counts toward the limit, up to 10 minutes in total
- [VSCode] Fixed a session closed while it was starting keeping its Claude Code process running until the start ended
- [VSCode] Fixed a mod's drawings disappearing from a long-open panel until the next turn on machines that also run an older Claude Code
- [VSCode] Fixed Past conversations hiding sessions when `claudeCode.claudeProcessWrapper` is set
- [VSCode] Changed background sub-agents to show as one status line under their Agent card instead of streaming every step into the chat; the full transcript stays in /tasks
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed folders in the composer's @ list showing no name in cloud sessions, where picking one added only a space instead of a mention
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude going silent in a thread when its channel becomes shared across Enterprise Grid workspaces mid-task; it now posts a one-time note to @-mention it in a new thread
- [Claude Tag] Fixed `@Claude !fork` typed outside a thread getting no visible reply; Claude now shows you a private note saying to run it from inside a thread
- [Code Review] Added review levels to Code Review: Owners choose Quick, Standard (the default), or Deep for the organization, and can give individual repositories their own level
- [Code Review] Added an option in Code Review admin settings to review every repository in a GitHub organization, including ones added later, without selecting them one by one
- [Code Review] Fixed pull requests opened within a minute or two of an admin turning on Code Review being silently skipped; they are now retried and reviewed

issues.title: Bug: Send button remains disabled globally after OpenAI usage is exhausted

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: rate-limits

labels.name: custom-model

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.924.20706

### What subscription do you have?

team

### What platform is your computer?

_No response_

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

In ChatGPT/Codex version `26.917.62051` & ‘26.924.20706’, once the OpenAI provider reaches its usage limit, the Send button remains disabled even after switching to a valid third-party provider.

The issue affects both existing tasks and newly created tasks. This indicates that the disabled state is not scoped to a single conversation and is not caused by the third-party provider.

## Environment

- Product: ChatGPT/Codex desktop app
- Version: `26.917.62051`
- Original provider: OpenAI
- Replacement provider: Valid third-party provider
- Date observed: September 24, 2026

## Preconditions

- The OpenAI provider has reached its usage limit.
- The third-party provider API is valid and reachable.
- The third-party provider can successfully handle requests independently.
- The provider switch is accepted by the application.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use the OpenAI provider in the desktop app.
2. Exhaust the available OpenAI usage or reach the provider limit.
3. Observe that the Send button becomes disabled.
4. Switch the provider to a valid third-party provider.
5. Select a compatible model.
6. Open an existing task and attempt to send a message.
7. Create a new task and attempt to send a message.

## Actual behavior

The Send button remains greyed out in both:

- existing tasks;
- newly created tasks.

The behavior persists after switching to a valid third-party provider. The third-party API itself is functional, so the disabled state is not caused by provider availability or API credentials.

## Expected behavior

After switching to a valid provider, the application should recompute the global composer availability state and allow the user to send messages.

Provider-specific usage exhaustion should not disable message composition globally after the active provider has changed.

## Impact

The user cannot continue working through a configured third-party provider after OpenAI usage is exhausted.

Because newly created tasks are also affected, the issue can make the entire desktop app appear unable to send messages until the client state is reset or the usage window recovers.

## Regression context

Previously, after OpenAI usage was exhausted, switching to a valid third-party provider still allowed messages to be sent. The current behavior appears to be a regression in version `26.917.62051`.

## Likely cause

The client may retain a global provider/quota failure state after the OpenAI provider becomes unavailable. The provider switch updates the selected provider but does not clear or recompute one or more global state values, such as:

- `canSend`;
- provider quota exhaustion;
- global request availability;
- composer disabled state;
- cached authentication or capability validation;
- an application-level error state.

Because both old and new tasks are affected, this state is likely held above the task/conversation level.

## Suggested fix

When the active provider, model, endpoint, or credential context changes:

1. Clear provider-specific quota and error state.
2. Recompute global composer availability.
3. Revalidate the selected provider and model.
4. Cancel or invalidate pending requests associated with the previous provider.
5. Enable the Send button when the new provider is valid.
6. If the new provider cannot be used for the current task, show a specific error instead of leaving the Send button silently disabled.

## Suggested regression test

```text
OpenAI provider reaches usage limit
→ Send button becomes disabled
→ switch to a valid third-party provider
→ select a compatible model
→ create a new task
→ Send button becomes enabled
→ message is submitted successfully
```

The test should also verify that an existing task and a newly created task behave consistently.

## Additional evidence available

- Desktop app version: `26.917.62051`
- Existing and newly created tasks are both affected
- Third-party provider API is independently verified as valid
- The issue is reproducible after OpenAI usage is exhausted

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start Codex desktop version `26.917.62051`.
2. Create or open a task using the OpenAI provider.
3. Consume the available OpenAI usage until the provider reaches its usage limit.
4. Confirm that the Send button becomes disabled/greyed out.
5. Switch the configured provider to a valid third-party provider with a working API key and endpoint.
6. Select a compatible model from that provider.
7. Try to send a short message in the existing task.
8. Create a new task and try to send the same message again.

The bug reproduces in both existing and newly created tasks. The Send button remains disabled after switching providers, even though the third-party API is independently verified to be valid and reachable.

This suggests that provider quota exhaustion leaves a global disabled state in the client. The state is not cleared or recomputed when the active provider changes.

A minimal configuration example is:

```toml
# Before: OpenAI provider reaches its usage limit
model_provider = "openai"
model = "<openai-model>"

# After switching: valid third-party provider
model_provider = "third-party"
model = "<third-party-model>"
base_url = "https://api.example.com/v1"
api_key = "<valid-api-key>"
```

The expected behavior is that the Send button becomes enabled immediately after the valid provider and model are selected, or after starting a new task.

issues.title: Windows Desktop + WSL2: inline Visualize silently fails because /mnt/c/... is normalized as a Windows root path

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Codex Desktop for Windows.

- Release shown in logs: `26.818.31338`
- Microsoft Store package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.818.3698.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`
- Bundled Visualize plugin: `1.0.22`

### What subscription do you have?

Not relevant to this local Desktop path-handling reproduction.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 x64 with the Codex agent configured to run in WSL2 Ubuntu.

WSL kernel:

```text
Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64
```

### What issue are you seeing?

An inline visualization created by a WSL2-backed Codex task does not render in Codex Desktop. The visualization placeholder disappears without a chart or a useful file-read error.

The agent receives a thread-scoped visualization directory on the Windows filesystem through its WSL mount:

```text
/mnt/c/Users/<windows-user>/.codex/visualizations/YYYY/MM/DD/<thread-id>
```

The agent writes a valid HTML fragment there and the final response references its absolute WSL path:

```text
visualize{"path":"/mnt/c/Users/<windows-user>/.codex/visualizations/YYYY/MM/DD/<thread-id>/minimal.html","mode":"wide","title":"Minimal visualization"}
```

The file exists. `wslpath -w` resolves it to the expected native path:

```text
C:\Users\<windows-user>\.codex\visualizations\YYYY\MM\DD\<thread-id>\minimal.html
```

The observed fragment was 34,069 bytes, below the 5 MB limit. Its JavaScript parsed successfully and the fragment had none of the disallowed document wrappers or escaped-markup artifacts. The content layer is therefore not the failing layer.

### Root-cause evidence

The packaged Desktop visualization read service receives the path, obtains the execution host's platform path implementation, normalizes the supplied path, performs containment checks, and then calls the execution host's `stat` and `readFile` methods.

With Windows path semantics, the relevant transformation is:

```text
input:      /mnt/c/Users/<windows-user>/.codex/visualizations/.../minimal.html
normalized: \mnt\c\Users\<windows-user>\.codex\visualizations\...\minimal.html
```

Node's Windows path implementation considers the input absolute. Its relative-path containment check also succeeds against a matching `/mnt/c/...` writable root. The read then reaches the native Windows filesystem with `\mnt\c\...`, which resolves on the current drive as the nonexistent mixed path `C:\mnt\c\...` instead of `C:\Users\...`.

This isolates the defect to the Desktop path boundary: a WSL absolute path is validated with Windows path semantics but is not converted to a Windows path before native file access. The Desktop log identifies the renderer platform as Windows and the task environment as WSL-disabled for Windows-native browser features:

```text
browser_use_availability_resolved available=false platform=Windows reason=wsl-disabled release=26.818.31338
```

The visualization read failure itself is not logged with the requested or resolved path, which makes the UI failure silent.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use Codex Desktop on Windows 11.
2. Configure the agent environment to use WSL2 Ubuntu.
3. Start a task whose visualization writable root is exposed to WSL under `/mnt/c/Users/<windows-user>/.codex/visualizations/...`.
4. Ask Codex to create a minimal inline visualization with the bundled Visualize plugin.
5. Confirm the generated fragment exists with `stat`.
6. Confirm `wslpath -w <absolute-fragment-path>` resolves to `C:\Users\<windows-user>\...`.
7. Let the response emit the inline visualization reference containing the absolute `/mnt/c/...` path.
8. Observe that the visualization does not render and no actionable error is shown.

### Expected behavior

Codex Desktop should preserve the filesystem authority associated with the path.

For an agent-created `/mnt/<drive>/...` path, Desktop should do one of the following before native Windows file access:

- convert it to the corresponding Windows path, such as `C:\Users\...`;
- delegate `stat` and `readFile` to the WSL execution host that created the path;
- materialize the fragment as a renderer asset through an explicit host-neutral transfer boundary.

If the read fails, the inline placeholder should remain visible and show the requested path, resolved path, execution host, and file-read error.

### Actual behavior

The app silently drops the inline visualization. The file remains present at the correct WSL and Windows-equivalent location.

### Related issues

- #32054 reports the same silent visualization disappearance when the renderer resolves a valid fragment under the wrong `.codex/visualizations` owner. That report is macOS and concerns workspace-relative versus home-relative resolution.
- #24268 records the same Windows + WSL mixed-path result, `C:\mnt\c\...`, in bundled plugin reconciliation.
- #29413 and #33560 record `/mnt/c/...` reaching native Windows browser runtimes without conversion.
- #32183 contains another observed `C:\mnt\c\...` access failure and groups related Windows + WSL path-boundary defects.

This appears related to those issues but is not an exact duplicate. It affects the inline visualization file reader and reproduces with the absolute path supplied by the visualization protocol.

### Privacy note

User names, thread identifiers, project names, and visualization contents are redacted. A minimal fragment and sanitized log excerpt can be supplied if needed.

```text

2. Open an existing automation's menu and choose **Run now**.
3. In the affected state, observe the `configRequirements/read` timeout toast.
4. Fully quit/reopen Codex and retry the same manual invocation; the reporter observes normal behavior returning temporarily.
5. The problem recurs after further use.

The trigger is intermittent; there is no deterministic minimal reproducer yet. Multiple tasks were present. Concurrency may be relevant, but is not established as the cause.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

labels.name: context
labels.description: Issues related to context management (including compaction)

labels.name: app-server

issues.body:
**Component:** Codex app-server daemon 0.163.0 (`codex app-server --remote-control --managed-daemon`, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl) on a Linux VM, serving long-lived threads for the Codex app. Custom provider via a local proxy in Responses-passthrough mode (OpenCodex 2.84.0 — the proxy was NOT restarted during the recovery below, which is part of the evidence). Catalog context window 1,000,000; effective `model_context_window` reported in `token_count` events: 950,000. `model_auto_compact_token_limit = 700000` set in `~/.codex/config.toml`.

**Observed behavior (2026-10-19, two threads on the same server):**

- Both threads reached a terminal `token_count` state of `total_tokens = 950,000` (exactly the window) with `last_tokens = 0`. Every subsequent turn failed with: "Codex ran out of room in the model's context window. Start a new thread or clear earlier history before retrying."
- The threads' real context, measured from the fresh `token_count` events after recovery, was ~143,625 and ~143,129 tokens — about 15% of the window.
- In an earlier episode on a sibling thread, `total_token_usage` behaved as a running sum of per-turn totals since the last compaction, and the baseline stayed pinned at 950,000 across a manual `/compact` (23,043-token summary): the reported total stayed ~1,020,527 while `last_token_usage` was 70,527.
- One affected thread recorded 36 auto-compaction events over its life and still ended up pinned. A healthy control thread on the same server compacted 24 times, never pinned, and has zero context errors.
- **Recovery:** restarting ONLY the app-server daemon (`codex app-server daemon restart`) made both "dead" threads immediately resume work: new `token_count` events with the real ~143k occupancy, zero context errors since, and the client-side context meter (ring) reappeared. No thread restart, no history clearing.

**Interpretation:** the effective context accounting seems to live in the app-server process memory, where it can pin at the window and survive compactions; it is only recomputed from the thread history when the daemon restarts.

**Expected:** context accounting should track the post-compaction baseline / last-turn usage. A thread at ~143k of a 950k window should never be rejected for lack of room, and a compaction (manual or automatic) should reset the baseline in the running server.

**Workaround:** restart the app-server daemon.

Related reports with different facets of the accounting problem: #53741, #49026.

Reported by RHODIZ IT LLC — production homelab running 4 long-lived Codex threads through this daemon.

## Summary
The built-in image generation/editing tool returned `moderation_blocked` for two consecutive ordinary terrain texture editing requests. Please investigate whether this is a false positive. I am reporting the failure, not requesting that safety checks be disabled.

## Environment
- Codex desktop on Windows: 26.1013.40934 (build 20770), prod channel
- App update check: up_to_date
- Windows 11 Pro 23H2, 64-bit, OS build 22631.2861
- Tool: `image_gen.imagegen`
- Underlying image model: not exposed in the tool response

## Task and reproduction
1. Supply image A: a portrait top-down ground texture containing dirt roads, soil regions and grass.
2. Supply image B: a landscape photo of dirt, grass, scattered stones and tire tracks, used only as a material appearance reference.
3. Ask to edit image A while preserving its road positions, widths, intersections and soil/grass boundaries, and adopt the natural surface appearance of image B without copying its road layout or tire tracks. Output one UE5 Base Color texture.

    "moderation_stage": "output",
    "categories": ["other"]
  }
}
```

A normal terrain-only Base Color edit, or investigation of the possible false positive and guidance on recovery.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.908.70816

### What subscription do you have?

Business

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex App, when used without explicit project and a custom permission profile, will have the sandbox deny every execution after the first.

codex-cli does not show the same behaviour (though of course always has some dir implicitely as project dir) unless you explicitely use /permissions.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Run Codex App with a permission profile.

```
default_permissions = "mine"

[permissions.mine]
extends = ":workspace"

[permissions.mine.filesystem]
":root" = "deny"
":minimal" = "read"
"/opt/homebrew" = "read"
"/opt/homebrew/var/mysql" = "deny"
"/usr" = "read"
"/bin" = "read"
"~/.ssh" = "deny"
"~/.env" = "deny"
"~/.bash_profile" = "read"
"~/.bashrc" = "read"

[permissions.mine.filesystem.":workspace_roots"]
"**/*.env" = "deny"
```

Start a chat, but OUTSIDE a project, you write: ```Please try calling "date"```
Output: The date
You write: "Again"
Output: "Couldn’t run date again: the updated sandbox blocks the command runner’s configured /opt/homebrew/bin/bash, and permission was not granted."

You write: "Show exact error message"
Output: "sandbox-exec: execvp() of '/opt/homebrew/bin/bash' failed: Operation not permitted"

You write "Run it through /bin/bash"
Output: "It still fails before executing the command because the runner itself launches the configured Homebrew Bash:"

Also, it's super irritating that the visually selected policy seems to change automatically after the first test.
Also, if it tries to request permission, you can give it but sandbox will still fail.

On Codex App, without projects, default behaviour is already buggy.
Within a project, changing the active permissions through the UI in any way will also trigger the bug and condemn the chat to all access failing.
On codex CLI, sandbox will stay stable until you call /permissions in any way. Even switching to "Full access" will immediately fail with:
```
failed to load AGENTS.md instructions for environment `local`: fs sandbox helper failed with status exit status:
71: sandbox-exec: execvp() of '/opt/homebrew/bin/codex' failed: Operation not permitted
```

The root cause of all this seems to be the `":root" = "deny"` entry in the config, even though it's officially in your documentation. Remove it from the profile (which I don't want), the problem vanishes.

### What is the expected behavior?

Reliable sandbox behaviour.

### Additional information

This might be related to https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/45657 - I am not sure. A sandbox that's tried to be constructed within the current sandbox might cause these problems.

issues.body:
## Summary
On Windows 10, the OpenAI Codex extension in Cursor 3.25.9 can answer text-only prompts, but file reads and terminal tool calls hang indefinitely. The Stop button can also remain spinning and fail to cancel the task. The standalone Codex Windows desktop app on the same machine executes terminal tools successfully.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 10
- IDE: Cursor 3.25.9 (previously 3.17.19)
- Extension: `openai.chatgpt` 26.715.61943 (also tested 26.721.30844)
- Bundled extension CLI: `codex-cli 0.145.0-alpha.27`
- Working standalone desktop CLI: `codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2`
- Extension process command (redacted path): `codex.exe -c features.code_mode_host=true app-server --analytics-default-enabled`
- Local Windows project/workspace; PowerShell terminal

## Actual behavior
- Text-only prompts return successfully.
- Reading a project AGENTS.md or executing trivial commands such as `cmd /c echo CODEX_SHELL_OK` or `Write-Output "CODEX_TOOL_OK"` may remain in a thinking/running state for minutes without returning tool output.
- Clicking Stop (or Esc) can fail to terminate the task; at times Cursor had to be forcibly closed.
- Session JSONL showed tool invocation, then `Script running with cell ID 1`, without expected output. A later `Script terminated` did not reliably unblock the UI.
- Cursor's ordinary integrated PowerShell terminal can execute commands and Git promptly.
- The Codex Windows desktop app executed `Write-Output "CODEX_DESKTOP_TOOL_OK"` successfully with exit code 0 in approximately 7 seconds, and completed ordinary local Git workflows.

## Selected logs/warnings (causality unconfirmed)
- `CANNOT use API proposal: chatSessionsProvider`
- `error boundary ... name=AppRoutes`
- `failed to load models cache: missing field base_instructions`
- `rollout ... .jsonl is empty`
- `thread-store internal error: failed to read canonical session metadata`
- `failed to set thread name`
- `unknown feature key in config: thread_tools`
- `Shell snapshot not supported yet for PowerShell`
- `Received broadcast but no handler is configured`

A read-only check confirmed that the user's `config.toml` exists and does **not** contain `thread_tools`. These messages are observations, not asserted root causes.

## Troubleshooting already completed
- Restarted/reloaded Cursor and tested single-project vs multi-root workspace.
- Tried extension versions 26.715.61943 and 26.721.30844.
- Renamed only the Codex cache directory to a backup, allowing a fresh cache to be generated; text chat worked but tool calls still hung.
- Verified project files and Git work in the regular terminal.
- Inspected process tree: Cursor's Node Utility process starts the extension-bundled `codex.exe` in `app-server` mode; `conhost.exe` was observed as a child. No causal claim is made from this.
- Compared bundled CLI and standalone desktop CLI versions and behavior.
- Authentication, sessions, SQLite databases and other local Codex data have been preserved.

## Expected behavior
File-reading and terminal tools should complete and return output, and Stop should promptly cancel a running tool/task without hanging the Cursor interface.

## Questions for maintainers
1. Are there known compatibility issues between Cursor 3.25.9 and Codex extension 26.715.61943 / 26.721.30844 on Windows?
2. Could app-server feature negotiation (including `thread_tools`) or session/thread-store handling affect tool invocation or cancellation?
3. Is there a fixed extension/CLI combination or non-destructive recovery procedure that preserves authentication, configuration and existing conversation history?

Related but not necessarily identical: #22393 (Windows extension unresponsiveness) and #29140 (`thread_tools` tool-call failures, closed after a reported fix). No full session logs are attached because they may contain private project information.

issues.body:
## Summary

In Codex Desktop on macOS, automatic context compaction consistently fails whenever it is triggered. The task runs normally before compaction, but once the UI enters `Context automatically compacting`, it reconnects and then reports a remote compact transport/decode failure.

This is not an isolated one-off failure: in my sessions, it happens every time context compaction is triggered, making long-running conversations unreliable and difficult to continue.

## Error

```text
Error running remote compact task: stream disconnected before completion: Transport error: network error: error decoding response body
```

The UI shows:

```text
Context automatically compacting
Reconnecting 2/2
```

and then the error above.

## Environment

- Product: Codex Desktop
- Platform: macOS
- Subscription: ChatGPT Pro
- Model shown in the affected session: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra
- App version: not visible in the captured screen; diagnostics were submitted from the affected session

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open or continue a long-running Codex Desktop conversation.
2. Let Codex work normally until automatic context compaction is triggered.
3. Observe `Context automatically compacting`.
4. The compact operation enters a reconnect cycle (`Reconnecting 2/2`).
5. It fails with:

```text
Error running remote compact task: stream disconnected before completion: Transport error: network error: error decoding response body
```

6. Continue using other sessions until compaction is triggered; the same failure recurs.

## Actual behavior

- The remote compact task disconnects before completion.
- The response body cannot be decoded.
- The current task is interrupted during compaction.
- Long-running conversations become unreliable because the failure occurs at the exact point where compaction is required to continue safely.

## Expected behavior

- Automatic compaction should complete successfully and preserve enough task state for the agent to continue.
- A transient transport failure should retry robustly or use a safe fallback.
- The thread should not become blocked or unreliable merely because it reached the compaction stage.

## Diagnostics

Feedback was submitted from the affected session with diagnostics enabled.

**Feedback ID:** `01a00ebf-d399-7373-975c-c359138dd909`

## Related reports

Similar symptoms appear in #31375, #32545, #38434, and #38861. This report adds a current macOS Codex Desktop reproduction using GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra, with a fresh Feedback ID tied to the affected session and the observation that the failure occurs every time automatic compaction is triggered.

Every /responses call from the Codex Desktop app returns two response headers that name a

model" buffering is enabled and points at gpt-6-luna. The product exposes no setting that

### Summary

In the **Codex GUI inside ChatGPT Desktop 26.924.22138 on Windows**, typing into an inline file review/comment box can move keyboard focus to the underlying source-file editor. The same keystrokes are then inserted into the actual file being reviewed.

This is reproducible with normal English input and is even more visible with a Chinese IME.

### Environment

- Platform: Windows
- App: ChatGPT Desktop
- Desktop version: `26.924.22138`
- Surface: Codex GUI → file diff/review → inline comment
- Input methods tested:
  - Direct English keyboard input
  - Chinese IME (candidate selection / composition commit)

### Reproduction

#### Case 1: English input

1. Open Codex in ChatGPT Desktop.
2. Open a file diff/review.
3. Add an inline comment and click inside the comment input box.
4. Start typing English text.

### Actual behavior

- Focus jumps from the inline comment box to the underlying source-file editor.
- The typed characters are inserted directly into the source file.
- The comment box may remain empty.

### Expected behavior

- Focus should remain in the inline comment input.
- Keystrokes entered into the comment UI must never modify the source file.

---

#### Case 2: Chinese IME

1. Open Codex in ChatGPT Desktop.
2. Open an inline comment box in the file review UI.
3. Start composing Chinese text in the comment box, for example typing pinyin for `你好`.
4. Select/commit the IME candidate.

### Actual behavior

- During or immediately after IME composition commit, focus moves to the underlying source editor.
- The committed Chinese text can also be inserted into the source file.
- In some cases the comment box receives the text while the source file receives the same committed text as well.

### Expected behavior

- IME composition and commit should stay fully contained within the comment input.
- The source editor must not receive keyboard/composition events from the inline comment UI.

### Impact

This is more than a focus glitch: simply typing a review comment can unintentionally modify the file being reviewed.

### Related issues

- #43510 — inline review comments can lose focus to another UI surface
- #26325 — annotation/comment input on Windows can leak keyboard events to the underlying surface

The behavior here appears related, but differs in that the leaked input reaches the source-file editor and causes actual file modification.

issues.title: Chrome browser-use hangs on JavaScript confirm() dialogs; handle confirm like alert/beforeunload or expose dialog handling

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of Codex / plugin are you using?

- Codex Desktop: 26.519.x on Windows
- Chrome plugin: `chrome@openai-bundled` / `26.519.31651`
- Codex Chrome Extension ID: `hehggadaopoacecdllhhajmbjkdcmajg`
- Browser backend: Chrome extension backend

### What issue are you seeing?

When a page opens a native JavaScript `confirm()` dialog during a Chrome browser-use action, the automation call hangs. In my case, itch.io uses `confirm("Remove this game from the collection?")` before posting a collection remove action. Clicking the page's `Remove...` link through the Chrome plugin opened the native confirm dialog, and subsequent browser-use calls timed out waiting on Chrome input / CDP interaction.

This is different from `alert` and `beforeunload`, which the bundled browser client already auto-handles. The current dialog handler appears to accept only those two dialog types, leaving `confirm` unresolved.

### Reproduction

1. Use `chrome@openai-bundled` with an authenticated Chrome session.
2. Navigate to a page that triggers a native `confirm()` from a normal click handler. Example class of flow: a web app's delete/remove button implemented as:

```js
if (confirm("Remove this item?")) {
  return $.post(removeUrl, withCsrf());
}
```

3. Click the triggering element via browser-use / Chrome plugin.
4. Observe the tool call hang or time out because the confirm dialog remains open.

### Expected behavior

The browser runtime should not hang on native `confirm()` dialogs. Either:

- handle `confirm` the same way as `alert` / `beforeunload` when the dialog is opened as a direct result of an approved browser-use action, or
- expose a supported dialog handling primitive so agents can accept/dismiss the dialog deliberately.

### Local diagnosis

In the bundled `scripts/browser-client.mjs`, the JavaScript dialog handler handles `Page.javascriptDialogOpening` but only accepts `alert` and `beforeunload`. A minimal local patch that fixed the hang was to include `confirm` in that accepted set:

```diff
- if (n !== "alert" && n !== "beforeunload" || typeof o !== "number") return;
+ if (n !== "alert" && n !== "beforeunload" && n !== "confirm" || typeof o !== "number") return;
```

After reloading the browser runtime with that change, the same itch.io remove flow completed successfully. I verified it by removing duplicate collection entries and then re-reading the collection pages; the duplicate check returned an empty list.

### Safety note

Automatically accepting every `confirm()` globally may be broader than desired. A safer upstream implementation could limit auto-acceptance to dialogs that are opened during an already-approved click/action, or expose explicit dialog handling to the agent layer. The main bug is that unresolved `confirm()` dialogs currently leave Chrome browser-use stuck with no recovery path from the normal tool surface.

### Why this matters

Many real web apps use native `confirm()` for low-level remove/delete actions. Browser-use can already click the initiating control and can handle some native dialogs, but this missing `confirm` case makes otherwise normal workflows fail mid-task.

issues.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex app 26.818.61809 on macOS, using the in-app Browser control capability.

### What feature would you like to see?

Surface native webpage `alert`, `confirm`, and `prompt` dialogs as structured in-app Browser state. The agent should receive the dialog type, message text, and origin, and should be able to accept or dismiss it. In-app Browser screenshots should also capture the visible dialog overlay.

If a dialog is blocking the page, Browser actions should report that condition instead of appearing to succeed or silently doing nothing.

### Additional information

Minimal reproduction:

1. Open a webpage in the in-app Browser.
2. Submit an incomplete form that triggers a native JavaScript alert, or wait for a site-rendered session-extension modal.
3. The human can see the dialog and its message.
4. Structured Browser control can report no active dialog, expose only the underlying DOM, or time out when clicking the visible button.
5. The agent cannot reliably read or dismiss the dialog and may incorrectly infer that the previous action had no effect.

Expected behavior:

- Emit a dialog-open event containing type, message, and origin for native dialogs.
- Make native dialogs available through the structured dialog API until accepted or dismissed.
- Capture visible native and site-rendered modal overlays in in-app Browser screenshots.
- Report an explicit blocking-dialog condition when underlying-page actions cannot proceed.
- Preserve this behavior for unattended workflows where the user is away from the computer.

Important scope distinction: screen-level Computer Use can see these rendered dialogs. The gap is specifically in the in-app Browser structured state and interaction layer. This is also distinct from #37855, which concerns clicking a button in a separate Chrome popup window.

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

When I submit a message in Work mode while using BYOK, I get this error:

```text
Error submitting message
Work browser access requires an authenticated account
```

The browser and computer are local resources on my machine. However, the client requires a ChatGPT account identity when initializing local browser/computer automation, even though model inference is configured through BYOK.

Inspection of the installed client suggests that `requireWorkBrowserIdentity` is enabled when `conversationDetailMode` is `STEPS_PROSE`. If a `node_repl` configuration exists but no cached ChatGPT authenticated principal is available, the client throws the error above.

This blocks message submission during tool initialization, before the agent can use any tools.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure a custom Responses API model provider using BYOK authentication, without signing in to a ChatGPT account.
2. Enable local browser/computer automation.
3. Select Work mode.
4. Submit a text message.

Relevant configuration:

```toml
[desktop]
conversationDetailMode = "STEPS_PROSE"

[features]
browser_use = true
browser_use_external = true
computer_use = true
```

Message submission fails with:

```text
Work browser access requires an authenticated account
```

No session ID or token/context usage measurements are available for the failed submission.


### What is the expected behavior?

Work mode should allow BYOK users to submit messages and use their own local browser/computer tools, subject to local permissions and approvals.

A missing ChatGPT account identity should not block message submission when model access is already configured through BYOK.

Switching out of Work mode or disabling local automation removes functionality I want to use and does not resolve the underlying compatibility issue.

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, the managed app-server daemon's background updater runs every hour and pipes the PowerShell installer into `powershell.exe` via stdin + `Invoke-Expression`. McAfee Real Protect blocks that script every time as fileless malware (`Real Protect-PSFL!…`). The user then gets an antivirus alert every hour, and the daemon never updates.

This looks like the missing piece for #48528. That report found the same hourly `Real Protect-PSFL` detections and the same `powershell.exe` command line, but could not identify the parent process. On this machine the 7 detections match the 7 `installer_run` failures in `daemon-updater.stderr.log` one-to-one, with the same timestamps.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Home, 10.0.26220, x64
- Antivirus: McAfee WPS 1.40.161.1 (active). Microsoft Defender is in passive mode and reports no detections.
- Codex CLI: `codex-cli 0.162.1` (npm)
- Managed daemon: `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\packages\app-server-daemon\releases\0.162.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\bin\codex.exe app-server --listen unix:// --managed-daemon`
- Codex Desktop (Store) 26.1007.2314.0 was also running. Its own `codex.exe` instances are separate processes and are not involved.
- `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\app-server-daemon\settings.json` does not exist, so the default settings apply.

## What happens

1. I started the Codex CLI for the first time that day at 16:55 local time (14:55 UTC). The CLI started the managed daemon and its updater (two `codex.exe app-server` processes from the release path above).
2. From then on the updater runs once per hour. It fetches the installer, which succeeds, and then runs the installer, which fails:

```text
{"stage":"installer_fetch","outcome":"succeeded",...}
{"stage":"installer_run","outcome":"failed","failure":{"kind":"other","os_code":null}}
{"stage":"scheduled_update","outcome":"failed","failure":{"kind":"other","os_code":null}}
```

3. The installer is started with this command line. The same string is embedded in `codex.exe`, next to `failed to invoke standalone Codex updater`:

```text
powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command [Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false); try { Invoke-Expression ([Console]::In.ReadToEnd()) } catch { Write-Error $_; exit 1 }
```

4. McAfee scans the stdin buffer through AMSI and blocks it. The PowerShell Operational log records event 4100:

```text
In Zeile:1 Zeichen:1
+ [CmdletBinding()]
Das Skript enthält schädliche Daten und wurde von Ihrer Antivirensoftware blockiert.
FullyQualifiedErrorId = ScriptContainedMaliciousContent,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.InvokeExpressionCommand
```

(German locale. In English: "This script contains malicious content and has been blocked by your antivirus software.")

5. McAfee `detection.log` entry, identical every hour:

```text
target:    [memory] size: 136344 bytes, app: powershell.exe 10.0.26100.9587, backing file: ''
sensor:    IAntiMalware
detection: Real Protect-PSFL!2BF5F369F936
result:    infected
```

## Correlation (UTC, 2026-10-13)

| McAfee detection | updater `installer_run failed` |
|---|---|
| 15:00:40.868 | 15:00:41.026 |
| 16:00:44.926 | 16:00:45.282 |
| 17:00:47.408 | 17:00:47.567 |
| 18:00:49.912 | 18:00:50.057 |
| 19:00:52.726 | 19:00:52.878 |
| 20:00:56.855 | 20:00:57.163 |
| 21:01:01.590 | 21:01:02.072 |

No scheduled task or other process starts `powershell.exe` at these times.

## Additional observations

- After the CLI exits, both daemon processes keep running. I then updated the CLI via npm, and the daemon from the old release path is still running. The hourly alerts therefore continue after the user has closed Codex, and nothing on screen points to Codex as the cause. This matches the lifecycle concerns in #51961 and #48195.
- To the user, this looks like "something on my machine runs a malicious PowerShell script every hour". When they ask Codex in a session, it correctly says that none of its session processes did this, which makes the cause even harder to find.
- I did not capture the blocked script content itself. 136,344 bytes is consistent with the current `install.ps1`. #36118 shows that McAfee also blocks the official `install.ps1` (verified hash) when it is run from disk, so this is most likely a false positive on the official installer, not a tampered download.

## Expected behavior

- The background updater should not depend on a stdin `Invoke-Expression` + `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` path. Security products classify that pattern as fileless malware. A native download, checksum verification and swap in Rust would avoid PowerShell entirely.
- If the installer run fails with `ScriptContainedMaliciousContent`, the updater should record that reason (instead of `"kind":"other"`), back off, and stop retrying every hour. Each retry raises a new AV alert.
- Closing the CLI should stop the daemon and the updater. If they must stay running, there should be a visible, documented way to opt out of daemon auto-start and auto-update.

## Related

- #48528: same hourly `Real Protect-PSFL` detections and the same command line, parent process not identified there
- #36118: McAfee blocks `install.ps1` during a manual `codex update`
- #51961, #48195: daemon and updater auto-start and persist without explicit opt-in

No antivirus settings or exclusions were changed. No raw logs, private paths or credentials are attached.

## What version of the Codex App are you using?

Windows installed package OpenAI.Codex: 26.908.4834.0 (read from Get-AppxPackage; About dialog version not independently checked).

## What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

## What platform is your computer?

Windows x64; OS version string: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0.
Japanese UI; Windows timezone: Tokyo Standard Time (UTC+09:00).
Observed on September 14, 2026.

## What issue are you seeing?

After creating an active daily automation for 10:00 Japan time, the user reports that the schedule is displayed as “毎週10時” (“weekly at 10:00”), despite the persisted automation configuration specifying a daily recurrence at 10:00, with minute and second both zero.

The saved configuration was read back after creation and again after the user reported the discrepancy. Both reads showed daily recurrence. The automation remained active, with local execution and the requested model/reasoning configuration.

Evidence boundaries: the weekly label is reported by the user. The reporting assistant independently verified the persisted configuration but did not capture or inspect the UI label. The exact affected UI surface (inline automation card versus settings detail) has not been isolated. No actual scheduled firing has yet been observed, so this report does not establish an execution-frequency bug or its root cause.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

Reported sequence, not yet independently reproduced on a clean installation:

1. In the Windows app, ask Codex to create a local automation that runs every day at 10:00 Japan time.
2. Create it through the app automation tool with daily recurrence, hour 10, minute 0, second 0, and active status.
3. Read back the saved automation configuration and verify daily recurrence.
4. Inspect the Japanese schedule label shown by the app. The user reports “毎週10時” instead of a daily label.
5. Re-read the configuration: it still specifies daily recurrence. No manual schedule-file modification was made.

## What is the expected behavior?

The schedule label should accurately describe the saved recurrence as daily at 10:00 (e.g. “毎日10時”). The label, saved recurrence, and scheduler should agree.

## Additional information

Existing issue #26633 concerns timezone/next-execution disagreement for a weekly schedule. This report concerns daily-versus-weekly Japanese wording; whether the underlying cause is related is unknown.

No full automation prompt, business/project names, account identifiers, local user paths, session transcript, credentials, or screenshots are attached. This report is submitted with the user's explicit authorization.

### What issue are you seeing?

Since October 19, 2026, Codex CLI 0.154.0 has repeatedly stopped during multi-step coding tasks with the following error:

"Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model."

The issue occurs with GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6 Sol, affecting both existing and newly created sessions. Short prompts generally succeed, but longer tasks involving multiple file reads and tool calls frequently terminate before completion.

Restarting the computer and Linux server, creating new Codex sessions, and switching models did not resolve the issue.

My ChatGPT Plus usage limits are not exhausted. At the time of checking, 97% of the five-hour allowance and 87% of the weekly allowance remained available.

Previous Codex logs also recorded:

- "We're currently experiencing high demand, which may cause temporary errors."
- "stream disconnected before completion: IO error: cannot decrypt peer's message"

These errors suggest that service capacity or streaming connection stability may be involved, but the exact cause has not been established.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Uploaded thread: 01a15741-77d5-7041-8e43-8ffc33bbc853

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should complete multi-step coding tasks without unexpectedly terminating due to capacity errors. If a transient service or connection failure occurs, Codex should retry or provide an actionable error message while preserving the completed work and allowing the task to resume.

### Additional information

Codex CLI runs on a shared Linux server through VS Code Remote-SSH. Network access is provided through an HTTP proxy forwarded over an SSH reverse tunnel from a Windows computer.

This configuration had worked reliably before October 19, 2026.

Connectivity testing through the configured proxy showed:

- 20 consecutive HTTPS requests succeeded.
- All 20 requests returned HTTP 200.
- The proxy exit was identified as being in the United States.
- Short HTTPS requests showed no connection failures.

However, these tests do not establish the stability of long-running WebSocket streams.

Codex logs confirm that model inference uses the responses_websocket transport. Some previous requests experienced TLS stream disconnections or high-demand responses.

The issue appears to have started on October 19, 2026, without an intentional change to the network setup.

01a15719-b503-7ab2-930e-8a285cc9f64a

issues.body:
## Environment
- Windows 11 Pro 26H2, OS build 26300.9550
- OpenAI.Codex Windows package 26.1007.2314.0
- Chromium module version from dump: 155.0.8059.40
- Sandbox service: running

## Observed behavior
After submitting high-resolution photo attachments from a Sony A7R V in a local task, the app launched its window but silently exited ~6 seconds later. `codex-windows-sandbox-service.exe` remained alive. Earlier, after switching to cloud execution, the Send button was greyed out; that issue may be separate.

Crashpad sidecar reported `capture_kind=crash`, `osarch=x86_64`, `ptype=browser`. WinDbg on the browser-process minidump reported:

```text
PROCESS_NAME: ChatGPT.exe
EXCEPTION_CODE: 0x80000003
MODULE_NAME: chrome
IMAGE_NAME: chrome.dll
FAILURE_BUCKET_ID: BREAKPOINT_80000003_chrome.dll!Unknown
Timeline.Process.Start.DeltaSec: 6
```

The preserved `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.codex-global-state.json` was ~211.79 MiB. Its `queued-follow-ups` field was ~211.53 MiB (99.88%). A structure-only scan detected two inline `data:image/` payloads: PNG 139.85 MiB and JPEG 71.67 MiB (encoded sizes), totaling 211.52 MiB. The old folder also held many large temporary copies of global state.

## Steps attempted
1. Verified `OpenAI.Codex` package status `Ok` and sandbox service `Running`.
2. Isolated `LocalCache\Roaming\Codex` alone: **still crashed**.
3. Renamed `%USERPROFILE%\.codex` to a timestamped backup (no deletion): **startup/login worked**. The fresh global-state JSON was around 234 KiB.
4. Some local-only conversation/project history disappeared from the UI with the fresh directory, so the backup was retained.

## Expected behavior
Large queued attachments should not make the desktop browser process crash at startup. If a queued item is too large or invalid, the app should safely reject or discard it with an actionable error, preserving accessible local history.

## Open questions
- Is persisting full image Data URLs inside `queued-follow-ups` expected?
- Can size limits / out-of-line attachments / startup recovery prevent failure?
- Is the greyed-out Send button in cloud mode related or unrelated?

## Confidence and privacy
The oversized queued state and recovery after isolating `.codex` are confirmed. The precise breakpoint cause and any causal relationship to cloud mode are **not confirmed** by a single-field A/B test. No private photos, authentication data, full state JSON or dump files are attached.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.71326 (unable to access "About Codex" dialog)

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

# [Windows] Codex 26.1007.9446.0 displays raw CSS throughout main window after update

## Environment

- **Application:** OpenAI Codex / ChatGPT for Windows
- **MSIX package:** `OpenAI.Codex`
- **Package version:** `26.1007.9446.0`
- **Internal application version:** `26.1007.71326` (from `owl-app.ini`)
- **Architecture:** Windows x64
- **Chromium runtime:** `155.0.8059.40`
- **Application shell:** Owl
- **Windows PowerShell:** 5.1, build `26100.9711`
- **Distribution:** Microsoft Store package

### Windows Operating System and Update Information

**Operating system:**
- Windows 11 Home, version 26H2
- OS build: `26300.9711`
- Architecture: x64
- Windows Terminal: `1.24.12741.0`
- Windows PowerShell: `5.1.26100.9711`

**Windows updates installed October 14, 2026:**

| KB Number | Windows Classification |
|---|---|
| KB5127648 | Security Update |
| KB5127647 | Security Update |
| KB5121794 | Update |
| KB5127694 | Update |

Additional updates installed in September 2026 and earlier were also present.

**Potential Windows update interaction:**

The Codex application update and several Windows updates occurred within approximately the same period on October 13–14, 2026.

The Windows updates required three system restarts. The Codex rendering failure was discovered during this update period.

Because both the Codex application and Windows were updated nearly simultaneously, it has not been established which update introduced the problem or whether an interaction between them is responsible.

The malfunction persists after the Windows updates completed and after multiple system restarts.

**Other application behavior:**

- Opera and other applications appear to function normally.
- GPU-accelerated video playback through YouTube and Rumble operates without observable problems.
- Windows Terminal and PowerShell function normally.
- A briefly observed blue PowerShell banner was identified as the normal `Get-ComputerInfo` progress indicator, not a rendering artifact.
- Codex continues to display raw CSS even when launched with `--disable-gpu`.

**Diagnostic conclusion:**

The near-simultaneous Windows 11 26H2 and Codex updates introduce the possibility of an application/operating-system compatibility regression.

No specific Windows update has been established as the cause. The problem remains reproducible under two separate Windows user accounts.

## Problem description

Following the most recent Codex update, approximately October 13–14, 2026, the application became unusable.

When launched, the main application window immediately displays raw CSS source text instead of the normal Codex interface.

The CSS fills the window, including the custom title-bar/frame region. It initially appears dimmed during window opening, then becomes fully visible.

The text is selectable and dynamically reflows when the window is resized.

The problem persists after restarting Windows, using Windows Repair, and launching Codex under a separate Windows user account.

## Actual behavior

The displayed text begins:

```css
/* Dependency CSS can load before app.css, so establish Tailwind's layer order here. */
@layer theme, base, components, utilities;

:root {
  --startup-background: transparent;
  --startup-logo-shimmer-base: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.24);
  --startup-logo-shimmer-peak: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.48);
```

The displayed text continues through extensive CSS declarations, including application styling and theme definitions, and ends with:

```css
:host { display: flex; }
```

The window title is `ChatGPT`.

Additional observations:

- The CSS text is selectable, but there is no visible text insertion cursor.
- Resizing or maximizing the window causes the CSS text to reflow.
- The CSS occupies the main interface, including the custom window-frame region.
- Normal project content is not visible underneath the CSS.
- Some project-editing interface elements appear intermingled with the CSS text.
- Project-editing text responds to mouse hover and displays tooltips.
- The project `...` menu renders normally above the CSS.
- The Rename dialog also renders normally above the CSS.
- Selecting a project through the system tray does not produce a usable project workspace.
- `Ctrl+R` produces no visible change.
- `Ctrl+Shift+I` does not open Developer Tools.

The behavior suggests that the application's main window is partially functional, but stylesheet content is being exposed as visible text.

## Expected behavior

Codex should display its normal project and conversation interface, with CSS applied as styling rather than rendered as document text.

Existing projects and conversations should remain accessible.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install or update Codex for Windows to MSIX version `26.1007.9446.0`.
2. Launch Codex.
3. Observe that the main application window displays raw CSS text instead of the normal interface.
4. Open the project-editing menu, where available.
5. Observe that the menu and Rename dialog render normally above the malformed main interface.

The failure was reproduced under two separate Windows user accounts on the same computer.

Under the second account, a three-option dialog containing Logout and Cancel appeared normally before the main window displayed the same CSS problem. No ChatGPT sign-in was required to reproduce the failure.

## Troubleshooting performed

The following did not resolve the problem:

- Multiple Windows restarts, including three restarts during Windows Update.
- Windows application Repair (completed successfully).
- Closing Opera and testing without the browser running.
- Testing with a separate Windows account and fresh Codex package registration.
- Attempting `Ctrl+R` and `Ctrl+Shift+I`.

Windows reports the package status as `Ok`, with signature kind `Store`.

A search of the Windows Application event log found no relevant Codex errors during the examined period.

No useful application diagnostic logs were found in the inspected user-profile package directories.

## Package-resource investigation

The installation contains:

```text
app/resources/app.asar
app/resources/owl-app.ini
app/resources/owl-electron-app.json
```

The ASAR archive contains:

```text
webview/index.html
webview/detached-window.html
webview/assets/index-373b55c7c328.js
webview/assets/app-shared-6ed15bfa827c.css
```

The startup HTML was extracted and inspected read-only.

It contains a properly formed `<style>` element with CSS matching the beginning of the text displayed in the malfunctioning window.

It also contains references to the main JavaScript entry point and external stylesheet.

The referenced resources exist in the ASAR index.

### Archive integrity verification

The installed `app.asar` was checked against the SHA-256 block hashes recorded in the package's `AppxBlockMap.xml`.

Results:

```text
Blocks checked:   8659
Hash mismatches:  0
Bytes checked:    567412548
Archive size:     567412548
```

Every checked block matched its recorded hash, and the verification covered the complete archive.

This provides strong evidence that the installed `app.asar` matches its package block map, although it does not independently verify every runtime executable or library.

## Possible cause

The precise cause is unknown.

The observations are consistent with a defect in main-window document construction, stylesheet injection, or rendering during application initialization.

The reproduction under a separate Windows account and successful ASAR integrity verification make corruption of the original user's application state less likely.

This is a hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause.

## User-data preservation concern

The existing Codex installation contains substantial development history, project configuration, conversation history, and custom settings.

Please provide a repair or update path that preserves:

- Existing Codex projects and project associations.
- Conversation and session history.
- Configuration files and custom instructions.
- Additional editable-directory settings.
- Existing source-code directories and other user modifications.

An in-place update that preserves application data would be strongly preferred over Reset or uninstall/reinstall procedures.

## Supporting evidence

Available for attachment:

1. Captured CSS text displayed in the malfunctioning Codex window.
2. Extracted `webview/index.html` from the installed ASAR archive.
3. PowerShell package and integrity-verification results.

The issue is reproducible across two Windows user accounts on the same computer.

--------
Addendum
--------
### Additional rendering corruption — October 15, 2026

The previously reported apparent recovery after selecting **Check for updates** was temporary and incomplete.

After entering full-screen mode using F11 and scrolling to the bottom of the visible CSS text, part of the normal Codex interface became accessible.

Selecting **Check for updates** and dismissing its dialog caused the interface to rearrange into an apparently normal layout. However, closer inspection revealed abnormal blank spacing between projects in the sidebar.

Returning from full-screen mode caused the application to revert to its unusable state, displaying raw CSS text.

Additionally, selecting an existing project task caused severe graphical corruption in the conversation pane. The text became a large, indistinct blur.

These observations suggest that the failure may involve Chromium's layout, compositing, or graphics rendering, rather than only incorrect stylesheet insertion.

The root cause remains undetermined.

issues.title: [Windows app] Local Work executor retries deterministic bundled-plugin copy failure every second (213,836 attempts)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From "About Codex" dialog)?

Installed Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.4894.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`.
Bundled `codex-app-tools`: `0.1.6`. The package version was verified locally; the About dialog version was not separately collected.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this diagnostic report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 10, build 19045, x64; packaged Windows desktop application.

### What issue are you seeing?

The Local Work executor repeatedly fails to copy a bundled plugin from the installed Windows package, then schedules another startup after **1,000 ms**, with no effective backoff or retry ceiling in the observed logs. The attempt counter reached **213,836**. Ordinary app restarts reproduce the copy failure and restart loop.

This report focuses on the **persistent retry behavior and recovery across launches**. The encrypted-resource copy signature is also reported in #49582 and #41164. #55417 describes a related plugin replacement failure that recovered after a few attempts; this installation kept retrying the same deterministic failure.

Sanitized diagnostic excerpts (separate events; paths shortened):

```text
2026-10-20T01:38:39.379Z info [tpp-local-executor]
  Starting Local Work executor attempt=213836

[tpp-local-executor] Local Work executor startup failed
  errorCode=UNKNOWN
  UNKNOWN: unknown error, copyfile
  '<PACKAGE>\app\resources\plugins\openai-bundled\plugins\codex-app-tools\.codex-plugin\plugin.json'
  -> '<USER_DATA>\executor-plugins\codex-app-tools\.codex-plugin\plugin.json'

[tpp-local-executor] Scheduling Local Work executor restart
  delayMs=1000 reason=startup_failure
```

The error stack passes through Node `copyFile`, `fs.cp` / `copyDir`, and the desktop executor's `readCapabilityRoots`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On the affected installation:

1. Start the official desktop app normally.
2. Inspect the Local Work executor startup messages in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Codex\Logs`.
3. Observe the same `UNKNOWN copyfile` failure and repeated `delayMs=1000` restart scheduling.
4. Quit and reopen normally. The same failure returns.

The bundled source files are readable and have the Windows `Archive, Encrypted` attributes. A direct Node `fs.cp(..., { recursive: true })` test against the original packaged plugin also fails with `UNKNOWN`.

Control experiment:

- Copy the resource file contents into a normal local directory using byte reads/writes.
- Verify SHA-256 against the package originals: **838 files, 49,220,670 bytes**, all matching.
- Repeat `fs.cp` from this local mirror: succeeds.
- Launch the official application with `CODEX_ELECTRON_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_RESOURCES_PATH` pointing to the mirrored resources root: the original `UNKNOWN copyfile` failure disappears.

This narrows the problem to copying resources from the packaged source on this machine. The exact Windows/Node encryption mechanism remains to be established.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Packaged bundled resources should be usable across ordinary app launches and updates without a custom resource mirror or launcher.
- Repeated deterministic local filesystem failures should trigger bounded retries/backoff and an actionable UI error.
- Plugin staging should reuse verified resources where appropriate and recover safely from partial staging.

### Additional information

**Workaround validation, 2026-10-20 (UTC+08:00):**

The official application was launched in its Windows package context with the resource override explicitly inherited by the child process. Package binaries and `app.asar` were left unchanged.

After the 10:45 restart, the original `UNKNOWN copyfile` count was zero. One transient `ENOENT unlink` occurred during startup; the executor connected to rendezvous on attempt 3 at 10:45:44 and remained connected through the final 10:51:38 observation. The staged plugin manifest matched the verified mirror.

The override is process-scoped. Launching through the normal shortcut omits it and previously reproduced the failure. A durable product fix is needed; future app updates have not been validated with this workaround.

Only sanitized error excerpts and plugin-copy validation results are included. Account/device identifiers, private paths, and raw logs are omitted.

## Summary
`codex doctor` reports an archived rollout missing from the state database and a duplicate rollout thread ID, although the SQLite database passes integrity checks. Two distinct archived rollout files share the same thread ID. There does not appear to be a documented, non-destructive reconciliation command.

## Environment
- Codex CLI: `0.163.0-alpha.10.2`
- macOS arm64 (doctor reports macOS 27.0.1)
- Desktop app: `26.1013.40934`
- State database: `~/.codex/state_5.sqlite`

## Observed behavior
```text
⚠ threads 2 issues - rollout files are missing from the state DB; duplicate thread inventory entries found
rollout DB missing archived rows 1
rollout DB duplicate rollout thread ids 1
rollout DB duplicate DB paths 0
```

Two different `.jsonl.zst` files in `~/.codex/archived_sessions/` contain the same primary thread ID in their filenames, with one also containing an additional UUID suffix. Both files exist, differ in SHA-256, and were backed up and verified. The `threads` table has only one row for that thread ID (archived=1), pointing to the file with the additional UUID suffix.

`PRAGMA integrity_check;` returns `ok` on the original state database and on the backup.

Running:
```text
codex migrate-rollouts --thread <affected-thread-id> --verbose
Scanned 2 rollout(s): 0 eligible, 2 already paginated, 0 skipped (0 empty, 0 busy), 0 failed.
already paginated <affected-thread-id>
already paginated <affected-thread-id>
```

`codex debug --help` and `codex debug app-server --help` do not expose an inventory repair command.

## Expected behavior
The archived rollout inventory should be consistent, or the CLI should provide a supported, non-destructive reconciliation workflow that preserves both histories.

## Request
Is there a supported safe way to reconcile the duplicate archived rollout thread ID and missing archived DB row without deleting either rollout or editing SQLite directly?

I have intentionally omitted private paths, conversation contents, credentials, and full diagnostic logs. I can provide a redacted doctor report if needed.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing
