prs.title: fix(core): name the replacement for legacy keys under providers
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56816

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A custom provider declared under the native `providers` key keeps its models but silently loses the fields that make it routable. `npm` and `options.baseURL` are dropped, the provider is still advertised by `opencode models`, and the first request then fails with `Unsupported package for <provider>/<model>: ` — an empty package name, which points away from the cause.

The cause is that the two keys are read by different code paths with different shapes. The legacy singular `provider` goes through `migrateProviders`, and `packages/core/src/v1/config/migrate.ts` is where the V1 spellings are translated (`npm` → `package`, `options` and `api` → `settings` / `headers` / `body`). The native `providers` key is decoded straight against `ConfigProvider.Info`, which has no `npm` and no `options`, and the decoder runs with `onExcessProperty: "ignore"` — so those fields vanish without a word.

This PR keeps the decoding exactly as it is and fixes the silence at both ends: the native path reports a V1 spelling through the same `unsupported` diagnostic the legacy path already uses for its own retired fields (`diagnoseProviderUnsupported`), and the request that uses a provider with no package now fails with a message naming the key to add.

| where | key | reported |
| --- | --- | --- |
| provider | `npm` | `package` |
| provider | `api` | `settings.baseURL` |
| provider | `options` | `settings`, `headers` and `body` |
| provider | `id` | `canonical` |
| provider | `whitelist` / `blacklist` | no replacement — plain unsupported wording |
| model | `id` | `modelID` |
| model | `options` | `settings`, `headers` and `body` |
| model | `release_date` | `releaseDate` |
| model | `tool_call` | `capabilities.tools` |
| model | `modalities` | `capabilities.input` and `capabilities.output` |
| model | `attachment`, `reasoning`, `temperature`, `experimental` | no replacement — plain unsupported wording |
| model | `provider.npm` / `provider.api` | `package` / `settings.baseURL` |

`whitelist` and `blacklist` deliberately do not point at `permissions`: those are tool permission rules and cannot hide or allow a model, so naming them would send users to a setting that does nothing. A V1 capability flag such as `reasoning: true` is not a rename of the structured `capabilities.reasoning` field it resembles either, so it keeps the plain wording rather than a hint that would not survive the copy.

`packages/core/src/config.ts` already turns every diagnostic into a `configuration normalization diagnostic` warning, but a warning in the log is not enough on its own — someone who hits the failure never looks there. So the request that uses such a provider now fails with

```
No package configured for example-provider/some-model: set "package" on its "providers" entry
```

instead of the empty specifier above. The model is still listed and still fails; what changed is that the failure says what to fix.

Scope stays narrow. Nothing is accepted, renamed or re-interpreted: a provider written in the native spelling produces no diagnostic at all, and one written in the V1 spelling keeps exactly the resolved configuration it has today — only the diagnostic and the error message are new. The issue's other two suggested outcomes (accept `npm`/`options` as aliases, or reject the entry outright) are config-surface decisions this PR does not take; happy to build either instead if a maintainer prefers it.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/core/test/config/normalization.test.ts` — provider-level spellings, model-level spellings including the nested `provider.npm` and the capability spellings, and a control that a fully native provider produces zero diagnostics and keeps `package` / `settings` / `modelID` / `releaseDate`.

`packages/core/test/config/provider.test.ts` — a provider registered from config with no `package` really does reach the resolver with `package === ""`, and resolving it produces the message above.

`packages/core/test/model-resolver.test.ts` — the same message without the plugin stack; the existing non-empty case still reads `Unsupported package for …: aisdk:@ai-sdk/perplexity`.

prs.title: fix(client): measure the SSE event size per frame, not per chunk
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56707

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

The generated Promise client appends each decoded chunk to `buffer` and checked `buffer.length` against the 16 MiB limit *before* it extracted any complete frame. The limit was therefore charged to whatever the transport happened to deliver together: two events of 9 MiB each, arriving in one chunk, tripped `SseEventTooLarge` even though neither frame is close to the limit, and the identical bytes were accepted when the same stream was split into 64 KiB chunks.

The guard now runs per frame instead of per chunk:

- the pre-drain check is gone, so nothing is rejected for the company it arrives in;
- each complete frame is measured as it leaves the buffer (`block.length > maxSseEventLength`), which keeps a genuinely oversized event rejected no matter how the bytes are chunked;
- the buffer is then measured again, which can only hold an unfinished frame by that point, so a stream that never sends a delimiter is still bounded — the case the issue asks not to lose.

I also renamed `maxSseEventBytes` to `maxSseEventLength` and commented what it measures. `TextDecoder` produces UTF-16 code units, so the old name promised a byte budget it never enforced: multibyte text can pass with more bytes than the number names. That is a naming fix, not a behaviour change — I left the budget and its unit as they were so nothing silently becomes stricter or looser for existing payloads; whether the contract should really be bytes is a separate decision.

The change is made in the generator template (`packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts`) and the client is regenerated, so the next `bun run generate` keeps it, rather than patching generated output by hand.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/client/test/promise.test.ts` gained three cases, each driving the real `make()` export with a `ReadableStream` backed `Response`:

- two 9 MiB events (about 18 MiB in total) delivered as one chunk are both yielded, and the same bytes in 64 KiB chunks yield the same two events;
- a single 16 MiB event is still rejected with `SseEventTooLarge` when delivered as one chunk *and* when delivered in 64 KiB chunks;
- a stream with no frame delimiter at all is rejected once it passes the limit.

`bun test test/promise.test.ts` → 43 pass / 0 fail. Against the unpatched generated client the same file is 42 pass / 1 fail: the one failure is the new one-chunk case, and the oversized-single-event test passes on both sides, which is what makes it a control rather than a second bug.

Also run: `bun run typecheck` in `packages/client` and `packages/httpapi-codegen` (both clean), the codegen suite (`bun test` → 98 pass / 0 fail), `bun run check:generated` (clean), and `oxlint` on the three touched files (0 warnings, 0 errors).

I did not run the TUI against a live server; the reproduction here is the generated client on its own, as in the report.

prs.title: fix(core): skip session warming while a turn is in flight
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56636

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Session warming sends a keep-alive request on a fixed interval, measured from when the last request **began**. It never asks whether the session is still working, so on a slow local model the warm request lands on top of the real one and the two compete for the same single slot. The reporter's logs show exactly that: the context reload is underway, and 10 minutes in a `warming session` request is sent, times out after 5 minutes, and is retried every 15 minutes — all while the original request is still pending.

The fix keeps the decision inside the plugin rather than the configuration: warming is only useful for an **idle** session, so a warm request is now skipped while the session has a real turn in flight, and warming resumes at the next interval once that turn settles.

How the in-flight state is known: the plugin subscribes to `ctx.event` and tracks `session.execution.started` in a set, removing the session on `session.execution.succeeded`, `failed` or `interrupted`. These events bracket a busy period exactly, and every terminal outcome clears them — which is why I did not use the `http.request` / `http.response` hooks from my earlier note: a request that fails or times out never reaches `http.response`, so a flag built on that pair would leak and stall warming forever.

The skip is a deferral, not a stop, and it is bounded by the window that already exists: the expiry check still runs first, so a turn that never reports an outcome cannot keep warming alive past its configured `duration`. In the reporter's case (30 minute default duration, 10 minute interval, a request that outlives both), no warm request is sent at all, and the next real request reschedules warming as usual.

Scope: this fixes the contending warm requests. The separate ~1 hour session stop described in the issue and in #55305 is not touched here.

### How did you verify your code works?

New test at `packages/core/test/plugin/warming.test.ts`, driving the real plugin against the plugin host stub with `TestClock`:

- an idle session is still warmed at the configured interval (control — this one passes without the change too);
- a session with `session.execution.started` and no terminal event receives **no** warm request across three intervals, and one arrives after `session.execution.succeeded` (fails without the change: three requests are sent while the session is working);
- a turn that never settles stops warming once the window expires, and does not resume when a terminal event finally arrives (also fails without the change).

Red before / green after, measured with only `warming.ts` reverted: **1 pass / 2 fail**, then **3 pass / 0 fail**. `packages/core` typecheck clean (`tsc -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.tests.json`), oxlint 0/0, and the neighbouring `test/plugin/plan.test.ts` still 12/12.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56127

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`toLLMMessages` lowered a tool call still in `streaming` state to the raw argument text when that text was not valid JSON. The Anthropic lowerer copies `input` onto the wire unchanged, so the request carried `tool_use.input: "not-json"` and Anthropic rejected it with `400 tool_use.input: Input should be an object`.

The streaming state stores the accumulated argument text as a `String` while every other tool state stores a record, so lowering now decodes the text as a JSON object and falls back to `{}` when it cannot: unparseable text, a truncated stream, or valid JSON that is not an object (an array, a number, `null`) all lower to an empty object rather than a non-object value. Nothing else changes — a streaming call whose arguments do parse still lowers to the parsed object, and running, completed and error states are untouched.

Regression test `lowers unparseable streaming tool arguments to an object` in `packages/core/test/session-runner-message.test.ts` lowers one assistant message containing five tool parts through `toLLMMessages`:

|---|---|---|
| streaming | `not-json` | `{}` |
| streaming | `["pwd"]` | `{}` |
| streaming | `{"command":"pwd"` (truncated) | `{}` |
| streaming | `{"command":"pwd"}` | `{ command: "pwd" }` |

prs.title: fix(app): stop following the end when a scroll moves away from it
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56285

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`handleListScroll` released the follow-the-end pin only for a held pointer or a native touch scroll, and every other upward scroll depended on an input handler to unpin first: the wheel handler for wheel, the touch handlers for touch. Two reported gestures produce neither. The custom scrollbar thumb calls `stopPropagation()` on its own pointer-down (`packages/ui/src/components/scroll-view.tsx`), so the timeline never records a held pointer and `pointerHeld` stays false for the whole drag. Autoscroll-style scrolling moves the offset with no pointer, wheel or key event at all. Both stayed pinned, so every size update while pinned scrolled the viewport back to the end on the next frame, which is the 1-frame oscillation in the report.

The fix decides from geometry rather than from the input device. The distance to the end (`maxScroll - scrollTop`) is what tells an arrival from a move away from it:

- A measurement adjustment moves the offset and the scroll range together, so the distance does not change. Prepending a history page and re-measuring a row above the fold both land here.
- A move away from the end grows the distance, whatever produced the scroll.
- Content shrinking under a viewport that is already at the end leaves the distance at zero, so the existing arrival rule still pins.

So the unpin condition becomes "the distance to the end grew", and the previous pointer/touch clause stays as an additional way in, since content can shrink during a held drag. The pin path is unchanged: every `scrollToEnd()` forcer is gated on `input.pinned()`, so once the view is unpinned no size update can pull it back.

I did not change the `arrived` heuristic or the paging thresholds. With the unpin in place the re-pin branch cannot run during a gesture, and `onHistoryScroll` is already called on every scroll event, so paging continues mid-gesture — the older-page loading in the report was reachable only after the view could stay away from the end at all. If a maintainer would rather see the pre-fetch threshold raised, that is a separate change.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added `packages/app/e2e/regression/timeline-scroll-unpin.spec.ts`, two cases over an 80-exchange session opened at the end:

- **Thumb drag**: drags the real `.scroll-view__thumb` to the top over 1 s and holds it, sampling the distance to the end every frame.
- **Autoscroll**: moves the offset up 600 px over frames with no pointer, wheel or key event.

Both assert the gesture reaches more than 200 px from the end, stays there, and never loses more than 50 px in a single frame.

Proof it is the change and not the harness — with only `virtualizer.tsx` reverted and the spec unchanged:

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| thumb drag | final distance **0 px** (snapped fully back to the end) | final distance > 200 px, no snap-back frame |
| autoscroll | one frame carrying the view back toward the end | no snap-back frame |

Both files pass `oxlint`. `bun run typecheck` in `packages/app` is clean; `bun run typecheck:e2e` reports only the four errors that are already on `dev` (`performance/terminals/probe.ts`, `performance/timeline/session-timeline-stream-probe.ts`, `regression/timeline-stream.spec.ts`), none in the new spec.

Neighbouring timeline specs on the same build: `timeline-history`, `timeline-geometry`, `timeline-cache`, `session-panel-scrollbar`, `timeline-stream` — 71 passed, 1 failed. prs.title: fix(core): honor the selected agent's configured model for new sessions
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55727

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A new session ignores the `model` configured for the agent it runs with. Passing `-m` on the command line works, but setting `model` under `agents.<id>` in the config (or in agent frontmatter) does not — the session starts on the catalog default instead.

`session.create({ location, agent })` deliberately takes no model, so a session row can legitimately be model-less. `SessionContext.load` then resolved the model from `selection.session` alone, and resolution fell through to the catalog default in `packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts`. The agent's own configuration was never consulted there, although the title and compaction paths already pass the agent's model.

The fallback now lives in one place — the `SessionContext.resolveModel` helper — and reads: the session's own model wins when it has one (an explicit `-m` or a picker selection is written to the session row, so it stays authoritative), otherwise `selection.agent.info.model` stands in before resolution reaches the catalog default.

Because the fallback sits in the shared helper rather than in `load`, it also closes the same gap at the two other call sites that passed a raw session and discarded the agent:

- `session/generate.ts` — transient generation
- `session/runner/llm.ts` — the manual compaction preview

`selectTitle` keeps the raw session-level resolution: it deliberately resolves overridden refs, and it already reads the title agent's own `model` itself.

prs.title: fix(tui): bind keypad mirrors for navigation keybinds
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55533

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Terminals that speak the kitty keyboard protocol report NumPad navigation keys as distinct keypad codes: Windows Terminal sends `CSI 57424 u` for NumPad End, `CSI 57423 u` for NumPad Home, and so on. OpenTUI decodes these correctly into keystroke names (`kpend`, `kphome`, `kpup`, `kpdown`, `kppageup`, `kppagedown`, `kpleft`, `kpright`), but the TUI's default keybindings only ever named the bare navigation keys (`end`, `home`, `up`, ...). No binding claimed the keypad names, so every NumPad keystroke was silently discarded — NumPad End does nothing while regular End scrolls to the last message.

This change adds the keypad mirror to every default binding that names a bare navigation key (33 defaults across diff, session, prompt, composer, and list navigation), establishing the invariant: **a default that binds a bare navigation key also binds its keypad counterpart.**

Two deliberate exceptions, both recording the same rule — Home and End belong to the focused prompt inside a session:

- `session.first` and `session.last` get no keypad mirror. #56910 removes plain `home` and `end` from those two transcript jumps so the caret keys reach the composer; mirroring Home and End onto the numpad there would hand the transcript back the keys on a numpad. They are exempt from the invariant, and the test says so with the reason.
- `input.line.home` stays `ctrl+a` only — regular Home in a text buffer means line-start, and mirroring Home there would make NumPad Home jump to the line start. `input.buffer.home` / `input.buffer.end` remain `none`.

The keypad names are already first-class in the stack: `@opentui/core` maps code points 57417–57426 to `kpleft`…`kpdelete`, and `@opentui/keymap` recognizes them as named single-stroke keys. This PR only extends the default definitions, so users who override any of these keybinds in config are unaffected, and keypad names were already valid in custom configurations.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New invariant test (`packages/tui/test/keybind.test.ts`): walks every default definition and asserts each bare navigation token is accompanied by its `kp*` mirror. Verified to fail with 34 violations against the pre-fix definitions and pass after.
- New end-to-end test (`packages/tui/test/keymap.test.tsx`): renders the real `Keymap.Provider` under `testRender`, feeds the raw byte sequences `\^[[57424u` and `\^[[57423u` through the renderer stdin (the exact sequences Windows Terminal sends for NumPad End and Home), and asserts the commands bound to `end,kpend` and `home,kphome` fire — using `diff.last` and `diff.first`, and asserting the transcript jumps stay silent.
- Updated the two existing assertions that pin exact default strings (`config-v2.test.tsx` defaults table, `mini/runtime.boot.test.ts` fallback expectations) to the new values.
- `tsc -b` clean; `oxlint` and `prettier --check` clean on the changed files; `bun test` over the touched suites (`config`, `config-v2`, `keybind`, `keymap`, `session-home`, `mini/runtime.boot`) is 62 pass / 0 fail.

prs.title: fix(cli): declare libc on published platform packages
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55225

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

npm picks a platform package by matching `os`, `cpu` **and `libc`**. Our published binary packages declare the first two and not the third, and an absent `libc` matches every libc — so a Linux x64 install gets all four x64 variants (`x64`, `x64-baseline`, `x64-musl`, `x64-baseline-musl`) when exactly one of them can run. That is the ~808 MB the issue measured. On `@opencode/cli-linux-x64@2.0.28` the manifest reads `{"os":["linux"],"cpu":["x64"]}`, and none of its 1036 published versions has ever carried `libc`; `@biomejs/cli-linux-x64-musl` declares `{"os":["linux"],"cpu":["x64"],"libc":["musl"]}` and does not have this problem.

Both scripts that write a binary package manifest were building the fields by hand, and both are fixed:

- `script/build.ts` writes the Bun-compiled packages. Its targets carry the ABI, so the field is `item.abi ?? "glibc"`.
- `script/build-node.ts` writes the Node SEA packages. Every Linux target there is glibc — `nodeTarget` resolves `@parcel/watcher-linux-*-glibc`, `@ff-labs/fff-bin-linux-*-gnu` and `@yuuang/ffi-rs-linux-*-gnu` — so it is `"glibc"` unconditionally, which is the same value `script/node-assets.ts` already passes to `getNodeAssets`.

The shared `packages/cli/script/platform-fields.ts` holds the field set so the two writers cannot drift apart again. `libc` is omitted off Linux because npm only consults it there.

This does not change how the CLI is built or how it runs. `script/postinstall.mjs` is already libc-aware — it detects musl through `/etc/alpine-release` and `ldd --version` and orders its candidates accordingly — so the runtime side was correct all along; only the manifests lied about it.

Not in this PR: the `-baseline` variants. They differ by AVX2 support, which npm has no field for, so an AVX2 host still receives both `x64` and `x64-baseline`. The issue's title names the missing `libc` field, and its own reproduction counts the four variants; separating the baseline pair is a different mechanism with a different fix, and this PR does not touch it.

One interaction worth knowing about: now that npm skips a variant whose `libc` does not match, the `installPackage` fallback in `postinstall.mjs` can reach a package name npm will refuse to place on a mismatched host. It is only reached when the correctly-patched binary is present but fails `--version`, and that path already treats a non-zero exit as "try the next candidate", so this is a worse error message on a path that should not be taken — not a regression in what installs.

### How did you verify your code works?

Three tests in `packages/cli/test/platform-fields.test.ts`:

- every Linux shape the two writers emit resolves to the right `libc` (glibc and musl, x64 and arm64);
- darwin and win32 carry no `libc` key;
- neither writer declares `os`/`cpu` inline any more, which is the regression that caused this.

The last one reads the two scripts' source, the same way `import-boundaries.test.ts` guards its own invariant. Without it the helper could be correct while a writer quietly went back to hand-writing the fields.

Both halves were shown to fail before the change: with only the `libc` line removed from `platformFields` the first test fails, and with `script/build.ts` reverted to its inline `os`/`cpu` the third fails.

`tsgo --noEmit` and `oxlint` pass over the changed files, with `tsgo` confirmed to reject a deliberate type error first. `bun test` in `packages/cli` is 330 pass / 1 fail; the failure is `test/acp/error.test.ts`, which also fails on a pristine `upstream/dev` checkout here, and the same suite shows 28 further failures until `XDG_*` is pointed inside the workspace, because the sandbox refuses writes to `~/.local/share/opencode/log`.

### Screenshots / recordings

_Not a UI change._

prs.title: fix(desktop): return the pages a cleared draft frees to the filesystem
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55282

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Fixes the `drafts.sqlite` half of #55282. That file never gives back the space a cleared draft used, so it stays at the high-water mark of the largest draft ever pasted into the composer — 153 MiB holding 0.81 MiB of live data on the reporting machine.

`openDatabase` opened the file with `journal_mode=WAL` and nothing else, so `auto_vacuum` stayed at its default `0` (NONE). A deleted row returns its pages to the freelist, where the next write reuses them, but the file is never truncated.

- `PRAGMA auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL` now runs before the journal switch. The order is load-bearing: switching the journal writes page 1, and SQLite only applies `auto_vacuum` while the file still has no schema. Reversed, the pragma is silently ignored.
- A file written before this change is still in mode 0, and only `VACUUM` switches it, so `openDatabase` adopts it there. The rewrite copies the live rows, which in a store of drafts is a rounding error beside the pages it returns.
- `reclaim` asks for the pages the delete freed. `INCREMENTAL` records freed pages across writes but truncates only when asked, so this one runs at the end of `collectBlobs` — the one place that retires a large chunk — rather than on a timer. When there is nothing to give back it costs about 1.4 µs, so it rides along with the collection.

Not in this PR: the `opencode.db` half. That 535 MiB `session.revert` cell is a live row holding a full unified diff in the legacy V1 `session` table, so no vacuum policy reclaims it — it needs remedy 1 or 2 from the issue, which is a separate change.

### How did you verify your code works?

Two tests, each asserting the reported quantity — bytes on disk — and each failing before the change at the assertion that names the symptom:

- `database.test.ts`: builds a file the way the previous release left it (mode 0, one 8 MiB row already deleted, one small row still live), then asserts `openDatabase` leaves it in mode 2, keeps the live row, and shrinks the file below 1 MiB.
- `drafts.test.ts`: drives the real store on a file — an 8 MiB chunk is uploaded and referenced, the draft is cleared, a due collection retires the chunk, and the file returns below 1 MiB. It is over 8 MiB before the change.

With the source reverted and the tests kept, both fail exactly there (`auto_vacuum` reads 0, the file stays at 8 MiB), so the tests measure the fix rather than passing around it. The mode ordering and the reclaim cost were measured against `node:sqlite` directly before any of this was written.

`tsgo -b` passes in `packages/desktop` (verified the gate can fail: a deliberate type error in `database.ts` reports `TS2322`). The full package suite passes under the pinned `bun@1.4.2` (the repo's `packageManager`, which is what `node:sqlite` needs): **132 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail** across 32 files.

I ran them anyway by preloading a `mock.module("electron", …)` stub that supplies only `app.getPath`, and both are green — **14 pass** and **3 pass**. That matters here because `extension/storage.test.ts` imports `openDatabase` from the file this PR changes, so its result is a real check on this change, not an assumption.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #55046

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The Context tab's "System Prompt" section read the text of the **last stored `type: "system"` message**. In this version those messages are the instruction updates a session announces mid-turn, not the prompt the model receives — so the section was hidden in a session that stored none, and showed a small update under the system prompt heading in one that did (#55046).

`packages/gui-extensions/src/context/tab.tsx` now:

- says the prompt is not stored, and where it comes from, instead of hiding the whole section. The report's expected behaviour allows an explicit "unavailable" state, and the client genuinely has no source for the assembled prompt: `packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts` (`baseTranscript`) builds it per request from the agent prompt plus the instruction baseline, and neither is in the message list the tab reads.
- lists the stored `system` messages as **instruction updates**, using the `description` the server already writes (`Instructions updated: <sources>`) as provenance, never as the system prompt.

The derivation moved into `packages/gui-extensions/src/context/instructions.ts` so it can be tested on its own.

Showing the assembled prompt verbatim would need a source for it on the client — the tab only reads stored messages today. I am happy to plumb that through as a follow-up if you would rather have the real text than the unavailable state.

### How did you verify your code works?

`bun test` in `packages/gui-extensions`: 180 tests across 33 files, **179 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail**. `tsgo -b` passes (verified the gate
can fail — a deliberate type error in `instructions.ts` reports `TS2322`, and the clean run exits 0). `oxlint` on the four changed files:
**0 warnings, 0 errors**.

⚠️ **Coverage, stated honestly**: the 4 new tests exercise `instructionUpdates()` — the derivation, which is the part that was wrong —
and `instructions.ts` exists only so that derivation can be tested on its own. **`tab.tsx` itself is not rendered by any test.** This package
has no `.test.tsx` files at all and no component-test harness, so there is no existing pattern for me to follow; adding one would be a
second, larger change. The label/visibility behaviour in `tab.tsx` is therefore verified by reading it against the report's reproduction
steps, not by an automated test.

New tests in `packages/gui-extensions/src/context/instructions.test.ts` cover the cases the reproduction names, plus the adjacent one:

- a fresh session (`user, assistant, idle`) stores no system message → no instruction updates, so the section shows the unavailable state instead of disappearing.
- an instruction update after `AGENTS.md` changes (`metadata.notice: "instructions"`) → reported as an update with its description, not as a prompt.
- the restart notice (`packages/core/src/session/execution/restart.ts`) is a `synthetic` message, so it is not an instruction update.
- a system message carrying no text is dropped.

The new tests are load-bearing: changing the filter in `instructionUpdates()` from `message.type !== "system"` to
`!== "user"` makes **2 of the 4 fail** (the fresh-session case and the restart-notice case), and restoring it returns them to green.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55216

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Dropping a second file into the composer did nothing: the first mention stayed alone, with no error. This makes the composer keep every mention it is asked to add.

`addMention` falls back to `lastIndexOf("@")` over the whole draft when the caller passes no range — which is what the drop handler (`addPart` → `draft.addMention(part)`) does. Once the draft holds a mention, that `@` belongs to the mention itself, so the fallback range started inside a mention part. `insertMention` only ever rewrites a text part, so no part matched and the prompt came back unchanged.

The fallback now only treats an `@` as a trigger when it sits in the same text part as the cursor — the only case `insertMention` can act on. When there is no such trigger, the mention is inserted at the cursor instead of being dropped.

`insertMention` also stops after the part it rewrites. A zero-width range at a part boundary matched both neighbouring parts, which duplicated the mention.

⚠️ **Possible overlap to flag for reviewers**: maintainer PR #54466 (`feat(app): reference sessions from the composer`) also edits
`packages/app/src/composer/editor/actions.ts`. This change is confined to `addMention`'s no-range fallback and `insertMention`,

### Issue for this PR

Closes #54059

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

A remote `service start` that exits non-zero is reported as a connection failure, even though SSH connected fine. `runSsh` (`packages/gui-extensions/src/ssh/command.ts`) classifies every non-zero exit as `SshFailure("connection")`, and the dialog renders `error.${code}`, so a failed `service start` reached the user as *"Could not establish the SSH connection"* — while the actionable remote error was captured and only kept in the hidden `SshItem.detail`.

prs.title: fix(core): import V1 MCP OAuth credentials during migration
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54879

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

V1 kept remote MCP OAuth tokens in `mcp-auth.json` under the global data directory. V2 never reads it, so after an upgrade the integration V2 derives for a remote server — `mcp_<sha1(name + "\0" + url)>` — has no credential row. `connectProvider` then finds nothing, falls back to an empty in-memory store, and every OAuth server reports `needs_auth` even though the V1 store still holds a valid refresh token.

This imports those entries in the migration that already imports the V1 provider credentials, keyed by the same integration the server registers under:

- `packages/core/src/mcp/integration-id.ts` — the id derivation, moved out of the MCP layer into a leaf module: the import re-derives it and the layer calls the same function, so the two cannot drift apart.
- `packages/core/src/database/migration/20261013150000_import_legacy_mcp_credentials.ts` — reads `mcp-auth.json` and writes one OAuth credential per usable entry: `access`/`refresh`, `expires` converted from V1's seconds to V2's milliseconds, the `serverUrl`/`tokenType`/`scope` metadata `toTokens` reads back, and the dynamically registered client the tokens were issued to — refreshing against a different client than the refresh token belongs to is rejected by the authorization server.
- Entries without a `serverUrl` or without tokens are skipped: V1 only ever read an entry back through a matching URL, and a login in flight has no tokens yet. An integration that already holds a credential keeps it, mirroring the existing provider-credential import.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New tests in `packages/core/test/database-migration.test.ts`: a `mcp-auth.json` holding a full entry (client info, scope, abandoned verifier and state), an entry without client info, and two unusable entries. They assert the two rows the import writes (including the millisecond expiry and the exact integration ids), that a credential written by a later V2 login for the same server wins, and that the source file is left byte-identical. prs.title: fix(cli): complete a tool call whose file name breaks the patch header
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54831

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Under ACP, a completed tool call gets its client diff from the patch the tool returned. `withCompletedDiffs`
(`packages/cli/src/acp/permission.ts`) wraps every fallible step of that per-file pipeline — `Patch.derive`,
`applyPatch` — except `parsePatch`:

```ts
const changes = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const parsed = parsePatch(file.patch)      // bare call: a throw here is a defect, not a typed failure
  const derived = yield* Patch.derive(...)
  return yield* applyPatch(...)              // already Effect.try
})
```

A patch header that a file name can break — the issue's `notes.txt\nx` — makes `parsePatch` throw
`Unknown line 5 "x"`. Because the call is bare, that arrives as a **defect** rather than a typed failure, and
the `Effect.orElseSucceed` that ends the pipeline only catches typed failures. The defect therefore escapes
`withCompletedDiffs` into the turn: the tool call never reports completion and the session ends with a JSON-RPC
internal error, which is exactly the symptom in the report.

The neighbouring `SessionUpdate` branch in `turn.ts` has no `catchCause`, while its `ChildUpdate` sibling does —
that is why this one defect takes the whole turn down rather than being logged and skipped.

The fix parses the patch through `Effect.try`, like its neighbours, so a patch that cannot be parsed yields no
client diff and the call still completes. I checked the other bare calls in that pipeline on the locked
`diff@8.0.4`: `structuredPatch` does not throw for this input, so this one guard is the whole fix.

### How did you verify your code works?

The new test in `packages/cli/test/acp/permission.test.ts` drives `withCompletedDiffs` with a patch whose file
name contains a newline.

- **Red first**: with the source change reverted, the test fails with the reported `Unknown line 5 "x"` raised at
  `permission.ts:97` — the same throw the issue describes, not a lookalike.
- **Green after**: the call completes, the client diff comes back empty, and no defect escapes the pipeline.

`bun test` over `packages/cli/test/acp/`: one failure, `error.test.ts` → *"reports an unavailable server when the
event stream drops its connection mid-turn"*. It reproduces identically on an untouched checkout of `dev` with
only this source change reverted (it needs a real socket to drop mid-turn), so it is not from this change.
Everything else passes.

`tsgo -b` exits 0, and `oxlint` reports 0 warnings / 0 errors on both changed files.

I have not exercised this end to end through a real ACP client — the reproduction above covers the completion
path the report names, and I would not claim more than that.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR Closes #54471 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Fixes the reported case where a list item, table cell or blockquote paragraph inside a message renders RTL text (Persian, Arabic, Hebrew) left-to-right. `markdown.css` only had: ```css [data-component="markdown"] > * { unicode-bidi: plaintext; } ``` `unicode-bidi` does not inherit, so that rule only ever applied to the **direct children** of the markdown container. Blocks nested inside them — `li`, `td`, `th`, and any `

` inside a `

` — fell back to the browser's default `unicode-bidi: isolate` and inherited the container's resolved `dir="auto"` direction. `markdown.tsx` sets `dir="auto"` from the first strong character of the whole message, so a reply that opens with a Latin heading (or inline code, e.g. `npm install`) makes every such nested block LTR, and their RTL content is laid out scrambled. I confirmed the browser UA stylesheet isolates exactly these elements (`address, blockquote, …, li, p, pre, table, td, th, …`), so the fix extends the plaintext rule to that set. Author-origin rules beat UA-origin rules regardless of specificity, so the low-specificity `:where()` form is enough, and keeping it in `:where()` avoids raising the selector's weight against the rest of the file. `div` is deliberately excluded: code blocks and Mermaid diagrams are wrapped in `[data-markdown-block]` divs and must keep `direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: isolate` — the regression test asserts that too. The regression came in with `6c3299103c` ("feat(app): add minimal RTL support (#40372)"), which added the `> *` rule. ### How did you verify your code works? Added a component test, `resolves the direction of nested blocks from their own first strong character` (`packages/session-ui/component-tests/markdown.spec.ts:815`). It mounts a fixture whose message opens with a Latin heading and then carries Persian content in a list (one RTL item, one LTR item), a blockquote paragraph and a table cell, waits for the fixture's `data-markdown-ready` attribute, and measures the computed `unicode-bidi` plus the visual order of each block's first and last text node in the browser. The test is a real regression test — it fails on the unpatched stylesheet and passes with the fix: - `bun run test:components markdown.spec.ts -g "resolves the direction of nested blocks"` on the pristine `markdown.css` → **1 failed** - the same command with this patch → **1 passed** - `bun run test:components markdown.spec.ts` → **29 passed** - `bun run typecheck` (`tsgo -b`) → exit 0 - `oxlint markdown.spec.ts` → 0 errors, 0 warnings ### Screenshots / recordings Not included — the measurements above are the difference between the two runs. Before the fix the nested blocks compute `unicode-bidi: isolate` and their first text node sits to the left of the last one; after it they compute `plaintext` and the RTL blocks order right-to-left. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Related: #26915, #50746

prs.title: fix(app): report composer attachment failures through onError
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #53867

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The composer starts attachment work without awaiting it — `void attachments.handlePaste(event)` and `void attachments.handleDrop(event)` in `packages/app/src/composer/editor/interaction.ts`, `void attachments.addAttachments(files)` from the editor's own drop handling, and the document-level `drop` listener, which cannot await either. Persisting an attachment can fail: `addAttachments` awaits the draft store (a rejected write when the destination cannot be written) and reads the file bytes before deciding between the inline and the upload path. `createComposerAttachments` already takes an `onError` callback, and `pick()` already routes its rejection there, but nothing connected that callback to a rejected `addAttachments`/`handlePaste`/`handleDrop`, so the failure escaped as an unhandled rejection and the composer showed nothing at all.

Every entry point now goes through one small wrapper that delivers the rejection to `input.onError`:

```ts
const report = <T>(operation: Promise<T>) => operation.catch(input.onError)
```

`addAttachments`, `handlePaste` and `handleDrop` are returned and registered through it, so the same failure reaches the composer whether the attachment arrived by paste, by drop on the composer, or by drop anywhere on the document. The promise shape is unchanged — the wrapper returns the operation's promise, so callers that await keep seeing the resolution value (or, for a caller that grew its own `.then`, no change beyond the rejection now also being reported).

This follows the path the file already uses for `pick()`, which does `.then(done).catch(input.onError)`.

### How did you verify your code works?

New `packages/app/test-browser/composer-attachment-errors.test.ts`, two cases that drive the real `createComposerAttachments` under Solid's `createRoot` with a draft store that rejects:

- an inline attachment (`addAttachments`) reports the failure to `onError` — the promise still settles, it does not reject
- a document-level `drop` reports the failure to `onError` instead of rejecting into the void

Both cases are a real gate: with only the source change reverted (the test kept in place), both fail, the second one on the unhandled rejection the report is about.

- `bun test test-browser/composer-attachment-errors.test.ts` → 2 pass / 0 fail

prs.title: fix(core): reconcile compatibility watches instead of rebuilding them
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54114

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`opencode.config.compatibility` rebuilt its watches every time it saw a change. `refresh()` opened with `FiberMap.clear(watches)` and then re-subscribed each compatibility directory, which defeats the `onlyIfMissing: true` on the `FiberMap.run` inside `watch()`: an event reaching the 100 ms debounce tore down every watch and attached them again, and attaching a subscription publishes again, so the debounce was handed a fresh event to consume. On a project with `./.agents/skills` the service settled into that cycle — `watcher subscribe` for that path grew without bound while no file changed, pinning the service at ~37% CPU and filling the log.

The change reconciles instead of clearing: build the plan of directories that should be watched, `FiberMap.remove` the keys that dropped out of it, and subscribe only the keys that are not already present. A directory whose resolved path has not changed keeps its watch, so there is no re-subscription to publish an event and the cycle has nothing left to sustain it.

I took this shape from the two places in the codebase that already work this way — `Config.reconcileWatches` in `packages/core/src/config.ts`, and `ConfigSkillPlugin.watchDirectory`. `refresh()` keeps its `lock.withPermit`, so the plan is not raced.

One honest limit: I could not reproduce the reporter's trigger here — it needs Linux inotify and, per the triage thread, the data directory coinciding with the config directory. What I verified is the mechanism the report named, watches being cleared and rebuilt per event, and that it is gone.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added `keeps a compatibility watch instead of rebuilding it on every event` to `packages/core/test/config/skill.test.ts`. It starts the plugin under the existing `Watcher.Test` layer, which records every `subscribe` call, asserts the compatibility directory is watched once, emits a single update beneath that directory, and asserts the directory is still subscribed exactly once. That last assertion fails on the unmodified source — the re-subscription this report is about is precisely what it catches — and passes with the change.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #54180

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Declining a tool call settles the turn through a bare `Effect.interrupt` with no reason recorded, so the settle path reads it as a `"shutdown"` interrupt. The claim therefore survives the drain, and the declined turn resumes after a server restart.

The fix gives that interrupt a name so the settle path can tell a deliberate user stop from a shutdown:

- `Coordinator` gains `stopReason(key, reason)` (`packages/core/src/session/run-coordinator.ts`), which writes `execution.interruptionReason`.
- The drain input contract gains `reportDeclined` (`packages/core/src/session/runner/index.ts`).
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts` calls `input.reportDeclined()` **before** its bare `Effect.interrupt`, and `runner/llm.ts` threads the callback from the drain input into the step.
- `packages/core/src/session/execution.ts` wires it to `coordinator.stopReason(sessionID, "user")`.

The settle path already does the right thing once the reason is not `"shutdown"` — `jobs.cancel` runs and the claim is released — so the declined turn no longer resurrects.

prs.title: fix(core): filter denied providers from the integration registry
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54145

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`enabled_providers` (and the `provider.use` deny statements it normalizes to) trims the provider catalog, but `/connect` reads a different registry: the integrations behind `integration.list`. So a machine locked to one custom provider still offered OpenCode Console, openai, github-copilot, amazon-bedrock, azure, Cloudflare, digitalocean and gitlab in the connect dialog.

A provider and the integration it connects through are the same identity. The catalog that defines a provider now records that identity on the integration it registers (`Integration.markProvider`, called from `plugin/models-dev.ts` and `config/plugin/provider.ts`), and the terminal policy transform removes an integration whose marker a `provider.use` statement denies. The filter reads the policy statements itself rather than a set another catalog produced, because the two catalogs fold independently: under `State.batch` each folds lazily on its own read, so a denied provider is already gone from the provider catalog by the time the integration catalog is folded.

Integrations registered under their own ID, such as the OAuth integration a remote MCP server registers (`mcp_<hash>`), carry no marker and stay governed by `integration.use`, so a provider allowlist does not hide MCP servers from the dialog.

`specs/v2/provider-policy.md` gains the same statement in the "Applying Provider Policy" section. The spec also lists a `hosted:<integration ID>` resource of `integration.use` that no code consumes yet; this change keys off `provider.use`, because that is what the legacy lists migrate to. Say the word if the `integration.use` spelling is the intended surface and I will switch.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/core/test/config/policy.test.ts` activates the models.dev and policy plugins inside a single `State.batch` — the shape real plugin activation uses — and asserts on `Integration.Service.list()`, the call `/api/integration` serves to `/connect`: a wildcard deny with one allow leaves only the allowed provider's integration, an `mcp_*` integration stays, lifting the deny restores the integration, and a config change reaches the registry without a manual reload. Deleting the `markProvider` call from `plugin/models-dev.ts` makes the batch case fail, so it exercises the mechanism instead of passing vacuously. `packages/core/test/fixture/policy.ts` needed an `integration` stub, because the shared host fake `die`s on services a plugin does not declare.

`packages/cli/src/commands/commands.ts` declare no params either, so both flags are rejected
outright with `Unrecognized flag: --standalone in command opencode mcp list`.

Commands that already behave correctly (`auth …`, `models`, `reload`, `session …`) declare
`...ServerParams` and pass `{ server: Option.getOrUndefined(input.server), standalone:
input.standalone }` into `resolve`. This PR does the same for the eight commands above:

- `packages/cli/src/commands/commands.ts` — `debug agents` / `debug config` / `mcp list`
  gain `params: ServerParams`; `mcp auth`, `mcp logout`, `plugin list`, `plugin check` and
  `plugin update` gain `...ServerParams` in their existing params objects.
- `mcp/list.ts`, `mcp/logout.ts`, `plugin/list.ts`, `debug/agents.ts`, `debug/config.ts` —
  the handler now takes its `input` and threads both flags into `ServerConnection.resolve`.
- `mcp/auth.ts` — the inner `authenticate` helper switches from `(name?: string)` to the
  command input so it can read both flags; `name` is still read with `Option.getOrUndefined`.
- `plugin/inventory.ts` — `inspect()` is shared by `plugin check` and `plugin update`, so its
  signature becomes `(args: ServerConnection.Args, selected?: string)` and it forwards `args`
  to `resolve`. `services/updater.ts` does not call `inspect()`, so nothing outside the
  command surface changes.

The fix is confined to the CLI: no server, protocol or schema surface is touched.

- a functional case that drives `mcp list --server <url>` against a local `Bun.serve` with

prs.title: fix(core): ask before shell commands in plan mode
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #53955

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

In Plan mode the agent is supposed to plan, not mutate the repository. The Plan agent's
permission set in `packages/core/src/plugin/plan.ts` denies the `edit` tool outside the Plan
directory, but it never declares a rule for the `shell` tool. `Permission.evaluate` uses
`findLast`, so every shell command falls through to the agent default (`* -> allow`) and
`bash` / `python` / `git` / `rm` / `mv` all run without any prompt. The Plan system reminder
is the only thing asking the model not to change files, and a model that ignores it can edit
the worktree through the shell — which is exactly what #53955 reports (the reporter saw a
shell command create `src/repl.rs`, edit and delete `src/main.rs`, and run `git add` /
`git commit` with no permission prompt).

The published agent docs describe Plan mode as setting both file edits **and** bash to
`ask`, so this is the documented behaviour not being implemented rather than a new policy.

The change is one additive rule:

```ts
item.permissions.push({ action: "shell", resource: "*", effect: "ask" })
```

The action string is `"shell"`, not `"bash"`: that is the tool's own `export const name =
"shell"`, and it is what `tool/plugin/shell.ts` passes to `permission.assert`. Read-only
commands keep working after one confirmation, while a destructive command now has to be
approved. `explore` is deliberately left alone — other built-in agents stay on the `* -> allow`
default, which an existing `test/agent.test.ts` case pins.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added a case to the existing `plan plugin mutations` block in
`packages/core/test/plugin/plan.test.ts`:

```ts
it.effect("asks before running shell commands", () =>
  Effect.gen(function* () {
    const { planAgent } = yield* run()
    expect(Permission.evaluate("shell", "ls", planAgent.permissions).effect).toBe("ask")
    expect(Permission.evaluate("shell", "rm -rf src", planAgent.permissions).effect).toBe("ask")
  }),
)
```

Red-baselined both ways on the current `v2` tip: with only the source hunk reverted to stock
the new case fails (`12 pass / 1 fail`, reading `allow`), and with the change it passes
(`13 pass / 0 fail`). `tsgo -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.tests.json` is clean for `packages/core`
and `oxlint` reports 0 warnings / 0 errors on both files.

prs.title: fix(core): ignore a corrupt cached project id
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #53991

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A git repo whose `.git/opencode` cache file holds control bytes (the report shows 40 NUL bytes) resolved to that value as its project id. `Project.cached()` read the file, called `trim()`, and handed whatever survived to `ID.make()`. `trim()` only strips whitespace, so NUL bytes passed through untouched and became the id.

The id is not just an opaque key: it is used as a path segment for the shell output directory (`<data>/shell/<id>`). A NUL byte in a path makes every later filesystem call fail with `path ... without null bytes`, which is the `UnexpectedStatus: 500` in the report, and the TUI cannot offer model selection for that project. Because the cached value was treated as authoritative, the same broken id was re-derived on every resolve — so the stale row stayed in `project` and the failure repeated, as @layermedya noted.

This change treats a cached value carrying control characters as absent, so resolution falls through to the sources that already work — @layermedya confirmed renaming `.git` away resolves the directory to a valid id. The cache stays a convenience rather than an authority: a corrupt file no longer becomes the id. `git log` on the region shows `cached()` was added as a fast path in front of the real resolution sources; rejecting a value that cannot be a valid id keeps that contract, and a usable cached value is still used unchanged.

### How did you verify your code works?

Two tests in `packages/core/test/project.test.ts`, beside the existing "returns previous cached id from common dir":

- `keeps a usable cached id` — a normal cached value is still used as both `previous` and `id`, so the fast path is unchanged.
- `ignores a corrupt cached id` — a cache file of 40 NUL bytes: `previous` is `undefined`, `id` resolves to the root commit id from the normal source, and the id contains no NUL byte.

Red/green on `v2` at `1a8988efe0`, pinned bun 1.4.2:

- before: `ignores a corrupt cached id` fails because `Received` is 40 NUL bytes instead of `undefined`
- after: both new tests pass

Full `packages/core` suite: 6519 pass / 49 fail after, versus 6518 pass / 50 fail before — the single delta is this new test. The 49 remaining failures are pre-existing on this machine and unrelated (pty, `Session.shell`, real-shell and ripgrep-dependent tests fail in this sandbox).

Also clean: `tsgo -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.tests.json` for `packages/core`, and oxlint on both edited files.

prs.title: fix(core): migrate V1 messages that predate required metadata
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #53971

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The V1 to V2 migration validates every legacy row against the current `SessionV1.Info`, so messages written before `agent`, the user `model` and the assistant `parentID` became required (OpenCode <= 1.0.65) fail decoding and are dropped one by one. When a session's rows all fail it lands in `session_v2` with no `session_message` rows at all, so the history disappears even though the V1 rows are intact. #53971 measured 4867 dropped rows and 64 empty sessions, and #52226 is the same shape.

Those fields are metadata rather than conversation content, so this recovers them in the migrator, immediately before the decode, instead of losing the history:

- `agent`: the row's own value, then `mode` (the pre-rename name of the field, which rows of that era carry), then the reply that handled the turn, then the session row, then the built-in default.
- user `model`: the reply that handled the turn, then the session row.
- assistant `parentID`: the nearest earlier user message, using the ordering the projection already relies on.

`packages/schema` is untouched; `SessionV1` stays the strict contract for current rows, so nothing else that decodes V1 data changes behaviour.

Rows that still cannot be resolved keep being dropped, but their `invalid-message` warning now names the fields no source could supply, so an operator can find the sessions that need a manual value instead of only a message id. Field-level detail for other undecodable shapes is #42671's scope, not duplicated here.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/core/test/v1-migration.test.ts` gains two cases built from the <= 1.0.65 row shapes: one where the metadata is derivable (both rows now migrate, in the right order, and the session picks up the agent and model) and one where it is not (the warning names `model` and `parentID`).

Red baseline: with the source reverted and only the new test in place, the derivable case fails with both rows reported as `invalid-message` for a session that should have migrated completely.

    bun test test/v1-migration.test.ts                                         # 28 pass
    bun test test/v1-migration.test.ts test/database.test.ts \

prs.title: fix(core): retry the WAL switch when another connection holds the lock
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes the `database is locked` half of #53879. The `CREATE TABLE ... already
exists` half is open in #50344 and is not duplicated here, so this does not
close the issue on its own.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`sqlite.bun.ts` and `sqlite.node.ts` switch a new database to WAL right after
opening it. That switch takes an exclusive lock, and SQLite does not run the
busy handler for a journal-mode change, so when two processes open the same
fresh database at the same moment the second one gets `SQLITE_BUSY`
immediately and the connection layer dies.

This retries the pragma while the result code is `SQLITE_BUSY`. Once either
connection has completed the switch the file is already WAL and the pragma just
reports that mode, so the retry converges at once.

I tried the `busy_timeout` route first, since #50344 sets it before the WAL
switch, and it does not cover this: with `busy_timeout = 5000` in place the
losing process still failed at about 5 ms, nowhere near the timeout. That is
why this is a retry and not a longer timeout.

### How did you verify your code works?

Two processes started together over one fresh database, the shape of the repro
in the issue.

Building only the connection layer, which is where this change lives:

- current `v2`: 7 of 8 runs lost a process, each with `SQLiteError: database is
  locked` at about 5 ms.
- with this change: 0 of 8.

Running the full bootstrap on the same two processes, this change still loses a
process occasionally on `v2` and the error is `table account_state already
exists`. That is the other half of the issue, the one #50344 closes by moving
the emptiness check into `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and I left it alone. The two
changes are independent; whichever lands second only needs a rebase.

`packages/core/test/database.test.ts` gains a test that holds the write lock
from a second connection while `Database.layer` opens the file. It fails on
current `v2` (`SQLITE_BUSY` at 7 ms) and passes with this change, after waiting
out the lock. `bun test test/database.test.ts test/database-migration.test.ts
test/database-drizzle.test.ts` is 32 pass. `tsgo -b`, `oxlint` and `prettier`
are clean.

### Screenshots / recordings

_Not a UI change._

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(core): follow a retargeted plugin directory symlink
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #53763

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A local plugin whose config-dir entry is a **directory symlink** is dropped from the running server once that symlink is repointed at another directory — what nix, home-manager, stow and dotfiles scripts do on update. The next reload of each Location, and every Location created afterwards, leaves it out, with no `failed` entry in `/api/plugin` and no log line. A restart loads the new target fine.

`ConfigPluginSource.scan` asked the runtime for the directory's entrypoints and then verified they stay inside that directory:

```ts
const entrypoints = Host.resolve({ directory: operation.target })
const root = await fs.resolve(operation.target)             // fresh realpath: the new target
const server = await fs.resolve(fileURLToPath(entrypoint))  // the runtime's cached old target
if (!FSUtil.contains(root, server)) return []
```

The runtime resolves a symlinked directory once and keeps that resolution for the life of the process, so after a retarget it kept reporting the old target while `fs.resolve` saw the new one. The two disagreed and the scan dropped the plugin entirely.

`Host.resolve` now follows a directory target's symlink before handing it to the runtime, so the entrypoints it returns belong to the directory's current target and agree with a fresh `fs.resolve`. That is one step in the shared resolver rather than one at each call site that happened to hit the stale cache: the TUI plugin loader (`packages/tui/src/plugin/context.tsx`) and `opencode plugin list` pass local plugin directories through `Host.resolve` too, and would otherwise keep resolving to a previous target. `PluginModule.load` re-resolves the entrypoint when it loads the plugin, so it needs this as much as the scan does — without it, a retargeted plugin goes on loading the previous target's code.

A directory that does not exist keeps resolving to no entrypoints instead of throwing, which is how a missing entrypoint already behaved.

While there I added a log line to the containment-rejection path. That path drops a plugin that exists and lives inside the config, and previously left no trace of why.

### How did you verify your code works?

Three tests, each checked against the unmodified source first:

- `packages/plugin/test/host.test.ts`, "resolves a directory symlink to its current target after it is retargeted" — resolve a symlinked plugin directory, repoint the symlink, resolve again and require the second directory's entrypoint. Against the unmodified `Host.resolve` the second assertion still reports the first directory.
- `packages/core/test/plugin/source.test.ts` — a config document pointing at a symlinked plugin directory; assert the scan lists the operation, repoint the symlink at a second directory, assert the next scan lists it again. On the unmodified source the second assertion sees `[]`.
- `packages/core/test/plugin/module.test.ts`, "follows a plugin directory symlink retargeted since the previous load" — load the plugin, repoint the symlink, load again and require the second directory's plugin. On the unmodified source the second load returns the first directory's plugin.

`packages/plugin` is 11 pass / 0 fail. `packages/core/test/plugin/` is 387 tests with 4 `supervisor-reload`/external-plugin timeouts, which appear in a different combination on each run of the *same* code, with and without this change (the previous tip of this branch measured 3 pass / 5 fail on that file alone). `tsgo --noEmit` is clean for both packages and `oxlint` reports nothing on the changed files.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(mcp): settle the tool registry when the server set changes
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #51089

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`mcp.add` answered 204 as soon as `Mcp.Service.add` resolved. That call awaits the connection, so `GET /api/mcp` already reports `connected`, but the registry a step reads is separate state: it only reloads when the `ToolsChanged` event reaches `McpTool` and the 100 ms debounce in front of `reconcile` fires. The only settle point, `McpTool.flush`, waits for the initial discovery, so `session/context.ts` could build the first step after `mcp.add` from the pre-add catalog. `mcp.remove` has the mirror problem: the removed server's tools linger until the debounce fires.

This keeps the debounce for background announcements and adds an explicit settle point for the routes that change the server set:

- `McpTool` exposes `refresh`, which re-reads `Mcp.tools()` and reloads the registry under the same semaphore the debounced path uses, so a refresh cannot interleave with a queued one.
- `mcp.add` / `mcp.remove` / `mcp.connect` / `mcp.disconnect` await it after the mutation, so answering 204 means the registry already reflects the change.

`flush` is unchanged: it stays the cheap "wait for the initial registration" that `SessionContext.select` awaits on every step.

Targeted at `v2` because `packages/core/src/tool/mcp.ts` and `packages/server/src/handlers/mcp.ts` do not exist on `dev`. `#51812` is the same family from a different trigger (first prompt after boot, no `mcp.add` involved) and is out of scope here.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test `refreshes the registry for a change that is still debounced` in `packages/core/test/mcp.test.ts`: registers the mock server catalog, changes it, publishes `ToolsChanged`, then awaits `refresh` and asserts the registry already serves the new tool without any clock advance, so the debounced reload cannot be what makes it pass. It fails on the unmodified tree.
- `bun test test/mcp.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 72 pass, 3 fail. Those 3 (`terminates MCP descendants after the wrapper exits successfully`, `MCP connection over the modern protocol`, `discovers and reads MCP resources through Code Mode`) fail identically on the unmodified tree on this machine.
- `tsgo -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.tests.json` in `packages/core`, `tsgo -b` in `packages/server`, and `oxlint` on the three files: clean. The typecheck is what covers the route wiring, since the handlers now require `McpTool.Service`, which the location graph already provides next to `Mcp.Service`.
- No live `PUT` check: every route in `packages/server/test` answers 500 on this machine on the unmodified tree too (`generate.test.ts`, `fs.test.ts`), so the ordering is covered by the test above plus the typecheck.

prs.title: fix(console): answer CORS preflight on every Zen API route
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #52178

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The Zen gateway answered the CORS preflight on the two model-list routes only. Every other route in
`packages/console/app/src/routes/zen/` exported its method handler but no `OPTIONS`, so a browser's
preflight fell through to SolidStart's route-not-found path and came back `404` with no
`Access-Control-Allow-*` header. The real request was never sent, while a plain `GET /zen/v1/models`
kept working - which is what made the gateway look fine from a terminal.

Still reproducible on the deployed site:

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -D - -X OPTIONS https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/messages \
    -H "Origin: http://localhost:8000" -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: POST" \
    -H "Access-Control-Request-Headers: x-api-key"
HTTP/2 404
```

This PR exports `OPTIONS` from every remaining route behind the gateway, answering it with the same
`buildOptionsResponse()` the two model-list routes already use:

- `/zen/v1/chat/completions`, `/zen/v1/messages`, `/zen/v1/responses`, `/zen/v1/systemone`,
  `/zen/v1/models/{model}`
- `/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`, `/zen/go/v1/messages`, `/zen/go/v1/responses`,
  `/zen/go/v1/systemone`, `/zen/go/v1/usage`

It also widens `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` to the key headers the gateway reads today:
`lib/inference-proxy.ts` takes `x-api-key` on the `/messages` routes and `x-goog-api-key` on the
Google route, and `anthropic-version` is forwarded to the inference service along with the rest of
the client's headers. The deployed preflight answers with `Content-Type, Authorization` alone, so
even the two routes that do answer the preflight are rejected by a browser as soon as an Anthropic or
Google client sends its key:

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -D - -X OPTIONS https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models \
    -H "Origin: http://localhost:8000" -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: GET"
access-control-allow-headers: Content-Type, Authorization
```

`OPTIONS` is served locally and never reaches the database, the rate limiters or the inference proxy,
so the change adds no cost to the real request path.

This is the preflight half of CORS only. The actual `POST`/`GET` responses are proxied to the
inference service and the console app adds no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` to them, so a browser
reads them only when that service supplies the header itself (the model-list routes answer with
`access-control-allow-origin: *` today, the `POST` routes do not). That app-side change is #41224,
which was closed as not planned, and this PR deliberately does not touch it.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/console/app/test/zenCors.test.ts` is new. It imports each route module through the same
`APIEvent` shape the server uses and calls `OPTIONS` directly, asserting `200` with
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, `POST` in `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`, and all five allowed
request headers present - one case per route, twelve in total. The resource layer
(`@opencode/console-resource`) is stubbed, because the route modules reach `lib/inference-proxy`,
which resolves SST-backed bindings at import time and a preflight never gets that far.

The assertions are on the preflight answers only, so on an unmodified tip the new file fails for every
route - the ten that export no `OPTIONS` at all, and the two whose `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`
omits the key headers - rather than passing vacuously.

`bun test` in `packages/console/app` passes: 12 new tests, 37 in the package. `oxlint` is clean on the
changed files. The only `tsgo --noEmit` diagnostic is `src/lib/aws.ts(2,27): Cannot find module
'aws4fetch'`, reported in my checkout because that dependency is not installed there; it is declared
in this package's `package.json` and unrelated to this change.

### Rebased onto the current default branch

The Zen routes were rewritten to delegate to `lib/inference-proxy` while this PR was open, and
`/zen/v1/systemone`, `/zen/go/v1/systemone` and `/zen/go/v1/usage` are served through the gateway as
well now, so the fix was re-applied on the current tip: the same `OPTIONS` export goes on all ten
routes that lack it, and each is covered by the test. The `zen/util` modules the earlier description
quoted (`handler.ts`, `provider/anthropic.ts`) no longer exist, so the header list above is justified
against `lib/inference-proxy.ts`, which is what reads those headers today.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(core): attribute migrated V1 sessions to the project of their directory
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #51176

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

The V1 to V2 migration copies legacy sessions as they are, and parks a session under the `global` pseudo-project whenever its `project_id` is not in the destination `project` table. V1 showed sessions by directory, so those rows stayed reachable there; V2 lists sessions per project, so after the migration they disappear from the directory that owns them. The transcript is intact, only the attribution is wrong.

The runtime already knows how to re-own such a row: `SessionProjector` adopts a session whose project is `global` (or the directory's previous identity) when `Worktree.Event.Resolved` fires for its directory. The migration never did the same, so a session copied after its directory had already been resolved stayed under `global` for good.

The migration now attributes a `global` session to the most specific known project directory containing it, using `project.worktree` together with the directories in the `worktree` table, and stores the subpath that directory implies. A session whose directory no project owns still falls back to `global` exactly as before, and the existing warning for a missing project is unchanged.

A database whose migration already completed is repaired the same way on the next start, so an existing install recovers without the `session move` workaround from the report.

The repair only touches rows this migration parked: a row whose project was already corrected by hand is left alone, including one that stays hidden because its `path` was never filled in. That state is only reachable by editing the database directly, so it is a note rather than a code path — `SELECT id, project_id, directory, path FROM session_v2 WHERE path IS NULL` lists the rows and they need the subpath their project implies (`''` at the project root; `NULL` does not match) or a `session move`.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/core/test/v1-migration.test.ts` gains two cases, both going through the real migration entry point (`V1Migration.run`), not a helper:

prs.title: fix(cli): read the api request body from a file or stdin
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #51199

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`opencode api` can only take the request body as an inline `--data` string. On Windows PowerShell and
cmd the shell splits an argument on whitespace before the CLI parses it, so a JSON body containing
spaces never arrives intact: the command answers `Expected a valid JSON body` (HTTP 400) or
`Unexpected positional arguments`. Quoting is the problem, not the fix, because the spaces and the
quotes both have to survive the same split.

`--data` now accepts the two sources curl uses for exactly this reason:

- `--data @body.json` reads the body from a file
- `--data @-` reads the body from stdin
- an inline value behaves exactly as before

The argument then contains no spaces, so there is nothing for the shell to split. This also helps
anywhere a body is long or generated rather than typed.

The change is confined to the `api` handler. `resolveBody` resolves the source before the request is
sent and fails through the existing `Error` path with the reason attached; the flag description
documents both new sources. Inline handling is untouched, so current callers are unaffected.

### How did you verify your code works?

`cd packages/cli && bun test --timeout 30000` — 9 pass, 0 fail. New cases cover an inline body used
unchanged, `@file`, a body file that cannot be read, a bare `@`, `@-` from stdin, and one case that
drives the real `api` handler against a local server and asserts the file body arrives intact with
`content-type: application/json`.

I also checked the new tests fail without the fix: removing the `@` handling from `resolveBody` fails
the file, stdin and command cases; leaving the handler on the raw `--data` value fails the command
case because the server receives the literal `@...` argument.

`bun run typecheck` (tsgo) passes, `bunx prettier --check` is clean, and `bunx oxlint` reports 0 errors
on the touched files (the 3 warnings in `api.ts` are pre-existing).

I did not run the command against a live server. `api` resolves the daemon transport, and
`transport()` is allowed to start or replace the registered server, which I did not want to do from a
development checkout.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #50969

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

On `v2`, `useConnected()` answers "does some integration have connections". On `dev` it answered "is a provider configured". The model dialog kept the old gates after that redefinition, so opening the model list while no integration was connected dropped the local favorites and recents and hid the `model.dialog.favorite` action.

A hidden action is not only invisible. `DialogSelect` registers its keymap entries from `shownActions()`, so with the action hidden nothing is bound to `ctrl+f` at all. That is why the dialog showed no favorite hint and why remapping the keybind to `Alt+F` or `F4` changed nothing: the binding was never registered.

Favorites and recents are client side preference state, so they no longer depend on integration connectivity:

- `showExtra` only checks `props.providerID`, so the Favorites and Recent sections are listed again
- the favorites list is read unconditionally while building the options
- the `model.dialog.favorite` action is always shown, which restores its hint and its keybinding

The integration entry (`model.dialog.provider`, titled `Connect an integration` / `View all integrations`) still depends on `connected()`. It is the one part of this dialog that is actually about integrations, so its gate is kept.

Two tests in `packages/tui/test/component/dialog-model.test.tsx` mount the real `DialogModel` on the `renderLocal` fixture, which serves no `/api/integration` route and therefore has no connected integration:
