prs.title: fix(web-shell): avoid flashing the credential form during boot token verification
prs.body:
## What this PR does The standalone auth gate now keeps a neutral `Connecting…` state while its first `/capabilities` probe verifies a credential supplied at boot, instead of painting the daemon-address and Bearer-token form for that round trip. The form is rendered only when the probe actually needs input: a 401/403, a network failure, or the 10-second timeout. The behavior is shared by the desktop shell and browser launches (`qwen serve --open`, `?daemon=`); there is no launcher-specific branch. The token probe, retry loop, 401 recovery, `role="status"` live region, and focus ordering are unchanged. ## Why it's needed Every cold start with a valid startup token briefly showed the full "Connect to Qwen Code" card before `/capabilities` resolved. The masked Bearer-token field was initialized from that startup token, so the window looked like a login prompt even though no credentials were needed. The card disappeared as soon as the probe returned 200; this is a visual-trust problem, not an authentication failure. Fixes #14755. ## Reviewer Test Plan ### How to verify 1. Launch Qwen Code Desktop with a valid startup token, or run `qwen serve --open` and open the printed URL. 2. Watch the window between the splash/page load and the workspace. The "Connect to Qwen Code" card with the daemon address and masked Bearer token must not appear. 3. Force a rejected credential (restart the daemon with a different token, or open a URL with a stale token). The gate must show the credential form with the invalid/expired-token copy. 4. Make the daemon unreachable or stall `/capabilities`. After the probe timeout, the gate must show the retry/form state. Expected: on the happy path the workspace appears without the credential form; every recovery path still exposes the form. ### Evidence (Before & After) Screen recordings supplied by the author (attach the three GIFs here before marking ready): - `splash-main.gif` — current `main`: the credential card is visible during the startup probe. - `splash-branch.gif` — this PR: the credential form is not painted; the workspace follows the brief neutral state. - `splash-branch-3s-delayed.gif` — this PR with a temporary 3-second probe delay, to make the neutral state observable. ### Tested on | OS | Status | | :--------: | :----: | | 🍏 macOS | N/A | | 🪟 Windows | ✅ | | 🐧 Linux | N/A | Windows: `StandaloneAuth.test.tsx` 55/55, `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, and Prettier. The desktop WebView was not rebuilt locally because this machine has no Rust/VC++ toolchain; the UI change is in the shared Web Shell component. ### Environment (optional) - `cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/StandaloneAuth.test.tsx` - Browser Web Shell served by Vite against the bundled daemon runtime for the visual checks. ## Risk & Scope - Main risk or tradeoff: if `/capabilities` is slow, the gate shows the neutral state for up to the 10-second probe timeout; the form then returns, and no auth check is skipped. - Not validated / out of scope: a rebuilt macOS/Linux desktop binary and an actual desktop WebView check on those platforms. - Breaking changes / migration notes: none. ## Linked Issues Fixes #14755.

prs.title: fix(core): key tool retry-loop counter on tool and cause class, not message text (#13073)
prs.body:
Fixes #13073 (item 1).

## Linked Issues

- `Fixes #13073` (item 1 — retry-loop counter keying; item 2 is separable and left for a follow-up)

## Root cause

`recordBatchRetryableToolError` (`packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts:2979`) keyed the validation retry counter on `` `${toolName}:${errorMessage}` `` — the tool name plus the **verbatim** error message. The #12970 reporter's six failures spanned three differently-worded messages for one root cause, so each wording started a fresh counter, the sibling-key pruning deleted the previous one, and `RETRY_LOOP_STOP_DIRECTIVE` never fired — six failures burned ~15 tool calls.

## What this PR changes

The counter key becomes `${toolName}:${causeClass}` where `causeClass` is a stable identifier (`'validation'` or `'truncation'`) chosen at the three call sites:

| Call site | causeClass | Directive family |
|---|---|---|
| bridge `INVALID_TOOL_PARAMS` pre-validation (`:3030`) | `'validation'` | `RETRY_LOOP_STOP_DIRECTIVE` |
| `Kind.Edit` truncated-write rejection (`:3187`) | `'truncation'` | `TRUNCATION_RETRY_LOOP_DIRECTIVE` |
| general invocation-validation failure (`:3266`) | `'validation'` | `RETRY_LOOP_STOP_DIRECTIVE` |

Differently-worded failures for the same tool and cause now accumulate toward `VALIDATION_RETRY_LOOP_THRESHOLD = 3`; the two classes stay separate so each directive keeps matching its own failure family. Under the coarser key the sibling-key pruning loops (in both `recordRetryableToolError` and the batch wrapper) and the batch wrapper's cross-batch counter restore become dead code and are removed.

The `Kind.Edit` narrow-key improvement #12982 landed is preserved: truncated-Edit rejections for the same tool share one counter and still reach the threshold.

## Preserved behavior

- Same-message repeated failures still count and still fire the directive at the threshold (existing test unchanged, green).
- Identical failures within one model-response batch are counted once (batch dedupe keyed on the new stable key; existing test unchanged, green).
- Counters are still pruned for tools absent from the current batch (`:2940-2955` — the prune parses the tool name before the first `:`, which matches the new key shape).
- `MAX_UNCONFIRMED_FORGET_DELETIONS` and the `/forget` model pin are untouched (different file, not part of this change).

## Risk & Scope

- **Coarser keying**: two genuinely different validation causes on the same tool now share one counter, so the stop directive can fire at the threshold across mixed causes. The directive is advisory text appended to the error (not a hard block), and the reporter's triage explicitly asks for accumulation across wording variants. If maintainers want finer separation, the natural extension is a cause-identifier returned by each validation site — a larger change touching each tool.
- **Item 2 of #13073** (per-call admission in multi-call turns) is intentionally out of scope: it is the scheduler's batch admission path, a different mechanism from the counter keying here. Separable per the maintainer's ruling on #12982.

## Tests

- New discriminating test: `accumulates differently-worded validation failures for the same tool into one counter (#13073)` — three validation failures across three turns with two distinct wordings trip the directive at the third turn. **Red under the old per-message keying (verified by stashing the source change), green at this head.**
- The mixed-error batch test's comment is updated to the new (tool, cause-class) semantics; its assertions still pass under both keyings (batch dedupe dominates within a batch).
- Full `coreToolScheduler.test.ts`: **467 / 467 green**.

## How to verify

1. Re-run `npx vitest run src/core/coreToolScheduler.test.ts` in `packages/core` — 467/467.
2. Reviewer probe for the old behavior: `git stash push -- packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts && npx vitest run src/core/coreToolScheduler.test.ts -t 'accumulates differently-worded'` → the new test goes red (counter restarts on wording change); `git stash pop` → green.
3. Wire-level check is not needed: the change is scheduler-internal state only (no request payload, no provider interaction).

## Tested on

| OS | Node | Result |
|---|---|---|
| darwin (aarch64) | v26.7.0 | coreToolScheduler.test.ts 467/467; prettier clean |

## 中文说明

<details>
<summary>根因与修法（中文）</summary>

`recordBatchRetryableToolError` 原本以 `toolName:errorMessage`（逐字错误消息）作为校验重试计数器的 key。#12970 报告者的六次失败横跨三条不同措辞的消息（同一根因），每条措辞各自开新计数器、旧计数器被同工具兄弟 key 清理逻辑删除，导致 `RETRY_LOOP_STOP_DIRECTIVE` 永不触发——六次失败烧掉约 15 次工具调用。

本 PR 把计数器 key 改为 `toolName:causeClass`，causeClass 是三个调用点上选定的稳定标识（`'validation'` 或 `'truncation'`）：同工具同因类别的不同措辞失败现在向同一计数器累积；两个类别保持独立，使 truncation 指令与通用 stop 指令各自匹配自己的失败族。在更粗的 key 下，两个函数里的兄弟 key 清理循环与 batch 包装层的跨批计数恢复都成为死代码，已移除。#12982 落地的 Kind.Edit 收窄 key 行为被保留。

新增判别测试：同一工具三次校验失败、横跨两种措辞，第三次触发 stop 指令（在旧 keying 下已实测变红）。`coreToolScheduler.test.ts` 467/467 全绿。item 2（multi-call turn 逐个准入）按维护者在 #12982 的裁定属可分离项，留作后续。

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): stop double-truncating web_fetch and keep the full text recoverable
prs.body:
> Split part ③ of #13652. Stacked on part ② (`feat/tool-result-recoverable-preview`).

## What this PR does

This PR keeps the full fetched text recoverable after web_fetch and the scheduler reduce the model-visible preview. web_fetch used to pre-cut every page with a private 100k `truncateText`, and the scheduler's 25k budget then cut the assembled body again — the model saw a twice-truncated page with no way back to the full text. The producer now keeps the complete extracted text, persists it through the shared spill path, marks the cache entry as reduced (tracked by content identity, so a failed spill write never fakes a recovery path), and adds a header line pointing the model at the saved file so read_file can page the full text back in. Because web_fetch's model-visible body starts with a metadata header rather than the truncation sentinel, the persistence gate no longer treats the starts-with check as idempotency proof for web_fetch — the tool goes through the same gate as every other tool. The preapproved-markdown passthrough now requires that nothing was reduced, since the producer's own stub lands just under the length cap.

## Why it's needed

Double truncation silently destroyed fetch fidelity (review threads R2-3 and R10-3 on #13652), and the previously truncated body had no recovery path at all: the model could not page the full page even when the answer was in the discarded middle.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` (both pass), then in `packages/core`: `npx vitest run src/tools/web-fetch.test.ts src/core/coreToolScheduler.test.ts src/tools/truncation.test.ts` — locally 678/678 passed. Behaviorally: fetch a large page, confirm the model-visible body carries the "Full extracted text saved to: …" header line, that a follow-up read_file against that path returns the discarded middle of the page, and that the full-text recovery pointer survives the scheduler's 25k budget pass. A large page can produce two artifacts: the complete producer text and a second copy of the reduced preview from the persistence gate.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (tool-internal behavior; verified by the unit suites above).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: removing the starts-with exemption for web_fetch means its bodies always traverse the persistence gate; the gate can persist the reduced preview again, while the producer artifact retains the complete text.
- Not validated / out of scope: an actual model read-back on this exact head and full CI on the stacked base are not established by the unit-test report above. The stacked tree equals the reviewed #13652 head modulo one main-side refresh of `hosted-workspace-tool-turn.test.ts`.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Split part ③ of #13652. Stacked on #14546.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

prs.title: feat(core): account tool result sizes from producer to injection
prs.body:
> Split part ① of #13652. Stacked at the bottom: part ② is #14546, part ③ is #14547.

## What this PR does

This PR makes every tool result carry an honest size story from the moment a tool produces it to the moment it is injected into a model request. A new measurement helper sizes `PartListUnion` payloads (text plus structured functionResponse values, with image estimates taken from the chat-compression config), and a small provenance record — raw size, applied budget, budget source, truncated flag — rides on the response parts through the persistence gate, the per-tool and combined truncation passes, the batch finalizer, hook rewrites, and the send guard. Each layer logs a `tool_result_size` event, and `LlmChat` logs `tool_result_injected` exactly once per result, pairing the raw size with what actually went to the model.

Producers now declare their raw output size instead of letting the scheduler guess: shell reports an unknown size when capture discarded output, SSH exec and self-bounded read_file/read-many and capped MCP resource reads declare unknown rather than a falsely equal raw size, and grep, ripGrep, web_search and the execution tool report the size of the unbounded body. Post-settlement throws, cancellations and hook replacements are treated as replacement outcomes that inherit nothing from the producer. Loaded or restored history and speculation-accept replays are marked as already injected so a retry never double-counts. To keep that exactly-once guarantee under retry, the dispatch closure now checks the abort signal at the start of every attempt instead of once before the retry loop — an aborted attempt must not run the provenance-marking loop, which would permanently suppress that result's one owed injection event. Abort stays a non-retryable failure, so retry outcomes are unchanged. A design document (EN + zh-CN) describes the accounting model.

## Why it's needed

Token burn from tool results was previously invisible: nothing recorded how large a result was when produced, which layer reduced it, or how much reached the model, so truncation bugs (including the silent self-bounding producers called out in the review of #13652) could not even be observed. This accounting is the foundation parts ② and ③ build on.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` (both pass), then the touched suites in `packages/core`: `npx vitest run src/tools/tool-output-size.test.ts src/tools/tool-response-finalizer.test.ts src/tools/truncation.test.ts src/core/coreToolScheduler.test.ts src/core/llm-chat.test.ts src/followup/speculation.test.ts src/telemetry/loggers.test.ts src/telemetry/metrics.test.ts src/tools/execution-tool.test.ts src/tools/grep.test.ts src/tools/ripGrep.test.ts src/tools/shell.test.ts src/tools/read-file.test.ts src/tools/read-mcp-resource.test.ts src/services/ssh-execution-environment.test.ts src/core/nonInteractiveToolExecutor.test.ts` and in `packages/cli`: `npx vitest run src/ui/hooks/useToolScheduler.test.ts src/serve/hosted-workspace-tool-turn.test.ts`. Locally observed: 1203/1203 then 902/902 passed in core and 283/283 in cli. For behavior, run any session with telemetry on and confirm `tool_result_size` events appear per layer and `tool_result_injected` once per tool call with raw vs injected lengths.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (telemetry and internal accounting; no UI change).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: provenance rides on shared `Part` objects via a symbol; the review threads R10-1/R10-2 from #13652 about mutation after batch-budget cuts carry over here and are called out for the reviewer.
- Not validated / out of scope: the recoverable-preview envelope and the web_fetch changes land in parts ② and ③.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; additive telemetry fields only.

Design docs: docs/design/tool-result-size-accounting.md and docs/design/tool-result-size-accounting.zh-CN.md.

## Linked Issues

Split part ① of #13652 (does not close it; #13652 is closed manually in favor of this stack).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

本 PR 是 #13652 拆分的第一片：让工具结果的大小从产生到注入模型全程可计量。新增测量助手对 `PartListUnion` 负载（文本与结构化 functionResponse，图像按 chat-compression 配置估算）计量，并把原始大小、生效预算、预算来源、截断标记作为 provenance 附带在响应 parts 上，贯穿持久化闸门、per-tool 与 combined 截断、batch finalizer、hook 改写与发送保护。每一层记录 `tool_result_size` 事件，`LlmChat` 对每个结果恰好在注入时记录一次 `tool_result_injected`，对比原始与注入大小。

各 producer 现在如实声明原始输出大小：shell 在 capture 丢弃输出时声明 unknown，SSH exec、自我限长的 read_file/read-many、被截断的 MCP resource 读取声明 unknown 而非谎报相等；grep、ripGrep、web_search 与 execution tool 上报未限长全文的大小。结算后抛错、取消与 hook 替换一律视为替换型结果，不继承 producer 的大小。恢复/加载的历史与 speculation 接受的回放会被标记为已注入，重试不会重复计数。为在重试下保住这一恰好一次的保证，发送闭包改为在每次尝试开头检查 abort 信号（此前只在进入重试循环前检查一次）——被中止的尝试不得执行 provenance 标记循环，否则会永久抑制该结果唯一应得的注入事件；abort 仍不可重试，重试结果不变。设计文档含中英文双版本。

动机：此前工具结果的 token 消耗完全不可见——无法知道结果产生时多大、哪一层削减了它、又有多少进入模型；#13652 评审指出的自我限长 producer 静默问题也因此无法观测。本计量面是第 ② 片与第 ③ 片的基础。

验证：`npm run build` 与 `npm run typecheck` 均通过；上述 core 单测 1203 + 902 全部通过，cli 283 全部通过。风险：provenance 通过 symbol 挂在共享 Part 对象上，#13652 的 R10-1/R10-2 关于 batch 预算变更后可变性的讨论随本片继续。范围外：可恢复预览 envelope 与 web_fetch 改动在第 ②③ 片。无 breaking change。

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): cap the prepare build heap and share the self-hosted Node preflight
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Installing the workspace through `npm ci` / `corepack pnpm install` runs `prepare`, which re-enters the root build. That build compiles `packages/cli`, and the heap headroom the root build script sets for that compile only exists because the root script sets it in `NODE_OPTIONS`; the per-package build script inherits whatever its caller carries, so the install path reached the same compile with the default heap and died of V8 heap exhaustion. This PR gives prepare's build invocation the same headroom, and preserves any `NODE_OPTIONS` the runner already set.

The SDK Java daemon E2E lane on the self-hosted pool carried its own copy of the Node preflight, which only fails when Node is missing entirely. A runner whose Node is merely too old therefore sailed past the check and OOMed inside the build instead of failing fast with the provisioning message. It now uses the shared preflight the other pool lanes already use.

## Why it's needed

`SDK Java (fast)` went red on PR #14737 before a single test ran, and the same signature reproduced on two different hosts (`ecs-qwen-hk3-22`, then `ecs-qwen-hk1-27` after a rerun), so it is not one broken machine. The heap cap introduced earlier (#11781) sits on the root build script only; the install-driven prepare path was never covered by it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the root package-scripts suite, which exercises prepare's step ordering and this new invocation: `npx vitest run scripts/tests/package-scripts.test.js` and `npx vitest run scripts/tests/sdk-java-workflow.test.js`. Both pass. To confirm the cap actually reaches the compile, run prepare with stub `husky`/`npm` on `PATH` and print `NODE_OPTIONS` inside the stubs: before this change the `npm run build` call carries no heap flag; after it, it carries `--max-old-space-size=4096`, and an incoming `NODE_OPTIONS` is kept in front of it. On the pool, the daemon E2E lane should either reach the tests or stop at the preflight with its provisioning message, never at a heap crash.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — CI and build-script change with no user-visible output.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests plus the stub witness above.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the self-hosted preflight now also warns (not fails) when the runner's Node is not 22.x. That warning is the point — a missing Node still fails the job before any build starts, which is the fast failure this issue asked for.
- Not validated / out of scope: whether the ECS hosts are provisioned with Node 22.x and have enough memory. That is an operations action (or flipping the kill-switch to route the lane to hosted runners) and no repository change can substitute for it.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Closes #14823

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

通过 `npm ci` / `corepack pnpm install` 安装工作区会执行 `prepare`，而 `prepare` 会再进入根 `build`。根 `build` 要编译 `packages/cli`，它为这次编译预留的堆余量只存在于根脚本设置的 `NODE_OPTIONS` 里；每个包的构建脚本只是继承调用方传来的值。于是安装路径用默认堆去跑同一段编译，最终因 V8 堆耗尽而失败。本 PR 为 `prepare` 的构建调用补上同样的堆余量，并保留 runner 上已有的 `NODE_OPTIONS`。

自托管池上 SDK Java daemon E2E 车道带有一份自己的 Node 预检，但它只在 Node 完全缺失时才失败。runner 的 Node 只是版本偏旧时会顺利通过该检查，然后在构建中 OOM，而不是以 provisioning 提示快速失败。现在它改用其他池车道已在使用的共享预检。

## 为什么需要

`SDK Java (fast)` 在 PR #14737 上一次测试都没跑就红了，且同一签名在两台不同宿主上复现（先是 `ecs-qwen-hk3-22`，重跑后是 `ecs-qwen-hk1-27`），所以不是单台机器损坏。此前引入的堆上限（#11781）只挂在根构建脚本上，安装驱动的 `prepare` 路径从未被它覆盖。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

运行根目录的 package-scripts 套件（它覆盖 prepare 的步骤顺序与本次新增的调用）：`npx vitest run scripts/tests/package-scripts.test.js` 与 `npx vitest run scripts/tests/sdk-java-workflow.test.js`，两者均通过。若要确认堆上限确实传到了编译，可用桩程序替换 `PATH` 中的 `husky`/`npm` 并打印其内部 `NODE_OPTIONS`：改动前 `npm run build` 那次调用不带任何堆参数；改动后带 `--max-old-space-size=4096`，且传入的 `NODE_OPTIONS` 保留在其前面。在池上，daemon E2E 车道应要么进入测试，要么在预检处以 provisioning 提示停止，而不再出现堆崩溃。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 属于 CI 与构建脚本改动，无用户可见输出。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

N/A —— 单元测试加上上述桩程序见证。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：自托管预检现在还会在 runner 的 Node 不是 22.x 时给出警告（而非失败）。这正是目的——Node 完全缺失时仍会在任何构建开始前让 job 失败，即本 issue 要求的快速失败。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：ECS 宿主是否已装 Node 22.x、内存是否充足。这属于运维动作（或将 kill-switch 置位把车道导回托管 runner），任何仓库改动都无法替代。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 Issue

Closes #14823

</details>

prs.title: feat(mods): support tool middleware in interactive terminals
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Enables the existing `tool.call` and `tool.check` Mod protocol for model-initiated tools in local Ink and OpenTUI main sessions. Each ordinary `next` starts a separately validated and authorized native attempt. Synthetic results and denials finish one logical call without inventing a native invocation; all real attempts retain their usage and write observations, while the model and recording receive one final result after middleware unwind.

Preserves native permission ceilings, classic hooks, live output, nested Code Mode approvals and client-initiated native tools. Session changes revoke old execution eligibility before configuration changes, failed switches restore a fresh owner, and cancelled approval continuations cannot start new permission side effects. Final rewritten and synthetic output uses the terminal output budget, including restored read details.

## Why it's needed

Interactive sessions currently reject explicit tool middleware registrations. Removing that gate alone would leave synthetic calls pending, expose intermediate native completions too early, and miss cancellation, permission and recording boundaries. This connects both terminal model-turn paths through the existing protocol and native tool pipeline.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Install an opt-in Mod that rewrites a model shell call from A to B. In each renderer, confirm that only B executes, the provider history retains the original call, and exactly one matching final tool response is recorded. A new ordinary turn should work afterward.
2. Exercise direct denial, a synthetic result, repeated ordinary `next`, catch replay and denial after native execution. Confirm zero native executions for synthetic/early-denied calls, all real retry effects, and one final logical result. A native ask or deny must remain authoritative even when a Mod allows it; every repeated attempt must get its own approval.
3. Cancel during approval or execution, replace/resume a session, and wait across the retained 60-second approval boundary. Old approval callbacks must not execute or change permissions, the old queue must drain, and the next turn and quit must complete. Nested Code Mode approval must remain visible; client tools must retain their native behavior.
4. Return a large synthetic read result under a small output budget and resume it. Confirm the provider, recording and restored read details consume the finalized response rather than the original large payload.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, at base `00f7093a711340258523e7eea5438cfb9c3f0a5c`, explicit `tool.call`, `tool.check` and `tool.*` registrations fail in both real terminal renderers with `not supported in terminal sessions`; provider requests and native executions remain zero. The independent Mods-disabled allow/ask/deny controls pass in both renderers.

After, at `857b199eadcb8d15948b1bb74f551966e4f89f05`, this excerpt comes from the actual Ink PTY. The native oracle ledger contains B once and A zero times:

```text
> RUN:ad7933243e6f
  ✓ Shell node oracle.mjs ad7933243e6f B (p02a-tool-ad7933243e6f)
    ORACLE:ad7933243e6f:B
  ◆︎ DONE:ad7933243e6f
  ◆︎ NEXT-OK:ad7933243e6f
```

The authored full matrix at `857b199eadcb8d15948b1bb74f551966e4f89f05` passes 30/30 cases with retries disabled: 12 real Ink PTY cases, 12 strict OpenTUI PTY cases and 6 headless regressions, using 82 localhost provider requests and 24 native ledger entries. Both PTY legs cross 60 seconds of pending approval and reject the old confirmation afterward. All PTY cases verify normal exit after `/quit`. A separate E2E report comment records hashes, validation commands, independent results and retained first failures.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Node 24.14.1; Bun 1.3.13 for strict OpenTUI |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not run locally |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not run locally |

### Environment (optional)

Base `00f7093a711340258523e7eea5438cfb9c3f0a5c`; final head `ee8b47be44630d3f0daaa6555a06efdb684fd53f`. Independent worktree and dependencies, pnpm 11.24.0, isolated homes/workspaces and a controlled localhost OpenAI-compatible provider. No paid model requests. Final bundle SHA-256: `31d7fc282e4e2e88b78d3660bd784e95b1e399e8d26f3dd37d3dbb632a5cdb7a`. Local build, bundle, typecheck, lint, changed-file formatting and focused tests pass; hosted CI and formal review are separate gates.

Final owner-context follow-up at `62e9ac7e3d41c0209d2fba4dc173e12ad6b4037b` explicitly restores the captured hook owner at the native attempt boundary after a worker callback hop. Its new AsyncResource regression fails before the fix and passes afterward; 100 focused tests, CLI typecheck/build, bundle, delta lint/format and diff checks pass. The 30-case full matrix above is pinned to 857b; the separate E2E report distinguishes independent final-head follow-up.

Review repair at `adfb0b9a6975425d4f863d788b0d58ab355fb09f` makes a revoked Mod generation reject after native cleanup instead of resolving without completion. OpenTUI drains UI-only terminal states and propagates that rejection to release the turn without delivering stale results or firing the success callback. Native scheduling that resolves before approval/completion still keeps its event queue open. This fixes the failed-resume rollback busy state and also drains old generators after successful session reset.

At adfb, author full workspace build/bundle/typecheck, four-file lint/format/diff checks and two delta self-audit passes pass; focused tests are 121 plus 13 Ink wrapper tests (the revised adapter file also passes separately with 12 overlapping tests). Independent source-integration verification passes 6 fixed probes and 1 successful-reset addendum, 104 focused tests, independent CLI build/bundle, and one real rewrite/next/quit smoke per renderer. The session-switch race is a controlled source-integration probe, not a claimed PTY race reproduction. The earlier full 30-case matrix remains pinned to 857b, and the owner follow-up evidence remains pinned to 62e; they were not rerun in full at adfb.

Second review repair at `ee8b47be44630d3f0daaa6555a06efdb684fd53f` clears the finished OpenTUI turn’s real approval state and its synchronous mirror under the existing turn-sequence guard, before starting any queued successor. This restores the composer after a revoked-owner rollback without another key or stale confirmation. Live approvals remain until their turn actually ends; an old reset turn cannot clear a fresh approval even when both use the same call ID. No new protocol field or callback is introduced.

Author validation at the R2 candidate: full build/bundle/typecheck, two-file lint/format/diff checks and two clean delta audits; one eight-file focused run passes 220 tests, including 24 live-turn tests. Before the two-line production fix, the added regression had three failures (error exit, abort exit and queued same-ID successor) and 21 passing controls/existing tests. Historical 857b/62e/adfb evidence above remains bound to its original SHA, not claimed as full R2 reruns. Independent verification at exact R2 `ee8b47be44630d3f0daaa6555a06efdb684fd53f` passes the same frozen 3/3 source-integration probes, 97 focused tests, independent CLI build/typecheck/bundle, and one strict OpenTUI normal rewrite PTY smoke with next-turn acknowledgement and `/quit` exit 0. The probe observes an empty real approval queue without manual dismissal, zero old native execution/confirmation calls, and fresh same-ID approval preservation. The PTY smoke has three localhost requests, one real B execution and one final successful tool record. This is controlled runtime race verification plus a normal PTY control, not a claimed PTY reproduction of the session-switch race; this R2 round did not rerun the historical full dual-renderer matrix.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: terminal tool middleware serializes logical calls. Each real attempt has its own native batch, so classic PostToolBatch runs per native attempt. The three-identical-validation-errors retry diagnostic does not accumulate across those independent schedulers; invalid inputs are still rejected and the 64-attempt cap remains. No-Mod sessions retain their existing scheduler and batching.
- Not validated / out of scope: P02b waiting-budget policy, remote/managed/ACP/agent hosts, active Mod tool APIs, Windows/Linux runtime testing, and paid-provider E2E. The current 60-second Mod root wall-clock still includes approval and native execution; this PR makes expiry drain safely and does not extend it.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: opt-in remains required. Existing trust, safe/bare, hooks-disabled, remote, sandbox, managed and agent exclusions remain. This feature touches core and CLI and requires formal maintainer review; it is submitted as a draft.

## Linked Issues

N/A

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

让已有的 `tool.call` 和 `tool.check` Mod 协议支持本地 Ink 和 OpenTUI 主会话中由模型发起的工具调用。每次普通 `next` 都开始一次独立的原生验证和授权尝试。合成结果和拒绝会完成一次逻辑调用，不伪造原生 invocation；每次真实尝试都保留使用观察和写后观察，模型及记录则在中间件完整收尾后只接收一次最终结果。

保留原生权限上限、classic hooks、实时输出、嵌套 Code Mode 审批和 client 发起工具的原生路径。切换会话会在配置变化前撤销旧执行资格，切换失败后恢复一个新的 owner，已取消的审批 continuation 不能再开始新的权限副作用。最终改写或合成的输出经过终端输出预算，包括恢复会话后的读取详情。

## 为什么需要

交互会话目前会拒绝显式工具中间件注册。只移除这个限制，会让合成调用持续 pending、过早交付原生中间结果，并遗漏取消、权限及记录边界。本 PR 通过已有协议和原生工具链连接两个终端的模型主回合入口。

## 评审者验证计划

### 如何验证

1. 安装一个将模型 shell 调用从 A 改为 B 的 opt-in Mod。在两个 renderer 中分别确认只有 B 实际执行，provider 历史保留原始调用，并且只记录一次配对的最终工具结果。后续普通回合应正常完成。
2. 验证直接拒绝、合成结果、多次普通 `next`、catch replay 和原生执行后拒绝。确认合成及执行前拒绝的原生执行次数为零，每次真实重试的副作用都保留，而最终逻辑结果只有一次。即使 Mod 返回 allow，原生 ask 和 deny 仍须保持；每次重复尝试都必须有独立审批。
3. 在审批或执行期间取消，替换或恢复会话，并跨过保留的 60 秒审批边界。旧审批回调不得执行或修改权限，旧队列必须完成清理，下一回合及退出必须正常。嵌套 Code Mode 审批应继续可见，client 工具保持原生行为。
4. 在较小输出预算下返回大型合成读取结果并恢复会话。确认 provider、记录和恢复后的读取详情均消费最终预算处理后的响应，而非原始大型内容。

### 前后证据

改动前，基线 `00f7093a711340258523e7eea5438cfb9c3f0a5c` 的两个真实终端 renderer 都以 `not supported in terminal sessions` 拒绝显式 `tool.call`、`tool.check` 和 `tool.*` 注册；provider 请求和原生执行均为零。独立的 Mods-disabled allow/ask/deny 控制组在两端均通过。

改动后，在 `857b199eadcb8d15948b1bb74f551966e4f89f05` 上，以下内容来自真实 Ink PTY。原生 oracle ledger 中 B 为一次、A 为零次：

```text
> RUN:ad7933243e6f
  ✓ Shell node oracle.mjs ad7933243e6f B (p02a-tool-ad7933243e6f)
    ORACLE:ad7933243e6f:B
  ◆︎ DONE:ad7933243e6f
  ◆︎ NEXT-OK:ad7933243e6f
```

作者在 `857b199eadcb8d15948b1bb74f551966e4f89f05` 上的完整矩阵在关闭重试的情况下通过 30/30：12 个真实 Ink PTY 场景、12 个严格 OpenTUI PTY 场景和 6 个 headless 回归，共 82 次 localhost provider 请求、24 条原生 ledger 记录。两端 PTY 都实际跨过 60 秒审批等待，并验证之后的旧确认无法执行。所有 PTY 场景都验证 `/quit` 正常退出。另附单独 E2E 报告评论，记录 hashes、验证命令、独立结果及保留的首次失败。

### 本地验证环境

| OS | 状态 |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Node 24.14.1；严格 OpenTUI 使用 Bun 1.3.13 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 本地未执行 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 本地未执行 |

### 环境补充

基线为 `00f7093a711340258523e7eea5438cfb9c3f0a5c`，最终 head 为 `ee8b47be44630d3f0daaa6555a06efdb684fd53f`。使用独立 worktree 和依赖、pnpm 11.24.0、隔离的 homes/workspaces 及受控 localhost OpenAI-compatible provider。没有付费模型请求。最终 Bundle SHA-256 为 `31d7fc282e4e2e88b78d3660bd784e95b1e399e8d26f3dd37d3dbb632a5cdb7a`。本地 build、bundle、typecheck、lint、改动文件格式检查和定向测试通过；托管 CI 和正式评审是独立关卡。

最终 owner-context 修复位于 `62e9ac7e3d41c0209d2fba4dc173e12ad6b4037b`：worker callback 跨上下文后，在实际原生 attempt 入口显式恢复捕获的 hook owner。新增 AsyncResource 回归在修复前失败、修复后通过；100 个定向测试、CLI typecheck/build、bundle、增量 lint/format 和 diff 检查均通过。上述 30 场景完整矩阵固定在 857b；单独 E2E 报告区分最终 head 的独立增量验证。

评审修复位于 `adfb0b9a6975425d4f863d788b0d58ab355fb09f`：撤销的 Mod generation 在原生清理结束后明确 reject，不再静默 resolve 且不交付 completion。OpenTUI 排空仅 UI 的工具终态，再将拒绝传递到回合收尾，释放 busy，不交付旧结果或触发成功回调。原生 schedule 在审批或 completion 前 resolve 时，事件 queue 仍保持打开。此修复覆盖失败 resume 回滚后的 busy 卡住，以及成功切换后旧 generator 的排空。

在 adfb 上，作者全仓 build/bundle/typecheck、四文件 lint/format/diff 和两次增量差异自审通过；定向测试为 121 个加 13 个 Ink wrapper 测试（修正后的 adapter 文件另跑 12 个重叠测试也通过）。独立源码集成验证通过 6 个固定 probe 和 1 个成功 reset 补验、104 个定向测试、独立 CLI build/bundle，以及每个 renderer 各一个真实 rewrite/下一回合/quit smoke。会话切换竞态使用受控源码集成 probe，不声称在 PTY 重现竞态。先前完整 30 场景矩阵仍固定在 857b，owner 增量证据仍固定在 62e；没有将它们改写成 adfb 全量重跑。

第二轮评审修复位于 `ee8b47be44630d3f0daaa6555a06efdb684fd53f`：在原 turn-sequence guard 内、启动排队的下一回合前，清除已结束 OpenTUI 回合的真实审批 state 和同步 ref。撤销 owner 的 rollback 后无需额外按键或调用旧确认即可恢复 composer。仍在执行的回合保留有效审批；reset 后旧回合迟到收尾不能清掉新回合的同 call ID 审批。没有新增协议字段或回调。

R2 candidate 的作者验证：完整 build/bundle/typecheck、两文件 lint/format/diff 及两次干净增量自审；单次八文件运行通过 220 测试，其中 live-turn 为 24 个。两行生产修复前，新增回归准确得到三个失败（error 退出、abort 退出、排队同 ID successor）和 21 个通过的控制及既有测试。前述 857b/62e/adfb 历史证据保持各自 SHA，不冒称 R2 全量重跑。精确 R2 `ee8b47be44630d3f0daaa6555a06efdb684fd53f` 的独立验收通过同一冻结源码集成 probe 3/3、97 个定向测试、独立 CLI build/typecheck/bundle，以及一个严格 OpenTUI 正常 rewrite PTY smoke（下一回合 ACK、`/quit` exit 0）。probe 观察到真实审批队列无需手动关闭即清空、旧 native 执行及确认调用为零、新同 ID 审批保持。PTY smoke 为三次 localhost 请求、真实 B 执行一次、最终成功工具记录一条。这是受控运行时竞态验证加正常 PTY 控制，不冒称在 PTY 重现会话切换竞态；本轮 R2 未重跑历史完整双 renderer 矩阵。

## 风险和范围

- 主要风险或取舍：终端工具中间件串行处理逻辑调用。每次真实尝试都有独立原生批次，因此 classic PostToolBatch 按原生 attempt 触发。相同验证错误三次后的重试诊断提示不跨独立 scheduler 累积；非法输入仍然被拒绝，64 次 attempt 上限仍保留。无 Mod 会话保留已有 scheduler 和批次行为。
- 未验证及范围外事项：P02b 等待预算政策、remote/managed/ACP/agent hosts、主动 Mod tool APIs、Windows/Linux 运行验证及付费 provider E2E。当前 60 秒 Mod root wall-clock 仍包含审批和原生执行等待；本 PR 保证到期后安全清理，不延长它。
- 兼容及迁移说明：仍须显式 opt-in。已有 trust、safe/bare、禁用 hooks、remote、sandbox、managed 和 agent 排除不扩大。本功能修改 core 和 CLI，需要维护者正式评审，因此以 draft 提交。

## 关联 Issue

N/A

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): add account-wide code review workbench
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a default-off Code Review workbench to Web Shell. It reads the daemon operator’s GitHub account through `gh` and shows open pull requests across repositories in “Created by me” and “Needs my review”; the latter combines review requests and assignments. Users can page through the inbox, filter loaded results, or paste a complete PR URL without selecting or cloning a repository.

The workbench provides overview, files and activity views, compact comments/reviewer/check summaries, and draggable side panes with keyboard resizing and persisted widths. Current-head checks collapse earlier attempts of the same workflow/event/job while retaining distinct jobs with qualified labels. Reviewer states and comment counts come from each reviewer’s latest review. Users enable the default-off workbench from Settings → Experimental. The switch is stored in User settings, respects System locks and ignores workspace settings; it remains available without a local workspace. Disabling hides the navigation entry, exits an open workbench and prevents disabled deep links from reading PRs. Older daemons hide the entry, and URL-enabled hosts support enabled PR deep links and browser history.

## Why it's needed

The existing repository PR dialog does not provide an account-wide place to triage authored PRs and incoming review work. A dedicated workbench lets users inspect PR state and CI alongside local sessions. This first phase establishes the read-only workflow and an explicit feature switch for later maintenance capabilities.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Connect Web Shell to a daemon with an authenticated `gh` account. The Code Review entry should initially be hidden. Open Settings → Experimental (through More when using the navigation rail), enable Code Review Workbench, and confirm the entry appears and both inbox groups span accessible repositories. Repeat without a selected workspace. Disable it again and confirm the entry disappears, an open workbench exits and direct links no longer load PR data. Reload to check persistence. A System override should lock the switch.
2. Open PRs with the same number in different repositories, paste a complete PR URL, change selections quickly, and load more results. Confirm selection identity uses the complete URL and delayed responses cannot replace the selected PR or mix accounts. Filtering applies to loaded rows; search limits remain indicated.
3. Inspect overview, patches and activity. Compare current-head checks and individual reviewer states with GitHub. Earlier attempts of the same job should collapse, while checks from different workflows/events remain distinguishable. Compact counts and GitHub links retain access to bounded results.
4. Drag both dividers, resize them with the keyboard, reload and try a narrow viewport. Confirm widths persist, content stays usable, and avatars have a fallback. Check English/Chinese and light/dark appearances.
5. Test the normal same-origin Vite development entry and a token-protected daemon’s direct `/code-review` link/reload. HTML must load while API reads remain authenticated. An embedded host without URL navigation should return to chat if the connected daemon loses code-review support.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the existing PR dialog at upstream base `a703a76ae2413601d77ca07dd1addaebba5fe148`, using synthetic fixture data (1440×1000, dark theme).

![Before: existing repository PR dialog using fixture data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qqqys/qwen-code/2d17de676b2767b517fc6e42a7ba55bbc56a9a7f/pr-assets/code-review-workbench/before-fixture.png)

After: the new account-wide workbench from the final local source, using synthetic fixture data (1600×1000, light theme). These show the old and new interaction surfaces; they are not a pixel-matched comparison of one PR. No private repository inbox data is included.

![After: account-wide code review workbench using fixture data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qqqys/qwen-code/2d17de676b2767b517fc6e42a7ba55bbc56a9a7f/pr-assets/code-review-workbench/after-fixture.png)

Local verification includes 47 core tests, 23 account-route tests, 22 workbench component tests and the 21-case Chromium fixture suite from implementation, with unchanged-source evidence checked before submission. The final integration fixes additionally passed 47 CLI static/pre-auth tests, 22 Vite tests, 3 focused App tests and a fresh final-source Chromium capture. The embedded-host and Vite defects were reproduced before their fixes; authenticated direct navigation was independently reproduced using the actual middleware sequence. The final full workspace build, workspace/integration typecheck, changed-file lint and formatting checks all passed; details are recorded in the accompanying E2E report.

The unified Experimental setting, entry visibility and deep-link gates passed 77 focused unit tests and the complete 24-case Chromium fixture suite with no retries on macOS / Node.js 22.17. The full workspace build, bundle, typecheck, changed-file lint/format and 36 built-artifact checks passed. This includes first enablement without a workspace, zero workspace-settings requests in that case, persisted toggles, disabled deep links, delayed enabled links and System locks. These are local results; hosted CI is reported separately.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ tested locally |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested locally |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

macOS, Node.js 25.9.0, local built daemon, Vite and Chromium. Browser scenarios use controlled fixture responses; separate read-only real-GitHub checks on public QwenLM/qwen-code #14338 at head `73165dbb1438b409b6b6fb7ec697595df98b8de5` matched all 54 current check tuples on 2026-10-18. That live sample predates only the final development-proxy, pre-auth-page and embedded-host wiring fixes; the GitHub reader and detail rendering are unchanged.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: this is an account-wide capability for clients authorized to the daemon, using the operator’s captured GitHub environment rather than a workspace identity. Reads are bounded and subject to GitHub rate/search limits. Enterprise avatar origins remain subject to the host’s CSP.
- Not validated / out of scope: hosted CI, Windows/Linux runtime behavior, exhaustive enterprise-server compatibility, review submission, GitHub mutations, background subscriptions and automatic PR maintenance. This is a draft for the first read-only phase.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no migration; `experimental.codeReview` defaults to false. The new APIs are additive, and legacy daemons do not expose the navigation entry.

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

### 改动内容

为 Web Shell 增加默认关闭的代码审查工作台。通过 `gh` 读取 daemon 操作者的 GitHub 账户，跨仓库展示「我创建的」和「待我审查」的开放 PR；后者合并审查请求和指派给我的 PR。可以逐页加载、筛选已加载列表或粘贴完整 PR 链接，无需选择或克隆仓库。

工作台提供概览、文件与动态视图，以及紧凑的评论、审查者和检查摘要。左右面板支持拖动、键盘调宽及宽度持久化。检查从当前提交读取，合并同一工作流、事件和任务的历史尝试，保留不同任务并补充区分标签。审查者状态与评论数来自各自的最新一次审查。工作台默认关闭，从「设置 → 实验性功能」启用后才显示代码审查入口；无本地工作区也能启用。开关保存到用户设置，遵循系统锁定并忽略工作区设置。关闭后隐藏入口、退出已打开的工作台，并阻止关闭态直达链接读取 PR。旧版 daemon 隐藏入口，启用 URL 导航的宿主支持开启态 PR 直达链接与浏览器历史。

### 为什么需要

已有的仓库 PR 对话框缺少一个跨账户仓库处理自己 PR 和待审工作的统一入口。独立工作台让用户在本地会话旁查看 PR 和 CI 状态。第一阶段提供只读工作流与明确的功能开关，为后续维护能力建立基础。

### 审查者验证步骤

1. 将 Web Shell 连接到已登录 `gh` 的 daemon。代码审查入口默认隐藏；从「设置 → 实验性功能」开启工作台（导航栏模式下先打开「更多」），确认入口出现且两个列表跨可访问仓库展示。没有本地工作区时也应能开启。关闭后应隐藏入口、退出已打开的工作台，并阻止直达链接读取 PR；刷新后状态应保留。系统覆盖设置应锁定开关。
2. 打开不同仓库中编号相同的 PR，粘贴完整链接，快速切换并加载更多。确认完整 URL 决定 PR 身份，迟到响应不会覆盖当前选择或混入其他账户的数据。筛选作用于已加载列表，搜索限制仍有提示。
3. 查看概览、补丁与动态，对照 GitHub 核对当前提交的检查以及各审查者状态。同一任务的历史尝试应合并，不同工作流或事件的检查应保留并能区分。紧凑计数与 GitHub 链接保留读取上限之外的访问途径。
4. 拖动两侧分隔线、用键盘调宽、刷新并缩窄窗口。确认宽度保留、内容可用、头像有降级显示，并检查中英文及明暗主题。
5. 验证默认同源 Vite 开发入口，以及启用 token 的 daemon 中 `/code-review` 直达和刷新。页面 HTML 应能加载，API 仍需认证。不启用 URL 导航的嵌入宿主在 daemon 不再支持代码审查时应返回聊天。

### 前后对比与验证证据

上方 Before 为上游基线 `a703a76ae2413601d77ca07dd1addaebba5fe148` 的既有 PR 对话框，使用合成测试数据，尺寸 1440×1000、暗色主题。After 为最终本地源码的账户级工作台，同样使用合成数据，尺寸 1600×1000、亮色主题。这是新旧操作界面的对比，并非同一 PR 的像素对照；截图不包含私有仓库收件箱信息。

实现阶段通过了 47 项 core 测试、23 项账户路由测试、22 项工作台组件测试及 21 项 Chromium 场景，提交前核对了未改动源码与既有证据。最终集成修复另通过 47 项 CLI 静态资源/预认证测试、22 项 Vite 测试、3 项 App 定向测试，并从最终源码重新采集 Chromium 截图。嵌入宿主与 Vite 问题均先复现再修复；认证直达问题使用真实中间件顺序独立复现。最终完整工作区构建、工作区及集成类型检查、改动文件 lint 和格式检查均通过，详情见附加 E2E 报告。

统一实验性设置、入口显示及直达链接限制已通过 77 项定向单测和完整 24 项 Chromium 场景，零重试；环境为 macOS / Node.js 22.17。完整工作区构建、bundle、类型检查、改动文件 lint/格式检查及 36 项构建产物检查均通过，覆盖无工作区首次开启且不请求工作区设置、开关持久化、关闭态直达链接、延迟读取开启态设置及系统锁定。这些为本地结果，远端 CI 单独报告。

### 测试平台与环境

macOS 已本地验证；Windows、Linux 未本地验证。环境为 macOS、Node.js 25.9.0、本地构建 daemon、Vite 与 Chromium。浏览器场景使用受控测试响应；另于 2026-10-18 对公开 QwenLM/qwen-code #14338 的提交 `73165dbb1438b409b6b6fb7ec697595df98b8de5` 做只读真实 GitHub 核对，54 项当前检查完整匹配。该真实样本早于最后的开发代理、预认证页面与嵌入宿主接线修复；GitHub 读取及详情渲染代码未变化。

### 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：这是授予 daemon 已授权客户端的账户级能力，使用操作者启动时捕获的 GitHub 环境，不使用工作区身份。读取有上限，并受 GitHub 频控与搜索限制；企业头像来源仍受宿主 CSP 约束。

prs.title: test: capture expected disk-full logs
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Captures and asserts the expected error output from unit tests that deliberately inject `new Error("disk full")`. The production logging paths remain unchanged, while the test fixtures no longer emit unqualified disk-full messages into shared CI logs.

## Why it is needed

Expected-failure tests currently print production-looking disk-full errors. Those lines can make unrelated CI failures look like runner ENOSPC incidents. Capturing the output in the tests preserves coverage of the logging behavior and makes real disk-full failures easier to distinguish.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused suites:

- `cd packages/acp-bridge && npx vitest run src/sessionArtifacts.test.ts src/bridge.test.ts`
- `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/run-qwen-serve.test.ts`
- `cd packages/vscode-ide-companion && npx vitest run src/webview/utils/imageHandler.test.ts`
- `cd packages/channels/qqbot && npx vitest run src/persistence.test.ts`

Confirm that all suites pass and that their output contains no unqualified `disk full` lines. The affected tests now also assert that the expected logger or stderr call occurred.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the passing suites printed messages such as `[ImageHandler] Failed to save image: Error: disk full`, `flushQQState write failed: disk full`, and artifact persistence failures containing `disk full`.

After: the same error paths remain covered and their log payloads are asserted, but the focused suite output contains zero `disk full` occurrences.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | N/A |
| 🪟 Windows | N/A |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Ubuntu 26.04, Node.js v22.22.2, npm 10.9.7.

Additional checks passed: Prettier, ESLint on all changed files, ACP Bridge and CLI typechecks, VS Code companion typecheck, QQBot build, and the repository build run by `npm ci`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Test-local stderr/logger spies must be restored; each new spy is scoped to its test and restored after use.
- Not validated / out of scope: Other intentional warning output unrelated to the injected disk-full fixtures.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. Production code is unchanged.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #8532

prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds two design documents under `docs/design/`: a code-grounded inventory of every place `Content[]`/`Part[]` chat history is mutated after a content generator produces it, stating precisely which of those mutation sites must preserve the `thought`/`thoughtSignature` reasoning-replay invariant that Anthropic's strict tool-use-chain contract depends on; and a confirmed-bug verdict document tracing a specific gap found while producing that inventory, where `--resume` can reconstruct the exact dangling-unsigned-thought hazard PR #8260 fixed for the live session path. No production code changes — documentation only.

## Why it's needed

PR #8260 fixed a chain of bugs in `geminiChat.ts`'s reasoning-episode consolidation logic, closed via a scoped multi-model architectural review. That review round surfaced a broader concern worth documenting in the repo rather than leaving scattered across PR comments and reviewer transcripts: the fix protects the live, in-memory session, but the mutation it applies (`coalesceRecoveryPairs`'s call to `dropDanglingUnsignedTrailingThought`) never reaches the on-disk JSONL transcript, because it runs strictly after that transcript was already written. A follow-up investigation, again using four independent reviewers on different model families working without coordination and then cross-checked against each other and against the actual code, confirmed that `--resume` reconstructs the pre-fix hazard shape from the unfixed on-disk record, via the Anthropic converter's `mergeConsecutiveAssistantMessages` pass, which runs before the signature-validity guard in the request-conversion pipeline. This is filed as a companion, actionable bug report separate from this PR (#8535) since it needs its own fix and test plan, not a docs change. Both documents are also referenced from #8533, the broader philosophical issue about whether `Content[]`/`Part[]` is the right shared representation for multi-provider reasoning content at all.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

This is a documentation-only PR. Read both new files under `docs/design/` and verify the cited `file:line` references resolve to the code they describe (all citations link directly to the exact commit they were verified against). No functional behavior changes, so there is nothing to reproduce or test beyond reading the documents for accuracy.

|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

N/A — no code paths exercised.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: none — additive documentation only, no code or behavior changes.
- Not validated / out of scope: the resume-divergence bug document is a static code trace, not an executed end-to-end reproduction against a live API; this is called out explicitly in the document itself and in #8535 as the recommended next step before any fix lands.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Related to #8533 and #8535.

prs.title: test(vscode-ide-companion): pin the html lang attribute escaping
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a regression test pinning the HTML escaping on the webview's `lang` attribute.

## Why it's needed

This PR originally carried the one-line production fix as well, stamping `vscode.env.language` into the template instead of the hardcoded `lang="en"`. That part is already on `main` — `WebViewContent.ts` now does `const language = escapeHtml(vscode.env.language || 'en')` and interpolates it — so the only thing left here is the test coverage that did not land with it.

`main` has tests for the `zh-cn` value and for the empty-string fallback to `en`, but nothing exercises a value that actually needs escaping. The `escapeHtml` call on that line is therefore unpinned: dropping it leaves the whole suite green, so a later refactor could silently remove the escaping on an attribute that is interpolated straight into the document.

The added case sets the language to `"><script>alert(1)</script>` and asserts the entity-escaped output, matching `escapeHtml`'s entity set in `webviewUtils.ts`.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

```
packages/vscode-ide-companion
  npx vitest run src/webview/providers/WebViewContent.test.ts   -> 14 passed
  npx eslint   src/webview/providers/WebViewContent.test.ts     -> clean
  npx prettier --check …                                        -> clean
```

Mutation check — remove `escapeHtml(...)` from the `const language = …` line in `WebViewContent.ts`:

```
× WebViewContent > escapes the language value in the html lang attribute
Tests  1 failed | 13 passed (14)
```

That is the only test that reds, which is the point: nothing else currently covers it.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (non-visual internal change, verified by unit test)

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: None. Test-only; no production file is touched.
- Not validated / out of scope: The `remoteName` handling `main` added to the same mock is left exactly as it is.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None

## Linked Issues

Refs #10373. The production change that issue asked for is already on `main`, so this no longer closes it.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

本 PR 现仅新增一个回归测试，用于固定 webview `lang` 属性上的 HTML 转义。

原先附带的一行生产代码改动（用 `vscode.env.language` 替换硬编码的 `lang="en"`）已经在 `main` 上：`WebViewContent.ts` 现为 `const language = escapeHtml(vscode.env.language || 'en')`。但随之而来的测试覆盖并未一起落地。

`main` 上已有 `zh-cn` 与空值回退 `en` 的用例，却没有任何用例使用需要转义的值，因此该行的 `escapeHtml` 没有被任何测试固定——移除它后整个套件仍然全绿，后续重构可能在无人察觉的情况下移除该属性的转义。

新增用例将语言设为 `"><script>alert(1)</script>` 并断言转义后的输出。变异验证：移除 `escapeHtml(...)` 后，仅该用例变红（1 failed | 13 passed）。

</details>

prs.title: docs(agents): add agent orchestration contract
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a design document that maps the agent orchestration contract across all six launch routes — in-process subagents, forks, named teammates, workflow agents, Cursor SDK, and Cursor CLI. It covers how a definition is resolved and which of its frontmatter fields are actually enforced, how capability is determined per route, how the model is selected, how workspace and lifecycle are decided, and how the two coordination control planes relate. It also records a set of drift gates, each naming an oracle, a RED, an adjacent control, and the exact consumers affected.

The document is derived from a source audit of the launch path. Every behavioral claim is stated against current source, and where something could not be verified it is marked unverified rather than asserted — three tuple rows carry that marker, and one rejection code is documented as having no locatable firing site. Findings are separated into source facts, confirmed defects, source-backed design gaps, design decisions taken here, and open product decisions that block specific delivery scopes.

It cross-references the eight issues filed from the same audit rather than restating them. Each of those issues owns one class and stands alone; none of them depends on this document to be actionable.

Documentation only. No runtime behavior changes.

## Why it's needed

The agent launch surface has grown six routes that diverge in ways that are individually reasonable and collectively hard to hold in one's head. During the audit the same questions kept getting re-derived from source: whether a definition's declared limits are actually applied, which parameter selects the model, whether a foreground agent is tracked in the background registry, what happens to a caller-owned worktree when an agent is backgrounded.

Two concrete symptoms motivated writing it down. First, several findings were difficult to describe consistently because the surface overloads three words — the same term names both an agent definition and a teammate label, "task" names both an agent run and a team work item, and one display field carries a different meaning depending on which route produced it. The document pins that vocabulary so downstream text can be consistent. Second, a fail-open behavior turned out to have a real consumer that nobody had identified, which only became visible once the routes were written down side by side.

The intended audience is a maintainer deciding whether a proposed change to one route breaks an assumption another route depends on. The drift gates exist so that question can be answered mechanically rather than by rereading the launch path.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

This is a documentation-only change, so the useful verification is whether the claims hold, not whether anything runs.

Spot-check the source-fact claims against the current tree. The document cites specific behaviors rather than gesturing at them, so any individual claim should be falsifiable by reading the cited area. Particularly worth checking, because they were the least obvious during the audit: which frontmatter limit fields the definition parser actually reads, what an empty `tools` array resolves to by the time the tool surface is prepared, and whether a foreground agent appears in the background registry.

Check that the rejection taxonomy matches reality. The document claims a specific set of launch rejections and, for each, whether it is raised during parameter validation or during execution. The rule it applies is mechanical: a rejection returned by parameter validation is validation-phase, everything else is execution-phase.

Check the marked-unverified items are genuinely marked rather than quietly asserted. Three route assignments and one rejection code are flagged as unconfirmed; those are the places where the document is deliberately weaker than the rest.

Formatting: `npx prettier --check docs/design/2026-08-18-agent-orchestration-contract.md`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — documentation only, no user-visible or TUI change.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — no runtime involved. Prettier verified locally.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a document describing runtime behavior can drift from it. The drift gates are written to make that detectable, but they are specifications rather than executable tests in this PR. The content is a snapshot taken against `b4f5079dc0`; two of the referenced issues were already resolved upstream before this was opened, and the document notes that.
- Not validated / out of scope: no gate is implemented here, and no code is changed. Several delivery scopes described in the document are blocked on open product decisions that are the maintainers' to make, not this PR's. Cursor-route content describes an integration that does not exist on `main`; it is included for completeness of the route map and is explicitly not a claim about upstream behavior.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Filed from the same audit, referenced without closing keywords since this document does not resolve them: #9430, #9431, #9449, #9450, #9509, #9510, #9514, #9515.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

新增一份设计文档，梳理 agent orchestration 契约在全部六条启动路径上的行为——进程内 subagent、fork、具名 teammate、workflow agent、Cursor SDK 和 Cursor CLI。内容涵盖：definition 如何被解析、其 frontmatter 中哪些字段真正生效、各路径的能力如何确定、模型如何选择、工作区与生命周期如何决定，以及两个协调控制平面之间的关系。文档还记录了一组漂移检测门（drift gate），每个都写明 oracle、RED、相邻对照以及受影响的确切消费方。

该文档源自对启动路径的源码审计。所有行为性结论都对照当前源码陈述；无法验证的部分被明确标记为未验证，而不是断言——有三个 tuple 行带有该标记，另有一个 rejection code 被记录为找不到触发位置。结论被区分为源码事实、已确认缺陷、有源码依据的设计缺口、本文档做出的设计决策，以及阻塞特定交付范围的未决产品决策。

文档引用了同一次审计中提交的八个 issue，而不是复述它们的内容。每个 issue 各自负责一个类别并可独立处理；它们都不依赖本文档才能被处理。

仅文档变更，不改变任何运行时行为。

## 为什么需要

agent 启动面已经发展出六条路径，它们各自的差异都算合理，但合在一起很难被完整记住。审计过程中，同样的问题被反复从源码中重新推导：definition 声明的限制是否真的生效、哪个参数选择模型、前台 agent 是否被后台注册表跟踪、当 agent 转入后台时调用方自有的 worktree 会发生什么。

有两个具体现象促成了这份文档。其一，若干发现难以一致地描述，因为该表面重载了三个词——同一个术语既指 agent definition 又指 teammate 标签，"task" 既指一次 agent 运行又指 team 工作项，还有一个展示字段会因产生它的路径不同而含义不同。文档固定了这套词汇，使下游文本能够保持一致。其二，一处 fail-open 行为原来存在真实消费方，此前无人识别；只有当各路径被并排写出来后才显现。

目标读者是需要判断"改动某一条路径是否会破坏另一条路径所依赖假设"的维护者。漂移检测门的存在，是为了让这个问题可以被机械地回答，而不必重新通读启动路径。

## 评审者测试计划

### 如何验证

这是纯文档变更，因此有价值的验证是结论是否成立，而不是能否运行。

对照当前代码树抽查源码事实类结论。文档引用的是具体行为而非泛泛而谈，因此任何单条结论都应可通过阅读所引区域来证伪。审计中最不直观、因而尤其值得核对的有：definition 解析器实际读取哪些 frontmatter 限制字段；空 `tools` 数组在工具面准备完成时解析成什么；以及前台 agent 是否出现在后台注册表中。

核对 rejection 分类是否符合实际。文档声明了一组特定的启动拒绝，并对每一个说明它是在参数校验阶段还是执行阶段触发。所采用的规则是机械的：由参数校验返回的拒绝属于 validation 阶段，其余均属 execution 阶段。

核对被标记为未验证的条目确实带有标记，而不是被悄悄断言。三处路径归属和一个 rejection code 被标为未确认；这些正是文档刻意弱于其余部分的地方。

格式：`npx prettier --check docs/design/2026-08-18-agent-orchestration-contract.md`。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A —— 纯文档变更，无用户可见或 TUI 变化。

### 测试环境

|    系统    |  状态  |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### 运行环境（可选）

N/A —— 不涉及运行时。已在本地通过 Prettier 校验。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：描述运行时行为的文档可能与实现产生漂移。漂移检测门的写法就是为了让这种漂移可被发现，但在本 PR 中它们仍是规格说明而非可执行测试。内容是针对 `b4f5079dc0` 的快照；其中两个被引用的 issue 在本 PR 提交前已在上游解决，文档中已注明这一点。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：本 PR 未实现任何 gate，也未改动任何代码。文档中描述的若干交付范围被未决产品决策阻塞，那些决策属于维护者，而不属于本 PR。Cursor 路径相关内容描述的集成在 `main` 上并不存在；纳入它是为了路径图的完整性，且明确不是对上游行为的声明。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 Issue

prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a troubleshooting entry for TUI flickering/tearing in web-based terminals (for example Alibaba Cloud Workbench), documenting the confirmed cause and the verified workaround (`ui.useTerminalBuffer: false`, optionally `ui.mouseTracking: false`). Docs only — no code changes.

## Why it's needed

Issue #8659 reports continuous flicker/tearing when Qwen Code runs in browser-based terminals. @doudouOUC confirmed the cause in the thread: `shouldUseVirtualViewport()` cannot distinguish web terminals (`TERM=xterm` on a TTY, no `COLORTERM`, no `TERM_PROGRAM`), so Virtualized History activates by default and its full-screen ANSI repaints overwhelm high-latency web terminals. The fix direction agreed in the thread is "docs + startup hint first, auto-detection later". This PR delivers the docs half so affected users can find the workaround today; the startup hint and auto-detection need a detection-heuristic design discussion (missing `COLORTERM` + `TERM_PROGRAM` alone false-positives on ordinary SSH xterm sessions) and are proposed as a follow-up.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Docs-only change. Confirm the new entry renders correctly in `docs/users/support/troubleshooting.md` (placed next to the other terminal-behavior entries: tmux trackpad, right-click/mouse tracking). The workaround itself was verified by the reporter in #8659: setting `ui.useTerminalBuffer: false` switches rendering to the append-only Static path and resolves the flicker in Alibaba Cloud Workbench.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — docs change.

|  🍏 macOS  |   N/A  |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Alibaba Cloud Workbench (browser-based terminal), TERM=xterm, no COLORTERM/TERM_PROGRAM — the environment from the original report.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: none identified; documentation only, workaround wording follows the maintainer's confirmed analysis in #8659.
- Not validated / out of scope: the startup hint and web-terminal auto-detection/fallback (needs design discussion on reliable detection signals; offered as follow-up).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Highlights

The bundled CLI 0.23.0 includes two fixes requested in #11022:

- Managed memory availability now respects the `memory.enableManagedAutoMemory` setting (#6941). Hosts that disable managed auto memory no longer see remember/dream requests admitted or managed-memory instructions in the system prompt; local patches can be removed.
- Size-triggered microcompaction now clears old tool results toward a low watermark (#8464), so it no longer rewrites another part of the conversation prefix on every subsequent turn. Provider prompt-cache reuse is preserved across long tool-heavy sessions, reducing cached-input cost.

issues.title: feat(config): optional knobs for the standing-instruction budget, and a visible notice when instruction content is trimmed or dropped

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: context
labels.description: Context management / context

labels.name: ux
labels.description: User experience, interaction, or presentation polish

issues.body:
## Problem

Standing instruction authority has two fixed ceilings, neither steerable by an operator, and both failure modes are invisible from the user's side.

**The ceilings (hard-coded, no config key).**

- `MAX_PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_BYTES = 48 * 1024` — `crates/tui/src/project_context.rs:384`. Everything that reaches the model as standing instruction authority — the repository-root → workspace `AGENTS.md` chain, the global fallback layer, `.codewhale/rules/*.md`, and any imported foreign files — shares this one budget. Documented as fixed at `config.example.toml:360`.
- `MAX_CONTEXT_SIZE = 100 * 1024` — `crates/tui/src/project_context.rs:366`. A context file over this is not trimmed: `load_context_file_with_symlink_policy` returns `Err(ProjectContextError::TooLarge)` (`:1083`; error text `crates/tui/src/project_context/types.rs:22`), the caller collects it as a warning and moves to the next candidate filename (`:565`), so that file's contribution is missing — while the chain still assembles ancestor files (`:620-665`) and merges the global fallback layer (`:684`, `merge_global_and_project_instructions` at `:946`). The agent then runs on a *broader* instruction set than the operator wrote, with nothing saying so.

`Config::instructions_paths()` selects *which* extra files load; their only ceiling is the fixed per-file truncation above, and no key controls either ceiling.

**Observed on a real workspace.** Global `~/AGENTS.md` = 54 KB, project `AGENTS.md` = 88,918 → 94,224 → 118,673 bytes over three days. The session log carries, once per launch:

```
WARN project_context: Dropping broadest-scope project instructions at the aggregate budget was=102031 now=49152 cap=49152
```

i.e. the broadest scope is dropped first, every session, and the project file has just crossed the 100 KiB line that turns it into a `TooLarge` skip.

**The notice gap — this is the part that hurts.** Nothing at session start says any of this happened:

- `as_system_block` (`types.rs:88`) emits instructions + rules + constitution; `ProjectContext.warnings` is **not** part of the prompt, so the model is not told either;
- the warnings surface only in `/context report` (`crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:500-508`) and `GET /v1/workspace/instructions` (the source map added in #6168);
- the trim itself is a `tracing::warn` (`project_context.rs:448`) plus a marker line inside the content (`:391`).

So an operator with a mature global + project instruction pair cannot tell that half their standing law was cut, or which file lost.

**The two ceilings behave differently for the same nominal 100 KiB, and the docs name a marker the code never emits — happy to split the marker-name fix into its own issue if you prefer.** `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:1261-1262` and `docs/zh_hans/CONFIGURATION.md:680` say of `instructions = [...]`: "Each file is capped at 100 KiB; oversized files are truncated with a `[…elided]` marker rather than skipped." The behaviour is real: `render_instructions_block` caps each source at `INSTRUCTIONS_FILE_MAX_BYTES = 100 * 1024` (`crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:98`) and truncates it (`:277-289`). What it emits is `[…truncated: N of M bytes omitted — consider splitting this instructions file]` (`:283`); the name `[…elided]` appears only in the rustdoc for `InstructionSource::File` (`crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:229`) and in those two docs. So the defect is the marker name, not the ceiling.

The asymmetry is the real problem: **the `instructions = [...]` array trims an oversized file and says so in-context; the `AGENTS.md` chain drops the file entirely.** One path is told to split its file; the other loses a layer and is told nothing.

## Proposed solution

Optional knobs, with today's behaviour as the default:

1. `[context] instruction_budget_bytes` (default 49152, with an absolute ceiling) — the shared aggregate budget. The `[context]` table already exists (`ContextConfig`, `crates/tui/src/config.rs:2332`; live key today: `project_pack`), so this is a new key, not a new table.
2. `[context] instruction_file_max_bytes` (default 102400) — per-file ceiling for the `AGENTS.md` chain, and for the `instructions = [...]` path, which carries the same 100 KiB cap hard-coded today.
3. **Skip vs trim stated explicitly, and the chain gets what the array already does.** For a file over the per-file ceiling, either trim with the marker the `instructions = [...]` path already uses (`crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:283`, including its "consider splitting" hint) or refuse with a message naming the file, the size, and the limit. Silently dropping a whole instruction layer should not be one of the options.
4. **A first-turn notice.** When content is trimmed or a candidate file is dropped, put one bounded line into the run's first turn — e.g. `project instructions: dropped <path> (118673 bytes > 102400); global layer trimmed to budget` — on the same disclosure channel as the sub-agent budget block, so the model can tell the operator and the operator sees it without running a report command.

## Use case

- A user whose global preferences and project `AGENTS.md` together exceed 48 KiB currently cannot tell which half the agent actually read. They discover it by noticing the agent breaking a rule that is written in the file.
- A project whose `AGENTS.md` legitimately needs >100 KiB (an architecture + invariants + workflow document) has no way to load it at all — the layer is dropped, and the failing file is named only in a warning that no default surface shows.
- Tuning: raising the budget for a documentation-heavy repo is a per-user decision, exactly what a config key is for.

## Alternatives considered

- **Split the files** (the workaround): the right first move for the reporter and it needs no code, but it does not solve the visibility half, and it does not help a project that needs >100 KiB.
- **Raise both constants, change nothing else**: makes the budget a moving target with no surface to see it, and a project file over the per-file ceiling would still disappear silently.
- **Keep the skip, fix only the docs**: the docs already claim truncation; making them match a silent skip keeps the operator blind.
- **Put every warning into the system prompt verbatim**: unbounded and re-sent every turn; a single first-turn notice costs one line.

## Impact

Standing instructions shape every turn, so a silent trim silently changes behaviour — and it is invisible in `/cost`, `/tokens`, and the context meter because those measure tokens, not sources. Affected: anyone with a mature global + project instruction pair over 48 KiB, and anyone whose project file crosses 100 KiB.

## Additional context

- Both ceilings and their failure messages verified against `upstream/main` `a2216fc0c`; behaviour reproduced with `codewhale 0.10.0 (dev)`.
- Existing markers: `project_context.rs:391` (broader-scope drop) and `:392` (rules block); `fragments.rs:309` (foreign rule trim).
- `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md` agent-ready standard: the reproduction above is exact and code-referenced.

issues.title: Engine silently freezes mid-run: user messages are persisted but never answered; no error, no log line, no crash entry

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: subagents
labels.description: Sub-agent orchestration, lifecycle, and completion handling

labels.name: reliability
labels.description: Reliability, flaky behavior, retries, fallbacks, and robustness

issues.body:
## Body

```markdown
### Environment

- codewhale 0.9.13 (Rust TUI), linux x86_64
- provider: zai, model: GLM-5.3-Flash
- posture: Ask / workspace-write

### Summary

During long, tool-heavy runs the engine stops producing model output mid-turn.
Everything the user types afterwards is persisted into the session journal but
never answered. The stall is completely silent: no ERROR/WARN in the TUI log,
no crash entry, the spinner just keeps absorbing input.

This happened twice in two independent sessions on consecutive days.

### Steps to reproduce (observed, not deterministic)

1. Run an interactive session with a long skill-driven task that issues many
   bash tool calls (session A), or a multi-turn task with tool approval
   round-trips (session B).
2. Mid-run, the model stops emitting output (session B stalled right after an
   assistant thinking block, before any text/tool output).
3. Send follow-up user messages. They are accepted and persisted.
4. No reply ever arrives; force-quit is the only way out.

### Observed evidence (timestamps UTC)

Session A `a69916b2…` (2026-09-14):

- TUI log `tui-2026-09-14-2784622.log` ends at `10:51:38` with
  `engine.turn completion settled status=Completed delivered=true`.
- The session demonstrably continued for hours after that line and stalled
  later. The entire stall window produced **zero** additional log lines —
  the freeze is invisible to the log.
- Journal tail contains three consecutive `user` entries with no assistant
  response after them (a Chinese follow-up question, `"hello?"`, and a
  `/feedback bug` draft request).
- On-disk session JSON is structurally intact: 95 journal entries, valid
  `leaf_id` pointing at an existing entry, undamaged parent chain.

Session B `53b16822…` (2026-09-15):

- Assistant emitted a thinking block, then stalled before any text or tool
  output. A later `"继续"` (continue) user message also got no response.
- On force-quit, the TUI logged **two** pending turns at the same moment:

  ```
  2026-09-15T03:27:48.318072Z  INFO engine.turn: engine turn completion settled status=Interrupted delivered=true
  2026-09-15T03:27:48.548725Z  INFO engine.turn: engine turn completion settled status=Interrupted delivered=true
  ```

  Note `delivered=true` even though the user received no model output for
  either turn — the flag does not mean the user saw anything.

- `~/.codewhale/crashes/` is empty in both cases.

### Expected

- A stalled provider stream should be subject to a read/response timeout and
  surface a visible error in the UI.
- Queued user messages during a stalled turn should be rejected or reported,
  not silently absorbed.
- `delivered=true` on an Interrupted turn should not be recorded when nothing
  was ever rendered to the user.

### Impact

Long tasks can absorb follow-up messages indefinitely with zero feedback. The
user cannot distinguish "still working" from "dead" and must force-quit, which
then triggers the separate resume bug (filed separately).

### Hypothesis (unconfirmed)

No network-layer logs are available, so the transport-side root cause is
unknown. Suspected: a zai streaming hang with no read timeout in the harness.
Regardless of the transport cause, the missing stall detection and the silent
absorption of user messages are harness-side gaps.

---
Sanitized log excerpts: see `attachment-issue-1-logs.en.md`.
```
