issues.body:
## Problem

Codewhale retries the provider in several places, and by default none of them is visible in the
transcript. An operator watching the TUI cannot tell these three states apart:

- (a) the turn is retrying and will recover;
- (b) the turn is retrying and will exhaust its budget;
- (c) the turn already failed and needs a manual resend ("продолжи").

That ambiguity costs time twice — first while waiting, then while diagnosing after the fact. The
counters already exist in memory (`turn.stop_diagnostics.stream_resumes`,
`transparent_stream_retries`, `empty_stop_retries`, `reasoning_only_reprompts`), but they reach
neither the transcript nor the turn inspector, and the retry events themselves only go to
`crate::logging`, which is stderr-only and gated on `CODEWHALE_LOG_LEVEL`
(`crates/tui/src/logging.rs:73`).

Current state, verified against `upstream/main` at `568abae0e`:

- transport retry — callback in `crates/tui/src/client.rs:3876` →
  `logging::warn("Isolated HTTP retry reason=… attempt=… delay=…s")`;
- transparent stream retry — `crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:5879` →
  `logging::info("Transparent stream retry {n}/{limit} …")`;
- stream-open retry (#6699) — `turn_loop.rs:1957`, and mid-stream resume — `turn_loop.rs:2188`:
  `Event::status("Reconnecting…")` **only when `attempt == 2`**, with no attempt number, no limit
  and no reason.

So a single retry is completely invisible; the second and later ones print a bare `Reconnecting…`;
and the number of attempts never lands anywhere the operator can read afterwards.

## Proposed solution

1. Emit one transcript line per retry attempt using the existing status channel
   (`Event::status`), naming the kind (transport / transparent / resume / empty-stop), the
   attempt/limit, and a one-line reason. Example below.
2. Emit a closing line when the turn recovers (`recovered after N retries`) and when the budget is
   exhausted (`gave up after N retries · last: …`), so the two cases are distinguishable without
   opening JSON.
3. Surface the aggregate counters in the turn inspector — attempts per kind, plus whether the budget
   was exhausted or never entered. That last distinction is the one that currently cannot be made at
   all, and it is exactly what makes a post-mortem guesswork.
4. Respect the existing quiet controls (`notifications.quiet`, `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2542`): a quiet
   run keeps the counts and only suppresses the per-attempt lines.
5. Headless (`codewhale exec`, stream-json) needs the same events on the stream channel — a script
   cannot read stderr.

## Use case

### Example — operator-visible

Today, a turn that retried ten times and recovered is indistinguishable from one that failed
outright:

```
⚠ Provider returned an empty response
Reconnecting…
[turn ends]
```

(the only signal is `Reconnecting…`, from the second attempt onward; it never says which attempt, of
how many, or why; for transport and transparent retries there is no signal at all)

Wanted:

```
↻ retry 1/10 · provider error frame: "Provider returned an empty response" — nothing streamed, re-issuing
↻ retry 2/10 · transport: connect timeout, delay 4.0s
✓ recovered after 2 retries (4.1 s)
```

and when the budget runs out:

```
✗ gave up after 10 retries · last error: Provider returned an empty response
```

### When this matters

Long autonomous runs (Operate / goal runs, unattended overnight work) are exactly where retries
happen most and where the operator is least able to watch. Without the line, a silently retrying
turn and a dead turn look identical, and the only way to reconstruct what happened is to read
`turn_outcomes` out of the session JSON after the fact.

## Alternatives considered

- **Verbose logging only** (`CODEWHALE_LOG_LEVEL=info`): available today, but it is stderr, it is
  off by default, and it does not survive in the transcript the operator scrolls through. It also
  cannot be seen in a headless stream.
- **A dedicated retry pane/rail**: heavier than the problem; a status line plus the counters in the
  existing turn inspector covers it.
- **Notifications only** (the existing sound/toast path): does not answer "how many attempts, which
  kind, did it recover", and it is the wrong channel for a turn that is still running.

## Impact

Every interactive session that hits a flaky provider or a slow proxy. Two concrete costs today:
waiting on a turn without knowing whether it is alive, and post-mortem archaeology — during this
report's own investigation the retry counters had to be reconstructed from session files and code
because neither the transcript nor the log carried them.

## Additional context

- The three states above are all reachable with the default configuration; nothing needs to be
  misconfigured for (a)/(b)/(c) to be indistinguishable.
- Related: #6700 (retry budgets as configuration) — visibility is the natural companion; #6699
  (stream-open retry) introduced one of the `Reconnecting…` sites.
- The `attempt == 2` gate reads like a deliberate "calm UI" choice (a quick recovery needs no
  notice). The ask is not to make every retry loud: one line per attempt, suppressible via the
  existing quiet setting, plus an always-available count in the inspector.

prs.title: ci(sync): skip the CNB mirror when its token secret is absent
prs.body:
## What

`sync` fails on every push to a mirrored branch when the `CNB_GIT_TOKEN` repository secret is absent: "CNB_GIT_TOKEN secret is not set; cannot push to CNB." That is a repository-secret state, not a property of the commit — forks can never inherit the secret, so they report a red check no contributor can fix.

A `credentials` gate job probes the secret and skips the push when it is absent, emitting a notice that names the missing secret. Configured repositories keep the previous behavior, including the existing hard failure inside the push step, which still covers a caller pinned to an older revision of this workflow plus the window where the secret is deleted between the gate's probe and the push step.

`docs/CNB_MIRROR.md` documents the skip path and distinguishes "skipped because absent or misspelled" from "failed because expired" in the rotation section.

## Tests

- Workflow-parse level: jobs `credentials` + `sync`, `sync.if = needs.credentials.outputs.configured == 'true'` (verified locally; CI exercises the rest).
- The skip path is exercised by forks of the repository, where the secret cannot exist.

Co-authored with @zhuowp (original patch in the Pinvou/CodeWhale fork, #64); adapted to this workflow's retry/concurrency/`workflow_call` plumbing.

No-Issue: CI-only; forks cannot inherit CNB_GIT_TOKEN, so Sync to CNB fails on every fork push

prs.title: perf(picker): stop rebuilding catalogs per model row when /model opens
prs.body:
## Summary

Opening `/model` froze the whole TUI. On a machine with 52 configured
routes and 3,444 catalog rows it took 3-4 seconds; it now takes ~150 ms,
measured both before and after with temporary in-process marks that are
not part of this PR.

Four independent causes, each fixed in its own commit:

**1. One relay's catalog was rebuilt once per model row.** Three separate
seams each repeated work that depends only on the route:

- `cached_entry_for_route` returned a deep clone of the whole cached
  entry, so every row cloned every offering. On a 176-model relay that
  was 30,976 `CatalogOffering` copies for one picker open.
- `catalog_offering_for_route` then rebuilt the provider's owned
  bundled + Models.dev row map per row, cloning ~60 rows and allocating a
  fresh `BTreeMap` each time.
- `resolve_for_model` re-ran the credential resolver (secret store
  included) and the auth-class classification per row, and
  `route_identity_for_model` inside it ran the class walk a second time.

`with_cached_entry_for_route` lends the entry to a callback;
`source_rows_for_provider` is memoized on the live generation;
`RouteReadinessScope` hoists the route-scoped readiness facts.

**2. `route_is_valid_for_model` re-projected the whole bundled catalog per
row.** It called `RouteResolver::new()`, and `new()` = `from_offerings(
default_offerings())`, which re-projects every text-chat row of the
committed Models.dev asset plus the corrections pass and the
de-duplication maps. On 176 rows that is 176 full catalog projections.
`RouteResolver::bundled()` now shares one `OnceLock`-guarded resolver;
`new()` and `with_configured_models` are unchanged for callers that add
route-specific offerings.

**3. The `auto` row built a full `ModelInventory` for one line of text.**
`auto_picker_hint` read four router facts and paid for every configured
route's every model through runtime route resolution: 308 ms of a
1048 ms build. The router block never reads `candidates`, so
`ModelInventory::auto_router_only` skips only the candidate loop. No
logic is duplicated.

**4. `offerings_for_provider_identity` scanned the whole merged catalog
per row.** It walked every offering and computed
`catalog_partition_key` -- a `trim().to_string()` -- for each one, so a
3,444-row build over a few thousand offerings spent tens of millions of
string allocations on provider lookups. This was the largest single
stage (662 ms of 757 ms). `SharedSnapshot` now carries a
`provider -> rows` index built once with the snapshot.

## Measurements

Stage marks from the temporary instrumentation, same machine, opening
`/model` once per run:

| stage | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` row | 308 ms | 1.1 ms |
| per-row metadata | 663 ms | 79 ms |
| per-row readiness | 16.8 ms | 13.5 ms |
| per-row receipt | 12.8 ms | 10.1 ms |
| per-row push | 12.3 ms | 4.7 ms |
| **total picker build** | **1048 ms** | **149 ms** |

Per-route detail moved with it: `openrouter` (390 rows) 108.6 ms ->
17.0 ms, `edenai` (334 rows) 95.9 ms -> 17.8 ms, `openai` (177 rows)
48.0 ms -> 7.7 ms.

These numbers come from one machine and are quoted as an indication of
which seams mattered, not as a guarantee. The next bottleneck on a
large-route setup is `cloud_facts::overlay::snapshot()`, which takes the
process-wide overlay **write** lock once per row for every non-custom
provider; this PR does not touch it.

## Correctness

Nothing here changes observable behavior; each commit is a caching or
hoisting change behind an existing seam.

- `catalog_offering_for_route` keeps all five outcomes exactly: listed
  (row cloned and completed from lower layers), fetched-but-unlisted
  (only an attested-unlisted row, never a fall-through to the bundled
  merge), `fetched_at == 0`, absent entry, and cache error.
- `source_rows_for_provider`'s memo key is `(live generation, cloud
  generation or a sentinel, live layer present)`. The generation is
  sampled **before** the caller reads `LIVE_SNAPSHOT`, the ordering
  `merged_snapshot` already documents, so a concurrent refresh cannot
  leave stale rows tagged with the current generation.
- `SharedSnapshot`'s index uses the same `catalog_partition_key`
  derivation and preserves offering order, so `offerings_for_provider`
  returns the same rows in the same relative order as the scan it
  replaces.
- `auto_router_only` cannot change a router field: every one of them is
  derived from `config` after the loop, never from `candidates`.
- `RouteResolver::bundled()` is `Self::new` under a `OnceLock`, and
  `new()` has no environment, config, clock or network input, so it
  cannot freeze a stale answer. `resolve` takes `&self`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Performance (no behavior change)

## Testing

- [x] `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- provider_lake model_picker provider_picker provider_readiness client::catalog_tests model_inventory pricing` -> **411 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored**
- [x] `cargo test -p codewhale-config --lib -- route::` -> **102 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored** (commit 2 adds a public API in this crate)
- [x] `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --lib` -> clean
- [x] `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on all four changed files -> clean
- [x] `cargo build --release -p codewhale-cli -p codewhale-tui` -> Finished
- [x] The reported symptom was re-measured end to end on the reporting
      machine: 3-4 s before the chain, ~150 ms after.

## Notes for review

- Two additions are worth calling out because they are not pure caching:
  a second permanently resident `RouteResolver::bundled()` projection
  (a few MB; the client already keeps one), and a 32-entry memo of
  provider partitions that is evicted alphabetically rather than by use.
- The `SharedSnapshot` index normalizes provider keys through
  `catalog_partition_key` (trimmed). No producer of padded provider
  strings was found, so this is a latent change, not an observed one.
- No new tests: project policy. The changed paths are covered by the
  existing suites above; a direct assertion that `bundled()` and `new()`
  resolve identically would be the one test I would add if asked.

## Related Issues

No-Issue: reported as local `/model` latency; no upstream issue was opened.

## Attribution

🤖 Generated by SpikeBot 000(CodeWhale-LOCAL)

prs.title: fix(tui): end a clipped /feedback description at a word, with an ellipsis
prs.body:
## What and why

The /feedback picker lets the card edge cut each option's description, so below about 80 columns the rows end mid-word with nothing to say the text was cut. At 40×12, before:

```
 │ ▸ 1. Bug report    Report a proble │
 │   2. Feature request    Suggest an │
 │   3. Security vulnerability    Rev │
```

After:

```
 │ ▸ 1. Bug report    Report a…       │
 │   2. Feature request    Suggest…   │
 │   3. Security vulnerability    Re… │
```

At 60×16 the third row went from "Review the security pol" to "Review the security…".

/mode had the same problem and truncates its hints at a word boundary at the width left after the prefix, so this does the same: it measures the number, label and gap that are actually painted and truncates the description to the rest with `codewhale_ratatui::text::truncate_words`. That's the same word-boundary cut, but it spends `...` in ASCII-safe mode, where the backend would otherwise draw `…` as a lone `.` and "Review the security…" would read as a finished sentence. The third row at 40×12 has three columns left, so it gets the shortest form, "Re…" ("Re." in ASCII-safe mode). It's still not a whole word, but it now shows it was cut. Where the descriptions fit, as at 80×24 and 100×32, nothing changes.

## Issue

No-Issue: /feedback descriptions are cut mid-word at narrow widths, no issue filed for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and opened /feedback at 40×12, 50×14, 60×16, 80×24 and 100×32, with this change and with a build of d5f6699cc (the file is unchanged since). 80×24 and 100×32 are byte-identical before and after; the three narrower sizes differ only in the description text.
- With `CODEWHALE_ASCII_SAFE=1` at 60×16, the third row reads `Review the security.` with only the first commit and `Review the security...` with the second. Outside ASCII-safe mode the second commit changes nothing: 40×12, 50×14 and 60×16 are byte-identical to the first commit's.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15349 passed, none failed, including the six feedback picker tests.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on ba6366bc5; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): drop the hotbar setup rows' description stub beside the detail pane
prs.body:
## What and why

From 100 columns up, /keys (Hotbar setup) puts the action list and the selected action's details side by side. The list column is then 40 to 48 wide, and the marker, recommended tag, name and status take 39 of it, so a row's description never gets more than nine columns. At 100×32, before:

```
 │app actions                              Command palette                                        │
 │▸  rec Command palette        ready    … palette.open                                           │
 │   rec Compact session        ready    …                                                        │
 │   rec Cycle reasoning        ready    … Category: app                                          │
 │   rec Operate mode           ready    … Status: ready                                          │
```

After:

```
 │app actions                              Command palette                                        │
 │▸  rec Command palette        ready      palette.open                                           │
 │   rec Compact session        ready                                                             │
 │   rec Cycle reasoning        ready      Category: app                                          │
 │   rec Operate mode           ready      Status: ready                                          │
```

At 120×32 and 140×40 the rows read "Open…", "Shrink…", "Step…", "Do…". The full description is already in the detail pane ("Open the command palette." further down on the right).

So when the layout is split, the rows leave the description out and the detail pane shows it. `render()` already has `layout.stacked`, so it's passed down to `action_row_line`. The stacked layout below 100 columns and the 80-column `render_lines` export keep their descriptions, and a disabled row's reason still follows its status.

## Issue

No-Issue: Hotbar setup rows show a lone "…" or one word of description beside the detail pane, no issue filed for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME and opened /keys at 60×16, 80×24, 97×30, 98×30, 100×32, 120×32 and 140×40, with this change and without it. The four stacked sizes (up to 98×30) are byte-identical before and after. At 100, 120 and 140 the rows end after the status column, and so does the slash tab at 100.

## What and why

When the frame is too short for all eleven /statusline items, the list shows what fits and scrolls with the cursor, but nothing says more items are below. At 40×12, before:

 │    [✓] Context window %  (token…)│ │

prs.title: refactor(commands): adopt portable core navigation Shapes (FEAT-031)
prs.body:
## Summary

Completes the **13-command core navigation slice** behind portable command Shapes, in preparation for later crate extraction. No intended user-visible behavior change.

Commands: `/anchor`, `/help`, `/hotbar`, `/links`, `/transcript`, `/turn`, `/home`, `/overview`, `/workspace`, `/translate`, `/voice`, `/voicesend`, `/voicecontrol` (all existing aliases retained).

- Commands own parsing, branching, formatting and rendering; host adapters supply typed facts and narrow effects. Shared metadata/results/actions/payloads have no App/TUI dependency.
- Keep the existing `u32` capability identities; use bits 30/31 for navigation/voice input. Unrelated commands do not gain these new facet slots. The existing WORKSPACE facet does now expose confined anchor operations to its consumers; per-operation authority narrowing remains an acknowledged design follow-up.
- Remove the obsolete App-bound implementations, retain confined anchor I/O and workspace semantics, and move the unchanged voice capture runtime outside the movable command closure. Builtin voice shortcuts cannot be hijacked by a shadowing user command.
- Compile the actual complete production root independently through unpublished `tests/portable-core-navigation`. Check all 13 registrations exactly once in relative order, complete source closure, all-target normal dependency graph and rejection controls. Integrate CI/developer routing and release-order validation.

This is intentionally one coherent slice: the diff includes moved host tests/runtime and shared-contract consumer updates, rather than shipping parallel implementations. **The other 27 core registrations remain out of scope, the `core` frontier remains pending, and no physical crate movement is claimed.**

## Current review follow-up — 6e73d36cb

issues.body:
## Bug type

Reliability / delivery race — an **ordinary inbound channel message** arriving mid-turn drops the in-flight turn's reply and stalls the session queue.

## Summary

If a WhatsApp message arrives while a turn is already running on the same session, two things happen:

1. The **in-flight turn's reply is silently dropped.** The model call returns `200` and the reply is persisted, but it is never handed to the channel — there is no `[whatsapp] Sending message` line for it.
2. The **queued message is held for minutes** before dispatch, even though the model call completed seconds earlier and the lane goes idle.

Net effect: send two messages in quick succession, get **one** reply, several minutes late, answering only the later message. The first reply is gone permanently.

This looks like the same defect class as #135132 (closed NOT_PLANNED) and closed PR #127122 — dispatch not consulting the reply-run registry that channel-delivered turns register in. The difference, and the reason I'm filing separately: **#135132 requires a cron `announce` job to collide with the turn. This needs nothing but a user typing a second message while the agent is working**, which is ordinary conversational behaviour and makes the blast radius much larger.

Notably, the `visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads` diagnostic quoted in #135132/#112259 **does not appear** in my logs. This drop leaves no log evidence at all — the only signal is the *absence* of a send line after a successful model response.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.6.34** (`5c38f99`), macOS (Darwin 25.5.0), Node v22
- Channel: WhatsApp (Baileys)
- Provider: local OpenAI-compatible proxy → Codex `gpt-5.6-terra` (previously reproduced on `gpt-5.5` — model-independent)
- `agentRuntime`: default (not `claude-cli`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a WhatsApp message to the agent; it begins a turn.
2. While that turn is still running (a few seconds in), send a second message.
3. The first turn's reply never arrives.
4. The second message sits queued for several minutes, then dispatches and replies.

## Evidence

Gateway log (`~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log`), 2026-09-08, local time, numbers redacted:

```
23:25:18.863 [whatsapp] Inbound message <A> -> <B> (direct, 85 chars)
23:25:19.982 [model-fetch] start  provider=freerouter model=codex/gpt-5.6-terra
23:25:24.937 [whatsapp] Inbound message <A> -> <B> (direct, audio/ogg; 1247 chars)   <-- arrives mid-turn
23:25:25.434 [model-fetch] response status=200 elapsedMs=5451 contentType=text/event-stream
                                    <-- NO "[whatsapp] Sending message" for this turn. Reply dropped.
23:29:11.989 [whatsapp] Inbound message <A> -> <B> (direct, 73 chars)
                                    <-- no model call at all; swept into the same hold
23:31:51.790 [model-fetch] start  provider=freerouter model=codex/gpt-5.6-terra
23:31:55.830 [model-fetch] response status=200 elapsedMs=4038
23:31:56.561 [whatsapp] Sending message
23:31:56.734 [whatsapp] Sent message (174ms)
```

Contrast with the two healthy turns minutes earlier on the same session, where each `model-fetch response` is followed within ~1s by `Sending message`:

```
23:09:45.029 start -> 23:09:50.612 response 200 -> 23:09:51.332 Sending message  ✓
23:09:56.141 start -> 23:10:00.211 response 200 -> 23:10:13.147 Sending message  ✓
```

The model is never the problem — every call in the failing window returned `200` in 4–6s.

## Hold duration is not a fixed constant

Four prior observations of the hold clustered tightly at **~736s** (735.237s, 736.201s, 736.245s — the last two matching to 44ms). The occurrence above released after **~387s**, roughly half.

So the delay is **not** a single hardcoded timer. I previously scanned both the host `dist/` and the WhatsApp plugin `dist/` for integer literals in `700000..780000` and found none outside theme colors — consistent with the value being composed rather than configured. Whatever computes it is state- or load-dependent.

One caveat I can't fully exclude: a read-only `channels.status` RPC was issued ~116s before the 387s release. I see no mechanism by which a status read would drain the queue, and the hold did not release immediately, but I'm flagging it rather than asserting a clean self-release.

## Ruled out

- **Stuck-session watchdog / #140401** — `grep -c 'stuck session'` over the entire live gateway log returns **0**. Also inapplicable: that abort fires on long *generations*, whereas the dropped reply here completed in 5.4s.
- **Lane starvation / #54488** — lane idle, `compactionCount: 0`.
- **The model** — all calls `200` in 3–7s.
- **WhatsApp disconnect** — no reconnect in the window; sends immediately before and after succeed in <200ms.

## Impact

Silent message loss during normal use. The user sees an unanswered message and no error; the agent's tool calls from the dropped turn **do** apply, so state advances while the confirmation vanishes. There is no retry, no dead-letter, and — unlike #112259 — no log line.

## Workaround

Wait for a reply before sending a follow-up. A mid-turn message costs several minutes *and* eats the previous reply.

## Related

- #135132 — same defect class, cron-announce trigger (closed NOT_PLANNED)
- PR #127122 — "serialize agent-command turns against live reply runs" (closed, not merged)
- #112259 — silently dropped inbound turn, no retry/dead-letter
- #54488, #90240 — inbound held for tens of minutes, different mechanisms

issues.body:
## Summary

Add a runtime-enforced checkpoint policy for long foreground agent runs so that, after a configurable silent-time or tool-call budget, OpenClaw publishes a meaningful status update and cleanly yields before more work is dispatched.

## Problem to solve

OpenClaw can stream tool activity and models can be instructed to send commentary during multi-step work. Neither mechanism guarantees that a direct foreground WebChat run will stop at a user-defined checkpoint.

In repeated real-world maintenance workflows, an agent was given explicit workspace instructions to:

- publish a user-facing status update at least every 30–45 seconds;
- stop after a small number of tool calls;
- report the verified state and exact next step before continuing.

The model sometimes followed those rules, but it also repeatedly continued with “one more check” and exceeded the intended stage boundary. One such run eventually ended with a timeout/abort before a final handoff. This is not primarily a tool failure: the missing control is a runtime-owned boundary around the *foreground agent loop*.

Current facilities solve adjacent problems but not this one:

- progress streaming shows activity but does not enforce a semantic checkpoint or yield;
- queue steering allows new user input at model boundaries but does not create a boundary on a quiet run;
- per-tool timeouts bound individual calls, not the number or duration of successive calls;
- the overall turn timeout aborts late and may provide no clean last-known-state handoff;
- TaskFlow provides durable background orchestration, but ordinary interactive WebChat work still runs as one foreground turn unless explicitly moved into a task flow;
- prompt or `AGENTS.md` rules remain model-behavior constraints and are therefore not reliable enforcement.

This makes users uncertain whether the agent is progressing, drifting into unrelated checks, or stuck. It also forces them to supervise or manually interrupt work that should be safely bounded.

### Reproduction pattern

1. Configure workspace instructions requiring a visible status every 30–45 seconds and a stop after a fixed number of tool calls.
2. Start a direct WebChat request that needs several diagnostic or implementation calls.
3. Observe that the agent may emit an initial preamble but continue beyond the requested time/tool budget.
4. The UI can show low-level activity, but there is no runtime guarantee of a concise checkpoint containing verified state, meaning, and next action.
5. If the foreground run later times out or is aborted, the user may receive no controlled yield or durable continuation point.

Because model behavior is nondeterministic, the exact number of calls varies. The reproducible architectural fact is that OpenClaw currently has no configurable foreground-loop checkpoint enforcement; compliance depends on the model following instructions.

## Proposed solution

Introduce an opt-in, runtime-owned checkpoint policy for foreground agent runs, with agent defaults and optional channel/session overrides. An illustrative shape could be:

```yaml
agents:
  defaults:
    foregroundCheckpoints:
      enabled: true
      maxSilentMs: 30000
      maxToolCalls: 4
      action: checkpoint-and-yield
```

The exact schema is only a suggestion. The behavioral contract is more important:

1. Track elapsed time since the last user-visible semantic update and the number of completed tool calls since that update.
2. When either budget is reached, do not dispatch another tool call.
3. At the next safe model boundary, require a compact checkpoint with:
   - the current phase;
   - the last verified state;
   - the meaning or risk;
   - the exact next step;
   - whether user approval is required.
4. Publish that checkpoint to the originating WebChat and persist enough continuation metadata to resume safely.
5. End/yield the foreground turn cleanly. A later user message or explicit continuation mechanism starts the next bounded stage.
6. If the model does not produce the checkpoint within a short grace period, emit a deterministic fallback status from runtime-known data and end the turn safely.

Safety constraints:

- Never cancel an in-flight tool solely because the checkpoint budget elapsed; enforce the boundary after the tool settles.
- Preserve existing per-tool timeout and abort semantics.
- Do not expose raw tool output, secrets, private paths, or hidden reasoning in the fallback status.
- Keep the feature opt-in and backward-compatible.
- Allow `status-only` as an alternative action for users who want periodic checkpoints without yielding.

## Alternatives considered

### Prompt or workspace instructions

This is the current workaround. It is useful guidance but cannot serve as enforcement because the same model that performs the work decides whether to stop.

### Existing progress streaming

Progress drafts improve visibility, but tool names or activity receipts do not provide a guaranteed semantic checkpoint or prevent another tool call from starting.

### Shorter overall turn timeout

A hard timeout limits total duration but terminates at the wrong abstraction level. It can interrupt useful work and does not guarantee a clean status, persisted checkpoint, or safe continuation.

### Per-tool timeouts

These protect individual tool calls. They do not bound a long chain of individually successful calls or extended model analysis between calls.

### TaskFlow/background tasks

TaskFlow is appropriate for work deliberately started as a durable background workflow. Requiring every non-trivial interactive request to be manually converted into TaskFlow leaves the common foreground WebChat path unprotected.

## Impact

- **Affected users:** operators using WebChat or another interactive channel for multi-step administration, coding, research, or maintenance.
- **Severity:** medium to high for consequential work; an uncontrolled long turn can waste time, increase risk, and erode operator trust even when individual tools are safe.
- **Frequency:** intermittent and model-dependent, which makes instruction-only mitigation difficult to validate.
- **Practical consequences:** repeated manual supervision, avoidable interrupts, lost handoff context after timeouts, unnecessary tool calls, and delayed work on other priorities.

This is especially relevant to service-first and approval-gated deployments where the operator expects short, understandable stages and must remain in control.

## Evidence/examples

Related issues cover important adjacent capabilities:

- #13207 — streaming progress and mid-run injection; its original report explicitly noted that manual checkpoint messages are behavioral/unreliable. It was later closed because streaming and queue steering shipped.
- #45522 — durable long-running orchestration and progress; closed after TaskFlow shipped.
- #100388 — WebChat compaction progress and diagnostics.
- #103461 — narrated agent status updates and activity receipts.
- #105622 — bounded tool execution and abort signals.
- #83966 — configurable timeout metadata for Codex plugin runtime tools.

None of these defines a runtime-enforced *foreground agent-loop* checkpoint based on silent time or completed-tool count, followed by a controlled yield and durable handoff.

Test environment where the gap was observed:

- OpenClaw `2026.8.2`
- Control UI / WebChat
- OpenAI Codex runtime
- multi-step maintenance and diagnostic workflows

No private infrastructure details or credentials are needed to reproduce the architectural gap.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

This request is not asking OpenClaw to expose hidden reasoning or raw logs. The desired output is a small, redacted operational checkpoint. It also does not replace TaskFlow; it provides a safe bridge between ordinary foreground conversation and work that should be promoted into durable background orchestration.

issues.title: Discord message abandoned with 'changed while starting work' while the restart-recovery turn holds the session
issues.body:
It looks like restart recovery and the Discord ingress drain are colliding over the same session, close to what #127195, #142012 and #51620 circle around. Here is one concrete, repeatable trigger in case it helps narrow it down.

What happens
1. The gateway restarts (launchd stop/start).
2. Restart recovery resumes the interrupted Discord channel session and holds it.
3. A queued or new message for that channel loses the race for the session and is abandoned after about 43 ms: Session "agent:main:discord:channel:<id>" changed while starting work. Retry.
4. The drain retries with backoff and the message stays pending until recovery ends. The user sees no reply and no signal.
5. It is answered after recovery, unless the wait passes the 300 s adoption stall, where it drops (#142012).

Seen
- Oct 7: two scheduled restarts, about 50 errors; one message waited 5 min, another 26 min.
- Oct 15: a restart for a state-database repair, 29 error pairs from 14:48 to 15:20 PT; two messages were each abandoned about 8 times before being answered. The first turns after that restart also logged "long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool".

Each attempt logs one diagnostic line (outcome=error duration=43ms) and one "discord message run failed" line with the same error.

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.8.1-beta.2 (8f382a2), Node 22.23.1, macOS 26.6.2 x64, launchd gateway; plugins anthropic, browser, discord, llama-cpp, memory-core. Not yet re-tested on 2026.9.x.

Workaround: we leave the message pending and raised the Discord adoption stall locally so nothing drops at 300 s. Nothing local addresses the race itself.

Would it be a bad idea for the drain to wait for restart recovery to release the session, instead of abandoning and retrying? Glad to pull logs from the next occurrence.

issues.body:
## Summary

`src/gateway/gateway-cron-placement.live.test.ts` ("writes allowed root replies and rejects a reassigned root's stale generation before execution") fails deterministically with `The forced cron run did not publish its completion record` on main (13/13 runs since 2026-10-08 15:50 UTC) and on every release/2026.10.5 candidate. 2026.10.4 and earlier lines pass it.

## Cause

Test drift from the intended behavior change in #165310 (compaction repeatedly fails when a session-bound cron job targets the same session): a session-bound cron claim now waits and retries while another writer holds the session.

The `HOOK_ROTATED` step pauses an agent run on the cron root session inside a reply hook, then calls `cron.run` with `mode: "force"` on that same session to rotate its generation. The forced run now waits for the paused writer, and the writer only resumes after the cron run completes, so the step deadlocks until its timeout. Earlier phases (including stale-generation rejection before execution) still pass.

## Proposed fix

Keep #165310's behavior (it fixes real compaction corruption). Rework the `HOOK_ROTATED` step to rotate the root generation through a path that does not wait on the paused writer, or assert the new contract (the forced run waits for the writer) and cover post-hook revocation separately.

## Release note

release/2026.10.5 skips only the `HOOK_ROTATED` iteration of this test, with a reference to this issue; `HOOK_ALLOWED` and all other phases still run.

issues.body:
### Version

`OpenClaw 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23)`

### Summary

`config_revision` is a **content hash** of scheduler definition state, not a counter. It therefore cycles: any sequence of writes that returns a job's definition to an earlier state reproduces the earlier revision value exactly. There is no monotonic witness for "this scheduler row has been mutated since I last looked", which makes a whole class of crash-recovery decisions undecidable for anything coordinating scheduler mutations from outside the gateway.

### What I measured

`cron_run_receipts.config_revision` on the installed build holds values of the form:

```
sha256:1G__-1NsDidK2gKeG5W0498-l5IDwhuiPYwavTPSiKk
sha256:1HOYtlFadU6BZwZ3msfTBkJXMzi1a_HnZ5SiMuagEA4
sha256:2SylwFJVGuO1-5Zz8IGZaV4qWH3GydRhR4T53pGtP4Q
```

A content hash over definition state. Disable a job and re-enable it and the value returns to what it was before, because the definition state did. That is correct for the job it does — detecting that a definition changed under you — and unusable as an ordering or write-count witness.

The nearest alternative, `scheduleActivatedAtMs`, does advance on a mutation, but it is generated *inside* the update transaction, so an external caller cannot record its post-write value before the write it is trying to survive.

### Why it matters

A supervisor that repoints a scheduler row does so as a multi-step sequence: disable the row, write the new payload, re-enable it. If it publishes a fence describing the change and then dies mid-sequence, crash repair has to decide between two histories that end in an identical state:

- **Stale crash:** the fence was published, the row was disabled, the process died. The row should be re-enabled.
- **Legitimate:** the repoint completed, the fence's publisher died before clearing it, and an operator disabled the row later. The row must be left alone — re-enabling it would revive something a human deliberately turned off.

Both end at a disabled row whose payload matches the fence's target, with the same fence body, the same publisher identity, and a `config_revision` that can be made equal by choosing a suitable starting state. The two histories differ only in **write count** — one write versus three — and nothing durable records write count.

Without a witness, repair must take the conservative branch and leave the row disabled, which strands the stale-crash case permanently. That is survivable but wrong, and it is only survivable because prevention (refusing to act when the row changed under the decision) keeps the state rare.

### What would fix it

Either of these makes the two histories distinguishable:

- **A monotonic mutation counter on scheduler rows** — a strictly increasing integer bumped once per applied write, exposed alongside `config_revision` and readable before a mutation. Content hashing and ordering are different jobs; `config_revision` should keep doing the first.
- **Persist a caller-supplied causal witness inside the same scheduler transaction as the mutation**, so an external coordinator can record "the revision immediately before my own write" atomically rather than racing it.

I am not asking for `config_revision` to change semantics — hashing definition state is the right primitive for change detection. The gap is that there is no second primitive for ordering.

### Reproduction

```sh
sqlite3 ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite \
  "select distinct config_revision from cron_run_receipts limit 5;"
```

Every value is a `sha256:` digest over definition state, with no ordering information.

issues.body:
**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.9.9 (bcfc888), `@openclaw/codex` 2026.9.9, macOS. Agent runs on the Codex app-server harness with a ChatGPT account; model `openai/gpt-5.6-terra`. `codexPlugins.enabled: true` with the curated Notion plugin enabled.

**What happens**
- In interactive turns, the Notion app tools work (`codex_apps.notion.fetch`, `notion-create-pages`, etc.).
- When the agent creates an automation from that same kind of turn with `toolsAllow` containing the Notion search/fetch tools plus `message`, the job is saved with only `["message"]`. No error, no warning.
- The saved job has `scheduledToolPolicy: { mode: "account", ... }` and no captured app authority. Scheduled runs get only `exec`/`memory_*`/`message`, and the agent reports "lacks current Codex app authority. Recreate or reauthorize this automation from a fresh authenticated Codex owner turn." Recreating the job as told gives the same result.
- Same result whether the creating turn came from Telegram or from `openclaw tui`.

**Expected**
Per docs (`plugins/codex-native-plugins.md#scheduled-automations`, `automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md#codex-apps-in-scheduled-automations`), a job created from an authenticated owner Codex turn should capture the app IDs and run with them. Or, if capture isn't supported for this auth mode, the create should fail with the documented recovery message instead of silently narrowing the cap.

**Repro**
1. Codex harness agent signed in with ChatGPT, Notion plugin enabled and working interactively.
2. In a chat turn: "Create a test automation, disabled, once next week, tools: notion search, notion fetch, message. Show the saved toolsAllow."
3. Saved `toolsAllow` is `["message"]`.

**Possible cause (from reading dist, not verified)**
In `run-attempt`, `codexAppsMayBeVisible` is `false` when `isCodexResponsesOAuth(connection.startupPreparedAuth)` (`inferenceAuth === "host-oauth"`). Then `resolveScheduledCodexAppCreatorCaptureDecision` returns `{ required: false, supported: false }`, so no app authority is captured and the requested app tool names are intersected away against the OpenClaw dynamic tool surface. But app tools are in fact visible on these turns. If that's right, either app capture should be supported for this auth path, or the create should be refused with a clear message.

**Workaround**
`toolsAllow: ["*"]` lets scheduled runs reach Notion, but loses the read-only cap.

issues.body:
## Summary

On 2026.10.5, transient session-state races during prompt admission are classified as `reason=unknown` model-candidate failures, so the model fallback chain advances to a different provider instead of retrying the same model. The user sees "↪️ Model Fallback: openai/gpt-6.1-sol (selected anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; unknown)" although the primary provider was healthy.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9), Linux gateway (systemd user service)
- Telegram direct session, agent main, primary anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (subscription token), fallbacks openai/gpt-6.1-sol, xai/grok-4.7, openai/gpt-6-astra, google/gemini-4-argon, anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5

## Observed (two occurrences on 2026-10-19, times PDT)

1. 14:34:43
   - `embedded run failover decision: stage=prompt decision=surface_error reason=none attempt=1 rotations=0 from=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 rawError=Persisted user turn changed before replay admission`
   - Then `model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 reason=unknown next=openai/gpt-6.1-sol`
2. 20:26:23: the same two lines, the same rawError, and the same jump to openai/gpt-6.1-sol.
   - At 20:31:15 a related error, `detail=Session reader operation is no longer current`, also produced `candidate_failed ... reason=unknown` and moved the chain further: google/gemini-4-argon to anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5.

**Context:** both times, the session transcript was being changed concurrently while the user's turn was admitted. Triggers included:
- a cron announce delivered into the same chat
- a background skill-workshop update
- exec completion events
- config hot reloads and a plugin reload ("Model runtime replacement is in progress")

## Expected

These errors are local session/transcript concurrency conditions, not provider or model failures.

- They should be retried on the **same** model, after re-reading the persisted turn or waiting for the reload or reader to become current.
- If they surface at all, it should be as a retryable local error, never as a model-candidate failure that advances provider fallback. Doing that switches the user to another provider and can change billing, behaviour and model quality.
- At minimum, classify them with a dedicated reason such as `session_state_conflict` rather than `unknown`, and exclude that reason from cross-model fallback.

## Actual

They are classified `reason=unknown`, which the fallback controller treats as a candidate failure. One user turn can then walk through several providers, each hitting the same local condition.

## Related

#165683 (same "persisted user turn replay-admission" error in Realtime Talk consult), #157255 (session lane not released after config-change errors; same root area).

## Impact

Unexpected provider switches; misleading "unknown" fallback notices. Frequent on busy sessions with background automations, twice in one evening here.

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, the `claude-cli` runtime hands the selected Anthropic auth-profile token to Claude Code with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_FILE_DESCRIPTOR=3` and a stdio[3] pipe (`"overlapped"` on win32 in `prepareSecretInputStdio`). Claude Code doesn't appear to pick up the token. It falls back to its own `claude auth login` credentials. As a result, every run uses the CLI's saved account, whichever profile OpenClaw selected. Switching to the next `auth.order` profile restarts the CLI but still sends requests from the exhausted account.

OpenClaw then marks the healthy profile as rate-limited, because it attributes the failure to the profile it thinks it used.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6, Claude Code 2.1.280, Windows 11 x64, native (no WSL), gateway run from `node dist/index.js gateway`
- All `anthropic/*` models use `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`
- Two setup-token profiles (`sk-ant-oat01-…`, different Claude subscriptions): `auth.order.anthropic = [anthropic:layne, anthropic:jill]`
- Claude Code on the host is logged in (`claude auth login`) to the **anthropic:layne** account

## Evidence

1. I called `/v1/messages` directly with each stored token:
   - `anthropic:layne` → 429, `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-7d-status: rejected` (weekly limit, resets Oct 3 22:00 UTC)
   - `anthropic:jill` → 200, `7d-utilization: 0.1`, `5h-utilization: 0.01`. It's a different `anthropic-organization-id`.
2. The gateway did switch the ltsa agent to jill. It restarted the CLI with the new profile and still got the layne account's weekly-limit error:

```
[agent/cli-backend] cli session reset: provider=claude-cli reason=auth-profile
[agent/cli-backend] cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown
[agent/cli-backend] cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-fable-5-1 ... reuse=invalidated:auth-profile
[agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-fable-5-1 activeSessions=2
[agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: ... durationMs=8261 error=You've hit your weekly limit · resets Oct 3, 10pm (UTC)
[agent/embedded] auth profile failure state updated: profile=sha256:b3f4ccf67e19 provider=anthropic reason=rate_limit window=cooldown reused=false
[model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-fable-5-1 reason=rate_limit next=none
```

`sha256:b3f4ccf67e19` = sha256("anthropic:jill"). The reset time in that error matches the layne account exactly. The jill account wasn't limited.

3. Runs on the layne profile (`sha256:9b9d3b00eada`) failed with the same message and reset time.
4. After I switched Claude Code's own login to the jill account (`claude auth logout` / `claude auth login`), all agents worked again. No OpenClaw config changed.

## Expected

The token from the selected profile is what Claude Code uses on Windows. If the fd handoff isn't supported there, OpenClaw should either use a Windows-safe transport or refuse to start the run, rather than silently falling back to the CLI's ambient login.

## Secondary observations

- An Anthropic weekly-limit error is classified as `rate_limit` with a 30–60 s cooldown (ltsa's `usageStats` showed `cooldownUntil` = failure + 60 s). The reset time is in the error text, so the cooldown could run until the reset instead of retrying the exhausted account every minute. Related to #158144.
- The `main` agent's `auth_profile_store` has `profiles: {}` (only `order` is set in `auth_profile_state`), so it always runs on the ambient login.

Related:
- #158144 covers a session staying pinned to a limited profile. This one covers the switch itself having no effect on Windows.
- #141196 was the same fd-3 handoff being ignored on Linux (Claude Code 2.1.251), closed 2026-09-07. It still happens on Windows with Claude Code 2.1.280.

issues.body:
## Bug description

On Windows, starting an OpenClaw update from the Control UI repeatedly freezes in the managed updater's `validating` phase. The Gateway stays reachable, the driver PID remains alive and consumes CPU, but `activeRun.updatedAtMs` and the step list stop advancing. No package activation begins and `after` remains empty.

The supported abandoned-update recovery succeeds, but retrying through the Gateway update action reproduces the same freeze at the same validation point.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: **2026.9.6** (npm global package install)
- Update target: **2026.9.7** (stable/latest)
- OS: **Windows_NT 10.0.26200 x64**
- Node.js: **24.19.0**
- Gateway service: **Windows Scheduled Task**
- Gateway bind: loopback
- Config validation: passes
- Free disk space: about 560 GiB

## Reproduction

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.6 as the Scheduled Task-managed Gateway.
2. Open the Control UI and start the available update to 2026.9.7.
3. Observe the managed handoff complete, followed by target resolution, snapshot-space preflight, and staging.
4. The run enters `validating` and stops recording progress indefinitely.
5. Confirm with `openclaw update status --json`: the driver is alive, `after` is `{}`, and `updatedAtMs` is frozen.
6. Run `openclaw update repair --yes --no-restart --json`. It reports the live but inactive driver and recommends stopping only that driver.
7. Stop the reported update driver, rerun repair, and confirm the abandoned run is reconciled while the Gateway remains healthy.
8. Retry only through the Gateway managed update action. The second run freezes at the same `validating` point.

## Reproduced runs

- First run: `2fd44e5e-4ca5-45ea-a7c4-d7fb1a700ffa`
- Retry: `c6f217f4-9958-4589-98ce-cc2711e217c4`

Both runs completed:

- managed-service update handoff
- target resolution
- snapshot-space preflight
- staging

Both then froze at:

```json
{
  "step": "validating",
  "status": "in_progress"
}
```

In both cases:

- `after` stayed empty
- the running version remained 2026.9.6
- the Gateway remained reachable
- no activation/package mutation was recorded

The handoff log stopped after messages equivalent to:

```text
managed update ownership transferred; validating while the gateway serves
starting managed update command: openclaw update --yes
managed update update command pid=<pid>
```

## Repair behavior

The first stuck driver was stopped only after `openclaw update repair` explicitly reported no recent activity and recommended stopping it through its owner/supervisor. Repair then reached a terminal success state and cleared the old `activeRun`. Doctor/plugin convergence was skipped because the supervised Gateway was still serving; the Gateway was not implicitly restarted.

The retry reproduced the exact same freeze, so process termination was not repeated.

## Expected behavior

Validation should either:

1. complete and proceed to snapshot/install/activation; or
2. fail within a bounded timeout with the exact validation substep and actionable error.

It should not remain indefinitely in `validating` with a live CPU-consuming driver and no state updates.

## Additional observations

- Snapshot-space preflight succeeded (roughly 273–292 MiB required).
- The npm-global installation reports a missing package lockfile, which appears normal for this install kind.
- There is official plugin drift: `tokenjuice` is on 2026.9.3 and its available target requires plugin API >=2026.9.7. It is unclear whether this contributes to validation.
- The Scheduled Task definition reports several fields as `current: null` versus installer defaults, but Gateway connectivity is healthy.

No secrets, authorization headers, pairing data, or full local logs are included here. I can provide a sanitized diagnostic bundle if maintainers request one.

Agent-prepared report, published with the operator's explicit approval. Private transcripts, account identifiers and raw dumps are omitted.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Native Codex child-completion delivery repeatedly fails before inference with `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` on the `agent_harness_completion` route, leaving the attempted continuation uncommitted.

### Steps to reproduce

No deterministic reproduction is currently available. The observed scenario was native Codex child-completion delivery to its requester: the active-requester wake reported `transcript_commit_wait_unsupported`, then the requester-agent fallback using `sourceTool=agent_harness_completion` failed before inference with `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED`. Three correlated failures on release 2026.9.7 are documented in the [evidence follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162637#issuecomment-5930534040). Their triggering ownership state and exact rejecting assertion were not captured. A separate successful handoff is only a control, not a reproduction of the failing branch. The [latest review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162637#issuecomment-5930123874) requests maintainer-assisted bounded diagnostic capture to distinguish these branches.

### Expected behavior

A native child-completion message is committed to the requester's transcript and resumes the parent. A later controlled completion using the same `sourceTool=agent_harness_completion` did both; this does not establish that it exercised the same guard branch as the failures.

### Actual behavior

Observed on 2026-10-01:

1. The active-requester wake reports `queue_message_failed reason=transcript_commit_wait_unsupported` while Gateway is live.
2. The requester-agent fallback uses provenance `sourceTool=agent_harness_completion`.
3. It fails before inference with `admitted run authority is no longer active`, whose nested cause contains `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED`.
4. The exact failed announce remains in pending inputs as `interrupted`, with `consumed_event_id=null` and no matching committed source-transcript identity. This is an observation, **not proof that missing transcript identity initiated the failure**.

The original defect remains unresolved, and the exact failing assertion branch is unknown. The successful control shows only that failure is not universal for this sourceTool.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.7

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS; Node.js 24.21.0

### Install method

npm global

### Model

The exact model selected for the failed continuations was not captured in the reviewed incident evidence. The rejection occurred before model inference, on the OpenClaw Gateway → native Codex harness completion path. Current configured defaults should not be treated as proof of the model selected for those historical attempts.

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Gateway -> native Codex harness. The observed failed continuation is rejected before model inference.

### Logs

Sanitized diagnostic excerpts (identifiers omitted):

```text
queue_message_failed reason=transcript_commit_wait_unsupported
admitted run authority is no longer active | Session ... changed while starting work. Retry. | SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Installed-source review:

- `getActiveAgentRunDelegatedAuthority` catches `context.assertSourceCurrent`, retains its first error as cause, and releases the claim.
- Native `createHarnessCompletionSourceAssertion` includes a prior assertion, exact session/owed-claim checks, and recovery-delivery equality/transcript-source validation.
- The recovery-delivery equality path can allow an uncommitted input, so pending-input state alone cannot identify the failing branch.
- Post-failure cleanup clears recovery fields; their absence in a later snapshot cannot establish the earlier transition.

### Impact and severity

Observed in one operator's delegated native Codex workflow. The parent continuation does not start for affected completion deliveries, interrupting follow-through despite retained child results. Repeated failures and one successful control were observed; frequency outside these observations is unknown. No claim of underlying transcript or memory corruption is made.

### Additional information

Related, not assumed equivalent:

- #161769 / #161788 concern the `subagent_announce` recovery-owner gate. The reviewed production diff extends that gate to `subagent_announce`, not `agent_harness_completion`; it does not establish a fix for this native route.
- #127195 describes the lack of diagnostic discrimination between source-assertion failures sharing the same message.

Requested maintainer diagnosis: identify or safely instrument the exact failing source-assertion branch, preserving structured stack/cause and pre-failure operational/source-run identity, recovery ownership and owed-claim state without logging message content. Please confirm whether native harness completion belongs under the recovery-owner fix or a separate issue.

No session reset, unsupported vendor patch, permission expansion or memory-setup change was applied as a fix.

Diagnostic caveat: a later local inspector experiment captured no failing frames. Timing and the matching dynamic-import error strongly implicate its cleanup in a separate Gateway crash and automatic restart; the log lacks inspector request-ID correlation. That experiment was retired. Neither its restart nor its empty capture is evidence for the original root cause, and this report is not asking to diagnose that separate experiment.

issues.body:
# Feature: bounded per-invocation input for `cron.run`

## Summary

Allow an authorized `cron.run` caller to attach bounded, non-persistent input
to one execution without editing the stored automation definition.

## Current behavior

On current main at `7dc4a94490cd`, `CronRunParamsSchema` is closed over the job
ID, run mode, and expected process identity. A `context` field is rejected. The
Gateway forwards only its caller-authority commit guard to `enqueueRun`, whose
options also contain only that guard.

The direct in-process `run(...)` path has a full-payload override for trusted
event-source callers. It clones that payload into the manual-run reservation,
but it is not available to queued Gateway callers and is not an external-input
contract.

This leaves integrations with changing trigger data to mutate the persistent
job, create one-off jobs, or encode external data outside the run request.

## Proposed contract for owner review

- Accept an optional string or JSON object on `cron.run` only.
- Render deterministically and enforce both schema and authoritative UTF-8 byte
  limits before admission.
- Treat the value as external untrusted input and bind its provenance and stable
  input identity at the pre-model boundary. Untrusted-content marking is not an
  authorization or prompt-injection boundary.
- Apply it to exactly one `agentTurn` or `systemEvent` execution and never write
  it to the stored job.
- Reject unsupported payload kinds rather than silently dropping the value.
- Acknowledge whether context was applied and log only content-free metadata.
- Preserve ordinary context-free runs byte-for-byte.
- Reject context on host-approved jobs unless the signed invocation format
  covers the exact context and its relevant policy fields.

## Decisions requested

1. Is per-run external input a supported public Cron use case?
2. Which payload kinds may consume it, and where should it appear in the prompt?
3. What provenance, stable identity, authorization, and approval binding are
   required before model submission?
4. What size, audit, recovery, and queued-run acknowledgment semantics should
   be permanent API guarantees?

Related issues `#107069` and `#160232` cover provenance and stable pre-model
input identity. They do not currently own this `cron.run` API. Broad issue
`#29442` covers unattended prompt-injection architecture and should inform, but
not substitute for, the decision above.

This is also distinct from delivered-message continuity (`#51430`), inherited
main-session state (`#54601`), and delegated OAuth requester authority
(`#102098`). Those contracts do not provide caller-supplied data for exactly one
run.

No PR is proposed until Cron and security owners choose the public boundary.

# Bug report (draft for OpenClaw GitHub): agent tool RPCs fail with "Gateway client authority closed before dispatching <method>"

**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200, Node 24.19.0.
**Setup:** single gateway on port 18789, launched by Task Scheduler (S4U, session 0); main agent on claude-cli runtime; Telegram channel; SQLite state store.

## Symptom

From inside the main agent's tool calls, every state-mutating gateway RPC fails immediately with:

```
Gateway client authority closed before dispatching sessions.patch.
Gateway client authority closed before dispatching message.action.
Gateway client authority closed before dispatching secrets.store.list.
Gateway client authority closed before dispatching sessions.list.   (intermittent)
```

Meanwhile, in the same session: inbound channel messages, agent turns, replies, scheduled jobs, and *external* WebSocket clients (standalone script using callGateway with the config token) all work.

## Timeline / what we ruled out

- First observed 2026-09-28 ~08:18 PT, minutes after an interactive `openclaw models auth login` session in which an auth-list subcommand hung and was force-killed.
- Survived: config hot reloads; a gateway self-restart via RPC on 09-28 (~15:29 PT) — note that restart's shutdown was recorded in `gateway_boot_lifecycle` as `outcome: "forced_stop", reason: "gateway.restart_close_failed"`; full credential rotation (gateway token + all device tokens) on 09-28; and a second, verified-fresh self-restart on 09-29 14:31 PT (new PID, clean boot) — **bug still present immediately on the fresh boot**.
- Not correlated with model/provider: occurs regardless of active model.
- `npm view openclaw version` = 2026.9.6 → already latest at time of writing.

## Possibly-related observations

1. `agent_database_leases` contained **two live leases for the same agent DB** under two path spellings — `C:\Users\david\...` and `\\?\C:\Users\david\...` (extended-length prefix), both attributed to the then-current gateway PID. Suggests a path-normalization miss in lease identity.
2. Persistent `slow SQLite session write` warnings on the main thread: `queueWaitMs` 3,700–23,000 ms (writerExecutionMs ~0–21 ms), operations `session.entry-replacements`, `session.maintenance.plan`, `session.transcript.turn`.
3. `openclaw models auth paste-token` reported success while the profile never appeared in `models auth list` — separately observed store log line: `auth profile store update failed: another OpenClaw process owns state-lifecycle` with the CLI still exiting success (silent-failure path in dist store module).
4. One earlier interactive `models auth list` process hung indefinitely and was force-killed; the first "authority closed" errors appeared shortly after.

## Impact

Agent cannot: switch session models, send proactive channel messages (`message` tool), create Telegram forum topics, or list/manage secrets — while all passive/turn-based functionality is unaffected. Workarounds in use: owner-side `/model` command, humans create topics, reply-path-only messaging.

## Repro (as best we can tell)

Unclear-trigger; possibly: interactive `models auth` CLI session crashing/hung while gateway is live → subsequent in-agent RPC clients permanently refused, surviving restarts. Happy to provide logs/DB snapshots on request.

issues.body:
## Problem

Closed issue #113440 requested a generic pre-effect authorization boundary for nested operations and was closed automatically as stale on September 25 with instructions to file a fresh issue if the gap persists. It still persists on current main (`648f82b0574ab7d07533c577f22f574648dee81a`).

`before_tool_call` authorizes the model-visible top-level invocation. Several tools resolve a more specific effect afterward, including:

- exec selecting the effective host, node, command, and working directory;
- `nodes` selecting a concrete node and invoke command;
- bundled MCP resolving server/tool identity;
- plugin tools dispatching an internal host-owned operation.

Current source has no `before_tool_operation` hook, operation authorizer binder, or common post-resolution/pre-effect callback. A policy can inspect raw top-level parameters but cannot authorize the exact resolved operation immediately before its first effect.

## Requested contract decision

Should the Plugin SDK define an opt-in, host-owned pre-effect authorization contract for an explicit initial set of resolved operation families?

The contract should decide:

1. The supported operation taxonomy and an explicit unsupported-path list.
2. Which owner resolves and snapshots target/action/arguments, and exactly where the first effect begins.
3. Bounded redaction-safe event fields and stable per-attempt identity.
4. Retry, cancellation, replacement, and target-change semantics.
5. Whether authorization attaches to existing trusted policies or a distinct hook family.
6. How mandatory authorizers are selected and retained across plugin reload/disable.

## Required composition semantics

For host-selected required authorizers, every authorizer must return an explicit pass for the same immutable resolved operation. A pass from one must not survive another required authorizer returning nothing, returning malformed data, blocking, throwing, rejecting, timing out, or observing cancellation. Registration order must not change the result, and late completion must not revive authorization.

This is narrower than changing ordinary optional hooks globally. The explicit-pass question is also recorded on #155346; that issue concerns host-resolved cross-agent session targets and is adjacent rather than a replacement for nested exec/node/MCP/plugin effects.

## Current-source evidence

- `src/plugins/hook-types.ts` exposes `before_tool_call` and `after_tool_call`, but no resolved-operation event or hook.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.ts` wraps the top-level tool execution; it does not bind a later family-specific authorizer.
- exec, nodes, and bundled MCP paths have owner-specific resolution and effect calls without one shared plugin authorization seam.
- Exact-name issue and PR searches found only closed #113440; no implementation PR exists. Merged #142661 preserves MCP App ticket authority for its own path and does not add a generic nested-operation hook.

## Acceptance evidence

Before implementation is considered complete:

- enumerate covered and unsupported effect families;
- prove denial before the first exec, node, MCP, and plugin-owned effect;
- prove all-pass and every failure mode in both authorizer orders;
- prove resolved target/argument mutation requires reauthorization or denial;
- prove stable attempt identity across retries without replaying stale authority;
- prove cancellation and plugin lifecycle loss fail closed with no late revival;
- keep event payloads bounded and free of credentials, private policy objects, and session contents;
- preserve ordinary behavior when no mandatory authorizer set is configured.

This is a security/SDK contract request, not a claim that current documented `before_tool_call` behavior is broken. Owner direction is requested before a fix PR.

issues.body:
## Problem

`sessions.create` can select a model, runtime, workspace, permissions, tools, and an optional initial turn, but it cannot attach bounded session-owned system context that should apply to later turns.

This is distinct from the existing prompt-extension surfaces:

- `before_prompt_build` lets a trusted plugin contribute dynamic context for a turn.
- Plugin next-turn injections are durable until consumed, but intentionally one-shot.
- Internal `extraSystemPrompt` parameters are invocation-scoped.
- Persisted CLI fields retain hashes/fingerprints, not the prompt text.

A client that creates a specialized session therefore cannot express durable session instructions through the public Gateway contract without installing a plugin or rewriting each turn.

## Requested contract decision

Would OpenClaw accept a create-only, bounded field for durable session system context, with server-authored provenance and explicit lifecycle semantics?

A safe shape should decide:

1. Whether this belongs on `sessions.create`, a plugin-owned session extension, or another API.
2. Whether requesting it requires `operator.admin` rather than ordinary `operator.write`.
3. The text/byte limit and whether blank input is omitted.
4. Whether adoption of an existing key may set or replace it.
5. What reset, fork, archive/restore, succession, and session-id rotation do with it.
6. Which runtimes must apply it, including WebChat/embedded and CLI-backed sessions.
7. Whether public session projections expose the text, a redacted marker, or only a hash.
8. How persisted data is authenticated so hand-edited or legacy fields cannot become system instructions.

## Current-source evidence

On current main:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions-create.ts` has no prompt/personality field.
- `src/config/sessions/types.ts` has plugin extensions and durable one-shot next-turn injections, but no session-owned persistent prompt text.
- `src/plugins/hook-before-agent-start.types.ts` supports `systemPrompt`, `prependSystemContext`, and `appendSystemContext` from `before_prompt_build`; those are plugin contributions evaluated at prompt-build time.
- `src/shared/session-method-scopes-base.ts` currently leaves ordinary `sessions.create` at `operator.write` unless an existing privileged field is requested.

## Acceptance evidence

A future implementation should include protocol validation plus end-to-end tests proving:

- over-limit input is rejected;
- only server-authored/provenanced state is applied;
- later turns receive the context across supported runtimes;
- lifecycle operations follow the chosen retention policy;
- callers lacking the chosen authority cannot set or replace it;
- untrusted persisted fields and public projections cannot inject instructions.

This issue seeks owner direction on the contract and authority boundary before a fix PR.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let the command palette (⌘K / Ctrl+K) run actions on the open conversation: Rename, Archive or Restore, Pin or Unpin, Mark as read or unread, Fork, and Delete.

### Problem to solve

The palette only offers page links, `/verbose`, and search. Typing "archive" or "rename" returns sessions whose titles contain those words, but never the action itself. To rename or archive the chat you are looking at, you have to leave the keyboard and use the chat header's `…` menu or the sidebar's context menu. Archive has ⌘⇧A, but Rename, Pin, Fork, and the rest have no keyboard route.

### Proposed solution

While a chat is open, add a **Current session** group to the palette with the same single-session actions the chat header menu offers for that session:

- Use the header menu's rules: an action appears only when the header menu would enable it (permissions, main-session protection, archived state, compact panes without a header, and so on).
- Run the action through the header menu's existing code, so archive keeps **Undo**, delete keeps its confirmation, and rename edits the header title inline.
- With an empty palette, list these after the navigation commands, so Enter still opens **New session**. When a search matches one, list it first, so "archive" + Enter archives the current chat.
- Act only on the active chat pane, like ⌘⇧A.

### Alternatives considered

- **More direct shortcuts** (one per action): harder to discover, and they would use up more key combinations.
- **A plugin**: the plugin manifest has no command-palette contribution point, and these actions belong to the session menu, not to a plugin.
- **An actions menu on each search result** (like Raycast's ⌘K on a row): useful later for acting on other sessions, but a bigger change than covering the chat you have open.

### Impact

- Affected: Control UI users who drive OpenClaw from the keyboard, in the browser and the macOS app.
- Severity: annoying; it breaks the keyboard flow for common session housekeeping.
- Frequency: every rename or archive done outside ⌘⇧A.

### Evidence/examples

Command palettes in VS Code, Linear, and Raycast run actions on the current item. Today, typing "Archive" or "rename" in OpenClaw's palette shows "No results found" when no session title matches.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

The chat pane already registers itself with the palette for slash commands (`COMMAND_PALETTE_TARGET_EVENT`), so the palette can get these actions the same way, without a new registration.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On the current `release/2026.9.7` candidate, transient foreign SQLite lifecycle contention can leave session-history eviction holding a terminated, never-used reclamation worker whose cleanup cannot complete.

### Steps to reproduce

Using an isolated test state:

1. Create an old historical transcript and its current successor.
2. In a separate native SQLite process, acquire `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` on the state lifecycle coordinator database.
3. Invoke `enforceSqliteSessionHistoryDiskBudget` with a budget just below measured usage.
4. Observe admission refusal before the dedicated reclamation worker receives its first request; coordination terminates that worker.
5. Release the foreign lock and retry cleanup/eviction.

The accompanying patch in #159919 includes a runnable regression adapted from the real contention fixture in #157064, plus native-worker retirement boundary tests.

### Expected behavior

Refuse the blocked attempt without deleting either transcript. After the foreign lock is released, retire the demonstrably unused, stopped worker and allow a later eviction request to remove only the eligible historical generation.

### Actual behavior

The blocked attempt reports `SQLite reclamation and cleanup failed`. Subsequent cleanup reports `SQLite reclamation Worker cleanup is uncertain; restart OpenClaw before deleting the owning agent`, although no request was dispatched and native worker exit is already proven.

### OpenClaw version

Unreleased `release/2026.9.7`, commit `beab1d9adec68ef1d37a12e3e8aed9bf6d82a65a`.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS; Node 26.10.0.

### Install method

Source checkout, frozen-lockfile pnpm installation, canonical Vitest runner with isolated synthetic state.

### Model

Not applicable: reproduced without model inference.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable: native SQLite and worker lifecycle only.

### Logs and evidence

On the unmodified candidate, the new suite reports **2 failed / 1 passed**. With only the narrow reclamation-owner fix, **3/3 pass**, including actual disk-budget eviction after releasing the foreign lock, preservation of the current transcript, refusal while an unused worker is still alive, and refusal after dispatch without a lease receipt.

### Impact and severity

Blocks the affected session-history maintenance/cleanup path after a transient contention condition. The deterministic fixture reproduces the failure; field frequency is unknown. No data loss was observed. This report does not claim to establish the original native cause of every `Agent database execution admission is closed` incident.

### Additional information

Related: #157064. The new regression adapts its existing history-eviction fixture, with credit to that contribution.

The proposed fix requires all four facts: dedicated transport, no dispatched work request, no lease receipt, and proven native exit. Pooled-worker custody and uncertain post-dispatch cleanup remain unchanged. No schema, stored-data, or retention-policy change.

This report targets the release candidate deliberately: current `main` (`90f63c185`) has already replaced the old lifecycle-coordinator admission path. Reproduction of this exact trigger on current `main` has not been established.
