- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (npm install, commit `3a9d69d`)
- Windows 11, embedded agents on Feishu/WeCom channels
- Model: `newapi/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (contextWindow 200,000)

# Summary

When a session overflows its context window and LLM auto-compaction also fails (because the compaction request itself exceeds the window), the error handler preserves the session mapping **and** the user-facing message recommends `/compact` and `/new`. Both recommendations are dead ends in this state:

- `/compact` → compaction request hits the same window → fails again (deadlock).
- `/new` → a new session is created, but the existing mapping is restored on the next inbound message, so the new session is abandoned after a few events and messages keep landing in the bloated session.

The message even states what happened ("I kept this conversation mapped to the current session") while simultaneously pointing the user at two actions that cannot work. Users end up running `/new` repeatedly, each time unknowingly bounced back to the overflowed session.

# Reproduction (observed in production, 2.5-day window)

1. A long-lived Feishu DM session (13 days, 1,405 transcript events, ~5.1 MB, preflight ≈ 219-231K tokens vs 200K window) overflows → `Context overflow: prompt too large for the model (precheck)`.
2. Auto-compaction attempts with `compactionTokens=219683` → exceeds the 200K window → `auto-compaction failed ... commit_no_archive` / `commit_failed`.
3. Error text: *"⚠️ Auto-compaction could not recover this turn. I kept this conversation mapped to the current session. Please try again, use /compact, or use /new to start a fresh session."*
4. User sends `/new` → new session created → next message → session mapped back to the bloated one → same error.
5. Repeat: 5 consecutive `/new` sessions over 2.5 days, each surviving only 5-6 events before being abandoned.

Session-store evidence (`session_windows`): new sessions created 09-13 02:56, 09-14 10:36, 09-15 01:10, 09-15 11:28, 09-15 11:45 — all 5-6 events, all abandoned; the pointer kept resolving to the original session.

# Code

`dist/agent-runner.runtime-*.mjs` (src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-error-handler.ts), both overflow-compaction-failure branches hard-code:

```js
return {
    kind: "final",
    payload: markAgentRunFailureReplyPayload({
        text: buildContextOverflowRecoveryText({
            duringCompaction: true,
            preserveSessionMapping: true,
            ...
```

and the message builder:

```js
function buildContextOverflowRecoveryText(params) {
    return (params.preserveSessionMapping
        ? "⚠️ Auto-compaction could not recover this turn. I kept this conversation mapped to the current session. Please try again, use /compact, or use /new to start a fresh session."
        : ...
```

# Why this is a trap

1. The advice contradicts the behavior: the session is preserved, so `/compact` (same deadlock) and `/new` (mapping restored on next message) cannot recover.
2. Nothing in the UI surfaces that the mapping is preserved or how to break the cycle. The working escape hatch is the CLI-only mechanical compaction (`openclaw sessions compact <key> --agent <id> --max-lines N`), which is nowhere referenced.
3. Only diagnostics: `context-overflow-diag` log lines comparing `preflightEstimatedTokens` vs the model `contextWindow`.

# Expected behavior

Pick any of (in increasing scope):

1. **Minimal — fix the message**: when `preserveSessionMapping=true`, drop the `/compact` and `/new` suggestions and instead tell the user the actual remedy, e.g. *"Auto-compaction failed because the session exceeds the model's context window. Run `openclaw sessions compact <session-key> --agent <agent-id> --max-lines 200` or switch this agent to a larger-context model."* At minimum, do not recommend `/new` when the mapping will be restored anyway.
2. **Better — make `/new` win**: when the user explicitly issues `/new`, honor it by clearing the overflow mapping (the preserve-mapping behavior makes sense for background continuity, not for an explicit user reset).
3. **Best — auto-recover**: on compaction failure, fall back to a mechanical truncation (keep last N lines) instead of failing the turn; this also addresses the deadlock class reported in #138599.

Related: #138599 (compaction deadlock when session exceeds compaction model window — this issue adds the misleading-recovery-text dimension and the `/new`-is-bounced behavior), #101868 (overflow give-up wedges session — same family, different branch).

Happy to provide the full `context-overflow-diag` lines and session-store dumps if useful.

— filed from a production install (7 bots, Feishu/WeCom) after 2.5 days of the loop being reproduced by an end user following the message's own advice.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On macOS, OpenClaw's bundled Sparkle `Autoupdate` process remained alive for more than three days and was observed using 77.8% CPU during a system load spike to 295.66.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The installed build and the current Sparkle appcast both reported version `2026.9.4` / build `2609000490`; after update processing completes, the updater should terminate rather than remain active for multiple days.

### Actual behavior

At 2026-09-15 11:59 JST, PID 98983 was observed with:

- Elapsed time: `03-01:18:27`
- CPU: `77.8%`
- Command: `/Applications/OpenClaw.app/Contents/Frameworks/Sparkle.framework/Versions/B/Autoupdate`

At the same time, system load averages were `295.66 166.45 80.47` on a 12-logical-CPU Mac. Other processes were also consuming significant CPU, so the updater was not the only contributor: `fseventsd` was at 165.8% and macOS `LoginItems` was at 199.1%.

During the next diagnostic probe, `Autoupdate` had exited. Load then declined from 295.66 to 122.84 and subsequently 83.13; a later snapshot showed 70.12% CPU idle. This records correlation, not proof that the updater caused the entire load spike.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (build 2609000490)

### Operating system

macOS 15.7.9 (24G830), MacBookPro16,1, 6-core Intel Core i7 / 12 logical CPUs, 16 GB RAM

### Install method

macOS app (`/Applications/OpenClaw.app`)

### Model

N/A — native macOS auto-updater; no model request involved

### Provider / routing chain

N/A — native macOS auto-updater; no provider involved

### Additional provider/model setup details

N/A

### Logs

```shell
$ uptime
11:59  up 8 days,  2:52, 3 users, load averages: 295.66 166.45 80.47

$ ps -axo pid,ppid,%cpu,%mem,state,etime,comm | sort -k3 -nr | head
26394     1 199.1  0.3 Ss      01:16:08 /System/Library/ExtensionKit/Extensions/LoginItems.appex/Contents/MacOS/LoginItems
  101     1 165.8  0.1 Ss   08-02:52:44 /System/Library/Frameworks/CoreServices.framework/Versions/A/Frameworks/FSEvents.framework/Versions/A/Support/fseventsd
98983     1  77.8  0.0 R    03-01:18:27 /Applications/OpenClaw.app/Contents/Frameworks/Sparkle.framework/Versions/B/Autoupdate

$ top -l 1
Processes: 896 total, 4 running, 2 stuck, 890 sleeping, 4081 threads
Load Avg: 114.69, 137.79, 75.59
CPU usage: 14.40% user, 15.46% sys, 70.12% idle
```

A stack sample could not be captured because the updater exited before the sampling probe.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshot or recording was captured. Evidence is the process and system snapshots above.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: one observed macOS installation of OpenClaw 2026.9.4
- Severity: high system-performance impact during the observed incident
- Frequency: one observed occurrence; deterministic reproduction is not yet available
- Consequence: the machine became heavily loaded and sluggish; OpenClaw's updater accounted for approximately 78% of one logical CPU during the spike

### Additional information

- `/Applications/OpenClaw.app` modification time: 2026-09-12 10:42:51 +0900
- The updater's elapsed time was approximately three days, aligning closely with the app's modification date.
- At inspection time, `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/main/appcast.xml` advertised 2026.9.4 / build 2609000490 as the latest version, matching the installed app.
- Memory pressure was healthy at inspection time; disk activity was approximately 7.16 MB/s, so neither appeared to be the immediate bottleneck.

issues.body:
## Summary

When pairing a second macOS device as a **node** to an already-configured remote Gateway, the onboarding wizard's "Connect your AI" / verification step (`openclaw.setup.activate.start` / `wizard.next`) hits a reproducible config-reload race that leaves the client stuck reporting settings are "saved but not active," even after restarting the Gateway.

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.9.4 (macOS app + Gateway, same version both sides)
- Gateway host: macOS 26.5.2, Mac mini (Macmini9,1)
- Client: macOS app on a second Mac, same LAN, connecting via `mode=remote, transport=direct, ws://<gateway-host>:18789`
- Gateway already has a fully configured, working model/agent (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`) — this is a *second device* joining an existing Gateway, not first-run setup.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Gateway host: have a working Gateway with an agent already configured and in active use.
2. On a second Mac, install/open the OpenClaw macOS app, choose "Connect to an existing Gateway," point it at the running Gateway (LAN `ws://` URL), authenticate.
3. Operator/dashboard connection succeeds fine (`openclaw-mac status --json` reports `primary.connection.state: "connected"`).
4. App proceeds into a **separate first-run-style onboarding wizard** (distinct from the working remote connection) that includes a "Connect your AI" step, even though the target Gateway already has AI fully configured.
5. That step calls `openclaw.setup.activate.start`, which initially returns:
   ```
   errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=OpenClaw setup is already in progress; try again when it finishes.
   ```
   This persisted for **hours** across many client-side app relaunches, force-quits, and even between actual Gateway process restarts that did not truly cycle the process (see below).
6. Root cause of that specific symptom: a stale lock file at `~/.openclaw/migration/onboarding.lock-target.lock` on the Gateway host, containing `{"pid": <gateway pid>, "starttime": <matching still-running process>}`. Because the lock's recorded PID+starttime matched the still-alive Gateway process, `setup.activate.start` kept treating a real in-progress session as still open indefinitely (no observed action ever cleared it on its own).
7. A `gateway.restart`-style RPC restart (via an internal admin/system tool) reported success (`"Scheduled Gateway restart" ... "done"`) **twice**, but verified via `ps` that the actual Gateway process PID/start-time never changed either time. Only a manual `launchctl kickstart -k gui/<uid>/ai.openclaw.gateway` on the host actually cycled the process (new PID confirmed).
8. After a genuine process restart, the `setup.activate.start` lock error was gone, and the wizard progressed (`openclaw.setup.detect` and `wizard.next` both returned success). However, the client then showed:
   ```
   Gateway settings are saved but not active yet. Wait for application or restart to finish, then retry verification.
   ```
9. Gateway log at the exact moment of that `wizard.next` success shows:
   ```
   ⇄ res ✓ wizard.next 1091ms ...
   config reload superseded: GatewayConfigReloadSupersededError: config reload superseded by a newer runtime config source
   config reload superseded: GatewayConfigReloadSupersededError: config reload superseded by a newer runtime config source
   ```
   This exact two-line sequence reproduced **identically** after a second genuine Gateway process restart and retry, i.e., it is not a one-off — every attempt at this step re-triggers the same reload race and leaves the client stuck at "Finishing AI setup" indefinitely (observed for several minutes with zero further RPC activity from the client) or reporting "saved but not active."
10. `openclaw config get agents` confirms no new agent/device entry is ever actually created by this flow — the step appears to be redundantly trying to (re)verify/(re)write the *existing* agent's model config rather than just confirming the existing config is usable, which seems to be the underlying design issue triggering the race.

## Expected behavior

- Pairing a **node** to a Gateway that already has a working, configured agent should not require re-running "Connect your AI" at all — or if it does for verification purposes, it should not attempt a redundant config write that races with the live config-reload path.
- `openclaw.setup.activate.start`'s "already in progress" lock should not persist indefinitely tied to a still-running process with no way to clear it short of finding and manually deleting `~/.openclaw/migration/onboarding.lock-target.lock`, nor should it require finding/removing that file manually at all.
- A `gateway.restart` administrative action should either actually restart the process or clearly report that it did not (it silently no-op'd twice while claiming success in our repro).

## Additional notes

- This was fully reproduced start-to-finish by a human working with an AI agent assistant that had direct shell/log access to the Gateway host throughout, so the above sequence is a first-hand, verified reproduction, not a guess from user-reported symptoms alone.
- Happy to provide further log excerpts if useful.

issues.body:
## Summary
Allow users to unpin Home from the Control UI Pages section without losing access to the underlying conversation.

## Problem to solve
Home is a permanent shortcut to the selected agent's main conversation, while other conversations can be organized into custom session groups. For users who organize their work in those groups, Home is redundant and its separate placement is confusing. The label also suggests an overview rather than a conversation.

## Proposed solution
- Keep Home pinned by default, preserving the existing experience.
- Allow unpinning Home through the existing navigation pin controls.
- When Home is unpinned, include its underlying conversation in the ordinary session list, respecting custom groups and existing filters. Users should be able to group it normally.
- Allow restoring Home through **Edit pinned items**. When restored, avoid duplicating the conversation in the ordinary list.
- Persist the choice through the existing UI preference mechanism.
- Treat this strictly as navigation customization: do not delete, archive, reset, replace, or reroute the conversation, and preserve its transcript and group metadata.

## Alternatives considered
- Rename Home to Main chat: clearer naming, but still forces a separate shortcut on group-oriented users.
- Hide Home without exposing its session: reduces clutter but makes the conversation difficult to find.
- Turn Home into a dashboard: a broader product direction, not necessary to address this navigation preference.

## Impact
Affected: Control UI users who organize conversations into custom groups.
Severity: usability friction, not a blocker.
Frequency: every sidebar interaction.
Consequence: a mandatory navigation item outside the user's chosen organization model.

## Evidence/examples
The sessions/sidebar documentation explicitly describes Home as the rolling main session and excludes it from the ordinary session list.

Related but distinct:
- #110296: Home dashboard and Pages shelf.
- #142970: Bot-mode presentation of one Home conversation.
- #139603: replacing an unhealthy Home session; this request does not change Home identity.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?
Yes. Implementation and focused regression coverage will follow in a linked PR.

issues.body:
## Summary

An agent's OpenAI OAuth auth profile cannot be resolved into a usable model route when the shared auth store's ownership is `state-db`, regardless of the per-agent `order.<provider>` state. The failure mode changes depending on whether an explicit order is set, but every combination fails. All requests silently fall back to the next configured model (e.g. deepseek) instead of using OAuth, so the symptom is invisible to end users but OpenAI/OAuth routing is effectively dead.

This may be the same root cause as, or closely related to, #145929 (`openclaw models auth logout` failing with "the auth store lock may be busy" even with zero other processes running and the gateway stopped) — both look like fallout from an incomplete migration path for the `state-db` shared-auth-store mode.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)
- Linux, running as a systemd `--user` service (`openclaw-gateway.service`)
- 4 agents configured: `main`, `tony`, `reed`, `star`, each with `model.primary: "openai/gpt-5.5"` and `fallbacks: ["deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"]`
- `config_machine_state` key `auth.sharedStore` = `{"location":"state-db"}` (i.e. the shared auth store lives in `$OPENCLAW_HOME/state/openclaw.sqlite`, table `config_machine_state`, rows `authProfiles.store` / `authProfiles.state`, not in an agent directory)
- Working, non-expired OpenAI OAuth credential present in the shared store (`type: oauth`, `chatgptPlanType: plus`, freshly re-authenticated via `openclaw models auth login --provider openai --agent main` during this investigation — token was rotated and confirmed valid, bug persisted unchanged)

## Reproduction

Tested every reachable state of the per-agent `auth_profile_state.order.openai` array (in each agent's `$OPENCLAW_HOME/agents/<id>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`) against live Telegram messages to all four agents. `openai:<oauth-account-id>` (oauth, email-based profile id) was the only credential present in the shared store in the later tests (a broken `openai:api-key` inline/billing-disabled entry was removed from the shared store partway through, see Notes).

| `order.openai` state | Result (from gateway journal) |
|---|---|
| `["openai:<oauth-account-id>","openai:api-key","oauth","api-key"]` (original) | openai attempted via api-key profile, real 429 billing error — oauth entry, though listed first, never seemed to be selected |
| `["openai:<oauth-account-id>","oauth","api-key"]` (api-key id removed) | `Explicit auth order for openai has no usable profiles.` |
| `["openai:<oauth-account-id>"]` (single valid entry — this was tony/reed/star's *original*, untouched state) | `Explicit auth order for openai has no usable profiles.` |
| key removed entirely (no explicit order) | `No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai.` |
| `["openai:<oauth-account-id>"]` again, after a **fresh OAuth login + full gateway restart** | `Explicit auth order for openai has no usable profiles.` (identical to before the fresh login) |

Every state falls through to `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` within ~1s via the normal model-fallback path, so there is no user-facing outage — just silent, total loss of OpenAI routing.

Representative journal lines (`journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway.service`):

```
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main error="Explicit auth order for openai has no usable profiles."
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=openai/gpt-5.5 candidate=openai/gpt-5.5 reason=unknown next=deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro detail=Explicit auth order for openai has no usable profiles.
```

```
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main error="No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai."
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=openai/gpt-5.5 candidate=openai/gpt-5.5 reason=auth next=deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro detail=No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai.
```

Notably, `openclaw models auth login --provider openai --agent main` (a normal, supported, interactive login) **writes the refreshed credential back into the shared `state-db` store** (confirmed via the store's `expires` timestamp changing) and **also re-adds `order.openai: ["openai:<oauth-account-id>"]`** to the per-agent local store as a side effect — i.e. the login flow itself reliably reintroduces the exact explicit-order state that triggers `"no usable profiles"`. There is no supported way, via this command, to create a genuinely agent-local (non-inherited) OpenAI OAuth credential for `main`.

## Suspected root cause (from reading the installed package's bundled source, `<npm-global-prefix>/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/*.mjs`)

- `isSharedMainAuthProfileAgentDir()` (`store-BxRoDWvl.mjs`) decides whether a given agent directory *is* the canonical shared-store owner by comparing `resolveAuthProfileDatabasePath(agentDir)` against `resolveAuthProfileDatabasePath(mainAgentDir)` — a **path-based** comparison. It does not consult `resolveSharedAuthStoreOwnership().location` (`path-resolve-CQ53Zb-k.mjs`), so when ownership is `state-db` (credentials live in `$OPENCLAW_HOME/state/openclaw.sqlite`, not in `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`), this function still returns `true` for `main`'s own directory — the "legacy-main" assumption baked into this comparison never got updated for the `state-db` migration path.
- `findPersistedAuthProfileCredential()` (same file) short-circuits on `isSharedMainAuthProfileAgentDir(agentDir)` and returns whatever it found in the **per-agent local store only**, without falling through to check the actual shared/state-db store, for any agent this function considers "the shared owner."
- Separately, `mergeAuthProfileStores()` / `runtimeInheritsMainState` (`legacy-source-diagnostic-D-_lsE4x.mjs`, `runtime-snapshots-DEZij4DX.mjs`, `runtime-state-Bzv-XW2N.mjs`) gate whether a per-agent runtime snapshot inherits credentials from the main store behind a `runtimeInheritsMainState === true` flag; it's unclear from the data alone whether/when this gets set correctly under `state-db` ownership, but the net effect matches: the per-agent snapshot's `profiles` map never actually contains the inherited oauth credential.
- `resolveAuthProfileOrderWithMetadata()` (`order-vvdJ1RGu.mjs`) and the route-compatibility check in `openai-model-routes-B7zoZLPw.mjs` (`reject("explicit-order", ...)` / the final `reject("configured-auth", ... "No route-compatible authentication source is configured for ${provider}.")`) are the two call sites producing the two observed error strings — both downstream of the same underlying gap (the profile never resolves as present/usable), which is why toggling `order.openai` only changes *which* of these two rejects fires, not whether the request succeeds.

## Impact

- Any agent whose auth store ownership is `state-db` cannot use an OAuth-authenticated OpenAI model at all; every request silently falls back to the next configured model.
- Because the fallback is silent and fast, this is easy to miss — the bots appear to work normally, just always answering from the fallback model instead of the configured primary.
- `openclaw models auth login` cannot be used to work around it, since it writes back into the same broken state as a normal side effect of promoting the newly-authenticated profile in the order.

## Suggested fix direction

Update `isSharedMainAuthProfileAgentDir()` (and any other path-identity-based "is this the shared owner" checks) to consult `resolveSharedAuthStoreOwnership().location` and, when `state-db`, compare against/read from the actual state-db-backed store rather than assuming the `main` agent's own directory is authoritative. Alternatively, ensure `runtimeInheritsMainState` (or equivalent) is reliably set for every agent — including `main` itself — under `state-db` ownership, and add a regression test covering "oauth profile lives only in the state-db shared store, an agent with an empty local store should still resolve it as a usable route."

## Notes

- A stray `openai:api-key` inline/config-derived pseudo-profile was found and removed from the shared store during this investigation (it was billing-disabled and unrelated to this bug beyond adding noise to `openclaw models auth list` output).
- The separate `openclaw models auth logout ... --agent main --yes` failure ("the auth store lock may be busy") was independently reproduced multiple times during this investigation, including with the gateway fully stopped and zero other node processes running — consistent with #145929 not being ordinary lock contention.

issues.body:
### What goes wrong

`openclaw browser snapshot` can print nothing and exit `0`. An empty snapshot is
reported as a successful capture, so a caller cannot tell "this page has no content"
apart from "the capture never happened".

### Why it matters

This is the silent-failure kind of bug. An agent driving the browser reads the empty
output, concludes the page genuinely has nothing on it, and takes a wrong branch —
typically "no results, give up" — while every surrounding status line still says the
run succeeded.

I hit this while running an unattended browser workflow against a live site. The
browser connection wedged, `snapshot` began returning empty output with exit code `0`,
and the workflow did nothing for roughly six hours. Nothing in the logs looked wrong,
because nothing had reported an error. A thrown error would have surfaced it in
minutes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the browser and open any page.
2. Get the browser into a state where the capture cannot happen — in my case the
   plugin's connection to Chrome had wedged; killing Chrome's renderer or closing the
   target from underneath the session also reaches it.
3. Run `openclaw browser snapshot`.

### Expected

A non-zero exit and a message saying the snapshot could not be captured.

### Actual

Exit code `0`, no output.

```
$ openclaw browser snapshot --limit 800 --timeout 120000
$ echo $?
0
```

### Where it comes from

`extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-inspect.ts` logs `result.snapshot` for the `ai`
format without checking whether it has any content, so an empty payload flows straight
through to stdout as success. With `--out`, the same empty payload is written over an
existing snapshot file.

An `ai` snapshot of a live page is never legitimately empty — the root element alone
produces output — so empty is always a failed capture and can safely be treated as an
error.

### Environment

- openclaw 2026.9.3
- Windows 11, Node 22
- Chrome, local managed browser profile

### Note

I have a small fix with tests ready and will open a PR against this issue.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug: message loss / incorrect WebChat state reconciliation.

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.4, Dashboard WebChat automatic TTS no longer preserves the assistant's detailed text together with its audio attachment.

With `tts.auto = "always"` and `tts.mode = "final"`, the detailed assistant text is visible while streaming. When the final TTS/audio update arrives, the Control UI replaces that text with the shorter TTS transcript instead of preserving the original text and attaching/merging the audio.

Changing to the valid `tts.auto = "tagged"` mode avoids the replacement, but a correctly formed `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` block emits no TTS event and produces no audio on the Dashboard/WebChat surface.

An explicit TTS tool invocation successfully delivers a separate audio artifact while the normal detailed text remains visible. This proves that the configured provider, voice synthesis, media route, and browser playback work.

### Steps to reproduce: `always`

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.4 and open a Dashboard WebChat direct session.
2. Configure:

   ```text
   tts.auto = "always"
   tts.mode = "final"
   ```

3. Ask the assistant for a detailed response whose spoken version is shorter than the visible answer.
4. Observe that the full text appears during streaming.
5. Wait for final TTS delivery/session reconciliation.

### Actual behavior: `always`

The detailed text disappears. Only the shorter audio transcript remains visible with the audio.

No message `delete` or `edit` action appears in the audit trail; the replacement occurs during final audio/session reconciliation.

### Steps to reproduce: `tagged`

1. Set:

   ```text
   tts.auto = "tagged"
   tts.mode = "final"
   ```

2. Return detailed visible text followed by a correctly closed block:

   ```text
   [[tts:text]]Short spoken summary.[[/tts:text]]
   ```

### Actual behavior: `tagged`

The visible text remains, but no TTS event, media artifact, or audio delivery occurs.

### Control test / workaround

Calling the explicit TTS tool with the same short summary produces playable audio in WebChat. Sending the detailed answer normally and the explicit TTS output as a separate artifact reliably preserves both.

### Expected behavior

- `always`: the final WebChat/session update preserves the original detailed assistant text and adds the generated audio attachment. It must not replace the original text with the spoken summary/transcript.
- `tagged`: a valid `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` block triggers synthesis and WebChat audio delivery.
- History reload and live state should agree on one assistant response containing the complete text plus audio, or on two linked artifacts without message loss.

This matches the behavior previously verified when closing #81468: the refreshed history should contain exactly one assistant message with both text and audio.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)`
- Surface: Dashboard / Control UI WebChat, direct session
- OS: Linux x86_64
- TTS provider: configured local CLI provider (synthesis works through explicit TTS)
- Reproduced repeatedly in the same session

### Related issues

- #81468 — prior WebChat final-media/session reconciliation bug; closed after text+audio merge was verified
- #57297 — missing WebChat TTS routing/playback telemetry; related observability gap, but not this message-loss regression
- #137281 — TTS directive parser can discard free-text colon tags; different tag form and failure mode

### Suspected boundary

The `always` symptom suggests that the audio-bearing `session.message` refresh is replacing the assistant display text with the TTS transcript instead of merging the attachment into the original final text. The `tagged` symptom suggests that tagged post-processing is not connected to the Dashboard/WebChat final pipeline in this release.

### Impact

High usability impact: users lose the detailed written answer whenever automatic TTS finalizes. Disabling automatic TTS preserves text but removes the configured voice behavior; explicit TTS is currently required as a workaround.

labels.name: stale
labels.description: Marked as stale due to inactivity

issues.body:
### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), Linux x64, systemd user unit
- Session primary model: a custom OpenAI-compatible provider, 256k context window
- Long-running main session with heavy daily tool usage

### Symptoms

When the session context approaches the budget, gateway-triggered auto-compaction repeatedly fails and stalls the whole agent run. Observed in one day: two stalled runs (`repeatedRequestNoProgressAge` growing to 491s before abort), three `Full summarization failed: partial summarization failure` events, and a single compaction model call that hung for **23.4 minutes** (`durationMs=1406379`) before being aborted.

### Evidence (journal excerpts, sanitized)

```
[context-pressure-diagnostic] admitted provider attempt for <primary-model> route=compact_only estimatedPromptTokens=249852 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=236000
[compaction] chunk summarization failed after retries; partial summary available
[compaction] Full summarization failed: partial summarization failure
[agent/embedded] context-engine compaction failed
[compaction-diag] end sessionKey=<main-session> trigger=budget provider=<primary-model> attempt=1 maxAttempts=1 outcome=failed reason=unknown detail=This_operation_was_aborted durationMs=1406379
[diagnostic] stalled session: ... reason=repeated_model_requests_without_progress classification=stalled_agent_run ... repeatedRequestNoProgressAge=491s recovery=none
[ws] res ✗ sessions.compact errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=Session <key> has queued work; retry after it finishes.
```

Also observed a second session (subagent) overshooting the window during compaction: `estimatedPromptTokens=315800` against a 256k window. Its compaction eventually completed, but the trigger point for the main session was already ~97% of the window (249,852/256,000).

### Problems

1. **Compaction routes to the session's primary model with no fallback.** The primary model was unstable that day; every compaction call inherits that instability. (Related: #138033 `feat(agents): label unresolved compaction model`, #133126 per-agent compaction overrides suggest this area is being worked on.)
2. **`maxAttempts=1` for compaction** while normal model calls use `maxAttempts=3` — a single failed call aborts the entire compaction with no retry.
3. **No timeout on compaction model calls.** Observed `durationMs=1406379` (23.4 min) with `timeoutMs=undefined`; the only backstop is the 30s stalled-session heartbeat, which needs several minutes of no-progress before killing the run. Users see the session completely frozen meanwhile.
4. **Trigger threshold too close to exhaustion** (~97% of window): the compaction request itself is a ~250k-token payload, so it is slow and failure-prone; messages keep arriving during compaction (overshoot observed).
5. **Positive feedback loop**: over budget → compaction request bigger/slower → fails → retry → stalled → abort → user retries → still over budget. Once the context is large, the session cannot recover without manual truncation.
6. **Partial summaries are discarded.** The journal explicitly logs `partial summary available`, then `Full summarization failed: partial summarization failure`. A degraded checkpoint would be far better than failing the whole compaction.
7. **Manual recovery path is blocked while queued work exists**: `sessions.compact` returns `INVALID_REQUEST: Session ... has queued work` — precisely when it is needed (compaction stuck with queued work). After the stalled run is killed, the same command succeeds in 269ms.

### Suggestions

- Configurable compaction model + fallbacks (aligns with #133126 / #138033)
- Configurable retry attempts for compaction calls
- A `timeoutMs` for compaction model calls
- Accept partial summaries as a degraded checkpoint instead of discarding them
- Allow manual `sessions.compact` to preempt or complete pending queued work (or document the recovery path)
- Expose the compaction trigger threshold so heavy-session operators can compact earlier

### Workaround (for other affected users)

Schedule a truncation-based compaction via cron/automation:

```
openclaw sessions compact <key> --max-lines 200
```

Pure truncation, no LLM call, cannot fail. Two daily runs keep heavy sessions well below the pressure threshold.

issues.body:
## Summary

When Anthropic (or Anthropic-compatible) streaming ends with truncated / unparseable tool-call argument JSON, current OpenClaw transport behavior is fail-closed: the run becomes `stopReason=error`, the partial `toolCall` is stripped from the turn, and the user-visible session looks aborted.

Anthropic's public docs recommend a different recovery shape for invalid/incomplete tool JSON, and a separate retry shape for `max_tokens` incomplete `tool_use`. This issue asks whether OpenClaw wants any of that recovery on `main`, without undoing the fail-closed work that prevents executing partial tool calls.

## Current behavior (locked by tests)

On Anthropic transport, cases such as:

- `stop_reason=max_tokens` mid-`input_json_delta`
- missing `content_block_stop` / incomplete tool call
- sealed block that still fails strict JSON object parse

result in:

- `stopReason=error`
- no executable / persisted `toolCall` on the turn
- no automatic `tool_result(is_error=true, INVALID_JSON=...)` continuation

This matches the direction of:

- #97140 / #97092 — ignore / scrub truncated non-`toolUse` tool calls (do not execute or replay)
- #126391 — reject malformed / unsealed streamed tool arguments at the provider boundary

Related earlier discussion that did not land as Anthropic-doc recovery:

- #63210 — detect/recover from `length` truncation (closed stale; previously needed product decision)
- #87571 — incomplete-tool-call retry PR (closed / superseded)

## Anthropic docs (upstream contract)

1. **Invalid / incomplete JSON from fine-grained tool streaming**  
   [Fine-grained tool streaming → Handling invalid JSON in tool responses](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/fine-grained-tool-streaming)  
   Do not run the tool; return a `tool_result` with `is_error: true` and content shaped like:

   ```json
   { "INVALID_JSON": "<the unparseable input you received>" }
   ```

2. **Incomplete tool use cut by `max_tokens`**  
   [Handling stop reasons → Incomplete tool use blocks](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/handling-stop-reasons)  
   Retry the same request with a higher `max_tokens` to obtain the full tool use (Tool Runner docs also advise not auto-appending the truncated assistant message when bumping the budget).

3. **Invalid tool input / missing params (already-complete `tool_use`)**  
   [Handle tool calls → Handling errors with `is_error`](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls)  
   Continue with `tool_result` + `is_error: true`; Claude may retry with corrections a few times.

Official Anthropic SDK Tool Runner does **not** auto-implement the `INVALID_JSON` wrapper; streaming parse failure surfaces as an error asking the caller to retry. The `INVALID_JSON` pattern is documented as an application-level recovery option.

## What this is / is not asking for

**Not asking to undo fail-closed:**

- Unsealed / incomplete tool calls must still never execute.
- Lenient "complete the partial JSON and run the tool" must stay forbidden.

**Asking for a product decision on optional recovery after fail-closed detection.**

## Proposed recovery (single pipeline)

Anthropic's docs describe two complementary recoveries for different failure modes. Treat them as **one pipeline**, not alternative product options:

```
classify failure
  │
  ├─ max_tokens / length and tool call incomplete
  │     → bump-budget retry first
  │       (do not append truncated assistant turn;
  │        retry same message prefix with higher max_tokens, bounded)
  │         ├─ success → normal tool execution
  │         └─ still incomplete / still invalid JSON
  │              → INVALID_JSON feedback (or surface error)
  │
  └─ sealable tool_use (id/name present; input can be a safe object)
        but arguments JSON invalid/incomplete
          → INVALID_JSON feedback:
            persist tool_use + tool_result(is_error, INVALID_JSON=raw)
            and continue the agent loop
```

### Bump-budget retry (`max_tokens` / incomplete tool use)

When `stop_reason` is `max_tokens` / `length` and the tool call is incomplete:

1. Do **not** append the truncated assistant turn.
2. Retry the same message prefix with a higher `max_tokens` (bounded attempts / ceiling).
3. If still incomplete after the budget, continue to `INVALID_JSON` feedback below, or surface error.

Note: if the configured cap is already high, bumping may be ineffective; chunking guidance remains relevant.

### `INVALID_JSON` feedback (narrow)

Only when a tool call is sealable enough to persist a valid Anthropic `tool_use` block (`id`, `name`, `input` as an object, e.g. `{}` or best-effort object) and no mutating tool from that turn has already executed:

1. Keep that `tool_use` in history.
2. Immediately append matching `tool_result` with `is_error: true` and `INVALID_JSON` wrapper containing the raw argument string.
3. Continue the agent loop so the model can correct / chunk.

Hard stop if pairing cannot be formed safely (same class of risk as orphan `tool_use` → next-request 400).

### Opt-out — Keep current fail-closed UX

No automatic recovery; keep error + scrub. Optionally improve operator-facing error text only.

## Local observation (non-blocking)

On one Anthropic-compatible gateway used for a smoke check, a docs-shaped history (`tool_use` with `input: {}` + `tool_result(is_error, INVALID_JSON=...)`) returned HTTP 200 and the model issued a corrected `tool_use`. That does **not** replace first-party `api.anthropic.com` proof for a future PR; it only suggests the docs recovery shape is worth deciding on.

## Question for maintainers

Is this recovery pipeline in scope for OpenClaw `main`, or should this stay fail-closed (opt-out) / live only in a fork or plugin?

If recovery is welcome, which gates should a follow-up PR implement (provider-specific vs all transports, attempt limits, side-effect guards, when bump-budget retry falls through to `INVALID_JSON` feedback)?

I can open a narrow PR after an explicit direction here.

issues.body:
## Summary

Allow an enabled bundle's unused language servers to remain cold until their capabilities are requested, while continuing to expose only tools supported by the server's initialize response.

## Problem to solve

Preparing an agent attempt currently starts and initializes every configured bundled LSP server before any LSP tool is invoked. A conversation that does not need code intelligence still pays the startup cost of those servers.

At OpenClaw commit `62f2180091350e8eba958b5d717819c4fbc63675`, `prepareEmbeddedAttemptBundleTools` awaits `createBundleLspToolRuntime`. That owner iterates configured servers serially, awaits each spawn/initialize, then materializes hover/definition/references tools from the returned capabilities. The existing runtime test explicitly expects processes to start during construction.

This is an optimization proposal, not a claim that the current initialization behavior violates LSP.

## Proposed solution

Use the existing tool discovery surface to represent configured LSP server descriptors without immediately constructing their execution runtimes. When discovery requests one server's capabilities, start that server, complete initialize, and return only its supported tools. Reuse the initialized runtime for later calls within the admitted lifecycle.

The linked standalone prototype demonstrates this boundary with the unmodified current LSP runtime. It is deliberately not integrated into OpenClaw's catalog or configuration. I would like maintainer guidance on the discovery contract before proposing the production change:

- Can the existing Tool Search/catalog owner admit deferred server descriptors, and which search/describe operation should materialize them?
- How should providers using a full, eagerly materialized tool list behave? The proposal should not silently remove their currently available LSP tools.
- What is the intended lifecycle owner for capabilities and warm LSP processes across attempts? Capability snapshots must not outlive their server/configuration/authority generation.

The production implementation must preserve deterministic collision handling and tool grants; revalidate admitted authority after awaited startup; share concurrent discovery; retain per-server diagnostics; support request cancellation; and join the current owned-stdio shutdown/descendant-extinction path. An unconfirmed cleanup must not become an automatic restart loop. The prototype does not establish these full host integration contracts.

## Alternatives considered

- Pre-register every possible hover/definition/references tool and initialize on execute. This advertises unsupported operations before the capability handshake, so it does not preserve the current discovery contract.
- Persist server capabilities and reuse them indefinitely. Capabilities belong to a live server/configuration generation; stale snapshots would select incorrect tools. The current project also requires lifecycle-owned storage rather than an ad hoc sidecar cache.
- Start all servers in parallel. This may reduce time spent waiting on multiple servers, but still starts unused processes. Earlier startup-concurrency work is relevant context, not equivalent to deferred discovery.
- Leave eager behavior unchanged. This keeps the current model-facing contract and may be preferable unless realistic end-to-end measurements establish sufficient benefit.

## Impact

Affected: agents with configured bundle LSP servers whose turns only sometimes need code intelligence. Consequence: avoidable preparation latency and processes on turns that never use those servers. Frequency depends on configuration and workflow. No broad production prevalence or real-server savings are claimed by this fixture.

Deferred startup moves initialization onto first discovery/use; first-use latency must remain visible in before/after evidence. A server used by every turn may gain little and can experience slower first tool execution after preparation.

## Evidence/examples

[Runnable prototype, source snapshots with hashes/license, reproduction instructions, and complete measurements](https://gist.github.com/yufanyang214-lab/6eae3d303673cf94a3265ba80f53454e).

A portable proof executes the exact pinned `agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`, pending-request registry, deferred helper, and owned-stdio close helper against real Node child processes speaking Content-Length framed LSP. The fixture advertises only hover and inserts a controlled 100 ms initialize delay per server. It makes no network/model calls and reads no user configuration.

Six behavior checks pass: eager unused-server startup; zero-spawn cold disposal; concurrent discovery sharing one server and a real hover result; failure diagnostics followed by explicit retry; disposal during startup; and per-request cancellation preserving the shared process. Only hover is exposed, and retained tools reject after disposal.

The linked `proof-output.json` records all five iterations per mode, medians, process counts, and child-reported RSS. The README summarizes the measurements. These are synthetic protocol-boundary results, not a Gateway benchmark or measurements of TypeScript/Python language servers.

Before a production PR: run the real bundle preparation/discovery/provider path; exercise actual supported language servers; validate ownership revocation, collisions, cleanup uncertainty, process-tree termination, and applicable eager-provider behavior; then run the focused repository tests and required build. No product patch, build success, or merge readiness is claimed yet.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance.

## Additional information

Source and related work:

- [Current LSP runtime owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62f2180091350e8eba958b5d717819c4fbc63675/src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts)
- [Attempt bundle preparation caller](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62f2180091350e8eba958b5d717819c4fbc63675/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bundle-tools.ts)
- [Current runtime tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/62f2180091350e8eba958b5d717819c4fbc63675/src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts)
- [MCP startup parallelism, merged #94230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94230)
- [Earlier MCP/LSP parallel startup proposal, closed #94779](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94779)
- [LSP disposal owner gate, merged #133340](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/133340)
- [LSP initialize contract](https://github.com/microsoft/language-server-protocol/blob/gh-pages/_specifications/lsp/3.17/general/initialize.md)

issues.body:
### Environment
- OpenClaw **2026.9.2 (3928bad)**, macOS 26.5.1 (arm64), node 26.5.0, ~52 agents on one gateway
- Primary model: `openai/gpt-6-astra` via ChatGPT-subscription OAuth
  (`agentRuntime.id: codex`, `api=openai-chatgpt-responses`, `route=native policy=hidden`)
- Fallbacks configured and **healthy the whole time**:
  `kiro-gateway/claude-opus-4.5` and `qwen-local/Qwen`, both present in
  `agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow`; no session-level model or auth overrides anywhere

### Summary
When a `server_is_overloaded` assistant error triggers the same-model transient retry, and that
**retry attempt** then dies with an error the classifier does not recognise, the run resolves to
`continue_normal` with `reason=none` and **the configured model fallback chain is never consulted** —
even though the primary is demonstrably down and the fallback provider is demonstrably up.

The classified reason from the *first* attempt is discarded by the *second* attempt's failure.

This is not #116315 (there the fallback model was missing from the agent catalog, and stale session
overrides bypassed the chain — neither applies here), and not #132611 (there `reason=overloaded`
reaches the chain correctly; here the reason never survives to the decision).

### Observed sequence (single run, from gateway.log)

```
10:23:37.660  embedded run prompt start: runId=4e10bbde... provider=openai api=openai-chatgpt-responses route=native policy=hidden
10:23:40.168  embedded run prompt end:   runId=4e10bbde... durationMs=6983
              assistant message: stopReason=error, errorCode="server_is_overloaded",
              errorMessage="Codex error: Our servers are currently overloaded. Please try again later."
10:23:41.226  embedded run start:        runId=4e10bbde...   <-- same-model transient retry, same runId
10:23:44.947  embedded run prompt end:   runId=4e10bbde... durationMs=3444
              assistant message: stopReason=error, errorCode=<absent>,
              errorMessage="Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn: <uuid>"
10:23:44.953  embedded run failover decision: stage=assistant decision=continue_normal reason=none
              attempt=1 retry=1 rotations=0 from=openai/gpt-6-astra
              rawError=Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn: <uuid>
```

The run then ends. No `rotate_profile`, no `fallback_model`. The end user gets a generic
`Agent run failed (model: openai/gpt-6-astra).` after ~28-67 ms of apparent work.

The identical shape reproduced in a second run the same minute (`runId=3b6290d4...`: 10:24:20
overload, 10:24:24 keyed-turn error, `reason=none`).

### Why the reason is lost
- `classifyAssistantFailoverReason` (`dist/embedded-agent-helpers-*.js`) builds its signal from
  `errorCode` / `errorType` / `errorMessage`. The overload attempt carries a structured
  `errorCode: server_is_overloaded` and classifies fine. The retry's error carries **no `errorCode`**
  and its text matches none of the message patterns, so classification returns `null`.
- `resolveRunFailoverDecision` (`dist/embedded-agent-*.js`) advances the chain only when
  `params.failoverFailure` is set, which follows from a non-null reason. With `reason=none` it
  returns `continue_normal` and the run ends.
- `mergeRetryFailoverReason` already threads the earlier reason through as `lastRetryFailoverReason`
  on the retry action, but the final decision is resolved from the **current** attempt's
  `failoverReason`, so the carried value never influences the outcome.

### Suggested direction
When an attempt exists only because a previous attempt was classified as transient, and that attempt
fails with an unclassified error, resolve the decision from the carried previous reason rather than
`none`, so the chain advances instead of the turn dying. Deliberately not proposing a specific patch
shape — the carried value already exists; the question is whether the decision should consult it.

### Secondary observation (may warrant its own issue)
The trigger for the failed retry is the keyed-turn guard
(`Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn`, `dist/session-manager-*.js`).
PR #133094 (`fix(agents): preserve keyed turns across compaction`, merged 2026-08-30) is present in
this build, yet the guard still fires — on the **failover/transient retry** path rather than across
compaction. Possibly related to #142224. 9 occurrences on this gateway on 2026-09-14 alone.

### Impact on this deployment (2026-09-14, one gateway)
- 65 failover decisions logged that day: **100% `continue_normal` / `reason=none`;
  0 `fallback_model`, 0 `rotate_profile`.**
- `openai/gpt-6-astra`: 175 runs, 31 `server_is_overloaded` failures (~18%).
- `kiro-gateway/claude-opus-4.5` the same day: 339 requests, **339 x HTTP 200**.
  `qwen-local/Qwen`: 152 requests, **152 x HTTP 200**.
- So every one of those 31 failures had a healthy, configured, allow-listed fallback available and
  did not use it. End users received "the AI service is temporarily overloaded" and no answer.
- The first `server_is_overloaded` in ~4 months of stored transcripts is 2026-09-08 — the day this
  fleet moved 47 agents onto `gpt-6-astra`. Daily counts since: 10 / 6 / 9 / 15 / 31.

Happy to provide redacted trajectory excerpts, the full failover-decision log lines, or a config
dump on request.

### Related work checked before filing
- #116315 — `server_is_overloaded` on ChatGPT-subscription OAuth. Different cause: there the
  fallback model was absent from the agent catalog and stale session overrides bypassed the chain.
  Here the fallback models are present, allow-listed, healthy, and there are no session overrides.
- #132611 — fallback chain not consulted on `reason=timeout`. There `reason=overloaded` reaches the
  chain correctly; here the reason never survives the retry to reach the decision at all.
- PR #141843 (open) — classifies untyped 5xx as `server_error` instead of `timeout`. Adjacent code,
  but it would not cover this case: the retry's failure carries no HTTP status and no `errorCode`
  (it is an internal `Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn`), so it classifies
  to `null` rather than to the wrong reason. The point here is the *loss of the previous attempt's
  already-correct classification across the retry boundary*.
- PR #133094 (merged 2026-08-30, present in this build) — preserves keyed turns across compaction.
  The guard still fires here, on the failover/transient-retry path rather than across compaction.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add an opt-in reset lifecycle notice for automatic idle and daily session rollovers without enabling verbose output.

### Problem to solve

When an explicitly configured idle or daily reset policy rolls a conversation over, the next reply arrives with no indication that the prior context window changed. The reply can therefore appear confused or discontinuous, especially when a short confirmation or follow-up crosses the reset boundary.

Verbose mode exposes a generic new-session identifier, but it also enables unrelated operational output. Internal `session:auto-reset` hooks cannot solve this reliably because automatic-reset events are dispatched independently of the successor turn and do not own its channel/thread reply destination.

### Proposed solution

Extend each session reset policy with an optional `notifyUser` boolean:

```json5
{
  session: {
    reset: {
      mode: "idle",
      idleMinutes: 60,
      notifyUser: true,
    },
  },
}
```

When an automatic idle or daily rollover occurs and the effective reset policy enables the option, prepend one concise status payload to the successor turn's normal reply:

- Idle: `🧭 Started a new session after the configured idle timeout.`
- Daily: `🧭 Started a new session at the configured daily reset boundary.`

The notice should use the normal reply finalization and channel/thread routing path, remain disabled by default, and replace the generic verbose new-session notice for that rollover so users never receive duplicates. Manual `/new` and `/reset` behavior should remain unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

- **Enable verbose mode:** too noisy because it exposes unrelated operational notices and session identifiers.
- **Send from `session:auto-reset` hooks:** the event is detached from the successor turn and has no authoritative reply destination.
- **Reconstruct channel routing from stored session state:** duplicates routing policy outside its owner and can send to stale rooms, accounts, or threads.
- **Send a separate out-of-band channel message:** risks ordering, threading, and duplicate-delivery problems.

### Impact

- **Affected:** Operators who explicitly enable idle or daily resets on messaging channels and direct chats.
- **Severity:** Moderate UX and workflow reliability issue; the user may not realize prior conversational context has rolled over.
- **Frequency:** Once per configured automatic rollover.
- **Consequence:** Confusing replies, repeated explanations, and ambiguous confirmation/follow-up messages.

### Evidence/examples

- #61238 documents user confusion and a confirmation workflow crossing a silent automatic reset boundary.
- #58758 established the same product pattern for dedicated, quiet lifecycle notices instead of requiring verbose mode; #67830 implemented `agents.defaults.compaction.notifyUser`.
- #55515 documents why duplicate generic and lifecycle-specific new-session notices must be avoided.
- #53364 demonstrates that system notices need the ordinary outbound channel/thread routing guarantees.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

### Additional information

The proposed setting is backward-compatible and defaults to `false`. Type- and channel-specific reset policy objects can set the same field under their existing override semantics.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.4, an active WebChat conversation using the native Codex runtime and `steer` queue experienced accepted user prompts reaching the model transcript 8–62 minutes late, alongside failed completion handoff, unconfirmed steering consumption, and session-lane waits up to 75.8 minutes.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The documented `steer` behavior is to deliver at the next available model boundary, or defer until the active run ends when steering is unavailable. Acceptance alone is not consumption, and ambiguous inputs must not be replayed automatically. A failed continuation should not silently strand interactive inputs behind long-lived session ownership.

References: [Queue modes](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/queue), [Codex queue steering](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/codex-harness-runtime/queue-and-feedback).

### Actual behavior

Observed during one long-running WebChat direct conversation with tool work and native child completions. Follow-up questions were answered much later, after intervening assistant output, making the conversation appear out of order and the assistant appear to ignore the user.

The local diagnostic compared preserved user submission timestamps against transcript append timestamps. Prompt text is omitted; each ID below denotes a separate submitted message. Times are 2026-09-13, UTC−04:00.

| Input | Submitted | Appended to model transcript | Delay |

| P1 | 20:55:01 | 21:51:27 | 56.4 min |
| P2 | 21:00:06 | 22:02:07 | 62.0 min |

| P7 | 22:03:36 | 22:31:36 | 28.0 min |
| P8 | 22:23:55 | 22:31:59 | 8.1 min |

**Scope:** this establishes delayed transcript delivery/recording and stale follow-up handling. Sampled user-to-user order remained sequential; arbitrary inversion of two user messages is not proved. Permanent message loss, duplicate execution, and duplicate billing are not established.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (`3a9d69d`)

### Operating system

Omarchy 4.0.2 (Arch-based Linux), kernel 7.1.9-arch1-2, x86_64; Node v26.8.1.

### Install method

Global Node package; local Gateway service.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

WebChat direct → local OpenClaw Gateway → native Codex app-server runtime. Exact model/provider route for each failed turn was not established by this diagnostic.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Queue mode: `steer`. Native subagent completion announcements were present in the affected session. This is an incident report, not a deterministic reproduction or a claim that every native child triggers the failure.

### Logs

Sanitized excerpts from the Gateway file log. Same date/time offset as the table; identifiers omitted. The earlier failed completion wake and later announcement cleanup were correlated by the local trace.

- Severity: blocks timely interaction and steering of ongoing work; repeated follow-ups receive stale answers tens of minutes later.
- Frequency: multiple delayed inputs in the same incident; frequency across other sessions is unknown.

At 22:35:48 UTC−04:00, `diagnostics.lanes` showed all queue counts zero and only the diagnostic turn active. This session's pending-input records had no queued/interrupted inputs, only three older cancelled records. The backlog had drained, but no root fix was applied. The announcement/ownership stall, unconfirmed steering, and prompt-mirroring rejection are correlated; the full causal chain is **not established**. issues.body:
### Summary

Chat messages that mix RTL (Persian/Arabic/Hebrew) and LTR text can render with a wrong base direction. The bubble's direction is currently decided **per message** from the first strong character (`detectTextDirection(markdown)` in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message-text.ts`), so any message that simply *starts* with a Latin token resolves to `ltr` and its RTL paragraphs lose their base direction: punctuation (`؟`, `.`, `،`) lands on the wrong side and neutral-separated RTL runs can appear reordered.

Expected behavior is **paragraph-level** resolution (like Telegram/WhatsApp): an English-first line stays LTR, a Persian paragraph below it resolves RTL, independently of the message prefix.

### Where

- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message-text.ts` — `<div class="chat-text" dir="${detectTextDirection(markdown)}">`: one direction for the whole message.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer.ts` — `target.dir = detectTextDirection(target.value)`: one direction for the whole draft, so a multi-line draft with an English first line drags the Persian line to LTR.
- `ui/src/styles/chat/text.css` — has cosmetic `[dir="rtl"]` overrides but no `unicode-bidi` rule, so nested blocks all resolve against the single inherited direction.

### Reproduction (UI locale non-RTL)

1. Send `AutoClaw چطور کار میکنه؟` → first strong char is `A` ⇒ `dir="ltr"` for the whole message; the Persian run renders with an LTR paragraph direction, so `؟` is placed on the wrong side and the sentence reads backwards.
2. Type a two-line draft (line 1 English, line 2 Persian) → the whole value takes one direction, so line 2 is misaligned while typing.
3. Control: `چطور کار میکنه؟ AutoClaw` (Persian-first) resolves `rtl` and looks correct — confirming the defect is per-message granularity, not the detector itself.

### Proposed fix

Paragraph-level auto resolution instead of per-message:

- `ui/src/styles/chat/text.css`: add `unicode-bidi: plaintext;` to `.chat-text` (keep `text-align: start` semantics; the existing `[dir="rtl"]` overrides can stay for explicit-rtl surfaces).
- `chat-composer.ts`: prefer `dir="auto"` on the textarea over writing a computed direction, so each line resolves while typing.
- Keep `detectTextDirection` for single-line surfaces (dividers, attachment labels, session chips) where per-message granularity is appropriate.
- Keep code LTR: `.chat-text :where(pre, code) { direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: isolate; }` (the sidebar reader already uses `unicode-bidi: plaintext` on `pre`, per its comment).

### Field evidence

The Zhipu **AutoClaw desktop app 1.18.5** (macOS x64), a downstream Electron build in this family, has no direction handling at all for its message containers (`.msg-body`, `.markdown-body`, `.msg-user-text-bubble`) or composer — no `dir` and no `unicode-bidi` anywhere, with `html lang="zh-CN"` ⇒ fixed LTR base. It reproduces the identical defect for both Persian-first and English-first messages. Applying per-paragraph `unicode-bidi: plaintext` + `text-align: start` at message-container and composer level (verified locally: assistant bubbles + user bubbles + composer) fully fixes rendering. That rule set is the minimal upstream equivalent for `.chat-text` / the composer here.

### Tests

`ui/src/lib/text-direction.test.ts` already covers detection. A small browser/DOM test asserting paragraph-level resolution for `AutoClaw چطور کار میکنه؟` (i.e. the `؟` placed after the RTL run, not on its start side) would lock the behavior.

## Silent Model Auto-Escalation to Sonnet + HIGH Thinking

### Summary
OpenClaw silently auto-escalated a session from Haiku (configured default) to Claude Sonnet with HIGH thinking enabled, burning ~$25 in unexpected API costs without user awareness or approval.

### Reproduction

**Trigger message (15:04:35 UTC, 2026-09-13):**
```
Remember that we talked about switching from Telegram to Signal?
```

**Keywords detected:** "Telegram", "Signal" (communication/routing context)

**What happened:**
1. User sent the above message in Signal channel (direct message)
2. OpenClaw initialized session `a665d66a-9b59-458f-9f97-8545285639e4` with:
   - Model: `claude-sonnet-4-6` (instead of configured default `claude-haiku-4-5`)
   - Thinking level: `high` (instead of `medium`)
   - Event type: `model_change` with `parentId: null` (root-level, not user-triggered)
3. Session ran for 90 minutes (15:04-18:11 UTC) with no user awareness
4. ~27 turns consumed ~8M tokens at Sonnet pricing
5. Cost: ~$25 (vs ~$2 on Haiku)

### Evidence

**Trajectory file entry (Line 1 of reset backup):**
```json
{
  "type": "model_change",
  "id": "95a15e18",
  "parentId": null,
  "timestamp": "2026-09-13T15:04:35.193Z",
  "provider": "anthropic",
  "modelId": "claude-sonnet-4-6"
}
```

**Session context:**
- File: `/home/axel/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/a665d66a-9b59-458f-9f97-8545285639e4.trajectory.jsonl`
- Start: 2026-09-13T16:31:30.958Z
- End: 2026-09-13T18:11:00.000Z (approximate)
- Tokens: 8M+
- Cost: ~$25

### Impact

- **User cost:** $31.62 burned today (2x auto-recharges triggered)
- **User expectation:** Haiku (default) should be used unless explicitly requested
- **User approval:** No `/sonnet` command, no explicit model switch request
- **Severity:** CRITICAL — Silent escalation to 12x more expensive model without warning

### Configuration

User's configured default:
```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "model": {
        "primary": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Questions

1. What auto-escalation rule triggered on "Signal" + "Telegram" keywords?
2. Why was this not user-visible or controllable?
3. Why was HIGH thinking enabled without request?
4. Can this be disabled or made opt-in?

### Expected Behavior

- Use configured default model (Haiku) unless:
  - User explicitly requests a different model (`/sonnet`, `/opus`, etc.)
  - User's config explicitly enables auto-escalation with opt-in warning
  - System error/fallback requires upgrade (should be logged and communicated)

### Actual Behavior

- Silent escalation to Sonnet based on unknown heuristics
- No warning, confirmation, or user visibility
- Runs to completion without user awareness
- Only noticed by user after reviewing invoice and token report

### System Info

- OpenClaw: 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f)
- OS: Linux 6.12.62+rpt-rpi-2712 (arm64)
- Node: v24.19.0
- Runtime: Direct (Signal channel)

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an optional sustained-failure gate to the channel health monitor: restart a non-terminal unhealthy account only after consecutive unhealthy passes (or sustained seconds), and emit an operator-visible notice on the first failed pass instead of restarting silently.

## Problem to solve

Verified in src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.ts: a non-terminal unhealthy verdict triggers a restart on the first failed pass, gated only by cooldown (DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_CYCLES = 2 cycles x DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS 5 min), DEFAULT_MAX_RESTARTS_PER_HOUR = 10, plus startup/connect graces. There is no consecutive-failure requirement and no notice before the restart. Single-pass snapshots flap — especially WhatsApp transport stalls — so the monitor can act inside a self-healing window with the operator learning about it only from the restart log line afterward.

Field case (2026.9.4, macOS, built-in WhatsApp, same install, gateway.log verbatim times):

```
10:15:11 [whatsapp] watchdog timeout (transport-inactive), retry ladder 1/12..4/12
10:32:09 [health-monitor] [whatsapp:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: disconnected)
10:32:10 [whatsapp] [default] starting provider (...)
10:32:11..37 ladder retries continue (408s)
10:33:58 channel serving again, no manual action
```

A second episode the same morning (Telegram, 2 min) self-recovered with no action at all. Whether the 10:32 restart helped or was redundant is unknown from these logs — which is exactly the legibility gap: with a first-failure notice the operator would have watched a known-transient window instead of discovering a restart after the fact.

## Proposed solution

Two backward-compatible additions (defaults = current behavior):

1. Consecutive-failure confirmation: e.g. channels.<id>.healthMonitor.confirmFailures (default 1 = today) or confirmSustainedMs — restart only after that many consecutive unhealthy passes. A healthy pass resets the counter (same reset semantics as the existing pendingContinuation logic).
2. First-failure notice: an info-level event (log + optional channel notice) on the first unhealthy pass stating which account, which reason, and how many more failing passes precede action — so flaps are observable without acting on them.

Suggested defaults: confirmation off (1) to preserve current behavior; notice on. Both per-account overridable like the existing healthMonitor.enabled scope.

## Alternatives considered

- Raising cooldownMs / lowering maxRestartsPerHour: slows all recovery including genuine stuck states; does not make flaps observable.
- External watchdog with grace timer (what we run today: 600 s grace, 3600 s between repairs, immediate attesa notice, zero restarts across both episodes): works but duplicates the monitor from outside; the semantics belong in the monitor.
- Doing nothing: acceptable if maintainers consider first-pass restart correct; then this issue documents the tradeoff and can close as decided.

## Impact

- Affected: operators of WhatsApp/Telegram channels with flaky transports (mobile networks, DNS holes).
- Severity: moderate friction + surprise restarts mid-recovery; worst case a restart resets an in-flight backoff ladder (the supervisor-ownership guard already avoids the worst of this).
- Frequency: transport flaps are routine; our box logged two in one morning.
- Related: #146999 (terminal classification) and #147160 discussions touch the same monitor; this proposal is independent of both outcomes.

## Evidence/examples

- Monitor decision chain: src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.ts (runCheckWork: evaluate -> skip terminal/blocked -> respect supervisor backoff -> cooldown -> hourly cap -> restart; no consecutive counter anywhere in the 347-line file).
- Our external watchdog logic (grace + attesa + recovery-cancel) in field use since August; both 2026-09-13 episodes recovered inside its 600 s grace with zero restarts.
- Honesty note: whether the 10:32:09 restart helped or was redundant cannot be determined from the surviving logs; the proposal asks for observability precisely so the next such episode is legible.

## Implementation intent

Maybe, with maintainer guidance — happy to implement the counter + notice behind the proposed keys once the shape is approved, with tests in the existing monitor suite.

## Additional information

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO beyond the above; will answer maintainer questions with log excerpts on request.

issues.body:
### openclaw@2026.10.5 is unbootable: model-registry imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/env-api-keys`, which `@openclaw/ai@2026.10.5` does not export

**Contract first:** `dist/model-registry-Cfl88QiZ.mjs` in openclaw@2026.10.5 imports the subpath `@openclaw/ai/internal/env-api-keys`. For that import to resolve, the `exports` map of the `@openclaw/ai` version resolved by openclaw@2026.10.5's dependency range (exact: `2026.10.5`) must define `./internal/env-api-keys`. It does not.

**Evidence (both published tarballs, 2026-10-20):**
- `npm view @openclaw/ai@2026.10.5 version` → `2026.10.5` (exists)
- `@openclaw/ai@2026.10.5/package.json` exports keys: `.`, `./providers`, `./transports`, `./diagnostics`, `./event-stream`, `./types`, `./provider-types`, `./validation`, `./internal/anthropic`, `./internal/google-model-family` — **no `./internal/env-api-keys`**
- `openclaw@2026.10.5/package.json` requires `@openclaw/ai: 2026.10.5` (exact)
- Fresh `npm install -g openclaw@2026.10.5` → gateway boot:
  ```
  Gateway failed to start: Package subpath './internal/env-api-keys' is not defined by "exports"
  in /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/node_modules/@openclaw/ai/package.json
  imported from /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/model-registry-Cfl88QiZ.mjs.
  ```
- Reproduction (no fleet needed): `npm install -g openclaw@2026.10.5 && openclaw gateway` → same crash. `openclaw --version` and `doctor` work; only the gateway boot imports model-registry, which is why basic smoke passes.
- Fleet impact: systemd crash loop (restart counter 35, restart-loop breaker tripped) on an npm-global install; rollback to 2026.10.4 restores service.

**Expected:** @openclaw/ai@2026.10.5 exports `./internal/env-api-keys` (as some prior version evidently did), or openclaw@2026.10.5 is republished against an @openclaw/ai that does.

**Suggestion:** add a boot-smoke to the release pipeline — `--version` and `doctor` do not import model-registry, so this shipped despite being unbootable on the primary install path (npm -g).

## Bug type

Behavior bug (live progress preview never appears; final delivery unaffected).

## Summary

With channels.telegram streaming.mode=progress and richMessages:true, the Gateway never creates the progress draft: today's gateway log shows 0 editMessageText against 1034 text delivery ok, and a September A/B found answerLane.stream never created in this combination.

## Steps to reproduce

1. OpenClaw 2026.9.4, npm global install, macOS 15.7.2 (x64), Node v24.18.0.
2. Telegram account config: streaming.mode=progress (toolProgress true), richMessages=true, verbose off. No per-account overrides (verified via config get + restart).
3. Have the agent do multi-tool work in a Telegram DM (several exec/tool calls over 30+ seconds).
4. Watch the chat and grep the gateway log for editMessageText.

## Expected behavior

A single progress draft appears and updates while the agent works (the documented progress mode), as it does with verbose on Exec bubbles and as answer previews do in other modes.

## Actual behavior

- No draft ever appears; nothing updates until the final answer lands whole.
- 2026-09-09 A/B on 2026.9.3 (same install, restart-verified, 16 config paths): rich:true+progress and partial+rich:true both showed zero editMessageText in the 10:40 log window — only text delivery ok for Exec bubbles; answerLane.stream was never created. rich:false+progress 3-step test executed the same day.
- 2026-09-13 on 2026.9.4 (this report): grep over today's gateway.log → editMessageText: 0, draft-stream/answerLane lines: 0, text delivery ok: 1034.
- verbose on remains the only working live signal (Exec bubbles), which is a workaround, not the documented progress draft.

## OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (3a9d69d); also observed on 2026.9.3 (2026-09-09 tests).

## Operating system

macOS 15.7.2 (x64).

## Install method

npm global (npm prefix -g = ~/.local).

## Model

DeepSeek (default route); September A/B ran on the same install via the default model route.

## Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> deepseek.

## Logs

Redacted counts from live logs (no content, no ids):

```
# 2026-09-13, 2026.9.4, progress + rich:true
editMessageText occurrences in gateway.log: 0
draft-stream|answerLane lines: 0
text delivery ok: 1034
# 2026-09-09, 2026.9.3, rich:true (progress and partial)
editMessageText in 10:40 window: 0
answerLane.stream: never created
```

## Impact and severity

- Affected: Telegram DM operators on progress+rich (the default pairing on 2026.9.x).
- Severity: workflow-friction (no data loss; finals deliver fine).
- Frequency: always in this combination across 5 days of observation (Sep 9 → Sep 13, two releases).
- Consequence: long work looks dead for minutes, then arrives whole; operators cannot distinguish stuck from working without verbose on.

## Additional information

- Distinct from #141528 (partial mode, 429 rate-limit, rich disabled — stream starts but slow). This is progress+rich:true where no edit is ever attempted.
- Last known good version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (no version pinned; operator recalls live tool-call drafts in older 2026.8.x but without a logged version).
- 2026-09-12 note: 1–3s tasks never show a draft regardless (draft lifetime shorter than client render) — the report above concerns 30s+ multi-tool turns where the draft should persist.
