issues.body:
## Summary
The Control UI model picker renders **all providers and all their models as one long flat list**. With a realistic multi-provider setup (local ollama + several cloud APIs + an aggregator, each with dozens of models), switching models becomes a scroll marathon, and identically-named models from different providers are easy to confuse. Please restore a two-column picker: **providers on the left, the selected provider's models on the right** (an earlier version had this layout).

## Problem to solve
**Steps to reproduce**
1. Configure multiple providers, each with many models (e.g., a local ollama with several models + a few cloud providers + an aggregator; different providers may even expose same-named models).
2. Open the model picker under the chat composer in Control UI.
3. Try to find or switch to a specific model.

**Actual behavior**
- One long flat list grouped by provider headings: every switch means scrolling past all other providers' models.
- Same-named models from different providers look identical while scrolling and are easy to mix up.
- The list keeps growing with every added provider/model - with enough providers it becomes unusable.

**Expected behavior**
Two-column layout: left column = provider navigation; right column = only the selected provider's models, scrolling independently. Opening the picker should pre-select the provider of the current model. (This existed in an earlier version; restoring it would fully solve the problem.)

## Proposed Solutions
1. Restore/implement the two-column picker in Control UI.
2. While waiting for an official fix, a community workaround already exists - **[ModelSelectorOpenClaw](https://github.com/Pondsi/ModelSelectorOpenClaw)** (MIT; made by me, this issue's reporter). It adds a provider rail (left) + per-provider model column (right) to the stock picker: browser-side DOM/CSS enhancement only; appends one `<script>` line to `dist/control-ui/index.html` (backs up first, idempotent, `-Remove` reverts), touches no packaged JS/CSS/service-worker, no network/telemetry. Also published on ClawHub: [clawhub.ai/pondsi/skills/modelselectoropenclaw](https://clawhub.ai/pondsi/skills/modelselectoropenclaw).

## Alternatives considered
- The picker's search box: helps with exact names but does not disambiguate same-named models from different providers, and does not help when browsing.
- A two-step dropdown (first provider, then model): more clicks; breaks the current single-menu habit.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.2 (3928bad)
- Windows 11 build 26200; Node.js v24.20.0
- Control UI in browser; models configured across multiple providers (local ollama + cloud + aggregator)

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.9.3 (1391f7c)**, gateway run via systemd user service, Linux x64
- Channel: **Slack, Socket Mode**, single account / single gateway
- Observed on 2026.9.3; the concurrent handler error below has been present since 2026.9.x and 8.2 as well

## Summary

Inbound Slack DMs occasionally reach the gateway as `user_request` envelopes with **no message text**. We confirmed at least one of these empty events was a duplicate/redelivery of a real user message whose text had already been delivered (with full text) ~13 minutes earlier and processed normally. So: **the duplicate delivery silently drops `message.text`**, and the agent receives an "empty" user turn.

## Observed timeline (2026-09-09, one DM channel, single day)

| Slack msg ts | What arrived at the gateway |
|---|---|
| 09:06:39 (`1788915999.182829`) | `user_request` envelope, **no text** (sent while agent was mid-turn running a long update task) |
| 12:59:40 (`1788929980.666589`) | same — no text, mid-turn |
| 14:01:52 (`1788933711.698769`) | same — no text, mid-turn |
| 14:27:24 (`1788935244.510769`) | no text — **user confirmed this message did contain text**; the same instruction had already been received with full text at ~14:14 and executed to completion |

- All four empty events arrived while the gateway/agent was busy processing a previous turn (tool execution in flight — e.g. at 14:28:45 the in-flight turn reported `tool_execution_started totalMs=80119`).
- After each empty event the agent ran an "empty" turn and the user had to re-send / poke ("hello?").

## Concurrent log noise (every inbound message)

Every inbound Slack message also logs:

```
[slack] handler failed: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'catch')
```

This fires in every send/receive window (present since 2026.9.x, and in 8.2 per our logs). We suspect a connection: the handler crashes before the event is fully processed/acked → Slack redelivers the event → the redelivered copy is processed via a degraded path that drops `message.text`.

## Expected

- Redelivered/duplicate Slack events should carry the original `message.text` (or be deduped by message ts/id so duplicates don't spawn empty turns).

## Actual

- Duplicate/redelivered events arrive as `user_request` with **no text**; the agent runs a turn against an empty message and the user's typed content is silently lost in that delivery.

## Impact

- Real message loss for the user: any message typed while the agent is busy may arrive empty. In our case the first delivery survived so the content was recoverable — but had the first delivery been the affected one, the message would have been gone entirely.

## Notes

- Gateway journal excerpts (redacted) available on request.
- Possibly related: #137799 (Slack outbound formatting on the same gateway).

issues.body:
**Symptom**
The model-name indicator near the Control UI message input starts blinking and the session becomes unusable. The client shows:

```
Error: Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
```

This has happened repeatedly. So far the only reliable recovery is a full Gateway restart.

**Root cause (found via gateway.log)**
A companion-app (macOS node) connection briefly drops while an agent turn is using computer/node tools:

```
... errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=UNAVAILABLE: COMPANION_APP_UNAVAILABLE: macOS app exec host unreachable ...
... errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=UNAVAILABLE: UNAVAILABLE: screen snapshot failed ...
```

Right after that, the same websocket connection starts failing every `chat.metadata` request for that session, repeatedly:

```
[ws] res chat.metadata errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=ChatMetadataSnapshotUnavailableError: prepared chat metadata owner is unavailable for agent "main" conn=...
```
(33 repeats over ~33 minutes in one occurrence, same conn id, same session)

**Unconfirmed hypothesis, now falsified in practice**
In one log sample, the failing connection recovered right after an unrelated config hot-reload event (`agents.entries.main.identity` change). We hypothesized a lightweight config hot-reload could substitute for a full restart, and set up a log-tailing automation (Gateway `schedule.kind="stream"` job watching for this error string) so the agent could self-heal without the user needing to restart.

**This did not work.** On the next real occurrence:
1. The user waited, nothing recovered, no proactive notice arrived, so the user restarted the Gateway manually (as before).
2. Checking afterward, the self-heal automation job itself was gone — a session-owned `schedule.kind="stream"` automation does not survive a Gateway restart, so it never got a chance to fire.
3. Separately, even if the automation did fire while the connection was stuck, there is no guaranteed way to notify the user through the very same broken connection/session before it recovers — so a silent "trying to fix it" state is possible, which is worse than just restarting.

**Ask**
1. Ideally: the per-connection "tool authority snapshot" / "chat metadata snapshot" should be invalidated/regenerated automatically when the underlying node connection recovers, so no external trigger (config reload or restart) is needed at all.
2. If a lighter recovery command is added (e.g. per-session/per-connection reset instead of full Gateway restart), it should be reachable/effective even while that session's own delivery path is degraded — otherwise self-heal from the affected agent is not reliable.
3. If automations are expected to help with self-recovery scenarios like this, they should be able to survive/re-arm across a Gateway restart (or there should be a gateway-level watcher independent of any single session).

**Environment**
- OpenClaw 2026.9.3
- macOS 26.6.2, Control UI (webchat) client

issues.body:
## Bug: bailian/qwen3.7-plus request failed — Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')

### Describe the bug

When using the `bailian/qwen3.7-plus` model through the WeChat channel (openclaw-weixin), the agent run fails with:

```
⚠️ bailian/qwen3.7-plus request failed. rawError=Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')
```

The API returns HTTP 200 with a valid SSE stream, but OpenClaw crashes while parsing the response. The built-in retry mechanism (3 attempts) also fails because it reuses the same session context, triggering the same parse error each time.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `bailian/qwen3.7-plus` as the model via the bailian provider (OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `https://coding.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1/chat/completions`)
2. Accumulate a long session context over time (cron tasks, image processing, multi-turn conversations)
3. Send a message in WeChat that triggers the model to return a response where a content field is undefined/null
4. Observe repeated failures

### Expected behavior

- OpenClaw should gracefully handle missing/null fields in the model response instead of calling `.trim()` on undefined
- The retry mechanism should consider resetting or trimming context when the same error repeats

### Actual behavior

```
[openclaw-weixin] embedded run agent end: isError=true model=qwen3.7-plus provider=bailian
error=⚠️ bailian/qwen3.7-plus request failed. rawError=Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')

[agent/embedded] [empty-error-retry] stopReason=error non-visible-output; resubmitting attempt=1/3
[agent/embedded] [empty-error-retry] stopReason=error non-visible-output; resubmitting attempt=2/3
[agent/embedded] [empty-error-retry] stopReason=error non-visible-output; resubmitting attempt=3/3
```

All 3 retries fail. Running `/new` to start a fresh session resolves the issue immediately.

### Workaround

Running `/new` to create a clean session fixes it. The problem only occurs in long-lived sessions with accumulated context.

### Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.8.2
- OS: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (x64)
- Node: v22.23.1
- Model: bailian/qwen3.7-plus
- Channel: openclaw-weixin
- API endpoint: https://coding.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1/chat/completions

### Additional context

- The API consistently returns HTTP 200 with `text/event-stream` content type — the failure is in response parsing
- Other models (qwen3.5-plus, qwen3.6-plus) were observed working fine in the same timeframe
- This has happened multiple times, not just once — it seems correlated with long session context

issues.body:
﻿**Version:** 2026.9.1 (npm dist), observed on the node/Talk gateway-relay path with `consultRouting: force-agent-consult`; the voice-call plugin path shares the serial-consult design.

## Summary
Realtime voice has no way to delegate work asynchronously. Every agent-backed turn blocks the conversational channel until its `openclaw_agent_consult` completes: consults are processed serially (`createRealtimeVoiceAgentTalkbackQueue` is an explicitly serial queue; the relay path gates admission per call), and with `autoRespondToAudio: false` (required to stop the provider fabricating direct answers), the model cannot hold a normal conversation while a consult runs. The result on a real call: the user asks something substantive, then experiences up to 100+ seconds of dead air (we measured 133s), and anything else they say queues behind the in-flight consult rather than being conversed with.

Text chat with the same agent does not have this limitation — the agent can spawn sub-agents/background sessions and keep chatting. Voice can't express that pattern natively.

## What exists vs. what's missing
- `submitToolResult(..., { willContinue: true })` + `buildRealtimeVoiceAgentConsultWorkingResponse` show the plumbing for interim results exists — but it emits a single holding message, not a resumption of normal conversation.
- The realtime model's tool surface (consult / control / describe-view) has no "start this in the background and return immediately" affordance.
- Workaround we're deploying: instruct the *delegated agent* to spawn a background session for long tasks and return a short "started — results will be posted to <channel>" answer within seconds. This works but pushes the product behavior into every deployment's agent prompts.

## Request
A supported async delegation mode for realtime voice, e.g.:
1. A consult variant (flag or separate tool) that dispatches the agent turn and returns immediately with an acknowledgement, keeping the conversational channel open;
2. Completed results injected mid-call as speakable items when they arrive (the `willContinue` path suggests this is close);
3. Concurrent consults, or at minimum a conversational track that stays live while one runs.

Framing: *realtime voice cannot delegate asynchronously; every agent-backed turn blocks the conversation.* Related: #139277 (client agent binding), #139278 (barge-in coupling), #139279 (no timeout/progress cue during consults — the symptom users feel from this same architecture).

### Summary

Follow-up to #75113 (transient tool status lines in streaming cards — shipped). Two related asks so that a whole turn (reasoning + tool calls + final answer) lives in **one card** with collapsible structure, and tool activity **persists** after the turn finishes:

1. Render reasoning and per-tool-call entries as native `collapsible_panel` elements inside the streaming/reply card (collapsed by default), instead of a transient status line + quote block.
2. Keep tool-call entries in the finalized card. Today `onToolStart → statusLine` renders a temporary line that is cleared on finalize, so after the turn ends the card shows no trace of what was executed.

### Current behavior (2026.9.2)

- Streaming card: reasoning streams into a "💭 Thinking" quote block; tool activity appears as a **transient status line** (`formatChannelProgressDraftLineForEntry`) that is wiped when the card finalizes.
- Finalized card: reasoning and tool calls are gone; only the answer text (plus header/footer) remains.
- The reply pipeline does not emit `collapsible_panel` at all — only direct Card Kit v2 card JSON authoring can use them today.

### Desired behavior

- One card per turn containing: collapsible reasoning panel, collapsible tool-call log (one entry per call: name, phase, duration, optionally truncated args), then the answer body.
- Panels persist after finalize (visible audit trail; users of long multi-tool turns repeatedly ask "what did it actually do?").
- Config gates, e.g. `channels.feishu.card.panels.{reasoning,tools}` (`enabled`, `defaultExpanded`), defaulting to current behavior for compatibility.

### Validated Card Kit v2 constraints (empirical, direct card API)

While prototyping this layout with hand-authored cards we confirmed on the current API:

- `collapsible_panel` accepts exactly `{tag, expanded, header: {title}, elements}`; `background_style` on the panel or header is rejected (200621), as is any element-level `options` key (230099/200621).
- `table.rows` must be object records keyed by `columns[].name`; array-of-arrays rows fail with 200914 (`rows invalid row idx`).
- Streaming cards carry `streaming_config.print_frequency_ms` (default 50) — relevant if panels are updated mid-stream.

Happy to share working card JSON for the panel layout if useful.

### Related

- #75113 (closed — transient tool status lines; this issue asks for the persistent/structured evolution)

issues.body:
## Environment

- openclaw v2026.9.1 (upgraded from 7.1), macOS, Slack channel via Socket Mode

## Summary

The 7.1 -> 9.1 upgrade removed the `healthState` field from the Slack channel health JSON, replaced by `lifecycle` / `lastError` (`src/gateway/channel-status-patches.ts`). An external watchdog on our box keyed its unhealthy test on `healthState != "healthy"`; the now-missing field read as "unknown", the test was permanently true, and it kickstart-restarted a perfectly healthy gateway every ~10 minutes for ~10.5 hours (61 restarts, every one logging `connected=true`, zero errors, healthy lifecycle).

That incident was our own script's fault in the proximate sense, but it doubled as an unplanned stress test of the gateway, so this report leads with the concrete regression trigger and follows with the two resilience/observability gaps the incident exposed. Filed as one issue because they reproduced together as a single incident.

### 1. Health JSON schema change shipped without a deprecation or migration signal

`healthState` was removed with no release-note callout and no transition mirror. Any external monitor reading the old field silently misclassifies a healthy channel (missing key), and the failure mode is the worst kind: the monitor "fails dirty" by taking corrective action against a healthy process.

**Ask:** call out health-JSON schema changes in release notes as a breaking change, and consider mirroring a deprecated `healthState` (derived from `lifecycle`) for one release cycle.

### 2. No backpressure / starvation visibility on ingress dispatch

During the post-storm backlog drain, events were admitted promptly to the durable queue (`channel_ingress_events`) but dispatched in bursts minutes later — we measured a peak oldest-pending age of ~6-7 minutes. Nothing in the health surface exposes queue depth or oldest-pending age, so an operator cannot distinguish "draining slowly" from "stuck" without opening the sqlite store directly. We also observed triggers firing with the message body only rendering a turn later during drain, which looks like loss until you check the store.

**Ask:** add queue depth and oldest-pending age to the channel health JSON.

### 3. Mid-turn kill restarts turns from scratch

Orphaned-turn recovery works (killed turns re-run, nothing is dropped), but all completed tool work inside the killed turn is redone from the beginning. Under a periodic external kill with a period shorter than turn duration — our exact situation at a ~10-minute cadence — any sufficiently long turn can never complete: an effective livelock. The process looks healthy the whole time.

**Ask:** coarse-grained turn checkpointing or partial-progress persistence, so a mid-turn restart resumes rather than replays.

## Evidence

- 61 SIGTERM restarts counted from the primary gateway log, first 00:54, last 11:24 local; every watchdog decision logged `connected=true err=0` — the gateway was healthy each time it was killed
- Zero message loss measured across the storm: a deliberately long (330-byte) test message with position tokens past the old clip boundary was stored byte-complete (330/330, mentions intact, byte-identical across both ingest lanes), completed `pending -> completed` at `attempts=0`, and rendered full-body in the following turn
- Peak oldest-pending age ~6-7 min during backlog drain (illustration of ask #2, not a steady-state figure)

## Positive note

`channel_ingress_events` durability worked exactly as designed under sustained restart pressure — every message survived 61 restarts byte-complete. The asks above are observability and resilience improvements, not correctness fixes.

issues.body:
### Version

`2026.7.1`, pinned by digest `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw@sha256:2f5ce8848a1a69b3c460622e566cb9395da9fd18d7ef7b038cd8e2c4f195decf` (the `:slim` tag's digest at pin time). Single gateway process, 9 agents, `claude-cli` runtime, Linux/arm64, containerized.

### Summary

A module-level singleton in `mcp-http-*.js` caches the in-process MCP loopback HTTP server and the runtime holding its ephemeral port. Nothing verifies the cached listener is still alive before handing its port to a new session.

If that listener dies for any reason other than the code's own graceful shutdown, every subsequent session is configured against a dead port and **every MCP tool call fails indefinitely**. Only a full gateway restart clears it.

### Impact

For a multi-agent deployment this is a silent, total loss of inter-agent messaging that presents as agents working normally:

- Agents kept functioning throughout — `Bash`, `Read`, `Edit` were unaffected.
- Only `mcp__openclaw__*` tools failed, so nothing looked broken from outside.
- It ran **undetected for roughly two days**. It surfaced only when a coordinating agent wrote seven work tickets and could deliver none of them.
- An earlier occurrence caused an agent to act for several hours on an instruction that had already been reversed — the correction was issued, accepted by the queue, and never arrived.

There is no health signal for this. A caller cannot distinguish "the recipient received this" from "the transport is dead", which makes the failure indistinguishable from a quiet period.

### Mechanism

1. `ensureMcpLoopbackServer()` binds a listener on an ephemeral port and stores the server plus its runtime in module-level state.
2. `prepareRun` calls `getActiveMcpLoopbackRuntime()`; if that state is populated it reuses the cached port and **skips** `ensureMcpLoopbackServer()` entirely.
3. That state is cleared only on the code's own graceful shutdown path. A listener dying any other way leaves the singleton populated and stale.
4. Every later session is then configured against the dead port. Connections are refused and each tool call fails as `tool_failed`.

### Reproduction

Observed rather than constructed: three consecutive failures in one session, each traced to a refused connection on the exact ephemeral port that session's subprocess had been configured with, while nothing in the container was listening on that port. Non-MCP tools in the same session succeeded before, between, and after.

To force it: kill the loopback listener without going through graceful shutdown, then start any new agent session and call any `mcp__openclaw__*` tool.

### Suggested fix

Either would be sufficient, and both look cheap:

1. Re-attach an `error`/`close` handler after a successful `bind` that clears the cached runtime, so the next `prepareRun` self-heals by re-binding.
2. Have `getActiveMcpLoopbackRuntime()`'s callers probe the cached port before trusting it, falling through to `ensureMcpLoopbackServer()` on failure.

A third, independently valuable: emit a log line or health signal when a tool call fails because the loopback is unreachable. **The absence of any signal is what turned a recoverable fault into a two-day outage.**

### Workaround

Restarting the gateway clears the singleton and restores service — symptom only; nothing prevents recurrence. We added an hourly canary that calls `sessions_list` from a cron-triggered session and alarms on failure, which bounds detection to one hour rather than two days.

### Possibly related

We also see agents intermittently calling bare tool names (`sessions_send`) rather than the prefixed form (`mcp__openclaw__sessions_send`); those always fail. Chronic but appears separate — mentioning only in case it shares a root.

﻿**Version:** 2026.9.1 (npm dist).

## Summary
When a realtime voice session dispatches a forced agent consult (`talk.realtime.consultRouting: force-agent-consult` on the Talk path, or `consultPolicy: always` on the voice-call plugin path), there is no per-consult timeout and no audible progress cue while the agent turn runs. If the agent takes long — we measured a 133-second consult on a real call — the caller hears complete silence for the entire duration, with no way to know whether the call is still alive. On a phone call this is indistinguishable from a dead line and callers hang up.

## Observed
- Talk path, forced consult dispatched, agent turn duration ~133s: zero audio frames sent to the caller between dispatch and the final spoken result. No keepalive, no interim "still working" utterance, no timeout/fallback.
- The harness has a `buildRealtimeVoiceAgentConsultWorkingResponse` mechanism and the proxy-mode prompt permits a short backchannel while waiting, but in practice nothing fires during a long consult on the Talk path.

## Requests
1. **Configurable per-consult timeout** — after N seconds, either speak a fallback ("this is taking longer than expected, I'll follow up") or return control to the realtime model, instead of waiting indefinitely on the agent turn.
2. **Periodic progress cue** — an optional short utterance or earcon every ~15-20s while a consult is in flight, so callers know the line is live.
3. At minimum, surface the consult-in-flight state to the integrator (event/webhook) so a custom cue can be injected.

Related: #139278 (barge-in disabled during forced consult makes the long silence worse — the caller can't even interject to ask if anyone is there and get a reaction).

issues.body:
## Feature request: user-facing notice for `before_tool_call` blocks (e.g. `userNotice` field)

### Problem
A `before_tool_call` hook that returns `{ block: true, blockReason }` produces a generic channel warning rendered by `dist/worker/worker.mjs` (`formatToolErrorWarningText`): `⚠️ 🎨 Image Generation blocked` / `⚠️ 🛠️ Exec blocked`.

For **policy-denial** blocks that wording is correct. But plugins also block tools to **defer/offload** them (e.g. a gate that blocks a long-running `image_generate` inline and has the agent re-run it as a background task). The work then completes successfully seconds later — yet the user has already been told it was "blocked", which reads as refusal/failure. Real user confusion reported.

`blockReason` is model-facing and deliberately excluded from user-visible surfaces (per docs/plugins/hooks.md, block reasons are sensitive), so there is currently **no supported way** for a blocking plugin to tell the user what actually happened.

Notably, `before_agent_run` blocks **do** support a user-facing `message` replacement — the concept exists, it's just missing at tool-call level.

### Proposal
Extend `BeforeToolCallResult` with an optional user-facing field, e.g.:

```ts
type BeforeToolCallResult = {
  block?: boolean;
  blockReason?: string;      // model-facing (unchanged)
  userNotice?: string;       // NEW: rendered to the channel instead of the generic "⚠️ <tool> blocked" line
  // ...
}
```

Rendering: when `userNotice` is set, the channel warning renderer emits it verbatim (sanitized) instead of `⚠️ <tool> blocked`. When absent, current behavior is unchanged. An alternative/complement: a `status: "deferred"` block kind that renders as `⏳ <tool> moved to background`.

### Why it matters
- Guard/offload plugins are a natural pattern (keep chat lanes responsive; push heavy work to subagents). Today every such block mislabels success as failure.
- The generic renderer cannot distinguish "blocked, will never run" from "blocked here, running in background" — only the plugin knows.

### Environment
OpenClaw 2026.8.2 (0965053), macOS arm64, multi-agent gateway.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression / behavior bug (visible progress is lost without an error)

### Summary

On OpenClaw `2026.9.1`, Codex app-server commentary is recorded in the OpenClaw transcript but never reaches the temporary Discord progress draft.

The final assistant reply is delivered normally. This is not merely the expected cleanup/replacement of a temporary draft: the Discord channel was inspected while the turn was still running, after multiple tools had executed and after the progress startup delay, and no progress message had been created.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.9.1 (ad6fe23)`
- `@openclaw/codex`: `2026.9.1` (official install, activated and loaded)
- `@openai/codex`: `0.152.1`
- Runtime/model: native Codex app-server, `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`
- Channel: Discord guild channel
- OS: macOS / Darwin 25.4.0 arm64
- Node: `v26.0.0`
- Session verbose mode: enabled
- Gateway and Discord channel: connected and otherwise healthy

Relevant effective configuration:

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "discord": {
      "streaming": {
        "mode": "progress",
        "progress": {
          "commentary": true,
          "toolProgress": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw `2026.9.1` with the official Codex plugin `2026.9.1`.
2. Enable Discord progress streaming with both `progress.commentary=true` and `progress.toolProgress=true`.
3. In a normal Discord channel turn, ask the Codex-backed agent to perform a multi-step task that invokes several tools.
4. Have the agent emit short assistant-authored commentary between tool batches.
5. Observe the Discord channel during the running turn, not only after the final answer.
6. Compare the live Discord messages with the stored OpenClaw transcript.

### Expected behavior

A temporary Discord progress message should be created and updated with commentary/tool progress while the turn is running. The draft may be cleaned up or replaced when the final answer is delivered.

This matches the documented behavior and the acceptance criteria from #83307 / #85200.

### Actual behavior

- Codex emits assistant commentary and continues executing tools.
- OpenClaw stores the commentary in the transcript.
- No temporary Discord progress message is sent at any point during the turn.
- Only the final assistant reply appears in Discord.
- Enabling verbose mode does not restore the progress draft.

### Transcript evidence

For affected assistant commentary records, the persisted message has no top-level `phase: "commentary"` and no `text_signature.phase`. Instead, it contains metadata shaped like:

```json
{
  "openclawStreamFallback": {
    "source": "segment",
    "itemId": "<redacted>"
  },
  "__openclaw": {
    "mirrorIdentity": "...:commentary:<redacted>"
  }
}
```

The commentary identity is therefore preserved internally, but the channel-facing progress path does not render it.

### Suspected boundary (inference)

This may be a Codex app-server projector / segmented-stream fallback regression: the commentary is recognized as a fallback segment and mirrored with commentary identity, but the Discord progress compositor may only receive/render an explicit commentary-phase event.

This is an inference from the persisted event shape and live channel behavior, not a confirmed source-level root cause.

### Reproducibility and impact

- Reproduced repeatedly in normal, non-queued Discord turns.
- Final replies are unaffected.
- Users see no natural-language status or tool progress during long-running tasks, making an active agent appear stalled.
- The behavior worked on an earlier installed release, but the exact last-known-good version was not captured.

### Related issues

- #88227 — nearly identical Discord symptom on an older release: progress/partial modes show only the final reply.
- #83307 — feature request and expected event plumbing for Discord commentary progress.
- #85200 — implementation of opt-in Discord commentary progress.
- #78070 — adjacent Telegram regression where verbose/progress previews disappear while final replies still arrive.

No existing issue was found that covers this exact `2026.9.1` + native Codex + normal Discord turn + `openclawStreamFallback` event shape.

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23)
- macOS 26.6.2, arm64 (Apple Silicon)
- Gateway: single process, launchd-managed (KeepAlive)

## Symptom
Since upgrading to 2026.9.1, scheduled cron-expression jobs intermittently fail to fire at their scheduled times. The scheduler's next-run stamp advances past the scheduled time, but no execution happens: no error, no failed run, nothing in the job history. The job config is valid (verified per job).

## Frequency
Intermittent — roughly 20-30% of daily scheduled fires are silently skipped. Observed daily since the upgrade (2026-09-03 through 2026-09-05).

## Evidence (one morning: 17 scheduled daily jobs due before 12:34 ET)
- 12 fired normally
- 5 were silently swallowed:
  - 4 jobs scheduled 08:55-09:30: no fire, no error, no run entry (last runs show 2026-09-03 or 2026-09-04)
  - 1 job scheduled 11:20: no fire
  - 1 job scheduled 11:30: no fire (recovered by manual force-fire at 12:24)
- A different subset was swallowed the previous two mornings (e.g., the same 11:30 job missed both 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-05)

## Recovery
Manual `openclaw cron run <id>` works immediately — the job executes, delivers, and re-anchors its schedule. No persistent corruption; only the scheduled fire is lost.

## Workaround in place
A watchdog interval job (every 30m) that compares each scheduled job's lastRunAtMs against its expected daily fire time and force-fires anything overdue past a 20-minute grace window.

## Notes
- The gateway process did not restart or crash during the affected window (uptime confirmed).
- Interval-style (every Nm) jobs appear unaffected — only cron-expression schedule fires are swallowed.
- Happy to provide additional run histories or diagnostics if useful.

issues.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw's SQLite-backed plugin/gateway state reliably corrupts ("database disk image is malformed", `ERR_SQLITE_ERROR`) when its state directory sits on a Docker Desktop macOS overlayfs mount (containerd-snapshotter overlay inside the VirtioFS-backed VM). Corruption is fast and deterministic under trivial write load, not a rare race. When it happens, the `openclaw` CLI fails to start ("Failed to open the plugin state database"), and — separately, see below — message delivery can silently fall back to a degraded path.

## Environment

- OpenClaw running inside a Linux sandbox/container managed by a third-party sandboxing tool, itself running under Docker Desktop on macOS (Apple Silicon), using Docker Desktop's default containerd-snapshotter storage driver (overlayfs backed by VirtioFS).
- OpenClaw version: 2026.6.11
- State directory (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`) is a path inside that sandbox's mounted state volume, ultimately backed by the above overlay/VirtioFS stack.

## Reproduction (root cause isolation, independent of OpenClaw's own code)

To rule out an OpenClaw-specific bug, we created a completely fresh, empty SQLite database on the same mount/filesystem (not touching any OpenClaw file), set `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;`, and subjected it to a trivial concurrent write workload: 8 threads × 200 inserts each (~1600 rows total — normally sub-second on any healthy filesystem).

**Result: the process hung indefinitely.** We killed it after 10+ minutes with no completion and no error — not a corruption, a hang, consistent with POSIX advisory byte-range locking (`fcntl`/`flock`) being broken or pathologically degraded on this mount. SQLite's WAL mode depends entirely on correct advisory locking from the underlying filesystem; when that's broken, the *actual* application-level symptom we saw in production was outright corruption rather than a hang (likely depending on which lock operation silently misbehaves), but the underlying defect is the same: this mount does not honor the locking contract SQLite WAL requires.

This points to a Docker Desktop / storage-driver issue, not (necessarily) an OpenClaw code bug — but OpenClaw is directly and severely affected by it in normal deployments, so we're filing here for visibility and to ask whether OpenClaw could detect/guard against this class of filesystem.

## Production symptom

Running OpenClaw as a long-lived gateway process on the affected host:

- `openclaw`/`openclaw message` CLI invocations began intermittently, then reliably, failing with:
  ```
  Config health-state write failed: database disk image is malformed
  [openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
  [openclaw] Reason: Failed to open the plugin state database. | database disk image is malformed | ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
  ```
- `PRAGMA integrity_check` against the corrupted DB showed dozens of "invalid page number" errors — real structural corruption, not a false alarm.
- A one-time manual repair (dump all live table rows, rebuild a fresh DB file, restart the gateway) worked, but corruption reliably recurred within roughly a minute of normal operation resuming, ruling out a one-off/rare event.

## Suggested mitigations worth considering upstream

- Detect known-bad filesystem/storage-driver combinations (e.g. Docker Desktop's overlay2/containerd-snapshotter on macOS) at startup and warn, or fall back to a non-WAL journal mode (`DELETE`/`TRUNCATE`), which doesn't depend on advisory locking in the same way, when such a mount is detected.
- Document this as a known-risky deployment target so others troubleshooting "database disk image is malformed" under similar container setups can find this quickly.
- Consider whether the plugin/gateway state DB could tolerate `busy_timeout` + integrity-check-on-open with auto-recovery, to degrade gracefully instead of hard-failing CLI startup.

## Secondary, related finding (separate from the corruption bug — flagging here since it surfaced in the same investigation)

`openclaw message send --channel slack --presentation '{"text": "..."}'` silently does not use `--presentation`'s `text` field as the delivered Slack message body — only `--message`'s value is what actually renders. This contradicts `--help`'s description of `--presentation` as carrying "text, context, dividers, buttons, selects". Reproduced directly: sent a message with a short `--message` and a longer, different `--presentation.text`; the delivered Slack message only contained the `--message` content. If this is expected/documented elsewhere, apologies for the noise — happy to open this as a separate, smaller issue if that's preferred.

## Severity

Requesting P0 / high-severity triage: this causes silent, reliable data corruption and CLI unavailability for a common deployment shape (containerized/sandboxed OpenClaw on Docker Desktop for Mac), and — via the secondary finding above — can also cause silent message-content loss even when the CLI is healthy.

issues.body:
## Summary

Expose cached provider subscription/quota windows as bounded, privacy-safe metrics from `@openclaw/diagnostics-prometheus`.

## Problem to solve

OpenClaw already retrieves structured provider usage through `usage.status`, including window labels, used percentages, reset timestamps, and snapshot freshness. The Control UI and session status can display those values, but `/api/diagnostics/prometheus` exposes no equivalent metric family.

Operators therefore cannot:

- graph remaining subscription allowance beside model reliability and latency;
- alert before an autonomous workload exhausts a 5-hour or weekly window;
- distinguish a genuinely low allowance from a stale/failed usage refresh; or
- use the same first-party authenticated metrics endpoint for both runtime health and provider capacity.

The current workaround is an external process that calls `usage.status`, sanitizes its response, writes Prometheus textfile metrics, and relies on Node Exporter. That duplicates OpenClaw's provider-usage semantics and authentication knowledge outside the Gateway.

## Proposed solution

Add low-cardinality gauges to `diagnostics-prometheus`, sourced from the existing stale-while-revalidate provider-usage snapshot rather than performing a provider API call on each Prometheus scrape.

Suggested minimal families:

```text
openclaw_provider_usage_used_ratio{provider="openai",window="5h"} 0.30
openclaw_provider_usage_reset_timestamp_seconds{provider="openai",window="5h"} 1788637148
openclaw_provider_usage_last_success_timestamp_seconds{provider="openai"} 1788622338
openclaw_provider_usage_last_attempt_timestamp_seconds{provider="openai"} 1788622338
openclaw_provider_usage_refresh_success{provider="openai"} 1
```

`remaining_ratio` should be derived as `1 - used_ratio` in PromQL rather than exported as a redundant series.

Privacy and cardinality constraints:

- never export account email, credential/profile key, balance details, request identifiers, prompts, or responses;
- normalize `provider` and `window` through the existing low-cardinality label policy;
- reuse the exporter's existing series cap and dropped-series counter;
- preserve the last good snapshot while separately reporting refresh success/freshness;
- document the semantics for multi-profile providers before exposing any profile dimension.

The current retained `UsageSummary` is not sufficient to produce the three
refresh metrics above: timeout retention deliberately substitutes the last good
provider snapshot and its `updatedAt`. These values must therefore be
producer-owned facts recorded by the provider-usage cache, not inferred by the
exporter.

### Proposed bounded snapshot contract

For a narrow first version, mirror the same account-selection semantics as the
unscoped `usage.status` RPC: metrics represent the credential currently selected
for the resolved default/legacy usage agent. Document that scope explicitly.
Do not expose an account-email or credential/profile label.

On a selected-credential or profile-order change, invalidate the previous
projection and remove its allowance series until the cache owner publishes a
successful observation for the new selection. This avoids silently presenting
old-account values as the newly selected account. A later multi-agent or
credential-keyed design can broaden the contract deliberately.

The cache-owned projection should retain, per provider:

- sanitized windows from the last successful observation;
- `lastAttemptAt`;
- `lastSuccessAt`;
- a bounded last outcome (`success`, `timeout`, `auth`, `rate_limit`, `billing`,
  `format`, or `unknown`); and
- selection invalidation/generation internally, without exporting credential
  fingerprints.

When the Prometheus exporter is enabled, it should acquire a bounded freshness
lease/interest from the cache owner. The cache owner—not the exporter HTTP
handler—should schedule deduplicated refreshes at an agreed cadence. The
Prometheus route remains a render of retained state and never performs provider
network work per scrape.

## Alternatives considered

1. **External Node Exporter textfile collector:** proven to work, but duplicates Gateway authentication, provider parsing, caching, failure semantics, installation, and lifecycle management.
2. **Prometheus scraping `usage.status` directly:** Prometheus does not natively transform Gateway JSON/RPC into metrics and would require another adapter.
3. **Alert only inside OpenClaw:** useful for notifications, but does not support historical dashboards, capacity planning, or correlation with latency/errors.
4. **Export account/profile labels:** rejected because it creates privacy and cardinality concerns. Multi-account attribution needs a deliberate contract first.

## Impact

- **Affected users:** operators running autonomous agents with subscription-backed providers and Prometheus/Grafana.
- **Severity:** moderate operational gap; it does not block model calls, but quota exhaustion can interrupt unattended work without advance visibility.
- **Frequency:** continuous for subscription-backed deployments.
- **Consequence:** custom credential-aware sidecars/scripts, fragmented monitoring, and no first-party capacity alerting.

## Evidence/examples

Verified on OpenClaw `2026.9.1`:

- `usage.status` returns two OpenAI windows (`5h` and `Week`) with `usedPercent`, `resetAt`, and `updatedAt`.
- `/api/diagnostics/prometheus` exports runtime model/tool/token metrics but no provider allowance or reset metrics.
- A five-minute external collector exported the proposed sanitized values through Node Exporter.
- Prometheus ingested both windows successfully, and Grafana rendered remaining allowance, reset countdowns, and feed freshness correctly.
- The working proof omitted account identity and OAuth data entirely.

Sanitized expected-versus-actual proof:

```text
$ openclaw gateway call usage.status --json | jq \
    '.providers[] | {provider, windows: [.windows[] | {label, usedPercent, resetAt}]}'
{
  "provider": "openai",
  "windows": [
    {"label":"5h","usedPercent":30,"resetAt":1788637148000},
    {"label":"Week","usedPercent":13,"resetAt":1789165183000}
  ]
}

$ query the authenticated /api/diagnostics/prometheus endpoint and filter for
  '^openclaw_provider_usage_'
# no output

$ curl -fsS http://node-exporter.example/metrics | \
    grep '^openclaw_codex_subscription_remaining_ratio'
openclaw_codex_subscription_remaining_ratio{window="5h"} 0.70
openclaw_codex_subscription_remaining_ratio{window="week"} 0.87
```

Correction to the external proof: its
`openclaw_codex_subscription_collector_success` metric means only that the
Gateway RPC and local transformation succeeded. It does **not** prove that a
fresh provider request succeeded, because the RPC can legitimately return a
retained last-good snapshot. The upstream feature should not copy that
limitation; refresh outcome must come from the cache owner.

Related work:

- #129327 requests proactive quota thresholds; first-party metrics would let existing Prometheus/Alertmanager deployments implement those thresholds without coupling core notification policy to one alerting system.
- #102807 documents multi-account/provider-keyed attribution ambiguity; this proposal intentionally avoids a profile label until those semantics are defined.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance. I can implement and test a focused change after maintainers choose the provider-usage-to-exporter boundary and confirm multi-profile semantics.

## Additional information

This is distinct from session token/cost metrics: it represents provider-reported subscription capacity windows, not locally accumulated tokens or API billing tiers.

After manual pairing on Windows (`openclaw browser extension pair --gateway-url

drive tabs.

# Issue 2: Provider-level headers override (User-Agent) causes "The selected model was not found by the provider" on relays with UA filtering

## Summary

Relay/aggregator endpoints behind Cloudflare that enforce User-Agent filtering cannot be used with OpenClaw 2026.9.1 custom providers, even though the same endpoint works perfectly with the required UA via curl. Configuring `headers.User-Agent` at the provider level (and also trying per-request `headers`) makes the upstream return 200 for `models` listing, non-streaming, and streaming chat — verified by direct curl — yet `openclaw agent` fails with:

```
The selected model was not found by the provider
```

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23), upgraded from 2026.8.2
- Windows 10 (10.0.19045)
- Custom provider, `api: openai-completions`, `baseUrl` = relay endpoint (host redacted: `<relay-host>`)
- Relay enforces UA allow-listing at the CDN edge (403 without the expected UA)

## Reproduction

1. Define a custom provider pointing at a UA-filtering relay:

```json
{
  "baseUrl": "https://<relay-host>/v1",
  "api": "openai-completions",
  "apiKey": "<redacted>",
  "headers": { "User-Agent": "<expected-ua>" },
  "models": [ { "id": "<model-id>" } ]
}
```

2. Curl sanity checks — all succeed with the UA header (and fail with 403 without it):
   - `GET /v1/models` → 200
   - `POST /v1/chat/completions` non-streaming → 200
   - `POST /v1/chat/completions` streaming → 200 SSE
3. `openclaw agent --message "hi" --json` → fails with `The selected model was not found by the provider`.
4. Tried both provider-level `headers` and request-level `headers` — same result.
5. Same provider with the key on a non-UA-filtering upstream works, isolating the failure to the UA header path.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** provider-level `headers.User-Agent` is applied to every outbound request to that provider, so behavior matches curl.
- **Actual:** OpenClaw reports the model as not found — which looks like a 404/model-resolution error on the surface, but the upstream returns 200 under curl with the same UA, implying the authored header override either (a) is not applied on the actual chat request path, or (b) triggers a validation branch in the request-authoring code that misclassifies the response.

## Diagnosis evidence

- Direct curl with/without UA against the same endpoint: 403 (no UA) vs 200 (with UA) — UA filtering confirmed as the gate.
- With `headers` configured, OpenClaw still fails on the chat call while `models` resolution succeeds — suggesting headers apply on some code paths but the authored chat request override path behaves differently.
- Error text (`model was not found by the provider`) does not match the upstream response (200), pointing at client-side classification rather than a genuine 404.

## Suggested fix directions

1. Audit the request-authoring path for custom providers: ensure provider-level `headers` merge into the actual chat completion request (and are not dropped/overridden by defaults).
2. When the upstream returns an unexpected shape with a non-404 status, surface the real status/body instead of mapping to "model not found".
3. Alternatively/additionally: document or provide a first-class `userAgent` provider option, since UA-filtering relays are common.

— Draft prepared for review; relay host, UA value, keys and model ids redacted.

issues.body:
## Bug: DeepSeek fallback fails with `tools[0]: missing field 'type'` when session switches from Anthropic-protocol model (MiniMax-M3)

### Environment
- OpenClaw version: 2026.7.2-beta.4 (installed 2026-07-31, no upgrade since)
- Primary model: `minimax/MiniMax-M3` via `anthropic-messages` transport (api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/v1/messages)
- Fallback model: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` via `openai-completions` transport (api.deepseek.com/v1/chat/completions)
- macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)

### Summary
When a session that has been running on an Anthropic-protocol model (MiniMax-M3) is switched to DeepSeek (`/model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`) **or** when OpenClaw auto-fallbacks from M3 to DeepSeek, requests that include tools fail with HTTP 400:

```
tools[0]: missing field `type` at line ...
```

Pure-text requests succeed (HTTP 200). Requests **without** tools also succeed. The failure only occurs when the request carries tools **and** the session previously ran on the Anthropic-messages transport.

### Root cause (verified against dist source)
1. Internal tool middle format is `{name, description, parameters}` (`openai-tool-projection-*.mjs` pushes `parameters: schemaProjection.schema`).
2. The Anthropic encoder (`anthropic-*.mjs`) emits `{name, input_schema}`.
3. When a session context already contains tools encoded with `input_schema` (from the Anthropic-protocol model), and the request is re-sent via the OpenAI-completions transport for DeepSeek, `normalizeDeepSeekToolSchemas(ctx)` in `dist/provider-tools-*.js` only cleans `anyOf/oneOf` union keywords — it does **not** map `input_schema` → `parameters`, and the OpenAI encoder only reads `tool.parameters`. Result: `tool.parameters` is `undefined`, no `type: "function"` wrapper is emitted, and DeepSeek rejects the payload.

### Evidence
- Direct curl tests to DeepSeek API with OpenAI-style schema `{type:"function", function:{name, parameters}}` → 200 for `deepseek-chat`, `deepseek-reasoner`, `deepseek-v4-flash`.
- Direct curl tests with Anthropic-style `{name, input_schema}` → 400 `missing field 'type'` for all three models. This is expected DeepSeek behavior; the bug is that OpenClaw does not convert schemas across protocol transports.
- Gateway log shows failures only after `sessions.patch` (model switch M3→deepseek) on tool-bearing requests: `2026-09-05T08:37 / 13:40 / 20:19 / 20:21` all 400; identical sessions on 8/24-8/28 without cross-protocol switch all 200.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run a session with `minimax/MiniMax-M3` (anthropic-messages transport) and use tools.
2. Switch the same session to `/model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`.
3. Send a message that triggers a tool call (e.g. "list files").
4. Observe HTTP 400 `tools[0]: missing field 'type'`; request retried/falls back or errors.

### Expected behavior
Tool schemas should be re-encoded per-transport on model switch/fallback: Anthropic `{name, input_schema}` should be converted to OpenAI `{type:"function", function:{name, parameters}}` when a request is sent through the openai-completions transport (and vice versa).

### Suggested fix
In `normalizeDeepSeekToolSchemas` (and the shared provider tool compat family hooks), normalize the tool's parameter schema source before cleaning keywords:

```js
let parameters = tool.parameters;
if (!parameters && tool.input_schema) parameters = tool.input_schema; // Anthropic → OpenAI
if (!parameters || typeof parameters !== "object") return tool;
const normalized = normalizeDeepSeekSchema(parameters);
return normalized === parameters ? tool : { ...tool, parameters: normalized };
```

More generally: the openai-completions transport should tolerate/convert `input_schema` from cross-protocol session history, or tool projections should be re-computed from the canonical source on every transport send instead of reusing protocol-specific encodings cached in session context.

### Workaround (local)
Patch `dist/provider-tools-*.js` `normalizeDeepSeekToolSchemas` with the snippet above and restart the gateway. Note: any OpenClaw upgrade overwrites this patch.

### Impact
- DeepSeek unusable as fallback/switch target on tool-bearing sessions that previously ran an Anthropic-protocol model.
- Affects any mixed-protocol fallback chain (Anthropic-compatible primary + OpenAI-compatible fallback).

issues.body:
### Environment
- OS: Windows 11 (build 10.0.26200, x64)
- Node: v24.20.0
- OpenClaw: 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23), npm global install
- Channel: Feishu direct (channel-only deployment)
- Session: main agent session (`agent:main`)
- UI: Control UI / web dashboard paired with the Gateway (http://127.0.0.1:18789)

### Summary
The automatic progress-card reminder is injected only into non-main sessions. From `docs/tools/progress-card.md`:

> "OpenClaw adds a short progress-card reminder only for non-main sessions when a web, iOS, Android, or macOS card renderer is paired with the Gateway and the run is not using the agent's utility model. Channel-only deployments such as a WhatsApp-only Gateway do not receive the reminder."

This leaves two gaps for users who follow the progress card from the UI:

1. **Main session gets no reminder at all.** A user chatting with the main agent over a channel (e.g. Feishu/WhatsApp direct) often also watches the session's progress card in the Control UI dashboard. Since the reminder is never injected into the main session, the agent receives no nudge to keep the card current, so the card frequently goes stale while long multi-step work runs. The card is the primary at-a-glance surface for someone not reading the transcript — exactly the case that needs a fresh card.

2. **Channel-only deployments get no reminder for any session.** In a deployment without a native mobile/desktop renderer (our case: Feishu only), even non-main sessions (cron, subagents) receive no reminder, because the reminder also requires a web/iOS/Android/macOS card renderer to be "paired". Users who do open the web Control UI to follow background runs still see stale cards there.

### Suggested fix (any of these, or combination)
- Inject the reminder into **main sessions too** when a UI/card renderer is present, not only non-main sessions. A simple change: treat the main session like any session that has a watcher.
- Or make the reminder **configurable**, e.g. `agents.defaults.progressCardReminder: "all" | "non-main" | "off"` (default stays `non-main`), so channel-first users can opt into reminders for the main session.
- For channel-only deployments: if the Gateway is paired with a web Control UI at all, that qualifies as a "card renderer paired" — inject reminders for sessions the user actually watches (at minimum the main session).

### Documentation gap
`docs/tools/progress-card.md` documents the non-main-only injection rule but does not explain how a main-session user who watches the card in the UI is supposed to keep it fresh, nor expose a config option to opt in. Worth documenting the rationale (main session = user is in the conversation itself) alongside a note that users may still watch the card via UI.

### Impact
Today a main-session user in a channel-only deployment who follows the progress card in the web UI sees a card that lags behind the actual work — and has no supported way to make the agent maintain it. The card's core promise ("the user follows it instead of reading the transcript") is weakest exactly in this setup.

## Summary

Add Catalan (ca) locale support to the OpenClaw Control UI, following the existing i18n pattern used by 20 other locales (es, fr, de, ko, etc.).

## Problem to solve

Catalan-speaking operators currently have no localized UI experience in the OpenClaw Control panel. All interface labels, navigation elements, and status messages are rendered in English only, forcing Catalan-speaking users to work in a non-native language. Catalan is spoken by ~10 million people across Catalonia, Valencia, the Balearic Islands, and other territories.

## Proposed solution

Follow the existing i18n pattern to add Catalan as a supported locale:

1. **Add `"ca"` to the `Locale` type** in `ui/src/i18n/lib/types.ts`
2. **Register `ca` in the lazy locale registry** in `ui/src/i18n/lib/registry.ts`
3. **Add `ca` entry** to `scripts/lib/control-ui-i18n-config.json`
4. **Create `ca.ts` virtual locale export** in `ui/src/i18n/locales/ca.ts`
5. **Create `glossary.ca.json`** with key terminology following the [Softcatalà style guide](https://www.softcatala.org/guia-estil-de-softcatala/tota-la-guia/)
6. **Initialize `ca.meta.json` and `ca.tm.jsonl`** for translation memory

The 6,356 translation keys will be generated via `scripts/control-ui-i18n.ts` using the glossary as terminology guidance.

## Glossary highlights (Softcatalà style guide)

| English | Catalan | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway | Passarel·la | Softcatalà terminology |
| Skills | Habilitats | |
| Plugins | Connectors | Softcatalà terminology |
| Settings | Configuració | |
| Workspace | Espai de treball | |
| Automations | Automatitzacions | |
| Tasks | Tasques | |
| Channels | Canals | |
| Memory | Memòria | |

The translation follows the [Softcatalà style guide](https://www.softcatala.org/guia-estil-de-softcatala/tota-la-guia/), which establishes conventions for software localization in Catalan:
- Use formal "vós" for user-facing messages
- Avoid unnecessary possessives ("el fitxer" not "el vostre fitxer")
- Prefer active voice over passive
- Omit "Sorry" / "Please" in UI messages
- Use gender-neutral forms where possible

## Alternatives considered

- **Browser-level translation**: unreliable for SPA, breaks dynamic content
- **Post-build string replacement**: fragile, lost on every update

## Related

- RFC 0024: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/42
- Korean locale request (similar pattern): #53345
- Localization runtime issue: #113105

## Summary

A Talk realtime voice session ended/expired server-side before the client could submit a tool result back, causing two consecutive failed round-trips from the same connection (mobile/Android client):

```
15:51:24 [gateway] talk realtime context: workspace bootstrap file IDENTITY.md is 4200 chars (limit 3937); truncating in injected context
15:51:33 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ talk.session.submitToolResult 1ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Error: Unknown Talk session
15:51:50 [gateway] talk realtime context: workspace bootstrap file IDENTITY.md is 4200 chars (limit 3937); truncating in injected context
15:52:13 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ talk.session.submitToolResult 0ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Error: Unknown Talk session
```

Two attempts, ~40 seconds apart, both hitting a session id the gateway no longer recognized — looks like a client retry against an already-dead session rather than a fresh session start. This is a different failure mode from the previously-fixed ownership race (#123596 / PR #135031 + #135423); that one was about *which agent* owns a session, this one is the session simply not existing anymore by the time a tool result is submitted.

## Environment

- openclaw v2026.9.1
- Client: mobile/Android app (same connection also made `device.pair.list` / `doctor.memory.*` calls immediately prior)
- 5 agents configured

## Ask

1. Investigate why the Talk session was unrecognized at `submitToolResult` time — timeout? session-store eviction? id mismatch on reconnect/retry?
2. Separately: the `IDENTITY.md truncating in injected context` warning fired on both attempts. This comes from a **hardcoded** `DEFAULT_REALTIME_BOOTSTRAP_CONTEXT_MAX_CHARS = 12000` total budget (split evenly across profile files, landing around ~3937 chars/file for 3 files) in `realtime-bootstrap-context-*.js` — there's no config path to raise it. Worth exposing this as a config option (e.g. `talk.realtimeBootstrapContextMaxChars`) rather than a fixed constant, since workspace profile files can legitimately exceed it (in our case it was mostly an inline base64 avatar data URI in IDENTITY.md, now fixed on our end by switching to a file path reference — but the budget itself is still a hardcoded, non-configurable constant).

I don't have a live repro session to attach right now, but wanted both findings on record together since they showed up in the same incident.

issues.body:
**Body:**

### Environment
- OS: Windows 11 (build 10.0.26200, x64)
- Node: v24.20.0
- OpenClaw: 2026.8.2 → 2026.9.1 (npm global install, `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\openclaw`)
- Service: Scheduled Task `OpenClaw Gateway` (InteractiveToken, LeastPrivilege, non-elevated)

### Summary
Updating from 2026.8.2 to 2026.9.1 via `openclaw update` (run as Administrator) installs the package successfully, but the update ends with **ERROR** and reason `service-revalidation-failed`. The managed Scheduled Task is left **disabled** and can no longer be modified from a non-elevated context (DACL changed), and the new `--task-supervisor` launch path fails on this machine. Three side effects:

1. **The Scheduled Task is left disabled** — `openclaw gateway start` fails with "the scheduled task is disabled".
2. **Stale gateway lock files remain** — `~\.openclaw\tmp\openclaw\gateway.*.lock*` pointing at dead PIDs cause the new gateway to silently exit on startup.
3. **The new `--task-supervisor` launcher does not work** — the relay worker exits within ~1 second (whole tree, exit code 0) and never spawns the gateway process; the gateway daemon itself starts fine when run directly.

### Repro
1. Run `openclaw update` as Administrator from 2026.8.2.
2. Package update succeeds, Doctor runs.
3. Update reports `service-revalidation-failed` → status ERROR.
4. `openclaw gateway start` fails (task disabled); `openclaw gateway install --force` regenerates `gateway.cmd` with `--task-supervisor`; relay exits immediately, gateway never starts.

### Log excerpts

`openclaw update` output (end):
```
Stopping managed gateway service before package update...
Stopped Scheduled Task: OpenClaw Gateway
  ✓ Updating via package manager (90.52s)
  ✓ Running doctor checks (80.56s)
...
Update Result: ERROR
  Root: C:\Users\72660\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\openclaw
  Reason: service-revalidation-failed
  Before: 2026.8.2
  After: 2026.9.1
Total time: 6m 29s
```

Doctor (during update) noted:
```
Gateway service ownership or manager identity changed; inspect it before restarting manually.
```

After the update, `openclaw gateway start` failed:
```
Gateway start failed: Error: schtasks run failed: 错误: 由于已禁用计划任务"OpenClaw Gateway"，其无法运行。
```

The generated launcher chain was `gateway.vbs → gateway.cmd → node ... gateway --port 18789 --task-supervisor < NUL`. The `--task-supervisor` relay (Job Object anchor, `dist/task-supervisor-*.js`) exited ~1s after launch (whole tree exit 0) without ever starting the gateway, both under the Scheduled Task context and in a local shell, with no log output.

### Expected
- Update completes successfully and the managed service is re-enabled/restarted automatically.
- The new `--task-supervisor` Windows launch path works, or falls back to the previous direct-launch path when the relay cannot start.

### Workaround (verified)
1. **Elevated repair**: run an elevated script (`Start-Process -Verb RunAs`) that does `Enable-ScheduledTask -TaskName "OpenClaw Gateway"` then `openclaw gateway install --force` — task returns to Ready/Running and regenerates the 2026.9.1 `gateway.cmd` / `gateway.vbs`.
2. **Remove stale locks**: delete `~\.openclaw\tmp\openclaw\gateway.*.lock*` (contents pointed at dead PID 460).
3. **Edit `gateway.cmd`** to drop `--task-supervisor < NUL` and run node directly (same as pre-2026.9.1 behavior):
   ```bat
   "C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe" --max-old-space-size=8192 C:\Users\72660\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\openclaw\dist\index.js gateway --port 18789
   ```
4. **Sync remaining plugin**: `openclaw plugins update @openclaw/feishu@2026.9.1` (last of 5 drifted plugins).
5. **Restart**: `openclaw gateway restart` → verified 2026.9.1 running, `/healthz` ok, `/readyz` ready. `restart` does not rewrite `gateway.cmd`.

### Note
Re-running `openclaw gateway install --force` regenerates `gateway.cmd` **with** `--task-supervisor`, reproducing the failure — the flag must be removed manually again.

### Documentation gap
`docs/install/update-troubleshooting.md` lists reason codes but does **not** document `service-revalidation-failed` (or `managed-service-handoff-failed` on this environment). The `--task-supervisor` Windows launch path (Job Object relay) is undocumented as a known-fragile path. Please add guidance for both, and consider a fallback to direct launch when the relay exits without starting the gateway.

issues.body:
**Environment**
- OpenClaw 2026.8.1-beta.3 (5831b80); `logging.redactSensitive` unset (default `tools`), no custom `logging.redactPatterns`
- OL9 ARM64, rootful Podman, shared netns control + browser, CDP attach, Playwright Chromium 145

**Symptom**
The built-in sensitive-value redaction treats the browser `act` parameter named `key` (a keyboard key name such as `Escape`) as a credential. Observed in one session, all three sinks:
- diagnostic log: `raw_params={"action":"act","kind":"press","key":"***",...}`
- persisted transcript (`transcript_events`): `"key":"***"`
- **the tool result returned to the model**: `Error: keyboard.press: Unknown key: "***"`

Because the rejected value is masked inside the very error that is supposed to explain the rejection, the model cannot see what it sent or how it differs from a valid key. It re-sent the identical call 39 times until the run was abandoned.

**Reproduction**
1. CLI: `openclaw browser press Esc` → error text shows `Unknown key: "Esc"` (the CLI sink does not redact).
2. Ask any agent: "call the browser tool once with action act, kind press, key Esc, then reply with the exact error text" → the reply is `Error: keyboard.press: Unknown key: "***"`.

Related: #68425 asks for a machine-readable marker on redacted output. This report is about (a) a field that should not be redacted at all and (b) redaction reaching into free-text error messages shown to the model.

**Proposed direction**
1. Field-name heuristics (`key`, `token`, …) should not apply to tool parameters whose schema declares them non-secret — e.g. a per-tool allowlist (`browser.act.key`) or a schema annotation the redactor honours.
2. Do not mask, in the tool result shown to the model, a value that came from the model's own arguments in the same turn (it already knows it).
3. At minimum, apply #68425's marker so the model can tell the value was masked rather than literally `***`.

**Workaround we're using locally**
None available: per the config schema, `logging.redactPatterns` is additive at the tool boundary and `redactSensitive:"off"` may still redact safety-boundary tool payloads. Only prose ("stop after two identical failures").

issues.title: [Bug]: Codex app-server 0.163.0 warns against the managed runtime pin 0.160.0

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.2 treats Codex app-server 0.163.0 as newer than its managed runtime pin of 0.160.0 and logs a warning on startup. A configured command that still points at a removed 0.159.3 release fails chat before that.

### Steps to reproduce

1. npm-global OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.2 (2b85c4c) on Debian 13.
2. Set `plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command` to a Codex standalone binary that reports `codex-cli 0.163.0`.
3. Restart the gateway and read the embedded-agent log.
4. For the failure that preceded this: point the same setting at the 0.159.3 standalone release after that directory has been removed, then send a webchat message.

### Expected behavior

The Codex plugin's supported floor is 0.149.0. An external app-server at 0.163.0 is above that floor, so startup should not warn that the binary is newer than the managed pin. Chat should run with the configured binary. A removed older release directory should not be required.

The installed plugin sets `CODEX_APP_SERVER_VERSION` to `"0.160.0"` and `MIN_SUPPORTED_CODEX_APP_SERVER_VERSION` to `"0.149.0"`. `assertSupportedCodexAppServerVersion` rejects versions below 0.149.0 and, when the detected version compares greater than 0.160.0, logs a warning and continues.

### Actual behavior

After the gateway restart, embedded startup logged this repeatedly:

```
[agent/embedded] codex app-server is newer than OpenClaw's managed runtime; continuing with normal startup validation detectedVersion=0.163.0 validatedVersion=0.160.0
```

The gateway stayed ready. No `CodexAppServerSpawnError` occurred after the command pointed at the 0.163.0 binary.

Before that change, the same setting pointed at the 0.159.3 standalone `bin/codex` and that directory was gone. Webchat turns failed with:

```
CodexAppServerSpawnError: Codex catalog updater cannot run: <codex-standalone>/releases/0.159.3-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex or its working directory was not found. Repair the executable or working directory and restart the Gateway.
```

The gateway process stayed up. `/healthz` and `/readyz` still reported ready while those turns failed.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10-beta.2 (2b85c4c)

### Operating system

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

not applicable

### Provider / routing chain

Codex app-server, external command

### Logs

```
[agent/embedded] codex app-server is newer than OpenClaw's managed runtime; continuing with normal startup validation detectedVersion=0.163.0 validatedVersion=0.160.0
CodexAppServerSpawnError: Codex catalog updater cannot run: <codex-standalone>/releases/0.159.3-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex or its working directory was not found.
```

### Impact and severity

Affected: this gateway with an external Codex app-server newer than 0.160.0, and earlier with the command still aimed at a removed 0.159.3 release.
Severity: annoying for the 0.163.0 warning. The missing 0.159.3 binary was blocking: webchat turns returned that spawn error.
Frequency: the warning logged on each embedded startup after the restart. The spawn error occurred on each webchat turn while the command pointed at the missing release.
Consequence: the running Codex is three releases ahead of the pin the plugin validates, and a command pinned to one old release directory fails closed when that directory is removed.

### Additional information

Related, not the same report: #162768. That issue is model discovery hardcoding `client_version=0.158.0`. This report is the startup check against `CODEX_APP_SERVER_VERSION` 0.160.0. Host paths are omitted. The 0.163.0 binary's `--version` output is `codex-cli 0.163.0`.

issues.body:
## Problem

Sub-agent runs can sit in `running` state indefinitely with zero output. From the parent's perspective this is indistinguishable from a healthy slow start. The actual cause is `openclaw:prompt-error` with `error: "aborted"` being mapped to `{ status: "timeout" }` — losing the distinction between startup abort and mid-run abort.

We observed **70 failing transcripts** matching this pattern across agents (62 `run_aborted`, 8 `startup_aborted`, 6 `empty_output_startup`).

## Root cause

The embedded run handler emits only three lifecycle phases: `start`, `end`, `error`. There is no `first-progress` signal, so the parent cannot distinguish a working child from a silently aborting one. A 45s abort looks identical to a 90-min hang until the wall-clock timeout fires.

## Proposed addition (additive, non-breaking)

Two new lifecycle event phases:

1. `first-progress` — emitted on first qualifying tool call or non-empty assistant text
2. `startup-failed` — typed failure with reason: `startup_aborted`, `startup_timeout`, `empty_output_startup`, `auth_failed`

Both are additive. Existing listeners use explicit string comparisons and already silently drop unknown phase strings — confirmed from source inspection.

## Update safety

- Additive only — no existing consumer changes required
- No breakage on update — unknown phases are silently dropped
- Plugin-SDK boundary not crossed
- External workspace watchdog (polling-based) works as interim without core changes

## Evidence

70 failing transcripts captured from live corpus. Representative fixture: `chunker/sessions/8cb62941`. Full design with 20 test cases and 4-phase rollout strategy available.

issues.body:
## Bug: Followup drain monopolizes session lane — causes indefinite inbound dispatch stall

**Version:** 2026.3.23-2 (not present in 2026.3.13)

### Symptoms
- After every agent turn, new inbound Discord DMs and WhatsApp messages are silently queued for 20-30 minutes before processing
- `sessions_send` does not fix it (queues behind same backlog)
- Only `SIGUSR1` (gateway restart / `resetAllLanes()`) resolves it immediately
- 100% reproducible on any session with active followup queue + compaction-heavy context

### Root Cause
`scheduleFollowupDrain` (in `pi-embedded-CbCYZxIb.js:94509`) starts an unbounded async loop after every turn. Each queued item (system events, subagent announces, WhatsApp reconnects) calls `runEmbeddedPiAgent` → `enqueueSession(() => enqueueGlobal(...))`, holding the session lane (`maxConcurrent: 1`) for the full turn duration including compaction + context engine maintenance. New user messages queue behind all followup turns with no preemption.

### Observed lane wait times
From diagnostic logs on `session:agent:main:main`:

| Time (Mar 25) | Wait (ms) | Wait (min) |
|---|---|---|
| 10:28 | 1,361,250 | ~22 min |
| 13:42 | 1,814,033 | ~30 min |
| 13:49 | 1,237,693 | ~20 min |

Log pattern: `lane wait exceeded: waitedMs=1814033 queueAhead=1`

### Contributing factors
- **Compaction safeguard** runs summarization API calls within the lane task (context chronically at 142% of budget, compactionCount: 14)
- **Memory flush** adds a full LLM call per compaction cycle (`compaction.memoryFlush.enabled: true`)
- **Ollama heartbeat/cron timeouts** (5 min each) consume global lane slots and trigger retry chains with 404 fallback failures
- **WhatsApp reconnects** generate bursts of system events (observed: 152 disconnect/reconnect events in one day) that each get processed as individual followup turns

### Setup context
- `session.dmScope: "main"` (Discord DM + WhatsApp share main session)
- 10 agents configured, multiple WhatsApp groups, Discord guild with ~15 channels
- Heartbeat: every 55m (was on `ollama/qwen2.5-14b-agent`, timeouts blocked global lanes)
- `contextPruning.mode: "cache-ttl"` (custom events at end of turn correlated with stall, but turning it off did not fix it — lane starvation is the real cause)

### Suggested fixes
1. **Cap consecutive followup drain turns** (e.g., max 3) before yielding to inbound queue
2. **Prioritize user messages over system events** in the session lane
3. **Run context engine maintenance (`afterTurn`/`maintain`) OUTSIDE the session lane task** — the lane should be released after `clearActiveEmbeddedRun`, not after post-turn cleanup
4. **Add a configurable aggregate timeout** for the full session lane task (not just compaction retry)

### Workarounds (config-level mitigations)
These reduce lane occupation time but do not fix the root cause:
```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      compaction: { reserveTokensFloor: 20000, memoryFlush: { enabled: false } },
      heartbeat: { model: "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5" },  // was ollama (5min timeouts)
    },
  },
  messages: { queue: { debounceMs: 5000 } },  // batch system events
}
```

### Reproduction
1. Configure a session with `dmScope: "main"` and multiple active channels (WhatsApp + Discord)
2. Enable compaction safeguard with memory flush
3. Send a message → agent responds
4. Wait 3-5 minutes, send again
5. Message sits in lane queue for 20-30 minutes (or indefinitely with ollama timeouts)

### Environment
- macOS 12.7 (x64), Node v24.13.1
- OpenClaw 2026.3.23-2 (npm global install)
- Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6 (primary), Ollama Qwen 2.5 14B (heartbeat/crons)
- Discord + WhatsApp + Telegram channels active

## Summary

After reviewing Anthropic's *Complete Guide to Building Skills for Claude* (Jan 2026), I audited all 52 built-in OpenClaw skills against the guide's best practices. The main finding: **34 of 52 skills (65%) are missing trigger phrases in their `description` field.**

Per the guide, a skill description must include both:
1. **What it does** (most skills have this)
2. **When to use it** — specific phrases a user might say that should trigger the skill (most skills are missing this)

Without trigger phrases, Claude has to guess when to load the skill, leading to undertriggering.

## Affected Skills (34)

`apple-reminders`, `bear-notes`, `blogwatcher`, `blucli`, `camsnap`, `discord`, `eightctl`, `gemini`, `gh-issues`, `gifgrep`, `gog`, `himalaya`, `imsg`, `mcporter`, `nano-banana-pro`, `nano-pdf`, `notion`, `obsidian`, `openai-image-gen`, `openai-whisper`, `openai-whisper-api`, `openhue`, `oracle`, `ordercli`, `peekaboo`, `sag`, `session-logs`, `sherpa-onnx-tts`, `songsee`, `sonoscli`, `spotify-player`, `summarize`, `tmux`, `trello`, `video-frames`, `voice-call`, `wacli`

## Additional Issues

- `canvas` skill has **no description field at all**
- `gh-issues` is at **4,995 words** — 5 words from the 5,000-word limit; any future edits risk breaking it

## Example Fix

**Before:**
```yaml
description: Gemini CLI for one-shot Q&A, summaries, and generation.
```

**After:**
```yaml
description: Gemini CLI for one-shot Q&A, summaries, and text generation. Use when user asks to "ask Gemini", wants a second opinion from another AI model, needs a fast summary, or requests generation without using Claude directly.
```

## Reference

Anthropic guide: https://resources.anthropic.com/hubfs/The-Complete-Guide-to-Building-Skill-for-Claude.pdf (p. 8–10 on description best practices)

Happy to submit PRs with fixes for any of these if that would help.
