issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`openclaw doctor` reports `Memory search provider is set to "gemini" but no API key was found. Semantic recall will not work without a valid API key.` while the provider key is configured as a store-sourced SecretRef, `openclaw secrets audit` reports zero unresolved refs, and `openclaw memory status --deep` shows embeddings ready with a fully built index for the same provider.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the Google provider key as a store SecretRef (the shape `openclaw secrets configure` produces), e.g. `models.providers.google.apiKey = { "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "GOOGLE_API_KEY" }`.
2. Enable memory search on that provider: `memory.search.provider = "gemini"`, `memory.search.model = "gemini-embedding-001"`.
3. Do not export `GEMINI_API_KEY` / `GOOGLE_API_KEY` in the shell, and have no Google auth profile in the auth-profile store (the key lives only in the secret store).
4. Run `openclaw doctor` (same result with `--deep`).
5. Compare with `openclaw memory status --deep` and `openclaw secrets audit`.

### Expected behavior

Doctor should treat a valid, configured store SecretRef as a configured credential (or as "configured, availability unknown in the CLI read-only path"), the way its sibling checks already do:

- The `memory.search.remote.apiKey` path in the same doctor check uses `hasConfiguredMemorySecretInput`, which accepts any configured SecretRef without resolving it (`src/commands/doctor-memory-search.ts` around the `hasRemoteApiKey` computation; test "treats SecretRef remote apiKey as configured for explicit provider" in `src/commands/doctor-memory-search.test.ts`).
- The shared read-only availability helper `resolveSecretRefReadOnlyAvailability` in `src/agents/auth-profiles/read-only-availability.ts` returns `undefined` (unknown), not `false`, for valid non-env refs whose provider matches the configured secrets provider.
- The doctor security check has a test "does not warn when model provider API keys are stored as SecretRefs" (`src/commands/doctor-security.test.ts`).

At minimum the message must not say "no API key was found" and must not recommend disabling memory search when the runtime is demonstrably working.

### Actual behavior

`openclaw doctor` (and `openclaw doctor --deep`) prints:

```
Memory search provider is set to "gemini" but no API key was found.
Semantic recall will not work without a valid API key.

Fix (pick one):
- Set GEMINI_API_KEY in your environment
- Configure credentials: openclaw configure --section model
- To disable: openclaw config set memory.search.enabled false
```

Same host, same config, same minute:

```
$ openclaw memory status --deep
Memory Search (main)
Provider: gemini (requested: gemini)
Model: gemini-embedding-001
Indexed: 545/545 files · 2924 chunks
Embeddings: ready
Vector store: ready
Semantic vectors: ready
FTS: ready
Embedding cache: enabled (4738 entries)

$ openclaw secrets audit
Secrets audit: clean. plaintext=0, unresolved=0, shadowed=0, storeResidue=0, legacy=0.
```

Root cause as read on current `main` (`d2f262ac22c`) and `v2026.8.2`:

- `hasApiKeyForProvider` in `src/commands/doctor-memory-search.ts` first calls `resolveEnvApiKey` (no env var set) and then `resolveUsableCustomProviderApiKey`.
- `resolveUsableCustomProviderApiKey` in `src/agents/model-auth-provider-config.ts` only handles `source: "env"` SecretRefs: for any other source `envVarName` is `""` and it returns `null`. On `v2026.8.2` the same function had an explicit `if (apiKeyRef.source !== "env") return null;`, so this is not a recent regression.
- The remaining branch short-circuits on `!hasAnyAuthProfileStoreSource(agentDir)` and returns `false` before `resolveApiKeyForProviderCore` is ever attempted, because the key is in the secret store, not an auth profile.
- The gateway runtime path (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-remote-client.ts`, `resolveApiKeyForProvider` when the provider owns the destination) resolves the same store ref fine, which is why embeddings are ready.

The gateway memory probe did not contribute a `ready` signal in this run either (the softer "API key was not found in the CLI environment ... gateway reports embeddings are ready" variant was not printed), so the operator only sees the hard failure text.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.1 (ad6fe23); logic verified identical on current `main` d2f262ac22c and on the `v2026.8.2` tag

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2 (Darwin 25.6.0)

### Install method

npm global (Homebrew node)

### Model

memory embedding: gemini/gemini-embedding-001 (chat model irrelevant)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> google generativelanguage (models.providers.google.baseUrl = https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta)

### Additional provider/model setup details

`models.providers.google.apiKey` is a `source: "store"` SecretRef pointing at the built-in `default` secrets provider (SQLite secret store). No `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` in the CLI or gateway service environment. No Google auth profile in the auth-profile store. `memory.search.remote` is not set.

### Logs

```shell
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23)

$ openclaw doctor --deep   # Memory search section
Memory search provider is set to "gemini" but no API key was found.
Semantic recall will not work without a valid API key.
Fix (pick one):
- Set GEMINI_API_KEY in your environment
- Configure credentials: openclaw configure --section model
- To disable: openclaw config set memory.search.enabled false
Verify: openclaw memory status --deep
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Config shape (values redacted):

```json
"models": { "providers": { "google": { "baseUrl": "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta", "apiKey": { "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "GOOGLE_API_KEY" } } } },
"memory": { "search": { "provider": "gemini", "model": "gemini-embedding-001" } }
```

### Impact and severity

- Affected: any operator who moved provider keys into the SQLite secret store (`openclaw secrets configure` / doctor migration) and uses a named memory embedding provider (gemini, openai, mistral, ...) rather than `memory.search.remote.apiKey`.
- Severity: misleading doctor verdict on a working default-path feature. The suggested fixes either do nothing (env var already unnecessary) or disable a working feature (`memory.search.enabled false`).
- Frequency: always, deterministic on this config shape.
- Consequence: operator cannot trust doctor for memory search; following its advice degrades the install.

### Additional information

Not a regression from 2026.9.1: the `source !== "env" -> null` behavior is present on the `v2026.8.2` tag. On this host the config was migrated to store SecretRefs and memory search was enabled on 2026-09-01, which is when the warning first became visible; earlier configs used a plaintext key, which doctor accepts. First known bad version not observed beyond that.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

OpenClaw 2026.9.5 cannot complete legacy session migration because several transcript headers do not match their original filenames, and session-sqlite recovery restores zero sessions.

[session-sqlite-1792462588630-0b6b8c8c.failure.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33696942/session-sqlite-1792462588630-0b6b8c8c.failure.md)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start with an OpenClaw 2026.4.15 state directory containing the legacy sessions.json store and JSONL transcripts.
2. Stop the Gateway, install OpenClaw 2026.9.5, and run `openclaw doctor --fix`.
3. Run `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite dry-run --session-sqlite-all-agents`.
4. Run `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite recover --session-sqlite-all-agents`.
5. Observe 53 session migration issues, `restored=0`, and errors stating `Primary transcript header does not match its original filename`.

### Expected behavior

OpenClaw should migrate valid legacy sessions and transcripts into SQLite while preserving the original history, archive or safely retain unresolved source files, and allow Doctor to complete so the installation can be upgraded normally.

[session-sqlite-1792462588630-0b6b8c8c.failure.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33697002/session-sqlite-1792462588630-0b6b8c8c.failure.md)

### Actual behavior

`openclaw doctor --fix` stops because the retained legacy sessions.json store requires migration. The session-sqlite dry run reports 53 issues. Recovery completes with `restored=0`, including four `Primary transcript header does not match its original filename` errors and multiple unverified active JSONL transcripts.

### OpenClaw version

OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)

### Operating system

Windows 11 (win32), Node.js v24.19.0

### Install method

npm global

### Model

n/a — the failure occurs during Doctor session migration before any model request.

### Provider / routing chain

n/a — the failure occurs before model routing.

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

```shell
OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)

`openclaw doctor --session-sqlite dry-run --session-sqlite-all-agents`:
- 1 target
- 55 legacy entries
- 55 SQLite entries
- 53 issues
- validated=55/16198 events

`openclaw doctor --session-sqlite recover --session-sqlite-all-agents`:
- restored=0
- skipped=0
- conflicts=0
- four historical transcripts report: `Primary transcript header does not match its original filename`

Doctor then stops with:
`Legacy session store requires migration at C:\Users\chencan2\.openclaw\agents\main\sessions\sessions.json`
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The sanitized session SQLite migration failure report is attached in the Summary section.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Windows installation upgrading a legacy OpenClaw 2026.4.15 state directory through 2026.9.5.
Severity: High; blocks Doctor maintenance and prevents normal Gateway startup with the existing state directory.
Frequency: Reproduces on every Doctor and session-sqlite recovery attempt with this state directory.
Consequence: The user must either abandon access to existing session history or use a separate clean state directory.

### Additional information

GitHub suggested #172109 as a potential duplicate, but that issue concerns duplicate session headers and `sqlite_transcript_count_mismatch`. This report concerns transcript header IDs that do not match their original JSONL filenames. The original archive and state directory have been preserved.

### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On native Windows, OpenClaw 2026.10.5 with the official Codex and Discord plugins repeatedly spends 69–89 seconds loading plugins; the concurrent main-session recovery worker times out before the Gateway reaches ready.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows x64 with Node 24.22.0 and OpenClaw 2026.10.5, configure the official Codex 2026.10.5 plugin as the agent harness and the official Discord 2026.10.4 plugin as an enabled channel.
2. Start or cleanly restart a local Gateway with both plugins enabled (15 plugins loaded).
3. Observe the startup timeline, event-loop delay, and `sidecars.main-session-recovery` result.

Controlled copied-state restarts on the same package/Node: neither external plugin: 1.34 s recovery / 0.68 s runtime post-bind; Codex only: 25.18 / 24.75 s; Discord only: 46.20 / 46.27 s; both: 70.14 / 70.25 s and recovery worker timeout.

### Expected behavior

The Gateway should keep its event loop responsive and complete main-session recovery without an internal timeout. On the same machine and release, a copied-state control with neither external plugin completed recovery in 1.34 s.

### Actual behavior

Repeated configured starts spent about 69–89 s in plugin loading while the concurrently queued main-session recovery worker did not begin until after its deadline. Recovery logged `WorkerTaskError: worker task timed out`; the Gateway then reached `ready` and Discord connected. One isolated 15-plugin run measured 84,650 ms `plugins.gateway-load`, 84,688 ms recovery scan, and about 84,759 ms maximum event-loop delay. A five-turn bounded post-ready CLI/Discord check succeeded, so this report focuses on startup.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)

### Operating system

Windows x64, 10.0.26100; Node.js 24.22.0; non-elevated process

### Install method

Project-local npm-locked OpenClaw package; official Codex and Discord plugins installed from ClawHub; local loopback Gateway

### Model

openai/gpt-6-astra (configured agent model; no model request is required to reproduce startup timeout)

### Provider / routing chain

Local OpenClaw Gateway → official Codex plugin / managed app-server → OpenAI. The observed startup stall occurs before an agent/model turn.

### Additional provider/model setup details

No additional details. No credentials or authentication profile information will be posted.

### Logs

```shell
Sanitized timeline excerpts / measurements:

- `plugins.gateway-load`: 89,068 ms in a configured 15-plugin start.
- Codex: module load 35,309 ms; registration 6 ms.
- Discord: module load 45,189 ms; registration 6,370 ms.
- `sidecars.main-session-recovery-scan`: `WorkerTaskError: worker task timed out` after about 89,094 ms.
- A timing-only probe queued the first recovery inventory worker request in 1 ms, but its task factory did not start until after an approximately 79-second plugin-loading stall. Once scheduled, inventory returned in about 2.2 seconds.
- Separate isolated run: `plugins.gateway-load` 84,650 ms; recovery scan 84,688 ms; event-loop maximum delay about 84,759 ms.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Node CPU profile of the isolated start, first 90 seconds (raw profile withheld locally because it contains private paths):

- `createPluginGenerationArtifact`: 70.9 s inclusive sampled time. Nested `captureDependencies` / `linkDependency`: 53.4 s; `copyPackage`: 55.2 s; `copySmallPluginSourceFile`: 38.3 s. These inclusive times overlap.
- Leaf `lstat`: 31.8 s; leaf `realpath`: 15.5 s. Stacks frequently pass through `withPluginSourceFile`, root-path admission, and package capture.
- `capturePluginNativeNamespace`: 0.18 s inclusive; `assertPluginNativeReferenceDirectory`: 0.08 s.

Related reports: #162514 (Windows source-capture / Discord bound-loader delay), #167466 (Windows startup filesystem activity in a different prepared-runtime path), and #167406 (Codex-enabled startup starvation on a different installation).

### Impact and severity

Observed on one Windows private Discord-bot installation. Repeated clean Gateway starts delayed bot availability by roughly 69–89 seconds and produced an internal recovery timeout. The Gateway reached ready afterward; no message loss was observed in the bounded post-ready check. This blocks treating restarts as reliable for unattended use.

### Additional information

Installed 2026.10.5 code starts recovery and plugin loading together in `startGatewayPostAttachRuntime`. Plugin candidate loading is synchronous in `loadOpenClawPlugins`, so the queued recovery worker can wait behind plugin work. The CPU sample locates most startup cost in dependency artifact capture/copy and repeated path checks. The exact safe fix is not established. Is there a supported cache or scheduling fix for this path?

A non-elevated file-symlink probe failed with “Administrator privilege required,” and a captured `codex.exe` is hardlinked, but native-reference validation was small in this CPU profile. A 2026.10.10 beta comparison did not load Codex or Discord, so it does not demonstrate a fix. No OS-wide setting, timeout, validation policy, or pinned package has been changed based on this diagnosis.

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows (managed-service install via `schtasks`), the gateway has three related reliability problems that together make restarts and updates fail very often ("pas na veel proberen" — only after many retries), and occasionally cause client-visible disconnects (`disconnected (1006): gateway websocket opening timed out after 15000ms`) right after a restart.

I initially suspected SQLite lock contention (similar to #100623 / #118719), but after digging into my own `~/.openclaw/logs/stability/*.json` and `~/.openclaw/logs/support/*.json` reports, I found three distinct, reproducible root causes instead. Filing them together since they all surface as "gateway won't restart/update cleanly" from a user's perspective, but a maintainer may want to split these into separate issues.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10/11 x64
- Node: 24.18.0 (bundled)
- Install: npm global, managed as a Windows service via `schtasks`
- OpenClaw version: 2026.9.8 (update failure below happened while updating from 2026.9.6, build `2026.9.6-release-eb377ac59e6c-2026-09-23T16-33-12.144Z`)

## Finding 1 — Startup can take minutes, with two phases dominating

From `logs/stability/openclaw-stability-2026-10-06T14-15-20-581Z-13908-gateway.stop_close_failed.json`, the diagnostic phase trace for a single gateway start shows:

```
plugins.runtime-post-bind        durationMs: 181604.6   (~181s / 3 min)
sidecars.control-ui-assets       durationMs: 265166.6   (~265s / 4.4 min)
gateway.ready                    durationMs: 189904.6   (~190s)
```

All other phases in the same trace complete in single-digit-to-low-hundreds of ms. These two phases are 2–3 orders of magnitude slower than everything else in the same startup. If this is typical on Windows, any external supervisor/health-check with a shorter timeout (or an impatient human retrying a restart) will conclude the gateway is stuck and kill/retry it before it ever finishes starting — which matches my real-world experience that restarts/updates often need several attempts before one "sticks."

## Finding 2 — Clean shutdown fails because 3 plugins don't release a resource within the 5s drain window

Same stability report, `reason: "gateway.stop_close_failed"`:

```
AggregateError: Gateway shutdown did not complete cleanly
  at runGatewayShutdownSteps (.../dist/server-shutdown-9EoJvj9Y.mjs:41:31)

Error: shutdown step failed (gateway close): Gateway resource cleanup failed
  | Plugin acpx cleanup failed (instance): Plugin acpx forced retirement after 5000ms: 1 still-running call(s), 0 retained consumer(s); resource cleanup remains pending.
  | Plugin duckduckgo cleanup failed (instance): Plugin duckduckgo forced retirement after 5000ms: 1 still-running call(s), 0 retained consumer(s); resource cleanup remains pending.
  | Plugin llama-cpp cleanup failed (instance): Plugin llama-cpp forced retirement after 5000ms: 1 still-running call(s), 0 retained consumer(s); resource cleanup remains pending.
```

Each of these three plugins (`acpx`, `duckduckgo`, `llama-cpp`) consistently has exactly **1 still-running call** that never finishes inside the 5000ms forced-retirement window, throwing `PluginInstanceDrainTimeoutError` and turning a routine restart/update into a hard shutdown failure.

## Finding 3 — Windows update fails with a permission error disabling the scheduled task

From `logs/support/openclaw-update-failure-425d8107_81c5_408d_b6a6_9672fb9192cc.json`:

```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "mode": "npm",
  "reason": "managed-service-stop-failed",
  "recovery": { "version": "2026.9.6", "service": "healthy" },
  "steps": [{
    "name": "managed-service-stop-failed",
    "exitCode": 1,
    "stderrTail": "Failed to stop managed gateway service before update: Error: schtasks disable failed: ERROR: Toegang geweigerd.",
    "failureFacts": [{
      "code": "managed-service-stop-failed",
      "message": "Failed to stop managed gateway service before update: Error: schtasks disable failed: ERROR: Toegang geweigerd."
    }]
  }]
}
```

`Toegang geweigerd` = "Access denied" (Dutch Windows). The updater shells out to `schtasks /change ... /disable` to stop the managed service before swapping files, and this fails outright with an access-denied error on this machine — blocking the whole update until a retry happens to succeed (possibly due to a race with the task scheduler, or privilege context differences between the calling process and the task).

## Why I'm filing this instead of just replacing SQLite

My first hypothesis was "SQLite is the bottleneck," since I keep seeing `SQLITE_BUSY`-style symptoms and the architecture issues above often coincide with a stuck restart. But the memory/worker telemetry in the same stability report shows SQLite access is already offloaded to dedicated worker threads (`sqlite-store.worker.js`, `openclaw-state-read.worker.js`, `session-accessor.sqlite-archive.worker.js`, etc.), not a single blocking call on the main thread. So the three findings above look like the more likely, more fixable causes of "gateway restarts/updates are unreliable on Windows" than the database engine itself.

## Impact

- Restarts/updates routinely need multiple attempts before succeeding.
- Occasional client-visible disconnects right after a restart: `disconnected (1006): gateway websocket opening timed out after 15000ms` — consistent with the gateway still being mid-startup (finding 1) or hung in a failed shutdown (finding 2) when a client tries to reconnect.
- `openclaw doctor` (with and without `--fix`) does not resolve any of this, which makes sense since none of these three issues are SQLite data/schema problems.

## Suggested next steps

1. Investigate why `plugins.runtime-post-bind` and `sidecars.control-ui-assets` can take minutes on Windows (possibly disk I/O, AV scanning, or a blocking network call during plugin/asset init).
2. Identify what the single "still-running call" is in `acpx`, `duckduckgo`, and `llama-cpp` during shutdown, and either let it cancel faster or extend/communicate the drain timeout.
3. Harden or fall back the `schtasks disable` step in the Windows managed-service updater so a transient/permission failure doesn't abort the whole update, and consider running it elevated or with a retry+backoff.

Happy to pull more raw stability/support JSON reports from `~/.openclaw/logs/` if that helps triage — I have several more of each from the last two weeks.

> Agent-written on behalf of @Oldrich333 · agent: hive-admin/executor · model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 · origin: agent-initiated

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

First start after any version change: agents deferred past the 5 s foreground admission budget prepare serially in background (~15–25 s each), and the unconfigured on-disk system-agent DB (`agents/openclaw`) fails that background preparation with a false "database configuration changed during startup inspection" → permanent `agent-database-inspection-failed` → `/readyz` 503 until the next restart.

### Steps to reproduce

1. State dir with ≥ 10 configured agents whose `openclaw-agent.sqlite` files total several GB, plus a leftover `agents/openclaw/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` (created by the system-agent path; `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId = "main"`, so `openclaw` is not in configured targets).
2. Clean stop on 2026.9.7, start 2026.9.8 (any VERSION change; same on the way back 9.8 → 9.7).
3. Watch `/startupz`, `/readyz` and the journal.

### Expected behavior

- Clean-close proof from the previous version either accepted or re-proved without serializing every agent behind the 5 s budget.
- A discovered but unconfigured agent DB either prepared like in the foreground path or skipped — never a refusal that only a restart clears.

### Actual behavior

- `canReuseOpenClawAgentIntegrityVerification` (src/state/openclaw-quarantine-store.ts) requires `record.app_version === VERSION`; the clean-close receipt only marks rows of the running VERSION → every agent DB `integrityGateReason=no-proof` after a version change → full integrity pass.
- foreground admission 7.2–7.6 s > `AGENT_DATABASE_STARTUP_WAIT_MS` 5 s (src/state/openclaw-database-preflight-agent-scheduler.ts, constant) → all 11 agents deferred.
- deferred preparation runs one agent at a time (`this.preparation` chain, src/state/agent-database-startup.ts) → `/startupz` `starting` (pendingReason `agent-database-inspection`) for 170–280 s after `[gateway] ready`; sessions of not-yet-admitted agents unavailable meanwhile.
- `agents/openclaw`: `activateGatewayAgentDatabaseStartup.prepareAgent` (src/gateway/server-agent-database-startup.ts) finds no configured target for it and throws `Agent openclaw database configuration changed during startup inspection` → `failPendingAgentDatabase` → `/readyz` 503 `failing: ["agent-database:openclaw"]`. Config did not change. Restart (proofs now valid, foreground 2.2 s, nothing deferred) → `/readyz` 200.
- Same state, same-version restart: foreground 2–4.8 s, nothing deferred, ready in ~60 s.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.7 (main 18b2c19b) ↔ 2026.9.8 (main 7bec812c)

### Operating system

Debian 12, systemd units, Node 24

### Install method

source checkout (pnpm build), one gateway per state dir

### Model

n/a (startup path, before any model call)

### Provider / routing chain

n/a

### Logs

```text
[gateway] startup phase: cli.bootstrap.admission.database-readiness 7595.7ms ... agentCount=11 schemaProcessCount=2 schemaInspectionCount=6
[state/agent-admission] Agent executor has not completed startup inspection and preparation. The 5 second foreground startup budget elapsed; inspection continues.
[gateway] ready
[state/agent-admission] agent database remains degraded agentId=openclaw ... reason="Agent openclaw database configuration changed during startup inspection"
[state/agent-db] slow OpenClaw agent database open agentId=executor elapsedMs=3361 ... integrityGateReason=no-proof integrityGateMode=tables integrityGateOutcome=healthy
[state/agent-admission] agent database recovered after background inspection and preparation   (one line per agent, 13–20 s apart)
```

### Impact and severity

- every version change: affected gateway's agents unavailable for minutes after `[gateway] ready`; health checks waiting for `/startupz` `started` time out.
- `/readyz` 503 after a successful start until a manual restart (orchestrators/health monitors treat the gateway as down).
- related, different contract: #152939 (readiness vs agent admission).

### Additional information

Measured on copies of the same state: repeatable (startup 48 s, admission 280 s, `agent-database:openclaw` refusal, restart → ready 49 s, readyz 200).

```text
OpenClaw requires working inference: The verified inference owner changed before validation completed. Retry the inference check.
```

Normal Gateway operation and the configured model route are healthy. This blocks managed configuration writes and managed Gateway restart.

- Primary: `openai/gpt-5.6-terra@openai:pavlov.mm@gmail.com`

issues.body:
## Problem

`memory.search.extraPaths` files are ranked with filesystem-mtime temporal decay. Stable matter, project, and runbook references therefore lose relevance simply because they have not been edited recently, while canonical undated memory remains evergreen.

## Proposed solution

Allow object-form `extraPaths` entries to opt matching files out of mtime decay:

```json5
{ path: "runbooks", pattern: "**/*.md", evergreen: true }
```

The policy should affect ranking only. It must not change source admission, provenance, trust, automatic-injection eligibility, or force reindexing. Canonical dated daily notes must continue to decay by their embedded date.

## Evidence

- A controlled memory benchmark showed mtime decay pushing stable reference files below fresher distractors.
- A six-case source/matter/time holdout across 45–365 day file ages reproduced the issue and passed with the proposed policy.
- The implementation has focused coverage for schema validation, path normalization, glob matching, duplicate policy, keyword/hybrid ranking, and canonical daily-note behavior.

issues.body:
### Summary

The gateway's own WAL auto-checkpoint on `state/openclaw.sqlite` is reported as blocked on every attempt since boot, and has **never completed**:

```
openclaw-state WAL checkpoint PASSIVE blocked by a reader
  state=blocked  checkpointedFrames=866  logFrames=17091
  consecutiveBlocked=14  lastCompletedAtMs=null  never_completed=true
```

The WAL therefore keeps growing (unbackfilled 41.5 MB at 15:33 → 65.7 MB at 19:09) instead of being checkpointed.

### Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.9.7 (c074824)**
- Windows 10.0.26200 (x64), Node v24.18.0
- State DB `state/openclaw.sqlite` ≈ 405 MB, `-wal` 47–73 MB

### What was ruled out

A Sysinternals **handle.exe** scan of all processes for `openclaw.sqlite`:

```
node.exe  pid: 33900  .sqlite  x7
node.exe  pid: 33900  -wal     x7
node.exe  pid: 33900  -shm     x1
```

**No other process holds any handle on the DB** — every handle belongs to the gateway process itself. This is not an external contender; the pin is **in-process**.

The gateway's own telemetry cannot name the holder either:

```json
"candidate_connection": {
  "connectionId": 2, "operation": "sqlite connection", "ownerKind": "worker",
  "threadId": 2, "ageMs": ~25200000, "transactionOpen": false,
  "trackedReaders": 0, "blockingOwner": "unknown",
  "readerCount": 0, "scope": "current-thread", "nativeStatements": "unobserved"
}
```

Note the internal inconsistency: it reports "blocked by a reader" while also reporting `readerCount: 0` and `blockingOwner: unknown`.

### Reproduction pattern

1. Maintenance stops the gateway, checkpoints cleanly, restarts:
   `[checkpoint] PASS | [('openclaw-agent.sqlite',(0,0,0)), ('openclaw.sqlite',(0,0,0))]` (12:00:01)
2. After restart (~12:03) the block immediately re-forms and **never** clears for the rest of the uptime (observed 12:03 → 19:05, 71 blocked records, `never_completed=true`).
3. Only another full gateway restart clears it.

### Correlated (NOT proven) impact

- `Agent run failed: the Gateway state database was busy (SQLite: database is locked)`
- repeated `cron: isolated agent setup timed out before runner start`

Same DB, same subsystem. Timing supports a link; no controlled reproduction was done, so causation is **unproven**.

### Suggested directions (guesses)

- Likely a long-lived connection or unclosed read snapshot inside the worker pool (threadId=2, `ownerKind=worker`) — a single un-reset statement pins the WAL.
- `blockingOwner=unknown` + `readerCount=0` + "blocked by a reader" suggests the reader-tracking path does not cover all connection kinds.

---
*Reported from a self-hosted single-user deployment. Paths sanitized.*

## Bug: turn claim still not released after lane timeout on 2026.9.5 — different trigger path than #137043, session permanently wedged for 90+ minutes

### Summary

On OpenClaw **2026.9.5** (ec9c1a1), a session's turn claim is not released after an internal lane task times out, leaving the session permanently wedged with **zero log output** until a full gateway restart. This reproduces the exact failure chain already described in #137043 (closed 2026-09-03 as "already implemented in main, fix not yet in a tagged release") and in a regression comment left on that same closed issue on 2026-09-17 (still reproducing on 2026.9.1). We're now seeing it on 2026.9.5, two separate occurrences on the same session in one day.

Opening a fresh issue rather than commenting further on #137043 since it's closed and the 2026-09-17 regression comment there never got a reply.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)
- Deployment: self-hosted, Docker, single-host, Telegram channel
- Model: local llama.cpp (OpenAI-completions transport)
- Session: `agent:clara:main` (direct, long-lived, never rotated)

### Reproduction (two occurrences, same day, same session)

**Occurrence 1 (2026-09-23, 15:26–15:33 local)** — self-recovered, but still hit the failure chain:

```
15:26:23  reset (new session)
15:26:28  user message received, embedded run starts
15:28:43  [diagnostic] stuck session: state=processing age=135s
          lastProgress=global_lane:wait_ended lastProgressAge=135s recovery=checking
15:28:43  recovery outcome: status=skipped action=keep_lane reason=active_reply_work
15:31:17  stuck session: age=289s (same session, recovery still skipped)
15:32:50  stuck session recovery reclaiming stale active reply work
15:33:05  stuck recovery: reply owner settlement timed out settleMs=15000
15:33:05  stuck session recovery: action=abort_embedded_run aborted=false drained=false released=1
15:33:21  lane task error: lane=session:agent:clara:main durationMs=413133
          error="Command lane \"session:agent:clara:main\" task timed out: abort grace 30815ms elapsed (task budget 14430000ms, elapsed 413133ms)" errorName=CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError
15:33:21  lane task error: lane=main durationMs=413178 errorName=CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError
```

Delivered to the user: `⚠️ This turn was interrupted because it stopped making progress. Please try again.` (traced to `dispatch-from-config-*.mjs`, emitted when `operation.result.code === "run_stalled"` and `staleExpiryReason` is `no_activity` or `stuck_recovery`).

**Occurrence 2 (2026-09-23, ~16:47–16:54 local)** — same session, did **not** self-recover:

```
16:49:56  stuck session: state=processing age=138s lastProgress=global_lane:wait_ended
          recovery=checking (same shape as occurrence 1)
16:54:18  stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted action=abort_embedded_run
          aborted=false drained=false forceCleared=true released=1
16:54:33  lane task error: lane=session:agent:clara:main durationMs=416599
          error="Command lane \"session:agent:clara:main\" task timed out: abort grace 30854ms elapsed (task budget 14430000ms, elapsed 416599ms)" errorName=CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError
16:54:33  lane task error: lane=main durationMs=416616 errorName=CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError
--- zero log output for 90+ minutes ---
```

Gateway process stayed alive (confirmed via `docker exec ... ps aux`, main process + workers still running, non-zero CPU), but produced no further log lines at all — not even the periodic `liveness heartbeat delayed` diagnostics normally seen every ~30s. `openclaw sessions list` continued to show the session with a stale `aborted` flag. Nothing reached the user or the session store until the gateway container was restarted manually.

Session context size was **not** a factor here (checked via `openclaw sessions list`: `0/95k (0%)` tokens on this session immediately after the wedge, right after a fresh reset) — this is a distinct trigger path from the compaction-related stalls (`#138599` et al.), consistent with the "any lane timeout can cause it" framing already noted in #137043 and with the 2026-09-17 regression comment there (nested cron lane / `skill-workshop-review` lane, no compaction involved either).

### Relationship to #137043

#137043 was closed 2026-09-03 with:

> Current main now force-settles the exact worker-placement claim when a stuck embedded run is cleared [...] The repair is main-only and has not reached a tagged release.

A 2026-09-17 comment on that same closed issue reported the identical failure chain still reproducing on a tagged release (2026.9.1), via a nested cron lane rather than the original model-fetch/skill-workshop-review triggers, and identified that the claim-release functions (`releaseTurn`, `failWorkspaceResultAndReleaseTurn`, `cancelWorkspaceResultAndReleaseTurn`) don't cover the timeout path specifically. That comment never received a follow-up.

We're now confirming the same thing again on 2026.9.5, two versions later, via yet another trigger (`global_lane:wait_ended` on the main session lane, no cron/skill-workshop involved). This suggests the 2026-09-03 fix addressed one specific code path (worker-placement claim settlement) but the general problem — a lane-timeout failure path that never calls any of the claim-release functions — is still open.

### Impact

- Session permanently wedged, zero log output, until a full gateway restart — no visibility into what's actually stuck.
- Happens via multiple, seemingly unrelated trigger paths (model fetch, skill-workshop-review, nested cron, and now plain `global_lane` wait on the main session with an empty context) — consistent with #137043's own framing that this is a general lane-timeout problem, not specific to one trigger.
- No workaround available from the deployment side beyond detecting the wedge externally (log silence after a `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError`) and restarting the gateway.

### Suggested fix direction

Same as identified in the 2026-09-17 comment on #137043: the lane-timeout failure path (`CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` → `settleFailure`) should release the admitted turn claim the same way the normal/forced/cancelled paths already do, rather than only being covered by the specific worker-placement settlement fixed in #137043.

Happy to provide the full `openclaw` container logs for both occurrences if useful.

issues.title: [Feature]: Exclude fenced dreaming ranges from memory-search indexing and recall signal

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: impact:session-state

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦞 diamond lobster
labels.description: Very strong issue quality with high-confidence source-level or clear reproduction.

issues.body:
### Summary

Dreaming Light/REM output is written under `memory/`, so it is embedded, retrieved by `memory_search` and staged into short-term recall — where it keeps accruing `recallCount` / `uniqueQueries` — even though the existing dreaming fence already guarantees it can never be promoted. Please apply the fence check earlier (indexing / staging / recall signal), not only at rehydration.

### Problem to solve

The promotion guards work correctly and nothing wrong has ever been promoted on our instance (`promotedCount: 0` throughout). This is **not a security issue and not a promotion-safety bug**. The problem is retrieval and recall-signal pollution, plus indexing/embedding work spent on content that is promotion-dead by construction.

Verified on OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8), single-user container, embedding provider `qwen3-embedding-4b`, `dreaming.storage.mode: inline`:

1. **Dreaming output is indexed.** `memory_index_sources` (`source='memory'`) contains the daily notes holding the fenced blocks (`memory/2026-10-13.md`, `memory/2026-10-14.md`).
2. **`storage.mode: "separate"` does not help.** On a second agent that previously used `separate`, the phase reports are themselves indexed: `memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-09.md` and `memory/dreaming/rem/2026-10-09..12.md` all appear in `memory_index_sources`.
3. **Fenced ranges are correctly excluded from promotion.** `rehydratePromotionCandidate()` calls `lineRangeOverlapsDreamingFence()` and skips any candidate whose line range overlaps `<!-- openclaw:dreaming:*:start/end -->`. We confirmed both top candidates fall inside fences, and nothing has been promoted.
4. **Recall signal still counts them.** Two dreaming blocks went from `rc/uq 3/3` to `6/6` and then to `7/7` — observed values during this audit — purely as a side effect of `memory_search` calls made while investigating.
5. **They therefore clear the numeric promotion gates.** With `minRecallCount=3 minUniqueQueries=3 minScore=0.75`, a read-only promote preview returned exactly two candidates, both fenced dreaming blocks, and they were the two highest-ranked entries in the store:

   | candidate | score | rc/uq | outcome |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `memory/2026-10-14.md` L1-11 (REM) | 0.793 | 7/7 | passes gates → dropped at rehydration (fence) |
   | `memory/2026-10-13.md` L63-95 (Light) | 0.754 | 6/6 | passes gates → dropped at rehydration (fence) |

   Genuine memory ranked below both (best non-dreaming entry: 0.668).
6. **Ranking, staging and recall signal are distorted even without a wrong promotion.** Fenced blocks win `memory_search` (a REM block was the top hit at 0.808 raw for several queries), occupy the head of the promotion ranking, and consume the `--limit` window, pushing real candidates out of the preview/apply window.
7. **Pruning a daily note does not prune the dreaming copies.** After we removed a line from `memory/2026-10-07.md`, the same text remained fully retrievable from the Light/REM blocks in `memory/2026-10-13.md` and `memory/2026-10-14.md`; removing it required editing dreaming-managed blocks by hand.
8. **The bundled `session-memory` hook has the same shape of problem.** It writes `<workspace>/memory/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md` with a hardcoded path and a header that always records session identity:

   ```
   # Session: 2026-10-08 11:29:59 Europe/Rome

   - **Session Key**: <session-key>
   - **Session ID**: <session-id>
   - **Source**: telegram
   ```

   That file was 180 bytes of pure session plumbing with no conversation content, and it was recorded as `originClass: agent`, so the provenance origin filter did not exclude it from promotion. A second artifact (rollover of a cron session) held the scheduled-job prompt plus its deliverable and reached the highest raw score in the store (0.874) while winning `memory_search` for unrelated queries.
9. **There is no `memory.search` path exclusion.** The documented keys are `enabled`, `extraPaths`, `fallback`, `provider`, `model`, `query`, `remote`, `sources`, `rememberAcrossConversations`, `store`, `citations`, `cache` — `extraPaths` only adds. Meanwhile `memory/.dreams/**` is already excluded from the index by an internal rule (6 corpus files on disk, 0 rows in `memory_index_sources` for both agents), so an exclusion mechanism exists but is neither configurable nor applied to dreaming output.

### Proposed solution

Apply the existing fence check earlier than rehydration: exclude fenced dreaming ranges at **indexing, staging and recall-signal** time, so they never become recall candidates and never accrue `recallCount` / `uniqueQueries`.

The fence parser already exists (`DREAMING_FENCE_START_RE` / `DREAMING_FENCE_END_RE` in `short-term-promotion`); today it is only consulted in `rehydratePromotionCandidate()`. Moving the same check upstream of staging would keep the current promotion behaviour identical while removing the ranking, staging and embedding costs.

### Alternatives considered

- Exclude `memory/dreaming/**` and/or fenced ranges from the retrieval corpus, the way `memory/.dreams/**` already is. Weaker: does not help inline mode, where the fence lives inside a daily note that also holds real memory.
- Add a configurable path-exclude to `memory.search` (today `extraPaths` only adds). Overlaps with #101422; useful but does not fix the inline case either.
- For `session-memory`: make the output directory configurable, or default it to a dot-directory (e.g. `memory/.session-memory/`) that the index already skips.
- For `session-memory`: make the session-identity header optional, and/or tag hook-written artifacts with `originClass: system` so the existing origin filter excludes them from promotion by default.
- `dreaming.storage.mode: "separate"` — does not solve it, see fact 2.

### Impact

- Affected: any installation with dreaming enabled and `memory/` as the memory root (default).
- Severity: medium — degraded retrieval quality and wasted embedding work; no data loss and no incorrect promotion observed.
- Frequency: every dreaming sweep and every `memory_search` that hits a fenced block.
- Consequence: dreaming echoes outrank durable memory in `memory_search`; unreachable candidates occupy the head of the promotion ranking and the `--limit` budget; chunks that can never be promoted still cost indexing and embedding on each sweep; content deleted from a daily note survives in the dreaming copies.

### Evidence/examples

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8), container, `qwen3-embedding-4b`, `dreaming.storage.mode: inline`.

Reproduction:

1. `dreaming.storage.mode: inline`; let dreaming write its Light/REM blocks into `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`.
2. Run a few `openclaw memory search --agent <id> --query "<phrase from inside a fenced block>"`.
3. `openclaw memory promote --agent <id> --min-recall-count 3 --min-unique-queries 3 --min-score 0.75 --json` → the fenced block is listed as a top candidate.
4. `openclaw memory status --agent <id> --json` → `audit.promotedCount` stays `0`.

Index evidence (`memory_index_sources`, `source='memory'`):

```
main      memory/2026-10-07.md  memory/2026-10-12.md  memory/2026-10-13.md  memory/2026-10-14.md
sentinel  memory/2026-10-12..14.md  memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-09.md  memory/dreaming/rem/2026-10-09..12.md
          (rows matching '%.dreams%': 0 on both agents)
```

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

- **Not a security issue and not a promotion-safety bug.** Both promotion guards (dreaming fence at rehydration, provenance origin filter for `untrusted`/`system`) behaved correctly in every observation; no incorrect entry was ever promoted. The request is to keep non-promotable material out of the retrieval/recall layer.
- Related issues found while searching open issues: #101422 (configurable recall-eligibility and index-exclusion paths — closest overlap with the alternatives above), #147433 (per-source balance between `memory` and `sessions`), #112349 (opposite symptom: gates not enforced), #136097 (admission exclusions for transcript indexing).
- Real session identifiers in the `session-memory` example above are scrubbed.

issues.body:
## Summary
Two OpenClaw defects affect a native approval-gated CLI turn. The first loses the history admission needed to complete an approved command. The second sends a synthetic native-auth marker through the HTTP Anthropic transport.

## Defect 1: approved exec returns `auth-unknown`

Environment: OpenClaw `2026.10.10-beta.1`, Claude CLI, native approval in a direct message.

Reproduction: issue one harmless command requiring native approval, choose Allow Once, and observe `approval-request-failed`; the command does not execute.

Observed evidence: `auth-unknown` at `14:09:16.471 PDT`, followed by a normal resumed CLI turn (`trigger=user useResume=true session=present reuse=reusable`). In `src/agents/cli-runner/history-boundary.ts:134-146`, `prepareCliHistoryBoundaryOnce` returns no writer when the session target, session id/key, or admitted-run assertion does not match. `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts:1463-1473` maps the missing writer to `auth-unknown`.

Expected: the approved continuation preserves the admitted session target and history boundary and executes exactly once.

## Defect 2: synthetic native auth is sent as `x-api-key`

After the healthy native CLI auth check, `extensions/anthropic/provider-discovery.js:177-203` returns `CLAUDE_CLI_NATIVE_AUTH_MARKER`; its catalog path at `:205-257` publishes the `claude-cli` backend with `api=anthropic-messages`. `provider-request-config-DSpBEbyp.mjs:255-262` applies the marker as the configured auth header, and `ai-transport-host-CcZkAnMD.mjs:393-447` sends the request. The service returns `401 invalid x-api-key` at `13:39:36.143 PDT`, `13:42:04.406 PDT`, and `14:09:29.421 PDT`.

These defects share runtime context but have different causes. The first is a history-boundary admission failure. The second misroutes native authentication into an HTTP API-key header. No supported configuration-only fix is known, and disabling the Anthropic plugin removes the Claude CLI provider.

## Requested fix

1. Preserve the matching session target, session id/key, and admitted-run assertion across an approved continuation. Add a regression test for a normal resumed approval.
2. Keep native CLI authentication on the CLI backend. Do not pass the synthetic native-auth marker to an HTTP provider as `x-api-key`. Add a regression test for model discovery and transport selection.
3. Document the supported behavior and failure diagnostics.

No credentials, customer data, user identifiers, Slack IDs, local paths, or host-specific details are included.

prs.title: feat(providers): add Bifrost provider and allow anonymous self-hosted gateways
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

[Bifrost](https://getbifrost.ai) is an OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway that unifies 20+ providers with failover, load balancing, and virtual-key governance. OpenClaw ships bundled providers for LiteLLM, SGLang, and vLLM, but not Bifrost — so operators had to configure it by hand in `models.providers`.

## What This Changes

**New bundled provider** (`extensions/bifrost`), built on the LiteLLM provider shape:

- Interactive setup asks for the gateway base URL, then whether a virtual key is needed, then lists the models the gateway advertises via `/openai/v1/models` and defaults to the first.
- Discovery failures name the reason (`HTTP 404`, `empty model list`, `unreachable`) before falling back to manual entry, and a config change during discovery aborts before credentials are sent to a stale endpoint.
- Non-interactive setup accepts `--custom-base-url`.

**Provider artwork**, which every other user-facing bundled provider ships and Bifrost initially did not:

- `extensions/bifrost/assets/icon.png` — 512×512, the official Apache-2.0 mark inverted to dark-on-white so it matches the other bundled provider icons, which are all light-background (verified: LiteLLM, SGLang, vLLM and OpenRouter icons are 0% transparent with a dominant white background). Geometry unchanged.
- `extensions/bifrost/assets/activity.svg` and `ui/public/provider-icons/ProviderIcon-bifrost.svg` — OpenClaw-authored gateway glyph (many upstreams converging on one routed endpoint), `currentColor` so it renders on light and dark. Neither Simple Icons nor LobeHub ships a Bifrost glyph, so these are drawn in-repo and labelled in-file as *not* a Bifrost trademark, matching the precedent where SGLang's activity icon is an unbranded server box.
- Registering `bifrost` in `PROVIDER_ICON_NAMES` also fixes a visible defect: `resolveProviderIconName("bifrost")` returned `null`, so the model picker was rendering a **letter "B"** avatar for this provider.

Provenance is pinned to upstream commit `a30e57dd` in `ATTRIBUTION.md`, following the format of the existing third-party entries.

**Two design decisions worth review:**

1. **Base URL is `http://localhost:8080/openai`**, Bifrost's OpenAI-compatible surface, not the core `/v1` API. Both serve chat completions, but only the `/openai` surface makes discovery and inference share one base URL. Bifrost's own OpenAI SDK and OpenCode guides use this path.

2. **Keyless gateways use `auth: "none"`.** A fresh Bifrost has no authentication — that's the documented zero-config default — so setup records the provider as explicitly anonymous rather than storing a key that resolves to nothing. This reuses the existing explicit-no-auth owner (`resolveExplicitProviderNoAuth`) instead of adding a second mechanism. Re-running setup for a URL change keeps an already-configured key.

**Shared-helper change:** `promptAndConfigureOpenAICompatibleSelfHostedProviderAuth` forced a non-empty API key, which pushed SGLang and vLLM users toward a placeholder value for servers that accept anonymous requests. It now accepts an empty key and records `auth: "none"`, matching what the config schema already models. The Bifrost provider does not use that helper — it uses the LiteLLM path, which already prompted for a URL and a key.

**Config-surface budget, raised deliberately:** the Bifrost plugin schema grows the plugin config surface from 4693 to 4714 keys (+21), which trips the `config-docs` baseline ratchet. I regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` and raised the budget in `config-baseline.counts.json` rather than leaving it failing. The +21 is the provider's own declared schema — a base URL, an optional virtual-key auth profile, and the provider's setup metadata — not a new core config surface. Core stays at 2565 and channel at 4043, both unchanged. If a maintainer would rather the provider ship without declaring those keys, say so and I will trim the schema rather than hold the budget increase.

## Evidence

Verified against a running Bifrost gateway at `http://bifrost` (port 80), with isolated state via `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

**Discovery through the production code path** (`discoverOpenAICompatibleLocalModels`, the real function the plugin calls):

```
base url passed to discovery: http://bifrost/openai/v1
discovery kind: success | rows: 12
first row: {"id":"Nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b","object":"model","owned_by":"nvidia","created":735790403}
rows reporting context_window: 6/12
```

**End-to-end agent turn** through the shipped CLI, provider configured with `auth: "none"`:

```
winnerProvider: "bifrost"
winnerModel: "Vercel/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free"
result: "success",  fallbackUsed: false,  runner: "embedded"
finalAssistantMessageRawText: "LOCAL_BIFROST_OK"
```

`openclaw models list --provider bifrost --refresh --json` returns the nested-slash key `bifrost/Vercel/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free` with `available: true`.

### Two findings the live gateway surfaced that mocks did not

**1. Model IDs are multi-segment.** Bifrost returns IDs like `Nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b` and `Vercel/alibaba/qwen3.7-flash`, so refs become `bifrost/<vendor>/<provider>/<model>`. Verified this round-trips exactly: `parseProviderModelRef` splits on the **first** slash (`packages/model-catalog-core/src/model-catalog-refs.ts:54`), and `normalizeAgentModelRefForConfig("bifrost/Nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b")` returns the input unchanged. The committed tests cover the single-slash case, so I noted this rather than claiming the nested case is regression-guarded.

**2. The gateway echoes a different model string than requested.** Requesting `Vercel/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free` returns `"model": "poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free"` — the `Vercel/` prefix is a routing selector the gateway drops when reporting the resolved upstream model. OpenClaw surfaces this as `modelRouteChange: "Model route changed: bifrost/Vercel/… → bifrost/poolside/…"`. **This is expected behavior, not a defect**: `agent-run-terminal-receipt.ts:66` reports `effective.responseModel || effective.model`, so it is faithfully relaying the gateway's echo. Worth documenting so operators don't read the notice as a misroute.

### Parity control

The `--refresh` path prints `Model discovery could not refresh all providers`. I checked whether Bifrost caused it by pointing the **proven LiteLLM provider** at the same gateway: identical warning, identical single-authored-model result. It's pre-existing behavior in an isolated state where credential-less bundled providers can't refresh, not a Bifrost defect.

### Live authority-chain proof on an enforcing gateway

The earlier anonymous proof ran against a keyless gateway, which cannot demonstrate the authentication defects. I repeated it against the same Bifrost deployment after enabling **Enforce Virtual Keys on Inference**, so it now rejects unauthenticated inference with `401 virtual_key_required`. That makes the defect observable rather than merely arguable.

Non-interactive onboarding with the key supplied **only through `BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY`** — no `--bifrost-api-key`, no inline `apiKey` — which is precisely the case the old `hasKey` check missed:

```jsonc
// config written by onboarding
"models": { "providers": { "bifrost": {
  "baseUrl": "http://bifrost/openai",
  "api": "openai-completions",
  "models": []            // non-interactive preset: discovery-backed
} } },
"auth": { "profiles": { "bifrost:default": { "provider": "bifrost", "mode": "api_key" } } }
```

No `auth` field is written, and the credential lands in the profile. Agent turn through the shipped CLI:

```
winnerProvider: "bifrost"
winnerModel: "Vercel/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free"
result: "success"        fallbackUsed: false      runner: "embedded"
authMode: "auth-profile"
finalAssistantMessageRawText: "KEYED_OK"
```

`authMode: "auth-profile"` is the load-bearing line: it shows the credential was resolved and sent, not silently stripped.

Now inject `auth: "none"` into that same row — which is exactly what the pre-fix code wrote — and re-run:

```jsonc
"bifrost": { "baseUrl": "http://bifrost/openai", "api": "openai-completions", "auth": "none" }
```

```
virtual key is required. Provide a virtual key via the x-bf-vk header.   (x8)
401
no winnerProvider, no fallbackUsed
```

Remove the field again and the same turn returns `RECOVERED_OK` with `authMode: "auth-profile"`. So the single `auth` field is the whole difference between a working and a failing credential: **live failure with the marker, live success without it.** This is the authority-chain evidence the review asked for, and it only became obtainable once the gateway stopped accepting anonymous requests.

The third instance has the same live shape. Starting from a row carrying `auth: "none"` alongside an active
`bifrost:default` profile, re-authenticating with the key and **no** `--custom-base-url` clears the marker and the turn
succeeds:

```
before:  models.providers.bifrost.auth = "none"   (profile bifrost:default present)
action:  onboard --non-interactive --auth-choice bifrost-api-key      (no --custom-base-url)
after:   auth = <unset>
turn:    winnerProvider: "bifrost"   authMode: "auth-profile"   fallbackUsed: false
         finalAssistantMessageRawText: "REAUTH_OK"
```

### Authentication defects found in review, and their regression proof

ClawSweeper's review found that Bifrost onboarding could discard a supplied credential. I confirmed both against source before changing anything, and traced the runtime consequence to `resolveExplicitProviderNoAuth`, which is terminal on `auth: "none"` and strips the `Authorization` header via `applyLocalNoAuthHeaders`.

1. **`applyBifrostConnection` merged `...existing` and only ever *added* the marker.** Re-running interactive setup against a gateway that now has a virtual key inherited `auth: "none"` through the merge and through `applyBifrostModelConfig` (`applyProviderConfigWithMergedModels` spreads `existingProviderRest`). The keyed branch now clears the marker, which is how the `omlx` and `llama-cpp` gateway providers already drop anonymous state once a credential exists.
2. **`runNonInteractive` inferred anonymity from `--bifrost-api-key` and the inline provider `apiKey` only**, while the delegated method also resolves `BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY` and existing profiles. A key in either of those made the wrapper write `auth: "none"`, which the delegate then preserved while saving the key it had just resolved. The ad-hoc check is removed: the delegated method owns the decision and returns `null` when no credential resolves, so this path always applies one.
3. **`runNonInteractive` still skipped the fix when `--custom-base-url` was absent.** My own refactor added an early return that handed the delegate the original config, so `applyBifrostConnection` never ran and an earlier `auth: "none"` survived — the delegate saved the key, the preset spread `existingProviderRest` through, and the marker stayed terminal. Caught in the Revision 2 re-review. This path always applies a credential, so a gateway already on file counts as configured: the base URL now resolves from the flag *or* the existing row, and either way the credentialed update runs.

Base-fail/head-pass evidence — both new tests fail against `4d2478c4a6` and pass against `838b5e17cc`:

```
pre-fix  (4d2478c4a6):  Tests  2 failed | 16 passed (18)
post-fix (838b5e17cc):  Tests  18 passed (18)

pre-fix failures:
  × clears a previous anonymous marker once the operator supplies a virtual key
  × stays credentialed when the key resolves from a profile rather than a flag
```

`resolveExplicitProviderNoAuth` is core-internal with no Plugin SDK subpath, so the tests assert its precondition — that `auth` is not `"none"` whenever a credential is available — rather than importing across the extension boundary.

### Gates on this head

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, and the `tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json` lane — pass
- `oxlint` on all changed files — clean
- `oxfmt --check` — clean; `format-docs --check` clean (1365 files)
- `docs:check-links` — 15646 links, 0 broken; `docs:check-config-examples` — pass
- `generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check` — pass after the budget raise above
- `pnpm plugins:inventory:gen` — no diff (artwork is not part of the generated inventory)
- Tests: **106 across the 9 Bifrost/SGLang/vLLM/shared-setup test files** (Bifrost 19 on this head), 561 package-manifest + extension-runtime-dependency contracts, 65 boundary invariants, 126 manifest-registry + bundled-manifest contracts, 31 provider-icon/public-asset — all pass

### Known Gaps

- **The UI browser-test project could not run locally.** Its Playwright Chromium binary is absent from this machine's cache (`chrome-headless-shell` not installed), so that project reports `no tests` with a launch error. This is environmental and unrelated to the change; every other project in the same run passed (3217 UI tests + 166 + 65). Worth a CI confirmation rather than trusting the local run for that project.

- **Full `pnpm lint` fails on three inherited `max-lines` violations** in files this branch does not touch: `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-warm-image-store.ts` (718/700), `extensions/oc-path/src/cli.test.ts` (1125/1000), `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts` (1028/1000). None are in `config/max-lines-baseline.txt`. Every file changed here lints clean.
- **Discovery contributed no additional models under `--refresh`.** The live catalog/discovery refresh path did not merge the gateway's 12 models into the model list; only the authored model appeared. LiteLLM against the same gateway behaves identically, so this is existing merge-mode semantics rather than something introduced here. The onboarding path *does* call discovery directly and receives all 12. This is the `models.mode=replace` half of #121584 ("Auto-discover all models when configuring a provider"): this PR delivers the interactive-configuration half, and does not attempt to close that issue — it carries `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` and `needs-product-decision`, so the refresh-merge semantics are a product decision, not a side effect of adding a provider.
- **Related pre-existing bug, not fixed here, and no issue tracks it:** the same helper still passes `initialValue: params.defaultBaseUrl` for its base-URL prompt, so a typed URL appends to the prefilled default under the shipped wizard. This is the defect #173164 fixed for LiteLLM, still live for SGLang and vLLM. Fixing it changes their behavior, so it is left as a follow-up rather than bundled here. I can file it as a separate issue if that is wanted.
- Interactive onboarding was not driven interactively over a pty; the base-URL and model prompts are covered by tests through the registered plugin.
- **Proof the review asked for that this head still does not carry.** I want to be explicit rather than let the checklist imply otherwise:
  - ~~*Authenticated onboarding against a real gateway.*~~ **Now closed** — see the authority-chain proof above: the credential reaches the gateway (`authMode: "auth-profile"`) and the anonymous marker alone flips the same turn from `KEYED_OK` to `401`.
  - *Revocation at egress.* The narrower half is still open: showing that a revoked or replaced setup authority blocks a credential-bearing request **before** any network effect. Deactivating the virtual key mid-flow would show Bifrost refusing it, which proves Bifrost's enforcement, not OpenClaw's. The OpenClaw-side proof needs a stale credential held locally while authority changes underneath it.
  - *The key is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`, not Bifrost's native `x-bf-vk`, and this must not be "fixed" with a static header.* **Now documented for users**, not just in this body: `docs/providers/bifrost.md` carries a support matrix stating plainly that a legacy key (no `sk-bf-` prefix) or a gateway with `auth_config.is_enabled` will not work, plus the `x-bf-vk` provider-row configuration to use in that case. Verified against a local listener that the configuration sends both headers, and that an unset env reference sends the literal `${BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY}` — which Bifrost rejects with `401` while ignoring the valid `Authorization` on the same request.

    **`x-bf-vk` takes absolute precedence over `Authorization` for virtual keys.** Bifrost does not fall back once `x-bf-vk` is present:

    | Request | Result |
    |---|---|
    | valid `Authorization` + empty `x-bf-vk` | `401 virtual_key_required` |
    | valid `Authorization` + literal `${BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY}` | `401 access_not_found` |
    | valid `Authorization` alone | `200` |

    So sending both is not a hedge — it is "`x-bf-vk` decides, `Authorization` ignored." Declaring `request.auth` or `headers` with a `${BIFROST_VIRTUAL_KEY}` reference would therefore send an empty or unresolved `x-bf-vk` whenever that variable is unset — which is every interactively-entered key — converting a provider that works today into one that returns `401` by default.

    **`x-bf-vk` must carry the resolved credential or be absent**, and no current seam can place a profile credential there: `SecretInput` accepts only `env`/`file`/`exec`/`store` refs with no auth-profile source; `apiKeyHeader` is hardcoded to the `api-key` header and only participates in Model Setup resume; `wrapStreamFn` explicitly excludes credential material; and `prepareRuntimeAuth` receives `apiKey` but can only return a replacement credential and base URL.

    Fixing this properly needs a narrow provider capability — declare a credential-header name, host places the resolved credential there — which is a Plugin SDK boundary expansion rather than a config change. Filed as #175583 rather than bundled here, so the shared-SDK decision can be made on its own merits and Bifrost's bundling question stays separate. The shipped path stays on `Authorization`, which is correct for `sk-bf-` keys with HTTP auth off; a legacy key without that prefix, or a deployment that later enables `auth_config.is_enabled`, would still fail.
  - *Shared SGLang/vLLM anonymous inference.* The shared helper's optional-key change is covered by `provider-self-hosted-setup.interactive.test.ts`; I have not run a live anonymous turn through SGLang or vLLM.
  - *Before/after model-picker screenshots.* The artwork is a visual change and the repo's gate wants inspected captures in the PR; none are attached yet. I rendered the assets at 16/28/64/96px locally to verify legibility, but a picker capture needs the UI browser-test project, which cannot run on this host — Playwright's `chrome-headless-shell` is absent from `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/`. CI's `checks-ui-e2e` is the available path.

### Data-model compatibility

No stored data changes shape. The provider adds a new `models.providers.bifrost` row and reuses the existing `auth: "none"` field that `ModelProviderConfig` already declares, so there is no migration and no change to how an existing config is read. The one behavior change to existing consumers is the shared helper's optional key, and that is the documented intent: a gateway that was previously forced to store a placeholder key can now record `auth: "none"` instead.
