prs.title: fix: make Daybreak independent of retiring model aliases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Daybreak workflows rely on Blue/Red aliases retiring October 28, 2026, and need explicit access-program selection independent of the replacement model and processing speed.

## User Impact

The chat menu shows **Access above Effort above Speed**, but only when the active account/model/runtime explicitly advertises a Daybreak program. Unavailable options are absent; unknown or empty capabilities hide Access entirely. There are no requested/reported status or explanatory paragraphs below Access. **Use model default** clears the session override; Standard is an explicit selection. If account capabilities no longer expose Access, **Clear saved Access** remains available in the model menu. Clearing is explicit; unavailable program choices and explanatory Access paragraphs remain absent.

The advisory Doctor check reports configured retiring aliases without rewriting models or account pins. **Automatic cyber failover now requires an explicitly configured model**; otherwise the original refusal remains terminal. Review saved session overrides and scheduled jobs separately before retirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the aliases retire. There is no universal successor or entitlement inferred from a model name, auth type, or another account. Program selection (`standard`, `daybreak_blue`, `daybreak_red`) remains independent of Fast/Ultrafast. Empty model configuration (`accessPrograms: {}`) leaves selection unspecified; null is invalid.

Authenticated ChatGPT model discovery supplies caller-specific program metadata. The Gateway projects it as optional `availableAccessPrograms.cyber` on each account/model/runtime choice, preserving unknown versus explicitly empty results. The existing account/catalog lifecycle owns invalidation; no new cache or state store is introduced. Saved session overrides are checked again at execution, and native Codex verifies the same client/account model catalog before its turn starts.

This OpenClaw integration supports the native Codex turn-scoped parameter with ChatGPT authentication and rejects explicit programs with native API-key authentication before submission. This is the integration’s current scope, not an upstream limitation: pinned Codex 0.162.1 rejects API-key programs when its separate feature is disabled and forwards them when enabled. **The Platform API integration currently has no supported entitlement-discovery source wired here, so its Access UI stays hidden.** Explicit model-level API configuration remains available and the provider enforces entitlement. Official Platform and ChatGPT Responses endpoints remain separate.

References: [Daybreak](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/daybreak), [Fast](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fast-mode), [Ultrafast](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ultrafast-mode).

## Evidence

- Published head `16aa4dfff846239fe9767a3ee7c2dd45064f3ea5` has the identical source tree (`399caf72275388b5f2a84c789f04d6319b9d334f`) as tested/reviewed merge commit `a2b0dad206446fc34d11a4b904e32e4aa86bff32`. This correction registers the full-product Daybreak test in the canonical real-Gateway build and private-server inventories, rather than the ordinary mock-UI lane. Exact head `095e68d95b54065f7daf2719dd8662da4a7ae005` received a clean ClawSweeper review (zero findings), but hosted [CI run 39363426943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39363426943) failed because that test was misrouted and `dist/index.js` did not exist. All formerly failing code/mock jobs passed. This is a test ownership repair, not a skipped scenario or a relaxed assertion. Current main `5d76621605588b17828be010bf8582ff5f321835` is integrated history-preservingly after actual merge conflicts; its equivalent ACP/history fixture repairs are retained. The corrected candidate passes all 192 CI routing/workflow tests and 31 native ACP consumer tests, full build, source/UI test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint and fresh P0–P2 scoped-clean review. The clean-checkout hosted-equivalent build and real-Gateway prebuilt lane also pass, executing desktop/mobile persistence, queued Blue→Standard/null updates and the final plugin request boundary under `ui-e2e-serial-standalone`. Line-cap and mock-factory ratchets pass. Exact-new-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper are pending; local passing results are not reported as remote success.

- The previous exact-head ClawSweeper review accepted the six public screenshots and real UI/Gateway/request proof, but found three test-integration issues. All three are repaired: exact native catalog outcomes include empty program metadata, the overflow runtime-plan fixture supplies its required transport, and isolated full-module mocks document their boundary. Hosted CI also exposed a retired ACP test-only import and an incomplete shared Custodian-history mock after upstream owner cutovers. The ACP fixture now captures the real registered public service; the history fixture returns a protocol-valid empty transcript. The new history regression fails before that fixture repair; the original 17 failing Custodian/setup/update E2E cases now pass without changed assertions or timeouts. No production behavior or compatibility guard was added for these fixture repairs.

- Real production-built UI → isolated Gateway → real `sessions.patch`/SQLite → queued admission → OpenAI plugin request-boundary E2E now covers desktop/mobile, Blue-to-Standard and Blue-to-default/null changes, both/Blue-only/unknown/unavailable choices, and stale-selection recovery. Only external catalog/Responses I/O is synthetic; this is not a production entitlement claim. This test found and now protects a first-account-selection defect: a cold private catalog must not erase the current authenticated shared observation; a published empty result still removes Access. The original run passed 7 UI E2E scenarios, 27 catalog regressions, 8 focused command/catalog tests, the full build, core/UI/source-test types and targeted type-aware lint. Counts overlap and are not additive. [Inspected before/after screenshots and full proof description](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177812#issuecomment-6281964647).

- Alias failover and empty-program regressions fail on their respective prior sources and pass with the fixes. The built isolated Doctor diagnostic reports configured references without changing configuration bytes; replacing those references clears the warning.
- Caller-specific metadata parsing, account/model/runtime/route isolation, native discovery lifetime, saved-override rejection, and native turn serialization have focused coverage. The authenticated capability parser regression fails on the prior published head.
- Actual production-built Control UI tests use **synthetic Gateway capability fixtures**, not a claim that any production account is entitled. Scenarios cover unknown, no access, Blue-only, and both programs, rendered control order, absent unavailable options, and save/reset requests.
- The supported upstream contract was personally inspected, including caller-specific `ModelAccessPrograms` and native model/list propagation. The pinned Codex 0.162.1 authentication behavior was checked directly in sibling source at `092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d`, `codex-rs/core/src/cyber_access_program.rs:37–60`: ChatGPT programs are forwarded, while API-key programs are feature-gated (disabled returns `InvalidRequest`; enabled forwards).
- The prior corrected UI/catalog source passed 163 command/runtime/UI tests, including five production-built desktop/mobile UI scenarios, plus 31 focused catalog/transport tests and the OpenAI metadata parser regression. That source also passed the full build, core/extension-test/UI typechecks, targeted lint/stylelint/format checks and five prompt-prefix stability tests. This is prior-head evidence for unchanged UI/catalog behavior, not current remote CI.
- Independent runtime verification then found that the real attempt-dispatch boundary dropped Access before the native plugin. The repair forwards the existing program value without new policy or state. Explicit Standard and Blue now reach the registered plugin callback through the real dispatcher, backend, and harness lifecycle; both regressions failed on the prior source. The repaired boundary and its command/native/transport siblings pass 99 tests, with two additional catalog isolation tests passing. The source-runtime build, core and affected agent-test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and line-cap checks pass. Fresh independent review of the four-file repair is P0–P2 scoped-clean. Two existing entitlement fixtures were made type-correct without weakening assertions.
- Direct agent commands now forward saved Access choices as well as chat turns, and unsupported CLI execution rejects them before starting a model call. The shared run-parameter assembly and harness test lane were extracted into coherent siblings, reducing the oversized owners without discarding coverage. Earlier session-scope checks and Doctor repeated-registration regressions passed; those remain separate prior-head evidence, not current CI.

- The latest review repair keeps a clear-only **Clear saved Access** action in the model menu when Access is hidden, and refreshes queued preferences through the existing session patch and admission owners. Blue-to-Standard and explicit-null transitions reproduced the stale-queue defect; additional delayed-admission regressions caught and now protect the detached run snapshot. Already-admitted turns keep their original selection. Six production-built desktop/mobile UI scenarios pass, including Blue saved before a Standard-only catalog refresh and explicit clearing through `sessions.patch`.
- The final repair passes 90 focused tests across queue/admission, session lifecycle, real bundled Doctor registration, and UI controls, plus core/UI and affected test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint/format, UI i18n/controller checks, and docs link checks. Fresh full-context P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Lifecycle-repair head `64d9f4d` has the identical source tree to tested/reviewed commit `86515985`. The redundant mocked registry call-count case was removed; real repeated bundled registration remains covered. This narrow repair adds no state store, entitlement policy, or runtime transport; earlier paid runtime evidence is reused, not rerun.

- The subsequent exact-head review confirmed both lifecycle fixes and identified one documentation mismatch with pinned Codex 0.162.1. The docs, matching native comment, test name, and this body now distinguish OpenClaw’s ChatGPT-only native integration scope from upstream feature-gated API-key support. No execution logic changed. All 18 native subscription-owner tests, formatting, docs links, and `git diff --check` pass. Prior head `380b556f` has the identical tree to validated documentation commit `4454d24c`. Earlier lifecycle/UI/runtime evidence remains applicable to unchanged behavior.

### Live API evidence and remaining gaps

Four bounded direct Platform Responses requests on October 19 returned HTTP 200, completed with `OK`, and reported Blue: GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra each with priority and ultrafast. Priority normalized to `fast`; no downgrade occurred. Total usage was 64 tokens. These direct requests verify only the tested project/time, not either application runtime.

After the dispatch repair, independent application-runtime verification on `46e86fd` confirmed both GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra on the OpenClaw runtime with Platform API authentication and Ultrafast: each request completed, returned exactly `OK`, reported the intended model and `daybreak_blue`, and served the requested `ultrafast` tier. Prior Fast runtime evidence for those two models remains applicable to unchanged inputs. Four native Codex subscription requests reached the repaired entitlement guard and were rejected **before inference** because both native model catalogs advertised Standard only; no fallback or Blue success is claimed. Explicit programs with native Codex API-key authentication remain unsupported. OpenClaw subscription runtime cases remain unverified because separate token-sharing authorization was not granted. The verifier’s bounded final rerun used six chat requests and two paid calls, costing $0.059019.

Latest-stable data compatibility was rehearsed from the published `2026.10.5` package to this candidate using synthetic configuration and a session created through the real stable Gateway. Candidate Doctor migrated shared schema 20→29 and agent schema 25→31; a cold candidate Gateway returned healthy and preserved the session identity, label, pin, effort and speed. Explicit configured primary/fallback model and account-profile references, model aliases, and auth-profile order/metadata remained exact. Doctor added normal defaults/metadata; whole-file byte identity is not claimed. This covers migration and boot, not packaged replacement or installed-updater activation. The uncredentialed baseline refused an explicit session model override, so that per-session model/account-pin cell is not claimed. Earlier successful native runs dropped the requested program and are not evidence of Blue execution; the repaired-source native results are the pre-inference entitlement rejections described above. A local max-lines-suppression check reported three unchanged inherited UI files; the previous hosted max-lines gate passed with warnings. No suppression was relaxed; one obsolete mock-factory baseline entry was removed. Merge conflicts were resolved by the history-preserving refresh above; exact-head hosted CI remains a separate gate. Before/after screenshots are published in the linked proof comment through the repository-documented managed `gh --attach` route, using the verified `roboclaw-bot` identity. All six public attachment URLs were retrieved with normal TLS verification and decoded successfully in Chromium.

Thanks to @VACInc for the report and the Daybreak/speed requirements.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4bb3b6e0-653c-489b-b976-1a2a8494a3d3)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/78033953-40ec-4f3a-8ea1-dd8ea5df6add)

prs.title: fix(discord): restore /status and active /steer on 2026.10.5
prs.body:
Closes #177443. Related: #169213 and #169319.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native `/status` failures on sessions with saved account selections and active `/steer` failures when the command and conversation have separate session reservations on OpenClaw 2026.10.5.

## User Impact

Status cards render without changing saved model/auth selections. Active native commands can steer the existing conversation run while retaining the command source's authority. No configuration change or migration is required.

**Maintainer decision:** This PR targets `release/2026.10.5`. Choose whether to deliver this release-branch repair or provide recovery through the next stable release. Current main uses a different steering controller (#175837). ClawSweeper recommends the release-branch repair; this PR does not claim the same steering defect on current main.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing reply runner reads the conversation through its own worker-backed session scope and retains the separate slash-source reservation for currentness and cancellation checks. Cross-session steering carries those checks through backend preparation and injection. Calls without an explicit target key retain the shipped V1 steering contract.

Rejected input from an aborted or released source is retired before deferred queue overflow/drain can replay or summarize it. Current-source rejection keeps normal fallback; accepted or indeterminate input remains consumed.

Direct status reuses the worker reader and gives model selection one coherent private entry/map snapshot without a persistence path. Rendering keeps the original saved selections and existing identity/authorization guards.

## Evidence

Reviewed head: `79347e597262943e506fc1bb1d38f48885ee4627`.

- **[Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39352850012) and [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39352850012/job/118411562302) passed.** The previously failing media shard actually ran all 20 media-path tests successfully.
- **[ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177451#issuecomment-6271830166):** diamond lobster **5/6 across readiness, proof and patch quality**, no findings, sufficient behavior proof. Its only remaining checkbox is the maintainer delivery decision above.
- **Final focused checks:** 61/61 across media paths (20), steering worker (14), and question recovery (27), 27.26s canonical serial invocation. Mock-export guard, scoped format/lint and whitespace checks pass. An initial sandbox-only loopback `EPERM` was resolved by running the complete isolated suite with loopback access.
- **[Final-head native revocation trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177451#issuecomment-6281558672):** three isolated cells traverse real source/target admission, the reply runner, registered Codex V2 backend, queue/client/physical writer and managed native app-server 0.160.0. The model peer is local and attachment-I/O timing is controlled. Current input reaches the same native turn; abort/release during preparation produces zero steering, fallback, new-run or retained queue/summary effects. Each original target completes normally and the native child exits. Source/fixture/binary hashes match before and after. Vitest duration 10.99s, test body 3.51s.
- **Live native Discord acceptance on earlier `8cf6137`:** `/status` and active `/steer` passed in both a parent and public thread. Status preserved both complete saved entries; steering consumed a new nonce and produced its replacement marker in the original turn. These live interactions were not repeated on the final head. One initial idle thread setup timed out before recorded backend work; a retry passed, and the timeout cause remains unproven.
- **Command breadth:** registry-driven specs, aliases and a dynamic skill; actual `Client.handleInteraction` coverage for parent/public/private threads, raw/hydrated status, ordinary dispatch, autocomplete, model pickers and denied senders/parents. These adapter fixtures establish routing and authorization boundaries; they do not claim live execution of every command.

<details>
<summary>Regression provenance, scope and size</summary>

Controlled comparisons isolate the published 10.4 to 10.5 regressions to the saved-selection guard introduced in #166985 and the retained-reader handoff in #166703. Compatible baseline inputs succeed on 10.4 and fail on 10.5; narrow diagnostic interventions reverse each failure without establishing a deployable fix by themselves. The final repair preserves the guards and ongoing source authority. Exact release bases: 10.4 `383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af`; 10.5 `1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8`.

The smallest complete stage is the requested published-release status/steering repair. It uses three existing production modules and adds no runtime owner, schema, public API, configuration option, controller replacement or test-only production hook. Both command failures and their distinct authority/read-only boundaries remain in scope.

| Against the release merge base | Added | Removed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Production, three existing modules | 53 | 18 |
| Regression tests and shared test helpers | 1,060 | 101 |
| Obsolete mock-baseline entries | 0 | 2 |

The complete changed-file simplification pass found no unnecessary new runtime machinery or duplicate failure group. Test growth covers separate source abort/release checkpoints, real negative-acceptance queue/summary custody, saved-selection normalization, and the requested Discord command/parent/thread matrix. Shared case modules reuse existing fixtures and satisfy parent-file line limits. The existing known-abort fast path is retained; it avoids constructing a combined signal and throwing for an already terminal input.

The isolated native-backend matrix passed on the final head. The older live Discord proof remains scoped to its named build. Total billed CI seconds and the marginal CI cost of the added tests are unmeasured. This evidence does not establish universal command reliability or select a release delivery path.

</details>

prs.title: docs(ollama): no alternative when cold embeddings time out memory search
prs.body:
Related: #114913

## What Problem This Solves

Ollama users whose first `memory_search` after a pause times out on a cold embedding model have no documented alternative.

## User Impact

They can keep the embedding model loaded, or try llmman, which can preload it and never unload it.

## Why This Change Was Made

One troubleshooting entry, plus `-1` and a preload note on the existing llmman page. No code. This is a workaround pointer, not a fix for #114913.

## Evidence

llmman 0.1.562, CPU only, `bge-m3`: first `/api/embed` took 2.2 s, then 0.02 s. After an idle unload it took 2.2 s again. With `LLMMAN_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 llmman serve embeddinggemma`, `/api/ps` showed `expires_at: null`, and `openclaw memory index --force` and `memory search` ran against it through `provider: "ollama"` with a single model load. Ollama was not run; `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1` is from its FAQ. `format:docs:check`, `docs:check-mdx`, `lint:docs`, `docs:check-links`, `docs:check-config-examples` and `git diff --check` pass. `autoreview` is not installed here, so it was not run.

prs.title: refactor(plugins): retire 13 top-level SDK methods
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Retire 13 top-level Plugin SDK methods with no observed direct consumers in the latest public ClawHub artifacts or bundled OpenClaw plugins, as requested by the maintainer.

Related inventory work: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175216 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175227. This consolidates the closed, unmerged removal proposals https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175225 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175233, plus the three approved registration capabilities.

## User Impact

**Breaking SDK removal:** the following top-level methods are no longer exposed. Existing grouped methods retain their behavior and lifecycle guards.

| Removed `api.*` method | Supported path |
| --- | --- |
| `steerActiveRun` | `api.session.workflow.steerActiveRun` |
| `emitAgentEvent` | `api.agent.events.emitAgentEvent` |
| `setRunContext`, `getRunContext`, `clearRunContext` | Corresponding `api.runContext.*` methods |
| `registerSessionAction` | `api.session.controls.registerSessionAction` |
| `sendSessionAttachment`, `scheduleSessionTurn`, `unscheduleSessionTurnsByTag` | Corresponding `api.session.workflow.*` methods |
| `registerCodexAppServerExtensionFactory` | `api.registerAgentToolResultMiddleware` |
| `registerHostedMediaResolver` | Directly loadable media URLs or allowed local paths; built-in Canvas URLs still work |
| `registerTextTransforms` | Provider/backend-owned `textTransforms`; no replacement for a global overlay |
| `registerAgentExecutorController` | Hosted AgentsAPI or externally managed `self_hosted` environments |

Operators with controller-owned AgentsAPI sessions must retire or migrate them using the previous host and original controller before upgrading. Old ownership records and configuration are preserved and rejected with migration guidance, including through Doctor repair. Published `resolveAgentExecutorController` imports remain valid, but calls report `PLUGIN_CAPABILITY_REMOVED`. Published Codex runner imports/types and explicitly supplied factory behavior remain supported.

**Coverage limitation:** zero observed consumers is not proof of universal absence. The October 19 public snapshot has 2,432 eligible plugins: 2,047 complete, 384 partial, and one failed inventory. The frozen bundled scan covers all 173 plugins: 165 complete and eight partial. Private plugins and separately installed dependency source are outside this corpus. The three broader registration removals have explicit maintainer approval without a new deprecation window.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the public methods together with their unused registry storage, capture/replay paths, global media/transform hooks, and managed executor machinery. Grouped APIs retain registration ownership and closure checks. AgentsAPI keeps externally managed execution, native cancellation, saved-session recovery and deletion rollback. Compatibility records and migration docs describe the remaining published imports and operator actions. Against the base: production/config +279/−915 lines, tests +473/−1,225, docs +182/−259; the small new Doctor contract prevents loss of retired ownership configuration.

## Evidence

- Fresh unfiltered, fully paginated ClawHub reads and Plugin Inspector 0.4.3 scan of frozen source `713ca224c42e67ada372cf53e3abd12c3868ee51`: all 13 exact `api-member:api.<method>` keys returned **0 public / 0 bundled** observed consumers. Source roster and input fingerprint were reverified after the scan. This was read-only; no production rescans or author notifications.
- **Actual registration API before → after:** all 13 top-level properties present → absent. Invoking the grouped API still stores/reads the same run context, registers one session action and returns the same successful steering result.
- **Doctor regression before → after:** the two enabled/disabled legacy-owner cases fail against the base because the retirement contract is missing; both pass here through real plugin discovery, validation and repair, retaining configuration unchanged. SQLite persistence tests reject legacy controller-owned run/reset/delete operations without losing the original rows.
- Focused behavior tests: 31 files / 563 cases passed. Final provider-transform, media and AgentsAPI cleanup verification: four files / 90 cases passed. The CI suppression-inventory failure is fixed by removing the obsolete hosted-media test entry; all four inventory tests now pass.
- `pnpm build` passed, including all 156 SDK export checks. Core and extension production/test typechecks and changed-file lint passed. The intentional configuration fingerprint was regenerated and passed the commit hook. The unused-export scan no longer reports the SDK retirement files.
- **Remaining check failures:** the local repository-wide scan reports unrelated UI suppression/unused-export findings and test-shard size limits. Guard, baseline and the three suppression files are byte-identical to the base. The relevant shard counts are gateway 725 → 725 and plugins 724 → 725 against a 720 limit. The broad loader suite could not run locally because its managed-Gateway artifact isolation guard refused preparation; the extracted provider-transform test passed separately.
- **Current CI blocker:** [production typechecking](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39342409207/job/118368027365) fails in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-lifecycle.ts:514` because `resumeStoredChatOutboxes` is referenced without an import. CI checks synthetic merge `166a90ff` against upstream `33f4915dc55cce9ee797876e699fbf9259191828`; that file is byte-identical in both (blob `ded760bdeb87fa34ad728485ec796bd905d33c54`). The PR makes no UI changes. The error is inherited from the newer upstream revision, not the original frozen audit base.
- **Existing Bun failure:** [the initial CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39341418343/job/118364175917) fails `hooks.before-tool-call.test.ts` for shared memory inside `Error.cause`. Running the unchanged production isolation helper from both the base and this PR under CI's Bun 1.4.3 yields the same result: cloning resolves and drops the cause. This PR does not modify that helper or test. The final head's hosted checks and ClawSweeper review remain pending.

<details>
<summary>Paired runtime output</summary>

```text
                                    before       after
all 13 top-level methods present     true         false
grouped runContext                  {retained:true} (same)
grouped registered actions          1            1
grouped steering                    {steered:true,runId:"proof-run"} (same)
```

The runtime probe imports the real API builder and executes through `runPluginRegisterSyncInRegistry`; it does not infer presence from source text. Codex contract reference inspected directly: sibling Codex checkout at commit `6be2a6ca952ac9f70676ce4dd07fda27175aa9dd`, `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs` and `codex-rs/protocol/src/dynamic_tools.rs`.

</details>

## Evidence

Cold combined run: 37.80 seconds (shared compiler preparation); final strict-typing correction rerun: 15 setup tests pass in 40.23 seconds, with test bodies under 0.1 seconds. CI timing pending.

## What Problem This Solves

Companion and activity recap runtime code still carries private dependency selectors whose alternate implementations exist only in tests. Heartbeat fixtures also substitute these boundaries through production option bags.

## User Impact

No user-visible change, migration, or action is expected. Existing model fallback, authorization, delivery, cancellation, and shutdown behavior remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Call the existing companion/activity model owners directly instead of threading test-only selectors through production. Fixtures now bind the real module or registered adapter boundary. Heartbeat fixtures use these native boundaries too, but its production option bag is retained in this PR. Public plugin SDK options and channel contracts are unchanged.

This is the first area split of a wider private-seam cleanup, kept separate from agent/tool/Doctor changes for CI attribution. Net production reduction after the CI-attribution drop: **6 lines** (6 added, 12 deleted), across **46 paths**. Fixture/test tooling grows by 411 lines, for 405 total lines added; this retains durable and native-path proof rather than replacing it with injected results.

None: no defensive guard or supported feature is removed. The retired fields select test doubles, not alternate serving behavior. The serving companion and activity constructors use native defaults; the heartbeat production bag remains unchanged from main. All current-authority, FIFO, accepted-write, durable-delivery, and settlement checks remain.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(cli): record trajectory events for pure Claude CLI runs
prs.body:
Closes #80667

**AI-assisted: yes.** The patch was authored by an AI coding agent, reviewed by a separate local review pass (one blocker and one contract gap found and fixed), and every command below was executed in this checkout.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: sessions that stay on the `claude-cli` backend for their whole lifetime never record runtime trajectory events, so `<session>.trajectory.jsonl` is never produced and post-mortem/export cannot see otherwise successful CLI turns.

Trajectory capture is on by default and documented to record `session.started`, `trace.metadata`, `prompt.submitted`, `model.completed`, and `session.ended` (`docs/tools/trajectory.md`). Only the embedded attempt path wired the recorder; the prepared CLI lifecycle (`src/agents/cli-runner.ts` → `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts`) called the CLI process with no recorder, and the only CLI-adjacent event was `model.fallback_step` from the fallback wrapper. A pure CLI run therefore wrote no lifecycle rows and never materialized a trajectory.

## User Impact

Turns served by the `claude-cli` backend now produce the same trajectory lifecycle events as embedded runs. `openclaw trajectory export` and post-mortem tooling see CLI-only sessions, including failures, aborts, timeouts, and CLI-internal recovery, instead of an empty trajectory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair reuses the existing SQLite trajectory recorder around the prepared CLI lifecycle; it does not add a store, schema, exporter, or config surface.

- New `src/agents/cli-runner/trajectory.ts` owns one recorder per prepared CLI turn: it skips `isolatedCompletion`, `controlOperation`, caller-owned `sessionManager`, and the existing `disableTrajectory` opt-out; records `session.started` + `trace.metadata`; and in a `finally` records exactly one `session.ended` before flushing through the existing `runAgentCleanupStep` budget.
- `runPreparedCliAgent` now settles through that wrapper while preserving the existing `complete` callback and `runWithCliHistoryWriter` boundary.
- `executePreparedCliRun` records `prompt.submitted` from the already-composed `sentPrompt` immediately before dispatch, and `model.completed` only after executor cleanup succeeds.
- The `disableTrajectory` opt-out is now honored end to end for CLI runs: it is part of `RunCliAgentParams`, forwarded by the embedded CLI backend dispatcher, and checked before recorder creation, matching `attempt-trajectory.ts`.
- Recording and flushing are best-effort: failures are logged and never change the CLI turn outcome.

Embedded-agent wiring, CLI auth/session/recovery, the SQLite schema and workers, and the legacy JSONL sidecar behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Red on base, green with the fix** (test-first; the suite was run before the production change):

```text
# before production change
Tests  7 failed | 3 passed (10)
# after (including two review-fix cases)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  12 passed (12)
```

The new suite drives a real child process through `runCliAgent` and reads the canonical SQLite store. It asserts the five events in order, plus failure, manual abort, timeout, disabled capture, default-on capture, `disableTrajectory` opt-out, isolated runs, CLI-internal recovery (two `prompt.submitted`, one `session.ended`), and cleanup failure.

**Regression runs:**

```text
agents-support: trajectory.test.ts + execute.executable-invocation.test.ts  14 passed
infra:          cli-runner.context-engine.test.ts + trajectory/runtime.test.ts  38 passed
agents-core:    cli-runner.terminal-failure-log.test.ts + cli-runner.helpers.test.ts  13 passed
```

**Checks:**

```text
tsgo core (tsconfig.core.json): pass
check:test-mock-exports --base HEAD^: Mock factory ratchet OK
oxfmt --check (6 files): All matched files use the correct format.
oxlint (6 files): Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
git diff --check: clean
```

**Proof boundary.** The test uses a real child process and the real recorder/store, so it proves the lifecycle boundary, ordering, and exactly-once ending without a model provider call. It does not run the actual `claude` binary; provider-specific output parsing is unchanged by this patch. `prompt.submitted` records the model-facing logical prompt (composed with the CLI prompt context), not literal argv bytes. On a CLI→API fallback both attempts record rows; trajectory export selects the newest `session.started` cohort, so the exported bundle reflects the settled attempt while earlier failed-attempt rows remain in the database (existing behavior for fallback attempts).

This revives the approach from #168556, which was closed only by the >20-open-PRs rule and had no review findings; the settlement hook moved since then and the patch was re-seated on `runPreparedCliAgent`.

prs.title: feat(cli): dismiss a pending DM pairing code
prs.body:
Closes #177870

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can dismiss a pending DM pairing request in the Control UI, but the CLI can only list or approve it.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw pairing dismiss <channel> <code>` removes that one pending request. The sender stays unapproved, is not notified, and is not bootstrapped as a command owner. Other pending requests stay in place, and the sender can request access again.

An unknown code exits non-zero and names `openclaw pairing list`. A blank `--account` is rejected. When a running Gateway owns the state directory, the CLI uses that Gateway. An older Gateway that does not advertise `channels-pairing-dismiss-owner-v1` does not fall back to a local write.

## Why This Change Was Made

`channels.pairing.dismiss` already removed a request by opaque id for the Control UI. The CLI now sends the same method with the pairing code, matching `pairing approve`, and the store deletes that code without writing `allowFrom`.

## Evidence

Store, Gateway method, command-catalog, and administrative CLI process tests cover the new path. The process suite runs the real CLI child for `pairing dismiss` when the Gateway is live, offline, missing the new capability, refuses the call, or drops the reply.

Shipped CLI, no Gateway running, isolated state directory. Two pending requests were seeded (`VK2U7PMX` for `sender-drop`, `YKHL5DQ6` for `sender-keep`). `channel_pairing_allow_entries` stayed empty.

```text
$ node dist/index.js pairing dismiss routing-fixture VK2U7PMX
Dismissed routing-fixture sender sender-drop.
exit:0

$ node dist/index.js pairing list routing-fixture --json
{
  "channel": "routing-fixture",
  "requests": [
    {
      "id": "sender-keep",
```

prs.title: refactor(plugins): remove unused private argument variants
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removes private plugin implementation arguments, fixed policy selectors and unread results that production callers never vary or consume.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Public Plugin SDK, config, CLI, protocol and persisted shapes remain unchanged. Authentication, SSRF and approval boundaries, real resource bounds, shutdown settlement, transport behavior and Phase E remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use each existing owner directly instead of carrying test-only dependency bags or default-only arguments through it. Tests mock canonical owners and keep the same behavioral assertions.

This is the plugin implementation area of a wider cleanup, split by area for CI attribution. After the rule-8 restoration below, net production reduction is **139 lines**; test/support growth is **56 lines**, across 43 paths, measured against the original PR base. These are candidate deltas, not landed credit.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Matrix profile uploads always use their existing 10 MiB limit. Neither production profile caller nor any test supplies the deleted private override. Both real media loaders, URL/path security checks, upload behavior and all consumed result fields remain unchanged.

- Codex app inventory always uses the existing one-hour cache lifetime, as the completed #78733 feature specifies. Remove the private TTL constructor field; tests advance their existing clock over the real hour. Account/thread identity, coalescing, narrow-target results, expiry and actual request-count assertions remain. Main's newer unread-result/diagnostic/revision cleanup is preserved in full.
- Codex desktop generation and CUA use the same real platform, filesystem watcher, fingerprint reader, driver factories and process facts already used by production. Replacement bags existed only in tests. Actual drivers, MCP, recording, authorization, cancellation and watcher shutdown remain; the live generation callback stays.
- IMAP uses the existing mailauth authenticator directly. #130230's actual DNS/DKIM/DMARC authentication and real TCP reconnect tests remain. The reconnect-backoff seam is deliberately retained because replacing that real-transport timing seam would cost more complexity than it removes.
- Telegram liveness consumes the timestamps its actual callers already capture; ingress uses its canonical transport. Keep monotonic stalled-clock proof, proxy/network behavior, close settlement, retry classification, acknowledgments and offsets. Only unused clock/label defaults and test-only transport injection disappear.
- Discord activity HTTP uses its canonical SSRF guard, file reader, logger, clock and preauthorization body budget; unread private fetch status disappears. The #107442/#166626 rate-limit algorithm and bounded-resource protection remain, as do actual body-deadline, OAuth and security checks.
- ClickClack owns the same 1,000 detached-binding limit in its retention module. Hermes discovery reads the same process environment/platform. No retention, schema, durability, migration-selection or profile behavior changes.
- Feishu drops default-only file/text/clock arguments and an unread computed root-comment field. Keep actual comment content, Unicode-safe truncation, scan limits, streaming backoff and recovery, including the mechanisms justified by #74237/#56981.
- QA Lab drops unused internal stdout-cap, grace and idle-null overrides while retaining real bounds and public environment/config inputs. Slack drops an unused authored-text override.
- Bundle detection, greeting facts, Gateway probes and TUI chat-log cleanup are deferred under the campaign's CI-attribution rule 8. Their four production owners and four associated changed suites are restored byte-for-byte to main `ec56c5956825a14ba253a463eb2efd0a19dfad82`, including main's newer native-manifest precedence guard. The original hunks remain on `deslop/z28-parked-plugin-ui-attribution-20261015` without a PR; only these eight paths are intended as parked work.
- Slack drops an unused private fallback-text field and two media timeout fields/forwards that no caller supplies; shared SDK fallback options and actual media budgets stay. Logical-message dispatch now requires the waiting callback every production call already supplies. Released twin claims still re-enter the retry owner for fresh admission; only the unused no-callback inline-retry alternative disappears. The real #143661 threaded-queue repair, deduplication, durability, FIFO ordering, migration fences and watchdogs remain unchanged.

No extra production failure scenario is accepted: these cuts remove unsupported internal alternatives and unread computation, not realistic-concurrency, durability or security guards. Provenance checks found completed features rather than dormant activation foundations.

## Evidence

- Current exact-head CI `39362314823` at `142ce6553906d060edff50686e12cd6723405f54` completed with six inherited mocked-Gateway UI failures and their aggregate `118441693562`. All 22 failed cases match the assertions or exact timeout locators in newest scheduled-main run `39360046029` at `84e1848acbc5b2a62a3bb84700783d71e5c27b43`; this goes beyond the gate's job-name-only classification. Every selected Node, type, lint, security and both real-Gateway UI jobs passed. No selected job was cancelled. Landing uses the native inherited-failure exception under the standing campaign authority, not a claim that failed CI is green.

- Rule-8 restoration proof passed: targeted nine-root native types, explicit type-aware lint, eight-file formatting and whitespace; 46 greeting/probe, 26 TUI chat-log and 22 bundle-manifest cases. All selected Node tests, types, lint, guards, security and both real-Gateway UI E2E jobs passed. No CI rerun was requested. This is failed historical proof, not a green claim.

No suppression/baseline edits, new skips or timeouts. New exact-head hosted CI is required after the repair push; prior-head results are not current-head proof.

- Matrix follow-on: six-root targeted native graph, scoped lint, format and whitespace passed. All 12 existing profile/action/startup cases passed across three suites in 7.74s wrapper (4.67s engine). Independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. No test or import changes. - Whole-tree caller, alias, export and SDK checks establish the fixed live values. Full owner/test/history inspection is retained per packet. The relevant Codex `app/read` and `app/installed` sibling implementations were personally inspected; their 100-ID, tool-inclusion, force-refresh, account and thread contracts remain unchanged.
- Forty-two paths have no drift from their earlier focused-proof inputs. The two Codex cache conflict paths retain all main-side changes and assertions; only the private TTL selector is removed. Fresh cache/inventory/thread-config proof passed **103 cases across three suites**, 225.72s wrapper including 85.8s cold worker preparation. Earlier unchanged packet-focused proof is reused.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): stop cache-prefix churn after child completion
prs.body:
Related: #146902 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Claude CLI prompt-cache rebuilds on managed local `claude-cli` sessions. Ordinary turns and verified child completions used different tool surfaces and system prompts, so a completion started a new cache prefix. ## User Impact Managed local `claude-cli` turns now use one OpenClaw-mediated tool surface for ordinary turns and completions. A completion no longer switches the session between Claude's native tools and the restricted MCP surface. **Behavior change:** on `main`, ordinary managed turns ran with `--setting-sources user` and Claude's native tools; only completion/restricted turns were isolated. All managed local turns now use the isolated path: OpenClaw's policy-filtered MCP tools, and no Claude user settings, `CLAUDE.md`/rules, auto-memory, user hooks/plugins, Chrome or extra native MCP servers. OpenClaw supplies instructions, selected skills and tools. Explicit native-tool selections, node execution, side questions and isolated utility completions are unchanged. Existing sessions take one cache miss on the first turn after upgrade. **Configured MCP servers stay available.** Because managed turns no longer hand MCP servers to Claude natively, OpenClaw now serves `mcp.servers` (and enabled bundle-MCP servers) through its own loopback bridge as `__` tools. Claude never connects to them directly. `tools.allow`/`tools.deny` decide what is listed, and ordinary and completion turns list the same catalog; a completion's narrower requester cap keeps the definition and refuses the call before it reaches the server (the gate from #176892). Each server's `initialize` instructions, which Claude used to get over its native connection, are returned whole from the loopback `initialize` reply (ordered by server name, only for servers with a listed tool; catalog capture follows #174396). The grant and completion-lineage check also runs again at every request to the configured server (tool calls, resource reads, prompt fetches and each list page), so a grant revoked or a completion reassigned while the call waits (for a reconnection or catalog refresh) cannot reach the server. Requester-scoped servers need a verified sender and are not offered on these turns. Thanks @holgergruenhagen and @cassthebandit for the reports. Tool authority does not change. #176892 on `main` already keeps catalogs stable for turns that were exclusive (explicit `tools.allow`) and gates owner-only and requester-capped calls at execution; this PR makes the default local Claude turn exclusive too, so it gets the same treatment, and routes configured MCP tools through that gate. The `transcripts` gap noted in earlier revisions is closed on `main` by #175309. Since #176577, a changed tool list starts a fresh native session, so the first turn of an existing session after upgrading starts one fresh Claude session (OpenClaw history is untouched). **Orphaned tool-call check.** Now that completions resume the parent Claude session, the existing orphaned-tool-use check could reset it right after a spawn turn: Claude Code logs `api-request-blob` records that repeat an already-answered tool call under `role: assistant`, so a finished turn looked orphaned until the final reply was written. The check now counts only `user`/`assistant` conversation records (`attempt-execution.helpers.ts`). **Stable `skill_workshop` on internal turns.** Only human turns get personal-library authoring, so completion turns published a different `skill_workshop` definition and missed the cache for profiled users (and, since #176587, token-authenticated clients). CLI turns without authoring now reuse the session's last human shape with an expired grant, the same approach goal continuation already uses. Personal-library calls are refused; Workshop calls through the workspace-default wrapper follow the ordinary no-grant rule (allowed unsandboxed, refused sandboxed), so internal turns neither gain nor lose Workshop access (`stable-skill-authoring.ts`). ## Why This Change Was Made Ordinary local bundled Claude turns now reuse the existing exact mediated projection that verified completions already required (`prepare-tool-policy.ts`). Bootstrap routing runs after the final tool projection, so mediated read/write count as file access, and the native skill plugin is skipped on exact runs so selected skills stay in the prompt (`prepare.ts`). For exclusive runs, `loopback-bundle-mcp.ts` leases the session's configured MCP runtime for the run and hands its tools to the loopback grant; `resolveGatewayScopedTools` puts them through the same policy pipeline and exact grant allowlist as Gateway tools (core names win collisions). The lease is released after the grant is revoked. Docs updated. Maintainer direction (@VACInc): keep native isolation on the managed path, with OpenClaw-owned instructions, skills and memory. ## Evidence - Focused tests on `ff09c14ef20` (rebased on `50520de188d`, none of the 138 new `main` commits touch this PR's files). Earlier full run on `baeb1a64d3f`: 1,649 tests pass across 145 CLI-runner, MCP, tool-resolution, session, Workshop and bundle-MCP files; the local `agent-bundle-mcp*`, `bundle-mcp*` and `execute-plugin.steering` failures fail identically on unmodified `main` on this host (MCP teardown custody), and CI runs them green. `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src`, type-aware lint and format pass. - **Gateway authority proof** (`mcp-http.configured-mcp-authority.test.ts`): real `prepareCliRunContext`, real loopback HTTP server and grant store, real session store, and a real streamable-HTTP MCP server with tools, resources and prompts. Allowed `probe__echo`, `probe__resources_read` and `probe__prompts_get` calls succeed, and `initialize` returns the server's 1,800-character instructions whole. For each of the three, the server then sends `tools/list_changed`; the next call passes the loopback check and waits on the catalog refresh, during which the server revokes the turn's grant in the grant store (`revokeMcpLoopbackClientGrant`) or moves the child's persisted `spawnedBy` to another requester. The call is refused (`Tool call authorization expired`) and the server never receives the `tools/call`, `resources/read` or `prompts/get`. Without this revision 5 of the 7 cases fail: the four resource/prompt cases and the instructions case. Workshop: after a human turn with personal-library authority, the completion turn lists the same `skill_workshop` definition, refuses `{action:"list", target:"personal"}` without reaching the human grant, and keeps unsandboxed workspace `list`. For a sandboxed agent (same workspace), the human and completion turns list the same Workshop surface and the completion's workspace `create` is refused with the workspace tree unchanged: under the default sandbox tool policy `skill_workshop` is not listed (`Tool not available`); with `tools.sandbox.tools.alsoAllow: ["skill_workshop"]` it is listed and the retained shape refuses it (`Workshop is unavailable in a sandboxed run without library-authoring authority`). - `prepare.configured-mcp` cases: allowed, denied by `tools.deny` (not listed, no instructions, server never called) and requester-capped (same catalog, call refused, server not reached). `prepare.existing-session` covers the upgrade: one fresh start, then the completion resumes it with the same tool hash. `attempt-execution` covers request echoes.
Gateway authority test output (ff09c14ef20) ```text ✓ serves complete configured-server instructions and bridged calls ✓ refuses probe__echo before server I/O after a revoked grant during a catalog refresh ✓ refuses probe__echo before server I/O after a reassigned completion lineage during a catalog refresh ✓ refuses probe__resources_read before server I/O after a revoked grant during a catalog refresh ✓ refuses probe__resources_read before server I/O after a reassigned completion lineage during a catalog refresh ✓ refuses probe__prompts_get before server I/O after a revoked grant during a catalog refresh ✓ refuses probe__prompts_get before server I/O after a reassigned completion lineage during a catalog refresh ✓ keeps a personal-default Workshop definition on a completion turn without its authority ✓ keeps a workspace-default Workshop definition on a completion turn without its authority ✓ refuses a sandboxed completion's workspace Workshop write under the default sandbox tool policy ✓ refuses a sandboxed completion's workspace Workshop write under the sandbox policy admitting skill_workshop Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 11 passed (11) ```
- **Live Anthropic, built Gateway plus real Claude Code 2.1.302** (Blacksmith Testbox, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` via `claude-cli`, WebChat `chat.send`, logging proxy in front of `api.anthropic.com`, a stdio `mcp.servers.probe` server). Flow: ordinary → `sessions_spawn` → completion → call `probe__echo` → ordinary ×2 → spawn → completion → ordinary. The table is from `b166c1cacaf` (base `7badd73ed35`). Rerun on `bf6e20403ea` (twice) and `b586a44a320` (base `453e508e45b`): all 12 parent requests carry one identical tool hash, no native session resets, completions 98.2–98.3%, ordinary 99.0–99.9%, `probe:KIWI` through the Gateway. Before the orphan fix, 2 of 3 runs on the rebased head reset the parent after the second spawn (`reason=orphaned-tool-use`). Cache hit = cacheRead / (input + cacheRead + cacheWrite): | turn | `main` 7badd73 | this PR b166c1c | |---|---|---| | first child completion | **0.0%** (35.2k written, new Claude session) | **97.7%** (0.9k written) | | second child completion | 94.5% | **97.9%** | | configured MCP tool call | works (Claude spawns the server) | works (`probe:KIWI`; only the Gateway spawns the server) | | ordinary turns | 99.3–99.5% | 98.8–99.2% | | user `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` sentinel | loaded | **excluded** | - **Live upgrade from v2026.10.5** (`213dd44de55`, same harness, Claude Code 2.1.304). The v2026.10.5 npm release runs two turns on a WebChat session (remember `MANGO-7731`; call `probe__echo PEAR` over Claude's native MCP connection). The same state directory is then upgraded to this branch (`openclaw doctor --repair` as `openclaw update` runs it) and the conversation continues with spawn → completion → `probe__echo KIWI` → ordinary turns. Session key, id and model are retained. The configured server is now reached only through the Gateway loopback (`probe:KIWI`), and the server instructions appear in all 14 post-upgrade requests that carry tools. The parent starts one fresh Claude session at the upgrade (`reason=mcp`), then all 12 parent requests resume it with one tool hash, 98.3–99.8% cache. The same driver on `main` `50520de188d` also resets once (`reason=mcp`), then sends completions to separate Claude sessions (0%, 83–92% cache) and changes the parent tool hash mid-session. - Two upgrade behaviors reproduce identically on `main` `50520de188d` and are not changed here: the first post-upgrade turn cannot recall pre-upgrade messages because history reseeding into the fresh Claude session is refused (`cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown`), and a `claude-cli` API key saved through OpenClaw on v2026.10.5 fails to authenticate after the upgrade (`The API-key profile belongs to another sign-in`). The upgrade run therefore authenticates through Claude Code's own credential, with no OpenClaw auth profile. - Request capture, parent session: `main` sends 73 tools / 42.5k-char system prompt on ordinary turns and starts a new Claude session with 49 tools / 29.3k on completions. This PR sends the same 50 tools (including `mcp__openclaw__probe__echo`) and identical system blocks on all 12 parent requests; every Claude launch, ordinary and completion, lists the probe tool. - Correction to an earlier revision: the "0% on the ordinary turn after a completion" WebChat result came from a faulty test driver. With the fixed driver, ordinary turns after a completion hit cache on both `main` and this PR. - The `gateway-cli-backend.live` cache probe also asserts cache reuse on the completion turn and the following ordinary turn. AI-assisted implementation by @Marvinthebored, with follow-up work co-authored by @VACInc. ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/13bde8a4-8871-483d-810e-9f67f6fd8bfc) - [Scope reduction, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/d0a61139-e2e3-46b9-ba68-6536a886cb28)

prs.title: fix: qualify PostgreSQL majors and repair stable adoption
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the published-stable SQLite → current → PostgreSQL adoption path, which could duplicate aliased stores, silently omit the port source, reject a valid lazy journal column, or leave local credentials bound to the old database. Qualifies PostgreSQL 16–18 with recorded full conformance runs.

## User Impact

Existing 2026.10.5 users can update through their installed updater, port their populated stores to PostgreSQL, and start the Gateway with their agents, sessions, memory, and local credentials intact. The docs state the tested scope: foreground macOS acceptance, no live inference without provider keys, and service activation covered separately by the signed-Mac/Parallels lane. Published 2026.10.5 has no PostgreSQL configuration schema, so a native stable-PG upgrade is not applicable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use physical identity to deduplicate supplemental updater discovery while preserving explicit registry spellings. Take the port's canonical state root from its existing owner. Complete the lazy deletion-journal column only in the private migration copy. Capture credential receipt metadata with the existing port artifacts and rebind it through the credential owner after durable port completion, preserving the local credential rows and provenance. No new schema, migration protocol, or readiness bypass. The simplification pass retained the existing owners and removed duplicate alias discovery. Delta: +249/−29 production lines, +326/−17 test lines, +128/−50 documentation lines.

PostgreSQL 18 rejects malformed JSON before its CHECK constraint in one catalog probe; accept either rejection while retaining strict row-rejection assertions. No CI matrix was added. A weekly sequential PG16/PG18 conformance job is recommended to catch future major-version differences without adding per-PR cost.

## Evidence

- `PGQUAL-MAJORS-UPGRADE`, local Homebrew PostgreSQL 16.15_1 / 17.11_1 / 18.6_1, unaccent 1.1, pg_trgm 1.6, pgvector 0.8.7. Full unsharded CI entry point on 16 and 18. Counts, source heads, bottle/source SHA256s, lock sizing, and the retained initial failures are in [the qualification record](docs/gateway/postgresql.md#server-major-qualification).
- PG16 full: 948 passed / 2 failed / 37 skipped; the three affected files passed once on PG16 and PG17 (10 tests each). PG18 full: 947 passed / 3 failed / 37 skipped; failed files passed on PG17 (9 tests) and PG18 with port/recovery (43 tests). Further PG18 journal regression: 25/25. Initial timeout/cleanup failures are not represented as clean full runs.
- Published stable installed-updater run `d3b04126-11d3-4f28-9dd0-146f9fe914b5`: exited 0 and activated the exact packed build `b1d415c2448f`. PostgreSQL port `aae1aaff-ec7e-4dac-afe6-7b46f8589867`: two populated stores, retained SQLite captures, foreground Gateway readiness, agent/session/memory continuity, Doctor/status. Unreachable-DSN Doctor returned exit 2 and `ok: false`. Matching pre-upgrade backup + exact stable package rollback passed the same continuity checks. [Cell table](docs/gateway/postgresql.md#published-stable-upgrade-qualification).
- Regressions reproduced before their fixes. Final PG17 credential/port/recovery/restore run: 46/46. Final PG18 credential/port/recovery run on integrated head `50e01a442f95`: 40/40, including all five credential cases. Core and scripts typechecks, targeted infrastructure/updater test typechecks, lint/format, docs checks, and independent P0–P2 review recorded locally. Full test-graph selection encountered pre-existing 725/726-root budgets in unchanged Gateway/plugin shards; all 29 compiler graphs passed, and the targeted graphs passed independently.

Main integration changed only the generated config fingerprint conflict; the runtime patch remained unchanged.

The queued Testbox lease was canceled; no remote workload or local Docker ran. Temporary Gateways use isolated state and foreground processes, with no LaunchAgent or Keychain changes. Local clusters and task-owned large artifacts are cleaned up after validation; installed Homebrew formulas and external-volume worktrees are retained.

prs.title: refactor(ai): simplify bounded tool preparation and report broken descriptors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Simplifies tool preparation and reports broken tool descriptors before sending a provider request instead of silently omitting them.

## User Impact

OpenAI and Anthropic now return the original descriptor-access error through their existing stream error path, matching Mistral. Valid tools, prompt ordering, schema validation/detachment, required/pinned/allowed tool choices, and public signatures remain unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared 128-level schema boundary makes the private generator trampoline and second cycle tracker redundant. HTTP-date grammar and the retained UTC roundtrip already enforce the removed component checks. Provider request lifecycles already own preparation errors, so descriptor-specific catch-and-drop plumbing adds a silent failure path. Mistral's empty-conversion recovery is unreachable after #173312 stopped filtering conversion failures.

This completes an AI-area residue under the campaign's floor waiver: **139 net production lines removed** (+73/-212), excluding tests/docs. It is not counted as a LARGE PR.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Removed unbounded-walk trampoline and repeated ancestor tracking: #152990 protected the human deep-schema report #152866; later #164836 installed the shared bounded/cycle-checking ingress owner. That protection stays, including Gemini reference-expansion depth/cycle handling. Ordinary recursion now operates only within its bound.
- Removed repeated HTTP-date integer/component checks: fixed-digit grammar supplies integers, and the retained UTC component roundtrip rejects calendar overflow. Strict weekday, century, timezone and leap-second semantics stay; 48,000 differential cases matched the baseline.
- Removed descriptor/inventory getter catch-and-drop: #92921 and #92896 introduced synthetic accessor fixtures plus live healthy-sibling probes, without a linked human actual-use report for throwing getters. A broken accessor now fails preparation visibly before any request; it no longer silently reduces the tool inventory. Malformed-schema validation/quarantine and tool-choice restrictions stay.
- Removed optional-description catch-and-continue under the same provenance: an accessor that throws now reports its original error rather than silently dropping its description. Ordinary absent/invalid optional descriptions retain their existing treatment.
- Removed Mistral zero-survivor recovery: #173312 changed conversion to map/sort without per-tool filtering. Its caller supplies nonempty input, so successful conversion cannot be empty. Conversion errors already reach the stream error owner; named-tool availability checks stay.

## Evidence

- New consolidated descriptor regressions: **14/14 failed on the pre-fix owners for the intended missing-error behavior**, then passed with the fix. The pre-fix path reached the safety payload hook instead of reporting the original getter error; the hook prevents network access. Public provider/transport boundaries assert original errors and no payload handoff, including a healthy sibling.
- **335/335 focused tests passed across 13 files**, serial maxWorkers=1, wrapper wall 277.77s. This includes both SDK providers, raw Anthropic transport, Responses replay/tool consumers, prompt-prefix stability, schema reuse, Mistral's three non-live suites, and the suppression ratchet. Cold agent compilation dominated (agent shard 226.69s); the ten package files took 8.31s. Hosted CI seconds pending.
- Earlier schema/date slice: **70/70 focused tests passed** in four files. After a test-fixture type correction, the affected Responses file was rechecked: **62/62 passed**, 4.48s Vitest / 9.40s wrapper. The fixture now uses the actual SDK request type, without casts.
- Targeted production/test typecheck, focused syntax lint, narrow formatting and `git diff --check` passed. No new suppressions or production import edges; broad graph/platform gates belong to exact-head PR CI under the local CPU limit.
- After relocating descriptor cases into a dedicated 103-line sibling, **246/246 tests passed across six changed package suites** (12.09s wrapper). All previously oversized files shrink; no baseline was changed. Targeted types pass after awaiting the raw transport's possibly promised stream. The final explicit-field table passes focused lint and all14cases (8.96s wrapper); suppression ratchet14/14 also passed.
- Fresh isolated review through P2 found one Mistral concern, rejected after verifying `toFunctionTools` maps and sorts without filtering: successful nonempty input cannot produce an empty set. The finding assumed the pre-#173312 quarantine implementation. Named-tool availability checks remain. The earlier production review was scoped-clean; no accepted/actionable finding remains.
- No live-provider or deployment claim: this changes local preparation failure handling, not a provider wire contract.

prs.title: fix(cli): recover supported Node runtime when launched from filesystem root
prs.body:
Closes #177739

## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw` is launched from `/` (the default working directory for launchd jobs and Linux system services) and the first `node` on PATH fails runtime admission, startup recovery should switch to a supported Node but instead rejects every candidate and exits 1. The fix lets recovery accept the same candidates from `/` as it does from any unrelated directory.

- Problem: launched from `/`, recovery rejects the managed Gateway service node, PATH nodes, and Homebrew nodes, so every run fails; if the job discards stderr the failure is silent.
- Solution: skip the workspace-owned exclusion when the canonical cwd is exactly POSIX `/`, since `/` contains every absolute path and cannot be an attacker-supplied checkout.
- What changed: `node-runtime-recovery.mjs` (`resolveRecoveryPath`) adds a `isPosixRoot` guard to the `excluded` predicate; `src/infra/node-runtime-recovery.test.ts` adds two POSIX-only regression tests (`it.skipIf(hostPlatform === "win32")`).
- What did NOT change: all non-root path protections (symlinked checkouts, workspace-owned parents, Windows task scripts, HOME trusted-root logic) remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cwd exclusion prevents a workspace checkout from supplying a malicious `node`; with cwd `/`, `path.relative("/", candidate)` places every absolute POSIX path inside `/`, so the guard rejects every candidate. POSIX `/` is the filesystem root and the standard launchd/systemd service start directory, not a checkout, so exempting it preserves the security invariant without weakening any real protection.

- Best fix: a single canonical-root exception at the existing exclusion site, the narrowest correction to the shared resolver.
- Alternative: exempt HOME, Windows drive roots, or UNC roots — rejected as broadening the trust policy unnecessarily.
- Risk / non-goals: Windows drive roots are intentionally not exempted; the POSIX-only regression tests are skipped on win32.

## User Impact

LaunchAgents and Linux system services that call `openclaw` through a PATH shim now recover to a supported Node instead of failing with exit 1. Behavior from `/tmp` and `$HOME` is unchanged.

## Evidence

Real launcher proof against head `048db1c` — launching `openclaw.mjs` (imports `./node-runtime-recovery.mjs` with `isPosixRoot` guard) under real Node 22.21.0 (fails admission: Node <24.16). Recovery probes **real** executables and respawns with **real** Node 24.19.0. No mocked probe/respawn.

### Raw terminal output (inline, head 048db1c7712a)

```
head sha: 048db1c7712a28bd565d2b987b607796e3b7151e
isPosixRoot guard in node-runtime-recovery.mjs: 2 match(es) (0=no fix, >0=fix present)
openclaw.mjs import: 24:} from "./node-runtime-recovery.mjs";
launcher: .../openclaw-wt-177739/openclaw.mjs (imports ./node-runtime-recovery.mjs with isPosixRoot guard)
launching node: .../v22.21.0/bin/node (fails admission: Node <24.16)
recovery node: .../v24.19.0/bin/node (admitted: >=24.16 + SQLite 3.53.3)
isolated HOME: /tmp/proof-home-XXX (never touches production)

--- Case 1: cwd=/ (fix) ---
  recovery: Retrying with ".../v24.19.0/bin/node" (managed Gateway service; ...)
  discovery source: managed Gateway service (via isPosixRoot guard, not PATH allowCwd)
  stdout: OpenClaw 1.10.0 (eced509)   exit: 0   recovered: YES

--- Case 2: cwd=/tmp (control) ---
  recovery: Retrying with ".../v24.19.0/bin/node" (PATH; ...)
  stdout: OpenClaw 1.10.0 (eced509)   exit: 0   recovered: YES — PATH (unchanged)

--- Case 3: cwd=<workspace> direct (sentinel) ---
  forbidden candidate: /tmp/proof-sentinel-XXX/node (sentinel 'node' inside workspace, discovery source: managed Gateway service)
  exit: 0   sentinel marker created? NO (rejected before probe AND replacement I/O)

--- Case 4: cwd=<workspace> intermediate-symlink (sentinel) ---
  forbidden candidate: /tmp/proof-safe-XXX/bin/node (parent symlink→workspace, discovery source: managed Gateway service)
  exit: 0   sentinel marker created? NO (rejected before probe AND replacement I/O)

--- Case 5: fresh-install startup from / (settings intact) ---
  recovery: Retrying with ".../v24.19.0/bin/node" (managed Gateway service; ...)
  stdout: OpenClaw 1.10.0 (eced509)   exit: 0   recovered: YES   command ran: YES

--- Case 6: upgrade startup from / (existing settings intact) ---
  recovery: Retrying with ".../v24.19.0/bin/node" (managed Gateway service; ...)
  stdout: 18789   exit: 0   recovered: YES   settings preserved: YES

--- Case 7: stable(eced509)→head(048db1c) upgrade from / ---
  stable launcher: /opt/Co-Claw/.../openclaw.mjs (build 1.10.0/eced509, no isPosixRoot guard)
  head launcher:   .../openclaw-wt-177739/openclaw.mjs (head 048db1c7712a, isPosixRoot guard present)
  [before] stable from / under v22: exit=1 recovery=NO => FAIL (bug present — no recovery from /)
  [after]  head from / under v22:   exit=0 recovery=YES (managed Gateway service) settings=preserved (port 18789)

=== VERDICT (head 048db1c7712a) ===
  cwd=/            recovered=true exit=0 => PASS
  cwd=/tmp         recovered=true exit=0 => PASS
  cwd=<ws> direct  sentinelNotSpawned=true exit=0 => PASS
  cwd=<ws> symlink sentinelNotSpawned=true exit=0 => PASS
  fresh-install   recovered=true cmdRan=true exit=0 => PASS
  upgrade startup recovered=true settingsPreserved=true exit=0 => PASS
  stable→head      stableFailed=true headRecovered=true settingsPreserved=true exit=0 => PASS
  ALL PASS — real probe/respawn + executable-sentinel rejection + stable→head upgrade from /
```

Cases 3-4: forbidden workspace candidate is a sentinel `node` writing a marker if spawned by probe or respawn; marker absence proves rejection before both probe and replacement I/O. Case 7: stable (eced509) from `/` fails exit 1 (bug baseline); head (048db1c) on the same state dir recovers and reads existing settings. Isolated temp HOME; no production files touched.

Regression tests in `src/infra/node-runtime-recovery.test.ts` (POSIX-only, skipped on win32). Before the fix both fail with `recovery did not spawn a replacement`; after the fix both pass (2 passed 62 skipped | 64 passed).

prs.title: fix(update): stop canary lint reporting its own loopback bind
prs.body:
Closes #177697

## What Problem This Solves

During `openclaw update`, the candidate lint warns `Gateway is only bound to loopback ... set gateway.bind=lan` even when the operator's config already has `gateway.bind: "lan"`.

## User Impact

The update log stops telling operators to change a bind setting they already have. The node-hosting check still runs against the real config: the updater runs it with `doctor --lint --only core/doctor/node-hosting-preconditions` once the update is active, the same way it handles the other deferred inspections.

## Why This Change Was Made

The update canary lints a copy of the config whose Gateway ingress is forced to loopback (`gateway.bind`, Tailscale off, token auth) so the test Gateway stays private. The node-hosting check reads exactly those fields, so in the canary it reports the copy, not the operator's Gateway.

The updater already holds back optional Doctor inspections (`updateWork: { kind: "inspection" }`) from the canary and reruns them after activation. This check was not marked, so it ran against the copy. Marking it as a run-scoped inspection moves it to that existing path. No new mechanism.

## Evidence

Regression test in `src/commands/doctor-lint.update-budget.test.ts` runs the real node-hosting check through `doctor --lint` in the update rehearsal environment, with a loopback-bound config that hosts nodes:

| | main (`c91613518f8`) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| canary lint | reports `node-onboarding-url` (test fails) | check deferred with `update-validation-scope`, no `node-onboarding-url` (test passes) |

Run in no-network `node:26-bookworm` containers on a Linux x86_64 machine, same test file on both trees.

### Real update proof

The repo's published-driver harness (`scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh`) installs published OpenClaw 2026.10.5 and runs `openclaw update --tag <candidate tarball> --yes --json`. The fixture config was changed locally (not in this PR) to `gateway.bind: "lan"` with `tools.exec.host: "node"`, and the update ran once with a tarball built from main and once with one built from this branch. Both updates finished `ok` with the Gateway ready.

| `core/doctor/node-hosting-preconditions` findings | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `candidate-doctor-lint` (the canary copy) | `node-onboarding-url`: "Gateway is only bound to loopback ... or set gateway.bind=lan", plus `node-onboarding-plugin` | `update-validation-scope` only: "Advisory inspection deferred until after update activation" |
| post-activation inspections (the real `lan` config) | not run for this check | `node-onboarding-plugin` only. No loopback warning, because the real bind is `lan`. |

Captured from `update --json` (`steps[].warnings`, `candidate-doctor-lint`):

```text
main:
Doctor lint warning [core/doctor/node-hosting-preconditions]: node-onboarding-url: Gateway is only bound to loopback. Set gateway.publicOrigin to your public HTTPS origin, configure plugins.entries.device-pair.config.publicUrl, enable tailscale serve, or set gateway.bind=lan. ...

this PR:
Doctor lint warning [core/doctor/node-hosting-preconditions]: update-validation-scope: Advisory inspection deferred until after update activation; required migration, config, plugin, and Gateway readiness checks remain enabled.: Run `openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/node-hosting-preconditions` after activation to complete this inspection.
```

Settings and data survive the update (this PR's run). After the update, the Gateway log shows the LAN bind is still in effect, and the harness's durable session written before the update reads back afterward:

```text
[gateway] ⚠️  Gateway is binding to a non-loopback address. Configure authentication before exposing to public networks.
[gateway] http server listening (0 plugins, 3.7s)
summary: phase=finished readyz=200 runningVersion=2026.10.5   durable-after: session agent:main:update-cell message preserved
```

### Real standalone Doctor proof

Outside an update, the check is unchanged. Plain `openclaw doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/node-hosting-preconditions` from this branch's build, in a no-network container, with node hosting configured:

```text
== gateway.bind=loopback
warning node-onboarding-url - Gateway is only bound to loopback. Set gateway.publicOrigin to your public HTTPS origin, ...
warning node-onboarding-plugin - The device-pair plugin is not enabled; node onboarding join codes and openclaw connect are unavailable.
== gateway.bind=lan
warning node-onboarding-plugin - The device-pair plugin is not enabled; node onboarding join codes and openclaw connect are unavailable.
```

A real loopback-only Gateway still gets the warning. A `lan` Gateway does not.

The `device-pair` warning is correct for this fixture, which disables plugins, and it still reaches the operator after activation. The post-activation inspection step exits 1 on both trees for the same pre-existing reason, so this change does not cause it.
