prs.title: fix: saved Gateway opens can fail when the Gateways menu closes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Addresses a source-identified race where closing the Gateways menu can disconnect a saved Gateway while its first window is still opening.

**Draft:** the exact-head native app/test build and 80 focused tests now pass in a disposable macOS VM. Pristine-base red/green reproduction and broader incident qualification remain outstanding; this is not a claim that the original reported incident is fixed.

## User Impact

The proposed change keeps pending and retained saved-Gateway windows out of idle probe cleanup, including non-menu dashboard opens and native chat windows. Explicit credential retirement, profile removal, and fleet shutdown remain unconditional.

Same-account renewal notification ordering and expiry surfacing as generic shutdown are still unresolved. This focused draft addresses only idle cleanup ownership; those other schedules still need native investigation before this can be considered an incident fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The connection fleet now owns retained consumer demand. Dashboard configuration holds demand before native preflight and transfers it to its window; native chat keeps it through opening and the retained window record. Closing or replacing a dashboard releases its old demand, while hidden windows remain consumers. Idle cleanup rechecks demand at the socket shutdown boundary instead of relying on the menu's private list of opening tasks.

The redundant menu-only tracking is removed. The two constructor dependencies let regression fixtures replace profile storage and transport without replacing fleet, connection, channel, or dashboard-preflight decisions. Origin, TLS trust, authentication, account-bound storage, and expected-chat-store checks are unchanged; there are no message-based error guards or mutation retries.

## Evidence

Native validation is bound to upstream head `fbb30e598cdad1e284058798bc6c6b5eaf80f2e5`, independently checked out by a standalone workflow in Jacqueline’s public fork—not the fork workflow commit. See the [validation report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177970#issuecomment-6282432918), [successful run and downloadable logs](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39361552642), [native job](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/39361552642/job/118428661548), and [pinned workflow](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/blob/0df832829e6ed9569fe3d9fdbe0d0c95df418135/.github/workflows/pr-177970-native.yml).

- **Native app/test build passed** on a dedicated GitHub-hosted `macos-26` VM: macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 26.4.1, Apple Swift 6.3.1, arm64. Compiler build time: **573.38 s**; Actions build step: **583 s**. Checkout credentials were not persisted; no operator credentials, personal configuration, or existing Gateway were supplied.
- **80 tests in 7 suites passed in 60.365 s**; launcher/Actions test step: **89 s**. Executed suites: `SavedGatewayOpeningLifecycleTests`, `GatewayMenuStatusStoreTests`, `GatewayConnectionDashboardIdentityTests`, `DashboardBrowserSessionTests`, `GatewayConnectionControlTests`, `ConnectSnapshotStoreGenerationTests`, and `DashboardEmbedCookieTests`. Execution used the repository’s `scripts/test-macos-native.mts default` launcher.
- **New lifecycle suite passed in 24.443 s:** queued idle cleanup during first-open configuration, hidden retained-window protection, retirement after close, and explicit credentials/removal/cancellation controls. The lifecycle case took **5.853 s**; the three interruption cases took **18.587 s** combined. These exercise the shared production owners, not actual AppKit menu/settings/bridge interactions; the cleanup gate is before the fleet disconnect call, not proof of every shutdown interleaving.
- **SwiftFormat 0.63.1 passed:** 0/414 files require formatting (6 skipped), plus 0/33 in the other macOS/shared scope. **SwiftLint 0.65.1 wrapper exited 0 with one file-length advisory:** `DashboardManager.swift` has 1,505 counted lines against the 1,500 limit. This is not zero-violation lint.
- **Source integrity:** the exact candidate SHA was checked before building; no tracked source changes remained afterward. `git diff --check` passed. The report and pinned source/workflow links preserve the results independently of that short-lived artifact.

prs.title: fix(meetings): one slow browser audio pull ends a talk-back call
prs.body:
Fixes #177633

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: one slow browser audio pull ends a meeting talk-back call. The browser audio transport closes the realtime bridge on the first failed pull, so a single browser request that misses its 5 s deadline drops the call, even though the page capture is still alive.

## User Impact

User impact: a talk-back (`bidi`) meeting call now survives one stalled audio pull. The participant loses at most the audio the page dropped while the pull was stuck. Two failed pulls in a row still end the call, and a capture the page reports as closed still ends it at once. No config or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createBrowserMeetingRealtimeAudioTransport` pulls captured audio from the page about three times a second. Any pull error called `fail()`, which stops capture and closes the bridge.

A failed pull does not mean the capture is gone. The node audio transport (`realtime-node-audio-transport.ts`) already tolerates transient input errors, counting `consecutiveInputErrors` up to 5. The browser transport now uses the same counter and warning, with a limit of 2: the page keeps only the newest audio (47 chunks) and closes a capture that goes 10 s without a pull, which two 5 s pulls reach. The count resets after the pull and any audio processing complete without an error, so unusable audio or a failed hand-off to the realtime engine still counts as a failure. Every browser safety and authority check still runs on every pull; nothing is skipped or cached.

## Evidence

### Live run

Live Slack huddle in a lab container: Linux, Chrome 155, OpenClaw built from #177357 (`83d04fa`) with #173898 applied, OpenAI realtime voice. Lab-only stage timing was added inside the browser plugin's `/act` route. IDs are placeholders.

Four talk-back runs failed 5–15 s after the join with `Meeting browser audio capture failed: Error: browser request timed out`. In each run, successful pulls finished their page work in about 3 ms. The failing pull in the clearest run finished its page work, then waited in the response's URL check until the request was cancelled:

```text
02:07:12.426 guard assert-done
02:07:12.426 fffvt evaluate-start
02:07:12.428 fffvt evaluate-end
02:07:12.681 fffvt guard-exit
02:07:12.682 post json-ok-start      <- resolveTabUrl -> navigation URL check (hostname lookup)
02:07:17.411 post released           <- request cancelled; 4.7 s with no further stage
02:07:17.413 Meeting browser audio capture failed: Error: browser request timed out
```

With the SSRF policy active, that check resolves the page hostname on every call. In the same container, 2 of 200 lookups of the Slack hostname took about 5006 ms, exceeding the audio pull's 5 s budget. In another run, the failing pull stalled before its page work started, at a step that run did not split further.

With the hostname pinned in the container's hosts file, a two-way conversation ran for 2 minutes: 371 audio pulls, no failures, and the participant heard the agent answer.

With this change (and #173898) and normal DNS, the same lab ran a two-way conversation for over 12 minutes. Four pulls stalled in the first 30 s; each was retried, participant audio resumed, and the agent kept answering the participant coherently for the rest of the call:

```text
03:07:16.375 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:24.193 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:33.775 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:41.694 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
```

Twelve minutes after the join, `slackhuddles status` still reported `inCall: true`, `audioInputRouted: true`, `providerConnected: true`, `bridgeClosed: false`, and the log had no `capture failed` or session-close entry. Before this change, every normal-DNS run ended at the first such stall. The live run used `8cc7ccc`; later commits only move the counter reset after audio processing and reword its comment; a stalled pull never reaches that point. The participant heard some agent replies cut short. The log shows four `audio output backpressured` warnings, which may explain them; that output path is not touched here and the cut-offs were not matched to log times.

### Tests

`realtime-browser-audio-transport.test.ts` adds "keeps the call through one stalled pull and ends it on a second in a row". It fails on `main` (the first rejected pull ends the call) and passes here. "ends the call when pulled audio keeps failing to reach the model" covers unusable audio and a failed hand-off twice in a row. All 35 `src/meeting-bot` test files pass, and `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` are clean.

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

- **Why not change the URL check.** Skipping it for audio pulls, or remembering a tab's approval, could miss a tab that moved to another page or a hostname that started resolving to a private address. Reducing the repeated lookups while keeping those checks is for the browser owners; the timing above is the evidence.
- **Related, not fixed here:** #173896 (audio stops when the join's requester disconnects; #173898 proposes a fix) must be fixed first for talk-back to reach this point. Caption reads still fail with `Gateway requester authority changed` after the join.

</details>

## What changed

Remove unread private installer integrity-return copies, skill notification metadata and snapshot-version copies, replay/worker-retention options, meeting-detection totals, unsupported-platform metadata, the background result's outer message ID, Slack's unused status-reader forwarding and copy-only assistant-context user ID, Perplexity's returned credential-source copy, and the private watchdog snapshot's unused transport-timestamp copy. Use Sets for five TUI ID-only collections and one bounded FIFO pruning path. Keep actual session observation timestamps/object identity, activity promotion, live/pending/confirmed stream protection, terminal membership and canonical history behavior. No visual/layout/text change, new dependency, schema/column, retention policy for persisted data, public API, config or protocol change. The original four-file UI slice has been dropped and parked after unresolved exact-head E2E failures; see below.

Current scope: **144 net production lines removed** (+41/-185) across38production files, excluding tests, fixtures, test-support/test helpers/test mocks/test harnesses, generated files, declarations and config ratchets. The watchdog slice removes 2 production lines and 26 net test lines; its integration still checks actual runtime-refresh diagnostic progress, admission, completed reply and bundle identity. The limiter drops only an unread remaining-budget return copy; throttle/window/cap/pruning and wire errors remain. Slack's assistant-context slice removes9 production lines and3 private-fixture lines; metadata/routing/auth oracles stay. Anthropic's private resolved options drop an unread retry-cap copy; the public option/host retry policy stay. Feishu retains its persisted timestamp/write/parser; its test checks actual stored values. Session progress drops46 production lines of test-only projection/imports; five callers observe native phase/outcome and the Gateway projector, preserving visibility, abort settlement and cleanup. The earlier179-net count included the now-parked35-line production UI cut.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

The original preference was introduced in direct commit `1bebcf8033e1e` without a linked age-eviction incident; the real cross-client/concurrent-stream fixes in #114504/#114443 and #38829 remain. A reobserved early ID may now be evicted ahead of a later stale ID after overflow; canonical history remains authoritative, and already-best-effort very late duplicate suppression can lapse for an evicted terminal ID.
- TUI overflow attempts to trim 201 entries to 150, rather than sometimes stopping at 200 after removing a small aged subset. This also applies to unprotected session observations; active, accepted-pending and confirmed streams remain protected, and ordinary membership is still bounded. No user transcript data is removed.

The other cuts remove only private result facts or test-only inspectors; no operating security guard, authorization revalidation, write settlement, bounded-resource algorithm or failure-handling path is removed. Public and persisted counterparts are deliberately retained. In particular, #82730's persisted Slack assistant metadata has always projected only channel/team/enterprise; its unused private user-ID copy is not part of that contract. The open ingress recovery work in #119395 does not introduce a reader or serialization dependency on that copy.

Feishu's completed identity-outage fix #112807 stores a provider-verification timestamp, which remains protected and validated. Only its unread private return copy disappears; the sole production caller projects identity only. The currently open lifecycle cancellation repair #162665 neither consumes this copy nor activates a dormant timestamp feature.

The completed session-controller cutover #175837 already moved public progress selection into the Gateway's physically scoped projector. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cached Exa/Tavily results and Teams parent context being reused by a different resolved credential when the request otherwise matches.

## User Impact

Each credential now receives its own result or denial. Repeated requests using the same credential still reuse the existing bounded cache. No configuration, protocol, persisted data, dependencies, or public SDK contracts change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The caches included request details but omitted the credential that determines the upstream answer. Add the existing SDK SHA-256 helper to their keys, using the actual resolved API key or Graph token. Teams' one-use key wrapper is replaced inline; cache TTL, bounds, cancellation, input validation, and authorization checks remain unchanged.

This is a bug-fix exception to the cleanup size floor: production +7/-5 (2 net lines added), six files total. It does not count as a large cleanup PR.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No authority or lifecycle guard is removed. A rotated credential starts a new cache entry; the prior bounded entry expires normally. This favors correct credential scope over reuse across token refreshes.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, four public-tool regressions failed as intended: Exa plus generic Tavily search, standalone search, and extract returned credential A's fixture response for B. The fixtures derive their content from the actual assembled authorization header; A/B/A proves isolation and exactly two physical requests.
- Two Teams message-handler regressions also failed as intended: A's readable parent leaked to B, and A's cached negative hid a parent B could read. Distinct bot app IDs, routes, and Graph tokens exercise the real handler; repeated B calls retain positive/negative caching.
- After the fix, 96 owner/sibling tests across seven files plus 14 lint-suppression checks passed in four serial shards, 200.89 seconds wrapper wall time. Existing cancellation, TTL, body limits, account authorization, parent formatting, and eviction cases remain green. New regressions perform no real network calls or sleeps; compiler/import preparation dominates wall time. Existing Teams parent-cache tests spend about 18 seconds in repeated module isolation; that setup was not added here. Hosted CI timing is pending.
- Focused six-file syntax lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Scoped import analysis covers 160 production files in the three plugins: zero runtime cycles or new static components.
- The remaining Teams bot-thread consumer suite passes all eight cases in 39.69 seconds wrapper wall time. Total focused owner/sibling coverage is 104 tests across eight files, plus 14 suppression checks. Independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean with final source verification.
- Package-boundary typechecking is not qualified locally because generated SDK declarations are absent. Exact-head hosted CI is the broad/type-aware gate; no broad local build or typecheck was run.
- Synthetic production-path proof only, not live Exa, Tavily, or Teams acceptance. Operator state and Gateway were not touched.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users listing sessions with `openclaw sessions list --json` could not distinguish archived sessions from active sessions because the JSON omitted `archived` and `archivedAt`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing archive timestamp through the shared display row, using the same presence check as the Gateway, including timestamp zero. Remove the one-use JSON helper and reuse the prepared model reference; production code decreases by three lines. Recorded runtime provenance remains unchanged, so this addresses only the archive metadata portion of [#124524](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/124524).

## User Impact

Single-agent and all-agent JSON inventories expose archive status while preserving existing model, provider, token, count and pagination fields. Internal display fields remain omitted. Thanks [@wangyan2026](https://github.com/wangyan2026) for the original fix and regression.

Related: [#124524](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/124524)

## Evidence

The [baseline run](https://github.com/steipete/openclaw/actions/runs/34316928126) built successfully and captured five missing-field observations: three shared-row projections and two real single-agent CLI rows. The job failed afterward because its preservation assertion rejected newly created empty WAL and shared-memory files; the main database bytes were unchanged. The later all-agent listing and post-read checks did not run.

Full source autoreview and both fresh committed-head reviews completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Pending: the independently reviewed combined proof retains those five observations, completes the missing baseline coverage, and checks the candidate through shared-row and real single/all-agent CLI flows with full-entry readbacks and complete database-image preservation. Candidate runtime results, repository tests/changed checks, exact-head CI and native landing are not yet complete.

## Real Behavior Proof

This section completes the after-fix CLI proof that the `## Evidence` section above marked as pending. The candidate runtime results below were captured against head `92025ff2dde787febc1cf9ed878957b2e75bc95f` (the current PR head after rebase).

**Behavior addressed**: `openclaw sessions list --json` omitted `archived` and `archivedAt` from each session row, so archived sessions were indistinguishable from active sessions in the CLI JSON inventory. After this patch, the shared display projection carries both fields through to single-agent and all-agent JSON output.

**Real environment tested**: Local checkout of `openclaw/openclaw` at commit `92025ff2dde`, branch `fix/sessions-list-archive-runtime-124524`, running the CLI via `node --import tsx src/index.ts` with an isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-proof` state directory. A SQLite session store was seeded with one archived session (`archivedAt` set to 1 hour ago) and one active session (no `archivedAt`), then read back through the real `sessions list` command path — not through unit-test mocks.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
# 1. Seed an isolated session store with one archived + one active session
#    (via the source SessionEntry writer, not a mock)
node --import tsx /tmp/create-archived-session-all.mts
# -> Store created at: /tmp/openclaw-proof/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/sessions.json

# 2. Single-agent JSON listing
OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-proof node --import tsx src/index.ts sessions list --json

# 3. All-agent JSON listing
OPENCLAW_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-proof node --import tsx src/index.ts sessions list --json --all-agents
```

**Evidence after fix**: Single-agent listing (`sessions list --json`):

```json
{
  "path": "/tmp/openclaw-proof/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite",
  "count": 2,
  "totalCount": 2,
  "limitApplied": 100,
  "hasMore": false,
  "activeMinutes": null,
  "sessions": [
    {
      "key": "agent:main:active-demo",
      "sessionId": "active-session-demo",
      "model": "claude-sonnet-4",
      "modelProvider": "anthropic",
      "contextTokens": 200000,
      "archived": false
    },
    {
      "key": "agent:main:main",
      "sessionId": "archived-session-demo",
      "model": "gpt-5.5",
      "modelProvider": "openai",
      "contextTokens": 200000,
      "archived": true,
      "archivedAt": 1789873765161
    }
  ]
}
```

All-agent listing (`sessions list --json --all-agents`):

```json
{
  "path": null,
  "stores": [
    {
      "agentId": "main",
      "path": "/tmp/openclaw-proof/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite"
    }
  ],
  "allAgents": true,
  "count": 2,
  "totalCount": 2,
  "sessions": [
    {
      "key": "agent:main:active-demo",
      "sessionId": "active-session-demo",
      "model": "claude-sonnet-4",
      "modelProvider": "anthropic",
      "archived": false
    },
    {
      "key": "agent:main:main",
      "sessionId": "archived-session-demo",
      "model": "gpt-5.5",
      "modelProvider": "openai",
      "archived": true,
      "archivedAt": 1789873765161
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- The archived session row emits `"archived": true` and `"archivedAt": 1789873765161` in both single-agent and all-agent JSON output.
- The active session row emits `"archived": false` and omits `archivedAt`, matching the Gateway's `entry.archivedAt !== undefined` presence check.
- Existing fields (`key`, `sessionId`, `model`, `modelProvider`, `contextTokens`, `count`, `totalCount`, `limitApplied`, `hasMore`, `path`/`stores`) are preserved unchanged.
- The all-agent listing aggregates across configured agent stores with the same archive metadata projection.
- This directly resolves the "candidate runtime results… not yet complete" gap noted in the `## Evidence` section above.

**What was not tested**: Gateway-mediated `openclaw sessions archive` command flow (requires a running Gateway); terminal table output (non-JSON) — though both paths consume the same `toSessionDisplayRow` projection that this patch extends. prs.title: fix(discord): codex detach and rebind are lost after a Gateway restart
prs.body:
Related to #175379

## What Problem This Solves

A Discord thread detached with a typed `/codex detach` can become bound again after the Gateway restarts. A typed `/codex bind` that moves a bound thread to a new workspace can also be undone by a restart.

## User Impact

Detached threads stay detached, rebinds keep their new workspace, and later binding changes remain durable. A refused write from a retired or revoked runtime no longer disables persistence for its replacement owner, and a refused binding change now reports a failure instead of success. No configuration change or migration is needed.

A row left behind by an earlier detach is still loaded at startup. That thread needs one more `/codex detach` on this build.

The repair includes core runtime-owned state stores, not only Discord. Telegram, ClickClack and Codex can reach the same checks, so their caller suites are included below. Matrix's separate no-instance repair is #177372.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord used to look up its plugin runtime when writing a binding. That lookup reads the runtime slot of the plugin instance currently running. A typed detach starts in the Codex instance, where the Discord slot is empty. The write threw `Discord runtime not initialized`, the manager changed memory and disabled persistence for the process, and the command appeared to succeed until restart.

Each Discord manager now retains its creating runtime and passes it into async and synchronous store opens. Session-wide idle timeout, max age and unbind helpers find the manager through the account registry. A private WeakMap in shared binding state gives those helpers the same retained runtime. Looking up an existing manager does not replace its runtime.

Core now checks a runtime-owned synchronous store at open and before all seven mutators. Update and deleteIf also check after their callback. Already-open handle reads are unchanged. None of these fences is removed by this follow-up.

The state runtime marks its own authority refusal with `PLUGIN_STATE_RUNTIME_INACTIVE`. The worker client preserves that observed refusal when a closed worker reply would otherwise lose it. Discord recognizes the refusal through the state-runtime SDK facade it already imports, drops the uncommitted write, leaves persistence enabled and rejects the async binding change with that error, so the caller does not report success. Async unbind, bind, detach and the session-wide idle timeout, max age and unbind updates reject in that window, send no unbound notification and publish no record. Synchronous compatibility calls still return null or an empty array. Activity touches stay best effort and resolve null without a write, so an inbound message in a bound thread is not failed by the touch. A deleted thread still closes its sessions after a refused unbind. That facade is a private-local subpath, so the new predicate export is outside the typed public API baseline. Real storage failures still disable persistence and apply the change in memory.

Manager method signatures, account queues and the runtime lookup for managers without a retained runtime are unchanged. Production changes span eleven files across Discord, core plugin state and its SDK facade, plus one re-export in the Discord test facade, which is not built or packaged.

Public SDK semantics change for retired runtimes. New synchronous opens and writes through retained synchronous handles now refuse work, and async binding changes through a retired Discord manager now reject. The added documentation sentence states this limit. Third-party impact is unknown, not zero. The public usage query on October 19 found no resolved references to this member, but its coverage was incomplete, with 2,047 complete artifacts out of 2,432 eligible, so it does not establish that no third-party plugin uses it.

## Evidence

### Current real-store tests, measured at `d5f8321`

The Discord ownership file has 55 cases. It uses the real registry lifecycle, binding service, manager and durable store, with a Codex caller and a separate Discord owner. Transport and ACP session lookup are stubbed. The core runtime file has 29 cases, including all seven synchronous mutators, callback-time revocation, and typed V2 refusal at open and worker commit. The Codex detach command file checks the exact reply `Codex command failed: Plugin "discord" runtime is no longer active.` for a refused detach and the restored native binding. Two guard cases check that non-refusal touch and unbind failures keep their current behavior.

The durable outcome of the 30-cell guard matrix is unchanged from `95d9afe` through `d5f8321`. All ten paths, sync and async touch, idle timeout, max age and unbind, plus async rebind and detach, read W / U / U at both. W means the intended durable change occurred and U means the complete stored snapshot stayed unchanged, in the order active, retired before stop, then stopped. The six retired-before-stop async cells now also assert the caller result. The touch resolves null and the other five reject with the typed error. Those assertions fail at `d1980ede`, where all six resolved with a success-shaped result.

A 45-cell probe, not committed, compared caller result, durable rows, memory, persistence flag, unbound notifications and the replacement owner's thread-2 write at `d1980ede`, `9e80b04` and `d5f8321`. No durable cell differs. Only the six retired-before-stop async results and the unbind and detach notification count changed.

Six new replacement-owner cases fail on `95d9afe`. They cover sync update, sync unbind and async update after retirement and revocation. The old owner cannot change durable rows, but the persistence flag goes off and the replacement's thread-2 is not stored. This follow-up keeps the flag on, keeps the refused memory change out and stores thread-2, and the async update case now also requires the typed rejection.

Three real SQLite trigger failures verify the old memory fallback for sync update, sync unbind and async update. Wrong versions that never latch, latch only on the async path, swallow every error, treat every storage error as a refusal, swallow the refusal for every manager mutation, or close sessions only after a successful unbind each fail a control or a new case.

| Check | Files | Passed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Changed test files | 5 | 161 |
| Discord thread bindings and listeners | 16 | 173 |
| All plugin-state suites | 14 | 154 |
| Telegram, ClickClack and Codex callers | 17 | 310 |
| Core dispatch binding activity | 4 | 163 |

Core and extension type checks, typed lint and formatting on the changed files, the SDK exports check, the test-api consumption contract and the targeted documentation checks passed.

Eight of the nine CI checks passed. Max-lines reports three UI files. The same command on an exact clean snapshot of `572cb278b24` reports the same three files with byte-identical output, and the UI tree is identical to that base. The seven ratchets used `--base 572cb278b24 --no-merge-base`.

CI seconds were not measured.

### Prior-head Gateway evidence, not rerun

The earlier Gateway record compares main `89e77376ccb` with local merge `3a4095bc93d`, representing the earlier `de7639b` repair. It is not evidence from any later head and was not rerun. Its typed detach reply predates the refusal path above.

| Observation | Main | Prior-head local merge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typed detach reply | Detached this conversation from Codex. | Same |
| Current instance at detach store open | Codex, runtime lookup failed | Codex, retained Discord runtime |
| Model requests from detach | 0 | 0 |
| Rows after detach, stop, fresh start | 1, 1, 1 | 0, 0, 0 |
| Binding after restart | Old binding returned | No binding |
| Plain message after restart | Restored binding route | Ordinary route |

A separate typed rebind run kept the new workspace through restart on the prior-head merge and not on main.

### Remaining limits

No real Discord account or bot, real model, native command in a DM, or bind after Always allow was exercised. The stand-in records interaction replies as channel messages, so ephemeral presentation is not claimed. Native slash routing in a bound thread is outside this PR.

The Gateway differential and full Discord extension project were not rerun for this follow-up. The typed detach failure reply was measured in the command test with the refusal injected, and the real store was measured to produce that refusal, but the two were not run together through a Gateway. How long a production Gateway stays between registry retirement and manager stop was not measured. A genuine storage failure still leaves the process in memory-only mode. A session-wide call that lands after the old manager stopped and before its replacement registers still goes through the ambient runtime lookup, and that lookup failure still turns persistence off, as on main. A session-wide update that spans two accounts stops at the first refused row and does not roll back earlier rows. Startup reconciliation does not catch a refused stale unbind. A refused thread-delete unbind leaves its row for the replacement owner's sweeper, which was read from source and not measured.

prs.title: fix(codex): recover remote turns and failed-thread handoffs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Overload retries and remote app-server disconnects can strand an accepted request, lose completed tool results, or block later requests. A Gateway restart can also replay work whose effects already happened.

## User Impact

Reconnect the accepted turn under its existing ownership and retain completed tools and history. When safe recovery cannot be established, end that request with a bounded failure and allow subsequent work. Automatic restart recovery does not start fresh inference that might repeat uncertain effects; explicit new requests can continue. If turn/start acknowledgement is lost, fail without replaying work whose ownership is unknown. Later explicit requests can start a new native thread; continuation history from the unacknowledged turn is not guaranteed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep one logical attempt across connections, acknowledge cached tool results, and reconcile the exact terminal native history when a completion notification omits earlier items. Persist accepted-turn ownership in the existing session binding so cold startup can settle only proven owned work. Preserve native history across settled-failure configuration handoff; unresolved accepted-turn recovery cannot discard its binding for a tool-catalog change. Ordinary tool configuration changes retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Baseline reproduction uses deployed d5 source and native 0.153.4. On the reduced candidate, 193 lifecycle/recovery tests, extension/core types, native lint and formatting pass; the standalone runtime PR also passes its 18 recovery tests. Real local Gateway/native runs cover same-model and model-fallback recovery plus lost-result and lost-completion Gateway process restarts: one tool effect, no automatic fresh inference after restart, retained tool history, and subsequent same/other conversations. These use a local fault provider. Managed DevBox plus real Slack acceptance is still pending and remains a merge prerequisite.

Known inherited CI exception: security-fast reports the same three dependency advisories as the release base; manifests and lockfile are unchanged. This is recorded as an exception, not green CI. No monorepo/native Codex changes or deployment.

Companion notification PR: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177809.

prs.title: fix(config): preserve whitespace in secrets provider file paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config set … --provider-source file --provider-path` trims the path before writing `secrets.providers.*.path`, so a credential file whose name ends in a space is silently rewritten to a neighboring path (or a missing path). The same trim hits `--provider-command` and `--provider-trusted-dir`, and resolution/exec validation previously re-trimmed via `resolveUserPath`, so a whitespace-bearing trusted directory could authorize the wrong neighbor executable.

## User Impact

User impact: provider builder paths keep their literal whitespace (matching `--batch-file` / `connect --target-file`), so trailing-space filenames no longer retarget the wrong secret file on disk. Whitespace-bearing `trustedDirs` authorize only executables literally inside that directory; the nearest neighbor without the trailing space is rejected before process creation. Ordinary paths without edge whitespace are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildProviderConfig` used `opts.providerPath?.trim()` (and `.trim()` on command / `normalizeStringEntries` on trusted dirs) before persisting into config. File/exec resolution used trimming `resolveUserPath`. Alix’s `#167116` already preserved connect target-file literals via `readNonBlankString`; this applies the same contract to the secrets provider builder and adds `resolveUserPathLiteral` for resolution + `assertSecureExecCommandPath`.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts`, `src/infra/home-dir.ts` (`resolveUserPathLiteral`), `src/secrets/exec-provider-path-validation.ts`, `src/secrets/resolve.ts`; regressions in `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts`, `src/infra/home-dir.test.ts`, `src/secrets/resolve.test.ts`
- Packaged CLI on head `bd8f2287fe3`: **shipped file-provider consume** (literal path beats distinguishable neighbor) + **real upgrade from npm `openclaw@2026.10.5`** (same `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`: file+exec providers still load/validate/resolve) + exec allow/deny-before-start (below)
- Dedup: no open PR on provider-path whitespace; distinct from Alix `#167116` (connect only) and `#167118` (UTF-8 config bytes)

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

1. `--provider-path` ending in a space must be stored literally.
2. **Shipped CLI must consume that literal file-provider path** (not a trimmed neighbor): `node openclaw.mjs config set … --dry-run` → `resolveSecretRefValue` → `readSecureFile(resolveUserPathLiteral(path))`.
3. Existing `secrets.providers` written by published **v2026.10.5** must still load, validate, and resolve after upgrading the same state dir to this PR head.
4. (Already shown) Whitespace-bearing trustedDirs authorize only the literal helper; neighbor rejected before process creation.

### Canonical reachability path (file-provider consume)

prs.title: refactor(process): remove retired queue deadline machinery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removes the command queue's retired deadline implementation after #175837 moved native execution deadlines into the session controller.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Native deadlines, cancellation, FIFO ordering, shared capacity, and raw-producer settlement remain controller-owned. No public option types or exported SDK signatures change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queue still contained a second timer/race owner, progress subscriptions, abort-grace timers, release listeners, and late-rejection cleanup after the cutover removed every production writer of those options. The controller now constructs fresh global queue options without timeout fields and holds capacity through raw task settlement. The queue can directly await that task, preserving its existing microtask scheduling.

This is an area-local residue under the campaign's 100-line floor waiver: **172 net production lines removed** (+3/-175), plus **245 net test lines removed** (+1/-246). Tests removed only exercise the retired queue timer; native deadline and settlement tests remain unchanged.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Queue-local task/progress/deadline racing is removed: #175837 (`36e277d76147a`) removed `withLaneTimeout` and all six queue timeout setters, replacing them with the native watchdog. This is a completed cutover, not dismissal of the original timeout problem; active execution still times out through that owner.
- Queue-local abort-grace/release subscriptions and late-rejection cleanup disappear with that unreachable timer path. The queue waits for raw settlement; ordinary cancellation still removes queued work, and controller timeout recovery still fences native work without releasing its capacity early.

## Evidence

- 89/89 focused tests passed in five files, three serial single-worker shards: suppression ratchet 14; queue/capacity 42; native controller/attempt controls 33. Wrapper wall 237.97s, dominated by cold compilation (process shard 119.86s, embedded-controller shard 78.06s); changed queue test execution itself stayed below one second per file. Hosted CI seconds pending.
- Targeted queue-root typecheck passed after including the repository ambient declaration roots. Initial scratch configuration omitted those roots and reported only `JSON.rawJSON`/`qrcode` ambient-type setup errors; no production change was needed.
- Focused syntax lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. No new suppressions or runtime import edges; all import changes remove edges or type-only names, so no new cycle can be introduced. Broad graph checks are left to exact-head PR CI under the campaign's local CPU limit.
- Fresh isolated review through P2: one finding rejected after checking package exports and SDK barrels. The internal callable queue is not a Plugin SDK entry point; the published `RunEmbeddedAgentParams.enqueue` is a caller-supplied outbound callback, and its option shape remains unchanged. Native controller consumption of deadline fields is also unchanged. No other findings.
- Reapplied onto fresh main `98e1f97672d4f`; the queue owners, retained controller callers, and selected tests were unchanged from the tested base. Reused that proof rather than repeating it. No live-provider, Gateway, or deployment claim.

prs.title: fix: avoid repeated client credential admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Census 37 measured six local identity operations at 104 SQL statements / 18 worker requests after the client credential cutover. Each call repeated full SQLite admission and crossed the worker boundary for open, execute, and close.

## User Impact

The same workload now uses **47 SQL statements / 6 requests**, preserving exact keys and tokens, app-first routing, old-client refusal, and bounded exclusive custody. There is no schema or data migration.

## Implementation and Custody

One worker request owns open → operation → close. Its worker retains schema/catalog/integrity facts keyed by device, inode, platform-normalized birthtime, and `user_version`. Every connection still validates private paths/modes, checks DELETE journal policy, and retains EXCLUSIVE locking.

Every operation, including reads, runs its combined receipt/version guard and row work in one immediate transaction. The strict custody regression shows why: `locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE` alone does not exclude another reader. Connections close before returning, so other CLI processes and the native app keep their existing maintenance contract.

The receipt is an on-disk cross-process migration-phase guard, never cached: another process can change `complete` to `copied` without changing identity or version. Unsupported versions are rejected before parsing receipt data. If a newer schema changes the receipt table's SQL shape, only that failed-query path reads `user_version` separately to preserve the same old-client refusal. Supported-version SQL errors remain unchanged.

The worker pool registers with the existing database resource drain. Drainage joins queued work, closes the worker, and discards admission facts. Replacement files re-admit; migration opens invalidate local facts. First-use schema creation retains its separate commit so cancellation of the first row write cannot strand an empty store.

## Evidence

The committed regression runs four create/load calls and two reads against a seeded local store. Fixture creation is outside the measured window; neither arm includes DDL. It counts actual worker SQL executions and requests without collecting credential bindings. The test fails on main at exactly 104/18 and passes with this change at 47/6.

| SQL class | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Journal policy | 6 | 6 |
| Exclusive locking policy | 6 | 6 |
| BEGIN / COMMIT | 24 | 12 |
| Standalone user_version | 6 | 1 |
| schema_version | 6 | 1 |
| Catalog | 30 | 5 |
| Integrity | 12 | 2 |
| Standalone receipt read | 6 | 0 |
| Combined receipt/version guard | 0 | 6 |
| Receipt seal write | 1 | 1 |
| Identity SELECT | 6 | 6 |
| Identity INSERT | 1 | 1 |
| **Total SQL** | **104** | **47** |
| **Worker requests** | **18** | **6** |

Real second-process regressions cover access between operations, in-place `copied` refusal, newer versions with changed receipt encoding or table layout, replacement re-admission, and maintenance drainage forcing fresh schema admission. Existing strict retained-custody and cancellation tests remain intact. The newer-format and renamed-table regressions were each observed failing before their fixes.

Local proof includes 30 final focused store/lifecycle/budget tests; 34 tests also covered the shared physical-identity helper before the final receipt-layout follow-up. Broader credential/identity/migration/restore/update coverage passed 128 tests, pairing/auth coverage passed 50, and Doctor installation coverage passed 25 with one platform-specific skip. The final Doctor failure-path replay passes. Core and infra/Doctor test typechecks, scoped type-aware lint, Kysely guard, format, runtime build, regenerated worker inventory and wrapper closure checks pass. The wrapper closure requires zero additions. All actionable independent Codex review findings are resolved.

Focused native migration tests include the Swift canonical receipt fixture. The standalone macOS verifier requires a packaged runtime and was not run. The runtime build exits successfully with the existing Russian locale catalog size warning; there are no UI changes.

The old credential broker backend and unused exports are removed. Production/tooling delta is +297/-116 lines (+181); test delta is +314/-18 (+296). Remaining growth carries per-operation authority, lifecycle drainage, typed error delivery, and compatibility refusal across the single-request transport. No aggregate latency or main-thread SQL reduction is claimed.

## CI

[Final-head CI run 39363534901](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39363534901) completed. All three PostgreSQL conformance commands ran and passed. All other selected jobs passed except the inherited UI timeout at `custodian-onboarding-locale.e2e.test.ts:50`, waiting for `.custodian__messages h2`. It also fails on [scheduled main run 39360046029](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39360046029/job/118424101603) and reproduced locally on clean main. Seven relevant source blobs are identical at the final tested merge, its main parent and the failing scheduled main. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception and preserves the failed UI/aggregate result.

prs.title: fix(matrix): show reasoning when explicitly enabled
prs.body:
Related: #81892

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix users enabling `/reasoning on` receive only the answer even when the model supplies explicit reasoning.

## User Impact

Authorized reasoning appears as separate quiet `m.notice` messages without replacing the answer preview or consuming its first-reply target. Authorized inline `/reasoning on` and `/reasoning off` affect only that turn. Turning reasoning off stops unsent chunks; notices already accepted by Matrix remain visible. Matrix still does not display `/reasoning stream` updates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Matrix opts into the existing reasoning payload lane and consumes a new optional `onReasoningVisibility` callback. Core binds each payload to its producing turn's authorized policy, including inline overrides, session identity, cancellation and delivery lifetime. Matrix checks that exact payload before each HTTP send, after asynchronous preparation and DNS resolution, and on redirects/retries. It no longer reconstructs permission from stored settings or defaults.

The callback is additive; no configuration or storage schema changes are required. Same-value `/reasoning off` writes revoke an earlier inline `on`. Queued turns retain their own policy; mixed-participant batches cannot inherit another sender's reasoning authority. Reasoning-send failures preserve existing answer drafts and original partial-delivery evidence.

## Evidence

### Current conflict repair against main `782e8d2f8364`

Commit `cb68597337cd` contains the exact candidate verified after the controlled sync. Main’s removal of `monitor/replies.ts` is preserved: reasoning uses the canonical inline Matrix dispatcher, retaining quiet notices, per-chunk and HTTP-handoff authorization, accepted partial receipts, and answer draft/reply-target behavior. The follow-up migrates the remaining consumer and failure tests and removes one obsolete mock-baseline row; the complete effective PR scope is 34 files.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Removes repeated internal preparation in plugin registration/installation and CLI help/status, leaving each existing owner responsible for its facts.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Command selection, help bytes, plugin consent/rollback, middleware policy, and status output remain unchanged. No new settings, dependencies, protocol, SDK, or persisted-data changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin path entry already classifies local input; its private directory adapter repeated that work and manually projected the same options. Middleware registration already normalizes scopes before composition. Help metadata already has a physical-file cache, and ESM already memoizes imported modules.

Use those owners directly: remove the directory adapter/option projection, compose admitted middleware scopes, unify nine command-help writers/dispatch, remove the extra help-field cache, and replace eleven import-promise caches with native imports at the same lazy branches. Keep the lazy channel barrel, without its extra namespace object. Four obsolete partial-mock baseline rows disappear because the mocks now preserve actual exports.

Net production LOC: **116 removed** (+81/-197), seven production files. Tests/support: net18 added; baseline: four rows removed. This is the lane's single residue packet under the campaign's100-plus-line residue rule, **not a LARGE cleanup PR**.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- An operator replacing a local plugin source immediately after initial classification now fails at the next real filesystem operation rather than an adjacent redundant stat. The old adapter was not a snapshot; source/artifact admission, final consent, live mutation authority, and commit/rollback remain. Feature foundation#171622 and its activations#171623/#171600 are merged; no inactive foundation is removed.
- A synthetic direct `null` metadata file beside valid parent metadata may advance to the parent on a later help attempt rather than retaining an outer field miss forever. The introducing characterization/refactor#133841 cites no human incident requiring that sticky miss. Physical-file success/miss caching and external shape validation remain.
- Admitted middleware scope values are retained rather than copied and normalized again. The introducing#109603 paired-runtime/matcher policy remains; both real producers normalize before handoff, and plugins must not mutate admitted values. External validation and per-tool effect policy remain unchanged.
- Plain module imports use native ESM memoization, not application promise caches. The loader refactor`db06fcd990ff9` and namespace consolidation`9648e7fecb282` do not establish an incident requiring another cache layer; existing lazy placement and factory/resource caches remain.

## Evidence

- Focused existing plugin installation/artifact/transaction suites:24cases passed, including real directory/archive consent and deferred rollback.
- CLI/help/entry/status focused replay:97cases passed; root and all nine command-help outputs retain exact bytes, physical metadata snapshots and cold-import behavior remain covered.
- Middleware normalization/pairing and captured-registration suites:16cases passed unchanged. Suppression suite14cases passed before publication.
- Targeted types for each touched graph, canonical-core typed lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Runtime/type-inclusive cycles were zero for the packet; the final middleware change adds no module edge and cannot add a cycle.
- Fresh independent P0-P2 review completed for each unchanged packet component; final middleware review also completed scoped-clean.
- Initial unified-help mock replay exposed three owned fixture failures: an unused one-shot return leaked into later command cases. Reset the unified mock between cases; retained assertions pass. No retries, increased timeouts, new skips or suppressions.
- Broad build/suite proof is intentionally deferred to hosted CI on the exact head under the shared-host budget. No live Gateway, production state, or external-channel claim.

Release-note context: internal cleanup only; no user action or migration.

### Exact-head hosted CI

Run [39362206642](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39362206642) completed on `b343fd02b1e6a345d183f4e3653e94b9525f65d5`. All 214 check runs were enumerated. One leaf and its aggregate failed; the only cancellation was advisory `auto-response`, not missing selected-suite proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Custodian E2E scenarios stall before their greeting because the shared mock Gateway returns an invalid empty object for the now-required history read. The mobile message-disclosure scenario can also read its temporary CSS height before the resize observer restores its measured clamp after collapsing.

## User Impact

No production behavior change. The mock Gateway supplies an empty Custodian transcript so onboarding scenarios can reach their existing assertions. The disclosure test waits for settled geometry before checking its exact restored height.

## Why This Change Was Made

After #177912 removed the old history advertisement guard, Custodian loads history before requesting its greeting. The shared fixture now returns a protocol-typed empty history, and a serialized WebSocket regression validates that response with the method absent from the advertised catalog. Scenario response overrides and advertisements are unchanged.

The disclosure test's failed CI assertion read a 105-pixel fallback immediately after collapse instead of the measured 100-pixel clamp. Waiting at that boundary uses the existing layout-settling helper and preserves every assertion.

## Evidence

- New mock response regression fails schema validation without the default; the full mock-gateway file passes with it (11 tests, 1.69 seconds Vitest / 2.80 seconds wrapper).
- Existing Chinese onboarding locale E2E: reproduced the original line-50 greeting timeout on `5a85669bb331`; passes with this fixture repair (1 test, 41.58 seconds including build/transform).
- Mobile disclosure reload/reveal case: reproduced the exact CI failure locally (105 versus 100 pixels); passes with the one-line collapse-settling fix (1 test, 33.35 seconds including build/transform).
- Independent review found no actionable issues through P2.
- Focused lint, typecheck, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

The prior-head CI run [39361576503](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39361576503) passed eight of nine mock-Gateway E2E shards and both real-Gateway shards; its only test failure was the disclosure assertion repaired here. That run is prior-head evidence. Current-head CI remains the broad gate.

This is a focused CI fixture repair; no production code is changed. The locale and disclosure scenarios are the scoped E2E proof; other scenarios were not individually rerun locally.

prs.title: fix(database): account, approval, and usage writes hold the SQLite writer during host admission
prs.body:
Related: #169260, #169283

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: personal model-account connect/link/unlink, operator-approval decisions, and auth-profile usage writes hold the shared-state SQLite writer while waiting for the host's first live-authority grant, so a busy Gateway main thread makes concurrent writes time out with `database is locked`.

## User Impact

User impact: when the Gateway main thread is slow, account connect/link/unlink, approval resolve/consume, and credential usage writes no longer hold the shared writer while they wait for their first authority check, so Gateway cron and cleanup writes keep their normal 5 s budget.

Trigger requires the same coincidence as #169260: a low-frequency interactive write overlapping a main-thread stall longer than the 5 s busy timeout. No deadlock. This is the same defect class #169283 repaired for update-history writers; its follow-up list named four producer groups but not the writers fixed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

These writers requested their first `transaction`-stage grant after `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. The host answers admission on its event loop, so any main-thread delay became writer hold time. `docs/reference/database-schemas.md` already requires the initial host grant before `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. Mirroring #169283, these writers now take the first grant before entering the write transaction; rows are still reread inside the transaction and the commit-stage grant still revalidates authority immediately before COMMIT. The host treats the transaction stage purely as an authority check, so a grant followed by a failed BEGIN leaks nothing.

Scope: `src/state/user-model-accounts.ts` (update/connect/link/unlink), the shared `transact()` helper in `src/gateway/operator-approval-store.worker.ts` (all `operatorApprovals.*` worker operations), and `authProfiles.enrollAuthorization`/`authProfiles.usage` in `src/agents/auth-profiles/store.worker.ts`. (The shared-auth profile store writer the branch originally targeted as `authProfiles.personalAccept` is named `enrollAuthorization` on current main; the same pre-`BEGIN` first grant is applied to it.) Remaining producers (#169283's listed follow-ups such as `writeAdmitted`, plus `sqlite-wal`/upload-store/session-accessor sites) are unchanged and stay as follow-up; a shared move of the initial grant into one owner would cover them.

No config, schema, timeout, retention, protocol, or update-behavior changes.

## Evidence

### Contention probes (writer-lock freedom during first grant)

Probes copied from `src/infra/update-run-contention.test.ts`: a competing connection attempts `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` while the host decides each admission stage; free means the writer lock was not held.

Before fix (touched source files reverted to `origin/main`, all fail):

```text
× leaves the writer free while the host decides credential update admission
× leaves the writer free while the host decides account connect admission
× leaves the writer free while the host decides link selection admission
× leaves the writer free while the host decides unlink selection admission
AssertionError: expected [ 'transaction:held', 'commit:held' ] to deeply equal [ 'transaction:free', 'commit:held' ]

FAIL leaves the writer free while the host decides approval admission
AssertionError: expected [ 'transaction:held', 'commit:held' ] to deeply equal [ 'transaction:free', 'commit:held' ]
```

After fix: `src/state/user-model-accounts-contention.test.ts` 4/4 (native path, one per edited writer) and the approval worker probe pass.

### Busy-host real-behavior proof (competing write during a delayed first admission)

Each of the four edited writers now has a test that holds the host main thread busy for 800 ms while the first `transaction`-stage admission of a real write is pending, and has a second worker thread attempt a full competing SQLite write in that window. With the fix, the competing write acquires `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and commits within milliseconds while the host is still busy — proving the writer lock is no longer held during the delayed first grant. Reverting the touched source files to `origin/main` makes every one of them fail with `database is locked`. The personal-credential probe now drives the `authProfiles.enrollAuthorization` worker write (upstream renamed the old `personalAccept` handler to `enrollAuthorization`; the acceptance path itself performs no SQLite write on current main).

Fixed code (`[ok]` — competing write committed while host was busy 800 ms):

```text
[busy-host proof]              initial approval admission answered after 800ms of host delay
[ok] competing write elapsed 9ms (host busy 800ms)
approval persisted after admission resumed: true

[busy-host account proof]      initial account admission answered after 800ms of host delay
[ok] competing write elapsed 10ms (host busy 800ms)
account persisted after admission resumed: true

[busy-host enrollment proof]   initial enrollment admission answered after 800ms of host delay
[ok] competing write elapsed 10ms (host busy 800ms)
authorization persisted after admission resumed: true

[busy-host usage proof]        initial usage admission answered after 800ms of host delay
[ok] competing write elapsed 26ms (host busy 800ms)
usage persisted after admission resumed: true
```

Pre-fix (`origin/main` sources, same tests, all fail — competing write blocked by the held writer):

```text
[FAILED] competing write elapsed 202ms: Error: database is locked   (approval)
[FAILED] competing write elapsed 202ms: Error: database is locked   (account connect)
[FAILED] competing write elapsed 202ms: Error: database is locked   (auth authorization enrollment)
[FAILED] competing write elapsed 201ms: Error: database is locked   (usage)
AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality
```

### Regression, typecheck, format

- Rebased onto current `main` (head `63d26593250`): the two rebase conflicts were resolved by keeping the pre-`BEGIN` first grant on main's evolved code — `authProfiles.personalAccept` became `enrollAuthorization` in `store.worker.ts`, and `connectUserModelAccount` kept upstream's authorization-id `writeProfile` signature while the transaction-stage grant moved before `BEGIN`.
- Regression suites pass on the rebased branch: `src/state/user-model-accounts.test.ts`, `src/gateway/operator-approval-store.worker.test.ts` (including the `["compare","transaction","commit"]` stage-order assertion), `src/gateway/model-account-connect.worker.test.ts`, `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-personal.worker.test.ts`, `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.write-admission.test.ts`.
- Targeted typecheck: `tsconfig.core.json` incremental plus the `state-logging`, `gateway-root`, and `agents-other` core-test shards; error set is byte-identical to the untouched baseline (pre-existing host-environment errors only, 0 new).
- `oxlint` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean, `git diff --check` clean.

Remaining out of scope (unchanged, tracked as follow-up): the other first-grant-inside-BEGIN producers such as `writeAdmitted` and the `sqlite-wal`/upload-store/session-accessor sites.

prs.title: fix(retry): prevent oversized deadlines from timing out immediately
prs.body:
Closes #176076

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes timeout races firing almost immediately when callers provide an oversized or infinite deadline.

## User Impact

Operations observed through the public Plugin SDK timeout helper no longer take the timeout path after roughly 1 ms or emit Node's `TimeoutOverflowWarning` for overflowing deadlines.

## Why This Change Was Made

`raceWithTimeout` passed its deadline directly to `setTimeout`. Node converts values above its timer limit to a 1 ms delay and emits an overflow warning. This change saturates only overflowing deadlines while preserving supported native deadlines exactly.

## Evidence

The branch is based on current `main`.

- Commit `05172b8` addresses the P2 review finding: `2,147,483,647` and fractional deadlines retain their exact native values; only values above Node's limit and positive `Infinity` saturate.
- Commit `2f7e02a` moves the production-loader integration into `packages/plugin-sdk/tests/time-runtime.test.ts`, the exact SDK shard selected by CI. The loaded external plugin imports `openclaw/plugin-sdk/time-runtime`, runs 20 ms delayed work with `Infinity` and `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, and asserts two `"done"` outcomes with zero overflow warnings.
- The duplicate retry-package behavioral case was removed; the public SDK package test remains the focused boundary regression.
- SDK documentation now describes narrow overflow saturation and exact native semantics for supported delays.

### Public Plugin SDK runtime trace

```text
{"preserved":[2147483647,1.5]}
{"timeoutMs":"Infinity","result":"done","elapsedMs":20}
{"timeoutMs":"9007199254740991","result":"done","elapsedMs":27}
{"overflowWarnings":0}
```

### Checks

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on all touched files — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint` on all touched TypeScript files — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Direct public-package runtime trace — passed.
- Local loaded-plugin execution reaches the production loader but is rejected before plugin registration because this Windows host uses Node 24.11.0 with SQLite 3.50.4; the repository requires Node 24.16.0+ or 26.1.0+ for WAL safety. The previous CI run proved this SDK shard is selected (4/4 boundary tests passed); the new run will include the loaded-plugin case in the same shard.

## Maintainer decision requested

This intentionally changes the documented public deadline policy from raw overflow behavior to narrow bounded saturation. Maintainer approval of that contract is requested.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Auth-profile bookkeeping transports previous state and timestamps across worker receipts solely to produce a verbose failure-state diagnostic. Nothing consumes that event in core. This leaves persistence and publication carrying an unnecessary second representation of their result.

## User Impact

Auth failures no longer emit the verbose state-transition warning. Actual failure/fallback diagnostics and persisted cooldown behavior remain unchanged; no operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove `auth_profile_failure_state_updated` and return the resulting `ProfileUsageStats` directly from personal/shared usage writers. Inline receipts retain only the store and publication facts their consumers need. Delete the test that only sanitized the removed output and migrate the existing usage fixture to the direct result.

Cooldown/WHAM decisions, credential equality, live authority, persistence, publication order, FIFO settlement and last-good selection are unchanged. Dropped-bookkeeping warnings and model-fallback diagnostics/coalescing remain. Public SDK signatures, including optional `runId`, remain unchanged. No schema, stored shape, permissions, retention, dependency or protocol changes.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Detailed failure-state transition logs are no longer emitted; operators retain the actual fallback/error diagnostics and stored cooldown state. The event was introduced as observation plumbing in #41337, not as a human-incident fix. Human report #56979 cites it among auth-failure log spam; this cut does not claim to resolve that entire report.
- Private worker receipts no longer retain diagnostic preimages or timestamps for hypothetical consumers. All current consumers use the resulting stats and publication facts. A future diagnostic consumer must explicitly request the information it needs rather than taxing every bookkeeping write.

prs.title: refactor(plugins): reuse transport and catalog owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin transports and provider registration still rebuild facts their existing owners already supply: offline catalogs are assembled and immediately reduced back to IDs, resolved speech requests are checked again, and private name-cache plumbing repeats an existing SDK cache. The same sweep exposed three concrete bugs: xAI shared cached answers across credentials, Azure's duplicate config reader let an environment-derived route override explicit configuration, and Tlon silently used a channel-close HTTP method Eyre does not support.

## What Changed

Use provider-owned static defaults directly in DeepInfra registration and keep only consumed live metadata. Preserve the public builder options and rich `DeepInfraSurfaceModel` shape, registered model IDs/order, native pricing, live catalogs and unknown-price behavior. Consolidate Azure field normalization without conflating strict raw-secret handling with direct provider-config handling. Let resolved ElevenLabs requests carry already validated fields through the private transport.

Delegate LINE's name-cache implementation to the existing SDK with stale reads disabled. Use Zalouser's authenticated session identity instead of another account-info request. Let the installed Google auth transport choose its route once and adapt that prepared route to guarded fetch. Remove unread voice-verification result metadata, duplicate QA catalog validation, Matrix migration pre-reservation/recensus, duplicate memory date formatting/sorting, and Feishu's optional typing-cleanup custody/retry state.

Scope: 32 files, **500 net production lines removed** (+160/-660), excluding tests/support, fixtures, generated files and declarations. No new SDK API, config key, persisted schema, retention, protocol version or dependency change. Actual HTTP protocol correction in Tlon preserves its existing cookie/SSRF/deadline owner.

## User Impact

Existing plugin features, configured defaults and public contracts remain. xAI answers are isolated by the resolved credential, explicit Azure routing wins over environment routing, and Tlon closes remote channels using Eyre's supported action. Optional typing cleanup and offline migration bookkeeping accept the best-effort cases described below; no operator migration or configuration change is required.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- DeepInfra no longer constructs unused offline surface projections or copies unread pricing/description/image defaults. #134893 moved real pricing to the native catalog; #84549 described future separate surface support, not a current activation dependency. Registered static providers remain authoritative when live acquisition is absent or fails. Public builder input types remain unchanged.
- Google Chat does not independently reread proxy environment, `NO_PROXY`, headers and route policy after Gaxios prepares a request. Gaxios 7.3.1 owns that preparation; transport localization #69812 and the later header fix did not establish a need for a second policy owner. A mid-call environment change does not retarget the prepared request. mTLS, OAuth transport, credentials and guarded I/O remain.
- Azure and ElevenLabs private transports do not revalidate/default fields that their own request resolvers already normalized. Public config/persona/override validation, voice/language validation where still needed, SecretRef handling, SSRF, content and size limits remain. Azure's shared field owner now also honors explicit region/endpoint over an environment-derived URL, matching the existing documented precedence.
- Feishu performs one best-effort typing-reaction deletion and releases the active key before awaiting it. #63785 introduced cleanup divergence as a prospective feature risk, not a human-filed deletion incident. A failed optional delete is logged but not retried by a later cleanup callback; an unsupported cleanup-before-start or reentrant start is not given a custody protocol. Normal add/delete, account policy and HTTP deadlines remain. Real callers already fire-and-forget cleanup, so no ordinary shutdown join is removed.
- LINE's existing five-minute, 1,000-entry name caches now use the SDK cache. Human-reported group-name/profile behavior #132098/#132108 is retained, including conversation/account keys, negative caching and one load for matching callers. At more than 1,000 simultaneous distinct cold lookups, SDK saturation degrades to the existing missing-name fallback; refresh eviction order may differ and cause another harmless name lookup.
- Matrix's offline migration no longer reserves a negative completion timestamp or rescans/reopens every retired legacy source. The reservation/certification paths came from synthetic #113487 coverage; the actual historical-root repair from human #112450 stays. Imported ingress tombstones commit before retirement. A foreign legacy writer during offline migration is unsupported; completion-write failure warns and may cause a harmless later rescan. Schema, stored completion shape, retention and ordinary restart durability are unchanged.
- Memory flush formatting uses the existing SDK day formatter after timezone normalization. In the unsupported Intl-fallback case, its established host-local fallback replaces a private UTC fallback. Dreaming cron removes duplicates in list order rather than sorting duplicates all destined for deletion; the selected survivor remains unchanged. Extraction #151713 was not an incident requiring the private implementations. Standalone session memory is untouched.
- Voice verification no longer returns unread diagnostic URL/version/ngrok fields already discarded by provider wrappers. The ngrok projection became orphaned when `ff11d879` removed the signature bypass. HMAC verification, trusted forwarding, replay ownership, releases and redacted failure reasons are unchanged.
- QA coverage trusts scenario IDs already validated at catalog ingress. #108429 retired the separate non-YAML catalogs and final option caller from #99628; #99627 was a design proposal, not a duplicate-ID incident. The actual YAML duplicate check and report/gate semantics remain.
- Zalouser consumes the authenticated zca-js session's `getOwnId()` instead of probing another account-info response and catching impossible local accessor failures. The pinned dependency sets `ctx.uid` during login before constructing the API. #32119 introduced the extra request during unrelated hardlink work; the real group-mention repair #33992 restored `getOwnId`, which stays authoritative here. Credential authority and mention/quote gating remain.
- xAI cache sharing remains available only for identical resolved credentials and request shape, with a SHA-256 digest rather than raw credentials in keys. No authorization guard is relaxed. Tlon now retires an Eyre channel with its supported PUT delete action, which already removes subscriptions; optional remote-close failure remains logged and local shutdown still completes.

## Evidence

Acceptance: preserve registered defaults, transport authorization, ordinary migration/restart and name-cache work counts; three bug reproductions must fail through their public production owners on the base and pass after repair. No live-channel, paid-provider, timing or production-wide performance claim.

- xAI: both A→B→A regressions failed on the original production code because B inherited A's answer. Fixed search and auth-lifecycle proof: 43 tests across three files passed in 157.77 seconds wrapper wall time; actual credential-derived synthetic HTTP answers and exactly two physical calls prove isolation and matching-credential reuse.
- Tlon: pinned Urbit `5a187fededc4582a34fcd6055c67bb63e0917b94` [rejects HTTP DELETE](https://github.com/urbit/urbit/blob/5a187fededc4582a34fcd6055c67bb63e0917b94/pkg/arvo/sys/vane/eyre.hoon#L2271), [parses the delete action](https://github.com/urbit/urbit/blob/5a187fededc4582a34fcd6055c67bb63e0917b94/pkg/arvo/sys/vane/eyre.hoon#L260), and [retires channel state, timers and subscriptions](https://github.com/urbit/urbit/blob/5a187fededc4582a34fcd6055c67bb63e0917b94/pkg/arvo/sys/vane/eyre.hoon#L3039). The real HTTP reconnect/close fixture now mirrors that contract. Base `close()` returned but left its channel present: intended final-state regression failure. An initial test-fixture placement error was corrected before this valid red proof; no product verdict is claimed from that setup failure.
- Azure: both explicit-region and explicit-endpoint cases failed on base through synthesis and voice discovery: the actual guarded HTTP requests went to the environment region instead. Independent review then found the environment-endpoint variant; that added public-boundary regression also failed before repair. The complete Azure owner suite (19 tests) plus all 14 suppression checks passed in 20.92 seconds wrapper wall time after the correction. No live Azure request was needed.
- Zalouser: base own-ID resolution made one unnecessary profile request; the existing restored-session fixture proves the zero-request contract while preserving the returned identity. No new production test seam.
- Earlier unchanged-input proof: Google Chat 16 tests/four files; Matrix migration 25 tests/four files; memory owners 66 tests/four files; voice verification 24 tests/one file all passed. These results are reused, not rerun.
- Combined retained owner/sibling proof: 296 tests across 24 files plus all 14 suppression checks passed eight serial Vitest shards in 588.58 seconds. This covers DeepInfra registration/live catalogs/provider surfaces, Azure routing, ElevenLabs synthesis/streaming, Feishu installed-SDK loopback, LINE account/conversation cache behavior, QA catalog/report semantics, Tlon real HTTP shutdown, and Zalouser credential/mention/quote siblings. Individual test execution remains short; most wrapper time was compilation on the shared host.
- Scoped cycle proof covers 1,568 production files across the 13 touched plugins: zero runtime cycles and zero new static strongly connected components against the branch base. Changed-file syntax lint, all 31 TypeScript files' formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. The initial independent P0–P2 review's sole Azure finding is repaired with red/green proof; final full-candidate independent review completed scoped-clean at P0–P2 with source verification passing.

Qualified package-boundary typechecking is unavailable locally without generated SDK declarations. Exact-head PR CI owns broad/type-aware proof; no broad local build, whole-graph typecheck, full check-changed or E2E suite was run. No operator Gateway or real OpenClaw state was touched.

CI repair: run 39359782741 found a type-aware test lint error in the new Azure route assertion (`String()` on a possible `Request`). The assertion now reads `Request.url` or the URL/string representation explicitly, keeping the exact expected routes. All 19 Azure tests plus 14 suppression checks passed in 13.83 seconds; focused syntax lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Independent incremental P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. This changes no production behavior or production LOC; the repaired exact head still needs hosted CI. No CI rerun was requested.
