prs.title: fix(feishu): reject synthetic reply anchors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In OpenClaw 2026.10.5, a Feishu send triggered by an internal session event can attach the event UUID as an implicit `replyToId`. The Feishu reply API only accepts native `om_...` message IDs, so the send fails with HTTP 400 / `99992354` and the message is silently lost. This fixes the anchor at the Feishu context boundary: synthetic IDs are rejected, while valid `om_` replies and topic/thread routing are preserved.

## Evidence

### Production behavior before the fix

- OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (`1b58cb9`), Feishu websocket channel, topic-style group (`groupSessionScope=group_topic`, `replyInThread=enabled`).
- 2026-10-19 07:37:35 UTC: user asks a long analysis task in a Feishu topic. The captured delivery route has `to=chat:oc_…` and `threadId=om_x…`.
- 07:39:39 UTC: streaming acknowledgement card closes; `dispatch complete (replies=1)`.
- 08:04:18 UTC: a background `exec` completion is delivered through `session-event-handoff`. Model calls return 200, then:
  - `POST https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/im/v1/messages/855a9b56-…/reply`
  - HTTP 400, `code=99992354` — "not a valid {open_message_id}"
  - `completion delivery failed (Error: Failed to route reply to feishu: Feishu card reply failed: ...)`
- 08:09 UTC: a later notification sent through the normal send path succeeds. The user sees only that last message; the analysis result is lost.

### Root cause

`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts` (added in v2026.10.5 by #167113) dispatches immediate notifications through ordinary session execution and sets `MessageSid: occurrence.id` (line 438), so the internal event UUID becomes the generic trigger ID.

The shared threading owner falls back to that ID because Feishu's threading adapter did not return `currentMessageId`. The final reply then carries the UUID as `replyToId`; Feishu's reply mode resolver prefers `replyToId` over the valid `threadId`. The reply API rejects it, and the existing fallback only recognizes withdrawn/not-found codes `230011` / `231003`, not `99992354`, so the message is dropped.

Before v2026.10.5 the `session-event-handoff.ts` file did not exist (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 753a7a57be1 v2026.10.4` is false), and the gateway journal showed no `99992354` failures. The Feishu send/reply logic is unchanged since 2026-08-18; this change fixes the channel boundary that the new core path exposes.

### Fix

- `extensions/feishu/src/threading.ts` / `threading-reply.ts`:
  - `buildToolContext` now returns `currentMessageId` only for native `om_...` IDs. The explicit `undefined` tells the shared owner to reject the generic trigger-ID fallback.
  - New `resolveReplyTransport` drops synthetic/non-`om_` reply targets (`replyToId: null`) while returning the original `threadId`, so the final reply still lands in the topic/thread; valid native `om_` targets are kept.
- Extracted the threading adapter into `threading.ts` to respect the repository's line-cap ratchet.
- Tests: `channel.threading.test.ts`, plus a core regression in `agent-runner-utils.test.ts` proving an adapter's explicit `undefined` wins over the generic fallback.

### Verification after the fix

- `pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/channel.threading.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/channel.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/outbound.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 153 passed
- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 11 passed
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check ...` → clean
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/feishu/tsconfig.json ...` → 0 warnings/errors
- `tsc -p extensions/feishu/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → clean
  (`pnpm tsgo:extensions` is blocked on this host by glibc 2.31 vs the prebuilt `tsrs` binary's GLIBC_2.32+ requirement)

## Behavior after the fix

- A completion/session event with an internal UUID no longer produces a `replyToId`; the message is delivered via the existing thread route (or as a normal message when no thread exists) instead of failing with 400.
- Normal inbound replies keep their native `om_...` anchors.
- Explicit native `replyTo` targets and topic/thread routing are unchanged.
- No config or migration changes.

## Related

- Fixes #167270 (same root cause; this report adds the 2026.10.5 exec-completion production path).
- Earlier attempts #167394 and #167425 were closed for lack of a reproducible production ingress; this report includes the live gateway timeline and the version boundary above.


## Review follow-up (`e67f806`)

- **Topic placement is preserved.** `resolveFeishuTopicAutoThreadAnchor` now takes the anchor from `currentMessageId` only when it is a native `om_...` id, otherwise from the retained native topic root (`currentThreadTs`); non-native roots are still rejected. The selector moved to `extensions/feishu/src/topic-anchors.ts` to respect the line-cap ratchet, and the message-tool send path is covered in `extensions/feishu/src/channel.topic-routing.test.ts`.
- **Removed the duplicated core test.** `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts` no longer carries the mocked-provider case; `reply-plumbing.test.ts` already proves that an adapter's explicit `undefined` suppresses the generic fallback.

The new synthetic-trigger send assertion fails on `6c8f62b` (the send has no `threadId`) and passes on `e67f806`. `tsc -p extensions/feishu/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, oxlint, oxfmt, and `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --staged` are clean.

prs.title: refactor(agents): publish workspace cache invalidation directly
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspace-state commits serialize setup rows, alias rows, complete hash sets and tombstones, but their only production subscriber merely checks whether any fact exists and invalidates the entire database projection. Attestation also duplicates the host dispatch/admission owner, and expiry maintains a cache-only settlement promise despite having native COMMIT receipts.

## What changed

- Publish one dirty marker instead of unused row/hash payloads, removing SQL RETURNING clauses used only to construct those payloads.
- Route the already-existing attestation worker command through the shared workspace operation owner. Preserve input capture, legacy callbacks, recovery holds and live authority; attestation retains its existing absence of filesystem-content guarding.
- Retire expired workspace file caches synchronously from acknowledged native COMMIT facts. Register this observer before projection publication, so later publication/reply failure cannot suppress known-commit invalidation. The existing database owner still joins accepted writes and retains FIFO settlement.
- Validate timestamps at the canonical worker/kernel boundary instead of repeating the same checks on the host. Keep persisted-row, filename/hash, alias, filesystem and deletion validation.

No schema, stored shape, permission, retention, public protocol or SDK signature changes. The receipt lifecycle, first-writer milestones, vanished-workspace protection, rollback, lost-reply recovery and ordinary restart durability remain.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Invalid timestamps now fail at the worker's existing pre-mutation validation; the host may open the state backend before reporting that error. The duplicate host checks came from the worker migration in #163496, not a separate human-reported requirement. Invalid timestamps still cannot mutate workspace rows.
- Detailed internal receipt payloads introduced by #168094 are not retained for hypothetical future consumers. The sole current consumer uses nonempty facts for invalidation; active receipt/authority/lost-reply machinery remains intact. A future row projection would need to add the facts it actually consumes.
- Successful upserts invalidate without checking a returned row. These owned statements insert or update; an unsupported external trigger suppressing a write would now cause an unnecessary reload, not invented cached state.

The expiry change is not a relaxation of write settlement: it replaces a cache-only completion bridge from #163496 with the native COMMIT observer already used by the publication owner. No live-authority or durability guard is removed.

## Size

Production: **100 net lines removed** (+72 / -172), across five production files. Tests: +13 / -16. This is a completed-owner residue under campaign rule 14, **not a LARGE PR**.

## Evidence

- Final focused owner suites: 34/34 passed, covering cache work-count reuse, native/worker writes, rollback, late recovery holds, revoked authority, lost replies, FIFO/close settlement, aliases, captured input and restart disappearance protection. Command wall 188.51 s including compilation; Vitest phase 56.02 s. The changed store suite exercises actual persisted state and worker lifecycle rather than mocks.
- Targeted five-root production types, scoped six-file lint, format and diff checks passed.
- Lint-suppression and native wrapper import-closure checks: 17/17 passed (21.43 s wall).
- Final independent review through P2 found no actionable defects. An earlier alleged missing recovery predicate was rejected by source evidence: the shared helper adds it from operation options, and attestation passes its parameters as those options.
- Runtime and static import-cycle checks both passed with zero cycles. Changed-check dry-run selected core/coreTests; its broad execution is deferred to exact-head hosted CI. No local full suite, build or E2E; PR CI is the broad gate under the campaign CPU budget.

The two changed tests now assert persisted alias timestamps, complete hash replacement and deletion results instead of unused private receipt payloads. Other behavior coverage is unchanged. No performance/latency claim.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve whitespace in node-host exec workdir paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Running a `system.run` command on a node host with a `workdir` whose name legitimately ends in whitespace (e.g. `/srv/data `) silently executed the command in a different directory (`/srv/data`).

- **Problem:** The node-host workdir flowed through `normalizeXxxString` calls that trim whitespace. The plan normalizer, approval binding/context resolvers, `resolveExecutablePathCandidate`, and `collectAllowAlwaysPatterns` all re-trimmed cwd, so a preserved-whitespace value was trimmed before reaching `child_process.spawn`'s `options.cwd`, and the plan-match check broke.
- **Solution:** Switch all cwd read sites on the node-execution path to `readNonBlankString` (preserves whitespace, rejects blank). Files: `bash-tools.exec-workdir.ts`, `invoke-system-run-plan.ts`, `invoke-system-run.ts`, `system-run-approval-plan.ts`, `system-run-approval-binding.ts`, `system-run-approval-context.ts`, `system-run-normalize.ts`, `executable-path.ts`, `exec-approvals-allowlist.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fixing only the cwd read sites was cancelled out by downstream trimming. `resolveExecutablePathCandidate` trimmed cwd before pinning `./tool`. `collectAllowAlwaysPatterns` trimmed cwd for grant hashing, scoping persisted authorization to the wrong directory — a security concern where approval for `/srv/data` could authorize `/srv/data ` or vice versa.

## User Impact

Commands on a node host whose working directory name contains leading or trailing whitespace now execute in the intended directory. Relative executables resolve correctly. Approval bindings and reusable grants distinguish whitespace-distinct paths, preventing cross-directory approval reuse. Non-whitespace paths are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Gateway-level proof (running Gateway kernel + real `child_process.spawn`)

| Scenario | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Authorized spawn in `data ` | `allowlist miss` ❌ | `ok: true`, stdout: `from-space-dir` ✅ |
| 2. Sibling grant rejected (grant `data`, launch `data `) | `ok: true` ❌ (cross-dir) | `allowlist miss` ✅ |
| 3. Revocation after launch (grant → ok → revoke → denied) | always `miss` ❌ | `ok: true` → `allowlist miss` ✅ |
| 4. Plan-match rejects mismatched cwd | `ok: true` ❌ | `approval requires matching plan` ✅ |
| 5. Record→replay→launch | plan cwd trimmed ❌ | plan cwd preserved, spawn ok ✅ |

RED on main: all 5 fail. GREEN after fix: all 5 pass.

### Cancelled approval replayed through node.invoke (terminal output)

Per review: a previously allowed, unconsumed recorded approval is cancelled via `forceDenyDetailed(cancelled)`, then replayed through the production `node.invoke(system.run)` guard (`sanitizeSystemRunParamsForForwarding`). The guard calls `consumeAllowOnce` which returns false — no process spawns.

```
--- Scenario 1: Cancelled approval, node.invoke guard rejects ---
[1] Creating approval (allow-once, unconsumed)...
  [create] record id=cancel-mvau0ndz cwd="/tmp/test-data " host=node
  [resolve] allow-once: ok=true (allowed, unconsumed)
[1] Approval id=cancel-mvau0ndz, decision=allow-once (allowed, unconsumed)
[1] Cancelling via forceDenyDetailed(cancelled)...
[1] Cancel outcome=already-terminal
[1] Snapshot: status=allowed decision=allow-once
[1] Sending node.invoke(system.run) approved=true runId=cancel-mvau0ndz...
[1] Guard result: ok=false code=APPROVAL_REQUIRED message=approval required
VERDICT 1: PASS — cancelled approval rejected before spawn

--- Scenario 2 (control): Valid allow-once, node.invoke guard passes ---
[2] Creating approval (allow-once, unconsumed)...
  [create] record id=valid-mvau0ql0 cwd="/tmp/test-data " host=node
  [resolve] allow-once: ok=true (allowed, unconsumed)
[2] Sending node.invoke(system.run) approved=true runId=valid-mvau0ql0...
[2] Guard result: ok=true approved=true
VERDICT 2: PASS — valid approval forwarded, spawn authorized

Chain: ExecApprovalManager.create → register → resolve(allow-once)
  → forceDenyDetailed(cancelled) sets approvalAuthority=()=>false
  → node.invoke guard: sanitizeSystemRunParamsForForwarding
  → consumeAllowOnce → isExecApprovalRuntimeActive=false → APPROVAL_REQUIRED
```

### Recorded-approval revocation + sibling-redirection (running Gateway, terminal output)

```
A.1 First spawn (allowed, cwd="data "):
  spawn code=0 stdout="from-space-dir" → PASS
A.2 Second spawn (authority consumed):
  ok=false error=APPROVAL_REQUIRED → PASS

B.1 Sibling cwd (request cwd='data', approval for 'data '):
  spawn cwd redirected to approved "data " → stdout="from-space-dir" → PASS

C.1 Denied authority:
  ok=false error=APPROVAL_REQUIRED → PASS (denied before spawn)

Overall: ALL PASS ✅
```

### Data-model compatibility (v2026.10.4 → candidate, binary replacement)

Manually swapped stable v2026.10.4 → candidate binaries loading the **same SQLite state**:

```
PASS (a) candidate loads stable SQLite — schema migration ok, Gateway ready
PASS (b) config preserved — openclaw.json intact
PASS (c) candidate creates approval on same store — ok=true
PASS (d) candidate reads grants from same store — ok=true
PASS (e) non-ws cwd grant hash identical — SHA-256 match (backward compat)
Overall: ALL PASS — existing data loads and works after upgrade
```

### Regression tests

```
exec-approvals-allow-always.test.ts: 44 passed
executable-path.test.ts: 34 passed | 2 skipped
invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts: 25 passed
system-run-approval-binding.test.ts: 33 passed
```

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor/setup can fail with `EXDEV` when an image-installed plugin's native companions and the OpenClaw home are on different filesystems.

## User Impact

Container users with a separate home/state mount can capture image-installed native plugin companions without the cross-device hardlink failure. No state-directory move, database migration, configuration bypass, or plugin disablement is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native companion capture now checks the source and capture devices before choosing a hardlink. A device mismatch selects the existing guarded copy owner. Same-device hardlinks and the restricted retained-NPM reference fallback are unchanged; source-boundary, destination-identity, content, and admission checks remain in place.

This is candidate-side capture behavior. Already-installed update/Doctor drivers retain their shipped behavior until replaced. The change adds no new flags or schema and does not weaken Doctor action authority. The complete diff is two production lines plus one 36-line regression in the existing artifact suite.

## Evidence

Real Linux red/green proof through `preparePluginNativeAdmissions` and `capturePluginGenerationArtifact`, not a mocked `fs.linkSync` failure:

- Baseline: upstream `07e3328ed3f74333e80072af207890204c82fec4` plus the new regression. **9 passed, 1 failed**; the only failure was the new case, with the actual kernel `EXDEV` at `README.md` in `linkPluginSourceFile`.
- Fixed: `50b6318585f2e06bc3fac4d0188d492599b981d2`. **10 passed, 0 skipped**, including the existing same-device, restricted fallback, host mismatch, recovery, and storage-placement cases. The normal commit hook preserved the tested source bytes.
- Linux x86_64 under Docker Desktop/Rosetta, Node `26.11.1`, pnpm `12.12.1`, UID/GID `1000`, network disabled during execution. The synthetic image fixture was on overlayfs (`st_dev=185`); the isolated state home was on `/dev/shm` tmpfs (`st_dev=249`). The regression asserts the devices differ, native bytes and the companion text survive, the captured file is on the state device, the source link count remains one, and the captured realpath is not the source.

Command used for both runs (separate invocation-owned transform-cache paths):

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.native-reference.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

Shortened synthetic paths in the baseline failure:

```text
captures image-installed native companions into a home on another filesystem
EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted, link
  <image fixture>/README.md -> /dev/shm/<state>/tmp/plugin-captures/.../content/README.md
Tests  1 failed | 9 passed (10)

Fixed:
Tests  10 passed (10)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 235.22s
```

Cost: fixed file duration `226.07s`, wrapper `235.22s`, external wall `239.61s` on this emulated host; the new case took `8.681s`. The existing real persistence cases took roughly 29–36 seconds each, and worker preparation took `53.596s`. This is a focused artifact/admission integration contract, not a performance benchmark; no sleeps, retries, or broader mocks were added. PR CI seconds are pending.

Additional checks passed on the same fixed source:

- Production core types: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`.
- Targeted maintained oxlint: zero warnings/errors on the two changed files.
- Maintained formatter check and normal pre-commit hooks.
- `git diff --check`; frozen lockfile unchanged.

Limits: this proves the complete artifact-capture boundary with synthetic native bytes and real filesystem devices. It does **not** claim an installed-package/full-Doctor run, native `dlopen`, all-plugin coverage, or live customer rollout qualification. No live state, release packages, or deployments were changed for this proof.

prs.title: refactor(plugins): remove duplicate lifecycle and recording owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several plugins still maintain a second owner or derived report after their consumer moved elsewhere. Matrix QA is the largest example: the QA Lab migration removed the manifest writer and scenario attribution calls, but retained the entire manifest, body-shape, sync-token and retry-analysis engine. The surviving media scenario only counts completed uploads.

## What changed

Reduce Matrix QA recording to normalized method/route/status observations, retaining the unchanged native-media YAML oracle, route normalization, fault injection, target switching, forwarding and shutdown. Delete its orphaned exchange-context hook. Remove orphaned parity-report statistics while keeping exact parity classification and failure precedence.

Delegate Nostr durable admission, LINE handoff settlement, and Nextcloud admission tracking to their existing SDK owners. Remove unread Nostr relay health scores, retaining circuit breakers and fallback; prefer the last successful relay. Use Feishu's existing SDK account selector and remove unread selection labels. Matrix DM classification consumes the identity already supplied by its callers. Browser HTTP requests use the guarded fetch owner's existing timeout composition. MSTeams stops writing an unread duplicate learning store; the actual reflection turn still persists in the original session. Mantis keeps its recovery lease markers, command settlement, recording parameters and deletion authority while dropping unread output copies and requiring the ownership receipt every real caller already supplies.

Eight plugins; 42 files; **974 net production lines removed** (+132/-1,106). Test/support changes are counted separately. No public config, SDK, protocol, schema, retention or dependency changes. Existing persisted learning rows and Doctor migration remain untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Matrix manifest, body-shape, token-continuity, retry and scenario-attribution projections are no longer produced internally. Original #100039 implemented feature proposal #100038, not an actual-use incident; migration #103589 (`ad34552473633`) removed their writer, docs and scenario callers. The retained upload oracle sees completed exchanges in completion order; it requires counts, not invocation ordering.
- QA parity no longer computes unread token estimates, statistics, delta envelopes or first-drift metadata. `c6aa8e74236f7` removed the renderer consuming them; exact prompt/tool/schema hashes, comparison modes and failure precedence remain.
- Nostr no longer ranks relays using lifetime/latency/recency scores from the original feature (`7b6cbf58697c4`); there is no measured win or human failure report requiring that projection. The last working relay stays preferred until it fails; breakers and sequential fallback remain.
- Nostr's speculative duplicate admission retry/drain queue is removed. Existing SDK admission owns its bounded retry policy, accepted append and stop settlement. Input validation, queue/rate bounds, first-failure latch and cursor-before-dispatch remain.
- LINE/Nextcloud no longer track the same accepted work twice. Existing ingress owners retain FIFO, deferred claims, migration-time admission and ordinary shutdown settlement. No write-capable shutdown contract is relaxed.
- Browser's duplicate timer/controller is removed. The SDK timeout begins after its own preparation, accepting that small timing difference; the real first-call startup fix #174755, abort input, response bounds and dispatcher release remain.
- Feishu no longer reports an unread selection-source label or repeats SDK selection policy. Authored-key mapping and credential/tool policy from #174809 remain. Matrix DM identity cannot fall back through a private cache: both production callers already supply the authoritative identity.
- MSTeams no longer writes the unread `feedback-learnings` copy introduced by #51808. Canonical reflection still dispatches into the original session and persists that turn; follow-ups/cooldown and historical rows are retained.
- Mantis no longer copies unread stdout/stderr into a private WeakMap or supports cleanup without a receipt that no real caller omits. Real warmup-abort lease recovery from #171482, original abort errors, full success output, stderr errors, inode/symlink checks and all write-capable work settlement remain.

## Evidence

- Initial QA parity/Nostr focused proof: 101 tests passed. Browser owner proof: 44 tests across six files passed.
- Continued account/spool/Matrix/MSTeams/Mantis owner proof: 178 tests across 21 files passed. All kept FIFO, migration-time admission, accepted-before-stop and cleanup tests remain.
- Matrix recorder/fault transport/harness plus Mantis visual, desktop-browser and Slack-desktop siblings: 69 tests across seven files passed in 37.21 seconds Vitest wall time. Loopback HTTP exercises native upload counting, exact minimal observations, normalization, fault removal, upstream errors, binary forwarding, origin/request/response bounds, and observer-error settlement. This is synthetic production-path proof, not live-channel acceptance.
- Scoped cycle checks: 1,497 production files for the continued cut and 519 QA/Nostr files for the initial cut; zero runtime cycles or new static components against the pinned base.
- Changed-file syntax lint and formatting pass; `git diff --check` passes. Assertion allowances shrink only: Feishu 3→2, retired recorder 1→0.
- All 14 required lint-suppression tests pass, 14.55 seconds wrapper wall time.
- Independent P0–P2 review completed scoped-clean with final source verification. The simplify pass retained one recorder and existing lifecycle/selection owners; no replacement abstraction was added.
- Initial exact-head CI exposed two attributable defects: Nextcloud Talk omitted the SDK-required synchronous `inspect` option alongside its asynchronous migration barrier; the Nostr Gateway test recorder observed `enqueue` but missed the SDK's real `enqueueAndClaim` admission path. Supply the required option and observe both real queue operations without changing their results. The repair replay passed all 45 Nostr/Nextcloud owner tests and all 14 suppression checks in 159.53 seconds wrapper wall time. No assertions, timeouts or retries were weakened.
- The PR-context check required the canonical authored section headings; this body now uses `What Problem This Solves` and `Evidence`.
- Repair head `b3c358ca0e1eee5ddb489fb1585a74ed68f1bd89`: fresh independent P0–P2 incremental review is scoped-clean with final source verification; both changed files pass focused syntax lint, formatting and `git diff --check`. Fresh exact-head CI is attached and pending; no green claim or rerun.

Qualified local package-boundary typechecking is unavailable without generated SDK declarations; exact-head hosted PR CI is the broad/type-aware gate. No broad local build, suite or whole-graph typecheck was run on the shared host.

prs.title: fix(workers): prevent attachment after caller authority closes
prs.body:
Related: #135838

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a cancelled or replaced dispatch attaching a worker and persisting a credential after its caller loses authority while waiting for the attachment queue or installation packaging.

## User Impact

- A closed caller cannot attach a worker after queue, packaging, or database-admission waits. A different live caller can still succeed.
- An attachment that already committed stays committed; cleanup of the previous tunnel epoch is joined before the existing credential response returns.
- No configuration, wire protocol, database-schema migration, public SDK change, or legacy-provider cutoff. This is the small attachment slice, not completion of the broader #135838 workstream.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the dispatch owner's existing assertion into the credential broker for both cold and prepared attachments. The broker composes it with service and prepared-placement authority, then carries that assertion into the existing native final-COMMIT admission. Postcommit custody and cleanup remain independent of the initiating caller; there is no new authority or persistence owner.

Contributor credit: @sallyom and @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @sallyom](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/70f8933b-db6b-4809-b9a8-941957263614)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/975070a4-9db3-41be-9ca5-c1b9d675d7ac)
- [Current-main refresh and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/759dece0-a599-40b4-9c13-84b15547b58e)

## Evidence

### October 20 current-main refresh

Reviewed candidate: `fdae9a040983406ce86a314ac2e0a081c90e46c4`, based on main `353c6989892e6f01ff7ff63931eb30da58cd99e4`. Resolved the credential-broker conflict while preserving main's service-error and turn-credential refactors. Updated the asynchronous dispatch harness and now-unconditional reader reuse. A later main advance to `dcd48b6aa5f2e68ef1a185872b4ad305e9172963` changes only two UI model-setup files; the refreshed candidate composes with it without conflicts. Removed the obsolete transaction-stage handshake case rather than restoring that retired boundary; the actual native final-COMMIT refusal and rollback/reopen proof remain.

- **Regression:** the seven current cases produce **six intended behavioral failures and one passing committed-custody control** without the production fix; **all seven pass** with it. This covers queued and packaging revocation, service shutdown, final native COMMIT refusal with persisted state checked after reopen, independent callers, cold dispatch forwarding, and joined postcommit tunnel cleanup.
- **Compatibility suites:** 174 passed and two recovery assertions failed across six sibling files. Both failures also reproduce with the PR's two production files and the device-test expectation restored to main, using the same six-file command and order; details below. No test was suppressed or weakened to hide them.
- **Static checks:** core production and gateway-other test typechecks passed; targeted lint reported zero errors/warnings; formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The normal commit hook passed, preserving both human coauthor trailers.
- **Independent canonical review:** scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings. Existing unguarded internal callers remain supported by the optional assertion; credential hashing, lifetime, owner epochs, delivery shape, worker protocol, configuration, and stored formats are unchanged.

The proof uses the real service, credential broker, delegated-authority registry, worker-backed SQLite admission/rollback/reopen, and tunnel lifecycle owner with controlled external boundaries. It is not a live cloud-allocation, external SSH-server, or installed-upgrade test. Exact-head public CI and required reviews remain landing gates; this refresh does not merge the PR.

<summary>Commands, inherited recovery failures, and test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/credential-attachment-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Process wall: baseline 30.08 s; fixed 30.75 s. The fixed final-COMMIT case took 600 ms. These are correctness runs with different stopping points, not a performance comparison. Current-head CI seconds were not yet available when these local checks completed.

prs.title: fix: activate a plugin when a configured provider endpoint matches its manifest
prs.body:
Related to #171853

## What Problem This Solves

Configuring a custom provider that points at a DashScope (Alibaba Model Studio) base
URL did not turn on the Qwen plugin, so the endpoint's runtime behavior (provider
failover classification, thinking handling) only applied once the plugin happened to
be enabled for some other reason.

Fixes: a plugin is now activated when the base URL of a configured provider matches an
endpoint that plugin's manifest declares.

- Problem: plugin auto-enable matched a configured provider only by *provider id*
  (`autoEnableWhenConfiguredProviders`) or by a configured model ref. A custom id such
  as `custom-dashscope` matched neither, even though its base URL is declared by the
  Qwen manifest under `providerEndpoints` (`modelstudio-native`).
- Solution: `resolveConfiguredPluginAutoEnableCandidates()` now also considers
  configured provider *endpoints*, via a new candidate kind
  `provider-endpoint-configured`.
- What changed: `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.shared.ts` (new
  `resolveConfiguredProviderEndpointCandidates()`),
  `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.types.ts` (candidate kind),
  `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.materialize.ts` (reason string),
  `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.test-helpers.ts` (fixture support for
  `providerEndpoints`), plus a new owner test.
- What did NOT change: `wrapQwenProviderStream` (`extensions/qwen/stream.ts`) still
  returns early for provider ids that `isQwenProviderId` does not hard-code. Gap 2 of
  the issue (thinking-payload translation for custom ids) needs the small design the
  issue asks for and is deliberately out of scope here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The activation planner is the only place that decides whether a plugin gets turned on,
and it already had the manifest endpoint declarations available; it simply never read
them.

- Best fix: reuse the shared endpoint matcher
  (`matchesPluginProviderEndpoint` / `normalizePluginProviderBaseUrl`) that
  `provider-config-owner.ts`, `provider-attribution.ts` and
  `manifest-model-suppression.ts` already consume, instead of introducing a second
  notion of "this base URL is DashScope".
- Alternative rejected: hard-coding DashScope hosts in the config layer duplicates
  manifest data, can drift from the manifest, and would not generalize to the other
  native endpoint classes the matcher already understands.
- Precedence: a provider id that a plugin already registers keeps the existing
  id-based activation and reason string; the endpoint path only fills the gap for
  custom ids, which mirrors how runtime hook selection already prefers exact ids.
- Risk / non-goals: activation is additive and only reads public config
  (`models.providers.<id>.baseUrl`). No auth, allowlist, or trust decision changes;
  disabling a plugin still wins over auto-enable.

## User Impact

A custom provider on a declared DashScope endpoint now behaves like the built-in
`dashscope`/`qwen` providers from the first request, without preloading the Qwen
plugin. Users who relied on the plugin staying off must keep disabling it explicitly,
exactly as for the built-in provider ids that already auto-enable.

## Evidence

Observed result - the new owner test goes red before the source change and green after:

```text
# before (resolveConfiguredProviderEndpointCandidates not yet wired in)
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run .../plugin-auto-enable.provider-endpoints.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 × activates the endpoint owner for a custom provider id 454ms
 ✓ keeps an exact registered provider id on its id-based reason 32ms
 ✓ leaves a custom provider id without a declared endpoint alone 11ms
 × matches a declared host suffix for a custom provider id 11ms
AssertionError: expected undefined to be true // Object.is equality
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)

# after
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/plugin-auto-enable --maxWorkers=1
 ✓ activates the endpoint owner for a custom provider id 388ms
 ✓ keeps an exact registered provider id on its id-based reason 3ms
 ✓ leaves a custom provider id without a declared endpoint alone 2ms
 ✓ matches a declared host suffix for a custom provider id 2ms
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  68 passed (68)
```

Input to output matrix (new test, `runtime-config` project):

| configured `models.providers` entry | declared endpoint | plugin enabled | reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `custom-dashscope` -> `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` | `baseUrls` match | yes | `custom-dashscope provider endpoint configured` |
| `dashscope` (id registered by the plugin) | `baseUrls` match | yes | `dashscope auth configured` (id path, unchanged) |
| `custom-endpoint` -> `https://llm.example.test/v1` | no match | no | - |
| `custom-intl` -> `https://team.dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` | `hostSuffixes` match | yes | `custom-intl provider endpoint configured` |

Also checked: `oxlint` (repo config) and `oxfmt --check` are clean on all five files.

What was not tested: no live Gateway run against a real DashScope endpoint was
performed; the evidence is the shipped activation entry point under the repository
test harness plus the existing 68-test owner suite.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `grep`/`git log` to trace the auto-enable candidate
pipeline and the existing endpoint-matching consumers, then implemented the fix and
the owner test in the local checkout. The implementer understands the code: the new
branch of the planner maps a configured provider base URL to the manifest-declared
endpoint owner, skipping ids that are already registered so existing id-based
activation reasons are unchanged. All evidence above is from real local execution.

prs.title: fix(cron): session maintenance reports a failure when sessions change mid-sweep
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: cron session maintenance logs a failure when a session is deleted or the session registry changes while the sweep is reading it.

## User Impact

User impact: that case is now logged as a deferred sweep with the retry time and the last successful sweep, and the next scheduled run, within 60 seconds, picks it up with fresh data. Unknown errors are still reported as failures, and a completed sweep logs its result.

## Why This Change Was Made

A snapshot invalidation during registry maintenance is an expected race with live session changes, not a fault. The maintenance owner now classifies it as a deferred read (`retryAtMs`, `lastSuccessAtMs`). The existing scheduler retries with fresh facts and never replays work a consumer has already entered.

## Evidence

- Published-driver update: in a disposable container, the published npm `latest` driver (2026.10.5) updated to a candidate packed from all six fixes together (commit `3331e8d12be`): update finished, `readyz` 200, running version verified, durable and incognito session data unchanged.
- Cron maintenance tests cover deletion and registry invalidation (deferred, with retry facts), unknown errors (still failed) and the completion log.
- Snapshot-owner and cron suites pass locally; independent API-only review found no P0–P2 issues.

prs.title: fix: contain bounded seed observer failures
prs.body:
## Summary

- Treat the bounded-seed `context_bounded` event as advisory: contain synchronous throws and rejected promises from the host observer, log the failure, and still return the bounded history.
- Preserve the existing awaited ordering and the authority assertion that follows the notification.
- Add regression coverage for both synchronous throws and rejected promises while history remains truncated after compaction.

Closes #177416

## Root cause

`prepareBoundedSeed` awaited `attempt.onAgentEvent` directly when `cut > 0`. Unlike the other observer paths in the harness, that call was not contained, so an observer failure rejected seed preparation and aborted the turn before the model call.

## Validation

Base-red proof: with only the `try/catch` temporarily reverted, both new cases fail on the unchanged source:

```text
× synchronous observer failure is contained  → observer failed
× rejected observer failure is contained     → observer failed
❯ prepare src/agents/harness/host-seed.ts:282:21
Tests  2 failed | 15 skipped (17)
```

Head-green results:

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/agents/harness/host-seed.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       17 passed (17)

OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.history-seed.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       15 passed (15)
```

Additional checks:

- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json src/agents/harness/host-seed.ts src/agents/harness/host-seed.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/harness/host-seed.ts src/agents/harness/host-seed.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit --pretty false` (exit 0)
- `git diff --check`

## Scope and limitations

The regression injects the failure at the advisory observer boundary. It does not make a live model/provider or Gateway call, and does not require external credentials. No external behavior is claimed beyond containing the observer failure and returning the bounded seed.

AI-assisted: yes


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a fresh native turn can fail before the model call when bounded-seed history is truncated and the advisory `context_bounded` host observer throws or rejects.

## User Impact

Fresh native turns continue with bounded history after a non-authoritative observer failure; the failure is logged instead of aborting preparation.

## Evidence

- Base-red proof: with the containment temporarily reverted, both new cases fail on unchanged source with `observer failed`; `2 failed | 15 skipped`.
- Head-green proof: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test src/agents/harness/host-seed.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 17/17 tests.
- Native history suite: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.history-seed.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 15/15 tests.
- Additional checks: focused `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit`, and `git diff --check` all passed.
- Scope and limitation: the failure is injected at the built-in harness observer boundary. There is no shipped CLI or Gateway option that supplies a throwing `attempt.onAgentEvent`, so this revision does not include a live provider or Gateway trace; producing one requires a test/debug injection seam or a real host callback failure.

prs.title: feat(cli): add pairing dismiss for pending DM requests
prs.body:
Closes #177870

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw pairing` exposes only `list` and `approve`, so an operator cannot remove a single pending DM pairing request from the CLI. The Control UI and the `channels.pairing.dismiss` RPC already support dismissal, but a headless or scripted operator can only approve the request or wait out the one-hour pending TTL. This adds `openclaw pairing dismiss <channel> <code>`: it deletes exactly the named pending request, works with no Gateway running via exclusive offline ownership, and reports an unknown code with an actionable error instead of a generic CLI failure.

## User Impact

Operators can now drop an unwanted or abandoned DM pairing request from the CLI without granting access, and scripts can dismiss deterministically. Existing `list` and `approve` behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI resolves the human pairing code through the existing CLI-shaped `channels.pairing.list` owner route (codes are what `pairing list` shows; the opaque `requestId` is not exposed there), then deletes that exact row through the existing `channels.pairing.dismiss` method with the computed opaque request id. Both calls go through `runWithLocalStateOwner`, so the command uses the owning Gateway when one is running and holds exclusive offline ownership otherwise. If the row disappears between the lookup and the delete, the command fails with the same actionable "No pending pairing request found for code ..." error.

Production changes are deliberately small:

- **`src/cli/pairing-cli.ts`**: the `dismiss` command, reusing `parseChannel`, `resolveAccountId`, and a shared `<channel> <code>`/`--channel <channel> <code>` argument helper extracted from `approve` (so the two commands cannot drift). Unknown codes throw `ExpectedCliError`, which the root CLI renders verbatim (plain `Error` is rendered as a generic "The CLI command failed.").
- **`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/channel-pairing.ts`**: add the optional `expectedOwnerId` field to `ChannelsPairingDismissParamsSchema`. `runWithLocalStateOwner` always injects this field into Gateway-dispatched params, and the schema is a closed object, so without it every CLI dismiss against a running Gateway is rejected by validation. Additive only; UI callers and the existing handler contract are unchanged.
- **`src/pairing/pairing-store.ts`**: add optional `assertCurrent` to `dismissChannelPairingRequest`, forwarded to the existing mutation admission, so the CLI's exclusive-ownership guard is revalidated before the SQL delete. No new store logic or state.

No new config option, flag, dependency, RPC method, capability, or protocol version bump. A dedicated CLI dismiss capability was considered but rejected: it would require advertising it in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.ts` plus a new server-side guard, adding files and behavior without changing the outcome; the existing method already requires `operator.pairing` (the CLI connects with the `operator.admin` superset), and `runWithLocalStateOwner` revalidates the owner immediately before dispatch.

Classification: `behavior-completing`.

## Evidence

### Proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `2c1045596c6741dd69ab6fb364b1af1fe5e6949c`
- Base SHA: `fd12f93cf4fd2cec0ce03be8f183a9dd1b41809e`
- Production entry: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts pairing ...` from source with `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-pairing-proof3`

- Decision surface: `pairing dismiss <channel> <code>`
- Readback: process exit code, `pairing list` output, and the real SQLite table `channel_pairing_requests`
- No Gateway was running for this state directory: zero `*.lock`/owner files under the state root before and after every run
- Cleanup: isolated `/tmp/oc-pairing-proof3` only; no production Gateway, session, token, channel, or config was touched

### Tests

`src/cli/pairing-cli.test.ts` extended (not duplicated) with 7 dismiss cases: positional/option/sole-channel argument routing, exact request-id deletion, `--account` forwarding, unknown code, row disappearing between lookup and delete, usage, and too-many-arguments.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/pairing-cli.test.ts
```

- Base production + new test: **7 failed | 13 passed** (20) in 38.9s wall; all seven dismiss cases fail with Commander's `process.exit` on the missing subcommand.
- Exact head: **20 passed** (20) in 3m22.8s wall (transform-bound cold cache: 97% transform). A prior head run was 3m35.8s.
- The base tree had a warm transform cache and the head run did not; the difference is transform time, not test work.

### Checks

- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit`: no errors in touched files. Remaining 8 errors are in untouched files: `src/agents/mcp-json-schema-validator.ts` (missing `fast-uri` in this shared install) and `src/process/darwin-process-inspection.ts` (Darwin-only typings on Linux).
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json --noEmit`: no errors in `pairing-cli.test.ts`; same 8 pre-existing/environmental errors.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on all five touched files: all formatted.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- Not run: `pnpm lint`/oxlint. The wrapper aborts on a stale `.artifacts/dist-artifacts.lock` in this worktree, and direct oxlint cannot load the repo's `tools/solid-lint` JS plugin because `eslint-plugin-solid` is absent from the shared install. This is an environment limitation, not a suppressed lint result.

### CI repair on head `ef4c2ff7c3c`

`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` flagged the pairing-store mock in this test file (it grew from two to four stubbed exports, so it stopped matching its grandfathered baseline entry):

```
src/cli/pairing-cli.test.ts: ../pairing/pairing-store.js
First-party mock factories must preserve real exports or explain isolation
```

The CLI fixtures must not open the pairing state DB, which is exactly the case the rule's annotation branch covers, so the factory is marked:

```ts
// mock-isolation: CLI fixtures must not open the pairing state DB; every store call is stubbed here.
```

The now-stale baseline entry was pruned with the ratchet's own `--prune` (shrink-only, `8187 -> 8186` exact factories), and the ratchet then reports `OK: 8186 grandfathered factories`. Re-ran `src/cli/pairing-cli.test.ts` on the amended head: **20 passed (20)**, 38.7 s (warm transform cache). No production code changed in this repair.

### Scope and risk

- Production files: **3** (`src/cli/pairing-cli.ts`, `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/channel-pairing.ts`, `src/pairing/pairing-store.ts`), **+111/−18** (+93 net).
- Test: `src/cli/pairing-cli.test.ts` +120/−1. Docs: `docs/cli/pairing.md` +37/−12.
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `parseChannel`, `resolveAccountId`, `listChannelPairingRequests`, `resolveChannelPairingRequestId`, `dismissChannelPairingRequest`, and `runWithLocalStateOwner`; no duplicate store owner.
- Config/default, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none beyond the additive optional schema field and the forwarded `assertCurrent`.
- Not tested end-to-end: the Gateway-running RPC branch (this proof runs offline by design). It is covered by the two-owner-call unit assertions and typecheck, but no live Gateway was booted with configured pairing channels.

<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

Maintainers may edit this branch. `pairing dismiss` deliberately performs a list-then-dismiss pair of owner-routed calls because the CLI accepts a human code while the existing dismiss method accepts only the opaque request id. If a future RPC accepts a code directly, this can collapse to one call without changing the command surface.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

Land-ready rationale: the gap is a documented CLI/Control-UI surface mismatch; dismissal already exists in the store and RPC; this change adds the missing CLI surface with a shipped-run base/head proof and a focused regression test.

Alternatives considered: (a) a new code-addressed dismiss RPC + capability, rejected for exceeding the 3-file/120-line budget and adding a protocol surface; (b) approving then removing the allowlist entry, rejected because it grants access as a side effect; (c) waiting out the TTL, rejected as the user-facing gap.

Scope statement: no changes to `list`/`approve` output, no new config/state, no protocol version bump.

</details>

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: malformed UTF-8 from a value file, piped value, or dotenv import can silently overwrite stored secrets/environment values with altered text.

## User Impact

User impact: malformed byte input fails before storage changes, including partial dotenv imports; valid UTF-8 and existing BOM/newline behavior remain supported.

No config defaults, storage schema, protocol, permissions, migrations, or upgrade behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the complete bounded input buffer before converting it to text, using the existing input-validation error and CLI exit-2 path. Both set/import and file/stdin use the same reader.

## Evidence

- Scenario: malformed UTF-8 set/import file/stdin input fails before stored entries change; valid UTF-8 and existing BOM/newline semantics remain supported
- Entry: node "$CHECKOUT/openclaw.mjs" secrets store set NAME --value-file FILE_OR_DASH; node "$CHECKOUT/openclaw.mjs" secrets store import --from FILE_OR_DASH --yes; disputed owner ran unmocked: src/cli/secrets-store-input.ts bounded readers; CLI validation mapper; actual SQLite secret-store persistence owner

Session Details needs a compact way to show subagent activity and open the relevant child session.

## User Impact

Shows individual subagents for collections of up to five on desktop or three on mobile; larger collections show status counts and open the full list. Working subagents appear first, and the collapsed section indicates ongoing activity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consumes the existing ordered roster and keeps child navigation separate from opening the full collection. Status remains accessible when visually hidden.

## Risk and coverage

The Details host composition is in #176653. This component adds no query or execution authority.

CI failed `chat-html-preview.e2e.test.ts` > “renders HTML with strict and retains Source in the same file tab”: after Edit file, the editable surface did not become available within 30 seconds (run 39339176045, job 118356668990). Remote desktops need sizing options that fill one viewport axis while allowing the other to scroll.

prs.title: feat(ui): refine session sharing controls and outcomes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session sharing needs to distinguish access mode, public links, and member selection while keeping mutation results and recovery feedback visible.

## User Impact

Adds a dedicated access-mode view, an inline public-link disclosure with copy feedback, and an on-demand people search. An empty loaded roster omits Message permissions; loading and error states remain available. The header communicates public sharing in its main control. Grouped member rows retain native keyboard navigation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keeps permissions, confirmation, reads, and mutations with the native session owner. Header callbacks forward operation outcomes so successful actions can update the menu. Retired mutations restore their previous state without creating an empty cache entry or overwriting a replacement operation. Opening Search focuses the newly rendered input without scrolling the surrounding page.

## Evidence

- The Sharing renderer suite passed all 13 cases in the combined UI run.

- Shared menu keyboard/navigation coverage passed all 23 cases; the changed file cost was 4.66 s with `pnpm test ui/src/components/solid/menu-navigation.browser.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`. The same file passed in WebKit (4.60 s wall).

- Sharing Search focus is applied after the input is rendered, without scrolling its container. The changed Sharing and mobile-menu files passed 28 cases together (`--maxWorkers=1`; 2.48 s wall); scoped independent review found no actionable findings.

- Header tests now check the icon-only Sharing control through its accessible name and centered icon, with both toolbar controls still actionable. The header file passed 45 cases (2.65 s wall), and the focused native geometry case passed (14.13 s wall), both with `--maxWorkers=1`. Scoped review found no actionable findings.

prs.title: feat(ui): add responsive session headers and detail panels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session headers, Details, and panel navigation need to stay coordinated as users switch layouts and open nested mobile pages.

## User Impact

Connects compact desktop controls and one resizable mobile Details/Panels sheet with Back navigation. The conversation, draft, and mounted file, Browser, Terminal, and Desktop content stay available through panel and viewport changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses the retained pane state for header and panel actions, connects mobile session and Machine destinations, and restores keyboard focus when split panes or nested pages close. Mock Gateway responses and browser scenarios exercise these session entry points. People loading updates no longer restart the retained page's own activation lifecycle.

Headers, Details, and the session rail use the shared direct Solid components while preserving the rendered controls, retained mobile pages, and existing panel actions. Elapsed labels in Subagents, Processes, Machine, and mobile Details use the same direct timer component, preserving their time format and cleanup.

Opening an attachment on mobile follows the destination selected by the content owner, so Files shows the selected document whether it occupies the main or side panel, while retaining the composer draft. Command-palette attachments retain consistent spacing.

Review keeps code folding available after all hidden context in a gap has loaded. Partially loaded gaps remain boundaries for syntax analysis, and edits stay visible.

## Risk and coverage

Responsive transitions, focus restoration, and retained panel state are the main shared regression areas. The published images show settled normal states; the panel-module load-failure state is not pictured.

A scoped `session-color.e2e.test.ts` run on an earlier candidate failed during the unchanged desktop roster-refresh segment. Two keyboard siblings passed; source comparison alone did not establish whether main also fails. The stale observable and runtime cause remain unresolved.

Offline header entry to Rename remains unavailable, and the desktop inline editor is absent after disconnect. The already-open mobile modal's queued Save/reconnect path passed; this does not establish offline initiation from the header.

An earlier broad core-test type check exceeded its file-count limit: Gateway had 725 test roots and plugins/platform had 724, against a limit of 720. The exact upstream base `eb60042` had identical root sets and type-check configuration. Selected UI type checks passed separately; this does not establish a full type-gate pass for the current integration.

Earlier composer fixture cases emitted non-failing strict-read warnings; their application callsite remains unidentified.

The latest local performance check exceeds only the Russian locale-pair limit: 310,025 gzip bytes against 307,200 bytes. An earlier comparison reproduced the same budget failure on upstream base `82ae08dd` at 310,890 bytes; no new upstream baseline run was performed for the latest integration. Startup, chat, new-session, and CSS budgets pass. No limit or baseline was changed.

Four completed local mocked-Gateway shards on `8f9deb25` (the same source tree as `19c35834`) passed 1,701 cases and failed eight across 395 files. These were Darwin arm64/Chromium runs with pinned Bun; they are partial coverage, separate from the focused passing results below. The failures were:

- Sign-in and setup: `model-provider-login.e2e.test.ts` — “keeps browser sign-in available while an OAuth callback is pending” (click timeout); `model-setup-cancel.e2e.test.ts` — “preserves a replacement tab's receipt when the old page confirms cancellation” (missing replacement receipt).
- Message display: `chat-user-bubble-disclosure.e2e.test.ts` — “keeps collapsed paragraphs readable after reload and browser reveal (mobile)” (105 px recollapsed height versus 100 px initially); `chat-flow.streaming.e2e.test.ts` — “shows turn metadata only after completion on mobile tap” (earlier assistant-bubble tap timeout).
- Links and search: `github-link-hovercard.e2e.test.ts` — “opens the current pull request permalink from cached card title and repo links” (navigation wait timeout); `chat-voice-transcript.e2e.test.ts` — “keeps one canonical Talk result and exposes its separate speech transcript” (Search messages did not open).
- Header and sidebar: `session-owner-assignment.e2e.test.ts` — “assigns an archived session to an offline teammate from the header” (Me assignee timeout); `sidebar-pinned-agents.e2e.test.ts` — “keeps row actions and pinned cards accessible at 1366 px” (empty computed SVG width versus 16 px).

The Talk transcript failure is a local shortcut mismatch: the test sends Control+F, while macOS uses Meta+F. The other seven failures remain unattributed; no fix or passing replay is claimed. The earlier owner-assignment passes below do not establish that the later header failure is resolved.

## Evidence

The integrated source prepared for publication passed 12 selected practical cases on macOS with repository-pinned Bun and Chromium (89.24 s total command wall):

- Three HTML sandbox cases passed (40.13 s), preserving script policy, Source/Preview switching, editing, retained documents, and the prohibition on unintended writes. The file-action helper waits for the native menu to finish opening; all scenario assertions and existing timeouts remain unchanged. Independent review accepted this fixture-readiness change. The underlying lost-click mechanism remains unproved.
- One simulated iOS-focus case passed (11.34 s). This checks the Chromium focus shim, not physical iOS or WebKit behavior.
- Two composer cases passed (3.76 s), retaining editing state, the field, and caret while the native menu owns focus and when empty composer regions are clicked.
- Six terminal docking cases passed (34.01 s).

All ten selected UI and UI-chat type-check graphs passed at the relevant changed boundaries (40.43 s total). All 43 source line-cap checks passed with unchanged thresholds (8.93 s). These are scoped checks, not a claim that every repository type graph or test suite passed.

A fresh `pnpm ui:build` passed on final commit `071d3bd0982a` (11.92 s). UI and UI-chat type checks, scoped lint, and formatting also passed on that commit. The performance check remains red only for the Russian locale budget described above. Existing non-failing Solid strict-read and bundler warnings remain recorded without suppression.

Earlier revision-specific browser and isolated-Gateway evidence remains historical; it does not turn the latest 12-case run into a full-suite or live-service result. The latest cases use mocked Gateway data and do not establish physical-device behavior or hosted Linux CI. Fresh hosted CI is required after publication; earlier public-head results do not certify this source.

<details>
<summary>Earlier scoped validation</summary>

These results apply to the revisions named below and are reusable only where their inputs remain unchanged. They do not establish hosted CI or a full-suite pass for the current source.

- Five mobile Details cases passed with the extended same-owner loading/ready regression (2.45 s wall). Retained mobile-page boundary coverage passed two unit cases (6.18 s wall) and two native scenarios (20.17 s wall); the DOM-identity negative control fails when retention is removed.
- The original Details → People flow was reproduced and then passed with stable activation. People → Sharing → Back → Close/reopen retained the same People DOM node. Participants rendered; the synthetic mention-directory request remained unavailable, so this is not a live directory-success claim.
- Practical Chromium checks verified composer focus/draft retention, panel Expand/Restore/Back/Close, task-progress retention, one scoped approval, rename Save/Cancel and deferred mobile Save, and terminal hide/reveal without a second open or attach.
- Scoped integration checks passed for metadata/header/notices, retained panes, and rendering/input budgets. The controller guard, UI and UI-test types, and import-cycle checks passed. The generated boot-module manifest includes `app-route-types.ts`. Scoped independent reviews found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

- Local integration validation passed the mobile Desktop close/reopen/dismissal case (13.31 s) and the two 320/693 px WebKit header cases (4.38 s), including the stronger control-content overflow assertion and Details sizing. The WebKit run emitted a non-failing `PaneDetails` reactivity warning.
- An integration pass completed production UI and the three relevant test type-check groups (7.55 s total), type-aware lint of the 13 changed files (9.92 s; zero errors, three reactivity warnings), the full controller guard (2.44 s), and the line-cap ratchet (0.70 s). Both guards compared explicitly with the integrated main base.

- The mobile Details browser test now awaits registration triggered by the production lazy import before checking its content. Root presence, native navigation, parking, and retained DOM assertions remain unchanged. The focused test passed (2.17 s command wall), followed by canonical Chat test types (1.93 s), lint, controller and line-cap guards, and scoped review. An unchanged ordered replay also passed; the exact CI timing cause remains unproven.

- Two updated integration cases passed locally (19.49 s command wall): native Environment/Changes navigation and active progress Hide after a same-session streaming update. Virtual-clock pauses begin after native readiness; the tests retain the final panel layout, saved-card, and visibility assertions. Six unchanged cases were not rerun.
- The two-test patch passed formatting, both owning E2E type graphs, lint, diff checks, and scoped review. It changes test timing and coverage only; production UI code is unchanged. This was a macOS Chromium run with the repository-pinned Bun runtime, not a hosted Linux CI or full-suite result.

- Two real-pane attachment cases passed (11.92 s command wall), covering Files in the main and side positions, the selected document contents, and retained composer text. The main-position case failed before the destination correction. UI and both owning E2E type graphs, scoped lint, formatting, and review passed.
- Command-palette attachment spacing and compact session-color checks passed all seven cases (28.71 s command wall). The color test now verifies the selected value through the compact Icon & color page after reopening it; the desktop assertions remain. UI E2E types, scoped lint, formatting, and review passed.

- Real isolated-Gateway tests passed for PR/CI reader lifetime (34.26 s test time), exact child/process inspection and Stop with parent-draft retention (8.60 s test time), and Review folding after context expansion (11.96 s test time; 24.94 s command wall). Reader/background results were reused unchanged; the final folding run used freshly built UI. Native control selectors and initial card expansion were updated while retaining target, content, refresh, and invalidation assertions.
- The folding regression failed before the analyzer fix and passed afterward. All seven parser cases passed (3.00 s command wall; 0.52 s Vitest, including 2 ms for the new case). Complete contiguous context crosses a retained expansion marker; partial, missing, or reordered context remains a boundary. Changed-file type checks, lint, formatting, the controller guard, and scoped review passed.

- Seven passing full-app cases from `37994b4e` are reused for `8f9deb25`, with a mocked Gateway: three session-admission/failed-startup cases (13.48 s command wall), two collapsed-rail status/model-menu touch cases (12.47 s), and two Processes/Subagents cases (12.82 s). They preserve queued follow-ups, drafts, confirmed-URL admission, keyboard access to Retry, model-menu interaction, and scoped Stop behavior.
- Owner-assignment tests now use the native mobile pressed buttons and their visible labels while preserving desktop menu roles, exact owner counts, disabled states, avatars, search, RPC, and keyboard assertions. All 12 cases passed (35.35 s command wall); the two final mobile checks passed in 17.87 s.
- Both phone stale-build recovery cases passed with normal and blocked service workers (34.78 s command wall). The tests read the same native owner controls while retaining exact Bob selection, reload bounds, one active shell, and no assignment mutation or model wake. These are test-only migrations; applicable types, lint, formatting, and scoped reviews passed on macOS with pinned Bun and Chromium.

- Direct header/Details validation passed 39 unit cases (8.11 s command wall) and 28 Chromium cases (10.03 s). UI/chat types, scoped lint, formatting, the controller guard, and review passed. These focused checks preserve native header actions, retained Details behavior, and the existing mobile presentation.

- A fresh `pnpm ui:build` passed on clean `8f9deb25` (11.72 s), and the emitted stamp matches that commit. Production UI types are reused from the reviewed callback correction (1.60 s). The performance check remains red only for the inherited Russian locale budget described above.

Validation used fixture-backed browser flows and real isolated-Gateway flows with fixture workspaces and upstream services. The latter ran on macOS with repository-pinned Bun and Chromium 156, without an external live API. These results do not establish physical-device behavior, a full-suite pass, or hosted Linux CI on the updated head. The reused seven-flow run uses a mocked Gateway and Chromium; its iOS focus shim does not establish physical iOS or WebKit behavior.

</details>

## Visual evidence

Captured before: `dccff201b07e`. Captured after: `5856f7237579`.

Synthetic fixtures and a mock Gateway show the integrated session UI at these revisions. These images are not isolated proof of this PR; stills do not establish interaction or live-service results.

prs.title: feat(ui): add session Outputs views
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated deliverables need a session-scoped collection that distinguishes files and dashboards from loading, unavailable, and empty results.

## User Impact

Adds desktop and mobile Outputs views. Desktop shows a compact preview with access to the Files catalog; mobile presents the complete generated-file collection and the session dashboard. Items open through native file and dashboard actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing assistant-artifact and board owners. The pane retains the collection only while presented, and opening or retrying validates the captured session, connection, and workspace identity.

## Risk and coverage

The session Details mounting is in #176653. File and dashboard opening still validate the current session, connection, and workspace.

Recorded CI run 39343253944, job 118370400581, timed out waiting for the global command-failure toast after a route switch in chat-send.test.ts. The test and 21 relevant owner, fixture, and configuration files match its tested main. The original full-file order passed unchanged locally (114 tests in 2.57 s; affected case 22 ms). The precise CI failure mechanism remains unresolved; the full 655-file shard was not replayed, and no toast or timeout change is included.

## Evidence

- The Outputs comparison below shows generated files and the dashboard entry with the surrounding mobile page.
