prs.title: feat(memory): support evergreen extra paths
prs.body:
Closes #151914

## What Problem This Solves
Stable reference documents indexed through `memory.search.extraPaths` lose ranking weight as their modification times age, even when their authority should not expire.

## Solution and User Impact
Add opt-in `evergreen: true` to object-form extra paths. Matching **noncanonical reference files** skip temporal decay in keyword, vector, and hybrid retrieval. Omission preserves existing behavior. Canonical dated memory notes and session indexed timestamps continue to decay normally, including remote-source timestamp handling on current main.

The flag changes ranking only: no trust, provenance, source admission, automatic injection, persistent memory schema, or index identity changes. Toggling it does not reindex or re-embed documents. Original feature and proposal: @esqandil; maintainer conflict repair and stronger regression coverage preserve that contribution.

## Evidence
Candidate: `f55fda2b1f8fe3e071242d25d2b1a73d17205216`; feature integrated with main baseline `77794e758c73e465b3c6b0a3a1c292e5c7139aa2`.

- **144 affected focused tests pass** across eight files after the latest main conflict repair (including fresh/reopened SQLite schema admission). Previous seven-file135test proof also passed. Coverage: actual SQLite manager/index/search, keyword/vector/hybrid retrieval, persisted false→true→false toggle, index identity and embedding stability, temporal timestamps, config validation, SDK paths, and CLI display behavior.
- Final schema/temporal recheck: **29 tests pass**. Regression check against baseline temporal implementation: three intended evergreen assertions fail while six controls pass; restored implementation is green.
- Registered **`pnpm openclaw memory index/status/search`** proof passes with isolated HOME/config/state/temp, no credentials or running service. Four indexed old/new/reference/daily-note sources retain the same SQLite inode and row digest through both policy toggles; only the selected old reference gains approximately4× weight. Canonical dated notes still decay. Provider-free CLI proof plus deterministic vector manager fixture is boundary proof, not a broad semantic-provider quality claim.
- Whole-file audit of every touched test file; silent FTS skip replaced by an asserted supported prerequisite. Removed synthetic-score coverage superseded by real manager boundary tests; retained distinct historical and failure-path cases.
- Focused production lint (seven core files), source line-growth guard, generated config-doc baseline check, and diff checks pass.
- Independent configured **OpenAI API-only review** of the complete feature tree (`90627edd15c391ff7799f96cad405de429d8ab70`): no actionable P0–P2 findings, including test quality. A subsequent import-only formatter correction at final tree `ffc45e8f333bcdbbf5940bec388d59f8b3eec1e4` received an additional full-module-context independent API review with no findings. No subscription fallback.
- After main advanced during auto-merge waiting, the native owner cancelled the retained request before head repair. The only new conflict was the generated config hash; native baseline refresh plus the actual config-doc generator/check regenerated combined/core hashes. All22other feature path blobs are byte-identical to the prior reviewed candidate. Fresh full-feature API review of tree `855bc1d78eadf56eac6aab0df8e04b349a9a4a42` found no actionable P0–P2 defects (diff + complete current memory-schema context; earlier whole-file audits retained, no independent test-execution claim).
- Previous exact-head CI run39354753414 exposed an import-order formatting defect in the restored label extraction. Fixed with the configured formatter, independently reproduced/rechecked all22 supported changed feature files; no behavior/test inputs changed, so earlier passing behavior proof is reused rather than claimed rerun.

### Local limitations / required CI
Exact-head GitHub CI remains required; the above does not claim it passed. Local type wrappers reject compiler declarations physically outside the checkout in the supported shared pnpm graph; no guard bypass or redundant private dependency graph was introduced. A broad local lint run was stopped after focused proof; three max-lines suppression errors were investigated and their UI/config inputs are unchanged from the main baseline. Any actual CI failures must still be classified and PR-caused failures repaired.

### Compatibility and Downgrade
The field is optional and rank-only. Older strict configuration schemas reject it: **remove `evergreen` entirely**, including `false`, from both global and per-agent extra-path entries before downgrading. No production config or live memory index was changed.

### Historical author evidence (not independently rerun)
The original PR body reported a Voyage-backed isolated CLI proof at `b16ce8dd0e25841ef64ee16ae21e9239839ded79`: governed target rank7→1, fresh rank1, and unchanged existing-index inode/chunk/embedding digest across the toggle. That is attributed historical evidence, not current-head CI or independently verified semantic coverage.

prs.title: feat(ui): refine browser navigation and recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Browser page update can overwrite a typed address when focus moves to Go, changing the intended navigation into Reload.

## User Impact

Preserves the address draft until submission, navigation, focus leaves the toolbar, or disposal. Keeps navigation and address controls in the rail, moves secondary actions into a menu, and exposes the reason Browser is unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retains editing ownership across Go focus changes and reuses the favicon cache. Retry repeats the failed operation on its native or remote backend; context resets retire the saved retry.

## What Problem This Solves

File previews need usable reading controls without losing edits, selection, or file identity when users switch views.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keeps presentation controls separate from the existing draft, save, and file-identity owners. SVG rendering no longer depends on an optional lightbox action. UI element declarations stay with their owning types so core test checks do not load the renderer dependency graph.

## Risk and coverage

File previews share draft, save, and file-identity state. Reader transitions must preserve unsaved input and text selection.

The quota-recovery saved-clear status failure was reproduced on pinned main `e75403f` with identical relevant sources. Authentication recovery succeeds while the UI status remains stale; no quota fix is included in this change.

prs.title: refactor: keep private provider operations in their owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private single-consumer operations expose modules, argument packets, and test-only entry points instead of living in the caller that owns their lifetime and prepared facts.

## What Changed

Fold OpenAI/Anthropic admin usage handoffs and OpenRouter/Venice/xAI usage leaves into their usage owners or registered hooks. Put image/video execution into the existing prepared task callbacks, prompt additions into shared attempt preparation, transcript image normalization into its walker, signed device proof into the existing connect-auth phase, ACPX lazy runtime registration into plugin registration, and APNs relay send orchestration into the dispatcher. Retire the old private leaves and exercise retained behavior through the surviving entry points.

Strict production delta: **+1,722 / -2,234 = 512 net lines removed**. Tests, fixtures, test-support, generated files, declarations, and metadata are excluded. Complete diff: +2,107 / -2,394 across 42 paths.

## User Impact

No intended capability change, migration, configuration, SDK, protocol, dependency, or persisted-format change. An adjacent ACPX correction lets catalog-only harnesses dispose without resolving runtime state; started/stopping services still settle through their captured context and stop promise. Actual dynamic imports remain lazy, including ACPX service loading and session-catalog registration. Keep credential/approval/current-authority boundaries, exact signed bytes and prompt ordering, body/deadline/resource bounds, realistic concurrency, paid-media persistence and salvage, batch rollback, and write-capable settlement.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- No speculative-race, security, durability, settlement, or concurrency guard is removed. This cut removes private forwarding and contextual DTO handoffs, not behavior.
- Private helper signatures are not public contracts; existing public entry points absorb their proof without introducing a production testing seam.
- Standalone Phase E session memory, its factory/registry/expiry/federation machinery and tests are untouched. The incognito change is prompt composition only.

## Evidence

- Fresh complete-packet independent review after accepted findings is scoped-clean at P0-P2 (0.96 confidence). An earlier pass caught requested video resolution missing from tool-result geometry after the fold. The existing public reference-position case was extended to assert the returned geometry and failed solely for missing resolution before repair (61.28s wrapper). The complete geometry packet now includes resolution again; both video owner/storage suites pass all 30 cases (165.12s wrapper), and the APNs test repair passes all 20 cases (55.08s wrapper). No public behavior is intentionally changed. Simplification/retained-boundary audit completed.
- Core and extension targeted native type graphs pass. Focused proof passed media tools (95), prompt/transcript and prefix stability (36), APNs (47), signed Gateway connect authentication (45), registered provider usage (48), and Anthropic catalog/lazy registration (41).
- The initial ACPX group passed 11 and failed two catalog-only disposal cases: replacing the old outer-service mock exposed unconditional state-directory resolution in the existing shutdown callback. Shutdown now uses only an already-started context or existing stop promise, without changing the two regression cases. The repaired extension native graph and all 13 public registration/startup cases pass (56.27s test wrapper).
- Selected static proof passed extension boundary guards, line caps, four wrapper/import-closure cases (24.22s wrapper), zero runtime cycles, zero Madge components, and formatting. Typed lint found an overly broad body stringification in one migrated APNs test; it now requires the actual JSON string without a cast. Assertion and mock ratchets identified four obsolete baseline entries, removed shrink-only. Final core native types, repaired typed lint, assertion safety (2,534 files / 5,827 grandfathered assertions), mock exports (8,189 grandfathered factories), all 14 suppression-audit cases (14.09s wrapper), and repaired formatting pass. The final all-changed source syntax pass identified shadowed outer usage-period names; mechanical renames preserve their values. The extension native graph, all 16 OpenAI/Anthropic usage cases (89.20s wrapper), all-changed syntax, all 14 suppression cases (12.02s wrapper), and usage formatting now pass.

- First exact-head CI39353867599 passed every planned test, type, security and other static job; its only failing leaf was check-lint-extensions-2 (118409064588), plus aggregate. The migrated ACPX registration test incorrectly awaited synchronous keyed-store construction. The one-line repair retains the call and assertion. Fresh independent repair review is scoped-clean P0-P2 (0.99); affected native types, all13 public registration/startup cases (215.34s wrapper), focused source-backed typed lint, all14 suppression-audit cases (12.14s wrapper), and formatting pass. The package-boundary lint invocation began broad SDK declaration preparation and was stopped to respect the CPU budget; it is not claimed passing. The supported source-backed targeted lint then passed without declaration preparation. New exact-head CI is the broad gate; no CI rerun was requested.

Broad proof is hosted CI on the exact pushed head. Local proof uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state, nice 10, serial focused Vitest with one worker, and targeted native type graphs. No local whole-graph typecheck, build, broad suite, E2E, live-service, device, or operator-state proof is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

Hiding task progress from chat should not make the saved plan unavailable in Details.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Separates the shared saved-plan presentation from the chat visibility filter. Native progress storage, refresh, settings, and card identity remain authoritative; session-scoped actions keep their existing guards.

## Risk and coverage

Hiding progress in chat remains a local visibility preference and does not remove the saved plan or stop work.

In the focused prefix validation, the preference scenario timed out on the first chat reload while waiting for the session roster. Its pre-reload saved-plan, live-update, and no-write assertions passed. The same boundary failed after the menu fix, including a run where the preference file executed first; the reload cause remains unresolved and post-reload assertions were not reached.

CI run 39345984670, job 118379244719, also failed while resolving a deferred `sessions.list` response after leaving and restoring the parent conversation. One diagnostic replay of the exact merge passed (14.37 s test time; 34.96 s Vitest duration), with both deferred responses present and resolved. prs.title: feat(ui): add desktop and mobile review controls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Review needs readable desktop and mobile diff layouts without losing file context, disclosure state, or the identity of the checkout being reviewed.

## User Impact

Adds desktop file navigation and view controls, mobile diff cards and Sync details, and separate controls for line wrapping, word changes, and split view. Refreshing retains compatible file presentation while stale diff and file-text responses remain excluded. Menus stay anchored to their trigger when the containing sheet moves.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keeps loading, request generations, caches, and gap expansion with the existing diff owner. Presentation modules share its live data and operations. Workspace consumers reuse the same uncommitted-diff request and result. Search focus and navigation scrolling follow settled DOM updates.

The Review panel and its menus render as direct Solid components, preserving the existing layout, disclosures, and menu behavior. Retired native adapters are removed.

## Risk and coverage

This changes shared diff rendering and loading as well as presentation. Stale diff and file-text responses must remain excluded.

The recorded unavailable-desktop-target timeout reproduced in isolated validation. A controlled lazy-publication delay subsequently reproduced a lost request, which the shared panel-readiness correction addresses. The original status-retry failure was not independently reproduced. The welcome-avatar case passed in isolation with matching main sources, but its original failed-shard timing remains unattributed; no avatar patch is included. The separate quota saved-clear status failure was reproduced on main.

## Evidence

- Recorded focused validation: Review panel and menu checks passed (45 unit and 1 Chromium cases; 5.80 s command wall).

- File/diff lifecycle checks passed: 98 cases across five unit files (4.98 s wall) and seven cases across three Chromium files (2.89 s wall).
- The new shared disclosure test passed both cases with `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/session-file-disclosures.browser.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1` (2.34 s wall; 8 ms test time). Its negative control fails when synchronous measurement commits are removed.
- The obsolete two-call `untrack` allowance for the diff panel is removed with those calls. Scoped independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

- Review focus and scrolling follow settled DOM updates. The focused run passed 25 unit and four Chromium cases (4.20 s wall), including the Search-focus regression; removing settlement loses the expected focus.

- Direct Solid panel validation passed all 25 unit cases (3.33 s command wall) and four Chromium cases (3.13 s). The rendered panel and existing expectations are preserved. UI and chat-test types, scoped lint, formatting, and review passed. This validates the focused panel candidate on macOS with pinned Bun, not a full-suite or hosted Linux CI result.

## What Problem This Solves

Inline execution approvals need a compact mobile layout while keeping the complete command, request details, and eligible decisions available.

## User Impact

Adds an explicit mobile presentation with expandable command details and a single row of decision buttons. Expanding details does not submit a decision. Updating the current request retains its disclosure; a new request starts collapsed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses native approval eligibility and decision handling. The mobile layout applies only to inline execution requests, leaving desktop, modal, and plugin approval presentations unchanged.

## Risk and coverage

Composer use of the mobile approval presentation is in #176498.

## Evidence

- Recorded focused validation: Execution-approval presentation checks passed (14 unit cases; 1.85 s command wall).

- Current CI: [WebKit menu checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39355387222/job/118409245507) failed the dark and light attachment/capability hover cases because the photo action was absent. prs.title: feat(ui): add resizable panel frame and mobile navigation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Desktop and mobile panels need consistent navigation and resizing without changing the saved desktop layout or discarding active panel resources.

## User Impact

Adds the shared panel frame, dock controls, tab launcher, and mobile panel navigation. Mobile views retain their route and geometry when hidden, and closing the final tab returns to chat through both the tab button and native keyboard command. Desktop dividers remain available at intermediate widths. Browsing inside Files preserves the selected panel. New tab starts the requested panel, and position controls retain keyboard focus during background refreshes.

Expanded Dashboards retain their controls, the desktop Share control aligns with its neighbors, and same-session updates keep an open progress menu available. Terminal docking controls refresh when the shared queue changes, so opening another terminal does not leave Dock to right incorrectly disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keeps panel resources with their existing owners and mobile presentation state with the pane. Async closing verifies the initiating mobile session before completing; clearing Side chat reports success before its panel closes. Lazy opening waits for its registered host before mounting. Scroll fades follow the scrollable content's own surface color. Panel closure waits for hosted-tab updates before checking completion, preserving canceled-close and Close all sequencing.

The mobile toggle follows whether the panel is currently presented, so it can reopen retained panels and switch from Details to Panels.

Headers and Details use the upstream direct Solid components and a narrow open handle, retaining the existing desktop controls, mobile presentation, and panel actions.

## Risk and coverage

Shared panel navigation, asynchronous closing, and lazy mounting affect retained resources and focus across session changes.

The stale Dock to right state was traced to queue transitions notifying only one terminal host. Notifications now refresh every bound terminal panel; existing handoff and admission guards remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Panel lazy loading, layout, and mobile-host checks passed: 21 tests (3.13 s command wall).
- The integrated panel-layout, rail-column, and sidebar-contract suites passed all 20 scenarios.

- File previews, process actions, platform captions, progress submission, and question takeover have passing native evidence across scoped runs (64.13 s shared invocation; the corrected 390 px question case passed in a separate 15.14 s invocation). The checks retain real input and exact geometry assertions.

- Hosted-tab updates settle before close completion is checked, preserving cancellation and Close all sequencing. All 39 existing sidebar/hosted-tab tests passed (5.63 s Vitest duration); independent scoped review found no actionable findings.

- Updated mobile panel navigation passed the selected Desktop open/reopen and reload cases (`session-active-resources.e2e.test.ts`, `--maxWorkers=1`; 2 cases, 27.84 s). On the locally integrated UI, the mobile close/reopen/dismissal case passed again in 13.31 s. These scoped runs preserve native navigation and the retained resource checks.

- Local repair validation through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` passed the native navigation and header cases (9 cases; 47.18 s), the final Dashboard checks (3 selected cases; 24 s), both Details/progress files (8 cases; 27.95 s), and native plugin UI coverage (6 cases; 23.15 s file duration).
- The tests now enter through the active pane and native panel controls, start virtual-clock pauses after panel readiness, and exercise Hide after a same-session streaming update. Existing focus, retained-content, geometry, request, and saved-progress assertions remain. Relevant types, lint, formatting, controller checks, and scoped review passed.

- The shared test helper now uses the Layout menu for main-pane Restore while preserving native side-panel Expand/Restore. The original split-view and reconnect cases failed before this routing repair and passed afterward; the Dashboard iframe-retention sibling also passed (32.06 s combined command wall for split view and the sibling; 11.39 s for reconnect). Test bodies, assertions, and timeouts are unchanged. Both E2E type groups, lint, formatting, and scoped review passed.

- The current sidebar-layout checks passed all 22 cases, including tab ordering, main/side focus, retained selection, and layout restoration. They ran with 60 cron cases in one 82-test invocation (3.79 s command wall; no separate navigation timing). Selected UI type checks, scoped lint, formatting, and review passed.

- Expanded mobile Restore now uses the native control inside the active sheet, rather than a Layout trigger behind its backdrop. Four mobile, dashboard, and desktop cases passed (22.33 s command wall), preserving iframe, draft, focus, and geometry assertions.
- The collapsed-rail status test resumes its virtual clock before viewport and layout-settlement work. Its original timeout reproduced before the correction; all four status cases passed afterward (24.20 s command wall). Both repairs change tests/helpers only; applicable types, lint, formatting, and scoped reviews passed.

- Direct header/Details validation passed the focused unit case (4.49 s command wall) and 27 Chromium cases (12.62 s). Production UI and chat-test types, scoped lint, formatting, the controller guard, and review passed. The checks cover this panel/navigation implementation without importing later composition changes.

- The terminal docking failure reproduced before the notification correction. All six original docking cases passed afterward (35.38 s command wall); the unmodified upstream control also passed all six (34.48 s). Sixteen handoff/reconnect unit cases passed (3.61 s). Types, lint, formatting, the controller guard, and scoped review passed, with no new tests or relaxed assertions.

Validation ran on macOS using the repository-pinned Bun runtime; browser checks used Chromium. They do not establish a full-suite or hosted Linux CI pass.

CI timing for the updated tests is pending; the measured local costs above are scoped runs.

Mobile pages provide presentation and navigation while existing session-menu and organizer owners perform actions. Rename retains the captured session identity and entered text while renewing request checks after reconnect. Mobile action pages close before opening actions such as Rename. Retained menu pages keep their visual state while subscriptions and pending focus work retire with their owning menu.

prs.title: refactor: remove redundant internal observation work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several internal read/observation paths repeat checks of facts their owners already admitted, or copy private decoded data no caller mutates. Delegated update repair also maintains counters solely for an unused trace summary.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Read-only observations accept the uncommon mid-call changes listed below; security effects, user-data durability, public configuration and SDK contracts remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the duplicate session-fact admission lookup, cold update-row copies, repair timing scaffolding, late triage recertification, repeated interrupted-update inspections, private snapshot whole-family recertification, and final already-admitted setup-channel ID check. Keep initial admission, rooted identity-bound copies, candidate identity and HTTP readiness, bounded deadlines, real writer/effect authority, FIFO, and write-capable settlement.

107 net production lines removed (+64/-171); 82 net test lines removed (+29/-111), plus two obsolete closed-mock baseline entries removed. This is a residue PR under the campaign's 100-line waiver, not a LARGE result. No public config, CLI, SDK, protocol, persisted schema, or durability change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A retained private snapshot edited after initial family admission no longer gets middle/end whole-family recertification. Its read owner has no writers; each copy still pins a rooted source identity. #176334 concerns private-image preparation cost, not a human concurrent private-byte mutation report. A violating private owner may now produce a stale copy or visible error; live database copying is unchanged.
- Another update or install during read-only triage can leave a stale verdict. Human #153378 and #148896, addressed by #153443/#148968, establish missing initial target/completion/context checks, which remain; they do not establish forced mid-observation mutation. The next invocation reads current reality.
- Another restart/install during interrupted-update observation no longer triggers extra generation/version inspections. #152202 describes real interrupted completion, so installed/serving candidate checks, plugin health, HTTP readiness and final current/latest/recovery/live-driver writer checks remain. A same-build restart may leave the observed PID stale; subsequent status refreshes it.
- An internal caller mutating admission-reader query/results is unsupported. The sole factory caller creates its query inline and only reads returned rows; warm reads already return decoded rows directly. Keep the measured cache/freshness from #157730 for human #157243 and actual authority checks. No runtime caller-mutation report was established.
- A plugin mutating its admitted setup ID during setup no longer receives an additional final duplicate diagnostic. The plugin value boundary forbids post-handoff mutation; initial setup/runtime entry/runtime export checks remain. #67200 establishes early admission/setter ordering, not a human post-admission mutation incident; #69479/#69042 cold-start behavior is unchanged.

The removed repair timing summary has no behavior fallback: all actual fence/requester/run checks remain. #147584 measured Windows snapshot-read cost; it does not establish an operator-facing trace contract. The session lookup removal retains the same scoped receipt admission and introduces no accepted weakening.

## Evidence

Focused tests, serial with one worker in isolated state: session facts/order/residency 18; unchanged private-fork coverage 16; update observations/readers/worker and Doctor refusal 40; repair/triage and lint-suppressions 42; plugin setup failures 3. All pass. Targeted ten-root types, exact nine-file typed lint using the canonical core configuration, format and whitespace pass. Runtime and type-inclusive import cycles: zero. Independent review completed scoped-clean for P0–P2; no actionable findings. Changed-check dry-run classified the paths; broad local execution was intentionally not selected.

Full loader setup/mismatch integration remains exact-head hosted-CI proof: its canonical local prerequisite expands to a broad runtime build, outside the shared-host local budget. No build, E2E, live deployment, broad typecheck, timeout increase, retry, skip, suppression, or CI rerun was used.

### CI repair

Initial head `3f9a4100806af4e14bd48d37bd1bfb45a0526663` completed CI run [39354033497](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39354033497). All 209 exact-head check runs were accounted for. Two jobs failed due to this change, plus their aggregate gate:

| Job | Cause and repair |
| --- | --- |
| checks-node-changed-compact-large-7 (118405100319) | Two watcher fixtures injected driver revival/newer completion through the removed inspection call. Move injection to retained HTTP readiness, returning successful HTTP fields. Keep every real final-writer refusal assertion. |
| checks-fast-baseline-ratchets (118405099653) | The revised restart-health mock omitted real exports. Preserve them with import-original pass-through in both affected suites and shrink their exact obsolete baseline entries. |
| openclaw/ci-gate (118410384373) | Aggregate of the two owned failures above. |

The cancelled metadata job 118404537301 has successful exact-head replacement 118404607172; no test suite is missing proof. No failure is classified as inherited, and no CI rerun was requested.

Focused pre-edit replay reproduced exactly the two watcher failures (142.63 seconds, including worker preparation). After repair, complete watcher coverage passes: 26 cases/69.26 seconds; health coverage: 11/19.83 seconds; lint-suppression coverage: 14/14.18 seconds. Targeted two-root types, typed lint, formatting and whitespace pass. Fresh independent repair review is scoped-clean P0–P2, with no actionable findings; the production diff is unchanged. Broad proof for the repaired head remains pending exact-head hosted CI.

prs.title: fix(update): WhatsApp's Baileys loses its long dependency and patch after updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the WhatsApp plugin can fail to load after an update because Baileys imports `long` without declaring it, and an updated install can contain unpatched Baileys files even though the lockfile records the patch.

## User Impact

User impact: Baileys always resolves `long`, and updates of source checkouts install the patched Baileys files. During the link refresh, a broken link to a dependency that the plugin declares optional is reported as a warning instead of failing the update; any other broken link still stops preflight.

These install changes take effect when the installed updater contains them, so the first update from an older release still uses that release's install steps.

## Why This Change Was Made

A hoisted layout hid Baileys' undeclared `long` import. An exact `packageExtensions` entry for `baileys@7.0.0-rc14` adds `long@5.3.2`, and the lockfile is regenerated. pnpm 12 can link package bytes from its global virtual store even when the lockfile records a patch hash, so candidate installs now use a project-local virtual store (`virtualStoreType: project`) while still reusing the configured package store. Source exposure can run another install after the build, so update preflight refreshes bundled plugin dependency links afterwards. A link whose target is missing is skipped with a warning only when the dependency is declared optional.

## Evidence

- Published-driver update: in a disposable container, the published npm `latest` driver (2026.10.5) updated to a candidate packed from all six fixes together (commit `3331e8d12be`): update finished, `readyz` 200, running version verified, durable and incognito session data unchanged.
- `test/scripts/baileys-materialization.test.ts` installs with real pnpm under isolated and hoisted layouts and checks that Baileys resolves `long` and that the patched bytes are on disk.
- Preflight reference test covers the relink after exposure; dependency-link tests cover broken links to optional and required dependencies.
- 51 affected tests pass locally; independent API-only review found no P0–P2 issues.

<details><summary>Follow-up not in this change</summary>

The dependency linker only links packages that exist in a plugin's `node_modules`; it does not compare them with the declared dependencies, so a dependency that was never installed is not detected here. That is unchanged from main and is now stated in the update docs. A declared-versus-installed check would also have to accept hoisted layouts, where a plugin's dependencies can live in the root `node_modules`, so it is left for a separate change.

</details>

prs.title: fix(update): preflight fails on hoisted installs and nested linked worktrees
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: update preflight fails on source checkouts whose dependencies are installed through a hoisted or global pnpm store, or that contain a registered linked Git worktree inside the checkout.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw update` on such a source checkout no longer fails its Control UI validator freshness check or its reference-source snapshot. Unknown nested repositories inside the checkout are still refused before the Gateway stops.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generated Control UI validators embedded esbuild comments naming the physical dependency path, so the same source produced different bytes under a different dependency layout and the freshness check failed. The generator now minifies whitespace, which drops those comments; the TypeBox license is kept and the executable output is unchanged. The generated files are regenerated here.

The reference-source snapshot treated any nested `.git` as an unknown repository. It now excludes only a worktree it can positively identify as registered to this repository (the worktree's `.git` file, its `gitdir` and its `commondir` must all point back to each other) and checks again before stopping the Gateway.

## Evidence

- Published-driver update: in a disposable container, the published npm `latest` driver (2026.10.5) updated to a candidate packed from all six fixes together (commit `3331e8d12be`): update finished, `readyz` 200, running version verified, durable and incognito session data unchanged.
- Generator test (`test/scripts-generate-control-ui-validators.test.ts`) generates the validators under two dependency layouts and requires identical output.
- Update build tests cover a registered linked worktree (accepted), an unregistered or mismatched nested repository (refused), and the recheck before stopping the Gateway.
- `pnpm ui:validators:check` passes on the regenerated output; independent API-only review found no P0–P2 issues.

prs.title: fix(update): settle state writers before Doctor schema repair
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Upgrading from published `openclaw@2026.10.4` could fail in candidate Doctor with `SQLite migration source changed after update capture.` Agent maintenance had finished, but its canonical SQLite handles were still open when the next private schema repair validated the source and tried to acquire exclusive custody.

Drain those prior state writers before schema repair. Their existing native-close receipts account for the legitimate maintenance writes, and the private repair can acquire exclusive custody. Keep post-repair cleanup for resources created by the repair. This replaces this PR's earlier source-consumption workaround, which incorrectly stopped capturing subsequent migrations and made normal credential repairs ineligible for automatic rollback.

The migration-attribution, result-capture and low-level repair modules now match main: no consumed-source set, no new receipt protocol, and no relaxed source validation. All migrations remain attributed. Genuine outside writes still refuse at the existing source guard and make rollback ineligible. #177831's accepted native-close interleaving tradeoff remains unchanged; none of its removed recertification checks are restored. The installed updater's protocol and credential cutover are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Local A/B: both predecessor-identity repair cases in `client-credential-update.test.ts` fail on prior PR head `0a8691aa4ef5` with `unchanged=false`, and pass on unmodified merge base `f6feb34da107`.
- The replacement regression uses real v20 preparation, version migration, an agent-maintenance lease, and the public asynchronous Doctor schema-repair entry point. With unmodified production code it fails at the original source-change guard. With the fix it succeeds and remains rollback-eligible. Its real outside-writer variant retains strict source refusal and `unchanged=false`, with the original capture preserved.
- `pnpm test src/infra/update-doctor-migration-attribution.test.ts src/infra/client-credential-update.test.ts src/commands/doctor-maintenance.database-writes.test.ts src/infra/update-doctor-result.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **31 passed**, including full public credential rollback. Three existing PostgreSQL-only cases require a configured server and were not exercised locally. prs.title: fix(docker): honor OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT when healthcheck config load fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the official Docker image and Compose health check report the container `unhealthy` when the config file fails to load (invalid JSON, unreadable, duplicate agent dirs, etc.), even though the Gateway is listening and serving `/healthz` on the port given by `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT`.

## User Impact

User impact: Docker deployments that set `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` stay healthy while their Gateway is reachable on that port, regardless of config-file state. The `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` override now acts as a true fallback like the lock port; a broken host config bind-mount no longer flips a healthy custom-port container to `unhealthy`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The health check resolved its probe port by loading the config and only then delegating to `resolveGatewayPort`, which reads `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` first. Because the config load can throw (invalid JSON, `INVALID_CONFIG` validation, duplicate agent dirs, unreadable file), any such failure bypassed the env fallback entirely and made the probe report unhealthy.

The env override is now resolved (via the existing `parseGatewayPortEnvValue` parser, no duplicated policy) before the config load, so it survives config-load failures. Port precedence is unchanged when config loads successfully: live lock → `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` → `gateway.port` → default/profile, matching `resolveGatewayPort`'s existing env-over-config rule.

This revision is rebased onto `upstream/main` `07e3328ed3f` and keeps main's async config loader (`createConfigIO().loadConfigAsync()`); the regression test was adapted to that async boundary.

## Real behavior proof

Ran the **built** healthcheck entry points against real loopback `/healthz` listeners, real config files on disk, and a fresh empty state dir (no gateway lock, so the lock-port path cannot mask the result):

- **after** = this branch's build: `node dist/docker-healthcheck.js` (the exact entry the Docker `HEALTHCHECK` runs)
- **before** = current `main`'s build (single-entry `tsdown` bundle of the pre-fix source)
- corrupt config = truncated JSON `{"gateway":{`, which provably makes `loadConfigAsync` throw (`JSON5: invalid end of input` — a trailing-comma object is valid JSON5 and does **not** reproduce the bug, so it was avoided)
- a real HTTP listener on the probes' port records each `/healthz` request, proving the probe reached a live listener

Scenario results (full transcript below):

| # | bundle | config | `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` | listener | exit | `/healthz` request seen |
|---|--------|--------|------------------------|----------|------|------------------------|
| S1 | after | corrupt | 19001 | 19001 | **0** | **yes** |
| S2 | before | corrupt | 19001 | 19001 | **1** | **no** |
| S3 | after | corrupt | 19001 | none | 1 | no |
| S4 | after | valid (`port: 19002`) | unset | 19002 | **0** | **yes** |
| S5 | after | valid (`port: 19002`) | 19001 | 19001 | **0** | **yes** |
| S6 | after | corrupt | unset | none | 1 | no |

The S1/S2 pair is the core pass/fail comparison: with an identical corrupt config, env port `19001`, and a live listener, the **before** bundle exits 1 and never reaches the listener (config-load failure kills the health check), while the **after** bundle exits 0 and hits `/healthz` on the env port. S3 and S6 confirm the failure path is real (no listener / no env → exit 1), S4 confirms the existing config-port behavior is retained, and S5 confirms the env override still wins over a valid config.

- Real-behavior proof above: built healthcheck bundles vs real `/healthz` listeners; before/after comparison reproduces the bug (S2) and proves the fix (S1); regression matrix S3–S6.
- Unit suite `src/docker-healthcheck.test.ts`: 6/6 passed, including the regression test `still probes the env port when config resolution throws` (adapted to `createConfigIO().loadConfigAsync()`, asserting the env short-circuit never consults config).
- Targeted tests after the rebase: `pnpm test src/docker-healthcheck.test.ts` 6/6 passed; `oxlint` 0 errors / 0 warnings and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files.

prs.title: fix(auth): tolerate invalid credential symlink targets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

External JSON credential discovery can abort with ENOTDIR when a credential symlink points beneath a regular file. The shared reader already treats missing targets and cycles as absent; this adds the distinct invalid-directory target case to that same owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep tolerant credential discovery at src/infra/json-file.ts rather than duplicating catches in each consumer. Chained-symlink resolution itself is already supplied by merged #157524; the remaining production change is ENOTDIR handling. Added filesystem regressions retain relative/absolute chains, invalid targets, dangling links and cycles.

## User Impact

An invalid legacy credential target no longer interrupts setup discovery, and readable symbolic links still reach their actual JSON payload. No configuration, default, protocol, schema, dependency, permissions or migration changes. No external authentication success is claimed. Current contribution: 2 files, production +5/-1 (net +4), tests +49/-0. AI-assisted implementation and independent source/proof review.

## Evidence

### Fresh shipped CLI and Gateway proof — October 20, 2026

- Product head: `786730fe85a60fb1698940f0b415feb3c856d8e6`.
- Authentic parent baseline: `a1a0ec6c5b553edca48d8d64f645dd0a8ae9bbc3`.
- Platform: Linux, v26.1.0, OpenClaw 2026.9.6; normal pinned-pnpm `pnpm build cliStartup` on each revision. Exact-head clean-source build stamps were checked before both runs.
- Same collector and scenarios on both revisions: SHA-256 `67bed47f29a5149374154506b03b3a6ca4db6be6005cc3b94c609bb7f449cc44`.

- Actual chain: public Gateway method → setup discovery → external executable discovery → Gemini legacy credential reader → shared JSON realpath owner. No production module was directly imported by this collector.
- External `gemini --version` discovery uses an explicitly controlled executable fixture. The OpenClaw Gateway, credential reader, filesystem and RPC output are real. This does not validate Gemini runtime/login or an external provider.

An owned synthetic HOME contains `.gemini/oauth_creds.json -> regular-file/credentials.json`, where `regular-file` is a file, not a directory. A legal control retargets the same link to `legal.json`. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two failures in the schema-29 local client credential cutover (#174599): large credential stores exceed SQLite's SQL-variable limit, and a subsequent Doctor NOCOW rewrite leaves the credential receipt bound to the replaced inode, preventing Gateway startup.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor --fix` preserves existing identities, device tokens, Gateway-scoped tokens, and IPC credentials through both extraction and verified btrfs file replacement. Neither repair changes the schema or requires new pairing. Runtime admission still refuses unrelated database replacements and incomplete receipts. Older native applications sharing the migrated local database still require the app update documented by the original cutover; this PR does not change that compatibility boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The extraction issued one INSERT per entire table. SQLite's default 32,766-variable limit fails above 5,461 six-column rows or 6,553 five-column rows. Reuse `chunkItems` for 500-row batches inside the existing transaction, including restored-native-source rebuilding. Exact-copy verification, custody, receipt publication, and source retirement retain their ordering.

Doctor's btrfs repair already verifies byte-identical replacements and retains each original inode. Its existing recovery-identity handoff now asks the credential owner to transfer a matching receipt under local custody. The original path/device/inode must match, current maintenance authority is checked before publication, and phase, provenance, and import claims remain intact. No runtime fallback or second migration owner is added.

## Evidence

A synthetic Linux rehearsal started with schema 28 from `b61b0809`, five agents, 5,000 sessions, 6,000 retained runs, and 600 paired clients. Transcript payloads were bounded: about 53 MiB total. No production state or credentials were used.

At 7,600 rows per credential table, the unmodified candidate failed in real Doctor with `too many SQL variables`; schema 28 and all source rows remained intact. Batching completed the version phase in **5.93 seconds**, preserving all **22,800 credential rows** and **600 pairing records** exactly, without migration warnings. All **600/600** existing-token Gateway handshakes passed: 100 each Control UI webchat, macOS, iOS, Android, CLI, and node protocol identities. Roles/scopes survived, no pairing requests appeared, and the real TypeScript IPC HMAC transport accepted the migrated credential and rejected an incorrect one.

Full packaged Doctor then reproduced the independent btrfs bug: exit 0 after **24.87 seconds**, exact rows preserved, but Gateway startup refused the stale receipt. The new regression reproduces that token-read failure, passes with the handoff, and keeps unrelated replacements refused. The fixed packaged run passed: **Doctor 21.70 seconds**, **Gateway spawn-to-ready 7.20 seconds**, and **600/600** old-token handshakes plus IPC accepted/rejected controls. Exact credential rows, pairing authority, and the new inode binding were verified immediately after Doctor. All owned processes exited cleanly and released the test port. The initial packaged browser probe correctly required a Control UI reload; loading the current bundle identity succeeded with the same token, without pairing or login.

SIGKILL before shared retirement and after shared COMMIT both resumed through Doctor with exact credential/pairing preservation; normal clients refused incomplete receipts. Updater recovery restored the captured schema-28 generation and local-store absence, rejected a poisoned orphan, and rebuilt it exactly on re-upgrade. A later pairing write correctly blocked restoration and remained intact. Physical NOCOW replacement also intentionally blocks automatic prior-generation restore; the successful rollback evidence covers migration before that replacement, and the existing physical-replacement refusal test remains green. Rerunning Doctor's repair owner on the stale post-NOCOW state also preserved all records and completed without warnings in **4.30 seconds**.

Focused proof: migration/update tests **25 passed**, with 3 environment-gated PostgreSQL skips; final migration fixture relocation **18 passed**. NOCOW/restore/maintenance proof **84 passed**, with 2 platform-dependent skips (74.26 seconds total wrapper time; restore file 55.48 seconds including compilation, command files 15.13 seconds). Changed-file formatting/lint, the earlier single targeted core tsrs check, export-name guard, **22 import-closure guard tests**, and independent P0–P2 reviews are clean. The added NOCOW regression fails on the base for stale credentials. macOS SQLite here allows 250,000 variables, so the large-row regression's failing-before evidence comes from real Linux Doctor.

The batching repair removes 6 production lines; the complete PR adds 50 net production lines because the missing verified-replacement handoff requires credential custody and original-generation matching. Tests reuse the relocated fixture. No Testbox/Crabbox leases were used. PR CI supplies broad validation.

These are synthetic protocol checks, not native-device UI tests. Version-phase and single-candidate timings are not A/B performance claims or a production outage guarantee. Full-volume backup, NOCOW copy, shutdown, and startup costs must be accounted for separately.

Packaged proof and final review used main `4bef0d760bc5` plus this change. A clean rebase onto `4dfd7e9f25e9` did not alter the credential or NOCOW owners; exact-head PR CI validates `6eaa52912855868a6c568045ef35a40568d85fe7`. The isolated run disabled bundled plugins and consequently emitted an unrelated missing-plugin health diagnostic; plugin health and native applications are not claimed as covered.
