prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. It ran 2026-09-18T15:49:35Z to 2026-09-18T17:47:43Z and finished **68 jobs succeeded, 3 failed, 3 cancelled, 3 skipped**. The run is terminally **non-green and release-ineligible**, and every residual is classified: - `agentic-gateway-methods` (job `105667082763`) was **cancelled at the workflow's exact 90-minute job limit** on the `ronan` seat while still heartbeating and emitting new log lines. The same shard completes on the `elliott` and `emeric` seats. This is seat throughput against a 5,231-test shard, not a product verdict — and that same cancelled log carries **111 `sessions.send-followup-status` lines, all 111 passing**, against the real stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` on the host that originally produced the `uses schema version 17` failure. - `hosted(agentic-agents-tools,auto-reply-reply-dispatch,…)` (job `105667083998`) received `The runner has received a shutdown signal` and exited 143. 778 passing test lines were captured and **no test failure precedes the signal**. Two further hosted jobs (`105667084144`, `105667084159`) are the same reclamation class. - `hosted(core-runtime-media-ui-3,core-runtime-infra-repo-tooling,…)` (job `105667084127`) is red only because `subagent-announce.live-tree-chain-proof` hit `sessions_spawn model "openai/gpt-6-astra" is not usable: The selected account ... unavailable`. That is an account provisioning gap, observed identically in six prior runs. - `aggregate + status` (job `105701732269`) is the expected fail-closed policy consequence of the residuals above, not an additional product-test failure. **No product-owned test failure and no routing failure occurred in this run.** Newly green on this exact head: the four re-laned toolchain shards `core-tooling-5`, `core-tooling-7`, `core-tooling-12` and `core-tooling-14` all succeeded on hosted runners after per-seat tooling failures, and `agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` succeeded on two different seats. The Mode-B planner identity digest `sha256:42dffd23ec447c6e4b726d0e6345f1dc2417801048aee49b96f3332233ef1f34` is preserved across those lane moves, so no shard identity changed. These residuals are runner, seat-throughput, and account-provisioning properties of the execution environment. They are not addressable inside this branch and are recorded here rather than presented as green. **Real environment tested:** An OpenClaw instance exercised live Discord ingress/egress and OTel/Tempo with content capture disabled. The full evidence chain, execution identity, ancestry, and materiality record are contained in the linked corpus rather than repeated here. **Observed behavior:** - A real retained ambient Discord event aged to 1,069,503 ms and was suppressed as `stale-ambient-backlog`; attempts remained zero. - A fresh addressed request completed with attempts zero and produced a visible response after 45.565 seconds. - Typed `continue_work` and bracket `CONTINUE_WORK` each armed and fired one five-second wake with granted provenance and completed Tempo model-call spans. - Cost-cap rejection passed an exact-source disposable fixture. - Max-chain matrix, scheduler, durable recovery, typed tool, and product delegate regression surfaces passed; the row remains partial because a docs-owned generated wrapper is stale. ### Evidence The canonical matrix contains 38 rows: **31 pass, three partial, one fail, and three missing** (`PROOFS/INDEX.json` -> corpus `7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567`). `R-CD-2` is the single fail. The partial rows are `R-CD-COLLECTION-ON-COLLAPSE`, `R-CD-TOKEN` and `R-RC-2`. The three missing rows are `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY`, `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2`. This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. The row's own `manifest` and harness `supporting_docs` pointers are currently **dangling on the docs default branch**: the harness exists but was never merged there. - `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2` each have a present manifest and failed only because the current-corpus input they read (overlap evidence file, exported trace tree) is absent. **Limits:** Historical live and Mode-B evidence for earlier heads is ancestry/materiality evidence, not exact-target execution. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Proven at `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`, receipts being the real stdout of the real runs committed under `gates/` and `mergeability/`: | gate | verdict | |---|---| | `pnpm tsgo:core` | **pass** rc=0 | | `pnpm lint` — oxlint core, extensions, scripts | **pass** rc=0 | | Gate 2.7 vs the absorbed base `715077a3be` | **pass** — 839 files, 466 GENUINE, 373 SAFE-NEW, **0 FROZEN-STALE**, **0 MIXED-CLOBBER** | | `vitest` rollback-custody regressions | **pass** 10/10 | | `vitest` delivery-queue + session-delivery | **pass** 124/124 | | `vitest` gateway maintenance + close + delegate-artifacts | **pass** 123/123 | | `vitest` production-boundary + spawn-cleanup | 28/30 — two tracked reds | **Diff size has not grown across four absorbs.** From the absorbed base — which is what this PR shows — the change is 839 files, +140,919 / −4,301, against 841 / +140,951 / −4,277 before this cycle. (`git diff upstream/main HEAD` reports 2,358 files, but that is the symmetric difference including upstream commits newer than the merge base, and is not what a PR shows.) The worktree was clean at publication: zero untracked files, no stray additions. **Two known reds, neither hidden nor softened.** `karmaterminal/openclaw#1356` is an order-dependent failure of the `operator-revoked` queued-collector cleanup: it **passes in isolation** with all four `cleanupComplete` operands true and the child session genuinely deleted, and fails only when the `operator-completed` arm has run first. Upstream's own test and test-support files for it are byte-identical to ours, so the divergence is product-side. `karmaterminal/openclaw#1350` is the streamed-text offset/fencing contract, pre-existing. **No live behavioral row was fired at this SHA, and none is presented as though it were.** The fleet that runs these behaviors serves composite `1baff536afa549fea75660403c453bbd265352c0`, a *divergent sibling* of the presented SHA rather than an ancestor of it — their merge-base is `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and neither is an ancestor of the other. A live fire on that runtime would be evidence about the composite, so every row is marked `not_fired_at_this_sha` instead of being carried over as a pass. The prior corpus at `3821eaef72` remains linked per row as the baseline to re-fire against. Live rows are unblocked by a redeploy onto a runtime that has this SHA as a git ancestor. That redeploy is itself a migration boundary: this head carries the agent schema bump **21 → 22** via `migrateTranscriptFtsRowSchema`, and the fleet serves 21, so it wants migration-success and rollback-compatibility receipts of its own. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: refactor(ui): share setup handling and existing view contracts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several setup and settings views repeat request handling or manually mirror types already owned elsewhere.

## User Impact

No intended visible change for valid Gateway responses. Setup cancellation, connection ownership, errors, retries and ready-only roster refresh remain intact. No configuration, schema, protocol, dependency or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share the Custodian retry/activation request envelope, derive view packets from their existing producers, and use Vite's canonical ambient types instead of four local declarations. The Custodian question adapter now normalizes display text without rechecking the typed Gateway contract or imposing a second choice policy.

This is a **118-net-production-line residue** (+47/-165; tests/declarations excluded), submitted under the campaign's residue floor waiver, not counted as a large cleanup PR.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Question object/option shape and 2–4 count: trust the Gateway-owned `SystemAgentChatQuestionSchema` instead of repeating its checks in the view. Introduced with the structured-question feature (#110242, `897198b9f539c`), not a cited human malformed-response incident. A future malformed producer is a Gateway contract defect, not a client compatibility path.
- Duplicate labels/multiple recommendations: inspected deterministic greeting, onboarding and wizard producers provide these choices; the original feature has no cited human report requiring a second view policy. If a producer supplies such choices, render them as sent rather than silently replace the card with prose. Whitespace normalization, empty display-text omission, reply/skip semantics and Gateway authorization are retained.

## Evidence

- Nine focused files: **58 tests passed**, including setup request ownership, structured choices, Memory/Security, Cloud Worker profiles and the four presentation catalogs.
- Targeted production type graph passed; selected test graph extends the official `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-pages.json` and includes both appearance-background browser fixtures.
- Suppression guard: **14 passed**. Runtime and static/Madge import cycles: **0**. Targeted type-aware UI lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Independent review: scoped-clean through P2.
- Inspected synthetic before/after captures below use isolated browser/runtime state and fixture Gateway responses, not a live account or the real OpenClaw home. The configured setup card, recommendations, skip and composer match visually; each capture issued one setup request and one greeting. This is visual fixture proof, not live-provider acceptance.
- Hosted exact-head CI is the broad gate; no broad local build or suite was run.
- CI corrections: canonical Vite typing exposed an obsolete local import-meta cast and redundant boolean comparison; the entry now uses `import.meta.env.PROD`. Service-worker proof passed 32 tests and suppression proof passed 14. Run 39353925487 then correctly required shrinking the assertion baseline for the deleted cast from one to zero. The exact baseline deletion passes the assertion-safety ratchet and suppression14 tests, with independent P0–P2 review scoped-clean. Both failures are ours, repaired without CI reruns, broader ignores or weakened assertions.

### Before

![Custodian before cleanup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/515bf48b-e935-405a-ad70-c5dda58a70bc)

### After

![Custodian after cleanup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c8dd705-f66e-4e89-b616-6bc4db683b33)


## CI repair

The initial exact-head CI passed all tests/types/browser jobs but exposed `ui/src/main.ts:49`'s redundant production-flag comparison after canonical Vite ambient types became available. This PR-caused lint failure was reproduced locally, then fixed by removing the obsolete local ImportMeta intersection and using Vite's boolean directly. The exact one-file lint now passes, all 32 focused service-worker tests and the 14-test suppression guard pass, and fresh independent review is clean through P2. No CI rerun, timeout increase, suppression or inherited-failure exception. Hosted CI on the repaired head remains the broad gate.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Under CI load, the reconnect test's four-second polling window can expire while reconnect, subscription recovery, and inbound dispatch are still progressing. The original release plugin shard logged the target test timing out after 4.617s.

## Fix

The cold-start test now waits for the inbound-produced signal through Vitest's abort-aware `withinTest` helper. On timeout or cancellation, the wait rejects so the existing `finally` aborts and joins the Gateway before teardown.

The socket-backed Gateway test sends its post-reconnect message only after the second ready state, then verifies the actual second room subscription keeps the initial activation floor.

## Evidence

prs.title: feat(telegram): support copy-text presentation buttons
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

- **Problem:** plugins cannot express a portable copy-to-clipboard control through message presentation.
- **Demand:** continues the missing capability first explored in #36105; current `main` still has no equivalent portable action or Telegram encoder.
- **Value:** Telegram gets a native `CopyTextButton`; channels without native support keep a safe, readable manual-copy fallback.
- **Smallest complete fix:** add one capability-gated shared action, Telegram encoding, and fallback behavior at every affected channel boundary.
- **Scope:** presentation payloads, shared limits, Telegram, and existing Discord/Slack/Feishu fallback owners; no raw Telegram button input.
- **Risk:** public additive SDK surface and message-delivery behavior; exact-value privacy, select budgets, mentions, locations, and edits are regression-covered.
- **Proof:** exact-head focused suites pass **127/127**; core and extension production/test typechecks, changed-file format/lint, assertion ratchet, and merge simulation pass.
- **Gap:** native Telegram Test Server send → tap → clipboard proof remains externally blocked on authenticated broker access.
- **Non-goals:** no callback reinterpretation, provider-keyboard takeover, Gateway/config change, or production activation.
- **Maintainer ask:** accept the additive portable `copy-text` contract and review the repaired exact head.

## What Problem This Solves

Add a portable typed `copy-text` presentation action. Telegram renders it as a
native Bot API `CopyTextButton`; channels without native support keep a readable,
safe manual-copy fallback.

This updates the existing contribution first explored in #36105. It does not
reintroduce the retired raw Telegram button input.

## Current maintenance head

- **Exact head:** `d3c9ca87eb7ce42243ff9f65796f474f8e8c6007`
- **Frozen base:** `cd57bc91d991ba1350009e935caaf21e70c09c89`
- **Shape:** one signed semantic commit, 45 files, +2,636/-343.
- **Merge simulation:** clean against the frozen base.

The frozen base has no equivalent portable `copy-text` presentation action or
Telegram `copy_text` encoder. Existing inline-code tap-to-copy behavior is a
separate rendering path and does not expose this capability to plugins.

## Behavior

- The message tool schema exposes a typed `copy-text` action with a required
  string value.
- The shared presentation adapter preserves the action only when a channel
  declares `copyTextButtons`; unsupported channels render readable manual-copy
  fallback while callback payload values remain private.
- Telegram emits `InlineKeyboardButton.copy_text` only for values satisfying
  the Bot API's 1–256-character contract. Values that cannot be encoded safely
  remain visible as escaped fallback instead of being silently rewritten.
- Native controls share Telegram's existing 100-action budget, including every
  option in a select that Telegram renders as an individual button. Every
  native select row is reserved before Discord-sized button selection.
- Direct Telegram sends retain authored select prompts while excluding native
  copy values from visible text.
- Standalone location sends never receive a synthetic text anchor.
- Provider-owned and usable legacy keyboards retain precedence; unusable legacy
  controls do not falsely displace a valid presentation keyboard.
- Drop-time copy identity keeps duplicate labels paired with the correct value
  when an action falls back after planning.
- Markup-only edits do not synthesize replacement body text. If a rejected,
  over-budget, or shadowed copy control needs readable fallback, the action
  returns a recoverable result requiring explicit content or caption.
- Discord long-copy fallback uses a complete collision-safe fence in every
  independently rendered fragment. Mention suppression derives from the exact
  rendered fallback text, including enabled and disabled labels.

## Evidence

Exact-head focused behavior suites pass **127/127** across the 14 changed test
files:

- shared payload, message-tool visibility, and presentation limits: **13**
- Discord delivery/fallback/mention boundaries: **93**
- Telegram native/fallback/direct-action paths: **19**
- Slack fallback: **1**
- Feishu fallback: **1**

The PR-wrapper runtime-closure suite also passes **19/19** after adding the new
payload fallback helper to the wrapper's explicit trusted inventory. This
repairs the only branch-owned failure found by the first hosted run.

Exact-head static gates:

- core production typecheck: pass
- core test typecheck shards: pass
- extension production typecheck: pass
- extension test typecheck: pass
- changed core/extension/script lint: pass
- changed-file Oxfmt and `git diff --check`: pass
- assertion-safety ratchet: pass; the branch shrinks the
  `outbound-components.ts` baseline from two assertions to one
- merge tree against the frozen base: clean

The canonical changed-check also reports two full-tree failures already present
unchanged in the frozen base: three pre-existing UI `max-lines` suppressions are
absent from their baseline, and the database-first guard flags two pre-existing
retired-runtime migration files. This PR does not touch those files. Hosted PR
CI is the authoritative broad gate for the published head.

The isolated worktree was hydrated with the frozen lockfile to run the pinned
toolchain. No lockfile or dependency declaration changed; no Gateway, runtime
configuration, credential, or production state was touched.

## Live proof state

No exact-head live Telegram send/tap/clipboard claim is made. Historical branch
proof is not used as a substitute for current-head evidence. Remaining live
proof requires an authenticated Telegram Test Server/broker route to send the
native button, tap it in a Telegram client, verify exact clipboard bytes, and
exercise invalid-value/edit fallback. That route is currently unavailable to
the contributor environment.

## Maintainer decision

This intentionally keeps `copy-text` as a portable, capability-gated
presentation action rather than a Telegram-local input. Maintainer acceptance
of that public SDK surface remains the upstream product gate.

AI-assisted implementation and tests.

prs.title: fix(ui): offer desktop setup instead of Retry when Host Desktop is off
prs.body:
Closes #174368

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the chat Desktop panel says "The requested desktop is unavailable. Retry when the machine is ready." and offers only Retry when the Gateway's Host Desktop is not set up, so retrying can never help (repro in the issue).

## User Impact

User impact: opening Desktop in a local chat on a Gateway without Host Desktop now says "Desktop access is not enabled on the Gateway host." and that the panel shares the Gateway host's screen, not the screen of the device running the browser, then fixes it in place. When no screen-sharing server is running, the panel shows the steps for the Gateway host (on macOS: System Settings, General, Sharing on the Gateway host Mac) and Check again, which shows Refreshing while it re-checks. When Screen Sharing is already running, it says which account the sign-in will use (a macOS user account on the Gateway host, or the desktop server's own password elsewhere) and offers Enable desktop access in OpenClaw to connections that can change config; everyone else is told that a Gateway administrator can enable it (with Check again). Both states note that the screen-sharing or desktop server may be reachable from other devices on the network. Once Host Desktop is on, the panel re-checks and connects to the same Gateway desktop without leaving the chat. Other machines, and offline or starting targets, keep today's message.

## Why This Change Was Made

For the Gateway host, the chat panel now asks the Gateway for the same Host Desktop setup check the Systems page uses and renders that setup state inside the panel, worded for the Gateway host.

The panel only accepted environments that already advertise a desktop. A Gateway with `desktop.host.enabled` off never advertises one, so the panel fell through to the generic notice. The setup discovery (`environments.list` with `includeDesktopSetup`), the setup state selection and the narrow `desktop.host.enabled` patch already existed in Systems. This change moves the state selection and the patch into one helper that Systems and the panel share, so policy and the authority check are not duplicated. The helper declares the narrow runtime-config shape it needs and imports nothing from the panel inputs, so `desktop-panel-inputs.ts` imports that type from the helper in one direction only. Systems keeps its own copy, which sits under the selected machine's row; the panel uses its own English keys that name the Gateway host (the browser is often on another computer), plus the account and network lines shown before consent.

| Chat desktop target and state | Panel shows | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gateway host, Host Desktop off, no screen-sharing server (macOS) | cause line naming the Gateway host / "Turn on Screen Sharing" / "On the Gateway host Mac, open System Settings ..." / network note | Check again: re-reads inventory, connects once Host Desktop is available |
| Same on Linux and others | cause line / "Set up a desktop server" / VNC or managed desktop steps for the Gateway host / "The desktop server may be reachable from other devices on your network." | Check again |
| Gateway host, Host Desktop off, Screen Sharing detected, connection can patch config | cause line / "Screen Sharing is available" / network note / account line (macOS user account on the Gateway host, sign-in prompt follows) / "Applies without restarting the Gateway." | Enable desktop access in OpenClaw: same `desktop.host.enabled: true` patch as Systems, then re-read and connect; a rejected patch shows the config error |
| Same on Linux and others | cause line / "A desktop is available" / network note / account line (the desktop server's own password) | Same |
| Same, connection cannot patch config | Same, Enable disabled, "A Gateway administrator can enable desktop access." | Check again |
| Gateway host, setup check reports `unsupported` | cause line / "Screen sharing needs attention" / setup steps plus the Gateway's reason | Check again |
| Gateway host, the setup check itself fails | Unchanged generic notice | Unchanged: Retry |
| Gateway host, Host Desktop on but nothing on the RFB port | Unchanged: the Gateway advertises a desktop, the panel connects and shows the existing disconnect reason | Unchanged |
| Node, worker, unknown source, or session without a desktop | Unchanged: "The requested desktop is unavailable. Retry when the machine is ready." | Unchanged: Retry |
| Target offline, starting, or inventory failure | Unchanged | Unchanged |
| Focused desktop window (document mode) and the docked picker outside chat | Unchanged (picker with notice) | Unchanged |
| Host Desktop on but the OS refuses the account | Unchanged: existing credentials prompt or disconnect reason | Unchanged |

How the issue's Expected behavior maps to the rows above:

| Expected behavior (issue) | Where it is met |
| --- | --- |
| Explain that Host Desktop is not enabled, distinct from missing Screen Sharing, offline, startup, or auth failure | Cause line on every Host-Desktop-off row; "Turn on Screen Sharing" vs "Screen Sharing is available" rows; offline/starting and OS-refuses-account rows unchanged |

| Retest and connect the selected desktop without other Settings pages | Check again and post-Enable re-check, then connect to the same Gateway desktop in the chat panel |

OpenClaw never turns on Screen Sharing itself or changes macOS permissions. The docs' Desktop section now mentions the chat panel path.

## Evidence

All of the following ran on one machine (macOS, Apple silicon) at the staged tree, base `714a6da6196`. The screenshots in Behaviour were captured one revision earlier; the only later change is the type import above (no emitted code), and the upgrade run below rendered the same text from the final tree.

**Behaviour.** Local chat, Layout, Toggle desktop panel. Panel text read from the DOM (`innerText`):

This panel shares the Gateway host's screen, not the screen of the device running this browser.` / `Turn on Screen Sharing` / `On the Gateway host Mac, open System Settings → General → Sharing. Turn on Screen Sharing, or allow the Gateway host account to Observe and Control in Remote Management, then check again.` / `Screen Sharing may also be reachable from other devices on your network.` / `Check again`

The Gateway config afterwards had `desktop.host.enabled: true`, and the panel showed the macOS account prompt (`Enter a macOS account allowed in System Settings → General → Sharing. ...`). No credentials were entered.

**Upgrade and existing settings.** Latest stable `openclaw@2026.10.5` (npm `latest`) was installed in a temporary directory. Its own CLI wrote each config (`openclaw config set --batch-file`, `meta.lastTouchedVersion: "2026.10.5"`) with a full `desktop.host` block using every key its schema accepts, and the stable Gateway booted on it (`[gateway] http server listening (15 plugins: ...)`, then `[shutdown] completed cleanly in 134ms`). The Control UI built from this tree connected to it. Paths are shown as `<arm-A>` / `<arm-C>`; the password file holds a synthetic value.

prs.title: fix(arcee): make OpenRouter onboarding runnable
prs.body:
Closes #112747

AI-assisted: implemented and verified with Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Arcee setup through OpenRouter should keep provider configuration, model references, and the stored OpenRouter credential under the same provider owner. The original July onboarding preset wrote an `arcee/...` route while storing the credential as `openrouter:default`, causing the first agent request to fail. Current main also has legacy auth-alias support; this PR makes new OpenRouter setup canonical and repairs previously persisted configuration.

The previous PR head had two compatibility defects: Doctor removed the old provider without migrating every agent model scope, and re-onboarding overwrote an existing shared OpenRouter endpoint/API mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

- New OpenRouter-backed Arcee setup selects `openrouter/arcee-ai/trinity-large-thinking` and owns its provider configuration under `models.providers.openrouter`.
- Doctor migrates defaults, keyed agent entries, legacy agent lists, primary/fallback references, model aliases, nested subagent/heartbeat/compaction/media selections, and explicit model-policy references before removing the old OpenRouter-backed Arcee catalog.
- Existing canonical model settings win on collisions. Migration is immutable and idempotent; direct Arcee configuration is unchanged.
- Both registered onboarding and the public catalog helper preserve an existing OpenRouter `baseUrl` and `api`, seeding defaults only when absent.
- Integration with current main preserves connection-only setup in merge mode and catalog seeding in replace mode, plus the eager public catalog helper. The Doctor repair is declared in the plugin manifest and uses the current lightweight migration SDK.

## User Impact

Fresh OpenRouter setup has matching credential and model ownership. Existing installations retain their proxy transport and authored model settings. Older OpenRouter-backed Arcee configuration can be repaired with `openclaw doctor --fix`; direct Arcee setup is unaffected.

## Evidence

### Current repair and upstream integration — 2026-09-17

Head: `54ab6358560c4f59a59b06bc820d335a5b08623d`. Rebased onto `9ace0a571f4151cd1f47eb8aaa7b8cc987c45cee` to resolve the actual merge conflicts; no unrelated main changes were reverted.

- Before the fix: five new regression cases failed and twelve tests passed on the old PR base. Failures covered defaults/entries/legacy-list migration and custom OpenRouter transport with and without an explicit API mode.
- Final current-main proof with Node 24.20.0 and pinned pnpm 12.4.0:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/arcee/doctor-contract-api.test.ts extensions/arcee/index.test.ts` — **39 passed**.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/plugins/doctor-contract-declarations.test.ts -t 'matches every resolvable artifact'` — **1 passed**, 1 unrelated state-migration case deselected.
  - Targeted `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Registered interactive/non-interactive setup, credential isolation, merge/replace behavior, public helper behavior, migration scope completeness, input preservation, and idempotence are covered.
- [GitHub checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/113097/checks) report the hosted CI status for the current head; the earlier head's green CI is not reused as current-head proof.
- No fresh paid model request or operator-Gateway deployment was performed for this repair. The historical live inference proof below belongs only to its explicitly identified earlier head.

### Historical live inference proof — original PR head

Performed on 2026-07-31 from PR head `f8ac6b1ce06ded770ee5325191fbfca274600bab` with a newly issued real OpenRouter credential. Private credential material was removed and never printed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): promote nodes that connect during approval
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A node can finish connecting while its first capability approval is being written. `node.pair.approve` previously captured the live connection before that wait. When it captured absence, the approval committed but skipped the newly registered connection, leaving an approved, connected node with an empty command list.

Select the live session in the existing committed-approval callback. Keep the exact pairing identity, previous generation, connection, and declared-surface checks before promoting it. This also removes the redundant pre-write pending lookup; no command registration, authorization policy, protocol, timeout, or retry behavior changes.

The regression registers a real `NodeRegistry` session while the handler enters its real pairing write. Before the fix, approval succeeds but the session still has `commands: []`; after the fix it must have `system.run` and the committed pairing generation. Existing token-rotation and replacement refusal assertions remain intact.

## Evidence

- Investigated hourly 39351108236, job 118395379563: the worker e2e observed an approved executor with `commands: []`.
- The original native worker e2e passed twice on macOS before the fix. The exact CI timing is therefore not claimed as reproduced. The deterministic approval-owner regression reproduces the same empty-command state on the original source.
- Compared the direct manifest, catalog, reconciliation and approval owners across `87692eba0956..353c6989892e`: unchanged. The pre-write snapshot predates that window; none of the listed suspects is attributed as a deterministic registration regression.
- Red: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'connects while its first surface approval is pending'` fails with expected `["system.run"]`, received `[]` before the fix.
- Green: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.test.ts test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-node-exec-routing.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes **16 tests**. This includes the original native command-routing/effect proof and existing token-rotation/replacement refusals.
- E2E runtime build, focused typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Production diff: +4/-6 lines; test diff: +42 lines. The temporary e2e diagnostic change was removed; its assertions and waits are unchanged.
- Independent P2 autoreview: scoped-clean.

prs.title: feat(sandbox): add lightweight local SRT backend
prs.body:
Related: #163540

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw needs a local sandbox backend that confines commands and file tools without Docker. This adds the `srt-sandbox` plugin through `registerSandboxBackend()`, configured for independent distribution (npm / ClawHub) rather than bundled inclusion, and corrects permission and process-lifetime defects in the original draft.

## User Impact

macOS uses Seatbelt; Linux uses Bubblewrap and seccomp. Private writable paths remain usable while restricted host workspaces, managed skills and readonly resources stay protected. Command descendants are swept on completion, failure, cancellation, timeout and owner death. Host runtime authority stays live: once the host revokes runtime authority, new commands, deferred exec specs, pin-owner mutations and broker policy writes reject immediately with the host's original error, while terminate/finalize/dispose/release keep working so cleanup stays available.

Windows execution is disabled before native provisioning with SRT 0.0.76. Configuration compatibility and read-only dependency discovery remain available, but every Windows command, preparation and filesystem entry rejects before account, credential, WFP or ACL mutation. The pinned installer cannot establish exclusive ownership of its shared account or safely cancel and reverse partial grants. Native Windows execution must remain disabled until an owner-aware provisioning API and the documented VM qualification are available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commands, buffered execution and file tools share one authoritative filesystem policy, including canonical aliases and nonexistent descendants of protected roots. Linux mounts writable ancestors of readonly roots as anchors so an ancestor rename cannot move a protected child. Supplied mutation pins must match the complete destination and remain live; expired, consumed and mismatched pins reject instead of resolving replacement authority. Host custody stays outside guest signaling permissions. All command routes use this custody. Before launching macOS guests, the existing Seatbelt profile is tightened to reject `setsid`, `setpgid` and `posix_spawn`, preventing descendants from leaving the owned process group. Ordinary fork/exec remains supported; spawn-based launchers, daemonization and job-control group changes are unsupported and fail closed. The pinned wrapper is decoded as literal argv without executing command bytes on a host shell; an unexpected wrapper rejects before launch. Buffered commands now start a fresh SRT process with the current policy; this adds per-command startup overhead. Startup-hook and loader environment variables are rejected before host interpreters launch. Container-style readonly resource path projection is unsupported.

The eight previous review findings are addressed as follows:

1. Workspace permissions: preserve `none`, `ro` and `rw`; protect canonical managed skills and readonly resources in command and file paths, including broad extra writable roots and symlink aliases.
2. Windows scope reuse: coalesce concurrent resolutions and reuse the same authoritative scope/policy across turns; reject different scopes and retired generations.
3. Windows provisioning retirement: remove the unsafe native provisioning path entirely. Execution rejects before installation or grants, including after retirement; no partial cleanup or shared-account adoption is claimed.
4. Streaming custody: host-owned liveness channels and guardians sweep descendants when the launcher or Gateway dies, while preserving output and exit status. Native macOS kernel restrictions prevent session/group-changing descendants from escaping that sweep; delayed-write proof covers ordinary buffered, broker and streaming routes.
5. Broker completion: execute buffered commands under independent host custody and sweep background descendants on success, failure and timeout. The session control process accepts health/policy RPCs only.
6. Windows network settings: reject all execution modes before persistent effects; runtime behavior, configuration hints and platform documentation agree.
7. Live runtime authority: the host's `assertRuntimeCurrent` callback is retained for the handle's lifetime and re-checked after every await, immediately before each effect-bearing operation — command launch (ordinary and broker routes), deferred exec specs, pin-owner spawns, owner RPC writes, and broker startup/health/policy writes. The deferred exec spec composes the caller's own `assertCurrent` with the authority recheck instead of discarding it. Rejection rethrows the host's original error unchanged; `allowFailure` does not swallow it; a rejected pinned mutation releases its held pin; a rejected broker launch handshake cancels the lease and closes the socket. Output-overflow termination stays independent of authority. An already-running command is not killed by the plugin on revocation; the core's cancel path handles running processes, and the plugin blocks every new effect.
8. Factory admission authority: the POSIX factory rechecks the host's `assertRuntimeCurrent` after dependency discovery and again after backend initialization, before the backend is published to the live-scope set. The existing catch stays the single cleanup path (no double dispose); a failed cleanup cannot replace the host's original error; and a provisioning-time revocation leaves no published handle or lingering proxy infrastructure. The exec-spec builder also closes any custody lease it opened itself on every failure path, so an early rejection no longer leaves a lease alive until scope teardown.

Distribution: the plugin now declares independent-distribution metadata following the existing `openshell` and `mxc` sandbox-backend conventions — `openclaw.release.publishToNpm`/`publishToClawHub`, install specs (`clawhub:@openclaw/srt-sandbox` / `@openclaw/srt-sandbox`, host floor matching `compat.pluginApi`), the root `!dist/extensions/srt-sandbox/**` package exclusion, README and `.npmignore` — and the generated inventory/reference docs list it under Official external packages. This matches the reviewer-recommended external-first route and VISION.md's preference for independently maintained optional plugins, and it gives the extension package-boundary tooling a packaged surface for srt-sandbox: previously the only `bundledDist:false` plugin without release metadata, which failed the boundary check with "No packaged surface for extension boundary: srt-sandbox". Maintainer confirmation of the external-first route (versus bundled sponsorship) is still requested in the PR discussion.

Session settings JSON and control messages are ephemeral runtime state, not a stored-data schema migration. Temporary command settings are removed by their custody finalizer, session settings are removed on disposal, and the existing configuration-contract tests cover the accepted settings. No database or user-state migration is introduced.

## Evidence

- Upstream `main` fetched and incorporated at `e43a62c404d457a7da2528e9b3e0dcaa09f98585`.
- Exact tested/pushed head: `0ed9a3717a31eb2e6c263dd4cd23440289e756e4`.
- Full exact-head SRT suite on macOS: 165 passed / 11 Linux-only skipped across 20 passed and 2 skipped files, zero failures. The earlier native Linux full-suite run below (120 passed / 16 macOS-only skipped) covers the permission, network and custody paths at a prior revision; a native Linux rerun at this head will follow with the gateway-level proof.

prs.title: fix: recover replies when compaction requests time out
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A compaction request timeout aborts its enclosing turn before existing client fallback can recover. An unfinished compaction deadline can also leave a session marked done rather than timed out.

## Fix

Keep request-local failures with the existing compaction owner. Extend existing terminal timeout handling to unfinished compaction, preserving completed answers, delivery custody, accepted continuations, external cancellation and whole-run deadlines. No new retries, configuration, schema or public SDK surface.

Thanks @enki for the fix and regression coverage. Contributor commits are preserved.

## Evidence

Built, isolated Linux Gateways on pinned main `7a628b0adaa045d1488f6f4fa1161312b9c8b1a8` and candidate `75faf616eabde98c20b4cf8bd65554e477c467f3`, configured through shipped commands, received authenticated `chat.send` calls and used the actual HTTPS/SSE transport against a synthetic local peer. Conversation state came from ordinary chat requests, not seeded transcripts. No fake timers or replaced abort callbacks were used in runtime proof.

The recovery fixture sends normal turns and usage, then stalls the actual native `compaction_trigger` request at a supported 2-second provider deadline. Two fresh main runs fail identically; the non-stalling native-compaction control succeeds. The candidate reaches existing client-summary fallback and returns its final on the original run:

```text
main, twice:
agent.wait status=error error="agent run failed" terminalReply.disposition=empty
sessions.describe status=done

main, non-stalling control:
agent.wait status=ok terminalReply.text=RECOVERED-P176096
sessions.describe status=done

candidate:
embedded run auto-compaction failed: reason=timeout
ChatGPT V2 compaction unavailable; falling back to client compaction
 auto-compaction succeeded; retrying prompt
agent.wait status=ok terminalReply.text=RECOVERED-P176096
sessions.describe status=done lastRunError absent
```

The separate terminal-error control uses supported `compaction.mode=default`, a 1-second run budget and 3-second compaction grace. A real SDK `incomplete/max_output_tokens` response with input usage 25000/output 10 triggers threshold compaction in a 32000-token model. Its summary stream continues meaningful reasoning until the run deadline expires:

```text
main:
agent.wait status=error error="agent run failed" terminalReply.text=PARTIAL-P176096
sessions.describe status=done lastRunError absent

candidate:
agent.wait status=error
error="Context compaction timed out before a response was generated. Please try again."
terminalReply.text=PARTIAL-P176096
sessions.describe status=timeout
lastRunError="Context compaction timed out before a response was generated. Please try again."
```

The summary uses the existing degraded-quality fallback: this proves recovery and reply delivery, not summary quality or an external-provider outage. All provider fixtures and conversation text are synthetic.

47 focused tests pass across `attempt-execution-phase.test.ts` and `terminal-timeout.test.ts`. The integration retains upstream watchdog attribution coverage and the compaction regressions. The cancellation regression now includes a completed answer: it failed before the timeout-ownership guard and passes afterward without restoring cancelled output. The owning agents-other test type graph passes after removing an obsolete lifecycle fixture property. A separate exact-head live `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` turn through the built CLI passed with its expected marker; its task credential was deleted.

Whole-diff simplification retained the existing owners without adding state or a second recovery mechanism. Production +34/-17 (net +17); tests +230/-48 (net +182). Remaining production growth distinguishes unfinished compaction from completed answers and keeps request-local failure ownership; test growth covers distinct fallback, cancellation, custody, continuation and terminal boundaries.

## Compatibility and merge danger

No migration, configuration or public contract expansion. Two-way door: reverting restores prior runtime behavior without changing stored formats. Blast radius is built-in OpenClaw runs that compact their model context; an incorrect change could misclassify a timeout or prevent recovery/delivery.

prs.title: test(postgres): qualify TLS and exec SecretRef connections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL TLS DSNs and exec-backed connection SecretRefs had driver/schema support without PostgreSQL-specific CLI and Gateway acceptance evidence.

Related: #177922.

## User Impact

Documents both connection surfaces as Supported on PostgreSQL 17. Use `sslmode=verify-full` with an absolute `sslrootcert` path for private CAs. The guide includes TLS-only server configuration and a plain-output exec provider example.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing connection owner already passes the DSN intact to `pg.Client`; no runtime repair or new configuration option was needed. The host resolves exec secrets before publishing database worker input. Extend the existing CLI and Gateway conformance cases to cover exec resolution, output/config redaction, failed providers, worker reuse, and restart without duplicating their expensive setup. The live TLS/SCRAM run also exposed a fixture defect: the limited-role schema-privilege test assumed passwordless authentication and inherited CONNECT. Give that synthetic role an explicit password and CONNECT grant so the assertion actually reaches the denied CREATE privilege; revoke the grant during cleanup.

The broader support matrix has landed. This diff updates its existing TLS and exec rows and their accompanying prose, with the detailed qualification linked from both references. Current main was merged to reconcile that overlapping documentation; prior live proofs are retained and final-head CI will run again.

## Evidence

Live fixture: Homebrew PostgreSQL 17.11, `unaccent` 1.1, `pg_trgm` 1.6, pgvector 0.8.7; throwaway CA/certificates, loopback port, synthetic role and isolated HOME/TMPDIR. The server had only `hostssl ... scram-sha-256` TCP rules. The full conformance harness uses an administrative fixture role because it creates/drops test databases, roles and extensions; initial CLI onboarding also succeeded before that role was elevated.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Env DSN, `verify-full` plus private CA | Real `pnpm openclaw onboard --non-interactive`, `doctor`, `status --deep --json`, Gateway readiness, and online deep status passed. Bridge reported TLS 1.3. |
| Exec DSN, same TLS parameters | Same CLI/Gateway flow passed; DSN/password absent from authored config, Doctor, status JSON and Gateway logs. |
| Wrong CA | Bridge and CLI refused: `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE`, `unable to verify the first certificate`. |
| Hostname mismatch | A localhost-only certificate with a `127.0.0.1` DSN refused: `ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID`. |
| Untrusted self-signed server | Refused: `DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT`, `self-signed certificate`. |
| `sslmode=disable` | Refused by server: `28000`, `no pg_hba.conf entry ... no encryption`. |
| Exec exit 23 / empty stdout | CLI and Gateway exited 1: `database.postgres.connection SecretRef is unresolved (exec:pgdsn:database-dsn). Configure a resolvable PostgreSQL DSN (prefer a SecretRef).` Even deliberate DSN output on provider stderr was absent from diagnostics. |

TLS negatives were exercised through the real bridge and CLI model listing, Doctor, and deep JSON status. Errors named the connection repair step and contained no DSN/password. No plaintext fallback was observed.

Commands (DSN supplied from the synthetic fixture, omitted here):

```sh
pnpm openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --auth-choice skip --skip-daemon --skip-channels --skip-skills --skip-search --skip-health --skip-ui --skip-hooks --workspace <isolated-workspace> --json
pnpm openclaw doctor --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions
pnpm openclaw status --deep --json
pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$TLS_DSN"
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$TLS_DSN" -- src/infra/database-engine/cli-oneshot.postgres.test.ts src/gateway/server-database-engine.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The focused TLS conformance run passed both changed files (7 tests; 298s wall including preparation, 218s test phase). The existing CLI flow took 131s and the Gateway exec/restart case 38s on this loaded host; reusing those flows avoids duplicate setup. The complete TLS conformance command finished: 565 tests passed; two fixture-related cases failed. The repaired search-admission file passes all 5 cases (55s wall including preparation, 13.8s test phase). The other case uses `port-command-proxy.test-support.ts`, whose packet-level COMMIT interceptor explicitly forces `sslmode=disable`; the TLS-only server correctly refuses it. That same fault-injection case passed on a separate throwaway plaintext server; an exact-final-head TLS rerun reproduces the expected refusal. All other TLS port/backup/recovery cases passed. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed on final head `abd8eb30511a0ae23683bb364c0b1e6266be612c`: [CI run 39357227624](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39357227624). Targeted typechecks, lint, format, config examples, MDX, link audit and glossary checks pass. The changed-path typecheck wrapper also reported an existing test-root-budget failure (gateway-root 725 / plugins-platform 726 versus advisory 720); all selected compiler graphs passed and this change adds no test files. Simplification retained the existing owners and setup; production delta is zero. Independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

prs.title: fix(doctor): unblock runtime cleanup under deserialized systemd managers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes update recovery where Doctor leaves retained runtimes behind because `systemd --user --deserialize=<fd>` prevents recognition of its same-UID `(sd-pam)` child.

Fixes #177876

## Why This Change Was Made

The census accepts the existing systemd user-manager argv or that argv with one numeric `--deserialize` argument. Linux, exact-binary, and same-UID parent checks still gate the PAM exemption.

## User Impact

Doctor can reclaim updater runtimes in this systemd re-exec case while continuing to retain unrelated or unverified processes.

## Evidence

- Linux behavior: On Docker Desktop's ARM64 LinuxKit VM, an Ubuntu 24.04 systemd 255.4 user manager ran as UID 1000 with `--deserialize=23`; its real `(sd-pam)` child had an unreadable `/proc/<pid>/cwd`. Stable `2026.10.5` Doctor retained the abandoned runtime with `Could not classify PID 8866: working directory is unavailable`. The PR build removed an abandoned runtime on the same Linux process view. The app container used host-PID visibility, a private `/tmp`, and a masked `/.dockerenv` marker; the systemd/PAM processes and procfs results were real, with no mocked process table.
- Live-holder check: Doctor retained a marked runtime while a live Node process referenced an entrypoint inside it, then removed it after that holder exited.
- Stable-to-candidate package replacement: npm latest was `2026.10.5` (`1b58cb9`). Replacing it with the locally packed PR build (`2b31880`, same package version) preserved these SHA-256 values byte-for-byte: config `0a9f0f140ecf0387e5993d82761a366873a260ac8a825bb27d53f1c1709b7764`, SQLite state `a7178b414156d2317e53be5958886d0ddfb54bf007683dd83d258ce55121ec0b`, and `MEMORY.md` `136c777444a736fee02df6c2960a9a47154a005ccf2de4a550ac5652abe6ef41`.
- Production-module regressions: base `353c6989892e6f01ff7ff63931eb30da58cd99e4` reports both PIDs with unreadable-cwd warnings; head `2b31880117efb52107a318f3ef5f1934c80102f7` passes. Standard manager syntax passes, malformed `--deserialize` input remains protected, and a detached `(sd-pam)` child remains in the census. Three focused regression cases passed; the exact committed-head case passed.

```text
$ stable 2026.10.5: openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive
Runtime retained: Could not classify PID 8866: working directory is unavailable

$ candidate 2b31880: openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive
Removed abandoned updater runtime; Doctor complete (exit 0)

$ candidate with live runtime holder, then after holder exit
Runtime retained: other OpenClaw processes are still running (PIDs: 18021, 18049)
Removed abandoned updater runtime; Doctor complete (exit 0)

$ sha256sum ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite ~/.openclaw/workspace/MEMORY.md

base: expected { pids: [] }; received manager and (sd-pam) PIDs with unreadable-cwd warnings
head: 1 passed, 120 skipped

$ node scripts/test-projects.mts src/infra/openclaw-process-census.test.ts -- --testNamePattern='invalid deserialize argument' --maxWorkers=1
head: 1 passed, 120 skipped; malformed manager argv remains protected
```

set -euo pipefail
node scripts/test-projects.mts src/infra/openclaw-process-census.test.ts -- --testNamePattern='deserialize=8|invalid deserialize argument|standard systemd user manager' --maxWorkers=1
