prs.title: refactor(sessions): reuse cancellation observation owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session admission and reply-run barriers build separate abort/timeout observers around owners that already provide those operations. The duplicate observers obscure the important distinction between withdrawing queued work and joining an admitted write-capable callback.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior or migration changes. Queued cancellation, primitive abort reasons, FIFO, live-authority checks, admitted-write settlement and successor fencing remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Await the canonical store writer directly, retaining only the caller's queued-abort error adapter. Reuse the shared finite-timeout and unlimited-abort observers for barrier waits. Keep producer custody, the absolute wait budget, source merging and physical-owner reselection. Remove trivial async/return-await wrappers that own no cleanup.

Net production LOC: **27 removed** (28 added/55 deleted), two owners. Two test files add105 lines for four distinct preserved boundaries; no existing assertions changed. This is the session-area slice of the observer cleanup, not a schema, durability, permission, public API, config, protocol, dependency or Phase E change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- The session writer no longer owns a second abort Promise/listener/race. The canonical queue already withdraws waiting work and joins admitted callbacks. Introducing controller foundation#175837 and queue correction#155288 were inspected; every actual FIFO/close-deadlock fix remains at its owner. No linked human hang requires the duplicate observer. Cancellation during an admitted validator still waits for that validator; queued Error identity and primitive-reason normalization are retained.
- Barrier waits no longer own a separate timer/listener cleanup ladder. Shared timeout/abort owners retain the existing finite false-on-timeout/abort result, unlimited cancellation and source-error propagation. Controller foundation#175837 is retained, not removed. The wait still cannot release a producer's fence: cancellation only stops observation. Absolute budgets, minimum1ms finite remainder and physical-owner selection remain.

## Evidence

Focused behavioral proof passes66 tests across five files:61 tests/four suites in382.5s wrapper, plus five selected follow-up admission/delivery cases in101.3s. The explicit follow-up name filter deselects64 unrelated cases; no source skips were added. ## What Problem This Solves

A transcript idempotency conflict can be retried and sent through the cross-provider fallback chain even though changing models cannot resolve it.

## User Impact

The run stops on the original transcript conflict without repeating the turn, trying another provider, or suspending the session for a model failure. The underlying transcript admission mismatch still needs investigation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize the transcript owner's existing conflict message in the shared terminal-error classifier already used by assistant retries and model fallback. No change to compaction, admission, or replay semantics.

## Evidence

On main `8082bfa81ab340099fcb09d36f8188b5666b3db7`, the embedded-entry regression observed 3 attempts for a thrown admission conflict and 12 for an assistant conflict, instead of one. Both existing keyed-turn controls passed. After the fix, all four entry regressions passed, preserving the original error and avoiding session suspension. The complete failover-error unit file passes (53 tests), including direct, cause-wrapped, and aggregate conflicts.

Validation used Node 26.11.1 on Windows with the existing mocked attempt boundary and isolated real auth/session storage; no live provider or paid API calls. Commands:

- `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts src/agents/model-fallback.run-embedded.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 27 passed, including all four transcript regressions; 9 other cases failed during SQLite temporary-file cleanup with Windows `EBUSY`. This is not a full-file pass.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/failover-error.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 53 passed.

prs.title: refactor(plugins): remove redundant component and lifecycle adapters
prs.body:
Related: #158398. Continues the maintainer-requested bundled-plugin cleanup; #177694 is the large-cut precedent.

## What Problem This Solves

Bundled plugins still carry parallel render, ingress, parsing, and QA-evidence adapters that duplicate responsibilities already owned by their wire format or the Plugin SDK.

## User Impact

No intended visual or feature change. Discord component payloads, modal mutation, authorization, approval handling, channel delivery settlement, and QA scenario coverage remain supported. No config, schema, protocol, dependency, or persisted-data changes.

Mattermost now uses the shared transient-network policy for idempotent DM-channel creation, including its additional fetch/TLS transport diagnoses; HTTP-status precedence and permanent send refusals remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord outgoing components now use typed wire objects rather than render-only subclasses, while incoming controls are handler descriptors. The public serializable component and mutable modal surfaces remain. IRC and Twitch delegate duplicate handoff/abort bookkeeping to the existing SDK ingress owner; Twitch retains its exact reply-lifecycle projection and manual deferred shutdown.

Browser, Mattermost, and Slack reuse existing SDK parsing/classification/truncation helpers. Matrix resolves account/auth context once through the shared client owner. QA fixtures share error decoration and evidence validation; unused QA metrics and Feishu success-trace projections are removed.

Production delta: **518 net lines removed** (+1,034/-1,552), excluding tests, static fixtures, generated code, and declarations. Shipped QA fixture runners are production orchestration, not static test fixtures.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Feishu no longer retains successful reply-list request IDs, text-length snapshots, or reply-source trace labels. These were introduced with #59129 without a cited human report requiring those success traces. API failure IDs, retry diagnostics, aborts, lookup behavior, and delivery remain; troubleshooting a successful lookup no longer has those redundant snapshots.
- Unconsumed QA request-count/system-prompt-size/output-tool-name metrics from #97478 are no longer calculated. The scenario's selected evidence and prompt-byte checks still run; an unrequested metric would need an explicit consumer before returning.
- Matrix's private unused timeout/final-URL projections are gone; callers retain their existing value/error/response behavior, not extra bookkeeping.
- The IRC/Twitch wrappers covered abort/handoff outcomes already handled by the shared ingress owner (#110914/#110852 versus #111186/#175459). This removes no settlement protection: the SDK remains authoritative, including accepted/deferred work and normal shutdown.

## Evidence

- Browser focused proof: 75 tests passed across parser/header CLI and dashboard ownership suites.
- Non-Discord plugin proof: 334 tests passed in 19 selected files across Feishu, IRC, Mattermost, Matrix, QA Lab, and Slack.
- Discord focused replay: all 281 tests passed across 18 selected files, including loopback component/modal payloads, approvals, question controls, argument menus, and model-picker flows. The initial five failures were in a helper that stringified the pre-wire class representation; it now uses the existing production serializer.
- Twitch focused proof: all 19 tests passed across durable-ingress and public-monitor suites, including restart recovery, adoption/defer/abort shutdown settlement, prefixes, attachments, and send failure. Final browser-utils replay: 21 passed.
- Focused syntax lint and format passed on all 52 changed files. Scoped cycle proof inspected 2,042 production files across the nine affected plugins: zero runtime cycles and zero new static strongly connected components versus the base. Independent P0–P2 review completed scoped-clean.
- The lint-suppression suite ran: 13 passed, one existing allowlist mismatch failed for `scripts/perf/chat-metadata-burst-measure.ts` (`@typescript-eslint/unbound-method`). That suppression and the test are unchanged from base `aad08acb950874054fbac1f68e6b33037f1b271c`; this diff introduces no suppressions. The allowlist is not weakened here.
- Package-boundary typecheck was attempted but is not qualified locally: generated Plugin SDK declarations are absent, producing missing-declaration and downstream inference diagnostics. The ordinary type-aware lint wrapper also attempts a broad artifact build; that task-owned preparation was stopped under the campaign host budget. Exact-head PR CI must supply broad type-aware proof.

The current-file collision audit includes 1,045 recent open PR records and fully paginated wide PRs, plus a 46-PR incremental refresh through 2026-10-20 00:39 UTC with no new overlaps. The only overlaps are minimal own-cut orphan migrations in `native-command.ts` (#120150) and `native-command-reply.test.ts` (#123837); unrelated command behavior and assertions are untouched.

### CI repair

Run 39349039582 on initial head 7cbc9e518ea453f2b21ce9b9a0c35b10e8457644 exposed three PR-caused failures, all repaired rather than attributed to baseline:

| Job | Cause and repair |
| --- | --- |
| check-prod-types | IRC's toolsBySender config is not structurally compatible with the SDK tree; restore the original tools-only projection. Explicitly return undefined on the monitor's normal path to satisfy its mixed callback return contract. |
| checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1 | The IRC adapter test expected local settlement that is now owned by the shared ingress monitor. Verify lifecycle forwarding and no premature adapter settlement instead. |
| checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-2-4 | Matrix mocks expected duplicate auth/account resolution before acquisition. The shared client owner resolves it; adapters forward config and the optional selector unchanged. Remove the obsolete mocked export and document network/crypto lease isolation, shrinking its three baseline entries. |

Focused red reproductions captured the IRC failure and both Matrix assertion failures. After repair, all 32 tests passed across the five selected IRC/Matrix files in 67 seconds total wall time (test execution under one second per file; compilation/import dominated). Changed-file syntax lint and format passed. Scoped cycle proof covered 282 production files: zero runtime cycles or new static components. The required suppression replay remained 13/14 on the same unchanged older-base mismatch described above. Fresh incremental P0–P2 independent review completed scoped-clean. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad/type-aware gate.

Run 39350808983 on repaired head 0f59da126f0d2ef6d7fab1020ee2600ccff9ff82 then found four stale assertion allowances in checks-fast-baseline-ratchets (job 118394731844). Shrink browser-cli-state from 1 to 0, Discord components.message from 8 to 1, Mattermost client from 6 to 5, and QA fixture-utils from 4 to 1. These are assertions this PR removed, not inherited failures. No runtime/test changes or expanded allowances. The incremental independent review is scoped-clean; the mandatory suppression replay remains 13/14 on the unchanged older-base mismatch, with no new suppressions.

prs.title: refactor: let authorized messages join the active execution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Authorized corrections and peer updates can wait behind the active execution they need to change. Admission mixes incoming-message facts with execution permissions; recovery can replace the original source identity; native acceptance can be mistaken for completed delivery.

## User Impact

Compatible input joins the exact active execution while preserving its runtime, workspace, policy origin and completion custody. Human messages keep their answer obligation after real acceptance. Busy peer sends, returned results and explicit `followup` input use that same admission boundary; rejected and uncertain delivery retain different custody.

## Why This Change Was Made

SessionController prepares a continuation against one captured operation and backend. Execution settings are captured at admission. Each arriving caller is authorized independently, with current source, scope, policy and target checks at the final enqueue. Opaque target lifetimes prevent a prepared send from silently reaching a successor. Rejection, valid-source deferral, source failure, acceptance, and unconfirmed consumption stay distinct.

Human attribution is separate from permission to answer a pending question. Bundled adapters migrate together; released external harnesses keep their question contract. Authenticated reconnects share device comparison identity while their authority remains separately revocable. Native confirmation deadlines end the caller's wait without releasing already accepted receiver custody; exact-thread handoff still waits for its native persistence owner.

This follows Codex's central principle: [steering appends attributed input to the existing TurnContext](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn_input.rs), with [acceptance separate from consumption](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/protocol/src/turn_input.rs). OpenClaw keeps its additional delegated and multi-user authorization checks. Temporal changes still require runtime checks; TypeScript does not make revocation or every invalid lifecycle state statically impossible.

No schema or dependency change. Runtime SDK compatibility remains; an existing test helper can select a genuinely registered bundled harness through its registrar-owned metadata.

## Relationship to the Earlier PRs

This revision completes the proposed alternative across all five direct steering/admission PRs, rather than only #174967's admission portion:

| Earlier PR | Included behavior |
| --- | --- |
| #174967 | Busy peers and returned results, explicit followup input, original source-turn identity, native-child result routing, ACK deadlines and exact-thread handoff. |
| #175763 | Frozen execution capabilities and current caller projection, including the actual fallback producer. |
| #175810 | Publication of the accepted terminal reply requirement. |
| #176245 | Accepted human reply obligations, durable transcript ordering and separate pending-question permission in embedded and native producers. |
| #176972 | Authenticated device comparison identity across separately revocable reconnects. |

The originals remain open for the maintainer's choice until replacement is accepted. Related recovery/native PRs #175845, #176086, #176087, #174900, #176311 and #177414 are checked as adjacent contracts, not claimed as superseded. Focused #177618 and #177661 repairs are included; Stop's pending-wake retirement is kept separate from recovery's owed-completion filter.

The cutover removes caller-side execution-authority reconstruction and special target-key routing restrictions. Historical reply accounting has one exact-operation owner, retained after retirement without consulting a successor. Leaf contracts avoid dependency cycles; public runtime compatibility is retained at the existing boundary. The additional code carries exact execution selection, caller preparation, historical reply accounting and custody through the existing owners; the tests cover their distinct failure boundaries.

## Maintainer Decisions

**Recommendation: adopt Codex-style active delivery for compatible busy input, including `followup`; do not retain mandatory separate-turn scheduling for that input.** The goal should be Codex-level responsiveness or better: a coordination update needs to reach ongoing work while it can still change the result. Mandatory separate-turn delivery can delay that update for tens of minutes or hours and can strand work waiting for the update itself.

This is a source-backed behavior comparison. Codex's [`followup_task` handler](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2/followup_task.rs#L42-L49) selects [`TriggerTurn`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/agent/types.rs#L56-L62): deliver to the active turn, or start work if idle. Its [tool contract](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_spec.rs#L217-L244) specifies message boundaries while sampling or delivery after the pending tool call. The proposal follows that active-delivery principle, but **exact human-versus-peer preemption parity remains unfinished**. The current Codex adapter sends both through `turn/steer`, which the app-server maps to user input. Native peer mail uses a distinct mailbox boundary. With instant interruption enabled this can make host peer delivery more aggressive than native peer delivery. No explicit `turn/interrupt` was added, but that alone does not prove equal output timing. The required fix must preserve each source kind through a runtime-independent contract and use each runtime owner's supported boundaries. Late peer mail after the answer boundary and explicit task/cancellation ownership remain distinct.

#160842 already adopted default steering for a parent's zero-wait send to its own busy child. Peter [explicitly approved that narrow change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160842#issuecomment-5882083686), preserving waited sends, ordinary peer targets and explicit `followup`. This proposal extends that accepted principle through the shared controller and explicitly asks to revise the remaining busy-followup contract; it does not treat the original focused repair as a mistake. Idle recipients still start normally. Compatible busy input joins one captured execution with its existing permissions and completion owner. Admission does not promise a separately correlated final response, and acceptance is not reported as consumption. Callers depending on the old separate-turn contract are an explicit compatibility consideration.

Accepted human input also strengthens an optional execution's answer obligation **only after proven backend acceptance**. The silence policy of background work should not erase an accepted human question. This OpenClaw-specific accounting rule changes no execution permissions or policy origin. Source, target, model-policy and pending-question checks remain required.

These are the requested product decisions, not claims of prior approval. Security-owner acceptance of the changed authority lifetimes remains a separate requirement.

### Authority boundary for security-owner review

Reconnect reuse is comparison identity only. `device-revocation.ts` matches the authenticated device-token identity, profile, role, effective scopes, client/transport attributes and Gateway policy owners; it retains separate currentness and revocation state for each admitted source. `operator-run-authority.ts` compares the complete retained owner/membership record and does not issue new permissions from equality. Native child input checks both live sources before comparing that identity.

Accepted continuation custody outlives a sender turn so ending that turn cannot discard accepted receiver work. It still uses the captured source's live revocation and policy checks; it cannot select a successor execution or replace the receiver's tools/workspace. The session-write repair preserves the narrower creator-bound `sessions.send` permission. The runtime evidence below supports specific boundaries, with unproven effects explicitly listed; it does not substitute for security-owner acceptance of these lifetime changes.

## Evidence

Current published source: `980116042b1bd9dbcc4470ca2a72c0ad4fe1f3ab`. Queued/stored-data proof revision: `b0d7186baf58b6785c1c3c4d9a761eabae1dfb6b`, with pinned upstream `782e8d2f836419978ef11684f98802b8a837d47e`. CI repair commit `2300290f1f0` preserves the earlier restored-wake and session-write authorization repairs.

### CI repair and upstream integration

Latest integration at `b0d7186baf5` resolves both GitHub-reported conflicts against upstream `782e8d2f836`: retains numeric OAuth status plus unconditional test cleanup, and upstream reconnect fixture settlement plus exact-one-retry checks. On this integrated tree, **179 tests across eight files** pass: steering/reply/requester authority, both conflict fixtures, restored-wake/queued-registry recovery and durable requester automation authority. Core and UI production typechecks, scoped lint/format, and fresh P0–P2 review of the manual resolutions pass. Independent source review found no directly overlapping production authority hunks. Hosted CI is pending. The stored-row recovery tests are owner-boundary evidence; fresh packaged compatibility and queued native effect proofs are recorded separately below.

The integrated source tree passes **134 tests across 10 focused files** (225 seconds including runtime preparation and cold compilation), the affected agent/Gateway test type graphs and UI production types, scoped lint/formatting, and the shrinking mock-factory ratchet. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the five-file CI repair found no actionable defects. A subsequent upstream xAI fixture failure is repaired in `d23f2c7090b`: pass numeric HTTP status 400 to the existing helper and always abort/join the test login. Its original failure reproduces; all 26 OAuth tests, extension test types, lint/format and independent P0–P2 review pass. Hosted CI on the new head is pending. The subsequent UI E2E shard failure is repaired in `8c962482a9b`: settle the pending synthetic reconnect before clicking Retry, matching the intended pending-attempt behavior introduced by upstream #177690. Both viewport cases reproduced the disabled-Retry failure before the fixture repair; afterward the full module-boundary browser file passes all 15 cases (69.96 seconds locally with existing system Chrome), with UI production types, lint/format and independent P0–P2 review passing. This is test-only; hosted CI on this revision is pending.

- Updated obsolete tool-description assertions to the proposed busy-input/followup contract.
- Removed one obsolete closed-mock baseline entry after that factory became partial.
- Seeded an already-migrated legacy NULL-draft publication row instead of downgrading the entire database; the dedicated migration suite still checks historical DDL and rollback, now with upstream migration custody. Production migration guards are unchanged.
- Controlled the native authorization-routing fixture’s monotonic clock: its CI case took 1.285 seconds against a one-second request budget. The separate deadline suite remains unchanged and passes; no production timeout or authorization check was relaxed.
- Preserved the literal type of `source-bound` in the continuation fixture.
- Restored the startup outbox-drain import missing from the pinned upstream tip; the consuming Gateway type graph and UI production typecheck pass.

The refreshed subset below is native evidence at `b579b5c49ca`. The later detailed historical sections retain their own recorded revisions. None is a wholesale native rerun of the newly integrated head. The signed rewrite `755a78d44bc` had the identical source tree to `03708862899`.

### Fresh queued continuation and stored-data proofs at `b0d7186baf5`

Three separate isolated Gateway/native cases passed and their actual receipts were independently audited:

- **Allowed effect:** a genuine managed child completed normally; its queued requester scope bound before acceptance while predecessor cleanup was held. After cleanup released, actual native inference consumed the child result and removed exactly one pre-created disabled synthetic job. One native call returned `{ok:true,removed:true}`; normal final matched the accepted Gateway run, logical session and selected native turn.
- **Exact queued-run Stop:** canonical cancellation selected only that accepted queued run. Terminal `stopReason: rpc`, no provider start, zero native continuation/removal.
- **Original-source revocation:** canonical device-token revocation matched the persisted original authenticated source device and committed after queued acceptance, before intentional gate release. The exact queued run terminated with `stopReason: rpc`, no provider start or native continuation/removal; no separate chat abort was used.

Complete canonical inventories captured before shutdown and all 18 raw cron-row columns equaled baseline minus only the target job for the positive case and stayed unchanged for both negatives. The raw SQL comparison also passed after shutdown. Each case joined its two native processes with exit 0/no signal, stopped the Gateway/provider and removed task state. All state/messages were synthetic; the provider was scripted and local. Actual native 0.163.0 was an explicit fixture override of the unchanged 0.162.1 source pin. Scheduling-only gates and passive observations preserved production authorization/mutation guards.

The genuine outbox remained dispatching at acceptance, as required by production custody. The positive collector observed natural retirement after final; no separate SQL absence snapshot was retained. Revocation unwound the held source operation, so no normal cleanup-release event was emitted. Physical native thread rotation occurred in the positive case; logical session and selected-turn correlation remain exact. This is core managed-child completion, not native collaboration child identity or scheduled execution. Earlier update-based attempts remain failed collectors with incorrect persisted-field expectations; they are not relabeled as passes. Manual outbox deletion before start was not performed and is not the production contract.

A separate real **2026.10.5 → candidate** packaged state handoff also passed: version-specific stable and candidate CLI/Gateway entrypoints, the same isolated synthetic state, stable stopped before canonical candidate Doctor/start. Exact physical session, label, one complete injected assistant row and the disabled job's complete 14-field/nested canonical object survived. Fresh candidate session create/update/inject/read succeeded with zero pending input. All 14 authenticated RPC receipts and both clean Gateway exits were independently checked; task state was removed. Doctor emitted setup/plugin warnings. This does not claim model completion, native execution, scheduled execution, delete, downgrade, rollback or every plugin migration; no manual SQLite writes were used.

### Newly identified native input-boundary gap

The exact native reference is [Codex 0.163.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012). Its [sampling loop](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L2869-L2937) checks peer-mailbox preemption after completed reasoning, commentary or partial-answer items. Human input follows a separate instant-interruption path. The [steer protocol](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs#L311-L340) exposes user input rather than typed external peer mail. The installed runtime CLI reports instant interruption enabled and deferred mailbox preemption disabled; older source defaults are not evidence of the deployed binary's behavior.

OpenClaw currently routes both kinds through user steering. That mapping does not reproduce the native peer mailbox. Source classification must survive admission and conversion, with distinct human-steer and peer-mail operations at each runtime sink. A local item-completed notification cannot atomically control a remote runtime's next item; blanket tool cancellation is not a substitute.

Three isolated production-boundary traces at `7daf590c302a5783c3b016759cc30967c307a5c7` now measure the distinction, using the real verified native 0.163.0 executable and a scripted loopback provider. Every producer was accepted while an explicit commentary item remained unfinished:

| Actual input route | Original recipient's first request containing the input |
| --- | --- |
| Genuine native collaboration child → parent | After commentary item completion, before response completion |
| Authenticated Gateway human → native user steer | After response completion |
| Real host `sessions_send(mode="steer")` → native user steer | After response completion |

The host-peer result is a **clean failing contract observation**, not a parity pass. Raw provider requests were observed before the helper's dispatch queue, so serialized dispatch did not manufacture the distinction. All three retain the original native thread/turn, one attributed input echo and normal parent/child finals. The host sender also finishes normally and its actual public tool result is accepted after consumption. All seven native processes exited zero/no signal; the Gateways/providers stopped and temporary task state was removed.

These are synthetic accounts, content and state. The unchanged source manifest pins 0.162.1; this proof explicitly overrides it to verified 0.163.0, with V2 collaboration, ResponsesLite disabled, actual instant interruption enabled and deferred mailbox preemption disabled. This WebSocket human branch drains the response; this is **not** a universal assertion about human mid-item interruption. Commentary is the measured phase. Pending tools, approvals, questions, other phases/transports and later changes are not covered. An initial module-import failure and two collector failures remain unqualified; corrected runs are separate. Raw captures remain private.

Exact native peer parity requires a supported app-server entry into the existing native mailbox; 0.163.0 exposes no such host operation. The bounded design binds mail to the exact active turn, preserves source attribution without replacing permissions, and returns accepted-but-unrecorded input when that owner closes rather than starting an unauthorized successor. No native fork, protocol change or binary update is shipped here. Agents API's installed SDK also exposes user messages rather than a peer mailbox. ACPX/Muse and legacy adapters cannot be assumed to support live peer delivery. Profile reassignment, model-policy membership and output-boundary parity remain open requirements.

### Cooperative wait wakeup at `980116042b1`

The built-in `subagents(action="wait")` previously observed child registry changes, timeout and abort, but not admitted input. It now observes the exact runtime input queue and returns `reason: "input"` for human input or peer mail, leaving the child running and completion delivery pending. This matches the cooperative-wait principle in Codex without changing model preemption. The observation capability closes with its tool invocation; retained callbacks cannot observe later runs.

The paired regression uses the actual Agent loop → actual subagents wait → admitted input → next synthetic-provider request. Both cases fail before the repair at the named missing-wakeup assertion and pass afterward, with the correction consumed once, child state/delivery unchanged and no cancellation. Six subagents tests and 40 existing stream-steering/async-tool tests pass; production and both affected test type graphs, scoped lint/format, line caps and independent P0–P2 review pass. Registry/read transport is scripted; this is not an authenticated Gateway or other-adapter timing proof. Queue and tool-invocation code were extracted coherently into sibling modules without a second scheduler or queue owner. This revision is not locally deployed. Process polling remains a separately identified observation-wait sibling.

### Native behavior refreshed on `b579b5c49ca`

Through `8c962482a9b`, the only changes from that tested revision were the xAI OAuth and UI module-boundary fixtures. The subsequent merge at `b0d7186baf5` integrates newer upstream production changes. These native traces therefore remain evidence only for their exact recorded revision and scenarios; they are not represented as native reruns of the newly integrated head.

A fresh canonical runtime build with private QA artifacts matches the clean source head. These runs use actual Codex **0.163.0**, an explicit override of the unchanged **0.162.1** manifest pin, a scripted loopback provider, synthetic accounts/state and real authenticated Gateway requests. No production data or live service is used.

| Boundary | Observation at `b579b5c49ca` | Qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native child after reconnect | Same device credential on a new connection; actual native send completes once; original child consumes the attributed update in its original turn and reaches its normal final. | Pass. Three native processes exit 0; Gateway/provider stop and synthetic state is removed. |
| Foreign-device native child control | Separately paired device with the same profile/scopes reaches the actual same-admitted-source refusal; zero native interaction receipts; original child finishes unchanged. | Pass. Two native processes exit 0; Gateway/provider stop and synthetic state is removed. |
| Revocation during input preparation | Earlier chat admission ACK; pause immediately after genuine caller preparation returns; revoke 37 ms after the gate, resume 19 ms later, original source check denies 6 ms later. Zero marker-bearing native input frames and zero marker rows among all six canonical transcript events. Revoked credential cannot reconnect. | Denial evidence confirmed; **overall clean-exit qualification fails**. Original native process exits by SIGKILL; every native process is joined, Gateway/provider stop and synthetic state is removed. No clean native final or old-socket post-revocation send is claimed. |
| Automation preparation and final effect | Positive actual native call persists a disabled job with genuine operator source. Second call pauses after actual creator capture; committed revoke follows after 83 ms; native cancellation precedes gate resumption 25 ms later; same-run source failure follows after another 55 ms. Both stored canonical job objects remain unchanged before and after cleanup; no negative job exists. | Pass for this bounded attempted mutation. Two native processes exit 0; Gateway cleanup errors zero. Cancellation precedes resume, so this does **not** isolate the cron commit guard, prove queued effects after requester/outbox retirement, or execute a scheduled job. |

The preparation barriers only schedule pauses around genuine owner preparation; they do not supply permissions or replace currentness checks. Native request/result bytes are observed unchanged. The input-revocation containment result remains an explicit failed overall qualification. Authenticated profile reassignment and model-policy changes remain uncovered; the older ordinary/followup traces below retain their stated earlier revisions.

### Session-write authorization review repair

Review identified a regression against merged #177565: using the `agent` method for steering incorrectly required general `operator.write`, excluding a creator with only `operator.sessions.read` and `operator.sessions.write`. The three steering mutation/caller assertions now use `sessions.send`, preserving creator, sandbox and foreign-child checks. Starting a new agent turn retains its existing `agent` authorization. Accepted receiver custody and settlement remain unchanged.

The canonical runtime build (including packaged private QA artifacts) passed at `03708862899`.

The four unchanged production-boundary authorization cases failed before this repair. With the repair, all **24 tests across the Gateway session-tool steering and session-send admission suites** pass, including owned-session/child admission and noncreator/foreign-child denial. Core typechecking, scoped lint/formatting and fresh independent P0–P2 review also pass. No test assertions or permission definitions were weakened.

<details>
<summary>Detailed boundary evidence, native traces and remaining gaps</summary>

### Existing steering and native evidence

The following results were recorded at **`0878af08a11a8b7b1ef7b7d79bd9af6d3b9e682e`**, not rerun wholesale at the new head:

- Original boundary regressions were restored from the five proposals and failed on the earlier partial revision before their missing owner paths were added. Producer tests exercise dispatch, fallback, embedded preparation, native settlement and authenticated Gateway custody, including source rejection and post-ACK uncertainty.
- CLI policy-refusal and TUI cancellation consumer regressions preserve false-acceptance, unchanged-input and zero-enqueue assertions. Stop retires a canceled child's pending wake without making it restart-recoverable.
- Six affected production/test type graphs, focused lint/format, assertion and line-cap ratchets, and runtime/full import-cycle checks passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defects. These remain results at the stated revision; exact-head hosted CI is the broad gate.
- Real isolated Gateway/Codex app-server proofs passed for authenticated same-device owner reconnect, ordinary busy-peer `sessions_send`, and explicit busy `followup`. Both peer sends used positive `timeoutSeconds: 5` and discovered/executed the actual native tool.

Those synthetic fixtures remain prior-head evidence. Revision `03708862899` repaired three authorization assertions on the steering path; the 24 focused authorization/admission tests above validate that delta, and the captures below exercise their stated paths at that revision. No whole-matrix native rerun at `03708862899` is claimed, and none of the older traces proves the newly repaired restored-wake path.

The native cases used actual exec checkpoints and a scripted loopback provider, with no paid/external model, injected sender authority, fingerprint, queue mode or native RPC result. Native **0.163.0** was an explicit QA override; the source manifest remained **0.162.1**. The exercised binary SHA-256 was `8813367285524ac798dd96d1b071aea30d58708c7226fd236cd275cf1cfdee31`.

| Case | Observed result |

The three positive cases stopped their isolated native, Gateway and provider processes and removed task state. Native ACK alone is not consumption proof: each positive receipt also records the subsequent provider request containing the unique synthetic input in the original turn and that turn's completed terminal.

The completion admission owner now excludes retired, killed or suppressed requester wakes before creating an unbound FIFO reservation. It rechecks current ownership and completion status after requester lookup while preserving the captured batch identity. This closes a startup/restoration path separate from yielded recovery selection and Stop.

The restoration candidate then passes **27 tests across two suites**, plus core types, scoped lint/formatting and fresh independent P0–P2 source review. Local deployment now includes this PR plus the installation's existing independent catalog, recovery, voice, tool-free session, and saved-input UI fixes. Readiness, health, and previously active plugins passed. In a synthetic diagnostic conversation, a correction sent during a read-only command was consumed by the original native run, which returned the corrected final; no inputs remained pending. Original-run correlation was independently checked against the tool-start event, correction attribution, terminal receipt, and retained final. Public authority-boundary traces above use isolated synthetic state. Cold-restart controls did not reproduce the base failure, so full-startup RED/GREEN evidence remains a gap; the earlier native steering captures do not substitute for it.

### Native-child reconnect evidence at `03708862899`

At `03708862899`, an actual advertised native `collaboration.spawn_agent` created a child and the original child turn was held at a real scripted-provider request. The parent completed normally, its authenticated client disconnected, and a new connection authenticated with the same device credential, profile and effective scopes. The initial collector mistakenly counted `item/started` and `item/completed` as two logical deliveries; its overall failure and intentional temporary-state retention remain recorded. An independent read of the unchanged native/provider/journal captures qualified the actual effect above by selecting the completed-phase receipt, checked every original owned process was gone, and then used the QA artifact owner to remove retained synthetic state. This is qualified captured-effect evidence, **not** a retroactively passing collector or a second positive run.

A separate control, using a different genuinely paired device with the same profile and effective scopes, **passed its corrected collector**: the real native-child boundary refused the source mismatch, emitted zero native child interaction completions, left the guidance absent from the original child, and let that child finish normally unchanged. Both native app-servers exited 0, Gateway cleanup had zero errors, and synthetic task state was removed. The positive and negative together exercise the child-source guard; the positive alone would not exclude its legacy both-sources-absent path. This restriction applies to retained native-child collaboration, not independently authorized ordinary human steering from another device.

Both cases use actual native **0.163.0** as the explicitly disclosed QA override described above. Native bytes and authorization decisions were not mocked; the local provider and V2 catalog metadata were synthetic fixture configuration.

### Native preparation-revocation trace at `03708862899`

An isolated Gateway built from `03708862899` used the same actual native 0.163.0 override and a scripted local provider. A disclosed task-only module hook inserted a scheduling wait immediately after the genuine `caller.prepareCurrent()` await in `prepareReplyMessageContinuation`, before its original currentness checks. It changed neither the prepared authority nor the native input bytes. The original generated owner module SHA-256 was `85413255ad4c5c9689ea9a1ee56f8f8897ec9b1a02193bda27b713ec8a129b7f`.

The one actual preparation gate entered, an independent authenticated administrator committed canonical device-token revocation 42 ms later, and preparation resumed 40 ms after that commit. The original source check then rejected with `operator source authority is no longer active`. Inspection of all recorded native `turn/start` and `turn/steer` frames found zero occurrences of the synthetic incoming marker; all six canonical transcript rows decoded successfully and none contained that marker.

The earlier chat admission ACK had already been returned. The initial collector incorrectly expected a pre-send authentication refusal, so its overall assertion failed; the later-boundary result above was independently reconstructed from the original gate/revocation/denial receipts, native frames and stopped canonical database. The original failure is preserved. All task processes were joined and synthetic state removed, but native shutdown required containment: this is **effect-boundary evidence, not an unchanged-binary or clean-exit pass**. Post-cleanup cancellation is not attributed to revocation alone. This case attempted no retained automation effect.

### Automation effect-boundary evidence at `03708862899`

A further isolated case used actual native `automations` calls in one original thread/turn. Its positive control created a **disabled future same-session job** and correlated the real native tool result with the stored job, including the genuine captured operator source. No scheduled action or external inference ran.

For a second create, a task-only scheduling hook paused the real Gateway `cron.add` handler after `captureCronCreatorSession()` had returned its actual operator source and currentness guard, before the existing validation/preview/add path. The original generated owner SHA-256 was `d353b8fe6319d6905af084bec3d78d2c0529d398f93fbbe57ed2d3f692a999f3`. An independent authenticated administrator committed device-token revocation 84 ms after the gate entered; the gate resumed 20 ms later. The actual correlated native tool result was unsuccessful with `OpenClaw dynamic tool call aborted.`; a source-currentness failure for the same operational run was recorded after resumption.

Inspection of **all stored automation rows** both before and after cleanup found zero attempted second jobs; the original positive job remained byte-equivalent. Both native processes exited 0 and the Gateway confirmed stop. The original collector still failed: it expected a tool result in a subsequent provider request, but revocation had canceled the native turn. Independent inspection instead correlated the actual native dynamic-call/result receipts, genuine capture receipt and canonical stored-job snapshots. No rerun or retroactive collector pass is claimed.

This proves the bounded attempted automation mutation had no durable effect after revocation during genuine source preparation. Native cancellation preceded gate resumption; the capture does **not** isolate a particular cron commit guard, establish a typed 403 response, or prove execution of a scheduled job. It also does not exercise a queued continuation after its requester/outbox has retired. The loaded Gateway scheduling instrumentation is disclosed; source authority and mutation decisions were not replaced.

Committed device revocation before a new send rejects both the stale socket and revoked credential, with zero original-turn steer/input. That control records a native interrupted terminal followed by existing process containment, `nativeExitClean: false`, and trajectory-retirement/unsubscribe cleanup warnings; it is **not** reported as a clean-exit pass.

The instrumented trace above covers revocation during genuine input preparation. The bounded automation-preparation effect above is covered; the fresh queued cases above establish allowed effects and cancellation/revocation with normal outbox lifetime. Authenticated profile reassignment, model-policy membership changes and exact human/peer output-boundary parity remain open. The child reconnect capture at `03708862899`/control captures above now exercise #176972's native-child source-identity guard; ordinary owner reconnect alone did not. Another paired device of the same human with independently valid explicit authority is not a forbidden principal under the existing contract; no blanket cross-device denial is claimed.

All test inputs and correlation results are synthetic. Raw auth/configuration, prompts, live identifiers, endpoints and local-state captures are not published. No live sessions, production state or Gateway service were changed for the prior isolated native proofs. Maintainer behavior/security decisions and the unproven boundaries above remain open.

Related: #177634

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins cannot judge image evidence through native TypeSafe Jev even though the Decision runtime already has a tagged V2 image contract.

## User Impact

Plugins can submit one PNG or JPEG image per evaluation to hosted Jev, with boolean, choice, and score questions. Images remain experimental. Local Kev and custom endpoints reject image input before dispatch; text behavior and plugin-owned credentials are preserved. There are no new configuration options, public batch fields, SDK exports, or agent tools.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the earlier referenced-assets proposal with the existing V2 image representation. The TypeSafe adapter translates the image into the vendor wire format and owns the experimental header. A small prepared-runtime compatibility repair lets the registered catalog owner declare an already-selected custom decision ID before the usual routing, capability, and auth checks; it does not fabricate chat capabilities or require users to register previously working text routes manually.

## Evidence

Fresh red/green proof at the real prepared-runtime boundary reproduces and repairs the custom-route regression: all 16 prepared-host scenarios pass, including undeclared/mismatched route refusal and existing auth, routing, cancellation, and deadline cases. The TypeSafe image suite passes 17/17. Core and owning test-shard typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, MDX, and diff checks pass.

The unchanged adapter candidate also has prior passing focused transport/image coverage, extension typechecks, SDK-surface checks, and plugin contracts. A prior broad changed-check run failed on UI max-lines suppressions, diffs/memory-wiki dead exports, and a SQLite guard unable to spawn `rg`; those failures have not been baseline-proved, and no fully green broad run is claimed. PR CI supplies the current-head broad result.

No live hosted TypeSafe image call has been demonstrated. Offline boundary tests use synthetic evidence and mocked transport; they do not establish vendor acceptance or visual accuracy. The requested redacted live proof remains a before-merge dependency, and no merge readiness is claimed.

prs.title: fix(codex): account and trace every provider response
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server can emit more than one `rawResponse/completed` notification during a single turn, especially around tool handoffs.

OpenClaw previously had two related observability gaps:

- `attemptUsage` retained only the final provider response, under-counting multi-response turns.
- Codex diagnostics emitted only one turn-level model-call span. Consumers that reconstructed individual LLM calls from transcript timestamps could place the LLM span after its tool call and make several calls overlap until the final answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Accumulate exact `rawResponse/completed` usage once per `responseId` for attempt-level accounting.
- Keep the final response's usage and `contextUsage` as the assistant/current-context snapshot, so summed billing buckets do not inflate the active context window.
- Emit one request-level `model.call.completed` diagnostic per unique response.
  - Response samples and tool lifecycle boundaries are buffered and paired by order at turn completion.
  - A tool start closes the current LLM interval; completion of the final active tool opens the next LLM interval.
  - This remains correct when Codex delivers `rawResponse/completed` after the tool triggered by that response has already run.
  - Parallel tools form one tool phase. When one provider response emits several sequential tools, the shortest surplus tool-to-tool gap is discarded instead of being reported as an LLM call.
- Add `sourceTimestampMs` to completed model-call diagnostics so the OTel recorder can backdate completed-only request spans to their real completion time.
- Attach exact per-response usage to request spans when present, while still emitting a timing span when Codex omits optional usage.
- Attach accumulated `attemptUsage` to the turn-level model span.
- Hash the upstream response ID before exposing it in diagnostics and deduplicate repeated completion notifications.
- Map `reasoningOutputTokens` into `reasoningTokens`.
- Reuse the same response accumulator in bounded/settled-turn paths.
- Fail closed to thread-last usage when an exact response aggregate becomes incomplete.

Transcript timestamps are intentionally unchanged: an assistant tool-call message records when the model produced the tool call, not when that provider request began. Per-response diagnostics now own the LLM timing boundary.

The assistant-completion idle timeout configuration is not part of this PR: `#97233` already exposed `appServer.turnAssistantCompletionIdleTimeoutMs` on current `main`.

This change was AI-assisted. I reviewed the diff and validated the event contract directly against `openai/codex` app-server source and a real app-server turn.

## User Impact

- Token and cost accounting is accurate for Codex turns containing multiple upstream responses.
- Current-context reporting continues to reflect only the latest provider response.
- OTel consumers can render:

  `LLM request -> tool execution -> LLM request -> tool execution -> final LLM request`

  without deriving LLM starts from assistant-message timestamps.

## Upstream Codex Contract

Checked against immutable `openai/codex@95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74`:

- [`rawResponse/completed` is emitted once per upstream Responses API completion with exact, non-accumulated usage](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/app-server/README.md#L1450)
- [`response_id` is required and `token_usage` is optional](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs#L1820-L1827)
- [The sampling loop alternates provider responses with tool work](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L137-L149)
- [`RawResponseCompleted` is emitted when the provider response completes](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L2348-L2360)

## Evidence

### Real App-Server Proof

Ran the local authenticated Codex CLI (`0.146.0-alpha.3.1`) as `codex app-server --listen stdio://` with raw events enabled. The prompt required two separate sequential shell calls followed by `DONE`. The proof script used an ephemeral thread and redacted response/tool IDs.

Observed lifecycle, relative to model-turn start:

```text
LLM response-1   0ms .. 8878ms      total=23030
tool-1                 8913ms
LLM response-2         8913ms .. 11874ms   total=23125
tool-2                           11896ms
LLM response-3                   11896ms .. 13492ms   total=23178
turn terminal                                      13496ms
```

No LLM request span overlaps either tool phase. In this run each shell command completed within the millisecond resolution of the captured events.

Redacted projected output:

```json
{
  "rawResponses": [
    {
      "responseId": "response-1",
      "usage": {
        "inputTokens": 22967,
        "cachedInputTokens": 0,
        "outputTokens": 63,
        "totalTokens": 23030
      }
    },
    {
      "responseId": "response-2",
      "usage": {
        "inputTokens": 23078,
        "cachedInputTokens": 22272,
        "outputTokens": 47,
        "totalTokens": 23125
      }
    },
    {
      "responseId": "response-3",
      "usage": {
        "inputTokens": 23173,
        "cachedInputTokens": 22272,
        "outputTokens": 5,
        "totalTokens": 23178
      }
    }
  ],
  "projected": {
    "attemptUsage": {
      "input": 24674,
      "cacheRead": 44544,
      "output": 115,
      "total": 69333
    },
    "latestResponseUsage": {
      "input": 901,
      "cacheRead": 22272,
      "output": 5,
      "total": 23178
    }
  },
  "requestSpanDurationsMs": [8878, 2961, 1596]
}
```

The accounting invariant holds:

```text
23030 + 23125 + 23178 = 69333
```

The latest context remains response 3 (`23178`), while turn accounting reports all three responses (`69333`).

### Additional Verification

- Final affected-surface tests:
  - 5 files passed, 182 tests passed.
  - Covers multi-response accumulation/deduplication, delayed response completion, sequential-tool gap collapse, native/dynamic tool boundaries, and OTel source-time backdating.
- Production and test typechecks passed for core and extensions.
- Targeted core/extension lint and formatting passed for all changed files.
- Repository guards passed:
  - max-lines and environment-variable ratchets
  - plugin SDK API baseline, exports, and surface budget
  - deprecated API usage and plugin boundary report
  - guarded/plugin-SDK wildcard re-exports
  - runtime sidecar baseline/loaders
  - dependency pins/package patches
  - import cycles and conflict markers
- `run-attempt` focused lane:
  - 143 tests passed, 4 tests failed.
  - The same four SQLite settled-turn/context-engine assertions were reproduced unchanged on latest `origin/main` before this timing change, so they are current baseline failures rather than regressions from this PR.

prs.title: fix: restore error messages dropped by Bun bare-header stacks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: user-visible diagnostic messages (version resolution failures, help display errors, unhandled rejections, main-session recovery warnings) are printed without their error message when the CLI/Gateway runs on Bun.

Bun's GC can materialize `Error#stack` with a bare header (`"Error\n    at ..."`) that drops the message V8-style stacks carry. Diagnostic paths that read `error.stack ?? error.message` then render a stack with no message, hiding what actually failed.

## User Impact

User impact: failures on Bun report the actual error message again; stacks that already embed the message are unchanged. Node-only installs are unaffected (their stacks already carry the message).

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical fix already exists upstream as `formatErrorStackWithMessage` in `packages/normalization-core/src/error-coercion.ts` (upstream PR #172774, already merged into base, already used by `formatUncaughtError`). This PR routes the remaining `src/` production `stack ?? message` reads through that helper: on a bare-header stack it restores `"Name: message"` and keeps the rest verbatim; otherwise it returns the stack/message exactly as before, so every replacement is equivalent-or-strictly-better.

`node-runtime-recovery.mjs` mirrors the helper inline because the pre-compile bootstrap cannot import compiled packages; the inline copy is byte-for-byte consistent with the canonical implementation and the file header documents the dependency constraint.

The 5 extension call sites (reached via the plugin-sdk error seam) still use the old expression; fixing them requires widening a frozen plugin-sdk export surface, so they are tracked as a follow-up for the next stable cycle rather than included here.

## Evidence

- Helper unit tests (5 cases) cover: bare-header restore, V8-style stack unchanged, custom error name on a bare header, no-name-line prefix, and no-stack fallback — `packages/normalization-core/src/error-coercion.test.ts`.
- `unhandled-rejections.fatal-detection.test.ts` uses an independent bare-header fixture (`"Error\n    at handlerThatThrew (source.js:3)"`) and asserts the exact restored output instead of re-applying the production formatter (ClawSweeper Tests feedback); all 12 tests pass.
- Rebased onto current `upstream/main` (`11d0c854192`); branch head is `58f53d53c9c`.
- Red-on-base/green-on-head on the revised registry test: HEAD passes 12/12; with `src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts` reverted to base `11d0c854192`, the same test fails with the bare `Error` header (`1 failed | 11 passed`), exactly the regression this PR fixes.
- Shipped Gateway proof: the built `dist/index.js` (`OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (58f53d5)`) loads a standalone plugin through `plugins.load.paths`; the plugin registers a real `onDiagnosticEvent` listener that throws a bare-header-stack error, and the migrated `diagnostic-events` reporter prints `Error: plugin diagnostic listener failed: disk quota exceeded` with the frame preserved. Full output above.
- Type/lint/format on the 14 changed files: oxlint 0 warnings / 0 errors; `oxfmt --check` clean; fallback `tsc` reports no diagnostics in any changed file. The repo `tsgo` wrapper could not run in this checkout because the local install predates the `tsrs` dependency; CI's production and test type lanes cover that gap.
- CI on `58f53d53c9c`: all product checks pass except two unrelated failures. `checks-node-changed-compact-small-4` times out in the untouched `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.fallback-transcript.test.ts`; the same test fails locally with all 12 PR source files reverted to base, so it is pre-existing/environmental. `Intersect shared OpenClawKit dead code` fails before scanning with `Error: Missing or ambiguous ios Periphery producer`; this PR changes no iOS/Swift files.
- `security-sensitive-review` / `ci-gate` still require a maintainer approval for the security-sensitive path change (`/allow-security-sensitive-change`); that is an approval step, not an author code action.

### Real behavior proof (Bun, newly migrated reporter)

ClawSweeper's remaining ask was proof from a **newly migrated** reporter, not the pre-existing `formatUncaughtError`. This exercises the changed **handler-failure reporter** in `src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts` end to end: a real Bun process imports the real module, registers a handler that throws a bare-header-stack error (the exact shape Bun's GC materializes, per the `error-coercion.ts` docstring), installs the real `unhandledRejection` handler, and triggers a genuine rejection, so the changed `catch` block formats the thrown error through `formatErrorStackWithMessage`.

Runtime: Bun 1.4.3, Linux x64. Driver (uncommitted temp script): installs the real listener, registers a throwing handler, then runs `Promise.reject(new Error("orphaned background compaction rejected"))`. BASE = `upstream/main` `11d0c854192`, HEAD = this PR `58f53d53c9c`:

```text
## BASE — upstream/main reporter (`err.stack ?? err.message`)
[openclaw] Unhandled rejection handler failed: Error
    at compactionRunner (session-store.js:412:7)
[openclaw] Unhandled promise rejection: Error: orphaned background compaction rejected
    at <repo>/.tmp/unhandled-proof.ts:14:20

## HEAD — this PR reporter (`formatErrorStackWithMessage`)
[openclaw] Unhandled rejection handler failed: Error: disk quota exceeded while compacting session store
    at compactionRunner (session-store.js:412:7)
[openclaw] Unhandled promise rejection: Error: orphaned background compaction rejected
    at <repo>/.tmp/unhandled-proof.ts:14:20
```

The BASE reporter prints a bare `Error` header with the message dropped; the HEAD reporter restores `Error: disk quota exceeded while compacting session store` and keeps the stack frames verbatim. Both runs exit 1. This is the revised regression shown failing on the base and passing on the head.

### Real behavior proof (shipped Gateway entry point)

ClawSweeper's remaining ask was a newly migrated reporter reached through a shipped CLI/Gateway entry rather than a direct module import. This run uses the built Gateway from this PR (`dist/index.js`, `OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (58f53d5)`, Node v24.18.0) and a standalone plugin enabled through `plugins.load.paths`. The plugin registers a real `onDiagnosticEvent` listener that throws an error whose `stack` is the exact bare-header shape Bun materializes (`"Error\n    at ..."`), then emits a real `webhook.received` diagnostic event. The migrated `diagnostic-events` listener-error reporter formats the caught error:

```text
2026-10-20T09:59:39.991+08:00 [diagnostic-events] listener error type=webhook.received seq=79: Error: plugin diagnostic listener failed: disk quota exceeded
    at pluginDiagnosticListener (diagnostic-failure-plugin.cjs:10:13)
```

The same Gateway process loaded the plugin and shut down cleanly:

```text
2026-10-20T09:59:40.066+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (1 plugin: diagnostic-failure-plugin; 11.0s)
2026-10-20T09:59:42.179+08:00 [gateway] [shutdown] completed cleanly in 162ms
```

Command (isolated HOME/state/config; plugin file listed in `plugins.load.paths` and enabled through `plugins.entries`):

```bash
OPENCLAW_HOME=... OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=... OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=... OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 \
  node dist/index.js gateway --port 19031 --bind loopback
```

### Red-on-base / green-on-head (revised registry test)

HEAD `58f53d53c9c`:

```text
$ pnpm test src/infra/unhandled-rejections.fatal-detection.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  12 passed (12)
```

Same test file with only `src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts` reverted to base `11d0c854192`:

```text
FAIL  src/infra/unhandled-rejections.fatal-detection.test.ts > process error handlers > continues past declining and throwing handlers, then stops at the first claim
- Expected: "Error: bare header message\n    at handlerThatThrew (source.js:3)"
+ Received: "Error\n    at handlerThatThrew (source.js:3)"
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 11 passed (12)
```

### Real behavior proof (Bun, pre-existing formatter surface)

Bun-run real behavior on the pre-compile `src/infra/errors.ts` public `formatUncaughtError` surface (already migrated before this PR), feeding the exact bare-header stack shape and comparing against the old `err.stack ?? err.message` expression:

```text
runtime: bun 1.4.3
error.message: "version resolution failed"
error.stack: "Error\n    at <anonymous> (src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts:102:84)"

BEFORE — old expression `err.stack ?? err.message`:
  "Error\n    at <anonymous> (src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts:102:84)"

AFTER — production formatUncaughtError (formatUncaughtError -> formatErrorStackWithMessage):
  "Error: version resolution failed\n    at <anonymous> (src/entry.version-fast-path.test.ts:102:84)"
```

Unit tests for the helper run under both Node and Bun (identical string logic, runtime-independent).

prs.title: fix(imessage): prevent reflected replies from triggering duplicate turns
prs.body:
Closes #135704

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an inbound iMessage reflection could trigger a duplicate agent turn when the reflected row carried the outbound message GUID only in `reply_to_guid`.

## User Impact

Verified self-chat reflections marked `is_from_me=false` no longer start a duplicate turn when their parent GUID and normalized body match a recorded send within four seconds. Authored inline replies marked `is_from_me=true`, normal direct messages, groups, different-body replies, and replies outside that window retain their existing behavior.

**Maintainer decision remains open:** an incoming human self-chat reply that repeats the same parent GUID and body inside four seconds is indistinguishable from a reflection using these fields and is also suppressed. A reliable native transport discriminator would be preferable; this update does not claim to eliminate that ambiguity.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reflected row has its own row ID/GUID; the outbound GUID appears only in `reply_to_guid`. The existing persistent echo entry owns the scoped GUID/body pair, so the narrow parent lookup uses that same record, requires explicit incoming direction and verified self-chat, and refuses ID-only memory fallback. Exact provider chat-id targets are included alongside the existing prepared conversation scopes. Confirmed reflections keep the `self-chat echo` classification so they do not exhaust the loop limiter.

The update retains current main's cache entries, normalization, mention/authorization policy, and database fixtures. The existing general matcher moves unchanged into the local echo-scope module to satisfy the source-size ratchet. Regression tests cover persisted GUID/body/age matching, legitimate inbound controls, and the monitor loop budget. No schema, configuration, public SDK, or native iMessage transport change.

## Evidence

Current source integration is `b8a56cbbbeb8` on pinned main `782e8d2f8364`. The normal controlled sync completed, and the complete nine-file source review found no blocking source issue. It preserves the parent-GUID, normalized-body, exact conversation/account scope, explicit incoming direction and four-second bound, along with main's current fixtures and runtime logging ownership.

- The official formatter passed for the nine changed TypeScript paths. All99 cases passed across the four canonical database-worker suites. Nine-file type-aware lint, separate strict production and test checks, and submitted-diff whitespace also passed on this current source.
- Initial current-source test attempts executed no cases: shared configuration first lacked the UI plugin dependency; after that owner was installed, shared worker preparation lacked QuickJS. Type-aware lint then stopped during canonical SDK declaration preparation with missing markdown dependencies and additional declaration diagnostics. These unsuccessful setup attempts remain in the evidence; they are not current behavior passes. The normal frozen dependency preparation, including configured lint-plugin dependencies and native install scripts, then completed. One disk-limit interruption and one bounded process-observation timeout were recorded separately; all owned processes joined. Final source checks passed without disabling the canonical compiler, type checks or lint rules.
- Updated-branch CI is tracked in this PR’s [Checks tab](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/137189/checks); no new-head remote CI result is asserted by these local checks.

Historical validation is kept under its original source bindings. The earlier integration on main `16f1ef80f9d5` passed 99 distinct cases across the four canonical extension database-worker suites: last-route monitor (26), inbound processing (15), self-chat dedupe (19), and cache lifecycle (39). After a test-local binding rename, the changed self-chat suite's 19 cases and strict test projection passed again; the three unchanged suites were not repeated. Targeted production and test checks used 43 and 47 direct roots with canonical strict options and ambient declarations; type-aware lint, formatting and submitted-diff whitespace checks also passed on that earlier candidate. These are historical results, not fresh tests or type checks on `b8a56cbbbeb8`.

The pre-sync source tree, later committed as `7a5e0f3399fa`, also retains its historical 99 scoped-test result. An actual isolated production Gateway on that head exercised iMessage monitor/state/turn/delivery through a synthetic external imsg JSON-RPC subprocess and loopback Responses provider. All three behaviors passed: the reflected row added zero model calls, while different-parent and different-body controls completed model turns and transport replies. All owned processes joined before offline SQLite inspection. Main has since changed other parser/monitor/client/send paths; this update does not claim a current whole-Gateway pass or rebind that historical runtime result.

Limits remain: no Messages.app/iCloud/native imsg hardware or real-tenant validation; no stable-release upgrade, downtime replay or attachment coverage. A human self-chat reply with the same parent GUID and same body inside four seconds can still be indistinguishable from a reflection; that bounded delivery-policy decision remains with the maintainer. No public config/schema/protocol or admission policy was broadened by this conflict integration.

prs.body:
Related: #160864. Stack unit 3 of 5; depends on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177940. Next: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177942.

## What Problem This Solves

Agent-created persistent watchers need current exec authorization and informed consent that covers execution after the conversation and automatic restarts.

## User Impact

With `tools.exec.ask: "always"`, the user receives an existing exec-approval question identifying the exact watcher, command, location, output behavior and persistent lifetime. Approval permits that saved watcher and its automatic restarts; denial, expiry or cancellation leaves the proposal unsaved and an existing watcher unchanged. The approval itself does not claim that saving or startup has succeeded.

This unit supports Gateway host execution. Sandboxed and node-only agents cannot use it to fall back to the host; D adds supported sandbox execution. Exec denial remains denial, and allowlist policy with asking disabled cannot authorize a persistent watcher. Existing full unattended execution remains available under its current policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind one-use approval to the exact proposal and execution identity, wait outside database/cron locks, then revalidate current authority and consume approval atomically with the job write. Publish the resulting receipt only after commit. New execution or explicit reactivation requires authority; disabling, deleting and equivalent resaves do not introduce an unnecessary approval.

Reuse the existing approval controls and presentation metadata for watcher-specific wording. No message-tool interface or new workflow-specific control is introduced. Optional presentation metadata adds no persistent table or schema-version bump. This does not guarantee consistency of unrestricted model prose or native Codex/Claude runtime enforcement.

Derived from the stream work by Agustin Rivera (@eleqtrizit); contributor credit is preserved in the commit.

prs.title: fix(matrix): stop seeding new thread sessions from the room transcript
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A new Matrix thread's session was forked from the room session: `handler-context.ts` set `route.parentSessionKey` to the room's `mainSessionKey` for every thread target, so `prepareReplySessionParentFork` copied the room's transcript — including earlier turns, tool calls, and tool results — into the thread's first prompt. The issue's `context-diag` capture shows a thread first turn starting with `messages=4 roleCounts=assistant:2,toolResult:1,user:1` inherited from unrelated room history.

The docs promise only the thread root as extra context, and Discord/Slack gate exactly this behavior behind an opt-in (`thread.inheritParent`, default `false`) that Matrix never got.

Fixes #176224.

## Changes

- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler-context.ts`: thread targets no longer request a parent transcript fork — `route.parentSessionKey` is always `undefined`. The room session is still carried as `route.modelParentSessionKey` (the restart-recovery / model-parent fact), mirroring Discord's disabled-inheritance shape. Thread sessions keep their scoped keys (`:thread:<id>`) and the thread root still rides along as supplemental context via the untouched `supplemental.thread` path.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` + `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.context.ts`: transcript inheritance and restart-recovery replacement are now separate facts in the shared lifecycle. Recovery admission and canonical tombstone replacement fall back to `ModelParentSessionKey` when the fork request is withheld, and the recovery fork only runs in the tombstone-replacement branch — ordinary first turns never fork. This preserves the recovery path deliberately enabled by aa3fb33ba8a (#130196) for eligible tombstoned thread sessions (unlocked, unbound, no prior fork, authorized human turn).
- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.test.ts`: the room-thread assertions now pin both isolation (`ParentSessionKey` absent) and recovery (`ModelParentSessionKey` set) at the existing handler boundary.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.hooks-and-send-policy.test-utils.ts`: core regression proving a human turn into a tombstoned, not-yet-forked thread session is still admitted and replaced via the model parent key.
- `docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md`: states the isolation behavior explicitly.
- The earlier `handler-context.test.ts` call-shape suite was removed per review: coverage lives at the existing handler boundary, which exercises the real core context builder.

## Evidence

Live proof driving the shipped Matrix handler-context assembly with the real core context builder (`src/channels/inbound-event/context.ts`) and the real finalize step, for a room-thread message rooted at "Plan lunch" (`extensions` harness semantics, terminal output):

After this fix:

```
=== Matrix thread message — finalized inbound context (real core builder) ===
thread target            "$lunch1"
SessionKey               "agent:main:matrix:room:room1:thread:$lunch1"
ParentSessionKey         (absent)                                <- no room transcript fork request
ModelParentSessionKey    "agent:main:matrix:room:room1"          <- restart-recovery source retained
ThreadStarterBody        "Plan lunch"                            <- thread root context retained
```

Before this fix (current main `d0e8fc8a103`), the same trace shows the fork request (`ParentSessionKey "agent:main:matrix:room:room1"`) and no `ModelParentSessionKey` — that request is what copies the room transcript into the thread's first prompt.

- Red/green regression: on base, a thread target's `route.parentSessionKey` receives the room session key; with the fix it is absent and `ModelParentSessionKey` carries the room key (asserted in `handler.test.ts` at the existing handler boundary, which runs the real core context builder).
- Full `extensions/matrix` suite: all passing (handler tests now 59/59 on the rebased head, including the new room-thread isolation/recovery assertions). Core `auto-reply-reply`: all passing for the touched area (`dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts` + `session-parent-fork-prepare.test.ts`, 298/298, including the tombstone-replacement regression); a full-project run earlier showed 9 failures that reproduce on main or flake under parallel load (media-history x8, module-identity x1) — unrelated to this change.
- Typecheck, lint, and format are clean: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:all`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxlint` (0/0 on changed files), `oxfmt --check`.

## Notes

- Model routing is unchanged: stored model overrides resolve through the derived parent of the `:thread:` session key (`resolveParentSessionKeyCandidate`), so a new thread still resolves the room's `/model` override exactly as before. (An earlier revision of this description incorrectly claimed the fallback was removed.)
- Compatibility: eligible tombstoned, not-yet-forked thread sessions remain replaceable after upgrade — recovery now sources from `ModelParentSessionKey` instead of the withheld fork request, so no stored session data loses its recovery path.
- Discord and Slack gate transcript inheritance behind an opt-in (`thread.inheritParent`, default `false`) that Matrix never got; this change aligns Matrix with that default without adding a Matrix-specific knob.
- The shared fork machinery in `src/auto-reply/reply/` keeps a single owner for both facts; Discord, Slack, and subagent forks are unaffected (their `ParentSessionKey` keeps precedence, `ModelParentSessionKey` is only a fallback).
- No new configuration options.
