prs.title: fix: ephemeral nodes fail to reconnect after setup code expires
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A provider that replays the original `connect <setup-code> --ephemeral` command after enrollment cannot reconnect once that code expires, even when the node still has a valid saved pairing. The CLI rejects the expired envelope before the existing credential owner can apply its saved-token recovery policy.

## User Impact

That narrow replay path can reconnect to the same Gateway using the saved device token. Ordinary cloud-worker resume already uses a separate `node run --ephemeral` path and is unchanged. Missing, invalid, or revoked device credentials do not gain authority; changed saved Gateway targets remain rejected. Manual enrollment, service/session-host modes, and join URLs still require an unexpired setup credential. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Allow expired decoding only for direct ephemeral setup codes and forward the expiry to the existing node-host runner. That owner discards expired bootstrap auth and suppresses ambient shared credentials when recovering the saved pairing. This adds no new credential store or parallel authentication policy.

## Evidence

[Inspectable real-Gateway proof and complete reproducer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177880#issuecomment-6280840860) include sanitized CLI/Gateway output, the wire trace, and the result receipt:

- Valid bootstrap enrollment saved a real node token; expired-envelope replay then authenticated with only that device token, despite valid ambient shared credentials.
- A real `device.token.revoke` RPC revoked that same token. Replaying it produced one rejected handshake (`AUTH_DEVICE_TOKEN_MISMATCH` / `device_token_mismatch`) before node admission, with no bootstrap/shared fallback. Post-revocation admissions: zero.
- All seven proof child processes settled, loopback listeners closed, and disposable state was removed.

Before the production fix, the regression failed with `Pairing setup code has expired.` while all five refusal cases passed. On repair head `294b304573a668f802e23c899123919466f1461e`:

- 55 focused tests passed under the pinned Bun fork: reconnect, existing connect CLI, node-host runner, and runner shutdown.
- All six reconnect cases also passed under Node.
- CLI graph typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, mock-export ratchet, and diff checks passed.

## Review Repair

The test now preserves the real runtime module's exports while overriding `defaultRuntime`. Its cleanup selects the foreground runner's last-registered SIGTERM handler instead of an earlier import/setup listener. No production authentication code changed in this repair; no timeout was increased or assertion weakened.

The original Linux CI log shows a successful connection before the 120-second timeout. That hang was not reproduced on macOS; fresh Linux CI must confirm the cleanup correction resolves it. Clawsweeper re-review and exact-head CI are pending.

The real proof exercises the source Gateway, registered CLI, node runtime, native SQLite, real RPCs, and loopback WebSockets with deterministic expiry. It does not establish packaged-launcher, cloud-provider/worker-lease lifecycle, Linux, or model-turn coverage. The six-case regression uses a fixed remote peer and inert command capabilities.

Local Auto Review returned HTTP 401 and was explicitly waived by the maintainer for this patch. No successful local Auto Review is claimed. No merge or auto-merge is requested.

prs.title: refactor(infra): trust successful private update writes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Package rollback and candidate preparation re-read private output immediately after successful filesystem or SQLite writes. The retained inputs have already been admitted; the second tree walk, launcher comparison, plugin hash and journal SELECT duplicate their owners' work.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change and no migration or operator action. Updates keep the same recovery, authorization and durability contracts; private successful-write corruption checks become best effort as described below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trust successful private copies/restores and return the journal transition's known committed facts. Keep retained-backup integrity before restoration, errors from every actual restore operation, external Git checkout verification, partial native-backup recovery, live effect authority, revision CAS, fsync and restart recovery. Remove the orphan comparison helper and the tests that inject only the retired private-output mutation checks.

Production delta: **103 net lines removed** (+35/-138), five production files. Entire change: seven files, +35/-207. This is a completed update-owner residue under the campaign's 100-line waiver, not a 500-line LARGE claim.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A same-principal writer can alter bytes exactly during a successful package restore or private launcher copy. Trust the successful operation rather than audit its output again; ordinary operation errors still make recovery unverified. The removed assertions were synthetic filesystem interposition tests, not a cited human incident. Native reread lineage: #138839; private launcher comparison: #147988/#153081. Keep #138839's actual partial-backup recovery and #153081's human-reported symlink metadata behavior.
- A successfully written private journal is not reopened solely to compare it with the row just supplied, nor is a successful transition reread before returning. SQLite commit errors still propagate; later independent opens validate persisted data. The durable journal introduced in #158491 remains intact, including CAS, live authority, crash recovery and directory persistence.
- Private disposable plugin copy output is not immediately hashed a second time. Source fingerprints and mutation-boundary checks, bounded copying, pool drainage and final code-link receipts remain. #166317 introduced the worker-copy path; keep its measured parallelism and source protection, remove only the successful output reread. Unexpected private-output corruption can fail subsequent inspection/rehearsal and be retried.

The forward EXDEV fallback is deliberately retained: human issue #164699, fixed by #164769, reports Docker OverlayFS rename failures despite matching filesystem device IDs.

## Evidence

- 225 focused tests passed across swap/integrity/platform/bounds/launcher/filesystem, journal, actual plugin workers/tree/scale, publication boundary/durability, preparation durability and copy scheduling; one existing Linux-only case skipped on macOS.
- Targeted typecheck for the five touched production roots passed.
- Actual retained swap/rollback fixture, five baseline and five candidate samples: retained-root lstat count **13 → 13**, restored-root count **14 → 1** in every sample. No wall-time or user-latency claim; the temporary proof-only fixture is not committed.
- Independent review completed. Its one alleged restore-error certification issue was disproved against every error branch: all clear the flag before returning or continuing; the existing EXDEV refusal regression passes. No actionable finding remains.
- Scoped lint/format and diff checks passed; runtime and static import cycle checks both report zero. Mandatory lint-suppression and native wrapper-closure suites passed 17/17. The final mechanical lint correction makes the remaining integrity import type-only; it does not change the reviewed algorithms. Hosted exact-head CI is the broad gate; no local broad suite/build/E2E.

prs.title: feat(cron): run persistent streams in their authorized sandbox
prs.body:
Related: #160864. Stack unit 4 of 5; depends on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177941. Next: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177943.

## What Problem This Solves

Sandboxed agents need persistent streams that stay inside their authorized sandbox and retain accountable process ownership across interruption and recovery.

## User Impact

Supported local Docker Unix-socket sandboxes can run a stream in a fresh dedicated container under current exec approval and sandbox policy, with no host fallback. Each attempt applies the configured image, mounts, user, network and resource limits; it does not reuse the ordinary agent container's writable layer or processes. Unsupported backends and remote Docker endpoints remain refused.

Each stream adds a separately limited container, so aggregate resource use grows. Files outside approved mounts disappear between attempts. Image tags and mounted files are not frozen for the watcher's lifetime. There is no autonomous execution lease: after controller loss, a workload may continue until recovery can stop it. Unknown cleanup retains custody and blocks replacement.

Stop and settle sandbox streams before downgrading, and preserve a verified backup. Older readers quarantine the distinct persisted `sandbox-stream` kind rather than run it on the Gateway; re-upgrade does not automatically restore quarantined jobs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep execution policy with the existing cron owner and container custody/workspace finalization with the sandbox owner. Recheck current session, operator, exec and sandbox authority before launch and while active. Recover against the original daemon and exact immutable container ID; prove removal or absence before settling workspace edits, deleting custody or starting a replacement.

The first-use `sandbox_persistent_execs` companion records cleanup custody without granting execution authority; schema version stays unchanged, and unused installations do not create the table. Ordinary registry writes, job deletion and quarantine preserve unresolved custody. No age-based expiry releases it.

Derived from the stream work by Agustin Rivera (@eleqtrizit); contributor credit is preserved in the commit.

## Evidence

- Seven sandbox owner files: 127 passed / 2 skipped, 311.884s grouped wrapper wall with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs … --maxWorkers=1`, on the recorded intermediate tree. Skips: real Podman cross-turn case and a filename case rejected by the filesystem. No Podman support claim follows from this proof.
- Six affected type lanes and scoped lint/format passed. Later hook extraction: four selected cases passed / 93 excluded, 78.997s; focused types/lint/format and narrow review passed. Group costs are not individual file wall times; CI seconds are not available.
- The independent review's original P2 ulimit finding is retained with its disposition: negative object limits cannot reach Docker through the unchanged canonical schema. Six canonical config-to-argv cases confirmed that path; unlimited string syntax remains valid. No actionable finding remains; the original review is not relabeled clean.
- Complete-stack installed Linux proof exercised affirmative approval, actual Docker start/stop, workspace reconciliation and empty final custody in 30.716s. Published-driver update and recovery proof, including their source qualifications, are summarized in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177943. Earlier negative Docker cells remain prior-head evidence.
- No broad conversational-prose guarantee or native Codex/Claude enforcement parity is claimed. This unit adds no separate visual surface.

prs.title: fix(sessions): preserve durable input and current execution authority
prs.body:
Related: #160864. Stack unit 1 of 5; base: `main`. Next: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177940.

## What Problem This Solves

Session admission and cleanup can lose an accepted input or retain stale execution authority when preparation yields, fails, or the session changes.

## User Impact

Accepted inputs remain durable through preparation and recovery, and tool execution and delegated work use the current session's authority. Failed or replaced turns settle their own state without clearing a successor's state.

This is a prerequisite for the stream lifecycle changes in the following units. Normal admission and lifecycle writes use the existing worker/actor owners. Existing upstream synchronous SDK compatibility paths retain their documented migration deadline; this unit adds no new synchronous carveout and changes no database policy, dependency versions, or schemas.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stage the original input against the initialized physical session before maintenance, retain its cleanup through runner exit, and await settlement on failure. Recheck source authority at tool preparation/execution and child registration, and keep transcript publication bound to the captured current owner. The same cut carries content-free execution policy through durable and native-memory session reads and preserves the package loading boundary used by these paths.

## Evidence

- Exact `e40a4a4506cb` source: 74 selected files verified, zero mismatches; 832 tests passed across 11 owner runs. Coverage includes pending-input consumption, queue admission, Gateway agent admission, delegated publication, readonly workers, and tool dispatch.
- Core and ten selected test type graphs, scoped lint/format, package postbuild checks and whitespace checks passed.
- Recorded test cost: 789.870 seconds summed wrapper wall for the 11 separate `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1` runs. This includes startup/preparation; CI seconds are not available. These are correctness-test costs, not application performance.
- Scoped independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Review used supplied changes; execution proof is separate.
- Composed package, recovery and performance evidence is summarized in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177943. It is whole-stack evidence, not an independent package or performance result for this unit.

Related: #160864. Stack unit 2 of 5; depends on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177939. Next: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177941.

## What Problem This Solves

Process cancellation and automation changes can report completion before cleanup is confirmed or report a committed change as rolled back when follow-up cleanup fails.

## User Impact

Stop results distinguish a requested cancellation from confirmed termination. Failed cleanup retains ownership for reconciliation and blocks replacement; rejected stream updates leave the existing source running. A committed update remains reported as committed even if later cleanup needs attention.

## Why This Change Was Made

Join process-tree and backend finalization, recheck process identity after awaited cleanup, and commit stream updates before stopping their prior source. Consume one-use approval only through its live owner and matching committed transaction, then acknowledge durable resolution before best-effort follow-ups. Preserve captured ownership through background-result publication. The existing sandbox lifecycle keeps setup and cleanup while sharing container allocation with the later stream adapter.

This depends on A's background-result mutation classification. It supplies the ordinary approval and container-allocation contracts used by C and D.

prs.title: fix(skills): explain malformed skills missing from CLI inventory
prs.body:
Closes #158816

## What Problem This Solves

Malformed installed SKILL.md files disappear from inventories without explaining why. Operators need the rejected file path and loading error, including when querying a running Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bounded rejection facts follow the canonical source reader, shared per-pass root reads, worker snapshots, local/remote preparation, skills.status and CLI formatters. Rejection facts participate in the worker fingerprint, so changing or removing an invalid file publishes a new inventory revision even when valid entries stay unchanged.

Current head `9173502aa874ab54661a0ea7da4d92557c474777` resolves three actual test-fixture conflicts against official main `dcaf3d92fcd208737f447fbc1eb3093182cc2c9b`. Main now uses native directory notifications with coalesced scans and safety reconciliation; its old minute polling stays retired. This integration retains main's watch-directory ownership, current fixture/binding cleanup and interface retirements. No parallel discovery owner or production test seam is added.

## User Impact

`skills list`, `info` and `check` explain rejected files in text and JSON. Valid siblings remain available and rejected files do not inflate loaded counts. Warnings update alongside main's published discovery facts. Output contains at most 64 diagnostics plus an omitted count, with bounded paths/messages and sanitized terminal text. No configuration, persisted-data migration, dependency or permission change is introduced by this feature.

## Evidence

- **Current source:** fresh canonical independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings (confidence 0.85). Its immutable review tree `48ea0449b5047ffaf2c318a5557316f97b16ed19` exactly matches the published head. Official pinned oxfmt 0.72.0/configuration and new-base `git diff --check` passed. No local fork source, tests or builds were executed.
- **Current CI:** [CI 39356864131](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39356864131) is queued for `9173502aa874ab54661a0ea7da4d92557c474777`. New-head execution is not yet claimed passing. The previous `f52bb29fdaaea8dd5d8561177fb377f6030fcf94` [CI 39008934366](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39008934366) did pass 47 jobs/29 skipped, CodeQL and ci-gate; that confirms the earlier inherited alias repair, not today's changed watcher integration.
- **Watch publication contract:** the former fake-minute regression is migrated into main's existing real native-watch case. With unchanged valid siblings, an invalid file's changed error and removal must produce actual watch notifications, higher snapshot revisions and exact new diagnostic facts. prs.title: fix(agents): preserve safe inspection and outcomes during recovery
prs.body:
Related: #160864. Stack unit 5 of 5; depends on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177942.

## What Problem This Solves

Restart recovery can prevent safe automation inspection, obscure canceled proposals, and let an automation result hide the foreground answer.

## User Impact

Recovery can inspect permitted `list/get/runs` state and continue otherwise-authorized work, including a requested file summary. Canceled approvals stay closed: recovery cannot reopen them, silently reuse their consent or duplicate a committed operation. Scheduler-wide status and mutations remain outside the recovery read surface. Foreground answers and typed automation results remain independently visible.

Cancellation does not terminate all work from the original request. Every subsequent operation still needs its own current authorization. Missing retained outcomes remain unknown. This preserves ordinary conversation, mixed requests and streaming without promising control over unrestricted model prose. Native Codex/Claude enforcement remains a separate coverage gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry replay safety on actual tool instances through wrappers and Tool Search, intersect reads with existing caller visibility, and publish bounded facts for the exact interrupted run under the live session writer claim. Read at most eight retained terminal approvals using existing retention; no data migration or general historical approval-card replay is added. Keep automatic results separate at the existing transcript grouping boundary.

## Evidence

- 214 focused passes: 123 unfiltered runtime, 22 selected recovery/history, 69 UI. Recorded wrapper wall: 182.610s unfiltered, 294.951s across seven filtered commands, 21.571s UI. Later byte-identical case movement added one execution / 45.694s and affected static checks. Commands use `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs … --maxWorkers=1`; grouped costs include preparation, and CI seconds are unavailable.
- Core/UI/affected test types, scoped lint/format and docs checks passed. Broad proof binds the recorded earlier tree; mechanical follow-up is separate. UI renderer warnings remain recorded, without claiming baseline equivalence. Scoped independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Complete-stack canonical Linux build/install, installed hard-restart recovery (32.950s), Docker settlement (30.716s), and published `2026.10.5` updater (406.904s) passed. Runtime source was `a76405954db3`; final `2a6fa9355836` differs only by +17/−15 in one E2E fixture, with zero production delta. These are composition proofs, not separate package tests for intermediate units. The updater cell preserves existing cron definitions; it does not prove continuous-stream handoff.
- Twelve physical process cases passed within an initially failed combined command. After two prerequisite-only fixture corrections, the registered cron E2E passed separately (one case, 85.270s wrapper wall). Installed recovery uses scripted inference and proves cancellation, rejection of old consent, mixed-request continuation, reconnect and deduplication; it is not live-provider prose-quality proof.

The fresh performance comparison is **the complete stack `2a6fa9355836` against its exact upstream base `08e32fdb4df0`**, using fresh canonical packages on the same isolated AWS host. All 16 profiles / 96 requests passed; no primary or whole-group regression threshold fired.

| Median wire latency (ms) | Upstream base | Complete stack |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Agent cold acknowledgment | 3050.998 | 2409.547 |
| Agent cold first output | 5320.342 | 4835.678 |
| Chat cold acknowledgment | 1235.381 | 1218.283 |

| Agent warm acknowledgment / first output | 23.149 / 168.193 | 22.717 / 166.868 |

Fixed ABBA/BAAB order, one cold plus five warm requests per profile; no excluded or replaced profiles. One adjacent Chat warm-ack pair flagged +7.495ms/+32.586%, while aggregate warm acknowledgment changed +0.436ms and neither group flagged. All Chat outputs streamed. Cold CPU windows were unscorable because process membership changed; warm CPU sampling can miss short-lived work, and RSS is summed post-turn rather than peak. This bounded workload establishes neither production tails nor per-unit attribution or universal equivalence.

prs.title: fix(doctor): preserve node-only identities during Mac packaging
prs.body:
## Problem

Mac runtime packaging fails its native-first credential-preservation assertion after Doctor adds an unexpected `primary` identity to the seeded `node` credential store. The source CLI bisect shows that Doctor creates the row before the worker starts; the worker preserves the rows it receives.

The first producer is `maybeMigrateHeartbeatCadenceToCron` → `resolveHeartbeatSchedulerSeed` → `loadOrCreateDeviceIdentity`. Doctor's Gateway health, pairing, memory and post-repair authentication reads independently use the creating authentication path. These behaviors predate #174599; that PR exposed them by adding Doctor to native-first verification and inspecting the local credential store.

## Change

Use the existing read-only identity/authentication modes throughout these Doctor paths, forwarding `sharedStateMode` through the bound Gateway request. Derive anonymous heartbeat anchors from the canonical state directory so changing working directory does not reschedule monitors. Retain the existing reachable-but-unauthenticated health result when the server denies a read scope.

Explicit runtime enrollment remains unchanged. The Mac verifier's exact seeded-row assertion remains unchanged. Regression tests cover empty and node-only stores, both heartbeat repair entry points, Gateway diagnostics, pairing, memory, authentication refresh, stable anchors and missing-scope responses.

## Validation

- Source Doctor/real-worker bisect and built-CLI creation trace: red before repair, all seeded identity/token/policy rows preserved after repair.
- Focused regression suites: 88 tests across eight files and 80 across five overlapping files passed; these counts overlap. The final terminal-mock correction passed all eight credential cases, its export ratchet, targeted TSRS, lint and format. Complete isolated review and the test-only follow-up review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- **Exact final head `d780174`: standalone arm64 runtime staging/verifier passed all six variants**, including all three native-first exact credential/token/policy comparisons. This is the packager's pre-signing verification path. No app installation/launch, app signing, Keychain or TCC changes.
- Real isolated auth-none Gateway: healthy/authenticated without creating `primary`. Doctor uses the default backend client admitted by that server.
- **Exact final-head PostgreSQL conformance completed: 938 passed, two failed, 37 skipped tests across all 141 files.** The only failures are existing unsorted-directory assertions at `src/state/openclaw-state-db.postgres.test.ts:210` and `:413`; both reproduce on clean main parent `df6a567b5b0263e582f145fe0768b43d868d8d07` with identical source and signatures. All seven default projects ran using Node 26.12.0, the pinned Bun runtime, PostgreSQL 17 and unaccent/pg_trgm/vector 0.8.7. No additional failure or hook timeout occurred. The exit-1 result is retained, not reported as green.
- [Normal final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39353191421) passed: 45 successful jobs, 27 skipped, zero failures.

The patch was refreshed onto main `1552523ed967d0b00b60d6a22ed0c6c15ebaf1a7`. All 18 recorded repair/authentication/helper/verifier files remain byte-identical across the rebase. Earlier CI found a new test mock-export defect, which is fixed. A superseded capacity fallback also encountered inherited UI failures, an SDK download failure and timing-sensitive existing tests; no failed result is relabeled as green, and no timeout or assertion was relaxed. The earlier auto-merge request was retired through native recovery before refreshing the head.

## What Problem This Solves

Tracked cancellation maintains a second copy of the shared async-resource lifecycle, making ownership and cleanup harder to maintain.

## User Impact

No user-visible change or migration. Cancellation, serving identity, foreground results, accepted-work cleanup and retention behavior remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tracked cancellation duplicates the shared async-resource owner's foreground settlement, child-work scope, parent cancellation, reference release, descendant drain and cleanup lifecycle. Keeping two copies makes this subtle ordering harder to maintain.

Move the internal helper beside runWithAsyncWorkResources and reuse that owner. A small contextual abort relay retains requester cancellation identity without holding the foreground producer or result. Migrate the three Gateway/MCP/plugin callers and existing test imports, including the native Node/V8 test's evaluated imports. No compatibility re-export or reverse import edge remains.

Net production LOC:29 removed (35 added/64 deleted), five production files/seven total paths. Test changes are imports only. This is a small area-sized retry under the coordinator's waived floor, not a broad replay of the parked patch.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Tracked cancellation no longer carries an independent copy of the resource lifecycle. Inspected identity repair#143305, resource consolidation#143716 and measured retention repair#174246 establish the behavior to keep, not a human-reported need for duplicate implementations. It now follows the canonical owner for settlement/drain/release; requester abort, parent close, foreign-context plugin identity and producer/result collection stay covered by unchanged tests.

The synchronous AsyncWorkScope.run placeholder and both synchronous/asynchronous drain cases stay byte-for-byte. Gateway retained scopes, released-chunk carriers/ancestry, live effect authority, FIFO, real cancellation/deadlines and accepted-write shutdown settlement remain. No public SDK/config/schema/protocol/dependency or Phase E change. No new heap measurement claim.

## Evidence

Focused six-file proof:111PASS/4shards,224.8s wrapper, including native V8 foreground/result collection with accepted descendants held, requester-vs-parent cancellation, foreign ambient plugin cancellation, actual loopback HTTP ownership and real MCP serving/cleanup. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: PowerShell completion falls back to filenames or root options after a quoted subcommand, such as `openclaw 'completion' --shell f` or `openclaw 'models' 'auth' --`.

## User Impact

User impact: quoted literal subcommands receive the same completions as their unquoted equivalents. Regenerate and reload installed PowerShell completion scripts to pick up the fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command-path parser now uses PowerShell's parsed value for string literals, so quote delimiters no longer become part of the command name. Other expressions retain their existing handling and are never evaluated.

## Evidence

## What Problem This Solves

UI leaf owners repeat checks already owned by typed same-version Gateway contracts, retain an unused Logbook poll, and expose dead loading/error state.

## User Impact

Configuration, protocol, schemas, dependencies, public plugin methods and stored data are unchanged. Authorization, current connection/session ownership, write ordering, draft recovery and real error paths remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trust the compact Cron row producer instead of checking each field a second time. Remove path-local identity-cycle guards around JSON config schemas; retain all edit validation and shared schema deduplication. Remove older-Gateway core-method fallbacks in Talk/Custodian, a duplicate environment advertisement check, pure formatter lifecycle checks, dead Activity waiting state and a test-only Dashboard error prop. The Dashboard test now exercises the real lazy-render error boundary.

This is a **115-net-production-line residue** across 14 production files, excluding tests/test support/declarations. It is not counted as a LARGE cleanup PR.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Compact Cron row shape: #153040 (`2a541edb0d15a`) introduced synthetic payload/alert proof, not a cited human malformed-Gateway incident. The canonical typed compact producer supplies these fields. A malformed future producer is its contract defect; page/cursor validation, unknown-event checks and snapshot recovery remain.
- Config schema identity cycles: #116282 (`183db47e97f59`) introduced schema-backed editing, not a cited human cyclic-object incident. JSON transport cannot carry identity cycles and schema normalization itself never supported them. An in-process cyclic schema is unsupported; authored config values, SecretRefs, numeric/default/resource limits and shared DAG deduplication remain checked.
- Talk core-method advertisement: `voicewake.get/set` are unconditional same-version core methods; the #137971 feature and #166682/#169046 moves do not establish an older-Gateway compatibility contract. Unsupported mismatched Gateways now fail visibly at the RPC; connected/read scopes and queued writes stay enforced.
- Custodian core chat/history advertisement: #123011 separated permission denial from older-Gateway messaging. Remove only the unsupported-version branch; strict `operator.admin` admission and live request ownership remain. Missing core methods surface ordinary request errors rather than a separate compatibility mode.
- Retired Channels formatter calls: #176042/#176129 are structural bridge extractions, not cited human incidents requiring pure string formatting to throw after retirement. Formatters now remain usable without a live view; every HTTP/config/login/confirmation/mount/refresh authority check stays in place.
- Cloud inventory advertisement was checked twice; `canCallGatewayMethod` still owns the same advertisement and scope decision. No boundary was removed.

## Evidence

prs.title: feat(mcp): per-request header provider for volatile turn attribution on OpenClaw-owned HTTP transports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Per-turn MCP attribution currently has to enter declarative server headers or the connection resolver. Declarative header changes invalidate the catalog; the reported Reef production measurement was **221 re-catalogs across 222 runs**. The existing connection resolver caches requester credentials for five minutes, and changed resolved headers rotate the connection. Neither path can provide fresh turn attribution while retaining a transport and its catalog.

This adds a separate plugin request-header provider for OpenClaw-owned MCP HTTP transports. Upstream main was checked at `7aaef70932b30f4d7410ae00aa65b07089de2ce0`; no equivalent provider existed.

**Deployment consumer.** The Reef embedder plugin (the same production deployment behind the measurement above) adopts this provider on release adoption: it moves `traceparent` and signed per-turn context headers off declarative server configuration and onto this seam, which retires the measured per-run re-catalog. Requester authentication stays entirely on the existing connection-resolver contract — this consumer sends attribution and turn-scoped credentials only, and its stable credentials are unchanged.

## User Impact

Plugins can attach `traceparent`, signed turn credentials, and optional direct-request credentials to individual MCP requests without rebuilding the catalog or connection. Stable authentication remains in static server configuration or the existing connection resolver.

The SDK infrastructure documentation includes registration and embedded-runtime usage. This contract covers OpenClaw-owned HTTP transports; external harness-native MCP clients need OpenClaw materialized tools to use it.

## Design

- Add `api.registerMcpServerRequestHeaderProvider({ serverName, resolve })`, following connection-resolver registration conventions. Resolver and header-provider registrations share per-server plugin ownership, and the connection resolver is authoritative regardless of registration order: a foreign provider is rejected when the resolver already exists and displaced (removed, error diagnostic on the provider's plugin) when the resolver registers later. Registry state is identical in both orders, so a declared server with a resolver is never partitioned as static.
- Only the host binds run identity. The embedded backend binds MCP attribution to the admitted run's actual `sessionId`/`sessionKey`/`runId` (internal `bindMcpRequestRun`), and the binding is revoked when that run settles. A context the host did not issue (forged) or whose run has settled (stale/reassigned) is dropped: the provider is not called and no volatile headers are sent. The public export from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` is `runWithMcpRequestMetadata(metadata, callback)` — caller tracing metadata only (e.g. `traceparent`), never identity.
- Capture only MCP attribution when materializing tools. Each retained tool/resource/prompt executor opens its own operation scope, preserving attribution under overlapping acquisitions and calls without capturing unrelated cancellation or runtime authority.
- Resolve volatile headers immediately before actual guarded HTTP fetches, including same-origin redirects and authentication/RPC retries. Streamable HTTP and SSE POST/EventSource paths share this boundary. Header values never enter server configuration, catalog identity, or the resolver rotation digest.
- Keep configured headers, authentication, and MCP protocol fields authoritative. Scope provider headers to the configured origin; register returned values and bare bearer tokens for secret redaction. Bound provider resolution to ten seconds and report provider failures without exposing plugin error contents.

## Correctness

Each operation owns an immutable context. Missing context explicitly clears inherited attribution and skips the provider. No transport stores a mutable latest-turn header map. Provider results are freshly merged into a new request header object and are not retained for redirect replay.

Initial SSE discovery can carry its discovery context. Shared streamable notification GETs and legacy SSE reconnects carry no volatile attribution. The streamable initialized-notification send has a short-lived scope so its shared stream parser and reconnect timers cannot retain the opening turn, including reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`. Resumable RPC streams retain their own still-active operation context. Completed scopes cannot supply headers to background callbacks.

Static authentication, requester credential revalidation/rotation, genuine configuration invalidation, `tools/list_changed`, and transport-close recovery retain their existing owners and behavior.

## Evidence

### Guarded caller-authority revalidation (Rev 24 P1, head `34a4b55ad`)

**Defect (ClawSweeper Rev 24).** `fetchWithSsrFGuard` asserts the captured guarded caller authority (`captureGuardedFetchRequestAuthority`, e.g. a live cron-root claim) *before* invoking the transport `fetchImpl`. The header wrapper is that `fetchImpl` and awaits `provider.resolve()`, so authority revoked during resolution was not re-checked before stable credentials and volatile headers reached the server.

**Fix.** `withMcpRequestHeaders` captures the guarded assertion on entry and re-asserts it immediately before dispatch, alongside the existing abort and run-context checks. A revoked caller gets the assertion's own error, and no request is sent.

**Final-effect proof.** The real-runtime e2e adds a call under `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` whose MCP run stays active. Caller authority is revoked while the provider is resolving. The call is rejected, and the recording loopback server's request count is unchanged (no request for `revoked_authority_operation`). **Regression-before-repair:** with the re-assertion removed, the same scenario fails with `promise resolved "{ content: [ ... ] }" instead of rejecting`, meaning the real server received and answered the revoked call. A matching unit case (`mcp-request-headers.test.ts`) fails without the fix and passes with it.

Redacted terminal capture (`OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`):

```text
[pr154043-proof] allowed: real tools/call arrived with volatile header present
[pr154043-proof] canceled: rejected before I/O, server request count unchanged; pending send settled
[pr154043-proof] shared transport: subsequent attributed tools/call succeeded
[pr154043-proof] foreign: forged and SDK-asserted identity reached the server unsigned; provider never saw victim-run
[pr154043-proof] reassigned: settled run's captured context reached the server unsigned; provider never saw it
[pr154043-proof] revoked authority: provider resolved, caller authority revoked mid-resolution; rejected before I/O, server request count unchanged
 ✓ test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts > PR #154043 real runtime proof > dispatches attributed calls and rejects canceled calls before HTTP I/O
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

At this head: focused suites 8 files / 156 tests passed; core `tsgo` passed; timeout-race ratchet clean for PR files; formatting and lint clean.

### Run-identity authority + final-I/O proof (Rev 22 security item, head `a6194b291`)

**Concern (ClawSweeper Rev 22).** The public `runWithMcpRequestContext` accepted caller-supplied `sessionId`/`runId`, and the documented provider signs those IDs, so a caller could assert a foreign run and obtain a signed header at final HTTP I/O. A captured context also stayed usable after its run settled.

**Fix — bind signed identity to admitted runs (the recommended option).**
- Identity is issued only by the host: `runEmbeddedAttemptWithBackend` calls the internal `bindMcpRequestRun` with the admitted run's identity, keeping enclosing caller metadata.
- Each issued context carries run authority that is revoked when the run settles. `getMcpRequestContext()` returns nothing for a revoked or never-issued context, so the provider is never invoked for it. A run that settles while headers resolve is refused before dispatch by the existing `MCP request context expired` check.
- The public SDK export narrows to `runWithMcpRequestMetadata` (metadata only). Plugins and embedded callers can no longer name a session or run.

**Final-effect proof.** `test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts` now also drives, on the same real MCP SDK client + guarded streamable-HTTP transport + recording loopback server:
- **Foreign:** a forged frozen context `{ runId: "victim-run" }` and the public SDK helper each reach the server with **no** attribution header; the provider never sees `victim-run`.
- **Reassigned/settled:** a context captured inside a run that has since settled reaches the server with **no** attribution header; the provider never sees it.

**Regression-before-repair.** With the old trust semantics temporarily restored (any context accepted, no revocation), the proof fails at final I/O. The server received a signed header for the forged run:

```text
- Expected
+ Received
  {
-   "attribution": undefined,
+   "attribution": "synthetic-victim-run",
    "rpcMethod": "tools/call",
  }
 ❯ test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts:193:75
```

Redacted terminal capture after the fix (`OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts`):

```text
[pr154043-proof] allowed: real tools/call arrived with volatile header present
[pr154043-proof] canceled: rejected before I/O, server request count unchanged; pending send settled
[pr154043-proof] shared transport: subsequent attributed tools/call succeeded
[pr154043-proof] foreign: forged and SDK-asserted identity reached the server unsigned; provider never saw victim-run
[pr154043-proof] reassigned: settled run's captured context reached the server unsigned; provider never saw it
 ✓ test/pr154043-real-runtime-proof.e2e.test.ts > PR #154043 real runtime proof > dispatches attributed calls and rejects canceled calls before HTTP I/O 61ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Unit coverage (`src/agents/mcp-request-headers.test.ts`) adds: forged identity never resolves headers, captured context revoked after its run settles, and a run settling mid-resolution refuses dispatch. `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.request-headers.test.ts` now holds each turn open across acquisition and execution, as a host run does, and asserts that a settled turn's executor sends no attribution. On the merged head (current main `3f7689e64`): focused suites (`mcp-request-headers`, `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime{,.request-headers}`, `mcp-transport`, `mcp-http-transport`, `mcp-http-fetch`, `backend`, requester-connect, `registry-registrars-network.mcp-request-headers`) 10 files / 159 tests passed; both PR e2e proofs passed; core `tsgo` passed; `plugin-sdk:surface:check` passed (budget pinned to exactly this PR's two exports); formatting and lint clean. The merge resolved main's `mcp-http-fetch.ts` redirect-policy refactor by applying the provider wrap inside the shared builder.

### Registration-order fix + authority-chain proof (head `2587f4f3`)

**Defect (ClawSweeper P1, Rev 8).** `hasMcpServerOwnerConflict` was first-registration-wins across both seams: a request-header provider registered first by plugin A caused plugin B's later `registerMcpServerConnectionResolver` for the same server to be rejected. `partitionMcpServersByConnectionScope` then found no resolver and classified the declared server as **static**, exposing its configured connection to requesters the resolver would have excluded. The PR's own registrar test pinned that behavior.

**Fix.** The connection resolver is authoritative regardless of order. `registerMcpServerConnectionResolver` still fails closed against a different plugin's resolver; against a different plugin's *provider* it now displaces it — the provider entry is removed and an error diagnostic is reported on the provider's plugin (`MCP server request header provider for "<name>" displaced: connection resolver registered by plugin "<resolver plugin>" owns requester admission`). `registerMcpServerRequestHeaderProvider` is unchanged (rejected when a different plugin owns either seam). Final registry state is identical in both registration orders. `docs/plugins/sdk-overview/infrastructure.md` states the rule.

**Regression proof, unit** (`src/plugins/registry-registrars-network.mcp-request-headers.test.ts`, `it.each(["provider","resolver"])`): with the registrar fix reverted, the provider-first case fails —

```text
AssertionError: expected [ { level: 'error', …(3) } ] to deep equally contain ObjectContaining{…}

- Expected:
ObjectContaining {
  "level": "error",
  "message": StringContaining "displaced",
  "pluginId": "plugin-a",
}

+ Received:
[
  {
    "level": "error",
    "message": "MCP server connection resolver for \"user-mail\" rejected: already registered by plugin \"plugin-a\"",
    "pluginId": "plugin-b",
```

prs.title: fix: keep session files within permitted workspaces
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Files can select the agent's shared host workspace instead of an isolated session's private workspace. That makes files created in the sandbox disappear from the Files panel while unrelated host files appear there. Session visibility can also let a sandbox-required reader inherit another conversation's unsandboxed host root. ## User Impact The Files panel and its preview and download routes use the workspace admitted for both the conversation and the current reader. Shared private conversations retain their creator's files. Missing private workspace state produces an unavailable result instead of falling back to the host. Ordinary read-only operators retain permitted reads, and explicitly configured read-only sandbox mounts remain supported. Managed project files keep their existing checkpoint and publication owner. The Changes view requires an admitted project checkout; an unmanaged private sandbox returns the existing `not_git` notice while its Files view remains available. This change requires no configuration or data migration. ## Why This Change Was Made File readers now reuse the sandbox runtime's existing namespace selection, including creator isolation, attached child workspaces and library selections. Reads of unisolated host roots also reuse the caller's existing sandbox policy. A managed worktree does not bypass that check merely because its commands can run in an optional sandbox. The same selection and current-authority checks cover file listings, search, previews, retained downloads, admitted project diffs and app file readers. Private sandbox Git metadata is never passed to the host diff reader. Retained reads are invalidated when the relevant session, library selection, configuration or caller policy changes. Existing path, symlink, hardlink and outside-root safeguards remain in place. ## Evidence An isolated local baseline reproduced the wrong-root behavior through the actual Files interface and Gateway requests: a synthetic host-only file was visible and downloadable while a file created in the private sandbox was missing. The relevant source inputs were qualified against the source baseline; this is not a claim that the complete current-main baseline was executed. The correction passed the real Gateway dispatch and HTTP-download scenario, including private and shared reads, missing private state, normal managed-worktree provisioning, guest-to-admin-session denial, read-only and admin controls, policy changes, and retained-download revocation. The complete correction passed 13 affected suites with 182 tests in 112.94 seconds through the native test-projects runner on Linux, with a 16-worker cap. All 38 affected canonical compiler graphs are covered by current checks and qualified unchanged earlier results; formatting and iteration lint pass. It checks retained app-file ownership changes, runtime-config revocation during a diff, and an actual session diff request that returns `not_git` without calling the host diff reader for private sandbox metadata. Earlier candidate and fixture failures are retained in the validation record. Independent review closed all production findings. The real-Gateway browser comparison passed on the source baseline and corrected head, including exact downloads, preview and reload. It uses a paired administrator viewing a configured sandbox; actual guest admission is covered separately by the role-bound Gateway/HTTP scenario. Separate live checks with existing guest and admin profiles also passed on a selected runtime containing this repair with retained older build inputs. Guests could list, search, preview, download exact file bytes, reload, and reopen a saved inline file link. Relative and absolute host-file reads, foreign private paths, and guest reads through a visible admin conversation were denied while the original synthetic host file remained present. Shared target-workspace reads and legitimate admin host and outside-root reads remained available. This is supplementary integration proof, not a full-current-main deployment. The final static correction documents intentional test-fixture isolation and removes its obsolete mock baseline entry. Formatting, lint and the mock-export check pass; this correction changes no runtime behavior or test assertion. The final independent review is clean. CI passes on the final head. ClawSweeper rates that same head Platinum for readiness and proof, with Diamond patch quality and no actionable findings; its earlier evidence request is closed. ### Inspectable permission and retained-download evidence
Recorded synthetic live file-read and download outcomes ```text # Recorded synthetic Files outcomes Captured from the running UI client and ordinary browser download on selected runtime46110002bf93db2af023262752dc5262a58dfd0d. Its Files repair is the reviewed701eb4f production change; successor075674d7 changes only a test comment and obsolete test baseline entry. This runtime is a selected composition, not all later main. Only local paths and the synthetic administrator-session key below are replaced with explicit placeholders. Result booleans, error wording, admitted scopes, sizes and hashes are preserved. No new execution or reconstructed HTTP response is presented. Guest scopes: ["operator.sessions.read", "operator.sessions.write"] Allowed guest sessions.files.get response projection: { "hostMarker": false, "ok": true, "packingText": true, "path": "weekend-packing.txt", "root": "/redacted-lab/private-guest-a" } Browser Download from that private file preview; saved bytes checked against the unchanged private source: { "bytes": 400, "sha256": "769a76e90acf25c14d21b784b2a4d9374f6b0b08dc5e193dcae95d84d7ebe1dc", "utf8Prefix": "Weekend packing checklist\n" } Guest sessions.files.get against the visible administrator session (relative and absolute host-file paths): [ { "message": "Your operator role requires a sandboxed session; create a new session instead of running in \"\".", "ok": false, "path": "files-boundary-host-only.txt" }, { "message": "Your operator role requires a sandboxed session; create a new session instead of running in \"\".", "ok": false, "path": "/redacted-lab/shared-host/files-boundary-host-only.txt" } ] Privileged control: the same synthetic host marker remains readable in the administrator-owned session: { "hostMarker": true, "ok": true, "packingText": false, "path": "files-boundary-host-only.txt", "root": "/redacted-lab/shared-host" } ```
The existing regression uses the production download handler through a real HTTP listener with authenticated role fixtures. It asserts that a previously issued download returns HTTP 404 after the workspace root, library selection, or current reader policy changes. These 404 outcomes are backed by the passing test assertions; no per-request HTTP response body was recorded, and the excerpt below is the original aggregate test output, not a newly captured HTTP transcript. ```text [test] starting test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts Test Files 13 passed (13) Tests 182 passed (182) Duration 106.79s (tests 45%, transform 40%, import 11%, worker 2%, setup 1%) ``` The source assertions cover [workspace-root revocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/075674d7fe47c453edd1dcd7b292cbe55946cec2/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.sandbox.test.ts#L206-L211), [library-selection revocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/075674d7fe47c453edd1dcd7b292cbe55946cec2/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.sandbox.test.ts#L263-L276), and [current-reader revocation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/075674d7fe47c453edd1dcd7b292cbe55946cec2/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.sandbox.test.ts#L456-L457). The [HTTP fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/075674d7fe47c453edd1dcd7b292cbe55946cec2/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.test-support.ts#L122-L141) calls the production handler. That [handler revalidates authority before preparing a response and returns unavailable before file-response headers when validation fails](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/075674d7fe47c453edd1dcd7b292cbe55946cec2/src/gateway/artifact-downloads.ts#L58-L130); streaming responses also revalidate before each chunk. Fixes #177740 ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Files shows the synthetic shared\-host file and omits the private sandbox file](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a265624-d5ff-4585-8c01-b4fb3340aa15) | ![Files shows the private packing list and omits the shared\-host file](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2e722bf-eabb-4547-b119-0b5207d2bdfc) | ### Open Files and reload, slowed 4× with 0\.8 seconds of initial loading trimmed https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/657b52b8-da23-4c50-b76d-f0b9704c0c1b ### Visual verification - Baseline: b6bd9e8bd0cad400b31a223a0c44f8494f5cfb87 - Exact head: `701eb4f68e9898fee71d40176bd318aed6683c1c` - Scenario: Open Files in a configured sandbox session, download and preview its file, then reload\. Browser viewport 1440 × 1000 with identical Files\-panel framing\. A paired administrator exercises this browser route; actual guest admission is proved separately\. - Runtime/build: Real Gateway from native\-verified source 701eb4f/tree 8c1913, build snapshot feb50296\. Original build stamp retained\. Unchanged UI asset SHA256 c5bb75717b2d8e3a849833567cceda838706e27befacd591d9833c47bd733936\. - Before: host\-only\.txt visible and downloadable; packing\-list\.txt absent - After: packing\-list\.txt visible and downloadable; host\-only\.txt absent - Download and reload: Exact downloaded bytes and saved reload passed in both scenarios - Actor and execution: Paired admin viewing a configured sandbox; zero model calls; real guest role matrix separate - Equivalent viewport, theme, fixture and route - Actual browser file actions and content assertions passed - Served UI asset bytes match the built bundle - Native source receipt binds the after build snapshot to the exact authored head - Original before and after recordings retained - Readable recording preserves the original action sequence, trims 0\.8 seconds of initial loading and plays at quarter speed; original recording retained

prs.title: fix(lmstudio): retry model loading after correcting credentials
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes LM Studio retries with corrected credentials inheriting another request's failed model-preload cooldown and missing the loaded-instance route.

## User Impact

Preload joins and backoff apply only to callers with the same effective request and agent scope. Corrected credentials, routing headers, or timeout budgets get their own preparation. Model identity, context protection, and waiter cancellation remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preload cache key currently omits authentication, headers, agent scope, and deadline. Resolve the request facts once before selecting a slot, hash the complete effective scope without retaining raw credentials in keys, and reuse those facts for loading.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No security guard or public contract removed. Existing earned preload sharing and load-failure backoff stay in place; distinct request scopes no longer share their outcomes. If credentials cannot be resolved, the existing warning-and-inference fallback remains, but that resolution failure is not cached under an incomplete identity. No model-load request is made on that path.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: through the real stream/auth/discovery/load owners with synthetic transport fixtures, a corrected request must discover/load and route to its returned instance after another scope fails. Interleaved matching callers must perform one load; callers differing in routing headers must perform two and retain their own instance routes. No wall-time or live-provider performance claim.

On base `782e8d2f836419978ef11684f98802b8a837d47e`, five of six new regression cases failed for the intended cooldown/instance-sharing defect; the matching-scope one-load control passed. All six pass with the fix. Another 42 existing focused tests pass across streaming, instance routing, model-load errors, and runtime auth. Four older stream cases initially exposed a mock returning bare `undefined` rather than the async loader's promised result; the mock now returns a resolved promise, with no production workaround.

Focused syntax lint and format pass on all three files; all 14 lint-suppression tests pass. Scoped cycle proof covers 17 production files with zero runtime cycles or new static strongly connected components. Independent P0–P2 review completed scoped-clean. Qualified package-boundary typechecking remains for exact-head CI because local generated SDK declarations are unavailable; no broad local build was run. This is synthetic production-owner proof, not a live LM Studio claim.

Production delta: 24 lines added net. This is a concrete adjacent bug fix, not a large-cleanup quota contribution.

The provider documentation file is already touched by active PR #175931, so this patch leaves it unchanged under the campaign collision rule; this body records the corrected behavior for release-note generation.

CI run 39350015878 on initial head fa062c229550989e88d4126ae4434bc837063142 found one PR-caused mock-exports ratchet failure: the test's real-module pass-through made its old closed-factory fingerprint obsolete. Remove precisely that baseline row; no new exception or runtime change. The targeted factory scanner confirms real exports are preserved, the 14 suppression tests pass again (12.64 seconds wall time), and fresh incremental P0–P2 independent review is scoped-clean. Remaining exact-head CI is still required.

CI run 39351131232, job 118401265387, found a PR-caused type-aware lint error in the new concurrent fixture: `StreamFn` can return synchronously, so its direct mapped results are not guaranteed Promise-like inputs to `Promise.all`. The map callback now explicitly returns an async result. Both calls still start concurrently, and all six scope/load-count regressions pass unchanged (187.28 seconds Vitest wall time, dominated by cold compilation); all 14 suppression tests pass again. Both shards completed in 218.58 seconds wrapper wall time. Fresh incremental P0–P2 independent review is scoped-clean with source verification. The prior pending auto-merge request was retired through native recovery before this head repair. No production behavior or test expectation changed.

prs.title: fix(ui): Show earlier loses keyboard focus while older history loads
prs.body:
Related: #149618

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a keyboard user who focuses the chat's "Show earlier" control loses focus to the page body as soon as older history starts loading.

## User Impact

User impact: keyboard and screen reader users stay on the control while older messages load (the focused control's name changes to "Loading earlier…"), and can press it again as "Show earlier" once the page lands, instead of being thrown back to the start of the page.

## Why This Change Was Made

The control is now marked busy with `aria-disabled` instead of the native `disabled` attribute, and ignores activation while loading. Native `disabled` makes Chromium blur the focused button at its next rendering step; `aria-disabled` keeps it focusable and still announces it as unavailable. That component guard is what keeps a press while busy from sending anything: the history loader's own guard only covers older-history loads, while the same busy state also covers chat loading, catalog loading and the cron run transcript. The busy look is unchanged (the only `:disabled` style was the hover suppression, now keyed on `aria-disabled`).

| Case | Expected outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Focus on the control, older history starts loading (Enter or the automatic load when the control scrolls into view) | Focus stays on the control; it reads "Loading earlier…", `aria-busy="true"`, `aria-disabled="true"` |
| Enter or click while loading | Ignored; no second `chat.history` request |
| Load finishes and more history remains | Focus stays on the same control, now "Show earlier", active again |
| Load finishes and history is exhausted | Not changed here: the boundary still unmounts and focus is not moved. That needs its own intentional focus transition (see the issue triage) and is left for a follow-up |
| Cron run transcript, which reuses the same boundary | Same component, same behavior; its existing paging test still passes |

## Evidence

All of the following ran on one machine at the staged tree, base `0631ad4046a`.

**Build.** Control UI built from this tree by the repo's bundled e2e lane (`pnpm test:ui:e2e`), Playwright Chromium headless, mock Gateway with `chat.history` held until released. Synthetic transcript ("Conversation message 41..80", 40 older messages available).

**Behaviour.** Same scenario on both arms: focus the "Show earlier" control, press Enter, wait for the held load, press Enter again, release the load. Values below were read from the DOM with `page.evaluate` two animation frames after each step.

Before (base production code):

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9de7ef8e99c4a2bcaa3cfd5e72d9f747d3c4a0be/pr-8-show-earlier-focus/before.png)

- While loading: `document.activeElement` = `body`; button text "Loading earlier…", `aria-busy="true"`, `disabled` attribute present.
- Focus log: `focusout BUTTON.chat-history-boundary__action -> null`.
- After the load lands: `document.activeElement` = `body`; button reads "Show earlier".

After (this PR):

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9de7ef8e99c4a2bcaa3cfd5e72d9f747d3c4a0be/pr-8-show-earlier-focus/after.png)

- While loading: `document.activeElement` = `button.chat-history-boundary__action`, matches `:focus-visible`; text "Loading earlier…", `aria-busy="true"`, `aria-disabled="true"`, no `disabled` attribute. No focusout events.
- Accessibility snapshot of the boundary while loading (Playwright `ariaSnapshot`, read from the DOM):
  ```
  - button "Loading earlier…" [disabled]:
    - status: Loading earlier…
  ```
  Playwright prints `[disabled]` for both native `disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"`, so this line is identical on both arms; the difference is that the button now keeps focus.
- `chat.history` requests after the second Enter: 1.
- After the load lands: `document.activeElement` = `button.chat-history-boundary__action`; text "Show earlier", `aria-busy="false"`, no `aria-disabled`.

**Tests.**

```
pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/chat-history-loading.e2e.test.ts   (5 consecutive runs)
      Tests  4 passed (4)   x5

pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/chat-history-loading.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.history-recovery.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/chat-history-empty-tail.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/claude-sessions.e2e.test.ts   (every e2e that drives the boundary)
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  21 passed (21)

pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-controller.test.tsx ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-history.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-history-loading.test.ts
      Tests  146 passed (146)
      Tests  62 passed (62)

pnpm test ui/src/pages/cron/run-transcript.e2e.test.ts   (cron consumer of the same boundary)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

Wall time per changed test file (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`; the e2e file via `pnpm test:ui:e2e <file>`, which includes the Control UI build). CI seconds will be added once CI runs.

| File | Wall time |
| --- | --- |
| `ui/src/e2e/chat-history-loading.e2e.test.ts` | 15.2 to 15.3 s over 5 runs (13.1 to 13.3 s test duration; new case 779 to 1051 ms) |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts` | 6.19 s |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-history.test.ts` | 3.25 s |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-controller.test.tsx` | 3.22 s |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-history-loading.test.ts` | 2.96 s |

The new e2e case is "keeps keyboard focus on the earlier-history action while older history loads". It focuses the control without scrolling it into view (scrolling there is reader intent that would start the automatic load and arm the next one), so Enter is the only trigger. The mock holds the `offset: 40` page until released and holds the staged next page (`offset: 60`) for the rest of the test, then asserts the request offsets are exactly `[40]` after a second Enter and a Space while busy, and exactly `[40, 60]` after the page lands. Four jsdom assertions that read `button.disabled === true` while loading now read `aria-disabled="true"`. The existing "click while loading does not call onShowEarlier" assertion in `chat-view.test.ts` uses a plain mock with no request owner behind it, so it now covers the click guard on its own: with only the guard removed it fails (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 2 times`, `chat-view.test.ts:933`). The shared `expectHistoryBoundaryState` helper is unchanged because Playwright's `isDisabled()` honours `aria-disabled`.

**Regression proof (red/green).** Production files reverted to the base, tests kept:

```
pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/chat-history-loading.e2e.test.ts
     × keeps keyboard focus on the earlier-history action while older history loads
AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality
 ❯ ui/src/e2e/chat-history-loading.e2e.test.ts:116:35   (focus check while loading)
      Tests  1 failed | 3 passed (4)
```

With the fix: 4 passed (above).

**Other checks.**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | pass |
| `oxlint` on the 6 changed TS/TSX files | 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| `stylelint` on `ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css` | pass |
| `pnpm format:check` on changed files | pass |
| `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` | pass (no copy changes) |
| `git diff --check` | clean |
| `pnpm changed:lanes --json` | lanes `ui`, `coreTests` |
| `pnpm check:changed` | typecheck UI and core tests, lint, stylelint, format, i18n and controller guards pass; 3 checks fail and fail the same way at the base with no changes: max-lines suppression ratchet (files this PR does not touch), core test shard root budget (725 and 724 roots over the advisory 720), unused-export scan (exports this PR does not touch) |

## Gaps, stated plainly

- History exhaustion is not handled: when the last page lands, the boundary unmounts and a focused control is still lost. That needs a deliberate focus target and is out of scope here.
- Proof is the mock-Gateway Control UI e2e in headless Chromium. No real Gateway replay, no Firefox/WebKit, and no screen reader run; the announcement claim rests on the accessibility snapshot.
- The regression waits two animation frames before each focus read. Measured without that wait: the base still reports the disabled button as focused during the busy check, so the red arm passes that check and fails only at the post-load focus check; the fixed code stays green either way (one red run and three green runs without the wait). With the wait the red arm fails at the busy check. A future engine change in Chromium's focus fixup timing could move where the red arm fails.
- The test does not cover the automatic load started by scrolling the control into view; it isolates Enter as the trigger so the request count is deterministic.

prs.title: feat(inworld): realtime voice provider for Talk and Voice Call
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators who chose an Inworld voice for Talk, voice notes or telephony TTS cannot use that voice in realtime (full-duplex) mode: OpenClaw's realtime voice registry only offers OpenAI and Google, each with vendor voices. Inworld's Realtime API runs STT, an LLM/router and TTS-2 on one WebSocket using the OpenAI Realtime protocol, so an Inworld realtime provider closes that gap with the same host contract (consult and end-call tools, barge-in, telephony audio) and no change for existing TTS users. Tracking issue: #168030.

## Summary

Adds a realtime voice provider to the official `inworld` plugin so Talk (`talk.realtime.provider: "inworld"`) and Voice Call (`realtime.provider: "inworld"`) can run full-duplex speech-to-speech on Inworld's Realtime API with Inworld TTS-2 voices, while the OpenClaw agent stays the brain through the shared `openclaw_agent_consult` / `openclaw_end_call` tools.

Closes #168030. Builds on #167951 for the `speakingRate` / `deliveryMode` naming.

## What changes

- `extensions/inworld/realtime-voice-*.ts`: WebSocket bridge modeled on the bundled xAI realtime provider (Inworld follows the OpenAI Realtime event protocol): `Authorization: Basic <apiKey>` with the dashboard credential, session URL `wss://api.inworld.ai/api/v1/realtime/session?key=…&protocol=realtime`, `session.update` carrying model, instructions, `audio.input/output.format`, STT model, `semantic_vad` (eagerness) or `server_vad`, `audio.output.{voice,model,speed}`, and `providerData` (`auto_tool_response: false`, TTS delivery/steering/segmenter, responsiveness; back-channel is rejected until the host has an out-of-band playback path). Tool calls are emitted at `response.done`; results go back as `function_call_output` followed by a host-owned `response.create`. Barge-in cancels and truncates playback. Inworld has no session resumption, so an unexpected close is terminal rather than retried.
- Lazy catalog descriptor keeps `ws` off the startup path; manifest declares the `realtimeVoiceProviders` contract and the `ws` dependency; `index.ts` registers the provider next to the existing speech provider.
- Audio: PCM16 24 kHz and G.711 µ-law 8 kHz, both passed through without host transcoding.
- Docs: `docs/providers/inworld.md` (new "Realtime voice" accordion), `docs/tools/media-overview.md`, generated plugin inventory. Config-doc baseline hash regenerated; counts unchanged (no new `configSchema` entries: realtime config lives under `talk.realtime.providers.inworld` / the voice-call realtime provider map like the other providers).

- `providerData`: a bounded passthrough for the documented Inworld extension sections only (`stt`, `tts`, `memory`, `responsiveness`; unknown sections rejected, 8 KiB cap). Typed settings win over it, and `auto_tool_response: false` is pinned after the merge so no passthrough can hand `response.create` back to the server.

Defaults preserved: nothing changes for existing Inworld TTS users; the realtime provider only activates when selected.

## Config example

```json5
{
  talk: {
    realtime: {
      provider: "inworld",
      mode: "realtime",
      transport: "gateway-relay",
      brain: "agent-consult",
      providers: {
        inworld: {
          apiKey: { source: "env", provider: "default", id: "INWORLD_API_KEY" },
          model: "openai/gpt-4.1-mini",
          voiceId: "Sarah",
          ttsModel: "inworld-tts-2",
          speakingRate: 1.0,
          deliveryMode: "BALANCED",
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Evidence

### Tests and gates

- `extensions/inworld`: 53/53 tests (20 new provider cases: metadata/capabilities, config normalization, session policy for both VAD modes and both audio formats, credential/startup failures, audio + playback marks + transcripts, tool call → result → `response.create`, suppressed results, server-VAD and host barge-in, terminal close, bounded `providerData` normalization, and the exact emitted `session.update` payload with the passthrough merged under typed keys and `auto_tool_response` pinned, back-channel config rejected and back-channel events tolerated without audio, marks or truncation), 2 lazy-descriptor cases.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint, oxfmt, `pnpm plugins:inventory:check`, `pnpm config:docs:check` all clean.
- Plugin contract suite: 1079/1079 on the rebased branch (capability-catalog, registry, extension-runtime-dependencies and runtime-api guardrails).

### Real behavior proof (authenticated, redacted live logs)

Run on 2026-10-09 against this branch at its base commit (dc46466756e, before the `providerData` passthrough commit, which only adds the bounded merge covered by the emitted-payload test) through the provider's own `createBridge` with a real Inworld key (header redacted), then through a second isolated Gateway (`--profile`, own port) built from this branch where `talk.catalog` reported the provider configured and ready and `talk.session.create` returned `provider: "inworld"` at PCM16 24 kHz.


### Spoken input, interruption and providerData at 183f08f6889 (historical run, authenticated, redacted)

Second live run, recorded at the earlier head 183f08f6889 (its `backchannel` settings are rejected by the current head's config normalizer; everything else in the run is unchanged code), through the provider's `createBridge` with PCM16 24 kHz. The two "user" utterances were synthesized with the plugin's own Inworld TTS and streamed as 20 ms frames like a microphone; `providerData` was set (`tts.segmenter_strategy: "sentence"`, `memory: { enabled: true, turn_interval: 2 }`, and at that time `backchannel: { require_pause: false }`) with `deliveryMode: CREATIVE` (`backchannel` had been set on this run; it is withdrawn in the head commit, see below), and the session was accepted (`session.updated`). The server detected speech, transcribed it, answered with audio, was interrupted by a second spoken utterance mid-answer (barge-in cleared playback, the response ended `cancelled` with `turn_detected`), transcribed the interruption, called `openclaw_agent_consult`, and the response carrying that tool call completed. Bounds: this is the provider's bridge driven directly, not a Gateway Talk or Voice Call session; the run ended at that tool-call terminal, before the tool-result continuation and the final spoken answer were awaited; no back-channel interjection fired.

```

```

Also addressed from review: back-channel is withdrawn rather than half-supported. Inworld delivers interjections out of band (`response.backchannel.audio.delta`, while the user is still speaking), and the host playback contract has no out-of-band channel today (the Talk relay sink requires a live response owner; Voice Call truncates every snapshot item on `speech_started`), so the adapter no longer accepts `backchannel` in config or `providerData`, never enables it, and tolerates stray `response.backchannel.*` events as diagnostics without delivering audio. The low-value lazy metadata test was removed; the branch is rebased on current main.

### Host-routed Voice Call at fe4765c713e (authenticated, redacted)

Outbound telephony call placed by the Voice Call plugin on a gateway built from this head (`openclaw voicecall call --mode conversation`, `realtime.provider: "inworld"`, Twilio), answered by a human and driven entirely through the shipped host path. Gateway journal, identifiers and numbers removed; counts are line counts from the plugin's own log lines.

```
20:02:11 [voice-call] Outbound call initiated mode=conversation
20:02:31 [voice-call] Serving realtime TwiML for Twilio call (direction=outbound-api)
20:02:31 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting (initialGreeting=queued)
20:02:32 .. 20:05:20  realtime local speech detected: 42 events
20:02:34 .. 20:05:20  realtime input transcript final=true: 13 user turns (104 partials)
2x        [voice-call] realtime outbound audio cleared by provider barge-in (caller interrupted mid-sentence; queuedBytes>0)
20:05:22 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized endReason=completed  (2 min 51 s)
```

What this does and does not show: the host-routed bridge ran a full spoken conversation over mu-law telephony with the caller interrupting twice and the provider clearing queued audio both times, and the call ended normally. The caller did not ask anything that triggered `openclaw_agent_consult` during this call (the test agent behind the bridge had no identity to consult), so tool-result continuation on the host path is covered only by the direct-createBridge runs above. The browser Talk button on that gateway's Control UI requested the client-owned session mode (`talk.client.create`) and was refused with INVALID_REQUEST (`use talk.session.create for gateway-relay`), so no browser realtime session was exercised; that path is not claimed here.

### Host consultation to spoken answer at fe4765c713e (authenticated, redacted)

Inbound Twilio call to a production gateway running this head with `voice-call.realtime.provider: "inworld"` (talker model on Inworld's router, voice Luna, `openclaw_agent_consult` wired to a real OpenClaw agent on its main session). The caller asked a question only the agent could answer. Gateway journal, identifiers and numbers removed.

```
21:29:52 [voice-call] Serving realtime TwiML for Twilio call (direction=inbound)
21:29:53 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting (initialGreeting=queued)
21:30:02 .. 21:30:51  5 final caller turns transcribed; 1 provider barge-in clearing 6,897 queued bytes (caller interrupted)
21:30:51 [voice-call] realtime tool call received tool=openclaw_agent_consult
21:30:51 [voice-call] realtime tool call executing tool=openclaw_agent_consult hasHandler=true
21:31:20 .. 21:31:31  two unrelated runs on the agent's main session finish (consult queued behind them: lane wait 40,003 ms)
21:31:46 [voice-call] realtime tool call received tool=openclaw_agent_consult   (model asked again while waiting)
21:31:46 [voice-call] realtime tool call sharing in-flight agent consult ageMs=54870
21:31:49 [voice-call] realtime tool call completed tool=openclaw_agent_consult status=ok elapsedMs=57939
21:32:07 .. 21:34:48  conversation continues: 15 further final caller turns
21:34:53 [voice-call] Max duration reached (300s), ending call   → Call finalized endReason=timeout
```

The operator on the call reported watching the consult arrive in the agent's chat, the agent compose its answer, and the realtime voice speak that answer immediately after; the voice-call host does not log output audio events, so the spoken continuation is evidenced by the completed consult followed by three more minutes of two-way turns. The 58 s consult round trip was dominated by a 40 s queue behind other turns on the same agent session, not by the provider; a dedicated consult agent avoids that. The call ended at the host's configured 300 s maximum, not on error.

## Out of scope

WebRTC / client-owned browser sessions and Inworld session tokens; Inworld's hosted memory as a replacement for OpenClaw memory (passthrough only, off by default).
