prs.title: feat(gateway): add deployment-scoped tool and action policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Deployment owners need to limit which Gateway tools and actions model-directed work can use, including administrator-started conversations and plugin-provided tools. `tools.gatewayPolicy` applies a tool allowlist and explicit action lists after ordinary grants, then authorizes final arguments after preparation and hooks.

Tools capture the deployment policy when assembled. Adding, changing or removing it requires Gateway restart or replacement after affected old work ends. Ordinary tool-policy reloads, direct human administration, native Codex tools and deployments without this setting keep their existing behavior.

Tool Search, Code Mode, HTTP/MCP invocation and dedicated workers share the policy rules. Both turn and stable session catalogs are filtered. Children retain their parent's applicable whole-tool restrictions and apply the deployment's action policy themselves. Workspace-dependent delegation uses the shared publisher schema and existing policy evaluator without inserting a callable publisher into the parent's catalog.

This provides [RFC-0021](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/2367) items **1/2**, caller-independent propagation for **3**, and native execution coverage for **8**. Automation restrictions, Codex adapter integration, OCE policy delivery and Harness-local protection remain separate work.

## Evidence

- Integrated main at `ba61d5d99526`, preserving stable session catalogs, expanded publication actions and brokered worker publication.
- Scoped lint, generated-config verification and whitespace checks pass. Independent correctness and maintainability reviews are clean after fixing an automatic-merge context error.

Media duplicate detection maintains a second request-start cache and joins it back to operations that already own the same work and completion lifetime.

prs.body:
Fixes #174336

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: embedded agents never receive an MCP server's initialization instructions, even when that server's tools are available.

## User Impact

User impact: the model receives the server's guidance for directly available tools. Deferred Tool Search and Code Mode discovery carry the guidance with the tool metadata instead. Servers without instructions keep their existing prompt and tool surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the MCP client's initialization instructions and carry them through the existing catalog and tool metadata owners. The prompt includes each directly available server once. Deferred discovery keeps its existing response budgets, includes an excerpt when needed, and points to the complete description when it fits. Model control tokens and application prompt delimiters are neutralized before delivery.

The contributor's commits and credit are preserved. This is the earlier, narrower alternative to #174425, which addresses the same issue.

## Evidence

Built Gateway, local stdio MCP server, recording OpenAI-compatible provider, and a real `openclaw agent` turn, all in an isolated container:

```text
                                   request  MCP tool  initialize instructions
main 7a628b0adaa, run 1              1        present   absent
main 7a628b0adaa, run 2              1        present   absent
candidate 4d46784da23, run 1         1        present   present
candidate 4d46784da23, run 2         1        present   present
main, no-instructions control       1        present   absent
candidate, no-instructions control  1        present   absent
```

Captured candidate system prompt:

```text
## MCP Server Instructions
Server-wide guidance published by the MCP servers behind the tools above; it applies to that server's tools.
### proof174342
MCP174342-INSTRUCTIONS: Before using lookup always confirm the account name.
```

The control's tool definitions are identical, and its system prompt is identical after normalizing only the separate proof workspace/repository paths. The frozen main artifact predates the next fetched main commit by one minute; that advancement changes no MCP, prompt, Gateway, or provider-request code.

The regression fails on main because the server guidance is absent, then passes on the candidate. Seven focused test files pass: 114 tests across four routed shards in 82.44 seconds, covering prompt delivery/revocation, resources and prompts, deferred discovery, Code Mode, client tool collisions, and prefix stability. The initialization-to-prompt regression file takes 30.94 seconds cold, predominantly transform time; its real protocol test bodies take milliseconds. Scoped formatting and lint pass. A separate `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` embedded turn completes successfully and returns the requested marker.

Merge danger: two-way door; reverting removes the prompt/metadata additions and writes no new persistent state or config. Blast radius: embedded agents using MCP tools, including deferred Tool Search and Code Mode discovery; native harness MCP clients are unchanged.

prs.title: perf(database): remove redundant admission and cleanup statements
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory rebuilds, plugin cleanup, and owner-profile updates execute database statements whose answers are already known or unused.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior or configuration change. Eligible operations do less database work; existing data repair, publication, and cleanup authority checks stay in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fresh private SQLite memory shadows already contain newly created STRICT tables and no FTS objects. Their existing caller-asserted `fresh` path now skips the legacy STRICT inspection and FTS catalog query. Canonical/non-fresh repair and collision detection, STRICT DDL, the FTS savepoint, final schema admission, and publication guards remain unchanged. PostgreSQL staging does not take this fresh path.

Plugin cleanup now requests retained deletion IDs through the existing read worker, using one dialect-neutral Kysely SELECT. It no longer loads the registry or wraps a single read in the full deletion-snapshot transaction. Startup migration and discovery still use the full snapshot. The narrow projection preserves retained IDs even when unused path JSON is malformed. Cleanup keeps per-store admission and its final destructive-effect check. The cleanup owner already catches advisory read failures and continues through per-store admission; the existing rejected-read regression proves that healthy configured stores are cleaned, retained deleted-store bytes remain unchanged, and per-store failures are returned. Registry retirement reports those failures while continuing sibling hooks. This change does not add a whole-pass abort or a new journal warning.

When an owner identity was returned by the tagged read in the same transaction, filling its missing display name no longer repeats `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. First-use identity creation and committed roster publication remain unchanged. No schema, cache, generation, freshness probe, cross-store commit ordering, or public SDK contract is added.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: frozen v3.1 workload, three alternating baseline/candidate pairs; report SQL statements, worker requests, and MAIN medians with ranges for boot, compaction/settle/idle, restart, and warm turns. Credit only attributed reductions, with no latency claim on the shared host. No new work in the touched operations or affected shared read families is accepted without explanation.

| Eligible operation | Statement reduction | Requests / MAIN |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Fresh SQLite memory shadow | 2 | unchanged |
| Cleanup retained-ID read | 4 → 1 | 1 / 0, unchanged |
| Existing identity, missing owner display name | 1 | unchanged |

Each removed statement has a regression that failed on the base. Cleanup also exercises pending → completed → removed journal changes through the real read worker, and the profile test verifies the committed display name through the roster snapshot. All 317 focused owner and consumer cases passed across the completed runs. The initial combined run found one test-fixture teardown leak: the SQL-observer preload outlived its temporary file. Closing the existing state worker before deleting the fixture fixed it; both subsequent 15-case cleanup runs passed. Production and all 29 selected test typecheck groups pass on the committed head. Type-aware changed lint, Madge (zero cycles), export collisions, T1 (177 → 177), compatibility (11 → 11), and the dialect ratchets pass. The SDK comparison reports no public API changes. Local check:changed exits nonzero only for baseline-reproduced UI line limits, core-root budgets (725/724 versus 720), and the same two unused UI exports; no new findings.

The separate live cleanup baseline/candidate pair starts isolated Gateways, retains a deleted agent with `deleteFiles:false`, and disables the bundled `llm-task` plugin without invoking its tool. Captured origin stacks prove exactly one cleanup-helper call in each arm: **4 SQL / 1 request / 0 MAIN → 1 / 1 / 0**. The retained database's bytes and inode remain unchanged, and both Gateways shut down cleanly. Earlier fixture attempts were rejected during startup contention or failed external-plugin generation before cleanup; they are not counted as successful proof.

All six completed frozen-v3.1 arms use baseline `9c98a4d04f2b0edce2b3c987769148df9eec3319` and reviewed candidate `29ddc640f34b16ace43f26cae17203c1e6b440e7`, in M1/C1/M2/C2/M3/C3 order. Counts below are median [minimum–maximum]. Whole/phase distributions contain three runs per side; warm distributions pool ten turns per run, thirty per side. SQL uses execution phase and requests use emission phase; causal warm counts follow the originating turn.

| Phase | Baseline SQL / requests / MAIN | Candidate SQL / requests / MAIN |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Whole workload | 3150 [3127–3162] / 867 [866–874] / 98 [98–98] | 3126 [3124–3130] / 866 [865–877] / 98 [98–98] |
| Boot | 312 [312–313] / 89 [89–91] / 50 [50–50] | 313 [312–314] / 91 [89–91] / 50 [50–50] |
| Connect + first turn | 560 [532–573] / 137 [123–137] / 0 [0–0] | 536 [529–569] / 126 [123–137] / 0 [0–0] |
| Second session | 494 [490–494] / 127 [126–127] / 0 [0–0] | 490 [489–494] / 127 [127–129] / 0 [0–0] |
| Cron | 247 [247–247] / 65 [65–65] / 0 [0–0] | 251 [247–252] / 66 [65–66] / 0 [0–0] |
| Compaction + settle + idle | 385 [385–386] / 87 [87–88] / 0 [0–0] | 383 [382–383] / 87 [87–88] / 0 [0–0] |
| Restart boot | 315 [315–331] / 106 [106–110] / 38 [38–38] | 315 [315–316] / 106 [106–106] / 38 [38–38] |
| Restart first turn | 232 [230–266] / 85 [83–85] / 0 [0–0] | 233 [232–237] / 83 [83–87] / 0 [0–0] |
| Warm causal | 51 [51–55] / 15 [15–16] / 0 [0–0] | 51 [51–55] / 15 [15–16] / 0 [0–0] |
| Warm execution windows | 52 [51–86] / 15 [15–30] / 0 [0–0] | 51.5 [51–73] / 15.5 [15–27] / 0 [0–0] |

The standard workload has **zero eligible cleanup-helper calls in all six arms**, so no cleanup saving is credited there. Its initial owner creation remains **30 SQL / 1 request / 0 MAIN** in every arm; it does not exercise the existing-identity display-name branch. The causally attributed saving is exactly **2 SQL per fresh shadow**, consistently **35 → 33**; canonical admission remains **65**. Combined `schema.admit` is therefore **100 / 2 / 0 → 98 / 2 / 0** in every pair. No worker request or MAIN reduction is attributed to this patch.

The raw whole-workload median difference (−24 SQL, −1 request) is not a causal savings claim. Untouched work varies even on the same source: M1/M2 differ by 23 SQL and 8 requests, and M3 alone executes `installStatusTracking` (33 SQL/1 request). Full-snapshot reads have identical medians of 53 SQL/11 requests, with baseline range 53–58/11–12 and candidate fixed at 53/11. Candidate C2 has 16 zero-SQL `scan` requests versus baseline range 5–8. The exact scheduling triggers behind every variation are not established.

Small phase increases stay in unchanged operations: boot's +1 median statement is delivery-queue counting moving from connect into boot (two statements over the whole workload on every arm); cron's +4 is auth-profile read-database acquisition moving from first/warm turns into cron (eight statements total on every arm). Restart connect+first has a +1 median: the median-selected baseline and candidate samples differ by one `usage-cost` statement. No individual restart operation has a higher SQL median; a median of phase totals is not the sum of operation medians. Other restart variation includes session maintenance, entry-list, cron settlement, and baseline-only install tracking. These are not added work in the touched paths. Every measured window's candidate/baseline median duration ratio is below 1.5 (maximum 1.30); no latency benefit is claimed.

The five shared-read families have **zero SELECTs in every raw and causal warm turn**, on both sides. Whole-workload SELECTs / containing requests have these medians and ranges; families overlap and must not be summed:

| Shared-read family | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact-entry facts | 18 [18–19] / 18 [18–19] | 18 [18–19] / 18 [18–19] |
| Actor hydration | 10 [10–10] / 5 [5–5] | 10 [10–10] / 5 [5–5] |
| Entry-cache snapshots | 7 [7–7] / 5 [5–5] | 7 [7–7] / 5 [5–5] |
| Row facts | 21 [19–21] / 12 [11–12] | 19 [19–21] / 11 [11–12] |
| Watermark reads | 4 [4–4] / 3 [3–3] | 4 [4–4] / 3 [3–3] |

All of these reads have zero MAIN statements. Row-fact median variation is not credited to this patch. Independent ledger reconstruction verifies all whole, phase, operation, request and causal totals; 19 SQL and 27–28 requests per arm remain explicitly classified as unknown operations, so this is not a claim of complete operation attribution.

The first C3 attempt reached restart but received `UNAVAILABLE` / `startup-sidecars` before the requested chat turn. Its incomplete sample is excluded. A single C3 replacement passed using the frozen harness's supported `--skip-build` on the same candidate build; the preceding five valid arms were retained. This is a setup/readiness retry, not a product fix or an inherited-failure claim.

Exact-head CI [39346642729](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39346642729) passes the applicable static/type/lint/architecture/ratchet checks and all three PostgreSQL conformance jobs. The aggregate fails only because [UI shard 5/8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39346642729/job/118381192584) times out on the 390px and 1280px sidebar-download recovery cases. Both exact signatures occur on [scheduled main 39342008977, job 118365882354](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39342008977/job/118365882354): the Retry now button remains disabled while reconnecting. This is recorded as inherited, with no rerun or fix claim.

Production delta: +70/-43 lines (net +27); test delta: +89/-6 (net +83). The small growth implements a dedicated narrow read in the existing dispatcher. Existing full-snapshot consumers retain their required path. Two isolated Codex reviews completed with no actionable findings. The query was then mechanically moved into the existing worker module; its SQL and behavior are unchanged. Exact-head PostgreSQL review approved this head; its initial description of advisory read failures is corrected by the existing cleanup-owner behavior above. prs.title: refactor(update): simplify private plugin preparation and retention
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private plugin update preparation repeats locator/config recertification, projects install records twice, and compares retained runtime fingerprints after already admitting the sources.

## User Impact

No feature, CLI/config key, SDK export, or persisted data shape changes. Updates retain private plugin copies, source-independent rehearsal, descriptor-safe copying, size limits, final link confinement, bounded concurrency, live authority, and write settlement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Project freshly read private install records directly through the inventoried paths. Remove repeated source/config binding checks and the extra record clone. Simplify private dependency completion and ordinary hardlink retention without old inode/ctime equality or its OverlayFS workaround. Plugin safety files still copy independently; hardlink failure still uses portable copying.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Record/config hashes and duplicate state-root/locator recertification: both phases receive one operation's captured inputs; the inspected introducing changes cite no human concurrent-edit incident. Mid-operation mutation is best effort. Every actual copied locator must still exist in the private projection before writing the private index; final private link confinement stays.
- Extra clone of freshly read private install records: projection owns these objects. Mutate that private result directly; neither the source database nor shared caller objects are modified.
- Rehearsal byte comparisons and caller-environment rechecks: this is private dependency completion, not live policy publication. The missing-import repair [#146616](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146616) does not establish a human environment-mutation incident. Existing private bytes remain untouched; missing dependencies copy safely under real supervisor/effect authority.
- Inventory inode/ctime equality and OverlayFS workaround: [#165982](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165982) addresses the human unchanged-file false refusal in [#164308](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164308). Retain regular files by hardlink without old stat equality; plugin safety files still copy, and ordinary hardlink failure falls back to copying. Concurrent source edits remain best effort.
- Same-inode serialization existed to avoid self-induced ctime mismatches in that fingerprint mechanism. The equality requirement is gone; tasks use the existing bounded four-task pool and drain before cleanup.

Measured copy workers [#166317](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166317), hardlink retention [#155977](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155977), and retired-workspace confinement [#159035](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159035) remain.

## Evidence

The current candidate removes **190 net production lines** (+28/-218). It is a residue, not a LARGE PR. Exact head `50867f9917c0f89e9336ab04e1612c746674cb63` passed [CI run 39350857993](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39350857993), including the previously failing suites and PostgreSQL proof unavailable locally. All 135 exact-head check runs were enumerated: no failed suites or pending checks. Four cancelled metadata-automation jobs are superseded by exact-head successful replacements: auto-response 118394676566/118394428429, label 118394460188, and dispatch 118394459513. No broad local build/typecheck, timeout increase, retry, skip, new suppression, CI rerun, rebase, or green-chasing push was used.

Focused five-owner proof passed 71 cases with one existing Linux-only skip on macOS. After accepting a fresh-review byte-ceiling finding, both retention suites passed 13 cases: the existing hardlink `lstat` now also rejects files larger than their inventory budget, with no extra I/O. Its regression failed before that guard. The original full-plan large-reply fixture and capture-budget assertion were restored with the restored plan schema; that case passed again (69,810,554-byte full plan, 25,440,405-byte worker projection, unchanged 64-MiB capture ceiling).

Targeted types, typed lint, format, whitespace, and runtime/type-inclusive cycle checks passed (both cycle counts zero). The suppression gate has 13 passes and one unchanged-base failure: `scripts/perf/chat-metadata-burst-measure.ts` has an unlisted `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method` row. Both that source and the suppression test are byte-identical to the pinned base; this PR adds no suppression or allowlist change. Broad check-changed execution is deliberately left to hosted CI under the campaign's local CPU restriction.

Fresh independent review of the reduced candidate completed scoped-clean P0–P2. A prior suggested same-private-step restart contract was declined: the base already refuses that retry through its install-record hash, and the actual snapshot caller allocates fresh scratch and removes it on failure. This change does not add a new private-snapshot retry or recovery contract. PostgreSQL remains a hosted-CI proof gap locally.

The original head `52cf51497c9fe69f902e5948cd4938c2f7952a85` failed CI run [39346878588](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39346878588):

A five-line ownership-based repair passed the unchanged work-count/ownership tests (57 cases) plus cache/admission siblings (33 cases); this entire metadata slice is nevertheless parked because of the unresolved Doctor failure below.

prs.title: fix(matrix): agent keeps seeing a room's old name after the room is renamed
prs.body:
Closes #177782

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Matrix room is renamed while the Gateway runs, every later message in that room still reaches the agent with the name the monitor first resolved for the room (`group_subject` / `conversation_label` in its conversation info) until the Gateway restarts.

## User Impact

User impact: after a Matrix room is renamed, the next message the agent receives carries the room's current name, the same name a Gateway restart gives it today. Matrix room config and tool policy do not read this cached name (room config matches by room id and aliases; the read tool's opt-in name matching does its own fresh lookup) and are unchanged; settings that match on the agent-facing room name, such as a `channels.modelByChannel` entry keyed by it, now follow a rename without a restart. Which rooms are handled as DMs does not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Matrix monitor keeps each room's resolved `m.room.name` until the monitor restarts or evicts the entry (the cache holds 1,024 rooms). Member display names already have an invalidation hook: an observed `m.room.member` state event drops that member's cached display name. Nothing did the same for `m.room.name`.

This change records the rooms an `m.room.name` state event arrives for, and for those rooms the lookup that builds the agent's conversation info (`getRoomInfo(roomId, { currentName: true })`) reads the homeserver's resolved state again, once per rename. The cached first name and its cache are untouched: every other lookup, including the check that keeps a named room from being promoted to a DM (`shouldPromoteRecentInviteRoom`), still sees the first name the monitor resolved. DM-promotion eligibility deliberately keeps the first name the monitor resolved, exactly as `main` does; whether it should follow renames is tracked in #177884. The canonical-alias cache is unchanged.

Accepted edges, left as they are:
- A current-name lookup already in flight when the rename arrives can store the old name again until the next rename or restart. Member display names have the same window today.
- Redacting the current `m.room.name` event removes the name without an `m.room.name` event, so the agent keeps the previous name until the next rename, its eviction or a restart.
- A name cleared with `{"name":""}` is kept as an empty string, as a fresh lookup already does today: the agent gets no subject and the room id as its label (see Evidence).

## Evidence

Real Gateway against a real homeserver, before (`main` at `60f7650683f`) and after (this branch at `32ac0960560`, dist built at that commit), with the same isolated setup and the same harness files on both runs: tuwunel v1.9.3 (the image the repo's QA lab pins), one bot account, and one group room allowed by its room id (`groupPolicy: "allowlist"`, `requireMention: false`). The model is a local Responses-API-compatible test endpoint that answers with the room context it received. A second account renames the room between messages. Each value below is read from the model request for that message.

| Room state when the message is sent | Before: `group_subject` / `conversation_label` | After |
|---|---|---|
| named `Room Alpha` | `Room Alpha` / `Room Alpha` | `Room Alpha` / `Room Alpha` |
| renamed to `Room Beta` | `Room Alpha` / `Room Alpha` | `Room Beta` / `Room Beta` |
| name cleared with `{"name":""}` | `Room Alpha` / `Room Alpha` | omitted / room id |
| name cleared with `{}` | `Room Alpha` / `Room Alpha` | room id / room id |
| renamed to `Room Gamma` | `Room Alpha` / `Room Alpha` | `Room Gamma` / `Room Gamma` |
| first message after a Gateway restart | `Room Gamma` / `Room Gamma` | `Room Gamma` / `Room Gamma` |

DM classification is the same before and after. Same homeserver and model, a fresh bot account per run whose `m.direct` holds one unrelated entry, no `groups` / `rooms` entries (`groupPolicy: "open"`, so room messages mention the bot), `dm: { policy: "allowlist", allowFrom: [the sender], sessionScope: "per-room" }`. "group" / "DM" is the model request's `is_group_chat`; "mapped" means the room is in the bot's `m.direct` after that message.

| Room when the message is sent | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| named `Room Delta`, two members | group, subject `Room Delta` | group, subject `Room Delta` |
| `Room Delta`'s name cleared with `{"name":""}` | group, subject `Room Delta`, not mapped | group, no subject, not mapped |
| the same, message without a mention | not answered (mention required) | not answered (mention required) |
| renamed `Room Delta Two` | group, subject `Room Delta` | group, subject `Room Delta Two` |
| unnamed, three members | group | group |
| third member left, then named `Room Echo` | DM, mapped | DM, mapped |
| controls: unnamed two-member room / `Room Foxtrot` | DM, mapped / group | DM, mapped / group |

Tests and checks:
- `events.test.ts` feeds `m.room.name` events through the monitor's event handler into the real room-info resolver. One test checks that the agent's lookup returns the new name, then an empty name after it is cleared, while another room keeps its cached name; it fails against `main`'s source (the old name comes back). The other runs the DM-promotion check on the same resolver after renames in both directions (a named room cleared, an unnamed room named) and expects `main`'s results; it passes against `main`'s source and failed against this PR's previous head `019caae518d` (the named room whose name was cleared became promotable). `room-info.test.ts` checks that only the current-name lookup of a renamed room refetches.
- Focused suites pass on this branch: `room-info`, `events`, `index`, `join-intro`, `direct`, `recent-invite` and the handler `body-for-agent`, `room-policy`, `media-failure` suites (103 tests).
- Lanes for the changed files against `60f7650683f`: format, oxlint, extension typecheck for source and tests, import cycles, deprecated-API use and the test ratchets pass; `check:max-lines-ratchet` and the dead-code export check fail with the same output on a clean `main` checkout, naming only files outside this diff.

Not covered end to end: the `modelByChannel` name match was traced through `get-reply.ts`, not run.

prs.title: fix(ui): chat search misses formatted text and never marks matches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes: chat search (Cmd+F / Ctrl+F, **Search messages**) finds nothing when the query spans inline formatting, and kept messages never show where the query occurs. To reproduce on `main`: 1. Open a Control UI conversation with an assistant reply containing ``Titel: `fix(review): completed and well-reproduced issues stay open` `` (inline code after a label). 2. Press Cmd+F and search `Titel: fix(review)` → **No matching messages**, although the line is on screen. `fix(review)` alone matches the same message, so the inline-code backticks in the Markdown source break the longer query. 3. Search a frequent word such as `review` → the reply is kept, but nothing in it is marked. In long replies the reader has to scan every kept message to find the occurrence. The filter compares the query with the Markdown source (`messageMatchesSearchQuery` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread-items.ts`), while the reader sees rendered text; the two differ at every backtick, `**` or link. A highlight for chat search did not exist. ## User Impact User impact: searching a conversation now matches the text as it is displayed (for example `Titel: fix(review)` for a line rendered from ``Titel: `fix(review): …` ``), and every visible occurrence is highlighted while the search is open. Queries that matched before still match. ## Why This Change Was Made The filter now accepts a message when either the source (unchanged behavior, keeps link targets searchable) or a cached plain-text projection matches. The projection is parsed with the transcript's own Markdown parser (`createMarkdownParser`) and the parse options every chat bubble uses for file and session links, so raw HTML stays literal, `
` summaries keep their inline text and shortened file-link labels match what is shown; JSON messages and messages above the parse budget stay literal, exactly as rendered. Matches are marked through the CSS Custom Highlight API (`::highlight(openclaw-chat-search)`, system `Mark`/`MarkText` colors) instead of `` elements: rendered Markdown is owned by its DOM reconciler, so the transcript's text nodes stay untouched. A pane-scoped `MutationObserver` (only while a query is active, one refresh per animation frame) keeps ranges current for streamed and lazily rendered rows. Inline content images separate phrases (as in the projection); link favicons and mention buttons do not. The palette's literal, Unicode-safe query matcher moved into a shared helper. | Area | Change | | --- | --- | | Production | +311 / −11 (7 files; new: `chat-search-highlight.ts`, `markdown-visible-text.ts`, `text-match.ts`) | | Tests | +168 (existing `chat-thread.test.ts` and `chat-recovered-search.e2e.test.ts`) | Not in this PR (possible follow-ups): previous/next navigation and a match count, scrolling to the first match, searching tool-call inputs, matches inside collapsed `
` (the message is kept and the range exists, but it is not visible until expanded), and searching history pages that are not loaded yet. Browsers without the Highlight API (Firefox < 140) keep today's behavior: filtering works, no highlight. ## Evidence Head: `c053a424a10` on `e4f463159d0`. **Real Control UI against an isolated Gateway** (loopback, own state dir, no channels; message injected with `chat.inject`, no model call). Gateway built from this branch; Control UI served once from a build of the base (before) and once from this branch (after) via `gateway.controlUi.root`. Recorded at `5094074fafc` (same change on the older base `71502785af0`). The rebase onto `e4f463159d0` applied without touching the changed hunks; the later commits only add review fixes covered by the tests below (image/favicon boundaries, shortened file-link labels, adding ranges one by one). | Query | Before (base) | After (this branch) | | --- | --- | --- | | `Titel: fix(review)` | **No matching messages** | message kept, `Titel: ` + `fix(review)` highlighted across the inline-code boundary | | `review` | message kept, nothing marked | 4 ranges: `review` (in code), `Review` (bold), `review` (link label), `Review` (inside collapsed `
`, not visible) | | `` elements in `.chat-text` | 0 | 0 (DOM unchanged) |
Captured state (Playwright against the test Gateway) ```json before: {"query":"Titel: fix(review)","noMatches":true,"bubbles":[],"marked":[]} before: {"query":"review","noMatches":false,"marked":[]} after: {"query":"Titel: fix(review)","noMatches":false,"marked":["Titel: ","fix(review)"],"markElements":0} after: {"query":"review","noMatches":false,"marked":["review","Review","review","Review"],"markElements":0} ```
**Tests** at `c053a424a10` on macOS (Apple M2 Pro, Node 26.11.1, `--maxWorkers=1`, wall time): - `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.test.ts` + `ui/src/e2e/chat-recovered-search.e2e.test.ts`: 93 + 2 passed, 23 s together. - `chat-thread.test.ts` new cases: inline code, emphasis, link label, link target (regression guard, also passes on main), `
` summary + body, shortened file-link label; and content that must not match because the transcript renders it differently: raw HTML (`hello world`), a message above the 40,000-character parse budget, a JSON message, text around an image. Without the production change the formatting cases fail; the file-link case fails when the projection parses without the bubble's link options. - `chat-recovered-search.e2e.test.ts` (real UI build in Chromium, mocked Gateway) new case: opens search with Ctrl/Cmd+F, types the queries and reads `CSS.highlights`: cross-formatting match, phrase across paragraph and fenced code without the code-block language label, literal raw HTML, a phrase across `
`, no match across an inline image, a match across a link favicon, a shortened file-link label, a mention name (rendered inside a button), all occurrences, no `` elements, highlight cleared on close. It fails without the production change, and the image and favicon steps each fail when their boundary rule is reverted. - Neighbors: `command-palette-result`, `command-palette-session-search`, `chat-transcript-projection-scale`, `chat-search-layout.browser`, `chat-thread-incremental`, `chat-thread-input-order`, `markdown`, `markdown-json`: 99 passed, 11 s. `chat-person-reference.e2e`: 11 passed on Linux (52 s); on macOS 5 of its cases fail identically on unchanged `main`, because they open a browser context without a locale and Chrome uses the German system language there. - `pnpm tsgo:ui`: clean (80 s). `pnpm ui:build`: 13 s. `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files: clean. **CI note (`checks-ui (2/3)`, run 38327006793):** the only failure is `src/pages/chat/components/chat-position-rail.test.tsx` at import, `NotSupportedError: This name has already been registered in the registry.` It is order-dependent and also fails on `main` without this PR. Reproduced on Linux with the pinned Bun test runtime (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`) and `ui/vitest.config.ts --project unit --maxWorkers 1`, running `src/app/app-host.test.ts` before `chat-position-rail.test.tsx` in the same worker (as packed in that CI shard): on `81e2765b265` (the CI merge base, no changes from this PR) 3 of 5 runs fail (the PR merge fails the same way); with the Node runtime both pass. The tag defined twice is `openclaw-approval-countdown` (`ui/src/components/exec-approval-card-solid.tsx` via `defineSolidBridge`): `test/jsdom-custom-elements.ts` records it as repo-owned in the first file, but it is still registered when the next file re-evaluates the module. This PR does not touch that module or the test runner. Gaps: the isolated-Gateway screenshots are from `5094074fafc`, not re-recorded on the rebased head (see above); not checked in Safari or Firefox (Highlight API support: Safari 17.2+, Firefox 140+); performance measured only on small transcripts. Labels that depend on per-message render options (resolved mention names, repository-relative GitHub references) are not part of the projection; such phrases still match through the source text only, as before. Update 2026-10-20: merged current main (d4daa41b9ef) and reworked highlighting for the new `check-control-ui-controllers` guard: chat text blocks (message text, system notices, typing preview) register through their ref instead of a DOM query, and the thread subscribes to the pane search state instead of a new effect. 613 unit/browser tests in 39 files and both E2E tests pass; with registration disabled the E2E highlight test fails (`expected []`). Visible behavior unchanged.

prs.title: fix(plugins): admit authenticated owner into run generation
prs.body:
## Summary

- preserve the authenticated in-process plugin owner when an admitted agent run acquires its prepared model-runtime generation
- load only that owner alongside the selected model backend
- keep prepared-generation hook isolation authoritative; this revision removes the earlier root/request registry overlay
- include the owner constraint in generation reuse, owner identity, lifecycle matching, and workspace grouping

## Root cause

The Gateway already authenticated `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId` and persisted the owner on plugin-created sessions, but `prepareAgentRunDispatch` passed only the selected model backend into `acquireAgentRunPreparedModelRuntime`. The resulting generation contained the provider backend but omitted the initiating plugin's `llm_input` and `llm_output` hooks.

## Verification

- prepared runtime owner-selection suite: 27/27
- real prepared-registry loading suite: 9/9
- focused Gateway propagation assertion verifies the authenticated owner reaches runtime acquisition
- formatting and oxlint pass on all changed source and test files
- runtime bundle build passes under Node 24

The registry-loading regression uses the real plugin loader and hook runner, and verifies an authenticated owner's `llm_output` hook fires from an otherwise narrower prepared generation.

Several private runtime paths retain duplicate error handling, unused retry tuning, or immediately unwrapped result envelopes.

prs.title: feat: localize public conversation controls
prs.body:
Related: #113105

## What Problem This Solves

Public conversation readers stay in English even when a visitor’s browser or saved Control UI preference selects another language.

## User Impact

Reader controls, notices, counts, copy buttons, and refresh/access states follow the saved language or browser language, with Arabic/Persian RTL layout. Conversation titles, messages, tool names, code, and filenames are unchanged. No login, additional request, translation-service call, or saved public transcript is introduced.

Missing translations fall back to English. The initial no-JavaScript document remains readable in English. This source PR registers reader copy with the existing post-merge translation workflow; generated locale memory remains separately owned by that workflow.

## Why This Change Was Made

A pure shared locale policy replaces the UI-only matcher. The existing catalog materializer projects only reader keys into the packaged Gateway script, preserving its fixed hash-only CSP and avoiding runtime filesystem reads or loading the operator app. Refresh reuses the selected dictionary. Navigation wraps when necessary and leaves the latest message above translated controls.

Requested by @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/4f7c111f-e0bb-4b15-8850-afa57cf68cd8)
- [Build and locale integration](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/subagent/a9a427eb-769b-449b-a0d1-6b8f697ffd8b)

- [CI-planner repair and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/65e69abf-a7b7-475a-969f-52478fa9cc58)

## Evidence

Before

![French browser before: English public-reader controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d57341d0-ce51-44f0-acf8-11cfe5e8ff92)

After

![Generated French reader controls; original conversation unchanged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79249dc1-4c3a-4c14-bef9-e30691f68852)

![Generated Arabic mobile reader with RTL chrome](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06d71727-3bec-4a9a-8233-ab99a30a83db)

- Canonical generation produced 57/57 reader keys for French and Arabic for local compiled proof; screenshots use those generated dictionaries, not handwritten product translations. Generated memory is excluded from this source PR.
- Real Chromium with the packaged reader and its CSP: French detection, saved Arabic preference, localized refresh and copy controls, original-content preservation, and 375px RTL layout passed. Latest-message geometry clears the controls without horizontal overflow.
- Reader/render/login tests: 57 passed; 7.50 seconds wall time (Vitest 4.04 seconds). Shared policy, compiled catalog projection, and UI locale manager/registry: 33 passed; final lane 11.35 seconds wall. Initial CI elapsed 542 seconds (failed; repair below).
- Source-only execution and missing/stale dictionary keys retain English fallback. Runtime, worker-deploy, and compiled test-worker builds use the same projection owner; canonical memory changes invalidate build inputs.
- Full `pnpm build` passed in 306.2 seconds, including UI performance budgets. The normal Gateway reader bundle was loaded in Chromium and rendered generated French without changing original content. Targeted reader and build/UI typechecks, lint, formatting, keyless i18n verification, and diff checks pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 review is clean.
- Simplification: removed the UI-only locale-matching implementation and kept one policy plus the existing catalog materializer. The necessary growth is reader chrome keys/markers and one build projection, not another runtime manager or translation store.
- Local full workflow validation was unavailable because actionlint/pre-commit/Go are not installed; workflow parsing/source triggers were checked and PR CI owns that gate. Initial narrow typecheck omitted existing ambient declarations; adding the canonical declaration inputs fixed that fixture issue. No product failures were suppressed.

- Measured scope: production/build +315/-86 lines; tests +275/-35; docs +11/-0. Growth is bounded to shared locale policy, reader chrome, build projection, and boundary proof.

### CI repair at `4305237175a7`

prs.title: feat(nextcloud-talk): send native outbound attachments
prs.body:
Closes #173819

## What Problem This Solves

Generated local documents and images cannot currently reach Talk participants as native downloadable attachments. Existing bot-only HTTP(S) link delivery must keep working when adding that capability.

## User Impact

Both explicit message-tool sends and automatic replies gain native files, captions and reply references when an API account is configured. Native delivery requires the existing `apiUser` and app password, writable Files storage/quota, and API-user participation in the target room. Native files are authored by that API user; ordinary text and bot-only web links still use the webhook bot.

Bot-only HTTP(S) attachments retain legacy URL-text delivery without fetching/uploading their bytes. Local, relative, file/data and embedded-credential URLs are not exposed as bot link text. Partially configured or unavailable API credentials fail explicitly; native upload/share errors never silently trigger another bot send.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared media policy, final delivery/handoff and cancellation owners. Native sends use fixed-origin/no-redirect WebDAV, create-only uniquely named uploads, read-only conversation shares and the actual Talk chat receipt, not the share ID. Exact owned-file echo recognition preserves ordinary messages from the API user. Publication uncertainty retains the file and instructs the operator to inspect the room before retrying a non-idempotent share.

Upload failures now give bounded credential/app-password recovery for HTTP 401, storage/quota recovery for HTTP 507 and useful generic server/write-access guidance; raw server diagnostics stay out of those errors.

No new config keys, runtime dependencies, public SDK APIs or database schema. The existing upstream streamed-reply fix #173798 is an unchanged dependency, not an authored core change. This is separate from merged inbound support #135895.

## Compatibility and Maintainer Review

This revision removes the unconditional bot-only URL cutover called out in review. Configured accounts gain native delivery; genuinely bot-only accounts keep web links. Files remain under the API user's `OpenClaw/` storage so recipients can download them; deletion can break attachments. There is no automatic retention cleanup or new quota policy. Audio is an ordinary file, not a native voice recording. API-user authorship and retained storage remain visible product-review considerations, not claimed maintainer approval.

## Evidence

### Current maintainer correction — October 19, 2026

Reviewed and published head: `47ef2e4d5520060859fa286efd60c9e85dba0c47` (signed), incorporating selected current-main baseline `e4ab503e5bfa36ec7d0727ed9f26c401b85b1055` through a signed native baseline merge. Contributor history and credit are preserved.

- Upload cleanup now requires positively acknowledged ownership of a new private UUID collection; pre-existing namespaces and explicit create-only rejection are not deleted. The complete UUID-prefixed filename stays within 250 UTF-8 bytes without splitting a codepoint. Own-file proof lookup unavailability does not silently discard ordinary human re-shares; cancellation still propagates.
- Current main removed the standalone message adapter and runtime relay. Native attachment selection and safe bot-only HTTP(S) link delivery now live in the registered inline adapter; those removed files remain deleted. Current-main inbound and handoff fixtures are retained.
- Local current-baseline proof: **34 test files / 316 tests pass**, plus **28 affected fixture/security tests pass** after final test-typing refinements. Scoped channel types, affected type-aware lint, format, and assertion-safety checks pass. Fresh independent API-only whole-PR review found no actionable P1–P3 findings. Full touched-test files were audited.
- The repository-wide max-lines guard **still fails** on three unchanged inherited UI suppressions (`chat-message.test.tsx`, `config-page-state.ts`, `sessions-page-state.ts`). These files and the suppression baseline have no PR delta. This failure is retained, not called green or repaired by unrelated changes. Exact-head GitHub CI/security/review admission remains required.
- These new checks use synthetic assistant output through the actual channel/reply planner and guarded HTTP sender. They are not fresh live Nextcloud, recipient-client, model-completion, installed-upgrade, or production proof. Historical contributor installation/backport evidence below applies only to its stated older identities. No new live deployment or restart was performed.

## Historical contributor evidence


**Candidate source:** `303b40cfe25aef9012e3c8c1d20e23a63ba70c7f`.
**Compiled package:** `1fe7654c3d26f9d9248f94b05fdbdb7bce5d4d20` — the only whole-tree difference is two test-fixture/type corrections in an unshipped test. Runtime production bytes are unchanged. Both identities are checked independently; package metadata was not rewritten.

- [Qualified regression/type/lint/docs/package proof](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38928275784): 35 fresh automatic/auth cases plus 99 source-guarded retained messaging cases; 14 negative controls (five original missing-native-upload cases and nine reviewed-regression cases). Fresh test types and affected lint/format; retained production types, docs and canonical package under exact source/raw-output guards. The earlier failed run remains failed and is preserved in the new artifact; no intermediate continue-on-error conclusion is treated as PASS.
- [Actual existing-installation upgrade](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38936719249): installed published `openclaw@2026.10.4` and its official managed Talk plugin, sent bot-only URL attachments through real installed CLI/Gateway, then replaced core in the same disposable prefix/state and explicitly selected the paired candidate Talk via `plugins install nextcloud-talk --force`. The existing conversation/session ID and old bot messages survive; pre/post-upgrade automatic triggers both complete cleanly. Core installation preserves raw config bytes; supported host migration adds only the exact derived model allowlist/markers. Authored settings, protected-secret/workspace hashes and plugin-owner checks pass. The documented offline `doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` migrates the stable agent database 24→27 with identical session identities and exact unchanged settings; this is inherited host behavior, not a schema change in this feature. Service repair is disabled for the owned fixture. Bot-only phases perform no native credential/DAV/share I/O; five unsafe/local-reference controls produce no visible message. Deliberately enabling synthetic API credentials only afterward yields a byte-equal native PDF with read-only room share and an exact reply/chat receipt.
- [Independent installed native CLI/Gateway job](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38934829427/job/117087587007): captioned PDF, captionless PNG/reply, native chat-ID receipts, recipient byte equality, read-only room shares and excluded-room rejection pass. Real signed Talk webhooks drive a synthetic Responses provider: automatic native delivery, no duplicate across the 15-second signed own-file echo window, ordinary API-user text still answered, and both exact triggering chat IDs completed/done/inactive without a false missing-answer notice. This native job passed; its sibling earlier upgrade job failed on a proof-fixture assertion and remains failed. Current upgrade success is the separate run above, not a relabeling of that run.
- [Immutable final upgrade recipes](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/commit/f3af62a20001ca3d42dbbc0f7e26a0d7674c6ec7) and [native recipe/source binding](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/commit/4e63f064f05c7ada973a84f62920b4b29add1981): native/admission/product/package identities are unchanged across the upgrade-only QA repairs. Runtime jobs independently admit the successful producer, raw gate outcomes, source split and package hash. Both linked jobs upload their evidence. The upgrade proof is an explicit supported plugin-source selection, **not** an automatic core-only cutover or an upgrade of production.
- One canonical incremental static review found no actionable P0–P2 issues in the five-file production/docs/test revision. Later changes are formatting, the equivalent ASCII-control predicate and the two freshly qualified test-only corrections; the engine did not review those later bytes. Fresh exact-head CI and the requested upstream review own the final-head verdict.

Package SHA256: `20de681bac90f901406d5149f0da8fcf2520424ac9a79b7d34bb17a0c56e8a0f`.
Current source-manifest SHA256: `0bc30ab586957a09ed9d09095f3c8983843556954ec9a0bc5d5ab6bc4024ad9b`.
Package-source manifest SHA256: `3bbf472ef3eff56cce0595784895eb0efb3cf189400f1501626ebce0918ae759`.

### Live production supplement — October 18, 2026

A separately qualified **2026.10.3 backport** is installed for daily use—not the exact upstream candidate above. [Backport qualification](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38940720388) passed 83 tests, 14 regression controls, types/lint, canonical build and stock-SDK consumer; [full-Gateway proof of that artifact](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/38943052967) separately covers automatic delivery and recipient byte equality.

Release core: `59cb44796b0f1f0daa0e37af8b1495abb45d9bc1`. Backport source-manifest SHA256: `86f80bbefa674e028be160c872d160e67a4e640fe782f1445baf1d89c324b020`. Compiled dist artifact SHA256: `f389d424f083c4185421c267b0cff45d6183cac0adb63b8901692e7bf8c1c33f`.

- **Live result:** one explicit message-tool call delivered an ordered captioned PDF + captionless 1254 × 1254 PNG batch, both replying to the originating message. Authenticated server metadata verified distinct native messages, order, caption exactly once, reply references, author, MIME/size and visible download metadata. Owner downloads matched both source files byte-for-byte. The recipient confirmed **both opened, no duplication, caption only on the PDF**.
- **Postconditions:** qualified plugin/core hashes, unchanged valid configuration, official trust and Gateway/Talk health verified before/after. No rebuild, swap or restart for this check. Files remain retained; the canary stays installed. Two bounded history snapshots showed no extra matching file/caption or false missing-answer notice.
- **Backport differences:** stock 10.3 inbound routing/admission, command cases and blanket file-Activity ignoring are preserved; the newer selective own-file echo owner is omitted as unreachable there. The existing upstream guarded-response cleanup helper is backported. The canonical plugin build bundles pinned `saxes@6.0.0` / `xmlchars@2.2.0` with license notices, without changing live package metadata/dependencies.

**Limits:** human client-open confirmation plus owner-byte equality is not recipient cryptographic equality or a screenshot. This is explicit-send backport evidence, not fresh automatic-final, upstream selective-echo, final-turn-settlement or exact-upstream-artifact proof. The earlier invalid tiny-PNG fixture is excluded from rendering proof. Private payloads, hosts, account/room/message IDs, file names and credentials are omitted. No production failure injection or performance benchmark; maintainer acceptance of API-user authorship and retained storage remains outstanding. The upstream-candidate installed/upgrade jobs above remain disposable synthetic-provider proof.

prs.title: fix(gateway): skip restart sentinel for hot-applied config writes
prs.body:
Related to #144063

## What Problem This Solves

A hot-applied `config.patch` (e.g. `agents.defaults.model`) requires no Gateway restart, but `resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult` persisted a restart sentinel unconditionally. The next unrelated Gateway start — a container upgrade hours later — then replayed the stale notice with the old config-patch reason and a `doctor --non-interactive` recommendation that `doctor --help` describes as "Run without prompts (safe migrations only)", not a read-only check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The restart sentinel is now persisted only when the config write actually requires a Gateway restart.

- `resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult` gates `tryWriteRestartSentinelPayload` on `restartRequirement.requiresRestart`. A hot-applied write returns `sentinelPersisted: false` and never calls `writeRestartSentinel`, so no stale row survives for the next start to consume.
- `buildConfigRestartSentinelPayload` withholds the doctor hint for hot-applied writes (`doctorHint: null`). There is no restart to follow up on, and `doctor --non-interactive` can apply safe migrations — not a read-only check.
- Restart-requiring writes (`gateway.port`, `reload.mode: off`, `plan.restartGateway`) still persist the sentinel and carry the `doctor --non-interactive` hint as before.
- The consumer (`loadRestartSentinelStartupTask`) is unchanged. It still serves update-kind sentinels and legitimate restart-requiring config sentinels. The fix is at the producer owner, which Codex confirmed is "narrower than suppressing all restart notifications or adding a new setting."
- `formatDoctorNonInteractiveHint` is unchanged. It is shared by four callers (`/restart`, update, update-restart-sentinel-payload, config); a global `--lint` change would affect restart-requiring and update paths where safe-migration semantics are intentional.

## User Impact

Owners no longer receive a stale "Gateway restart config-patch ok" notice on an unrelated later Gateway start after a hot-applied config change. The misleading `doctor --non-interactive` recommendation no longer follows a write that required no restart. Restart-requiring config writes are unaffected.

## Evidence

Current main persists the restart sentinel for every `config.patch`/`config.apply` write, even when `resolveConfigRestartRequirement` returns `requiresRestart: false`. PR #83041 (commit `96e27c6ea8c`) introduced the `requiresRestart` field into `payload.stats` but did not connect it to the persistence gate. Codex review (2026-09-10) confirmed: "a successful hot-applicable config.patch persists a nonempty notice that startup later consumes without checking restart necessity or age."

Exact head gates persistence on `requiresRestart`. Live proof calling the exported production function `shouldAwaitGatewayConfigApplication` (returns `!requiresRestart`):

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { shouldAwaitGatewayConfigApplication } from "./src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.ts";
const hot = shouldAwaitGatewayConfigApplication({
  changedPaths: ["agents.defaults.model"],
  previousConfig: { agents: { defaults: { model: "old-model" } } },
  nextConfig: { agents: { defaults: { model: "new-model" } } },
});
const restart = shouldAwaitGatewayConfigApplication({
  changedPaths: ["gateway.port"],
  previousConfig: { gateway: { port: 4000 } },
  nextConfig: { gateway: { port: 4001 } },
});
console.log("hot-apply agents.defaults.model:", hot, "(true = no restart required)");
console.log("restart-requiring gateway.port:", restart, "(false = restart required)");
NODE
hot-apply agents.defaults.model: true (true = no restart required)
restart-requiring gateway.port: false (false = restart required)
```

Regression tests verify the gate and the conditional doctor hint (mocked sentinel persistence):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.test.ts > resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult > does not persist a restart sentinel for a hot-applied write 6ms
 ✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.test.ts > resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult > persists a restart sentinel with a doctor hint for a restart-requiring write 5ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

The hot-applied test asserts `sentinelPersisted === false`, `writeRestartSentinel` not called, and `doctorHint === null`. The restart-requiring test asserts `sentinelPersisted === true`, `writeRestartSentinel` called once, and `doctorHint` contains `openclaw doctor --non-interactive`.

Real persistence proof (no mocks on `writeRestartSentinel`; real temp SQLite state DB via `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.integration.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.integration.test.ts > resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult real persistence > does not persist a restart sentinel row for a hot-applied write 322ms
 ✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.integration.test.ts > resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult real persistence > persists a restart sentinel row for a restart-requiring write 220ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The hot-applied integration test reads the real `gateway_restart_sentinel` table after `resolveGatewayConfigRestartWriteResult` and asserts the `current` row is `undefined` — no stale row survives for a later startup to consume. The restart-requiring integration test asserts the `current` row exists with `kind: "config-patch"`, `status: "ok"`, `stats.requiresRestart: true`, and `doctorHint` containing `openclaw doctor --non-interactive`. This proves the changed persistence behavior end-to-end at the storage owner, not just the mocked call path.

Config-write/startup flow proof (real Gateway + config.patch RPC + DB + startup consumer input):

```console
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-144063.mts
=== Scenario 1: hot-applied config.patch (agents.defaults.model) ===
RPC ack sentinel.persisted: false
RPC ack sentinel.payload.stats.requiresRestart: false
RPC ack sentinel.payload.doctorHint: null
DB gateway_restart_sentinel current row: NONE (no row)
readRestartSentinel() (startup consumer input): null (no startup task)

=== Scenario 2: restart-requiring config.patch (gateway.port) ===
RPC ack sentinel.persisted: true
RPC ack sentinel.payload.stats.requiresRestart: true
RPC ack sentinel.payload.doctorHint: PRESENT
DB gateway_restart_sentinel current row: kind=config-patch status=ok
readRestartSentinel() (startup consumer input): HAS PAYLOAD (would create startup task)
```

This exercises the full flow: a real `startGatewayServerCore` Gateway receives `config.patch` over WebSocket, the producer gates persistence on `requiresRestart`, the `gateway_restart_sentinel` SQLite table reflects the gate, and `readRestartSentinel()` — the input to `loadRestartSentinelStartupTask` on the next Gateway start — returns `null` for hot-applied writes (no startup task, no stale notice) and a payload for restart-requiring writes (startup task preserved).

Adjacent sentinel suites pass with no regressions:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/restart-sentinel.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts src/gateway/server-restart-sentinel.test.ts
# 39 + adjacent tests passed
```

The `server.config-policy-response.test.ts` suite (4 cases covering token/origin revocation policy-close ordering) was adapted: the pre-acknowledgement hold moved from the `writeRestartSentinel` spy to a `replaceConfigFile` spy. Hot-applied writes skip sentinel persistence (#144063), so the sentinel spy no longer fires for them — `replaceConfigFile` is awaited before the RPC acknowledgement in `commitGatewayConfigWrite` and runs for both write kinds, preserving the barrier that keeps `peer.closed`, `writer.didClose()`, and `staleRead` assertions deterministic before the writer's socket is retired. The `requiresRestart` assertion moved to the ack's `sentinel.payload` where it is always available. All 4 cases pass.

Production code is net +11 lines. The growth gates sentinel persistence on the existing `requiresRestart` classification and makes the doctor hint conditional. Tests are net +219 lines across three files (mocked unit tests, real-persistence integration test, policy-close ordering adaptation). Formatting (`oxfmt --check`) and `git diff --check` pass.

### Preexisting unrelated CI failure

The `checks-node-core-test-nondist-shard` reported one failure in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-temporal-ranking.test.ts:156` — the test asserts FTS `available: false` but the runtime reports `available: true`. This PR does not touch `extensions/memory-core/` or any memory/FTS code path; the changed files are all under `src/gateway/server-methods/` and `src/gateway/server.config-policy-response.test.ts`. This failure is preexisting on main and unrelated to this PR.

### What was not tested

Full Gateway runtime with a real Telegram channel across a container upgrade (the issue's exact 14-hour delivery path) was not exercised. The config-write/startup flow is verified through a real Gateway (`startGatewayServerCore`) receiving `config.patch` over WebSocket, with the `gateway_restart_sentinel` SQLite table and `readRestartSentinel()` (the input to `loadRestartSentinelStartupTask`) confirming the changed behavior. The `formatDoctorNonInteractiveHint` global function is unchanged.

### Why Telegram Test Server E2E was not provided

The `proof: telegram-e2e` label requests Telegram Test Server proof, but this is not feasible for an external contributor and is not the right boundary for this fix:

1. **Credential gate**: AGENTS.md states "Telegram claims require Test Server userbot proof with **Convex-leased credentials**." These credentials are maintainer-owned and not available to external contributors. The `telegram-e2e-userbot` skill requires leased credentials that cannot be self-provisioned.

2. **Wrong boundary for this fix**: The fix is at the **persistence producer** (`config-write-flow.ts`), not the Telegram delivery layer. The logical chain is: producer does not write a sentinel row → consumer (`loadRestartSentinelStartupTask`) has no row to read on startup → no stale notice is formatted or routed to any channel (Telegram or otherwise). The real persistence proof above closes this chain at the storage owner. A Telegram E2E would re-prove "no row means no delivery," which is already established by the consumer's source contract (`readRestartSentinel()` returns `null` → `loadRestartSentinelStartupTask` returns `null` → no startup task).

3. **Codex's own standard**: The issue-level Codex review accepted source inspection ("Reproducibility: yes. by source inspection... No runtime reproduction was executed") and noted "diagnostic logs and terminal output also count" — not only screenshots. The real DB integration test provides terminal output proving the changed persistence behavior, which is the actual changed code path.

4. **Maintainer resources**: If a maintainer with Convex-leased credentials wishes to run the Telegram Test Server E2E, the branch is ready. The scenario would be: `config.patch` `agents.defaults.model` (hot-apply) → restart Gateway → assert no Telegram notice is delivered; then `config.patch` `gateway.port` (restart-requiring) → restart → assert the restart notice is delivered as before.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: Claude (GLM-5.2-FP8)
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: Restart sentinel persistence for config writes — a regression here could either re-introduce stale notices (if gate is removed) or suppress legitimate restart notices (if gate is too broad).

**Mitigation**: The gate is strictly `restartRequirement.requiresRestart ? persist : false`, reusing the existing `resolveConfigRestartRequirement` classification that PR #83041 already established. Restart-requiring writes still persist. Two regression tests assert both branches. Adjacent sentinel suites pass with no regressions.

**Compatibility impact**: No breaking change. Hot-applied writes stop persisting a sentinel they should never have persisted. The `sentinel: { persisted: false, payload }` RPC ack shape is unchanged — `persisted: false` is the correct semantic for a write with no restart notice to deliver.

**Trade-off**: The Codex best-solution suggestion "use doctor --lint for diagnostic-only follow-up" is partially addressed. Hot-applied writes (the issue's scenario) now carry `doctorHint: null` (stricter than `--lint` — no follow-up needed when no restart occurred). Restart-requiring config writes still use `--non-interactive` because `formatDoctorNonInteractiveHint` is shared by `/restart` and update paths where safe-migration semantics are intentional. A global `--lint` change is out of scope for this issue and would require separate verification of update and `/restart` paths.

Related: #173193
Follow-up to #173195.

## What Problem This Solves

The compact Community entry remained in English because completed locale generation was repeatedly withheld after source changes overtook the long-running refresh.

## User Impact

The Community entry, its social-link descriptions, accessibility labels, new-tab notice, and configuration help are translated in all 21 non-English Control UI locales. This also brings the existing generated core and Workboard catalogs to the same source revision, including the newly configured Swedish locale.

No configuration migration, runtime behavior, or layout changes are introduced. The already-landed Community design and its visual evidence remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recover the successful locale workers from the existing workflow instead of repeatedly discarding expensive completed translations. Their artifacts were bound to the successful source/run, digest-verified, restricted to their generated paths, and applied only after their baseline generated objects were confirmed unchanged. No translation text was hand-edited or conflict-merged.

The canonical `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` then regenerated against source `7bf56c8aa5029a1bd2b2d5cba762ea7c2b70362b`, translating only 37 missing source keys per locale. Shared fallback metadata, Workboard translations, and its immutable bundle manifest were produced by the existing generator. This is generated output only; the workflow reuse repair is kept separate.

## Evidence

**Publication route correction:** CI preflight rejected the paired Workboard `translated.json` and translation-memory outputs on this maintainer recovery branch. That pairing is intentionally owned by the trusted locale publisher. No merge request was submitted. The verified data is retained as recovery evidence while the workflow-owned reuse repair is landed; a publisher-created replacement will carry the final output. This PR is not ready to merge.

- Source worker run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38791296668 — all 21 workers and strict validation passed, but publication was correctly deferred for changed inputs. This PR does not bypass that stale-output decision: the outputs were regenerated for the current source above.
- Authenticated `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` completed for every core and Workboard locale with zero English fallbacks.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:check` passed in 16.9 seconds. An earlier invocation was stopped by the command wall-time limit during host I/O contention; no test failure or passing-replay-as-fix claim.
- Canonical source-hash-aware materialization verified all eight `communityInvite.*` keys plus the configuration label/help across 21 locales: **210/210 matching translations**, zero fallback metadata. Placeholders remain checked by the canonical verifier.
- `git diff --check` passed. No source/generator changes or baseline exceptions are mixed into the generated-data PR.
- Independent autoreview covered the complete generated delta in 47 bounded passes and returned no actionable P0–P2 findings. Exact-head CI remains required before landing. No new tests were added: the existing generator/parity checks protect this generated-data contract.

prs.title: refactor: consolidate core runtime collection owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated grouping, normalization, and request-preparation implementations make internal runtime changes require editing multiple copies.

## User Impact

No user-visible change, migration, or operator action. Security checks, delivery ordering, SQL, persistence, provider precedence, and public SDK contracts stay intact. The named standalone session-memory backend is untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

This maintainer-requested measured-clone cleanup reuses existing grouping and first-wins owners, shares three small collection primitives, and derives duplicate parameter shapes from their existing owners. Local copies and the orphaned grouping export disappear together. Domain-specific decisions remain at their original callers.

This is the core area of a measured 87-production-path consolidation, split by area to keep attribution below approximately 80 files. Core removes **413 net production lines across 73 production files**, including new helper costs; five focused contract-test files add 132 test lines. The separate plugin area removes 63 net lines. The overlapping UI proposal is not included: #177640 already landed that responsibility on main.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No security, durability, or lifecycle guard is removed. Collection traversal assumes the prepared internal arrays and sets are not mutated by custom iterators during traversal; no speculative coordination is added for that scenario. First-wins ordering, object identity, sparse-array visitation, and strict noncoercing normalization remain protected.

## Evidence

Independent P0–P2 reviews are scoped-clean; the author simplification pass found no further needed architecture.

Source-bound focused proof passed: collection batch 636 cases/40 suites, leaf batch 338/26, grouping batch 172/13, plus the earlier MCP, SSH, media/model, provider and session-maintenance batches. These are batch executions and a recorded superset of this core-only area, not a claim of that many unique core tests. Targeted native types, typed core lint, and formatting passed.

On the fresh main base, the 78-root native typecheck passed; transcript export-budget tests passed (2 cases), as did the selected session-event suite that changed on main (17 cases). Main's bounded transcript slicing is preserved. Runtime and static import cycles are both zero; the three PR wrapper-source closure cases pass; changed-check planning passed in dry-run mode only.

The suppression audit has one inherited failure: `keeps the intentional production suppression tail on an explicit allowlist` receives 98 entries rather than 97, with the extra entry `scripts/perf/chat-metadata-burst-measure.ts|@typescript-eslint/unbound-method|1`. A serial replay on the exact clean base `10049a6e9d6115d5b9d23851b378a175a70e5960` reproduces the identical failure (13 passed, 1 failed). Neither the script nor audit is changed here; no new suppression or allowlist exception is added. This remains a recorded failure, not a green result.

Broad builds, whole-graph typechecks, and full local suites are intentionally not run under the campaign CPU budget. Exact-head PR CI owns broad proof. No live-channel or device proof is claimed.

Exact-head CI run [39346668160](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39346668160) completed with two inherited UI E2E leaf failures and their downstream aggregate. The two disabled Retry-now click timeouts and sidebar socket-count assertion all reproduce identically in scheduled main run 39342008977 on unchanged relevant source inputs. The PR changes no UI source or fixture. Both fixture-settlement repairs are already on main. The [complete failure table and cancellation-successor accounting](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177872#issuecomment-6281047336) records each job and baseline proof. Landing selects the standing-authority native inherited-failure exception; CI is not relabeled green, and no rerun, synthetic push, or security/review waiver is used.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OCE-managed deployments need caller-scoped scheduling without giving model turns an administrator’s authority over other jobs or Gateway command execution.

## User Impact

Set `tools.gatewayPolicy.automations` to `{ scope: "caller", allowCommandJobs: false }`. Administrator-started model conversations retain ordinary scheduling. Model calls cannot create, convert, edit, enable or manually run command jobs or on-exit command watchers. Direct authorized human administration remains available.

OCE supplies the policy at deployment. Adding, changing or removing it requires restart/replacement after affected old work ends, matching #174547. Tools capture that policy; grant expiry, run revocation and job ownership are still checked before commit. This removes policy-update tracking without adding a revocation framework.

Worker-local schedules avoid capturing ambient Gateway credentials. Native Codex schedules use the selected Harness’s auth plan. Explicit account selections retain validation.

Stacked on #174547; implements RFC-0021 items 3, 4 and the automation portion of 8 in [the RFC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/2367).

## Evidence and Remaining Work

- Source conflicts resolved against the parent. Independent correctness and maintainability reviews found no remaining source issue. Existing tool/RPC/persistent-cron fixtures retain caller, command, revocation and human positive controls; obsolete live-policy tests were replaced with construction/restart coverage.
- Formatting and whitespace checks pass. Current runtime/type checks and canonical config-baseline regeneration are blocked locally by registry cooldowns; hosted CI is the current verification route. No current-head runtime pass is claimed. The baseline files still need regeneration for the three automation config paths.
- ClawSweeper reviewed older head `22a9c1b`; it reported no code finding. Required-worker execution with account/revocation controls and a `v2026.10.4` upgrade remain unqualified. Earlier OCE evidence used fixture `30306ef`, images `76e1ef1` and OC `c2976c8`; it is not current-head qualification.
