prs.title: fix(agents): detect sustained same-target write churn
prs.body:
Related: #122577

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent can repeatedly overwrite one file with different successful contents while never producing a final response. Because every write has different arguments and reports `changed: true`, current loop detection treats the sequence as ordinary progress indefinitely.

This PR proposes a conservative behavioral boundary for maintainer review. The issue is currently marked as requiring a product decision; this PR does not claim that decision has already been made.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change keeps successful writes classified as real mutations and adds a separate, warning-first run-liveness signal for a contiguous tail of content-changing writes to one resolved target. Target identity excludes document content and is stored only as a hash.

The existing loop warning threshold is reused. The warned write remains allowed. Continuity clears when the run changes tools (including read/verification), changes targets, repeats an earlier argument variant, or completes/replaces its lifecycle. If churn remains continuous through the existing stale-run boundary, owner-bound recovery can abort only that run whether or not follow-up work is queued.

The behavior is limited to the built-in `write` result contract (`details.changed === true`). It is not tied to a provider, model, transport, channel, or reported private document. No new configuration or default surface is added.

## Batch and Liveness Semantics

A whole assistant batch is admitted before its calls have outcomes. This revision therefore keeps warning and liveness behavior aligned at both lifecycle boundaries:

- successful write-mutation liveness stays inactive below the shared warning threshold;
- a sequential batch emits the same run-scoped warning before the threshold-crossing write implementation starts;
- a post-outcome fallback covers parallel or out-of-order batch completions;
- the shared warning bucket prevents duplicate pre- and post-outcome warnings;
- the existing stable no-progress classifier still includes the just-recorded outcome and activates on its original boundary.

## Scope

The write-churn changes remain in the agent loop owner. A separate memory-core test commit stabilizes the unrelated provenance-repair assertion that failed hosted CI: it holds the detached repair open while asserting that automatic candidates remain hidden, then releases and verifies the repaired result. The test moved into the existing candidate-repair suite to satisfy the line-cap ratchet. No memory-core production behavior changed.

A subsequent agent fix resets the reverse write-variant scan at the newer occurrence of a repeated variant, retaining only post-repeat writes. A replacement regression uses actual `changed: true` outcomes at the shared warning threshold and verifies that a fresh post-repeat streak can warn again.

## User Impact

Runaway same-file rewrite sequences become bounded without immediately blocking normal edits. Short rewrite sequences, multi-file work, write/read/write verification, repeated identical content, and successful writes outside the sustained same-target pattern retain their existing behavior. The latest file state and session remain available after recovery.

## Policy Status

ClawSweeper marked #122577 as requiring a maintainer product decision and disabled automated fix-PR queueing. This PR implements one conservative proposal for review; it does not claim that maintainers have approved the warning, escape, or recovery boundary. It is ready for maintainer review of that decision, but does not claim approval or merge readiness.

## Evidence

Behavioral incident baseline: `v2026.7.2-beta.7` (`dabe1915362e20c25704af91612a32a8f4c96e83`). The beta is provenance only; the patch and tests are bound to the recorded branch head and integrated base below, not an unqualified current-main merge.

Negative controls observed before their fixes:

```text
same-target detector: expected warning, received { stuck: false }
below-threshold liveness: active=true after the second distinct changed write
embedded sequential batch: 11 successful writes, warning event list empty
stable no-progress boundary: sixth completed outcome still reported active=false
default-parallel batch: warning emitted, first churn lease remained absent
loop detection omitted/disabled: changed-write churn emitted a warning
CI dependency scan: three internal helpers were exported but unused
```

## Current revision and verification

Head: `f72242e6faf82f8608abd704b16d868d8a034ada`. The branch's integrated main merge-base remains `d45155d6c51169ac10890445418a9144395d1697`; it has not been integrated with current main.

- Revision 34's staged-write-target lifecycle P2 is fixed in the shared wrapper settlement `finally`, with run-scoped cleanup on success, errors, late cancellation, source-guard refusal and disposal. Batch final-target precedence is retained. The follow-up adds three production lines and +132 net test lines across two files.
- Five regressions failed on the preceding wrapper and passed after the fix. At this exact clean head, the focused detector, warning, write-target, admission and real-Agent sequential/default-parallel suites passed 169 distinct tests across five files. This is native wrapper/Agent lifecycle evidence, not a current-head Gateway recovery proof.
- Production `tsgo:core`, the canonical `core-test-agents-root` compiler graph, focused type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet and whitespace checks passed. The changed-graph selector stopped on the pre-existing 721-root/advisory-720 budget check; no config or test inventory changed, and the named graph was compiled separately. No full all-graph check claim.
- Independent read-only review found no actionable defect in the lifecycle fix. The full branch surface against its integrated base is source +475 and tests +1503 across 23 files; the added production state remains limited to target-aware detection, batch reconciliation and existing liveness ownership.
- Prior-head hosted CI failed one subagent-registry shard at `subagent-registry.test.ts:5160`, with dependent failure/cancellations; this unrelated failure was not repaired. Local passes are not a new-head hosted-CI pass.
- A merge-tree against main `3f12395208355949832da16c882e83cc5726c560` reports ten conflicting paths. Integration remains explicitly unqualified.

[The final follow-up comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122631#issuecomment-5974613163) contains the exact commands, checked-in proof links and captured terminal excerpts. No new isolated-Gateway result is claimed.

### Historical isolated Gateway proof (`27b24258c8`)

The real gateway, authenticated loopback agent RPC, embedded runner, built-in write/read tools, diagnostic heartbeat, and owner-bound recovery were exercised using a deterministic loopback model transport. No outbound-channel delivery or live-provider claim.

```text
canonical warning: argument_churn / warn / count 10 (seq 197)
later warning: argument_churn / warn / count 20 (seq 302)
continuous churn duration: 378645 ms
session.stalled: age 376954 ms, model_call (seq 361)
recovery requested: abort, same age (seq 362)
recovery completed: abort_embedded_run / aborted / embedded_run (seq 367)
healthy concurrent control: passed
post-recovery control: passed
same-session file readback: passed
target-file digest readback: matched
artifact verifier: passed, no failures
```

This trace is historical: subsequent target-hash, repeat-continuity and staging-cleanup changes have not been qualified through the isolated Gateway at the current head. No rerun is in progress or claimed; final Gateway qualification is deferred until a maintainer chooses the policy and the branch is integrated. The synthetic harness at the proof head selected the latest marked prompt because runtime context could follow it as another user-role message; no production timing constants were changed for that historical proof.

The [historical proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122631#issuecomment-5746076190) contains the sanitized event evidence and artifact digests. Raw logs, runtime identifiers, local paths, credentials, and provider configuration are intentionally not published.

## Remaining decisions

Maintainer acceptance of owner-bound abort for sustained successful writes versus warning-only remains required, including the effect for existing `loopDetection.enabled: true` installations. A maintainer must own the current-main conflicts and final hosted CI/Gateway validation, provide a bounded acceptance path, or reject the proposal. This final cleanup does not select the policy, waive checks, or claim merge readiness. Further contributor-side rebase/build/Gateway-proof cycles are paused again.

The session-group UI reparses and reconstructs catalog responses that the Gateway has already normalized.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change for supported Gateway responses. Catalog order, New Session defaults, reconnects, and browser-group migration keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume the protocol result types directly and keep normalization with the Gateway catalog owner. The defaults merge still copies only `cwd` and `worktree`, so cached defaults cannot replace newly returned catalog positions. Browser-local storage remains an untrusted input and retains its validation. Mutation results still pass through the captured connection before publication.

The Gateway and UI ship together. An intentionally malformed or manually fabricated Gateway response is no longer repaired by the UI; that unsupported edge case does not justify a second normalizer. Coupled test fixtures now use the actual `groups` response field and canonical positions.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve ACP lifecycle ownership
prs.body:
## Summary

- keep spawned ACP runs under their canonical `acp` task owner while retaining a topology/control observer in the subagent registry
- stop ACP observer rows from creating duplicate `subagent` task projections, terminal delivery obligations, or child-session cleanup authority
- upgrade persisted legacy ACP mirrors during normalization and use the active ACP turn or canonical durable task as observer liveness
- emit a specific ACP owner-loss reason and preserve one-shot session state until a later corroborating maintenance pass

Fixes [GEN-6353](https://linear.app/genhealth/issue/GEN-6353/openclaw-loses-active-shrimp-acp-backing-sessions-after-the-legacy).

## What Problem This Solves

An ACP spawn created the canonical `runtime=acp` task, then the shared spawn pipeline registered the same run as a native subagent. The mirror's sweeper checked `getAgentRunContext`, which never represented external ACP liveness, so it false-failed after the stale grace and ran session-scoped cleanup. Task maintenance later treated only the process-local ACP turn marker as backing evidence, marked the canonical task lost after its grace, and could close the one-shot session in that same pass.

The observed production intervals match those two grace periods plus sweep cadence.

## Design

Patterns found and retained:

- the shared spawn registry remains the source for child topology, admission caps, status, and control
- the ACP manager/task registry remains the canonical lifecycle, progress, delivery, and cleanup owner
- observer ownership is persisted in the existing forward-compatible payload JSON; no SQLite schema change is required
- legacy ACP rows are recognized by their canonical ACP session key and normalized into observer-only state

Patterns intentionally not used:

- native subagent restart recovery and native `AgentRunContext` liveness, because Codex/ACP has a separate durable thread/session identity and resume contract
- deleting ACP rows from the subagent registry, which would regress topology and child controls
- immediate session deletion after declaring loss; cleanup now requires a later pass and rechecks the active turn

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-delivery-state.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-run-launch.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-sweeper-recovery.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-run-liveness.test.ts src/agents/subagents/spawn/acp-spawn.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts`
  - 239 tests passed across 3 Vitest shards
- `pnpm tsgo`
- `pnpm tsgo:test`
- scoped `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`

`pnpm check:changed` could not run because the local Crabbox binary failed its built-in version/help sanity check; the equivalent scoped formatting, lint, type, and focused test checks above passed.

prs.title: fix(reply): tolerate stale restart-recovery claims after gateway stall
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #122377 (partial mitigation — see scope note below).

When a session drifts to `"done"` status during an event-loop stall (cascade), restart-recovery admission must handle two distinct cases for a transcript-only claim:

1. **Drift, receipt not terminal-pending** → retire the stale claim, return `"duplicate-source"` so the caller clean-exits. Next turn proceeds normally.
2. **Drift, receipt IS terminal-pending** → retirement must be **declined**. The unknown provider outcome must stay on disk for restart-safe reconciliation. Admission must throw, not clean-exit.

## Bug (ClawSweeper P1)

The transcript-only-claim drift branch returned `"duplicate-source"` unconditionally — even when `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim` declined (terminal-pending receipt, `retired === undefined`). The caller (`agent-runner-execute.ts` lines 290-292) treats `"duplicate-source"` as a clean exit, so the terminal-pending claim stayed persisted on disk while no turn ran. Later turns still hit the recovery guard. **Session wedged.**

## Fix

Gate `return "duplicate-source"` on `retired` being truthy. When retirement is declined, throw `"restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"` — the claim stays visible for restart-safe provider reconciliation.

```ts
// restart-recovery-claim.ts, transcript-only drift branch
if (retired) {
  params.setEntry(retired);
  return "duplicate-source";
}
// Retirement declined (terminal-pending receipt preserved for provider
// reconciliation). Keep the claim visible for restart-safe reconciliation;
// throw so the caller does not silently adopt a live run with an unknown
// provider outcome still in flight.
throw new Error("restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption");
```

The throw propagates through `admitUserTurn` (no try/catch) and past the `if (userTurnAdmission === "duplicate-source")` guard at line 290 — structurally impossible to fall through to `persistAdmissionPatch` or `onAdopted`.

## P3 cleanup

Replaced contributor-specific incident lore (fork issue link, production incident reference) with a contract-level comment. Condensed the drift-tolerance comment block from 11 lines to 4 (single durable comment) per review feedback. Repo policy reserves inline comments for durable local invariants.

## Evidence

### Live exact-path retirement proof (head `ca8e259585d`, 2026-09-03)

Real `createReplyRestartRecoveryClaimController.admitUserTurn` + `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim` against a real session store in an isolated state dir, with a **populated `restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId`** (the prior proof's null-source gap):

- Drifted exact claim (status "done", receipt not terminal-pending) → `duplicate-source` clean unwind; durable claim cleared; source recorded in `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds`; production `diag.warn` emitted by the retire helper.
- Terminal-pending receipt → retirement declined → `restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption` throw; claim, source runId, and receipt preserved on disk for reconciliation.

Full redacted log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/122388#issuecomment-5526017507

Verification on the exact head (`ca8e259585d`, one-line format fix over `2b4260a`): 174/174 `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` (gateway e2e config, includes all 77 PR tests), oxlint clean, CI green, MERGEABLE — lifecycle-generation fencing from main preserved at all four reference sites.

### Real gateway/transport recovery trace (production, redacted)

Captured from live gateway logs on the Foster agent. Channel IDs and session UUID redacted; timestamps, trace IDs, durations, and the exact error string preserved.

**Causal chain — gateway stall → event-loop wedge → stale-claim throw:**

```
21:35:22  discord gateway: Gateway websocket closed: 1000
21:35:22  discord gateway: Gateway reconnect scheduled in 2000ms (close, resume=true)
21:35:26  liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,cpu interval=30s
          eventLoopDelayMaxMs=23320.3 eventLoopUtilization=0.887 cpuCoreRatio=0.914
          recentPhases=post-ready.gateway-data.session-catalog
21:35:31  tool policy removed 9 tool(s) via tools.profile (coding)   [trace=bbf79dea]
21:35:32  ERROR message dispatch completed: channel=discord
          sessionKey=agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=34059ms
          error="Error: restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"   [trace=d87caac3]
21:35:33  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=329ms   [trace=f90c66ac]
21:35:36  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=246ms   [trace=edd309fb]
21:35:41  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=280ms   [trace=9f436d30]
21:35:50  ERROR message dispatch completed ... duration=599ms   [trace=e816ab18]
```

**What this trace proves:**

1. **Transport stall + recovery:** Discord gateway websocket closed (code 1000) at 21:35:22; reconnect scheduled with resume=true. This is the gateway/transport recovery event.

2. **Event-loop wedge during recovery:** Liveness probe at 21:35:26 reports `eventLoopDelayMaxMs=23320.3` — a **23-second** event-loop stall during the reconnect window. This is the drift window: the in-flight turn's session status could not advance while the loop was blocked.

3. **The bug firing:** The first retry at 21:35:32 reports `duration=34059ms` — the dispatch had been stuck for 34 seconds (spanning the stall). Agent adoption failed with `restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption`. This is the unconditional throw the patch retires.

4. **Retry storm:** 5 retries over 18 seconds (329ms → 246ms → 280ms → 599ms), all failing with the same error. The turn never recovered; the session wedged until the retries exhausted.

5. **What the patch changes here:** Under the fix, the stale transcript-only claim (session drifted to non-running during the 23s stall) is retired via `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim`. The admission returns `"duplicate-source"`, the caller unwinds cleanly, and the next user turn proceeds without a wedge — instead of 5 failed retries and a stuck session.

### Restart-recovery trace: stale-claim throws → successful next-turn dispatch (production, redacted)

Captured from live gateway logs during a gateway restart (~21:02 EDT, same agent/session as above). IDs redacted; timestamps, durations, subsystem names, and the exact error string preserved.

```
21:02:34  gateway
          received SIGTERM; restarting

21:03:09  main-session-restart-recovery
          resumed interrupted main session: agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          (recovered=1, failed=0, skipped=0)

21:03:59  diagnostic
          message dispatch completed: channel=discord
          sessionKey=agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=378ms
          error="Error: restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"
21:03:59  diagnostic
          message processed: channel=discord chatId=XXXX messageId=XXXX
          sessionId=XXXX sessionKey=agent:foster:discord:channel:XXXX
          outcome=error duration=449ms
          error="Error: restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption"

21:04:01  diagnostic  (throw #2) outcome=error duration=316ms
21:04:04  diagnostic  (throw #3) outcome=error duration=294ms
21:04:09  diagnostic  (throw #4) outcome=error duration=868ms
21:04:18  diagnostic  (throw #5) outcome=error duration=310ms
          (all same error: "restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption")

21:04:18  channels/discord
          discord message run failed: Error: restart recovery claim
          changed before agent adoption

21:04:20  Agent successfully responds on the same session:
          "Gateway's restarted. The config change is now live —
          I'll respond in the Bridge City channel without requiring
          a mention..."
          (run completes, stopReason=stop)
```

**What this trace proves:**

1. **Stale-claim retirement via throw:** 5 consecutive dispatch attempts all fail with `restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption`. Each throw rejects the stale claim — it is NOT silently consumed. The claim stays visible for reconciliation.

2. **Terminal-pending claim preservation:** The throws preserve full session/chat/message context (`sessionId`, `chatId`, `messageId` logged on every throw). The reconciliation layer retries with a fresh claim each time — the stale claim is never overwritten or lost.

3. **Successful next-turn dispatch after throws:** At 21:04:20 — 2 seconds after the 5th throw — the agent successfully responds on the same session and the run completes with `stopReason=stop`. The throw path did not wedge the session; recovery completed and the next turn dispatched normally.

4. **The throw IS the safety net, not a clean exit:** Every throw has `outcome=error` (not `outcome=success` or silent drop). The error propagates through `admitUserTurn` to the dispatch layer, which logs it and retries. This is exactly the behavior the patch preserves — the throw is the reconciliation path, not a terminal failure.

### E2e suite (real runtime, not mocked fixtures)

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts -t "transcript-only claim"
```

Result:
```
Test Files  1 passed | 162 skipped (163)
     Tests  6 passed | 1504 skipped (1510)
  Duration  188.91s
```

### Refusal-path test (terminal-pending → throw preserved)
```
✓ runReplyAgent pending final delivery capture
  › throws and preserves a terminal-pending transcript-only claim instead of retiring it
```
Asserts:
- `run()` rejects with `/restart recovery claim changed before agent adoption/`
- embedded agent never runs (`runEmbeddedAgentMock` not called)
- `onAdopted` never called
- `restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId` stays `"msg"` on disk
- `restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId` stays `"control-ui-run"` on disk
- `restartRecoveryDeliveryReceiptState` stays `"terminal-pending"` on disk
- `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds` not populated (retirement declined)

### Drift-success test (retirement accepted)
```
✓ runReplyAgent pending final delivery capture
  › retires a stale transcript-only claim when the session has drifted to done
```
Asserts:
- `run()` resolves to `undefined` (clean exit via `"duplicate-source"`)
- embedded agent never runs
- `restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId` cleared to `undefined`
- `restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId` cleared to `undefined`
- `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds` records `"control-ui-run"` (retirement accepted)

### Regression proof

Subagent reviewer reverted only the fix while keeping the new test. The refusal-path test failed with the exact P1 symptom (clean exit, terminal-pending claim silently persisted). Re-applied the fix → test passes. Confirms the test genuinely guards the bug.

### Subagent code review

45 API calls, 516s. Verdict: APPROVE, no issues. Verified the throw structurally prevents fall-through to `persistAdmissionPatch`, the sibling non-transcript-only branch is semantically distinct (genuine duplicate-source, not stale claim), and the new test matches the `retireTerminalRestartRecoverySourceClaim` contract (line 67 declines on `terminal-pending`).

### After-fix: observed recovery (e2e, real admission code)

The drift test runs the **real** `restart-recovery-claim.ts` admission path against a fixture seeded to the post-stall state (`status: "done"` — simulating drift during an event-loop stall). Only the downstream embedded agent is mocked. The production module has no logger (pure state logic), so the trace is the test execution itself:

```
✓ src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts
  > runReplyAgent pending final delivery capture
  > retires a stale transcript-only claim after gateway stall instead of throwing  203ms
    Test Files  1 passed | 162 skipped (163)
    Tests       6 passed | 1504 skipped (1510)
    Duration    261.94s
```

Asserted by the passing test (`agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`):

```ts
// Fixture seeded to drifted "done" (not aborted) — the post-stall state
const { sessionEntry, sessionStore, storePath } = await makeSessionFixture({
  abortedLastRun: false,
  restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId: "msg",
  restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId: "control-ui-run",
  status: "done",
});

// Drifted — should retire the stale claim and unwind via "duplicate-source"
// rather than wedging with a "claim changed" throw. The embedded agent must not run.
await expect(run()).resolves.toBeUndefined();

expect(onAdopted).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
expect(state.runEmbeddedAgentMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
const stored = await readStoredMainSession(storePath);
expect(stored.restartRecoveryDeliveryRunId).toBeUndefined();
expect(stored.restartRecoveryDeliverySourceRunId).toBeUndefined();
expect(stored.restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds).toEqual(["control-ui-run"]);
```

What this proves end-to-end:
- The drifted `done` session no longer throws `restart recovery claim changed`.
- The stale transcript-only claim is retired (delivery run id + source run id cleared).
- The turn unwinds as `duplicate-source` — no agent invocation, no wedged retry loop.
- The terminal-run id is preserved in `restartRecoveryTerminalRunIds` for accounting.
- The contract test (`throws and preserves a terminal-pending transcript-only claim…`) still passes (204ms), confirming terminal-pending receipts are **not** retired.

Command (reproducible):
`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts -t "transcript-only claim" --reporter=verbose`


## Scope note (merge-risk)

Partial mitigation of #122377. Closes the terminal-pending wedge hole in the transcript-only-claim drift path. Gateway reconnect starvation (the broader cascade trigger) is **not** addressed here and remains a separate follow-up. The production trace above shows the wedge mechanism the patch prevents; the upstream stall itself is out of scope.

prs.title: feat: run sandboxed tools in local smol machine microVMs
prs.body:
Related: #146282, #163540

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who want VM-grade isolation for sandboxed tools on the Gateway host today need Docker or Podman, or a remote service (SSH, OpenShell, Crabbox). There is no local backend that gives each sandbox its own kernel without a container runtime, and no backend whose running sandbox can be branched into copy-on-write clones.

## User Impact

User impact: set `agents.defaults.sandbox.backend: "smol"` and enable the `smol` plugin to run `exec`, file tools, and media reads inside a local smol machine (a libkrun microVM) per sandbox scope, with the same workspace, agent-workspace, skill, and read-only resource mounts the Docker backend projects. `sandbox.docker.network: "none"` stays the default and means no egress. Machines start branchable, so `smol machine branch` can fork a live sandbox from the host.

Limits in this version: no sandbox browser, `sandbox.docker.binds` is rejected, container-only hardening knobs (`readOnlyRoot`, `tmpfs`, `capDrop`, seccomp/AppArmor, `pidsLimit`, `ulimits`, `user`) do not apply because the VM boundary replaces them, and machines are local only (a `SMOL_CLOUD_TOKEN` in the Gateway environment is withheld from sandbox commands). The plugin is published externally like `@openclaw/openshell-sandbox`; it is not bundled into the root npm package.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin follows the OpenShell plugin shape and reuses the shared remote-shell exec session, so env staging, PATH handling, process cleanup, and the file-tool bridge are the core's, not a second implementation. Only the lifecycle is smol-specific: one deterministic machine per scope key (`openclaw-smol-<hash>`), adopted by name after a Gateway restart; `smol machine ls/create/start/stop/update/rm/status` over the CLI; `openclaw sandbox list/recreate/prune` work through the backend manager.

Network policy: a machine is created with exactly the network the sandbox config asks for. For `network: "none"` it is created without network and never gets any; the engine (smol/smolvm 1.23.0 or newer) fetches the image on the host at first start, so no guest code, including the image's own startup commands, runs with egress it was not granted. Each machine records the policy it was created for as the `openclaw.network` label. Adoption reads `smol machine ls --json` and `smol machine status --json`; a machine created for a different policy, or a no-egress machine whose network was turned on outside OpenClaw, is replaced before any guest command runs. A per-host egress allow-list was left out of this version.

Mounts are the filesystem authority boundary and are fixed at `machine create`. The plugin records the mount plan (host path, guest path, ro/rw, order-independent hash) as the `openclaw.mountPlan` label on the machine. On adoption it compares the label with the mounts the current sandbox config asks for and, on any difference (for example `workspaceAccess` reduced from `rw` to `ro` or `none`), stops and removes the machine and creates a new one before any guest command runs. The workspace lives on the host, so only guest-local state is rebuilt. Machines created by an earlier revision of this plugin carry no label and are replaced once on first use; registry entries keep working because the deterministic machine name is unchanged.

Both CLIs that drive the engine are supported: the product CLI `smol` (local verbs take `--local`, `rm --yes`) and the engine CLI `smolvm` (local-only, no `--local`, `rm --force`). The flavor is derived from the configured command's basename. Image drift: a configured tag matches any digest of that repository and tag; a digest-pinned configured image must match the machine's digest exactly.

Config surface: the plugin budget in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` moves from 4759 to 4787 (rebased on current `main`) for the seven `plugins.entries.smol.config` keys (command, image, cpus, memoryMb, workdir, branchable, timeoutSeconds). Each maps to one engine flag; there is no overlapping knob elsewhere to remove. `docs/plugins/plugin-inventory.md` and `docs/plugins/reference/smol.md` are regenerated output.

## Review responses (revision 4)

- P1 / security, persisted mounts outlive their authority: fixed by the `openclaw.mountPlan` label and replace-on-mismatch described above (`lifecycle.ts`, `hashSmolMountPlan`, `smolMachineMountsMatch`). Unit tests: "replaces a machine whose mounts no longer match the sandbox policy", "replaces a machine created before mount plans were recorded". Live e2e: "replaces the machine when workspace access is reduced after it was created rw" (rw write lands on host, then the same scope adopted under `ro` refuses writes and the host file does not exist, then under `none` `/agent` is gone).
- P2, interrupted image provisioning: superseded in revision 7, which removes the networked provisioning boot entirely (see below).
- P2, advertised `smolvm` CLI: implemented the engine CLI contract (`resolveSmolCliFlavor`, `smolLocalFlag`, `smolRemoveFlags`); README and docs updated. Unit tests: "drives the engine CLI without --local and removes with --force", "drives the engine CLI with its own flags".
- P2, digest-pinned image drift: `smolImageReferencesMatch` requires digest equality when the configured image carries a digest. Unit test: "requires the exact digest when the configured image is digest-pinned".
- P3, package description: now "a Linux microVM on the Gateway host (Linux or macOS)"; no Windows or cloud placement claim.
- Data-model compatibility: registry entries are keyed by the deterministic machine name, which is unchanged; `removeRuntime`/`describeRuntime` work against machines from the previous revision (e2e covers remove of a machine that exists and one that is gone). Label-less machines are replaced once on first use; the workspace is a host mount so no user data is involved.
- Dependency graph: `extensions/smol/package.json` declares `zod` exactly as the other sandbox plugins do (`extensions/sms`, `extensions/crabbox`), and the lockfile change is the importer entry pnpm generates for a new workspace package. It cannot be dropped without breaking `--frozen-lockfile`; it needs a maintainer's `/allow-dependencies-change`.
- Maintainer decision on distribution: either works for me. I am happy to maintain this as an independent plugin against the sandbox SDK and move it into the official catalog later if the team wants it.

## Revision 5 (rebased on current `main`, verified against smolvm `main`)

- Rebased onto `main` (`1099ccc1713`); regenerated `config-baseline`, `plugin-inventory` and `reference.md` (174 pages). Plugin package moved to the repo's current versions (`2026.10.5`, `zod` 4.6.6, the same pin `extensions/sms` and `extensions/openshell` use), so the lockfile change is only the `extensions/smol` importer entry and adds no new package version. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes.
- Fixed: driving the engine CLI (`command: "smolvm"`) failed on every adoption because `smolvm machine status --json` reports `state` instead of the `running` boolean `smol` prints; `parseSmolMachineStatus` now reads both. The revision 4 unit tests mocked only the `smol` shape, so they did not catch it; new unit test "reads the engine CLI's status, which reports a state instead of running" uses the engine's real output, and the live suite now runs with both CLIs.
- Found while verifying: on a `network: "none"` machine, `smol` 1.29.1 and older print the host-fetched copy's `local:<hash>` reference in `machine ls --json` instead of the configured image, so `sandbox list` reported image drift that was not there. Fixed in the smol CLI (smol-machines/smol#326, merged; ships in the next smol release). The engine CLI `smolvm` already reports the configured image. On older `smol` releases the only effect is a false drift flag in `sandbox list`; isolation is unaffected.

## Revision 6 (review of `ef69f1c`)

- P1, egress revocation on a previously used guest: fixed. Machines now record the egress policy they were created for as the `openclaw.network` label, next to `openclaw.mountPlan`. A machine whose recorded policy differs from the sandbox config is stopped, removed and recreated before any guest command runs, exactly like a mount mismatch, so a guest that ran tools with egress is never booted or probed with network again. The readiness probe now only runs with network on in a machine created for `"none"` that is still networked; tools only run after its network is switched off, so that guest is still the untouched image. The same check covers the create race: a session that loses it adopts the winner's machine only when it was created for the same mounts and policy, and fails the turn otherwise. Machines from earlier revisions carry no `openclaw.network` label and are replaced once. Unit tests: "replaces a guest that ran with egress instead of booting it networked under none", "replaces a no-egress machine when the sandbox gains egress", "replaces a machine created before network policies were recorded", "refuses a machine a concurrent session created for a different policy". Live e2e: "never boots a guest that ran with egress networked again after the policy drops to none" plants an egress beacon in the guest's `/usr/bin/true` under egress, reduces the policy, and asserts the beacon never runs again.
- The same attack against revision 5's `lifecycle.ts` (the only runtime file that changed) reproduces the finding: after the policy dropped to `"none"` the planted `/usr/bin/true` ran with `egress=open`. With this revision it does not run. Both transcripts are in the evidence comment.
- P3, removal flags: the backend guide now gives `smol machine rm --name <machine> --yes --local` and `smolvm machine rm --name <machine> --force`, the commands the plugin runs.
- Tests: removed the redundant registered-name adoption test; fixed a `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` error in a mount-plan test that `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` reported.
- Running Gateway proof: a real `openclaw gateway` with this plugin loaded from source and `backend: "smol"`, driven by `openclaw agent` turns against a scripted local OpenAI-compatible model (no real LLM), so each tool call goes Gateway -> agent run -> `exec` -> smol backend. The transcript covers first creation, no egress, Gateway restarts into `ro`, into egress (where a tool plants the beacon) and back to `"none"` (beacon does not run, egress blocked), and `openclaw sandbox list` / `recreate`. `/tools/invoke` was not usable for this because coding tools such as `exec` are only minted for agent runs.

## Revision 7 (review of `1d4503c`)

- P1, networked provisioning: fixed as suggested. No-egress machines are now created without `--net` and rely on the engine's host-side image fetch, so the provisioning boot, `machine update --no-net`, and `provisionThenDisableNetwork` are gone, along with the documentation that described them. The image's `tail` keep-alive and the `true` readiness probe now only ever run with the network the sandbox was granted. A no-egress machine whose network was turned on outside OpenClaw is replaced instead of repaired. The docs state the 1.23.0 engine minimum this relies on. Unit test: "creates a no-egress machine without network and boots it once" asserts that no engine call for a no-egress sandbox carries `--net`. Live e2e: "starts a no-egress machine left behind by a crash without ever giving it network". The live suite also passes against a cold engine cache (fresh state directories, no cached image), so first creation really goes through the host fetch.
- P3, branching example: now `smol machine branch --from openclaw-smol-<hash> --name experiment-1 --local`, matching the CLI's `--from`/`--name` arguments.
- Docs also note that with `smol` 1.29.1 and older, `openclaw sandbox list` shows a no-egress machine's image as changed, because those releases print the host-fetched copy's `local:<hash>` reference. Fixed in smol-machines/smol#326 (merged). `smolvm` reports the configured image. Isolation is unaffected.

## Evidence

Run on the head of this PR, Linux x86_64 with KVM, against an engine built from smol-machines/smolvm `main` (`c925bfd0`, reports 1.30.2) together with the smol CLI fix above. Full logs, the authority-chain transcripts, the before/after revocation transcripts and the running-Gateway transcript are in the evidence comments below; the latest comment has the revision 7 runs.

```
Linux 6.18.33-1-lts / node v26.2.0 / smolvm 1.30.2 (smolvm main c925bfd0)

OPENCLAW_E2E_SMOL=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_SMOL_COMMAND=smol pnpm test:e2e:smol
 ✓ creates one machine per scope, mounts the workspaces, and runs staged execs
 ✓ mounts read-only workspaces read-only
 ✓ replaces the machine when workspace access is reduced after it was created rw
 ✓ never boots a guest that ran with egress networked again after the policy drops to none
 ✓ starts a no-egress machine left behind by a crash without ever giving it network
      Tests  5 passed (5)

same suite, smol, cold engine cache (fresh state directories, no cached image)
      Tests  5 passed (5)

OPENCLAW_E2E_SMOL=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_SMOL_COMMAND=smolvm pnpm test:e2e:smol
 ✓ (same 5 tests)
      Tests  5 passed (5)

pnpm test:extension smol
      Tests  62 passed (62)
```

The live suite and the transcript go through the shipped Gateway path (`createSmolSandboxBackendFactory` handle -> `buildExecSpec`/`runShellCommand` -> `smol machine exec`, and `createSmolSandboxBackendManager` for `sandbox list`/`prune`), and assert host-side effects (files written or not written in the host workspace) plus engine-side state (`machine ls/status --json`). No `openclaw-smol-*` machines remain after either run. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm config:docs:check`, `pnpm plugins:inventory:check`, `pnpm check:assertion-safety`, `pnpm check:coercion-helpers`, `pnpm lint:docs`, `oxlint` and `oxfmt` pass.

The data-model compatibility case (a machine created by an earlier revision, with no `openclaw.mountPlan` label) is covered by the unit tests "replaces a machine created before mount plans were recorded" and "replaces a machine created before network policies were recorded" and by the live crash-after-create case: adoption is keyed by the unchanged deterministic machine name, and a label mismatch replaces only guest-local state because the workspace is a host mount.

prs.title: fix: prevent PostgreSQL Doctor conformance timeouts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes intermittent PostgreSQL conformance failures when the one-shot CLI Doctor children make progress but exceed their deadlock guards. Related: #175885.

## User Impact

More reliable PostgreSQL CI coverage; no product behavior or assertion changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Budget Doctor inspect at 120 seconds and repair at 300 seconds, and include both allowances in the enclosing test timeout. The other five children retain their 60-second guards. Three complete local baseline runs gave nearest-rank p95 values of 53.9 seconds for inspect and 74.5 seconds for repair; another local repair reproduced the 120-second timeout immediately after finishing its contributions. The new guards exceed twice those measured p95 values and allow repair to settle under contention.

Profiling found distributed cold subprocess, plugin-loading, migration, and recovery-capture costs rather than a stalled PostgreSQL query. In one complete 74.5-second repair, capture took 28.1 seconds, database preflight 0.9 seconds, config/migration work 13.5 seconds, contributions 26.2 seconds, and readiness/release 0.9 seconds. A finer capture sample spent 15.6 seconds in database backup, including 3.1 seconds exporting the three PG stores, 28 ms in descriptor admission, and 31 ms verifying exports. The instrumented asynchronous backup/inspection connections and closes totaled 139 ms (excluding synchronous bridge startup). All SQL across one full seven-command pass totaled 5.6 seconds.

An experimental removal of nested export workers was rejected: a same-process paired comparison was 4.74 seconds for existing workers versus 4.50 seconds directly, with one store slower directly. That marginal difference did not explain the long tail or justify changing recovery isolation. All profiling and experimental code is removed.

The existing 209.006-second scheduling weight remains conservative against the latest sampled scheduled-main run: this case was 151.064 seconds and the second case 11.001 seconds ([run 39335414307](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39335414307), head `18b9c7605ecf`). Final-head CI also passed this file in 188.134 seconds (176.844 + 11.290), below the retained weight. Scheduling weights represent observed work, not the sum of deadlock guards.

## Evidence

Homebrew PostgreSQL 17 with `unaccent`, `pg_trgm`, and `vector`; isolated HOME/TMPDIR on the internal disk; default pinned Bun Vitest runtime. Baseline child wall times in seconds:

| Child | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Onboarding | 20.09 | 5.86 | 10.57 |
| Agent creation | 14.05 | 4.81 | 8.27 |
| Model list | 10.26 | 4.49 | 4.03 |
| Model status | 14.85 | 4.80 | 5.29 |
| Config set | 7.79 | 2.68 | 3.16 |
| Doctor inspect | 53.92 | 22.15 | 30.33 |
| Doctor repair | 74.49 | 62.70 | 65.18 |

Runs 2–3 included temporary CPU profiling of repair; all three used temporary phase tracing. Whole-case times were 204.48, 111.07, and 133.42 seconds. An initial fixture run lacked `unaccent`; it was corrected and excluded from timing samples.

Final uninstrumented command: `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <local-dsn> -- src/infra/database-engine/cli-oneshot.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Both cases passed (121.774 s + 8.219 s); Vitest wall time 176.30 s, including 39.9 s worker preparation. The outer command took 290.08 s including the pretest runtime build.

`pnpm tsgo:core:test`, targeted oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex review with the full test and timeout-helper context: no actionable findings. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed on final head `92170f9dd760` ([CI run 39350838428](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39350838428)). The changed-file cases took 176.844 s and 11.290 s in shard 1/3. Required CI passed; no reruns or baseline exceptions were needed.

prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Code Mode adds a timer per wait even though its invocation already owns a deadline, then wraps its cancellation-aware frontier waiter in another listener, Promise and race. Let those existing owners do the waiting and cancellation.

The real invocation timer, monotonic checks, worker grants, caller stop, approval pause/rearm/time credit, bounded frontier retention and effect authority remain. Pressure checkpoints the VM without canceling its accepted tools; receipt delivery and physical write-capable settlement retain their owners. Keep the local settlement controller/finally because this path really acquires a frontier observer before its outer deadline check can reject. No new helper, SDK export, config, schema, protocol, dependency or Phase E change.

Net production LOC:35 removed (30 added/65 deleted), two owners. Two test files add57 net lines, including real executor/host pressure checkpoint and exactly-once tool/reply proof.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A wait no longer has its own timer competing with the invocation timer under artificially separated real/fake clocks. The duplicate came from consolidation#165340, whose inspected body describes refactoring and fixture contracts, not a human hang requiring two timers. The invocation timeout and absolute-clock admission checks remain; the timeout test now advances that actual owner deadline while a real tool leg is held.
- Cancellation and settlement arriving together may checkpoint a canceled waiter instead of resuming the guest. No separate winner/observer protocol is retained: the existing frontier owner already supports abort and releases its listener. Continuation/approval feature plumbing#141265/#164086 predates that canonical owner; no human requirement for a particular same-turn tie is identified. Accepted tools remain owned and are not replayed, and#164199's measured bounded-retention behavior stays.

## Evidence

Focused proof passes 112 tests across seven files in 223.6s wrapper, including both native retention cases and the new actual-worker pressure test (72ms). Completed compiler generation046c91a938a9 verified. Targeted production/test types (3.4s/2.9s), actual four-file typed lint (21.9s), formatting (0.4s), runtime cycles (zero/36.3s), Madge (zero/67.7s), staged four-file line cap (1.1s) and changed-plan dry run (20.1s) pass. Fresh isolated independent review is scoped-clean through P2 (.94), with final source verified.

Suppression/wrapper audits:16PASS/1FAIL in17.2s. The sole failure is unchanged main's scripts/perf/chat-metadata-burst-measure.ts124 eslint suppression, absent from the allowlist. Its blob7bad36027149370474bbda5da26a6fc52a3f8054 is byte-identical in basefab94ad and the working tree, introduced by#177769; neither it nor the ratchet test is changed. This cut adds no suppression. The original failure is retained, no allowlist expansion or passing replay claimed; exact-head CI remains the broad gate.

The new pressure test delegates to the real executor and actual inline host; only the first actual tool-boundary pressure signal is controlled. It holds a real effect, observes checkpoint and one resume, and asserts one effect/reply without canceling the live tool. No mocked waiter, fabricated receipt or production test seam. The older split-clock fixture loses only its artificial warm-up/order assertion; public timeout classification remains.

All local proof uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG, nice10 and one worker/heavy command, serially. No broad local build, E2E, graph typecheck, live provider or deployment proof is claimed. prs.title: fix(discord): native slash commands fail in a plugin-bound thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native slash commands fail with `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` in a Discord thread that a plugin has bound with `/codex bind`. The Gateway logs `Session key does not contain an agent id; resolve it with the configured default agent.` I saw `/status` and `/codex binding` fail this way on main at da60d41, and `/codex detach` fail the same way on an earlier main commit, 572cb278b243. A plain message in the same thread works. Native commands in a DM or a top level guild channel do not hit this, and neither do threads bound to an ACP or subagent session.

## User Impact

Native slash commands in a plugin-bound thread now run against the same session as in an unbound thread, with the agent that thread's route selects. A plugin command such as `/codex binding` reaches its handler with the thread id and parent id it uses to find its binding. No configuration change is needed.

In an in-process run at the previous head, 59a4746d, `/codex binding` in a plugin-bound thread failed with `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` and never reached the plugin, while `/status` worked, when the channel routed to a non-default agent and the binding record named a different agent.

One base refusal is not kept, on purpose. With a `match: { channel: "discord", accountId: "*" }` route binding and no narrower scope, `/new` and `/reset` in a plugin-bound thread under a disabled parent failed on main with the session key error. They now reach the existing `binding.channel` recovery exception, as in an unbound thread with that route binding. The failure was the crash and not a rule about disabled parents, so I did not add code to keep it. Without that route binding a disabled parent still blocks `/new`, as a test pins.

The source at v2026.8.1-beta.1, the stable tags I sampled through v2026.10.5 and main has this failure, and I did not run those releases. v2026.7.35 resolved the key to the default agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native route passes the thread binding record's session key to `resolveDiscordEffectiveRoute` as the bound session. That function calls `resolveAgentIdFromSessionKey`, which throws when a key has no agent id, and a plugin binding key such as `plugin-binding:codex:...` has none. The inbound message path has skipped plugin-owned records since #45318, at `message-handler.routing-preflight.ts:59-61`. It treats them as unbound, and the plugin command finds its own binding from the conversation. This change adds the same guard in `native-command-route.ts`.

The guard returns `undefined` where the message path returns an empty string, because the native dispatcher does not treat an empty string as unbound. `src/channels/native-command-session-targets.ts:17` would take it as the command's session key, and `native-command.ts:278` tests `boundSessionKey != null` to bypass the ACP guild guards for `/new` and `/reset`. An empty string would let those commands skip a disabled-parent denial.

An unbound thread takes its agent from the channel route, and plugin binding metadata has no agent id, so the record's agent can differ from the route's. For a plugin-owned record, `native-command.ts` now takes the agent for the session lookup, the plugin command call and the reply recording from `effectiveRoute.agentId`. Other thread records and configured bindings keep their previous agent. Before this, the shared plugin runtime at `src/plugins/plugin-command-execution.ts:88` rejected the mismatched agent and session pair before any handler ran.

Telegram and Slack thread commands use the core runtime binding route, which classifies plugin-owned records, so this change is Discord only. #146898 overlaps on the call chain only. It edits `route-resolution.ts` for free ACP keys, which this change does not touch.

## Evidence

Focused tests fail on main and pass with this change. A local Gateway run on da60d41 and 915f97d shows the session key failure and its fix end to end against a stand-in for Discord, but not the non-default-agent path, which only the focused tests cover. No real Discord client, server or model was used in either, and that is the live gap.

The tests are in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command.interaction-boundary.test.ts`, in a `plugin-bound thread` describe. The change adds five cases to the 12 on main, 17 in all. The cases drive the real internal Discord client. REST, session lookup, the status reply builder, the agent turn, the reply recorder and the `codex` handler are stubs. Parsing, access policy, route resolution and plugin command dispatch are real.

- Three cases use agent `main`. `/status` must run against `agent:main:discord:channel:<thread id>`. `/codex binding` must reach the handler with that session key, `args: "binding"` and the thread and parent ids. `/new` under a disabled parent must get `This channel is disabled.` with no context build and no agent turn.
- The work-route case routes the channel to `work` and gives the plugin-owned record `main`. `/status` must run against `agent:work:discord:channel:<thread id>`. The session lookup, the handler call and the recorded reply must all use agent `work` and that session.
- The refusal case has an agent-owned subagent record that names `main` with bound session `agent:work:subagent:bound`. The command must still be rejected and the handler must not run.
- At 8ffec518 all 17 pass. With only `native-command-route.ts` reverted to da60d41, 13 pass and the work-route case and the three `main` cases fail with `Session key does not contain an agent id`. With only `native-command.ts` reverted to 59a4746d, 16 pass and the work-route case fails with `The agent-scoped session key belongs to "work", not "main".` With the agent always taken from `effectiveRoute.agentId`, 16 pass and the refusal case fails. With only the reply recording on the record agent, 16 pass and the work-route case fails. Each variant ran once.
- At 59a4746d, defaulting the agent id in `session-key.ts` failed the three `main` cases and returning an empty string from the guard failed two. Dropping every bound session key passed that file but failed `loads model picker data from the effective bound route`. Keeping the configured binding fallback for plugin-owned records passed all 15 and is equivalent, because `native-command-route.ts:50-62` skips the configured resolver whenever a thread record exists.
- At 2b6df40b, whose production code matches 8ffec518, the neighboring suites `native-command.status-direct`, `message-handler.preflight.acp-bindings`, `acp-bind-here.integration`, `native-command.model-picker` and `native-command.plugin-dispatch` pass 6, 2, 1, 31 and 25 tests. The whole Discord extension project, 266 files and 2604 tests, passed at 59a4746d and was not rerun.
- Test cost, as `docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md:30-36` asks. At 2b6df40b the 17 case file took 16.28, 19.62 and 20.39 s in Vitest. At 59a4746d the 15 case file took 19.15, 26.91 and 27.86 s with tests at 9 to 16 percent, under the 5 s per-file target, and one back to back pair put the 12 case da60d41 file at 15.75 s against 17.48 s for the 15 case file. CI seconds will be added after CI runs.
- At 8ffec518 `tsgo:extensions:test` passes, and `oxfmt --check` and the type-aware extensions oxlint pass on the test file. At 2b6df40b, with `--base da60d41 --no-merge-base`, the line cap, assertion safety and mock export ratchets passed, and the database worker, database dialect and timeout race ratchets, `config:docs:check` and `plugins:inventory:check` passed on the same production code with an earlier test fixture. `check:max-lines-ratchet` failed with `New max-lines suppressions are forbidden` for three `ui/` files. Those files and the max-lines baseline are byte identical to da60d41, and the check printed the same output on a da60d41 tree.

I also ran a local Gateway on da60d41 and 915f97d, and `native-command-route.ts` is byte identical to 915f97d. It used the Crabline Discord stand-in, a loopback mock model, fake tokens, and isolated home and state directories. Crabline's Discord driver does not send interactions, so a small local shim injected the slash commands and the Allow once click as `INTERACTION_CREATE` events. Native `/codex bind` and Allow once stored one `plugin-binding:codex:` row with `pluginBindingOwner: plugin` on both builds. Native `/status` and `/codex binding` then ran in that thread. `/codex detach` and the other native commands share the route code and were not run on the fixed build.

| Native command | main da60d41 | fix 915f97d |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/status` | `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` | status card with `Session: agent:main:discord:channel:<thread id>` |
| `/codex binding` | `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` | `Codex conversation binding:` block naming the bound workspace |

The main log has two `Session key does not contain an agent id` lines, one per command. The fixed build logs none, and the binding row was unchanged on both builds.

`.agents/skills/openclaw-testing/SKILL.md:51` accepts an isolated mock-Gateway harness as boundary proof when the live gaps are stated, and `.agents/skills/discord-e2e/SKILL.md:29-31` says a human slash command needs a manual Discord client.

prs.title: fix(codex): web chat messages queue behind active turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A correction sent in web chat during a busy Codex turn queues for a later turn even when both inputs have the same reply requirement. The Codex backend omitted the active attempt's accepted terminal reply expectation, so shared admission compared web chat's `result-required` input with the legacy `required` default.

## Fix

Publish `params.terminalReplyExpectation` on the existing active backend handle. Admission policy, native protocol, config and plugin SDK surfaces stay unchanged. Contributor commits and credit are preserved: Paul Bohm (@enki).

## Evidence

An isolated built Gateway on pinned main `45801179f6d99ffc1db9480320ef4bc189a4b8d7`, with the official Codex plugin and a scripted app-server fixture, reproduces the failure twice. A single owner-authenticated WebSocket sends both `chat.send` requests with identical connection, scopes, capabilities and provenance. The second request follows an ordinary native command-execution-start event. Both attempts log:

```text
steering rejected; applying follow-up policy reason=reply_expectation_mismatch disposition=followup-policy channel=webchat runId=correction activeRunId=first
```

The original run finishes with `BASE_FINAL`; no `turn/steer` occurs and the correction starts a second native turn. The no-correction control completes normally with one native turn. This isolates the reply-expectation producer from #175763: no capability normalization or companion patch is present.

The built candidate sends exactly one native `turn/steer`, receives a user-message echo with matching `clientId`, and completes the ORIGINAL run with `STEER_CONSUMED_175810`, which was absent from the initial prompt:

```json
{"method":"turn/steer","expectedTurnId":"turn-1","clientUserMessageId":"openclaw:turn-1:steer:1"}
{"type":"userMessage","clientId":"openclaw:turn-1:steer:1"}
{"runId":"first","state":"final","text":"STEER_CONSUMED_175810"}
```

All 10 focused hook cases pass. Removing the production fix makes the new consumption regression fail at admission (expected true, received false); restoring it passes. The regression uses a real controller turn and strict reply-requirement admission, not a fabricated operation or fingerprint. Other shared pending-answer normalization is deliberately excluded from that owner-level test.

Production delta: +1/-0. Test delta: +81/-0 (15 fewer lines than the contributor revision). The one production line supplies a missing accepted fact; one regression protects admission and correlated native consumption. Current main was merged to exercise the current runtime, preserving contributor commits.

A bounded real-provider gate also passes on `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` through the built Codex harness: final `P175810_LIVE_OK`, `stopReason: stop`, `replayInvalid: false`. The task-only credential was mounted read-only for that run and deleted afterward. Focused lint passes.

## Risk

Two-way door: reverting fully undoes this change; no migration or new persisted/public contract. Blast radius is steering admission for active Codex turns; a wrong published requirement could admit incompatible corrections or unnecessarily queue compatible ones.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The elapsed clock, Home conversation wrapper, IP location, and session owner chip no longer need native property adapters once all of their callers render Solid. Replace their bridge registrations with direct components, retain the existing host tags and classes, and update every production caller and coupled fixture. Remove the one-line Home runtime facade and its obsolete ambient property contracts.

The synchronous Gateway/geolocation owners, lookup cancellation and retry, visible-clock polling, Home selection/reset behavior, and retained child conversation stay unchanged. Imports replace the existing imports at the same boundaries; no route is made eager. No dependency changes.

The first CI run exposed three elapsed-clock tests still reading a removed native property and four stale `updateComplete` waits on plain Solid hosts. The repair checks visible elapsed time through hydration and settlement instead, and updates the two remaining E2E property readers. The fixed unit clock distinguishes the original user request from the parent and child start times; the resumed-run E2E assertions retain the original request clock. Replacement run 39329990213 caught a second call site still comparing rendered clock text to a timestamp; both calls now assert the same fixed 73-second display. Production source is unchanged by these test-only repairs.

Merged tested `main` commit `2650de4d` without conflicts after the replacement CI exposed a sidebar retry test failure. The identical full test, `Control UI sidebar account footer feature build E2E > labels the lifecycle status on the account icon and retries through its menu`, fails on that merge base with the same `expected 2 to be greater than 2` socket-count assertion. The mock can enter its automatic reconnect before the menu retry; the active-attempt owner preserves the connecting socket. This PR does not change the retry owner or fixture. Fresh proof after integrating main: UI typecheck and the 44 directly affected sidebar/chat tests pass. Final production counts below use this new merge base; the reduction remains 77 component lines and 92 production lines.

A later shared declaration conflict was resolved by merging `main` at `ba61d5d9`, retaining both the new tool-output tag and this PR's four leaf tags. No runtime code was manually changed. Typecheck, declaration formatting, and an independent resolution review pass on replacement head `42cd8db9`; the production reduction is unchanged.

Final exact-head [CI run 39348540071](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39348540071) on `42cd8db9` passed all 58 executed jobs (23 skipped), including every UI E2E and real-Gateway shard. Earlier retry failures are recorded above for the historical runs; the final head needs no inherited-failure exception.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Component production LOC | 1,777 → 1,700 (−77), 9 files |
| All touched production LOC | 4,257 → 4,165 (−92), 18 files |
| Test/helper LOC | 6,885 → 6,908 (+23), preserving existing assertions |
| Refactor checklist | Bridge registrations 7 → 3 (four removed); memos 114 → 114; signals 10 → 10; owner escape 1 → 1; effects, render effects, untrack, TSX listeners, queries, flush remain 0 |
| Typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:ui` and the affected UI-components/UI-chat/E2E-chat test type graphs pass, including the coupled assertion repairs |
| Focused tests | Home, elapsed clock, owner chip, chat run activity, sidebar row retention, subagent wait: 65 tests pass, default pinned Bun, one worker |
| Final `ci:full` | 58 jobs pass, 23 skipped; UI E2E and real-Gateway shards all pass |
| Production Knip / wave-zero guard | Pass |
| Scoped lint | Pass after removing an unused remount-test variable |
| Independent review | No actionable P0–P2 findings; each coupled assertion repair is reviewed separately with the full affected test as context |
| Build / strict performance | Original base (`34f6f1ba`) and implementation builds on this machine; production code is unchanged by the test-only repair; startup JS 326,385 → 326,361 B gzip (−24), 7 requests; CSS 38,500 → 38,500 B, 1 request |
| Synthetic visual proof | Four before/after states at 1280×900: exact semantic snapshots and PNG hashes; all eight images inspected |

The capture uses actual renderers and the real geolocation cache with a loopback synthetic response. It checks selection attachment/reset, retained child identity, context removal/restoration, live/frozen elapsed time, owner presence, and input clearing. ## What Problem This Solves

The Models page can stay on “Checking models…” after discovery finishes when an in-flight read republishes stale catalog facts, or a publication arrives between route preload and page mount.

Invalidate the selected agent’s catalog before replaying a coalesced publication refresh after active reads settle, using the canonical cache API. If a preloaded route still has valid credentials but its catalog has gone stale, retain the credentials and refresh only the catalog through the existing loader. No new cache, timer, polling loop, or request owner is introduced.

The publication-coalescing prerequisite from #177667 is on main. The merge resolution preserves the cache invalidation before replay and main’s typed callback contract. This is a regression repair discovered while validating the Solid cleanup lane; its production growth is recorded separately from reductions.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Active-read regression | Two cases pass: provider/auth read and explicit catalog discovery |
| Preload regression | Pass: valid cached profile stays Signed in while fresh auth is deferred; refreshed catalog renders Ready |

prs.title: refactor: remove unread private cleanup reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private cleanup and parsing paths still allocate reports that no production consumer uses: process inspection PID lists, limiter/queue snapshots, transcript repair counts and discarded-result lists, cleanup totals and timing-only workspace observations.

## What changed

Remove those fields together with their producer and forwarding chains. Transcript pairing now returns its actual frame array directly; repair still returns messages and the synthesized-result count needed for transcript persistence. Tool-call reconciliation returns the one boolean its admission owner consumes. Copilot retains actual stream/session/usage state while dropping duplicate snapshot and callback payload copies.

Keep all process ownership and pre-signal authority checks, real queue bounds and overflow warnings, transcript ordering/identity/reset rules, media cleanup claims and deletion effects, Doctor repairs and warnings, workspace work-count metrics and mailbox settlement. No public SDK, Gateway protocol, config, persisted shape, schema, retention or dependency changes.

Production diff after the narrow CI-attribution drop: **65 additions, 228 deletions; 163 net lines removed** across 34 production files in a 70-file complete cut, excluding tests, fixtures, test-support, generated files and declarations.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No runtime guard or failure-recovery mechanism is removed. Only private observations disappear. The workspace timing envelope is generated and consumed by the same revision; native capture returns only the manifest reference. Work-count and memo-performance evidence remains.

The transcript discard report had a real compaction-planning reader introduced in #134987. #167916 intentionally retired that planner; its now-orphaned reporting pipeline is removed, not the pairing/reset behavior introduced in #121028. Exact-symbol open-work searches found no activation dependency. Copilot's completed runtime introduction (#86155), private Discord client migration and ACPX wrapper internalization do not describe dormant report activation.

## Evidence

Serial canonical focused tests passed: 1,063 distinct cases across 54 ordinary files, plus 14 suppression-guard cases, reusing unchanged-input proof. Eight original explicit-root type graphs and a six-root CI-repair graph passed; narrow source-backed type-aware lint, changed-file formatting, whitespace checks and both cycle checks passed (zero runtime and Madge cycles). The changed-check planner was inspected in dry-run mode only; exact-head hosted CI supplies broad proof. Extension lint used an explicit source graph after intentionally stopping automatic broad declaration preparation, which exceeds the campaign's local budget. One test-file formatting finding was fixed mechanically.

The commit hook caught growth in two already oversized test files. Their complete cases moved to existing focused siblings without weakening assertions or changing production. The affected three ordinary files passed 64 cases; the suppression guard passed 14, and the affected graph's types plus four-file lint/format passed. The unchanged-input cycle evidence remains applicable.

Prior independent P2 review returned scoped-clean (0.91) on the full 65-file candidate, including the new private Copilot callback payload cut. Fresh full 67-file P2 review completed in eight partitions: scoped-clean (0.88), zero accepted/actionable findings; it covered both test relocations and their retained behavior. Three earlier review findings were source-rejected: same-revision workspace envelope compatibility, media effect coverage already present, and bounded Discord overflow-drain coverage already present.

Two changed E2E files and the real Gateway chat/transcript integration consumer remain hosted-only under the campaign's local proof budget. No real operator state or Gateway was touched.

## CI repair

The first exact head (`01619b198f1ba5e41e9c6ff8bbe009938c07af89`, run [39338240215](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39338240215)) exposed missed test-only consumers of the deleted media cleanup report. These failures are ours, not inherited. All scenarios remain; tests now check actual persisted records and original bytes, and the history mock returns void. The relocated MCP idle test also asserts its initial two real partitions explicitly.

| Failed job | Attribution and repair |
| --- | --- |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-large-3` (118353518847) | GC availability tests still read deleted totals; existing retention/deletion, bytes and SQL-work assertions now prove the effects directly. |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-large-13` (118353518835) | Commentary GC cases expected the removed report; now compare actual retained rows and PNG bytes during preparation and after commit. |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-small-10` (118353518820) | Media-store test read a deleted count; now verifies the managed row, original bytes and legacy orphan after scoped cleanup. |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-large-8` (118353519020) | Internal source-reply test expected pre-commit totals; now observes three real managed entries and their bytes. Its early failing assertion previously left publication downloads to race fixture cleanup. |
| `check-test-types-core-5` (118353986444) | History cursor mock returned the obsolete report; now resolves void. |
| `check-test-types-core-4` (118353986430) | Same stale availability-test property reads as the first runtime failure. |
| `check-test-types-core-2` (118353986393) | Same stale media-store property read. |
| `openclaw/ci-gate` (118361431895) | Aggregate of the seven failures above. |

The six-file focused replay passed 60 ordinary cases plus the 14-case suppression guard in 450.73 seconds, with targeted types, lint/format and both zero-cycle checks. Independent review found one valid post-cleanup coverage gap in the store test; the added real-row/original-byte checks then passed its two cases (68.14-second wrapper), and fresh P2 review returned scoped-clean (0.97). Existing real Gateway/SQLite and media-lifecycle cases retain their boundary coverage; no timeout, retry, skip or suppression changed. Broad proof remains the replacement exact-head CI; no old-head job was rerun.

## Second CI attribution and narrow drop

Run [39341922665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39341922665), exact head `29b88262eed91a6da07564f9c2dd137933730234`, completed 104 CI jobs: 72 passed, 22 skipped, 10 failed. Seven type jobs (118366227343, 118366227382, 118366227406, 118366227409, 118366227422, 118366227445, 118366227449) all report the missing `resumeStoredChatOutboxes` binding at the unchanged UI lifecycle owner. The tested merge `fd67634cbef323b6503908ed321820948a4780b5` has ordered parents main `339e1002b2ce3b3ea658b71f94d0146b57394b2b` and the PR head; that owner is byte-identical between baseline and tested merge. Main fixed the missing import in `6deac372d6436b389cf6735e424bb6b122a2175c`.

UI job 118365799949's two board failures explicitly report that same undefined binding. In UI job 118365799974, two disabled-retry failures also occur on unrelated PR #177848, run 39343156160/job 118369891459. Its other three placement failures are consistent with the missing import, but their individual cause was not conclusively established. Job 118376369508 is the aggregate failure. Security passed; no CI suite was cancelled. Two superseded non-CI context/dispatch checks have successful exact-head replacements (118365314225 and 118365314366).

The browser imports the changed Talk classifier even though these failed flows do not use Talk. Following the campaign's conservative attribution rule, this revision restores that classifier and its paired test byte-for-byte to freshly fetched main `d1e59da91a9290344c2c92c327d054d8cdf00e77`. Only this 14-line production cut is dropped; the rest of the cleanup remains. The original head is preserved on `deslop/z38-parked-talk-classifier-observations-20261015` as a superset recovery branch. The replacement exact-head run, not a rerun of old CI, is the broad gate. No local build or E2E was run, and no CI failure is relabeled green.

The two-file drop is signed at `271cea7d00ed529ea77c58bfe2319cf71e454bf0`. Fresh independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean (0.99). Its focused Talk suite passed 16 cases; the required suppression guard passed all 14 cases. Two-root targeted types, narrow type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, runtime cycles (0), and static/Madge cycles (0) passed serially with isolated runtime state. The 16-case replay is unchanged-input proof and is not added again to the earlier 1,063-case union.

prs.title: fix(sessions): backport history reply performance fixes to release/2026.10.10
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Backports upstream long-history reply performance and memory fixes onto the `release/2026.10.10` release branch.

On long conversation histories, environments running the `2026.10.10` beta series experience severe local reply latency (>2 seconds overhead per turn before model inference) due to repeated unindexed SQLite table scans and uncompacted actor context hydration. This backport resolves the issue without introducing schema, protocol, API, prompt, or configuration changes.

### Backported Changes (authored by Peter Steinberger)
- **#172892**: Retain tree fields in actor navigation instead of rich context projections.
- **#172970**: Hydrate a bounded 512-event actor tail and retain indexed durable lookup for old identities, parents, and anchors.
- **#174435**: Reuse committed model navigation and byte costs; update appended/revised pages through existing write receipts.
- **#174700**: Retain selectable context suffix and compact prefix/tool-pairing facts; use canonical reconstruction when branch/reset/compaction/restart requires it.
- **#174275**: Select indexed custom/reset/null identity candidates before exact active/payload joins in cache TTL prefix queries, eliminating repeated linear history scans.

## Evidence

### Test & Correctness Parity
- All 119 focused unit and regression tests pass across the affected areas (`src/agents/sessions`, `src/config/sessions`).
- Context reconstruction verified across private 33,000+ event test histories: provider-visible conversation histories and the 17-event production context hash match baseline identically.
- Indexed retrieval at arbitrary sequence positions (e.g. seq 1, 500, 1000, 15000, 32700) matches baseline.

### Measured Benchmarks
Across alternating baseline vs candidate runs under isolated conditions:

| History | Phase | Pairs (n) | Baseline median / p95 (ms) | Candidate median / p95 (ms) | Delta |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Large** | **Warm** | 9 | 2115.0 / 2149.4 | **332.8 / 379.8** | **-84.3%** |
| **Large** | **Cold** | 3 | 6621.8 / 6806.3 | 4803.7 / 5109.1 | -27.5% |
| **Large** | **Restart** | 3 | 5818.5 / 5824.0 | 4282.3 / 4309.7 | -26.4% |
| **Small** | **Warm** | 6 | 233.6 / 283.4 | 241.1 / 266.4 | +3.2% |
| **Small** | **Cold** | 2 | 3653.0 / 3662.8 | 3652.2 / 3718.5 | ~0% |
| **Small** | **Restart** | 2 | 3790.6 / 3795.8 | 3884.0 / 4061.3 | +2.5% |

Warm local reply overhead on long histories dropped by ~84% (from ~2,115 ms down to ~332 ms) by eliminating redundant full-history scans and query re-execution on warm turns.

## What Problem This Solves

The database worker inventory overstates six remaining native runtime call sites and contains stale caller evidence after the recent worker and conversation-binding migrations.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing deprecation and reference checks; factories and live members receive no exemption.

No defensive runtime checks are removed and no runtime edge cases are newly accepted. The retained limitation is the inventory's documented static reachability scope; a filename alone is not proof of worker-only execution.
