prs.title: fix(config): accept web search provider ids that differ only in case
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`tools.web.search.provider` is matched case-insensitively at runtime, but the config validator compared the authored string verbatim, so a correctly spelled provider id written with different casing was a **fatal** config error:

```
$ cat openclaw.json
{"tools":{"web":{"search":{"enabled":true,"provider":"Brave"}}}}

$ openclaw config validate
  - tools.web.search.provider: unknown web_search provider: Brave
```

The runtime owner lowercases the configured value before matching manifest ids (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`: `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(search.provider)` then `provider.id === raw`), so `Brave`, `BRAVE`, and padded spellings all resolve to the same `brave` entry. Only the validator disagreed, and because config validation is fatal the user loses the whole config (every unrelated setting in that file stops loading) over a value the resolver would have used.

Same class and same shape as #176990 (`talk.provider` mixed-case keys), which landed this week.

## Fix

Compare the normalized value against the same ids the resolver matches, instead of matching the raw text:

```ts
const normalizedProviderId = normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(trimmed);
if (activeProviderIds.includes(normalizedProviderId)) return;
...
resolveWebSearchInstallCatalogEntries().find((entry) => entry.provider.id === normalizedProviderId);
```

Deliberately does **not** loosen matching beyond runtime parity: the runtime lowercases the configured value only and compares ids exactly, so the validator mirrors that rule and nothing else. Manifest ids stay the authority — this does not accept aliases, prefixes, or ids that the resolver would not resolve. Error messages still print the authored text (`unknown web_search provider: Brave`).

One file of production code (+8/−2), one new test case in the existing config suite. No new option, no config surface, no state.

## Evidence

Environment: Node v24.18.0, repo source tree run through its own CLI entry (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts …`), isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` containing only:

```json
{"tools":{"web":{"search":{"enabled":true,"provider":"Brave"}}}}
```

Base tree = `dd4eff8648a` (production files restored from `up-main`, test file kept). Head = `c0c1eaed902` (same patch rebased onto current `main` `97b01621f9f`; diff unchanged at 2 files, +16/−2).

| Cell | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openclaw config validate` | **exit 1**, `- tools.web.search.provider: unknown web_search provider: Brave` | **exit 0**, `Config valid: /tmp/oc-ws-cap/openclaw.json` |
| `openclaw infer web providers --json` | **exit 1**, `OpenClaw config is invalid`, no provider selected | **exit 0**, `{"available":true,"configured":false,"selected":true,"id":"brave","envVars":["BRAVE_API_KEY"]}` |
| `pnpm test src/config/config.web-search-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | **1 failed / 7 passed** (`expected false to be true`) | **8 passed** |

The second row is the runtime cross-check: on the head tree the CLI loads the same config and the resolver selects `brave`, which is the entry the validator previously refused to let it see. On the base tree the config never gets that far — validation is fatal before the resolver runs.

The new case asserts `ok` **and** an empty `warnings` array for `Brave`, `BRAVE`, and `" brave "`, so a future change that silently downgrades these to warnings (which would have the same practical effect of surfacing a config the user did not write) fails the test.

Timings on this head (`c0c1eaed902`, Node v24.18.0): the config suite is transform-bound — base-production run `205.7 s` test / `220.7 s` wall, head run `152.9 s` test / `167.9 s` wall. CI is the broad proof.

### Upgrade cell (published driver → candidate)

Driver = published npm tarball `openclaw@2026.10.5` (`OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)`), installed fresh in an isolated prefix. Candidate = this head `c0c1eaed902`, run from source through `src/entry.ts`. Both sides used a fresh, separate `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; the config files were byte-identical before the runs (`cmp` identical, sha256 `dbb2d56c1eac09047805f38bb6b9343d14ef3fbab27c715d8fa96760d128aeb7`):

```json
{
  "tools": { "web": { "search": { "enabled": true, "provider": "Brave" } } },
  "agents": { "defaults": { "workspace": "/tmp/ws" } },
  "gateway": { "port": 12345 },
  "logging": { "level": "debug" },
  "channels": { "telegram": { "enabled": false } }
}
```

| Driver | `openclaw config validate` | Exit | Config sha256 before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| published 2026.10.5 (`1b58cb9`) | `- tools.web.search.provider: unknown web_search provider: Brave` | **1** | `dbb2d56c…aeb7` → `dbb2d56c…aeb7` (unchanged) |
| candidate `c0c1eaed902` | `Config valid: /tmp/oc-upgrade-post/openclaw.json` | **0** | `dbb2d56c…aeb7` → `dbb2d56c…aeb7` (unchanged) |

After the candidate run the file is still byte-identical (`diff -u` empty, no rewrite, no dropped keys), and each unrelated setting reads back: `agents.defaults.workspace = /tmp/ws`, `gateway.port = 12345`, `logging.level = debug`, `channels.telegram.enabled = false` (plus `tools.web.search.provider = Brave`). On the same candidate state, `infer web providers --json` marks `brave` as the only entry with `"selected": true`, so the resolver consumes the same value the validator now accepts.

Update mechanics: config validation runs in the CLI process that is already running, so upgrading changes validation behavior for an existing config without rewriting it — no migration step and no file change, which is exactly what the two sha256 rows show.

prs.title: fix(auth): keep Codex disclosure checks off the Gateway thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex account usage, diagnostics uploads, and supervision could synchronously read auth-profile SQLite rows on the Gateway thread while checking authority at disclosure or dispatch.

## User Impact

These paths retain their final credential and account checks while reading persisted auth profiles through the existing worker. A credential revoked during preparation still prevents disclosure. There are no schema, configuration, retention, or upgrade changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The auth-profile runtime carries admitted sources into a scoped effect reader. Each fresh read groups the selected agent and shared sources into one state-worker request, bypassing runtime snapshots and cached rows. The existing credential-publication, receipt, and revision owners supply the zero-SQL check immediately before the effect. PostgreSQL reads use one snapshot per store without the writer advisory lock. Writes, eager lock ordering, cross-store commit order, and durability are unchanged.

Codex performs the fresh dispatch check after client acquisition and awaited sandbox checks, immediately before physical dispatch. Personal accounts retain their published-credential authority and explicit account selection. The private synchronous effect-selection path and its callers are removed. An accepted effect is not retrospectively rejected during reader cleanup.

The four native write/transaction kernels remain necessary for worker execution, CLI maintenance/rollback, and the published synchronous SDK through December 31, 2026. Remove their MAIN reachability with that SDK in the first January 2027 stable release; retain the caller ratchet meanwhile. This PR removes bundled synchronous disclosure and conditional-convergence routes, rather than all six native expressions in the static inventory.

## Evidence

Focused regressions exercise real auth storage and writers, snapshot bypass, one worker request for selected sources, and zero Gateway-thread SQL at usage and diagnostics boundaries. The four usage/diagnostics cases fail on the base specifically at the MAIN-SQL assertions. The stronger revocation regression does `read -> await revoke -> assertCurrent` with no intervening reread. Convergence, rollback, personal-account authority, request authority, and supervision are covered.

Two Codex review rounds completed. The first caught an asynchronous dispatch guard that the usage helper was not forwarding; the helper and regression were repaired. The second found no actionable P0–P2 issue. Later changes restore an explicit compatibility binding, shorten an equivalent publication wrapper, and strengthen the existing revocation regression.

Final head `cc47b5e628fe757f4994dac0bfd4cc96a5ebba19` repairs the one original CI failure: compatibility tracing could not follow the loader through the object-rest binding. The full database-worker ratchet now passes locally (T1 178→178, compatibility 10→10), without increasing an allowance. The no-reread revision regression passes for both stores. Follow-up verification passed 22 store cases and 292 additional cases across 27 consumers, type-aware core lint, core typechecking, format, and the line-cap ratchet. prs.title: fix(anthropic): stop reporting success after OpenClaw MCP startup fails
prs.body:
Closes #176138

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Claude CLI turns reporting success and retaining a reusable process after startup explicitly reports that the OpenClaw MCP server is not connected.

## User Impact

Users now receive a concrete startup error instead of a successful turn missing its Gateway tools. The failed process is retired and joined, so the next turn starts a fresh process. A connected OpenClaw server remains reusable even if an unrelated optional MCP server failed; initialization records without an OpenClaw entry retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI runtime previously read `system/init` capabilities but ignored MCP server status. It now sends a non-connected `openclaw` entry through the existing session-close owner before accepting more output. This preserves the established cleanup and per-turn authority paths. It adds no timeout override, automatic replay, dependency, or permission change.

## Evidence

- On upstream `66485231`, the two new subprocess regressions for `failed` and `pending` MCP startup incorrectly resolved with success. With this fix, the actual executor/stdio transport rejects, unregisters the session, waits for the original PID to exit, and starts a different PID at turn 1 for the next request.
- The new four-case suite passes, including connected-server reuse and initialization without an OpenClaw entry. It takes 27.24 seconds wall time including worker preparation, about 1.7 seconds executing tests.
- `pnpm test:extension anthropic --maxWorkers=1`: **415 passed, 1 skipped** across 36 files, **53.81 seconds wall time**. The existing Linux-only OOM-score case is skipped on macOS. Coverage includes CLI protocol, transport shutdown, permissions, steering, background work and credential cleanup.
- Extension production and test typechecks (`pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`), targeted repository lint, four-file formatting and `git diff --check` all passed.
- OpenClaw's isolated `autoreview` with the complete runtime, transport, process owner and fixture context found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The independent review was static; the reviewer did not execute tests.

### Review follow-up (26931797)

The startup error now tells the operator that the CLI process was retired and that retrying the request starts a fresh process, addressing the P3 recovery-guidance finding.

Executed the production executor/stdio transport with **real installed Claude Code 2.1.278**, an isolated temporary HOME/config/workspace, a real loopback HTTP MCP server, and a loopback Anthropic-protocol response stub. With MCP returning 503, Claude Code reported `openclaw` failed and OpenClaw rejected the turn with the recovery instruction; PID 48912 had exited and the live handle was absent. After restoring the local MCP endpoint, the next request started PID 48932, returned `offline-probe-ok`, and left a healthy idle handle. Both model responses came from the local stub; no paid/provider request, user credential, or real Gateway state was used. This was a one-off runtime probe rather than a new dependency on Claude Code in the default suite.

The Anthropic lane including that probe passed **416 tests, 1 skipped, 37 files**; the four permanent MCP lifecycle cases pass with the new error text. Changed-file formatting and diff checks pass. This follow-up changes only the error text and its existing assertion; it adds no persisted configuration/state or lifecycle logic.

### Captured runtime proof (26931797)

The following excerpts are from the retained output of the real-Claude run described above, not a simulated terminal transcript. The test used the production `collectClaudeCli` executor/stdio path with the installed Claude Code binary; only the HTTP MCP/API responses were supplied locally. The first request received HTTP 503 from MCP. After the rejection and process-exit assertions passed, the same harness restored MCP and submitted the next request. No provider credentials or external model API were used.

Captured test command and output (unrelated test output omitted):

```text
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-extension.mts anthropic --maxWorkers=1
 ✓ |extension-providers| extensions/anthropic/cli-runtime.real-mcp-probe.test.ts > rejects real failed MCP startup and recovers with a new real Claude process 1873ms

 Test Files  37 passed (37)
      Tests  416 passed | 1 skipped (417)
   Start at  01:16:25
   Duration  61.82s (tests 56%, transform 36%, import 6%, setup 1%)
```

Captured JSON written by that test after the failed-process exit, absent-session, different-next-PID, successful-result and idle-session assertions all passed:

```json
{
  "cliVersion": "2.1.278",
  "failedPid": 48912,
  "nextPid": 48932,
  "rejection": "Error: Claude Code started without the OpenClaw MCP server (status failed). The CLI process was retired; retry the request to start a fresh process.",
  "messageRequests": 2,
  "requests": [
    "HEAD /api/hello",
    "POST /mcp",
    "POST /mcp",
    "POST /v1/messages?beta=true",
    "HEAD /api/hello",
    "POST /mcp",
    "POST /mcp",
    "POST /mcp",
    "GET /mcp",
    "POST /mcp",
    "POST /v1/messages?beta=true"
  ],
  "recovered": true,
  "realProviderRequests": false,
  "isolatedHome": true
}
```

`messageRequests: 2` counts requests served by the local Anthropic-protocol stub. `requests` contains paths only; no endpoint addresses, credentials or user configuration are included. The temporary probe was removed from the published tree after execution, so the default test suite does not require a locally installed Claude Code binary. This demonstrates CLI startup failure/recovery and process replacement, rather than a live Gateway deployment or a real model response.

Stable-release configuration compatibility was also executed: the official npm `openclaw@2026.10.4` package was verified against its published SHA-512 integrity, then its real `config patch --stdin` and `config validate --json` commands produced and validated an isolated existing configuration. At exact PR head `26931797`, the production config readers accepted that file and preserved the workspace, primary model, alias, `claude-cli` runtime selection and tool-denial settings. The original configuration bytes remained unchanged. This covers existing stable-release configuration; it does not claim a running Gateway or state-database upgrade.

Local validation used Node 24.21.0 and pinned pnpm 12.11.1. A real Gateway handshake timeout, native Windows run and full repository suite were not executed. The CI gate and associated applicable checks have passed on `26931797`. The completed bot re-review accepted the captured runtime proof, reported no actionable findings and marked this head ready for maintainer review. Human maintainer review and merge remain pending.

The agent avatar picker mirrors the overlay owner's open state through a manual redraw subscription and writable signal.

## User Impact

Full CI exposed a missing focus precondition in the native overlay presentation test. Its Tab branch now awaits focus on the submenu action before sending Tab. It does not force focus or weaken the dismissal/modal assertions. The test gains three lines; production remains −9.

Run [39333476193](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39333476193), at `4e68ab3be69090a1759127b2a2682b3566750109`, passes the avatar tests and fails three test names:

Both device cases fail during identity setup with `DeviceIdentityStorageError`: the custom database path is no longer accepted; the error requires `<client-root>/client/credentials.sqlite` and `env.OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Both exact test names reproduce the same failure in one run on merge base `af42ae0c190f608dcb1bb375212245ca54c6198f`. No device implementation or test changes are included here.

The menu case passes once on the same exact base. The scheduled-main UI unit shard also passes, so it was not waived as inherited. Source inspection found that the fixture awaited visibility and hit testing, while the Tab handler requires focus inside the menu. The added awaited assertion checks that precondition without manufacturing it. The CI log lacked active-element evidence; delayed focus is a hypothesis, not a claimed proven production root cause.

Earlier quota-status failures were not a matching inherited set. After their main-owned repair #177593 landed, main was merged and all three passed in run [39320548351](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39320548351). That run failed only core type/lint diagnostics matching scheduled main [39320267109](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39320267109). Native admin recovery stopped before dispatch on UNKNOWN mergeability and shared quota. Main was merged again to force recomputation and incorporate the core repair. No unlanded branch was merged, no main commits were replayed, and the confirmed-cancelled auto request has not been re-armed.

## Current-head inherited failures

Current head `d4d1d96559aeb2a0a78c049d2101c6ca927805f2` passes all UI unit shards and selected static checks in [39340667580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39340667580). The three retry tests pass on older merge base `af42ae0c`; those passes are not inherited-failure evidence. Its sibling tests close the pending mock attempt before Retry; these fixtures omit that precondition. Scheduled main provides the exact matching-name evidence.

prs.title: feat(channels): show restart recovery attempts in status
prs.body:
Closes #133064

## What Problem This Solves

openclaw channels status shows whether each account is running and connected, but it drops the Gateway's existing reconnectAttempts fact. During recovery, a stopped account can therefore look unexplained unless the operator switches to JSON and inspects the raw snapshot.

Issue triage confirmed this is source-reproducible, owner-local, and queueable: the Gateway already returns the fact, while the human formatter never reads it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing channel-status formatter now appends restarts:<count> for finite positive integer attempt counts. Zero, absent, negative, fractional, and non-numeric values remain quiet.

This uses the Gateway snapshot as the sole source of truth. It does not change restart policy, retry budgets, account state, probing, persistence, JSON output, or plugin behavior.

Existing-solutions preflight: --json plus an external query is the only built-in workaround. A plugin or library cannot repair a missing projection in OpenClaw's core CLI formatter, so the narrow formatter owner is the appropriate boundary.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish an ordinary stopped account from one actively progressing through channel recovery or carrying a terminal restart-attempt count, without leaving the normal status command.

The count describes the current snapshot's recovery attempts; it is not a lifetime total or a remaining-budget calculation.

## Evidence

### One-worker test cost and current-head CI — October 9, 2026

PR head `b6249371e03cf535daeaa461e09bf75ca78400f6`, tree `19017be7a707067aad69c40d06a712e98cbee2c1`. A clean isolated checkout with its own frozen dependencies ran the prescribed command once on Node 24.16.0 / pnpm 12.5.1:

```sh
pnpm test src/commands/channels.surfaces-signal-runtime-errors-channels-status-output.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

All **9 tests passed**, exit 0. The local cold run took **124.32s** wall time; the native wrapper reported **123.44s**, and Vitest reported **116.63s** with 94% transform, 3% import, and 2% worker time. Native preparation recorded a compiler-cache miss after 14.728s and a completed generation in 85.785s. These are preparation and complete invocation measurements, not 124 seconds of assertions. The nine displayed per-case timings sum to **155ms**; the added restart-count case reports **7ms**. Those rounded case timings exclude the complete file lifecycle and are not a before/after benchmark.

The existing [CI run 37732331059](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37732331059), targeting the same PR head, completed successfully. Its checkout/workflow SHA was GitHub merge commit `8f216173166177c3d7d4206baf2ec75c33a5570f` (PR head merged into base `19435cb4e0339c2d3b1f6f54765ce8b9b10fe562`); this is CI merge-checkout evidence, distinct from the local exact-head run. Its [changed-1 job 113164399191](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37732331059/job/113164399191) records this exact file with inner parallelism 1: **9 tests passed**, **4.84s** Vitest duration and **6.23s** native-wrapper duration. The displayed case timings total **27ms**, including **2ms** for the restart-count case. The job as a whole took **143s** (05:27:20–05:29:43 UTC on October 8); its 86-second test step includes other files. Neither is this file's execution time.

The changed assertion stays in the existing formatter suite, uses its fake clock, and adds no process, polling, real sleep, or external service. CI's Vitest file duration is 4.84s against the five-second test-time target; the complete native-wrapper invocation is 6.23s. The long local cold wall reflects existing import/compiler preparation. Closes #133227

## What Problem This Solves

Vault and 1Password human-readable SecretRef status commands did not confirm the selected provider alias. Operators with custom or multiple aliases had to repeat the command with --json to inspect that existing canonical field.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each plugin now prints the providerAlias already returned by the shared inspectProvider owner, after its JSON early return. Both Commander tests configure two providers and explicitly select a non-default alias. Shared selection, ambiguity checks, readiness inspection, and credential handling remain unchanged.

Existing-solutions preflight: JSON exposes the field but does not make the documented default text command self-confirming. No additional plugin, configuration, or library is needed. The existing Vault --provider-alias documentation remains accurate.

## User Impact

Vault status prints `Provider alias: corp-vault`; 1Password SecretRef status prints `Provider alias: corp-onepassword` when those aliases are selected. This is one additive text line in each owner. prs.title: fix(skills): Workshop reviews fail for Codex-backed agents
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes automatic Skill Workshop reviews using the embedded OpenClaw runtime after a Codex-backed conversation, which can fail when the Gateway does not own that runtime's inference credentials.

## User Impact

Eligible conversations can run background learning through the runtime that completed the foreground work, without adding review turns to the conversation or modifying its transcript.

Attached native sessions with a separate credential-owning connection remain unsupported for automatic reviews; they fail closed and can still use foreground learning. Codex has no equivalent to the embedded runtime's 2,048-output-token cap: its two-minute deadline and eight-tool-call budget are not a token or spending cap. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the completed runtime into the existing private-review runner and retain the existing model/auth route, source-authority checks, cancellation, foreground yielding, restricted `skill_workshop` surface, and no-retry policy.

Codex reviews use a fresh ephemeral thread with the bounded source excerpt, without saving a conversation binding or running managed native hooks. The native integration also exposed two prerequisites fixed here: preserving the detached excerpt allowance and using the supplied configuration for native execution-policy checks.

The scope is configured-runtime support, not supervised-connection inheritance or a new runtime framework. Existing routing, admission, tool-budget, and context owners are reused; the hardcoded embedded-runtime override is removed. Most added code is regression coverage and the real-native fixture, which caught evidence loss that helper tests missed.

## Evidence

- Final focused run: **81/81 tests passed** across native integration, runtime setup, model/auth ownership, and execution-policy authority checks.
- The real repository-pinned Codex binary, with a private home and a synthetic loopback Responses endpoint, receives recent user/tool/assistant evidence and only `skill_workshop`. Oversized old history and foreground/workspace/client-tool instructions are excluded. Source transcript and durable session rows stay unchanged; no native rollout remains after joined shutdown.
- Earlier affected suites passed for review restrictions and budgets, source revocation, prompt-prefix stability, isolated Gateway review/notice/history behavior, detached lifecycle, managed-hook restrictions, and existing native/incognito behavior. Unchanged-input results were reused.
- Red/green regressions cover detached lifecycle, explicit-configuration policy, and the detached context allowance.
- **10 final static checks passed**, covering targeted typechecks, lint, formatting, plugin import boundaries, and whitespace. Build prerequisites passed through the test runner.
- Publication checks caught growth in an oversized binding-test file. Its existing coverage was preserved, and the detached managed-hook regression was moved to the smaller restricted-continuation suite. Both affected suites then passed **123/123 tests** in 31.52 seconds wall time, with extension-test typechecking, targeted lint, and formatting passing again. Production code was unchanged. Hosted CI timing is not yet available.

**Review status:** draft pending completion of the repository's Auto Review check. The isolated reviewer failed before producing a report with OpenAI Responses authentication errors (HTTP 401), including after the supported process-local credential-selection recovery. This is reviewer unavailability, not a clean review or a code finding.

**Coverage gap:** the native protocol proof uses synthetic provider responses, not live-provider authentication. The isolated remote attempt never obtained a host and was stopped; no live credential staging or provider call occurred. Deployed account/connection behavior remains unverified. Broad repository coverage belongs to PR CI.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #177859. Operators cannot select declared private Proxmox Crabbox workers because OpenClaw always forces public transport and rejects Tailscale metadata.

## User Impact

Adds explicit `settings.network: "tailscale"` for cold native Proxmox Linux workers, with private transport throughout provisioning and lifecycle inspection. Public remains the default and still rejects Tailscale objects, including disabled objects. AWS provisioning still requires no instance profile. Warm/prepared workers, reserves, desktops and protected setup secrets are unavailable for this opt-in.

Requires the native device-receipt/routing contract in openclaw/crabbox#2910 (current source contract inspected at `5278730354c241ef70d71badbee410bf6f84d4dd`); published Crabbox 0.78.1 does not supply it. This PR does not install either runtime, configure Serve, grant Proxmox permissions, or deploy a broker. Live VM/device cleanup and dispatch remain operator validation after coherent deployment. No merge or deployment is requested here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing plugin owns the setting, command context and admission decision. Allocation/run carry the explicit network and join policy; inspect retains private routing; heartbeat renews the already admitted lease with its supported provider/ID/idle-timeout/JSON arguments; admission requires matching lease identity, ready/error-free/enabled metadata, CGNAT IPv4 and actual device identity. Crabbox owns generation-bound receipt persistence, immutable fixed-lease replay, QGA-pinned SSH and network-independent stop. Normal authenticated OpenClaw node enrollment is reused. There is no public/LAN retry and no new state owner or protocol.

Simplification: one shared network-argument builder and one inspection network-policy check replace hardcoded call-site choices; AWS provisioning admission stays at its existing boundary. Existing public warm-image keys remain unchanged. Necessary growth versus base: production +130/-23 lines, tests +332 lines plus one existing database-worker lane entry, docs +52/-1 lines (no schema/store changes).

## Evidence

- Red-before: the added provider/profile cases failed on base `45801179f6d` at the missing network-setting contract.
- Final private-network/profile proof: **44 passed**, two files, **37.44s wall** including cold database-worker compilation (test execution below one second per file). The sibling suite preserves the existing database-worker process policy and avoids growth in the oversized provider suite.
- Reused unchanged production-path sibling proof: provider, cancellation, enrollment/replay and preparation **199 passed / 10 existing platform-dependent skips**, six files, **99.82s wall** before the test-only extraction. Command, inspect, heartbeat and lifetime coverage also passed (**190 tests**, six files, **17.18s wall**). These runs overlap; counts are not additive. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Scoped Crabbox production and test typechecks; touched production/test lint; format, `git diff --check`, line-cap ratchet, documentation lint/config examples and **15,729 internal links** pass.
- Initial independent isolated Codex review was clean at `780a0f9`. Fresh whole-patch P0–P2 review of the repaired candidate is complete: it supports the lifecycle/catalog repairs. Its sole remaining desktop suggestion was declined because `parseCrabboxProfile` already rejects Proxmox desktops through `CRABBOX_DESKTOP_PROVIDERS` before private admission (`crabbox-worker-profile.ts:206`). No accepted remaining finding. Reviewer did not execute project code or verify live connectivity.
- Synthetic external-process fixtures prove admission, consistent private argv, readiness waiting, wrong/malformed metadata rejection, fresh-provider replay, fixed-policy conflict handling, cancellation custody and exact-lease stop. They do not prove native connectivity, daemon dispatch, broker issuance or live VM/device cleanup.

## Hosted review follow-up

At `4952840ffb14a6392aa923443aad54c3ed1378aa`:

- Fixed [P1 lifecycle policy drift](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177863#discussion_r4320154758): definitive parsed network-policy rejection now stops renewal and returns `unknown`, allowing the existing Gateway owner to withdraw dedicated attestation and request teardown. Transport failures remain exceptions; provision admission and cleanup remain strict.
- Fixed [P2 unsupported private placement choices](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177863#discussion_r4320154765): private catalog projections expose Linux only, without mutating the shared public catalog.
- Red-before repair: **3 failed / 18 passed**, at the expected lifecycle-status and OS-catalog assertions. Green-after repair: **122 passed**, four files / two owning shards, **11.61s wall**. Includes active renewal cessation, transport-uncertainty preservation, same-lease teardown, private catalog projection and unchanged public choices.
- Scoped production/test typechecks, touched lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet and normal commit hooks pass. No checks bypassed.

Prior-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39346966375) for `4952840ffb14a6392aa923443aad54c3ed1378aa` is **not green**. At 2026-10-20 00:29:27Z: 16 main jobs passed, 26 skipped, ten queued with no runner assigned (`blacksmith-16vcpu-ubuntu-2404`, `runner_id: 0`, queued since 00:21:21Z); no main jobs were still executing and no failure was reported. This is an external runner-assignment block, not passing proof for the queued jobs. Exact-head Security Review, Node Runtime Conformance, Scaffold Validation, OpenGrep and Workflow Sanity passed. CodeQL/Periphery scan jobs were scope-skipped, not scan passes. No observed workflow-approval prompt, no rerun/runner-policy change/bypass. Prior-head results are not current-head proof. The earlier `780a0f9` run encountered unassigned Blacksmith runners, later began progressing, and had no observed failure before this substantive repair push. No CI-approval bypass or own merge.



## Heartbeat CLI contract repair

Head `795f9e4844140c486ebac579c5599720d6c16231` fixes the P1 private-renewal failure: Crabbox heartbeat has no `--network` flag, so the prior private argv failed before backend access and could not refresh idle expiry. Removed that flag only from heartbeat; allocation, inspect and run keep their supported network-selection flags. Private admission still requires fresh inspection and bound device identity; definitive drift still withdraws active status and stops renewal. The lifecycle/catalog review repairs remain intact.

- Strengthened the existing provider-boundary drift regression with a strict parser fixture for the actual `internal/cli/heartbeat.go` options at Crabbox `5278730`. It validates provider, exact lease ID, idle timeout and JSON before recording renewal. It proves initial private renewal, continued renewal under transport uncertainty, and cessation after definitive drift; it no longer equates an attempted command with successful renewal.
- Red on `4952840`: zero successful renewals / one expected regression failure, 20 passes. Green after the one-line production fix: **122 tests / four files**, **18.81s wall** across two owning shards (14.81s database-worker shard, 0.579s profile shard; individual test execution below one second per file). Hosted CI seconds for the new head are pending.
- Actual Crabbox `5278730` CLI parser boundary check also passes (1.297s package time): old argv yields `flag provided but not defined: -network`; fixed argv passes parsing and reaches the intentionally unconfigured Proxmox backend. This is parser compatibility proof, not live backend renewal or connectivity.
- Scoped production and Crabbox test typechecks, touched lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting, diff/line-cap checks and normal commit hooks pass. No dependencies, CLI-wide flags, policy guard or live runtime changed.
- Fresh isolated whole-patch P0–P2 review completed **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings. Reviewed staged bytes were committed unchanged. Static review did not execute project code or verify live counterpart integration.

The `795f9e4` heartbeat-only head was superseded by the final private-attestation repair below; its CI is prior-head evidence. No merge, deployment or live mutation was performed.


## Final successful-invalid private attestation fencing

Current source head `10bb769a218b95c166211ef3884042133d9efc99` also fixes [the newly reported malformed-attestation P2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177863#discussion_r4320243583) and the identity sibling found in fresh review. Successful private inspection output that cannot be parsed or names a different lease now uses the existing policy-error type; lifecycle returns `unknown`, stops renewal and withdraws dedicated admission through the existing Gateway owner. Failed commands and transport observations remain exceptions; public parsing/identity errors, strict provisioning cleanup and Linux-only placement remain intact. No new state or guard bypass.

- Malformed metadata red proof: one expected failure / 21 passes on `795f9e4`. Fresh review then found the identity sibling; its regression failed separately (one expected failure / 22 passes) before repair.
- Final focused proof: **124 passed / four files**, **13.14s wall** across two owning shards (9.88s database-worker shard, 0.551s profile shard; each file's test execution below one second). New-head hosted CI seconds are pending. Prior proof counts overlap and are not additive.
- Scoped production and Crabbox test typechecks, touched lint with zero warnings/errors, format, diff/line-cap checks and normal commit hooks pass on the final candidate. Actual Crabbox CLI parser compatibility proof above is reused because heartbeat argv is unchanged by this follow-up.
- Fresh isolated whole-patch P0–P2 review after both repairs is **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The staged reviewed bytes were committed unchanged. Review was static; no live integration claim.

At 2026-10-20 00:39:01Z, exact-head [main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39348814178) is `pending` with no jobs exposed yet; [Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39348806219) is `in_progress` (resolve passed; actual review running). No failing result is reported, but this head is **not CI-green**. The available new-head data does not establish a sustained runner-assignment block; the older Blacksmith queue remains prior-head evidence. No extended unchanged-CI wait, rerun, cancellation, runner-policy change, bypass or merge. Parent retains final CI/independent QA and deployment gates. No deployment, live lease or access-configuration mutation.

prs.title: refactor(ui): share activity and session input validators
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated activity and session-input validation carries duplicate checks for shared schema shapes.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Canonical schemas, exported validators, accepted and rejected payloads, and lazy module boundaries stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing shared TypeBox compiler introduced for approvals in #177791 within these two groups, then regenerate their standalone modules. Other generated groups change only compiler temporary names. There are no new dependencies, runtime imports, state owners, or test edits.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI typecheck | Pass |
| Existing generated-validator test file, default pinned Bun, one worker | 23 passed |
| Canonical schema / captured base / candidate comparison | All 1,990 cases agree across 15 validators |
| Other generated groups | AST-equivalent after normalizing compiler temporary names |
| Focused lint | Pass |
| Production Knip | Pass |
| Solid guard | Pass; all touched-file idiom counts remain zero |
| Independent P0–P3 review | Complete, no actionable findings |
| Base and head UI builds + strict performance | Pass |
| Startup JavaScript | 326,138 → 326,146 B gzip (+8 B, within the 64 B build-variance allowance); 7 requests unchanged |
| Startup CSS | 38,564 B gzip; 1 request, unchanged |

Production LOC across the six changed files is **3,067 → 2,958 (−109)**. The UI scope contributes **2,677 → 2,569 (−108)**; the generator is **390 → 389 (−1)**. Activity shrinks by 34 lines and session-input by 74. These generated files have no max-lines baseline entries to lower.

No screenshots are needed: this changes generated validation code only, with no markup, CSS, routes, host tags, or selectors. Broad suites run in PR CI with `ci:full` because these validators have many consumers.

## Runtime tradeoff

This is a code-reduction change, not a runtime-speed claim. Five interleaved samples of 20,000 checks after warm-up measured the following medians on the same host. The generated candidates are byte-identical to the measured candidates, and the base schemas/generator match the measured base.

| Validator | Base → shared (ms per 20,000 checks) |
| --- | --- |
| Activity item | 1.357 → 1.615 |
| Observer digest | 1.778 → 1.925 |
| Narration | 1.124 → 1.206 |
| Reaction | 1.140 → 3.666 |
| Runtime restriction | 3.497 → 3.740 |
| Goal update | 3.361 → 2.172 |
| Goal clear | 1.448 → 1.451 |
| Repository | 0.497 → 0.553 |
| Voice change | 0.323 → 1.798 |

The largest measured increase is about 0.13 microseconds per check. That small local cost is accepted for removing duplicate generated code; these numbers do not measure an end-to-end UI flow.


## Inherited CI failures

Run [39345270291](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39345270291) tested merge `b79ab89cdf71a9d2650decf9dc675dd903467e47` with main parent `10049a6e9d6115d5b9d23851b378a175a70e5960`. Every selected job except two UI E2E shards passed or intentionally skipped, including security and both real-Gateway shards. The three failing names are:

- `Control UI module boundaries > Gateway recovery while a module is unavailable > keeps recovery available after a sidebar download failure at 390px`
- `Control UI module boundaries > Gateway recovery while a module is unavailable > keeps recovery available after a sidebar download failure at 1280px`
- `Control UI sidebar account footer feature build E2E > labels the lifecycle status on the account icon and retries through its menu`

All three also fail in the latest completed scheduled main run [39342008977](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39342008977). The two buttons remain disabled/busy and the footer socket count remains unchanged because the offline mock leaves an active connection attempt pending after the Retry feedback change in #177690. A focused reproduction on main `08d04a9d7b97e50849ba089c3837d2e1c3c4f7fd` fails all three identically. The test fixtures have since been repaired on main in `92bd521fabf` and `b7d10aac604`.

Nine relevant test and retry implementation blobs are identical between this PR's tested merge and its main parent. No retry implementation changes are part of this PR. The native inherited-failure route uses the exact-name evidence above; this run is not described as green.

prs.title: feat: enable native plugin UI without a Labs opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installed native plugin interfaces still require a separate Labs opt-in even though the same infrastructure already serves bundled plugins.

## User Impact

Enabled user-installed plugins can show native UI by default, without a Labs detour. Existing explicit `gateway.controlUi.experimental.customPlugins: false` values remain off; there is no new configuration key or migration.

**Upgrade behavior:** when the key is omitted, already-enabled plugins may begin loading their native browser UI after upgrading. Native UI is trusted, unsandboxed code running with each signed-in viewer's Gateway permissions. Existing authentication, scope, provenance, asset grants, and lifecycle checks remain unchanged.

Install surfaces explain that plugins may include browser code; installed details and existing enable reviews identify native UI from the inspected manifest. No extra modal, checkbox, or permission gate is added. All plugin APIs retain their existing experimental API-stability policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move browser-execution disclosure to ordinary plugin installation and enablement instead of hiding the whole capability behind Labs. Keep the existing advanced opt-out for compatibility, and share the effective default between admission and browser refresh notifications. Update authoring guidance, agent instructions, and recovery hints so they no longer direct users to the removed switch.

## Evidence

- Red-before-change regressions for the Labs row, native asset default, and disclosures; green on this candidate.
- 140 graduation tests across 9 files passed (105.41s wrapper wall time, including compilation). Focused metadata tests (60 across 3 files) and disclosure tests (57 across 4 files) also passed; CI seconds are not yet available.
- Real isolated Gateway: explicit false stays off; clearing the override restores native UI and notifies connected clients without restart or backend replacement. Existing asset authentication and revocation tests remain green.
- Actual Chromium Control UI with synthetic Gateway fixtures: native/backend-only enable flows, persistent details, direct catalog install disclosures, unchanged install requests, and Labs removal passed.
- Core/UI typechecks, targeted lint, CSS lint, formatting, i18n verification, Swift/Kotlin protocol checks, docs examples, and 15,727 internal documentation links passed.
- Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

**Packaged upgrade qualification: FAILED.** [Package Acceptance run 39346958288](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39346958288) resolved and validated the exact PR source `3ba3b394ca7bc0b65801fdfed66c85c602263ce8` (package SHA-256 `10dde0d358fb5eff7999a61a31c2ecef7e7b22790586a7bf26919c5559ae0eef`). Package integrity, npm install acceptance, and image preparation passed. The selected `published-upgrade-survivor` lane from published stable `openclaw@2026.10.5` failed in `update-candidate`, at Doctor's `state-schema` step: **“SQLite migration source changed after update capture.”** Subsequent migration steps were blocked by that refusal; the updater retained its synthetic recovery artifacts rather than automatically restarting or rolling back unverified database writes. [Retained diagnostics](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39346958288/artifacts/12232583369).

The failing guard is in unchanged updater/migration code, but a baseline counter-run has not established whether this is inherited or fixture-related. Upgrade qualification therefore remains blocked; no guard was relaxed and no rerun was requested merely for green. This was an isolated CI fixture, not the live Gateway.

**Other current CI:** [`android-test-play`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39346806961/job/118381782995) also failed: `NodeRuntimeAgentSelectionTest.publicationsRefreshOnlySelectedAgentCatalogsWithoutDiscovery` timed out after 2,000 ms (1 failure / 3,567 tests). That failure is recorded separately; its attribution is not established by this upgrade run.

Inspected synthetic-data before/after images are included below.

### Enable review

<details>
<summary>Labs graduation and direct-install disclosure</summary>

#### Labs

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Labs with Custom plugin UI switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e406da4-ed2a-4f75-b8c2-5abacdbadcda) | ![Labs after removal of Custom plugin UI switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01d8f7a0-4a9a-4516-92a0-a5edded4da95) |

#### Direct catalog installation

Catalog metadata does not reliably declare a native entry, so the pre-install explanation is qualified rather than inferred from UI capabilities.

</details>

## Contributor credit

Requested and designed with @jalehman.

## Work sessions

prs.title: fix(ui): prevent agent images from clipping in session rows
prs.body:
Closes #177854

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agent images are clipped in the Sessions table when the identity also has an emoji fallback.

## User Impact

User impact: image avatars fill their circular chips on desktop and narrow screens.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chip's flex override places the image beside its hidden fallback. Removing the three competing layout declarations lets the shared avatar grid stack both layers while retaining the chip's size and shape.

Thanks to @DonnieFi for the report and detailed reproduction. This patch and its browser regression were developed independently.

## Evidence

- Extended the existing bundled Control UI Sessions test at 1440 px and 390 px. Both cases fail on base `9721116c77a7`: the decoded 18 px image starts 7.48 px left of its container. Both pass with this change; image and container bounds match. Final run: 2 tests, 3.63 s test time / 21.99 s command duration.
- All 82 tests in the seven affected avatar/chip consumer files pass (7.43 s command duration), including Sessions, Activity, Cron and Usage.
- UI CSS lint, touched-test lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Independent local autoreview is scoped-clean through P2.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui` cannot start: the declaration-input containment guard rejects the borrowed dependency junctions. No typecheck or full-suite pass is claimed. Local Windows verification used the existing installation (Vite 8.3.2 / Vitest 5.0.1, versus checkout pins 8.3.4 / 5.0.3); the application's source and workspace packages came from the pinned checkout.

Screenshots show the production bundle, a synthetic avatar and a mock Gateway. No live model or provider calls were made. Before uses the base CSS; after applies only this patch.

prs.title: refactor(ui): derive capabilities from their operation owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session and channel capability declarations repeat the operation signatures maintained by their concrete owners. Keeping both copies synchronized adds code and makes a signature change easy to miss.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Public methods, optional arguments, and restricted capability surfaces stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

Derive the session and channel capability members from their concrete owners and put parameter annotations at those owners. Session capability still excludes internal lifecycle operations, and its factory keeps the public return annotation. Shared session contracts live in a type-only leaf module so concrete owners do not import back through the derived capability. Overlay and plugin capability contracts remain explicit to preserve their acyclic dependency boundaries.

Production LOC: **7,858 → 7,756 (−102)** across 28 files. Test LOC: unchanged. The denominator includes the session owners whose type imports moved to the leaf module. This is a net-negative checkpoint toward the lane target of 4,442 lines from the 222,085-line scope baseline.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` (tsrs) | Pass |
| `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` | Pass, zero cycles |
| Targeted type-aware lint and format | Pass, including the six previously failing unbound-method references |
| `pnpm deadcode:knip` | Pass |
| Independent Codex P0–P2 autoreview | Fresh final patch review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; prior index-only findings remain resolved |
| Emitted JavaScript AST comparison | Identical for all 27 changed existing modules; new `session-types.ts` emits no JavaScript |
| Solid effect/render effect/untrack/listener/query/flush/owner-capture counts | Unchanged; type-only changes |

The final `ci:full` run [39344084145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39344084145) completed with two failed browser jobs and their aggregate gate. Every other selected job passed or intentionally skipped, including all UI unit and real-Gateway shards, production types, lint, and security checks.

The three failed test names also fail in the latest completed scheduled main run [39342008977](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39342008977):

- `ui/src/e2e/boot-module-boundaries.e2e.test.ts > Control UI module boundaries > Gateway recovery while a module is unavailable > keeps recovery available after a sidebar download failure at 1280px`
- `ui/src/e2e/boot-module-boundaries.e2e.test.ts > Control UI module boundaries > Gateway recovery while a module is unavailable > keeps recovery available after a sidebar download failure at 390px`
- `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-account-footer.e2e.test.ts > Control UI sidebar account footer feature build E2E > labels the lifecycle status on the account icon and retries through its menu`

The failures are the existing offline retry fixtures: they leave a synthetic connection attempt pending while the UI correctly disables concurrent retries. Main already contains the fixture repairs. Both failed jobs tested merge `7d6fd3b5b016d9195eee081e548c1410433bf2a1`, with ordered parents `fab94ad28b430bf48ef1a3ffba3a96a91c8cc086` and this exact PR head. All six inspected test and runtime input files are byte-identical to that actual CI parent. The retained evidence includes exact names, logs, source object IDs, and the completed scheduled-run reference. This PR uses the documented inherited-failure recovery route; these browser cases are not claimed green.

No runtime or startup import changes; no UI build or screenshots are needed for type-only declarations. Broad proof runs in PR CI with `ci:full` because these are shared capabilities.

prs.title: fix: show primary failures alongside fallback login errors
prs.body:
Closes #165135.

## What Problem This Solves

A failed primary attempt disappears from the channel reply when the fallback model also fails while refreshing its OAuth login. The shared formatter already receives the ordered attempts but returns only the final provider's login guidance.

## User Impact

The reply distinguishes the primary failure from the failed fallback. A provider-matched hard refresh deadline is reported as a timeout, without claiming that the login expired or exposing raw runtime diagnostics or channel profile IDs. Explicit expired/invalid-login recovery and single-attempt wording remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing reply formatter now prefixes OAuth guidance with safe classified primary-attempt copy, and includes the failed-fallback count for longer chains. Unknown failures use generic copy and direct operators to logs. The broad failover timeout category also includes DNS/transport failures, so it alone cannot establish a refresh timeout.

This fixes reporting. It does not change credential storage, refresh/retry policy, permissions, or the underlying MCP cleanup/OAuth incident.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `02061fc69e117cd80d8ada456087bf1cc124e15f`, a normal merge of official main `131b59288f32d478f9cef689b03ca417e309a17a` into the existing PR. The upstream diff remains the original three files (+144/-3); no new production or test behavior was authored in this maintenance.

- The original real `executeAgentTurn` → error-handler → formatter reproduction failed without the patch (1 failed/25 unselected; 97.491 s including import/wrapper work). Its five regressions cover the deadline, longer chains, invalid login, ordinary transient failure, and transport failure that must not be called a timeout, with private-diagnostic controls.
- On the current merged tree, all **15 execution authentication cases and 21 formatter cases pass**. The native two-file command took **199.514 s**, including a **65.851 s** compiled-worker rebuild; Vitest reported 85.26 s and 35.76 s for the two files. The existing execution fixture runs actual reply settlement and formatting with an injected embedded-runner failure; this is not a live provider/channel proof. Most execution-file time is existing transformation/import work; this boundary also proves caller error precedence and reply settlement beyond formatter-only cases.
- The two current queued-followup custody cases pass, with 243 unrelated cases unselected. The native focused command took **756.599 s**, including native E2E build preparation; Vitest reported **157.15 s**. These are existing main tests, with unchanged deadlines, assertions, and fixtures.
- Targeted production/test types, type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap, mock-export and assertion-safety guards, docs sanity and diff checks pass. Fresh independent P0–P2 CLI review is scoped-clean; its final pass contains the complete three-file patch (earlier passes carry source/status context).

[Old CI 37245417264](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37245417264) remains a failed run on `6594310b304534a26a2e780fcd255456ba6ddbeb`: the old 224-case runner file had 223 passing cases and failed `releases a queued followup after the pending tool delivery idle bound`. That checkout also contained a separately reviewed Doctor resolution, so the replay is not pristine-main or published-package proof.

[Shakker's merged fixture repair #165250](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165250), commit `75b8ce01b85ea0fc777f4b5deac572bd1a5e89f6`, synchronizes the clock advance with the real drain and awaits terminal completion before inspecting the old registry. This merge preserves that current contract and its authorship. Passing the current cases does **not** mean the retired release-at-30,000-ms assertion was replayed or restored.

**Current-head broad CI:** [Natural CI 39339198467](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39339198467) completed **success** on `02061fc69e117cd80d8ada456087bf1cc124e15f`: **67 jobs, with 38 successful executions and 29 skipped**. prs.title: fix(worker): preserve reconciled files during fast-forward
prs.body:
Related: #137011
Follow-up to #137392

## What Problem This Solves

Replacement cloud workers already fetch and conservatively fast-forward a pushed session branch before each turn. This follow-up closes the remaining mixed-reset safety gaps:

- incoming file/directory shape changes must preserve dirty, untracked, ignored, case-aliased, index-flag-hidden, nested-repository, and submodule-backed local paths;
- clean tracked paths must not permanently block a valid remote file/directory replacement;
- a turn fenced while the replacement is already in progress must still finish materializing the checkout instead of stranding it;
- Git pattern characters in a real local path must be treated literally;
- large unrelated ignored trees must not exceed the bounded Git command output;
- subagent authority tests must await the lifecycle owner's Gateway root work instead of relying on a fixed polling window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker still inspects only components of incoming added paths. A collision is classified with literal Git pathspecs: dirty, untracked, ignored, or gitlink-backed paths skip the fast-forward and preserve local bytes; only a provably clean tracked file/directory blocker is recorded, removed after the ancestry-safe mixed reset, and then materialized from the fetched head. Gateway reconciliation remains file-only and owns no Git history recovery.

Removing a tracked blocker is only safe when the checkout proves the local bytes are reproducible from the index. Two classes of local state fail that proof, and a third issue decides whether the removal survives a fenced turn; each is a separate guard:

**Git index flags.** `git update-index --assume-unchanged <path>` and `git update-index --skip-worktree <path>` mark an entry as one Git should not consult, so later local edits to that path produce an empty status report while the working-tree bytes still differ from the index. The classifier reads the index tags with `git ls-files -v --stage` and authorizes removal only for a plain cached (`H`) entry; `h` (assume-unchanged), `S` (skip-worktree) and `s` (both) are treated as obstructions that keep the local bytes and skip the whole fast-forward.

**Nested repository metadata.** Git never reports `.git` entries, so an empty status cannot prove that a tracked directory holds no repository the worker initialized inside it. A recursive removal would delete that `.git` directory, including its commits, refs and stashes. Before authorizing removal the classifier walks the collision path and every directory that holds tracked entries under it, and rejects the path when any of them contains `.git` metadata.

**Fenced turns.** The mixed reset advances HEAD before the replacements are materialized, so the removal and materialization steps cannot be abandoned once they start. A fence that lands between two removals would otherwise return with tracked files missing, and every later turn returns before repairing them, because the local head already equals the pushed head. The classifier still honors the abort — a fenced turn never starts the credentialed fetch, never decides a collision, and never begins the move — while the bounded local move the same turn already began completes: the reset, the removals and the replacement checkout no longer observe the abort, and each step stays bounded by the turn's own timeouts.

Subagent lifecycle completion is registered as Gateway root work, and task finalization occurs before that root is released. The authority regression now waits for the canonical registry/root-work drain before asserting the terminal task projection; it does not increase a timeout or weaken the authority assertion.

The cloud-worker session lifecycle page now states that a collision skips the whole fast-forward rather than the update for a single path. It also scopes what may be replaced: the incoming path applies only where the local path is a tracked file or directory that Git reports clean and that holds no local work Git cannot see, such as an index flag or a repository created inside it, and every other obstruction keeps the local bytes.

## User Impact

A replacement worker can pick up safely pushed session history without discarding reconciled workspace bytes or getting stuck behind a clean tracked file/directory shape change. A turn that is fenced while the replacement is already underway still finishes it, so the next turn never inherits a checkout that is missing tracked files it can no longer restore. Local edits hidden by a Git index flag and repositories the worker created inside tracked directories are no longer removed. Real conflicts continue the coding turn with the existing bounded warning. Divergent history, same-path edits, local deletions and submodules remain untouched.

## Evidence

This follow-up removes one obsolete `src/node-host/node-worker-workspace.ts` allowance from `config/assertion-safety-baseline.txt`: the canonical assertion count is zero, so its old count of one must be omitted. Production code, tests and documentation are unchanged from published `63e9268d…`. The new candidate tree is `5d6ea56a9bf5990377aa85c4c30dd8ff37e1a5a0`; its complete submitted diff is `42e4960e0847cc945820be22975047db206538fee87e8d936fe3f6d75540752c`. New validation still ran with precommit HEAD `63e9268d…`; no future commit SHA is assumed.

| Baseline follow-up validation | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Official format check on the changed baseline text | N/A: unsupported TXT target; original native/bounded exit 2 and outer strict exit 1 retained (all roots joined). This is not format PASS |
| Canonical assertion-safety CLI, fixed comparison at published `63e9268d…` | PASS (new candidate; canonical current production-source assertion scan, including workspace) |
| Normal frozen root dependency installation | PASS for the separate task-owned guard environment; hooks, TLS, integrity and lockfile policy retained |

The assertion CLI reads the current governed production sources, including the workspace file. Its fixed comparison commit controls allowances; it does not turn this into an empty changed-source selection. The official formatter rejected its only TXT target because all matched files were ignored: its original native and bounded exit codes are 2, inner exit is 2, and outer strict exit is 1 with all roots joined and no remaining actors. Those FAIL verdicts and error logs remain intact. Format is N/A for this exact unsupported data-file target, never format PASS; the passing validation for this follow-up is the canonical assertion check. No unrelated supported file was added to obtain a green format result.

**Prior-head runtime applicability, not a new runtime execution.** The original seven-file NodeHost result (85 passed / 1 skipped), normal six-owner headless private-QA build and four-turn whole-runtime proof remain bound to their original candidate `85e4ca7307afd06aff40e2cc2f79c8a46050bb5f` and complete diff `03cd747d190fcfcb6533aa93c595d137bf9d6a566b587c18683a9fbeb96c4d1d`, subsequently committed as `63e9268d…`. Their original native source HEAD was `cb1f6975…`. The one-line allowance change has no runtime-executed or imported behavior; an immutable source-equivalence qualification links those unchanged business sources to this baseline-only candidate. No test, build or runtime run was repeated or relabelled.

In that original v15 run, four real Gateway turns completed. The first three reused one managed worker while background/retained-command work or a supported physical preview owner held the base checkout. After natural release, the fourth used a replacement worker and fast-forwarded to the pushed commit while preserving tracked and private untracked bytes and materializing the remote file-to-directory replacement. Three witnesses matched descriptor, per-turn private GitHub profile and managed-exec `GH_TOKEN`; `GITHUB_TOKEN` was empty and device ambient credentials differed. Direct NodeHost preview proves physical custody only.

The original runtime completed in 100942 ms; its strict observer accepted native exit zero with all roots joined, no remaining actors, observer errors, supervisor signals or force. The harness exited naturally with code zero. Gateway exited zero after ordinary SIGTERM within its unchanged 30-second grace; all eight cleanup checks passed and all five captured PID/start identities were dead. The original source, dependency, dist and compiled-worker binding receipts retain their original hashes and verdicts.

The complete original source snapshot includes the assertion-baseline file; it is not claimed byte-identical after this follow-up. Exact candidate-tree comparison permits only that one data-file deletion. The prior runtime's environment/argv and artifact seals remain historical, unchanged evidence. Its task-owned resource was ordinarily detached after publication and assessment. The new guard installation has separate ownership and dependency metadata, including potentially different module/store paths; it is not a replay of the old physical runtime environment. No fresh runtime or build PASS is claimed for this follow-up.

Earlier actual failures retain their verdicts and evidence: source/fixture/setup errors, transport scope failure, Data-floor interruptions, and a Gateway disk-admission failure before any completed turn. The earlier 292-pass result and v13 proof remain historical at their original source binding. Storage preservation, process joining and this baseline update do not turn any failed attempt into PASS.

Main's credential clearing/refresh, process framing, device-folder consent and canonical-path custody remain unchanged. Private checkout admission remains the fifth turn-builder slot. The subagent-authority regression is already in main and has no submitted source change; no fresh authority-suite PASS is claimed.

Execution evidence is headless on Darwin. Model Responses and the TLS issuer are task-owned loopback fixtures; real Git uses a local bare repository. Gateway, paired NodeHost, compiled managed worker and NodeHost-owned preview are real. Preview is called directly through NodeHost, without Control UI. No live cloud backend, real GitHub-account certification, Linux run or global exclusion of arbitrary external writers is claimed. Standalone CLI remains a separate route without a NodeHost lease. Hosted checks for the new commit are not inferred from these local results.

prs.title: fix(build): stabilize declaration cache reuse
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes package builds whose runtime chunk layout changes when declaration emission is toggled. Stable outputs avoid invalidating restored declaration caches. Current main's final runtime-only build pass remains unchanged; this repair addresses the package graph producer rather than removing that existing mitigation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime JavaScript and declaration emission now use separate, stable tsdown config partitions for AI and all workspace packages, including agent-core, while preserving main's consolidated full declaration program and SDK-only selection. The build wrapper owns DTS mode for the default, main, and AI configs, including CAC's `--dts=true` and `--dts=false` forms; arbitrary custom configs and `--no-config` retain their original arguments.

The compiler-input snapshot, cache namespace algorithm, cache format, dependencies, and environment surface are unchanged. The shared config-splitting helper is reached through the canonical generator import closure, so edits invalidate the producer stamps without a new hard-coded input list. Current package compiler options, runtime-cache ownership and runtime-only plugins remain intact. Cleanup now receives the same effective DTS mode as compilation.

## User Impact

Warm full builds can reuse restored declaration artifacts after runtime-only rebuilds instead of recompiling all declaration groups. Explicit DTS CLI overrides continue to work without recombining the runtime and declaration graphs.

## Evidence

### Published Current-Main Correction
