prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse diff results across checkout churn
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated session diff polls discard useful cached results when a checkout exceeds the revision scanner's 10,000-observation limit, or when ignored output/index stat refreshes change its filesystem fingerprint. The existing metrics show misses but not their causes.

## User Impact

Unchanged full-diff polls can reuse results on oversized active checkouts. Bounded checkouts also reuse summaries across irrelevant churn. A bounded Prometheus counter explains cache misses. No configuration or state migration is required.

Oversized summaries retain their existing 10-second fallback. Running a full status scan on every summary poll would cost more than retaining that summary.

## Change

Git's read-only porcelain-v2 status inventory owns semantic HEAD/index/untracked state; changed-file metadata and existing configuration/ref/attribute dependencies complete the revision. Index stat refreshes and ignored output no longer invalidate the displayed diff. Previously displayed paths preserve nested attribute dependencies and patch eligibility (file type and hardlink count), including committed changes with a clean status.

A bounded worker-local memo uses the existing complete filesystem fingerprint and 10,000-observation budget to preserve zero-Git idle validation. Any filesystem change revalidates through Git; only the semantic revision invalidates the diff. Memo identity includes checkout, environment, summary mode, and displayed paths; worker retirement and the 64-entry bound own its lifetime.

`openclaw_diff_cache_misses_total{method,reason}` accepts exactly ten reasons: `cold`, `evicted`, `pending`, `no-revision`, `oversized`, and changes to HEAD, index, untracked set, worktree metadata, or other metadata. Request shapes retain independent entries; recent capacity evictions are remembered within the existing cache bound. Labels contain no paths, session IDs, or revision values.

Related: #177195, #177476.

## Evidence

Acceptance specified before measurement: real `sessions.diff` RPC; identical synthetic fixtures; three tabs; 250 ms polling; one-second identical tracked saves, Git status, and ignored build rotation. At least two concurrent A/B pairs with CPU halves swapped. Require unchanged response hashes, real edits reaching every tab, fewer collections/higher hit rate on the repaired path, and no material paired latency regression. Small idle reads are a separate control.

Completed runtime comparison, before the final hardlink-eligibility repair, uses common base `cee90c3af2bd8fd8da8b598803ed30086437dd1a`, with actual baseline/candidate source views verified inside Git workers. Candidate runtime SHA-256: `5e84e61159228ac4e369b0e3da60b4a561baa047ef44211d6f940fdc74c64487`. The 267,000 extra tracked files are empty, generated sequentially; each large fixture occupies about 27 MB. Preparation uses CPUs 64–95; concurrent measurements hold the exclusive lock and use 96–111/112–127, swapped next pair. `mpstat -P 96-127` is recorded per pair; outside load is context, not an exclusion rule.

Times below are p50 / p95 / p99 in milliseconds. A is baseline, B is candidate.

| Workload / pair | A latency | B latency | Cache hits A → B | Diff collections A → B |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Large full / 1 | 225.482 / 364.616 / 415.105 | 115.850 / 137.361 / 144.188 | 0/180 → 243/243 | 60 → 0 |
| Large full / 2 | 246.985 / 393.530 / 408.681 | 131.409 / 176.066 / 242.386 | 0/174 → 231/231 | 58 → 0 |
| Large summary / 1 | 8.766 / 14.794 / 241.099 | 9.218 / 15.149 / 187.412 | 327/336 → 327/336 | 3 → 3 |
| Large summary / 2 | 9.404 / 15.869 / 264.169 | 9.802 / 14.733 / 243.305 | 327/336 → 327/336 | 3 → 3 |
| Small churn / 1 | 4.181 / 43.041 / 49.382 | 4.420 / 11.250 / 12.105 | 249/339 → 348/348 | 30 → 0 |
| Small churn / 2 | 3.656 / 43.087 / 45.925 | 3.528 / 10.250 / 11.581 | 252/339 → 348/348 | 29 → 0 |
| Small idle 120s / 1 | 3.131 / 4.417 / 5.102 | 2.807 / 4.298 / 5.517 | 1416/1419 → 1419/1419 | 1 → 0 |
| Small idle 120s / 2 | 3.527 / 5.884 / 14.863 | 3.632 / 6.305 / 10.193 | 1413/1413 → 1413/1413 | 0 → 0 |

Large full polls improve by a mean paired 112.604 ms at p50 (47.71%), 222.360 ms at p95 (58.79%), and 218.606 ms at p99 (52.98%). The median reduction is slightly below 50%, while both pairs are about 1.9× faster with clear tail/work-count gains. Across both pairs, 118 collections disappear and hits rise from 0/354 to 474/474.

Large summaries preserve their fallback: mean paired p50 +0.425 ms (+4.70%), p95 −0.391 ms, p99 −37.275 ms. Candidate reports all 18 misses as `oversized`. Small-churn evidence, retained from the behavior-equivalent memo implementation, improves aggregate hits 73.89% → 100%, removes 59 collections, and reduces p95/p99 about 75%, with p50 +0.055 ms.

The two final 120-second idle controls contain 2,832 RPCs and 944 polling rounds per side. Mean paired p50 −0.109 ms (−3.66%), p95 +0.151 ms (+2.23%), p99 −2.128 ms (−11.64%); candidate hits 2,832/2,832 with zero collections. Each candidate run performs one initial status then zero Git. This resolves the earlier small-idle hold: four prior 30-second controls showed p50 +0.032 ms, p95 +0.682 ms, and p99 +1.669 ms (+24.34%), which prompted the final simplification and longer predeclared controls. Those earlier results remain recorded; no first polls or outliers are removed from either set. The measured polling workload has no material latency regression.

Mean measured CPU busy percentages across the allocated halves were 12.63/21.73 for summary pairs, 11.77/16.59 for full pairs, and 2.43/13.43 for idle pairs. These snapshots include benchmark work and co-resident load; they do not purport to isolate external CPU. All six final paired runs completed successfully, and all owned benchmark processes have exited.

All completed churn pairs preserve identical response hashes and pass real-edit visibility. Full-diff edits reach every tab on the first poll. Those individual edit controls take A ~220/219 ms and B ~309/340 ms: a real miss still pays for semantic status before collection, so this is not a claim that changed reads are faster. Oversized full-hit validation still spends median 105/118 ms in Git; it does not reach the bounded checkout's zero-Git fast path. Large-summary edits may remain stale under the existing TTL; all measured controls become visible within 0.75 seconds.

Rerun the committed workload on separate seeded fixtures/source views, with the stated host lock/CPU policy:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/checkout-diff-measure.ts \
  --state-dir "$fixture" --boundary rpc --port "$port" \
  --tabs 3 --background 0 --maintenance 0 --agents 0 \
  --poll-ms 250 --churn-ms 1000 --duration-ms 30000 \
  --start-at "$paired_start" --output "$result"
```

Seed large fixtures with `--seed --tracked 267000 --untracked 4`; use `--tracked 0` for small fixtures. Add `--summary` for summaries. Idle controls use the small fixture, `--summary --churn-ms 0 --duration-ms 120000`. The harness records response hashes, work counts, miss reasons, and first/eventual edit visibility, saves evidence before assertions, and rejects late visibility successes. Initial loader-overlay attempts were excluded because the overlay did not reach Git workers; a separate initial large-summary attempt lacked baseline output and is not an A/B result.

## Validation and Limits

The real-Git regression fails on the original owner (ten extra collection commands after ignored/index churn) and passes with the fix. Focused proof includes 36 session RPC tests, 13 revision tests, 20 cache-owner tests, five existing worker diagnostics tests, and six Prometheus catalog/stage tests. Changed-file formatting/lint and one native core typecheck passed. Independent Codex reviews are clean at P2, including the final mode/harness changes and CI repairs.

ClawSweeper's follow-up found that a clean committed file could retain a withheld patch after its second hardlink was removed. The real-Git regression reproduced the missing patch before the repair and passes afterward. Semantic revalidation now observes mode and link count for displayed files absent from Git status, within the existing observation budget. It does not hash their modification times. The zero-Git memo return and oversized-summary fallback are unchanged. The paired timings above precede this final correctness repair; no new timing claim is made for it. The repaired revision passed all 69 focused revision/cache/RPC tests and independent review.

CI found an obsolete mock exception (removed) and two test-only TS2339 errors (fixed by discriminant filtering before name filtering, matching the existing test). ClawSweeper's redundant mocked forwarding test was removed. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was used; PR CI owns broad validation under the requested compute limits.

Final exact-head CI [39345394981](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39345394981), on `b9fe6dc8fc273156920c240f67eed8b9b9e8424c`, completed with all selected jobs passing except [UI shard 1/2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39345394981/job/118377183524) and its downstream aggregate gate. Its only failed tests are the 390px and 1280px sidebar-recovery cases in `ui/src/e2e/boot-module-boundaries.e2e.test.ts`: both time out after 30 seconds clicking the disabled `Retry now` button with `aria-busy="true"`, at `gateway-module-boundaries.test-support.ts:57`. The other 89 tests in that shard pass. Security-fast, dependency review, and security-sensitive review pass.

These are inherited failures. The scheduled-main run [39342008977, job 118365882354](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39342008977/job/118365882354), on `87692eba0956c2200e94f5dc3370e15012250cac`, reproduces both exact cases and signatures. That main job has additional failures; the attribution here is specifically for these two matching cases. Current PR CI checked out merge `d5e122ac794aa3c3c5797612b7ffb96c0f79b17f`, whose parents are main `10049a6e9d6115d5b9d23851b378a175a70e5960` and the reviewed PR head. Its complete UI tree (`db6ca677f0f8a42d8b017e5161f2e74088095492`) and Gateway-client tree (`2ace54cc18f06225a49dd71d7c1a1a454ec5bebf`) exactly match that main parent. Main change #177690 introduced pending-retry behavior and updated sibling fixtures; the failing helper still clicks before ending its synthetic pending connection. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception; failed CI is not described as green or rerun to chase a pass.

ClawSweeper completed review of the current head with no actionable findings, and the independent final repair review is clean. The export-name collision guard passed, as did all 22 tests in `eager-import-closure.test.ts` and `pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts` with one worker.

Runtime production delta is +289 lines, required by bounded diagnostics/worker forwarding, semantic and nested-attribute dependencies, and preserving the measured zero-Git idle path. Benchmark delta is +141; test delta is +231. The prescribed non-test/non-doc-path stat is +453, including benchmark/README/ledger changes. No schema, dependency, configuration, or permission change. Production miss causes still need confirmation after a separately authorized deployment.

## What Problem This Solves

Chat recovery and full tool output still carry native adapters even though their production callers already render Solid components.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery keeps its host/identity lifetime, live callback, actual connection check, and storage authority fences. Tool output keeps its keyed request lifetime and stays behind the existing detail-panel lazy import.

Native-only fixtures now mount the same components through the existing Solid helper. They retain recovery retirement, stale-response, literal-output, clipboard, and download assertions. The source-E2E server pre-optimizes Testing Library to avoid reloading when that helper is imported. The New Session attachment fixture awaits its existing lazy preview before making unchanged removal assertions. No dependency, production timing fallback, or new helper is added.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI type checking (`pnpm tsgo:ui`, tsrs) | Passed on final head |
| Wave-zero controller guard | Passed; all ratchets unchanged |
| Three directly changed unit files | 32 tests passed; default pinned Bun |
| Production Knip | Same five existing export names on exact base and final head; no new findings |

| Real-Gateway CI | Two device-identity setup failures reproduced by exact test name on the actual tested main baseline; inherited-failure exception below |
| Source-E2E dependency repair | Storage-failure case reproduced before and passed after pre-optimizing Testing Library |
| New Session lazy-preview fixture repair | Same removal assertions pass after explicit dynamic-import settlement; full UI CI passed |

This is a nonvisual lifecycle refactor: rendered tags/descendants and CSS are preserved, so no screenshots were captured. No boot import or lazy boundary changed. The two focused E2E fixture repairs were driven by CI, with their original assertions retained. No local full suite or parity run was used.

Production Knip reports `collectEntriesForBranchSummaryFromBranches`, `generateBranchSummary`, `TreePreparation`, `PackageSource`, and `WarningSettings` on both exact original merge base `7a1f8b2e5cb341cb0dc15348e535d572cbf60c81` and final head. All subsequent production Knip runs retained the same findings; no ignores were added.

### Inherited CI failures

CI tested merge `cfd37ef8ac569f3cbc6d76bd5680f997e2fb48a3`, whose first parent is main `e559b9eaad7e85fb62384f1a16f7dcc2d44c5c11` and second parent is this PR's `0a21968015a0af07058a8c8652d20deb50df69e5`. Both failing tests also fail on a clean checkout of that exact first parent:

- `Control UI browser platform family with a real Gateway > keeps signed browser identities while rendering fresh and legacy Mac and iPad labels`

Both throw `DeviceIdentityStorageError` at `src/infra/device-identity-store.ts:41`: their fixture identity filenames do not satisfy the canonical `client/credentials.sqlite` path. The PR does not change either fixture or the identity owner. The earlier scheduled main run on `08e32fdb` passed these names, so it is **not** used as inherited-failure evidence. Attribution uses the actual tested main commit and matching failures, before any browser interaction.

The exact-base reproduction used the canonical local E2E config, default pinned Bun, `--maxWorkers=1`, and only these two files. Both failed identically (2 tests, 59.18 s test duration). The runner's required baseline runtime/UI build completed first. Native admin evidence retains checkout, clean-tree, command, failure logs, hashes, and complete failed-job accounting. prs.title: fix(migrate): reject malformed UTF-8 in Claude migration sources
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw migrate claude` reads every Claude JSON source through one helper,
`extensions/migrate-claude/helpers.ts` `readJsonObject`, which decoded with a lossy
`fs.readFile(path, "utf8")`. Invalid bytes became U+FFFD and were imported into OpenClaw config:

- project `.mcp.json`, `~/.claude.json` (including its per-project entries), and Claude Desktop
  `claude_desktop_config.json` become `mcp.servers.*`;
- `.claude/settings.json` / `.claude/settings.local.json` and their user-level counterparts are
  parsed for the manual-review items.

A truncated write or a Windows-1252 file therefore imports mojibake, the plan reports no error,
and the original bytes are gone from the target. Base `af49c87f393`, MCP server URL
`https://mcp.example/café` followed by one invalid byte (`0xFF`):

```
"value": { "filesystem": { "url": "https://mcp.example/café�" } }
```

## Fix

`readJsonObject` now reads the bytes once and validates them with `node:buffer` `isUtf8` before
decoding. Invalid bytes throw the same vocabulary as the open Hermes sibling (#176668) and the
existing Claude instruction/command guards:

`Source file is not valid UTF-8: <path>. Re-encode it as UTF-8 and retry migration.`

Absent or unreadable optional sources still return `{}`, and a valid-UTF-8 file with bad JSON still
returns `{}` (the `JSON.parse` stays inside its own `try`/`catch`). One production file, +13/−1.

Classification: behavior-completing.

Precedent: #176668 (open Hermes sibling, same wording/shape), #168536 and #172953 (existing Claude
command/instruction UTF-8 guards). There is no `extensions/migrate-codex`; the in-tree Codex
migration reads its JSON through `@openclaw/fs-safe` for model refs and plugin manifests, not into
imported config or credentials, so it is not this shape.

## Evidence

Environment: Node v24.18.0 in `lexiflow-all:latest`, one isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` per run,
CLI invoked through the repo entry: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts migrate ...`.
The state used by every run was initialized by the released CLI
`OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)` (`config set gateway.port 18099`) so bundled providers load exactly
as in an installed upgrade. Base is the exact PR base commit `af49c87f393` (fresh `git archive`,
not a patched older tree); base and head differ only in the two touched files
(`helpers.ts` md5 `13b6187cdb26b71e78689e7c0032beeb` → `cdb2a017e1298ddc075f10cdfe9400bb`).

Fixture, `fixtures/bad/.mcp.json` (one MCP server, `xxd` at the URL):

```
0000030: 6578 616d 706c 652f 6361 66c3 a9ff 227d  example/caf..."}
```

Base, plan (`migrate claude --from /ws/fixtures/bad --dry-run --json`) → **exit 0**, the plan
carries the replacement character:

```
"value": { "filesystem": { "url": "https://mcp.example/café�" } }
```

Base, apply (`migrate apply claude --from /ws/fixtures/bad --yes --no-backup --force --json`)
→ **exit 0**; the target `openclaw.json` is written with the corrupted value and
`efbfbd` byte count **1**:

```
0000240: 6d70 6c65 2f63 6166 c3a9 efbf bd22 0a20  mple/caf.....".
```

Head, same two commands → **exit 1**, no plan is produced and no target file changes:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Source file is not valid UTF-8: /ws/fixtures/bad/.mcp.json. Re-encode it as UTF-8 and retry migration."
  }
}
```

`openclaw.json` md5 is `1ac91e3d8ba8fdc44eda8cda2b8d07c2` before and after the head apply;
`U+FFFD` byte count **0**.

### Control: valid multibyte text still imports, byte-identically

`fixtures/good/.mcp.json` uses `café😀` (bytes `63 61 66 c3 a9 f0 9f 98 80`). Base and head plan
JSON are byte-identical (`diff -q` → identical) and both show
`"url": "https://mcp.example/café😀"` with `U+FFFD` byte count 0. Head apply on that source
→ **exit 0**, the URL is imported as `https://mcp.example/café😀`, and the written `openclaw.json`
contains **0** `efbfbd` bytes — nothing over-rejects.

### Regression tests

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/migrate-claude/provider.test.ts`

- Base production code + new tests: **2 failed | 33 passed (35)**. Both new rejection tests fail
  because base plans the mojibake'd MCP server instead of rejecting; the valid-multibyte control
  passes.
- Head: **35 passed (35)**.

Cases: malformed project `.mcp.json` rejects with the path, malformed `.claude/settings.json`
rejects with the path, and a valid `café-😀` MCP URL is planned unchanged.

## Not tested

- The CLI cell drives a project `.mcp.json`; `~/.claude.json` and the Desktop config go through the
  same `readJsonObject`, and user level `settings.json` is covered only by unit reasoning, not a
  separate CLI capture.
- Claude has no credential importer, so the credential half of the shape does not apply here.
- Windows path handling is not exercised.
- No docs change: `docs/cli/migrate.md` documents which Claude inputs are imported, not an encoding
  contract, and the open Hermes sibling #176668 already owns the encoding accordion in that page;
  touching it here would overlap that PR.

prs.title: fix(codex): steer busy sessions and unblock thread handoffs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Messages and peer results sent to a busy agent can wait behind the work that needs them, while an exact-thread handoff can wait indefinitely for a Codex process retained by another session. This routes busy peer input through the existing active queue, preserves its original source identity across recovery, and waits for the retired thread rather than requiring its entire process to exit.

## User Impact

An eligible busy recipient accepts compatible ordinary messages and explicit followup into its active input queue and confirms transcript persistence, without promising a separate completion. Origin or destination-policy mismatches retain separately authorized new-turn admission; explicit steering still rejects mismatches. An idle recipient starts a turn and can return a correlated completion. Self-send, paused-child resume, provenance/display, generation checks, and native writer locking retain their existing owners. Accepted input stays in receiver custody; RPC acknowledgment is not transcript-consumption proof, and confirmation waits settle within their existing request budget.

Two related delivery failures are also repaired: a captured receiver that finishes before admission can retain the ordinary follow-up path after source revalidation, and fresh native child input uses internal completion rather than requiring the child to have a messaging tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the recipient’s active queue for dependency input, preserve the original source identity during recovery, and release only the exact retired native thread before handoff. Known receiver settlement before admission must remain distinct from an authority refusal; native child follow-ups must retain their existing internal completion owner.

## Behavior decision

The [review asks whether busy explicit followup should return active-queue admission instead of a separate completion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174967#issuecomment-6228365441). I recommend the busy/idle distinction because dependency input must be available to the work that needs it. The [earlier owner decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160842#issuecomment-5882083686) expressly preserved separate-turn followup; this proposal deliberately changes that contract.

Codex supplies a concrete reference, rather than just a naming analogy. Its [followup_task handler](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2/followup_task.rs#L42) selects TriggerTurn. The [delivery-mode contract](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/agent/types.rs#L59) means active-turn delivery or starting work when idle, through the [shared messaging owner](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/83086188ae0614bd882818ff1aa23f3194962012/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2/message_tool.rs#L41).

This PR follows that distinction: [busy delivery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e2bdba716822faadd21508f8b0e2ff98fd425b18/src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts) returns admission, preserving receiver custody and uncertainty; idle delivery retains a new turn and correlated completion. Consumption still waits for supported checkpoints, including tool completion. Successful busy admission waits for transcript persistence; it promises neither model consumption nor a separate reply. A backend that cannot provide durable steering is never injected and instead uses the existing single durable queued-delivery path. The compatibility cost is real: callers using busy followup specifically to obtain a separate correlated completion lose that behavior. The requested owner decision is whether dependency-delivery liveness justifies that change; Codex precedent and the supplied runtime captures support it but do not confer approval.

## Evidence

### Current upstream integration and durable steering

Head `2656d7eab75b472a642f2a261028bfd65617d236` merges previous public head `e2bdba716822faadd21508f8b0e2ff98fd425b18` with pinned upstream `0cd30da1a3483f7358a7364cba2f1f7133f25a06`, preserving both histories and resolving all five conflicts. It adopts #176587's durable steering/restart contract while retaining the proposed busy ordinary/explicit-followup routing. Active sends wait for transcript persistence; the sender's reply-wait budget does not weaken the admission deadline. Unsupported durable steering is rejected before injection and takes exactly one durable queued path.

The additional `agent-step` caller now carries the existing durable Gateway operation into active delivery and uses the returned fallback operation. Its regression traverses the actual communication, continuation and controller owners: zero volatile injections, one durable returned-result admission, original source/recipient generations, selected requester identity, provenance and one input idempotency key. Removing that production propagation makes the regression fail at the missing returned admission; restoring it passes. Accepted-unconfirmed input still never replays.

The real-loop steering matrix holds a provider response past the reply-wait budget, proves no premature durable acknowledgement, then releases it and verifies one persisted attributed input without another turn. It covers explicit followup as well as ordinary/explicit steering and own-child delivery. The earlier Codex confirmation timer fix remains unchanged: caller waiting can expire while accepted batches retain receiver custody until late consumption or exact run closure.

**177 focused checks across nine suites pass**, including native confirmation/late-consumption custody and the corrected retained-peer fixture. Core production and four owning test type graphs, scoped typed lint/format, unchanged mock/assertion/line-limit ratchets, the production build, and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. The fixture counts transcript messages separately from their session header; no assertion or baseline is weakened. No new queue, store or authority grant is introduced.

Current-head CI is pending. Real final-native-effect proof for the selected retained requester, unselected identity and revocation during awaited preparation, latest-stable upgrade, security-owner approval and the explicit-followup behavior decision remain outstanding. Historical runtime captures below remain revision-qualified; no deployment or upstream merge is claimed.

### Prior upstream integration — `701a1dec`

Head `701a1dec571ddc83135556d535d6bba81617694d` merges pinned upstream `550c55a807016cef74550ef3ebfb788022056349` into the published `1faeec0fa56bf4212470fe98f84d3d4077cd04b5` candidate. This specifically integrates the overlapping original-request reply-admission changes from #176697 and independent continuation custody from #176769. It does not restore retired queue maps, old target modules, finished tool authority, or a parent recovery claim that upstream deliberately separated from independent continuation ownership.

A completed peer's result now uses the original accepted send's host-held reply admission, exact source and recipient session incarnations/lifecycle revisions, current communication policy, and independently retained live operator authority. The busy-recipient path consumes that prepared admission through the existing active queue. Delivery routing continues to use the canonical logical store identity; the communication reader's physical database path is not reused as a controller scheduling scope. Only the selected requester identity survives the sender's finished invocation; operational run, receipt, full-permission override, approval handles and tool grants do not. Default cleanup and private child completion keep their existing owners. Selected participant scope intersection, device/source revocation, release and Gateway replacement remain enforced.

The actual detached reply-flow regression is red with the pinned upstream `runAgentStep`: after a genuine accepted original request, it dispatches another `agent` turn instead of steering the busy requester. With the fix, accepted and unconfirmed results enter the busy requester's input once, and the receiver can persist its attributed transcript record after forwarding custody ends. Replaced recipients and lifecycle changes remain rejected. The new focused spec uses real endpoint reads, storage, communication admission, original acceptance and continuation ownership; only the Gateway transport response, backend queue and participant observation are fixtures. The upstream five-route original-endpoint/reply-policy matrix remains intact. Two redundant whole-sentence description assertions were removed; generated prompt snapshots still own exact wording.

**409 focused tests pass across 26 files.** Coverage includes native accepted-versus-consumed steering, exact-thread release, native child completion, recovery source preservation, original-send admission, requester/source/receiver revocation, independent continuation custody, selected participants, FIFO settlement and persistence after sender release. Acceptance is not consumption, and indeterminate delivery is never replayed.

Production core, Codex and owning agent/Gateway test type graphs pass, as do scoped typed lint, formatting, changed-source line-cap growth, generated prompt snapshots and import-cycle checks. The canonical production build passes (3m 10.3s). Fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable code defect. Exact current-head native/provider consumption and stable upgrade were not rerun. Earlier captures below remain revision-qualified; these synthetic owner tests do not close that runtime gap or confer enforced security approval.

The change retains the existing delivery, communication, continuation and lifecycle owners, with no new manager, schema, cache or public configuration. Busy explicit followup remains the maintainer behavior decision described above. Exact-head hosted CI and the required security-owner approval remain separate gates; prior-head CI is not substituted.

### Earlier synthetic runtime evidence and its limits

Earlier matching combined local builds, rather than this exact public binary, exercised an isolated authenticated Gateway with real Codex 0.163.0 and an external provider. They observed a busy recipient consuming a followup marker in its own provider final, an attributed worker result reaching the busy requester before its provider final, and receiver settlement falling back once to the same physical conversation. Reset after generation preparation rejected the stale delivery, with no marker written to the original transcript or steered into the original native turn.

An exact native handoff capture closed the retired target thread, then resumed it in the successor process while the old process retained a readable idle sibling. A stable-version synthetic upgrade used the stable CLI to write state, stopped that Gateway, ran canonical candidate Doctor migration, and preserved the session ID, transcript count and marker. This PR adds no schema. These remain revision-qualified historical proofs; they were not rerun on this integration.

A separate observed-ready saved-child run resumed the same physical child on a distinct run and returned its fresh provider-final marker through the parent's real sessions_send result. It did not enumerate the child's dynamic catalog or directly map the child session to a native thread. Exact message-less catalog/availability behavior remains supported by the separate controlled owner tests, not that external-provider capture.

All examples and test receipts are synthetic. No private logs, credentials, connection details, native identifiers, or real user data are published. The operator's combined local deployment and its RPC/plugin health checks are operational evidence, not proof of this exact PR binary or every historical queueing failure. This integration's real external-provider consumption and upgrade paths remain unrun.

prs.title: fix(exec): report a run with no captured exit code as failed, not completed
prs.body:
Related: #146426

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a command whose supervised process terminates without ever reporting an exit code is recorded as a successful exit-0 completion, so a run that never produced a status surfaces as success instead of a failure.

## User Impact

Runs that end without a captured exit code now report failed, with the reason shown to the user, and automation reading the exec outcome no longer sees a false success for them. Commands that do report a code — including signal and timeout paths — are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildExecExitOutcome` coerced a null exit code to `0` and still treated the record as a normal exit, so a run that never produced a status took the completed branch: `status: "completed"`, `exitCode: 0`, no failure reason, and an `exec.process.completed outcome:completed` diagnostic.

A null code is not evidence of success. `RunExit.exitCode` is nullable by contract. The outcome now takes the existing failure path, which already classifies this shape as `aborted` and renders "Command aborted before exit code was captured" — so the null is preserved rather than replaced by a sentinel.

This covers the three points in the issue's proposed change: (1) a null code is no longer success, (2) the null is preserved in the payload — the failed branch already returns `exitCode: params.exit.exitCode`, and (3) the regression test asserts the null code survives.

Scope note: a process killed by a signal is unaffected. Signal kills arrive as `reason: "signal"` with a null `exitCode`, which never took the completed branch. This fix is specifically the `reason: "exit"` record that never captured a code.

Non-goals: the supervisor's reason vocabulary and the signal/timeout classifications are untouched. No new config, protocol, or persistence surface.

## Evidence

The normal CI refresh adds no new PR fix code. Linux CI checked out merge `c5e83abc96e7c65ae93bdb15c6718c9618f37720`, whose parents are base `2d305eb2061955123f799c97c108ea8718fba392` and updated PR head `34664c114b9b5d18d83568efa7d129299a33f879`. The merge and PR head have the same Git tree.

- [Foreground failures: 10/10 passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39338150948/job/118353210631), including the unknown-exit-code regression.
- [Real process/session integration: 12/12 passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39338150948/job/118353210606), including all five previously failing notification cases and the current main fixture's additional case.

These are hosted Linux/Bun suite results, not duplicate local test runs. The 23:22 UTC snapshot still contained pending checks; it is not an overall CI-pass claim.

Current full-range Git whitespace check passed. The normal captured-evidence/source qualification check also passed, verifying the exact CI checkout, equal Git trees, suite cases and immutable logs. These checks add no new local compiler, type-aware lint, formatter or runtime result.

The exact nullable-exit classifier is unchanged from the published repair. Current main process/cancellation/finalization owners remain in place. The earlier real Linux relay/anchor reproduction remains historical under its original source and is not upgraded to this merge head. This host does not supply a new Linux `/proc` or installed-service proof; no unrelated full Gateway replay is claimed.

The archived Linux null-trigger observations below are the original author's trace. That archive does not contain an independent Linux native receipt or an exact execution commit. The separate historical Darwin supervisor receipt covers ordinary stdout/UTF8 controls, so it is not presented as a native reproduction of the null-trigger.

<details>
<summary>Original historical evidence (original source/platform bindings retained)</summary>

The following original observations and failures are historical, not re-labelled as current execution.


### A real run reaches this record on Linux — no stub anywhere in the chain

The producer is OpenClaw's own service-child relay host. On non-Windows, `createChildAdapter` takes that path whenever the run owns its process tree or `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER` is set (`src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts:150-154`), which is the path a non-PTY exec under an installed service is supervised through.

The trigger: an anchor that loses host-side authority while the command is still alive and outlives the graceful-cancel window.

1. exec starts `/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c 'trap "" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done'` — a command that ignores SIGTERM.
2. The anchor process receives SIGTERM out of band. The host never calls `kill()`, so its `requestedSignal` stays unset.
3. The anchor's own handler runs `requestCleanup("parent-lost")` and signals its process group; the command ignores it.
4. The 5 s `GRACEFUL_CANCEL_TIMEOUT_MS` grace expires with no root result, so `closeAuthority(reason, hardKill=true)` runs `process.kill(0, "SIGKILL")`. The anchor and the command die together, before any `root-result` is sent.
5. The host sees the closing receipt and observes the group's disappearance (`ESRCH`) with no root result, so `finishAuthorityClose` closes authority as `rootResult = { code: null, signal: requestedSignal ?? null }` → `{ code: null, signal: null }`.
6. The supervisor maps that record to `reason: "exit"`, `exitCode: null` — exactly what `buildExecExitOutcome` receives.

Both rows below are real processes: the real supervisor, the real relay host, a real anchor, and the real `runExecProcess` entry point. Nothing is stubbed, mocked, or injected, and the teardown is a real signal to a real process.

| Step | Observed |
|---|---|
| Real supervisor + relay host + SIGTERM-ignoring command | `RunExit { reason: "exit", exitCode: null, exitSignal: null }` |
| Same teardown at `runExecProcess` **before** this change | `status: "completed", exitCode: 0` — 3/3 runs |
| Same teardown at `runExecProcess` **after** this change | `status: "failed", exitCode: null, failureKind: "aborted", reason: "Command aborted before exit code was captured"` — 3/3 runs |

<details>
<summary>Before the change — a run with no captured status reports exit 0</summary>

```text
=== A: real supervisor, real relay host, real process ===
[A]   pid=2067050 argv=/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c trap "" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done
[A] SIGTERM -> anchor 2067029 at +61ms
[A] waited 5089ms after the signal
[A] RunExit {
  "reason": "exit",
  "exitCode": null,
  "exitSignal": null,
  "oomScoreWrapperSelected": true,
  "durationMs": 5797,
  "stdout": "",
  "stderr": "",
  "timedOut": false,
  "noOutputTimedOut": false
}
=== B: real runExecProcess entry point ===
[B] SIGTERM -> anchor 2068103 at +71ms
[B] waited 5103ms after the signal
[B] ExecProcessOutcome {
  "status": "completed",
  "exitCode": 0,
  "exitSignal": null,
  "exitReason": "exit",
  "durationMs": 7027,
  "aggregated": "",
  "timedOut": false,
  "noOutputTimedOut": false
}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>After the change — the same teardown reports failure with the null preserved</summary>

```text
=== A: real supervisor, real relay host, real process ===
[A]   pid=2065282 argv=/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c trap "" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done
[A] SIGTERM -> anchor 2065267 at +61ms
[A] waited 5090ms after the signal
[A] RunExit {
  "reason": "exit",
  "exitCode": null,
  "exitSignal": null,
  "oomScoreWrapperSelected": true,
  "durationMs": 5736,
  "stdout": "",
  "stderr": "",
  "timedOut": false,
  "noOutputTimedOut": false
}
=== B: real runExecProcess entry point ===
[B] SIGTERM -> anchor 2065793 at +51ms
[B] waited 5081ms after the signal
[B] ExecProcessOutcome {
  "status": "failed",
  "exitCode": null,
  "exitSignal": null,
  "exitReason": "exit",
  "durationMs": 6484,
  "aggregated": "",
  "timedOut": false,
  "noOutputTimedOut": false,
  "failureKind": "aborted",
  "oomScoreWrapperSelected": true,
  "reason": "Command aborted before exit code was captured"
}
```
</details>

Repeated runs of the identical probe are stable in both directions: 3/3 `completed` with `exitCode: 0` before the change, 3/3 `failed` with `exitCode: null` after it.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction (scratch probe, run from the repository root; not part of the change)</summary>

```ts
// tmp-probe.mts — real runExecProcess, real supervisor, real anchor
import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { runExecProcess } from "./src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.js";

const PROGRAM = 'trap "" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done';

function ppidOf(pid: number): number {
  try {
    const match = /^PPid:\s+(\d+)$/m.exec(readFileSync(`/proc/${pid}/status`, "utf8"));
    return match ? Number(match[1]) : -1;
  } catch {
    return -1;
  }
}

// Our own anchor only: anchor -> relay -> this probe.
function findAnchorPid(): number | undefined {
  for (const entry of readdirSync("/proc")) {
    if (!/^\d+$/.test(entry)) continue;
    const pid = Number(entry);
    if (pid === process.pid) continue;
    try {
      if (!readFileSync(`/proc/${entry}/cmdline`, "utf8").includes("service-child-group-anchor")) {
        continue;
      }
    } catch {
      continue;
    }
    if (ppidOf(ppidOf(pid)) === process.pid) return pid;
  }
  return undefined;
}

const handle = await runExecProcess({
  // exec runs this as the `-c` program of its own shell, so that shell is the
  // root process and it ignores SIGTERM itself.
  command: PROGRAM,
  workdir: "/tmp",
  env: { PATH: process.env.PATH ?? "" },
  usePty: false,
  warnings: [],
  maxOutput: 100_000,
  pendingMaxOutput: 100_000,
  notifyOnExit: false,
  timeoutSec: null,
});

const deadline = Date.now() + 15_000;
let anchorPid: number | undefined;
while (anchorPid === undefined && Date.now() < deadline) {
  anchorPid = findAnchorPid();
  if (anchorPid === undefined) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 25));
}
if (anchorPid === undefined) throw new Error("anchor process never appeared");
process.kill(anchorPid, "SIGTERM");
console.log(JSON.stringify(await handle.promise, null, 2));
```


### Sibling paths through the same entry point

Same real entry point, no signal interference, after the change:

| Command | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `true` | `completed`, `exitCode 0` |
| `exit 3` | `completed`, `exitCode 3` |
| unknown command | `failed`, `exitCode 127`, `shell-command-not-found` |
| `kill -9 $$` | `failed`, `exitCode null`, `exitSignal SIGKILL`, `exitReason signal`, `failureKind signal` |

Only the null-code `"exit"` record changed classification; the signal, not-found, and ordinary exit paths are untouched.

### Regression coverage

| Path | Mode | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| New case in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts` | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts` | Before fix: FAIL — 1 failed, 21 passed. After fix: PASS — 22 passed |

| Repo gate | `pnpm check:changed` | pass (`GATE_EXIT=0`; lanes core+coreTests, oxfmt, typecheck, lint, all guards) |

The unit-level case asserts the same record through `runExecProcess` at the seam the existing exec suites use, so the fix stays covered in CI without depending on process signals. Before the fix it failed as `expected { status: 'completed', exitCode: 0 } to match { status: 'failed', exitCode: null }`.

### What was not tested

- No Windows host was available. The relay-host closure above is now reproduced on Linux; the Windows job-object hard-kill path (`useWindowsJobAnchor`) is still unexercised, and it is the likeliest other producer of this record.
- The last settle that can still carry a null code is unreachable by construction, not untested: the PTY adapter's `dispose()` settle is a no-op because the supervisor disposes only after that adapter's `wait()` has already resolved, and `settleWait` ignores a second settlement.
- The reproduction above constructs the trigger deliberately (out-of-band SIGTERM to the anchor plus a command that ignores SIGTERM) rather than waiting for it to happen in the field; it exercises real shipped code, but no production incident was captured.
- No live channel or Gateway proof: the change is local to exec outcome classification.

## Merge conflict resolved and validation refreshed

This revision resolves the merge conflict against `main` that ClawSweeper recorded as the only
remaining item, and re-runs the focused exec validation on the resulting head.

The branch was rebased onto current `main`. The only content conflict was in
`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts`, where `main` had in the meantime moved the
suite to a `fullExec()` / `tool.execute()` idiom and dropped the direct `runExecProcess` call this
branch's test used. The conflicted region was therefore taken from `main` and the regression test was
re-expressed in the current idiom with the same assertions — `status: "failed"`, `exitCode: null`,
`failureKind: "aborted"`, `exitReason: "exit"`, and the reason text
`Command aborted before exit code was captured`. `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` auto-merged

Environment limitation: this rebase and validation run happened on `darwin` (macOS), where the

prs.title: fix(gateway): retain device source identity across reconnects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After an authenticated Control UI device-token connection reconnects, a new parent turn can receive a different model-source identity from a native child still running under its valid retained source. Native `collaboration.send_message` and `followup_task` then fail the existing “same admitted model source” check. The CLI presents that refusal as “Native hook relay unavailable,” although the request reached the Gateway and the child continued running.

## User Impact

An established browser device-token connection can reconnect and keep comparison identity with its retained work. Each request still owns a separate live authority. The native guard still checks both sources, and the child keeps its original model authority and admission ceiling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fix the identity issuer. Share a comparison record only when the host-verified device credential generation, profile, role, scopes, client/origin, policy generations and exact access/ingress owners match. The existing revocation owner retains records only while captured work holds them. A host-transferred principal can use that record; a copied client cannot borrow it.

Different devices, rotated tokens, profiles, reduced scopes, unproven authentication and distinct access grants stay separate. Reconnect matching grants no replacement permissions. No configuration, protocol, schema, native-model guard, or credential-storage change is introduced.

## Evidence

Pinned upstream: `4cae0b38205b30b14fc8460af5bd5a7e5b36095e`. PR head: `571a7309562fa2f876558d1d9ddfd730650b6891`.

- Synthetic production-dispatch/issuer regression reproduces the identity mismatch before the fix: both retained and reconnected authorities are current but their source identities differ. The fix preserves identity while keeping the authority objects distinct.
- `142` focused tests pass on this upstream port, covering reconnect, trusted principal transfer versus copying, release, device/token/profile/scope separation, access revocation and changed model ceilings, plus existing Gateway authority and native-hook/model-source controls.
- Production core and owning Gateway root/server type graphs, scoped typed lint, formatting, whitespace and line-cap checks pass. Fresh independent review through P2 found no actionable findings within the supplied patch/context.

The same five-file fix was deployed on the operator's combined local runtime at `b879038f33ca0bbf93b8fc040145fabd93c1aee5`, where 139 focused tests, the production build and operational acceptance passed. The Gateway is healthy; existing session identities and plugin states were preserved. This PR is the clean source port to newer upstream, not a claim that its exact binary was deployed or rebuilt.

The historical hook refusals were correlated with the source-identity error and a browser reconnect. Historical logs do not record credential fingerprints, so exact token continuity was not reconstructed. The dispatcher regression proves the issuer mechanism; actual model consumption of a native child message after reconnect remains unrun. Absence of new errors is not consumption evidence.

All fixtures and published examples are synthetic. No real transcripts, private logs, credentials, connection identifiers or user data are included. New-head CI is pending.

### Current upstream integration

Current head `1abc8946beab69ea04c42b21d7f649c0e992aa1e` resolves the reported conflict against upstream `9509fc22`. The source-comparison buckets and the upstream continuation-policy authority owner are both retained. Reconnect comparison still requires the exact authenticated device-token generation, profile, role, scopes, transport policy and live owner; it does not replace either request’s execution permissions.

**103 focused checks pass in eight owning suites** (94.5 seconds canonical wrapper wall time), covering reconnect identity, worker/source lifetime, independent module instances, restart recovery, in-process continuation custody and authenticated dispatch. Core and extension production types, both Gateway test type graphs, scoped typed lint, formatting and line-cap/mock/assertion ratchets pass. A fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defect; reviewers did not run the project. The canonical production build passes in 2m 50s.

The required real-native reconnect/foreign-device/revocation proof is being qualified separately against this exact built head. No new native-consumption success is asserted yet. The security-owner review remains required. All test identities, state and provider inputs are synthetic; no operator Gateway changes.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): per-agent verboseDefault is ignored by replies, /verbose, /status and openclaw agent
prs.body:
Closes #177612

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent's `agents.entries.<id>.verboseDefault` is accepted by config and shown by the native `/verbose` menu, but that agent's replies, text `/verbose` and `/status`, and `openclaw agent` runs still use `agents.defaults.verboseDefault`.

Related: #73680 (the verbose half only; per-agent `elevatedDefault` is untouched).

## User Impact

User impact: setting `verboseDefault` on one agent now changes that agent's verbose behavior (tool summaries, tool-failure details) and what `/verbose` and `/status` report. Agents without their own value keep the global default, and a session `/verbose` override still wins.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reply path already reads the agent entry for thinking and reasoning defaults, and the native command menu already reads the agent's verbose default through `resolveAgentConfig`, but the run itself read only the global default. The reply-run resolution and the `/verbose` / `/status` level resolver (also used by the plugin SDK status runtime) now read the agent entry first, and `openclaw agent` reads it through `resolveAgentConfig`, which already merges it. The mixed-message directive lane now receives the agent entry too, so a `/verbose` (or `/reasoning`) query inside a normal message reports the level the turn actually runs with; that lane had never been given the entry since per-agent defaults were added. The docs now list the per-agent key.

Not changed here (follow-ups):
- Tool-event visibility fallbacks still seed from the global default when a session or run carries no verbose level (`tui.ts`, `tui/embedded-backend.ts`, and the Gateway's `chat-history-handler.ts` / `server-chat.ts`). All four files are at or over the line cap, so the same change needs a module split first.
- The native-command `/status` fast path, the `session_status` tool, and the Control UI's client-side bare `/verbose` ignore verbose defaults entirely, the global one included.

Both lookups agree: the reply path reads the raw agent entry like the adjacent thinking and reasoning defaults, `openclaw agent` reads the merged `resolveAgentConfig` value, and both fall back to the global default for agents without an entry.

prs.title: fix(discord): batch queued messages by thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
When a user sends several Discord messages while an earlier turn is still running, the next follow-up turn should be able to see the whole compatible queued intent instead of only the last message. At the same time, Discord transport must keep every inbound event flowing into core admission so active-run steering and `/stop`-style control inputs are not delayed behind a local plugin queue.

Related: openclaw/openclaw#103287

## Summary
- remove the previous Discord-local same-session batch lane from `message-run-queue.ts`
- keep Discord inbound work event-keyed through the plugin queue so each message reaches core admission promptly
- carry Discord batch message IDs through typed preflight/finalized context fields when the dispatcher has an aggregate context
- add core follow-up queue support for aggregate `messageIds` on collected follow-up runs
- project collected queued message IDs into execution context as `MessageSids`, `MessageSidFirst`, and `MessageSidLast` while keeping `MessageSid` as the current/latest message
- add a focused Discord dispatcher boundary proof that two debounced Discord source messages become one processed turn with both source IDs preserved

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

### Ephemeral Gateway + qa-channel proof on pushed head

Verdict: PASS on pushed PR head `6df1189d660a9320a83f04408154e1a502581ff6`.

This is the new qualifying proof path requested by ClawSweeper: it starts an ephemeral Gateway child, enables the real `qa-channel` plugin against the QA bus, uses the `mock-openai` provider, injects three inbound channel events, and verifies that the two queued channel messages become one executed provider turn.

Committed proof test:

- `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/qa-channel-queued-message-ids.e2e.test.ts`

Redacted runtime evidence from the test:

```json
{
  "transport": "qa-channel",
  "provider": "mock-openai",
  "gateway": "ephemeral-child",
  "receivedMessageIds": [
    "qa-msg-pr122238-active",
    "qa-msg-pr122238-queued-first",
    "qa-msg-pr122238-queued-last"
  ],
  "collectedProviderRequestCount": 1,
  "queuedNeedlesPresent": [true, true],
  "sameSessionForAllIngressMessages": true,
  "executedTurnChannel": "qa-channel",
  "executedTurnChatId": "pr-122238-qa-channel",
  "secrets": "none"
}
```

What this proves at the boundary ClawSweeper asked for:

- `qa-channel` receives three real inbound channel messages via the QA bus, including explicit provider message IDs.
- All three inbound messages resolve to the same Gateway session.
- While the first turn is active, two later source messages are queued through core admission.
- The queued pair is collected into exactly one mock-provider request, and that executed request contains both queued source bodies.
- This path does not mock Discord preflight or processing; it exercises a complete mock-channel/mock-provider/ephemeral-Gateway run.

Current-main merge evidence:

- Pushed PR head: `6df1189d660a9320a83f04408154e1a502581ff6`
- Current `origin/main`: `39b39ca6eec684f0675cd93500646b578f6e7021`
- Local merge-result proof head: `a2e0665c9e326483afd190bc01629645cd59b502`
- Merge parents: `6df1189d660a9320a83f04408154e1a502581ff6` + `39b39ca6eec684f0675cd93500646b578f6e7021`
- Merge status: conflict-free `ort` merge

Additional code cleanup in this proof update:

- Removed Discord preflight `batchMessageIdFirst` / `batchMessageIdLast` fields.
- The finalized context now derives `MessageSidFirst` and `MessageSidLast` from the aggregate `batchMessageIds` array, avoiding duplicate Discord-only preflight fields.

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/qa-channel-queued-message-ids.e2e.test.ts
-> 1 file passed, 1 test passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.batch-ids.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.context.test.ts
-> 2 files passed, 15 tests passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/queue.collect.test.ts
-> 2 files passed, 138 tests passed

pnpm oxlint <touched files>
-> passed

pnpm tsgo:core
-> passed

pnpm tsgo:test:root
-> passed
```

Known local check limitations:

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` currently fails outside this PR's touched area because optional extension dependencies are not installed locally: `node-llama-cpp`, `@tencent-connect/qqbot-connector`, and `silk-wasm`.
- A direct `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --project extensions/discord/tsconfig.json` also hits existing generated/dist type skew plus an unrelated `provider.acp.ts` unknown-error diagnostic. The focused Discord Vitest suite and touched-file Oxlint are green.


## Behavior Boundary Evidence
The after-fix boundary is owned by core follow-up collection rather than a Discord pre-admission lane:

- `message-handler.batch-ids.test.ts` proves the Discord debounce dispatcher emits one merged turn while preserving every source Discord message ID.
- `message-handler.context.test.ts` proves typed Discord batch fields project into finalized Discord context as `MessageSids`, `MessageSidFirst`, and `MessageSidLast`.
- `queue.collect.test.ts` proves separately enqueued follow-ups `m-1` and `m-2` are collected by the core queue into one execution call with `messageId === "m-2"` and `messageIds === ["m-1", "m-2"]`.
- `followup-turn-execution.test.ts` proves aggregate queued IDs are projected into the executed turn context while keeping the latest ID as `MessageSid`.

prs.body:
## Disposition: cleanup restored and parked

The original two-file cleanup is restored to fresh main because the unqualified post-deploy navigation-count failure's canonical import graph reaches both changed files, and the campaign does not permit a local browser/build baseline replay. No cleanup lines are landed or credited. Original source is preserved at deslop/z34-parked-network-ui-reachable-20261015, exact1a898d27347c4ac62134f49e81a3364a06c6673c. The now-empty PR is closed after one rollback push. The original proposal and proof below are historical, not a claim of current diff or green CI.

## What Problem This Solves

Response-body readers maintain a second abort listener, settlement flag and Promise chain around an existing shared abort observer. Fetch also composes the same caller signal outside a builder that already owns composition.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Keep real network/idle deadlines, caller stop, bounded reads, transport release and security checks. No configuration, schema, SDK export, dependency, protocol or Phase E changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing abort observer for body reads and let the existing fetch timeout builder compose caller cancellation. The DNS part of this parked family already landed separately in #177781 and is not included or counted here. Net production LOC:32 removed (32 added/64 deleted), two owners; tests unchanged.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Reader cancellation now begins after the shared race selects rejection, rather than inside a private abort listener. That avoids cancellation-to-EOF turning a deadline into success; cancellation remains observed but deliberately not awaited because a retained capture tee can wait on the live caller. The actual stalled-response repair from #106035 stays, including its timeout, idle refresh, normalization and native cleanup.
- If a custom fetch ignores an already-aborted caller signal, the existing builder now suppresses its later duplicate timeout warning. A second composition is not needed for that misleading log. The caller reason and post-header body cancellation repair from #102951 stay: native AbortSignal.any remains connected, and cleanup only clears the timer.

## Evidence

Focused final-source tests:98 passed across eight files.65 owner/authority/release cases147.1s wrapper; real retained capture-tee case1PASS38.1s; proxy SSE/native abort6PASS10.5s; preview parser/security suite23PASS53.9s; media read/save/idle cases3PASS71.1s. Named selections deselect unrelated cases; no skips, assertions or budgets were edited.

Targeted production/test types7.3s each, actual typed lint36.3s, formatting0.7s and suppression/wrapper closure audits17PASS20.4s pass. Runtime cycles0/30.4s, Madge0/39.2s, staged two-file line-cap3.2s and changed-plan dry run10.6s pass. No broad local build or graph typecheck is claimed. Every local command uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG, nice10 and one worker/heavy command.

Fresh independent review completed with final-source verification and one reported P1. Rejected after source/test verification: it claimed cleanup detaches a parent relay, but the current builder has no relay and cleanup clears only the timer. The unchanged post-header caller-cancellation case passed. No actionable finding remains; this is not described as a clean reviewer verdict. Author simplification and caller/test audit completed; exact-head hosted CI remains broad proof.

Hosted run39341807034 currently has two qualified inherited failures; remaining jobs are still pending, so this is not final gate admission. Job118366258097 reports an untouched UI missing import at chat-pane-lifecycle.ts514, introduced by main revert#177760. The tested merge173ab2dc has exactly main parentaf7b93c's UI blob; a narrow byte-identical-owner replay reproduces TS2304, with an additional recorded temporary-snapshot Solid-resolution gap. Job118365410428 fails xAI's monotonic polling case at696: one poll instead of more than one. One serial exact-CI-merge/main-parent replay fails identically on both revisions (173.9s/97.4s wrapper), with no source/assertion/budget changes. The new fixture from#174227 passes an object to the existing numeric HTTP-status argument. These are not called flaky, fixed, or passing; the two backend changes remain intact. Fresh main-flakes and all six latest completed schedules were checked before attribution.

prs.title: feat(plugins): identify retained references blocking reload
prs.body:
Related: #165059

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin reload drain timeouts report a reference count without identifying the host acquisitions that keep the plugin alive.

## User Impact

Administrators can inspect current plugin reference IDs, acquisition owners, reasons, ages, and cleanup state through `plugins.inspect`; drain logs include bounded, owner-redacted snapshots. This adds diagnosis, not force-release or changed reload behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing instance lifetime owner now records scalar acquisition facts beside its authoritative live tokens. Agent preparation, generation leases, invocation scopes, and service startup supply host attribution where available; unknown owners remain explicit. Inspection requires current administrator authority and the request's Gateway registry, returns at most 64 references with an omitted count, and never executes plugin code.

Acquisition ownership is not proof that a session is still executing or that a plugin leaked. In particular, a reload requested by a turn retaining the plugin can wait on itself, but aggregate counts alone cannot establish that cause. No payloads or cleanup error text are included.

## CI follow-up status

Current remote head remains `dde9e3e9c4e2194558ba8e5d0ad03fd743164aa7`. Completed CI run [37852731605](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37852731605) tested merge `03b24fe6d97b6341dee485ebee0469933b161cda` with main `6ae2aee12eb0641b623e8c34840b47de9cff2022`. The branch began on freshly fetched main `8879e5ef4b98e7ff17b0ac04e7695f66f3e143b2`, not an intentionally stale checkout.

**Seven red rollup entries are five failed test jobs plus two aggregate gate statuses—not seven independent defects.** There are 81 successful and 20 skipped workflow jobs. No unchanged CI reruns, weakened checks, or merge were requested.

- **PR-caused defects: fixed.** The initial Madge type-import cycle triggered 57 cancellations, not 57 independent failures. The subsequent missing wrapper-inventory entries were also ours. Commits `3321e15bd97d7b38af72ef37b3770ade4f2f1c58` and `dde9e3e9c4e2194558ba8e5d0ad03fd743164aa7` repair these; architecture, wrapper inventory, typechecks and lint are green on the current head. All **15 new diagnostics cases pass in CI**, with 0.418 seconds summed test-body time (shared setup excluded).
- **Node changed-1: inherited, reproduced.** The skill-refresh E2E creates a managed worktree from a local-only repository without an origin or explicit base. Main's remote-default admission rejects that fixture. The identical missing-origin failure reproduces on exact CI main `6ae2aee12eb0641b623e8c34840b47de9cff2022` without this PR (48.72s). Introduction: `253d988bfd8d39ee19b5f788950532a07d7a9061`. A separate local spawn-broker cleanup warning is not the hosted failure; recovery state remains preserved.
- **Node compact-large-3-2: inherited fixture defect, causally reproduced.** The metadata-reader test resolves its drain milestone on both pre-quiescence retained-work waiting and later ordinary-call draining. The former correctly leaves `acceptingCalls=true`. Adding one controlled retained-work hold reproduces the exact assertion failure on both PR head and exact CI main (baseline 144.32s runner wall, 42.093s test body). A phase-specific observation passes the existing case (67.06s runner wall) and all 208 cases in the same 11-file shard on Node 24.19.0 with eight workers (124.24s). Fresh structured review is clean. Main independently landed the same phase-boundary repair in `f59e40793210d69e73bdc6695040fde0a69fed5c`; the duplicate local patch was removed, keeping this PR narrow. The original CI acquisition identity was not logged and remains unknown; the fixture defect does not require inferring that identity.
- **UI shards 3/9 and 7/9: inherited.** Exact CI main reproduces the suspended-dashboard and sidebar roster timeouts plus the stale prompt attachment (three failures, same assertions). Bootstrap request parking from `d51345aaf72cbfb13e1e31c081ecb4f15096cab8` parks the roster for 60s while these fixtures require it within 30s before they can resume admission; main fixes the fixtures in `9d606a28e0d5d10fcc77cc70ac810f782e0e6770`. Draft retirement from `082c68a9cbd83c20579e6e532d82e08cff17996f` starts IndexedDB cleanup without awaiting it before navigation, and both failing draft tests close the document immediately after the URL changes. The durable-writer variant did not reproduce locally; its cause is supported by that exact shared cleanup/navigation path and mocked Gateway execution, not by a passing rerun. Main fixes retirement-before-navigation in `a5106ecf04913d4ff5374d0991dac148faf06510` and strengthens fixture retirement waits in `114d443b2f8e6d7459491b627f363a8a2a631f22`. These browser fixtures replace the Gateway WebSocket with a mock; this PR's server retention code is not executed.
- **Android Play: outside this PR's executable/data path.** `ChatCompletedWorkLayoutTest.earlierTextAndToolResultReplacementRefreshesAnUnchangedTail` times out after 1s at line 478; 3,556 other tests pass. The test uses Android `ScreenshotFixture` mode and a literal in-process `chat.history` response, not a TypeScript Gateway. Android sources and build/dependency inputs match the exact baseline. The PR does change schema input to native generation, so source-path exclusion alone is insufficient: rerunning the actual Kotlin generator on exact CI main, then with the PR's two schema-file changes, produces **byte-identical GatewayProtocol.kt and OpenClawProtocolConstants.kt**. Native generation also succeeded in CI. Thus the diagnostics changes cannot supply different code/data to this assertion. The exact Android scheduling/loading condition that exceeded 1s remains unproven; no Android reproduction or timeout increase is claimed.
- **Aggregate gates:** the failed Actions `openclaw/ci-gate` and commit status summarize these job failures. The separate Security Review publisher succeeded; its red commit status is not an additional security finding.

CI remains historically red on this head because of these evidenced inherited failures. No new source push or rebase was made merely to obtain green status; the branch remains mergeable, and this task does not authorize merging. The new diagnostics do not identify the original live Knowledge holders until deployed and observed.

## Evidence

- Deslop follow-up: **15 newly added test cases**, down from 22 (6 reference/lifetime cases, 7 inspection cases, 2 drain cases). Existing suite totals below are regression coverage, not tests added. Production TypeScript net growth fell from **436 to 413 lines**; test TypeScript net growth fell from **566 to 495 lines**.
- Fixed the PR-created static import cycle: execution-frame type contracts now import schema-derived retention facts from the existing leaf type module, not the runtime diagnostics implementation. The full `pnpm check:architecture` command passes, including both runtime and Madge import-cycle scans.
- Follow-up lifetime/access regression run: **83 tests across 8 files passed** (101.64s). The retained consumer lifecycle extraction remains necessary to satisfy the existing lifetime-owner line cap; no new lifecycle policy or release path was introduced.
- Initial PR regression run: **145 tests in 13 files passed** (126.31s), including real instance references, GC/lifetime regression coverage, multiple owners, derived consumers, release, pending/failed cleanup, bounded payload-free output, administrator revocation, and request-registry isolation.
- Shared plugin contracts: **1,140 tests in 48 files passed** (244.38s).
- Earlier wider reload/local-command regression run: **252 tests in 14 files passed** (341.98s); this preceded the mechanical consumer/value-association extraction.
- After the final limit-normalization correction, all **6 diagnostics cases passed** again (48.16s). The reduced **7-case inspection suite passed** independently (18.64s).
- CI source-closure repair: the new runtime modules are now included in the existing trusted-wrapper inventory. The original inventory failure reproduced locally; all **17 existing eager-import closure cases passed** after the two-line correction (27.62s), with a clean fresh autoreview. No new tests or relaxed checks were added.
- Follow-up static proof: core typecheck, all **27 core-test typecheck graphs**, changed-file lint, formatting, whitespace, and line-cap ratchet passed.
- Follow-up structured autoreview: **no actionable findings**. Accepted the first review’s request to preserve existing finite/integer limit normalization; the final review covers that correction.
- Full build passed (245.4s). Formatting, documentation links, protocol generation/determinism, core typechecking, all 27 core-test typecheck graphs, and pre-deadcode changed-file guards passed. The build preceded removal of three unused private-helper export modifiers; focused validation covers that final cleanup.
- `pnpm check:changed` stopped at the dead-export scan. Three diagnostics-only unused exports were made private; the remaining unrelated `ClientVoiceToolEffect` export in `src/talk/client-voice-session-store.ts` is unchanged from the base and has no external references there. It is recorded separately, not suppressed. Both production and full-tree dead-export rechecks report only that Talk export; the script-export scan passes. All remaining selected guards passed when run separately: changed-file lint, native schema, database-first storage, media roundtrip, runtime sidecars, import cycles, webhook/pairing boundaries, and final core typecheck. No checks were suppressed.
- Build warning tracked separately: startup JavaScript gzip 365.2 KiB versus the 364.7 KiB budget; build exited successfully. Baseline attribution is not established, and no budget exception was added.

<summary>Changed test costs</summary>

Each command was `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. Wall times include normal runner/compiled-worker preparation; tests introduce no real waits or polling. CI values sum per-case durations from run `37852731605`; they exclude shared worker/build/setup cost and are not end-to-end shard wall time.

prs.title: docs: propose personal identity for native local connections
prs.body:
Related: #162164

## What Problem This Solves

A native app connected to its local Gateway cannot infer personal identity from that person's separate browser sign-in, but keeping personal sign-in on a separate remote/saved-profile path does not solve normal local Primary attribution.

## User Impact

No runtime change in this draft. It proposes an explicit personal sign-in journey for normal local Chat, Quick Chat, and Dashboard while preserving literal loopback transport, local lifecycle, optional Shared owner, and separate node/device credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

The document proposes Core-owned, revocable continuation of verified personal admission, bound to the paired device and intended Gateway. Initial Tailscale Serve admission and authenticated local data transport are separate steps. It reuses existing profile, pairing, native authentication intent, and TLS owners rather than inventing another identity store or treating shared credentials as a person.

This is a **design-review draft**, not a working fix or an accepted authentication API. Core must settle issuance/persistence, local server trust and rotation, provider validity/revocation, and Dashboard retirement before implementation. The document maps two subsequent code slices: Core/shared admission, then macOS Primary consumption. Existing iOS and Cloudflare work retains its attribution and scope. This advances, but does not close, the umbrella.

## Evidence

The proposal identifies source owners at main `6070074dabf6b45f74d4039590cd307640317862`, distinguishes the iOS contributor candidate from shipped functionality, links primary standards, and specifies the required positive/negative final-effect proof. No implementation tests, native runtime, installed-state upgrade, or live provider acceptance are claimed.

Documentation sanity passed: the repository docs inventory discovers the page; direct MDX 3.1.1 compilation and YAML frontmatter parsing passed using an existing installation. The normal pre-commit hook passed using the repository-required oxfmt 0.68.0 from an existing tooling owner, with no dependency installation or hook bypass. The normal repository MDX wrapper could not run without an owned dependency installation in the new worktree. No full build or product suite was run for this docs-only proposal.

I requested a second opinion from Daybreak through Codex AutoReview on this one-document design proposal before publication. The review completed with no P0-P2 findings. Its scope covered the proposed security boundaries and the distinction between requirements and implemented behavior; unchanged source and external PR contents were not supplied. This is an AI-assisted design review, not Core acceptance, a security certification or runtime proof.

`git diff --cached --check` passed for the sole added document. No runtime, source, tests, dependencies, configuration or release files are changed.
