prs.title: feat(subagents): carry a machine-readable reason on a registry-settled yielded collector
prs.body:
Related #165685

#164445, which this PR was stacked on, has merged (squash `e02ae3ecb66`). This branch merges `origin/main` at `bda0e040fec`, so `git diff origin/main...HEAD` is this PR's change only: 8 files, 49 insertions, 10 deletions (production 4 files +15/-3, tests 1 file +25/-5, docs 3 files +9/-2).

Simplified before review (the repo's `pr-simplify` pass, after the merge): the earlier revision also had an `agents.run` bridge assertion (that bridge reads the same `completionResult` projection as `agents_wait`), an `outputSchema` plus `reason` case (two independent spreads on one path), a standalone ordinary-failure test (now one assertion in the existing ordinary collector test), a settle-yielded unit test for a frozen completion the sweeper never settles, and an `agents_wait` unit test (its schema half is now one `Value.Check` on every real wait result in the integration test). Those are gone, as are restatements in the three docs. Reduction against the previous revision's own change (merged onto the same main): 10 files +211/-14 to 8 files +49/-10. Production behavior is unchanged.

Scope: part 1 of #165685 only (the machine-readable reason on a registry-settled yielded collector). Part 2 (leaf diagnostics) is not in this PR. ClawSweeper's comment on the issue says `agents_wait` stays collector-only and leaf diagnostics belong to `subagents list`, so this PR makes no leaf change and claims none.

## What Problem This Solves

A caller of `agents_wait` cannot tell a collector the registry sweeper settled as failed, because it was parked in a legacy yield with no recorded outcome, from a collector that failed for an ordinary reason: both come back as `status: "failed"` and only the free-text `error` differs.

Since #164445, the registry sweeper settles a collector that an earlier version persisted as yielded without a collector completion. A row with a recorded `ok` outcome keeps it and settles as `done`. A row with no recorded outcome settles as `{ status: "failed", error: "Collector yielded under a build that predates the admission gate, ..." }`. Recovery code that wants to rerun only that case has to match the English sentence in `error`, which is a message and not a contract.

## User Impact

`agents_wait` gains one optional field, `reason`. The `agents.run` host bridge returns the same completion object, but the Code Mode guest helper turns any non-`done` completion into a `SwarmAgentError` carrying only `runId`, `status` and a detail string, so guest code does not see `reason`; this PR does not change that helper. It is `"yielded_without_result"` only on a collector the sweeper settled as failed from a legacy parked yield with no recorded outcome. Every other completion has no `reason` key: a legacy `ok` collector settled as `done`, a legacy collector settled with its own recorded `error`, ordinary failures, killed, timeout, done, and schema errors are unchanged.

No config, schema, or migration changes. `status` keeps its four values. Nothing settles earlier, later, or differently, and no stored outcome changes; only the recorded fact is new. A collector settled by a build without this change has no `reason` and keeps returning exactly what it returned before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The settle path already knows why it is completing the run: `settleYielded: true` on the completion request, and the outcome it settles with. The reason is recorded where the collector completion is frozen (`updateSwarmCollectorCompletion`), as one optional member of the existing `collectorCompletion` payload, then projected by `completionResult()` in `agents-wait-tool.ts`.

- `subagent-registry-lifecycle-completion.ts`: passes `"yielded_without_result"` to `updateSwarmCollectorCompletion` only when `completeParams.settleYielded === true` and the row being settled has no recorded `execution.outcome`, which is exactly the case where the sweeper substituted the diagnostic error. `settleYielded` has one producer, the sweeper's `settleUnreachableYieldedSubagentRun`, which settles with the row's recorded outcome when there is one and with the diagnostic error otherwise. A settled row with a recorded `ok` or `error` outcome keeps that outcome and is not marked. A row cannot acquire a recorded outcome while yielded (`pauseSubagentRun` in `subagent-registry-run-pause.ts` deletes any recorded outcome when it parks the row), so a recorded outcome on a yielded row is a legacy shape. `planTerminalCompletion` returns before any mutation when a settle request meets a run that is no longer yielded.
- `swarm-collector.ts`: records the reason on the completion it creates. A collector whose completion is already frozen returns before the write, so a frozen completion is never rewritten and never gains a reason.
- `subagent-registry.types.ts`: `reason?: "yielded_without_result"` on the persisted collector completion.
- `agents-wait-tool.ts`: `reason` added to `CollectorCompletionSchema` (`additionalProperties: false`) and to `completionResult()`.
- Docs: `docs/tools/swarm.md` (result shape, and a sentence telling callers to branch on `reason` rather than `error` text), `docs/tools/subagents/tool-reference.md`, `docs/concepts/subagent-yield-handoff.md`.

Why this is not a persisted-schema change: the collector completion lives inside `subagent_runs.payload_json`; an optional key is absent on every existing row and read as undefined. No column, index, or migration changes, and `docs/reference/database-schemas` is untouched. Existing rows are never rewritten to add it: a frozen completion returns before the write, and only a completion created by the failed settlement carries it. The `$.collectorCompletion.*` retained-payload and session-list path lists in `subagent-registry.store.sqlite.ts` do not name `reason`, and `projectSubagentRunForSessionList` copies only `status`, so the field does not enter any trimmed projection. `CHANGELOG.md` is release-owned and is not edited.

The one other consumer of the schema, the `agents.run` host bridge, reuses `waitForCollectorCompletion`, which reads the same `completionResult()` projection, so its result carries the field with no further change and the `agents_wait` assertions cover it. The Code Mode guest helper (`code-mode-swarm-controller-source.ts`) reads `error`, `schemaError`, and `result` only, throws `SwarmAgentError` for a non-`done` status, and is unaffected.

## Contract choices

- Shape: a one-member literal `reason: "yielded_without_result"` on the collector completion, not a new `status`. #165685 asks for a field `agents_wait` callers can branch on without parsing `error`; keeping `status` at its four values leaves every existing consumer of the union untouched. The schema is a single `Type.Literal`; a later cause would widen it to a union of literals without touching `status`.
- Surface: `agents_wait` (and the `agents.run` host bridge result, which is the same object), which is what #165685 asks for. The Code Mode guest error, session list and board projections are unchanged.

## Contract table

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Collector parked in a legacy yield with no recorded outcome, settled by the registry sweeper | `status: "failed"`, `error` unchanged, `reason: "yielded_without_result"` |
| Same collector with an `outputSchema` and no captured structured output | `status: "failed"`, `schemaError: "structured_output was not called"` and `reason: "yielded_without_result"` together |
| Collector parked in a legacy yield with a recorded `ok` outcome, settled by the registry sweeper | `status: "done"` with the reply its yielded turn ended on, no `reason` |
| Collector parked in a legacy yield with a recorded `error` outcome, settled by the registry sweeper | `status: "failed"`, `error` is the recorded error, no `reason` |
| Collector failed or interrupted for any other cause (run ended with outcome `error`, completion frozen as `failed` by the normal terminal path) | no `reason` |
| Collector `done`, `killed`, or `timeout` | no `reason` |
| Collector whose completion is already frozen when a settle request arrives | no `reason`, completion unchanged |
| Collector settled by a build without this change | no `reason` |
| Unknown `reason` value in a result | not declared: `CollectorCompletionSchema` has `additionalProperties: false` and declares `reason` as the single literal |
| `status` values | unchanged: `done`, `failed`, `killed`, `timeout` |

`reason` is independent of `schemaError`: it is present exactly when the registry settled the collector as failed, whether or not a schema error is also recorded.

auto_merge.commit_title: feat(subagents): carry a machine-readable reason on a registry-settled yielded collector (#165797)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* fix(subagents): collector wait pends forever when persisted yielded

- add resolveYieldedRunContinuation as the owner of whether a yielded run
  can still be continued: a collector without a recorded result never can
- the registry sweeper settles such a row through the existing completion
  owner with an explicit settleYielded request, keeping the yield time as
  endedAt, so agents_wait on a collector persisted yielded before the
  collector-yield fix returns failed with a diagnostic instead of pending
- the settleYielded opt-in applies only while the row read inside the
  mutation is still yielded, so a late request cannot rewrite a run that
  has since resumed or finished
- move the stale-active and unreachable-yield settlement into
  subagent-registry-sweep-settle.ts to keep the sweeper under its line cap
- nothing new is persisted; no schema, tool parameter or snapshot changes

* fix(subagents): leaf stays yielded when no continuation in 24 hours

- resolveYieldedRunContinuation now also answers for a leaf: once 24 hours
  have passed since the pause, measured from the execution.endedAt that
  markSubagentRunPausedAfterYield already records (never earlier than the
  row's creation), no continuation is expected and the sweeper settles it
  as error through the completion owner, keeping that time as endedAt
- a run that still owes a wake to unfinished children stays continuable:
  the pending-children selection is shared with the execution observation
  instead of duplicated, and wakeOnDescendantSettle rows stay untouched
- a collector with a frozen result is never replaced by the age expiry
- also settles leaf rows that older builds left parked; nothing new is
  persisted, no tool parameter or snapshot changes
- tests: legacy rows in both persisted shapes, an expired leaf, restart
  before and after the bound, a continuation racing the sweeper at the
  bound, and planner level guards for kill-owned and resumed rows

* docs(subagents): document settlement of parked yielded runs

- tool reference: the fixed 24 hour bound for a paused child, the
  collector settlement on the first sweep after restore, and why a
  legacy collector settles as error where a new one ends as an ok terminal
- yield handoff: the owner of whether a paused run can still be continued

* fix(subagents): message wait settled as expired when a yielded run is swept

- Settle only a collector that yielded without a recorded result; a declared
  message wait, a paused leaf of any age and an orchestrator waiting on
  descendants stay continuable.
- Drop the 24 hour leaf expiry, its diagnostic, the createdAt clamp and the
  pending-children extraction that only existed for it.
- Cover both persisted legacy collector shapes (outcome absent, outcome ok)
  and keep the original yield time as the end time.
- Document that a declared message wait is not bounded by this settlement.

* fix(subagents): kill claim cleared when a settle request races a stop

- Refuse a yielded settle inside the completion mutation when the current
  row is kill-owned, using the same predicate the sweeper checks.
- A claim keeps its pause reason, so the old guard accepted the stale
  request and the kill branch cleared the newer claim.
- Cover a claim published while the settle request waits for the terminal
  completion lock, then the kill completing as a cancellation.

* fix(subagents): name the missing side in the legacy yielded collector diagnostic

- The diagnostic now says the collector was parked by a build that predates
  the admission gate, has no recorded collectorCompletion, and that nothing
  can continue it.
- It tells the operator to rerun the collector and end its turn normally
  instead of calling sessions_yield. Status stays failed; no logic change.
- Tests pin the new text via the "no recorded collectorCompletion" fragment.

* test(subagents): satisfy the mock-exports ratchet in the settle-yielded test

- Spread the real agent-bundle-mcp-tools module via importOriginal and
  override only retireSessionMcpRuntimeForSessionKey, as check:test-mock-exports requires.
- Test behavior is unchanged; the other PR test files had no findings.

* feat(subagents): carry a machine-readable reason on a registry-settled yielded collector

- agents_wait completions gain an optional `reason`, set to "yielded_without_result" only when the registry sweeper settles a legacy parked collector
- the reason is recorded on the existing collectorCompletion payload at settle time; no new status literal and no storage migration
- every other failed, killed, or timed-out collector omits `reason`; when anything settles is unchanged
- documented in the agents_wait result shape and the yield handoff notes

* test(subagents): pin yielded collector exclusions at the real registry

- Restart integration gains two collector controls: one with a recorded result, which the sweep leaves untouched, and one whose stop is claimed, which completes as a cancellation
- Remove subagent-registry-run-pause.test.ts and subagent-registry-sweep-settle.test.ts; their cases are covered through the persisted registry

* fix(subagents): keep a legacy collector's recorded outcome when settling

- A legacy yielded collector with a recorded execution outcome settles with that outcome, its end time and the reply its yielded turn ended on, the same result a collector that yields now gets
- Only a row with no recorded outcome settles as the diagnostic error
- Reply capture no longer refuses a yielded run that no continuation can reach
- Restart integration test pins both shapes through agents_wait: ok returns done with the reply and no error; absent returns failed with the diagnostic

* test(subagents): prepare the runtime config snapshot in the settle-yielded test

* fix(subagents): mark a settled yield only when the row had no recorded outcome

The reason keyed off the settled outcome being an error, so a legacy yielded
collector whose recorded error outcome the sweeper kept would have been marked
too. Key it off the fact the docs describe: the row had no recorded outcome and
the sweeper substituted the diagnostic. Cover the recorded-error shape.

* simplify: drop duplicate collector reason tests and doc restatements

- Remove the agents.run bridge assertion: the bridge reads the same completionResult projection as agents_wait.
- Remove the outputSchema plus reason case: schemaError and reason are independent spreads on one path.
- Fold the ordinary-failure case into the existing ordinary collector test as one assertion.
- Remove the frozen-completion unit test: the sweeper never settles a collector with a frozen completion, and the early return predates this change.
- Replace the agents_wait unit test with a schema check inside the integration wait surface; drop the unknown-literal and duplicate ordinary assertions.
- Shorten the completion comment and the three doc paragraphs to the one new fact each.

---------

Co-authored-by: Mitchell Etzel <etzelm@users.noreply.github.com>

prs.title: improve(test): speed up package recovery integrity assertions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The package recovery integration test spends most of its runtime deeply comparing snapshots that contain a multi-megabyte runtime bundle.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The existing recovery proof runs faster while retaining checks that rejected stale commands leave file contents and inodes unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compare the ordered inode arrays and use `Buffer.equals` for each file’s exact bytes and length. The same real package build, detached recovery commands, four-file snapshot, and three stale-command rejection cases remain. No fixtures, cases, timeouts, or retries change. Binary mismatch diagnostics become a boolean assertion rather than a large object diff.

## Evidence

- Earlier AWS diagnosis on `2a49c621e7f7` measured 58.975 seconds across the three nested snapshot comparisons. With this assertion change, the package case took 4.437 seconds (63.630 seconds in the diagnostic baseline); the full two-case file passed in 34.034 seconds wall time. These are observations on that historical source, not a current-head benchmark guarantee.
- [Prior candidate and negative-control run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ad84041a32e5d067fd67d84887699cce): a temporary one-byte mutation in the recovery-helper snapshot failed at the new byte comparison, as intended. The negative control was removed after proof.
- [Current candidate AWS proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_55bc87f386c7f9fae00ac170e2a411ff): pinned base `ab6d6bdc504b` plus this exact patch; both existing cases pass. `pnpm test test/scripts/managed-handoff-build-config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`: **39.078 seconds wall**, package case **4.430 seconds**. AWS `m7a.xlarge`, Node 24.21.0, repository-pinned Bun. Format, targeted lint, and the owning `test-root-scripts` type graph pass. [Type-check proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f633918b064b4e795db278f1fbaa4966) took 17.492 seconds wall.
- The changed-path type-check selector failed on inherited graph-size limits (`gateway-root`: 725 roots; `plugins-platform`: 724; limit: 720). This patch changes no root membership or compiler configuration. Its fallback compiler checks passed; the direct owning-graph check above also passed. No limits were changed.
- [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39340461091) completed successfully on head `a0e3bbd30212`: **16 jobs passed, no failures**. The [tooling job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39340461091/job/118360947627) ran both edited-file cases: **11.327 seconds reported file duration**, including **7.651 seconds** for the package case.
- Fresh independent review: no actionable findings through P2. [Hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177821#issuecomment-6279675802): no findings or before-merge items; platinum readiness/proof, diamond patch quality.

The investigation began with a historical 120-second CI timeout. Its exact cause and attribution to the earlier campaign remain unproven; this PR removes a separately measured assertion bottleneck.

LoC churn against the pinned base `ab6d6bdc504b`: **tests +5 / −1 (6 changed lines; net +4)**; production, documentation, configuration, and dependencies: **0**. The four extra lines preserve ordered inode and exact byte checks without adding a helper or permanent test cases.

prs.title: feat(subagents): show how long a continuable yielded leaf has been paused
prs.body:
Related #165685 This covers part 2 of #165685 only (pause age) and does not close it. The continuation stage vocabulary (never enqueued, enqueued, accepted, applied) is not included, and `agents_wait` is unchanged. There is no expiry, and nothing about when a run settles, sweeps, restores or wakes changes. ## What Problem This Solves A parked leaf that waits for a message shows no pause age, so an operator cannot tell a leaf paused a minute ago from one paused two days ago. On a real isolated Gateway, `subagents list` for a leaf paused about 1.8 days earlier reports only `waiting for external continuation`. The entry carries the wait kind, `deliveryStatus`, runtime and `endedAt`, but no age. ## User Impact `subagents list` entries and the native `subagents action=wait` run snapshots gain an optional `pausedForMs` for a yielded leaf that only an external continuation can resume. The list line reads `waiting for external continuation, paused 1d 19h`. Nothing else in either output changes, and the field is absent for every other run. No config, schema, migration or prompt change. The tool schema and description are unchanged, so no prompt or tool-schema snapshot moves. ## Why This Change Was Made The review of the issue asked for additive fields derived from registry-owned facts, and said pause age alone cannot establish a continuation stage. This change ships only the age. - The yield records its pause time as `execution.endedAt`. `markSubagentRunPausedAfterYield` also sets `pauseReason`, makes the execution terminal, and clears the outcome, `endedReason`, archive deadline, cleanup state, delivery state and captured result; `endedAt` is the one of those writes that the age reads, so no new persisted field is needed. - `resolveYieldedLeafPausedForMs(entry, observation, now)` (`subagent-execution-observation.ts`) returns `now - endedAt` only when the existing observation reports a `waiting` / `external` wait, the run is terminal, it is not a collector, and `endedAt` is a finite number. A parent waiting on announced children observes `kind: "children"` and gets nothing. - `subagents list` calls it with the observation it already computed and the list context's `now`, and appends `, paused ` with the existing `formatDurationCompact` (spaced). - `subagents action=wait` calls it with an observation built from full run rows that include the announced children of each yielded run. Both paths hand `observeSubagentExecution` full rows from `prepareSubagentRunReadSnapshot`, so a parent whose children exist only in persisted rows is classified the same way in both. The wait snapshot is handed only the selected runs, so `prepareSubagentRunsSnapshotForRunIds` takes a `yieldedChildren` option (set by the wait only): the read scope and selection add the children of selected yielded runs, and the consumed map carries them for observation only. Waits that select no yielded run read exactly what they read before. - The wait `attention` check still observes with no children (existing behavior); a code comment says so. `docs/tools/subagents/tool-reference.md` documents the field next to the list and wait output. Tests: one SQLite-backed tool test covers both outputs and the persisted-only parent; one unit test covers the guard cases. An earlier revision also had an in-memory list test; every mutation it caught is caught by these two, so it was removed. ### Is `endedAt` stable while a run stays paused? Two callers mark the same row for one yield: `subagent-registry-requester-yield.ts` (`Date.now()` at its commit) and `subagent-registry-completion-runtime.ts` (`terminal.endedAt` from the lifecycle end event). When both run, the second write replaces `endedAt` if the values differ. Calling the real function twice with timestamps 4000 ms apart gives `endedAt` 50000000, then 50004000, and a third call with the same value does not mutate. The age can therefore shift by the delay between those two events of one turn end. That is a bounded imprecision, not a drift: it is the gap between two events of the same turn, small next to the hours and days this field exists to show. That gap was not measured on a live yield. Paths read for any rewrite of `endedAt` on a row that is still paused: - Settle: the completion path in `subagent-registry-lifecycle-completion.ts` returns early for a yielded row unless the reason is killed (the `pauseReason === "sessions_yield"` guard comes before any write). Interrupted recovery is refused for a yielded row in the same file and in `subagent-registry-restart-recovery.ts` / `-helpers.ts`. - Kill: a killed completion clears `pauseReason`, so the row is no longer listed as a paused leaf (`isYieldedSubagentRun` also excludes kill intent, kill reconciliation and killed end reasons). - Restore: `subagent-registry-restore.ts` only resumes rows; its writes touch `suppressSessionEffects` and queued collectors, never `endedAt`. - Sweeper: `subagent-registry-sweeper.ts` sets `endedAt` only for rows that have none; session cleanup is deferred for yielded rows (`isSessionCleanupDeferred`); the orphan path reuses the existing `endedAt` and goes through the settle path above. - Adoption of a paused row by its continuation (`subagent-registry-run-recovery.ts`) replaces it with a new run id, so the paused row is superseded rather than rewritten. - Collector rows write `endedAt` in `swarm-collector.ts` and are excluded by the `collect` guard. - Startup settlement of requester continuations without a saved operator source (#175033) writes `delivery`, `suppressCompletionDelivery` and `cleanupHandled` on a paused row (and drops an orchestrator's `wakeOnDescendantSettle`) and leaves `execution.endedAt` and `pauseReason` alone (checked field by field on the seeded rows in both Gateway arms). I found no path other than the two yield callers that rewrites `endedAt` on a still-paused row. A later yield of the same resumed run restarts the age, which is the intended reading. ## Contract choices 1. Age only. `pausedForMs` is the only new vocabulary, and no continuation stage is reported. The registry holds no field that records an authoritative enqueued, accepted or applied fact (`requesterSettleWake.pauseNotice` records a wait registration, and `delivery.status` is cleared by the pause), so a stage would need a new recorded fact. Reporting a stage from the age alone would claim something the registry does not know. 2. A future `endedAt` (clock skew) gives `pausedForMs: 0`. The field's presence means "this is a continuable yielded leaf", and that is true regardless of clocks, so it is not dropped when the clocks disagree. The list line shows no age only when the value is exactly `0`, because `formatDurationCompact` renders nothing for `0`. The observation test asserts the `0`. 3. Open question for the owner: main lists a yielded row whose completion delivery it has marked `failed` (`permanent_failure`, no saved operator source) as `waiting for external continuation`, so this change gives it a `pausedForMs` too. That follows main's observation rather than adding a delivery guard here; whether such a row should show an age is part of the same direction decision as the field itself. ## Contract table | Case | `pausedForMs` | List line | |---|---|---| | Yielded leaf, terminal, no pending announced children | `now - execution.endedAt` | `waiting for external continuation, paused 1d 19h` | | Parent yielded while an announced child is pending (in memory or only in persisted rows) | absent | `waiting on 1 child` | | Collector row carrying a yield | absent | unchanged | | Running run | absent | unchanged | | Ordinary finished run | absent | unchanged | | Yielded row marked killed | absent (not listed active) | unchanged | | Yield row with no `endedAt` | absent | unchanged | | `endedAt` in the future | `0` | the line omits the age | ## Evidence All of the following ran on one machine (Mac Studio) after merging main `09cf9282b8f` into this branch as merge commit `4b2a9973805`. The merge resolved two conflicts with #170998, which moved the read-scope merge into `mergeSubagentRunReadScope`: the `yieldedChildren` expansion now sits in that function's `runIds` branch, byte-identical apart from one indent level, and the registry test sits after the test #170998 added. `git diff 09cf9282b8f...4b2a9973805` is the same 8 files, +225 / -16, as before the merge. The merge commit's tree is `e9933d7baf0297245e91dc66b35bbfd4e4ad6673` (`git rev-parse 4b2a9973805^{tree}`); the evidence was produced on the unsigned commit `f68a4d3331d` with that same tree, before signing. Every section below was rerun on that tree; BEFORE is a clean build of `09cf9282b8f`. The expansion inside `mergeSubagentRunReadScope` runs only for the wait's `runIds` scope and only when a selected run is yielded; every other scope of that function returns the same output as on main. ### Real built Gateway, before and after Each arm is its own checkout with `pnpm install` and `pnpm build`, started as `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port

--bind loopback --auth token --token x --allow-unconfigured` with `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` pointing at an isolated state directory. No model provider is configured, because neither read runs a model. The state was seeded once with main `09cf9282b8f`, through the production registry persistence path (`persistRegistryFixture` into a real SQLite database), and each arm starts on a byte-identical `cp -a` copy restored to the same path. The rows are a parked leaf paused 43h12m before seeding, an orchestrator paused 50h with one announced child that was still running when seeded, and a collector row carrying a yield. `subagents list` and `subagents action=wait` are read through `POST /tools/invoke` with `sessionKey: "agent:main:main"`. BEFORE is `09cf9282b8f`, AFTER is `4b2a9973805`. On this base, startup recovery settles what a seeded row cannot keep (main #175033 settles requester continuations whose original operator source was not saved, without inventing one): it marks the announced child interrupted by the restart, and sets `delivery.status: failed` with "The original operator source was not saved for this requester continuation" on the leaf and the orchestrator. It does not touch `pauseReason`, the terminal status or `execution.endedAt` of either yielded row, it does the same in both arms, and both arms still list the leaf as `waiting for external continuation` and the orchestrator as `waiting on 1 child`, because the child's completion announcement is still pending. Persisted `subagent_runs` rows, SHA-256 of `SELECT * FROM subagent_runs ORDER BY run_id` (4 rows each time): | Point | BEFORE | AFTER | |---|---|---| | Restored copy | `242774eb1d7d` | `242774eb1d7d` | | After Gateway start (startup recovery writes) | `e064e6d9715b` | `6635846e9823` | | After both reads | `e064e6d9715b` | `6635846e9823` | | After Gateway stop | `e064e6d9715b` | `6635846e9823` | The two arms differ after start only in the timestamps startup recovery writes for the announced child (`execution.endedAt`, outcome, delivery timestamps), which are wall clock at each start. Every yielded row is identical between the arms. The reads write nothing in either arm. Both arms log the same two warnings, both about the seeded running child that has no process behind it: `subagent completion authority was not restored runId=run-announced-child` ("Subagent restart recovery lacks its original operator source") and `Subagent announce flow failed during cleanup for run run-announced-child: Error: Subagent completion authority is no longer active`. BEFORE, `subagents list` text: ``` active subagents: 1. restart-recoverable work (model n/a, 1m) waiting for external continuation 2. restart-recoverable work (model n/a, 1m) waiting for external continuation 3. restart-recoverable work (model n/a, 1m) waiting on 1 child recent (last 60m): (none) ``` AFTER, `subagents list` text: ``` active subagents: 1. restart-recoverable work (model n/a, 1m) waiting for external continuation 2. restart-recoverable work (model n/a, 1m) waiting for external continuation, paused 1d 19h 3. restart-recoverable work (model n/a, 1m) waiting on 1 child recent (last 60m): (none) ``` Line 1 is the collector row, line 2 the parked leaf (`endedAt` 1792126057701), line 3 the orchestrator. List entries and wait runs, extracted from the two JSON responses of each arm: ``` BEFORE list run-collector status="waiting for external continuation" pausedForMs=(absent) BEFORE list run-parked-leaf status="waiting for external continuation" pausedForMs=(absent) BEFORE list run-awaiting-orchestrator status="waiting on 1 child" pausedForMs=(absent) BEFORE wait reason=attention BEFORE wait run-parked-leaf status=waiting endedAt=1792126057701 pausedForMs=(absent) BEFORE wait run-awaiting-orchestrator status=waiting endedAt=1792101577701 pausedForMs=(absent) BEFORE wait run-collector status=waiting endedAt=1792274377701 pausedForMs=(absent) AFTER list run-collector status="waiting for external continuation" pausedForMs=(absent) AFTER list run-parked-leaf status="waiting for external continuation" pausedForMs=156026931 AFTER list run-awaiting-orchestrator status="waiting on 1 child" pausedForMs=(absent) AFTER wait reason=attention AFTER wait run-parked-leaf status=waiting endedAt=1792126057701 pausedForMs=156026963 AFTER wait run-awaiting-orchestrator status=waiting endedAt=1792101577701 pausedForMs=(absent) AFTER wait run-collector status=waiting endedAt=1792274377701 pausedForMs=(absent) ``` `156026963` ms is 43.34 hours: the 43h12m seeded pause plus the time between seeding and the read. The wall clock taken right after the AFTER reads was 1792282084708, which minus `endedAt` is 156027007, 44 ms after the wait value. List and wait agree for every shape here: the leaf has an age in both, the orchestrator and the collector have none in either. The persisted-only parent cannot be constructed against a live Gateway. A Gateway restores every persisted row into its in-memory registry at start, so the orchestrator's announced child above is also in memory. That case is proven in the registry test below, on a real SQLite registry whose in-memory registry is empty. ### Tests At `4b2a9973805`, one `pnpm test` run over the two changed test files plus `subagent-list.test.ts` (3 Vitest shards), 15 passed, 0 failed: | File | Result | |---|---| | `subagent-execution-observation.test.ts` | 4 passed | | `subagent-list.test.ts` (not changed by this PR; main now has 8 tests here) | 8 passed | | `subagents-tool.registry.test.ts` | 3 passed (main's 2, including the 5,000-run control-scope bound from #170998, plus this PR's 1) | Owning directories at `4b2a9973805`, `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/ src/agents/tools/` (6 Vitest shards). The runner stops at the first failing shard and the command did not go green in one run on this machine, so it was run three times and shard 6's three files were then run on their own: ``` Test Files 34 passed (34) Tests 302 passed (302) Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 42 passed (42) Test Files 45 passed (45) Tests 805 passed (805) Test Files 54 passed | 1 skipped (55) Tests 750 passed | 1 skipped (751) Test Files 1 failed | 125 passed | 1 skipped (127) Tests 1 failed | 1941 passed | 1 skipped (1943) Test Files 3 passed (3) Tests 90 passed (90) ``` That is 3930 passed, 2 skipped and 1 failed. The failure is `web-fetch.sandbox.test.ts` ("stages readable output without granting guest writes in a read-only workspace"), which calls GNU `stat -c` and fails on macOS `stat` (`stat: illegal option -- c`); it fails the same way alone on main `09cf9282b8f`. Shard 3 failed in two of the four full runs on `swarm-tools.integration.test.ts` (see below) and passed in the other two. `swarm-tools.integration.test.ts` "spawns text and structured collectors ... drains them in completion order" fails intermittently with `expected [ 3, 1 ] to deeply equal [ 1, 3 ]`. The assertion records which collector launch finishes its structured-output call first; launch 1 builds the child tool set cold and launch 3 warm, so they race. It fails on main `09cf9282b8f` too. Counted runs on this machine (load average 25 to 68): main's production code failed 4 of 19 (2 of 13 in a separate main checkout, 2 of 6 in this branch's checkout with main's versions of the five production files), this branch failed 13 of 23 (7 of 13 alone, 4 of 6 in the same in-place comparison, 2 of 4 full lane runs). The assertion fires before any `subagents` wait runs, and this change adds no import and only constant-time work on the spawn path, so I found no mechanism for the higher rate on the branch; it is reported here rather than called noise. The registry test persists a leaf and an orchestrator with an announced child into a real SQLite registry and reads both `subagents list` and the native wait snapshot through the tool, with nothing seeded into the in-memory registry. The orchestrator's announced child therefore exists only in persisted rows, and the test asserts the orchestrator gets no `pausedForMs` in either output. It fixes `Date` with `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["Date"] })` and `vi.setSystemTime` and asserts exact ages. The observation test passes `now` explicitly and needs no timers. Ordinary finished, running, killed and collector runs are covered once, in the observation test, because they all fail the same guard in `resolveYieldedLeafPausedForMs`; the list and wait outputs only forward its result. ### Regression proof Each production behavior was mutated in place at `4b2a9973805`, the two new test files were each run on their own, and the tree was restored (`git status` clean afterwards). Every failure is an assertion failure; the first one in each failing file is quoted. | Mutation | `subagent-execution-observation.test.ts` | `subagents-tool.registry.test.ts` | |---|---|---| | drop the collector guard | fails: `expected 90000000 to be undefined` | passes | | drop the `external` wait-kind guard | fails: `expected 90000000 to be undefined` | fails: `expected { runId: 'waiting-orchestrator', …(8) } to not have property "pausedForMs"` | | drop the terminal-status guard | fails: `expected 90000000 to be undefined` | passes | | measure from `createdAt` instead of `endedAt` | fails: `expected 207717711911 to be 90000000 // Object.is equality` | fails: `expected +0 to be 155520000 // Object.is equality` | | list entry omits the field | passes | fails: `expected undefined to be 155520000 // Object.is equality` | | list line omits `, paused ` | passes | fails: `expected 'active subagents:\n1. parked-leaf (mo…' to contain 'waiting for external continuation, pa…'` | | wait run omits the field | passes | fails: `expected undefined to be 155520000 // Object.is equality` | | wait observes with no children | passes | fails: `expected { runId: 'waiting-orchestrator', …(8) } to not have property "pausedForMs"` | | wait does not read yielded children into its snapshot (`yieldedChildren: false`) | passes | fails: `expected { runId: 'waiting-orchestrator', …(8) } to not have property "pausedForMs"` | | wait observes in-memory children only (`subagentRuns.values()`) | passes | fails: `expected { runId: 'waiting-orchestrator', …(8) } to not have property "pausedForMs"` | | the merged read scope skips the yielded-children expansion (`const yielded = false`, in `mergeSubagentRunReadScope`) | passes | fails: `expected { runId: 'waiting-orchestrator', …(8) } to not have property "pausedForMs"` | Every mutation is caught by at least one of the two files. The last three are the persisted-only parent; the eleventh mutates the conflict-resolved code itself: with either mutation the orchestrator whose announced child exists only in persisted rows gets an age. On main `09cf9282b8f` with these two test files copied in, both fail (`resolveYieldedLeafPausedForMs is not a function`; `expected undefined to be 155520000 // Object.is equality`). With the production code restored, both pass. ### Measured test cost Measured at `62da7f32daa`, before the merge, and not rerun after it: the two test files are unchanged by the merge apart from main's own registry test, which this PR does not own. Method: `pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`, three runs per file, wall time from `/usr/bin/time -p`. The Mac Studio was carrying unrelated load from other sessions (1-minute load average 37 to 51 during these runs), so these are upper-end numbers. No CI run exists yet for this commit; a changed file runs again in every CI run that selects its lane. | File (lane) | Tests | Vitest duration, runs 1 / 2 / 3 | Wall, runs 1 / 2 / 3 | This PR's test, runs 1 / 2 / 3 | |---|---|---|---|---| | `subagent-execution-observation.test.ts` (unit-fast) | 4 | 2.82 / 2.00 / 1.10 s | 8.29 / 5.86 / 4.63 s | 0 / 0 / 0 ms | | `subagents-tool.registry.test.ts` (agents-tools) | 2 | 42.05 / 24.50 / 28.12 s | 52.06 / 29.92 / 33.88 s | 1154 / 673 / 575 ms | The registry file exceeds the 5 s target because of its existing transform and import cost (transform plus import is 90% to 92% of its duration); this PR adds one test of about 0.6 to 1.2 s. It boots one real `withOpenClawTestState` SQLite state, the same fixture the file already uses. The contract is that the wait path reads announced children from persisted rows, which no cheaper layer exercises, because the in-memory registry is exactly what a cheaper test would seed. `subagent-list.test.ts` is no longer changed by this PR. ### Other checks | Check | Result | |---|---| | `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 pnpm check:changed --base 09cf9282b8f` | exit 1 on two steps, both reproduced unchanged on a clean `09cf9282b8f` worktree and both about files this PR does not touch: `max-lines suppression ratchet` (new suppressions in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`) and `core tsgo graph boundary` (`gateway-root: 728` and `infra: 741` test roots over the 720 limit). The other 32 steps pass, including line-cap growth ratchet, SQLite worker, SQLite dialect, test timeout race and first-party mock export ratchets, format changed files, typecheck core, typecheck core tests, lint core changed files (0 warnings, 0 errors) | | `node --import tsx scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts` (the step skipped above) | exit 1 on 30 entries, the same 30 on main `09cf9282b8f`; none is in a file this PR touches | | `git diff --check 09cf9282b8f...4b2a9973805` and `oxfmt --check` on the 8 changed files | exit 0 | ## Gaps - The age is a fact about when the yield was recorded. It does not say whether a continuation was sent, accepted or applied. - `endedAt` can be rewritten by a few seconds when both yield callers mark the same row (see above); that gap was not measured live. - Wall clock skew between the host that wrote `endedAt` and the host that reads it shows up directly in the age. A future `endedAt` reads as `0`. - Real-Gateway coverage uses a copied, seeded state directory, not a leaf yielded live by a model turn. The seed goes through the production registry persistence path. - The persisted-only parent is covered by the SQLite-backed registry test, not by the live Gateway run, for the reason given under Evidence. - On the new base, startup recovery marks the seeded yielded rows' completion delivery failed, because a seeded row has no operator source a real Gateway can restore. The age reads only `pauseReason`, the execution observation and `execution.endedAt`, none of which that write changes. A leaf yielded live by a model turn was not run. - The wait `attention` check observes without children, so a parent waiting on announced children is in `attention` while correctly having no `pausedForMs`. This is existing behavior and is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(sessions): long transcripts pin a database read snapshot while being decoded
prs.body:
Closes #171467
Related: #160386

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a gateway with a long-running session, a memory session-index pass over a large transcript holds a SQLite read transaction on the agent database open for the whole time it takes to decompress, parse and project the transcript (the fenced transcript read used by hydration and SessionManager open shares the same in-transaction decode; it is not changed here, see Gaps), which logs `slow SQLite transaction hold ... operation="session transcript export snapshot"` (on current main also `operation="session transcript export batch"`, the memory batch) and keeps agent-database WAL checkpoints from completing.

#171467 is scoped to exactly this defect: the agent-database export snapshot is held across decode and parse of a whole transcript (and, in the memory batch, of every transcript in the group). Its expected behavior, quoted: "Exports of one large transcript should not stop passive checkpoints on the agent database from completing." That is what this PR delivers for the export snapshot reader and for the memory export batch; the readers it leaves alone are listed under Gaps. #157092 reported the same hold earlier and was closed by #157278, which bounded the retained projection memory and added the reset-boundary path; on main the export still decodes, parses and projects inside the read transaction, and three of the #160386 reports below post-date #157278.

Four commenters on #160386 report exactly this line (1.0 to 6 s per hold on stores from about 260 MB to 2.6 GB, hundreds of times a day), and a fifth reports testing this approach on a 115 KB transcript. The `openclaw-state WAL checkpoint TRUNCATE remained busy` reports in the thread concern the shared-state database, which this reader never opens; they are a separate holder and are not addressed here.

#160386 is a P0 umbrella with several independent contributors. This PR is the repair for one of them, the agent-database export snapshot hold. The others stay with their own open issues: the shared-state read-admission seal (`STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED`, #162085 and #160521), shared-state release stalls and session-write latency (#161439, #163748), and Gateway native-memory growth with session SQLite stalls (#170179). That is why #160386 stays `Related:` and the closing keyword is on #171467, which covers this contributor alone.

## User Impact

User impact: for transcripts above 4 MiB in the memory batch, and above 2 MiB in the export snapshot reader, a reader snapshot stays open only for the export head and one slice of at most 2 MiB of payload text (plus the row that crosses it) at a time, instead of for the whole transcript, so passive WAL checkpoints on the agent database can finish while exports run. The memory session-index batch transaction still reads the transcripts the worker's retained-snapshot cache admits (at most 4 MiB) as it does on main; larger transcripts, which that cache never retains, are read after it, in slices. This applies to SQLite; PostgreSQL reads as on main.

No transcript content, ordering, fence, byte budget, incremental export rule, cold-transcript handling or export result changes. Each slice holds at most 2 MiB of decoded payload text (plus the row that crosses that budget), produced by the same SQL decode function the old path uses, and parsed and released before the next slice is read. No memory improvement is claimed. Through the shipped plugin-SDK entry with and without an enforced total-process cap, the before and after lifetime footprints overlap (12 interleaved runs per side at three settings, tables under Memory). This does not claim to resolve `STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED` (see Gaps).

Cost: warm exports of the large session take longer after the change. Mean of the three warm exports (rounds 1 to 3) over all 12 runs per side: 2.7% longer without a cap (1162.9 against 1131.9 ms), 2.5% longer at the 768 MiB cap and 1.5% longer at the 896 MiB cap (tables under Memory). In exchange the reader snapshot is released between slices, and with exports running passive checkpoints backfilled every frame in 233 of 242 attempts after the change against 14 of 252 before it (Evidence). With exports running, a writer on another session completed 5.8% fewer appends, and its p99 append latency rose from 5.7 to 7.0 ms to 9.7 to 11.1 ms (PASSIVE arms, Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

`docs/reference/database-schemas/integrity-and-recovery.md` says periodic agent maintenance "keeps the shared WAL backfilled" with passive checkpoints, and that a reader-blocked checkpoint is recorded as blocked rather than complete. A reader that holds its snapshot across seconds of work defeats that. Nothing in the history says the parse had to sit inside the transaction: `9d5615cee1c` moved preparation to a worker and left the decode where it was.

Each slice is one read transaction; the slices of one read are tied together by the transcript context version, not by one SQLite snapshot (see Gaps). The first read transaction resolves the fence, the export statistics and rewrite generation, the incremental-export decision (`previous`, `throughSeq`, unchanged), the session key and the transcript context version (`readTranscriptContextVersionInTransaction`: rewrite generation, highest raw seq, `transcript_updated_at`) together with the first slice. Each slice selects its rows' payload text through `transcriptEventJsonSql`, the same SQL decode the whole-transcript read uses, so per-row decode work and memory are unchanged; `JSON.parse` and the projection run after the slice's transaction closed, and each captured string is released as it is parsed. The slice budget counts each row's payload bytes with the existing `transcriptEventReadBytesSql` (`coalesce(event_utf8_bytes, octet_length(event_json))`): the decoded size for compressed rows, not their stored size, because the slice holds decoded text. Every later transaction first re-reads the context version and continues after the last captured seq only while it is unchanged; that version is the token `SessionManager` writes already validate their loaded bytes against, and the in-place rewrite and suffix paths change it (`rotateTranscriptGenerationInTransaction`, `touchTranscriptMutationInTransaction`). If it changed, the slices read so far are dropped and the transcript is read inside one transaction, exactly as on the base. A transcript under the budget is read in one transaction, as before.

The memory session-index batch (`prepareSessionMemoryEntries`) reads a group of transcripts of one agent database inside one read snapshot through the batch export owner `readTranscriptExportSnapshotsFromDatabase` (#175174), which reads the group's statistics in one query and the requested rows in set-based queries. It keeps that snapshot for every transcript the worker's retained-snapshot cache admits: at most `MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES` (4 MiB) of recorded size. Those transcripts are read, parsed and projected inside the batch exactly as on main. For a transcript above that limit the batch owner, given `deferAboveBytes: MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES`, still computes the head (fence, statistics, generation, cold check, incremental decision, byte admission check), records the transcript context version in that head from the same snapshot, and leaves its rows out of the row query. After the batch transaction closed, each marked transcript is read through the sliced reader above, under the same current-turn fence admission (`runWithSessionTranscriptReadFence`), with the same retained incremental projection (`previous`) and the same cold handling (`SessionTranscriptColdError` becomes `{ cold: true }`, which sends the caller through archive restoration). No slice runs inside the batch transaction, and no new threshold is introduced into the batch: the only boundary is the one the cache already draws; the export snapshot reader uses the new 2 MiB slice budget.

PostgreSQL keeps main's reads: `readTranscriptExportSnapshotsFromDatabase` ignores `deferAboveBytes` on a PostgreSQL connection, so the memory batch reads every transcript in its read-only snapshot and the export snapshot reader gets the whole snapshot in one transaction with main's statements (one payload query, no context-version read). The checkpoint stall is SQLite WAL specific, while on PostgreSQL slicing would refetch the remaining suffix per slice (the bridge buffers each result) and take `pg_advisory_xact_lock` per slice (`runSqliteDeferredTransactionSync`). The check sits in the owner both entry points share.

That boundary is the owner's recorded retention limit. The batch was introduced on main in `8e02d1ae9694393d84ea51bb573a93bb7212a0f1` (PR #170404, "Reduce per-source worker transactions and preparation overhead by reading bounded source groups together"), on top of the retained-snapshot cache from `a00f58286fa` (PR #170302). #170302 records: "The cache retains at most 16 transcripts of at most 4 MiB each; larger/evicted transcripts use the full read path." #170404 records that groups are "bounded to eight sources, 128 publication rows, and the existing transfer budget; an oversized single source retains its atomic streamed replacement", and that "all sources use their pass snapshot and later transcript notifications catch subsequent writes." This change keeps the group bound and the retention limit and departs from one statement: a transcript above the retention limit no longer uses the pass snapshot. It is read after the batch in version-checked slices, and a later write is caught by the next transcript notification, which #170404 already relies on. In #170302 "full read path" means a non-incremental read, which #170404 placed inside the batch; only those transcripts move out of it. The batch transaction's decoded payload is bounded by the group bound times the retention limit (eight sources of at most 4 MiB), where on main it was unbounded. #175174 (merged 2026-10-17) moved the batch onto one export owner and records: "One export owner reads metadata for the group and fetches requested transcript ranges in set-based queries. Payload queries are bounded by session count and the existing source-size estimate; oversized individual sessions run alone." This change keeps that owner as the only place the head is computed, for both the batch and the sliced read, and uses the same source-size estimate as its boundary; it departs in that a session above the retention limit is read after the batch snapshot in version-checked slices rather than alone inside it. #175174 also records: "An archive transition after the pinned read snapshot is observed by the next read; the current export remains snapshot-consistent." Each transcript read after the batch remains internally consistent through the version check; it is not consistent with the batch snapshot of the other sources, which is the tradeoff this PR asks the owner to accept.

The head the batch already read is reused. In its first slice's transaction the sliced reader reads the current transcript context version; when it equals the version the batch owner recorded in that head, the head (statistics, generation, cold check, incremental decision, session key) is used as it is and no statistics are read a second time. When the version differs, the head is read again in that transaction through the same batch owner for that one transcript, under the same fence, and that owner records the new version. Both cases are pinned by tests.


Callers of the export snapshot reader: the memory session entry and entries (`buildSessionEntry`, `buildSessionEntries` through `prepareSessionMemoryEntries`, and the worker's single-entry snapshot request), explicit Memory Core source inspection (which goes through the same worker batch since #175174), the in-process `buildSessionEntry` fallback, and reset recall (`projection: "reset-boundary"`, still one transaction). On SQLite, an export with rows to read now reads the transcript context version with its head and again in every further slice; an export with no rows to read (an empty transcript or an unchanged incremental export) and every PostgreSQL export do not read it. The fenced reader `loadTranscriptReadSnapshotSync` (hydration, `SessionManager` open and reload, the incognito history worker, the bundled session-memory hook capture, `loadTranscriptEventsSync` callers, `prepareTranscriptCommit`) is unchanged; its hold was not measured and is listed under Gaps.

### The change in one sentence

On SQLite, read the payload text of a whole transcript in slices of at most 2 MiB of payload bytes, one read transaction each, through the existing SQL decode, parse every slice after its transaction closes, and continue only while the transcript context version is unchanged, in the export snapshot reader; and have the batch export owner leave the rows of transcripts above the memory worker's existing 4 MiB retention limit to that reader after the batch's read snapshot instead of inside it, reusing the export head the batch already read while the transcript context version is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Diff shape and contract table</summary>

Diff shape (9 files, 836 insertions, 54 deletions against the base):

- `session-accessor.sqlite-read.ts`: `readTranscriptExportSnapshotsFromDatabase` takes an optional `{ deferAboveBytes }`; a transcript above it that has rows to read gets `deferred: { afterSeq, throughSeq, version }` (the transcript context version, read in the same transaction) and stays out of the row query; never on PostgreSQL. `readTranscriptExportSnapshotReadOnlySync` takes an optional `batchHead` (a deferred snapshot from that owner) and reads through `readTranscriptExportInSlices`, with its read-only deferred transaction and the batch owner for its one request as the head reader; main's private one-request wrapper is no longer needed and is removed. `loadTranscriptReadSnapshotSync` is unchanged.
- `session-accessor.sqlite-export-slices.ts` (new): `readTranscriptExportInSlices` (head in the first slice's transaction or the reused batch head, deferred rows in version-checked slices parsed after each transaction, reset navigation and the no-rows case in one transaction) and the slice query (`seq`, `transcriptEventJsonSql`, `transcriptEventReadBytesSql`). It opens no database itself. It is a separate module because `session-accessor.sqlite-read.ts` is at its `max-lines` budget on main (696 of 700 counted lines; type-aware oxlint `max-lines` still passes with this change).
- `session-transcript-read-bytes.ts`: the 2 MiB slice budget `TRANSCRIPT_PAYLOAD_SLICE_BYTES`, next to `transcriptEventReadBytesSql`, which defines the bytes it counts.
- `session-memory-entry.worker.ts`: the batch passes `deferAboveBytes: MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES` and keeps each deferred snapshot; those are read after the batch with `readTranscriptExportSnapshotReadOnlySync` and that snapshot as the batch head, inside `runWithSessionTranscriptReadFence`, with the same options and cold handling.
- `session-accessor.sqlite-read-hold.test.ts`: new regression test.
- `session-accessor.sqlite-read-hold.postgres.test.ts`: PostgreSQL regression test, added to `scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs`.
- `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`: lists the new runtime module.
- `scripts/database-worker-inventory.mjs`: adds `readTranscriptExportSnapshotReadOnlySync.transaction` to that reader's reviewed worker operations, because its read-only open now sits in the `transaction` callback; regenerating the inventory on main and on this branch then differs only in line numbers.

Contract table

| Case | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| Export snapshot of plain and zstd rows, default projection | same `events`, `stats`, `sessionKey` as before; parsing happens after each read transaction closes |
| Export snapshot with `projectEvent` (memory session entry) | projection runs after the transaction closes, once per event, in sequence order (pinned by test) |
| Incremental export (`previous` set, same generation) | same rule as before: rows after `previous.throughSeq` only, `previous.events` prepended, `generation` and `throughSeq` returned; no row read when nothing was appended (pinned by test, one row per slice) |
| Export snapshot with `projection: "reset-boundary"` | unchanged: small native navigation projection, still read inside one transaction |
| Transcript larger than the slice budget | read in slices of at most 2 MiB of payload, one transaction each, parsed in between (pinned by test with a 1-byte budget: one row per transaction) |
| Memory batch, transcript within the retained-snapshot limit (at most 4 MiB, `MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES`) | read inside the batch transaction, as on main (pinned by test with a 3 MiB transcript: one transaction) |
| Memory batch, transcript above the retained-snapshot limit | head only inside the batch snapshot (from the batch owner), rows in slices after it; same entry content as an in-batch read; entries keep their order (pinned by test: small, large, small) |
| Memory batch, transcript above the retained-snapshot limit, unchanged between the batch transaction and its read | batch head and statistics reused, no second statistics read (pinned by test) |
| Memory batch, transcript above the retained-snapshot limit, changed between the batch transaction and its read | head re-read under the same fence (pinned by test) |
| Memory batch, current-turn fence | the read after the batch transaction keeps the request's fence admission, unchanged or changed in between (pinned by test) |
| Memory batch, retained incremental projection | a transcript read after the batch transaction continues from the worker's retained projection: only the appended row is read and parsed, unchanged or changed in between (pinned by test) |
| Memory batch, cold transcript | `{ cold: true }` both when the batch transaction sees the archive (as on main, pinned by `session-memory-entry.worker.test.ts`) and when the transcript is archived between the batch transaction and its own read (pinned by test) |
| Compressed rows that decode to more than they store | budgeted by decoded payload bytes, so a slice never holds more decoded text than the budget plus one row (pinned by test) |
| Plain rows whose stored bytes exceed their string length (CJK text in a UTF-8 store, any text in a UTF-16 store) | budgeted by `transcriptEventReadBytesSql` (recorded UTF-8 bytes, else `octet_length` in the store's encoding), not string length (pinned by test with CJK rows in a UTF-8 store, in one case with the compressed rows) |
| Transcript rewritten, appended to, or otherwise versioned between slices | slices dropped, whole transcript reread inside one transaction, result equals a single-snapshot read (pinned by test) |
| `maxEventBytes` exceeded | still rejected in the first transaction, over the whole fenced range, before any payload is read (the batch owner's check, which runs in the head) |
| Compressed row whose recorded length is wrong | same `Compressed transcript payload length does not match` error from the same SQL decode as before, also from a later slice (pinned by test; passes on the base too) |
| Reader inside a writer transaction (`loadTranscriptEventsFromDatabase` callers: message cut, parent session, recovery, mirror, incognito lifecycle) | deliberately unchanged, see Gaps |
| PostgreSQL, transcript above either limit | as on main: memory batch in its one read-only snapshot without `pg_advisory_xact_lock`; export snapshot reader in one transaction; one payload query each, with rows that each fill a 2 MiB slice (pinned by PostgreSQL test); the export snapshot reader issues main's statements (statement probe, Evidence) |
| Fenced read (`loadTranscriptReadSnapshotSync` and `loadTranscriptEventsSync`, all callers) | unchanged from the base: one transaction, decode and parse inside it, see Gaps |

</details>


## Evidence

Everything below ran at tree `193d85a895d` (head `40d498e64ce`), base `288dd0a8a6257829b479eaa1d70042c06284549d`, on one machine on 2026-10-18: builds 19:01 to 19:11 UTC, arms 19:11 to 19:28 UTC, gates and suites from 19:28 UTC; the PostgreSQL runs and reds 2 to 12 ran at commit `f2f82cf7ad3`, which has the same tree. Size against the base: production +264 / -53, tests +569, scripts +3 / -1. Against the previous head `cb24f3731c1`: production +137 / -232, tests +102 / -240, scripts -1 (the slice-loop module folded into the export slice reader; see Diff shape and the test list below). "Before" is a clean worktree of the base with its own install and build. Machine: Apple M3 Ultra, 512 GiB, macOS 27.0.1, Node v24.21.0, pnpm 12.11.1. Other work shared the host (load averages about 9 to 15 during the arms); before and after runs were interleaved where repeated so drift lands on both sides.

### PostgreSQL

PostgreSQL 17.11, `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres -- src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-read-hold.postgres.test.ts` (a transcript above 4 MiB of two 2.5 MiB rows, each filling a 2 MiB slice, statements recorded on the `openclaw.database.statement` channel): `Tests  2 passed (2)`; with the lane neighbours `session-turn-resident.postgres`, `session-actor.conformance` and `transcript-reports.conformance`, 10 + 11 passed. With the PostgreSQL check removed from `readTranscriptExportSnapshotsFromDatabase` (`&& !isPostgresSqlConnection(database.db)`), both fail (excerpt; the BEGIN diff line repeats three times):

```
 ×  ... > memory batch reads a large transcript in its read-only snapshot without the writer lock 379ms
   → expected [ …(4) ] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]
    "BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY",
+   "BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED; SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(?)",
 ×  ... > single export fetches every payload with one query 40ms
   → expected [ …(3) ] to have a length of 1 but got 3
      Tests  2 failed (2)
```

A one-off probe recorded every PostgreSQL statement of one export snapshot read of that transcript: the base and this head issue the same four statements (`diff` empty). The previous head `cb24f3731c1` issued a fifth, the transcript context-version `SELECT`; this head reads the version only for a transcript it defers, which PostgreSQL never does.

### Build

`pnpm build` exit 0 on both trees: after `[build-all] phase timings: total 3m 0.4s`, before `total 3m 23.6s`.

### Behaviour: before and after on one fixture

Real seam: `buildSessionEntry`, which runs `prepareSessionMemoryEntries` (the memory export batch) in the session-transcript worker, on one synthetic agent database built at the base by the harness writer (`persistSessionTranscriptTurn`) and cloned from one pristine copy for every run: 1200 sessions of six 600-byte messages plus one 24,000-event session in which tool results dominate (3,974 user and assistant messages of 700 bytes and 20,026 tool results of random-word text averaging about 30 KB, 26 of them about 1.1 MB; 608 MiB of decoded payload, 302 MiB as stored, 20,026 rows zstd-compressed), the shape reported on #160386. The agent database is 372.3 MiB and the pristine state directory is 386 MiB (`du -sh`). One before/after pair.

During 20 s of back-to-back exports of the large session, a second connection attempts `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` with `busy_timeout = 0` every 40 ms while a writer appends to another session every 20 ms:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TRUNCATE attempts refused as busy | 429 of 509 (84%) | 272 of 485 (56%) |
| TRUNCATE attempts completed | 80 | 213 |
| peak WAL size (MiB) | 18.5 | 0.5 |
| `slow SQLite transaction hold` lines (whole run) | 23 | 1 |
| exports completed in 20 s / mean wall time (ms) | 18 / 1168 | 17 / 1204 |
| 4 sequential exports (ms) | 5391 / 1163 / 1118 / 1119 | 5523 / 1182 / 1175 / 1154 |
| writer appends in 20 s | 743 | 567 |
| writer append p50 / p99 (ms) | 3 / 10 | 7 / 11 |
| main thread event-loop p99 / max (ms) | 6.3 / 6.5 | 6.3 / 9.2 |

`TRUNCATE` completes about 2.7 times as often (213 against 80). Every hold line on the before side is the memory batch snapshot (`operation="session transcript export batch"`). The after side logged one, before the round 0 line, so for the first, cold export (shortened `database=` path):

```
[sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite transaction hold async=false callbackKind=application-transaction database=<state>/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite operation="session transcript export batch" elapsedMs=1155 phases={"beginMs":0,"sqlMs":1155,"hostAdmissionWaitMs":0,"databaseAdmissionWaitMs":0,"commitMs":0} isMainThread=false mode=deferred pid=89362 threadId=2 thresholdMs=1000
```

Under this aggressive probe the writer completes 24% fewer appends in 20 s (567 against 743); a completed TRUNCATE resets the WAL and holds writers while it runs, and the after side completed 133 more of them. This was not measured separately. In the PASSIVE arms below, which use what agent maintenance uses, appends are 5.8% lower on the mean.

Writer throughput with PASSIVE checkpoints only (what agent maintenance uses). Same fixture clone per arm, 20 s per arm, writer appends to another session every 20 ms, with warm-up; the probe, when present, runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)` every 250 ms and counts a checkpoint as complete when every frame was backfilled. The exports + PASSIVE arm ran three times per side, interleaved; values are repetition 1 / 2 / 3, then the mean:

| exports + PASSIVE probe | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| exports | 18 / 18 / 18 | 17 / 17 / 17 |
| appends | 867 / 865 / 865 (mean 865.7) | 814 / 814 / 818 (mean 815.3) |
| append p50 (ms) | 2.6 / 2.6 / 2.6 | 2.8 / 2.8 / 2.8 |
| append p99 (ms) | 6.0 / 5.7 / 7.0 (mean 6.2) | 10.6 / 9.7 / 11.1 (mean 10.5) |
| checkpoints complete / incomplete | 5 / 79, 6 / 78, 3 / 81 (14 / 238 in total) | 78 / 3, 76 / 4, 79 / 2 (233 / 9 in total) |
| peak WAL (MiB) | 42.3 / 55.5 / 45.5 (mean 47.8) | 2.9 / 3.0 / 2.9 (mean 2.9) |
| `slow SQLite transaction hold` lines | 18 / 18 / 18 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

Other arms, one run per side:

| arm | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| writer only, PASSIVE probe, no exports: appends / p50 / p99 (ms) | 823 / 2.3 / 9.4 | 821 / 2.3 / 10.1 |
| writer only: checkpoints complete / incomplete, peak WAL (MiB) | 79 / 0, 2.2 | 79 / 0, 2.1 |
| exports, no checkpoint probe: exports / appends / p50 / p99 (ms) | 18 / 863 / 2.6 / 6.3 | 17 / 836 / 2.8 / 6.0 |
| exports, no checkpoint probe: peak WAL (MiB), hold lines | 83.3, 18 | 56.7, 0 |
| exports + PASSIVE probe (this pair run, not counted above): appends / p99 (ms), checkpoints complete / incomplete, peak WAL (MiB) | 861 / 6.7, 4 / 80, 54.8 | 813 / 10.2, 74 / 6, 2.8 |

With exports running, passive checkpoints backfill every frame in 233 of 242 attempts (96%) after the change against 14 of 252 (5.6%) before it, and the WAL peaks at a mean of 2.9 MiB instead of 47.8 MiB. In all three repetitions the writer's p99 append latency is higher after the change (9.7 to 11.1 ms against 5.7 to 7.0 ms) and its append count is lower (814 to 818 against 865 to 867; the mean is 5.8% lower). The writer-only arm runs no export code (821 against 823 appends).

### Memory

**Total-process memory under an enforced cap.** The cap runs drive the built `dist/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-sessions.js` (the `openclaw/plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-sessions` entry that memory-core calls), so the read runs in the real transcript worker inside a production-sized process: one warm small-session export, then four exports of the large session. A supervisor polls `proc_pid_rusage(RUSAGE_INFO_V4)` every 2 ms and `SIGKILL`s the process as soon as the kernel-tracked lifetime maximum physical footprint (`ri_lifetime_max_phys_footprint`, the accounting macOS per-process memory limits use) exceeds the cap, the way a cgroup `memory.max` OOM kill ends it. The kernel keeps that high-water mark itself, so a peak between polls is not missed. 1 GiB is the documented absolute minimum host memory (`docs/install/raspberry-pi.md`, `docs/help/faq-first-run/providers-and-hosting.md`), applied here to this one process. Fresh process and fixture clone per run.

<details>
<summary>Cap supervisor (Python 3.9, full source)</summary>

```python
# Enforced total-process memory cap for one child process on macOS.
# Polls proc_pid_rusage(RUSAGE_INFO_V4) every 2 ms. The kernel tracks the
# lifetime maximum physical footprint itself, so the verdict does not depend
# on catching the peak in a sample: once that high-water mark exceeds the cap,
# the child is SIGKILLed, the way a cgroup memory.max OOM kill ends it.
import ctypes, os, signal, subprocess, sys, time
cap_mib = float(sys.argv[1])
cmd = sys.argv[2:]
libproc = ctypes.CDLL("/usr/lib/libproc.dylib")
buf = (ctypes.c_uint64 * 64)()
RESIDENT, FOOTPRINT, LIFETIME_MAX = 6 + 2, 7 + 2, 28 + 2  # +2: the 16-byte ri_uuid prefix
def usage(pid):
    if libproc.proc_pid_rusage(pid, 4, ctypes.byref(buf)) != 0:
        return None
    return buf[RESIDENT], buf[FOOTPRINT], buf[LIFETIME_MAX]
mib = lambda n: round(n / 2**20, 1)
child = subprocess.Popen(cmd)
peak_rss = peak_fp = life = 0
killed = False
while child.poll() is None:
    u = usage(child.pid)
    if u:
        peak_rss, peak_fp, life = max(peak_rss, u[0]), max(peak_fp, u[1]), max(life, u[2])
        if not killed and life > cap_mib * 2**20:
            os.kill(child.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
            killed = True
    time.sleep(0.002)
rc = child.wait()
print(f"CAP capMiB={cap_mib:g} exit={rc} killedByCap={killed} lifetimeMaxFootprintMiB={mib(life)} sampledPeakFootprintMiB={mib(peak_fp)} sampledPeakRssMiB={mib(peak_rss)}", flush=True)
```

</details>
