prs.title: fix(feishu): preserve group route for mirrored oc replies
prs.body:
Refs #58537. This PR fixes the normal mirrored Feishu group-reply route path, but intentionally does not auto-close the broader issue because proactive bare-target sends and duplicate-session cleanup may remain separate maintainer scope.

## Summary

- preserve Feishu group session identity when a delivery-mirror reply resolves a bare `oc_...` target from the matching current Feishu group session
- trust directory-resolved Feishu group targets when building outbound session routes
- keep ambiguous bare `oc_...` targets direct when there is no group context, preserving the existing compatibility boundary
- keep bare Feishu user/open IDs direct when shared target resolution only supplied a normalized fallback group hint

## Why this shape

`oc_...` IDs are compatibility-sensitive because prior history says they can be ambiguous. This fix does not revive the broad "all bare oc_ is group" rule. It only promotes the route to group when OpenClaw already has group evidence: either the current session key is the same Feishu group conversation, or target resolution came from a directory-backed group match. Normalized fallback hints are not trusted for group promotion, so bare Feishu user/open IDs remain direct.

## Public surface

- No config surface changes.
- No plugin public contract/API changes.
- No migration or startup reconciliation behavior added.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed:
A normal Feishu group reply/delivery-mirror path can recreate a phantom `agent:main:feishu:direct:oc_...` session because the route resolver sees a bare `oc_...` target and loses the existing group identity.

Real environment tested:
WSL Ubuntu 24.04, OpenClaw checkout `/root/src/openclaw-87774-proof`, PR head `245e28e44bc3a8d7bc774690dbd2bf84212b6b12`, production Feishu channel route resolver `extensions/feishu/src/session-route.ts:resolveFeishuOutboundSessionRoute`, and focused Feishu/outbound runtime tests.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Ran a source harness through the production Feishu resolver for three redacted route/session cases: matching current Feishu group session, directory-resolved group target, and normalized fallback user target.
2. Reran focused Feishu/outbound validation: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/channel.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.card-action.test.ts src/infra/outbound/outbound-session.test.ts src/config/sessions/delivery-info.test.ts --reporter=dot`.
3. Reran changed-file static checks: `CI=true pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/feishu/src/session-route.ts extensions/feishu/src/channel.test.ts`, `CI=true pnpm exec oxlint --tsconfig ./tsconfig.json extensions/feishu/src/session-route.ts extensions/feishu/src/channel.test.ts`, and `git diff --check`.

Evidence after fix:
```json
{
  "head": "245e28e44bc3a8d7bc774690dbd2bf84212b6b12",
  "productionResolver": "extensions/feishu/src/session-route.ts:resolveFeishuOutboundSessionRoute",
  "proof": [
    {
      "label": "matching-current-feishu-group-session",
      "input": {
        "target": "oc_group_chat",
        "currentSessionKey": "agent:main:feishu:group:oc_group_chat:topic:om_root:sender:ou_user"
      },
      "route": {
        "sessionKey": "agent:main:feishu:group:oc_group_chat",
        "baseSessionKey": "agent:main:feishu:group:oc_group_chat",
        "peer": { "kind": "group", "id": "oc_group_chat" },
        "chatType": "group",
        "from": "feishu:group:oc_group_chat",
        "to": "oc_group_chat"
      },
      "noDirectPhantomForOcGroup": true
    },
    {
      "label": "directory-resolved-group-target",
      "input": {
        "target": "oc_directory_chat",
        "resolvedTarget": { "kind": "group", "to": "oc_directory_chat", "source": "directory" }
      },
      "route": {
        "sessionKey": "agent:main:feishu:group:oc_directory_chat",
        "baseSessionKey": "agent:main:feishu:group:oc_directory_chat",
        "peer": { "kind": "group", "id": "oc_directory_chat" },
        "chatType": "group",
        "from": "feishu:group:oc_directory_chat",
        "to": "oc_directory_chat"
      },
      "noDirectPhantomForOcGroup": true
    },
    {
      "label": "normalized-fallback-user-stays-direct",
      "input": {
        "target": "ou_user",
        "resolvedTarget": { "kind": "group", "to": "ou_user", "source": "normalized" }
      },
      "route": {
        "sessionKey": "agent:main:main",
        "baseSessionKey": "agent:main:main",
        "peer": { "kind": "direct", "id": "ou_user" },
        "chatType": "direct",
        "from": "feishu:ou_user",
        "to": "ou_user"
      },
      "noDirectPhantomForOcGroup": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Observed result after fix:
The production Feishu resolver preserves `feishu:group:oc_...` session identity when the current session proves the bare `oc_...` target is the active group, and when a directory-backed target resolution proves a Feishu group. It does not promote normalized fallback user/open IDs to group routes.

Supporting checks:
- Focused Feishu/outbound Vitest passed: 5 files, 218 tests.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check` passed.
- Targeted `oxlint` passed with 0 warnings/errors.
- `git diff --check` passed.

What was not tested:
No live Feishu/Lark OpenChat account was available in this session, so this proof does not include an actual Feishu network send. Proactive context-free sends and duplicate-session cleanup remain out of scope for this PR.

prs.title: Add core snapshot provider proof
prs.body:
## Summary

- Adds a core SQLite snapshot provider proof under `src/snapshot`, not an extension/plugin.
- Proves the first step of the RFC's safe-sync-file story: turn a live SQLite database into a verified artifact + manifest that a file-syncing host can persist.
- Adds a local `SqliteSnapshotProvider` backed by a manifest + compact `database.sqlite` artifact repository.
- Builds on #94646's database-first layout: global/control-plane SQLite and per-agent/data-plane SQLite are the long-term targets; this PR proves the mechanism against one explicit DB reference.
- Shares the SQLite `VACUUM INTO` primitive with the existing backup path through `packages/memory-host-sdk`, including sqlite-vec loading and compact-snapshot behavior.
- Proves committed WAL-mode state is captured without asking hosts to sync live `*.sqlite-wal`, `*.sqlite-shm`, or `*.sqlite-journal` sidecars.

## Why this matters

Scout/Lobster-style hosts persist OpenClaw by syncing files when they are saved. A live SQLite directory is the wrong durability boundary: the main `*.sqlite` file can be incomplete without WAL state, and unmanaged file deltas over live SQLite can observe DB pages, WAL frames, and sidecars at different moments.

This PR proves the safer core boundary: SQLite materializes a clean artifact first, the provider verifies it, and the host can sync the completed artifact set instead of the live DB working set. WAL bundles remain a metrics-gated Phase 2 after verified snapshot artifacts and cursors exist.

## Scope

This is PR 1 from the snapshot RFC roadmap: core provider proof only. It intentionally does not add `openclaw snapshot ...` commands, backup command integration, remote storage, leases, scheduling, WAL bundles, or failover orchestration.

RFC context: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/20
Database-first state layout: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94646
Related storage discussion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90370

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/snapshot/snapshot-provider.test.ts` - passed, 1 file / 6 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/sqlite-vec.test.ts` - passed, 1 file / 9 tests
- `node_modules\.bin\oxlint src\snapshot packages\memory-host-sdk\src\host\sqlite-snapshot.ts packages\memory-host-sdk\src\engine-storage.ts src\infra\backup-create.ts` - passed
- `git diff --check` - passed

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Core SQLite snapshot provider can create, verify, list, and internally restore compact snapshot artifacts from SQLite databases, including WAL-mode state. This proves the safe sync artifact boundary for the database-first SQLite target model landed in #94646.

Real environment tested:
Windows source checkout at `C:\src\openclaw-snapshot-pr1`, Node/Vitest source harness against `node:sqlite`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/snapshot/snapshot-provider.test.ts`
2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/sqlite-vec.test.ts`
3. `node_modules\.bin\oxlint src\snapshot packages\memory-host-sdk\src\host\sqlite-snapshot.ts packages\memory-host-sdk\src\engine-storage.ts src\infra\backup-create.ts`
4. `git diff --check`

Evidence after fix:
- Snapshot provider test passed: 1 file / 6 tests.
- SQLite vec/shared primitive test passed: 1 file / 9 tests.
- Oxlint completed cleanly for changed provider/shared files.
- `git diff --check` completed with no whitespace errors.

Observed result after fix:
The source harness creates a WAL-mode source database, snapshots via the core local provider, verifies the manifest and artifact, restores to a fresh path, and reads both pre-WAL and committed-in-WAL rows from the restored database. It also covers failed create cleanup, artifact tamper detection, signed `user_version`, same-millisecond snapshot IDs, and stale restore-target WAL sidecar removal.

What was not tested:
Public `openclaw snapshot` CLI, backup command integration, object storage providers, scheduled snapshots, WAL bundles, leases, and fresh OpenClaw state-dir boot proof; those are intentionally later PRs.

prs.title: Add named snapshot database targets
prs.body:
## Summary

This is PR 3 in the snapshot stack. It makes the core snapshot command understand OpenClaw's named SQLite databases instead of requiring operators to know internal file paths.

Adds:
- `openclaw snapshot create --target global --repository <dir>` for the shared state database
- `openclaw snapshot create --agent <id> --repository <dir>` for a per-agent database
- selector validation so `--db`, `--target`, and `--agent` remain mutually exclusive

Keeps:
- explicit `--db <path>` from PR 2 for non-OpenClaw or advanced caller paths
- local snapshot repository semantics from the provider proof

## Why

Ryan's issue (#94675) called out that live SQLite files and their WAL/SHM companions are not safe sync artifacts for hosted deployments. PR #94646 made the database layout more explicit by separating shared state from per-agent state. This PR uses those core path helpers so snapshotting can target the logical OpenClaw database units directly:

- global control-plane state: `state/openclaw.sqlite`
- per-agent data-plane state: `agents/<agent>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`

That keeps the operator-facing contract small: ask OpenClaw for a syncable snapshot artifact, not for a copy of whatever live SQLite files happen to exist on disk.

## Stack

- Depends on #94717
- Builds on #94694
- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#20
- Related: #94675, #94646

## Scope

This PR does not add object storage, scheduling, restore-on-boot, leases, or WAL bundle deltas. Those stay in later phases. This only proves the CLI can name OpenClaw's own SQLite targets and resolve them through core-owned path helpers.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
`openclaw snapshot create` can now create snapshots from named OpenClaw database targets (`--target global`, `--agent <id>`) without requiring users to locate and pass live SQLite paths manually.

Real environment tested:
Windows checkout at `C:\src\openclaw-snapshot-pr1`, source test harness with temporary SQLite databases and local snapshot repositories.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/snapshot.test.ts src/cli/program/register.snapshot.test.ts src/snapshot/snapshot-provider.test.ts`
2. `node_modules\.bin\oxlint src\commands\snapshot.ts src\commands\snapshot.test.ts src\cli\program\register.snapshot.ts src\cli\program\register.snapshot.test.ts`
3. `git diff --check`

Evidence after fix:
Vitest passed 3 shards: `src/commands/snapshot.test.ts` (6 tests), `src/cli/program/register.snapshot.test.ts` (7 tests), and `src/snapshot/snapshot-provider.test.ts` (5 tests). `oxlint` and `git diff --check` completed with no output.

Observed result after fix:
The command resolves `--target global` to the shared OpenClaw state database, resolves `--agent "Ops Team"` to the normalized per-agent database path, records default manifest ids/kinds for both, preserves explicit `--db`, and rejects ambiguous selector combinations.

What was not tested:
No live gateway runtime, object storage upload, scheduled backup loop, restore-on-boot path, lease/failover path, or WAL bundle/delta behavior was tested in this PR.

## Summary

- Adds a core `openclaw snapshot` CLI surface, not a plugin/extension command.
- Wires `snapshot create`, `snapshot list`, `snapshot verify`, and `snapshot restore` to the local SQLite snapshot provider from PR 1.
- Makes the safe-sync-file workflow user-accessible: create a verified SQLite artifact + manifest that a file-syncing host can persist instead of syncing the live SQLite working set.
- Registers `snapshot` in the core command descriptor catalog, lazy command registry, and command startup policy.
- Positions the CLI as the proof surface for #94646's database-first SQLite layout: today it accepts explicit DB paths, and later PRs can map friendly names to global/control-plane and per-agent/data-plane DBs.
- Covers command registration plus create/list/verify/restore command behavior against a real SQLite database.

## Stack

- Depends on #94694
- Database-first state layout: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94646
- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/20

## Scope

This PR keeps snapshot explicit and opt-in, but core-owned. It does not make every OpenClaw SQLite database automatically durable, does not add object storage, does not add scheduling, and does not change the runtime database choice.

The point is narrower: give operators and Scout/Lobster-style hosts a command surface that can produce and verify the completed artifact set. Hosts should sync that artifact set, not live `*.sqlite`, `*.sqlite-wal`, `*.sqlite-shm`, or `*.sqlite-journal` churn. WAL bundles remain a metrics-gated Phase 2 after the full snapshot command is proven.

prs.body:
## Summary

- Prevent Tool Search catalog setup from crashing when a tool exposes unreadable schema metadata.
- Skip catalog entries whose `parameters` or MCP metadata cannot be safely read and fingerprinted, while preserving readable tools in the same catalog.
- Apply the same guard to appended client tools so a single malformed client tool does not break the compact prompt surface.
- Out of scope: adding new diagnostics UI for skipped Tool Search entries; this PR keeps the agent session bootable and covered by focused regression tests.

## Linked context

No linked issue.

Related: continuing tool-schema fuzzing hardening across OpenClaw agent/tool surfaces.

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? Maintainer fuzzing lane.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Tool Search compaction could throw while reading or fingerprinting a malformed tool schema, preventing the agent run from starting with Tool Search enabled.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw sparse GWT on branch `fuzz-tool-schema-next45-20260602`, Node/Vitest through repo wrappers.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-search.test.ts -- --reporter=dot`; `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/tool-search.ts src/agents/tool-search.test.ts`; `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`; `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main`.

Evidence after fix: Focused Vitest passed 1 file / 27 tests on rebased head `d2f740672a4`; oxlint exited 0 for the touched files; diff check exited 0; branch autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings with `overall: patch is correct (0.82)`.

Observed result after fix: Tool Search compaction and client-tool catalog append skip unreadable schema entries and keep readable entries registered instead of throwing.

What was not tested: Full repo test suite and live provider/tool-search runtime sessions were not run locally; broad changed-gate proof is being run separately through Crabbox after PR creation.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: Local checkout is a sparse Codex worktree, so broad `pnpm` gates are routed remote per repo policy.

Before evidence: Regression tests construct tools with throwing `parameters` getters and nested throwing schema getters; without the guard, catalog entry creation/fingerprinting would throw.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-search.test.ts -- --reporter=dot`
- `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/tool-search.ts src/agents/tool-search.test.ts`

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Added Tool Search tests for unreadable plugin tool schemas during catalog compaction.
- Added Tool Search tests for unreadable client tool schemas during catalog append.

What failed before this fix, if known?

- Reading `tool.parameters` or recursively fingerprinting `entry.parameters` could throw before Tool Search had a chance to register the compacted catalog.

If no test was added, why not?

- Tests were added.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. Malformed/unreadable tools are skipped from Tool Search instead of crashing catalog setup.

No.

No.

Tool availability: unreadable tools are no longer discoverable through Tool Search.

How is that risk mitigated?

Only entries whose schema metadata cannot be read and fingerprinted are skipped; readable entries in the same catalog remain available, and the behavior is covered for both plugin and client tool paths.

Await remote changed-gate proof and maintainer review.

Author is running remote `pnpm check:changed` proof after PR creation.

None yet. Local and branch autoreview both reported no accepted/actionable findings.

releases.body:
## 2026.10.10-beta.2

### Highlights

### Changes

### Fixes

- Workspace safety: reject a multi-file `apply_patch` before changing files when a later update target is missing or its context does not match, preserving the original workspace for the next attempt. Commit-time I/O failures can still leave partial effects. (#160409; related #117742 and #127496) Thanks @masatohoshino, @obviyus, and @yetval.
- Tool policy: run plugin `before_tool_call` hooks in standalone `openclaw agent exec` sessions so plugin tool guards take effect. (#159333; fixes #158824) Thanks @joseairosa and @obviyus.
- Buzz: reconnect when a relay closes during NIP-42 authentication without terminating the Gateway or interrupting other channels and sessions. (#170591; fixes #147269) Thanks @masatohoshino, @obviyus, @jarvis-modern-mail, and @RomneyDa.
- macOS downloads: save dashboard and conversation attachments through the native Save dialog while keeping the current page open. (#173654) Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen.
- OpenRouter onboarding: accept valid API keys with the default `openrouter/auto` model instead of rejecting setup with a route mismatch. (#173292; related #162798) Thanks @chandraveshchaudhari and @obviyus.
- macOS setup: let fresh native profiles start the Gateway and complete automatic setup, including when supervised startup needs a retry. (#173246)
- Gateway startup: follow a replacement model-runtime refresh instead of exiting when initial preparation is superseded. (#173366; related #173357) Thanks @Jackten and @RomneyDa.
- Gateway logging: keep serving and shut down normally when a deleted temporary-directory backing path makes daily log rollover fail. (#160433; fixes #130807) Thanks @masatohoshino, @obviyus, @WadeOwenWatts, and @Patrick-Erichsen.
- Gateway stability: stop session diff capture from opening live SQLite and hard-linked files, preventing SIGBUS crash loops when the shared-memory file is truncated. (#174017)
- Native app updates: let Doctor finish agent database upgrades on native-first profiles instead of reporting success while the Gateway refuses to start on an older schema. (#174297)
- Cron: plan history maintenance from run identities and load full payloads only for rows it updates, so large cron histories no longer exhaust the SQLite worker's memory and take channels down. (#174530; fixes #174078) Thanks @wangmiao0668000666, @RomneyDa, and @asikorskiy.
- Windows Claude CLI: stop every turn with a stored Anthropic credential from stalling until the no-output watchdog when Claude Code never reads the credential pipe. (#174571; fixes #174204) Thanks @RomneyDa and @scalesmart.
- Plugins: restore the SDK facade exports that published external plugins still import, so those plugins load again. (#173777; fixes #173386) Thanks @RomneyDa and @FtlC-ian.
- Chat tools: keep the chat usable after removing a tool server that failed to start, cleaning up its failed startup before reporting the launch error. (#171397) Thanks @joelagnel.
- Updates: bound the post-activation Doctor step by the update's allowance instead of waiting indefinitely with the Gateway down. (#173862)
- Updates: keep Gateway-managed source updates from failing with missing backup modules after the runtime is replaced. (#173587) Thanks @vishnusenthil-16.
- Updates: make `openclaw update --no-restart` honest for npm, pnpm, and bun installs, which restart themselves after the package is replaced, record the update as successful, and keep a still-serving older build unverified. (#173409, #174649; fixes #171311) Thanks @RomneyDa and @mwbroxson.

### Complete contribution record

This audited record covers the complete v2026.10.10-beta.1..f90bd063751f2448330ee6abbb4c894508600d63 history: 24 in-range PRs + 0 retained seed-only PRs = 24 unique PRs. The generation manifest also supplies direct commits as editorial input; the grouped notes above prioritize user impact.

issues.title: Expose retained cron run history through the agent tool

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

The scheduler retains the last 20 executions per job, but the cron tool only exposes the latest run status through list. In a chat-only workflow, users cannot ask for the last few execution times, durations, and errors to investigate intermittent failures.

### Proposed Solution

Add a history action requiring job_id, with an optional limit (default 5, range 1–20). Read existing CronRunRecord entries newest first, including time, status, duration_ms, and error. Reuse the job/runtime timezone and allow inspection of disabled jobs. Do not change scheduler storage or execution.

### Alternatives Considered

Use WebUI or inspect jobs.json manually. Repeated list calls only show the latest execution and cannot recover earlier retained errors.

### Related Component

Other

### Additional Context

This builds on the storage added in #1838. It is separate from pause/resume (#6313) and delivery/archive management (#5620). A focused implementation passes 183 cron tests. Deleted jobs, including automatically deleted one-time tasks, remain unavailable; execution history does not include task output or confirm delivery.

issues.title: Add OS-level sandboxing for tool execution via sandlock
issues.body:
## Problem

Nanobot gives the LLM full shell execution and filesystem access via `ExecTool`. The current security model relies on regex-based command blocking (9 deny patterns) and string-level path checks (`restrict_to_workspace`). These are bypassable — encoding tricks, aliases, scripting languages, or indirect execution can evade pattern matching. There is no kernel-level enforcement.

This matters because:
- LLM-driven execution is inherently unpredictable — the model decides what commands to run
- External web content fetched as context creates prompt injection risk
- Subagents and MCP server tools expand the attack surface
- A single bypass means full access as the nanobot user

## Proposal

Integrate [sandlock](https://github.com/multikernel/sandlock) — a lightweight Linux process sandbox that uses Landlock, seccomp-bpf, and user namespaces to confine processes without root or containers.

Sandlock would add kernel-enforced boundaries to each tool execution:

| Current defense | Sandlock addition |
|---|---|
| Regex command deny-list | seccomp-bpf syscall filtering at kernel level |
| String path checks | Landlock filesystem whitelisting (read-only / read-write paths) |
| No network restrictions | TCP port + domain allowlisting |
| No resource limits | Memory, process count, CPU, open file caps |
| No privilege escalation defense | User namespace confinement |

### Integration points

1. **`ExecTool` (`agent/tools/shell.py`)** — wrap `asyncio.create_subprocess_shell()` in a sandlock sandbox with per-execution filesystem + network + syscall policy
2. **Subagent spawning** — each subagent inherits sandbox constraints via sandlock's per-PID policy propagation
3. **MCP tool execution** — sandbox MCP server processes independently
4. **Cron tasks** — scheduled tasks run confined by default

### Characteristics that make this a good fit

- **No root required** : runs as the nanobot user
- **~20ms startup overhead** : negligible vs LLM inference latency
- **Python API** : `pip install sandlock`, simple decorator or context manager
- **Per-process granularity** :  each tool call gets its own sandbox
- **Linux-only** :  matches nanobot's primary platform; Docker users on macOS/Windows get it for free inside the container

### Example usage

```python
from sandlock import Sandbox

sandbox = Sandbox(
    fs_read=["/workspace", "/usr/lib", "/usr/bin"],
    fs_write=["/workspace/output"],
    net_allow=["api.example.com:443"],
    max_memory_mb=512,
    max_procs=10,
)

result = sandbox.run(["bash", "-c", user_command])
```

## Alternatives considered

- **Docker per-execution** — too slow (~200ms+ startup per tool call) and heavy
- **firejail** — requires root or setuid binary
- **bubblewrap (bwrap)** — viable but lower-level; no Python API, no resource limits without cgroups
- **Regex hardening** — fundamentally flawed as a security boundary (deny-list vs allow-list)

## References

- [sandlock GitHub](https://github.com/multikernel/sandlock)
- [Landlock LSM](https://landlock.io/)
- [seccomp-bpf](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/userspace-api/seccomp_filter.html)

issues.title: Allow web_fetch to continue beyond truncated text

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

web_fetch returns only the first maxChars characters of extracted text. When truncated is true, an agent has no way to read the remaining sections without requesting an increasingly large prefix, repeating content in its context.

### Proposed Solution

Add a nonnegative character offset and return nextOffset and totalLength for text results. Apply the slice after extraction and keep the untrusted-content banner on every chunk. Offset defaults to zero; image results and network policy stay unchanged.

### Alternatives Considered

Increase maxChars and fetch the same prefix again, or use an external fetch tool. A continuation offset allows bounded tool results with the existing extractors.

### Related Component

Other

### Additional Context

A focused implementation covers Jina, readability, and plain text. Related tool and network-security tests pass (105 tests). Each call fetches the URL again, so content or extractor changes can shift offsets; this limitation is documented.

issues.title: Add optional pagination to list_sessions

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

list_sessions returns every other persisted session in one tool result. As conversations accumulate, an agent cannot request a bounded page of handles, even when it only needs to inspect a few sessions.

### Proposed Solution

Add optional nonnegative offset and positive limit parameters. Paginate the existing handle order after excluding the current session. Keep the JSON array result and the current full-list behavior when the parameters are omitted.

### Alternatives Considered

The agent can discard extra handles after reading the full result, but that still consumes context. Changing the default limit would also change existing behavior.

### Related Component

Other

### Additional Context

A focused implementation and documentation are ready. The related session tool and handle tests pass (29 tests), including page boundaries, current-session exclusion, and invalid input.

issues.title: Allow the cron tool to pause and resume scheduled jobs

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

The scheduler and WebUI can enable or disable a scheduled job, but the cron tool only exposes add, list, and remove. A chat user who wants to pause a recurring task must use WebUI or delete and recreate it, losing the original job ID and run history.

### Proposed Solution

Add enable and disable actions backed by CronService.enable_job(). Add include_disabled to list so the agent can find paused jobs; keep the current enabled-only default. Preserve the existing schedule, linked chat, and run history. System jobs remain protected, and jobs without a linked chat cannot be enabled.

### Alternatives Considered

Use WebUI, or remove and recreate the job. The former is unavailable in a chat-only workflow; the latter discards the existing job identity and history.

### Related Component

Other

### Additional Context

Checked main 1f8e49c. A focused implementation reuses the existing scheduler method without changing storage. The cron suite passes with 185 tests, including pause/resume persistence and protection checks. I can contribute the PR.

A small set of default location shortcuts would make the picker easier to use from the start. ## Screenshot ### Proposed Solution ## Suggested improvements - Add a “This PC” entry or a drive list for switching between drives. - Add a “New folder” action. - Provide default shortcuts to common locations while keeping Favorites and Recent projects. - nanobot-api container constantly exiting and restarting (probably normal)

prs.title: feat(tui): render Mermaid diagrams as terminal images
prs.body:
## Why

The TUI currently leaves Mermaid fences as source. Render completed diagrams as real terminal images with Pele 1.6.0, while retaining the original source and a keyboard-operated viewer.

Related to [NAN-288](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-288).

## What changed

- Add transparent inline previews after streaming completes, plus `Ctrl+G` / `/diagrams` for zoom, pan, diagram selection, source viewing/copying, cancel/retry, and returning without losing the draft or reading position.
- Rasterize Pele SVG with resvg and matching fontkit measurements in one owned child process. Bound source/output/pixels, retained images, queue depth, and runtime; release off-screen images and cancel/reap obsolete work. Invalid, oversized, or unsupported diagrams retain their source.
- Pin rendering dependencies, prepare target-specific native bindings, include their notices/relinking information, and cover streaming, source retention, cancellation, image disposal, and viewer behavior.

## Scope

TUI presentation and packaging only. WebUI rendering, gateway execution, session storage, and model-context content remain unchanged. Diagram layout and rasterization use the same installed fonts; unavailable fonts/glyphs and unsupported italic styles produce source feedback.

## Tradeoffs

A separate native process makes font/raster heaps reclaimable after completion or cancellation; process startup and font loading remain costs. In a 16-cycle viewer run, sampled TUI private memory stayed within 666–688 MiB, ending below the first sample; the largest sampled render-child private memory was 613 MiB, with at most one child. Pixel budgets are not a whole-process memory cap.

## Blast Radius

The Markdown code-fence hook, theme changes, viewer focus, transcript/session teardown, and native TUI packaging are affected. Keep the compiled entry statically linked so OpenTUI's parser-worker assets continue to load; ordinary Markdown and code were checked in the standalone Windows executable.

## Verification

Bun 1.3.13, Windows x64 baseline, base `909b277e7a5a7ecd2aebdba9611e5febe86988d9`:

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun run check`, and `bun run check:imports`: passed.
- `bun test`: **273 passed**, 0 failed.
- `bun run test:imports`: **41 passed, 1 skipped**, 0 failed; the existing Vite-registry integration case is skipped.
- `bun scripts/prepare-target.ts win32-x64`, `bun scripts/build.ts win32-x64`, `bun scripts/release-notices.ts win32-x64`, and `python scripts/package-release.py win32-x64`: passed. The independently extracted archive passed all nine manifest checks and runs without `node_modules`.
- Actual WezTerm `20260917-114457-b09b56c2` / Kitty graphics: source and compiled paths exercised Chinese flow/sequence diagrams, long labels, an 8078-pixel-wide diagram, zoom/pan, scrolling, pane resize, streaming completion, history/session switches, drafts, dark/light backgrounds, ordinary Markdown/code, explicitly disabled image protocols, invalid/over-limit source, and cancellation/reaping followed by successful rendering.

Terminal checks used a task-isolated deterministic gateway fixture, not a real model or production sessions. The publication cleanup only removes a trailing blank line in an erased type declaration. Large-diagram/resize/memory/motion evidence also predates an empty-viewer-only caption/navigation fix; their rendering and ownership paths are unchanged. Screenshots, motion capture, command logs, and snapshot hashes are retained with the local verification artifacts.

Linux/macOS, other terminals, Sixel, real-model/persistence E2E, and lone-Esc timing remain unverified. The final OS clipboard readback was skipped to preserve existing non-text clipboard content; exact source copying is unit-tested, and the terminal copy action was exercised. CI results are pending.

prs.title: fix(webui): make browser notification failures actionable
prs.body:
## Why

Refs [NAN-227](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-227).

Browser notification opt-in can fail silently, and the `Notification` constructor can throw on mobile browsers. Make permission and delivery failures actionable while keeping alerts bounded by the page's actual capabilities.

## What changed

- Add a separate **Settings → Notifications** destination with independent browser-notification and completion-sound switches. Use compact grouped rows, shared help hints, visible recovery guidance, and an opt-in-only test action. Update all ten locales and the WebUI guide.
- Deliver through an active service worker, with bounded permission, readiness, and display waits. Probe the notification protocol so an older worker produces an explicit retry/reload message. Permission revocation disables the local notification preference; allowing permission again still requires explicit opt-in.
- Observe live task events outside the mounted chat, use generic task-status text, and deduplicate across tabs/reconnects. Route clicks to the owning gateway/chat with normal authentication; remote views can reveal only an existing online connection.

## Scope

The existing browser-preference key and default-off behavior are preserved. Completion sound remains an independent page chime; its trigger behavior is unchanged. This changes the frontend and service worker, not backend execution, session storage, model prompts, or tool schemas.

This does not add Web Push or an all-gateway notification center. New task alerts depend on an open, connected, non-suspended page. Temporary chats require their original connection.

## Tradeoffs

An active worker that implements the notification protocol is required; there is no unverified constructor fallback. **Test notification** reports submission to the browser, not confirmed OS display. Worker receipts are limited to 256 events within 24 hours; restricted browser storage can reduce deduplication after a worker restart.

## Blast Radius

Touches settings routing/localized copy, the client-side live-event subscriber, service-worker notification handling, and the remote-host reveal bridge. The main compatibility risks are stale workers and notification click routing across independently updated pages/hosts. These still need the real-device/upgrade acceptance below.

## Verification

- Focused WebUI regression: **11 files / 417 tests passed**, covering notifications, the worker, client lifecycle events, host sessions/bridge, settings/app integration, preferences, sound, and localization.
- `bun run lint` and `bun run build` passed on the final working snapshot. Build uses the production TypeScript configuration; it is not an all-test-source TypeScript pass.
- Client import-boundary scan and its 38 contract tests passed before the final class/copy-only refinements; those refinements do not change imports or dependencies.
- Real isolated gateway and HeadlessChrome: CDP-controlled permission grant/revocation, explicit re-enable, preference persistence, and a test submission through the real worker-backed notification path. `getNotifications()` returned the submitted notice. Earlier real-worker two-tab probing returned `submitted` and `skipped` for one identity.
- Checked Chinese/English/French, light/dark, desktop/390px/320px, keyboard help, and Chromium touch emulation. Ordinary rows remain 60px with a 44px test-action touch target; long labels wrap without horizontal overflow.
- A full-suite attempt after integrating main was **not green**. Subsequent focused reruns passed; two `temporary-chat-navigation` failures also reproduced on unchanged main. No full-suite pass is claimed, and no unrelated navigation fix is included.

### Outstanding draft acceptance

- A user-operated OS permission prompt, visible system banner, and clicking a real OS notification.
- Android Chrome, iOS normal tab/Home Screen, and the reported embedded browser.
- Complete old-page/new-worker and new-page/old-worker upgrade flows, plus multi-host end-to-end notification clicks.

Responsive screenshots, Chromium touch emulation, and browser submission are not proof of device support or OS-banner visibility. No production gateway was restarted, and no production browser permission or provider credentials were changed.

prs.title: fix(agent): add size guardrails to Dream memory files and requests
prs.body:
## Summary

PR #5622 fixed Dream's system-prompt duplication bug, but as a side effect
removed the only existing size cap on SOUL.md / USER.md / memory/MEMORY.md
(the old `_DREAM_FILE_EMBED_CAP = 8000` mechanism). Since then these
Dream-managed files can grow unbounded and get injected into every regular
turn's system prompt with no limit, and Dream's own consolidation request
has no check against the model's context window either.

This adds two related guardrails:

**Per-file display cap** (`nanobot/agent/context.py`, `nanobot/agent/memory.py`)
- Regular turns: SOUL.md/USER.md/MEMORY.md are truncated at markdown `## `
  section boundaries when they exceed `max_file_chars` (default 8000,
  configurable via `agents.defaults.memory.maxFileChars`) — trailing
  complete sections are kept, a note tells the model to call `read_file`
  for the full content. A single section that alone exceeds the budget
  (e.g. a large file under one heading) is hard-truncated by character
  count so the limit always holds.
- Dream turns are exempt: Dream is the sole writer of these files and needs
  the full view to avoid overwriting content it can't see. Detected via the
  existing `session_key.startswith("dream:")` convention.
- Writes (`write_memory`/`write_soul`/`write_user`) warn once per file when
  oversize but never block or truncate — Dream stays free to write, pruning
  stays Dream's own MECE responsibility.

**Dream request token budget** (`nanobot/agent/memory.py`, wired into the
`/dream` command and the periodic cron job)
- `dream_prompt_within_budget()` estimates the assembled Dream request
  (mirroring `Consolidator._input_token_budget`, and sharing its safety
  buffer constant) and, if it's over budget, halves the history batch and
  retries down to 1 entry. Estimates against the actual restricted Dream
  tool set (`store.build_dream_tools()`), not the caller's full tool
  registry, so the estimate matches the real request size.
- Distinguishes "no history to process" from "history exists but doesn't
  fit even at the minimum batch" so the user gets an accurate diagnostic
  instead of a misleading one.

## Why

Without these, a long-running Dream deployment could grow these files
without any pressure toward the context window, since #5622 removed the
only cap and never added a replacement. This restores an equivalent
safety net at both points where these files matter: display (regular
turns) and the Dream request itself.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests for section-boundary capping (including the case where a
  single section alone exceeds the budget) and Dream-turn bypass, in
  `tests/agent/test_context_builder.py`
- [x] New tests for write-side warnings in `tests/agent/test_memory_store.py`
- [x] New tests for the budget check (fits/shrinks/over-budget/zero-window,
  and that the estimate uses the real restricted Dream tools) in
  `tests/agent/test_dream.py`, including an end-to-end test driving a real
  `dream:` session through `AgentLoop.process_direct`
- [x] Full test suite passes (`pytest`), `ruff check`, `basedpyright`

prs.title: Checkpoint completed tool results at execution-batch boundaries
prs.body:
Closes #5747

## Problem

During a multi-tool response the durable runtime checkpoint only existed in two shapes: `awaiting_tools` with every call pending, and `tools_completed` with every call done. If tool A finished, tool B started and the gateway crashed before C ran, the checkpoint on disk still said all three were pending. Recovery then threw away A's real result and lost the evidence that a side-effecting tool had already run.

## Change

- `execute_tool_calls` takes an optional `on_batch_complete` callback. It is awaited after every execution batch that leaves further calls pending, with the `(tool_call, result)` pairs completed so far and the calls not started yet. The existing batching (`_partition_tool_batches`) defines the boundaries; nothing is reported after the last batch, the caller already owns that checkpoint.
- `AgentRunner` passes a callback that emits an `awaiting_tools` checkpoint at each boundary: `completed_tool_results` holds the finished calls' normalized tool messages (same builder as the final `tools_completed` payload, so the rows are identical), `pending_tool_calls` the rest. No `provider_state` is attached, so the partial shape is never treated as synchronized.
- `runtime_checkpoint_is_well_formed` accepts the partition for `awaiting_tools`: completed and pending ids must be disjoint, cover the assistant's tool-call ids exactly, contain no duplicates, and at least one call must still be pending (an all-completed turn is `tools_completed`). The legacy all-pending shape stays valid.
- `restore_runtime_checkpoint` needed no change: it already keeps completed rows and materializes `Error: Task interrupted before this tool finished.` rows for pending calls; the web UI still lands in `awaiting_user` / `tool_state_unknown` and never resumes the pending calls.

Invariant: `completed_ids ∪ pending_ids == assistant_tool_call_ids` and `completed_ids ∩ pending_ids == ∅`.

## Non-goals (as in the issue)

No automatic replay, no new ledger or scheduler, no exactly-once guarantee, no change to ordinary agent behaviour or public configuration.

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_runner_tool_execution.py`
  - `test_tool_execution_reports_completed_batches_before_pending_work`: concurrent (`[read_a, read_b] | [write_a]`) yields one boundary with both reads completed and the write pending; sequential yields a boundary after each of the first two calls; never after the last batch.
  - `test_runner_checkpoints_each_completed_tool_batch`: checkpoint phases become `awaiting_tools (all pending) → awaiting_tools (A completed, B pending) → tools_completed → final_response`; the partial payload carries A's real result, shares the assistant message, and has no provider state.
- `tests/session/test_recovery.py`
  - `test_partially_completed_tools_keep_results_and_interrupt_the_rest`: after a restart A's saved result is kept, B becomes an interrupted result, recovery waits for confirmation, nothing is enqueued.
  - `test_partial_tool_checkpoint_partition_is_validated`: legacy shapes accepted; partition accepted; overlap, gaps, duplicates and an all-completed `awaiting_tools` rejected.

`tests/agent`, `tests/session`, `tests/webui`, `tests/channels` and `nanobot/channels`: 4464 passed locally (the 5 failures are the pre-existing Windows/no-Node ones). `ruff check` clean on the touched files.

prs.title: fix(webui): recognize typed session handles as references
prs.body:
## Why

Typing or pasting a valid session handle could leave it as plain text unless that session had already been selected in the draft. This also omitted the structured reference when sending, so identical text behaved differently depending on how it was entered.

Fixes [NAN-286](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-286).

## What changed

- Resolve session mentions against the available session catalog using the existing mention parser; menu selection and sidebar dragging are no longer prerequisites.
- Pin resolved session identities across catalog refreshes, and persist the same active references used for highlighting and sending. Keep session/App/MCP name precedence consistent with the palette.
- Add behavioral regressions for typing, clipboard paste, deduplication, editing, late catalog loading, draft restoration, name collisions, stable queued references and the eight-chat limit; update the user guide.
- Use the same text-derived references and insertion eligibility for palette completion, drag preview and drop; protect handle reuse and the eight-session limit.
- Remove the unused private `WebuiSessionAccess._metadata()` helper; keep the active async validation path unchanged.
- Recognize handles separated by Chinese/ASCII punctuation without spaces, using the same boundaries for highlighting, palette completion, drag/drop and sent-message links. Embedded email/path handles remain plain text.

## Scope

Behavior changes remain frontend-only; the backend diff only removes an unused private helper. No new API, persistence format, dependency, or backend access-policy changes. Unknown handles remain plain text; titles are not addresses. More than eight distinct references still produce an explicit send error rather than silently losing references.

## Blast Radius

Composer highlighting, outbound session-reference metadata, sent-message mention rendering, drafts and queued guidance. The shared parser also renders existing App/MCP mentions. Existing bindings intentionally retain their session identity when the sidebar catalog refreshes; backend validation remains authoritative when sending.

## Verification

### Punctuation-boundary fix (`2e64d3fb8`)

- Regression-first: the previous code failed **8 relevant cases**; after the fix the focused four-file suite passed **269 tests**.
- Full WebUI Vitest suite via Node: **168 files / 2,952 tests passed**.
- WebUI lint, production build (including TypeScript), client import boundaries and `git diff --check` passed. Import-checker tests: **41 passed**, one Windows-only case skipped on Linux.
- Built WebUI through a separate authenticated loopback gateway and bundled Chromium: the reported `@bime、@luma， @luma` input highlights all occurrences; native clipboard paste, punctuation-adjacent completion without extra leading spaces, and native sidebar drag passed.
- Real outgoing WebSocket data preserves the original text and attaches two distinct target identities; persisted transcript and reload retain all three reference links. Nine punctuation-separated references are explicitly rejected without sending. Embedded email/path handles remain plain text. No browser console, page or HTTP resource errors were observed.
- The disposable gateway was stopped and its runtime removed after verification; the existing user acceptance instance and daily gateway were left untouched. Live model responses, coverage and the full browser suite were not rerun for this fix.

### Follow-up cleanup (`098a1c1fe`)

- Full WebUI Vitest suite via Node: **168 files / 2,944 tests passed**.
- Python session-reference and session-handle tests: **19 passed**. Ruff and Python import-boundary checks passed.
- WebUI lint, production build (including TypeScript), client import boundaries and `git diff --check` passed. Import-checker tests: **41 passed**, one Windows-only case skipped on Linux.
- Built WebUI through an isolated gateway and bundled Chromium: palette completion, native sidebar dragging, outgoing reference identity, persisted reference metadata, and correct reference links after reload passed. No unexpected browser console or page errors were observed.

### Earlier feature verification (`8fcd7d7e9`)

The coverage and full browser-suite results below are historical evidence for the original feature commit; those two checks were not rerun for either follow-up.

- Regression-first: the original implementation failed seven relevant cases; the focused four-file suite now passes all 209 tests.
- Full WebUI suite and coverage: **168 files / 2,941 tests passed**, with 93.58% statement/line coverage and 88.04% branch coverage.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run build` (including TypeScript), `bun run check:imports`, and `git diff --check` passed. Import-checker tests: 41 passed, one Windows-only case skipped on Linux.
- Full `bun run test:browser`: **94 passed**.
- Built WebUI through an isolated gateway and real Chromium: typing without selection, system clipboard paste, duplicate/case-insensitive handles, unknown handles, outgoing reference identity, persisted-history reload, palette completion and native sidebar dragging passed. Light/dark screenshots are attached to NAN-286.

The isolated provider deliberately points to an unused loopback port: this verifies reference admission and persistence, not live model behavior, and makes no paid model requests. No native mobile/Windows/OS-IME acceptance was performed. No production configuration, sessions or running service were modified.

prs.title: feat(update): integrate managed installs and recoverable in-app updates
prs.body:
## macOS Dock lifecycle integration (2026-10-19)

**Still not activated or release-ready. Do not merge or publish yet.** PR head and latest acceptance source: `de6fa805f7914adc63dd6d579c63e50ca530536b`. This adds the approved original cat on its white tile; it does not add an OS login service, native window, updater, or execution owner.

- Official installer-managed `nanobot webui` auto-detaches as before. Its gateway owns the optional Dock connection after activation, so returning to the terminal does not remove the icon. Attached/source launches retain their client-scoped lifetime.
- Upgrade, ordinary restart and automatic recovery recreate the icon after gateway activation. Stop or gateway death releases it. Multiple launchers share one helper. Closing the icon hides the shortcut, not the service or tasks; another explicit launch or service restart restores it.
- `--no-dock` opts out; detached mode remembers desktop intent in a small instance-local runtime marker, without credentials or URLs. The stdlib AppKit helper has no installation/data lease, and is absent from frozen worker/recovery dependencies. Optional icon failures do not prevent WebUI startup or restart. No dependency/compiler download or global app installation is introduced.
- The existing foreground Dock work is integrated here without changing the developer's checkout. Main was synchronized through `f57018aa7`. Existing maintainer work in stacked **#6280** is neither duplicated nor merged: its catalogue revalidation, recovery-consent and orphaned-preparation fixes remain a separate pending review dependency.
- Integration checks exposed two main/PR interactions, now repaired: TypeScript React declarations no longer override Bun runtime module resolution (a real Bun SSR regression protects packaging), and the About startup skeleton shares the updated settings layout rather than shifting when live content appears.

### Verification for this addition

Latest macOS arm64 private candidate `317df2bd29c8d614efb4103075d1049e41d5fc9a` (`0.3.7.dev2026101902`) is a version-only child of the named source. Native wheel SHA-256: `f491f051a7c426b21237065e8629c210575b189dbdca038259e533c492192aeb`. This is an isolated test identity, not a published/reserved release version.

- All nine native packaged scenarios / fifteen hops passed with Dock lifecycle checks: healthy/consecutive/skipped-Preview upgrades, candidate import/startup failure, backup-write failure, worker exit, partial metadata loss and interrupted restoration. Each restored service then updated to the unchanged healthy target. Configuration/source bytes, canonical SQLite records, authenticated transcript history, scheduled deliveries, continued writes and a second ordinary start were preserved.
- The actual previous Dock-enabled package (`0.3.7.dev2026101901`, SHA-256 `8451f3190939adde6475ac59a2bbdf68f3f20f1ae88494644842e67726084f45`) ran its own updater to the latest candidate: healthy upgrade and backup-failure recovery followed by a fresh healthy upgrade, two scenarios / three hops. Separately, the earlier candidate from source `8dd814829` passed nine scenarios / fifteen hops and the retained pre-Dock `0.3.6.dev2026101701` baseline passed three scenarios / five hops. Those earlier results are not relabelled as latest-package historical compatibility.
- An additional latest-installed-package probe verified repeated auto-detach launches produce one icon, opt-out/helper exit leaves the gateway running, gateway SIGKILL removes the icon, the next start restores it, and a missing icon asset cannot block restart. Data preservation/continued writes passed. Initial supplemental attempts inherited the developer checkout as the child working directory and loaded old source; after isolating the working directory as well as interpreter/account, the full probe passed. No production assertion or timeout was weakened. All test-owned services/helpers were stopped afterward.
- Native AppKit OS-reopen opened a real browser page; shared-client and abnormal-client cleanup passed on the unchanged native helper. This is not an automated physical Dock click or new visual sign-off; the approved image bytes are unchanged. The latest installed-release probe served all 378 WebUI assets, executed the native TUI protocol probe without downloads and gracefully stopped a ready gateway.
- Latest-source SQLite/navigation/settings/gateway/Dock/restart/architecture checks: **471 passed / 1 skipped**. Update/UI/build regressions: **102 passed**. Four About skeleton browser cases pass across languages and viewport sizes. Earlier scoped regression groups were **684 passed / 6 skipped**, **298 passed / 1 skipped**, and **52 packaging/build tests**; groups overlap and are not summed. Full Ruff, focused strict Python types, production/browser TypeScript, Bun production build, scoped ESLint and all 13 Python import-boundary rules pass. Whole-test TypeScript has pre-existing diagnostics with byte-identical before/after output, not claimed green.
- A full local installed-Chrome browser run passed 93/94; the unchanged Mermaid viewer test intermittently failed to dismiss its dialog (focused three-repeat check: two passes, one timeout). Its cause remains unconfirmed; it was not hidden by retries, weakened or changed in this Dock patch. CI has its independent result.
- [Latest-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39233966260) is complete: **9/9 SUCCESS** on the first attempt for head `de6fa805f`. WebUI passed 2,978 unit/integration tests and 94 browser tests. Linux Python 3.11/3.14 each passed 10,650 broad tests (61 skipped) and 170 serial CLI tests (1 skipped), with 85.80% combined 3.14 coverage. Windows passed 10,334 broad tests (142 skipped), 170 serial CLI tests (1 skipped), its isolated update/process groups, and 78 installer tests (1 skipped). Groups overlap and are not summed. Superseded/cancelled runs and earlier green runs below are not current-head approval.
- Linux x64 and Windows x64 native packages each passed **nine packaged scenarios / fifteen hops**, preserving config, canonical/display history, scheduled deliveries, continued writes and final stopped listeners; restored services then completed fresh healthy updates. Their reports bind CI merge `26e7454fa2628c8f76a83767f8442c7b8fe912f7`, with verified parents main `8778c697744f8334c5794cd37502e8eb77ee5585` and PR head `de6fa805f`. Native-wheel SHA-256: Linux `80e14d76789c2def5f65c71487753f81d814411d0e2798c0e2162e537c2884bc`; Windows `01526e600f56239a14d479d82600911c5f4c0bffa9db9469ed89cef6a4f707cb`. Both installed-release probes served 378 assets and bundled native TUI without frontend tools/downloads. The Windows standalone startup probe uses process-tree termination for cleanup, not graceful shutdown; actual restart/recovery is covered separately by the update journeys. These are not macOS native Dock evidence or the local candidate's bytes. The earlier local broad regression crossed a host wall-clock jump and correctly rejected an expired plan; its full rerun passed with the deadline unchanged.

Private transport/fault fixtures do not establish signed public-download acceptance. Signing remains disabled; no tag, release, catalogue, PyPI publication or daily configuration/chat data was changed. The existing release gates and #6280 review dependency still apply.

---

## Historical approval and recovery evidence (2026-10-17; not current-head CI)

**Not activated or release-ready. Do not merge or publish yet.**

The approval environment now requires independent review (no self-review or environment admin bypass, main-only). Existing main branch rules are unchanged. The signing enable variable remains absent; no signing workflow, tag, release, PyPI upload or catalogue write was performed.

This pass rejects malformed bundles before trust-service refresh and verifies that a failed second approval check never requests gateway shutdown. Stable and Preview still require the same fixed official manual-workflow identity, with no unsigned/checksum-only fallback.

Native acceptance now covers consecutive upgrades and a fresh healthy update after each restored service, retaining the same account and conversation history. Private feed generations advance and observed versions are never overwritten. Backup-write failure persists through the first job's automatic retry, but not a separately confirmed next job. The Windows native job budget is 60 minutes (individual subprocesses remain bounded); completed per-case reports survive a later failure. The previous cancelled Windows run was not a completed acceptance pass.

Current head: `0c6e0981073c6138c3627b24d25ea13f39e6149a`. [Current CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39005971036) is complete: **9/9 SUCCESS**. The controlled same-commit Python 3.14 rerun passed 10,347 tests (61 skipped), plus 166 serial CLI tests (1 skipped); combined coverage is 85.66%. Its first full-suite attempt passed 10,346 tests but failed one existing process-tree liveness assertion (child not confirmed stopped within three seconds). The affected shell/exec-session code and helper are unchanged from the preceding green head; five local focused repeats and 59 related tests passed, which is not Linux reproduction or a root-cause fix. No assertion or timeout is weakened. The first failure remains recorded with no confirmed root cause. Only that failed job was rerun; the native jobs' first-attempt bytes/reports remain authoritative and were not rebuilt.

Main advanced during acceptance to `508cedff3` (durable scheduled delivery). The integration retains its outbox owner and adds that store to the existing lease/backup inventory. Scheduled writes and replay participate in runtime admission; parked gateways cannot initialize the lazy database. No data is moved and no second migration is introduced.

An actual retained updater then exposed a compatibility defect: the new restart coordinator computed the latest data inventory, which exceeded the old immutable reservation. Automatic recovery restored the old service, but that is not a successful upgrade. The fix issues only the reviewed old grant, keeps the new lazy store under a separate ordinary lifetime lease, and defers its writes until activation. Missing authority for any other existing store still fails closed. A real parked-gateway regression reproduced the failure before the fix and passes for both scopes afterward; protocol 1 and old reservations are not rewritten.

Latest local evidence: 130 intersecting regressions and 108 update-job/stop/restart checks passed after the main merge. The compatibility fix passed 35 data/backup/profile/restart tests, an additional 10 data-lease checks, touched lint, focused strict types and all 13 import-boundary rules (groups overlap).

The new macOS arm64 native candidate passed all nine scenarios/15 hops, preserving pending scheduled-delivery records as well as configuration, canonical/display history, continued writes and second starts. Both actual retained baselines (the recent pre-outbox updater and an earlier pre-SQLite updater) passed four scenarios/seven hops each, including post-restoration updates. The actual installer serves 377 WebUI assets and bundled native TUI without frontend build tools and stops its ready gateway cleanly. Candidate `423ff3aa2b0e1c4a88d72270cddc6ce3b71ea7d7` is a private version-only child of the current head; native-wheel SHA-256 `2b1d47abeb9327f5c5cd9ef9913a38d9bf79dcab3e9a145e2eaec10a03fddc3c`.

Latest Linux x64 and Windows x64 native packages each passed the same **nine scenarios/15 hops**, including pending delivery rows, all five restored-service follow-up upgrades and final listener cleanup. Reports bind CI merge `3df7943b89ba4f251161c0adaa4db2f0841a3473`; its verified parents are main `508cedff3` and this PR head. Healthy-wheel SHA-256: Linux `bc129097e4d23596b5bb3c32eda5116faef22df83c7a054dfb553e1673146f80`; Windows `b3eca621b7d2cc684c8b4c738af02a8b42b5b9029acfce42b8245d4598702d0e`. The separate Windows startup probe terminates its process tree for cleanup; it does not claim graceful shutdown. The update journeys exercise actual restart/recovery separately. Windows 3.14 also passed 10,040 broad-suite tests (133 skipped), 166 serial CLI tests (1 skipped), 76 isolated update-job tests (5 skipped); its process/installer job passed 59 process tests and 78 installer tests (1 skipped). These overlapping groups are not summed.

Prior-head evidence: `83d5dfcb7` completed [CI 39002575097](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39002575097), **9/9 SUCCESS**. Linux x64 and Windows x64 each passed nine native scenarios/15 hops; macOS arm64 passed that matrix plus four retained pre-SQLite scenarios/seven hops. Config, canonical/display history, continued writes and stopped listeners were verified separately. Those packages predate the new outbox integration and are not evidence for the current target bytes. Earlier 53 trust/stop/probe, 108 channel/plan/feed/WebUI, 86 pip/uv and 170 base-merge checks remain scoped prior evidence, not summed totals.

An earlier CI run exposed a 15-second cold PowerShell ACL/cleanup probe timeout. Its bounded budget is now 60 seconds with every security assertion retained; production browser behavior is unchanged. Windows source-path assertions compare escaped literals. The latest Windows checks and full CI run are now complete as recorded above.

The incremental approval-patch security review found no confirmed blocking issue in its six changed source files and required callers. This is not an exhaustive audit of the entire PR. Private lifecycle fixtures substitute signature admission; they do **not** prove official signed public continuity.

Remaining release gates: the real official signed old→candidate→next/public-download acceptance; independently reviewed runtime dependency inventory/enforcement and trusted original-owner bootstrap; final same-batch native platform coverage and maintainer/license handoff. Approval authenticates the nanobot artifact, not all owner-selected dependencies, reproducible builds or benign source. It cannot promise protection after full repository/host compromise or 100% availability.

---

## Summary

Integrate managed installation, prebuilt release candidates, exact-version updates, failure recovery and one shared WebUI flow.

This continues chengyongru's work in #5817; its commits and attribution remain intact. #5817 is closed as a duplicate of this PR. Candidate preparation from #6154 is already incorporated. #6146 is the design record. Review this PR as the integration target; do not merge the incorporated branches again as independent updaters.

Ordinary users install prebuilt WebUI and native TUI packages without Bun or Node. Maintainers decide when to request a candidate. There is no scheduled daily packaging or automatic publication.

## User flow and installation ownership

The sidebar and Settings → About share confirmation, progress and saved-job recovery. The gateway selects an exact target, stages and verifies files, obtains stop/install/restart consent, waits for reviewed runtimes to be idle, installs offline and verifies the restarted gateway. Refresh, reconnect and duplicate requests read the same job. Installed package metadata alone cannot prove success.

| Installation | Supported route |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh official installer | Dedicated environment, selection receipt and persistent gateway; inline update and bounded automatic service recovery for eligible layouts. Interrupted first installs retain their owner for retry. |
| Verified POSIX uv 0.11.16 registry tool | Inline update preserves the uv receipt, extras, constraints and additional packages. Saved-job/original-launcher recovery remains available; this does not convert the install to a managed environment. |
| Other uv, pipx, ordinary pip venv | Owner-specific in-app guidance: correct machine/environment, stop and backup steps, applicable copyable command, original-launcher restart and authenticated running-version verification. Unknown extras, fixed sources, unsupported layouts and GitHub-only Preview targets do not receive guessed registry commands. |
| Source, Docker, services, Desktop | Use the original owner/deployment route. Source `update`, `--check` and opt-in `--dev` keep their existing restrictions; source is not Preview. Preserve container volumes. Native Desktop keeps the distributor's updater. |

Only affected background gateways restart, not the computer. Stopped profiles stay stopped. Active tasks and other writers block shutdown. Remote mutations require the existing explicit package-install permission. Displaying or copying guidance never executes it.

## Stable and Preview

**Receive preview updates** is visible, off by default and installation-scoped. Saving it does not authorize installation.

- Offer only a newer compatible Stable or Preview target. Installing a final does not unsubscribe from Preview.
- Turning Preview off does not downgrade. Keep a newer installed Preview until an eligible final appears.
- Reject stale preference revisions and reviewed plans after a channel change. Active/admitted jobs must finish or recover first.
- Preserve withdrawal history, offline errors and incompatible-release explanations. A verified newer final can remain available when the Preview index is unavailable.
- Use complete PyPI artifacts for Stable discovery and a protected catalogue with immutable manifests for Preview. Revalidate exact targets, approved HTTPS hosts, pinned DNS, checksums, sizes and catalogue history.

Stable patches can ship between monthly feature releases. Preview can be prepared as frequently as maintainers request. Candidate preparation and approval to publish its exact artifacts are separate actions. No timer, automatic channel enrollment or public feed is enabled here.

## Ownership and dependencies

- `update_service` owns update policy and saved-job operations. WebUI and CLI are consumers, not alternate executors.
- Agent/session owners expose generic admission, shutdown and pending-work contracts. They do not import update policy.
- Installation/data leases are shared primitives. The updater and ordinary runtimes use the same ownership checks.
- Frozen worker/recovery code can run outside a broken application environment. Do not collapse this independent boundary into the live UI or gateway.
- The protected restart adapter composes the existing CLI launcher; it does not construct a second AgentLoop. Executable import rules restrict this integration to the required startup/process contracts.
- Packaging scripts are preparation tools, not another runtime updater. Feed/plan persistence imports the atomic-file primitive directly rather than the broad model/token helper module.

Previous simplification removed the unmounted prototype updater, duplicate state/lock ownership and pass-through methods without removing supported flows. The current integration preserves main's settings-domain controllers rather than restoring the old flattened controller.

## Failure recovery and compatibility

Eligible managed installs preserve the original program and dependencies before mutation. An independent frozen supervisor can retry the admitted target once. If that fails before activation, it can restore the original program and restart reviewed gateways **only if protected user data is unchanged**. Journaled renames support interrupted restoration. The UI reports **Previous version restored**, not update success.

Recovery never replaces current configuration or chats with an old backup. Activated or data-changing candidates cannot be downgraded automatically. Missing base Python, corrupt backups, persistent storage/ownership failure or loss of both recovery processes can still need an operator. There is no boot-time recovery service or zero-failure guarantee.

Fresh official installation intentionally changes to managed/persistent defaults. Existing installation ownership and protocol 1 remain supported. Optional wire additions and old saved-job behavior remain compatible.

Latest-base integration includes main's SQLite session owner (#5943). Runtime drain precedes backup; the scoped session directory includes the database and sidecars. Do not treat older JSONL-based packaged acceptance as proof for this new base. This update implementation does not add another session migration or storage root.

## Earlier installation-matrix verification (2026-10-16)

Evidence head: `dbba58a058a5d588ae1c7d775bfc3263896c92e9`. [That-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38910467525): **all nine checks passed**, including Windows installer checks. This is historical evidence; the latest results are recorded at the top. No merge or release is authorized.

- Real installed-process acceptance on macOS arm64 completed **21 consecutive upgrade/recovery steps**. It covered the official managed installer; uv 0.11.16 inline updates; ordinary pip; pipx 1.8.0 and 1.17.12 (pip backend), including custom constraints/index options; pipx 1.17.12 with its uv backend; and editable source updates with real Git fast-forward and WebUI/TUI builds.
- The same managed account moved from Stable to Preview, skipped Preview versions, reached a final, restored after a bad candidate, then successfully accepted another update. Turning Preview off did not downgrade or restart. A corrupt download was rejected before shutdown. Repeated confirmation did not restart the completed job.
- Each step checked the running gateway, retained configuration and history, canonical SQLite records separately from display transcripts, continued writes, another ordinary start and final listener cleanup. Private synthetic versions and controlled transport are labelled fixtures, not historical or public-download evidence.
- This found a real pipx defect: a generic upgrade can discard the original requirement constraints and pip options. Guidance and both bootstrap scripts now refuse that unsafe route for customized records, without changing the installation owner or exposing private options. Ordinary installs still update; custom-owner reinstall trials retained the original settings across two upgrades. The exact manual handoff documents its base-installation scope.
- The existing eight-scenario packaged recovery probe also passed again on macOS. The harness now reuses seed/snapshot/data checks for consecutive updates and uses the production channel revision and preparation route. No second updater was added.
- **172 focused update/import-boundary tests passed**. **83 real offline installer/hand-off tests passed**, including the four new pipx policy cases. Test groups are not summed. Touched Ruff, shell syntax, diff checks and focused production strict types passed.
- The new Linux x64 and Windows x64 native packages each passed **8/8 installed upgrade/recovery journeys**. Their reports bind CI merge `0d06065e470154847ce222b0646315654a760a76`; its parents are main `559107172` and this head `dbba58a05`. Healthy-wheel SHA-256: Linux `915187e88dd803cdc9033b9a1fd8e04714f668194b2deeb820cca4ed1567e2cd`; Windows `b3b832568e0f10b6c28e0f0498c14251b8467b7e0db79fa1da6cbca52fec9f8a`. All data-preservation, continued-write, second-start and listener-cleanup assertions passed. The separate Windows startup probe uses forced cleanup; it is not graceful-shutdown evidence. The update journeys exercise actual stop/restart/recovery separately.
- Docker volume-preserving replacement was not exercised in this local matrix because the daemon is unavailable. The existing Docker CI is a build/startup/permission check, not that upgrade proof. Final five-platform artifact acceptance, historical public bootstrap coverage and public downloads remain release gates.

Prior head: `d6c7d6c8f479ead2804ca2558232b0358db51078`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38902530604): **all nine checks passed**. PR remains open, mergeable and review-required; it has not been approved, merged or released.

| Native execution | Package identity | Managed upgrade/recovery |

| Linux x64, Python 3.11.17 | CI merge `751bc1fe53bce50baf2a63e5c8b6f236bd8ee9f3`; SHA-256 `6177af18fcad97c44220af2b833e45d279292005ccc6b2d3895184c274290227` | 8/8 passed |

The CI merge's parents are verified as main `559107172a39b22bda0c4a2d3b58d9e63e0ea32d` and that prior PR head. Linux and Windows reports also confirm real installation, 377 bundled WebUI assets, native TUI protocol 1 without downloads and gateway readiness. The separate Windows startup probe uses forced cleanup and does not claim graceful shutdown; the eight update journeys exercise the actual stop/restart/recovery path and verify listener teardown.

- Native Linux and Windows CI now run the **installed package** through eight managed upgrade/recovery journeys, not just startup. The manual candidate workflow applies the same probe to its assembled Linux wheel. Small reports record the target SHA-256, candidate identity, outcomes and cleanup; no success report is emitted on failure.

- An actual packaged trial reproduced a production defect: after a busy gateway refused shutdown, the recovery supervisor waited five minutes for that healthy gateway's live lease. It now returns the refused-stop result immediately when shutdown was not committed; committed shutdown recovery remains intact. **124 focused regressions passed**, including unchanged-data and post-activation rollback guards. Ruff, focused strict types and Python import boundaries passed.
- macOS arm64 candidate `0.3.6.dev2026101601`, candidate commit `d729478aee7779f4e00f509b7b4c74bfd4081050`, source `dc1688ba0`, passed fresh official installation plus all eight packaged paths, including the final harness rerun. These are real installed-process journeys, not public-download or interactive-browser E2E. Recovery never rolls user data back to an old backup. macOS x64 and Linux arm64 native execution, public-baseline bootstrap for the other supported platforms/owners, and a single final approved release batch remain separate release gates.

## Earlier SQLite integration verification

Earlier integration head: `aa6a067d48339b1ed9d8eee15c1f4637639309ba`, including main `8f6a5594fbc0b79b0d9e3d8e82a864bdddf330b9`.

Reproduced that exact `ProcessLookupError` before the fix; **33 execution-budget/process-reaping tests passed** afterward, including the two disappearance cases. - #6154 records candidate `0.3.6.dev2026101102`, candidate SHA `1833bd2c6114486edf0863ccb12daac21eaeac5e`, source SHA `32a6705e5d7c860fdc5c8e55f84792fa8751cb6c`. These files are not rebuilt or relabeled as current-head artifacts.

Daily configuration and chats were not modified. Test groups overlap and are not added together.

## Release gates — still required

- [ ] Maintainer review/approval and merge; coordinate the incorporated #6154 and design #6146.
- [ ] Select actual versions and source. Existing users need their original installation method for the first updater-enabled release.
- [ ] Confirm the distributor can honor the three-year corresponding-source/relinking offer in `tui/SOURCE_OFFER.md`; verify pinned notices and source availability.
