prs.title: fix(update): close revalidation and recovery gaps
prs.body:
## Why

Stacked follow-up to #6168, targeting `codex/live-update-ui`. This addresses the three confirmed review findings: [catalogue history at handoff](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6168#discussion_r4302673476), [stale first supervisor launch](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6168#discussion_r4302673485), and [interrupted preparation recovery](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6168#discussion_r4302673488).

## What changed

- Reuse the installation's `releases` cache for final handoff revalidation, so a catalogue rollback cannot erase an already observed withdrawal before shutdown.
- Validate confirmation identity before the first supervision journal is published, and keep recovery/restoration bound to that confirmation while allowing an admitted completion to outlive its launch window.
- Offer **Review update** for preparation jobs restored after reconnect. Clear the saved job only after successful gateway settlement, then show a fresh review requiring another installation confirmation; keep refused or lost responses recoverable.

## Scope

The three update-flow fixes and their regression tests, plus documentation cleanup. The update guide now focuses on user actions and recovery; a separate `docs/update-protocol.md` owns developer API and lifecycle rules. The quick start and CLI reference link to the owning guide, the release checklist removes repeated explanations, and Markdown paragraphs use one source line each.

No dependencies, capabilities, persistence formats, release artifacts/workflows, or installation permissions change. Normal preparation confirmed in the current tab continues without an extra recovery prompt; handoff settlement remains gated by its existing optional capability.

## Blast Radius

Final pre-shutdown release checks, automatic-recovery supervisors, and restored WebUI update dialogs. Stale supervisor launches now stop before taking a newer confirmation's recovery budget. Preparation settlement still relies on the gateway's real ownership checks, refuses live owners, and does not prepare or install another update automatically.

## Verification

Documentation follow-up checks: Markdown AST inspection across nine related pages found no manual paragraph wraps and validated 231 local links. All 18 release-guide headings and nine command blocks were preserved. `tests/test_documentation_build.py` passed **3 tests** with one Windows-only skip; the actual documentation build hook copied all **60 documents** byte-for-byte in a disposable tree, including the new protocol guide. CLI flags were checked with isolated `nanobot update --help`; no update or publication was run.

The behavioral checks below ran at `66f6da20b6a492be931756102544cb495b7f7516`. The follow-up changes only Markdown; runtime code, tests, configuration and dependencies are unchanged, so those results are carried forward rather than presented as reruns.

- Python 3.12: `pytest -q tests/test_update_jobs.py tests/test_update_stop.py tests/test_release_feed.py tests/test_release_trust.py tests/webui/test_update_plans.py tests/test_update_plan.py tests/test_update_channels.py` — **237 passed**, two metadata deprecation warnings. A host-only launcher used symlinks for disposable fixture venvs because this standalone Python cannot execute copied binaries; updater code and frozen helpers were unchanged.
- `cd webui && bun run test` — **2,841 passed** across 163 files. `bun run build`, `bun run lint`, and `bun run check:imports` passed; `bun run test:imports` passed 37 tests with one Windows-specific skip.
- Touched-Python Ruff, focused basedpyright, Python import boundaries, and `git diff --check` passed.
- All three new regression scenarios failed on the original implementation before passing with the fixes. The supervisor regression uses real frozen supervisor/worker processes and offline pip in disposable fixture installations, with synthetic preflight/restart bodies.
- Chromium plus an isolated gateway: both saved preparation phases survived refresh, settled to `preparation_failed`, and opened a new review without sending prepare/execute/retry. A real preparation lease produced 409 and preserved read-only recovery. Saved jobs were synthetic and only the fresh-plan response was substituted; this is not a crash-to-upgrade E2E. Browser, lease child, and isolated gateway were cleaned up.
- Linux-only local verification; no Windows/macOS or public-release installation claim. The existing Test Suite workflow only triggers for PRs targeting `main`, so this stacked PR does not automatically receive that CI matrix.

prs.title: feat(web-search): add Serply (Google Search API) provider
prs.body:
## What

Adds [Serply](https://serply.io) as a web search provider, following the same pattern as the existing Serper provider (#4406). Serply is a Google SERP API; selecting it routes the `web_search` tool through `https://api.serply.io/v1/search/` with the user's own API key.

## Why

Gives users another API-key-backed Google search option alongside Serper, useful when they already hold a Serply key or want an alternative to avoid rate limits on free backends. Like every other keyed provider, it falls back to DuckDuckGo when no key is configured.

## Notes

- Serply support is optional, and behavior is unchanged when `SERPLY_API_KEY` is unset. The provider falls back to DuckDuckGo without a key, matching Serper and the other keyed providers.
- Follows the existing provider pattern in `nanobot/agent/tools/web.py`: an entry in `SEARCH_PROVIDER_OPTIONS` (which feeds the WebUI settings picker and CLI onboarding), a branch in `_effective_provider`, and a `_search_serply` method mirroring `_search_serper`. The request sends an explicit `User-Agent` because Serply sits behind Cloudflare, which rejects requests without one.
- Tests added in `tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`, mirroring the six Serper tests: keyless concurrency fallback, mocked search (URL, headers, params, formatting), env key resolution, DuckDuckGo fallback, HTTP error, and rate limiting. Network is mocked.
- Docs updated in `docs/configuration.md`: provider table row, config example, and the provider enum. See the [Serply documentation](https://serply.io/docs) for the response fields used (`results[].title/link/description`).

## Testing

- `uv run python -m pytest tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py -q`: 51 passed (45 existing plus 6 new).
- `uv run ruff check nanobot/agent/tools/web.py tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`: all checks passed.
- `uv run basedpyright nanobot/agent/tools/web.py`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- Live-tested against the real Serply API with a valid key: `execute(query="retrieval augmented generation", count=3)` returned three normalized results in the shared plaintext format, and `_effective_provider()` resolved to `serply` with a key and `duckduckgo` without one.

Disclosure: I work with Serply. Happy to adjust scope, naming, or drop this
entirely if it isn't a direction you want for the project.

prs.title: fix(webui): merge consecutive waiting messages
prs.body:
## Why

While a response was running, typing `1` + Enter, `2` + Enter, then empty Enter sent only `2` and left `1` behind. Separate queue items and a latest-item shortcut made continuous guidance overtake itself. Treat it as one waiting message instead.

Related: [NAN-285](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-285). Desktop and narrow screenshots are attached there.

## What changed

- Accumulate consecutive input in order and use one complete-message sender for canonical completion, empty Enter, Send now and the send arrow; replace independent queue rows/reordering with one editable/deletable preview.
- Preserve attachments, quotes and captured session targets; validate aggregate ingress limits before clearing input, fold legacy v1 queues without clipping text or excess editable attachments.
- Keep pending delivery owned by its topic across composer unmounts; preserve a manual draft after Stop or failed upload, including navigation during acceptance.

## Scope

WebUI composer behavior, draft restoration, translations, documentation and regressions. Backend scheduling, protocol and NAN-275's stale-browser-queue authorization policy are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

Continuous queued inputs are now intentionally one send/edit/delete unit. Text uses newline separators, and multiple selections share one quoted-context block. Legacy aggregates over current limits remain editable rather than being silently split or truncated.

## Blast Radius

All WebUI composer variants share the pending-message behavior. Existing draft attachments and session targets can restore over the current send limits so users can remove excess content; sending still validates the complete payload.

## Verification

- `bun run test` — **2933 passed**, 168 files.
- Focused composer, draft storage, attachments, pending-message and thread-shell tests — **302 passed**.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports` — passed.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` — **fails** with the same 473 baseline diagnostics; normalized file/code/message comparison has no added or removed diagnostics.
- Real Chrome / production bundle / isolated gateway / local deterministic model fixture: reproduced the original overtaking, verified whole-message forced and automatic sends, persisted transcript, refresh/edit, Stop, and failed attachment upload followed by navigation and retry. Desktop and 390px layout inspected. No external-model or real-touch-device run.

Browser evidence is pinned to `590c33ce3`; the follow-up only removes mention clipping when restoring an over-limit edited legacy draft, with a failing-then-passing refresh regression and final-head tests. None of the recorded browser scenarios changes under that delta.

The final full suite passed without changing unrelated tests or timeouts; earlier runs had unrelated file-preview/temporary-navigation timing failures, recorded with the local evidence. User visual acceptance remains pending.

prs.title: fix(providers): preserve Chat Completions refusal responses
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix the Chat Completions adapter ignoring refusal fields, which loses the model's refusal explanation and can trigger empty-response retries.

Preserve refusal text in both non-streaming and streaming responses, and map it to nanobot's existing internal `refusal` finish reason. The change is limited to the provider adapter and its regression tests.

## Root Cause

The Chat Completions API exposes refusal text separately through `message.refusal` for non-streaming responses and `delta.refusal` for streaming responses. A refusal can still arrive with `finish_reason: "stop"`, so forwarding the upstream finish reason alone does not identify it as a refusal.

For example, the [official Structured Outputs guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs), with **Chat Completions** selected, shows a refusal response whose message contains `role` and `refusal`, with no `content` field:

    {
      "choices": [{
        "index": 0,
        "message": {
          "role": "assistant",
          "refusal": "I'm sorry, I cannot assist with that request."
        },
        "finish_reason": "stop"
      }]
    }

nanobot already recognizes `"refusal"` as an internal finish reason, but the Chat Completions adapter did not translate these refusal fields into that internal representation. It also omitted the refusal text when collecting response content.

Consequently, a response containing refusal text but no ordinary content—whether `content` was absent or explicitly null—could be parsed as:

    LLMResponse(content=None, finish_reason="stop")

The runner can treat this result as an empty response and retry, even though the model has already returned a refusal explanation.

The existing handling of `"content_filter"` does not cover this case: content filtering and a model-generated refusal are distinct API outcomes. This issue concerns Chat Completions; the Responses API uses a different refusal content-block format.

## Changes

- Preserve non-streaming `message.refusal` text in the returned `LLMResponse`.
- Accumulate streaming `delta.refusal` fragments and forward them through the existing content callback.
- Set the internal finish reason to `"refusal"` when refusal text is present, including when the final stream chunk reports `"stop"`.
- Add parameterized JSON and SSE regression tests using the real OpenAI SDK with an HTTPX mock transport.
- Include ordinary-content controls and verify final text, streaming deltas, finish reasons, token usage, and absence of tool calls.

Production changes are limited to `nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py`. The fix reuses existing downstream refusal handling without changing the runner, retry policy, configuration, or Responses API.

## Result

Refusal explanations remain visible to callers instead of being discarded. Streaming callers receive the refusal fragments as they arrive, and the final response preserves the complete text with `finish_reason="refusal"`.

For the example above, the adapter now returns:

    LLMResponse(
        content="I'm sorry, I cannot assist with that request.",
        finish_reason="refusal"
    )

This allows downstream code to distinguish a refusal from an empty response with a normal `"stop"` finish reason. Ordinary text responses retain their existing behavior, and token usage remains available.

## Test

Before the fix, both refusal regression cases failed: JSON and SSE responses returned `content=None` with `finish_reason="stop"`. Both ordinary-content controls passed.

After the fix:

- **362 tests passed** across custom-provider parsing, OpenAI compatibility, Responses parsing, LLM response contracts, and runner error handling.
- Ruff passed for both modified files.
- BasedPyright reported **0 errors and 0 warnings** for the modified provider.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The regression tests exercise real SDK JSON and SSE parsing with controlled HTTP responses. The non-streaming refusal fixture uses `content: null`; the streaming fixture supplies refusal fragments without ordinary content. These tests verify adapter output and streaming callbacks.

prs.title: fix(webui): keep CLI Apps reads off the event loop
prs.body:
## Why

A cache-only CLI Apps list can spend seconds scanning a slow or mounted PATH. Its async API helper did all configuration, cache and executable discovery work synchronously, so it also stalled unrelated WebUI HTTP requests. Move the whole local read behind one worker-thread boundary, without changing the synchronous manager used by tools and skills.

## What changed

- Offload manager/config creation, cached full or installed-only payload construction, freshness checks and empty-catalog fallback together; keep background refresh task/throttle state on the event loop.
- Offload disk reads and atomic writes in the existing asynchronous registry refresh while retaining asynchronous HTTP and cache fallback behavior.
- Add real-helper regressions for full and nonempty installed-only reads, cancellation without late refresh, async cache IO/fallback, and authenticated socket HTTP progress while a real executable probe is held.

## Scope

Tracks [NAN-268](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-268), a child of NAN-33. No UI/schema/protocol, package metadata, install/update/uninstall/run, PATH, dependency or TTL/snapshot changes. Installed-only still skips refresh and omits `catalog_refresh_pending`; existing full-list content/source/status and empty-cache behavior remain covered.

## Tradeoffs

This fixes event-loop responsiveness, not the time needed to finish the list. Cancellation stops waiting but cannot stop an already-running filesystem probe, and enough slow readers can still occupy the shared default executor. A local read now publishes refresh intent only after payload/fallback succeeds: cancellation or a failing fallback no longer starts a late background refresh. No persistent cache, dedicated pool, global lock or single-flight policy is introduced.

## Blast Radius

Affects the WebUI CLI Apps HTTP/message list helper and disk IO during its background registry refresh. The manager remains synchronous for its other consumers, and management/execution actions continue performing their own live checks. Existing auth, error, sorting/merging and action tests are included in the full Python suite. The wire format and independently upgraded client/host contract do not change.

## Verification

Local Linux / Python 3.12.10 on the independent worktree, with all extras/dev and channel dependencies:

- Baseline RED: four new helper/refresh tests and both real HTTP list variants failed against the original implementation; finite independent watchdogs prevented hangs. Candidate focused suite: **194 passed**.
- `ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py scripts/check_import_boundaries.py`, `basedpyright`, `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` and `uv pip check`: passed.
- `python -m pytest -n 4 --dist loadfile --ignore=tests/cli/test_commands.py --cov=nanobot --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered -q -o faulthandler_timeout=60 --durations=25`: **9,777 passed, 51 skipped**, 226.49 s.
- `python -m pytest tests/cli/test_commands.py --cov=nanobot --cov-append --cov-report=term:skip-covered -q --durations=10`: **163 passed, 1 skipped**; combined coverage **86.18%** (required 75%).
- Separate documented gateway CLI process with isolated home/config/workspace/cache and a test-only held executable probe: unauthenticated list 401; authenticated full, nonempty installed-only and 2/4 concurrent full lists all returned 200 after release. `/api/workspaces` and `/api/settings` completed **before** release in every case (observed 1.944–50.522 ms). Owned gateway shut down; temporary runtime removed and both ports released.
- Read-only implementation/simplify review found no blocking issues. No browser/frontend build claimed: UI and wire behavior are unchanged; the public proof is authenticated HTTP.

### Fixed-104-row comparison

Same Python/dependencies/real manager, frozen 104-app caches and original 80-entry PATH; no profiler, network refresh, fake probe delay or reduced probe count. Each installed-state workload has one warmup per variant and five interleaved AB/BA pairs. Primary zero-installed maximum-loop-lag median: **11,329.47 ms → 0.846 ms**; list-wall median: **11,334.38 ms → 10,126.62 ms**. List completion still takes roughly 10–12 seconds; this is responsiveness evidence, not a list-speed or tail-latency guarantee.

| Fixture / variant | List wall ms (min / median / max) | Per-run max loop lag ms (min / median / max) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0 installed / baseline | 9775.50 / 11334.38 / 12225.69 | 9770.64 / 11329.47 / 12220.77 |
| 0 installed / candidate | 9246.05 / 10126.62 / 10632.67 | 0.442 / 0.846 / 0.855 |
| 1 installed / baseline | 9965.43 / 11671.06 / 12248.75 | 9960.51 / 11666.14 / 12243.83 |
| 1 installed / candidate | 10891.58 / 11541.86 / 12018.13 | 0.757 / 1.030 / 13.144 |

Fresh-interpreter first reads are reported separately (not filesystem-cold). Finite 2/4-reader group loop lag: baseline **22,155.46 / 39,250.12 ms**, candidate **0.836 / 1.355 ms**; each group has only one sample, so no throughput-scaling or unbounded-starvation claim. All full reads returned 104 apps with 187 native `which` calls; all 42 reads succeeded, and the entire JSON payloads matched across variants with **no fields ignored**. Twelve child processes exited/reaped and isolated temporary data was removed. Shared-host scheduling/filesystem-cache variance is not controlled. [Full method, first-read/concurrency tables, provenance and verification record](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/document/nan-268-验证与固定负载对比-pr-6275-5d9c9b7e1290).

### Current-head CI

[Run 39046013881, attempt 2](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39046013881/attempts/2) is pinned to `5e3698b5e6acf6770478d5aae5a187e92d3bf255` and succeeded. All applicable current-head checks passed: Linux 3.11, Linux 3.14 + coverage, Windows 3.14, Windows process compatibility and Docker; unrelated frontend jobs were skipped by path detection. The successful Linux/Docker/Windows-process results carry forward from attempt 1 on the same unchanged head; only the failed full Windows job was rerun.

The first Windows 3.14 full-suite attempt had one failure (9,649 passed / 119 skipped): the unchanged Slack late-result test timed out during its two-second `SessionState.aclose` cleanup. Its routing assertions precede cleanup; the stack does not traverse the changed CLI Apps read/refresh paths. Original failure logs are retained. Exactly one evidence-based complete Windows rerun succeeded with **9,650 passed / 119 skipped** plus serial CLI **163 passed / 1 skipped**. No source, timeout, test-selection or workflow change/waiver was used to remove the failure; the initial cleanup timing failure remains disclosed rather than claimed fixed.

prs.title: refactor(agent): deduplicate model request preparation
prs.body:
## Why

Normal model requests and no-tools recovery requests duplicated context preparation and provider-context assembly. Share this preparation without combining their different streaming, response-observation, cancellation, and usage-accounting behavior.

## What changed

- Replace `_build_request_kwargs` with `_prepare_model_request`, which prepares the governed messages and assembles generation settings and provider context for both paths. Malformed-call recovery continues to use the prepared messages.
- Attach streaming callbacks conditionally, then dispatch normal requests through a single provider call site.
- Add a regression covering two malformed tool-call responses followed by successful no-tools recovery, including tool suppression, callback selection, transcript content, and usage from all three requests.

## Scope

Only `nanobot/agent/runner.py` and `tests/agent/test_runner_core.py` change. No changes to `AgentLoop`, scheduling, provider retries, public APIs, configuration, persistence formats, or dependencies.

Production code decreases by 15 lines; the regression adds 58 test lines. The runner retains 28 methods and gains no classes. This is request-preparation deduplication, not a full lifecycle redesign or a performance/token-use improvement.

## Tradeoffs

Usage accounting and request completion remain at their existing call sites. No-tools finalization observes responses and handles exceptions in a different order from normal tool-capable requests; forcing those stages into one helper would require modes or callbacks and risk changing behavior.

## Blast Radius

Both main-agent and subagent execution use the shared runner. The affected contracts are governed request payloads, generation/preset propagation, streaming callbacks, and recovery usage totals. The refactor retains `tools=None` for no-tools requests and preserves the existing cancellation, reasoning-close, compaction, and accounting order.

## Verification

[Full pre-PR CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39048081173) passed all nine jobs on commit `d8830d4463fe74a73bf9d3efe77920299faaafec`: Python 3.11, Python 3.14 with coverage, Windows Python 3.14, Windows process compatibility, WebUI, Linux/Windows TUI, Docker, and change detection.

Local Linux/Python 3.12 verification with all extras and channel dependencies:

- Full Python/channel suite plus serial CLI tests: **9,936 passed, 52 skipped**, no failures; combined coverage **86.18%**. Skips include platform-specific checks and two unchanged Feishu collection guards.
- `python -m pytest -n 4 --dist loadfile --ignore=tests/cli/test_commands.py --cov=nanobot --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered -q -o faulthandler_timeout=60`
- `python -m pytest tests/cli/test_commands.py --cov=nanobot --cov-append --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered -q`
- `ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py scripts/check_import_boundaries.py`
- `basedpyright` — 0 errors or warnings.
- `python -B -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` — 10 rules, 160 files passed.
- `uv pip check` and diff whitespace checks passed.

Additional public SDK HTTP/SSE smoke verification used `Nanobot.from_config`, `stream`, and `run` with the actual configured provider and a local scripted model endpoint. A real file-tool run completed in two requests; empty-response recovery completed in three requests with no tools in the final wire payload. Both scenarios verified output, usage, and nonempty preset/generation settings. All owned resources were cleaned up; this was protocol verification, not a paid/live-model evaluation.

prs.title: fix(webui): preserve list semantics around links
prs.body:
## Why

Fix [NAN-269](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-269): a normal Markdown list item containing a web link could be flattened into a single compact preview. The replacement consumed nested items, inline formatting, additional link destinations, ordered markers, and task status; desktop truncation then hid part of the resulting label.

## What changed

- Classify compact previews at the Markdown AST boundary, where the parent list type and the entire item structure are available. Only a non-task unordered item consisting of one plain-text title, one line break, and one HTTP(S) URL-only link is eligible. Custom link labels, tooltips, prose, additional blocks, and additional links stay ordinary Markdown.
- Pass validated preview metadata to the list renderer instead of recursively flattening React descendants. Keep the existing compact row, title cleanup, and favicon fallback unchanged.
- Add real-component regressions for the complete reported message, distinct link targets, nested/ordered/task lists, structural boundaries, unsafe protocols, all static/streaming/preserved-layout combinations, streaming completion, and a preview gaining more streamed content.

## Scope

Only the Markdown renderer and its tests change. No dependency, styling, transport, gateway, authentication, production configuration, or unrelated PR changes. Compact previews still work without a Sources heading, including URL-only angle autolinks and hard line breaks/CRLF. Formatted titles and ambiguous structures deliberately retain their original Markdown semantics.

## Blast Radius

This affects compact-preview eligibility in shared WebUI Markdown rendering. The important regression risks are suppressing legitimate previews or replacing content that carries additional semantics; both positive preview tests and negative structural cases exercise the actual parser and renderer.

## Current snapshot and verification

Rebased onto latest fetched `main` **`756f6a6fe5012fb59e690850d2a41517e116c786`** at the user's request. Current head: **`7cff9781b461cc650ba480e774ed0697f7cee7ac`**, one task commit above that main, published with an explicit `--force-with-lease` for the previous head. One renderer conflict was resolved by keeping main's `!documentPath` boundary: document previews never opt into chat compact previews or load favicons. A document-mode regression was added; no other PR or daily gateway configuration was changed.

- Fresh focused run: `bun run test src/tests/markdown-text-renderer.test.tsx src/tests/file-preview-panel.test.tsx src/tests/preview-pane.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1` — **3 files / 138 passed**, including **121 renderer tests**.
- Fresh full `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1` — **160 files / 2,812 tests passed**, exit 0, on this exact head.
- ESLint, production build/TypeScript, frontend import boundaries, import-checker tests (**37 pass / 1 Windows-only skip**), Python import boundaries, and `git diff --check` — passed. Existing large-chunk and test-environment warnings remain in raw logs.
- Real Chromium on this head's production bundle and an authenticated isolated Gateway: desktop **1440×1050**, narrow **390×1050**, original/controls, refresh/replay, distinct targets, nested/ordered/task lists, compact rows, and intentionally induced favicon-to-globe fallback — passed. Real composer SSE was observed in flight, completed, and replayed after reload, preserving **2 top-level + 3 nested items**, **4 code tokens**, and the bold **#6269** PR label only.
- The new main's real Markdown file-preview path also passed: title-plus-URL stays ordinary, external embeds remain links, fragments do not navigate to chat, **zero external HTTP requests** were observed, and Source/Preview toggles work. No browser runtime exceptions or unexpected console errors; auth 401 and induced icon 404s are expected.
- The original regression-first 18 failures and old-head results remain historical evidence, not fresh executions. Local Python unit tests were not run because the available runtime venv lacks test dependencies; the current backend's provider/stream path was exercised through the real Gateway. CI skips are not counted as test passes.
- [GitHub CI for the current head](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39049950177): **success**. Detect changes, WebUI and Docker passed; Python/Windows/TUI jobs were skipped by changed-path scope, not counted as test passes.

**Visual report and replacement instance:** [NAN-269 verification and isolated acceptance](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/document/nan-269-pr-6276-验证与隔离验收-bbd29886fd11) (Linear workspace access required). The latest section identifies this head; older sections/screenshots are explicitly historical. A new screenshot shows this head's chat and document preview together. Current raw screenshots/results, per-command receipts, range-diff, and reproducible scripts are retained outside tracked source at `/home/cyr/.nanobot/workspace/tmp/nan-269-rebase-20261018/`.

The old acceptance instance was stopped and its data retained. A replacement, persistent, authenticated interactive instance is running at **`http://127.0.0.1:18769/`** from this exact head. It has independent OS HOME/nanobot home/configuration/workspace/sessions and uses a loopback deterministic SSE fixture model, with no production keys or sessions. Original repro, boundary controls, real streaming, and a guarded Markdown file-preview fixture are available. The newly generated password is read locally from the private path in the report; never publish its contents. The report includes safe SSH tunneling and scoped status/stop instructions.

The PR is **not merged**. Human visual acceptance remains pending. The replacement instance remains running after handoff.

prs.title: fix(deepseek): align model capabilities with the official API
prs.body:
## Why

DeepSeek serves both legacy Flash names through the current multimodal `deepseek-flash`, but nanobot silently removes images for `deepseek-v4-flash`. Model discovery also discards official capability metadata and suggests generic reasoning levels. Keep immutable compatibility facts in the existing provider model registry and normalize advisory discovery metadata at the settings boundary.

## What changed

- Resolve Flash aliases through shared model metadata and preserve image input on Chat Completions and Responses; Pro remains text-only. Keep wire model IDs and existing official/proxy API routing unchanged.
- Validate catalog output limits, modalities and supported/default thinking levels, with known-model fallback. Preserve the explicit `none` control even when the live catalog lists only enabled thinking levels; distinguish it from provider-default and keep custom strings usable.
- Extend the settings DTO with optional fields, reuse the existing picker without frontend provider branches, and document naming, budgets and deferred search support.

## Scope

Tracks [NAN-271](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-271). This PR was initially published as **Draft** at `b0eb7608517`; bounded real-key verification subsequently passed on `2ecebac8a96fd96ea94c47898e9984a2baac5844` before requesting Ready for review.

Does not enable standalone DeepSeek Search/Fetch, Pro hosted search, Anthropic Messages or Files; does not migrate cross-provider reasoning configuration. Does not rewrite users' model IDs or change existing preset budgets, API routing, credentials or services. Catalog output limits remain advisory; existing new-preset context initialization is unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

Runtime image policy uses the immutable provider record, not online discovery or a new network/cache service. Valid online metadata takes precedence over static fallback, with a known explicit off control separate from enabled thinking strengths. Raw `api_capabilities` is not forwarded: its Messages behavior has no adapter consumer here.

The suspected Responses reasoning-history incompatibility did not reproduce: a real Chat-history reconstruction containing `output_text` reasoning parts returned HTTP 200 and the expected synthetic token. The shared OpenAI converter therefore remains unchanged; this single successful case is not a guarantee about every future endpoint or payload.

## Blast Radius

DeepSeek message sanitization and additive model catalog fields. Unknown/custom models retain manual values and do not inherit DeepSeek model facts. The existing picker tolerates hosts without the new fields; older clients can ignore the optional additions. Other providers' request conversion and third-party naming/routing are unchanged.

## Verification

- Documentation-only follow-up `6736f5f0e` reorganizes `docs/providers.md`: DeepSeek has its own section, Muse guidance is under OpenCode, and general preset guidance is shared. All 21 JSON examples and 22 local links/anchors passed checks; documented API defaults were checked against the provider registry. Runtime/frontend/test sources are unchanged from `2ecebac8a96f`, so existing code verification is carried forward without new live API calls.
- Relevant provider/settings suite: **1624 passed** (`PYTHONPATH=tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/providers tests/webui/test_settings_routes.py tests/webui/test_settings_models.py tests/webui/test_settings_api.py -q --disable-warnings`). Legacy-alias regression demonstrated before the fix; updated the existing text-only image test to use nonvisual Pro instead of the now-visual Flash alias.
- Model-settings frontend suite: **75 passed** (`PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:$PATH /home/cyr/.bun/bin/bun run test src/tests/settings-models.test.tsx --reporter verbose`, in `webui/`).
- Full repository Ruff and BasedPyright: passed, 0 type errors/warnings. Python import boundaries: passed. `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports`: passed (37 tests, one Windows-only case skipped on Linux). `bun run lint` and `bun run build`: passed; build retains the bundle-size warning.
- Isolated gateway + Chromium, synthetic local catalog: `max`, `none`, Default and a custom effort each saved and survived reload; no browser runtime/console errors. Catalog fields reached the existing picker. Owned gateway, fixture server, browser and ports were cleaned up. This browser check is not a real model call.
- **Real DeepSeek official API**, locally configured credential loaded only in-process: **14/14 HTTP 200 requests and 26 checks passed on code head `2ecebac8a96fd96ea94c47898e9984a2baac5844`**, plus one earlier successful `/models` discovery request (15 total, within a 16-request budget). The initial discovery exposed that live `supported_levels` omits `none`; a failing regression and the final normalization correction cover that observation.
  - Authenticated `/v1/models`: real max output, modalities, enabled levels/default retained; explicit off control preserved.
  - Chat Completions and Responses basic calls with `none`: expected marker returned, no thinking content.
  - Canonical Flash and both legacy aliases × both APIs: in-memory blue PNG retained on the wire and correctly identified (6 calls).
  - Both APIs: low-effort streaming function call, reasoning deltas, synthetic tool result and final answer; Responses continued from raw provider state (4 calls).
  - Chat-history reasoning reconstructed into Responses without saved Responses state: expected token returned.
- Only synthetic prompts/image/tool results were sent; no user chats/files. Each model call capped at 1024 output tokens, SDK retries disabled. Reported aggregate usage: 3054 input / 137 output tokens, including 765 cache-read input tokens; billing was not queried. No keys, headers or raw configuration were committed or published.

Local evidence (not committed) is retained under `.nanobot-workflows/runs/deepseek-nan271-20261018/` in the agent workspace, including exact-head live JSON, first discovery, red/green logs and browser evidence. Python checks were rerun after the final normalization correction; unchanged frontend/build/browser evidence is carried forward because its source and DTO contract are unchanged. Remote CI on the current head is still queued/in progress, not reported as passed. Live coverage is Linux/Python 3.12 with OpenAI SDK 3.33.0 against official Flash; Pro image policy and proxy routing have offline regression coverage, not live third-party/proxy validation.

prs.title: perf(webui): reuse versioned history navigation snapshots
prs.body:
## Why

Unchanged WebUI history and message-navigation requests introduced in #6299 still rebuild display data before returning 304. Repeated directory reads also redo canonical recovery across the conversation. Validate the committed inputs before construction and reuse the current bounded projection.

Fixes [NAN-281](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-281). NAN-273's consumed-follow-up fix remains intact.

## What changed

- Read SQLite's existing session generation/revision without decoding history or metadata, and bind page/directory validators to that version plus the transcript artifacts.
- Return valid 304s before replay; share the existing 8-entry navigation LRU across directory reads and missing-user recovery. Do not cache or issue a stable validator when inputs change during construction.
- Build signature-position indexes once on cache misses instead of repeatedly scanning canonical suffixes, preserving unique-in-suffix matching and recovered input identity/time.

## Scope

Backend history/navigation reads and focused regression tests only: six files, no frontend protocol, schema, dependency, or configuration changes. No changes to follow-up acknowledgment transactions or production data.

## Tradeoffs

Any committed session revision conservatively invalidates the projection, including metadata-only updates. Snapshots retain summaries and recovered users, not full canonical answers. First recovery may still read canonical history; a full directory 200 still serializes all summaries.

## Blast Radius

WebUI history pages and message navigation, particularly normal missing-user backfill. Regressions cover canonical-only corrections with unchanged `updated_at`, concurrent updates, eviction, ambiguity/alignment, and session replacement; existing rotation, pagination, and distinct-input tests remain in the exercised suites.

## Verification

Compared exact current main `103840171b47a811b0119462bb5c569fe521ca0a` with `7a0da08a39b4a35c5e1c1bd60aed28dbe22108ac`. Five alternating real-Gateway pairs on the same shared Windows host, identical synthetic fixtures/configuration, actual frontend `since + If-None-Match` protocol. Wall values are medians of five per-run medians; CPU is the median of real interpreter-process batch CPU/request averages.

| Directory conditional request | Before → after wall | Before → after CPU/request |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Normal 10,000 turns | 63.096 → 5.785 ms | 57.292 → 4.557 ms |
| 2,000 turns, only the last user transcript missing | 198.606 → 5.798 ms | 194.010 → 3.906 ms |

All 2,940 measured/initial responses passed status/content checks; all fixture hashes matched. Independent counters confirm no replay, view construction, canonical-history read or recovery matching on valid 304s. Ten full page/directory responses match across snapshots after excluding opaque revisions/runtime workspace scope. [Full methods, ranges, results, attribution and limitations](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/document/nan-281webui-历史缓存修复与性能对照-49bf9284d52a).

- `python -B -m pytest tests/webui/test_prompt_index.py tests/utils/test_webui_transcript.py tests/session/test_sqlite_storage.py -q`: **100 passed**. The new cache-hit regression first failed in both normal/backfill cases on unfixed code.
- `python -B -m pytest tests/session tests/webui tests/utils/test_webui_transcript.py nanobot/channels/websocket/tests -q`: **1514 passed, 21 skipped, 2 failed**. Both Windows remote-discovery failures reproduce on the exact base export; they remain failures.
- Six related frontend Vitest suites: **202 passed**; `bun run build`: **passed**. Full-project TypeScript typechecking was not run.
- Full Ruff and Python import-boundary checks: **passed**. Explicit-interpreter BasedPyright on the four implementation files: **0 errors**. Full-project BasedPyright: **2 errors** in unchanged Windows `setproctitle` imports, identically reproduced on the exact base; not a pass.
- Private Chromium + isolated Gateway/built WebUI: recovered input identity/time, authenticated 304s, directory search/cross-page loading, canonical-only timestamp invalidation and one-prompt delta, refresh, and 390px layout passed; no console/page errors. No real-model execution or browser CPU/paint benchmark.
- All task-owned Gateways were removed and ports released; private Chromium closed. No production restart or data cleanup.

prs.title: feat(webui): render Mermaid diagrams with Pele
prs.body: ## Why Mermaid fences currently remain code in the WebUI. Render them locally with Pele as the only diagram engine, while keeping the original source available and untrusted diagram computation outside the UI thread. Refs [NAN-146](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-146). ## What changed - Dispatch code fences once from Markdown's `pre` renderer. Actual message completion enables lazy diagram rendering independently of preserved streaming layout; generating replies keep readable, copyable source. - Render with Pele 1.6.0 in terminable module Workers, then display bounded, validated SVG documents through ``. Add source/diagram switching, copying, an enlarged keyboard/zoom/pan/pinch viewer, local errors and cancellation on source/conversation/visibility changes. - Extract the existing image viewport without changing gallery navigation, add all ten locales and a foundation-gallery example, and upgrade Streamdown to 2.6.0 to remove its native mermaid.js dependency tree. Both package-manager locks and bundled license notices are updated. ## Scope Frontend-only rendering and viewing. No gateway protocol, stored message format, model prompting, image-delivery feature, native Mermaid fallback, or historical PR restoration. Read-only Markdown document link/resource restrictions remain in place. ## Tradeoffs Inert image documents and killable Workers are preferred over Pele's DOM mount API or inline SVG. Diagram links and external images are disabled; diagram labels are not selectable in the image, but source remains selectable and copyable. Syntax/layout follow Pele rather than full mermaid.js compatibility. Theme recoloring preserves the camera; layout changes are deferred while the enlarged reader is open. Two rendering slots, four admitted waiting jobs, per-diagram limits and shared byte/pixel budgets bound resources. Shared-capacity pressure waits for released assets instead of permanently rejecting valid source. Normal admission remains at 7 MiB / 24 million pixels within 8 MiB / 32 million pixel totals, leaving one maximal replacement inside those totals. Template storage, old images and decoding replacements are all counted. Each image reserves its fixed encoded SVG bytes plus a bounded 4 KiB palette allowance, capped at the existing 1 MiB output limit, rather than a flat 1 MiB per image; the reservation stays constant across themes so recoloring can progress while old images remain visible. Unsupported Worker/OffscreenCanvas capabilities retain source with an explicit error. The application keeps its direct remend 1.3.0 repair behavior; Streamdown's own patch dependency resolves separately to 1.3.1, with `parseIncompleteMarkdown={false}` still set. ## Blast Radius Markdown code-block dispatch and Streamdown are shared by messages and file previews. The neutral image viewport also serves the existing photo lightbox. Focused coverage protects ordinary Markdown/math/code/path behavior, same-source streaming completion, photo navigation, output policy, worker deadlines, stale results and budget recovery. ## Verification Latest quota follow-up source snapshot: `51c7db8fb613a96a2f2d0427530e114bcf014047`. Commands run from `webui`: | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | `bun run lint` | PASS | | `bun run test -- --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1` | PASS — 2,898 tests / 166 files | | `bun run build` | PASS — production typecheck and production asset build; lazy-entry guard passed | | `bun run check:imports` | PASS | | `bun run test:imports` | PASS — 42 tests | | `bun run test:browser` | PASS — 18 Chromium cases, including eight diagram cases | | `bun x tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` | FAIL — 471 diagnostics, byte-for-byte identical to an archived `103840171b47a811b0119462bb5c569fe521ca0a` checkout installed from its original lockfile | The initial default-parallel `bun run test` failed (2,884 passed / 10 failed). Missing coverage for the newly extracted gallery component was added; the final complete two-worker run above passes without extending test timeouts. The full-project typecheck remains a failure, not replaced by the production build. Real browser checks cover flowchart/sequence/state, Chinese subgraphs and long labels, emoji, measured emphasis, light/dark palettes, 390px layout, source/copy/viewer controls, focus restoration, source and conversation changes, oversized/malicious input without external fetches, and a genuinely blocked Worker timing out while siblings complete. A separate isolated gateway served the production build and deterministic saved transcripts: Chinese diagrams, zoom/drag/reset/Esc, source switching, theme updates, refresh replay, session-local errors and lazy Settings entry were checked. Its dummy provider does not exercise real-model generation. The earlier broad production-gateway check preceded quota follow-ups. A new focused production-build/gateway run on the current quota code verified twelve Chinese-labeled small diagrams simultaneously inside the viewport (30,296 encoded Blob bytes in light mode), light/dark/light updates without rerunning Pele, source/diagram switching and zero live diagram Blobs or Workers after changing sessions. The owned verification gateways and browsers were cleaned up. Verification was on Windows Chromium with mobile-width emulation; physical mobile devices and Firefox/Safari were not exercised. The browser specs capture reproducible screenshots; local production/browser evidence is retained with the task record. No merge or Linear completion is included. ## HoverHint follow-up Snapshot: `e72452fac7139e7eeec7b5fd6bef2662e3f8130c`. The Mermaid toolbar's Copy source and Enlarge diagram actions now use the shared `HoverHint` for localized hover/focus labels, preserving clipboard, keyboard and viewer behavior. Focused checks on this exact source: 8 diagram browser tests and 11 Mermaid/lightbox unit tests passed; browser-config typechecking, touched-file ESLint and production build passed. Dedicated Chromium checks confirmed both hints in light/dark themes and in the actual production-build chat instance. The two requested showcase instances remain available for user feedback. prs.title: fix(webui): isolate transcript replay from live observers
prs.body:
## Why

Switching away from a running topic and returning could hide earlier tool calls while later calls continued to appear. `onChat` mixed live multicast observation with destructive single-consumer replay: a task observer could consume the transcript's pending events, and any remaining observer prevented new transcript events from being buffered.

## What changed

- Make `onChat` live-only and add exclusive `onTranscript` delivery for the stream hook: ordered pending replay once, followed by live events.
- Buffer whenever the transcript owner is absent, independently of passive observers; clear the owner alongside existing temporary-chat disposal.
- Add real-client/task-provider/stream-hook regressions for both subscription orders and observer-only intervals; migrate existing replay/fencing assertions and document the ownership contract.

## Scope

Fixes connected topic switches for events already received and retained in the existing queue. Preserves run-ledger fencing, task HTTP hydration, attach/reconnect behavior, regular 2,000-frame retention and temporary-chat lifecycle. No gateway/wire, active HTTP merge policy, dependency or production-data changes. True offline gaps, evicted events and general snapshot/live convergence remain outside this PR.

Issue: [NAN-283](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-283). [Design and staged/global comparison](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/document/nan-283-方案重放所有权修复与全局同步重构取舍-a55863babf47), including the attached real-browser before/after screenshot.

## Tradeoffs

This establishes the missing ownership boundary now without a protocol migration. A global per-session canonical-base/live-overlay owner is the stronger long-term design, but needs gateway snapshot watermarks, stable open-stream identity, pagination coverage and client/host capability handling. A frontend store alone cannot establish that cut. The staged approach leaves those gaps and some later hook/Shell migration work; its observer/delivery boundary can remain when the synchronization owner replaces the hook.

## Blast Radius

Per-chat client delivery and the single stream projection subscriber; task/model listeners retain live observation. The main regression risk is losing or duplicating replay during unmount/resubscribe. Registration-identity cleanup and real-client tests cover ordered once-only delivery, passive listeners, terminal pruning and temporary cleanup.

## Verification

Verified source: `e1015a6717ad47bd2b9422e65d488776526e583d`, based on `5d886fbb20b1e13187c583e884f1cba7e70c7fa9`.

- New integration regression on baseline: **2 fail / 1 pass control**; fixed suite passes.
- `bun run test --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2`: **2,862 passed**, 164 files. The initial default-worker run alongside heavy checks failed 5 loading/role waits; the complete bounded-worker rerun passed without source or timeout changes.
- `bun run test:browser`: **86 passed**, including browser TypeScript compilation.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports` (**38 passed**) and `bun run build`: passed; build reports the existing chunk-size warning.
- Full-project `tsc --noEmit`: **fails**, with **473 diagnostics on both baseline and fixed source**, identical ignoring positions. Production/browser TypeScript checks above pass.
- Isolated real gateway + production WebUI + Chromium + real `read_file`, using a gated loopback SSE provider with dummy credentials: baseline ordinary return shows **4/6** tools; fixed ordinary and temporary returns show **6/6** ordered tools, checkpoint text and actual results **before reload**, then clear Stop normally. Multiple ordinary runs agree. Restoration starts no extra tool-enabled Agent sequence. No page JS errors; initial/new-session history HTTP 404 console entries are retained in the evidence.
- Task-owned fixture/browser servers cleaned up; no shared runtime or production instance restarted. Full source/bundle hashes and raw logs/tapes are retained with the linked issue's evidence report.

prs.title: fix(agent): project safe execution activity across channels
prs.body:
## Why

Native `exec_session` observer waits were presented as completed user operations, exposing internal handles and inflating activity counts even while the command was still running. Project owner-observed execution facts at the shared public progress boundary so WebUI and other channels receive meaningful command status instead of internal control calls.

Refs [NAN-262](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-262).

## What changed

- Add opt-in execution contracts and typed return-point facts to native shell tools. Preserve model-facing results and execution ownership; successful waits, input management and inventory calls remain silent, while real results and control failures remain visible.
- Derive public text and structured activity together, preserving mixed-tool order and existing progress/hint settings. Apply the same read-only projection before history detail, summary and count calculation.
- Render localized execution activity in WebUI. Keep core protocol 1 with optional `webui.execution-activity.v2`, safe legacy text fallback and a separate optional `execution_detail` field.
- Follow-up `ffb5f36fc` / `4f67ca784`: reuse public batching, remove duplicate history filtering, lazily stop soft-page counting at its budget, and reuse wire events only for the requested detail group. These changes remove **15 net production lines** versus the initial PR; the new regression checks protect complete delivery with bounded projection work. Synchronize five existing test-double/expectation modules with the new internal registry contract, fixing the initial Python CI failures without production fallbacks or timeout increases.

- Channel follow-up `baa78d967`: discriminate public execution items before interpreting ordinary tool fields. Linear sends native thoughts (running states ephemeral, outcomes persistent); opt-in Weixin sends native text items using the shared command-status formatter. Preserve ordinary tool actions, Linear redaction/retry identities, and Weixin causal order, shared run ID, progress cap and final-reply quota reservation. Replace the duplicated Telegram real-shell scenario with a focused send-adapter/HTML-escaping/topic test; real execution remains covered once at the shared boundary.

## Scope

Covers native command launch/control activity, shared channel delivery, WebSocket live events and WebUI history/replay. Does not rewrite saved conversations, filter assistant prose, copy stdout into progress, or introduce background command monitoring. No dependencies or configuration defaults change.

## Tradeoffs

Terminal status is reported when an existing tool return observes it; an unobserved background command does not gain an automatic completion push. Legacy records without typed terminal facts cannot recover precise historical exit results. Historical compatibility adds a public projection pass; measurements below do not establish a universal zero-regression guarantee.

## Blast Radius

Touches tool-result reporting, progress hooks, Linear/Weixin native progress adapters, Telegram delivery tests, WebSocket activity classification and WebUI transcript projection. Ordinary and third-party tools retain their default presentation, including tools with the same names that have not opted in. Mixed records retain causal order and stable replay identities. Detail-event retention is request-local and restricted to the requested group; ordinary history responses do not retain those payloads.

## Verification

Latest published source: `baa78d9673d28cf707ad4db2015ac06b579b892c`, direct parent `4f67ca7842a36f61ea7ac104caf98dcd637b104a`. This follow-up changes only two channel adapters and three channel test modules; shared execution/projection, WebUI/history, dependencies and defaults are unchanged.

Fresh channel-follow-up verification:

- Regression-first: 13 expected failures against the pre-fix adapters, with the narrowed Telegram test already passing. Final related matrix: **561 passed**, exit 0, covering the three channel packages, real shared shell/progress, runner integration, channel manager and WebSocket outbound delivery. Adapter cases include started-vs-end, completion, exit 7 with incomplete output, timeout, stop and control failure; Weixin mixed progress retains the cap, run ID and final reply.
- Full Ruff, Python import boundaries (10 rules / 167 files) and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh full backend BasedPyright remains **FAIL: 1025 errors**, normalized added/removed 0/0 against the recorded local diagnostic baseline.
- Latest-head [CI run 39229504997](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39229504997): **in progress** after a bounded 300-second observation. Linux 3.11, Linux 3.14 + coverage (including strict BasedPyright), Docker and Windows process compatibility passed; WebUI and Windows full-suite jobs were still running at readback. No background watcher is retained.

Inherited performance/shared/UI evidence below retains its original snapshot identity. Performance-follow-up source: `4f67ca7842a36f61ea7ac104caf98dcd637b104a`. Benchmark source is its clean automatic integration with main `af68da3280c87316f00240de62b1f27056892ab1`, tree `80521d843f0427ab9b2fc1e144c8547f966812bb`; exported Python files were compared with that exact tree. Main already includes PR #6301, so its navigation-cache improvement is not attributed here.

- Previous-head focused Python integration/regression matrix: **559 passed, 1 skipped**, exit 0. The skip is unavailable Windows symlink creation. Includes all affected runner/hook fixture modules, real shell waits/results, complete/deferred history, counts, WebSocket delivery and the Telegram send adapter.
- Previous-head separate serial CLI matrix: **163 passed, 1 skipped**, exit 0; the skip is unavailable Windows `termios`. Full Ruff, Python import boundaries (10 rules / 167 files) and `git diff --check` passed.
- Previous-head [CI run 39222769201](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39222769201) **passed**: Python minimum 3.11, latest 3.14 + coverage including strict BasedPyright and serial CLI, Windows 3.14, Windows process compatibility, WebUI tests/browser regressions/build, and Docker.
- Five interleaved benchmark rounds per snapshot, 80 synchronous handler requests per round/workload plus real authenticated loopback HTTP. Ordinary response payloads were semantically identical across snapshots; legacy-control removal was checked separately. In a 300-call dense turn, stored projection calls fell **901 → 339 per page** with complete deferred-detail delivery. Detail serialization is now once per event; the regression test checks actual delivery as well as work counts.
- Real native shell: five rounds of 100 zero-duration observations and two actual one-second waits, then successful completion. No measured observer slowdown; running observations emitted no public wait activity. This evidence uses the unchanged native execution/progress files from the final source.
- HTTP RTT varied substantially even on unchanged prompt/304 paths. Final dense-page CPU medians were main 22.85 ms / initial PR 28.71 ms / follow-up 25.59 ms, with overlapping run ranges; the remaining main-versus-head difference is recorded rather than presented as zero regression. Full latency, output/error counts, CPU ranges and separate memory/profile evidence are recorded in the NAN-262 implementation document.

Unchanged frontend evidence inherited from initial head `3a3ec064b`: 262 focused Vitest tests across eight files, frontend import checks/self-tests, lint and production build passed; that head's WebUI CI also passed. The later changes are Python-only. Initial isolated gateway/browser acceptance covered completion, exit 7, stop, actual eight-second timeout, stale-handle failure, two real observer waits per scenario, live/history agreement, Working/Stop, refresh/reconnect and desktop/narrow layouts. Frozen protocol-1 client parsing accepted actual current-host history for all five scenarios; deferred-field compatibility used an explicit fixture, not an old graphical browser.

The initial local full-project checks failed with unchanged baseline diagnostics: backend 1025/1025 (the local environment lacks channel dependencies) and frontend 471/471, normalized added/removed 0/0. Initial-head strict backend CI passed with installed channel dependencies, while its Python tests failed on the 18 now-repaired contract/fixture cases. Final-head CI results are recorded separately above; these earlier local failures are not relabeled as passes.

Limits: no real-model performance or multi-user/p99 guarantee is claimed. The isolated gateway uses a deterministic local provider. Native real-shell execution is checked at the shared owner/progress boundary. Telegram, Linear and Weixin exercise their real send adapters against fake external API boundaries; real external delivery remains unverified. Collector/incomplete-output categories have typed test coverage rather than live fault injection. User visual feedback remains pending. The original preview was stopped under the recorded request to shut down all test instances; this follow-up did not restart it.

prs.title: fix(session): preserve checkpoints across metadata updates
prs.body:
## Summary

Allocating a session handle during an in-flight turn rewrites the main JSONL metadata. Its newer file timestamp then makes the runtime-checkpoint overlay look obsolete, so restarting loses completed tool results and the checkpoint's provider state.

Preserve the transcript's timestamp on the temporary metadata-only replacement, after flushing its contents and before fsync/atomic rename. Full session saves still advance the timestamp and supersede older checkpoints. This keeps metadata updates streaming and avoids loading or rewriting the session through its runtime cache.

## Validation

- Two regressions fail on unmodified `835cac0`: handle allocation followed by a real `RecoveryCoordinator.scan()` loses a completed result, and a metadata update loses checkpoint/provider state on a long session.
- Python 3.13.14 / Windows: `pytest tests/session -q` — 113 passed, 2 skipped.
- Scoped Ruff and BasedPyright for the session store pass; `git diff --check` passes.
- Uses temporary session files and restarted managers; no model calls. The full repository suite and Linux were not run locally.

Found through source inspection. This preserves an existing checkpoint across metadata updates; it is separate from #5748's additional tool-batch checkpoint boundaries.

prs.title: feat(tools): add DeepSeek Search as a web_search provider
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds DeepSeek as a new `web_search` provider backed by the standalone DeepSeek Search API (`POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search`).

This is a search-only backend, independent of the selected chat model. Its key is configured through `tools.web.search.apiKey`, independently of the model-provider key. Explicit `${VAR_NAME}` references use the existing configuration resolver; no environment key is read implicitly. It does not inject provider-hosted search into chat completion requests. It follows the provider layout established by AnySearch (#5607) and Bocha (#4182).

## Motivation

DeepSeek's Search API is a first-party, AI-oriented search endpoint with model-readable summaries (`summary`), relevance/authority scores, and support for search operators (`site:`, `lang:`, `after:`, `before:`, quoted phrases). Users already holding a DeepSeek key can now use it for `web_search` without adding another vendor.

Because the API bills per successful request (¥5 / 1,000 requests) and returns summaries written for models to read, it is a good fit for agent workflows; requests that fail or return no results are not billed.

## Changes

- `nanobot/agent/tools/web.py`
  - Add `_DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_API_URL`, `_DEEPSEEK_MAX_QUERY_CHARS` (128), `_DEEPSEEK_MAX_RESULTS` (50), `_DEEPSEEK_MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS` (500), `_DEEPSEEK_ERROR_DETAIL_MAX_CHARS`, and `_DEEPSEEK_RETRY_DELAY_S`.
  - Register `{"name": "deepseek", "label": "DeepSeek", "credential": "api_key"}` in `SEARCH_PROVIDER_OPTIONS`, which drives both the CLI wizard and the WebUI settings list.
  - Dispatch in `execute()` and read `tools.web.search.apiKey` without an automatic environment-key fallback. Missing credentials return an actionable error without switching to DuckDuckGo.
  - Add `_search_deepseek()` with local query validation, plus `_deepseek_is_retryable()`, `_deepseek_text()`, and `_deepseek_error_detail()`.
- `tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`
  - Add `deepseek` to the keyed-provider concurrency parametrization.
  - Cover provider registration, credential resolution, query boundaries, result formatting, retries, and error handling.
- `tests/webui/test_settings_api.py`
  - Cover configured credentials, rejection of environment-only setups, and preservation of explicit environment references across settings updates.
- `docs/configuration.md`
  - Add a short DeepSeek section with a config example, the query limit, pricing, QPS, and an official API documentation link.
  - Add `deepseek` to the `tools.web.search` provider table.
- `webui/src/tests/provider-brand.test.ts`
  - Assert the existing bundled DeepSeek brand asset is reused for the search provider.
- Search settings use the existing required-key validation and controls, without DeepSeek-specific credential metadata or locale strings.

### Implementation notes

- **Query validation** trims surrounding whitespace, preserves valid Unicode queries and search operators, and rejects blank or over-128-character queries locally. It does not silently truncate or rewrite the search request.
- **`count`** is clamped to the API's 1–50 window inside the provider. The tool-level `execute()` path caps at 10 for every provider (and the tool schema advertises the same bound), so the wider API range only matters if the tool-level limit is raised later.
- **Results** use `summary`, falling back to `snippet`; each result's text is capped at 500 characters before `date` is prefixed. The cap was added after testing the live API: real `summary` values reach ~4,500 characters (the docs say 600–800), and ten uncapped results cost ~35,700 characters (~10k tokens) per call. With the cap the same call returns ~6,400 characters (~1.8k tokens). `need_content` is always `false` so page bodies never enter the model's context.
- **Errors**: 401 and 402 get actionable messages (402 points at top-up); 408/429/5xx are retried once after 1.0 s, matching the Brave provider; other 4xx are not retried and surface `error.message`, tag-stripped because the upstream body is untrusted. Timeouts and transport failures return a distinct message; unexpected transport errors report the exception type only, with the detail logged only when tool log content is allowed.
- **Secret hygiene**: the key only appears in the `Authorization` header. It is never logged, and error text is built from the status code and the response's `error.message` only.

## Current configured-key follow-up (`fda5fdf4c`)

- Read only `tools.web.search.apiKey`; remove the automatic `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` fallback, its dedicated resolver, Settings exception/metadata, frontend state, and the two environment-key strings in all 10 locales. Generic explicit `${VAR_NAME}` configuration references remain supported. Other providers are unchanged.
- Compress the configuration documentation to the example and two short paragraphs.
- Fresh Python regression command: `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py tests/webui/test_settings_api.py tests/config/test_env_interpolation.py tests/agent/test_runtime_refresh.py tests/tools/test_search_tools.py tests/tools/test_tool_loader.py -q` — **370 passed**. Fresh frontend command: `bun run test -- src/tests/settings-capabilities.test.tsx src/tests/i18n.test.tsx` — **43 passed / 2 files**.
- Fresh changed-file Ruff, Python import boundaries (10 rules / 160 files), three changed production modules' basedpyright, WebUI lint/import boundaries (365 files), production build, and `git diff --check` — **passed** on the exact committed source snapshot. Full-project typechecks were not rerun; earlier Windows failures remain recorded below.
- No browser, model, or paid Search run was made for this credential-source change. Earlier environment-only UI evidence below belongs to the earlier implementations. No retained runtime or production instance was restarted. Final-head CI is checked separately from these local results.

## Earlier independent-key follow-up (`387f051b2`)

- Revert the provider-key sharing follow-up (`a28fbc8a0`) and its dependent test-fixture change (`04f13d44e`) after maintainer feedback. The convenience did not justify adding DeepSeek-specific state and configuration wiring through the generic tools and agent paths. No replacement credential-sharing abstraction was added.
- Restore independent Search credentials: `tools.web.search.apiKey` first, then `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. `providers.deepseek.apiKey` is not read for Search. The Git tree at `387f051b2` is identical to pre-sharing `49f84fbd6`; earlier query validation, explicit missing-key errors, environment support, and billing-UI cleanup are preserved.
- Fresh regression command: `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py tests/webui/test_settings_api.py tests/agent/test_loop_tool_context.py tests/tools/test_tool_loader.py tests/agent/test_runtime_refresh.py tests/agent/test_subagent.py tests/agent/tools/test_subagent_tools.py tests/tools/test_search_tools.py tests/tools/test_private_tool_logging.py -q` — **423 passed**. Fresh frontend regression command: `bun run test -- src/tests/settings-capabilities.test.tsx src/tests/provider-brand.test.ts src/tests/i18n.test.tsx` — **65 passed / 3 files**.
- Fresh changed-file Ruff, Python import boundaries (10 rules / 160 files), WebUI lint/import boundaries (365 files), production build, five touched production modules' basedpyright, and `git diff --check` — **passed**. Full Python typecheck — **failed with the same 2 errors** in unchanged `nanobot/cli/process_identity.py:17`. Full frontend typecheck — **failed with 469 diagnostics**, matching the earlier identical source snapshot. Build success is not a full-project typecheck PASS.
- No new browser, model, or paid Search run was made for this exact rollback. Earlier browser evidence below retains its original snapshot identity and applies to the restored tree. No retained runtime or production instance was restarted. Final-head CI is reported separately from these local checks.

## Earlier UI consistency follow-up (`49f84fbd6`)

- Remove the DeepSeek-only billing notice and its wrapper, all 10 locale entries, and the corresponding test expectation. The provider row now uses the shared layout; environment-backed credentials and save behavior are unchanged.
- Fresh `bun run test -- src/tests/settings-capabilities.test.tsx src/tests/provider-brand.test.ts src/tests/i18n.test.tsx` — **65 passed / 3 files**. Fresh `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, and `git diff --check` — **passed**.
- Full frontend typecheck — **still fails with 469 diagnostics**. A same-dependency CompilerHost comparison against `34402dc0c` found the same 469 diagnostics and no additions.
- Read-only checks against the rebuilt isolated WebUI in English (1440px) and Chinese (390px), dark mode: the special notice is gone, the environment-key source remains visible, and neither view has horizontal overflow. No additional model or Search requests were needed for this UI-only change.
- Earlier backend and Agent/Search evidence below is carried forward because this follow-up changes only the UI notice, locale entries, and one test expectation. It was not rerun for this commit.

## Earlier follow-up verification (`34402dc0c`)

- Fresh backend regression run: `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py tests/webui/test_settings_api.py -q` — **215 passed**.
- Fresh frontend regression run: `bun run test -- src/tests/settings-capabilities.test.tsx src/tests/provider-brand.test.ts src/tests/i18n.test.tsx` — **65 passed / 3 files**.
- Fresh touched-file Ruff, import boundaries (10 rules / 160 files), and `git diff --check` — **passed**.
- WebUI lint/build and touched-module basedpyright — **passed on the identical source snapshot before commit**, carried forward by unchanged file hashes and staged diff; not rerun for publication.

Full frontend typecheck — **fails with 469 diagnostics**; comparison against the original PR head under the same dependencies found the same 469 diagnostics and no additions. These remain failures, not a full-project PASS.

Settings were checked in English/Chinese, desktop/390px, light/dark; an environment-only key supported provider selection and a persisted timeout change without storing the secret. This source-bound evidence also predates the commit.
- Full Python suite was not rerun for this follow-up. Original author results below belong to the pre-follow-up source and environment.

## Original author verification (before follow-up)

Targeted suite:

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py -q --no-header

```


```
$ .venv/bin/ruff check nanobot/agent/tools/web.py tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py tests/webui/test_settings_api.py
All checks passed!

$ .venv/bin/basedpyright nanobot/agent/tools/web.py
0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
```

```
$ cd webui && bun run test -- provider-brand
✓ src/tests/provider-brand.test.ts (22 tests)
```

Project-wide type check (same command CI runs, after `install_channel_dependencies --all-channels`):

```
$ .venv/bin/basedpyright
0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
```

Full Python suite:

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --no-header
18 failed, 9983 passed, 15 skipped, 3 warnings in 356.67s
```

All 18 failures are environment-specific and unrelated to this change: 17 in
`tests/tools/test_seatbelt_native.py` (the macOS sandbox launcher) and 1 in
`tests/test_benchmark_session_storage.py` (a timing benchmark). CI on the PR is
the authoritative run.

Frontend tests were run on Node v26 with
`NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage`, because that Node version exposes
an experimental global `localStorage` that the current vitest setup does not
expect. The flag only affects the test environment; no frontend source changed.

Covered cases in `tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py`:

1. Success — asserts URL, headers, and body (`query`, `count`, `need_content: false`), and formatting.
2. `summary` preferred over `snippet`; `snippet` fallback when `summary` is empty; whitespace-only `summary` falls back to `snippet`; fields are stripped; `date: null` tolerated.
3. Empty results return the shared "No results for" text, not an error.
4. Explicit environment references resolve through the shared configuration mechanism. Missing configured credentials return an error without any request, even when `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is set.
5. Valid 128-character CJK and astral-plane emoji queries are preserved; overlong and blank queries are rejected without a request; surrounding whitespace is stripped.
6. `count` clamping (0→1, 100→50) at the provider boundary, and the tool-level 10 cap.
7. 401/402/403 do not retry and return the expected messages.
8. 408/429/500/503 retry once and succeed; 408/429/500 exhaust the retry budget and fail cleanly.
9. Timeout returns an actionable error; unexpected transport errors report the exception type without internal detail.
10. Malformed result entries are skipped without crashing; non-JSON 200 bodies are reported; oversized summaries are capped.
11. Error text never contains the API key, and relayed upstream messages are stripped of markup.
12. WebUI requires a configured search key, rejects environment-only setups, and preserves explicit `${VAR_NAME}` references on later settings saves.

Unit tests use `monkeypatch` on `httpx.AsyncClient.post` and never reach the network. Retry tests also stub `asyncio.sleep` so the suite stays fast. The original test list has been updated above to reflect current credential and query behavior.

## Original author live API verification (before follow-up)

The following records the original implementation and its historical live probes. Its truncation behavior has since been replaced by local rejection; the follow-up real Agent/Search check is recorded above. The original implementation was exercised against the real endpoint with a valid key:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Success path, Chinese query | 200; `summary`, `snippet`, and `date` parsed correctly |
| Search syntax passthrough (`site:`, `lang:`, `after:`) | 200; results restricted as requested |
| 200-character CJK and 150-emoji queries through the tool | 200 — local truncation prevents the 400 the API returns above 128 characters |
| Raw 200-character query sent directly | 400 `'query' must be at most 128 characters` (confirms the upstream length limit; current code rejects locally) |
| `count=100` at the provider boundary | clamped to 50; raw `count=51` returns 400 |
| Blank query | rejected locally, no request sent |
| Invalid key | 401 message; the key is absent from the output |
| Burst of 20 requests | 14 × 429 (`Your current QPS: 5`), confirming the documented limit |
| Tool call during a real 429 | retried after ~1.0 s and recovered |
| `date: null` | present in real results; rendered without error |
| Ten results, before/after the summary cap | ~35,700 chars (~10k tokens) → ~6,400 chars (~1.8k tokens) |

This testing found and fixed four issues that unit tests could not: unbounded
summary size, a whitespace-only summary hiding the snippet, unstripped markup
in relayed error messages, and raw transport-error detail in the tool result.

## Scope / Non-goals

- **No Fetch.** `POST /v1/tools/fetch` remains deferred. This PR leaves the existing Jina Reader/local extraction path unchanged; no Fetch provider expansion is included.
- **No LLM provider changes.** `nanobot/providers/`, the DeepSeek model registry, and model request assembly are untouched. No provider-hosted `web_search` tool is injected.
- **Separate from #6283.** This PR adds standalone search only and does not change model request assembly or the DeepSeek model registry.
- **`ori_question` and `localization`** are not sent; they are optional and not needed for a generic search tool.
- **No new dependency.** Uses the existing `httpx` client and the existing provider patterns.

## Decisions / remaining question

1. **Credential choice.** Search reads only `tools.web.search.apiKey`; missing credentials fail explicitly. An explicit `${VAR_NAME}` reference can use an environment variable through the shared config resolver. Search does not implicitly read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` or `providers.deepseek.apiKey`.
2. **Fetch stays deferred.** Retain Jina Reader/local extraction for now; this PR does not commit to a follow-up Fetch integration.
3. **Should the tool-level `count` cap be raised?** The API supports up to 50, but `execute()` caps every provider at 10. Left unchanged to avoid changing behavior for all providers.

## Checklist

- [x] `git diff --check` passes on the follow-up patch
- [x] Changed Python files pass `ruff` (E, F, I, N, W)
