prs.title: fix(email): avoid repeating configured reply subject prefixes
prs.body:
## Summary

Email replies recognize an existing `Re:` prefix, but do not recognize the configured `subjectPrefix`. When an incoming subject already has a custom reply prefix, sending a reply adds it again.

Examples from the SMTP send regression:

| Configured prefix | Incoming subject | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AW: ` | `aw: Invoice #42` | `AW: aw: Invoice #42` | `aw: Invoice #42` |
| `回复: ` | `回复: Invoice #42` | `回复: 回复: Invoice #42` | `回复: Invoice #42` |

Recognize the configured prefix case-insensitively while preserving the existing `Re:` behavior. Subjects without a reply prefix still receive the configured prefix.

## Tests

Extend the existing mocked SMTP send test to cover default prefixes, new custom prefixes, and already-prefixed subjects with case differences and Unicode.

- Before the fix: the two custom-prefix regression cases fail; the three control cases pass.
- After the fix: all 136 tests in `nanobot/channels/email/tests` pass.
- `ruff check nanobot/channels/email/runtime.py nanobot/channels/email/tests/test_email_channel.py`: passed.
- `basedpyright nanobot/channels/email/runtime.py` with the development virtual environment: 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

SMTP is mocked; no real emails or model API calls are sent.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to investigate the issue, implement the patch, and run the regression checks.

prs.title: fix(webui): show route-aligned skeletons from first paint
prs.body:
## Why

Refreshing a standalone page can show chat-shaped placeholders, a generic settings placeholder, and finally the page's own skeleton. Align the first paint with the requested route and keep its layout stable through bootstrap, lazy loading, and the initial data read.

## What changed

- Generate document-level skeleton markup and critical CSS from the same `StartupSkeleton` used by React. Restore the route family, sidebar preference, locale, and theme before app startup; preload the full stylesheet without blocking the skeleton and await it before mounting React.
- Calibrate existing catalog, marketplace, model, MCP, directory, and file-preview skeletons against rendered content. Add first-load skeletons for the topic list, settings sections, automation views, skill details, session automations, and Linear members.
- Keep cached content during background refresh, preserve session/skill identity boundaries, and let independently loaded settings sections render without waiting for the global settings snapshot. Add browser geometry, startup, accessibility, and refresh regressions.
- Match the new-chat skeleton to the real hero grid, header, Composer width/height and controls, including mobile bottom docking and the compact-Composer container breakpoint. Add comparisons against the real ThreadShell rather than a separately drawn reference.

## Scope

Frontend loading presentation and the state needed to distinguish first load from revalidation. No model execution, gateway protocol, configuration schema, dependency-version, or backend storage changes.

## Tradeoffs

Inlining the route-aware skeleton increases the HTML payload. Final-head controlled replay observed +85.5 ms cold-ready and +37.0 ms cached-refresh median on mobile 3G, alongside earlier skeleton paint (2,932→536 ms). The host experienced substantial CPU/memory pressure, limiting small-delta attribution; the confirmed compressed-document increase is 3,703 bytes versus the original branch base. Timing ranges, bundle sizes, controls, and limitations are recorded in the [final-snapshot performance and visual note](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6303#issuecomment-6261807897). This reports a measured cost rather than claiming zero regression.

## Blast Radius

WebUI document startup, lazy route fallbacks, and the listed first-load surfaces. The stylesheet promotion path is exercised against production assets with the full stylesheet and entry script independently held back. Cached refreshes retain their existing content and actions keep their existing progress indicators. The real chat components are unchanged by the new-chat follow-up.

## Verification

- [Final-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39213842411) at `df7d80e013312ccdf5aa37d2fbb7e2aac3335488`: **PASS** for WebUI (2,859 unit tests across 163 files, 86 browser tests, lint/import checks, production build) and Docker. Unrelated Python/TUI jobs were skipped by the change filter. Review is still required; no merge performed.
- `bun run build`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports`, and `git diff --check`: PASS. Build retains the existing large-chunk warning.
- Focused Vitest run across nine affected files: **336 passed**.
- `bun run test:browser browser/startup-shell.spec.ts browser/skeleton-layout.spec.ts browser/skeleton-additions.spec.ts browser/new-chat-skeleton.spec.ts`: **76 passed**, including 14 comparisons to the real ThreadShell across responsive/sidebar layouts, English/Chinese, and light/dark. Production checks passed all eight new-chat viewport/sidebar combinations through document/CSS/bootstrap/lazy handoffs, plus the existing eight Skills/Apps/Channels/Automations × mobile/desktop checks. Main geometry matches the actual page within its existing 1px camera anchor.
- Paired production-build replay, seven alternating runs per side for mobile 3G and desktop: 28 timed runs, identical API reads and workload row counts, no HTTP/request/page errors or fixture misses, cached scripts on refresh, unchanged source/assets. Detailed ranges, profiles, host-load limitations, and artifact binding are in the note above. No live-catalog or real-model acceptance is claimed.
- Full-project `tsc --noEmit --pretty false -p tsconfig.json`: **FAIL**, 471 diagnostics. Diagnostic blocks match baseline `53e0edf709b12730bf75cef5b343e3aef86548c0` after removing source positions; this is not a passing typecheck. The production build's narrower typecheck passes.
- An earlier expanded local unit run hit the baseline-reproduced `file-preview-panel.test.tsx` Markdown-heading timeout (394 passed / 1 failed). No timeout change or unrelated fix is included; the complete unit suite subsequently passed in the final-head CI above.

prs.title: fix(agent): keep idle compaction from archiving a running direct turn
prs.body:
# Fix idle compaction archiving a turn that is still running (#6214)

## Problem

`AgentLoop._check_expired_sessions_if_due` reports
`self._pending_queues.keys()` as the set of sessions with an in-flight turn.
The only writer of `_pending_queues` is `_enqueue_session_message` — the bus
path. `process_direct` takes the session lock and never enqueues, so a turn
running through it is invisible to the idle-compaction guard:

- `nanobot/agent/loop.py:1324` (before: `active_session_keys=self._pending_queues.keys()`)
- `nanobot/agent/autocompact.py:73-79` — two predicates, both must hold to archive:
  `key in active_session_keys` (skip) and `_is_expired(updated_at)`
- `_pending_queues` writers: `loop.py:888/894/897/1380/1389/1446/1453/1497/1675` — all
  bus-path; `process_direct` (`loop.py:2498`) is not among them

The turn's own persistence does not rescue it: the user message is saved once at
turn start (`_persist_user_message_early` → `sessions.save`), and after that
mid-turn state goes to the sidecar via `save_runtime_checkpoint`
(`loop.py:1017` → `session/manager.py:1108`), so `updated_at` rests at turn start
for the whole turn. Both predicates therefore hold and an archive is scheduled
for a turn that is still running.

No messages are lost — the live turn's final `sessions.save()` overwrites the
summary checkpoint the archive wrote — but the compaction is wasted, and it
repeats on every direct turn that outlives `sessionTtlMinutes` (default 15 min).

`process_direct` is not an edge path. It is the entry point for the API server
(`api/server.py:350`, `:394`), the SDK, one-shot CLI (`cli/agent.py:246`),
gateway runtime (`cli/gateway_runtime.py:586`, `:655`), builtin commands
(`command/builtin.py:487`) and the top-level entry (`nanobot.py:197`, `:280`).

## Fix

Register direct turns so the guard can see them (the guard's view), rather than
refreshing `updated_at` mid-turn:

- `_direct_turn_sessions: set[str]` on `AgentLoop`
- `process_direct` adds its key before taking the session lock and discards it
  in the existing `finally`, so failures release it too
- `_check_expired_sessions_if_due` passes
  `self._active_session_keys()` = `set(self._pending_queues) | _direct_turn_sessions`

This keeps the meaning of `_pending_queues` ("this session has an inbound
queue") intact and adds no new concept — a running direct turn is what
`active_session_keys` already means.

Refreshing `updated_at` instead was considered and rejected: it does not fix the
case where the turn starts on an already-expired session, and it would make long
turns (cron, goals) never go idle, raising token cost. `updated_at` also drives
`prepare_session`'s reload decision, the summary's `last_active`, and session
list ordering.

Because several unit tests construct `AgentLoop` via `__new__` and attach only
the attributes the method under test needs (6 such tests), the new set is read
defensively rather than becoming a hard dependency of `process_direct()`.

## Verification

Repro script (blocked `chat_stream_with_retry`, real guard, real active set) —
four assertions, A/B against the unpatched tree via `git stash`:

| | unpatched | patched |
|---|---|---|
| direct turn visible to the guard | FAIL (`_pending_queues=[]`) | OK (`_direct_turn_sessions=['cli:direct']`) |
| `updated_at` frozen during the turn | OK (unchanged, issue premise) | OK |
| archive scheduled for a running direct turn | **FAIL** (`background_tasks=1`) | OK (`0`) |
| summary clobbered by the live turn's save | **FAIL** (`after_archive=set after_turn=None`) | OK (nothing archived) |

Three tests added to `tests/agent/test_auto_compact.py::TestProactiveAutoCompact`:

- `test_direct_turn_is_reported_as_active` — blocked direct turn is not
  archived, transcript unchanged
- `test_direct_turn_archives_after_it_completes` — registration is released, so
  the next idle tick archives normally
- `test_direct_turn_released_after_failure` — a failed turn must not leave the
  session registered for the life of the process

All three fail on the unpatched tree (`3 failed, 52 passed`) and pass after
(`55 passed` in that file).

Full suite: **8387 passed, 121 skipped, 4 deselected** in 678s. The 4 deselected
are this workspace's known environment failures. No pre-existing test changed
behavior.

One note worth flagging: the first full-suite run caught
`tests/test_openai_api.py::test_process_direct_accepts_media` failing with
`AttributeError` on the new attribute. That test builds `AgentLoop` via
`__new__` and attaches only the two attributes the method under test needs —
an existing pattern in this repo (6 sites), not a dirty test. Rather than
adjusting their test, the new set is read defensively so `process_direct()`
gains no new hard attribute dependency.

Full evidence chain, including two of my own assumptions that were wrong and
cost me a false repro: `repro/6214-idle-compact-direct/EVIDENCE.md`.

## Uncertainties

- I did not run the reporter's original repro verbatim; my script measures the
  same predicates with fewer variables. The code-line correspondence is
  verified, the exact script is not.
- The lock-ordering interaction (direct turn holding the session lock while
  `compact_idle_session` wants it) is analysed, not measured under interleaved
  turns.
- I have not confirmed with a maintainer that the fix belongs in the active set,
  as the issue itself flags ("only a suggestion").

Full evidence chain, including two of my own assumptions that were wrong and
cost me a false repro: `repro/6214-idle-compact-direct/EVIDENCE.md`.

## Summary
Fixes #6285.

Default DuckDuckGo search had no retry/backoff. `ddgs` often raises `No results found` for transient rate/anti-bot rejections (not a genuine empty result set), so back-to-back `web_search` calls in one turn fail with a misleading error. Brave already retries once on HTTP 429; this mirrors that for DuckDuckGo.

## Changes
- Add `_is_duckduckgo_transient_rejection` for the misleading `No results found` / rate-limit style failures.
- `_search_duckduckgo` retries once with a 1s backoff on those rejections.
- Genuine empty lists still return `No results for: …` (unchanged).
- After a failed retry, return a clearer error that names rate-limit/block and suggests spacing calls.

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run python -m pytest tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py tests/tools/test_private_tool_logging.py` — 93 passed
- [x] `ruff check nanobot/agent/tools/web.py tests/tools/test_web_search_tool.py` — clean
- New cases: retry recovers after one rejection; clear error after two rejections; empty list stays a non-error “no results”

prs.title: fix(docker): make first-run Compose services usable
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #6165.

The issue reports that a fresh `git clone && docker compose up` produces a nanobot that is unreachable on every published port, with `nanobot-api` crash-looping. Confirmed at the code level and reproduced end-to-end against the committed compose file:

- `entrypoint.sh` only bootstraps `config.json` when `RENDER=true`, so a local `docker compose up` starts with no config at all.
- The resulting default binds are container-local: `GatewayConfig.host` and the WebSocket channel's `host` both default to `127.0.0.1` (`nanobot/config/schema.py`, `nanobot/channels/websocket/runtime.py`), so the ports the compose file publishes (`8765`, `127.0.0.1:18790`) can never reach them — `curl` gets `Connection reset by peer`, matching the issue.
- `nanobot-api` is started with `serve --host 0.0.0.0` but no `api_key`, so the non-loopback auth guard rejects the host and the process exits (1) into the compose `restart: unless-stopped` loop — the "constantly exiting and restarting" container from the issue.

Reproduction log (before this change): gateway healthy but `WebSocket server listening on ws://127.0.0.1:8765/`; `curl` 8765/18790 → exit 56 (reset); api restart loop with `Error: host 0.0.0.0 is available beyond this device but api_key is not set.`

### Change

- Default Compose startup keeps both the gateway and OpenAI-compatible API running. `serve` reuses the existing unconfigured-provider runtime when provider/model setup is incomplete. Authenticated chat-completion requests return HTTP 503 with `configuration_error` before executing a turn, for both regular and streaming requests. Health and model-discovery endpoints remain available; API authentication requirements are preserved. Restart the API after configuring a model to load those settings, as with other configuration changes.
- First-boot Docker configuration uses Python models, JSON serialization, secure random credentials, and atomic `save_config`. A shared file lock serializes initialization when both services start. The entrypoint drops to UID 1000 before initialization, matching bind-mount ownership and the Compose capability boundary. Existing configurations and credentials are preserved.
- In Compose, only gateway/API startup without an explicit config selector triggers default-instance initialization. Explicit `--config path`, `--config=path`, `-c path`, and `-cpath` remain owned by the CLI: the selected configuration is preserved and no default config is created. CLI commands, including first-time non-interactive `onboard`, retain their original behavior without an extra overwrite prompt.
- `NANOBOT_WEB_TOKEN` and `NANOBOT_API_KEY` can supply first-boot credentials; generated credentials are printed by whichever service initializes the config. Deployment documentation uses combined Compose logs, leads with startup and WebUI model setup, and documents API setup errors. The image includes `curl`; Render retains its template/environment-reference flow.
- Docker CI checks the actual service lifecycle, credentials, API setup errors, container recreation, read-only mounts, the legacy onboarding command, and all four explicit config-selector forms on both gateway and API services. Test fixture writes use the container runtime UID so the smoke test also works for non-root CI runners.

### Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix

### Related Issue

- Fixes #6165

### Testing

Current source snapshot: `33af3b1df23493baf8582ec061dddf8ba7931acf`, rebased onto `main` at `53e0edf709b12730bf75cef5b343e3aef86548c0`.

- Windows: `tests/test_docker_config.py`, `tests/test_openai_api.py`, and `tests/cli/test_commands.py` — **198 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Shell syntax (`bash -n entrypoint.sh`), Ruff and strict BasedPyright for `scripts/docker_compose_smoke.py`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Ubuntu 22.04 under WSL2, Docker Engine 29.1.3: complete Dockerfile build from an archive of the exact commit, including compiled WebUI and default WhatsApp dependencies. The Compose smoke test passed as a non-root host user (UID 1001): **15 PASS groups**, including **8 explicit-selector service cases**.
- Generated and special-character credentials: both default services start; WebUI login accepts the persisted credential and rejects incorrect passwords; API health remains available before model setup; authenticated regular and streaming requests return HTTP 503 with `configuration_error`. Exactly one service initializes the shared config.
- First-time `docker compose run --rm --no-deps -T nanobot-cli onboard` succeeds without an overwrite prompt. Container recreation preserves provider settings and credentials despite changed environment values. Restarting the configured API enables authenticated model discovery.
- All four config-selector forms on both services preserve the selected file byte-for-byte, use its credentials, and create no default config. A controlled real-container A/B with the previous versus fixed entrypoint reproduced the bug: before, the selected API key returned 401 and the default-instance key returned 200; after, the selected key returned 200, the default-instance key returned 401, and no default config was created.
- A read-only config mount exits with code 1, writes no config, and prints no successful login message. Owned containers, Compose networks, and the temporary image were cleaned up.
- Authentication and API behavior were verified through real HTTP endpoints. No real model requests or browser interaction were exercised in these remote Docker checks.
- Current-head CI: **all 9 checks passed** for `33af3b1df`, including Docker, WebUI, Linux/Python 3.11 and 3.14, Windows/Python 3.14, Windows process compatibility, and both TUI jobs: [Test Suite](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39197012055).

Earlier rebase validation at `bfedab999957823a999023cd6cf708bcfcfcfe99` passed 37 focused tests and 590 broader regressions (2 skipped), Ruff, Python import boundaries, and touched-source strict BasedPyright. The older [nine-check CI run at `dfe3199d0`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38373244018) is historical. The obsolete 45-second Windows handoff timeout patch was dropped during rebase; current main's serial execution, 15-second deadline, and native-stage diagnostics are preserved.

issues.title: Desktop: user message disappears from transcript when compaction merges it into a preceding model_switch notice
issues.body:
### Bug Description

After switching models mid-session, the next user message vanishes from the Desktop transcript if context compaction runs during that turn.

The message is not lost: the model received it and answered it, and it is still in `state.db`. It is just no longer rendered. The assistant's reply appears with no user message above it.

### state.db rows for the affected turn (times UTC+8)

| id | role | time | active | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7873 | user | 10:42:08 | 0 | `display_kind=model_switch`, uid `2e0b9e10db…` |
| 7874 | user | 10:42:19 | 0 | the real user message, uid `075bb81265…` |
| 7883 | user | 11:01:35 | 1 | `[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY]` summary |
| 7887 | user | 11:01:35 | 1 | uid `2e0b9e10db…` (same as the model_switch row), `display_kind=NULL`, `absorbed_message_uids=["075bb81265…"]`; content = model-switch notice + "\n\n" + the user message |

### Comparison
In the same profile, 9 other compactions absorbed a real user message into the `[CONTEXT COMPACTION]` summary row instead. I opened one of them (a session from Oct 13), and the absorbed user message still renders correctly there. The only failing case is when the absorbing row is a `model_switch` notice.

### Possibly related (minor)
In that Oct 13 session, the restated request `[STILL IN PROGRESS — this is the active request, restated after the compaction boundary …]` followed by the original question is rendered as a visible user bubble, so it looks as if the user sent it a second time.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an existing Desktop session.
2. Switch the model from the model picker (a `model_switch` notice is inserted as a user-role row).
3. Send a message that triggers a long turn (several web searches), so automatic compaction runs before the turn finishes.
4. After the turn completes, scroll back to that turn.

### Expected Behavior

The user message is shown above the assistant's reply.

### Actual Behavior

The assistant's reply is shown with no user message above it. The model-switch notice is hidden as usual, and the user message is hidden with it.

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Not attached: `hermes debug share` would upload private session content and config. The relevant `state.db` rows are included in the Bug Description instead.
```

### Operating System

macOS 27 (Apple Silicon)

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

v0.22.2 (commit d923a5e), source install, Desktop built locally with `hermes desktop --force-build`, stable channel

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Compaction merged the two consecutive user-role rows (model_switch notice + real user message) into one row that kept the **model_switch row's identity** (same `message_uid`), with the user message's uid moved into `absorbed_message_uids`. Desktop then appears to treat that row as the model-switch notice and hide it, taking the absorbed user text with it. I haven't traced the exact Desktop code path, so this part is inferred from the data.

Related: #140650 reports the same merge (`_merge_consecutive_users` keeping the model_switch identity) from the agent-loop side (wrong current-turn anchor). This report is the Desktop transcript side.

Workaround: send a short throwaway message after switching models before the real prompt, or switch models in a new session.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

_No response_

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.title: Multiplexed gateway: session.usage (and usage.bars / billing.state / subscription.state) fetch Nous account info with no profile scope
issues.body:
### In plain terms

**The problem:** one gateway now serves several profiles at once. Before code reads a setting like the Nous portal address, it has to say which profile it's working for. If it doesn't, the gateway refuses the read so it can't hand over another profile's setting by mistake.

When a client asks for usage numbers (`session.usage`), the gateway checks your Nous credits, but it never says which profile it's checking for. The read is refused, a warning is logged, and the code falls back to the default production portal. On a single-profile setup the answer comes out the same, so nobody notices. On a profile set to use a staging portal, the request goes to the wrong portal. It may also read the wrong profile's login, which would show one profile's credits in another profile's chat. That part is still unconfirmed.

**The fix:** when a request belongs to a session, run it as that session's profile before doing any work, the way other profile-aware requests already do. Then the read is allowed, uses the right profile's settings, and the warning stops.

### Details

On a multiplexed gateway, `session.usage` runs its Nous credits fetch with no profile scope. The handler is registered with `@_session_method` (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py:1448`), which resolves the session but never applies `_profile_scoped`. The call chain is `nous_credits_lines()` → `agent/account_usage.py::_fetch_portal_account` → `get_nous_portal_account_info(force_fresh=True)` → `resolve_nous_access_token` → `_nous_portal_base_url`, which reads `HERMES_PORTAL_BASE_URL` unscoped. `get_secret` raises `UnscopedSecretError`, and `auth_nous.py::_scoped_operator_override` logs `nous: HERMES_PORTAL_BASE_URL/NOUS_PORTAL_BASE_URL unreadable — no profile secret scope on a multiplexed call` and treats the override as absent.

**Repro:** on `main` at `cc6b1f2` (same code at `0b10b9f`), with multiplexing active, open a new session from a client that calls `session.usage` at session start (for example a relay client). The warning fires about 0.5 s after `ws accepted`. Desktop doesn't call `session.usage` at session start, so it doesn't trigger this. Captured stack:

```
rpc_dispatch pool
→ tools/daemon_pool.py:35 _run_with_context
→ hermes_cli/nous_account.py:329 get_nous_portal_account_info
→ hermes_cli/nous_account.py:370 _fresh_account_info
→ hermes_cli/auth.py:1815 resolve_nous_access_token
→ hermes_cli/auth.py:1844 _resolve_nous_access_token
→ hermes_cli/auth_nous.py:219 _nous_portal_base_url
→ hermes_cli/auth_nous.py:182 _scoped_operator_override (warning)
```

**Impact:**
- **Confirmed:** a profile's portal override is ignored on this path, and the fetch goes to the production portal.
- **Needs confirming:** whether the unscoped handler also reads the launch profile's Nous auth state, which would show the launch profile's credits in another profile's session.

**Same pattern:** `usage.bars`, `billing.state` and `subscription.state` (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py:1819-1850`) also reach portal fetches without `_profile_scoped`.

**Suggested fix:**
1. Bind the session's profile runtime scope in `_session_method`/`_session_arg` from `session["profile_home"]`, the same way `_profile_scoped` already handles a `session_id`. That covers every session-bound handler in one place. The narrower option is to wrap these four handlers in `_profile_scoped`.
2. Add a test that runs `session.usage` with multiplexing active, and asserts that no `UnscopedSecretError` is raised and that the session profile's override is used.

### Bug Description

Skill discovery is slow with a large skill library on Python 3.14. `pyproject.toml` pins `ruamel.yaml==0.18.16` on 3.14 so `ruamel.yaml.clib` is not required, which leaves the pure-Python parser for every `SKILL.md` frontmatter.

Profiling `_find_all_skills()` with about 960 skills shows almost all of the time in `hermes_yaml.safe_load` called from `agent.skill_utils.parse_frontmatter`: about 10 ms per document on our x86 host, so about 9 s per scan. The same frontmatters are parsed again by `scan_skill_commands` (slash-command catalog) and again after every catalog cache expiry. Under concurrent requests in one process we logged `commands.catalog` stages of 50 s typical and up to 139 s.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Python 3.14 (no `ruamel.yaml.clib`) with roughly 1,000 skills installed.
2. Open the command palette, or call `tools.skills_tool._find_all_skills()` and `agent.skill_commands.get_interactive_skill_commands()` in a fresh process.
3. Profile: `parse_frontmatter` → `hermes_yaml.safe_load` dominates.

### Expected Behavior

Each distinct frontmatter is parsed once per process; later scans reuse it.

### Actual Behavior

Every scanner and every rescan parses every frontmatter again.

### Affected Component

Skills (discovery and slash-command catalog)

### Operating System

Linux (AlmaLinux container, x86-64)

### Python Version

3.14.7

### Hermes Version

v0.21.7; `parse_frontmatter` is unchanged on main

issues.title: _find_skill parses the YAML header of every skill it walks past, even when a folder name matches — each skill_manage call costs one header parse per installed skill

labels.name: type/perf
labels.description: Performance improvement or optimization

labels.name: tool/skills
labels.description: Skills system (list, view, manage)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
**Version:** hermes-agent `d923a5eb48` (Release 0.22.2); `tools/skill_manager_tool.py` on `main` is
byte-identical (checked 2026-10-16). Windows 11; Python 3.11.16 (core venv) and 3.14.7 (desktop app).

**What happens**

`_find_skill(name)` walks every skills root and, inside the same loop, calls
`_read_frontmatter_name()` (a YAML parse) on every folder whose name does not match, before it
reaches the folder that does. So a lookup for a skill that is N-th in the walk order parses N-1
SKILL.md headers, although the folder-name match never needs them. The docstring already describes
the intended order: "a frontmatter match is only considered after the whole scan found no
directory/categorized match".

Each `skill_manage(action="patch")` resolves the skill three times, so one patch on a skill late in
the walk order parses about 3 × (installed skills) headers. The walk order also differs between
interpreters (here the first folder walked is a different skill on 3.11.16 and on 3.14.7), so which
skills are slow to edit changes with the Python version. One header parse took 0.21 ms on 3.11.16 and
0.57 ms on 3.14.7 in this install.

**Repro** (run from a hermes-agent checkout; builds 100 synthetic skills in a temp `HERMES_HOME`):

```python
"""Repro: tools.skill_manager_tool._find_skill parses the YAML header of every SKILL.md it walks past
before it reaches the folder whose name matches, so every skill_manage call on a skill that is late in
the walk order pays one header parse per skill installed.

Run from a hermes-agent checkout: python repro_find_skill.py
Uses $HERMES_HOME if set (a scratch directory with no skills), otherwise a new temp directory.
Builds 100 synthetic skills; touches nothing else.
"""
import json, os, sys, tempfile, time
from pathlib import Path

home = Path(os.environ.get("HERMES_HOME") or tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="find-skill-repro-"))
os.environ["HERMES_HOME"] = str(home)
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
skills = home / "skills"
assert not any(skills.rglob("SKILL.md")), f"{skills} must hold no skills yet"
for i in range(100):
    folder = skills / f"cat{i % 10}" / f"skill-{i:03d}"
    folder.mkdir(parents=True)
    (folder / "SKILL.md").write_text(
        f"---\nname: skill-{i:03d}\ndescription: Use when testing skill lookups, case {i}.\nversion: 1.0.0\n"
        "metadata:\n  hermes:\n    tags: [testing, lookup, repro]\n    related_skills: [skill-000]\n---\n\n"
        "# Repro skill\n\nbody line\n", encoding="utf-8")

import tools.skill_manager_tool as sm  # noqa: E402

parsed = 0
_read = sm._read_frontmatter_name


def _counted(path):
    global parsed
    parsed += 1
    return _read(path)


sm._read_frontmatter_name = _counted
order = [d.name for d in sm._iter_skill_dirs(skills)]
print(f"Python {sys.version.split()[0]}, {len(order)} skills")
for name in (order[0], order[len(order) // 2], order[-1]):
    parsed = 0
    t = time.perf_counter()
    assert sm._find_skill(name), name
    print(f"  _find_skill({name!r}): folder {order.index(name) + 1} of {len(order)} in walk order, "
          f"{parsed} SKILL.md headers parsed, {(time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000:.1f} ms")

last = order[-1]
parsed = 0
t = time.perf_counter()
for n in range(20):
    out = json.loads(sm.skill_manage(action="patch", name=last, old_string="body line\n",
                                     new_string=f"body line\nadded line {n}\n"))
    assert out.get("success"), out
print(f"  20 x skill_manage(action='patch', name={last!r}): {time.perf_counter() - t:.2f} s, "
      f"{parsed} SKILL.md headers parsed")
```

Measured output (before → with the diff below):

| | Python 3.11.16 | Python 3.14.7 |
|---|---|---|
| `_find_skill`, folder 100 of 100 | 99 headers, 107.5 ms → 0 headers, 9.3 ms | 99 headers, 110.0 ms → 0 headers, 5.7 ms |
| 20 × `skill_manage(action="patch")` on that skill | 5940 headers, 4.17 s → 0, 1.60 s | 5940 headers, 6.05 s → 0, 1.35 s |

**Real-world effect.** Approving three pending `skill_manage` batches (56 patch operations, 97
installed skills, Python 3.14.7, through `handle_pending_subcommand`) took 25.3 s; a second set of 28
operations took 11.1 s. A profile put 97 % of the time spent inside `skill_manage` in `_find_skill`
(16,340 header parses for 172 lookups). With the diff below: 6.3 s and 3.0 s, zero header parses,
and the resulting skill files are byte-identical (same tree hash).

**Suggested fix** — scan folder names first, read headers only when no folder matched. The
result is the same by construction: a folder or categorized match anywhere wins and returns the
first one in walk order, as today; the frontmatter fallback, including the ambiguity refusal, runs
only when the whole scan found no folder match, as the docstring says.

```diff
--- a/tools/skill_manager_tool.py
+++ b/tools/skill_manager_tool.py
@@ -252,7 +252,11 @@
     directory/categorized match, so one skill's frontmatter cannot shadow another
     skill's directory. A display name held by two or more distinct skills resolves to
     nothing: like skill_view's same-tier collision refusal, refusing to guess beats
-    silently mutating the wrong skill; the directory name still resolves."""
+    silently mutating the wrong skill; the directory name still resolves.
+
+    The scan runs in two passes: folder names first (no file reads), SKILL.md headers only when
+    no folder matched. Reading every header on the way to a folder match made each lookup parse
+    one YAML header per skill walked past it."""
     from agent.skill_utils import get_all_skills_dirs
     local_root = None
     if "/" in name or "\\" in name:
@@ -263,11 +267,8 @@
                 "skills dir resolve failed; categorized lookups fall back to the unresolved path",
                 exc_info=True)
             local_root = _skills_dir()
-    display_matches: list[Path] = []
-    seen_display: set = set()
-    for skills_dir in get_all_skills_dirs():
-        if not skills_dir.exists():
-            continue
+    roots = [skills_dir for skills_dir in get_all_skills_dirs() if skills_dir.exists()]
+    for skills_dir in roots:
         for skill_dir in _iter_skill_dirs(skills_dir):
             if skill_dir.name == name:
                 return {"path": skill_dir}
@@ -276,6 +277,10 @@
                 if (resolved.is_relative_to(local_root)
                         and resolved.relative_to(local_root).as_posix() == name):  # POSIX form
                     return {"path": skill_dir}
+    display_matches: list[Path] = []
+    seen_display: set = set()
+    for skills_dir in roots:
+        for skill_dir in _iter_skill_dirs(skills_dir):
             if _read_frontmatter_name(skill_dir / "SKILL.md") == name:
                 key = skill_dir / "SKILL.md"
                 with suppress(Exception):
```

**How it was checked.** The current and the patched `_find_skill` were run side by side on both
interpreters and returned the same folder (or `None`) for every lookup:
- 19 synthetic lookups covering a frontmatter name equal to another skill's folder name, one display
  name held by two skills (refused by both), a display-only name, categorized paths, a skill in
  `skills.external_dirs`, an external folder named like a local display name, and missing names;
- 195 lookups on a copy of a real 99-skill tree: every folder name, categorized path and frontmatter
  name.

The repository's pytest suite was not run (pytest is not installed in the local runtime); the
existing `tests/tools/test_skill_manager_tool.py` lookup tests are the natural place for a regression
test that counts `_read_frontmatter_name` calls on a folder-name hit.

**Left out on purpose.** With the fix, the remaining lookup cost is the directory walk itself:
`skill_manage` still resolves the same skill about three times per operation, and each lookup walks
the tree again (in the replay above, 261 lookups for 84 operations, each starting a new walk). Resolving once per call would be
a separate, larger change.

**Related.** Open PRs #125441, #110349, #112404, #81771, #60960, #44210 (symlink support) and #132957 (project skill dirs) rewrite the same loop without changing this cost; whichever lands second needs a rebase.

issues.title: perf(gateway): inline_bootstrap_argv re-runs its regex parse on every liveness probe
issues.body:
`gateway/status_inline_source.inline_bootstrap_argv()` re-parses the
inline bootstrap source with regexes on every call. The profiles list
endpoint runs a liveness check per profile, so the same command line
is parsed repeatedly under the GIL.

Observed: ~4% of GIL-held samples; ~25 ms per call on a real gateway
command line.

Local fix we run: memoize the parse on the token tuple
(`functools.lru_cache(64)`), return a fresh list per call, and expose a
cache-clear helper for tests. ~25 ms -> ~1 ms.
Happy to open a PR.

issues.title: perf(config): load_config cache thrashes between scoped and unscoped callers
issues.body:
`_LOAD_CONFIG_CACHE` is keyed by `str(config_path)` only, but `${VAR}`
refs expand against `os.environ` outside a profile secret scope and
against the profile `.env` inside one. Unscoped callers (DB opens,
watchers) and scoped turns therefore invalidate each other's entry, and
every crossing re-parses config.yaml under `_CONFIG_LOCK`.

Observed: ~18 ms per crossing on a real config; it showed up as one of
the GIL hot paths while desktop RPCs timed out at 30s.

Local fix we run: key the cache by (path, active secret scope), so each
scope keeps its own entry. Crossing cost: ~17.7 ms -> ~0.02 ms.
Happy to open a PR.

issues.title: perf(config): require_readable_config_before_write re-parses config.yaml on every call
issues.body:
Plugins that resolve their state home through
`require_readable_config_before_write()` call it from every tool hook
(pre/post/transform). Each call opens config.yaml and runs a full strict
YAML parse, so a busy gateway parses the whole config several times per
tool call while holding the GIL.

Observed (py-spy --gil, ~11 concurrent desktop sessions):
- ~9% of GIL-held samples were inside this function
- one call on a real config: ~18 ms
- desktop RPCs (session.resume/create) hit the 30s request timeout
  while the gateway logged `loop stalled >10s`

Local fix we run:
- cache the successful parse keyed by `utils.file_signature(stat)`
- skip caching when `mtime_is_racy`
- never cache failures (malformed/unreadable files are still refused
  on every call)
- return deep copies

Result: ~18 ms -> ~0.2 ms per call; config tests unchanged.
Happy to open a PR.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

When using Hermes Agent CLI (v0.21.5) on the _mkm-integration branch paired with a local 9Router Proxy (v0.5.104), the agent enters an unbreakable cascade fallback loop that always terminates at key/openai/gpt-6.1-sol with an HTTP 404: No active credentials for provider error, even though no OpenAI API keys are configured.
This behavior triggered immediately after a local OpenAI-Compatible provider was introduced to the 9Router dashboard, causing the agent's auto-discovery registry to prioritize it heavily over working local routes.

Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a local 9Router instance with an active CodeBuddy bridge that only has access quotas for Gemini models (gemini-3.5-flash-lite).
2. Add a non-functional or unauthenticated custom OpenAI-compatible provider configuration to the 9Router dashboard.
3. Start the terminal session using the Python source engine script since binary execution fails due to a broken subcommands module path (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli.subcommands.sessions').
4. Attempt to query the agent using an unauthorized custom model route (e.g., cbai/deepseek-v4.1-flash).
5. Notice that 9Router rejects the payload with an HTTP 400: request illegal (failed channel verification) due to missing IDE extension fingerprints (User-Agent).
6. Observe the agent failing to stop at the first error, cascading through all models, and completely locking the session into gpt-6.1-sol.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a local 9Router instance with an active CodeBuddy bridge that only has access quotas for Gemini models (gemini-3.5-flash-lite).
2. Add a non-functional or unauthenticated custom OpenAI-compatible provider configuration to the 9Router dashboard.
3. Start the terminal session using the Python source engine script since binary execution fails due to a broken subcommands module path (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli.subcommands.sessions').
4. Attempt to query the agent using an unauthorized custom model route (e.g., cbai/deepseek-v4.1-flash).
5. Notice that 9Router rejects the payload with an HTTP 400: request illegal (failed channel verification) due to missing IDE extension fingerprints (User-Agent).
6. Observe the agent failing to stop at the first error, cascading through all models, and completely locking the session into gpt-6.1-sol.

### Expected Behavior

The agent should gracefully halt execution and display the initial upstream API connection error (HTTP 400 Request Illegal / Channel Verification Failure) to the user immediately. If a fallback mechanism is triggered, it should only cycle through validated, active provider routes within the local configuration file rather than triggering a cascading failure down to a hardcoded, unauthenticated global default model ('gpt-6.1-sol').


### Actual Behavior

When the primary provider model request is rejected by the local proxy, the agent automatically falls back through multiple arbitrary engines before getting stuck in a permanent, non-retryable 404 loop against a ghost custom OpenAI route.

Full terminal logs/output:

⚠️ Model fallback: cbai/deepseek-v4.1-flash via custom unavailable (request format rejected)
⚠️ Model fallback: gemini/gemini-3.8-flash via custom unavailable (model not found)
⚠️ Model fallback: gemini/gemini-3.5-flash-lite via custom unavailable (model not found)
❌ custom rejected the request and retrying won't help: HTTP 404: No active credentials for provider: openai-compatible-chat-bb116dda-b924-4023-93a8-d449038cdc69
💡 Model 'key/openai/gpt-6.1-sol' isn't available on custom. Pick another with /model.


### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only), Telegram

### Debug Report

```shell
Command `hermes debug share` could not be executed due to the subcommands module importing crash (`ModuleNotFoundError`).
```

### Operating System

Windows 10 (Windows Terminal with Administrator Privileges)

### Python Version

3.12.14

### Hermes Version

v0.21.5+7091.g93c9360 (mkm-integration branch)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
The CLI binary execution layout is completely blocked on this branch due to internal project dependency layout discrepancies:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "D:\hermes-agent\hermes_cli\main.py", line 407, in <module>
    from hermes_cli.subcommands.sessions import build_sessions_parser
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli.subcommands.sessions'

Additionally, launching via raw source `run_agent.py` script returns:
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tools.environments.base_session_env'
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'agent.secret_sources._cache'
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The issue resides in the automated engine fallback policy layout inside `hermes_cli` and the auto-discovery registry components. When an upstream model endpoint throws an HTTP 400 parameter formatting or proxy validation error, the tracking logic fails to classify it as a non-recoverable client environment error. Instead, it systematically traverses all objects registered in the local runtime database cache workspace—including newly added placeholder custom providers—until it encounters the hardcoded global ultimate endpoint fallback handler without validating active API token mappings beforehand.


### Proposed Fix (optional)

1. Wrap the provider fallback discovery mechanism in a validation loop that filters out connections where `isActive: false` or those lacking actual assigned local/cloud credential mappings.
2. In `hermes_cli/main.py` or the core fallback array runner, intercept structural HTTP 400 (Request Illegal / Client Channel Rejections) early to prevent cascading registry loops.


### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.body:
## Bug Description

A Bot-mode chat (the never-resetting main bot session) resolves `/model` switches against a **frozen policy snapshot taken at session creation**, not against the live config. Any custom provider added *after* the bot chat was created is invisible to it: the desktop model picker fails with `model_resolution_failed`, while the exact same switch works fine in Sessions-mode chats (each snapshots the current config at creation).

Because Bot chats are explicitly "one continuous conversation" and their compaction rotation creates lineage children that **inherit the parent's frozen policy verbatim**, there is no normal way to ever see a newly added provider in a Bot chat — the registry ages forever with the session.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Bot-mode chat (e.g. on 2026-09-26) with provider `lenovo` configured.
2. Later (2026-10-18) add a new custom provider `honor` to `config.yaml` (`providers.honor` with `base_url`, `key_env`, etc.).
3. In the Bot chat, `/model honor/glm-5.1` (or pick it from the desktop model picker).
4. → `model_resolution_failed`.
5. The same `/model honor/glm-5.1` in a freshly created Sessions-mode chat succeeds.

## Root Cause

- `hermes_state_local.commit_local_session()` reserves the row/route/"immutable policy" together and rejects re-commits whose request differs (`invalid_params`), so the policy never updates.
- The canonical `/model` path (`gateway/session_mutation_model.py: prepare_model`) runs `switch_model()` against `config_json` frozen inside the `gateway.local_policy.v1:<session_id>` `state_meta` row — the provider registry from creation day. An unknown provider → `RuntimeStoreError('model_resolution_failed')`.
- Verified: calling `switch_model()` directly with the *live* config resolves the same target successfully (only a soft warning that the model is absent from the endpoint's `/v1/models` listing), so the resolver itself is fine — it's the frozen snapshot that's stale.
- Compaction rotation creates a lineage child (`parent_session_id` → bot chat) whose own `gateway.local_policy.v1` receipt contains the **parent's** provider registry unchanged. `/compact` therefore does not refresh anything.
- `local_receipt()` reads the snapshot with no signature/integrity check (noted only to rule out tamper-protection as the reason it can't be refreshed).

## Expected Behavior

One of:
- `/model` in a Bot chat merges the *live* provider registry with the frozen one (the frozen policy should govern things that must stay stable, not hide providers the user configured since);
- or a supported way to re-bind a Bot chat's policy (e.g. a `/policy refresh` or the compaction rotation re-snapshotting current config);
- at minimum, the `model_resolution_failed` error should say *why* ("provider 'honor' is not in this chat's frozen policy snapshot; start a new bot chat or ...").

## Actual Behavior

Opaque `model_resolution_failed` from the desktop model picker, with no log entry in `gateway.log` and no hint that the provider list is frozen at creation date.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (HONOR laptop)
- Version: Hermes Agent v0.22.2+1632.gb3c2883 (2026.9.24), desktop app
- Bot chat created 2026-09-26; provider added 2026-10-18; compaction rotation observed to inherit the stale registry (children created 2026-10-18 lack the provider too)

## Workarounds Considered

- `/compact` → does not help (lineage inherits the parent's frozen policy).
- New bot chat → works (fresh snapshot) but defeats the purpose of the persistent main bot chat.
- Hand-editing `state_meta` → technically possible (no integrity check) but obviously unsupported and risky.

issues.title: Gateway: an admission-observation hook so producers (webhook) can publish ordered delivery lifecycle events on the unified runtime
issues.body:
## Problem

Since the unified gateway runtime (#106742), a webhook delivery is a durable `session_admissions` row that the `SessionAuthority` claims and runs. That is a better model, but it removed the only seam where a plugin could observe a webhook delivery's lifecycle. #127054 (ours) added `gateway_platform_event` types `delivery_received` / `delivery_completed` on the old dispatch path; it no longer applies to `main`.

Consumers of those events (audit trails and incident records for alarm webhooks, completion notifications) need two ordering guarantees, and neither can be built from the adapter alone today:

1. **Receipt before start.** `delivery_received` must be dispatched before the run can start, because consumers key state on the per-delivery `chat_id` and correlate the run's `post_llm_call`. A consumer that has not seen the receipt has nowhere to put the report.
2. **Completion after the reply.** `delivery_completed` must come after the reply leg has run. The terminal admission row is committed before delivery (`session_settlement_recovery`), so "the row is terminal" is not "the reply was attempted".

We tried two adapter-level designs and an adversarial review broke both. These are the reasons, so nobody repeats them:

- **Emitting before the commit** (after `_webhook_retry`, inside `_delivery_turn`) is not exact. A caller cancelled during the shielded admission write releases the delivery lock while its commit can still land, so a retry sees no row and emits a second receipt. An exception from `admit_producer` also does not prove the delivery was not committed.
- **Installing a claim hold in the admission's `then` follow-up** runs after the worker thread's commit, so an already-active drain can claim the row in between.
- **Waiting on `authority.waiters`** misses several paths:
  - `_pause` and uncertainty release waiters while the row is not terminal;
  - `_resolved_unknown` never wakes a waiter registered later;
  - when resolution races the recovery stamp, the drain (not `deliver_resolved`) still owns the reply.
- **An ambient context variable as the observer** leaks into drains and background tasks spawned in that context, so it can observe unrelated admissions.

## Proposal

An internal, write-scoped observation handle on the authority. It is opt-in per admission and platform-agnostic, and nothing changes for callers that do not use it:

```python
obs = authority.observe_admission(request)     # reserved BEFORE the admission write; scoped to that one write
receipt = await <admission write>(..., observation=obs)
# inside the inserting transaction / follow-up:
obs.row, obs.inserted                         # insertion provenance from the transaction itself (not a pre-read)
# producer side:
await publish_receipt(...)                    # async, outside the write
obs.release_start()                           # idempotent; the claim of this admission waits for it
await obs.wait_delivery_settled()             # latch allocated at reservation time
obs.abandon()                                 # profile retirement / shutdown: never fabricates a terminal outcome
```

Guarantees it would provide:

- **Claim reservation before visibility.** The claim gate refuses the admission until `release_start()`, and the reservation exists before the row can be read by any drain. That covers retargeted or rotated sessions too.
- **Exactly one owner per durable admission.** `inserted` is True only for the transaction that inserted the row; replay, reconcile and retired-replay return False. An ambiguous write error reconciles against the reserved identity.
- **One settlement signal per admission, set once and exception-safe.** It fires after the reply attempt in the drain tail (`deliver_settled`, including when marker release raises), after a cancelled queued admission settles, and after resolved delivery. It is deferred to the drain when the drain still owns the reply, and it covers manual and unattended-unknown resolution (`resolve_unknown_as_owner`).
- **Retirement integration.** Observations belong to their authority; retirement wakes and joins them and releases reservations.
- **Out of scope / documented:**
  - Boot recovery: a restart loses process-local observers, which is best-effort as before.
  - Coalesced superseded delivery ids are not durably deduplicated, which is existing behaviour.
  - Observers must not block: a synchronous plugin callback cannot be pre-empted by an asyncio timeout.

On top of that, the webhook side is small: a `webhook_lifecycle` module, which also keeps `webhook.py` under its size threshold, plus the unchanged event contract from #127054 (payload `version: 1`).

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is an observation handle on `SessionAuthority` acceptable, or would you rather expose a narrower primitive, such as an admission hook point you own?
2. Is "reservation before visibility" better done as a pre-write row state, or as a loop-side reservation keyed by request identity that the claim gate checks?
3. Would you take this as two PRs: the authority hook with tests, then the webhook events on top?

We run an equivalent design locally on the runtime: a pre-commit claim hold plus a post-delivery signal. We're happy to do the work once the shape is agreed. Related: #127054, #84834, #80533.

issues.title: [Bug]: Desktop API-key cards show blue configured dots for unset Coding Plan keys via shared DashScope fallback
issues.body:
## Bug Description

In Desktop **Settings → Providers → API keys**, configuring only an ordinary DashScope key lights the same blue status dot on both Alibaba Coding Plan cards, even though their dedicated key inputs are empty and still display the paste-key placeholder.

This is a **configuration-state presentation bug**, not a claim that every blue dot is intended to be a live connectivity check. The UI does not distinguish a directly configured credential from an inherited fallback, and the lit dot conflicts with the empty primary input. For ordinary DashScope versus Coding Plan this distinction matters: Alibaba documents their keys/endpoints as non-interchangeable.

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed in an existing Windows Desktop setup; investigation was read-only:

1. Have only `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` set among these Alibaba key variables.
2. Leave `ALIBABA_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY`, `ALIBABA_CODING_PLAN_CN_API_KEY`, `ALIBABA_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY`, and `ALIBABA_TOKEN_PLAN_CN_API_KEY` unset.
3. Open **Settings → Providers → API keys**.
4. Compare each row's status dot with its primary key input.

## Actual Behavior

| Card | Dedicated primary key present | Observed dot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Alibaba Cloud DashScope (China) | Yes: shared `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` | Blue |
| Alibaba Cloud (Coding Plan) | No | Blue, with an empty primary input |
| Alibaba Cloud (Coding Plan, China) | No | Blue, with an empty primary input |
| Alibaba Cloud (Token Plan) | No | Unlit/gray |
| Alibaba Cloud (Token Plan, China) | No | Unlit/gray |

Read-only local status resolution reports both Coding Plan profiles as `configured=true`, with `key_source=env:DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`. Their own key variables are absent. This establishes fallback selection, **not** successful authentication or subscription entitlement. No model requests were made for this investigation.

## Expected Behavior

Preserve separate regional/provider cards and backwards-compatible credential resolution, but make the displayed credential state accurate:

- Distinguish **dedicated key configured**, **fallback/shared key detected (not verified for this route)**, and any separately verified connectivity state.
- An empty dedicated Coding Plan input should not show the same undifferentiated configured indicator as a directly populated credential.
- If a fallback is supported, identify its source visibly instead of silently inheriting the other card's dot.
- Do not require automatic/billable inference just to render the settings page.

## Root Cause Analysis

The installed packaged frontend contains the following logic; the same relevant expressions are present on upstream main at `0b10b9f8155a7ecadd8c540b87712c791b5c8ac9`:

1. [`buildProviderKeyGroups`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/0b10b9f8155a7ecadd8c540b87712c791b5c8ac9/apps/desktop/src/app/settings/providers-settings.tsx#L74-L140) expands `provider_profiles` for a shared variable into multiple card-scoped entries. The primary field can be the unset dedicated key, while the group flag is:

   ```ts
   hasAnySet: entries.some(([, i]) => i.is_set)
   ```

2. [`ProviderKeyRows`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/0b10b9f8155a7ecadd8c540b87712c791b5c8ac9/apps/desktop/src/app/settings/credential-key-ui.tsx#L285-L325) paints the dot from that broad group flag, rather than from the primary credential or a source-aware credential state:

   ```tsx
   group.hasAnySet ? 'bg-primary' : 'bg-(--ui-stroke-secondary)'
   ```

3. Runtime catalog metadata associates `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` with `alibaba` and `alibaba-cn` as a primary credential, and with `alibaba-coding-plan` and `alibaba-coding-plan-cn` as a non-primary fallback. Consequently, the same set fallback lights both otherwise-empty Coding Plan cards. The group predicate also includes non-key settings, so it is broader than credential presence.

Vendor contract: Alibaba's [Coding Plan overview, “获取套餐 API Key 和 Base URL”](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/coding-plan) explicitly distinguishes Coding Plan credentials/endpoints from ordinary pay-as-you-go DashScope credentials/endpoints. A generic shared-key presence flag cannot establish access to those plans.

## Affected Component

Desktop provider/API-key settings; provider catalog credential-state presentation.

## Debug Report

Not uploaded: the issue is supported by the observed UI, narrow credential-presence/source projections, and deployed frontend logic. Full logs/configuration and the original screenshot are omitted to avoid exposing account or credential data.

No configuration, credentials, active model, or provider defaults were changed during investigation. Source inspection confirmed the relevant logic on current main; the newest upstream Desktop build was not installed or interactively retested.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Python: 3.14.7
- Installed version output: `Hermes Agent v0.22.2 (2026.9.24) · upstream a62979dc · local d923a5eb (+3240 carried commits)`
- Installed checkout revision: `d923a5eb487a17c0a68801bba9ef0f56c81040a8`
- Upstream source snapshot inspected: `0b10b9f8155a7ecadd8c540b87712c791b5c8ac9`

## Related, but distinct

- #99385 (closed): preserving multiple provider identities for one shared environment variable. This report is about misleading status after those cards are represented, not a request to merge/hide them again.
- #136791 and #107473: doctor probe/source-reporting problems. This report concerns the Desktop settings dot, without any connectivity probe.

## Suggested Regression Coverage

Render the key groups with only `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY.is_set=true` and the dedicated Coding Plan keys unset. Assert that the fallback source is explicitly identified and that empty dedicated-key cards are not indistinguishable from directly configured ones. Also cover a non-key override being the only set field.

issues.title: [Bug] Editing pyproject.toml without re-locking uv.lock puts a self-managed install in a permanent boot loop: every launch refuses with "an update is still running" for an update that does not exist
issues.body:
## Summary

Editing `pyproject.toml` **without** re-locking `uv.lock` puts a self-managed source install into a permanent boot loop. Every launch attempts the source-update completion tail, the tail needs the checkout lock, and the next launch is refused with a message that names a running update that does not exist:

```
hermes: source-update completion failed: an update is still running; wait for it to exit, then relaunch Hermes; running with the previous dependencies — run `hermes update` to finish it
```

The message is misleading: no update is running. The refusal comes from the tail's own lock attempt.

This is **not** a Windows-only path and **not** the `Sec-MS-GEC` 403 described in #140990 / #137944 (that one is a TTS-synthesis failure; this one is an install-state deadlock that blocks every launch).

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.2 (git install, detached HEAD at `d923a5eb48`, tag `v0.22.2`)
- macOS 27.0.1 on arm64 (Apple Silicon), bundled Python 3.14.7
- PM-managed install, `updateMechanism: self` (`install-stamp.json`)
- 11 profiles share the one checkout (default, orchestrator, research, research-agent, writer, reviewer, analyst, ppt-master, doc-writer, devops-engineer, accessibility-auditor)

## How the state was reached

`pyproject.toml` was edited to bump one optional extra, but `uv.lock` was not regenerated:

```toml
# pyproject.toml
-edge-tts = ["edge-tts==7.2.7"]
+edge-tts = ["edge-tts==7.3.1"]
```

`uv.lock` still resolved `edge-tts==7.2.7` (both the package entry and the `requires-dist` specifier).

## Root cause

**1. A `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` divergence makes the venv "not current", and the launch path never repairs it.**

`Venv.expected_stamp()` (`pm/packages.py:425`) folds `_uv_lock_digest(self.project_root() / "uv.lock")` into the stamp, and `pm/install.py:893` reports `venv: out of sync with uv.lock` whenever the recorded stamp no longer matches. The recorded stamp is what the installed environment was reconciled against; once `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` disagree, the recorded stamp and the recomputed one no longer agree, and the install reports:

```
$ hermes pm doctor
venv: out of sync with uv.lock
```

Verified causally on the affected machine by restoring `uv.lock` from `HEAD` (7.2.7) while leaving the edited `pyproject.toml` (7.3.1) in place — the verdict flipped immediately:

```
$ # uv.lock = HEAD (7.2.7), pyproject.toml = 7.3.1
venv_is_current = False
activate problems = ['venv: out of sync with uv.lock']
check_runtime = install out of sync (venv: out of sync with uv.lock) — run `hermes pm install`
```

and flipping `uv.lock` back to the re-locked 7.3.1 file plus re-running `hermes pm install` restored `venv_is_current = True` / `activate problems = []`.

**2. `prepare_launch` therefore tries to run the completion tail on every launch.**

`hermes_cli/venv_sync.py:403`:

```python
elif not owed_to_cli and (not current or pending.is_file()):
```

`not current` is true, so every launch enters the owed-tail path.

**3. The tail takes the checkout kernel lock, and the next launch is refused.**

`hermes_cli/venv_sync.py:407-409`:

```python
lock = UpdateLock(install_root=root, checkout_first=False)
if not lock.acquire():
    raise RuntimeError("an update is still running; wait for it to exit, then relaunch Hermes")
```

`hermes_bootstrap.py:608` catches that `RuntimeError` and degrades to the previous dependency generation, printing the message above. The dependency generation is *not* rolled back — the install keeps running on the previous one, and the obligation stays armed.

**4. Nothing in the launch path repairs the lock.**

`hermes pm lock` is the only thing that re-resolves `uv.lock` from `pyproject.toml` (`pm/cli.py:24`), and it is a manual command. Neither `prepare_launch`, `pm.activate()` nor `pm.check()` detects or repairs a `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` divergence — `pm.activate()` only reports it (`pm/install.py:894`).

So the loop is self-sustaining: the install can never become current again without a manual `hermes pm lock` + `hermes pm install`, and the message it prints names a phantom updater.

## Reproduction

From a self-managed git checkout at a clean `v0.22.2`:

```bash
# 1. Edit one extra pin, leave uv.lock alone
$ python3 - <<'EOF'
import re, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("pyproject.toml")
p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('edge-tts = ["edge-tts==7.2.7"]',
                                   'edge-tts = ["edge-tts==7.3.1"]'))
EOF

# 2. The lock is now out of date with pyproject.toml
$ hermes pm doctor
venv: out of sync with uv.lock

# 3. Every launch now attempts the tail; hold the checkout lock to simulate
#    the concurrent tail/update that the refusal reports
$ python3 - <<'EOF'
import fcntl, os, time
p = ".git/hermes-update.lock"
fd = os.open(p, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)
fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
os.write(fd, f"{os.getpid()}\n{int(time.time())}\nct:0.000\n".encode())
time.sleep(60)
EOF

# 4. In another shell: the exact reported error
$ hermes chat -q "hello"
hermes: source-update completion failed: an update is still running; wait for it to exit, then relaunch Hermes; running with the previous dependencies — run `hermes update` to finish it
```

## What the diagnostic showed

- The checkout lock **record** (`.git/hermes-update.lock`) named a pid that was no longer running, and `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` on the same file succeeded — i.e. **no process held the kernel lock**, yet the launch was still refused.
- `hermes_cli/update_lock.py:1068` (`_lock_holder`) treats "recorded owner is dead but the lock is still held" as the `held` verdict, and `read_live_update()` keeps a dead marker when `checkout_lock_held()` is true (`update_lock.py:917`). The message therefore reads as "an update is running" even when the only thing alive is a leftover record.
- A stale **v1** profile marker (`<profile>/.hermes-update-in-progress`, pid + `started_at`, no `ct:` line) from an unrelated earlier run also existed and blocks `legacy_profile_claims()` until it is removed — another reason the refusal outlives its cause.

## Impact

- **Every** launch of every profile that shares the checkout prints the error and continues on the previous dependency generation.
- The exit code path is silent: the CLI still works, so the failure is easy to mistake for noise, but the install is permanently one `hermes update` behind and the completion obligation is never discharged.
- The remedy the message suggests (`run 'hermes update' to finish it`) does **not** fix it, because the problem is not an unfinished update — it is a `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` divergence that `hermes update` will stash and restore rather than relock. Users are sent to the wrong remedy.

## Suggested fix

Two independent improvements; either one breaks the loop.

**a) Detect the `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` divergence and say so.** When `prepare_launch` finds the venv not current, check whether `uv.lock` is still consistent with `pyproject.toml` (`uv lock --check`, or the same comparison `pm/cli.py` already performs). If they diverge, the actionable message is *"pyproject.toml was edited without re-locking; run `hermes pm lock`"*, not *"an update is still running"*.

**b) Do not blame a running update for a tail's own lock contention.** When the checkout lock is held and the recorded owner is dead (the `held` verdict at `update_lock.py:1068`), the message should name what actually holds it — a leftover record plus the tail — instead of reporting a nonexistent updater. `_lock_holder` already distinguishes this case; `describe_holder()` (`update_lock.py:962`) already has wording for it (`"; its owner exited but a process it started still holds the checkout"`), but the `venv_sync` path raises a bare `RuntimeError` and drops that context entirely.

Optionally: teach `prepare_launch` to relock automatically when it detects the divergence, since the divergence is always a local, self-inflicted edit that `uv lock` can resolve deterministically.

## Workaround (verified on the affected machine)

```bash
hermes pm lock      # re-resolve uv.lock from pyproject.toml
hermes pm install   # re-sync the venv so the recorded stamp matches
```

After this:

```
venv_is_current = True
activate problems = []
check_runtime = None
```

and all 11 profiles launch clean — verified by running `hermes -p <profile> chat -q ok` for every profile and asserting zero occurrences of the error string.

Separately, stale marker files that outlive their process must be cleared by hand:

```bash
find ~/.hermes -maxdepth 3 -name "source-completion-pending" -delete
find ~/.hermes -maxdepth 3 -name ".hermes-update-in-progress" -delete   # after confirming each named pid is dead
```

## Notes

- The `edge-tts` pin itself is a separate, already-reported problem: #140990 and #137944 (Windows `Sec-MS-GEC` 403). Upstream 7.3.1 does contain the locale-independent date-parsing fix that a local fork was carrying (`drm.py` uses `email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime` instead of `strptime`), so on macOS the bump is benign — but this issue is about the **lock/state deadlock**, not about TTS failing to synthesize.
- Reproduced on macOS 27.0.1 arm64; the underlying state machine in `venv_sync.py` / `update_lock.py` is platform-independent, so the same loop should be reachable on Linux and Windows wherever `pyproject.toml` is edited without a relock.

issues.title: [Bug]: Desktop Messaging shows "Needs setup" forever for token-free platforms (WhatsApp, webhook, A2A, ...): scoped _platform_enablement requires a required env var
issues.body:
## Bug Description

On the **profile-scoped** Messaging read (the request the desktop app's Messaging page makes), every platform with no required credential always reports `configured: false`. Its card shows two **Needs setup** pills and an orange sidebar dot even when the platform is enabled, every field reads **Saved**, and the gateway reports it `connected`.

This is a reporting bug, not a functional one, but it reads as if setup never finished.

It affects every catalog entry with an empty `required_env`. On 0.22.2 those are `whatsapp`, `yuanbao`, `api_server`, `webhook`, `a2a`, `msgraph_webhook`, `relay`, and `whatsapp_cloud`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pair WhatsApp (Baileys bridge) and enable it. The profile `.env` has `WHATSAPP_ENABLED=true`, and `config.yaml` has `platforms.whatsapp.enabled: true`.
2. Start the gateway. `gateway_state.json` reports `whatsapp: {state: connected}`, and the log shows `✓ whatsapp connected`.
3. Open the desktop app and go to **Messaging → WhatsApp**.

## Expected Behavior

The card reflects the live state, with no "Needs setup".

## Actual Behavior

The card shows `state: not_configured` (the "Needs setup" state pill) plus the `!configured` "Needs setup" setup pill, and the sidebar entry is flagged.

## Root Cause Analysis

In `hermes_cli/web_routers/messaging.py`, the scoped branch of `_platform_enablement` does this:

```python
configured = bool(required) and all(env_on_disk.get(key) for key in required)
```

For a token-free platform, `bool(required)` is `False`, so `configured` can never become `True`. The unscoped branch instead uses `GatewayConfig._is_platform_connected`, which for WhatsApp returns `True` through `WHATSAPP_ENABLED`. Running the same platform through both branches on one machine gives `scoped=False → configured: true` and `scoped=True → configured: false`.

The same line is still on current `main` (line 166). This is a sibling of #104614, where the scoped branch reported Disabled for token platforms enabled through `.env`, and it is related to #133442.

## Proposed Fix (tested locally)

A token-free platform has no credential to check, so its setup signal is being switched on: either `enabled: true` in `config.yaml`, or the `<ID>_ENABLED` flag that the setup wizards write to the profile's `.env`. An explicit `enabled: false` still wins.

```diff
+def _env_flag_on(value: Any) -> bool:
+    return str(value or "").strip().lower() in {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}
+
+
 def _platform_enablement(
@@
             # Setup writes credentials without a platforms entry; explicit disable wins.
             raw_enabled = plat_cfg.get("enabled")
+            if not required:
+                # Token-free platforms (WhatsApp's QR-paired bridge, webhooks, A2A, ...) have no credential
+                # to check, so being switched on IS their setup: config.yaml ``enabled: true`` or the
+                # ``<ID>_ENABLED`` flag setup writes to the profile's .env.
+                configured = raw_enabled is True or _env_flag_on(env_on_disk.get(f"{platform_id.upper()}_ENABLED"))
             enabled = False if raw_enabled is False else bool(raw_enabled) or configured
```

The regression tests are in `tests/hermes_cli/test_messaging_scoped_tokenless_platforms.py`. They cover five cases:

- an enabled token-free platform is configured;
- the env flag alone configures and enables it (the `hermes whatsapp` CLI path writes no YAML entry);
- an explicit YAML disable still wins;
- an untouched platform stays unconfigured;
- a credentialed platform still needs its token.

The two new-behavior tests fail on 0.22.2 and pass with the fix. With the fix, the related messaging and profile test files (`test_served_profile_mirror_platforms`, `test_web_server_messaging_*`, `test_whatsapp_*`, `test_setup_hidden_env`, `test_web_server_profile_unification`) give 65 passed. The 9 remaining failures (7 in `TestProfileScopedChatPty` and 2 in `test_whatsapp_missing_runtime`, which trip the home-I/O guard on this machine) fail identically on unmodified 0.22.2 on this Windows host, so they are unrelated to this change.

## Environment

- **Affected component:** desktop app / dashboard, Messaging
- **Messaging platform:** WhatsApp, plus the other token-free platforms listed above
- **Operating system:** Windows 11 Pro
- **Hermes version:** 0.22.2 (`d923a5eb48`)
- **Python:** bundled 3.14
