issues.body:
# macOS 12 (Monterey): the pinned PM Node (>= v25) can never install — staged binary aborts with a dyld libc++ symbol, and every Node-dependent feature stays broken

### Bug Description

On macOS 12 the PM `node` entry can never install. The pinned official darwin-x64 build
(`node 26.7.0` in `pm/lock.json`) requires `__ZNSt3__122__libcpp_verbose_abortEPKcz` from
`/usr/lib/libc++.1.dylib`, a symbol macOS 12's libc++ never exported. The staged binary dies
with SIGABRT before it can print anything, so `pm/install.py:457` raises
`staged entry failed verification` and PM refuses the entry.

Because nothing in the failure path can succeed on this host, the install is retried forever,
and everything that consumes the PM Node stays broken:

* `hermes dashboard` — `→ Building web UI…` then the same verification error; never reaches
  `HERMES_DASHBOARD_READY`
* `hermes --tui` / `hermes desktop` — same wall
* PTY sessions (`hermes_cli.web_server: pty start failed: InstallError: node: staged entry
  failed verification …`)
* write-time Node linters — skip with `… not available (Hermes-managed Node not installed)`
* `hermes update` — `⚠ Update follow-up 'dependencies' did not finish: node: staged entry
  failed verification … (dependencies not installed yet — the next launch retries)`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Host: macOS 12.7.4 (Monterey, Intel x86_64), Hermes `v0.21.7+144.g3f2abce` (2026.9.24),
   git install, `pm/lock.json` pinning `node 26.7.0`.
2. `hermes pm install node`:

```text
  node: 100.0%  27.8 MiB / 27.8 MiB
  node: unpacking
✗ node: staged entry failed verification: /Users/<u>/.hermes/tools/.staging-l9eoc281/tree/bin/node --version exited -6: dyld[20735]: Symbol not found: (__ZNSt3__122__libcpp_verbose_abortEPKcz)
  Referenced from: '/Users/<u>/.hermes/tools/.staging-l9eoc281/tree/bin/node'
  Expected in: '/usr/lib/libc++.1.dylib' — retry, or run `hermes pm doctor`
```

(an earlier install attempt also reports it as a `hermes update` follow-up):

```text
⚠ Update follow-up 'dependencies' did not finish: node: staged entry failed verification: /Users/<u>/.hermes/tools/.staging-yz83u8oj/tree/bin/node --version exited -6: dyld[20882]: Symbol not found: (__ZNSt3__122__libcpp_verbose_abortEPKcz)
  Referenced from: '/Users/<u>/.hermes/tools/.staging-yz83u8oj/tree/bin/node' Expected in: '/usr/lib/libc++.1.dylib' — retry, or run `hermes pm doctor` (dependencies not installed yet — the next launch retries)
```

3. Host-only probe, no Hermes involved — the pinned artifact alone cannot run here:

```bash
curl -O https://nodejs.org/dist/v26.7.0/node-v26.7.0-darwin-x64.tar.xz
tar xf node-v26.7.0-darwin-x64.tar.xz
./node-v26.7.0-darwin-x64/bin/node --version
# dyld[33348]: Symbol not found: (__ZNSt3__122__libcpp_verbose_abortEPKcz)
#   Referenced from: '…/node-v26.7.0-darwin-x64/bin/node'
#   Expected in: '/usr/lib/libc++.1.dylib'
# Abort trap: 6   (exit 134)
```

4. Consume any Node feature, e.g. `hermes dashboard` → fails in `Building web UI…`;
   `hermes pm doctor` reports the node row as unsatisfied and only ever offers `retry`.

Measured boundary on this host (official darwin-x64 tarballs from nodejs.org, `bin/node --version`):

| Node version | Result on macOS 12.7.4 |
| --- | --- |
| 22.22.2 (bundled `$HERMES_HOME/node`) | runs |
| 24.14.0 | runs |
| **24.21.0** | **runs — newest working line** |
| 25.9.0 | `dyld: Symbol not found … libc++.1.dylib`, SIGABRT |
| 26.0.0 / 26.7.0 / 26.11.1 | `dyld: Symbol not found … libc++.1.dylib`, SIGABRT |

### Expected Behavior

PM should install a Node the host can actually execute — or fail once, with a remedy that names
the host-compatibility cause — instead of a permanent retry loop that leaves the dashboard, TUI,
PTY sessions, linters and `hermes update`'s dependency follow-up broken.

### Actual Behavior

Every attempt retries the same doomed install. The user-visible message is the generic
`retry, or run hermes pm doctor`, and `hermes pm doctor` repeats it — no mention that this
host's macOS is simply too old for the pinned Node major.

### Affected Component

- CLI (interactive chat)
- Setup / Installation
- Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

- N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

Not uploaded: `hermes debug share` pushes system info, config and recent logs to a paste
service, and secret redaction is off by default on this install, so I did not want to publish
that unprompted. Happy to add a report (or a `--local` excerpt) on request — the relevant log
lines are pasted inline above.

### Operating System

macOS 12.7.4 (build 21H1123), Intel x86_64 (`Darwin 21.6.0`)

### Python Version

3.14.7 (`$HERMES_HOME/tools/python-3.14.7+20260901-darwin-x64`)

### Hermes Version

`Hermes Agent v0.21.7+144.g3f2abce` (2026.9.24), git install, `main @ 3f2abce7f4`

### Additional Logs / Traceback

`~/.hermes/logs/agent.log` (repeats on every launch):

```text
2026-10-12 23:01:33,018 WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: pty start failed: InstallError: node: staged entry failed verification: /Users/<u>/.hermes/tools/.staging-l9eoc281/tree/bin/node --version exited -6: dyld[20735]: Symbol not found: (__ZNSt3__122__libcpp_verbose_abortEPKcz)
2026-10-12 23:01:47,476 WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: pty start failed: InstallError: node: staged entry failed verification: /Users/<u>/.hermes/tools/.staging-la62exn8/tree/bin/node --version exited -6: dyld[20769]: Symbol not found: (__ZNSt3__122__libcpp_verbose_abortEPKcz)
```

`~/.hermes/logs/update.log`:

```text
⚠ Update follow-up 'dependencies' did not finish: node: staged entry failed verification: … — retry, or run `hermes pm doctor` (dependencies not installed yet — the next launch retries)
```

### Root Cause Analysis

1. `pm/lock.json` pins `node` to a single version for every target (`26.7.0` today), and
   `Nodejs` (`pm/packages.py:492`) stages the official tarball for it.
2. `pm/install.py:457` requires the staged entry to answer `node --version`. On macOS 12 that
   probe cannot succeed: official darwin-x64 builds from v25 on are linked against a newer
   libc++ that exports `std::__1::__libcpp_verbose_abort`; `/usr/lib/libc++.1.dylib` on macOS 12
   predates it and `/usr/lib` is SIP-protected, so there is nothing to repair on the host. This
   is the same failure class other projects hit on Monterey (Cursor CLI, Cloudflare `workerd`,
   LLVM toolchains).
3. `Nodejs.repair_staged_verification` (`pm/packages.py:525`) already exists for exactly this
   shape of problem — a host library the staged binary needs — but only for Linux
   (`libatomic.so.1`, `pm/libatomic.py`). The darwin analogue has no repair path, no fallback to
   a runnable major, and no host-compatibility classification.
4. `source_build_env()` → `pm.ensure("npm")` / `source_product_current()` mean the failure is
   sticky: the build receipt cannot be read without PM's Node, so every launch re-attempts the
   doomed build.
5. Side finding while looking for a manual escape: `hermes pm lock --bump node 24.21.0` cannot
   be used to drop a major. It resolves artifacts for every target first and aborts on the
   Termux row (`nodejs_24.21.0-1_aarch64.deb` → HTTP 404; the Termux repo carries only
   `26.4.0-1`), after downloading ~350 MB of archives it then discards.

### Proposed Fix

1. **Host-compat gate for the pinned Node (preferred).** When `target == current_target()`,
   pick the newest candidate that the host can actually run — e.g. filter
   `Nodejs.latest_versions()` (`pm/packages.py:519`) through a cached probe, or extend
   `repair_staged_verification` to recognise the darwin dyld/libc++ symbol failure and fall back
   to the newest runnable major (`24.x` on macOS 12), mirroring the existing Linux
   `libatomic` retry.
2. **Minimum: make it diagnosable.** Classify
   `Symbol not found … Expected in: '/usr/lib/libc++.1.dylib'` (and the `exited -6` form) as a
   host-too-old condition, and print a remedy such as *"this host's macOS is older than the
   pinned Node major requires; newest compatible major: v24; re-pin with …"* instead of
   `retry`.
3. **Optional:** a documented way to pin a Node major / bring your own Node — overlaps with
   #130574.

Verified workaround used here (digests taken from the upstream-published `SHASUMS256.txt`
files, so no archive has to be downloaded; the Termux `linux-arm64-bionic` row is preserved
because upstream publishes no 24.x `.deb`):

```bash
python3 pin-node-macos12.py       # rewrites pm/lock.json -> packages.node = 24.21.0
hermes pm install node npm
hermes pm doctor                  # ✓ node 24.21.0, ✓ npm 12.0.2
hermes dashboard --no-open        # ✓ Building the TUI → ✓ Building the web UI → HERMES_DASHBOARD_READY port=9119
```

The rewrite goes through `pm.lock.Lockfile.set_pin()`/`save()` so the schema, file lock and
stale-row check stay intact; the full script can be pasted in a follow-up comment if useful.

### Related issues

- #137491 — same symptom (`staged entry failed verification`, missing C++ symbols) but a
  different root cause: Fedora 44 / glibc, not darwin libc++
- #134029 — `hermes pm update node` pin resolution HTTP 404 (node lock/mirror drift)
- #126934 — stale `$HERMES_HOME/node` kept as the user's node/npm forever after a PM install
- #130574 — feature: allow skipping the managed Node runtime (host-provided nvm/system)
- #84127 (closed) — earlier host-compatibility precedent on Intel macOS

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Yes — happy to send a PR once the approach is agreed; I would implement option 1 + 2 above and
add a regression test that fakes a staged binary which exits -6 with the libc++ symbol error.

issues.body:
# Feature: show usage/cost segments in the DESKTOP status line (parity with the TUI chrome)

## What the TUI already has

`ui-tui/src/components/appChrome.tsx` (the `StatusRule` component) renders a full usage rule:

- context read-out, `used/max` tokens with an `~` marker when estimated (`usage.context_used`, `usage.context_max`, `usage.context_estimated`), collapsing to `12k tok` on narrow terminals
- a context fill bar from `usage.context_percent`
- cache-hit percentage (`◎ {usage.cache_hit_pct}%`)
- a cost segment (see the comment "we shed the least important pieces first (cost → ...)")
- compressions, dev-credit spend, battery, latency / tokens-per-sec

All of it is gated by `display.status_bar.fields` (`null` = user has not customised → everything shows).

## What the desktop app shows today

The desktop window's bottom status line, on v0.21.5+3049.g802ae85 / Windows 11, reads:

```
⌘ Gateway ready   📁 _AgenticOS   ↻ 100%   ⚡ 137 t/s   ↗ GPU 3% · 15G/16G   ⚡ Smart   # v0.21.5+3049 (update)
```

No tokens, no context, no cache-hit %, no cost — even though the desktop is served by the same backend, and `ui-tui/src/gatewayTypes.ts` already declares the cost fields for the desktop payload (`cost_status`, `cost_usd`) alongside the usage block the TUI chrome consumes.

## Request

Add the usage segments (at minimum: context `used/max` + %, cache-hit %, session cost) to the desktop status line, honouring the same `display.status_bar.fields` gate as the TUI so users can trim it. Default on, or opt-in — either is fine; today the only way to see cost/context live inside the app is the TUI.

This is not something a plugin can fill in: general plugins can register hooks, tools and CLI commands, but there is no UI/chrome slot for them (unlike, say, a dock/status-slot extension point). A cost plugin can only expose the numbers through `hermes cost` or a tool call, which does not give the always-visible read-out that makes spend visible while working.

Note the related gap in the same area: core prices DeepSeek at off-peak rates only, with the peak multiplier documented in `agent/usage_pricing.py` but never applied, so any cost shown in chrome would also need that fix to be accurate during peak windows (#88374).

## Environment

Hermes Agent v0.21.5+3049.g802ae85 (2026.9.24), desktop app on Windows 11, provider `deepseek`.

## Summary

On v0.22.2 (Windows MSIX, gateway `d923a5eb48`), a session's runtime can end up with `model` from a local provider (Strata, llama.cpp on 127.0.0.1:8080) paired with `provider: xiaomi`. Every turn then goes to the Xiaomi endpoint with a local model id and dies with `HTTP 400: Unsupported model <id>` (`failure_reason=model_not_found`).

## Evidence (agent.log, same machine)

```
2026-10-16 23:59:19 provider=xiaomi base_url=https://token-plan-sgp.xiaomimimo.com/v1 model=qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs
  -> HTTP 400: Unsupported model qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs  (session 20261016_214329_fe2bb9)
2026-10-18 00:31 / 00:56 agent_init provider=xiaomi model=qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs  (no preceding switch log)
2026-10-20 10:23:31 provider=xiaomi model=swift-1.5-iq3_s -> HTTP 400: Unsupported model swift-1.5-iq3_s  (session 20261019_235128_e08893)
2026-10-20 10:24:15 Model switched in-place: swift-1.5-iq3_s (xiaomi) -> swift-1.5-iq3_s (strata)
```

The 10:24 line shows the pair (model=swift…, provider=**xiaomi**) existed *inside a live session* — not the composer draft state that #125336 fixed. Re-selecting the model from the STRATA group heals it (pair rewritten atomically).

## How to surface it in the UI

The composer model menu injects the current model's row into the provider group matching `current.provider` (`groupModels`, model-catalog-menu.tsx #57534). When the pair is torn, a local Strata quant ("Qwen3.8 Flash Next UD IQ4_XS") renders **checked inside the XIAOMI MIMO group**. Clicking it re-persists `provider=xiaomi`, so the state self-perpetuates.

## Environment

- Windows 11, desktop MSIX 0.22.2 (10/15), gateway from same commit, single install (no dual-install involved).
- `providers.strata` = llama.cpp-family server on 127.0.0.1:8080, one model loaded at a time; `providers.strata.default_model` currently empty.
- Xiaomi (MiMo token-plan) is the profile default provider.

## Suspected shape

Some path applies a model-only update (model string set, provider left at the profile default `xiaomi`) — candidates: session.create with a composer manual pick whose provider is empty, and a live-session switch where provider resolution falls back to the profile default. A gateway-side coherence gate (reject/repair model∉provider-catalog pairs, at least for providers with a declared `models:` list) would harden all paths at once.

## Repro

Intermittent ("sometimes"), correlates with switching between xiaomi and strata models, and with opening a new chat after viewing a session that ran a strata model. Deterministic repro not established.

- delegation.model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5 (also reproduced with claude-opus-5.5 children)

### Repro
1. Start any session on a Claude model via provider nous.
2. Ask it to delegate_task one child: "Read these 15 files one per turn with read_file, then give a
   one-line summary of each." Use any 15 files of a few KB each, e.g. agent/*.py in the hermes-agent repo.
3. Grep agent.log for the child's "API call #N" lines.

### Observed (child session: 16 calls, 55 s wall time, so the 5m TTL cannot be the cause)
```
#1   in=16745   write=16741
#2   in=19319   cache=16741 (87%)
#6   in=47883   cache=16741 (35%)
#9   in=91286   cache=16741 (18%)
#16  in=133539  cache=16741 (13%)
```
Session totals: input 1.19M, cache_read 251K (21%), cache_write 16,741. The only cache write is
the system prompt.

Same pattern on two longer Opus children:
- 106 calls, context grew to about 314K, cache read fixed at 20,065 on every call, 9.5% hit rate
- 45 calls, 16% hit rate
In both, cache_write_tokens equals the single system-prompt write. Later breakpoints are never
even written.

### Expected
The cached count climbs with the conversation (rolling last-N markers), giving over 70% hits after
the first few calls. Top-level sessions on the same provider, model, and day do this (73-98%).

### Possibly related
One top-level CLI session showed the same flat pattern for 19 calls (cached fixed at about 30K while
input grew from 30K to 89K), then recovered on its own at call 20. So the root cause may be a state
where non-system markers are dropped or ignored. Short, fully machine-driven children may never
leave that state.

### Upstream
Every response, broken and healthy alike, comes back with msg_vrtx_* ids (Vertex), so this is not
the OpenRouter-passthrough case that agent/nous_wire.py handles. Both the healthy top-level
sessions and the stuck children went through the same upstream.

### Related
- #133575: same "stuck at a fixed floor, never advances" signature, on a different provider
(claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental). There is one difference: there, write grows every call
(the cache is written but not read back). Here, write is 0 after call #1 (the history is never
written at all). It could be the same root cause or a sibling bug.
- #71576 (closed): Portal does not support sticky routing for Anthropic.
- #103563 (closed): postmortem classifying "stuck/non-advancing" cache.

### Suspected area
apply_anthropic_cache_control / _can_carry_marker on the envelope layout with tool_part_markers=True
for nous. Child history is mostly role:tool results, and the Portal is documented as relocating
part-level cache_control onto tool_result blocks. The missing cache writes suggest those markers
are not honored. This is unverified.

issues.body:
### Problem

`browser_vault action=enter_code` can't be used on messaging platforms. On Discord, the gateway never registers a code prompt callback (`agent/vault_backends/unlock.py` `get_code_prompt_callback()` returns `None`), so `enter_code` returns `prompt_unavailable` even in a live DM with the account owner:

```
{"success": false, "error_type": "prompt_unavailable", "error": "app.talkspace.com asks for a one-time code and this session cannot ask the user (headless/cron/API). Save an authenticator key for this login so codes can be generated automatically."}
```

The tool description also forbids the agent from typing a code the user pastes in chat. As a result, any site that sends SMS or email codes (no TOTP option) can't be logged into from a gateway chat. Many banks, healthcare portals and pharmacies only offer SMS or email codes, so this blocks a large share of real errands. In my case it was a therapist portal, sending an urgent medication refill request.

### Suggested fix

Have the gateway register a code prompt for platforms that can collect input privately, and gate it to the session owner:

- **Discord:** post an ephemeral button ("Enter code for app.talkspace.com"). The button opens a modal with one short text input. The value goes straight into the callback, so it never appears in the transcript or the channel history. Only the authorized user who started the turn can open it.
- **Telegram / Slack:** use a similar private flow, or a one-time reply that the adapter intercepts and deletes before it reaches the agent or the session log.

`can_prompt_here()` already returns False for cron, webhook and `-q`, so interactive DMs would be the only path that gains this ability.

### Environment

Hermes Agent v0.22.2 (2026.9.24) stable, Linux, Discord gateway, 1Password service-account backend.

issues.title: [Bug]: Fallback-minted Gemini thought signatures are replayed to the primary on later turns; a 422 from the primary makes the fallback permanent for the session

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

issues.body:
### Bug Description

When a turn falls back from the primary provider to a `vertex` fallback, the Gemini thought signatures that Vertex returns are stored in the session history with no record of which route minted them. From the next turn on, Hermes restores the primary and replays those Vertex signatures to it, because the replay gate only asks whether the target model looks like Gemini, not whether the target minted the signature.

My primary is a custom OpenAI-compatible gateway serving a Gemini model. It rejects signatures it did not issue with HTTP 422:

```
signed or encrypted reasoning from another provider has no representation in Gemini generateContent for <upstream>; request <id>
```

Hermes classifies that 422 as a plain `format_error`, does not strip anything, and activates the fallback. The fallback answers and adds more Vertex signatures to the history. On the next turn the primary is restored, gets the same 422, and the cycle repeats. After one fallback, the primary never serves that session again until the session is reset.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a primary that serves a Gemini model under an id containing `gemini`, behind an endpoint that does not accept signatures minted elsewhere, and Vertex as the first fallback:

   ```yaml
   model:
     default: gemini-3.8-flash
     provider: custom:<name>        # OpenAI-compatible gateway in front of Gemini
   fallback_providers:
     - provider: vertex
       model: google/gemini-3.8-flash
   ```

2. Start a session (CLI or gateway) and make the primary fail once for any reason that activates the fallback (outage, 429, an unrelated 4xx). In my case the first fallback came from an unrelated 422 on a replayed `reasoning` field.
3. On that turn, let the Vertex fallback make at least one tool call (it returns `extra_content.google.thought_signature`).
4. Send another message. The primary is restored, receives the Vertex signatures, returns 422, and the fallback runs the turn. Every later turn does the same.

Offline check of the gate (run from the repo root, no network):

```python
from agent.transports.chat_completions import ChatCompletionsTransport
from agent.reasoning_carriers import shape_wire_carriers

SIG = "minted-by-vertex"
history = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "list files"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "c1", "type": "function",
        "function": {"name": "terminal", "arguments": "{}"},
        "extra_content": {"google": {"thought_signature": SIG}}}]},
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c1", "content": "ok"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "Done.", "reasoning_details": [
        {"type": "hermes.native_assistant", "extra_content": {"google": {"thought_signature": SIG}}}]},
    {"role": "user", "content": "next"},
]
base = "https://gateway.example/v1"
for model in ("gemini-3.8-flash", "my-alias"):
    wire = shape_wire_carriers(history, model=model, base_url=base)
    wire = ChatCompletionsTransport().convert_messages(wire, model=model, base_url=base, provider="custom")
    print(model, sum(str(m).count(SIG) for m in wire))
```

Output at 8f5693af41:

```
gemini-3.8-flash 2
my-alias 0
```

Both Vertex signatures (the tool-call one and the text-turn one) go to the custom gateway only because the model id contains `gemini`.

### Expected Behavior

- A thought signature is replayed only to the route that minted it. Signatures from another route are left off the wire, and stored history keeps them so a later return to the minting route can still replay them. This is the rule Hermes already applies to Codex encrypted reasoning items and to private `<provider>.native_assistant` reasoning records.
- If a route still rejects replayed signed reasoning, Hermes strips the signatures and retries once on the same provider, and remembers that for the session, instead of aborting to the fallback on every turn.

### Actual Behavior

- The primary gets the fallback's signatures on every later turn and answers 422 within 0.2 to 0.7 s of the turn starting.
- The 422 is not retried or repaired. `Fallback activated` fires and the whole turn runs on Vertex.
- Each fallback turn stores more Vertex signatures, so the session never recovers by itself.

Measured on one long-lived gateway session:

- The first two fallbacks in the session were caused by a different 422 (the gateway rejecting a replayed `reasoning` field, a separate problem). Those two fallback turns stored 11 assistant messages carrying Vertex-minted signatures.
- Every later user turn (4 of 4) then hit the signature 422 above and ran entirely on Vertex: 16 main calls and 2 background-review calls, each with 128k to 150k input tokens. They stored 16 more signed messages, 27 in total (22 on tool calls, 5 on text turns).
- After the first fallback the primary did not serve a single request in that session. Across all its fallback turns the session made 29 Vertex calls, about $1.40 of estimated metered usage.
- For comparison, a fresh session on the same primary made 90 calls with 0 errors, and its history had 0 signatures (the gateway returned none).

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)
Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram (where I saw it; the code path is not platform-specific)

### Debug Report

Not attached: `hermes debug share` would upload config and logs that include private endpoint details. Sanitized excerpts are below, and I can share more on request.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (LXD container)

### Python Version

3.14.7

### Hermes Version

`hermes --version`: v0.22.2+2123.g8f5693a.dirty (2026.9.24), upstream 8f5693af41, OpenAI SDK 2.24.0. The only local change is in `gateway/session_controls.py` and does not touch this path. Between 8f5693af41 and `main` at 9cb34e9e28 (2026-10-19), none of the files below changed except `agent/error_classifier.py`, which only gained an unrelated reasoning-effort rule.

### Additional Logs / Traceback

One turn, with session, thread and endpoint fields redacted:

```
INFO agent.turn_context: conversation turn: session=<redacted> model=gemini-3.8-flash provider=custom platform=telegram history=135 msg=<redacted>
ERROR agent.chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 422 - {'error': {'code': None, 'message': 'signed or encrypted reasoning from another provider has no representation in Gemini generateContent for <upstream>; request <id>', 'param': None, 'type': 'invalid_request_error'}}
WARNING agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3, not retryable) error_type=UnprocessableEntityError provider=custom base_url=<redacted> model=gemini-3.8-flash summary=HTTP 422: signed or encrypted reasoning from another provider has no representation in Gemini genera
INFO agent.chat_completion_helpers: Fallback activated: gemini-3.8-flash → google/gemini-3.8-flash (vertex)
INFO agent.conversation_loop: API call #1: model=google/gemini-3.8-flash provider=vertex in=128311 out=10 total=128321 latency=8.2s
```

The same sequence repeats on every later user turn of the session.

### Root Cause Analysis

Line numbers are for 8f5693af41. They are the same on `main` (9cb34e9e28) except in `agent/error_classifier.py`, where the `main` lines are given in brackets.

1. **Signatures are stored without their issuer.**
   - Tool-call `extra_content` is copied verbatim into history: `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:1629-1631` (`_assistant_tool_call_dict`).
   - The text-turn signature is stored as a `hermes.native_assistant` record: `agent/reasoning_carriers.py:42-50` (`carrier_record`), attached at `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:1734-1738`.
   - Neither records the provider, host or model that produced the signature.

2. **The replay gate checks the target, not the origin.** `_model_consumes_thought_signature` (`agent/transports/chat_completions.py:271-284`) returns True when the model id contains `gemini` or `gemma`, the provider is gemini, vertex or copilot, or the host is a Google host. That one predicate decides replay in three places:
   - Tool calls: `convert_messages` (`chat_completions.py:534`) through `_sanitize_message` (`:499-502`).
   - Text turns: `_route_reads` (`agent/reasoning_carriers.py:88-96`, model only) through `shape_wire_carriers` (`:139-147`), called at `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:1466-1467`.
   - The strict-API sanitizer: `agent/reasoning_params.py:222-236`.

   So any Gemini-looking target receives every Gemini signature in the history, whoever minted it. The docstring at `chat_completions.py:454-456` states the intended rule for private carriers ("another provider's signed replay is meaningless (or rejected) elsewhere, and stored history keeps it for a return to the original provider"), but it is enforced only for `reasoning_details` records whose type a profile declares, not for Gemini signatures. Codex Responses already does this properly: it stamps `_issuer_kind` / `_issuer_model` and drops foreign items at replay (`agent/codex_responses_adapter.py:22-36`, `:467-500`).

3. **Nothing recovers from the rejection.**
   - The 422 goes through `_classify_image_tool_422` to `_V_FORMAT_ERROR` (abort and fall back): `agent/error_classifier.py:1215-1219` [1246-1250], `:1229` [1260], `:473`.
   - The `thinking_signature` repair in `agent/turn_recovery.py:454-484` is reached only by Anthropic-style 400s (`error_classifier.py:860-863` [887-890]) and strips only `reasoning_details`.
   - `record_reasoning_field_rejection` (`agent/message_sanitization.py:978`) handles only named reasoning fields with unknown-field wording.
   - Nothing strips `extra_content`.

4. **Turn-scoped fallback makes it permanent.** `restore_primary_runtime` (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:1428-1492`) runs at the start of every turn (`agent/turn_context.py:1079`). Each turn therefore replays the poisoned history to the primary, gets the 422, falls back and adds more foreign signatures.

### Proposed Fix

1. **Stamp the issuer when the signature is captured.** Add the minting route to the tool-call `extra_content` and to the `hermes.native_assistant` record, for example `(provider, base_url host, model)` from the existing `reasoning_route_key` (`agent/message_sanitization.py:945`), as Codex does with `_issuer_kind` / `_issuer_model`. Keep the stamp off the wire.
2. **Replay a signature only to the route that minted it.** In `_sanitize_message`, `_shape` / `_route_reads` and `_sanitize_tool_calls_for_strict_api`, keep a signature only when its stamp matches the active route. Unstamped legacy history can keep today's behaviour. When a Gemini 3 target needs a signature on a tool call whose own signature was dropped, send the `skip_thought_signature_validator` sentinel, which the native adapter already uses (`agent/gemini_native_adapter.py:79-81`, `:351`) and open PR #104345 adds to the chat-completions transport.
3. **Add a safety net.** On chat-completions routes, treat a 400 or 422 whose body mentions signed or encrypted reasoning or a thought signature as a signature rejection. Strip `extra_content` from the request for one retry on the same provider, and record it per route for the session the way `record_reasoning_field_rejection` does, so the cost is one failed request per session at most.

Related:
- #36907 is the Gemini to Gemma direction. The fix proposed there (#49218) narrows the model-family predicate, which cannot help when both routes serve Gemini.
- Open PR #116252 adds recovery for Gemini's own 400 "Invalid thought signature", but its match (status 400 and "thought signature" in the body) would not catch a 422 with this wording, and it strips canonical history.
- #136486 has the same "rejection never learned, every turn falls back" shape for a different field.

**Workaround:** start a new session (`/new`). I also set a daily session reset on the gateway so a session cannot stay stuck on the fallback for days.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.body:
On Hermes Desktop 0.22.0 on Windows, connected to a shared Hermes backend 0.22.2, multiple idle conversations can remain blank with the Loading session overlay while the footer says Backend ready.

A target-only native SDK openSession refresh with refreshInPlace:true, awaitHydration:true and expectHistory:true recovered the affected conversations. We verified visible transcript content afterward, no new messages added, and preserved drafts and tab layout. No restart, message replay, source edit or injected CSS was used. This is a recovery workaround, not prevention.

A separate warm-tab trace attributed most of the blocking time to style recalculation forced during scroll restoration. That does not establish the cause of the persistent loader. Hide code diffs improved measured switching time but did not resolve the reported severe lag.

We could not find a supported setting for ordinary chat-pane retention, transcript render budgets or scroll restoration in the installed SDK and reviewed official policy owners. Lowering retention is an unproven candidate and may increase remount cost.

Please advise which bounded, sanitized diagnostics would help identify the loader failure and an official correction. We are avoiding private patches so stock updates remain maintainable.

prs.title: feat(line): native outbound file delivery via send_document
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Implements native outbound file/document delivery (`send_document`) in `LineAdapter` using LINE Messaging API's native `file` message type.

Previously, `LineAdapter` did not implement `send_document()`, falling back to `BasePlatformAdapter`'s generic notice: *"File delivery is not supported on this platform"*. When agents generated reports, PDFs, CSVs, patches, or downloadable files, users on LINE could not receive them.

LINE Messaging API natively supports file messages (`type: "file"`), requiring:
- `title`: File name (capped at 100 characters per LINE API specification).
- `size`: File size in bytes (up to 300 MB limit).
- `originalContentUrl`: Public HTTPS URL serving the file.

This PR adds:
1. `LINE_FILE_MAX_BYTES = 300 * 1024 * 1024` and registers `"file"` in `_OUTBOUND_MEDIA`.
2. Implements `send_document()` on `LineAdapter`, serving the file over HTTPS via `_serve_file()`, enforcing title truncation (100 characters), extracting size, and delivering the native file message along with an optional text caption bubble.
3. Updates `_check_media_file()` docstring and `platform_hint` to reflect document/file delivery support.
4. Comprehensive unit test suite in `tests/gateway/test_line_plugin.py` covering successful file delivery, custom file names, title truncation, caption attachment, missing file errors, missing public URL checks, and size limit checks.

## Related Issue

Fixes #

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/line/adapter.py`:
  - Added `LINE_FILE_MAX_BYTES` (300 MB).
  - Added `"file"` entry to `_OUTBOUND_MEDIA`.
  - Implemented `send_document()` in `LineAdapter`.
  - Updated `_check_media_file()` docstring and `platform_hint` in `register()`.
- `tests/gateway/test_line_plugin.py`:
  - Added `TestSendDocument` test class covering:
    - `test_send_document_success`: Verifies message shape (`type: "file"`, `title`, `size`, `originalContentUrl`).
    - `test_send_document_with_caption`: Verifies multi-message batching of file + caption.
    - `test_send_document_custom_file_name_and_truncation`: Verifies custom `file_name` and title truncation to 100 characters.
    - `test_send_document_file_not_found`: Verifies preflight error for non-existent paths.
    - `test_send_document_blocked_without_public_url`: Verifies public HTTPS URL requirement.
    - `test_send_document_size_limit_exceeded`: Verifies rejection when file exceeds 300 MB.

1. Run unit tests:

prs.title: fix(deps): bump npm packages to clear apps/desktop audit findings (C0 H0)
prs.body:
## Summary

`apps/desktop` is **not** one of the npm scopes `hermes doctor` audits (`--workspaces=false` on the root, `--workspace web`, `--workspace ui-tui`, and the WhatsApp bridge), and it carried advisories the rest of the tree did not:

```
apps/desktop  C2 H3 M6 L8  total 19
  CRITICAL  simple-git <=4.0.1
  CRITICAL  @simple-git/argv-parser <2.0.1
  HIGH      electron <=41.10.5
  HIGH      @xmldom/xmldom <=0.8.14
  HIGH      extract-zip *
```

This brings it to **C0 H0** without touching the scopes `hermes doctor` does audit (they stay at 0).

## Changes

**`apps/desktop/package.json`**

- `simple-git` 3.36.0 → 4.0.2 — closes both criticals. v4 is breaking and the app is adapted:
  - the named import replaces the removed default export (`git-review-ops.ts`);
  - v4 drops guarded env keys from the spawn env and throws when one is passed explicitly, so the
    Windows no-console path pre-filters the env via a new `gitEnvForSimpleGit()`. The filter keeps
    `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` (declared through the new `allowEnvironment` option) and the `HERMES_*` host
    markers, and drops `GIT_*`, `EDITOR`, `VISUAL`, `PAGER` — strictly more restrictive than v3, without
    enabling the `allowUnsafeEditor` / `allowUnsafePager` / `allowUnsafeSshCommand` escape hatches.
  - v4 accepts a restricted custom binary without v3's console warning; the test now asserts the
    warning is gone.
  - `execGit` (push/auth) does not go through simple-git and keeps the inherited env.
- `electron` 40.10.2 → 41.10.7 — closes the sandbox HIGHs. The 40 series has no patch for
  `GHSA-9f4c-93c8-jc8g`; OSV reports **zero** advisories for 41.10.7.

**`package.json` (root)**

- `overrides`: `axios` 1.20.0, `joi` 18.2.9, `fast-uri` 3.1.8, `"@xmldom/xmldom@^0.8"` 0.8.15.
  The xmldom pin is range-scoped so the newer, non-vulnerable `0.9.10` copy under `tests-js` is not
  downgraded and `npm ls` stays free of `invalid` entries.
- `allowScripts`: `electron@40.10.2` → `electron@41.10.7`, so the postinstall that fetches the
  Electron binary still runs.

**`package-lock.json`** — regenerated for the Electron 41 tree (`@electron/get` 2.x, `got`,
`global-agent`, `roarr`, `sprintf-js` and `extract-zip` drop out; `@electron-internal/extract-zip`
comes in).

## Verification

```
npm audit --json --workspace apps/desktop            C0 H0 M2 L8
npm audit --json --workspace apps/desktop --omit=dev  C0 H0 M2 L8
npm audit --json --workspaces=false                   0
npm audit --json --workspace web                      0
npm audit --json --workspace ui-tui                   0
(cd plugins/platforms/photon/sidecar && npm audit)    0
npm ci --ignore-scripts                               exit 0
npm run typecheck                                     exit 0
npx eslint <4 changed electron files>                 exit 0
npx vitest run --project electron <2 test files>       22 passed
npm run build                                         exit 0
```

Every pin's `integrity` in the lockfile matches `npm view <pkg> dist.integrity`, and the lock has no
registry entry missing `resolved`+`integrity`.

## Review

Read-only audit by the security-audit profile: 9 gates, all `pass` after one correction round
(the `@xmldom/xmldom` lock entry was missing `resolved`/`integrity`; that was fixed and re-verified).
Reports: `/home/BG/.hermes/profiles/paulo/audits/t_f706ab89/` and `/home/BG/.hermes/profiles/paulo/audits/t_42f33c06/`.

## Caveats

- **The Electron 41 runtime is not exercised by this PR.** `npm run build` succeeds, but on a
  headless Linux host the Electron binary cannot start (`chrome-sandbox` is not setuid root), so
  boot, sandbox and updater behaviour are only proven by the upstream CI or on the maintainer's
  machine. Please treat the major Electron bump as needing a desktop smoke test.
- `extract-zip` (HIGH, `*`, no fixed release published) leaves the tree only as a consequence of the
  Electron bump — Electron 41 depends on `@electron-internal/extract-zip` instead.
- Residual, unchanged from the base: `@tailwindcss/typography` and `postcss-selector-parser`
  (moderate; the only fix is a breaking downgrade) and 8 low findings in the markdown renderer chain.
- `npm ls` still reports two `lightningcss` entries as `invalid`; those are pre-existing and
  byte-identical in the base lockfile.

prs.title: fix(lsp): native wrapper outranks staged POSIX shim across bases
prs.body:
## Symptom (Windows)

`_existing_binary()` returns the extensionless POSIX shim npm stages next to its `.cmd` wrapper,
and launching it dies with **WinError 193** — the failure mode this module's own docstring
documents as the thing to avoid. It happens whenever the shim and the wrapper live in *different*
base directories.

## Root cause (on `main`, with the lines)

The within-base ordering is already correct. `agent/lsp/install.py:94`
(`_native_binary_candidates`) returns platform-native candidates "most runnable first", and its
docstring at `:97`-`:100` states the hazard precisely:

> On Windows the `.cmd`/`.exe`/`.bat` wrappers come BEFORE the bare name: npm writes a POSIX
> `#!/bin/sh` shim under the bare name next to its `.cmd`, `os.access(X_OK)` is always true there,
> and `CreateProcess` on the shim fails with WinError 193.

The defect is in how the caller consumes that ordering. `agent/lsp/install.py:124`
(`_existing_binary`) iterates

```python
for staged in (c for base in bases for c in _native_binary_candidates(base, is_windows=win)):
```

That is **base-major**, so every candidate of base 1 is tested before any candidate of base 2.
With `bases = [hermes_lsp_bin_dir()/name, _npm_bin_dir()/name]`, base 1's bare staged shim
(`exists()` true, `os.access(X_OK)` true on Windows) is returned before base 2's genuine `.cmd`
wrapper is ever considered. The ordering guarantee the helper documents — and honours within one
base — does not survive being applied one base at a time.

## Fix

Hoist the native candidates across **all** bases above all bare paths: wrapper variants for every
base first, then the bare bases. Non-Windows behaviour is unchanged (`bases` as-is), and the
bare name stays as the documented last resort for genuinely extension-less executables.

Class check: this is the sibling call path of the already-correct helper, not a competing
implementation — `_native_binary_candidates` stays the single authority on suffix order, and the
fix composes it across bases rather than duplicating its logic.

## Tests

`tests/agent/lsp/test_windows_binary_resolution.py` — real files created on disk across two bases.

- On base (`0b10b9f8155`, fix absent): **3 failed** —
  `test_existing_binary_prefers_native_candidate_across_bases[.cmd | .exe | .bat]`.
- With the fix: **5 passed / 1 skipped**. The skip is the POSIX-precedence case on a Windows host,
  which is the expected platform split, not a coverage gap.

## Footprint

Rung 1: corrects ordering inside the existing resolution path. No new config, no new env var,
no change to the install recipes.

prs.title: fix(checkpoints): pre-stage size gate + process-tree kill on git timeout
prs.body:
## Symptom (this is a real, dated incident, not a hypothetical)

On 2026-10-11 a checkpoint capture against a watched workdir that contained a **1.2 TB VHDX**
staged the disk image. The capture's `git add -A` outlived its parent: on Windows a killed parent
does not reap children, so git kept writing `tmp_pack` files for **3.5 hours after the tool call
returned**, reaching **~310 GiB** of garbage in the shared store before anything stopped it. This
is the condition that later made the checkpoint store report over its configured cap.

## Root cause (on `main`, with the lines)

`tools/checkpoint_manager.py:357` (`_run_git`) is the single git entry point for the checkpoint
path. On timeout it terminates the child and returns; it never calls
`kill_process_tree()`, which already exists at `hermes_cli/_subprocess_compat.py:738` and is
exactly the Windows-correct tree kill. There is also no `start_new_session` / process-group
establishment, so there is no group to kill even if a caller tried. And nothing bounds what gets
staged: a watched directory is staged wholesale regardless of the size or kind of what's inside.

Confirmed absent on `origin/main` today: no `_stage_bytes_scan`, no `_MAX_STAGE_BYTES`, no
disk-image extension excludes, no `start_new_session`, no `kill_process_tree` call in the
checkpoint path (`grep` for each returns nothing in `tools/checkpoint_manager.py`).

## Fix — three layers, all in the existing path

1. **Refuse before staging.** `_stage_bytes_scan()` walks the workdir and sums candidate file
   size; if it exceeds `_MAX_STAGE_BYTES` (10 GiB), the capture fails *with a message naming the
   offending path* instead of starting a write it cannot finish. Disk-image extensions
   (`vhdx`, `vhd`, `qcow2`, `qcow`, `vmdk`, `evm`) are excluded from staging outright — a
   checkpoint of a raw VM disk is never useful.
2. **Make the kill real.** Child git processes are started in their own session
   (`start_new_session`) and a timeout now calls `kill_process_tree()`, so the tree dies on
   Windows instead of orphaning.
3. **Nested gitlinks** are handled so a nested repo does not defeat the scan.

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_checkpoint_incomplete_nested_git.py` — real temp workdirs, real git.

- On base: **1 failed** (the nested/incomplete case).
- With the fix: **1 passed**.

## Footprint

Rung 1: hardens the existing checkpoint path using the existing `kill_process_tree` helper. No
new tool, no new env var, no config surface (the cap is a module constant, deliberately not a
user-facing knob — behaviour knobs belong in `config.yaml` and this one has no legitimate reason
to move).

prs.title: fix(tools): judge the tool-result envelope, not payload words
prs.body:
## Symptom

Structured tool failures are reported as successes. A tool result of `{"ok": false}` — the shape
our own tools emit — reaches the guardrail as "no failure", so the retry/blocking logic never
sees it. Conversely `{"ok": true, "error": null, "message": "complete"}` is reported as a failure
because the *keys* `error`/`message` are present.

## Root cause (on `main`, with the lines)

Two independent defects, both found by running a payload-contract table rather than by reading
the diff:

1. `agent/tool_guardrails.py:219` (`classify_tool_failure`) parses the result with
   `safe_json_loads()`, defined at `utils.py:601` as
   `try: json.loads(text) except (JSONDecodeError, TypeError, ValueError): return default`.
   Passing an already-parsed **dict** raises `TypeError` inside `json.loads`, so the call returns
   `None` — every dict-shaped tool result silently classifies as success. Verified directly:
   `safe_json_loads({"ok": False})` → `None`.
2. `agent/display.py:1018` (`_detect_tool_failure`) gates on key *presence* (`"error" in data`)
   and then on `data.get("error") or data.get("message")`, i.e. it reads payload vocabulary
   instead of the envelope. Success payloads carrying a null `error` field read as failures;
   `{"success": false}` reads as success.

## Fix

Judge the **envelope**, not the words inside the payload. Adds
`structured_tool_result_failed()` in `agent/tool_result_classification.py`, which accepts the
dict-shaped result directly (no re-parse) and decides from envelope keys. Upstream's
`has_failure_marker()` and `shape_failure_error()` are kept and remain the authority for
text-shaped results; substring scanning now runs **only** on genuinely unparseable text.

Class check: both consumers of failure classification (`display`, `guardrails`) route through the
new predicate, so the fix is not one-sided — the same payload cannot read as failed in the UI and
successful in the guardrail.

## Tests

`tests/agent/test_tool_failure_payload_semantics.py` — a payload contract table over envelope
shapes, not source reading.

- On base (`origin/main`, fix absent): **108 failed / 116 passed**.
- With the fix: **224 passed / 0 failed** via `scripts/run_tests.sh`.

`python scripts/check` (CI's blocking lint set, 12 checks) passes.

## Footprint

Rung 1 of the ladder: extends existing classification code in place. No new tool, no new
`HERMES_*` variable, no new config key.

prs.title: fix(desktop): keep primary session rows' owner when the window is pinned to another gateway
prs.body:
## Problem
With two gateways registered (this device + an SSH box), viewing the SSH gateway with **Gateway & profile** grouping shows a local-only profile (e.g. `laptop`) nested under the SSH gateway. Clicking its sessions loads forever, and the group's Screen portal sits on an unknown status, because Desktop dials `conn:<ssh>::laptop`, a profile that doesn't exist on that host (`Passive read: no warm backend for "conn:butler::laptop"`).

## Cause
For a registry-pinned all-profiles list, `mergeRemoteProfileSessions` merges the primary backend's local rows with the registry rows. The primary rows carry no `connection_id`, and the renderer's `stampActiveConnectionOwner` stamps every untagged row with the **active** connection, so the local rows get filed under the pinned remote gateway.

## Fix
- `tagPrimarySessionRows` (profile-session-routing.ts) fills in `connection_id` on untagged primary-aggregate rows with the connection that actually served them. It does nothing when the request is unpinned or pinned to the primary itself, so single-gateway and on-primary behavior is unchanged.
- The aggregate and sidebar-slice paths pass the pinned connection id through. The primary's connection id is resolved passively (`ensureBackend(null, { passive: true })`, falling back to `local`), so a sidebar refresh never dials.

## Tests
- New unit test in `profile-session-routing.test.ts` (79/79 pass)
- `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit` clean; eslint has no new findings

prs.title: fix(mcp): one repeatedly rejected tool no longer pauses every tool on the server (#47851, salvage #114077)
prs.body:
When one MCP tool keeps rejecting calls, Hermes now pauses only that tool. Before this, the whole server was paused for 60 s, including the sibling tool the model needed to recover (`search` after a failed `edit`).

Fixes #47851. Salvage of #114077 by @liuhao1024, whose two commits are cherry-picked with authorship intact. Inspired by paperclipai/paperclip#16890 ("keep sibling tools available after transient calls"), which fixed the same symptom in their MCP gateway.

## Changes
- `tools/mcp_tool.py`: `_bump_server_error(..., application=True, tool_name=…)` records each tool that struck during an all-application streak (`_server_breaker_application_tool`, a set). A transport strike anywhere in the streak clears the scoping, so the whole server is blocked again exactly as #10447 requires.
- `tools/mcp_tool_handlers.py`: `_check_circuit_breaker(server, tool)` lets tools that never struck through while the open state is application-only. `tool_name` now reaches every path that records an outcome: first attempt, stdio respawn retry, OAuth retry and session-expired retry. The open-breaker message names the paused tool and offers "use a different tool on this server".
- When a sibling tool succeeds, the breaker closes through the existing `_reset_server_error` health signal.

**Unchanged:** the strike accounting (business errors still count, per #10447), the threshold/cooldown, and whole-server blocking for any transport failure. No new config.

## Hardening on top of #114077
- Rebased across ~20k commits of main: resolved the `native_images` handler return and the `_NEEDS_REAUTH_MSG` detail arg, and moved the `Dict` annotations to `dict`.
- Cut the tests from 3 to 2 invariant tests by folding the "two broken tools don't unblock each other" case into the sibling-tool test.

## Validation
| | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| **Live repro:** real `hermes chat -q` (OpenRouter, claude-haiku-4.5) + real stdio MCP server (`edit` always errors, `search` works), 3 edit calls then search; results read from the run's `state.db` | 4th edit: "MCP server 'vault' rejected the last 3 calls…"; **search: same pause error, server never reached** (server log: 3 edit, 0 search) | 4th edit: "The last 3 calls to MCP tool 'edit'… were rejected… use a different tool on this server"; **search: real result** (server log: 3 edit, 1 search) |
| `tests/tools/test_mcp_circuit_breaker.py` | 2 new tests FAIL | 10/10 pass |
| `scripts/check --only health` | | 0 blocking, 0 advisory |

Other `tests/tools -k mcp` reds (`test_explicit_mcp_schema_reload`, `test_mcp_shared_connection_resolved_identity`) fail the same way on a pristine origin/main tree in this environment, so they are unrelated.

**Root cause:** the breaker key is per server, so an open state reached only because the server returned `isError` for one tool also short-circuited every other tool on a healthy transport.

## Ours vs Paperclip (#16890)
Paperclip stopped marking the whole connection unhealthy for non-auth call failures (timeouts, 5xx, JSON-RPC errors), so health is judged per invocation. Hermes keeps its stricter #10447 rule (repeated failures still pause a retry storm), but scopes the pause to the tools that failed when the transport is provably fine. That keeps the retry-storm protection Paperclip gave up while fixing the same "healthy sibling tools disappear" symptom.

## Infographic
![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaf1601/wniIEu6L9MaD7Jy51VyYW_gbdMi1n5.png)

prs.title: Stable installs on the gateway runtime are held at their build, not offered or refused v0.22.2 (#140729, #139099; salvage #140215 #140778)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A stable-channel install whose sessions already use the gateway runtime no longer gets stuck on v0.22.2. Desktop, the dashboard and `hermes update --check` stop offering it, and `hermes update` holds the install where it is (exit 0) instead of refusing it as a downgrade on every attempt.

This merges the two halves that were open separately, plus the review findings on both:

- **#140215** (the check side): `source_check` and `--check` ask the same `downgrade_refusal` question the updater asks, and report the release as **held** rather than available.
- **#140778** (the apply side, @unsupportedpastels carrying @arcabotai's #140741): when the *channel* picks a release that predates the runtime, `hermes update` stays on HEAD, says why, and finishes like an up-to-date run. An explicit `--branch` to a pre-runtime ref is still refused.

Each half alone leaves a broken loop. With only the check fix, Desktop says "held" but `hermes update` still exits 1. With only the apply fix, Desktop keeps offering a release the update then holds. Together the offer and the update agree.

```
→ This build is newer than the stable release d923a5eb487a: that release predates the gateway runtime your sessions use, so there is nothing to update to yet.
  Hermes stays on f2a4b4393280 until a newer stable release ships. To follow every commit instead: `hermes update --set-channel main`.
✓ Holding at this build until a newer stable release ships.
```

## Related Issue

Fixes #140729
Fixes #139099 (the "shouldn't say there is an update available" half; teknium: *"The block on 'updating backwards' is intended - not a bug. The bug is the error should make it clearer … and shouldn't say there is an update available"*)
Refs #134889 (GW-19), #140762

Supersedes #140215 and #140778. Both stay open until this lands.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

Every contributor commit is cherry-picked unchanged with its authorship. The only conflict was both PRs adding a test at the end of `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_downgrade_guard.py`; both are kept.

**From #140215** (@ethernet8023)
- `update_downgrade_guard.would_refuse`: the read-only twin of `downgrade_refusal`, sharing its profile scan and target test, so the check and the update cannot disagree.
- `source_check` reports `updateAvailable: false, held: "downgrade"`; `channelProtocol` 1 → 2 so old cached statuses get re-checked.
- `hermes update --check` prints "Holding at this build".
- Desktop: `held` on `DesktopUpdateStatus`, a `heldBody` line, copy in all 9 locales.

**From #140778** (@arcabotai, @unsupportedpastels)
- `hold_channel_release_behind_runtime` in `update_cmd_check.py`: for a channel-selected release only, pins the target to HEAD when `downgrade_refusal` would refuse it.
- "This build is newer than" (the release sits beside `main`, not behind it) and a held closing line instead of "✓ Already up to date!".
- `test_the_runtime_schema_marker_is_still_in_this_trees_state_schema`: if the DDL drifts from the marker, CI fails instead of the hold silently pinning installs.

**Follow-up 1: Greptile's three findings on #140215**
- `--check` asked the rollback question before the refusal, so a release this checkout already contains printed "`hermes update` moves it back to that release" while the update holds. The refusal now comes first.
- The 24h `source_check` cache kept the verdict, so an offer cached before the first runtime turn stayed on offer after it. The hold is re-asked on cached channel results (a local git + sqlite check, no network).
- The dashboard `/api/hermes/update/check` endpoint turned the hold's `behind: 0` into "You're on the latest version." Desktop's remote-backend card also returned its generic line before looking at `held`. The endpoint now carries `held` + the release version, `mapBackendCheck` keeps them, and the held line comes before the backend fallback.

**Follow-up 2: @DavidMetcalfe's review on #140215**
An install that tracks only `main` never has a release cut beside it until `hermes update` fetches it. The check never fetches, so `cat-file -e` failed, the guard's "a git failure proves nothing" rule answered "offer", and Desktop kept the green Update button for exactly the installs #139099 is about. (The maintainer clone I checked does not have `d923a5eb487a` locally.)
- `target_predates_runtime` takes an optional `remote` answer for a target that is not local. The check surfaces pass one that lists the release's root tree from the GitHub API and reads its `hermes_state*.py` from raw.githubusercontent.com (no API quota). Both paths share the marker and the module pattern (`STATE_MODULES`, `defines_runtime`), so they cannot drift.
- It only runs when a store has runtime history and the commit is absent. A definite verdict is cached per SHA for good (a commit's tree never changes). Any failure (truncated tree, unreadable module, network) answers "can't tell" and keeps the old behaviour (offered).
- `hermes update` is unchanged: it fetches the release first and stays git-only.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_channel_release_hold.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_downgrade_guard.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_downgrade_guard_named_profile.py tests/hermes_cli/test_source_check.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_cmd_check.py`
2. Desktop: `npx vitest run src/store/updates-backend-check.test.ts src/components/update-status.test.tsx` from `apps/desktop`.

**Red without each fix** (source hunk reverted, tests kept):

| Test | Fails without |
|---|---|
| `test_update_channel_release_hold.py`, 4 hold cases (#140778) | the hold: `SystemExit: 1` at the downgrade refusal |
| `test_check_holds_a_release_that_update_would_refuse[in-history]` | refusal before rollback in `--check` |
| `test_stable_release_the_updater_refuses_is_held_not_offered[False]` (cached offer) | the hold on cached results |
| `updates-backend-check.test.ts`: "names a held backend…" | endpoint/`mapBackendCheck`/ordering; got "The backend is running the latest version." |
| `test_an_unfetched_release_is_judged_from_github[True]` | the GitHub lookup. The release exists only on origin, and the test asserts it is not local first |

**Live probe** (real git, release tag cut beside `main` and before the runtime, install cloned with `main` only so the release commit is absent, real runtime ledger rows in `state.db`; only the GitHub responses are served from loopback):

| Case | `origin/main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| no runtime history | offered | offered |
| runtime history, cached check | offered | **held** |
| runtime history, forced check | offered | **held** |
| dashboard `/update/check` | "You're on the latest version." / offered | carries `held`, held message |

**Real GitHub**, `_github_predates_runtime` on real commits:

| Release | Verdict | Requests | Second call |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.22.2 `d923a5eb487a` | predates the runtime | 34 (1 API + 33 raw, ~1.1 MB, all modules lack the marker) | 0, cached |
| current `main` | has the runtime | 4 (stops at the first match) | 0, cached |

The `hermes update` CLI runs (reported topology, Desktop hand-off argv `--yes --keep-stash --channel stable`, recorded stable channel, `--branch` still refused, control) are in teknium's review and @unsupportedpastels' retest on #140778. That code is unchanged here, and its tests pass on this base.

**Suites:** every test file that references the update, check or guard code (`_cmd_update_impl`, `downgrade_refusal`, `update_downgrade_guard`, `update_cmd_check`, `select_apply_target`, `_finish_already_up_to_date`, `check_for_updates`, `check_hermes_update`, `source_check`): 50 files, 853 passed, 0 failed, 48 skipped. Desktop: `tsc --noEmit` (both configs), eslint, prettier, vitest 33 passed.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate (#140741 closed into #140778; #140742 closed; no other open PR touches this)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (related suites only, see above; CI runs the full matrix)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: NixOS (Linux 7.2)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A (git probes go through the existing no-prompt runners; `check-windows-footguns.py` clean; not run on real Windows or macOS)
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Credit

- @arcabotai (stewarded by @felirami): the apply-side hold, the wording and closing-line fix, the schema-marker pin (#140741, carried on #140778).
- @unsupportedpastels: carried #140741 into #140778, the reported, Desktop and recorded-stable test shapes, and the move out of `update_cmd.py`.
- @DavidMetcalfe: the unfetched-release gap and the GitHub-lookup approach (`Co-authored-by` on that commit). He also reviewed #140741.

prs.title: fix(agent): bound stale-stream re-kills so a wedged reader cannot loop forever
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Bounds the stale-stream re-kill loop. When a stale kill's socket shutdown does not unblock the reader, the monitor used to re-kill the same attempt every stale window forever: `_count_stale_attempt` counts each attempt once **by design** (`_stale_counted_attempts`), and the cross-call breaker (`_check_stale_giveup`) is only consulted when a NEW call starts — which never happens while the worker is parked. Every re-kill also refreshed the activity heartbeat (`_touch_activity`), so the kanban wedge reclaim (`DEFAULT_CLAIM_HEARTBEAT_MAX_STALE_SECONDS`) never saw the worker as wedged either. #141098 measured 1,231 re-kills over 3.5 days with a fresh `last_heartbeat_at` throughout.

An attempt is now abandoned once it has been re-killed past its patience window: the **later of three stale windows and the attempt's read timeout**. Wall clock, not a kill count — a short stale budget re-fires many times inside one read timeout, so a count bound would either abandon recoverable attempts or let production re-kill for hours. The windows floor keeps the bound on the loop's own clock, so the verdict does not *depend* on the read timeout firing (in #141098 it never did, across 3.5 days of re-kills); the read-timeout leg keeps it from preempting the one mechanism that can still end a parked read by itself. On abandonment:

- the monitor stops killing and returns. **Worker path:** `run()` raises, and the message carries the same give-up phrases as `_check_stale_giveup`'s error, so it classifies as `timeout` + `_ABORT_FALLBACK` and the caller **walks its fallback chain** instead of replaying the same wedged route until its retry budget is gone. **Inline path** (`should_use_direct_api_call`: cron turns, delegated children): the caller is parked in the read on its own thread, so the verdict *cannot* fail that call — it ends the re-kill loop, the status churn and the heartbeats, and the read timeout (or a turn-level watchdog) remains the exit. Stated in `_abandon_stale_attempt`;
- a wedged attempt claims no liveness from any source: re-kills stop touching the heartbeat, `_heartbeat()` returns without touching, and only the first kill of an attempt shows the `reconnecting...` status (the abandonment emits its own line);
- the attempt's own socket-shutdown recovery is untouched: the abandon verdict cannot preempt the read timeout, because the window starts at the first kill, which is already inside it.

This is the failure-mode half of the same family as #110769/#141098; the first-kill reconnect path, the cross-call breaker accounting, and `_abort_for_interrupt` are unchanged. Related: #139348 (post-chunk idle bound / monitor resilience) touches the same monitor but not this accounting — rebased on `fd905d2926`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #141098

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/chat_completion_stream_monitor.py` — new `_stale_kill_patience`, `_note_stale_kill` (per-attempt re-kill bookkeeping + display/liveness), `_abandon_stale_attempt`, `_attempt_is_wedged`, `_raise_wedged_stream`; the monitor loop returns once the current attempt is wedged.
- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` — `_count_stale_attempt` reports whether it counted; `_kill_stale_stream` delegates its tail to `_note_stale_kill`; `run()` raises the actionable wedge error instead of returning `None` for an abandoned call.
- `tests/agent/test_stream_stale_rekill_bounded.py` — new: the monitor stops, the window is per attempt and holds on the loop's own clock, a wedged attempt claims no liveness (heartbeat included), the raised error classifies for fallback, the wedged call ends with the error, and a recoverable kill is never called wedged.

Review follow-ups on the four findings from @ranggaoscar are in `d863ff4b03`: the wedge error moved off `unknown`/no-fallback onto the give-up classification, liveness is gated at every source (heartbeat included) instead of only the kill path, the inline limitation is stated where it applies, and the patience window was re-anchored on the loop's own clock.

## How to Test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_stream_stale_rekill_bounded.py -q
# head (d863ff4b03): 7 passed
# base (main @ 5fc490e2b3, same test file copied into a clean worktree): 6 failed, 1 passed
```

Base failures (`agent/` untouched at `5fc490e2b3`):

```

  AssertionError: the monitor kept re-killing a stream whose reader never unwound
  (32 kills in 10s and still running)
FAILED test_wedged_stream_fails_the_call_instead_of_re_killing_forever
  AssertionError: the call never ended: the monitor re-killed a reader the kill could not unblock
FAILED test_the_patience_window_is_per_attempt
FAILED test_the_bounds_floor_is_the_loops_own_windows
FAILED test_a_wedged_attempt_claims_no_liveness_from_the_heartbeat
FAILED test_the_wedge_error_classifies_as_a_transport_failure_for_fallback
  AttributeError: '_StreamingCall' object has no attribute '_note_stale_kill'   # new API
PASSED test_a_kill_that_does_unblock_the_reader_is_not_called_wedged            # green on base: the common path
```

Regression set on the same machine (Windows 11, Python 3.14.7):

```

  tests/agent/test_stream_stale_circuit_breaker.py tests/agent/test_stream_wait_notice.py \
  tests/agent/test_local_prompt_progress.py tests/agent/test_stream_interrupt_abort_socket.py \

  tests/agent/test_direct_contexts_stream_inline.py -q
# 61 passed, 2 failed — both failures pre-existing on this host (named below)
```

directory sweeps were not run): **1083 passed, 38 skipped, 7 failed**, and all 7 failures reproduce

prs.title: fix(gateway): admit completion wakes whose thread metadata drifted
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A Discord thread's persisted origin keeps its creation-time `chat_name` plus the `auto_thread_created` / `auto_thread_initial_name` creation flags, while a later in-thread message carries the thread's *current* title and no flags. When a background `delegate_task` child completed, `snapshot_automation` compared the latest committed native admission's full source against the wake's origin-derived source, so those three mutable keys raised `admission_conflict` (`RuntimeStoreError` at the source comparison). The wake became `WakeNotAccepted` → the delivery settled as a defer → `delivery_attempts` returned to 0 → the loop retried every ~5 s forever. The ledger stayed `state=completed, delivery_state=pending` and the parent never resumed until a human continuation recovered it.

This is the residual after #139026 (which fixed the same refusal for a `message_id`-only difference): per the follow-up report on the issue, the persisted origin versus the latest native admission still differed in exactly `auto_thread_created`, `auto_thread_initial_name` and `chat_name` after `message_id` was excluded.

The fix: none of these keys enters `build_session_key` or authorizes anyone (the session key is built from platform / chat_type / chat_id / thread_id / scope / participant), so they are joined with the already-excluded `message_id` reply anchor in a named `_NON_IDENTITY_SOURCE_KEYS` set that `_route_identity` strips before the comparison. Every routing/authorization identity check is unchanged: user, thread, scope/guild, parent channel, transport/platform, profile, adapter identity, and session ownership.

## Related Issue

Fixes #139135

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/session_automation.py` — `_route_identity` now strips `chat_name`, `auto_thread_created` and `auto_thread_initial_name` in addition to `message_id`, via a named `_NON_IDENTITY_SOURCE_KEYS` frozenset with a comment explaining why those keys are not routing/authorization identity; the comparison-site comment in `snapshot_automation` was updated to match.
- `tests/gateway/test_automation_notification_category.py` — added `_thread_native_owner` (a shared-thread session whose origin carries the creation-time title + auto-thread flags and whose latest native admission carries the renamed title without the flags) and two regressions: the drifted-metadata completion wake admits and stays idempotent, and a different speaker in the shared thread is still refused with `admission_conflict` (a shared thread's session key carries no user, so only this source comparison catches the impostor).

## How to Test

1. `python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_automation_notification_category.py -q` — 18 passed (16 pre-existing + 2 new).
2. Without the production change, `test_native_completion_wake_admits_when_thread_metadata_drifts` fails with `RuntimeStoreError: admission_conflict` raised from `snapshot_automation`'s source comparison — exactly the refusal the issue reporter reproduced offline — while the refusal-side test still passes, proving the new exclusion does not weaken identity checks.
3. Broader neighbourhood: `python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_authority_automation.py tests/gateway/test_automation_compression_media.py tests/gateway/test_automation_retry.py tests/gateway/test_busy_wake_admission.py tests/gateway/test_completion_admission_compression_race.py tests/gateway/test_admission_results.py tests/gateway/test_internal_wake_reply_anchor.py tests/gateway/test_watch_automation_identity.py tests/gateway/test_async_delegation_session_binding.py tests/gateway/test_native_admission_metadata.py tests/gateway/test_discord_admission_thread_exemption.py tests/gateway/test_completion_admission.py -q` — 115 passed. Observed result: all pass, including the #139026 reply-anchor and source-drift regressions.
4. `python scripts/check` — 12 checks, ok (0 blocking code-health findings).

prs.title: fix(state): treat the legacy 'webui' source label as a local account
prs.body:
## Symptom

Sessions persisted with `source = 'webui'` (relay / Android surfaces) are not recognised as
legacy-local. They fail `legacy_account_label()` and are therefore refused by
`authorize_history()` even when they belong to the local account — the history is present in the
DB and unreachable.

## Root cause (on `main`, with the line)

`hermes_state_local_migration.py:15`:

```python
LEGACY_LOCAL_SOURCES = frozenset({'cli', 'tui', 'gui', 'desktop', 'oneshot', 'tool', 'acp'})
```

`'webui'` is absent from both `LEGACY_LOCAL_SOURCES` and `LEGACY_CREATION_SOURCES`.

Per the rubric ("before you call it a bug, verify the claim **and** the intent"), I checked
whether this is a load-bearing exclusion: `git log -S webui` over the repo shows the label was
**never** present in either set. So this is an unhandled label, not a deliberate isolation —
unlike profile separation, which is intentional and is left completely alone here.

## Fix

Adds `'webui'` to `LEGACY_LOCAL_SOURCES`. Deliberately narrow:

- `LEGACY_CREATION_SOURCES` unchanged (`'webui'` is not a surface alias of anything).
- The **foreign-owner refusal path is untouched**: a row whose `user_id` belongs to another
  account still returns `legacy_account_label(row) is False`, keeps its `_owner_user()`, and
  `authorize_history()` still raises `reason='not_found'`. Adopting the label does not widen
  access to anyone else's history.

## Tests

`tests/gateway/test_legacy_webui_source.py` — imports `Principal`, `SessionDB`,
`validate_legacy_row`, `legacy_account_label`, `LEGACY_LOCAL_SOURCES`, `authorize_history` and
asserts behaviour against a temp DB (no source reading). Covers **both** directions: adoptable
when the owner matches, refused when the `user_id` is foreign.

- On base: **3 failed**.
- With the fix: **3 passed** via `scripts/run_tests.sh`.

## Footprint

Rung 1: one entry in an existing frozenset, wired into the existing migration/authorization
machinery.

prs.title: feat(webhook): publish delivery lifecycle events to plugins
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Webhook agent runs have no observer surface today. A plugin cannot learn that an authenticated delivery arrived, what body it carried before the route `script` rewrote it, or how the run ended. This PR publishes two `gateway_platform_event` types from the webhook adapter (payload `version: 1`), following the existing per-event contract style (Telegram/Discord):

- `delivery_received` — once per agent-run delivery (direct or coalesced settlement), after authentication, filters, idempotency and the route script, and before the run starts. Payload: `route`, `delivery_id`, `webhook_event_type`, `chat_id` (the per-delivery session chat), `profile`, `created_at`, `prompt`, `payload` (body after the script) and `raw_payload` (body as received when a script ran, else `None`).
- `delivery_completed` — the same fields plus `outcome` (`success` / `failure` / `cancelled`), once per delivery at the true end of the run (`on_processing_complete`), after cleanup of the per-delivery session has been attempted.

Use cases: audit trails and incident records for alarm webhooks, completion notifications, metrics — without patching the adapter.

## Design notes

- The snapshot lives in `event.metadata["webhook_lifecycle"]`, not in the TTL-pruned `_delivery_info`, so a completion after a long run still has its data, and it holds independent copies of the bodies, so both events describe the delivery as it arrived even if the run mutates `raw_message`. Completion is deduplicated via `event.metadata`, the same pattern as #80533, so the two compose.
- `_spawn_agent_run` keeps its synchronous, Task-returning interface (the coalescer depends on it); the task awaits the receipt event, then `handle_message`, so observers can key state on `chat_id` before any turn hook for that chat fires.
- Each event is a fresh deep copy, isolated from the run; the callbacks of the hook share that one copy (the dispatcher passes one payload to each), which the docs state. Route configuration (including the HMAC secret) and request headers are never included. Observer exceptions are logged at debug and never affect the run or session cleanup; callbacks run inline, so a slow observer delays dispatch (documented).
- The raw body is deep-copied only when the route has a `script`.
- `deliver_only` and `cron_job` routes do not fire these events (they have no agent-run lifecycle).
- Privacy: the payloads carry the full authenticated request body; the hooks docs say so explicitly, including that outbound webhooks subscribed to this hook receive it.
- Correlating the agent's final report is out of scope here: consumers match `post_llm_call` on the same chat, which needs the chat identity from #54452.

Related: #80531 / #80533 / #85645 (completion scripts at the same seam), #84834, #54452, #73559.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking; additive event types on an existing hook)
- [x] Tests
- [x] Documentation

## How to test

`python -m pytest -q tests/gateway/test_webhook_lifecycle_events.py tests/gateway/test_webhook_*.py tests/gateway/test_gateway_platform_event_hook.py`

The new tests cover: receipt before the run with the body before/after the script, the ingress body surviving a run that mutates `raw_message`, `raw_payload is None` without a script, a single completion with outcome, completion after `_delivery_info` pruning, observer copy isolation, failing/absent observers, coalesced settlement reporting the settled event, and no events for `deliver_only`.
