prs.title: fix(models): accept a bare-array /models payload in probe_api_models
prs.body:
## Problem

`probe_api_models()` assumes every `/models` response is the OpenAI envelope:

```python
for item in data.get("data", []):      # hermes_cli/models.py:2721
```

Providers that answer with a **bare JSON array** of model objects raise
`AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`. Together AI does exactly that today
(`https://api.together.ai/v1/models` → top-level array of 269 objects).

The probe's caller swallows the exception (`_discover_endpoint_models()` →
`except Exception: pass`), so discovery returns `None` and the picker falls back to the
persisted `providers.<slug>.models` catalog. Net effect on the user: **that provider's model
list is frozen**, new models never appear, and "Refresh Models" re-fails identically because
the crash is deterministic. Nothing is logged.

Fixes #141782.

## Approach

The module already has the normalizer for both shapes — `_payload_items()`:

```python
data = payload.get("data", []) if isinstance(payload, dict) else payload
return [item for item in data if isinstance(item, dict)] if isinstance(data, list) else []
```

So the fix is to use it instead of hand-reading `["data"]`, and drop the now-redundant
per-item `isinstance` (the helper already filters non-dict entries):

```diff
         probed = []
-        for item in data.get("data", []):
-            if isinstance(item, dict) and note_catalog_item(item):
+        for item in _payload_items(data):
+            if note_catalog_item(item):
                 continue
             probed.append(item.get("id", ""))
```

Net **−1 line** in `hermes_cli/models.py`. That is deliberate: the file is on the code-health
`FILE_LINES` ratchet (3002 on `main`, over the 2000 target, may only go down), so the change
cannot carry an explanatory comment block. The reasoning lives in the commit message and here.

No behavior change for envelope-shaped providers; non-dict entries in either shape are still
dropped, as before.

## Tests

New file `tests/hermes_cli/test_models_probe_payload_shapes.py` (behaviour contracts, no
source reading):

| Test | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `test_probe_accepts_bare_array_payload` | array payload → ids returned |
| `test_probe_accepts_envelope_payload` | envelope payload → ids returned (guard against regressing the normal path) |
| `test_probe_drops_non_object_entries_in_either_shape` | non-dict entries dropped in both shapes |

Sabotage run (regression test proven to bite on base code, fix stashed, `--file-retries 0`):

```
2 failed, 1 passed
FAILED test_probe_accepts_bare_array_payload
FAILED test_probe_drops_non_object_entries_in_either_shape
E   AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'
hermes_cli/models.py:2721: AttributeError
```

With the fix restored: `tests/hermes_cli/test_models_probe_payload_shapes.py` +
`tests/hermes_cli/test_models.py` → **79 passed, 0 failed** (`scripts/run_tests.sh`).

`python scripts/check --commit HEAD`: **12 checks, ok** (health, ruff, guards).

Live verification against the real endpoint, same key, before/after:

```
before: AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'
after:  216 chat ids, including deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
```

(216 not 269 because the probe drops generation-surface rows via `note_catalog_item` — expected.)

## Risk / scope

- One function, one expression. No signature, cache-key or wire-protocol change.
- `_payload_items()` is already the module's decoder for tagged catalogs, so this converges on
  one shape-decoder instead of adding a second.
- Sibling sites (`_fetch_live_catalog_index`, the anthropic fetch, the AI-gateway fetcher at
  `models.py:2259/2266/2867`) still read `data.get("data", [])` directly. I left them alone
  deliberately: each is wrapped in its own `except` that returns `None`, none is on the picker
  discovery path for a `providers:` entry, and folding them in would grow a ratcheted file.
  Happy to do them as a follow-up if you'd rather have the whole class in one diff.
- **Sequencing with #104220** ("guard /models null data payloads from crashing model picker"):
  that PR touches this same loop for `data: null`. The bare-array case is a different shape
  (envelope absent entirely, not `null`); a fix for one does not cover the other. Whichever
  lands second needs a small rebase — flagging it rather than guessing your preferred order.

Adds `deed-page` as an optional productivity skill. It is shipped but not active, the same way `here-now` ships. prs.title: perf(backend): start the host toolchain probe when the TUI and Desktop backends boot
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A chat's first system prompt includes the host toolchain line from `tools/env_probe.py`. Building that line takes about five python/pip subprocess calls, ~0.5 s. The result is cached per process, so only the first prompt pays.

Who starts the probe today:

- The messaging gateway starts it at boot (`_start_gateway_early_environment_probe`, #106064).
- Everything else starts it in `AIAgent` init (`agent_init.py`), which is the fallback.
- The TUI and Desktop/dashboard backends rely on that fallback only.

Desktop creates a chat's backend session when its first message is sent (`createBackendSessionForSend`). So for the first chat after each backend start, the probe begins during that chat's agent build, and the first turn's prompt build waits for it in `get_environment_probe_line`.

This PR starts the probe when those backends boot, the way the gateway already does:

- `tools/env_probe.py`: `warm_environment_probe_at_boot()` is the gateway's boot helper, moved here unchanged. It honours `agent.environment_probe: false` and never raises.
- `gateway/run_bootstrap.py`: calls the shared helper. Behaviour is unchanged.
- `tui_gateway/entry.py`: warms after `gateway.ready`, next to the `/model` picker prewarm, in the same idle window while the user types.
- `hermes_cli/web_server_app.py` (`standalone_lifespan`, the Desktop/dashboard backend): warms next to the other off-thread boot work.

Remote terminal backends keep their current behaviour. `get_environment_probe_line` still returns "" for them, and the gateway's boot helper never checked the backend either.

## Related Issue

None found. #131416 and #131420 gate the remote-backend probe, a different code path.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `tools/env_probe.py`: `warm_environment_probe_at_boot()`.
- `gateway/run_bootstrap.py`: the private helper is replaced by the shared one.
- `tui_gateway/entry.py`, `hermes_cli/web_server_app.py`: one call each.
- `tests/tools/test_env_probe_boot.py`:
  - the boot warm runs the probe once, and the first prompt reads the cached line;
  - `environment_probe: false` starts nothing;
  - an unreadable config does not raise.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_entry_environment_probe_warm.py`: the real `entry.main()` warms once, after `gateway.ready`. It reuses the harness in `test_entry_picker_prewarm.py`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_boot_environment_probe.py`: the real dashboard app lifespan warms once.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/tools/test_env_probe_boot.py tests/tui_gateway/test_entry_environment_probe_warm.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_boot_environment_probe.py tests/tools/test_env_probe.py tests/gateway/test_startup_environment_probe.py -q`
2. Time a first turn as Desktop sends it. In a fresh process with a fresh `HERMES_HOME`:
   - start the probe, as the backend now does at boot;
   - wait 2 s, standing in for the user typing;
   - call the TUI gateway's `session.create` and then `prompt.submit` against a local fake provider;
   - measure from the `conversation turn:` log line to the provider request.

   Compare with a run that skips the first step.

## Evidence

- Claim class: unit tests prove the wiring. Latency is measured in process, with the backend boot simulated by starting the probe, not end to end through the Desktop app.
- E0: `scripts/check` → `scripts/check: 12 checks, ok` (code health: 0 blocking, 0 advisory).
- Tests, command 1 above → `22 passed`.
- Red on the base: with the `entry.py` and `web_server_app.py` hunks reverted, both wiring tests fail.
- Wider: `pytest tests/tui_gateway tests/tools/test_env_probe.py tests/tools/test_env_probe_boot.py tests/gateway/test_startup_environment_probe.py tests/gateway/test_startup_model_context_warmup.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_boot_environment_probe.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_profiles_off_loop.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_skew_exit.py` → `11 failed, 2761 passed, 12 skipped, 1 error`.
  - The error is a missing optional `aiohttp`.
  - 8 failures (`profiles_list_*`, `status_profile_home`) fail the same way on `main` (86fa9e6ca1).
  - The other 3 fail only in the full run, and pass on their own on both `main` and this branch.
- Boot cost: the lifespan call imports `tools.env_probe` and reads config before `yield`. Measured at ~0.75–1.2 ms and ~0.6 ms in fresh interpreters. The probe itself runs off-thread.
- Review (cross-model, read-only), no findings:
  - the gateway keeps the same gate and startup position;
  - no wrong-profile line: the cache is host data, and each call resolves the scoped backend first (SSH and Docker bypass a populated cache);
  - sessions with the probe disabled never read it.
- Where turn 1 waits, on the base. A stack sampler over all threads ran from the `conversation turn:` log line to the provider request. The turn thread was inside `get_environment_probe_line` for 75 of 172 samples, waiting on the probe worker that `AIAgent` init had started during the build.
- Latency (E2). Fresh process per run, throwaway `HERMES_HOME`, fake provider on loopback, 5 alternating pairs, medians; Apple M4 Pro:

  | | turn start → provider request | `prompt.submit` → provider request |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | base | 912 ms (833–935) | 2618 ms |
  | probe started at boot | 372 ms (360–375) | 2041 ms |

  The ~0.55 s saving applies to the first chat after each backend start. Later chats in the same process already find the probe cached. The probe's cost depends on the host's Python setup.
- The TUI pre-builds its agent at launch, which already starts the probe. So in the TUI the gain shows only when the first prompt is sent within about half a second of that build finishing.
- Not proven: time to first token through the Desktop app, and Windows timings.

prs.title: fix(kanban): fail the delegate-child write fence closed when the delegation context is un-evaluable
prs.body:
The delegate-child write fence computes its verdict from `agent.delegation_context`, but
`tools.kanban_tools._delegation_ctx` returned its `default` (`False` == "not a delegate
child") out of a bare `except Exception`. A process that could not evaluate
`agent.delegation_context` therefore had the fence's own verdict computed as **allow**, and
only the board-connection layer stopped the write — reporting an error that misattributes
the cause.

Reproduction, measured on current `main`: with `agent.delegation_context` made
unimportable, a delegate child's board write passes the fence and is refused later at
`hermes_cli/kanban_db_connect.py` with `ModuleNotFoundError: import of
agent.delegation_context halted`. The write is still blocked, but by a guard further down
and with an error that points at the wrong cause.

### The fix

- `_delegation_ctx_or_none()` reports "un-evaluable" distinctly, and the write fence
  **refuses** on it for every caller instead of assuming, logging a `WARNING` that names the
  real cause.
- No env-bit escape: the `owned = os.environ.get("HERMES_KANBAN_TASK")` allow-branch is
  removed, so the only outcome that permits a board write is a definite "not a delegate
  child" (`verdict is False`). An un-evaluable context refuses even for a dispatcher-owned
  worker, because the escape bought no reachable write: every board write goes through
  `kanban_db_connect.connect()`, which imports the same `agent.delegation_context` module
  unwrapped and dies one step later with an opaque `ImportError` anyway. Reading "unknown"
  as "allow" on an identity gate is the silently-disabled gate this guard exists to remove.
- Read-only / visibility gates keep their previous defaults — `_delegation_ctx(...,
  default)` stays fail-open because it is hints/visibility only; only the write fence
  changes behaviour.

### Tests

`tests/tools/test_delegate_kanban_isolation.py` gains three tests (`+116/-0`; the file holds
10):

- `test_unavailable_delegation_context_direct_fence_refuses_an_owned_worker` — the
  direct-fence assertion from the review: `agent.delegation_context` unimportable,
  `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` present, `_reject_delegated_child_mutation` called directly, so a
  pass cannot come from `kanban_db_connect.connect()`'s later import failure;
- `test_unavailable_delegation_context_cannot_mutate_the_board` — the **invariant**: neither
  an owned nor an unowned caller moves board state (task status, run status and comments read
  straight from the board file);
- `test_unavailable_delegation_context_fence_refuses_when_the_process_owns_no_task` — the
  un-evaluable branch refuses here, with the audit line (`un-evaluable`) captured.

Run at `d77213b0c7` — `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_delegate_kanban_isolation.py`,
receipt `evidence/t_f1f2beab/pytest_settree.txt`: **10 collected → 8 passed, 2 failed**. Both
failures are the pre-existing `home_io_guard` environment artifact ("TEST BUG: file I/O
against the REAL hermes home"), reproduced identically on a control tree carrying the branch
WITHOUT this change → **0 regressions from this change**. Negative control: with the
`owned = os.environ.get("HERMES_KANBAN_TASK")` allow-branch restored, the direct fence test
fails with `DID NOT RAISE _Reject`.

At this head `tools/kanban_tools.py` is byte-identical to the revision measured above; the
test file has since taken upstream linter-only edits to its pre-existing tests (still 10
tests). The full `pytest tests/ -q` was not run on this host.


## Related Issue

Related Issue: none

prs.title: docs(cli): document the six undocumented hermes update flags
prs.body:
## Problem

`website/docs/reference/cli-commands.md` documents only 6 of the 12 flags `hermes update` actually accepts:

```
hermes update [--gateway] [--check] [--plan] [--no-backup] [--backup] [--yes]
```

**Reproduction:** run `hermes update --help` (or read `hermes_cli/subcommands/update.py` on current main) — the parser registers `--keep-stash`, `--branch`, `--switch-branch`, `--no-gateway-restart`, `--force`, and `--force-venv` in addition to the six documented flags. All six undocumented flags are real, shipped behavior: `--no-gateway-restart` is the documented cron/automation path (already covered in prose on `website/docs/getting-started/updating.md` §"Automated updates from inside the gateway"), `--keep-stash` is what the desktop updater invokes, and the two Windows guards (`--force`/`--force-venv`) are the only way to proceed past concurrent-process detection.

## Fix

- Extend the usage synopsis to the full flag set.
- Add a row for each missing flag to the `hermes update` option table, with descriptions matching the parser help and the existing prose pages.

This is documentation-only; no behavior changes.

## Why not an alternative

The prose guide already documents these flags, so the reference page is the one stale surface. Rewriting the guide would duplicate content; a "see also" pointer alone would leave the canonical flag table incomplete for anyone using the reference as the authoritative CLI surface.

## Validation

- Every flag added to the table exists verbatim as an `add_argument` in `hermes_cli/subcommands/update.py` (lines 13–75); after this change the table covers every flag the parser registers (checked programmatically: no `add_argument` flag missing, no table row naming a flag the parser lacks).
- Flag descriptions cross-checked against `hermes_cli/subcommands/update.py` help strings and `website/docs/getting-started/updating.md`.
- Markdown table integrity: all edited rows keep the 3-pipe 2-column shape of the surrounding table.

- `pin` / `unpin` — set/remove the durable "keep" flag (exempt from `sessions.auto_archive`, drives the Desktop sidebar's Pinned section)
- `pinned` — list pinned sessions (`--json`)
- `import` — import Claude Code / Codex CLI sessions into the store (`--from claude|codex`, optional path)

**Reproduction:** run `hermes sessions --help` on current main, or read `hermes_cli/subcommands/sessions.py` — the five subcommands are all wired up and functional, yet absent from the reference.

## Fix

Add one row per missing subcommand to the sessions table, with descriptions and flags taken from the parser help text. Documentation-only; no behavior changes.

## Why not an alternative

The subcommands are fully implemented and user-facing (pinning is a documented Desktop feature; import is the advertised path for migrating from Claude Code/Codex per its parser description). Leaving them out of the reference forces users to discover them via `--help`. There is no prose page that documents them, so the reference table is the right (and only) place.

## Validation

- Each added subcommand name and flag (`--json` on `pinned`, `--from`/`path` on `import`, `--dry-run`/`--no-backup` on `clean-markers`) matches `hermes_cli/subcommands/sessions.py` verbatim.
- Post-change, the table covers every subcommand the parser registers (checked programmatically against the `add_parser` calls).
- Markdown table integrity: all edited rows keep the 3-pipe 2-column shape of the surrounding table.

prs.title: fix(kanban): resolve a new card's board from the store it lands in
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`create_task()` decided where a new card belonged by asking the session which board was current, while the row itself went to whichever store the connection opened. Those two disagree whenever `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` is set, because the pin outranks the board slug (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:473-493`). The row could then land in one board's store stamped with another board's project, `workspace_kind=worktree`, and a `branch_name` resolving under that other board's repository, so a worker claiming the card would build and push in the wrong repo. That is the normal environment for a dispatcher-spawned worker, since the dispatcher injects the pin into every worker.

I hit this while filing cards onto another board from a session: the row landed in the pinned store and came out owned by the board the session sat on instead.

The store is the only reliable answer to which board a row is about to land in, so this makes the store the authority:

- `board_for_db_path()` (`:496`) is the inverse of `kanban_db_path()`: root store -> `default`, `<boards_root>/<slug>/kanban.db` -> `<slug>`, anything else -> no board identity.
- `_board_for_connection()` (`:523`) reads that back off the connection (`PRAGMA database_list`) and prefers it over the board the caller declared.
- `create_task()` (`:1313`) resolves the board that way before deriving any column, so the row's project follows the store it lands in.

Preferring the store over the declared board is deliberate: when the pin is set, the declared board is exactly the value `_board_path()` just discarded, and trusting it is what produced the bug. A store with no board identity (a copy, a relative path, `:memory:`) does not guess; it falls back to the declared board and behaves as before. An explicit `workspace_kind` or `project_id` still wins.

## Related Issue

Fixes #109435

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`: added `board_for_db_path()` and `_board_for_connection()`; `create_task()` now resolves the board from the connection's store before deriving board-derived columns.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_board_project.py`: two behaviour tests, red on main and green with the change.

118 insertions across those two files, nothing else touched.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_board_project.py -q` -> `7 passed`. With the source change stashed, the two new tests fail: `test_create_task_uses_the_store_board_not_the_session_board` and `test_create_task_inherits_from_the_store_board`.
2. The repro from #109435, run against a hermetic `HERMES_HOME`, three creates in one pass: pin at the root store with the session on the project-scoped board, the same with `--workspace scratch`, and the inverse (pin at the scoped store, session on `default`). On main the first row comes out `<project>|worktree|scoped/<id>` and the inverse row loses the project; here the first is `None|scratch|` and the inverse row inherits the scoped project and its worktree.
3. `pytest tests/hermes_cli -q`, same tree both ways: 27 failed / 307 passed with the change, 29 failed / 305 passed without it. Apart from the two tests above the failure sets are identical, so nothing else regressed. Those 27 fail on a clean checkout too (they are tied to this machine's paths and notification setup).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(kanban): ...`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate. Closest neighbours: #74395 (the dashboard's `POST /tasks` did not forward the resolved `board=` into `create_task()`), #70865 (create-time validation for un-dispatchable worktree cards, also inside `create_task`), and #29145 (rejecting a relative board `default_workdir`). None of them touches which board a create reads its project from.
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I ran the files this change touches, not the full suite — `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_board_project.py -q` → **7 passed**, and `pytest tests/hermes_cli -q` → **27 failed / 307 passed** with the change vs **29 failed / 305 passed** without it (identical failure sets apart from the two new cases). Those 27 fail on an unmodified `main` on this machine, so the suite-wide box cannot be claimed here either way — see the note below.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.5.2 (darwin/arm64)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A: no docs needed, the two new helpers carry docstrings
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered [cross-platform impact](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A: pure `pathlib` and `sqlite3` work with no OS-specific calls, and a Windows store path still compares through `Path(...).parts`

Note on the suite-wide box: this checkout shows 27 failures in `tests/hermes_cli` on unmodified main, so "the whole suite passes" is not a true statement on this machine either way. What I can show is that the diff does not change the failure set, and step 3 above is that comparison.

prs.title: fix(agent): re-fold the active /goal and its contract at the compaction boundary
prs.body:
## Problem

`/goal` state lives in `state_meta`, not in the transcript. The model sees it only as a user message — the kickoff, and the `[Continuing toward your standing goal]` prompt queued between turns. The todo list, by contrast, is re-folded into the transcript at **every** compaction boundary (`_fold_todo_snapshot`).

So whether the goal and its completion contract survive a compaction depends on where the goal text happens to sit when the cut lands:

- **Active turn opened by a goal prompt:** survives (the active request is kept in the tail).
- **Active turn opened by something else** (a real user interjection, a busy-steer, a `/heartbeat` tick, a `/loop` tick while the goal is parked): after a mid-turn compaction the goal and contract exist only inside the summary's **lossy free-text `## Goal` section**. `agent/context_compressor.py` writes that slot as model-authored prose ("What the user is trying to accomplish overall"), so **Verification, Constraints and Stop condition are routinely paraphrased or dropped** for the rest of the turn — exactly the fields the judge later enforces. Losing them lets the agent drift from the contract that decides continuation.
- **Gateway hygiene compaction** (in place, between turns, before the next message is appended): if that next message is not a goal continuation, the turn starts from a summary where the goal is free text only.
- **Third-party context engines:** any engine that does not reproduce the built-in active-request anchor drops the goal.

Reported as #133643.

## Fix

Give `/goal` the todo list's own machinery.

- `hermes_cli/goals.py`: factor the goal+contract body out of `GoalManager.next_continuation_prompt` into a shared `_goal_body_block()`, so the continuation prompt and the preserved block render the same contract fields from one place. Add `render_preserved_goal_block()` (active + not parked only) under a distinct, non-imperative header `[Your standing /goal was preserved across context compression]`, and `goal_is_parked()`.
- `agent/conversation_compression_goal_fold.py` (new topical sibling, kept out of the `conversation_compression` facade to respect its line cap): `fold_goal_snapshot()` mirrors `_fold_todo_snapshot` — strips any earlier preserved goal block (refresh, never stack), folds the live active-goal block into the trailing user row the todo fold already produced (so two synthetic user rows never sit adjacent), and appends a flagged row only when the tail is not a user row.
- `agent/conversation_compression.py`: the compaction commit boundary now calls `fold_state_snapshots()` (todo fold + goal fold) instead of the bare todo fold; the goal row is registered as synthetic (`_goal_snapshot_synthetic` flag + header prefix) so provenance/scaffolding classification (#69292) is unchanged and the row is never treated as human intent.
- Folds **nothing** for a goal the judge marked done, a paused/cleared goal, or a parked (waiting) goal — no resurrection (#34197). Skipped on a continuation-opened turn, where the goal is already verbatim in the request.

Carve-out respected: `next_continuation_prompt` output is byte-for-byte unchanged (only refactored through `_goal_body_block`).

## Why not a whole new mechanism

The todo list already solves exactly this ("state that lives outside the transcript but must survive compaction"); the goal is the one remaining such state. Reusing the fold keeps one code path and one set of provenance flags.

## Validation

- `tests/agent/test_goal_snapshot_fold.py` (new, 11 tests): contract carried verbatim; refresh-not-stack across two boundaries; merge into a trailing real user row (provenance stays real); done/paused/cleared/parked fold nothing; no duplicate on a continuation turn; an unavailable store preserves the pending snapshot; header literal stays in sync; and an **end-to-end** run through `compress_context` asserting the active goal + contract survives a compaction exactly once.
- Regression: `tests/hermes_cli/test_goals.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_goal_command.py`, `tests/gateway/test_goal_status_notice.py`, `tests/gateway/test_goal_resume_restart.py`, `tests/agent/test_context_compressor_zero_user_provenance.py`, `tests/agent/test_compression_rotation_state.py`, `tests/agent/test_skill_todo_retention_parity.py`, `tests/agent/test_in_place_compaction.py`, `tests/agent/test_compression_boundary.py`, `tests/agent/test_salvage_grown_transcript.py` — **all pass** (≈230 tests).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` (per-file isolation, CI parity); `python scripts/check` → 11 checks, ok (ruff + code-health ratchet clean; the new module keeps `conversation_compression.py` at its line cap).

fixes #133643
---

prs.title: fix(agent): stop turns on typed native tool-output rejection
prs.body:
## Summary

Stop the current turn when an OpenAI-compatible endpoint reports the exact structured native tool-output rejection contract:

- `code == "unavailable_tool_call"`
- `type == "model_output_error"`
- `source == "tensorfold.tool_output_guard"`

All three fields must match in the SDK exception body (inner body or enclosing `error` object). Message text alone, missing/changed fields, unknown codes, and ordinary HTTP 500 responses do not trigger this path.

This is a response-handling fix, not a backend integration, tool-output parser, or model-output repair feature.

## Behavior

- Classify that exact contract as terminal, without retries, fallback, compression, or credential rotation.
- Check before provider recovery and before the streaming HTTP-500 non-streaming unmask probe.
- Preserve exactly one existing `api_request_error` lifecycle notification with `retryable=False`; a truthy hook return cannot recover the rejected turn.
- Surface an explicit failed final response even if content/tool deltas were already delivered; do not convert the rejection into partial success or execute its pending tool call.
- Leave unrelated provider/recovery branches unchanged, including the newer reasoning-level handling already on this base.

## Regression coverage

`tests/agent/test_native_tool_output_error.py` uses actual `AIAgent` construction/conversation execution, the actual OpenAI client and HTTP decoder, and an ephemeral loopback HTTP server. It does not import another checkout, vendored backend code, or private audit fixtures.

Coverage includes HTTP-500 JSON, HTTP-500 streaming handshake, HTTP-200 SSE errors, SSE errors following visible content plus tool deltas, and both absent/truthy error-hook returns. Assertions check one completion request, terminal failure metadata, lifecycle dispatch, no recovery/compression/credential rotation/fallback, no partial-success stub, and no tool dispatch. Control cases exercise successful text and tool calls (including exact tool-call ID and tool-result association) and ordinary HTTP-500 recovery, each streaming and non-streaming. Classifier cases check exact structured recognition and malformed/near-match negatives.

The only fixture tool is a deterministic in-process echo handler. Network connections in this test are restricted to loopback; user state is redirected to a temporary home. Recovery entry points are fail-fast spies in rejection tests; the partial-result helper is wrapped rather than replaced by a synthetic success response.

## Validation actually run

Base: `9cb34e9e285dadd0c6d2463e9b094052530fc365`.

Standalone-unittest environment: Python 3.14.7, OpenAI SDK 2.24.0, httpx 0.28.1, using existing runtime dependencies.

- Unmodified base plus the new regression file: `python -m unittest discover -s tests/agent -p test_native_tool_output_error.py -v` — exit 1, 3 methods run, 9 failing assertions/subtests. The normal/tool/ordinary-500 control method passes; terminal classification and wire regressions fail.
- Patched tree: same command — exit 0, 3 methods pass, including all internal subtests.
- Patched tree: `python -O -m unittest discover -s tests/agent -p test_native_tool_output_error.py -v` — exit 0, 3 methods pass. Assertions use unittest methods, so optimization does not remove them.
- `git diff --check` — exit 0.

### Targeted canonical pytest and lint verification

An initial canonical-run attempt failed before collection because no prepared pytest environment existed. That attempt is preserved; it was not counted as a passing test run.

A separate temporary environment was then provisioned with the project's pinned pytest 9.1.1, pytest-asyncio 1.3.0 and Ruff 0.15.10; existing runtime dependencies were exposed read-only. Using the runner's documented explicit `HERMES_PYTHON` override, a sandbox HOME, clean environment, one test worker and bounded CPU affinity:

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh -j 1 tests/agent/test_native_tool_output_error.py tests/agent/test_error_classifier.py tests/agent/test_error_classifier_observed.py tests/agent/test_turn_api_error_stream_parse.py tests/agent/test_strict_api_validation.py tests/agent/test_direct_contexts_stream_inline.py
```

The actual per-file canonical runner completed: **6 files, 218 passed, 0 failed**. The observed-classifier suite also retained one existing expected failure. This includes pytest's conftest/autouse fixtures and the new real-agent loopback tests, not just the standalone unittest fallback.

Ruff checking the three changed production files and new test file returned exit 0 with no diagnostics. This is a targeted CPU regression run using existing runtime dependencies, not a full managed dependency-lock reproduction, full-repository suite, or claim that all upstream health checks passed. No live environment or dependency/configuration files in the contribution were changed.

All executed tests are CPU-only synthetic protocol fixtures: no real model, GPU, TensorFold runtime/server, native build, container build, paid API, or live provider test. No claims about GPU correctness, backend guard implementation, or inference performance.

## Independent review

A separate AI-assisted source review and repeat normal/optimized real-agent loopback runs found no blocking issue for this narrow draft. The reviewed source/test hashes match the submitted files. This does not replace human maintainer review, full-repository CI, UI/gateway integration testing or live backend validation.

## Files

- `agent/error_classifier.py`
- `agent/turn_api_error.py`
- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`
- `tests/agent/test_native_tool_output_error.py`

No runtime dependency/configuration changes. This is an AI-assisted contribution; no human review or deployment acceptance is claimed. Raw local evidence is kept outside the contribution; only portable source and tests are included.

prs.title: perf(version): read the release with one git call instead of the full provenance walk
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

In a git checkout without an install stamp, which is how most Hermes installs run (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent` is a clone), every Hermes process runs the full git provenance walk while it imports. That is 7 git subprocesses:

- `rev-parse HEAD`
- `branch --show-current`
- `log -1`
- `status --porcelain -uno`
- `tag --merged HEAD`
- `rev-list --count`
- `rev-parse --short`

It runs at import because module-level code reads `get_version_info().base_version`. Examples:

- `FastAPI(version=…)` in `hermes_cli/web_server.py`;
- the User-Agent strings in `hermes_cli/models.py`, `hermes_cli/model_catalog.py` and `hermes_cli/auth_constants.py`;
- the provider plugins' default headers (Fireworks, xAI, GMI, Kimi, OpenCode Zen, router), reached from `import hermes_cli.config`.

`tests/conftest.py` already works around the cost: "~0.55 s per process in a large local clone".

`base_version` alone needs one of those calls: the merged-tag walk, or the CalVer describe when no semver tag is merged. This PR resolves it with that one call and keeps the full walk for the callers that need the other fields:

- `get_base_version()` returns `get_version_info().base_version`, with the same precedence: already-cached info, then the install stamp, then git, then `"unknown"`. Its git step resolves only the release.
- `_git_release()` is the release resolution, factored out of `_git_version_info()` unchanged. `get_base_version()` and `get_version_info()` share one per-process copy, so a later full walk does not repeat the tag query. A process that needs the full walk, such as the CLI banner, still runs 7 provenance git calls, not 8.
- `_git_version_info()` itself stays fresh. `update_cmd_maint._checkout_version` (the `vA → vB` completion line), `venv_sync` and `source_stamp.write_source_stamp` call it directly after moving the checkout in the same process.
- `get_code_identity(refresh=True)` and `_reset_version_info_cache()` clear both caches.
- Every production read of `get_version_info().base_version` now calls `get_base_version()`: 42 sites, mechanical. Callers that read other fields (`derived_version`, `commit`, `source`, …) still use `get_version_info()`.

## Related Issue

None found. #140340 (open) adds a `tag --points-at HEAD` step to the same base-version computation. After this PR that logic has a single home, `_git_release()`. Whichever lands second moves it there; its `distance = 0` fits the `(base_version, distance)` tuple.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/version_info.py`:
  - `_git_release`, the cached `_process_git_release`, and `get_base_version`;
  - `_git_version_info(…, release=None)`;
  - the cache resets.
- 39 files: `get_version_info().base_version` → `get_base_version()` (42 reads).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_version_base.py`:
  - `get_base_version()` equals a cold `get_version_info().base_version` for semver tags, CalVer only, no tags, a stamp, a malformed stamp, and no repo;
  - a cold `get_base_version()` runs exactly one git command, and a following `get_version_info()` runs 7 in total with one tag query;
  - `get_code_identity(refresh=True)` re-reads a new tag;
  - a seeded cache (the conftest seed) runs no git and reads no stamp;
  - with the process cache warm, a direct `_git_version_info()` sees a tag added since, while `get_base_version()` keeps the running process's identity.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_version_base.py tests/hermes_cli/test_version_info.py tests/hermes_cli/test_source_stamp.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_version_report.py tests/hermes_cli/test_version_command.py -q`
2. Count git calls. Put a `git` shim that logs its argv first on `PATH`, then run `python -c "import hermes_cli.config"` from a clone without an install stamp. With a throwaway `HERMES_HOME` there are 7 lines on `main` and 1 here.

## Evidence

- Claim class: unit tests prove equality, freshness and call counts. Import time and git calls are measured on this machine in fresh processes, not across the fleet of install shapes.
- E0: `scripts/check` → `scripts/check: 12 checks, ok` (code health: 41 files, 0 blocking, 0 advisory).
- Tests: command 1 → `34 passed`.
- Wider: the version, header and update suites below → `6 failed, 242 passed` here vs `6 failed, 232 passed` on `main` (86fa9e6ca1). The 6 failures are the same on both. They come from cross-file interference in one process and pass file by file.
  - Suites: `test_version_*`, `test_update_*`, `test_source_stamp`, `test_banner_*`, `test_dump_git_commit`, `test_commit_build_updates`, `test_plugin_install_manifest_version`, and the provider-header, Fireworks, Perplexity, Gemini TTS, xAI and portal-tag tests.
- Red: the moved-checkout test fails when `_git_version_info()` reuses the process cache, the first revision's bug, which review caught.
- Import cost (E2). Fresh interpreter, throwaway `HERMES_HOME`, this checkout (202 tags), Apple M4 Pro, 7 alternating rounds after one warm-up round, medians:

  | import | git calls, main → this PR | main | this PR |
  |---|---|---:|---:|
  | `hermes_cli.config` | 7 → 1 | 266 ms | 124 ms |
  | `hermes_cli.web_server` (Desktop/dashboard backend) | 7 → 1 | 613 ms | 470 ms |

  Every Hermes process imports `hermes_cli.config`. The saving grows with checkout size: `status` and the tag walk dominate on large or cold clones.
- Review:
  - The first revision cached the release inside `_git_version_info()` itself. With the process cache warm, an in-process update would have printed `v0.21.4 → v0.21.4` and stamped the old release. Fixed, with the moved-checkout test above.
  - A second, read-only review of the final commit found nothing:
    - a warmed cache plus a moved temp checkout gave `✓ Update complete! (v0.21.4 → v0.22.0)` and a stamp `baseVersion` of `0.22.0`;
    - both refresh paths re-read tags;
    - 38 of the 39 switched modules import cleanly in fresh interpreters (`acp_adapter.server` needs the optional `acp` package on `main` too);

prs.title: docs(cli): document the missing `hermes cron` subcommands
prs.body:
## Problem

The `hermes cron` section of the CLI reference contradicts itself and omits three
shipped subcommands. Its usage line already advertises `runs` and `incidents`:

```
hermes cron <list|create|edit|pause|resume|run|remove|status|runs|incidents|doctor|tick>
```

…but the subcommand table below documents neither, and `notepad` appears in neither
place even though `hermes cron notepad` is a real, shipped command.

Reproduction:

```bash
$ hermes cron --help
usage: hermes cron ... {list,create,add,edit,pause,resume,run,remove,rm,delete,status,runs,history,incidents,notepad,doctor,tick} ...

$ grep -n 'notepad' website/docs/reference/cli-commands.md   # no match before this change
```

## The fix

Add the three missing rows (`runs`, `incidents`, `notepad`) to the `hermes cron`
table, matching the parser's own order and flags, and add `notepad` to the usage
line so it lists every subcommand.

## Why not another approach

The section is the authoritative per-subcommand reference for `hermes cron`; the
rows are the smallest slice that makes the table agree with `hermes cron --help`.
No new page is warranted for three subcommands of an already-documented command.

## Validation

```bash
$ hermes cron runs --help
usage: hermes cron runs [-h] [--limit LIMIT] [job_id]
   job_id         Optional job ID filter
   --limit LIMIT  Rows to show (1-500)          # default 20 in the parser

$ hermes cron incidents --help
usage: hermes cron incidents [-h] [--state {detected,alerted,resolved,closed}] [{list,ack}] [incident_id]

$ hermes cron notepad --help
usage: hermes cron notepad [-h] job_id [{get,set,delete,list}] [key] [value]

$ python3 website/scripts/check_doc_links.py   # -> OK
```

Every documented flag/value matches the parser above.

Two per-command option lists in the CLI reference are incomplete, and the `hermes logs`

```bash
usage: hermes doctor [-h] [--fix] [--live] [--ack ADVISORY_ID]

Unknown component: 'bogus'. Available: agent, cli, cron, gateway, gui, tools

Unknown log: 'boguslog'. Available: agent, desktop, errors, gateway, gui, handoff, mcp, update
```

prs.title: feat(desktop): redesign Capabilities catalog (Skills, Plugins, Connectors, Tools)
prs.body:
## Summary

Redesign the desktop Capabilities page (Skills, Plugins, Connectors, Tools) around a card-catalog surface, using Hermes theme tokens so it follows every theme in light and dark.

### Catalog redesign (desktop)

- Skills and Plugins browse through a native card catalog: bento shelves that work out their tile mix before placing anything — 2×2 showcases (entries with art only), two-wide cards and single cards, with `w = 4R − 3s − k` so every row fills edge to edge; no holes, no full-width filler. Categories with fewer than 3 entries share a "More to explore" shelf; plugins with an unlisted category file under General.
- Plugins discovery runs in the catalog's three tiers, read from the feed's `tier` ([#139983](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/139983)): **Official Plugins**, **Verified Plugins**, then the community category shelves. Every shelf orders by stars, then name; artwork only decides which shown card takes a 2×2 showcase. Every card with art shows it. The filter bar's second facet is **Tier** on Plugins (Official → Verified → Community; installed-only values like bundled/user/git fold into those), and Official/Verified badges are toned like the installed-plugin pill. Skills keep **Source** (their registry).
- The card catalog replaces the iframed docs-site picker (`/docs/plugins?embed=picker`) that main embedded on Plugins; its pane, `CATALOG_PICKER_URL` and its strings are gone. Installs from a card, the `hermes://plugin/install` deep link and the setup-chat plugin card all go through the same install path as before.
- Tools uses a feature row (Essentials before real usage data exists), themed two-column lists, and a toolset's settings in a dialog instead of a side panel.
- Connectors keeps its directory rows and drops the duplicate title; groups use the shared section heading.
- All four tabs share one content column, one centred scroller and one search field (`CapabilitySearch`: boxed, the tab's name as scope badge, the tab's actions at the end, data-derived "Try …" hints on Skills and Tools). Shared rhythm tokens set the gaps on every tab. Filter segments size to their labels (`SegmentedControl sizing="content"`).
- Cards have no border at rest and keep their per-card accent gradient, softened. On hover an arc fades in and sweeps the edge; every card runs the sweep on the document timeline, so moving to the next card carries it on instead of restarting. Hover paints instantly everywhere; only the exit eases. DESIGN.md's Motion section states the rule.
- Official entries get first-party artwork with a theme tint. Catalog data, install state, filters, detail dialogs and plugin/skill management stay on the existing feeds and stores.

### Featured picks, shared by the site and the app

- `apps/shared/src/catalog-curation.json` holds an ordered `featured` list per kind next to the artwork; changing the pick is a one-line edit.
- `extract-skills.py` / `extract-plugins.py` stamp a 1-based `featured` rank into `skills.json` / `plugins.json`, the files both the site and the app read.
- `pickFeatured` in `apps/shared` rotates through the ranks weekly so both surfaces show the same entry; falls back to newest official entry with art, then most-starred official entry with art. Never reads download counts.
- The desktop hero shows the featured entry's own artwork as a right-hand panel; `claude-subscription-directsdk` joins the head of the featured plugin rotation. A storefront-style revisit is tracked in [#141360](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/141360).
- `/skills` and `/plugins` get a matching hero card (author, title, description, tags, action bottom-right, accent wash), shown while browsing everything and hidden under search, filters and the Desktop picker.

## Conflicts resolved against main

This builds on the catalog module that #119381 introduced and #131252 reverted. The module is re-introduced here:

- **Catalog module restored**: `apps/desktop/src/app/capabilities/catalog/` (browser, cards, detail, filters, download deadline, pointer, store, skill-catalog, update-skills-button) plus the `masonry`/`reel` UI primitives and `apps/shared` `catalog-browse.ts` / `catalog-install.ts` — all from the working branch state.
- **i18n**: the `catalog` namespace restored in `en.ts` + `types.ts` and the five translated locale overlays (ar, ja, ru, zh, zh-hant); `locales/_keys.desktop.json` regenerated via `npm run i18n:keys`; `overlay-gaps.json` ratcheted with the repo's official `OVERLAY_GAPS_UPDATE=1` flow.
- **Kept main's newer work**: Settings ▸ Plugins settings pages (gear routes there with the profile hand-off; the in-tab `PluginSettingsForm` stays for the catalog detail pane), `requires.gpu` / `unsupported_gpu` server tone, the unified-package name resolver's package-folder join in `plugin-packages.ts`, the segmented-control no-wrap fix (with the branch's `sizing` prop added on top), and the `hermes://skill/install` deep link that #131252's follow-up kept. Also kept: switching a unified package's Agent half on turns its desktop half on (`enablePackageDesktopHalf`, `keepUserChoice`), and skills from `skills.external_dirs` stay editable in place (`skill-provenance.ts`, #108032).
- **UI primitives merged, not taken wholesale**: `OverlayNavItem` gains `leading`/`pressed` while keeping main's ancestor-row styling and third-level nav; `SidebarPanelLabel` gains `meta`; `Button` gains the `chip` variant; `Checkbox` gains `CheckboxMark`; `SearchField` regains `leadingContent` and the `box` variant on top of main's version.
- **`apps/shared/src/index.ts`**: catalog exports re-added alongside main's newer exports (update-debt etc.).

prs.title: fix(mcp): scope application-strike breaker openings to the rejected tool
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

When an MCP tool returns a business error (`result.isError = true`), the call still counts toward the server's circuit breaker — that is deliberate, per #10447 (a model rapid-fire retrying a failing tool must be stopped). But once the breaker opens on a streak made up **entirely** of such application strikes, it currently short-circuits **every** tool on that server for ~60s, even though the server answered every call and is perfectly healthy.

That severs the model's normal recovery route. The concrete case from #47851: a vault server's `edit` misses its `old_text` anchor three times, the breaker opens, and the `search` tool — the one the model needs to find the correct anchor — is also blocked for 60s. The open-breaker message added in #11113 even tells the model to "fix the arguments … or use a different approach", which the same open state then forbids.

This PR scopes an all-application open state to the tool whose rejections tripped it:

- `_bump_server_error(..., application=True, tool_name=...)` records the rejected tool when the streak crosses the threshold (`_server_breaker_application_tool`).
- `_check_circuit_breaker(server_name, tool_name)` lets every **other** tool on the server through; the rejected tool itself still short-circuits with the honest "rejected" wording (#10447's retry-storm protection is untouched).
- A success on any sibling tool is the existing unambiguous health signal: it resets the breaker, so the rejected tool becomes dispatchable again immediately instead of after the 60s cooldown.
- Any transport strike in the streak drops `_server_errors_all_application`, which clears the per-tool scoping and restores today's whole-server blocking.
- The open-breaker message now names the paused tool and explicitly offers "use a different tool on this server" — which is now actually true.

This is intentionally narrower than "never count business errors" (the approach of the earlier closed PRs #40951/#47898/#47918/#47955): the default strike accounting stays exactly as #10447 requires, and no new config surface is added (that direction lives in #90072 / #68455, which this PR complements rather than duplicates).

## Related Issue

Fixes #47851

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/mcp_tool.py` — new `_server_breaker_application_tool` state; `_bump_server_error` accepts `tool_name` and records/clears it alongside `_server_errors_all_application`; `_reset_server_error` clears it.
- `tools/mcp_tool_handlers.py` — `_check_circuit_breaker` takes `tool_name` and passes sibling tools through an application-only open state; message names the paused tool; `_record_call_outcome`/`_dispatch` thread `tool_name` from `_make_tool_handler`.
- `tests/tools/test_mcp_circuit_breaker.py` — new regression test (rejected tool blocked, sibling tool callable, sibling success closes the breaker, transport strike reverts to whole-server blocking); stub cleanup helpers also reset the two per-server dicts.

## How to Test

1. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_mcp_circuit_breaker.py -q` — Observed result: `9 passed` (8 pre-existing + 1 new).
2. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_mcp_multiplex_connection_keys.py tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py tests/tools/test_mcp_trust_gating.py tests/tools/test_mcp_tool_session_expired.py tests/tools/test_mcp_tool_401_handling.py tests/tools/test_mcp_stdio_children_dead.py tests/tools/test_mcp_stdio_fastfail_reconnect.py tests/tools/test_mcp_structured_content.py tests/tools/test_mcp_resource_content.py tests/tools/test_mcp_lazy_start.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_call_mcp.py -q` — Observed result: `219 passed`.

prs.title: fix(kanban): cap concurrent workers per board with kanban.max_spawn_by_board
prs.body:
## Problem

`kanban.max_spawn` is a single ceiling applied to every board's tick, and the host budget `kanban.max_in_progress` is shared first-come. A board with a deep queue spends the whole host budget, so every board ticked after it spawns nothing — one busy board starves the rest. The only per-board lever today is `set-dispatch on|off`, which is all-or-nothing and also stops that board's reclaim/promotion.

## Fix

Add opt-in `kanban.max_spawn_by_board` — a mapping of board slug to a positive-int ceiling (config.yaml only; no new env var). It is read into the dispatcher settings and resolved to **one board's ceiling per tick** at the `tick_once_for_board` call site, where it is passed as that board's `max_spawn`.

- The ceilings **allocate** the existing host budget; they never raise it. `_tick_spawn_budget` still applies `max_in_progress` across every board, so a board capped below the host budget can never hold more than its ceiling and leaves the remainder to the other boards, whatever order they are ticked in.
- A board not named keeps `kanban.max_spawn`, so an **absent or empty map is today's behaviour exactly** (opt-in, backward compatible).
- Defensive parsing: a non-mapping value, a ceiling below 1, and a slug not in the board inventory are each **ignored with a warning naming the entry** — never fatal, and never able to disable the global cap. A read failure of the board inventory fails open (keeps the map), so it cannot drop a real ceiling.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_per_board_spawn_ceiling.py` covers: absent/empty map unchanged; a named board's ceiling applies while others keep the global one; a ceiling limits its board while other boards still spawn; caps summing above the host budget never exceed it; a busy board cannot starve a quiet board; uncapped boards keep today's behaviour; invalid values and unknown slugs are ignored with a warning; an unreadable inventory fails open.

```
$ python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_per_board_spawn_ceiling.py -q
11 passed
```

Diff: 3 files, +337/-2 — one settings field + resolver, one small parse helper, a one-line change at the tick call site, a commented config default, and the tests.

- **TTS `language` setting:** Fish added an optional BCP-47 tag to text-to-speech on 16 October. It changes how numbers, dates and units are spelled out, and word timestamps; it never changes the voice. The plugin exposes it as `tts.fish-audio.language` and as a `fish_speak` argument, and drops an invalid tag instead of sending it.
- **`drama-3-preview` retired:** Fish's docs no longer list the preview id, and Fish serves unrecognized model ids as `s2.1-pro`. The plugin no longer offers it, and a profile still set to it now speaks with `drama-3`.

**Catalog entry changes**
- `sha`, `version` and the image URLs only. The description, disclosure, known issues, `requires_hermes` (`>=0.21.6`), capabilities and screenshots are unchanged. The new setting sends nothing beyond the text request already disclosed.

**Checks**
- The release acceptance suite ran at the merged tree before tagging, driving the real CLI, chat commands, tools, gateway routes and Desktop. It passed its gate on Hermes v0.22.2 (66 rows pass, 10 xfail on filed host bugs) and on the evaOS runtime. The new `A-TTS-LANG` row checks that the request carries the configured tag.
- `validate_plugin_catalog.py` passes, every image URL returns 200, and `scripts/scan_plugin_payloads.py` (rule 17) is clean on the pinned tree.

No new routes, tools, hooks or dependencies.

prs.title: security: guard .hermes.md as project-context instruction file; add protected_instruction_allowlist_dirs
prs.body:
## What

`.hermes.md` / `HERMES.md` is loaded as project context at **priority 1** and has **no write guard**, while every other project-context instruction file does.

The prompt builder enumerates project-context types first-match-wins:

```
# agent/prompt_builder.py (upstream main)
# Project-context types in priority order: the first type with any non-empty file wins, later types are
# shadowed. ...
_CONTEXT_FILE_CANDIDATES = {
    "hermes_md": _hermes_md_candidates,   # .hermes.md / HERMES.md — nearest match walking parents to the git root
    "agents_md": _agents_md_candidates,   # AGENTS.md chain, git root -> cwd
    "claude_md": _claude_md_candidates,   # CLAUDE.md, cwd
    "cursorrules": _cursorrules_candidates,
}
```

So `.hermes.md` **shadows every `AGENTS.md` in the tree** — and `_find_hermes_md` walks parents up to the git root, so a match planted high in the tree wins from anywhere below it.

The write gate protects this set:

```python
# tools/file_tools_write_guards.py (upstream main, line 189)
_PROTECTED_INSTRUCTION_BASENAMES = frozenset({
    "agents.md", "claude.md", "soul.md", ".cursorrules"})
```

`.hermes.md` is in neither that set nor the config globs, nor the immediate-parent `.hermes` rule (which matches a file whose *parent directory* is named `.hermes`, not a file named `.hermes.md`).

## Why it matters

The gate's own rationale is that instruction files are a prompt-injection **persistence** vector, and that basenames match in ANY directory "because project-context instruction files are loaded from cwd trees — an AGENTS.md anywhere the agent might later run from is a live target". `.hermes.md` is exactly such a file, and a *higher*-priority one: it is the single instruction file an injected agent can rewrite with **no approval dialog at all**, from the position that outranks the guarded one.

## Repro

In a project directory:

```
cp AGENTS.md .hermes.md      # no approval prompt
# a subsequent targeted patch on .hermes.md -> no approval prompt
# the same writes against AGENTS.md prompt every time
```

Measured 2026-10-12 against a fork checkout of upstream main.

## The change

1. **Add `.hermes.md` and `hermes.md` to `_PROTECTED_INSTRUCTION_BASENAMES`.** Both spellings, because `_find_hermes_md` probes both; matching is case-insensitive, so this covers the loader exactly.

2. **Implement `security.protected_instruction_allowlist_dirs`** — an operator-declared list of absolute directory prefixes whose whole subtree is exempt from the gate, checked BEFORE the basename match.

Part 2 rides with part 1 because closing the guard also closes the only dialog-free path operators have for project instruction files. The exemption is the supported way to keep one: it is config-only (`config.yaml` is hard-blocked from agent writes, so an exemption is always a human declaration, never a self-grant), it is `realpath`'d on **both** sides so a symlinked directory or a symlinked target cannot evade it, it matches on a path boundary (`/work` does not exempt `/workshop`), and the gate stays ON everywhere else.

```yaml
security:
  protected_instruction_files: true
  protected_instruction_extra_patterns: []
  protected_instruction_allowlist_dirs: []   # e.g. ["/opt/sandbox"]
```

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_file_write_safety.py` + `tests/tools/test_protected_instruction_cli_channel.py`.

Two-arm run on the pushed tip, same invocation both arms:

```
BASE (unmodified):  1 failed, 73 passed, 6 skipped
GREEN (this branch): 1 failed, 85 passed, 6 skipped
```

The one failure is identical in both arms and is an artifact of running the suite inside a git worktree of a live install (the test resolves a real hermes-home path); it is unrelated to this change.

The added tests cover: `.hermes.md`/`HERMES.md` now prompt on every protected-name path shape (deny / once / yolo / case-variant / traversal / multi-file patch); the allowlist exempts each protected basename inside the declared tree; the gate stays on outside it; a symlinked allowlist entry still matches; a sibling prefix (`/work` vs `/workshop`) is not exempt; and the real config reader surfaces the key end-to-end.

prs.title: fix(state): reap orphan message rows and merge both FTS5 indexes in state.db auto-maintenance
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`messages.session_id` references `sessions(id)` and the schema declares no `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so a session row removed while foreign-key enforcement was OFF (a legacy importer, an older writer that never issued `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, a bulk cleanup) strands that session's whole transcript in `messages` **and in both FTS5 shadow indexes** (`messages_fts` + `messages_fts_trigram`) forever. The session-level retention policy can never age it out: it deletes sessions, and there is no session left to grow old.

The trigram index leaks hardest. `messages_fts_trigram_delete`'s `WHEN` clause requires the message's session row to still exist — exactly false for an orphan — so it never fires and the orphan's segments stay in the trigram index permanently. The FTS merge only ever ran inside `vacuum()`, which the freelist-ratio gate skips precisely on a dense store: the one case where the merge is the only reclaim available.

This PR makes the standing state.db auto-maintenance own both gaps:

- **`SessionMaintenanceMixin.reap_orphan_messages()`** — deletes `messages` rows whose `session_id` names no session, purging the trigram index **explicitly** (the FTS5 `'delete'` command, bounded to the rows the index actually holds via `messages_fts_trigram_docsize`) before the `DELETE` fires the standard `messages_fts` trigger. A store with no trigram index (older CJK-less store) is handled: the purge is skipped and the reap still runs.
- **`maybe_auto_prune_and_vacuum()`** — after pruning, it reaps orphan messages (before the merge, so the merged index does not carry their segments) and merges **both** FTS5 indexes on every run, independent of the VACUUM gates. Reaped rows count toward the VACUUM admission.
- **`_record_state_db_maintenance()`** — one row per run, in `state_meta['last_state_db_maintenance']` (cheap to read back) and appended to `<home>/logs/state-db-maintenance.jsonl` (per-run history): the counters the run produced plus the store geometry after it. Never raises — a bookkeeping failure must not fail maintenance.

## Related Issue

No issue filed; found while investigating the unbounded growth of a long-lived production `state.db` (the trigram index alone held ~42 % of the file, and nothing ever reaped the orphan rows feeding it).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_state_maintenance.py` — add `reap_orphan_messages()`; wire the orphan reap + `optimize_fts()` into `maybe_auto_prune_and_vacuum()`; add `_record_state_db_maintenance()`; document the new result keys on the method.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_state_db_reap_orphans_fts_optimize.py` (new) — 3 tests: orphans are reaped while a live session's rows are spared (both FTS indexes drop the orphans, and the no-op reap returns 0), both indexes are optimized even when `vacuum=False`, and one recorded row per run that agrees with the jsonl history line.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_startup_maintenance_lease.py` — lease-renewal count 4 → 6: the two new long steps renew the armed watchdog lease.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/hermes_state/test_state_db_reap_orphans_fts_optimize.py tests/hermes_state/test_startup_maintenance_lease.py -q` — all pass.
2. Reproduce the leak pre-fix: the three new tests are red on the base commit (`reap_orphan_messages` does not exist, no `fts_indexes_optimized` key, no `last_state_db_maintenance` row). The orphan test builds the orphan the only way one can be born on a store that enforces foreign keys — with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` — and proves both FTS indexes drop the rows.
3. On a real store, one `maybe_auto_prune_and_vacuum()` run with the fix records `state_meta['last_state_db_maintenance']` and appends a matching `logs/state-db-maintenance.jsonl` line; `fts_indexes_optimized` is ≥ 2 even when the run declines to VACUUM.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate (none found for orphan reaping or FTS optimize in `state.db` maintenance)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — the two affected test files pass; the whole suite was not run in this environment
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes — not run in this environment
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 27.0.1 (arm64), Python 3.14 / 3.11

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (docstrings on the changed methods) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A, no config change

```
{"at": 1791542xxx.xx, "page_count": 959306, "page_size": 4096, "freelist_count": ..., "retention_days": 5, "pruned": 0, "closed": 0, "reaped_orphan_messages": 0, "fts_indexes_optimized": 2, "vacuumed": false, "error": null}
```

prs.title: fix(approvals): `hermes approvals test` must see a pattern-key standing approval
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes approvals test` renders a false `ask-approval` for a command the runtime would
auto-approve, whenever the standing approval is expressed as a PATTERN KEY.

Step 6 of the dry-run tester (`hermes_cli/approvals_test.py`) decided "permanently
approved" with `approval_floors._command_matches_permanent_allowlist(command)`, which
compares the command TEXT or a shell-style glob. The runtime gate consents by PATTERN KEY:
`approval._is_permanently_approved(pattern_key)` under cron/-q deny mode and
`approval.is_approved(session_key, pattern_key)` in the human gate. Every `[a]lways`
choice persists a key, and the entries already in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` are keys — so the
CLI reports `ask-approval` for a standing approval the runtime honours.

Why it matters: this CLI is the surface an operator or a lane uses to CHECK whether a
standing approval is in effect. A false `ask-approval` reads as "the approval you granted is
not working", which pushes the reader toward re-granting it, widening it, or routing around
the guard — the exact failure mode the approval layer exists to prevent.

The fix is the shape the issue describes: step 6 detects the pattern first (the same
`detect_dangerous_command` call step 7 already made) and reports allow when the command's
key is permanently approved, keeping the existing text/glob check for manual entries. The
evaluation ORDER is unchanged.

## Related Issue

No upstream issue exists for this: it was measured on a live install and is reported here
with the full repro in "How to Test". The defect and its proof are self-contained in this
PR.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/approvals_test.py` — step 6 now consults the pattern-key set
  (`approval._is_permanently_approved(pattern_key)`) as well as the text/glob allowlist;
  `detect_dangerous_command` is hoisted to step 6 and reused by step 7. Module docstring
  updated to match.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_approvals_test.py` — new `TestPermanentAllowlistConsentKinds`
  class (5 rows) covering BOTH entry kinds.

## How to Test

Repro on `main`, fresh processes, both `HERMES_HOME` settings:

```
command_allowlist: []                       -> runtime _is_permanently_approved(key)=false
                                               runtime is_approved(session,key)=false
                                               approvals_test helper           =false
command_allowlist: [<the pattern key>]      -> runtime _is_permanently_approved(key)=TRUE
                                               runtime is_approved(session,key)=TRUE
                                               approvals_test helper           =false   <-- stale
```

`approvals-test-matrix.json` is byte-identical with and without the key present.

Worked example (`git push --force-with-lease origin <own-branch>`, pattern key
`git force push (rewrites remote history)`) — parity probe over BOTH runtime predicates:

| allowlist | runtime human gate allows | runtime cron deny-mode allows | CLI verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[]` | false | false | ask-approval |
| `[<pattern key>]` | true | true | **allow** (was `ask-approval`) |
| `[recursive delete]` | false | false | ask-approval |
| `[podman *]` | true (text/glob floor) | true | allow |

1. `hermes approvals test -- <command>` with the command's pattern key in
   `command_allowlist` now prints `allow` (exit 0) instead of `ask-approval` (exit 2).
2. A manual `podman *`-style glob entry still allows a matching command.
3. A key for a DIFFERENT pattern, and a glob that does not match, still report
   `ask-approval`.

Tests: the key row is red on the base (`1 failed / 19 passed`) and green after
(`20 passed`). The 9-file approval suite shows an identical 27-failure set before and
after (all 27 pre-existing in this environment), 293 passed after vs 288 before.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — see "How to Test" for the exact
      files and the pre-existing failures in this environment
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs) — the
      repo's own pre-commit lint chain ("lint python", ruff) passed on this commit
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 27.0.1 (arm64)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — the tester's module
      docstring now names both `command_allowlist` entry kinds
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) — N/A, pure Python logic
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

\`\`\`
detect_dangerous_command -> is_dangerous=True key='git force push (rewrites remote history)'
allowlist=[]              -> runtime _is_permanently_approved=False  CLI verdict='ask-approval'
allowlist=[<pattern key>] -> runtime _is_permanently_approved=True   CLI verdict='allow'
allowlist=['podman *']    -> CLI verdict for 'podman run ...' = 'allow'
\`\`\`

prs.title: fix(approvals): a git global flag no longer defeats the destructive-verb rules
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes a whole-family bypass in the dangerous-command approval rules: every git row was spelled
`\bgit\s+<verb>`, so a git **global flag** before the subcommand defeated the rule entirely.

```
git push --force origin main                 -> gated
git -C /tmp/repo push --force origin main    -> NOT gated   (no approval on any surface)
```

The same defeat reaches `reset --hard`, `branch -D`, `branch --delete --force` and `clean -fd`
(`git -C /x reset --hard HEAD~1`), and the `systemctl stop/restart/disable/mask` row
(`systemctl --host user@prod stop hermes-gateway`).

## Changes Made

- `tools/approval_detection.py`: ONE shared prefix fragment, `_QUOTED_GLOBAL_FLAGS`, is inserted
  between `\bgit\s+` and the verb in **every** git row. It is the module's existing
  `_GLOBAL_FLAGS` grammar plus a quoted-value branch, because a git global flag's value may be a
  quoted string containing whitespace (`git -C "/opt/a b/clone" push -f`). Both quantifiers stay
  possessive, so a long flag run that never reaches the subcommand fails in linear time instead of
  holding the GIL (#129281).
- The `systemctl` row takes `_GLOBAL_FLAGS` directly (systemctl has no quoted space-bearing value
  to support).
- `_GLOBAL_FLAGS` itself is untouched: docker/podman keep the one-whitespace value rule, pinned by
  `test_approval_global_flag_scan.py::test_value_whitespace_decisions_are_unchanged`.
- Row **order and descriptions are unchanged** - order is the mechanism (the first matching pattern
  wins). This change is orthogonal to the `git push --force-with-lease` key and its scope guards.
- Tests: a pinning corpus in `tests/tools/test_approval.py` (global-flag spellings for push/reset/
  branch/clean plus the `systemctl` rows, and the verb-adjacency cases that must stay clean), an
  invariant that **every** git row and the systemctl row carries the shared prefix, and termination
  rows in `tests/tools/test_approval_global_flag_scan.py`.

## Related Issue

No upstream issue - filed from a downstream deployment.

- Related to the `git push --force-with-lease` key PR: same file and same family, **not superseded**
  by this one. This change widens the existing bare force-push rows; that one adds a new row ahead
  of them. They compose, and either can land first.
- #129281 is the backtracking fix whose `_GLOBAL_FLAGS` grammar this reuses.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing

Measured on a fresh interpreter against a 45-row detect corpus and 26 rows that must stay clean:

- detect rows missing before: **41**; after: **0**.
- clean rows changed: **0** (no new false positive).
- verb-adjacency guards hold: `git -C repo commit -m "push --force to main manually"`,
  `git -C /x log --grep=push -f`, `git -C /x stash push -m wip -f` all stay clean - a global flag
  does not license a pre-verb match on quoted prose.
- 58-repetition flag runs (`--opt val --flag=x -q - ` x58, `-C "/a b" ` x58) stay in the 3-16 ms
  range: no backtracking blowup.
- Suite (`tests/tools/test_approval.py`, `tests/tools/test_approval_global_flag_scan.py`):
  178 passed / 1 skipped before, **185 passed / 1 skipped** after. The 6 new tests are red on the
  unpatched detector and green on the patched one.

Accepted cost, documented rather than hidden: two new prompts of a class the detector already
fires on - `echo "git -C /x push -f origin main"` and `git commit -m "document the git -C /x push
-f recipe"`. The contiguous spellings of the same prose already prompt today; this reaches the
`-C` spelling, so the class is not widened, only its coverage.

The obvious alternative - `\bgit\b[^;|&\n]*?<verb>`, dropping the requirement that the verb sit
immediately after the flag run - was measured and rejected: it adds 4 real false positives on live
commands (`git -C repo commit -m "push --force to main manually"`, `git commit -m "push -f to main
manually"`, `git -C /x log --grep=push -f`, `git -C /x stash push -m wip -f`).

Same class, deliberately **not** fixed here (reported, not bundled): the `_CMDPOS`-anchored
`systemctl (poweroff|reboot|halt|kexec)` row takes the same prefix defeat
(`systemctl --host user@prod reboot`).

prs.title: fix(approvals): give git push --force-with-lease its own key, guarded to non-main destinations
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Gives `git push --force-with-lease` its own dangerous-command pattern key, with scope guards that keep `main`/`master` and bulk pushes on the bare force-push key.

## Related Issue

No upstream issue — filed from a downstream deployment. Related PRs that touch the same guard family and are **not** superseded by this one:

- #29114 — adds the same distinct key. It has no destination guard, so allowlisting the lease key there also pre-approves `git push --force-with-lease origin main`; this PR keeps that on the bare key (see below).
- #29237 — takes the opposite route: skip approval outright for a leased push to a branch whose name contains `/`. This PR does not skip approval, it makes the leased verb *consentable on its own* (default stays deny), which composes with an allowlist rather than a branch-name heuristic.
- #134631 — scopes the `--force` flag patterns to one command segment; this PR uses the same `[^;|&\n]` segment bounding for its new patterns.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/approval_detection.py`: new pattern key `git push --force-with-lease (lease-checked force push)`, emitted by a pattern that matches only the lease-checked form (`--force-with-lease`, `--force-with-lease=<ref>`) and is placed **before** the existing `--forc[a-z]*` / `-f` patterns.
- Scope guards placed before it (`detect_dangerous_command` returns the first match), so the authorization "your own branch only" is expressible — a leased push to a destination the command names as `main`/`master` keeps the BARE key:
  - bare, `+name`, `refs/heads/name`, `src:name`, `HEAD:name`, `"name"` spellings, in either flag order;
  - the bulk `--all` / `--mirror` / `-a` forms, which are never "one branch".
- Bare `--force` / `-f` patterns are unchanged, and an abbreviated spelling (`--force-with-leas`, which git resolves to the lease flag) does not match the new key: it falls through to the bare key and fails closed.

Why it matters: the only existing key for the whole class is emitted by both the `--forc[a-z]*` and `-f` patterns, so an allowlist entry for the lease-checked form necessarily also pre-approves bare `--force`, `-f` and any destination. With a distinct key, an unattended (`-q`) session can be given exactly the leased verb through `command_allowlist` while `main` and bare rewrites stay refused (default remains deny for both).

## How to Test

```bash
python -m pytest tests/tools/test_approval.py -q                    # 181 passed, 1 skipped
python -m pytest tests/tools/test_command_guards.py tests/hermes_cli/test_approvals_test.py \
```
