issues.title: Telegram: URLs with an odd number of underscores never deliver (chat-adapter pinned 3 versions before the upstream fix)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## Summary

Every NanoClaw install running Telegram is on `@chat-adapter/telegram@4.29.0`, which permanently fails to deliver any message whose whole-message count of unescaped MarkdownV2 markers (`_ * ~ \``) is **odd**. Upstream fixed this in **4.32.0**; trunk still pins 4.29.0.

The most visible symptom: **OneCLI connect links never arrive on Telegram.** They always carry exactly one underscore (`&agent_name=`), so that feature is 100% broken on Telegram today.

## Root cause

In `@chat-adapter/telegram@4.29.0`:

- `LINK_URL_SPECIAL_CHARS = /([)\\])/g` — `escapeLinkUrl` escapes only `)` and `\` in a link target, so a raw `_` in a URL survives into the rendered MarkdownV2.
- `trimToMarkdownV2SafeBoundary` then counts unescaped markers across the **entire message**. An odd count reads as an unpaired entity, and it truncates the message at that marker — destroying the link's closing `)`.
- Telegram rejects the send with `can't parse entities: Can't find end of a URL`.

Note this is purely an adapter-side counting bug. Per the MarkdownV2 spec, only `)` and `\` require escaping inside a link target, so an unescaped `_` there is **legal** — the URL was never the problem.

## Reproduction

Driving the real adapter send path with a stubbed `fetch` on 4.29.0:

```
IN : Connect here:\n\nhttp://127.0.0.1:10254/p/x/connections?connect=gmail&source=agent&agent_name=Nano

SENT: "Connect here:\n\n[http://127\.0\.0\.1:10254/...&agent\_name\=Nano](http://127.0.0.1:10254/...&source=agent"
                                                                                          ^^^ truncated, ")" gone
```

Because parity is a whole-message property, two single-underscore URLs cancel out — which makes this look intermittent. It is fully deterministic for any message carrying a single URL with one underscore:

```
BREAK  https://example.com/post?utm_source=newsletter
BREAK  https://github.com/foo/my_repo
BREAK  https://pypi.org/project/python_dateutil
OK     two URLs, one underscore each (parity cancels)
OK     https://example.com/hello (control)
```

That intermittency is likely why this has gone unreported despite affecting common URLs.

## Upstream fix

Fixed in `@chat-adapter/telegram@4.32.0`: `findUnescapedPositionsOutsideCode` gained a `linkCloseBracket` tracker that skips everything inside a `](...)` target. Confirmed by bisect:

```
4.30.0 : buggy
4.31.0 : buggy
4.32.0 : FIXED   <- boundary
4.33.0 … 4.38.1 : FIXED
```

## Why the fix hasn't propagated

`.claude/skills/add-<channel>/SKILL.md` pins adapter versions exactly, so a published upstream fix never reaches users automatically. Eight adapters are pinned at `4.29.0`, in lockstep with `chat: 4.29.0` in `package.json` — and `scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts` enforces that lockstep:

> `@chat-adapter/slack pinned 4.29.0 but our chat core is 4.38.1 — a @chat-adapter/* adapter must match the chat package`

So the correct fix is a coordinated bump of the chat core and all eight adapter pins together, not a Telegram-only change.

## Scope

- Telegram only — `trimToMarkdownV2SafeBoundary` lives in `@chat-adapter/telegram`, not the shared `chat` package.
- Affects only messages whose whole-message unescaped-marker count is odd. Prose markers are escaped by `escapeMarkdownV2`, so in practice this means URLs, whose targets are left raw.

## Verification notes for the bump

The two `4.29.0`-keyed workaround comments in `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts` were re-checked against 4.38.1 — the chat core still does not dispatch `member_left_channel` and still exposes no `entities` array on assistant events, so both workarounds remain correct.

Behavior change worth flagging: 4.32.0+ introduces a `sendRichMessage` path attempted before `sendMessage`. It is a one-shot probe — on failure the adapter sets `richMessagesAvailable = false` and falls back permanently — so it is not per-message overhead, but it is new surface.

PR follows.

issues.title: [capability] Credential connections: allow a path prefix for several services behind one host
issues.body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

We run several MCP services behind one HTTPS ingress host, each under its own path prefix (`/service-a/…`, `/service-b/<group>/…` and others), and each needs a different credential. Each agent group is granted only its own secrets. With #4106 a skill can describe a credential for one exact path, but not for a prefix. So these credentials are created by hand in the gateway (OneCLI secrets with `--path-pattern '/service-a/*'`, and so on), outside the seam.

### What should be possible?

A skill declares a credential connection whose `path` ends in `/*`. The gateway limits injection to that prefix: OneCLI `pathPattern`, Iron rule `paths`. Setting up such a service then becomes a skill step instead of a manual gateway edit.

### What kind of skill is this?

Operational host skill

### Who benefits?

Operators who put more than one credentialed service behind one hostname, such as a reverse proxy fronting several MCP servers. That's common on single-host installs where each service otherwise needs its own DNS name and certificate.

### What have you tried?

Creating path-patterned secrets directly in OneCLI and granting them per agent group. It works, but the seam has no record of them, and every new service is a manual step.

### What would this change?

Following the outline in https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4106#issuecomment-6271433414:
- core accepts a trailing `/*` on `path`;
- each gateway adapter gets tests that pin what it matches for a prefix;
- `PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_CONNECTION_SEAM_VERSION` goes to 3, so a skill that needs prefixes refuses an older core.

Exact paths stay unchanged.

### How could we test it?

Per-gateway adapter tests: a prefix matches requests under it, and does not match a sibling path that shares the leading characters (for example `/service-a-x/`). Plus the seam's refusal test for a prefix on a store without `connectionPaths`.

### Can you help maintain it?

- [x] I can help maintain this skill.

issues.title: update-nanoclaw skill refresh: local adapters fail validation or get overwritten, no opt-out

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## What happens

The update's skill refresh thinks every channel import in
`src/channels/index.ts` came from a skill. That is not always true. Two
things break:

**Case 1: my own adapter blocks the update.**

- I have an adapter that lives in my tree. I wrote it. There is no
  `.claude/skills/add-<name>/SKILL.md` for it.
- The refresh fails with `Missing .claude/skills/add-<name>/SKILL.md`.
- One failed skill blocks the whole `validate` phase. The update stops.

**Case 2: my replacement adapter gets silently swapped back.**

- I replaced `src/channels/matrix.ts` with a native adapter (the direction
  PR #2844 explored before it was closed).
- The refresh overwrote it with the `@beeper/chat-adapter-matrix` bridge
  copy from the `channels` branch. It also re-added that dependency and its
  pnpm patch to `package.json`.
- Then `validate` committed all of it. No warning.
- Same problem for small local patches on skill-installed adapters (in my
  install, the WhatsApp voice note flag). But the silent adapter swap is
  the sharp end.

## Why it happens

At `ad8837c8`:

- `detectInstalledSkills` reads the barrel imports. Every import becomes
  `add-<name>` (`scripts/update-skills.ts:93-95`).
- No `SKILL.md` = hard error (`scripts/update-skills.ts:159`).
- A `SKILL.md` with zero directives = also a hard error
  (`scripts/update-skills.ts:163`).
- `validateUpdate` runs the refresh, throws if any skill failed, then
  commits everything the refresh wrote
  (`scripts/update/transaction.ts:308-310`).

Nothing in this chain can say "this adapter is mine, leave it alone". Copy
directives always overwrite. So a deliberate replacement looks the same as
stale skill output.

## How to see it

**Case 1:**

1. Create `src/channels/foo.ts` that self-registers.
2. Append `import './foo.js';` to `src/channels/index.ts`. Commit.
3. Run the update. `validate` fails:
   `Missing .claude/skills/add-foo/SKILL.md`.

**Case 2:**

1. Replace `src/channels/matrix.ts` with your own code. Commit.
2. Run `validate` on an install that has `add-matrix`.
3. Your file comes back as the registry copy, inside the
   `chore: refresh installed skill payloads` commit.

## Suggested fix

Give forks a supported opt-out. Two ideas:

- A frontmatter flag in `SKILL.md` (for example `refresh: local`). The
  refresher reports the skill as refreshed and touches nothing.
- For case 1: treat an import with no matching skill as "local, skipped"
  plus a warning, instead of failing.

My current workaround: a marker `SKILL.md` per local adapter, with one
idempotent `nc:append` directive (the barrel import line, already present).
It passes the checks and the refresh becomes a no-op. It works. But it is a
trick, not a contract. And the zero-directive error message ("cannot be
refreshed headlessly") reads like the goal was completeness, not banning
local adapters.

## Related, but not blocking

- #3451 fixes companion-import attribution. It keeps the missing-skill
  failure for unclaimed imports on purpose, so it does not cover case 1.
- #2844 (closed) is why a fork may carry a replaced Matrix adapter at all.

Assisted by Claude; reviewed and verified by a human before submission.

issues.title: Resend channel can't send: null thread id falls back to a platform id the adapter rejects

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

`015a7fe9` (main), with `/add-resend` on adapter 0.1.1 and 0.3.0 (pin bumped in #4042)

### Host platform

All (macOS and Linux)

### What happened?

The Resend (email) channel receives mail but can't send. Agent replies and the hello from "Connect yourself" never go out.

Email is a non-threaded channel, so `deliver()` gets a null thread id. The bridge then falls back to the platform id (`src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts:821`, `const tid = threadId ?? platformId;`), which for Resend is the two-part `resend:<address>`. The Resend adapter's `decodeThreadId` rejects that with `Invalid thread ID format`, so the send throws.

Found by @amit-shafnir while reviewing #4042. It is reproduced at code level on both adapter versions, not yet on a live install. The reply changes listed in #4042's release note aren't visible until this is fixed.

### What did you expect?

A reply to an email thread, and the first-contact hello, are sent through Resend.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. On a branch with `/add-resend` applied (adapter 0.1.1 or 0.3.0), call the bridge's `deliver('resend:you@example.com', null, …)` with any text.
2. Observed: it throws `Invalid thread ID format` from the adapter's `decodeThreadId`. Expected: the message is sent.

prs.title: feat(providers): add pi agent provider (/add-pi payload skill)
prs.body:
## Type of Change

- [x] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [ ] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - README, CONTRIBUTING, or docs only

## Description

**What** — Adds [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) (pi Coding Agent) as an optional agent provider, installable with the `/add-pi` skill. This is the restructured version of #3857, which targeted the `providers` branch. It now ships the way `/add-opencode` does on `main`: the skill carries its provider as a payload and needs no separate branch.

**Why** — pi is a lightweight coding agent with server-side sessions and MCP support; this makes it a per-group provider choice alongside `claude` / `opencode` / `codex` (`ncl groups config update --provider pi`).

**How it works**

- `payload/container/agent-runner/src/providers/pi.ts` — `AgentProvider` over the in-process pi SDK (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, pinned 1.3.0). No `pi serve` process and no SSE: the whole server-lifecycle complexity class of the OpenCode provider does not exist here. Continuation = pi session file path; activity on every SDK event; fail-closed memory hook; one-shot empty-resume fallback.
- `payload/container/agent-runner/src/providers/mcp-to-pi.ts` — bridges the core's MCP servers to pi `customTools` in process (stdio + Streamable HTTP, per-process lifecycle, lazy reconnect, `isError` → throw, JSON-Schema `pattern` stripped because some model APIs reject the regex dialects MCP servers ship).
- `payload/src/provider-contracts/pi.ts` (host) + `payload/container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts/pi.ts` (runtime) — seam version 1. The host contract declares the `AGENTS.md` project document, the group's `.pi-shared` state volume mounted at the agentDir, pi's skill backings/views, and the `auth.json` stub file; the runtime contract declares the permission stance, `textDelivery: 'result'`, and XML slash-command formatting.
- `payload/setup/providers/pi.ts` — the setup picker entry, gateway auth hook, and install check.
- `payload/src/providers/pi.ts` — the host container-config adapter (`PI_AGENT_DIR`, plus optional `PI_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS` / `PI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER` / `PI_DEFAULT_MODEL`).

**How the review points from #3857 are handled**

1. **Payload skill on `main`.** The whole provider lives under `.claude/skills/add-pi/` (`SKILL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `REMOVE.md`, `apply-fixtures.json`, `payload/`). `SKILL.md` is a parser-applyable set of `nc:` directives: copy the payload, append five barrel imports (host/container providers, host/container contracts, setup), install the pinned runner dependency, build, test. No branch fetch, no `PI_REF`, no per-group overlay propagation. `setup/providers/skill-descriptor.test.ts` lists the newly offered skill.
2. **Credentials come through the gateway.** No personal `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` is copied anywhere. The container writes fixed `gateway-managed` placeholders into the group's pi agentDir before each session open (`payload/container/agent-runner/src/providers/pi-auth.ts`), and the selected gateway replaces them on the wire by destination host. ChatGPT subscription auth is pi's `openai-codex` provider, which reuses the gateway's Codex/ChatGPT login; because pi decodes the access token for the account id, the placeholder is a syntactically valid JWT carrying the placeholder claim. API-key providers get a placeholder `api_key` entry, and `provider-auth pi` stores the real key through `getCredentialStore().connection(target)` (observing the entry first, as the seam requires), recording the provider ids in `PI_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS`. A real login already in the agentDir is never overwritten.
3. **`bun.lock` / npm registry.** The skill no longer commits `container/agent-runner/package.json` or `bun.lock`; the pinned dependency is installed at apply time by the `nc:dep` directive, and the pin is registered in `.github/skill-pins` so Dependabot tracks it and `skill-pins:sync` writes future bumps back into SKILL.md. Locally regenerating that install against the default npm registry produces a lock with zero `registry.npmmirror.com` URLs (the #3857 lock had 260).

**Model selection follows the SDK, not a hardcoded id.** Model ids change between pi releases (0.85.1 ships `deepseek-v4-flash`; 1.3.0 calls it `deepseek-flash`), so the provider resolves the start provider/model from pi's own runtime catalog (`getAvailableSnapshot` / `getModel`) and writes that into `settings.json`. Operator-authored values are never overwritten. Verified across both versions with no code change.

**Two things a reviewer should know**

- **The secret still has to be granted to the agent.** The credential seam stores secrets but never assigns them, and `/add-opencode` has the same manual step ("follow the selected gateway skill to grant it to agents"). OneCLI's `secretMode` is `selective`, so an ungranted key reaches the provider as `401 access restricted`. SKILL.md documents it.
- **Setup's own ping is not proof the model call worked.** It reports "Your assistant is ready" whenever the chat command exits 0 with any output, and a failed pi turn answers with the generic "The agent run failed" notice. Verify with a real reply and `continuation:pi` instead; SKILL.md says so explicitly.

**How it was tested**

- `scripts/provider-contract-verifier.ts --required-declared pi` — **passed** (host deps, runtime deps, host build, host provider-contract tests, runtime typecheck, runtime provider-contract tests, host/runtime contract inventories, runtime conformance test files).
- Container suite: **673 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail**. Host suite: **3613 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail**. `skill-pins:check` clean.
- End-to-end on a fresh clone of this branch: `bash nanoclaw.sh` → pick pi → DeepSeek key stored in the gateway → skill applied (14 files, 5 barrels, pin 1.3.0, image SDK 1.3.0) → group switched to pi → real reply, session continuation, and `continuation:pi` in the session's `outbound.db` `session_state`. A WeChat channel was installed onto the same install afterwards, so the channel/provider split was exercised too.
- Testing was done against a OneCLI gateway at 1.45.0 (newer than the 1.42.0 pin in `/add-onecli`), so the grant step used its `PUT /v1/agents/<id>/grants/secrets/<id>` API. This payload itself calls no gateway management API — only the credential seam — so the pinned 1.42.0 gateway is unaffected.

**Usage** — On an installed system: run `/add-pi`, then `ncl groups config update --provider pi` and `ncl groups restart` for the chosen group. Configure credentials with `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth pi` (ChatGPT via the gateway's Codex login, or a stored API key), then grant the secret per the gateway's skill. Model selection lives in the group's `data/v2-sessions/<group>/.pi-shared/settings.json`.

Note for reviewers: the **Provider contract** workflow was stuck in `action_required` on #3857 (first-time contributor). It needs a maintainer approval click to run here too. #3857 is superseded by this PR; it can stay open until this one merges.

## Rebased onto current `main`

Rebased after #4104 (`/add-codex` payload), #4107 (`/add-cursor` payload), #4105, #4106 and #3980 landed. Two conflicts, both list-append in shared files: `setup/providers/skill-descriptor.test.ts` now expects `codex, cursor, opencode, pi`, and `.github/skill-pins/package.json` carries this branch's pin alongside upstream's.

Upstream changes that touch this work, checked rather than assumed:

- **#3980 (first-chat ping)** fixed the very problem SKILL.md used to warn about: a failed pi turn's notice is now scored as a failed first chat instead of a green result. The doc now states the post-#3980 behaviour.
- **#4105 (shared exchange archive)** is for providers whose harness keeps no on-disk transcript. pi's session JSONL *is* its transcript — the continuation token is that file's path — so it needs no archiver, unlike Codex.
- **#4106 (credential connection path)** is unnecessary here: pi's provider entry is a key on exactly one host, so host-scoped injection is what we want.
- **#4104 / #4107** moved Codex and Cursor to the same payload-skill shape this PR uses, so the structure now matches three siblings.

Verification on the rebased branch: container `bun run typecheck` clean and the pi suites at 65 pass; host `tsc --noEmit` clean; host `vitest run` has one failure in `setup/gateways/selection.test.ts` ("detects an installed gateway from inside a nested pnpm") that reproduces on a clean `upstream/main` tree with this payload removed — it is a pre-existing flake under parallel load, not a regression here.

## For Skills

- [x] SKILL.md contains instructions, not inline code (code goes in separate files)
- [x] SKILL.md is under 500 lines (274)
- [x] I tested this skill by applying it onto current `main`, running the provider-contract verifier, and completing a real end-to-end install on a fresh clone

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Hands the photos and PDFs a user sends to the provider as structured attachments, so a vision model sees the file instead of a line saying it exists.

- **Problem**: core puts attachments in the prompt text only. The `/add-opencode` payload (https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3733) already turns structured attachments into file parts, but core never sends any, and the payload would throw on this PR's original shape (no `sourceMessageId`).
- **Fix**: `extractAttachments` builds `PromptAttachment[]` (source message id, name, mime, staged path; string fields only) for each file the host staged, and the poll loop passes it to `query()` and to follow-up `push()`. The text line stays, so a provider that ignores the field is unchanged. The payload forwards only JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP and PDF, identified by their first bytes, and keeps everything else (including incomplete entries) as prompt text.
- **Out of scope**: remote URLs (never fetched, still prompt text). https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/2618's content blocks can build on this type.

Related: https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/2618, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/1683 (host-side staging, does not touch this seam). No issue: the payload's file-part path has been unreachable since #3733 merged.

New poll-loop test checks that `query()` and `push()` both receive the attachments (fails if either argument is removed). The Claude provider still gets the text line and compiles against the wider `push`.
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/test-registry-skills.ts add-opencode`: PASS (apply, remove, re-apply, typecheck, image build, 139 payload tests: each media type, mislabelled and unsupported files, unusual names, and core's `extractAttachments` feeding the payload's `buildPromptParts`).

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Moves NanoClaw to OneCLI gateway 1.45.0 and CLI 2.11.0, the required stop before 2.x, and decides what a new agent group may use now that 1.44+ starts every agent with no grants. Supersedes #4082 and keeps chiptoe-svg's commits.

- **Problem**: on 1.44+ a new group's OneCLI agent holds nothing, so it cannot reach its model. Working out a group's secrets from other agents' grants widens or narrows access depending on history nobody can see.
- **Fix**: NanoClaw records the id of each model credential its provider logins save, per install, and on every spawn attaches the ones for the provider the group runs (an older install with nothing recorded is matched once by the names NanoClaw writes, and duplicate names are refused). Tool secrets and app connections are opt-in: `/add-vercel` now asks which groups and picks its token by host, and Tavily's paid-key upgrade attaches its key to the group. A new `pre-upgrade-check.sh` runs before the pin is saved and stops on anything the conversion deletes or changes.
- **Out of scope**: `/add-dial-tool` (stacked PR on `feat/dial-tool-grants`, merges in the same sitting), per-group model keys (#3205), docs portal pages.

## Related work

Supersedes https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4082. Related: https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3532, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3205, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4052, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4036.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- add-onecli payload suite applied per `nc:copy` (SDK 2.2.1), plus `tsc` over the applied files: 156/156. Full vitest and `tsc` pass.
- Tests cover each rule (model credential only, the spawn path passing the provider, repair on the next spawn, provider switch, late login, one-time name match only when nothing is recorded, duplicate names refused, `/add-vercel` token choice, the record lock, 1.42 no-op, every upgrade-check exit) and failed when the rule was broken on purpose.
- VM end to end, all pass: fresh 1.45 install, 1.42 to 1.45 upgrade (check stops before the pin is saved, 0 failed conversions), restore rollback, `/add-codex` after groups exist plus a provider switch.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [x] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
[BREAKING] The OneCLI gateway pin moves to 1.45.0 (CLI 2.11.0). Detect: `docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' onecli` shows an older tag. Why: OneCLI 1.44 replaced secret modes with per-agent grants, and 1.45 is the last version that converts existing installs. Fix: follow docs/onecli-upgrades.md before restarting; its check stops if the conversion would delete your rules. Existing groups keep what the conversion gives them; new groups get only their model credential. On a 1.42 gateway, new groups still get every key until the gateway is upgraded. To give a group a tool, re-run that tool's skill (for example `/add-vercel`) and pick the group; with `/add-tavily-tool`, re-run its Phase 5 so paid-key upgrades attach the key. Rollback: restore the database backup the guide takes.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Credential scope narrows: a new group gets only its own provider's credential. The record holds secret ids only (`data/onecli/provider-credentials.json`, mode 0600); no secret value passes through NanoClaw. Core gains one provider-name field; it names no provider or gateway.

## Summary

Ports `/add-dial-tool` to OneCLI agent grants so Dial keeps working after the 1.45 pin move in https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094. Merge right after it.

prs.title: fix(agents): refuse a new agent whose group folder is invalid
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Every way of creating an agent from a typed name now checks the group-folder rule before writing anything, and before any admin is asked to approve it, the same way on every install. The paths fixed: `create_agent` with and without a template, the "Connect new agent" name reply in the channel-registration DM, and the two operator init scripts. Before, a long name created an agent that could never start, "Global" took the reserved `global` folder that the other create paths refuse, and a templated request was only refused after an admin had approved it.

- **Problem**: a group folder is carried verbatim as a runtime label. That means at most 63 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, alphanumeric at both ends; `global` is also reserved. The template path and `ncl groups create` check this rule. Four create paths never did:
  - `create_agent` and the registration DM derive the folder from the name (`normalizeName`, `toFolder`) with no length cap, dedupe it with `-2`, `-3`, … and write the group. A 70-character name, or a 62-character name that collides and becomes 64 characters with `-2`, got a group row that the spawn path refuses on every wake (`labelValueLegal`, `src/container-runner.ts`). Meanwhile the requesting agent was told the agent was created, or the admin got "Agent created and connected".
  - A name like "Global" normalizes to the reserved `global`. These two paths created it as `global` on a fresh install, or as `global-2` where a v1 migration left `groups/global` on disk (`setup/migrate-v2/groups.ts` copies it).
  - `scripts/init-first-agent.ts` builds `dm-with-<name>` and `scripts/init-cli-agent.ts` builds `cli-with-<name>` (or takes `--folder`) with no check, so a display name of 56 characters (`dm-with-` is 8) or 55 characters (`cli-with-` is 9) made a group that can never spawn.
- **Fix, `create_agent`**: the guard precheck, `validateCreateAgent`, works out the folder the create would take and refuses before the guard decides. A group-scope request for such a name never reaches an admin's approval card, and a global-scope one is refused the same way. The plain path dedupes with `-2`, `-3`, … (`newGroupFolder`, now in `src/group-folder.ts`); a templated request uses the template stamp's own rule (`templateFolder`, taken out of `createAgentFromTemplate`: `-<8 hex>` on a clash) and nothing is fetched. A folder that is already invalid skips the dedupe, so "Global" is refused on every install, in the same order the template path uses. This is a behaviour change: on `main` it was created. The precheck re-runs on the approved replay, and `performCreateAgent` checks again before it writes, so a name taken between the card and the tap is still refused. The requesting agent gets `Cannot create agent "<name>": Invalid group folder "<folder>" — <reason>. Nothing was created.` No truncation, same as the template path.
- **Fix, registration DM**: `createNewAgentGroup` (`src/modules/permissions/channel-approval.ts`) uses the same `newGroupFolder` and, writing nothing, returns the reason instead of a group. The name interceptor (`src/modules/permissions/index.ts`) replies in the same DM with the same words the agent gets: `⚠️ Cannot create agent "<name>": Invalid group folder "<folder>" — <reason>. Nothing was created. Reply with another name:`. It re-arms the name prompt, so the next reply is taken as the name, and the registration stays pending. If that reply can't be delivered, the prompt is dropped, but only if it is still this registration's: a prompt the approver opened for another channel meanwhile is kept.
- **Fix, init scripts**: both call `assertValidGroupFolder` before `createAgentGroup`, and now create the agent group before the user row, so a refused folder writes nothing. Run by hand, the script prints the reason as one line and exits 1 (`init-cli-agent` used to print a stack trace). In the setup wizard the step fails as before and the reason is in `logs/setup-steps/`; the wizard's display-name prompt does not check length. A reused group is left as it is.
- **Reasons named**: `assertValidGroupFolder` now says what is wrong: `reserved`, `too long: N characters, at most 63`, or, when a clash suffix pushed it over, `too long: 64 characters, at most 63 ("<base>" is already taken)`. The old text only described the shape rule, which "global" meets. The template path and `ncl groups create` get the same plain reasons.
- **Removed**: the hand-rolled `path.resolve(...).startsWith(GROUPS_DIR)` check in `create_agent`. `normalizeName` only emits `[a-z0-9-]`, so that check could never fire, and the folder rule covers it anyway. The two copies of the dedupe loop (`create_agent`, registration DM) are now the one `newGroupFolder`.
- **Other create paths checked**: the template path, `ncl groups create` and `setup/register.ts` already check the folder. `createNewAgentGroup` has no other callers on `main`, `channels` or `providers`.
- **Not changed**: the first name prompt's delivery failure (`Reply with the name for your new agent:`) drops the prompt the same unguarded way. It is already on `main` and outside this PR.
- **Not changed**: a group-scope request whose name matches one of the requester's existing destinations still cards the admin and is refused only after approval (`createAgent`'s destination check). It is on `main`, and slack-agent-flow's resume path relies on that check running after the hold, so it is not moved here.

```mermaid
---
config:
  look: neo
---
flowchart LR
  subgraph before["Before"]
    direction TB
    b1["`**any of the create paths**
    name of 70 chars`"] --> b2["`**folder derived, deduped**
    folder of 70 chars`"]
    b2 --> b3["`**group row written**
    caller told it was created`"]
    b3 --> b4["`**every wake: spawn refused**
    folder is not a legal label`"]
  end
  subgraph after["After"]
    direction TB
    a1["`**any of the create paths**
    name of 70 chars`"] --> a2["`**folder worked out first**
    an invalid one is not deduped`"]
    a2 --> a3["`**folder rule checked**
    before any card or write`"]
    a3 --> a4["`**refused, nothing written**
```

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Codex agents signed in with ChatGPT reply on main's Codex pin (0.162.1) again, behind both credential gateways.

- **Problem**: Codex 0.156.0+ looks up auth.json `tokens.account_id` in `wham/accounts/check` before any model call. Both stand-ins carry a placeholder (OneCLI `onecli-managed`, Iron `nc-codex-token-v1`), so it fails with `selected workspace missing from routing discovery`. Main's pin 0.162.1 (#4069, unreleased) has this bug; v2026.10.0 shipped 0.155.1.
- **Fix**: the stand-ins carry the login's real workspace id; tokens stay placeholders. OneCLI: the adapter reads the id OneCLI already stores as secret metadata (`/v1/secrets`). Iron: sign-in records it with Iron's other non-secret IDs. Pin stays at 0.162.1; the 0.163.0 bump is left for a separate PR.
- **Existing installs**: OneCLI needs nothing. Iron logins saved before this keep the placeholder and log a warning; Iron can't read stored values back, so they sign in once more.

## Related work

Targets main; supersedes #4130, whose commit 211e6cd3 it carries, so the net change is the stand-in fix; the pin stays at main's 0.162.1. #4130 (pin 0.155.1) stays a draft only for a release cut before this is approved, and closes once this merges. Upstream: openai/codex#47374.

- Codex 0.162.1, Iron + ChatGPT (new device pairing) -> id `ecda…4361` recorded and staged -> reply `144`.
- Codex 0.163.0: same two runs reply `144`; Iron + API key (unchanged `apikey` stand-in) replies `144`. The workspace check is identical in both versions.

```release-note
Codex ChatGPT logins work behind OneCLI and Iron Proxy on Codex 0.162.1. Iron Proxy users who connected Codex with ChatGPT before this release sign in once more. Detect (from the NanoClaw folder; works while the service is stopped): `f=data/session-materials/iron-control/codex.json; [ -f "$f" ] && grep -q '"mode":"chatgpt"' "$f" && ! grep -q '"accountId"' "$f" && echo affected`. <!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->
```

## Summary

Makes step 7 of the `/add-imessage` removal work on a real install by handing it to `ncl messaging-groups delete`.

- **Problem**: step 7 deleted the wirings, then the iMessage messaging groups, with raw SQL while sessions, DM cache entries, pending approvals and channel destinations still pointed at them. With `foreign_keys=ON` the second DELETE fails after the wirings are already gone.
- **Fix**: step 7 now loops over `bin/ncl messaging-groups delete --id`, which #4103 turns into a one-transaction cascade with tests. One copy of the cascade, so the next table that points at groups or sessions can't break this step on its own.
- **Stacked on #4103**: merge #4103 first. The second restart from the earlier SQL version is gone, because the delete now runs inside the host. Step 6 now restarts with `bash setup/lib/restart.sh`, which waits until the new host answers, so step 7 cannot race startup.

## Related work

Stacked on #4103 (base is its branch). Same class of bug as #2525. Replaces the inline SQL version (00ff42c0) per Amit's review.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`

## Summary

`refresh-agent-image` now opens one `agent-images.json` PR for each hardened image the AWS worker promotes, listing it under its release. prs.title: fix(cli): cascade dependent rows in ncl messaging-groups delete
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes `ncl messaging-groups delete` remove the rows that point at the group, so it stops failing with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`.

- **Problem**: the generic delete ran one `DELETE FROM messaging_groups`. Any wiring, session, DM cache entry or pending approval for the group made it fail. The add-emacs and add-wechat REMOVE.md steps send users to this command.
- **Fix**: a custom `delete` shaped like `groups delete`. One transaction clears the group's sessions and their rows (questions, approvals, claims, delivery attempts, wake signals), then channel destinations, DM cache, pending sender and channel approvals, and wirings, then the group. It returns per-table `removed` counts and refreshes live session mailboxes, as `destinations remove` does. It also clears the chat's dropped-message row. Sessions other chats or agents still use are kept: the one an agent reuses across agent-shared chats moves to another of its agent-shared chats (or to none), and any session in a conversation with another agent (sent or received, answered or not) stays with no chat, so it carries on. A session with no chat takes the next agent-shared chat that resumes it, routing included, so cards and questions reach that chat. The gateway approval coordinator now releases a held request whose row was deleted instead of holding its slot forever (this also covers `groups delete`). A decision a human already claimed still wins.
- **Out of scope**: session folders under `data/v2-sessions/` stay on purpose (history; a container may still mount them until the sweep stops it).

## Related work

No issue. Same tables and order as the add-imessage removal fix, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4102, and the same pattern as the `groups delete` cascade, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/2525.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/cli/resources/messaging-groups.test.ts` -> 23 passed. New tests seed every dependent row for two groups with foreign keys on, delete one, and check the other group, its rows and its session's `inbound.db` destinations; they also cover the kept agent-shared session (moved with its routing, kept with no chat, mixed wiring modes, detached chats), sessions with a peer-agent conversation (sent, unanswered, not self-sends), binding a chatless session on resume (and undoing it when routing fails) and dropped-message rows. On main the delete fails with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway-approval-coordinator.test.ts` -> 76 passed. New tests delete a held approval's row (before and during expiry) and check the hold settles and frees its slot, and that a claimed approve survives shutdown after its row is gone. Each fails without its fix.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup's first-chat check no longer fails a slow first reply, such as a local model loading for the first time.

- **Problem**: the ping gave up after 30 seconds. A first reply waits on the sandbox, the agent runtime and the model, so an install with a local model always timed out here.
- **Fix**: wait 2 minutes, then ask "Keep waiting?" (2 more minutes per yes) or skip. A skip says the assistant is still starting and points to `pnpm run chat hi`, with no troubleshooting note or debug offer. Without a TTY it stops after 2 minutes. While waiting, each stage prints with its own time: message received, sandbox started, agent runtime started, waiting for the model's first reply. Stages come from the session row, its sandbox status and the heartbeat file, so they work for any provider and gateway.
- **Out of scope**: provider detail such as "model loading 40%". An optional provider hook can add it later.

## Related work

Builds on https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3980 (merged), which changed the same files.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

`ask_user_question` returns an error a few seconds after the host gives up delivering its card, instead of waiting out its timeout (300 s by default).

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds the Cursor Agent SDK provider payload, built on the provider contracts.

- **Runtime contract**: `provider-contracts/cursor.ts` registers execution policy (constant: Cursor's disallowed tools), inference and MCP resolvers, the memory session hook, and exchange archiving; `providers/cursor.ts` registers the factory only, so the module also loads on a core without the contract. `cursor.conformance.test.ts` runs the exported conformance suite. The preCompact hook returns `user_message`, the field Cursor copies into the compaction request. sessionStart still returns `additional_context`.
- **Host contract**: data only. `AGENTS.md` composed by core from declared facts (Cursor's native override files, skills at `/workspace/agent/.cursor/skills`), state volume `.cursor-shared` → `/home/node/.cursor`, skill backing under `.cursor/skills`. The provider-owned AGENTS.md writer is deleted; the legacy adapter contributes only the placeholder `CURSOR_API_KEY`. Mounts, env, and state directory are identical to the previous adapter.
- **Credentials stay behind the gateway**: the container holds a placeholder key; the gateway injects the real one on `api2.cursor.sh` and `api.cursor.com`. A new test runs the real provider and SDK behind a local CONNECT proxy and TLS origin and asserts every request tunnels through the proxy, the key exchange carries only the placeholder, RPCs carry only the short-lived exchanged token, and a decoy key never appears on the wire or in argv. When the proxy URL has userinfo, that CONNECT carries `Proxy-Authorization`, percent-decoded so it matches Bun fetch.
- **Fails closed on HTTP/2**: Cursor's server can force the SDK onto HTTP/2, which Bun's `node:http2` sends around any proxy. When a proxy is configured the provider refuses such a session (hook on `tls.connect` at dial time, since Bun snapshots builtin modules at first import) with a clear error naming the authority; a test forces the server-side flag and asserts the refusal with zero direct connections. `NANOCLAW_EGRESS_LOCKDOWN=true` is the operator-side layer that also fails any bypass at the network.
- **Setup**: `setup/providers/cursor.ts` registers the auth walkthrough (Cursor-account sign-in or dashboard key, minted into a 0600 file handed to the gateway CLI) and the install check.

Targets the providers branch, which is what `/add-cursor` copies from. Trunk install skill: nanocoai/nanoclaw#3355. prs.title: fix(cli): clear host rows and refresh destinations in ncl groups delete
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Closes two gaps in `ncl groups delete` that the `messaging-groups delete` fix found, and stops other writers putting the deleted rows back.

- **Host rows**: the delete left `session_claims`, `delivery_attempts` and `wake_signals` rows for the group's sessions. These tables have no foreign key, so nothing removed them. They are now deleted in the same transaction, before the sessions, and counted in `removed`.
- **Live destinations**: it deleted other agents' destinations that pointed at the group but did not refresh those agents' session mailboxes, so a running agent kept the deleted name until its next spawn. After commit it now re-projects destinations for each owning agent, as `destinations remove` does.
- **Writers racing the delete**: `setStopIntent`, `recordDeliveryAttempt` and `writeWakeSignal` no longer write rows for a deleted session. A racing restart could re-insert a claim that made the live container skip its teardown and gateway release; an in-flight delivery could write back an attempt row nothing removes. This also covers `messaging-groups delete`.

Out of scope: guarding `tryClaimSession`. Startup adoption reads a refused claim as a live peer and would leave a just-deleted session's container running.

## Related work

Pair with https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4103 (`ncl messaging-groups delete`): same tables and pattern, no shared files, either can merge first. Original cascade: https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/2525. The delivery and wake guards come from a review by my production NanoClaw agent.

## Summary

prs.title: fix(discord): connect the Gateway through Node's env proxy
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets the Discord Gateway connect on hosts that reach the internet only through an HTTPS proxy.

- **Problem**: with `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` / `--use-env-proxy`, `fetch` goes through the proxy, so Discord REST works. The Gateway doesn't: `@discordjs/ws` dials it with the `ws` package, which opens TLS itself and ignores the env proxy, so the connection gets reset. Discord looks connected but never receives messages.
- **Fix**: when a proxy is set (`HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`, either case) and Node's env proxy is on, `discord.ts` loads `@discordjs/ws` with `ws.WebSocket` briefly pointed at the native `WebSocket` (which does honor the env proxy), then puts it back straight away. `@discordjs/ws` reads `require('ws').WebSocket` once at load, so only the Gateway gets the native constructor.
- **Scoped to Discord**: the swap is synchronous and restored in a `finally`, so other `ws` users see the real package. That includes Slack Socket Mode, which passes an options object the native `WebSocket` would drop.
- **Why not an option**: neither `@discordjs/ws` 1.2.3 nor `@chat-adapter/discord` 4.29.0 lets callers pass a WebSocket implementation. The adapter builds its own `Client` without passing through `ws` options.
- **Load order**: `@chat-adapter/discord` moves from a static import to a dynamic `import()` inside the (already async-capable) factory, so the swap runs before discord.js loads. The type still comes from a type-only import.
- **Node version**: the check reuses `nodeHonorsEnvProxy` from `setup/service.ts`, now living in `src/env-proxy.ts` (re-exported from `setup/service.ts`) so `src/` can import it. On a Node that ignores the flag (23.x, 22 before 22.21, 24 before 24.5) nothing is swapped.
- **Observable and safe**: it logs `Discord Gateway routed through the env proxy` when the swap ran, warns and skips it if `@discordjs/ws` was already loaded (the swap would do nothing), and falls back to starting Discord without the swap, with a warning, if module resolution throws.
- **Unchanged without a proxy**: no proxy or no env-proxy flag means nothing is patched and the adapter builds exactly as before.

## Related work

No issue. Pairs with #3901 (the host launcher side of running behind an HTTPS proxy). That PR gets the service's REST traffic through the proxy; this one covers the Discord Gateway WebSocket, which it can't reach.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/discord.test.ts src/channels/discord-registration.test.ts` -> 16 passed
  - `isEnvProxyActive`: off with no proxy, off with a proxy but no env-proxy flag, on via `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, `--use-env-proxy`, and `NODE_OPTIONS`
  - `withNativeWebSocket`: the native constructor is visible only while the gateway loads, and gets restored even when loading throws
  - `isEnvProxyActive`: off on a Node version that ignores the flag (23.11.1, 22.20.0)
  - `resolveGatewayModules`: resolves the same `ws` copy `@discordjs/ws` loads, in the installed layout, and reports whether the gateway was already loaded
- Run behind a proxy (local only): a CONNECT proxy on 127.0.0.1, `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, Node 25.8.2, a stand-in gateway at `ws://gateway.test:19001` that the proxy maps to a local `ws` server. With the swap, the proxy saw `CONNECT gateway.test:19001` and the gateway accepted the shard. Without it, `@discordjs/ws` dialled the host directly and failed to resolve it. This host cannot reach Discord, so this was not run against the real Gateway or a real corporate proxy.
- Manual smoke (tsx): loaded `@discordjs/ws` through the helper with a stand-in native class, then called `WebSocketShard.connect()` -> the shard built the stand-in (`native:wss://…?v=10&encoding=json`), and `ws.WebSocket` was restored to the real class afterwards
- `pnpm run typecheck` -> no errors in the changed files; 28 errors in untouched files on the base branch (local-web, canvas-actions, slack-onboarding, slack-room-membership)
- `pnpm exec eslint src/channels/discord.ts src/channels/discord.test.ts` -> 0 errors (2 existing `no-explicit-any` warnings)
- `pnpm run format:check` -> clean
- `pnpm test` -> the only failures are in untouched files on the base branch: registration tests for channels the barrel doesn't import on this branch (gchat, github, matrix, …), local-web suites, and `slack-raw-text`
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Discord now connects behind an HTTPS proxy when Node's env proxy (NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY / --use-env-proxy) is on.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

No new credentials or inputs. Behind a proxy, Gateway traffic, including the bot-token IDENTIFY handshake, now goes through the proxy the operator already set. It stays inside TLS (the proxy sees the destination host and a CONNECT tunnel, not the token), the same exposure REST traffic already has. Nothing changes when no proxy is set.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Long approval cards now post in full, split into text blocks that fit each platform's per-block cap. A card is refused only when its channel cannot show it in full, and the agent is told why.

- **Problem**: approval questions had no length limit, while chat platforms cap how much text one card or one text block shows.
- **Fix**: the bridge posts card text as several blocks of at most 2,000 characters after `escapeCardText` (`splitCardText`), keeping code fences intact; the resolved card splits the same way. A channel that caps the whole card declares `maxCardTextLength`; a longer card is refused with a `CardTooLongError` whose reason `requestApproval` passes to the agent. `ncl` approvals and every `requestApproval` caller are limited to 2,000 characters of title plus question (`MAX_CARD_QUESTION_LENGTH`), checked before any card or pending row. `ask_user_question` refuses over-long questions before posting.
- **Out of scope**: per-channel `maxCardTextLength` values live on `channels` and follow separately. An agent's own question card refused by a channel still waits out the tool's timeout; a separate fix covers that.

## Related work

Stacked on #4090, which changes the same card code. Merge #4090 first, then retarget this PR to `main`. No issue: found internally. Safe to review directly: a refusal happens before any card or pending row exists.

prs.title: feat(container): pull the hardened image published for each release
prs.body:
## Summary Hardened installs now pull the image built from their own release, listed in `agent-images.json` on `main`, instead of the `versions.json` pin frozen inside each release. - **Problem**: the hardened image is built from a release after it ships, so it can never be in that release's `versions.json`. Every release since August still pins `hardened-2026-08-24`, so these installs are stuck on an old Claude Code and can't use Opus 5.5. - **Fix**: `agent-images.json` on `main` maps each release to its image. `container/pull.sh` and `--step registry --status` both take the entry for the newest release in the checkout's history that has one, through one shared script, `container/release-image.sh`. If no release is listed at all, they fall back to the `versions.json` pin. - **Check**: `verify-agent-image` verifies each new or changed entry against its release tag: `org.opencontainers.image.version` and `.revision` labels, that tag's `bun.lock`, and the publisher's cosign signature. The signature check now blocks the merge; before, it only reported. - **Out of scope**: the workflow that opens list PRs (#4010 and a follow-up stacked on it). ```mermaid --- config: look: neo --- flowchart LR subgraph before["Before"] direction TB i1["install on v2026.10.0
container/pull.sh"] -->|reads its own checkout| v1["versions.json pin
hardened-2026-08-24"] end subgraph after["After"] direction TB i2["install on v2026.10.0
container/pull.sh, --status"] -->|release-image.sh| l2["agent-images.json
on upstream/main"] l2 -->|entry for v2026.10.0| g2["image built from v2026.10.0
signed, reviewed"] l2 -.->|no release listed at all| v2["versions.json pin"] end before ~~~ after classDef inst fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#54aeff,color:#0a3069 classDef bad fill:#ffebe9,stroke:#ff8182,color:#82071e classDef good fill:#dafbe1,stroke:#4ac26b,color:#044f1e classDef neutral fill:#f6f8fa,stroke:#d0d7de,color:#1f2328 class i1,i2 inst class v1 bad class l2,g2 good class v2 neutral style before fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:5 5,color:#57606a style after fill:none,stroke:#8c959f,stroke-dasharray:5 5,color:#57606a ``` The install reads the list from the official remote (`upstream`, or `origin` when it is `nanocoai/nanoclaw`, the same rule `/update-nanoclaw` uses), fetching its `main` first, best effort. While a new release's image isn't listed yet, an install keeps the previous release's image rather than dropping back to the August pin. ## Related work Stacked on top of this: #4140, the refresh workflow change that opens the `agent-images.json` PRs, built on #4010. Merge this one first: before it, `verify` treats a list change as "nothing to verify". ## Change kind - [x] `kind/bug` - [ ] `kind/feature` - [ ] `kind/documentation` - [ ] `kind/cleanup` - [ ] `kind/hardening` ## Validation - `vitest run setup/lib/release-image.test.ts setup/lib/registry-state.test.ts` → 22 pass. These run the real `release-image.sh` in scratch git repos: an official remote with a list on `main`, and an install cloned from it. Covered: exact release, newer list fetched with `--fetch`, `upstream` preferred, a non-official `origin` ignored, rc skipped, dot-exact keys, fallback to an older listed release, never a release the checkout doesn't contain. - `vitest run setup/ container/ scripts/update` → all pass. The update e2e tests need `--testTimeout` on a loaded machine and are untouched by this change. - Real `container/pull.sh` on a scratch install cloned from a bare `nanocoai/nanoclaw.git` with `{"v2026.10.0": }` on `main` → `Using the image published for v2026.10.0.`, then tagged it. - `verify-agent-image` steps run locally: the resolve step on four cases (no change, new entry, tag not digest, unknown release); label checks against the real v2026.10.0 image's labels (pass) and with a wrong revision, version or lock (each fails); `cosign verify` against the real image (publisher identity passes, another identity blocks). - [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not) ## User and release impact - [ ] No user-visible behavior change - [x] User-visible change — release note below - [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback ```release-note Hardened installs now pull the image built from their own release, listed in agent-images.json, so a new hardened image reaches them without a new release. Run `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step registry -- --refresh` to move onto it. ``` ## Security and trust boundaries Which bytes a hardened install runs is now decided by `agent-images.json` on `main`, not by the install's own checkout. That file changes only through a reviewed PR, and `verify` requires on each entry the publisher's keyless signature (`AGENT_IMAGE_SIGNER_IDENTITY`) over the exact digest. The release, commit and lock labels live in the signed config, so the signature covers them too. Fork PRs get no OIDC token, so they cannot pass `verify`. Installs still don't verify signatures themselves, as before. ## Skill delivery - [x] Not a skill - [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above ## AI assistance - [ ] AI tools or agents helped produce this change - [ ] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

<details>
<summary>Original description by @shachartal</summary>

Fixes #3569.

## What this fixes

`@chat-adapter/telegram@4.29.0` permanently fails to deliver any message whose whole-message count of unescaped MarkdownV2 markers (`_ * ~ \``) is **odd**. The most visible symptom is that **OneCLI connect links never arrive on Telegram** — they always carry exactly one underscore (`&agent_name=`).

`escapeLinkUrl` escapes only `)` and `\` in a link target, so a raw `_` in a URL survives into the rendered MarkdownV2. `trimToMarkdownV2SafeBoundary` then counts unescaped markers across the entire message, reads the odd count as an unpaired entity, and truncates there — destroying the link's closing `)`. Telegram rejects the send with `can't parse entities: Can't find end of a URL`.

Upstream fixed this in **4.32.0** (`findUnescapedPositionsOutsideCode` now skips `](...)` targets). Confirmed by bisect: 4.30.0/4.31.0 buggy, 4.32.0 onward fixed.

## Why this bumps everything, not just Telegram

Adapters pin `chat` exactly, and `scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts` already enforces the lockstep:

> `@chat-adapter/slack pinned 4.29.0 but our chat core is 4.38.1 — a @chat-adapter/* adapter must match the chat package`

Bumping Telegram alone fails that test and yields two copies of `chat` in the store. So this moves the chat core and all eight adapter pins together, plus two other hardcoded `4.29.0` pins that would otherwise drift (`setup/install-github.sh`, the `skill-directives` fixture).

## Verification

Same repro through the real adapter send path with a stubbed `fetch`, before and after:

```
before (4.29.0)                     after (4.38.1)
BREAK  ?utm_source=newsletter       OK  ?utm_source=newsletter
BREAK  /foo/my_repo                 OK  /foo/my_repo
BREAK  ...&agent_name=Nano          OK  ...&agent_name=Nano
```

Test suite: `4 failed | 2058 passed`. The 4 failures are `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts`, which fail **identically on pristine `origin/main`** in the same environment — pre-existing and unrelated to this change. Everything else, including `skill-conformance` and `skill-directives`, is green. `pnpm run build` clean. The `pnpm-lock.yaml` delta is `chat` only.

## Two things reviewers should know

1. **The `4.29.0`-keyed workaround comments in `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts` were re-verified against 4.38.1**, not blindly renumbered. The chat core still does not dispatch `member_left_channel` and still exposes no `entities` array on assistant events, so both workarounds remain correct and only their version references changed. The `TODO(member-left)` stays open.

2. **New surface in 4.32.0+:** a `sendRichMessage` path is attempted before `sendMessage`. It is a one-shot probe — on failure the adapter sets `richMessagesAvailable = false` and falls back permanently — so it is not per-message overhead, but it is worth a look. It arrives with the fix and cannot be avoided by picking 4.32.0 instead.

## Note on the underlying pattern

Exact version pins in `SKILL.md` mean a published adapter fix never reaches users automatically — this one sat available for six releases. Might be worth a periodic pin-refresh check, but that is out of scope here.

Only Telegram was runtime-verified, as that is the adapter installed locally; the other seven pins are lockstep-consistency changes covered by the conformance test.

prs.title: feat(add-apple-container): run v2 agent sessions on Apple container instead of Docker (macOS)
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-apple-container`, a session-driver skill that runs each agent session on Apple's `container` runtime instead of Docker, on macOS. We have run v2 agent sessions on Apple container since June 2026: on a personal install first, and since August on a multi-user install.

- **Why**: by design, Apple container runs each agent session in its own lightweight VM with its own kernel; Docker Desktop and similar tools run every container inside one shared Linux VM. Apple container is Apache-2.0, whereas Docker Desktop is free only for small businesses, personal use, education and non-commercial open source ([license](https://docs.docker.com/subscription/desktop-license/)). With Apple container, memory also follows sessions: each session's VM has its own limit (1 GB by default) and returns its memory to macOS when that session ends. Docker Desktop runs one VM for all containers, allowed up to half the Mac's memory by default, and frees it only when the VM shuts down after five minutes with no containers running ([Resource Saver](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/use-desktop/resource-saver/)).
- **Skill**: the driver, its registration module and its tests ship in `.claude/skills/add-apple-container/payload/` (the `/add-onecli` shape). Apply copies them into `src/drivers/`, appends one import to `src/drivers/installed.ts`, and sets `NANOCLAW_RUNTIME_DRIVER=container`. `REMOVE.md` reverses all of it. Docker stays the default.
- **Driver**: no `--security-opt`/`--pids-limit` (the CLI rejects them; the pids cap becomes `--ulimit nproc`); `host.docker.internal` in env values rewritten to the bridge gateway IP, looked up from `container network inspect default` on every spawn (the subnet can move on a runtime restart); a failed lookup fails the spawn; nested file mounts never passed to the runtime (they replace the parent share, apple/container#2148): dropped when identical, otherwise copied into the parent share without following symlinks; JSON listing filtered by label client-side; `container system start` when the runtime is down; no sidecar containers.
- **Trunk, update drain** (`scripts/update/service.ts`): Apple container has no `ps` and no `--filter`, so cutover could not list containers and every update refused. Containers are now listed through one helper; Docker keeps its exact `ps --filter --format` call. On Apple container anything not yet `stopped`, including `stopping`, counts as alive.
- **Trunk, image build** (`container/build.sh`, only when `CONTAINER_RUNTIME=container`): passes `-m 8G` (the default builder VM runs out of memory), and prunes dangling images after a build (replaced images leak their snapshot, apple/container#2164).
- **Limitations**: Apple silicon, macOS 26 and `container` 1.5.0 or newer. A nested file mount replaces its parent share (apple/container#2148); the driver handles this as described above. Container egress can stop after a host network change, macOS update or reboot (apple/container#1986, open); `container system stop && container system start` restores it.
- **Rollback gap (not fixed here)**: a rollback does not restart gateway-role containers on Apple container. `restartGatewayContainers` calls `restart -t`, which `container` 1.5.0 does not have, and the printed manual hint uses Docker syntax (`ps -aq --filter`). A gateway running in Docker, such as iron-proxy's, is not seen by the Apple drain or restart.
- **Out of scope**: remote OneCLI gateways, a startup wait for the runtime's XPC service, and the agent-runner config-read retry (see Related work).

## Related work

No issue. It is safe to review directly because the driver only loads when an install applies the skill and sets `NANOCLAW_RUNTIME_DRIVER=container`, and the two trunk edits are gated on `CONTAINER_RUNTIME=container`, leaving Docker installs on the same commands. Overlapping Apple container PRs, all written against the pre-driver-seam `container-runner.ts`/`container-runtime.ts`:

- #2609 (file mounts, `host.docker.internal`, user mapping): covers nested file mounts and the `host.docker.internal` rewrite (resolved from `container network inspect default`, not a hardcoded `/etc/hosts` line). Does not cover its root-start plus `setpriv` user mapping; this driver uses the Docker driver's `--user`.
- #2649 (skip nested file mounts): covered inside the driver, without a trunk change.
- #2650 (retry the `container.json` read on a mount race): not covered.
- #2809 (Apple container runtime plus remote OneCLI gateway): covers the runtime switch, host-gateway rewrite, label-scoped orphan cleanup and `system start`. Does not cover the remote gateway, the host-side forwarder, or the `$HOME`/`TMPDIR` check.
- #1107 (remove the `.env` `/dev/null` shadow mount): that mount no longer exists in trunk; nothing to cover.
- #1128 (wait for the XPC service before startup): partly. `ensureReady` starts a stopped runtime; it does not wait for the service after a reboot.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm run format:check`, `pnpm run build`, container `tsc --noEmit` -> clean.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` (full) -> 281 files passed, 2 skipped; 3561 tests passed, 15 skipped.
- `scripts/update/service.test.ts` -> 46 passed. Red-proof: with upstream's `service.ts`, the 4 new Apple tests fail; treating only `running` as alive fails the `stopping` test. The existing Docker tests assert the unchanged `docker ps --filter ... --format ...` argv and pass before and after.
- Skill applied twice with `applySkill` on a clean `upstream/main` worktree -> first run wrote 6 files, appended 1 line, set 1 env key, built; second run changed nothing. `grep -c apple-container-registration src/drivers/installed.ts` -> 1.
- Installed tests, `pnpm exec vitest run src/drivers/` with `container` 1.5.0 on `PATH` -> 178 passed, 1 skipped, including the real-binary contract test (4 passed; it skips itself where the binary is absent).
- Gateway lookup red-proofs: adding a host-interface fallback on an inspect failure fails the inspect-fails test; returning a hardcoded address when `ipv4Gateway` is missing fails the no-ipv4Gateway test; caching the gateway per driver instance fails the moved-subnet test.
- Registration red-proof: deleting the `installed.ts` line turns both cases in `apple-container-registration.test.ts` red.
- Trunk driver conformance suite (`src/drivers/conformance.test.ts`) with an Apple container harness added locally -> 60/60 passed; removing the driver's `--label` args turns 3 red. Not shipped: the suite has no factory for out-of-tree drivers, and copying the trunk file into a payload is against the skill rules. A `defineSessionDriverConformance`-style factory would be a separate PR.
- `REMOVE.md` followed on the same worktree -> `git status` clean, `git diff upstream/main` empty (apply left an empty, git-ignored `.env`).
- `scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts` lints and stub-applies the skill -> passes.
- Live: v2 agent sessions have run on Apple container since 2026-06-18, about four months: a personal install from June, and a multi-user install (11 agent groups on one Mac, macOS 26.7) since 2026-08-07, through `container` 1.5.0 (upgrading through 1.0.0, 1.2.2 and 1.4.1). The workarounds in Limitations come from that use.
- **Not run in upstream CI**: the payload tests. `vitest.config.ts` excludes `payload/`, and `scripts/test-registry-skills.ts` only picks up registry-branch skills and provider payloads, so nothing in CI applies this skill or runs its tests. `apple-container-cli-contract.test.ts` needs a reachable `container` runtime and skips without one.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New /add-apple-container skill: run agent sessions on Apple's container runtime (macOS 26, Apple silicon) instead of Docker. Updates now drain Apple container sessions correctly.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Containers: each session is a separate VM. `no-new-privileges` has no equivalent on this runtime; `--cap-drop=ALL` and `--init` are kept.
- Mounts: a nested file mount loses its read-only protection, because it reaches the guest through its writable parent share. When the content differs, the host copies the file into the root of a writable, non-install parent share via a temp file and rename; it never writes through a symlink, never blocks on a FIFO, and refuses read-only shares, install surfaces and deeper paths.
- Credentials: unchanged. The gateway proxy URL is rewritten from `host.docker.internal` to the bridge gateway IP; nothing new enters the container environment.
- Update drain: Docker installs keep the same command. On Apple container a list or parse failure refuses cutover rather than reporting drained.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

prs.title: fix(update-skills): attribute a barrel import to the skill that appends it
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

**What** — `detectInstalledSkills` attributes a channel-barrel import to the skill that actually appends it, instead of assuming every import has its own `add-<name>` skill.

**Why** — `/add-slack` appends two imports to `src/channels/index.ts`: `slack.js` and its `slack-a2a-guard.js` companion. Detection maps each one to `add-<name>`, so the refresh looks for a skill that does not exist and fails:

```
Missing .claude/skills/add-slack-a2a-guard/SKILL.md
```

`refreshInstalledSkills` treats that as a failed skill, which blocks `/update-nanoclaw` validation on any install with Slack. I hit this on a routine update.

**How it works** — ownership is read from the skills' own `nc:append to:src/channels/index.ts` directives: an import a skill declares belongs to that skill, and a skill owning several imports is refreshed once under its own name. An unclaimed import still maps to `add-<name>`, so a channel installed without a skill is still reported — the missing-skill check keeps its point. A `SKILL.md` that fails to parse simply claims nothing; refresh reports the parse failure itself with a better message than detection could.

**How it was tested** — two cases added to `scripts/update-skills.test.ts`: the companion case (asserts one entry, not two) and an unclaimed import (asserts `add-<name>` attribution still happens). I verified the companion test fails on `main` and passes with the fix. Full file green (6/6), `tsc --noEmit` clean, and the real update that surfaced this now validates end to end.

## Summary

Setup's first-chat ping no longer counts the agent's "run failed" notice as a working assistant.

The wizard shows the agent's error line (kept out of `setup.log`) with the log files and troubleshooting docs. A notice with no error of its own now apologizes and links the same docs.
- **Out of scope**: a notice arriving more than 2s after a partial reply still reports `ok` (the same silence window as main).

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

prs.title: fix(add-dashboard): read transcripts without loading whole files
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Keeps the `/add-dashboard` pusher working when an agent's transcript gets large.

- **Problem**: the pusher reads transcripts with `fs.readFileSync(…, 'utf-8')`. Past ~512 MB (Node's maximum string length) that throws `Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters`. `collectContextWindows` doesn't catch it and `collectSnapshot` uses `Promise.all`, so the whole snapshot fails: the dashboard stops updating and the error is logged every minute. `scanJsonlTokens` catches it and silently drops the file from token totals.
- **Why a normal install hits it**: the agent-runner rotates transcripts at 12 MB, but only when a container starts. A busy agent's container is never idle long enough to be restarted. We saw one container run ~9.5 h on a single long task, with image tool results, and its transcript reached 540 MB.
- **Also below the limit**: every 60 s the pusher re-read every transcript of every agent from byte 0. That costs CPU and memory in proportion to the whole history.
- **Fix**: files are never read whole any more.
  - Context window: read the transcript's last 256 KB, doubling the window until a usage line is found.
  - Token totals: a per-file cache of `{ inode, offset, entries }`. Each snapshot reads only the appended bytes, in 1 MB chunks, and holds a half-written last line until it is complete. A file that shrank or was replaced is read again; files that disappear are dropped from the cache.
  - Log backfill: read the last 512 KB of `nanoclaw.log` for the 200 lines.
  - A transcript that vanishes between the directory walk and the read (e.g. rotated away) is skipped, not the whole snapshot.
- **Same output**: on a 100 MB transcript the snapshot's `context_windows` and `tokens` are identical before and after.
- **Trade-off**: the token entries now stay in memory between snapshots (one small object per assistant call) instead of being rebuilt every minute.
- **Out of scope**: which transcript counts as "live" (the newest `.jsonl`, which can be a subagent's), and when the agent-runner rotates transcripts.

<details>
<summary>Before / after numbers</summary>

A fake data dir with one transcript of 200 KB tool-result lines plus an assistant usage line after each. One snapshot through `startDashboard()` (vitest), peak RSS from `/usr/bin/time -v`.

| Transcript | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 100 MB | snapshot in 626 ms, peak RSS 456 MB | 234 ms, 155 MB, identical snapshot |
| 600 MB | **no snapshot** (error at start and again at 60 s), peak RSS 1.17 GB | 1.06 s, 158 MB; totals correct (3,139 requests) |

Later snapshots read only the bytes appended since the previous one.
</details>

## Related work

No issue: this is a self-contained fix inside `.claude/skills/add-dashboard/resources/`, with its tests. #3417 also edits `dashboard-pusher.ts` (shutdown wiring, SQL, docs); its hunks don't overlap these lines.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New tests in `dashboard-pusher.test.ts`, driven through `startDashboard()` like the existing one:
  - `finds the last usage line behind a long tail, without reading the transcript whole`
  - `reads only appended bytes, and counts a half-written line once it is complete`
  - `starts over when a transcript is replaced by a smaller one`
  - `still posts the snapshot when a transcript vanishes mid-read`
- Same tests on the old pusher -> 3 of the 4 fail (the "replaced" test guards the new cache, so it passes on both).
- Fresh clone, skill applied per `SKILL.md` steps 1–3 -> `pnpm run build` OK -> `pnpm exec vitest run src/dashboard-pusher.test.ts src/dashboard-wiring.test.ts` -> 7 passed.
- Same clone: `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` -> OK; `prettier --check` on the changed files -> OK.
- Same clone: `pnpm exec vitest run` -> 3569 passed, 1 failed: `src/group-skills.test.ts` › "resolves the legacy shape to the same anchored result as the segments form", which also fails on untouched `main` in our environment.
