prs.title: fix(security): authenticate loopback webhook to prevent action forgery (GHSA-h9g4-589h-68xv)
prs.body:
# fix(security): authenticate loopback webhook to prevent action forgery (GHSA-h9g4-589h-68xv)

## Summary

Fixes a missing authentication vulnerability (CWE-306) on the local forwarded-gateway webhook server introduced in `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts`. Any unprivileged process on the same host could POST a forged `GATEWAY_INTERACTION_CREATE` payload to the unauthenticated `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/webhook` endpoint and cause `setupConfig.onAction(questionId, selectedOption, userId)` to fire with attacker-controlled values, injecting forged button-click responses into NanoClaw's host response pipeline.

Closes #2970

---

## Root Cause

`startLocalWebhookServer` bound a plain `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1` and passed **every** POST body directly into `handleForwardedEvent(...)` without any proof that the sender was the expected gateway adapter. The loopback address was the only trust boundary.

```ts
// BEFORE — no authentication at all
const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
  req.on('end', () => {
    const body = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString();
    handleForwardedEvent(body, adapter, setupConfig, botToken) // ← no secret check
```

## Fix

A **256-bit cryptographically random secret** is generated with `crypto.randomBytes(32)` when the server starts. The secret is embedded as a path segment of the webhook URL handed to `startGatewayListener`:

```
http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral-port>/webhook/<64-hex-char-secret>
```

Every incoming request is validated using **`crypto.timingSafeEqual`** before any body is read. Requests with a missing or wrong path receive `HTTP 401` immediately:

```ts
// AFTER — constant-time secret check before body is touched
const secret = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex');
const expectedPath = `/webhook/${secret}`;

const pathMatches =
  reqPath.length === expectedPath.length &&
  crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(reqPath), Buffer.from(expectedPath));

if (!pathMatches) {
  res.writeHead(401, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
  res.end('{"error":"unauthorized"}');
  return;
}
```

The only component that ever sees the full URL is `startGatewayListener`, which is the legitimate gateway adapter. No other process on the host can guess the 64-character hex secret.

### Design decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Secret in URL path (not header) | No interface change to `GatewayAdapter.startGatewayListener` — it already receives and uses `webhookUrl`. A custom header would require adapter changes. |
| `crypto.randomBytes(32)` → hex | 256 bits of entropy from a CSPRNG; hex encoding is URL-safe without escaping. |
| `crypto.timingSafeEqual` | Prevents timing-oracle attacks even though loopback RTT already makes them impractical. Defence-in-depth. |
| Length check before `timingSafeEqual` | `timingSafeEqual` requires equal-length buffers; the explicit length check is the short-circuit, not a timing leak, because the length of the correct path is not itself secret. |
| Path stripped of query string | `req.url` may include `?…`; splitting on `?` ensures query params don't accidentally match a partial path. |

---

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts` | Import `crypto`; generate per-instance secret; validate path before body read; update URL returned to caller |
| `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.test.ts` | Add 4 new security regression tests covering: valid PoC payload accepted, PoC-path (no secret) rejected with 401, wrong-secret rejected with 401, control case (non-`ncq:` id) accepted but dispatches no action |

---

## Test Coverage

New describe block: **`startLocalWebhookServer — authentication (GHSA-h9g4-589h-68xv)`**

```
✓ returns 200 and dispatches onAction for a valid POST to the secret URL path
✓ returns 401 and dispatches no onAction for a POST to /webhook (no secret — PoC path)
✓ returns 401 and dispatches no onAction for a POST with a wrong secret
✓ returns 200 but dispatches no action for a control POST (non-ncq custom_id) to the correct path
```

The last test mirrors the advisory's control case: the loopback is reachable and returns 200 for authenticated callers, but non-`ncq:` payloads don't reach `onAction`, demonstrating the fix doesn't break normal event forwarding.

---

## Affected Versions

- **Vulnerable:** `nanoclaw <= 2.1.17`
- **Patched:** this PR (current `main`, `v2.1.53+`)

## CVSS

`CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L` — **Medium (6.6)**  
CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds a stale policy that only looks at items waiting on their author. Label clearing is live from merge; marking and closing stay in dry run.

- **Population**: issues labelled `triage/needs-repro` or `triage/needs-author` (stale at 21 days, closed 14 days later) and PRs labelled `triage/needs-author` (stale at 21 days, closed 21 days later). Each label means a maintainer read the item and asked its author for something. An author answer (comment, push, or review reply) removes the triage label and `stale`, so an answered item leaves the population.
- **Live from merge, labels only**: the `answered` job in `stale.yml` runs before each stale run and removes the triage label (and `stale`) when the item's author answered after the ask: a comment, a review or review-thread reply, their own commit, or a force-push. Only the author counts: a maintainer's "Update branch" merge, rebase, push or comment never clears a label.
- **Dry run**: the `stale` job has `debug-only: true`, so it marks, comments and closes nothing. Arming is a separate PR with its own checklist.
- **Out of scope**: any general-inactivity sweep. Most idle items are waiting on us, so a bot must not close them. Backlog cleanup stays a human batch close under [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#core-or-your-fork).

<details>
<summary>Notes</summary>

- Exempt: `kind/security`, `kind/hardening`, `priority/critical`, `priority/high`, `good first issue`, `help wanted`, `core-team`, `triage/keep` (the manual freeze), plus anything with a milestone or an assignee, and draft PRs.
- Close messages point to a new PR or issue, because an outside author cannot reopen an item the bot closed. No response-time promise.
- Pins: `actions/stale@4391f3da… # v11.0.0`, `actions/github-script@3a2844b7… # v9.0.0` (both latest). Runner `ubuntu-26.04`.
- Known gaps: a push or review reply in the minutes between the `answered` job and the stale job on a close day does not save the PR (`actions/stale` re-checks comments itself). An author who answers only by pushing from a commit email not linked to their account is missed until they comment; the arming PR checks the dry-run logs for this.

</details>

## Related work

No issue. Closing ships in dry run and the live part only removes labels, so it is safe to review directly.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`

## Validation

- `vitest run scripts/stale-workflow.test.ts`: 11 pass. The test runs the `answered` job's answer check straight from the workflow text: maintainer "Update branch" merges (the #1938 and #1604 shapes), rebases, force-pushes, comments and reviews do not count; the author's own commits (local, cherry-picked or web editor), force-pushes, comments and review replies do.
- Read-only replay of the whole `answered` job against live PRs, label writes stubbed: #1938 and #1604 keep the label (both lost it before this fix), while #3462 (author comment), #4087 (review-thread reply) and #3857 (author comments) clear it.
- Population on 2026-10-19: no open issue or PR carries a trigger label (the 5 labelled on 2026-10-02 were closed by hand on 2026-10-16), so the first run removes and marks nothing.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes the host's `container.json` rewrite safe when the file is not mounted read-only in the session.

- **Problem**: `materializeContainerJson` rewrote `groups/<folder>/container.json` with a plain `writeFileSync`, which follows a symlink at that path and blocks on a FIFO. Docker mounts the file read-only, so this only matters for a driver that doesn't (the Apple container skill in #3503 drops that mount).
- **Fix**: open with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK` and rewrite in place only when it is a regular file; otherwise unlink the entry and create a new file with `O_EXCL`.
- **Why in place, not temp + rename**: a rename gives the file a new inode, which detaches the read-only mount held by a running session of the same group. Reproduced on Docker Desktop's Linux kernel: after a rename the running session could write the file; after an in-place rewrite it could not.

Out of scope: the composed `CLAUDE.md` still uses temp + rename and has the same detach issue; separate follow-up.

## Related work

Related to #3503: should land before it, since that driver drops the read-only `container.json` mount.

prs.title: fix(signal): consolidate attachment, DM-routing, and outbound-queue fixes
prs.body:
## Summary

Consolidates the Signal adapter fixes from two of my stale PRs into a single, current patch against `channels`:

- Every attachment type (images, voice, general files) is staged to disk and forwarded through the same mounted-inbox mechanism every other chat adapter uses, replacing the old image-only path that spliced an unmounted local path into message text.
- Audio arriving alongside caption text, and attachment-only Note to Self messages, are no longer silently dropped.
- A per-file `[<name> could not be read]` note replaces a missing/unreadable/oversized attachment instead of dropping the whole message. `SIGNAL_MAX_INLINE_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` caps inbound attachment size (default 20MB).
- DM `platform_id`s are consistently `signal:`-prefixed everywhere (inbound, Note to Self, and `openDM`), so a cold-DM'd approval card lines up with the user's real reply instead of living in an orphaned `messaging_group`.
- Outbound sends queue while the TCP connection to signal-cli is down, and flush in order on reconnect, instead of being dropped.
- Voice audio is forwarded as a file attachment alongside the transcription placeholder, so it isn't lost when transcription is unavailable.

## Replaces

- #3693 — fix(signal): queue outbound sends while disconnected; forward voice audio without transcription
- #3142 — fix(signal): forward image/file attachments through the mounted inbox instead of a dead path (connector portion only — the SKILL.md portion is split into a companion PR, see below)

Both are stale; I'll close them once this is up. This PR is functionally independent of them (built from the current, tested state of my install) rather than a rebase.

## Companion PR

Docs for these changes are split out to keep this PR connector-only: #3838, against `main`.

## Related — independent overlapping fixes

Not written as a fork of either, but this PR's diff functionally overlaps with two other open PRs I don't own:

- #3799 (@gbmerrall) — attachment staging via the session inbox
- #2689 (@klingel) — DM `platform_id` consistency, `isMention`, and `ask_question`/approval delivery

I can't close PRs I don't own, so leaving these for the authors/maintainers to reconcile — flagging so reviewers don't duplicate review effort or land both independently.

Also related but out of scope for this PR (different file, not touched here): #3563 (@Agi-Asi) — a `setup/signal-auth.ts` probe-timeout fix. My install carries the functional intent of that fix too, but it's a `main`-branch, trunk-owned file, not part of either the connector (`channels`) or skill (`main`-SKILL.md) split — no PR opened for it as part of this cleanup.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run build`
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/signal.test.ts src/channels/signal-registration.test.ts` (all passing)
- [x] Verified manually against a live signal-cli daemon (image, PDF, and audio-with-caption delivery; outbound queue-and-flush across a disconnect)

## Summary

- The launchd plist and systemd unit generated by `setup/service.ts` use a hardcoded PATH missing `/opt/homebrew/bin` (Apple Silicon Homebrew) and the node binary's directory
- On Apple Silicon Macs, this causes the service to crash on boot because `container` (Apple Container) and `node` binaries aren't found
- Adds `path.dirname(nodePath)` and Homebrew paths to the generated PATH

- [ ] Verify service starts without "command not found" errors

prs.title: ci: check the signal-cli hash and open an issue for new releases
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Keeps the Linux signal-cli pin from going stale or wrong without anyone noticing.
- **Problem**: `setup/install-signal-cli.sh` pins `VERSION` and `SHA256` (https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4093), and upstream warns that releases older than three months may stop working. Dependabot has no ecosystem for a GitHub release tarball, signal-cli has no advisory feed, and Renovate has never run here (https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3978). A fix, security or otherwise, only shows up as a new release.
- **Hash check**: a step in the `skill-pins` CI job fails when `SHA256` is not GitHub's `digest` for `signal-cli-${VERSION}-Linux-native.tar.gz` (one API call, no download). A duplicate `VERSION=` or `SHA256=` line fails first with its own message. On a mismatch it offers the new `SHA256="…"` line only when the PR bumps `VERSION`; otherwise it says the release asset changed after it was pinned and not to re-pin in an unrelated PR.
- **Weekly issue**: `signal-cli-release.yml` (Mondays, or run by hand) opens one issue per newer stable release once the release and its Linux asset are 3+ days old, with the two lines to paste. Actions cannot open PRs here, so an issue is the reminder. It finds earlier issues by exact title, open or closed, so it never opens a duplicate.

## Related work

Follow-up to https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4093. No issue: CI and a scheduled job only, no runtime change.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run scripts/signal-cli-release-issue.test.ts` -> 5 pass, offline (stub `gh`).
- Full host suite -> 282 files, 3554 tests pass (15 skipped).
- The exact CI step text, run under `bash -e` against GitHub: pin 0.14.9 and a four-part 0.14.4.1 pass; a wrong hash, a VERSION bump with the old hash, a second `SHA256=` or `VERSION=` line, and a missing tag fail, each with its message.
- Weekly script against GitHub with only `gh issue create` stubbed: pin 0.14.9 -> "current"; pin 0.14.8 -> would open "signal-cli 0.14.9: update the Linux pin" with the right lines. Same under macOS bash 3.2.
- The workflow's first real run needs main: run it by hand after merge.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [x] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
NONE
```

## Security and trust boundaries

`ci.yml` adds a read-only `gh api` call with the job token (`contents: read`). The new workflow has `issues: write` only, runs only in nanocoai/nanoclaw, and checks out with `persist-credentials: false`. Release data is untrusted: the version and digest are regex-checked before they reach the issue body.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): rotate transcripts between warm turns
prs.body:
## Summary
Transcript rotation now runs between completed turns in warm queries, preventing recurring tasks from keeping an oversized session alive indefinitely.

- **Problem**: Rotation only ran when the container started, so frequent scheduled tasks could grow a transcript without bound.
- **Fix**: Check provider-owned transcript limits at idle turn boundaries. When rotation is needed, end the old query, clear its continuation, and process the next task in a fresh session.
- **Regression coverage**: A scheduled-task integration test verifies rotation and a fresh continuation on the next turn.

## Related work

Closes #3732

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec prettier --check container/agent-runner/src/poll-loop.ts container/agent-runner/src/integration.test.ts container/agent-runner/src/providers/types.ts container/agent-runner/src/providers/claude.ts container/agent-runner/src/providers/claude-history.ts` -> pass.
- `pnpm dlx bun x tsc --noEmit` -> pass.
- `pnpm dlx bun test --isolate src/integration.test.ts src/turn-routing-regression.test.ts src/providers/claude.rotate.test.ts` -> 27 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm dlx bun test --isolate` -> 473 passed, 3 skipped, 5 failed on this Windows environment. Failures are in mailbox-context and memory-scaffold fixture reads, plus task-script tests that expect Unix `/tmp` paths.
- Regression test covers scheduled task runs on a warm query and confirms the next query gets no old continuation.

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — transcript caps now also apply to warm task sessions.
- [ ] Breaking change

```release-note
Long-running scheduled task sessions now rotate oversized or aged transcripts between turns.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

No permission or credential boundary changes. Rotation runs only after a turn completes and before the next turn starts.

prs.title: fix(setup): add /opt/homebrew/bin to launchd plist PATH
prs.body:
### Problem
On Apple Silicon Macs with docker installed from brew the host process crash-loops at startup with `/bin/sh: docker: command not found`, eventually hitting the circuit breaker and stalling setup. Affected: anyone whose `docker`/`podman` CLI comes from Homebrew (e.g. users following `/convert-to-podman`, brew-installed Docker without Desktop, or Apple Container).

### Root cause
`setup/service.ts` writes a hardcoded `PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:~/.local/bin` into the generated plist. On Apple Silicon, Homebrew lives at `/opt/homebrew/bin` — that's where brew-installed `podman` (and any `docker` symlink pointing at it) live. launchd jobs don't inherit the user's interactive shell PATH, so those binaries are invisible to the host process.

This has gone unnoticed because most Mac users run **Docker Desktop**, which installs `docker` at `/usr/local/bin/docker` regardless of CPU arch — already on the plist PATH. The bug only bites the smaller cohort of Apple Silicon users whose container runtime comes from brew. As Podman + Apple Container adoption grows, more users will hit this.

### Fix
Prepend `/opt/homebrew/bin` to the macOS plist PATH. Harmless on Intel Macs (the directory doesn't exist; brew there uses `/usr/local`). Linux systemd unit unchanged.

### Validation
- 10/10 `setup/service.test.ts` tests pass with updated expectation
- Live plist patched + `launchctl bootout`/`bootstrap` cycle: clean start, host stays up, no error log entries
- End-to-end `pnpm run chat hi` returns a real reply from the agent (validates host process → CLI socket → container spawn → Claude API via OneCLI gateway)

issues.body:
# Daily ironclaw failure taxonomy — 2026-10-19

## Suites analyzed
- [officeqa (57 non-pass)](https://nearai.github.io/benchmarks/#/runs/ironclaw/officeqa/4bbe8fbb-dfb5-42a7-aac8-423dd28635d2) — This officeqa run's 57 non-pass tasks are almost entirely genuine model-quality errors by DeepSeek-V4-Flash over OCR-digitized Treasury Bulletins: every representative trajectory shows ironclaw's read/grep/shell/result_read tools succeeding and returning the correct source text, while the model selects the wrong cell/row/year, applies a wrong formula, or (UID0032) literally computes the right answer in one shell run and then submits a different, wrong one. A secondary model behavior drives the HTTP-signature cluster: the model abandons the provided document and tries live external APIs (FRED/BLS/measuringworth), which are correctly denied or fail, leaving it with garbage (UID0221 returned 1061243697 vs an expected 1061). The only harness defect is cosmetic and confirmed live: http.rs:492 labels a denied egress request as InputEncode ('the tool input could not be encoded'), misdirecting model recovery but changing no verdict. No harness fault drives any failure in this run; the dominant numeric-extraction category recurs from the prior run.

_ironclaw rev(s): b0b999d96781516ee05e6ba961d6f3ead900da96_

## 🔧 Harness fix candidates (ranked by blast radius)

| # | Category | Tasks | Suites | Confidence | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | HTTP egress denial mislabeled as InputEncode | 2 | officeqa:2 | 0.86 | `crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/first_party_tools/http.rs:492, crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/services/tests.rs:412, crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/tests/first_party_runtime_contract.rs:342` |

### 1. HTTP egress denial mislabeled as InputEncode — 2 tasks
**Root cause:** In crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/first_party_tools/http.rs the http_error() classifier maps RuntimeHttpEgressReasonCode::RequestDenied (produced by RuntimeHttpEgressError::Request, i.e. an egress request rejected at validation/sanitization — http.rs:551) to RuntimeDispatchErrorKind::InputEncode (http.rs:492). InputEncode's stable string is 'input_encode' with model text 'the tool input could not be encoded' (result_meta.rs:198), which is semantically wrong for a denied request. The sibling line 493 already maps PolicyDenied correctly, and a dedicated NetworkDenied kind exists for exactly this case ('Network egress denied by policy. Never retryable', result_meta.rs:207-210).

**Fix:** Change the RequestDenied arm at http.rs:492 to map to RuntimeDispatchErrorKind::NetworkDenied (preferred — a request rejected by egress validation/policy is a non-retryable network denial, matching result_meta.rs:207-210; PolicyDenied is an acceptable alternative) instead of InputEncode, so the model sees an honest 'egress denied' outcome rather than 'the tool input could not be encoded'. Update the pinned expectation in first_party_runtime_contract.rs:341-343 (and the http_error_kind helper at :782) and the RequestDenied assertion context in services/tests.rs to the new kind; add/adjust a regression assertion that a RequestDenied egress error never surfaces as InputEncode. Reserve InputEncode strictly for genuine argument-encoding failures.

_Files:_ `crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/first_party_tools/http.rs:492`, `crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/src/services/tests.rs:412`, `crates/kernel/ironclaw_host_runtime/tests/first_party_runtime_contract.rs:342`

prs.title: feat(mcp): sign in to remote MCP servers with OAuth
prs.body:
## Summary

Remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP / SSE) can now sign in with MCP OAuth 2.1, so users no longer have to create an API key in the provider's dashboard and paste it into a header.

OpenClaw v2026.8.1 already implements the whole flow: discovery, dynamic client registration, PKCE, the loopback callback on `127.0.0.1:8989`, token storage and refresh. This PR only:

1. writes `auth: "oauth"` into `openclaw.json`, and
2. drives `openclaw mcp login | logout | status` from the MCP page.

The gateway reads the stored token on every request, so signing in takes effect **without a gateway restart**.

## Related Issue

None.

## Changes Made

- **Config** (`src/shared/mcp/auth.ts`, `mcpStore.ts`)
  - New optional `auth?: 'oauth'` on remote servers.
  - Only `'oauth'` is persisted, and stdio servers never carry it, so existing data is unchanged.
- **openclaw.json and gateway sync** (`openclawConfigSync.ts`, `mcpRuntime.ts`)
  - OAuth servers get `auth: "oauth"`.
  - The `authorization` header is dropped, because OpenClaw ignores it on OAuth servers and logs a warning. Other headers are kept.
- **CLI driver** (`src/main/mcp/mcpOAuthCli.ts`, new)
  - Runs the OpenClaw CLI the same way the gateway is started: Electron with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`, the same state dir and config path, plus the secret env vars referenced as `${VAR}` in `openclaw.json`.
  - `login` streams stdout and opens the printed authorization URL once with `shell.openExternal`. Only a bare http(s) line counts as a URL.
  - If OpenClaw cannot bind the loopback port, it still exits 0 but saves no token. The driver detects this and returns `callback_unavailable` **before** opening the browser, so the user is not sent to a dead redirect.
  - Success requires "credentials saved" in stdout.
  - Only one sign-in can run per server at a time.
  - `status --json` is parsed defensively, tolerating log lines around the JSON.
- **IPC**
  - New channels `mcp:oauthLogin`, `mcp:oauthLogout` and `mcp:oauthStatus`.
  - Login syncs `openclaw.json` first, so the CLI sees the server that was just saved.
  - Server keys reuse `safeServerKey()` from the config sync.
- **UI**
  - The server form has a new **Authentication** choice: *None / headers* or *OAuth sign-in*.
  - Tool preview is skipped for OAuth servers, since they answer 401 until signed in.
  - Server cards show a *Signed in* or *Sign-in required* badge, a **Sign in** button (shown as *Waiting for browser…* while in progress), and a **Sign out** menu item.
  - `mcp status` runs only when at least one server uses OAuth.
- **Docs and i18n**
  - zh/en strings.
  - Design doc in `specs/features/mcp-remote-oauth/`.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [ ] Manual testing performed (in the Electron app; see notes below for what was run against the real OpenClaw CLI)

Commands run:

- `tsc` for the renderer and electron configs: clean.
- `npm run compile:electron`: clean.
- `eslint --max-warnings 0` on all changed files: clean.
- `vitest` for `src/main/mcp`, `src/main/ipcHandlers`, `openclawConfigSync.runtime.test.ts`, `src/renderer/components/mcp` and `src/renderer/services`: 903 passed, 5 skipped (the skips are baseline).

New tests:

- `mcpStore` round-trips `auth`.
- `openclawConfigSync` writes `auth: "oauth"` and drops the `authorization` header.
- `mcpOAuthCli` (9 tests, fake child process), covering:
  - URL extraction, including rejecting `file:` and `javascript:` URLs
  - status parsing
  - successful sign-in
  - still-valid stored credentials
  - busy callback port
  - non-zero exit
  - concurrent sign-in
  - missing runtime

Real CLI check: I ran the compiled `mcpOAuthCli` against an **OpenClaw 2026.8.1 runtime** with an isolated state dir and a production MCP server that implements MCP OAuth (discovery + DCR + PKCE).

- `mcp status --json` was parsed as `unauthenticated` before sign-in and `pending-authorization` after the authorize page opened.
- `login` completed discovery and dynamic registration. The authorization URL was extracted and "opened" exactly once (`…/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=…&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:8989/oauth/callback&…`). The run then hit the expected timeout because I did not finish the browser step.
- With another process listening on `127.0.0.1:8989`, `login` returned `callback_unavailable` in about 1s and opened nothing.

## Screenshots (if applicable)

Not included. I did not run the full Electron app for this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [x] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [x] Changes to IPC communication
- [ ] Changes to window management
- [ ] None

## Additional Notes

- **Why the CLI and not the gateway RPC:** OpenClaw exposes MCP OAuth only through `openclaw mcp login|logout|status`. The login command prints the URL instead of opening a browser, which lets the app keep control of `shell.openExternal` and validate the URL first.
- **First turn after sign-in:** if the gateway already tried the server and got a 401, OpenClaw retries the tool catalog about 5 seconds later. A message sent right after signing in may still miss that server's tools. Later turns have them.
- **Token identity:** OpenClaw keys stored credentials by server name + URL. Renaming a server or changing its URL therefore requires signing in again, which seems like the right behavior.
- **Out of scope:**
  - The existing Qichacha integration (`oauthProvider: 'qichacha'`) is untouched.
  - Marketplace entries cannot declare `auth: 'oauth'` yet. That could build on this PR separately.

prs.title: feat(mcp): sign in to remote MCP servers with OAuth
prs.body:
## Summary

Remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP / SSE) can sign in with MCP OAuth 2.1 instead of a pasted API key. OpenClaw v2026.8.1 already runs the whole flow (discovery, dynamic client registration, PKCE, loopback callback, token storage and refresh); LobsterAI writes `auth: "oauth"` into `openclaw.json` and drives `openclaw mcp login | logout | status`.

This PR brings **@alison-xx**'s #2874 (opened against `main`) into `release/2026.10.19`, plus a follow-up commit with fixes and UI polish from review and in-app testing. The two original commits are unchanged and keep @alison-xx as their author.

## Related Issue

Includes #2874 by @alison-xx.

## Changes Made

**From #2874 (@alison-xx)** — `3b46ffd`, `3f5c3ac`
- Optional `auth: 'oauth'` on remote servers, written to `openclaw.json` (the ignored `authorization` header is dropped).
- `mcpOAuthCli` driver: runs the OpenClaw CLI like the gateway does, opens the printed authorization URL once (http/https only), detects a busy loopback port before opening the browser, parses `mcp status --json`.
- IPC `mcp:oauthLogin`, `mcp:oauthLogout`, `mcp:oauthStatus`; an Authentication choice in the server form; zh/en strings; design doc.

**Follow-up** — `37db4f6`
- **Cancel and cleanup:** a pending sign-in can be cancelled (new `mcp:oauthCancel` IPC). Every pending `openclaw mcp login` is stopped on app quit, so none keeps `127.0.0.1:8989`.
- **Token cleanup:** before a server is deleted or loses its OAuth identity (rename, URL change, auth turned off, switch to stdio), its tokens are cleared, so they don't linger or come back when the same server is re-added.
- **Disabled servers:** they are treated as not loaded, and sign-out syncs `openclaw.json` first. This fixes a false "sign-out failed" right after a toggle, when the status read still saw the old config.
- **CLI errors:** color codes and unrelated `[config] warnings` lines are stripped. "No MCP server named" maps to `server_not_loaded` with a clear message.
- **JSON import:** keeps `auth: "oauth"`.
- **Card UI:** "Sign in" reuses the marketplace Qichacha capsule and wording, placed at the bottom right of installed cards so the header stays name + toggle. It turns into Cancel while the browser step is pending. Badges only show state (Authorizing… / Authorized). The detail dialog shows the authorization state and a Sign in / Cancel action, with Sign out in its footer.
- **Card cleanup:** installed cards no longer repeat the URL/command in the badge row; the description line already falls back to it.
- **Copy:** the form says tool preview isn't available for OAuth servers, instead of promising it after sign-in.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

- `npm test`: 7592 passed, 157 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `src/main/skills/skillManager.watcher.test.ts` (a file-watcher timing test, untouched by this branch); it timed out under full-suite load and passes when re-run alone (2/2).
- `tsc` (renderer) and `npm run compile:electron`: clean. ESLint with `--max-warnings 0` on all changed files: clean.
- New unit tests cover cancel (CLI killed, port freed), sign-out mapping, best-effort token cleanup, the identity-change check, CLI output cleanup (using real stderr captured from the runtime), and JSON import of `auth`.
- **End-to-end against the real OpenClaw v2026.8.1 runtime**, with a local MCP OAuth server (DCR + PKCE + approval page):
  - sign-in through the loopback callback; a second sign-in reuses the stored token;
  - deny on the approval page fails cleanly;
  - `openclaw mcp probe` lists the server's tools with the stored token;
  - revoking tokens server-side moves the state to pending, and signing in again works;
  - cancel frees port 8989; a busy port returns `callback_unavailable` without opening the browser;
  - sign-out and best-effort cleanup clear the token.
- **UI:** the real `McpManager` was rendered in a browser harness with a mocked bridge and checked in zh/en and light/dark: every sign-in state, cancel, the detail dialog, and the stale-status race after disabling a server.
- **Manual:** tested in the Electron app by @wangning.

## Screenshots (if applicable)

Installed card, bottom row:

| State | Badge row |
| --- | --- |
| Not authorized | `Custom` `http` ……… **Sign in** (capsule) |
| Authorizing | `Custom` `http` `⟳ Authorizing…` ……… Cancel |
| Authorized | `Custom` `http` `Authorized` |
| Disabled | `Custom` `http` |

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [x] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [x] Changes to IPC communication
- [ ] Changes to window management
- [ ] None

- **IPC:** new channels `mcp:oauthLogin`, `mcp:oauthCancel`, `mcp:oauthLogout`, `mcp:oauthStatus`.
- **OpenClaw config:** remote servers with `auth: 'oauth'` get `auth: "oauth"` in `mcp.servers`, without an `authorization` header. Signing in needs no gateway restart, because the gateway reads the stored token on every request.
- **Runtime:** the main process spawns short-lived `openclaw mcp …` CLI processes (Electron as Node, same state dir, config and secrets as the gateway); a pending login is killed on cancel and on app quit.
- **Storage:** `auth` is an optional field in the existing `mcp_servers.config_json`; there is no migration.

## Additional Notes

- **Credit:** the feature design and first implementation are @alison-xx's (#2874). Squash and merge-commit merges both keep their commits' authorship.
- **Disabled servers:** they can't be signed out until re-enabled, because the CLI only resolves servers in `openclaw.json`. For the same reason, deleting a disabled OAuth server leaves its tokens in OpenClaw's state.
- **Token identity:** tokens are keyed by server name + URL, so a rename or URL change requires signing in again.
- **Out of scope:** marketplace entries can't declare `auth: 'oauth'` yet.

prs.title: feat(providers): refresh builtin default models
prs.body:
## Summary

Refreshes the builtin default model lists for DeepSeek, Moonshot, Qwen, Zhipu, MiniMax and Xiaomi so each provider lists its latest model first, and switches the global default model from the retired `deepseek-reasoner` to `deepseek-v4-flash`.

Only the system defaults change. Saved user configs are not migrated: existing provider model lists and the selected default model are left exactly as they are.

This replaces the approach in https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2859, which filtered still-served model IDs out of saved configs on every startup and reset default models across providers.

## Related Issue

N/A

## Changes Made

| Provider | New default list (first = default) | Moved to `legacyModels` |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek | `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro` | `deepseek-reasoner` (retired 2026-07-24) |
| Moonshot | `kimi-k3`, `kimi-k2.7-code`, `kimi-k2.6` | `kimi-k2.5` (sunset 2026-08-31) |
| Qwen | `qwen3.8-max`, `qwen3.7-plus`, `qwen3.8-flash` | `qwen3.6-plus`, `qwen3.5-plus` |
| Zhipu | `glm-5.3`, `glm-5.3-flash`, `glm-5.1` | `glm-5`, `glm-4.7` |
| MiniMax | `MiniMax-M3`, `MiniMax-M2.7`, `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` | `MiniMax-M2.5` |
| Xiaomi | `mimo-v2.6-pro`, `mimo-v2.5` | `mimo-v2.5-pro` |

- **`legacyModels`:** a new optional field on provider definitions. These models are no longer seeded into new configs, but `ProviderRegistry` still uses them for image / thinking / context-window lookups. Without it, saved entries that rely on registry metadata would silently change behavior, for example losing the `qwen3.6-plus` image-support repair or the `glm-5` thinking flag.
- **Runtime-supported IDs only:** every new default is a model the pinned OpenClaw runtime (v2026.8.1) already handles. Three newer IDs were left out on purpose:

prs.title: feat(cowork): show turn credits and model preset for IM and cron runs
prs.body:
## Summary

Turns started from the desktop already show their credits when they use a package model. Turns that OpenClaw starts on its own, from IM messages and scheduled tasks, now show them too, along with the 快速/旗舰 preset label.

These runs have no client trace. Their model requests still carry OpenClaw's own `traceparent`, and lobsterai-server already records usage by that trace. So the client only needs to learn which trace belongs to which local turn.

- **Plugin:** `lobster-model-routing` registers `model_call_started`. For each run it reports the package-model trace once to the local token proxy (`POST /lobsterai/native-run-llm-traces`), along with the resolved model and the virtual preset (`yd-fast`/`yd-ultra`) when one was used. The proxy answers locally and forwards nothing.
- **Binding:** `nativeRunTurnUsage.ts` keeps traces and media task ids per run id. When the turn ends, `CoworkTurnUsageService` binds them to the run's synced user message (`llmTrace`, `turnMediaTaskIds`, `modelPresetId`/`resolvedModelId`). It then settles through the existing `GET /api/usage/llm-traces/{traceId}`. Desktop traces registered for `chat.send` are ignored.
- **When settlement runs:**
  - Turns the adapter follows settle on `complete`/`error`, using the turn's run ids. This covers cron runs.
  - IM runs often have no local turn and only get `sessions.changed` lifecycle events. They now sync the conversation history on lifecycle end, then settle.
- **Retried cron runs:** OpenClaw gives each attempt its own trace. Those traces are stored as `relatedTraceIds`, and their summaries are merged.
- **Safety:**
  - Usage is never bound to a user message that was answered before the run started. This uses OpenClaw's run start `ts`.
  - History reconciliation now keeps usage/preset metadata when it replaces user messages.
  - Persisting falls back to the replaced copy of the message.
- **UI:**
  - IM/cron replies take the preset label from their user message, for example `快速（deepseek-flash）`.
  - The model label is removed from under user input. It now only shows after replies, on desktop too.
- **Dev tooling:** the startup sync of `openclaw-extensions` now removes a stale precompiled `.js` bundle when the TypeScript source changes. Before, OpenClaw kept loading the old bundle until `npm run openclaw:precompile` ran.

The server API is unchanged.

## Electron-specific behavior

- **OpenClaw plugin:** `lobster-model-routing` adds a `model_call_started` hook. In dev, the change is picked up after the extension sync and a gateway restart. Packaged builds precompile it as before.
- **Token proxy:** adds a loopback-only route behind the existing inbound proxy token.
- **Runtime/IPC:** `CoworkRuntime` gains optional `getTurnRunIds`. The adapter gains an `onChannelRunEnded` option. There are no new IPC channels: credits still reach the renderer through `cowork:stream:turnUsage`.
- **Storage:** IM/cron user messages may now carry `llmTrace`, `turnUsage`, `turnMediaTaskIds`, `modelPresetId` and `resolvedModelId` metadata. There is no schema change.
- **Load:** each IM turn end now triggers one extra `chat.history` sync. Each settled turn makes one usage summary request per trace.

## Not covered

- Messages from before this change get no credits or preset label.
- Subagent runs keep the existing behavior.
- IM replies on `yd-fast`/`yd-ultra` can show an OpenClaw "Model Fallback" notice. That comes from the virtual model routing added on 10-16, not from this change, and is tracked separately.

## Testing

- Added Vitest coverage for:
  - trace merging
  - the native run registry
  - the proxy route
  - binding, the stale-turn guard and replaced-message persistence
  - IM lifecycle settlement
  - reconciliation metadata carry-over
  - the reply preset label
  - stale bundle removal
- `npm test` passes except for unrelated suites that fail only under full-suite load and pass in isolation.
- CI eslint on touched files, `npm run compile:electron` and `npx tsc --noEmit` pass.
- Manually checked in `npm run electron:dev`:
  - credits show for a scheduled task and for WeChat messages
  - `快速（deepseek-flash）` shows on IM replies
  - no model label shows under user input

prs.title: feat(desktop): add custom and animated GIF companion skins, screenshot tools and follow-ups
prs.body:
## Summary
Add portable desktop customization and interaction improvements while preserving LobsterAI's built-in skins and branding.

- **Custom companion skins:** upload PNG/JPEG/WebP or animated GIF, preview, save multiple named skins, switch, rename/delete, and restore the default. Static images support scale/position adjustments and normalize to 512×512 PNG. GIFs retain their original frames, timing, transparency, loop metadata and aspect ratio in previews and on the desktop; static crop controls are hidden for GIFs.
- **Cowork follow-up suggestions:** show one contextual suggestion after a completed reply. Tab inserts an editable draft and Escape dismisses it; it never auto-sends. Requests use existing model configuration, a 10-second timeout, scoped caching and stale-response protection.
- **Screenshot tools:** adjust the region, annotate shapes/arrows/pen/mosaic/text, undo, copy, save, ask LobsterAI, extract text or translate. Independent Cowork tasks preserve the unsent composer draft and provide retry after failure.

## Electron-specific behavior
- Custom images stay in the local profile under content-hash filenames. Static formats accept uploads up to 5 MB; GIFs up to 2 MB, with each dimension between 128 and 2048 pixels. Validate GIF structure, frame bounds, byte limits, file ownership and content hash before restoration. Preserve GIF bytes instead of flattening through canvas or Electron nativeImage.
- Keep sandboxing and main-frame/sender checks; only the main settings window can mutate skins. Existing PNG profiles remain compatible. The desktop image element stays mounted across task mood changes.
- Keep per-display screenshot capture and explicit crop approval. Add preload bridges for local skin management, isolated screenshot tasks and suggestions.
- No server API, database migration, bundled runtime change, billing or private cloud image-generation dependency.

## Validation
- GIF follow-up: **166 tests passed across 5 files**, covering local persistence/restoration/deletion, malformed and oversized GIFs, forged types, symlinks, unchanged animation bytes, editor behavior, stable desktop image mounting and companion manager regressions.
- Renderer TypeScript (`tsc --noEmit`), Electron compilation, production build and changed-file ESLint (zero warnings): passed. `git diff --check`: passed.
- Windows Electron 43.5.0 component smoke: real upload decoding, animated editor preview, original-byte apply callback and desktop character playback passed. Captured two distinct rendered animation frames. The fixture mounts the actual editor and character components; it does not exercise the full app IPC/window lifecycle.
- Earlier base contribution: 241 focused tests passed, 1 macOS-only test skipped, plus renderer/main type checks, lint and production build.

## Screenshot
Actual Electron component smoke using a generated two-frame fixture:

![Custom GIF preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alison-xx/LobsterAI/feat/companion-customization-cowork-suggestions/specs/features/desktop-companion/custom-gif-preview.png)

## Remaining manual coverage
Full-app native file-picker/IPC roundtrip, restart across actual profile sessions, multi-monitor/DPI behavior, OS clipboard/save dialogs, and live-model OCR/translation/suggestions still need manual desktop acceptance. The component smoke and automated tests do not claim that coverage.

prs.title: feat(providers): support OpenAI Responses and Gemini formats for custom providers
prs.body:
## Summary

Custom model providers can now use the **OpenAI Responses** and native **Gemini (generateContent)** API formats, on top of OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic. Both reuse OpenClaw's native transports instead of adding LobsterAI-side protocol code.

- **Settings UI:** the API format radio buttons become one dropdown. Custom providers list OpenAI Chat Completions, Anthropic, OpenAI Responses and Gemini; built-in providers keep Chat Completions and Anthropic only.
- **Storage:** Responses is a sub-mode, `ProviderConfig.openaiApiMode`, stored next to `apiFormat: 'openai'`. Older builds therefore fall back to Chat Completions. Gemini is stored as `apiFormat: 'gemini'` on custom providers only.
- **OpenClaw config sync:** Responses mode maps to the `openai-responses` transport (a pasted `/responses` suffix is stripped). Custom Gemini maps to `google-generative-ai`, with a versioned base URL that keeps relay path prefixes and adds `/v1beta` when no version is given.
- **Other callers follow the same choice:** the connection test (native `generateContent` probe for Gemini) and provider export/import, plus the compat proxy, legacy chat path and native Gemini clients for titles and quick answers.

### Why built-in providers don't get Responses yet

Several OpenClaw provider plugins are tuned for Chat Completions:

- The DeepSeek V4 and Xiaomi MiMo thinking wrappers inject Chat Completions fields regardless of transport. This is still true upstream in v2026.10.4.
- Moonshot's Kimi K3 runtime profile requires Chat Completions.
- Volcengine Ark rejects unknown Responses fields.

So the option is limited to custom providers for now.

## Electron-specific behavior

- **OpenClaw config:** changes only for custom providers set to Responses or Gemini. The gateway picks the new transport up through the normal config sync.
- **Provider export:** writes `openaiApiMode` only when it is Responses, so default exports stay importable by older builds with the strict schema.
- **Renderer config normalization:** keeps `apiFormat: 'gemini'` on custom providers. It used to coerce unknown formats to Anthropic.

## Summary
Restoring a data-migration backup from inside the running app fails and rolls back because the "clear old data" step hits `EBUSY` on `userData/Partitions`. prs.title: fix(openclaw): let callers apply a pending deferred gateway restart
prs.body:
## Summary
While a config-driven gateway restart is deferred, starting a new session is rejected with "please try again later" even when the gateway is already idle.

## Related Issue
N/A

## Changes Made
- Root cause: after an MCP/config change that needs a restart, `scheduleDeferredGatewayRestart()` queues the restart until workloads drain (polled every 3 s). Meanwhile `waitForOpenClawConfigApply()` returned the pending/overdue status for every caller as long as `deferredRestartReason` was set, without checking whether the gateway was idle.
- How it is triggered: change MCP servers or config while a task is running (or right before starting a session). The restart is deferred, and the next session start bounces with the "applying configuration" message until the poller happens to fire.
- Fix: extract `admitPastDeferredGatewayRestart()` (`src/main/libs/openclawDeferredRestartAdmission.ts`) and use it in `waitForOpenClawConfigApply()`:
  - idle gateway (the same busy check the poller uses): apply the deferred restart immediately and continue;
  - active workloads: wait up to 45 s for the scheduled restart to land, then await the resulting config apply and continue;
  - still queued after the wait (or re-deferred): return the existing pending / overdue status unchanged;
  - a failed config sync is surfaced instead of the generic pending message (`executeDeferredGatewayRestart()` now returns the sync result).

prs.title: fix(media): check user intent before generating paid images and videos
prs.body:
## Summary
The media model selection stays active across messages, and the media generation callback only checks that a model is selected (`resolveMediaGenerationGate`, `src/main/mediaGenerationPolicy.ts`). The chat model can therefore start a paid image or video generation when the user did not ask for one. On a downstream build we saw a refusal ("No image is needed this turn. The user asked not to generate images…") passed as the prompt, rendered into a picture and billed. This PR checks the user's intent before a generate request is submitted, and tightens the per-turn media instruction.

## Related Issue
N/A

## Changes Made
- New `src/main/mediaGenerationIntentGuard.ts`, used by `handleMediaGenerationCallback` right after the existing selection gate and before any cost confirmation. It cancels a generate request (status `cancelled`, with a corrective tool result for the model) when:
  - the latest user message, or an earlier one that no newer message overrides, asks to stop or pause image/video generation. An explicit generation request or a follow-up on earlier media ("make the background red", "another one") lifts the pause.
  - the tool prompt is a refusal or meta instruction instead of a visual description. Negative visual constraints ("no text or watermark", "不要生成图片边框") are still allowed.
  - the assistant asked the user to confirm the media in this turn and has no answer yet. An answered `AskUserQuestion` call resolves it, so generation right after the answer is not blocked.
- Skin workflows (`SkinRuntimeController.hasActiveWorkflow`) only get the prompt check, because they drive their own generation steps.
- `buildMediaGenerationTurnInstruction`: generate only when the current message asks for media; stop requests persist; wait for answers to confirmation questions; the prompt must describe visual content; no simulated tool calls via shell/echo.

prs.title: feat(cowork): add Auto and Max model modes
prs.body:
## Summary
Adds two per-session model modes to Cowork. **Auto** picks a suitable model for every turn. **Max** runs a conversation on the model the user chose as their strongest. The routing policy is derived locally from the models the user can already use and can optionally be overridden in Settings. Nothing changes for users who don't pick either mode.

## Related Issue
N/A

## Changes Made
- **Auto classification** (pure heuristic; no extra model call, latency or tokens): image attachments → vision; roughly ≥6k estimated tokens of prompt plus selected text → long context; fenced code, source-file references or code keywords → code; everything else → general. Precedence: vision > long context > code > general.
- **Policy derivation** (`src/shared/cowork/autoModelRouting.ts`). Candidates are the enabled provider models plus server models that are accessible and pass the existing server run gate. Defaults:
  - general = the session / agent model;
  - code = general;
  - vision = general if it reads images, otherwise the first image-capable model (same provider preferred);
  - long context = the model with the largest known context window, only when it is strictly larger than the general model's.
  Overrides that point at a model that is no longer usable are ignored; anything unresolved falls back to the agent model.
- **Settings**: Settings → Agent Engine → "Auto / Max models" lets users override the general, code, vision and long-context models and choose the Max model. Stored in the Cowork config as `autoModelRouting`.
- **Visibility**: Auto is offered when at least two usable models exist. Max is offered only when a usable Max model is explicitly configured; it is never guessed. Neither is offered for IM-managed sessions.
- **Auto semantics**: stored as the reserved ref `lobsterai/__auto__` in `session.modelOverride` and re-resolved on every turn; the resolved model is patched for that turn only. The sentinel is never written back, never sent to the gateway (selecting Auto stores it locally without a `sessions.patch`), never appears in the outbound prompt, and is skipped by the run gate, thinking-level resolution, error details and the gateway model-echo sync. The selector shows a subtle "This turn: <model>" hint driven by the display-only `cowork:session:modelAutoResolved` event.
- **Max semantics**: a per-session flag that overlays the current selection (an explicit model or Auto). Turning it off restores the previous selection, because the selection itself is never modified.
- **New task**: the home / new-task selector supports Auto and Max for the task it starts; the agent's default model is never changed. Agent configuration and scheduled-task selectors are unaffected.
- **Persistence**: new `cowork_sessions.max_mode INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` column added through a required migration following the `thinking_level` pattern; forks carry Auto and Max over. New IPC: `cowork:session:setMaxMode`.

prs.title: feat(openclaw): keep user overrides in openclaw.user.json across config syncs
prs.body:
## Summary
LobsterAI regenerates `openclaw.json` on every config sync, so users who hand-edit it (e.g. to enable enhancement plugins or tweak OpenClaw options) lose their changes on restart. Instead of a "protection" switch that freezes the file — which would stop model, IM, MCP, skill and agent changes from reaching the gateway and can break startup when ports or plugin paths change — this adds a persistent user override layer: `openclaw.user.json` next to `openclaw.json` is merged on top of every rendered config.

Merge order: LobsterAI-generated config → user overrides → enterprise config (enterprise still wins).

## Related Issue
User feedback: manual `openclaw.json` edits are reset after restart; request for a protection toggle.

## Changes Made
- **Override layer** (`src/main/libs/openclawUserConfigOverlay.ts`): JSON5 file (comments, trailing commas), JSON Merge Patch semantics (objects merge, arrays replace, `null` removes). `plugins.allow` / `plugins.load.paths` are unioned so users can't drop bundled plugins; `plugins.allow` stays sorted so repeated syncs are stable.
- **Protected paths** are ignored and reported: `gateway.auth/mode/port`, `meta`, `agents.defaults.sessionStore`, `plugins.installs`, `plugins.slots.memory`, LobsterAI-internal plugin entries, and `$include` anywhere.
- **Removal works**: the renderer copies existing `gateway`, `plugins.entries` and unknown top-level keys back from the file, so a deleted override would otherwise linger. The paths each sync applied are recorded (kv) and reverted from the base before the next render, only where the value is still what was applied. `createOpenClawConfigTarget` gains an optional merge base / extra owned sections; `baseRaw` stays the real file so the rebase propagates removals.
- **Fail-safe**: a syntax error keeps the last valid overrides. If OpenClaw rejects the config (`config.apply` → `Rejected`, or startup "Invalid config"), overrides are suspended and the config is retried without them (the gateway is restarted once on startup failure); if it still fails, overrides are restored and not blamed again. Quick Repair also suspends overrides until the user applies them again.
- **Settings card** in Agent Engine → 运行维护: enable toggle, state (missing / active / parse error / suspended / disabled), overridden and ignored paths, OpenClaw's rejection detail, Open File / Show in Folder / Apply. zh + en strings.
- **IPC**: `openclaw:userConfig:*` (constants in `src/shared/openclawUserConfig/constants.ts`), handlers in `src/main/ipcHandlers/openclawUserConfig/handlers.ts`, exposed as `window.electron.openclaw.userConfig`.
- `json5` added as a runtime dependency (was dev-only transitively). It's imported as `json5/lib/parse` because the package's ESM entry has only a default export, which broke the Vite-bundled main process with a named import.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): let managed workspaces follow a relinked target
prs.body:
## Summary

A macOS user reported that every main-agent message failed with `workspace path alias points to a different current target`. Their logs show the cause: the user keeps the agent workspace in OneDrive, so the agent replaced `openclaw/state/workspace-main` with a link to the OneDrive folder. OpenClaw v2026.8.1 had already recorded the original real path in `workspace_path_aliases`. Once the path resolved somewhere else, it refused every message, including heartbeat runs, until the database was edited by hand. This happened twice: on 10-17, and on 10-18 after a data-migration restore, which skips links, put the empty template back and the agent linked it again.

## Changes

- **OpenClaw patch** `scripts/patches/v2026.8.1/openclaw-managed-workspace-alias-follow.patch` (changes only `src/agents/workspace-state-store.ts`, plus tests). It applies to workspace paths strictly below `LOBSTERAI_MANAGED_WORKSPACE_ROOT` that still exist. For those paths:
  - Alias rows pointing at an older target are ignored, and the current target's own records are used.
  - The next state write repoints the stale rows and logs a `workspace` warning naming both paths.
  - The previous target's records are left in place, not moved. Moving its file attestation would make OpenClaw report the linked folder as vanished.

  Missing paths keep their stored owner, so vanished-workspace protection is unchanged. Other paths, and processes without the variable, keep upstream's fail-closed behavior. Upstream #133198 (v2026.9.4) only improves the error and adds a confirmed `doctor --fix` rebind, so the README says to keep an equivalent of this patch after upgrading.
- **Environment:** the Gateway and the startup compatibility/repair helper now set the variable to the OpenClaw state directory (`OPENCLAW_MANAGED_WORKSPACE_ROOT_ENV` in `src/shared/openclawEngine/constants.ts`).
- **Error message:** the remaining alias errors map to `coworkErrorWorkspaceAliasRepointed`, with zh/en text in both the renderer and main-process i18n.
- **Patch bookkeeping:** a strong validator in `apply-openclaw-patches.cjs`, a README section, the patch added to the reviewed v2026.8.1 patch list, and a patch-content test that keeps the variable name in sync.

## Electron-specific behavior

- Adds one environment variable to the OpenClaw Gateway process and to the startup compatibility/repair helper processes.
- No IPC, storage schema, or config changes. The OpenClaw runtime must be rebuilt to pick up the patch.

## Testing

- All 67 v2026.8.1 patches apply to a clean tag checkout, and strong validation passes.
- OpenClaw: 8 new cases (6 store, 2 end-to-end through `ensureAgentWorkspace`). The end-to-end case relinks a seeded workspace to a "synced" folder that already holds agent files; messages succeed and no `BOOTSTRAP.md` is created. The control case without the variable reproduces the reported error. The 37 related workspace and migration test files (495 tests) pass, and `tsgo` core has 0 errors.
- LobsterAI: the full `npm test` run passes (7421 tests), targeted tests pass again after rebasing on the latest release branch, ESLint is clean on changed files, and `compile:electron` passes.
- **Not yet done:** in-app validation with a rebuilt runtime. Steps: initialize the main agent, quit, replace `openclaw/state/workspace-main` with a link to a folder that already holds agent files, and restart. Messages must succeed, the linked folder must not get a `BOOTSTRAP.md`, and the Gateway log must show `Workspace path alias now follows its current target.` once.

prs.title: test(openclaw): keep repair prune fixture mtime independent of the real clock
prs.body:
## Summary

`openclawCompatibilityRepair.test.ts > retained runs lose regenerable caches but keep state and site data, and the manifest records it` fails on `release/2026.10.19` since roughly 2026-10-17 11:00 UTC.

**Root cause (test-only):** `backupRuns()` sets each fixture run's mtime last, but this test then writes the snapshot manifest into `runs[0]`, which bumps that directory's mtime to the real clock. The prune runs with an injected `NOW = 2026-10-17T12:00Z` and treats any run with `NOW - mtime < 1h` as possibly in progress, so once real time passed `NOW - 1h`, `runs[0]` was skipped and its caches were not stripped.

**Fix:** restore `runs[0]`'s mtime after writing the manifest. `pruneOpenClawRepairBackups` is unchanged; treating a run with a future mtime as in progress is the intended conservative behavior (covered by the `oldest-named` in-progress case).

The other fixed-clock disk cleanup tests (`openclawSessionImportArchiveCleanup`, `openclawSessionStoreTempCleanup`) already set mtimes after writing, so they are not affected.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/main/libs/openclawCompatibilityRepair.test.ts src/main/libs/openclawCompatibilityRepairCore.test.ts src/main/libs/openclawStartupDiskCleanup.test.ts src/main/libs/openclawRepairSnapshotPaths.test.ts`: 70 passed
- [x] `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0 src/main/libs/openclawCompatibilityRepair.test.ts`: clean
