issues.title: [Feature]: Plugin-facing theme extension point (semantic token override layer)
issues.body:
## Summary

The Console theme system added in #7741 lets **users** pick a palette (6 built-ins) and customize accent / hover / background / surface / radius. But **plugins** still have exactly one theme knob: `window.QwenPaw.chat.theme.set(pluginId, { colorPrimary })`. Plugin authors who want deeper theming (backgrounds, glass / `backdrop-filter`, full palettes) have no official hook, so they end up injecting CSS.

Proposal (for discussion): add a **plugin-facing semantic token override layer**, built on QwenPaw's *own* semantic tokens rather than the upstream UI library's raw tokens — so plugins can theme deeply **without coupling to upstream upgrades**.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Problem / Motivation

1. **Plugin theming is one-dimensional today.** The plugin theme API only accepts `colorPrimary` (see `plugins/types/qwenpaw.d.ts` and `plugins/hostSdk/install.ts` → `themeFieldMap`). Everything else is unreachable from a plugin.
2. **The marketplace already proves both the demand and the fragility of the workaround.** Appearance plugins such as *QwenPaw Skin Studio*, *background-wallpaper*, and *No Glass (Flat UI)* all describe themselves as "pure frontend, zero-dependency" — i.e. they inject CSS and poke the DOM directly. That breaks whenever the Console's markup or styles change.
3. **Why not simply expose the upstream tokens?** Because `plugins/types/qwenpaw.d.ts` deliberately keeps the public surface stable *"across vendor upgrades"* — exposing the upstream UI library's raw tokens would couple every plugin theme to that library's token names. The layer worth opening is **QwenPaw's own semantic layer**, part of which already exists (see #7682).

## Proposed Solution

Two steps, in order:

1. **Own the layer.** Make the Console's theming go through **QwenPaw-owned semantic tokens** (semantic role names → mapped internally to whatever the underlying UI library expects). #7682 ("use semantic tokens in SettingsCenter") is already a step in this direction.
2. **Open the layer to plugins.** Add a plugin API to override those semantic tokens, with the same disposable / registration semantics as the rest of the plugin SDK, e.g.:

```js
const dispose = window.QwenPaw.chat.theme.overrideTokens("my-plugin", {
  "surface":         { light: "#ffffff", dark: "#1f1f1f" },
  "chat.background": { light: "#fafafa", dark: "#111111" },
  // ...any semantic token; both light & dark required, so an override
  // never goes illegible when the user flips the color scheme.
});
```

Because plugins override **QwenPaw's semantic names**, an upstream library upgrade only changes QwenPaw's internal mapping — plugin themes keep working. That removes the exact risk that motivates keeping the surface closed today.

Happy to start with a **minimal first cut** (e.g. the handful of tokens the Console already uses for surface / background / border / text) and grow from there, rather than a big-bang "full skin system".

## Alternatives Considered

- **Status quo — each plugin injects CSS.** Works, but fragile and duplicated; breaks on Console changes; no clean restore. (This is what marketplace appearance plugins do today.)
- **Expose the upstream UI library's raw tokens directly.** Rejected — couples plugins to upstream token names and contradicts the existing "do not expose vendor config" design intent.
- **Only widen the current scalar list** (accent / surface / radius / …). Helps a little, but still cannot reach backgrounds / glass / full palettes.

## Additional Context

- Related: #7741 (merged — 6 palettes + accent/hover/background/surface/radius), #7406, #5909, #6312 (superseded by #7741), #7287 (external frontend gateway — `not_planned`).
- **Reference design**: DeepSeek Harness ships exactly this — `ctx.theme.overrideTokens(source, tokens)` plus a `ThemeDefinition` type (alias-token overrides, light + dark required), documented as *"Third-party themes can register alias-token overrides through `ctx.theme`."*
- Marketplace plugins currently working around this: `@osier-yi/qwenpaw-dream-skin`, `@levodoubt/background-wallpaper`, `@erickcharles/qwenpaw-no-glass`.

## Willing to Contribute

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

---

### 中文摘要

Console 的主题系统（#7741）让**用户**能换 6 套预设、自定义 accent / 背景 / 表面 / 圆角；但**插件**目前只有一个主题接口 `chat.theme.set(id, { colorPrimary })`。插件想深度定制（背景、毛玻璃、整套配色）没有官方入口，只能注入 CSS —— 市场里的外观类插件（Skin Studio、背景壁纸、去玻璃化）都是这么干的，Console 一改版就失效。

建议：**在 QwenPaw 自己的语义 token 层上加一个面向插件的覆盖接口**（而不是暴露上游 `AgentScope Runtime WebUI` 的原始 token）—— 这样上游升级时插件主题不受影响（只需 QwenPaw 内部重新映射）。愿意在讨论通过后提 PR，可先做最小版本。

issues.title: send_file_to_user audio file permanently wedges the session — LM Studio's 400 At most 0 audio(s) may be provided in one prompt. is not recognized by the audio-fallback / media-capability classifiers
issues.body:
This is a third rejection shape of the family documented in #7015 (fixed by #7024) and partially addressed by the still-open PR #7654.

When the agent delivers a local audio file via send_file_to_user, the file is delivered successfully, but the tool result's output keeps the audio DataBlock (media_type: audio/mpeg, source: file://…) in the persisted session history. On every subsequent model call in that session, OpenAIChatFormatter (whose input_types defaults include audio/*) serializes the block into an input_audio part and the local endpoint rejects it:

Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'At most 0 audio(s) may be provided in one prompt. (parameter=audio)', 'type': 'BadRequestError', 'param': 'audio', 'code': 400}}
Because neither reactive classifier matches this wording, QwenPaw's strip → retry → learn recovery never triggers:

_is_audio_fallback_error() (qwenpaw/agents/react_agent.py) currently requires DashScope-specific markers (internalerror.algo.invalidparameter, "incorrect modal", "was entered", "may not be supported by the model", "wrong position") — none appear in this response.
The error also fails every _EXPLICIT_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_PATTERNS regex (it contains no "does not support" / "is not supported" / "unsupported modality" phrasing).
Result: the exception propagates to the user, no rejects_audio capability is learned, the block remains in history, and every subsequent message in the session fails identically — the conversation is permanently unrecoverable from the user side (6/6 consecutive user messages failed across ~50 minutes in my repro) without manual history surgery.

Related PR(s): #7015 / #7024 (same wedge mechanism, DashScope shape), #7654 (open; adds DashScope URL-shape and llama-server audio input is not supported 500 — does not cover this shape).

Security considerations: None. No credentials or file contents are included; all details below are sanitized.

Component(s) Affected
 Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
 Console (frontend web UI)
 Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
 Skills
 CLI
 Documentation (website)
 Tests
 CI/CD
 Scripts / Deploy
Environment
QwenPaw 2.2.1, Python 3.12, Linux (aarch64)
Provider: lmstudio (local OpenAI-compatible server), model qwen3.8-flash-next (text + vision; audio input limit = 0)
Channel: WeChat personal (the console channel reproduces the same failure; the channel is not the cause)
Steps to Reproduce
Use an OpenAI-compatible local model with no audio input support (LM Studio / vLLM-family engine).
Have the agent generate a small .mp3 (e.g. via edge-tts) and deliver it with send_file_to_user — the file is delivered successfully.
Send any plain-text message in the same session.
Keep sending messages — every subsequent request fails with the same 400.
Actual Result
Every subsequent model call in the session fails with BadRequestError 400: At most 0 audio(s) may be provided in one prompt. (parameter=audio). No strip-and-retry occurs, nothing is learned into ModelCapabilityCache, and the session is dead until a human removes the block from sessions/<channel>/…json.

Verified with the runtime's own formatter: formatting the poisoned assistant message produced an input_audio part (~92 KB wire); after removing the block from the session JSON, the same format call emits 0 input_audio parts and the image blocks in other messages remain intact.

Expected Result
The audio-fallback path should classify this response, strip audio, retry, and learn rejects_audio for the model — like the DashScope shapes from #7015 / #7654 — so at most one turn degrades instead of the whole session dying.

Root cause (verified in installed 2.2.1 source)
agentscope.formatter.OpenAIChatFormatter.input_types defaults to ["text/plain", "image/*", "audio/*", "application/pdf"]; QwenPaw does not narrow this for models without audio capability.
The tool-result audio DataBlock is persisted into session history by send_file_to_user, so it is replayed on every request.
react_agent._is_audio_fallback_error() is DashScope-wording-only, and _EXPLICIT_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_PATTERNS has no pattern for at most N <modal>(s) may be provided in one prompt / (parameter=<modal>), so both recovery gates evaluate False and the error is re-raised.
agents.audio_mode = "auto" only governs inbound audio (transcription/placeholder); outbound tool-result media blocks bypass it entirely.
Suggested fix
Add a request-scoped pattern like at most \d+ (audio|image|video)s? may be provided in one prompt (and/or \(parameter=(audio|image|video)\)) to the audio-fallback / unsupported-media classifiers — most naturally as an extension of #7654, ideally mapping the parameter field so an image/video variant also routes to the correct stripping path.
Longer term, consider sanitizing (or capability-gating) non-text blocks in send_file_to_user tool results before persistence, so a delivered file never becomes model input in the first place — the delivered artifact is for the user, not the model.
Additional notes
Workaround in the wild (what unblocked the session): back up sessions/<channel>/<user>.json, replace the audio DataBlock inside the tool-result output with a text note, save. Session state is re-read from disk per request, so no restart is needed. Happy to contribute a regression test fixture reproducing this response body.

issues.title: [Bug] Feishu channel fails with 426 Upgrade Required when HTTP(S)_PROXY is injected without NO_PROXY for feishu.cn
issues.body:
## Summary

When QwenPaw runs in an environment where `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` are injected but `NO_PROXY` does **not** include `feishu.cn`, the Feishu channel cannot connect at all:

- The WebSocket long-connection thread fails repeatedly
- Outbound `tenant_access_token` requests fail
- Every HTTP call to `open.feishu.cn` returns `426 Upgrade Required` from the proxy

## Environment

- QwenPaw 2.1.0 (installed package), Python 3.11
- Containerized Linux deployment
- `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` (and lowercase variants) injected into the process environment
- `NO_PROXY` does not contain `feishu.cn`

## Symptoms

`app.err.log` fills with:

```
urllib3.exceptions.MaxRetryError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='open.feishu.cn', port=443):
Max retries exceeded with url: /callback/ws/endpoint
(Caused by ProxyError('Unable to connect to proxy', OSError('Tunnel connection failed: 426 Upgrade Required')))

requests.exceptions.ProxyError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='open.feishu.cn', port=443): ...
```

Counters over roughly one day: `ProxyError` 14,570 / `426 Upgrade Required` 14,561 / `feishu WebSocket thread failed` 3,647.

The process itself looks healthy (`/api/version` returns 200), so the failure is silent from a monitoring standpoint.

## Root cause

`lark_oapi` uses `requests` internally, and `requests` honours `HTTP(S)_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY` from the environment. Two calls are affected:

1. `POST https://open.feishu.cn/callback/ws/endpoint` — WS endpoint negotiation
2. `POST https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal`

Note that `lark_oapi`'s WebSocket transport already passes `proxy=None` when building the connection (`_ws_connect_kwargs()`), so the WS socket itself bypasses the proxy — but the HTTP calls that precede it do not.

QwenPaw's own client is also proxy-aware by default, in `app/channels/feishu/channel.py`:

```python
self._http_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
    timeout=30.0,
)                                   # trust_env defaults to True

self._client = (
    lark.Client.builder()
    .app_id(self.app_id)
    .app_secret(self.app_secret)
    .domain(sdk_domain)
    ...
    .build()
)
```

## Suggested fixes

1. Build the Feishu-bound httpx client with `trust_env=False` (or explicit `proxies=None`):
   ```python
   self._http_client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0, trust_env=False)
   ```
2. For the `lark_oapi` client, propagate a proxy/`NO_PROXY` setting if the SDK supports it; otherwise document that `NO_PROXY` must include `.feishu.cn`.
3. Document required `NO_PROXY` entries (`feishu.cn`, `.feishu.cn`, `larksuite.com`) for containerized deployments behind a proxy.
4. Optionally add a config switch such as `channels.feishu.bypass_env_proxy` (default `true`), so a misconfigured platform proxy does not silently kill the channel.

## Workaround

Adding `.feishu.cn` to `NO_PROXY` in the process environment fixes both the WS connection and outbound messages (verified by exporting `no_proxy` / `NO_PROXY` in the supervisor command that launches the app).

## Additional suggestion

A startup health check that probes `open.feishu.cn` and logs a clear, actionable error would make this much easier to diagnose — currently the channel simply stays silent while the error log fills up.

issues.title: [Bug]: Allow configurable console basename for reverse-proxy subpath deployments

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## Description

The Web Console hardcodes its router basename to `/console`, which means it cannot be served under an arbitrary subpath (e.g., `/qwenpaw/`) behind a reverse proxy. This blocks a common self-hosted deployment pattern: multiplexing multiple services on a single domain, where each service lives under its own path prefix.

The only way to serve the console under a custom subpath today is to patch `CONSOLE_BASENAME` in the source and rebuild the frontend, which forks the user from upstream releases.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install QwenPaw and start it: `qwenpaw app`
2. Put a reverse proxy (Caddy, Nginx, Traefik) in front of it
3. Configure the proxy to serve QwenPaw under `/qwenpaw/` instead of `/` or `/console/`
4. Navigate to `https://your-host/qwenpaw/`

## Actual Behavior

The SPA loads but renders blank. Browser console shows:

```
Failed to load module script: Expected a JavaScript-or-Wasm module script but the server
responded with a MIME type of "text/html".
```

The root cause is in `console/src/utils/navigationMode.ts`:

```typescript
const CONSOLE_BASENAME = "/console";

export function getRouterBasename(pathname: string): string | undefined {
    return /^\/console(?:\/|$)/.test(pathname) ? CONSOLE_BASENAME : undefined;
}
```

When the browser URL is `/qwenpaw/`, the regex doesn't match, `getRouterBasename()` returns `undefined`, and React Router boots without a basename. It then tries to match `/qwenpaw/` as a route, fails, and renders nothing.

## Expected Behavior

The router basename should be configurable at build time, so users can deploy the console under any subpath without patching the source. For example:

```bash
VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME=/qwenpaw npm run build
```

And the resulting bundle should detect that `/qwenpaw` is the basename, route all SPA navigation relative to it, and emit asset URLs prefixed with `/qwenpaw/assets/`.

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** QwenPaw, version 2.2.1
- **Install method:** uv / pip / Docker
- **Deployment:** Reverse proxy (Caddy) in front of `qwenpaw app`
- **OS:** macOS 15 (also affects Linux/Docker deployments)

## Proposed Fix

Make `CONSOLE_BASENAME` read from an environment variable at build time, with `/console` as the fallback for backward compatibility:

```typescript
const CONSOLE_BASENAME =
    import.meta.env.VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME || "/console";

export function getRouterBasename(pathname: string): string | undefined {
    const escaped = CONSOLE_BASENAME.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
    return new RegExp(`^${escaped}(?:/|$)`).test(pathname)
        ? CONSOLE_BASENAME
        : undefined;
}
```

This preserves the current default (`/console`) so existing deployments are unaffected. Users who need a custom subpath set `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME` before running `npm run build`.

## Additional Context

- This is a common pattern for self-hosted apps. Grafana (`root_url`), Jellyfin (base URL), and Vaultwarden (`DOMAIN`) all support configurable subpaths.
- The related issue #2171 already notes that the console build can be polluted by generic shell variables like `BASE_URL`. Namespacing the new variable with `VITE_` avoids that class of bug.
- Discussion thread with full reverse-proxy setup details: [link to your article or a gist]

## Activity

- [x] I searched for existing issues and didn't find a duplicate
- [x] I'm willing to submit a PR if the maintainers agree on the approach

issues.title: [Bug][Telegram] Channel ignores reply_to_message — quoted context never reaches the agent (other channels implement this)
issues.body:
## Summary

When a user replies to a message (quote) in Telegram, the Bot API delivers
the quoted message in `update.message.reply_to_message`. The Telegram
channel adapter never reads this field, so the agent receives only the
user's new text — the quoted context is silently dropped.

## Current behavior

- `app/channels/telegram/channel.py`, `_build_content_parts_from_message()`
  extracts text/caption, entities, photo and media — but never touches
  `message.reply_to_message`.
- `reply_to_message` has **zero mentions** in the entire codebase
  (verified via code search).
- User-side effect: replying "what about this?" with a quote gives the
  agent no idea what "this" refers to.

## Expected behavior

Consistency with other channel adapters that already implement
quoted-message context:

- **Feishu**: `parent_id` → `_process_quoted_message()`
  (`app/channels/feishu/channel.py`)
- **DingTalk**: `isReplyMsg`/`repliedMsg` → `_process_quoted_message()`
  (`app/channels/dingtalk/handler.py`)
- **WeChat**: `ref_msg` → `_process_quoted_ref_msg()`
- **OneBot v11**: quoted segments → `_with_quoted_context()`

All of them prepend the quoted content with a `[Quoted message]` label —
an established house pattern that the Telegram channel does not follow.

## Suggested fix

In `_build_content_parts_from_message()`: if `message.reply_to_message`
is present, prepend a `TextContent` part following the same pattern:

​```
[Quoted message]
<author>: <text, truncated to ~500 chars>
​```

Optionally skip when the reply targets the bot's own last message, to
avoid re-injecting long assistant outputs.

## Environment

- QwenPaw 2.2.2 (verified in installed package)
- Also absent in current `main` (verified via GitHub code search)

## Related

- #5110 — Console-side "quote to follow-up" feature; same underlying need
  (quoted context injection), different surface. If a shared
  `quoted_context` message field lands there, the Telegram adapter could
  feed it the same way.

issues.title: [Bug]: v2.2.2 conversation switching does a full message re-render behind a blocking ready-gate — tens of seconds UI freeze with rich content (tables/code blocks); 2.2.1 unaffected
issues.body:
## Update (2026-10-19): root cause corrected after deeper investigation

Two separate issues were conflated in the original report:

1. **The long freeze (deterministic, product bug)** — NOT caused by large stream event counts or data size. Measured case: 110 messages / 1.87MB / 364 table rows / 33 code blocks. Timeline: backend session reads <1s, agent rebuild ~2s, the remaining ~40s is frontend rendering. Root cause in 2.2.2:
   - `ChatSessionActivation.setSessionMessages(..., {activate:true})` replaces the whole message array on every switch → full remount of all messages
   - messages are rendered via react-markdown with no virtualization/memo
   - new `ChatSessionTransition` hides content behind `visibility:hidden` + loading until `sdkSessionAdapter` marks the session ready → the full render time is presented as a blank freeze
   2.2.1 has none of these three components, and reuses the existing message list instead of remounting — the same conversation switches instantly.

2. **The SIGBUS crash (environment, not product bug)** — the backend was running from `AppTranslocation/...` (Gatekeeper temporary copy) all day; that directory was reclaimed by macOS. All processes mapping `libpython3.11.dylib` from that path died simultaneously (4 processes, same second, same dylib, two offsets). Reinstalled from /Applications with no Translocation: no crash, zero AppTranslocation warnings. The "spawned children" were 3 workers of an independent Python process (PID 15414), not spawned by the Tauri shell; Tauri's `events.rs` only records backend exit and does not auto-restart.

Suggested fix for issue 1: keep the previous message list visible while the next session renders (or render progressively), and add a ready-gate timeout (e.g. 3-5s) so a slow render never becomes an indefinite blank screen.

---

## QwenPaw Version

- **v2.2.2** (Desktop, macOS arm64) — affected
- **v2.2.1** — same workload, NOT affected (verified side-by-side on 2026-10-17)

## Description

Switching to a conversation whose agent has just finished (or is still producing) a **very large stream output** causes an extremely long load, and on v2.2.2 it can escalate into a full backend crash leaving the desktop window frozen (no response until app restart).

Quantitative context from my logs: the affected conversation regularly finishes turns with `console stream done: event_count=` between **11,000 and 45,000** events (normal conversations are tens to hundreds). The session JSON itself is small (~64KB–1.8MB) — the heavy part is replaying tens of thousands of streamed events on first switch.

**Related PR(s):** #7956 (conversation-switch refactor merged into 2.2.2), related issue #8274 (same switch-reload path, milder symptom: lost pending input)

**Security considerations:** none (no auth/config exposure involved)

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2 (crash reproduced 3/3); 2.2.1 (same load, healthy)
- **OS:** macOS 15.x arm64 (Mac mini, 16GB), OS build 25E253
- **Install method:** Desktop app (DMG)
- **Python version:** bundled runtime (3.11)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Let an agent run a conversation that produces a very large stream output (event_count in the tens of thousands).
2. While that turn has just finished (or while still streaming), switch away to another conversation in the Console, then switch back / to another large-output conversation.
3. On v2.2.2: the UI freezes for a very long time; in the worst case the whole backend dies and the desktop window stays frozen until app restart.
4. On v2.2.1 with the same conversation and the same switching pattern: load completes, backend logs stay continuous (no multi-second gaps), no crash.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual (v2.2.2):**
  - Switching right after a large stream (`console stream done`, event_count=11132 at 21:32:45) → desktop main process spawns a new `qwenpaw` child process ~1s later → the child **instantly SIGBUSes**; this reproduced **3/3 times with the identical crash address**:
    - `EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGBUS / KERN_MEMORY_ERROR)` at `libpython3.11.dylib + 0x89B18C` (`_sock_call_ex`) for the spawned children
    - The long-lived backend process (12.5h uptime) died in the same second at `libpython3.11.dylib + 0x8C5CD0` (`_PyZlib_Malloc`, i.e. while decompressing the session data stream)
    - 4 processes died within the same second (3 spawned children + the backend); backend log stops mid-initialization (`Governance started` / `scroll: wiring components`)
  - Even without the crash, first switch into a 10k–45k-event conversation takes an extremely long time (tens of seconds of UI freeze with no progress feedback)
- **Expected:**
  - Switching into a conversation with a large stream history should load progressively (chunked replay, loading indicator), stay responsive, and never take down the backend
  - If the reload path fails, the desktop should detect the dead backend and recover (like #7128 already does for Windows WebView2) instead of leaving a frozen window

## Additional evidence

- v2.2.1 same-day control: 8 turns with event_count between 4,957 and 35,294, switching between them repeatedly — backend log timestamps remain continuous every second, zero crashes, no long freezes.
- 4 macOS `.ips` crash reports captured (same second, same exception type, two distinct offsets inside `libpython3.11.dylib` as above). Happy to share sanitized copies if useful.
- Environment note: my setup includes a custom local reverse proxy and three small plugins (context folding / style guard / request guard), but all of them operate at the Python-object/HTTP layer; the crash is at the mmap page level (two abstractions below), and v2.2.1 with the identical environment handles the same load fine — so I believe the environment factors are not the cause. **[Corrected 2026-10-19: the environment WAS the cause of the SIGBUS crash — see Update above; it was AppTranslocation, not the plugins/proxy.]**

*Disclosure: this issue was drafted with AI assistance based on my locally captured logs and crash reports; I have reviewed the content and the data above comes from my own machine.*

issues.title: [Design] Media in chat history: 48 MB request bodies, permanently wedged sessions, and the cost they carry
issues.body:
# [Design] Media in chat history: request-body limits, permanent session wedges, and the cost they imply

## What happened

A WeChat session became unusable with:

```
openai.APIStatusError: Failed to buffer the request body: length limit exceeded
runtime: unhandled error session=wechat:o9cq80yMaOuq…
```

The error dump was **48.9 MB**. The session JSON was **48.7 MB** and held **43 media blocks**, replayed in full on every turn.

Provenance of those 43 blocks (decoded bytes):

| producing tool | blocks | MB |
|---|---|---|
| `view_image` | 24 | 17.39 |
| `send_file_to_user` | 14 | 11.50 |
| `desktop_screenshot` | 5 | 6.51 |
| **total** | **43** | **35.40** |

Three distinct failure modes, often conflated:

1. **Request rejected** — the payload exceeds an undocumented endpoint limit, so the turn dies with a generic "internal error".
2. **Session permanently wedged** — the offending blocks are *stored in history* and replayed, so every later turn fails the same way. The only cure today is editing the session file offline.
3. **Cost has two bills.** The same media is re-uploaded on every turn. The provider does cache the message prefix (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash bills a cached token at roughly 10% of the input price), so repeated image *tokens* are cheap — but the **upload is never cached**: every turn still carries the full body and still has to fit the endpoint's body limit. Token cost and byte cost are separate bills.

## Why the existing guards do not catch this

- `CappingFormatterMixin` caps **each block** at `MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` (2 MB) and substitutes a text placeholder — it applies to images, audio and video (`providers/capping_formatter.py:53,85,107`). All 43 blocks were **below 2 MB**, so nothing was capped. There is no *aggregate* budget.
- Context compaction (`scroll`) triggers on **tokens**, not bytes: `trigger = cfg.trigger_ratio * agent.model.context_size` (`agents/context/scroll/manager.py:535`). A 2 MB screenshot is cheap in tokens and expensive in bytes, so the compaction log shows `outcome=at_or_below_trigger` while the request body is already 48 MB.
- `_FORMATTER_SEEN_MEDIA_KEYS` dedupes identical sources **within one request** only (`agents/model_factory.py:137`), not across turns.
- Provider prompt caching saves tokens, not upload volume: the body must still be sent.

## How media gets into the request at all

`send_file_to_user` does not send anything itself — it returns a `DataBlock(file://…)` plus "File sent successfully." (`agents/tools/send_file.py:88`). The channel delivers that block when it renders the tool result (`app/channels/renderer.py` → `FileContent/ImageContent` → channel `_send_media_file`). The **same block** is also stored in `agent.state.context` and, on every later request, promoted into an `image_url` part (`_promote_tool_result_videos`, `promote_tool_result_images` at `model_factory.py:2459,2467`).

So delivery and model input share one representation, even though they are different concerns.

## Questions for maintainers

1. **Should a delivered file be model input at all?** A `send_file_to_user` result only needs to tell the model "sent X, here is the path". We would like a way to mark tool-result media as delivery-only so the formatter replaces it with text while the channel still sends the file. Is a flag on the block (or a tool-level declaration) the preferred shape, or should the tool return a text-only summary and push the file out of band?
2. **Can images reuse the existing 2 MB placeholder path?** Lowering `MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` would work mechanically, but it would blind genuine vision tasks (screenshot analysis) and makes cache prefixes jitter around the threshold. Would a *source-aware* policy (delivery vs. inspection) be acceptable?
3. **What is the right request-size contract?** Is there a documented/derivable `max_request_bytes` per provider we can budget against, or should the harness keep a conservative default and treat "length limit exceeded"/413 as a recoverable signal?
4. **Cache interaction.** Eliding media changes the wire prefix at that
position, so the suffix after it is re-billed for that one turn. Eliding
as late as possible (only media from *previous* turns) keeps that suffix
small; trimming deeper history ("keep the last N turns") moves the
invalidation further back and costs more. Which trade-off do you prefer:
keep the bytes (full upload each turn, prefix cache intact) or elide near
the tail (small per-turn suffix re-bill, bytes gone)?

## Proposed shape (for discussion, not implemented here)

- **P0 — delivery/context separation.** Tool-result media from delivery tools becomes a text reference in the request; channel delivery is untouched.
- **P1 — media by reference.** Context stores `{path, sha256, media_type, dims, bytes}`; bytes are inlined only for an explicit `view_image`/`view_video` and only for that request.
- **P2 — byte budget + recovery.** Before sending, budget the inline-media bytes; if over, elide oldest media deterministically; on `length limit exceeded`/413, retry once with media stripped and persist the degradation so the wedge does not repeat.

## Impact

Without at least P2, any chat that accumulates screenshots eventually wedges permanently and silently, and the operator has to repair the session file by hand. With P0 only, roughly a third of the payload in our sample disappears — the majority (`view_image`, `desktop_screenshot`) remains.

Happy to send a PR for whichever slice maintainers consider appropriate; the smallest one that fully prevents the wedge is P2 (with P0 as a cheap complement).

## Refinement: media is turn-scoped, not history-scoped

A further observation makes the budget-only approach look unnecessarily weak:
once the model has looked at an image (`view_image`) and written its
understanding into the following assistant text, re-uploading the pixels on
every later turn buys nothing.

- The information the model still needs is the *conclusion* plus a way to look
  again — not the bytes.
- Prompt caching lowers the *price* of replaying the prefix; it never
  removes the upload. On a 1M-token input window the binding constraint is
  the request body, not the context window, so a later turn still pays full
  bytes for content the model has already processed.
- The existing "inline everything in history" behaviour is a storage choice,
  not a requirement of the API.

Concrete rule we would propose: a media block stays inlined only for the
**current turn** — i.e. until a final assistant message (text, no tool calls)
has been produced after it. After that it becomes a reference:

```
[image viewed: C:\...\slide_v_zh_00002_.png (PNG, 1280x800, 0.74 MB)
 — re-open with view_image if it needs another look]
```

The reference keeps the path, so the model can re-inspect on demand at the cost
of one tool call instead of megabytes on every turn. This is also
cache-friendly: the elision point is deterministic and only moves when new
content arrives.

For the session in this report that alone would take the request from 48.9 MB
to roughly the size of the current turn's media (a few MB), instead of the
34.6 MB of history above.

Two residual concerns, both covered by the byte budget rather than by this
rule: a single turn may still view many large images at once, and a
delivery-generated file should never be inlined at all (P0).

## Model capability note

The endpoint used here is `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash): natively
multimodal with **Text + Image** input, a 1M-token context, and prefix caching
(cached tokens billed at roughly 10% of the input price). Two consequences:

- The earlier "text-only endpoint" framing is wrong for images: images are a
  supported input and the request schema accepts `image_url`. The failure in
  this report is **size**, not capability.
- Video is still not an input modality (`Text, Image`); the endpoint rejects the
  `video_url` part outright (`422 unknown variant video_url`), so QwenPaw's
  video handling (substitute unless `supports_video` is explicitly true) stays
  correct.

issues.title: Bug: source-group headers overlap their first sidebar conversation
issues.body:
## Description

In the sidebar's source/group mode, moving a normal conversation to **Scheduled
task conversations** or **Conversations with subagents**, expanding the group,
then hovering/selecting its first conversation makes the conversation background
overlap the bottom of the group header.

Reproduced on official main `7cb6234f25798ee8fe1554206942ad87b65fe73d`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Switch the sidebar to source/group mode.
2. Long-press and drag a conversation from an ordinary group to either fixed
   scheduled-task or subagent group.
3. Expand the destination group and hover its first conversation.

Expected: the source header and conversation have separate backgrounds.
Actual: the conversation background starts 4px before the header ends.

## Cause and proposed fix

The virtual list allocates 36px to every group header. An ordinary header uses
32px height + 2px top and bottom margins = 36px. The fixed source headers instead
use an 8px top margin, so need 42px. Reserving 42px only for `cron`/`subagents`
headers restores the intended 2px gap without changing the theme or drag logic.

I have reproduced this with real pointer dragging against fixture HTTP responses
and prepared a small fix with regression tests.

issues.title: [Bug]: `reload_agent()` does not fire `workspace_created` hooks, so runtime hooks registered via `register_runtime_hook()` are silently dropped

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
# Title

`reload_agent()` does not fire `workspace_created` hooks, so runtime hooks registered via `register_runtime_hook()` are silently dropped

# Body

**Version:** QwenPaw 2.0.1

## Summary

`MultiAgentManager.reload_agent()` builds a brand-new `Workspace` and atomically swaps it in, but never calls `_fire_workspace_created_hooks()`. Since `register_runtime_hook()` relies on the `workspace_created` hook to actually attach a runtime hook to a workspace, every runtime hook registered by a plugin is silently lost on the first reload after the plugin is installed.

The failure is silent: installation logs look completely normal, and a plugin that inspects `workspace.plugins.hook_registry` right after load will correctly report its hooks as attached — because at that moment they are. The reload happens a second later and replaces the objects that were inspected.

## Details

`register_runtime_hook()` (`plugins/api.py`) does not attach anything directly. It registers:

- a startup hook `rt_hook_<plugin>_<name>` (priority 65), which attaches the runtime hook to workspaces that exist at plugin-load time, and
- a `workspace_created` hook `rt_hook_ws_<plugin>_<name>` (priority 65), which is supposed to attach it to any workspace created later.

`_fire_workspace_created_hooks()` is called from exactly one place — the first-creation path in `MultiAgentManager.get_agent()`:

```
src/qwenpaw/app/multi_agent_manager.py:160
```

`reload_agent()` (`multi_agent_manager.py:352`) starts a new instance, swaps it into `self.agents` under the lock, and gracefully stops the old one. There is no `_fire_workspace_created_hooks()` call anywhere on that path:

```
$ grep -n "_fire_workspace_created_hooks" src/qwenpaw/app/multi_agent_manager.py
160:            await self._fire_workspace_created_hooks(
189:    async def _fire_workspace_created_hooks(workspace_info: dict) -> None:
```

The replacement `Workspace` therefore carries a fresh `HookRegistry` holding only the built-in hooks from `bootstrap_plugins` (`hooks=6` in our logs), and the plugin's runtime hooks are gone with the old object.

## Reproduction

1. Write a plugin that calls `register_runtime_hook()` for, say, `Phase.POST_RESPONSE`, with a callback that logs unconditionally.
2. Install it via the plugin UI on a running instance (hot install).
3. Observe the install succeed and the hook register.
4. Observe the automatic zero-downtime reload in the log:
   ```
   New workspace instance started
   Workspace instance replaced
   Old workspace instance stopped ... Zero-downtime reload complete
   ```
5. Send a chat turn. The hook never runs.

## Workaround

Both of these go through `get_agent()`'s first-creation path and do re-attach the hooks:

- restart the process, or
- disable then re-enable the agent — `PUT /api/agents/{agentId}/enabled` with `{"enabled": false}` then `{"enabled": true}` (`toggle_agent_enabled` calls `stop_agent()` + `schedule_agent_startup()`).

Note that `/restart` and `/daemon restart` do **not** work: `run_daemon_restart` (`runtime/commands/daemon.py:143`) calls `manager.reload_agent()`, i.e. the very path that drops the hooks.

## Suggested fix

Call `_fire_workspace_created_hooks()` on the reload path too, after the new instance is swapped in. The hooks are written to be idempotent per-workspace (they attach to the workspace passed in `workspace_info`), so firing them for a replacement workspace should be safe.

A secondary issue worth considering: `bootstrap_plugins` re-runs for the new workspace but the plugin-provided runtime hooks do not, which makes the two categories behave differently across a reload. Unifying them would avoid this class of bug entirely.

issues.title: [Bug]: Thinking strength slider has misleading fill and flickers on save
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

Reproduced in v2.2.2 and in the official main branch at `697aeb669f42f223d060772eb7a313eec78ebd20`.

## Description

The thinking/reasoning strength slider colors its entire rail even when a lower
strength is selected. The label and thumb change correctly, but the colored bar
continues past the thumb to the maximum end. This makes selected and unselected
strengths harder to distinguish and can suggest maximum strength visually.

The cause is in `console/src/features/thinking/thinking.module.less`: the full
rail has the gradient background while the value-dependent track is transparent.
The budget-with-off override also colors the full rail.

**Security considerations:** Display only; no model requests, permissions, or credentials are involved.

**Related PR:** #8287

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- Install method: source
- Visual reproduction: Chrome 155, actual official ThinkingControl rendered with fixture values

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a model with declared reasoning effort levels or a thinking budget.
2. Open the thinking-strength control in the Console.
3. Select a lower strength/budget, then compare the filled bar with the thumb.
4. Repeat with the compact control in model settings.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** The entire rail remains colored, including the unselected portion to the right of the thumb.
- **Expected:** Color only the selected portion up to the thumb; keep the remaining rail neutral using the existing theme tokens. If the effective default has not been resolved, do not imply a selected amount.

## Logs / Screenshots

The following are isolated renders of the actual official component with fixture
values, not mock drawings. They contain no user or business data.

| Current behavior | Proposed improvement |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AGImentu/QwenPaw/b1ee2c08233b3dc233af62eafa990ec4b99f1012/before-light.png) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AGImentu/QwenPaw/b1ee2c08233b3dc233af62eafa990ec4b99f1012/after-light.png) |

[Dark theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AGImentu/QwenPaw/b1ee2c08233b3dc233af62eafa990ec4b99f1012/after-dark.png) and
[browser assertion report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AGImentu/QwenPaw/b1ee2c08233b3dc233af62eafa990ec4b99f1012/result.json).

## Additional Notes

I have prepared a small fix that reuses the existing slider track width and the
existing `--app-accent` / `--app-fill-strong` tokens, with no new dependencies or
changes to model execution. The official-base frontend suite and build were run;
full details will be included in the linked PR.

## Related save-feedback behavior

The same control also flickers during preference writes: the entire panel is
marked busy/disabled, while the panel still receives the old confirmed strength
instead of the preview. With a slow request, clicking High can briefly show Low
again and the rail/title dim until the response arrives.

The complete fix is in the existing PR #8287: neutral unselected fill plus stable
immediate preview, ordered writes, failure rollback, and chat-scoped pending work.
It also preserves the official advanced decision-setting control for existing
and new chats.

Complete local verification: 491 frontend files / 5,145 tests passed with coverage;
format/check, production build and `pre-commit run --all-files` all passed.
An actual official SessionThinking browser fixture with 650 ms simulated saves
passed 322 renderer-state samples, real mouse clicks/dragging and the advanced
switch check. No real backend or business data was used.

[Slow-save proof report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AGImentu/QwenPaw/8affc7d0a4601f5c9a9a1f5cf590d965d81b656b/saving/result.json)

issues.title: [Bug]: Injected context blocks (system-info / system-notification) are delivered to channel users as reply text
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2 (pip install; `qwenpaw-2.2.2.dist-info`)

## Description

Framework-generated markers are stored inside **ordinary assistant text** and then forwarded to channel users as if the assistant had written them:

- `<system-notification>` … `</system-notification>` — the background tool-call hint built by `make_offload_hint_msg()`.
- `<system-info>` … `</system-info>` — compressed-context / continuation notes.

`MessageRenderer.message_to_parts()` forwards every `ContentType.TEXT` block unchanged. The display flags cannot prevent this: `show_thinking`, `show_tool_calls` and `show_tool_results` only gate structured block types (`THINKING`, `*_TOOL_CALL`, `*_TOOL_CALL_OUTPUT`). A synthetic hint is a plain `TextBlock`, so no flag applies to it.

Two independent paths produce such text:

1. `src/qwenpaw/tool_calls/_hint.py::make_offload_hint_msg()` builds

   ```python
   notification = TextBlock(type="text", text=("<system-notification>\n" ...))
   ...
   return Msg(name="system", role="assistant", content=[notification] + result_blocks)
   ```

   The docstring states the blocks are flattened on purpose, "so that provider formatters treat it as an ordinary assistant message". No metadata marker is attached, so a renderer cannot distinguish the hint from real reply text.

2. Scroll context compression / continuation notes carry `<system-info>` blocks; those bytes can also lead a user-role or assistant text block.

**Related PR(s):** #7835 (same class of problem, different source: auto-memory recall payload; that PR adds a message-level metadata guard). This report needs a text-level guard because the two sources above carry no marker.

**Security considerations:** no credential exposure. It is a leak of framework internals to end users, and it can make a bot appear to emit control-looking markup.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2
- **OS:** Windows Server 2022
- **Install method:** pip
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

Deterministic, no channel required:

```python
from qwenpaw.app.channels.renderer import MessageRenderer
from qwenpaw.schemas import Message, MessageType, RunStatus, TextContent

msg = Message(
    type=MessageType.MESSAGE,
    role="assistant",
    content=[TextContent(text=(
        "<system-notification>\nBackground tool call `x` completed.\n"
        "</system-notification>\nDone."
    ))],
    status=RunStatus.Completed,
)
msg.object = "message"
print([p.text for p in MessageRenderer().message_to_parts(msg)])
```

Real-world path: let the agent start a background tool call. `_hint.py` appends the hint message to the agent context, and the next rendering of that message reaches the channel.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** the channel bubble contains the raw `<system-notification>` / `<system-info>` block, including the tool-call id and completion state.
- **Expected:** the marker stays internal. Either it is not persisted as renderable assistant text, or the display layer drops it while the live context keeps it — the same contract `strip_headline()` already uses for `⟦ … ⟧` headlines.

## Logs / Screenshots

Measured on this installation (`conversation_history`, 1,809 rows): **58 assistant rows begin with `<system-notification>`**. Example row (seq 1883):

```
<system-notification>
Background tool call `execute_shell_command` (id=call_00_...) completed with state=success. Result below.
</system-notification>
```

Renderer (upstream `main`, `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/renderer.py`, line 399):

```python
if ctype == ContentType.TEXT and getattr(c, "text", None):
    text = strip_headline(c.text)
    if text:
        result.append(TextContent(text=text))
```

## Additional Notes

I have a small display-layer fix ready that follows the existing `strip_headline()` contract: `strip_injected_context()` removes only **balanced blocks at the start of a text block**, leaves the stored text untouched, and is a no-op for prose that mentions a tag (for example inside backticks). 6 unit tests plus 1 renderer test, all lint gates green. Happy to open a PR if this direction is acceptable — or, if you prefer to fix it at the source (tag offload hints with metadata and skip them in renderers, as #7835 does), I can follow that instead.

A separate symptom we also see is fragments of reasoning text inside the reply; that looks like a different problem and is not covered by this report.

issues.body:
# [Plugins/HarmonyOS] 移动端本地插件宿主：请求标准化 `window.QwenPaw` 契约 + 数据面桥 + 分发验签 + PawApp 门控统一


## 背景 Background
我们维护两样东西：

1. **QwenPaw 鸿蒙原生 App**（bundle `io.agentscope.qwenpaw.mobile`，对齐上游 PR #7378 的 `app.json`；ArkTS/ArkUI，147 文件 / 约 45k 行），其中已建成**端侧本地插件宿主**：`pluginhost/` shell（`index.html` + `host.js` + vendor UMD，`HOST_SHELL_VERSION=8`）+ ArkWeb 装载页 + 设备 ZIP 安装器（沙箱 `plugins/<id>/`）+ `qpwFile` 文件桥 + NotificationKit 系统通知。
2. **AgentTeams 工作台插件**（`agentteams-qwenpaw-workbench`，全栈插件）：Python 后端 **54 个端点**（聚合/转发 AgentTeams Controller、Matrix、Higress Console、SGLang）+ 前端约 1.9MB 单文件 bundle。它目前跑在 QwenPaw 服务端宿主里（web console）。

**我们想做的事**：让全栈插件**不依赖 QwenPaw 服务端**、直接装进移动 App 本地宿主运行（"端侧独立宿主"）。为此我们做了真机级 PoC，结论：

- ✅ **前端半边零改动可用**：把真插件装进端侧 shell，`window.QwenPaw` 注入、`registerRoutes → 1 route`、完整工作台渲染成功（单请求加载 1.85MB bundle，无附加资源）。
- ✅ **应用内通知已通**：插件 `new Notification(...)` → shell 桩 → `window.prompt('qwpaw.notify|{t,b}')` → ArkWeb `onPrompt` → NotificationKit 系统通知中心，端到端实测成立。
- ❌ **数据面被端侧 shell 受控 503**（`host.js` 把一切 http(s)/根相对请求拦成 offline 响应）→ 插件进入"Controller not connected"空态。**独立宿主的插件如何访问"用户授权的服务端"，目前上游没有定义。**
- ❌ **契约无权威源**：实测上游 web console 2.2.2 的 host 面与其自家 `docs/plugins.zh.md` 不一致（文档列出的 `useTheme/useLocale/useSelectedAgent/useCurrentSession/host.fetch` 在 bundle 里均不存在）、无任何宿主形态/环境声明槽位、无 `chat` 命名空间。

**术语澄清（重要）**：我们主张把两个概念分开——**宿主形态**（server / local / desktop，架构属性，声明式）与**连通性**（数据面可达与否，会随时变，探测式）。上游若提供 boolean `isOffline` 来表达宿主形态，会把两者混为一谈，必然误判（独立宿主但数据面可达 ≠ 离线；服务端宿主但后端挂了 ≠ 在线）。建议契约直接使用两轴结构（见议题 1）。

---

## Background 
We maintain two things:

1. **A native HarmonyOS QwenPaw app** (bundle `io.agentscope.qwenpaw.mobile`, aligned with upstream PR #7378's `app.json`; ArkTS/ArkUI, 147 files / ~45k LOC). It already ships a **device-local plugin host**: a `pluginhost/` shell (`index.html` + `host.js` + vendor UMDs, `HOST_SHELL_VERSION=8`), an ArkWeb page, a device-ZIP installer (sandbox `plugins/<id>/`), a `qpwFile` file bridge, and NotificationKit system notifications.
2. **The AgentTeams Workbench plugin** (`agentteams-qwenpaw-workbench`, a full-stack plugin): a Python backend with **54 endpoints** (aggregating/proxying AgentTeams Controller, Matrix, Higress Console, SGLang) plus a ~1.9MB single-file frontend bundle. Today it runs inside the QwenPaw **server** host (web console).

**Goal**: run the full-stack plugin **without any QwenPaw server**, installed in the mobile app's local host ("device-standalone host"). Our device-level PoC results:

- ✅ **Frontend half works with zero changes**: the real plugin loads in the device shell — `window.QwenPaw` injected, `registerRoutes → 1 route`, full workbench renders (single request for the 1.85MB bundle, no extra assets).
- ✅ **In-app notifications work end-to-end**: plugin `new Notification(...)` → shell stub → `window.prompt('qwpaw.notify|{t,b}')` → ArkWeb `onPrompt` → NotificationKit system notification center (verified on device).
- ❌ **The data plane is deliberately 503'd** by the device shell (`host.js` turns every http(s)/root-relative request into an offline response) → the plugin shows a "Controller not connected" empty state. **How a plugin in a standalone host may reach "user-authorized backends" is currently undefined upstream.**
- ❌ **No authoritative contract**: upstream web console 2.2.2's host surface does not match its own `docs/plugins.zh.md` (documented `useTheme/useLocale/useSelectedAgent/useCurrentSession/host.fetch` are absent from the bundle), there is no host-form/env declaration slot, and no `chat` namespace.

**Terminology (important)**: we propose to separate **host form** (server / local / desktop — an architectural property, declared) from **connectivity** (data-plane reachability — dynamic, probed). A boolean `isOffline` used to express host form conflates the two and will misclassify (standalone host with a reachable data plane ≠ offline; server host with a dead backend ≠ online). The contract should use the two-axis shape in Topic 1.

---

## 议题 1 · 官方「端侧独立宿主」契约（含环境两轴）
### Topic 1 · An official "device-standalone host" contract (with the two-axis env)

**现状 Current**：各壳各自实现 `window.QwenPaw.*`。我们实测对比：鸿蒙端侧 shell（v8，约 700 行 `host.js`）实现了 `{host, menu, route, slot, chat, audit, memoryBackends, registerRoutes, registerToolRender}`；web console 2.2.2 与文档互相矛盾且缺环境槽位。结果是插件写作者只能靠 feature-detect 猜测宿主能力，跨端移植无保障。

**Current**: each shell implements `window.QwenPaw.*` independently. Our measurement: the HarmonyOS device shell (v8, ~700-line `host.js`) implements `{host, menu, route, slot, chat, audit, memoryBackends, registerRoutes, registerToolRender}`; web console 2.2.2 contradicts its own docs and has no env slot. Plugin authors can only feature-detect and guess; cross-host portability is not guaranteed.

**诉求 Ask**：

1. 发布一份**端侧独立宿主契约规范**：哪些命名空间是必须的、语义、生命周期（装载/卸载/`dispose`）、错误上报约定。我们的 `host.js`（v8）可作为参考基线提交（同许可，可整体或按段引用）。
2. 契约必须包含**环境声明**（两轴），并明确**不推荐**用 boolean `isOffline` 表达宿主形态：

   ```ts
   window.QwenPaw.host.env = {
     kind: 'server' | 'local' | 'desktop',        // 轴 A：宿主形态（声明式，决定插件后端在不在）
     caps: { net: boolean, secureStore: boolean, notify: boolean }, // 轴 B：能力位
     apiVersion: '1.x',                            // 契约版本握手
   }
   ```

3. 命名纪律：`standalone/local` 描述宿主形态；`offline` 只描述连通性（如 `dataPlane: 'offline'`）。两者不得互相借用。

**Ask**:

1. Publish a **device-standalone host contract spec**: which namespaces are mandatory, their semantics, lifecycle (load/unload/`dispose`), error reporting. Our `host.js` (v8) is offered as a reference baseline (same license; adoptable wholesale or per-section).
2. The contract must include the **two-axis env declaration** above, and explicitly discourage a boolean `isOffline` as a host-form signal.
3. Naming discipline: `standalone/local` for host form; `offline` only for connectivity.

**不解决的后果 Consequence if not addressed**：每个壳各自实现、插件不可移植；"全栈插件"在移动端永远只能看空态（我们 PoC 的现状）。

---

## 议题 2 · 数据面桥的官方语义（让独立 ≠ 离线）
### Topic 2 · Official semantics for the data-plane bridge (standalone ≠ offline)

**现状 Current**：独立宿主下的插件需要访问**用户自己授权的服务端**（例如插件自己的后端、或用户配置的数据源）。当前鸿蒙端侧 shell 的选择是"一律 503"——把"独立"实现成了"离线"。

In a standalone host, plugins must reach **user-authorized backends** (e.g. the plugin's own backend, or user-configured data sources). The HarmonyOS shell's current choice is "503 everything" — it implements "standalone" as "offline".

**诉求 Ask**：上游定义端侧独立宿主下插件访问用户授权服务端的标准方式。我们的提议（两侧工作量均已按此估算）：

- 端侧原生网络桥，仿照既有 `qpwFile` 范式：

  ```js
  window.qpwNet.request(url, init)   // 端侧发请求，无 CORS；凭据由宿主安全存储注入，不进 WebView
  window.qpwNet.stream(url, init)    // SSE/流式（端侧长连）
  ```

- 或并入 `host.fetch`：**按连接态/白名单放行，而不是按宿主形态一刀切**；白名单 origin 由宿主声明并展示给用户。
- 凭据安全底线：令牌类凭据必须走端侧安全存储（鸿蒙 HUKS），**禁止落 localStorage**（WebView 内明文，任何脚本可读）。我们的插件持有 Matrix access_token + Controller token（含 Docker 代理，等效宿主机权限）+ Higress admin token——这类凭据进 localStorage 是移动端不可接受的安全边界问题。
- 明确"全栈插件"的端侧化边界：哪些能力宿主保证（网络/存储/通知），哪些插件自管。

**Ask**: define the standard way for a plugin in a standalone host to reach user-authorized backends. Our proposal (effort on both sides already estimated against this design):

- A device-native network bridge, following the existing `qpwFile` pattern:

  ```js
  window.qpwNet.request(url, init)   // device-side fetch, no CORS; credentials injected from host secure storage, never into the WebView
  window.qpwNet.stream(url, init)    // SSE/streaming (device-side long connection)
  ```

- Or fold it into `host.fetch`: **allow by connection state / whitelist, not by host form**; whitelisted origins declared by the host and visible to the user.
- Credential security floor: token-class credentials must live in device secure storage (HUKS on HarmonyOS); **localStorage is forbidden** (plaintext in the WebView, readable by any script). Our plugin carries a Matrix access_token + Controller token (with Docker proxy — effectively host-level) + Higress admin token; putting those in localStorage is an unacceptable mobile security boundary.
- Define the boundary for "full-stack plugins": which capabilities the host guarantees (net/storage/notify) and which the plugin manages itself.

**工作量参考 Effort reference**：端侧桥 3–6 人天（含白名单 UI + 流式）；插件适配层 2–4 人天。我们插件 54 端点中约 25–35 个为纯透传/聚合（可端侧化），其余为有状态/派生逻辑。

---

## 议题 3 · 通知载荷规范与点击定位（应用内）
### Topic 3 · Notification payload spec & tap routing (in-app)

**现状 Current**：应用内通知已可用——插件 `new Notification(t, {body})` → 宿主桩 → 系统通知，端到端实测通过。当前缺口是**载荷语义与点击行为未定义**：插件只能传 `{t,b}`，宿主无法区分审批/任务/告警，也无法把"点通知"路由回插件内对应页面。

**Current**: in-app notifications already work — plugin `new Notification(t, {body})` → host stub → system notification, verified end-to-end. What is missing is **payload semantics and tap behavior**: plugins can only pass `{t,b}`, so the host cannot distinguish approval/task/alert, nor route a notification tap back into the corresponding plugin page.

**诉求 Ask**：

1. 定义**通知载荷规范**（向后兼容扩展）：

   ```json
   { "t": "title", "b": "body", "kind": "approval|task|alert", "target": "worker:<name> | room:<id>" }
   ```

   `kind` 供宿主选择系统槽位/优先级；`target` 供宿主把通知点击透传给插件并定位到具体页面（宿主以 query/hash 形式带入 WebView）。
2. 通知去重/冷却建议（轮询型插件会重复产生同类事件）。

**Ask**:

1. Define the **notification payload spec** (backward-compatible extension):

   ```json
   { "t": "title", "b": "body", "kind": "approval|task|alert", "target": "worker:<name> | room:<id>" }
   ```

   `kind` lets the host pick the system slot/priority; `target` lets the host pass a notification tap through to the plugin and locate the specific page (delivered into the WebView as query/hash).
2. Guidance on dedup/cool-down (polling plugins emit repeated same-kind events).

---

## 议题 4 · 插件分发与验签
### Topic 4 · Plugin distribution & signature verification

**现状 Current**：移动端"设备 ZIP 安装"（把插件 ZIP 直接装进 App 沙箱）目前**无签名、无来源校验**——任何 ZIP 都能装。桌面/web 侧的 ZIP/URL 安装同样没有验签。这在移动端是安全边界问题（插件前端可执行任意 JS，宿主注入的是带凭据能力的 SDK）。

Mobile "device-ZIP install" (drop a plugin ZIP into the app sandbox) currently has **no signature and no source check** — any ZIP installs. Desktop/web ZIP/URL installs have no signature verification either. On mobile this is a security-boundary issue: plugin frontend can run arbitrary JS and is injected with a credential-bearing SDK.

**诉求 Ask**：

1. 定义插件**签名机制**（建议：manifest 内嵌签名 + 宿主侧公钥校验；签名主体 = 插件作者/官方）。
2. 定义**来源白名单**语义（官方分发渠道 vs 用户显式信任的本地 ZIP——后者需用户确认风险）。
3. 明确签名/验签失败时的 UX（安装拒绝文案、已有插件的更新验签）。

**Ask**:

1. Define a **plugin signature scheme** (suggest: signature embedded in the manifest, verified by the host against a public key; signatory = plugin author / official).
2. Define **source whitelist** semantics (official distribution vs user-explicitly-trusted local ZIP — the latter requires an explicit risk confirmation).
3. UX for signature/source failure (install rejection copy, signature check on plugin updates).

---

## 议题 5 · `plugin_type` / PawApp 门控与 `entry_page` 语义统一（"列得出、打不开"）
### Topic 5 · Unify `plugin_type` / PawApp gating and `entry_page` semantics ("listed but not openable")

**现状 Current**（实测上游 2.2.2）：

- web 端 `/apps/` 加载器要求 `plugin_type === "app"`，否则报 `PawApp frontend plugin not found`；
- 而 `GET /api/pawapps` 按 `meta.pawapp` 收录并返回 `entry_page`；
- 移动端（PR #7378 的 Expo 版）硬编码 `WebView ${baseUrl}/apps/{id}`，无视 `entry_page`。

结果：一个 PawApp 插件可能**列得出、打不开**（列表有、加载器拒）。

Measured on upstream 2.2.2:

- the web `/apps/` loader requires `plugin_type === "app"`, else `PawApp frontend plugin not found`;
- while `GET /api/pawapps` indexes by `meta.pawapp` and returns `entry_page`;
- mobile (the Expo app in PR #7378) hardcodes `WebView ${baseUrl}/apps/{id}`, ignoring `entry_page`.

Net effect: a PawApp plugin can be **listed but not openable** (shows in the list, rejected by the loader).

**诉求 Ask**：统一三处口径——收录条件（`meta.pawapp` vs `plugin_type`）、加载器门控、`entry_page` 的消费（各端加载器都应尊重 `entry_page`；缺省时才回退 `/apps/{id}`）。我们端侧已按 `entry_page` 适配（URL 参数 `qpw_pawapp_route`）。

**Ask**: align the three surfaces — inclusion condition (`meta.pawapp` vs `plugin_type`), loader gating, and `entry_page` consumption (every host loader should honor `entry_page`; fall back to `/apps/{id}` only when absent). Our device host already adapts via `entry_page` (URL param `qpw_pawapp_route`).

---

## 议题 6 · 契约版本握手
### Topic 6 · Contract version handshake

**现状 Current**：`packages/qwenpaw-api-contract` 已有基础，但插件 manifest 没有向宿主声明"我需要的宿主契约版本"，宿主也不做兼容检查——契约一旦演进，老插件/新宿主（或新插件/老宿主）的行为是未定义的。

`packages/qwenpaw-api-contract` exists, but the plugin manifest does not declare the host-contract version it needs, and hosts do no compatibility check — once the contract evolves, old-plugin/new-host (or new-plugin/old-host) behavior is undefined.

**诉求 Ask**：插件 manifest 增加 `host_api_version`（或复用 `qwenpaw_version`），宿主装载时做兼容检查，不兼容时给出**降级提示**（而不是静默失败或白屏）。配合议题 1 的 `env.apiVersion` 双向握手。

**Ask**: add `host_api_version` to the plugin manifest (or reuse `qwenpaw_version`); hosts check compatibility at load time and show a **graceful degradation message** on mismatch (not silent failure or a blank page). Pairs with `env.apiVersion` from Topic 1 for a two-way handshake.

---

## 议题 7 · 全栈插件（带独立后端）在移动宿主的官方定位
### Topic 7 · Official positioning of full-stack plugins (with their own backend) in mobile hosts

**现状 Current**：像我们这样的全栈插件（Python 后端 + 前端 bundle）装进移动宿主只有两个自然形态：**端侧化**（把后端逻辑用 TS/ArkTS 重实现）或**远端化**（后端留在某个服务端，移动端经网络访问）。目前没有官方推荐路线，也没有官方"移动端插件后端"承载方案。

A full-stack plugin like ours (Python backend + frontend bundle) has only two natural forms in a mobile host: **device-side re-implementation** (port backend logic to TS/ArkTS) or **remote** (backend stays on some server, mobile reaches it over the network). There is no officially recommended route and no official "mobile plugin backend" hosting option.

**诉求 Ask**：请上游明确：

1. 推荐路线（我们倾向"宿主提供数据面桥 + 凭据安全存储，后端留服务端或按插件粒度端侧化"的混合形态，见议题 2）；
2. 是否提供官方"插件后端承载"方案（如官方 sidecar/云函数模板）；
3. 全栈插件在应用商店审核语境下的合规口径（网络权限、自托管后端披露）。

**Ask**: please clarify:

1. The recommended route (we favor a hybrid: host provides the data-plane bridge + secure credential storage, backend stays server-side or is ported per-plugin — see Topic 2);
2. Whether an official "plugin backend hosting" option will exist (e.g. official sidecar / cloud-function template);
3. Compliance guidance for full-stack plugins under app-store review (network permissions, self-hosted backend disclosure).

---

## 我们的立场与可贡献资源 Our position & what we can contribute

- 我们**不是只有诉求**：鸿蒙端侧宿主 shell（`host.js` v8，两轴 `host.env`、`qpwFile` 桥、Notification 桩 + `kind/target` 载荷）是**可运行的参考实现**，愿意整体或按段贡献进上游（`packages/` 下建 `qwenpaw-device-host` 或等价物）。
- 我们已完成真机级 PoC 与逐条兼容矩阵（宿主提供 ↔ 插件需要，14 项对照），可作为契约规范的验收用例。
- 我们建议的讨论顺序：**议题 1（契约）+ 议题 2（数据面）是核心**，其余五条为配套；可一次 RFC 讨论收口。
- 若上游对方向无异议，我们可按议题 1 的 API 形状先行单侧落地（我们的 shell + 插件已按两轴契约 v1.0 落地），等上游规范后对齐。

We are **not just asking**: the HarmonyOS device host shell (`host.js` v8 — two-axis `host.env`, `qpwFile` bridge, Notification stub with `kind/target` payload) is a **working reference implementation**, and we are willing to contribute it upstream (e.g. as `packages/qwenpaw-device-host` or equivalent).
We have a device-level PoC plus a 14-item compatibility matrix (host provides ↔ plugin needs) that can serve as acceptance cases for the contract spec.
Suggested discussion order: **Topics 1 (contract) + 2 (data plane) are the core**; the other five are supporting and could be settled in one RFC.
If the direction is agreed, we will proceed unilaterally on our side with the Topic-1 API shape (our shell + plugin already run on the two-axis contract v1.0) and align once the upstream spec lands.

---

## 附录：证据索引 Evidence index（均可公开复现）

| # | 证据 | 位置 |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | 端侧宿主 shell（host.js v8 / 两轴 env / qpwFile 桥 / Notification 桩） | 鸿蒙 App `entry/src/main/resources/rawfile/pluginhost/`（可提 PR 贡献） |
| E2 | PoC：真插件零改动装载渲染（registerRoutes 1 route、85k 字符渲染、单请求 1.85MB） | 复现步骤见我们提交的 PoC 脚本（http 静态服务 + 等价 URL 参数） |
| E3 | 通知端到端（prompt 载荷 `{t,b}` / `Notification.permission='granted'`） | 同 E2 环境控制台断言 |
| E4 | 上游 2.2.2 文档 vs bundle 不一致（`useTheme` 等 5 项文档有/bundle 无；无 env 槽位；无 `chat` 命名空间） | `docs/plugins.zh.md` vs `console/assets/index-*.js` |
| E5 | PawApp 门控不一致（`/apps/` 要 `plugin_type==="app"`；`/api/pawapps` 按 `meta.pawapp`；Expo 硬编码 `/apps/{id}`） | `app/routers/{frontend_plugin,pawapps}.py`、PR #7378 `pawapp/[id].tsx` |
| E6 | 全栈插件端点面（54 端点；25–35 可端侧化 / 其余有状态） | 我们插件仓库 `agentteams_connector/`（公开） |
