issues.title: [Bug] QQ group messages silently dropped on 2.2.2
issues.body:
# [Bug] QQ group messages silently dropped on 2.2.2 — gateway dispatches `GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE`, but `_MESSAGE_EVENT_SPECS` only knows `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE`

## Environment
- QwenPaw **2.2.2** (upgraded from 2.2.1, agentscope 2.0.10)
- Channel: QQ official bot, **group** chat
- Linux

## Symptom
After upgrading 2.2.1 → 2.2.2, the bot stops receiving **group** messages: @-mentioning the bot in a group produces no reply at all. Direct messages (`C2C_MESSAGE_CREATE`) keep working, and sending messages *to* the same group works fine. Reconnecting the WebSocket and fully restarting the app do not help — both connections reach `READY`, and no group event is ever logged.

## Root cause
A temporary log line in the gateway dispatch handler showed the event types actually dispatched:

```
dispatch seen t=READY s=1
dispatch seen t=GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE s=2 keys=['author','content','group_id','group_openid','id','message_scene','message_type','timestamp']
```

`_MESSAGE_EVENT_SPECS` in `qwenpaw/app/channels/qq/channel.py` registers only:

- `C2C_MESSAGE_CREATE`
- `AT_MESSAGE_CREATE`
- `DIRECT_MESSAGE_CREATE`
- `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE`

`GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE` is missing, so `_handle_msg_event()` hits `spec is None` and returns silently — group messages are dropped with no log line, which makes this hard to diagnose.

## Fix that worked locally
```python
"GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE": _MessageEventSpec(
    message_type="group",
    sender_keys=("member_openid", "id"),
    extra_meta_keys=("group_openid",),
),
```

Group messages are delivered again after adding this entry.

## Notes
- Not caused by the replayed-event guard from #8006 — no "duplicate dispatch" warnings were logged while the issue was happening.
- Probably worth keeping **both** `GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE` and `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE` registered, since the dispatched name may depend on bot type/permissions.

issues.title: [Bug][Console] Wheel scrolling in a long conversation gets stuck: transcript height re-estimation snaps the view back 1.1-2.2k px
issues.body:
### QwenPaw Version

2.2.2 (QwenPaw Desktop, Windows 10 AMD64, WebView2 / Edge 155.0.4283.45)

Bundle under test: `console/assets/chat-vendor-BLoJqpIE.js` (mtime 2026-10-15 14:25). Captured on 2026-10-16.

### Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Core / Backend
- [ ] Channels
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

### Description

Plain mouse-wheel scrolling in a **long** conversation cannot make progress: every 1.5-2.2 s the transcript is thrown back 1,100-2,200 px, so the user ends up scrolling in place. No navigation action, no streaming answer and no new message is involved - the recording below is a pure wheel-scroll session in an already-finished conversation.

After the snap-back the view lands exactly on the *new* maximum scroll offset (see the arithmetic below), which is what makes me think the transcript total height is being re-estimated while the user is scrolling, and the scroll offset is then clamped to it instead of being anchored.

### How this was measured (read-only)

The app was started through the official `qwenpaw-desktop-debug.cmd`, which only adds `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=9222` on `127.0.0.1`. Over that port a small recorder attached to the page:

- passive listeners for `wheel` (capture, `{passive:true}`) and `scroll` on the transcript scroller, recording `{scrollTop, scrollHeight, clientHeight, elements matching [data-role][id], elements matching [class*="anchor"]}` for every event;
- a `MutationObserver` on the same subtree, plus console/exception capture.

No input was synthesized and no DOM was modified. Raw JSONL trace (1,600+ events) kept locally.

### Observed loop - 15 consecutive identical cycles

One cycle, verbatim from the trace (identical numbers repeated 15 times between 19:03:12 and 19:03:38):

```
wheel  dy=+100  scrollTop=-1563  clientHeight=648  scrollHeight=3312   <-- last position the user reached
scroll          scrollTop=-3799  clientHeight=648  scrollHeight=5548   <-- +2236 height jump, 1 ms later
scroll          scrollTop=-2745  clientHeight=648  scrollHeight=3394   <-- -2154, 15 ms later
scroll          scrollTop=-2663  clientHeight=648  scrollHeight=3312   <-- -82, 17 ms later: view snapped back
wheel  dy=+100  scrollTop=-2563  ...                                   <-- the user keeps scrolling from here
```

The last two offsets are exactly the *bottom limit of the shrunken content*:

```
-(3312 - 648) = -2664   (observed -2663)
-(3394 - 648) = -2746   (observed -2745)
```

so the browser is not "animating back" - the offset the app wanted (`-3799`, valid while `scrollHeight` was 5548) becomes out of range when the content shrinks to 3312 and gets clamped to `-2664`.

Net effect per cycle: the user wheels from `-3699` down to `-1563` (2,136 px of progress), then is pushed back to `-2663`, i.e. **zero net movement**; the view is stuck oscillating between `-1563` and `-2663`.

### The height keeps changing although the message set does not

In every sampled frame during the loop:

```
document.querySelectorAll('[data-role][id]').length        = 25   (constant)
document.querySelectorAll('[class*="anchor"]').length      = 64   (constant)
scrollHeight over the same second: 3312 / 3394 / 5138 / 5548 / 8969
```

Largest single jump seen: `scrollHeight 4942 -> 8969 (+4027)` with `scrollTop -1411 -> -5437`, then back down to `-2745 / -2663` within 20 ms. Average per-item height implied by these numbers swings between ~130 px and ~360 px for the same items, so item heights are clearly being estimated rather than measured. No `mutate` events accompany the jumps (the mutation observer reports nothing in that window).

### Code pointer

In `console/assets/chat-vendor-BLoJqpIE.js` every transcript item is rendered with:

```js
{ contentVisibility: "auto", containIntrinsicSize: "auto 160px" }
```

and the scroller itself:

```css
.qwenpaw-bubble-list-scroll { height:100%; width:100%; overflow:auto; scrollbar-gutter: stable both-edges; }
.qwenpaw-bubble-list { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:24px; padding:16px 16px 0 16px; }
/* in -order-desc mode: ::before { height:16px } ::after { height:70px } */
```

Hypothesis: items that are scrolled out of view are laid out with the 160 px intrinsic placeholder instead of their real height, so the transcript's `scrollHeight` changes while the user scrolls, and because nothing re-anchors the scroll offset, the browser clamps it to the new maximum - which is the snap the user sees.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a long conversation (the one recorded had 64 anchors / 25 rendered bubbles).
2. Scroll continuously with the wheel toward the newer end.
3. Every ~1.5-2.2 s the transcript jumps back and the scroll position cannot advance past a certain point.

### Expected behaviour

Wheel scrolling should move the transcript monotonically, and `scrollHeight` should not change unless the transcript content actually changes.

### Related issues

- #8186 / PR #8214 - "message-navigation jump overrides manual wheel scrolling". That one requires clicking a navigation entry first; this report uses no navigation at all and still reproduces.
- #8251 / PR #8273 - navigation directory accuracy. Also requires the navigation panel; unrelated to wheel-only scrolling.
- The bundle recorded here (2026-10-15) predates #8273, but since neither repro path uses the navigation panel, I do not expect #8273 to change this behaviour.

### Suggested fixes

- Re-anchor on height change: record the offset of the first visible item before the transcript's height changes and restore the same visual offset after it, instead of letting the browser clamp `scrollTop`.
- Do not rely on `contain-intrinsic-size` placeholders for the transcript (measure items, or cap the discrepancy), so that total height stays stable while scrolling.
- Guard the automatic "scroll to bottom / scroll to active item" path so it cannot run while a user wheel gesture is in flight (this is the part that #8214 started).

issues.title: [Bug]: Global /chat/<id> deep link fails across agents; same-agent deep link also fails to activate the session

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.1 (self-hosted, pip install)

## Description

Two related symptoms when opening a chat session via a `/chat/<id>` **deep link** (e.g. from an external plugin/integration):

1. **Cross-agent deep link**: with current agent = A, opening `/chat/<UUID of a session belonging to agent B>` keeps the page in A's context; the target session never loads. The URL is NOT rewritten and does NOT fall back to some specific old session — it simply fails to enter the target session.
2. **Same-agent deep link**: even when `localStorage['qwenpaw-last-used-agent']` matches and the session id belongs to the current agent, the deep link does **not activate** the target session; the page stays on the previous view.

Clicking a session in the sidebar always works ("switch agent → toast → click session"), which shows the **URL path and the click path are two different code paths with unequal capabilities**.

**Security considerations:** none (UI routing/session activation only).

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.1
- **OS:** Linux (containerized self-host; console on :8088)
- **Install method:** pip
- **Python version:** 3.11

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set current agent context to A (e.g. `localStorage['qwenpaw-last-used-agent']='A'`).
2. Open `http://<host>:8088/chat/<session UUID that belongs to agent B>` in a new tab → page stays in A's context, target session unreachable.
3. Set `localStorage['qwenpaw-last-used-agent']` to the correct agent, open `/chat/<session UUID of the SAME agent>` → agent context is correct, but the session is still not activated.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** deep link leaves you in the wrong/no session, silently; no error UI.
- **Expected:** `/chat/<id>` reliably activates the target session.

## Suspected root cause (source reading, line numbers from `console/src/`)

**Symptom 1 (agent context scoping):** `pages/Chat/index.tsx:1256` `resolveBackendChatId(chatId)` → `sessionApi.getSessionIdentity` (`:1097-1126`) → `findSession` (`:1040-1044`) only searches **the current agent's** `sessionList`. A foreign-agent id yields `backendChatId = undefined` → `sessionScope` (`:1263`) becomes `{agentId: currentAgent, sessionId: targetUUID, chatId: undefined}`. The global route's agent context comes from `useAgentStore.selectedAgent` (`agentStore.ts:17/48-62`, backed by localStorage `qwenpaw-last-used-agent`); the URL carries no agent segment.

Note: the fallback chain at `:1249` (`chatId ?? validLastActiveChatId ?? "new"`) is NOT triggered in the deep-link case (chatId is non-empty) — worth checking so the fix doesn't target the wrong line.

**Symptom 2 (activation path inequality):** `pages/Chat/components/ChatSessionInitializer/index.tsx` — the URL-driven effect (`:71-129`) early-returns **silently** when `!sessions.length` (L72), and does nothing when its three-way id match fails (`:108-115`); whereas the sidebar click handler (`:136-189`, `qwenpaw:sidebar-select-session`) explicitly does `preloadSession → getEffectiveSessionId → navigate(replace) → setCurrentSessionId`. The two paths have unequal capabilities.

## Logs / Screenshots

Runtime check from our integration:

```
set localStorage['qwenpaw-last-used-agent']='default'
open /chat/<frontend-agent session UUID>
=> final URL keeps the target UUID; agent context renders "Current Agent Default"; target session not loaded

set localStorage['qwenpaw-last-used-agent']='frontend'  (correct agent)
open /chat/<same-agent session UUID>
=> agent context correct, but session still not activated
```

## Additional Notes

- We are shipping a **plugin-based workaround** (same mechanism as our "Markdown User Messages" plugin) so this does not block us, but the proper fix belongs in core.
- Any of these would close it for us: (a) on resolution failure, look the id up across agents and switch context automatically; (b) document an agent-scoped route (e.g. `/agents/<agent>/chat/<id>`); (c) make the URL path behave exactly like a programmatic sidebar click (align the `ChatSessionInitializer` effect with `handleSelectSession`) and show an explicit error instead of silently staying.

prs.title: fix(providers): bound inline media per request, not just per file
prs.body:
## Summary

The per-file inline cap (`MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES`, 2 MB) does not bound the
**request body**. Media counts ~0 tokens, so token-based context eviction
never fires, and a session that accumulates many *in-spec* images keeps
sending a multi-megabyte body on every turn. Once a gateway's byte limit
answers 413 the session is unusable until the history is stripped by hand.

This adds a cumulative inline-media budget to the shared capping
formatters, so the request body is bounded independently of tokens.

Refs #7671

## What Problem This Solves

The reporter's incident: a design-review session accumulated ~20 MB of
inline base64 screenshots — every one *under* the 2 MB per-file cap — and
every subsequent turn failed with provider 413 until the session JSON was
surgically stripped. A 2,979,813-byte PNG also became
`[Image unavailable: ... exceeds the 2097152-byte image limit.]`, i.e. an
image marginally over the line was dropped even though a slightly smaller
version would have been fine.

PR #7965 fixed the Scroll-side half (reclaim historical media, fold media
into the existing compression flow) and explicitly listed this as remaining:

> **Out of scope / TODO** — HTTP request-body limits: accumulated media can
> still exceed a gateway's byte limit without exceeding the token threshold.

This PR closes that TODO.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/providers/capping_formatter.py`:

- New `max_total_bytes` field (default `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` = 8 MB
  = 4× the per-file cap; `0` disables it, restoring per-file-only behaviour).
- `_maybe_cap_total` spends the budget as each media source is formatted and
  returns a placeholder once the next one no longer fits.
- `_cap_media` runs the per-file cap first, so a file that is already a
  placeholder is never charged to the budget.
- Every `format()` scopes the budget to its own call via a `ContextVar`, and
  resets it in a `finally`.

Because formatting walks the conversation oldest-first, spending the budget
as it is spent **keeps the newest media and drops the oldest** — the
direction the issue asks for.

A `ContextVar` rather than instance state, because formatter instances are
shared across concurrent requests and a running total on the instance would
let one session spend another's allowance
(`test_concurrent_requests_do_not_share_a_budget` pins this).

Placeholder wording distinguishes the two causes, and every provider shape
is preserved: Chat Completions / Anthropic / DashScope `{"type":"text"}`,
Gemini `{"text"}`, Responses API `{"type":"input_text"}`.

## Evidence

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers/test_capping_formatter.py -q
45 passed
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetEndToEnd` drives the **real** formatters (OpenAI,
Anthropic, Gemini, DashScope, and the Responses formatter) over a
three-image conversation with a budget that fits only one:

```
[media omitted from model context: this request already inlines 513 bytes
 of media, exceeds the 900-byte per-request limit]     <- oldest, dropped
[media omitted from model context: ... 900-byte ...]   <- middle, dropped
{"inline_data": {...}}                                 <- newest, inlined
```

Each of the 6 budget tests fails with the cumulative check neutralised
(verified by reverting `_maybe_cap_total` to a no-op):

```
FAILED test_budget_spends_down_and_then_caps
FAILED test_undersized_media_still_spends_the_budget
FAILED test_oldest_media_dropped_newest_kept[_CappingOpenAIFormatter]
FAILED test_oldest_media_dropped_newest_kept[_CappingAnthropicFormatter]
FAILED test_oldest_media_dropped_newest_kept[_CappingGeminiFormatter]
FAILED test_oldest_media_dropped_newest_kept[_CappingDashScopeFormatter]
6 failed, 38 passed
```

Wider runs — no regressions; the failures listed are pre-existing on clean
`main` in this environment (git-version dependent, and two need a real
container runtime):

```
$ pytest tests/unit -q
# main:               23 failed, 17021 passed
# this branch:        23 failed, 17037 passed   (+16 = the new tests)

$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00) / mypy   # clean
```

## Notes for review

- **The default changes behaviour**: a request that used to inline ~20 MB of
  media now inlines 8 MB and placeholders the rest. If you would rather this
  be opt-in, set `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES = 0` and I will drop the
  default; the plumbing and tests are unaffected.
- `model_factory`'s tool-result video path (`_video_oversize_placeholder`)
  applies its own per-file cap and is untouched — it does not go through
  these formatters, so it is not covered by the cumulative budget. Worth a
  follow-up if you want one budget for both paths.
- The issue's other asks (auto-downscale an oversized attachment instead of
  dropping it, and making the cap configurable per provider) are not
  included; the cap is already a provider field, so only the downscale is
  new work.

prs.title: fix(agents): recognize LM Studio at-most-zero audio rejection (#8171)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After `send_file_to_user` delivers an audio file, the tool-result keeps an audio `DataBlock` in session history. On later turns, `OpenAIChatFormatter` serializes it as `input_audio`. LM Studio (OpenAI-compatible, audio input limit = 0) rejects with:

```
Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'At most 0 audio(s) may be provided in one prompt. (parameter=audio)', 'type': 'BadRequestError', 'param': 'audio', 'code': 400}}
```

Neither `_is_audio_fallback_error()` nor `_EXPLICIT_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_PATTERNS` matched this wording on `main`, so strip → retry → learn never ran and the session stayed permanently wedged.

This is a third rejection shape in the family of #7015 / #7024. Open PR #7654 covers DashScope URL-shape and llama-server `audio input is not supported`, but **not** this LM Studio `At most 0 audio(s)` body — verified against #7654's diff before opening this PR.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8171

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Ready for review

## What Changed

- Extend `_is_audio_fallback_error` to recognize `at most N audio(s) may be provided in one prompt` and the accompanying `(parameter=audio)` / `param: audio` markers so the existing strip → retry path learns `rejects_audio`.
- Keep image/video `at most N` limits off the audio-strip path (they stay request-scoped media signals and do not teach `rejects_media` for a pure audio cap).
- Regression tests: classifier True/False cases + strip-and-retry / learn for the LM Studio body.

## Evidence

**Before the fix** (classifier False → error re-raised; session stays wedged):

```
classifier RuntimeError: False
classifier FakeAPIError(status_code=400): False
explicit unsupported-media pattern hits: NONE
strip-retry path: RAISED RuntimeError
provider calls: 1
force_strip_audio after raise: False
```

**After the fix:**

```
classifier RuntimeError: True
"At most 0 image(s) ... (parameter=image)": False for _is_audio_fallback_error
pytest tests/unit/agents/test_react_agent_scroll_seen.py tests/unit/agents/test_react_agent_media_strip.py
56 passed
```

## Testing

```bash
pytest tests/unit/agents/test_react_agent_scroll_seen.py \
  tests/unit/agents/test_react_agent_media_strip.py -q --tb=short
```

Happy to adjust if maintainers prefer folding this into #7654 instead of a focused follow-up.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Update QwenPaw Data to 1.0.3 for QwenPaw 2.2.2, with shared model configuration, datasource-aware dataset selection, user-scoped analysis sessions, and QwenPaw-Data runtime 0.3.3.

- **Use Main Chat models by default.** Analysis inherits the workspace model; summaries and DataBridge follow analysis. Optional overrides use the same provider configuration. Credentials resolve server-side for each new turn, and model changes preserve conversation memory.
- **Fix dataset selection and reload.** Load datasets from the selected datasource and include the user's selections in analysis requests.
- **Refresh the Data app interface.** Update the embedded analysis console and simplify model settings, with app-specific connections available under Advanced. Build the Context console from the pinned `v0.3.3` release.
- **Improve runtime startup and compatibility.** Isolate the app's service environment, check required runtime capabilities, and require QwenPaw-Data 0.3.3 across the app manifest, installer, and optional Python dependencies. This includes the final-response stream fix and validated dependency upgrades.
- **Return actionable model errors.** Missing model selections, unsupported providers, and missing credentials return HTTP 409 before submitting an analysis.
- **Preserve Windows service lifecycle.** Run sidecar modules in the supervised Python process on Windows, preserving the PID across startup and shutdown. POSIX retains exec-based startup.
- **Scope session access.** Bind session requests to the authenticated user, workspace, and app.

Changes cover the Data app, its tests, optional Python runtime dependency minimums, and its CI/release workflows. Most changed files are generated assets in the embedded console snapshot.

## Evidence

- 238 Data-app tests passed locally after review fixes; all applicable pre-commit checks passed for the seven changed files, including workflow linting.
- HTTP regression tests verify actionable 409 responses for missing models, unsupported providers, and missing credentials, without submitting a chat or exposing credentials.
- Real local service lifecycle tests verify supervised PID identity, shutdown, restart, credential refresh, environment isolation, and arguments containing spaces. Both POSIX startup and the in-process module path pass on macOS. The focused runtime checks also passed on native Windows and Linux at `3b05cdc2`; the same [successful workflow run](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/actions/runs/39291518437) passed the Data UI build/tests. Lifecycle assertions verify both process exit and endpoint shutdown.
- Earlier app validation: 3 UI tests, TypeScript/Vite and Context console builds, embedded-console checksums, and packaged app contents passed.
- Managed-service smoke testing on QwenPaw 2.2.2 verified runtime startup, capability discovery, and cross-user session isolation. The latest merged runtime also passed local service health, model inheritance, datasource discovery, and GAAP dataset checks.
- The companion 0.3.3 release PR validates all four wheels and source distributions, installed versions, package imports, CLI startup, and dependency compatibility.

## Release and upgrade

**Release prerequisite completed:** [QwenPaw-Data #97](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw-Data/pull/97) is merged, and all four 0.3.3 packages plus the [`v0.3.3` GitHub release](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw-Data/releases/tag/v0.3.3) are published. The app's main-branch packaging workflow builds the Context console from that tag; a missing tag prevents packaging. App version remains 1.0.3.

Older sessions without ownership metadata remain on disk but need explicit ownership migration before appearing in scoped session lists. See `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-data/RELEASE.md` for upgrade and release instructions.

prs.title: feat(skills): make skill-pool downloads cancellable jobs (#8126)
prs.body:
## Description

Downloading a skill from the skill pool is currently a blocking request:
`POST /skills/pool/download` only answers when the whole install finished.
For a large pool, or a slow connection, that can take minutes with no way to
stop it from the Console, and the server keeps installing even after the user
walks away.

This PR turns the download into a cancellable job, following the design note
that was reviewed and approved on the tracking issue
(https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8126#issuecomment-6210083224 —
"Thanks for the plan. (a) is good.").

What it does:

- Adds `POST /skills/pool/downloads`, which returns `202` with an opaque job id
  instead of blocking.
- Adds `GET /skills/pool/downloads/{job_id}` and
  `DELETE /skills/pool/downloads/{job_id}`. Job states are `running`,
  `cancelling`, `completed`, `failed` and `cancelled`.
- Leaves the existing blocking endpoint untouched, so current callers keep
  working.
- Moves the per-workspace lock from the request handler to the job, so the lock
  is released at a safe point when a job is cancelled instead of being held for
  the lifetime of an HTTP request.
- Reuses the existing failure rollback for cancellation: a cancelled job never
  leaves a partially installed skill behind, and never deletes the skill that
  was already installed, nor its settings.
- Drives the Console broadcast preview through the job, shows `Cancelling`
  until cleanup has finished, keeps its own polling interval with no fixed
  timeout, and never exposes the job id in the UI. A completed install still
  wins over a concurrent cancel.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8126

**Security Considerations:** No new authentication or authorization surface.
The endpoint keeps the existing workspace/session checks, and job ids are
generated server-side, opaque, and not surfaced to the user.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [x] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

      (`--all-files` was not run; the changed files are listed in Evidence)
- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed) — no user-facing docs change required
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

```bash
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/unit/agents/skill_system tests/unit/app/routers -q
```

```bash
node ./node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -b --noEmit
node ./node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js <changed console files>
```

Manual check of the new flow:

1. Open Settings → Skill Pool, pick a skill with a slow pool source, press
   Download.
2. The modal shows the job running; pressing Cancel switches it to
   `Cancelling` and the button stays disabled until cleanup finished.
3. Afterwards the skill list is unchanged: no partial skill is installed, and
   the previously installed skill and its settings are still there.

prs.title: feat(chats): persist per-chat approval level on the server
prs.body:
# feat(chats): persist per-chat approval level on the server

## Description

The console chat page has a per-chat "Tool Approval Mode" toggle, but the per-chat value only ever lived in **browser localStorage**, carried per request via `request_context.approval_level`. Switching device or browser lost the per-chat level, and the scope was documented nowhere (see #8180).

This PR gives the level a **server-side home on the chat** — chat metadata plus read/write endpoints — following the exact pattern the app already uses for the sibling session settings (session model, thinking preference, project dirs). The console toggle now reads and writes the server for existing chats; the per-request carry is kept as a fallback so **no existing client needs to change** (clients that never write the field keep today's behavior byte-for-byte).

Resolution priority after this change:

1. the level **persisted on the chat** (new; cross-device),
2. the client-carried `request_context.approval_level` (unchanged; fallback),
3. the agent-level default from `agent.json` (unchanged).

Mid-turn semantics are unchanged: a level change applies from the next request; an in-flight run keeps its resolved level.

Related: #8180 (this PR implements its option 2 — "the server should own a session-scoped field, with the current per-request mechanism kept as a fallback").

## Change

22 files:

**Server (5)**
- `src/qwenpaw/services/session_approval.py` *(new)* — reads the persisted level from chat meta (`meta["runtime_context"]["approval_level"]`); malformed stored values resolve to "no override" rather than steering a turn to the wrong level.
- `src/qwenpaw/app/chats/manager.py` — `set_session_approval_level`: set/clear under the manager lock, same read-modify-write shape as `set_session_model` / `set_session_thinking` / `set_session_project_dirs`.
- `src/qwenpaw/app/chats/api.py` — `GET` and `PUT /chats/{chat_id}/approval-level`; the PUT body is `{"level": "STRICT" | … | null}` (case-insensitive, validated against `ToolExecutionLevel`; `null` clears the override → chat follows the agent default).
- `src/qwenpaw/hooks/request_setup/contextvars_hook.py` — at request setup, the persisted level replaces the client-carried value in `request_context` when present; best-effort read (any lookup problem falls back to carried/agent default, never blocks a turn).
- `src/qwenpaw/governance/tool_adapter.py` — resolver docstring updated to the three-tier priority.

**Console (9)**
- `console/src/api/modules/chat.ts` — `chatApi.getApprovalLevel` / `setApprovalLevel`.
- `console/src/pages/Chat/components/ApprovalLevelToggle.tsx` — for existing chats: load the server value on mount (localStorage becomes a cache/offline fallback); persist on change; a new "Follow agent default" entry clears the override; a user selection mid-load is never clobbered by a stale response; if the server rejects a write the UI rolls back to the previous level with an error toast — the level is a security control and must not silently display a value the server never stored (the same treat-failure-as-failure convention upstream #8188 applies to approval decisions). Draft chats (no chat id yet) keep pure-local behavior; a preference chosen before the chat exists is adopted onto the server when the chat loads with no persisted level.
- `console/src/pages/Chat/index.tsx` — pass `agentId` for the `X-Agent-Id` header.
- `console/src/pages/Chat/components/ApprovalToggle.test.tsx` — three new component tests (server value wins over local cache; local preference adopted when server has none; rollback + error toast when the server rejects a write, with the optimistic flip asserted via a deferred PUT).
- `console/src/pages/Chat/ChatPage.coverage.test.tsx` — chat API mock extended with the two new methods.
- `console/src/locales/{en,zh,ja,id,pt-BR,ru,vi}.json` — `toolExecutionLevelTooltip` rewritten to the now-true wording ("stored on the server so it follows you across devices; other chats use the agent's default level") + new `followAgent` / `followAgentDesc` / `persistFailed` keys.

**Docs (2)**
- `README.md` / `README_zh.md` — new "Scope" sub-bullet under Tool Guard: agent-level default in the agent config; per-chat override stored server-side with the chat, cross-device, takes precedence; per-request carry kept as fallback; mid-turn changes apply from the next request.

**Tests (3, new)** — `tests/unit/services/test_session_approval.py`, `tests/unit/app/chats/test_api_approval_level.py`, `tests/unit/hooks/test_contextvars_hook_approval.py`.

**Compatibility note:** `vi.json`'s entire `agentConfig.toolExecutionLevel` block (title / level names / descs, 11 keys) was missing from upstream — the Vietnamese console rendered English fallbacks for the whole approval menu. This PR restores the block (Vietnamese) while adding the new keys.

## Verification

- **Python**: 36 new unit tests (meta reader, manager setter against the real `JsonChatRepository`, both route endpoints incl. 404/422/validate paths, hook reader incl. "never raises") + regression across `tests/unit/{app/chats,hooks,governance,services}` — **814 passed, 2 skipped**. `black --line-length=79`, `flake8`, `pylint` (repo hook args), `mypy` — no new findings in touched files.
- **Console**: vitest over `src/pages/Chat` + `src/api/modules` + approval hook — **98 files / 1222 tests passed** (re-verified on the tree merged with upstream `main` `02b6a6d0`, which includes the #8188 approval-race fix); `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- **Backward compatibility**: a client that never calls the new endpoints is unaffected — the hook only overrides `request_context.approval_level` when the chat has a persisted value; otherwise the carry/agent-default path is untouched.
- Manual check after merge (5 steps):
  1. Chat A: set approval level to STRICT → `GET /chats/{A}/approval-level` returns `STRICT`; the value survives a page reload.
  2. Open the same agent's chat B → B shows the agent-level default, not STRICT.
  3. Open chat A in another browser/incognito profile (or clear localStorage) → the trigger still shows STRICT (server value).
  4. Select "Follow agent default" in chat A → override cleared, trigger shows the agent default; `approval_level` is `null`.
  5. Vietnamese UI: the approval menu renders fully in Vietnamese (previously English fallback).

---


**说明**

控制台会话页有按会话的「工具审批模式」开关，但按会话的值此前只存在**浏览器 localStorage** 里，通过 `request_context.approval_level` 逐请求携带——换设备/浏览器就丢了，且作用范围无任何文档（见 #8180）。

本 PR 给该等级一个**服务端的家：存在 chat 元数据里 + 读写端点**——完全沿用应用已有的会话级设置模式（session model / thinking / project dirs）。控制台开关对已存在的会话改为读写服务端；逐请求携带保留为兜底——**任何现有客户端无需改动**（从不写新字段的客户端行为与今天逐字节一致）。

改动后的解析优先级：

1. **chat 上持久化的等级**（新增，跨设备）；
2. 客户端逐请求携带的 `request_context.approval_level`（不变，兜底）；
3. `agent.json` 的 Agent 级默认值（不变）。

回合中语义不变：改等级从下一次请求生效，进行中的 run 保持其已解析等级。

关联：#8180（本 PR 落地其选项 2——「服务端应拥有会话级字段，现有逐请求携带机制保留为兜底」）。

**改动**

22 个文件：

**服务端（5）**
- `src/qwenpaw/services/session_approval.py`（新）— 从 chat meta 读持久化等级；存储值畸形时解析为「无覆盖」而非把回合带偏。
- `src/qwenpaw/app/chats/manager.py` — `set_session_approval_level`：管理锁下读-改-写，与 `set_session_model` / `set_session_thinking` / `set_session_project_dirs` 同构。
- `src/qwenpaw/app/chats/api.py` — `GET` / `PUT /chats/{chat_id}/approval-level`；PUT body `{"level": "STRICT" | … | null}`（大小写不敏感，按 `ToolExecutionLevel` 校验；`null` 清除覆盖→跟随 Agent 默认）。
- `src/qwenpaw/hooks/request_setup/contextvars_hook.py` — 请求建立时，chat 上有持久化值则替换客户端携带值；尽力读取（任何查询问题回落携带/Agent 默认，绝不阻塞回合）。
- `src/qwenpaw/governance/tool_adapter.py` — 解析函数文档串更新为三层优先级。

**控制台（9）**
- `console/src/api/modules/chat.ts` — `chatApi.getApprovalLevel` / `setApprovalLevel`。
- `console/src/pages/Chat/components/ApprovalLevelToggle.tsx` — 已存在的会话：挂载时读服务端值（localStorage 降级为缓存/离线兜底）；改动即持久化；新增「跟随 Agent 默认」入口清除覆盖；加载期间用户的选择不会被陈旧响应覆盖；**服务端拒绝写入时 UI 回滚到变更前的等级并弹错误 toast**——等级是安全控制，不能静默停留在服务端从未存储的值（与上游 #8188 对审批决策「失败即失败」的惯例一致）。草稿会话（尚无 chat id）保持纯本地行为；建会话前选的偏好在会话以无持久化值加载时自动上服务端。
- `console/src/pages/Chat/index.tsx` — 传 `agentId`（X-Agent-Id 头）。
- `console/src/pages/Chat/components/ApprovalToggle.test.tsx` — 新增 3 条组件测试（服务端值优先于本地缓存；服务端无值时采用本地偏好；服务端拒绝写入时回滚+错误 toast——用 deferred PUT 同时断言乐观态与回滚）。
- `console/src/pages/Chat/ChatPage.coverage.test.tsx` — chat API mock 补两个新方法。
- `console/src/locales/{en,zh,ja,id,pt-BR,ru,vi}.json` — `toolExecutionLevelTooltip` 改写为现在的真实语义（「保存在服务端、跨设备一致；其他会话用 Agent 默认」）+ 新增 `followAgent` / `followAgentDesc` / `persistFailed` 键。

**文档（2）**
- `README.md` / `README_zh.md` — Tool Guard 下新增「作用范围」子弹：Agent 级默认在 agent 配置；按会话覆盖存在服务端随会话存储、跨设备、优先；逐请求携带保留为兜底；回合中改动从下一次请求生效。

**测试（3，新）** — `tests/unit/services/test_session_approval.py`、`tests/unit/app/chats/test_api_approval_level.py`、`tests/unit/hooks/test_contextvars_hook_approval.py`。

**兼容性说明**：`vi.json` 的整个 `agentConfig.toolExecutionLevel` 块（title / 四档名称 / 四档描述共 11 键）在上游缺失——越南语文档的控制台审批菜单整体渲染英文回退。本 PR 恢复该块（越南语）并补入新键。

**验证**

- **Python**：36 条新单测（meta 读取器、对真实 `JsonChatRepository` 的 manager setter、两个路由端点含 404/422/校验路径、hook 读取器含「绝不抛异常」）+ `tests/unit/{app/chats,hooks,governance,services}` 回归——**814 passed, 2 skipped**。`black --line-length=79` / `flake8` / `pylint`（仓库钩子参数）/ `mypy` 触达文件无新增违规。
- **控制台**：vitest 覆盖 `src/pages/Chat` + `src/api/modules` + 审批 hook——**98 文件 / 1222 测试全过**（在与 upstream main `02b6a6d0`（含 #8188 审批竞态修复）的合并树上复验）；`tsc --noEmit` 干净。
- **向后兼容**：从不调新端点的客户端不受影响——hook 只在 chat 有持久化值时覆盖 `request_context.approval_level`，否则携带/Agent 默认路径原样不动。
- 合并后手动验证（5 步）：
  1. 会话 A 设 STRICT → `GET /chats/{A}/approval-level` 返回 `STRICT`；刷新页面不丢。
  2. 打开同 Agent 的会话 B → B 显示 Agent 默认而非 STRICT。
  3. 换浏览器/无痕窗口打开会话 A（或清 localStorage）→ 开关仍显示 STRICT（服务端值）。
  4. 会话 A 选「跟随 Agent 默认」→ 覆盖清除、`approval_level` 为 `null`。
  5. 越南语界面：审批菜单完整渲染越南语（此前英文回退）。

---

## Evidence

prs.title: refactor(console): improve usability, resilience, and responsive UX
prs.body:
## Summary

This draft consolidates the Console UI/UX refactor into one integration branch, focusing on practical usability, visual consistency, responsive behavior, state correctness, resilience, and bounded performance.

The work follows the repository design guidance and mouse-first interaction checks. It includes the reviewed fixes accumulated across the refactor workstreams and the latest upstream main synchronization.

## What changed

### Interaction usability

- Restored pointer interaction for settings drawers, selectors, popovers, and sidebar tooltips.
- Improved touch targets and mobile interaction for chat submission, files, channels, sessions, and inbox actions.
- Added clearer labels and interaction states for composer actions, settings controls, provider actions, navigation, and skill filters.
- Improved keyboard behavior for the files navigator and sidebar session navigation.
- Preserved selected and hover states with consistent visual feedback.

### Responsive and visual refinement

- Improved layouts across desktop, tablet, and mobile breakpoints.
- Kept environment actions, channel switches, session headers, inbox controls, files panes, token range controls, security selectors, and debug controls accessible at constrained widths.
- Standardized sidebar, settings navigation, cards, loading states, and popup styling.
- Prevented drawer, wheel picker, and activity rail overflow.
- Used available container width rather than viewport assumptions where required.

### State correctness and recovery

- Prevented stale agent-owned requests and mutations from overwriting current state.
- Added or refined load failure, empty state, retry, and recovery handling across chat history, sessions, inbox, files, imports, tools, ACP, heartbeat, voice, backups, MCP, skills, and channels.
- Isolated overlapping actions and drafts by agent or row ownership.
- Preserved form state and adjacent values while removing invalid or inactive payload fields.
- Removed duplicate form defaults and improved settings search and route behavior.

### Performance and runtime quality

- Deduplicated polling and shared desktop approval polling state.
- Deferred and bounded raw tool formatting.
- Bounded mobile session rendering and reduced file tree refresh work.
- Avoided stale async completions and unnecessary hidden-state work.
- Migrated supported Ant Design popup and loading APIs in locally owned paths covered by this refactor.

## Validation performed

- Targeted component and interaction tests were run for modified areas.
- Mouse-first validation used the existing frontend at http://127.0.0.1:5176.
- Responsive checks covered representative desktop, tablet, and mobile widths.
- Verified examples include:
  - environment Edit and Delete actions across six widths;
  - SIP and MQTT form defaults and mobile switch containment;
  - sidebar quick-settings, Appearance, and Theme popup interaction and cleanup;
  - popup hit targets, neighboring-field isolation, and intercepted payload behavior.
- The final bounded network validation continued zero non-GET requests to the real backend.
- No full npm build, test, or format command was run, in accordance with repository validation rules.

## Known limitations and exclusions

- Models were not comprehensively audited in the later full-control pass. Existing model-related changes incorporated from earlier reviewed work remain in this branch.
- SIP LiveKit-to-dev runtime acceptance is DEFERRED/U. The code and focused tests are present, but the bounded mouse run did not produce a dev-mode PUT, so runtime acceptance is not claimed.
- The remaining fresh Security-page overlayClassName warning is DEFERRED/U and dependency-owned. Evidence attributes it to @agentscope-ai/design 1.0.29 Button to SparkTooltip behavior, not the locally repaired Sidebar popovers.
- Dependency forwardRef development warnings remain unchanged and are not claimed as fixed.

## Current status

Completed and reviewed in the final closeout:

- environment container responsiveness;
- channel form default handling;
- mobile channel switch containment;
- locally owned Sidebar popup class migration;
- previously integrated responsive, recovery, state ownership, interaction, and performance workstreams.

The branch is intentionally opened as a draft so CI, final review, and any requested dependency or SIP follow-up can be handled before merge.

## Follow-up plan

1. Run CI and address only evidence-backed failures.
2. Perform final PR review against the documented UI/UX requirements.
3. Decide separately whether to upgrade or patch @agentscope-ai/design for the dependency-owned Tooltip warning.
4. Revisit the SIP runtime lifecycle only if the deferred scope is explicitly reopened.
5. Continue the remaining all-control inventory in a separate scoped pass; do not infer untested controls as passed.
6. Keep Models as a separately scoped audit unless explicitly included.

prs.title: fix(acp): preserve task results after long tool calls
prs.body:
## Summary

QwenPaw's ACP server can exit non-zero after a task has already been solved.
This change keeps long-running turns alive and normalizes only the task-failure
classes confirmed by benchmark evidence. Unexpected internal exceptions still
raise `RequestError` and remain visible.

## Problem

In a 14,580-trial run, QwenPaw produced 21 `NonZeroAgentExitCodeError` cases
(21 / 3,645 = 0.58%). 11 had already received a full verifier score, all
SWE-bench. Root causes:

- Runtime heartbeats were dropped by `_EnvelopeTracker`, and continuous tool
  progress events also produced no ACP frames, so clients closed the connection
  during long shell commands.
- `prompt()` converted every exception into `RequestError.internal_error`.
- Aliyun `data_inspection_failed` / `inappropriate content` errors were not
  classified as content safety.

## Changes

- Forward runtime heartbeats as `tool_call_update(in_progress)` for active tool
  calls.
- Add a 20-second frame-level keepalive based on actual ACP emissions, covering
  continuous but unmapped tool progress events.
- Normalize only:
  - `content_safety` → `stop_reason="refusal"`
  - `StreamIdleTimeoutError` → `stop_reason="end_turn"`
  - ACP transport disconnect (`Connection closed` / `transport closed` /
    `BrokenPipeError`) → `stop_reason="end_turn"`
- All other exceptions keep the original `RequestError` and non-zero exit path.
- Reuse `classify_model_error()` for content-safety decisions.
- Restrict `ConnectionError` handling to ACP transport signatures.

## Failure scope

| Failure | Count | Treatment |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| ACP client disconnect | 10 | Normalized |
| Stream idle timeout | 6 | Normalized |
| Content moderation | 5 | Normalized |
| `ApiRateLimitError` | 856 | Out of scope |
| Agent timeout / verifier / artifact errors | 19 | Remain visible |

prs.title: feat(recording): add reusable record and replay workflows
prs.body:
## Description

Adds a bundled Record & Replay plugin for QwenPaw Desktop on macOS 14+. The plugin records a minimized semantic event stream, lets the user review and select local evidence, previews the exact model payload, requires one-time consent, generates an editable Skill draft, and materializes the approved Skill into the active Agent workspace. Later execution uses the normal Skill/tool path and the optional Computer Use plugin; there is no Record-specific replay engine or DSL.

The implementation keeps one existing **QwenPaw Computer Use.app** Helper and adds a versioned `event_stream` contract beside the existing `computer_use` contract. The plugin owns UI, API, recording/learning services, consent, and workspace persistence. HostRuntime owns authenticated Helper discovery and launch. The Helper owns TCC permissions, capture-time privacy filtering, process-wide device coordination, the visible recording indicator and emergency stop, and short-lived sealed staging artifacts. No second Helper, plugin-owned secret, Python-to-Rust callback channel, or runtime code signing is introduced.

The final scope is one complete feature commit rebased onto `upstream/main@dbff215b5`. Experimental probes, validation transcripts, unused frame schema, migration-only routes, and unrelated runtime/build changes from development were removed. Stable architecture and security invariants are documented in `docs/design/record-and-replay.md`.

**Related Issue:** N/A

**Security Considerations:** Capture is events-only. Raw key text, clipboard/content values, secure-field labels, sensitive titles, excluded applications, absolute coordinates, local paths, and screenshots are excluded before durable import or model transfer. Native minimization and Python import validation are separate trust boundaries. Staging is owner-only, reference-scoped, sealed before import, TTL-limited, and explicitly released. Model generation requires a short-lived consent token bound to the reviewed evidence.

prs.title: fix(channels): carry Telegram quoted reply context into the agent
prs.body:
## Description

The Telegram adapter never reads `message.reply_to_message`, so a quoted message is dropped before it reaches the agent. A user replying "what about this?" leaves the agent with no idea what "this" referred to.

This is the odd one out rather than a missing feature: Feishu (`parent_id`), DingTalk (`repliedMsg`), WeChat (`ref_msg`) and OneBot (quoted segments) all surface the quoted parent already.

**What's broken and how it works.** Telegram delivers the quoted parent on `message.reply_to_message`. Nothing read it, so the handler built a content list containing only the user's own text. `_extract_query_from_payload` and `_extract_chat_name` both read the *first* text part, so the quoted context never existed as far as the agent was concerned. A `/stop` sent as a reply to a quoted message is therefore not recognised as a control command either — it arrives as ordinary chat text, and `is_control` is False.

**What this changes.** Read the quoted message and append it as a `[Quoted message]` text part, falling back to its caption when it carries media rather than text, and cap the quoted text so a long quote cannot flood the context window. +323 lines, no existing line modified.

**One deliberate ordering choice.** The quoted part is appended *after* the user's own text. `_extract_query_from_payload` and `_extract_chat_name` read the first text part, so a leading quoted block would hide control commands such as `/stop` and mis-name the chat. An adversarial review pass caught this: prepending it made a `/stop` sent as a reply stop being recognised, which is the same class of bug this PR fixes.

Two points I raised on the issue and did not decide unilaterally: the ordering above, and whether the attacker-controllable author prefix should be rendered at all (`[Quoted message] alice_h: hi from alice` — the name comes from the quoted message, so it is untrusted text landing in the agent's context). Happy to change either.

**Related Issue:** Refs #8329

**Security Considerations:** The quoted text and the quoted author's display name are attacker-controllable and reach the agent's context. The text is length-capped. I have not stripped the author name in this patch — that is the second question above.

## 背景

本 PR 将模型管理、智能体运行配置和对话模型选择按作用域重新分层，并补齐思考能力联动、自动保存和响应式验证。

prs.title: feat(agent): add /steer command for mid-execution guidance (#1775)
prs.body:
Fixes #1775.

## What Problem This Solves

Today there is no way to correct the agent while a turn is already running:
stopping the turn loses all progress, and waiting for it to finish means
irrelevant work keeps accumulating. `/steer <guidance>` fills this gap — it
lets the user hand the agent mid-flight guidance that takes effect on the
**next** agent turn without stopping anything.

```
/steer Focus on the error handling first
```

## How it works

- `qwenpaw/steer/store.py` — per-session hand-off buffer with a 10-minute
  TTL.
- `qwenpaw/steer/handler.py` — the `/steer` command; records the text.
- `qwenpaw/steer/hook.py` — `SteerInjectionHook`, a `HookBase` subclass at
  `PRE_AGENT_BUILD`, drains the buffer and calls `inject_context`.
- Registered in `bootstrap_factory`'s `builtin_hook_clses` and in
  `collect_builtin_command_specs()`.

## Why not true mid-execution steering

Dispatching inside a running turn needs changes to the reply loop that the
current runtime does not expose safely; injecting at `PRE_AGENT_BUILD`
achieves the same user-visible effect (the next turn follows the guidance)
without touching turn-dispatch internals.

## Evidence

- Manual run: with a long turn in flight, issuing `/steer Focus on the error
  handling first` returned an immediate acknowledgement; the subsequent turn
  opened with the injected context and the agent addressed error handling
  first (observed via turn context log).
- Without `/steer`, the same run ran to completion with no guidance applied.
- Buffer drain is one-shot: a second turn does not re-apply stale guidance;
  guidance older than the 10-minute TTL is dropped.

prs.title: feat(agents): stop replaying media the model no longer needs
prs.body:
## Description

Every request re-uploaded every image and video block stored in history. A screenshot-heavy WeChat session reached a **48.9 MB** request body; the endpoint rejected it with

```
openai.APIStatusError: Failed to buffer the request body: length limit exceeded
```

and because the block lives in `agent.state.context`, every later turn failed the same way — the session stayed wedged until the file was edited by hand.

### Why the existing guards miss it

- `CappingFormatterMixin` caps **each block** at 2 MB. All 43 blocks in that session were below the cap, so nothing tripped.
- Context compaction triggers on **tokens** (`trigger_ratio * context_size`), and image tokens are cheap while their bytes are not — the log showed `outcome=at_or_below_trigger` at a 48 MB body.
- Prompt caching does not help either: a cache hit lowers the *price* of replaying the prefix (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash bills cached tokens at ~10% of input), but it **never removes the upload**.

### What this changes

Two rules, applied **only to the per-request copy** (stored history and channel delivery are untouched — `_normalize_messages_for_formatter` already deep-copies):

1. **Delivery is not context.** Media returned by `send_file_to_user` is never model input: the channel ships the file, so the model gets a reference instead of the bytes.
2. **Consumed media is not re-sent.** Media belonging to a completed turn (an assistant message with text and no tool calls, followed by something newer) has already been turned into text by the model, so it becomes a reference:

```
[image not re-sent to the model: slide_v_zh_00002_.png (image/png, 0.74 MB)
 at D:\...\slide_v_zh_00002_.png — call view_image again if another look is needed]
```

Only the **current turn's** media stays inline. That keeps the newest message working, including a top-level `view_audio` / `view_image` data block stored in an assistant message. A second look now costs one tool call instead of re-uploading megabytes on every turn.

Properties worth noting:

- **Deterministic** for a given history, and the boundary only moves forward, so prefix-cache churn is confined to the turn boundary rather than rewriting the conversation each request.
- Runs **before** `_prepare_media_sources`, so elided media is never read from disk or base64-encoded.
- **Kill switch:** `QWENPAW_DISABLE_MEDIA_ELISION=1`; extra delivery tools via `QWENPAW_DELIVERY_ONLY_TOOL_RESULTS=a,b`.

## Evidence

- Session in the report: 43 media blocks, 35.4 MB decoded (`view_image` 24 / 17.39 MB, `send_file_to_user` 14 / 11.50 MB, `desktop_screenshot` 5 / 6.51 MB); request dump 48.9 MB.
- With these rules only the current turn's media is inlined (typically 0–3 blocks); everything older becomes a one-line reference. Delivery is unaffected because channels render the tool-result block, not the formatter output.
- `pytest tests/unit/agents/test_media_turn_scoped_elision.py` → 11 passed (including a test that the stored `Msg` list is not mutated, and one that a current-turn `view_audio` block stays inline).
- `pytest tests/unit/{agents,channels,app}` → 9065 passed, 22 skipped, 4 failed. The 4 are the pre-existing `test_offloader.py` retention failures (they fail on a clean `origin/main` worktree on this Windows host as well).
- `black --line-length=79`, `flake8`, `mypy` (0 errors) and `pylint` (10.00/10) clean on the changed files.

## Not in this PR (deliberate)

- **No aggregate byte budget.** One turn that views many large images can still exceed an endpoint limit; that case would still need a manual session repair. A byte budget (and a retry on `length limit exceeded` / 413) is the natural follow-up, but it adds config surface and is better discussed separately.
- **No storage-side change.** Media still lives in the session as base64; this PR only stops replaying it. Storing `{path, sha256, dims}` instead is the longer-term direction (see #8335).

## Related

- **#8335** — design discussion: 48 MB bodies, permanent wedges, the two cost bills
  (tokens vs bytes), and the roadmap for media-by-reference.
- This PR implements the **S1 + S2** slice of that design. The aggregate byte
  budget and the oversized-body retry described there are intentionally left
  out, so **#8335 should stay open** to track them.

> Note for reviewers: this PR is intentionally *not* a closing reference. GitHub
> only auto-links an issue when the body says `Fixes #n` / `Closes #n`; this one
> is a partial implementation, so link it manually from the sidebar ("Link an
> issue") if a sidebar link is preferred.

prs.title: feat(mail): support custom IMAP/SMTP servers via provider "custom"
prs.body:
## Description

The managed mailbox workflow (Settings → Agent Management → Email Management) only accepts the built-in personal domains plus three Chinese enterprise providers, although `qwenpawmail-mcp` already honours `QWENPAWMAIL_IMAP_HOST` / `QWENPAWMAIL_SMTP_HOST`. A self-hosted mail server or any provider outside that table cannot be connected at all — the docs currently say so explicitly.

This PR adds a `custom` mail provider whose IMAP/SMTP host and optional ports live on `AgentMailCredential`:

- `config.py`: new fields `imap_host`, `imap_port`, `smtp_host`, `smtp_port`; they are part of the mailbox identity, so changing a host is treated as a different account and requires the credential again.
- `routers/agents.py`: accepts `provider: "custom"`, validates hosts (same syntax rule as custom domains) and ports (1–65535), and rejects host fields for any other provider. Well-known domains still cannot be combined with a provider.
- `mail/driver_config.py`: the generated DriverCard passes the configured hosts to `qwenpawmail-mcp`; ports default to 993 / 465 (implicit SSL, matching the MCP's `IMAP4_SSL` / `SMTP_SSL`).
- `mail/monitor.py`: `resolve_imap_host()` returns the configured host for `custom`, and the monitor connects on the configured port instead of a hard-coded 993.
- Console: "Other (custom server)" appears in the provider select for a custom domain and shows IMAP/SMTP host + port fields; the payload only carries host fields with the custom provider. A dedicated (to-be-registered) mailbox keeps the provider-backed options only. Strings added to all seven locales.
- Docs: `mailbox.en.md` / `mailbox.zh.md` describe the option and the SSL-only limitation.

`CUSTOM_PROVIDER` is defined next to `ENTERPRISE_PROVIDERS` in `qwenpawmail_mcp.providers` so router, driver card and monitor share one constant.

**Related Issue:** none found for custom IMAP/SMTP hosts.

**Security Considerations:** credentials keep the existing path (encrypted `credentials.yaml`, runtime credential binding); only public endpoint data is added to `agent.json` and the DriverCard. Hosts are validated against the existing domain regex before reaching the subprocess environment.

- [x] New feature

- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] `npm run format` (tsc + prettier) and `eslint` pass on the changed console files
- [x] Tests run locally and pass (see Evidence)
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

1. Settings → Agent Management → create/edit an agent → Email Management → *Manage your personal mailbox*.
2. Enter a custom domain (e.g. `example.org`), choose provider **Other (custom server)**, fill IMAP host / SMTP host (ports default to 993 / 465), enter the mailbox password, save.
3. In the agent chat: "Check my mailbox authentication and list all mail folders" → `check_auth` reports `imap_ok` / `smtp_ok`, `list_folders` lists the folders.
4. Set *Wake for every email*; `mail_state/monitor.json` records the baseline UID and a new message shows up in the Console Inbox.

## Evidence

Unit tests (12 new tests were written first and failed with `"AgentMailCredential" object has no field "imap_host"` before the implementation):

```bash
pytest tests/unit/routers/test_agents_mail_validation.py tests/unit/app/mail tests/integration/test_mail_monitor_module.py -q
337 passed in 18.05s

pytest tests/unit -q -n 4 --ignore=tests/unit/hub
5 failed, 13224 passed, 17 skipped in 139.97s
# the 5 failures are unrelated to this change: 3× tests/unit/cli/test_hub_cmd.py (module 'docker' missing in the local venv),
# test_acp_available_commands (xdist timeout), test_tools_router_web_search_config ("Agent 'default' changed on disk" under -n 4)
```

Live verification against a self-hosted mailbox (Dovecot/Postfix on a hosting provider, custom domain, IMAP 993 / SMTP 465), running `qwenpaw app` from this branch with a separate `QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR`:

- `POST /api/agents` with `provider: "custom"` → 201; `GET /api/agents/<id>` returns the hosts and no secret.
- Generated `drivers/mcp/qwenpawmail.yaml` carries `QWENPAWMAIL_IMAP_HOST`, `QWENPAWMAIL_IMAP_PORT: '993'`, `QWENPAWMAIL_SMTP_HOST`, `QWENPAWMAIL_SMTP_PORT: '465'` plus the `mail/qwenpawmail` credential reference.
- `GET /api/mcp/tools/qwenpawmail` → 22 tools.
- Chat: `check_auth` → `{"imap_ok": true, "smtp_ok": true, "imap_host": "<custom host>", "smtp_host": "<custom host>"}`; `list_folders` → INBOX, INBOX.Archive, INBOX.Sent, INBOX.Drafts, INBOX.Spam, INBOX.Trash, INBOX.Notes.
- Push mode `agent_all`: `mail_state/monitor.json` written with `last_uid` / `uidvalidity`; a test message sent to the mailbox produced a `new_email` inbox event (`source_id: _mail_monitor`, `uid` = baseline + 1) within seconds and woke the agent (pending `get_message` approval under the default `ask` policy).

prs.title: feat(providers): refresh MiniMax presets and runtime for M3.1 Flash
prs.body:
Reason: QwenPaw's MiniMax presets still recommend M3 and expose older text models, while M3.1 Flash requires adaptive thinking and a different effort contract.

## What Problem This Solves

Flash is missing from the bundled direct-provider choices. Existing generic thinking controls can request disabled thinking or a legacy token budget, which are invalid for Flash. Older MiniMax text options also remain in ordinary catalog and discovery lists.

This refreshes the existing international and China direct providers to recommend `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`, followed by `MiniMax-M3`, with a 1,000,000-token context and 524,288-token output capacity. Flash exposes low/medium/high/xhigh/max effort (default max), always uses adaptive thinking, and strips disabled/budget/service-tier overrides at the final request boundary. M3 retains adaptive/disabled thinking, defaults to the Anthropic API's disabled behavior, and removes unsupported effort controls.

Older MiniMax text models leave ordinary built-in defaults, templates and discovery candidates. Exact-ID metadata, saved models, user catalog overlays and custom-provider discovery remain available. The OpenCode catalog and Creator picker use the verified `minimax-m3.1-flash-free` route alongside existing M3; OpenRouter remains API-driven. The gateway's published output limit is kept separate from direct API capacity. Creator text/VLM output-capacity lookup recognizes both current direct models. Other providers and image/video generation are unchanged.

## Evidence

The committed `tests/unit/providers/test_minimax_current_models.py` invokes the actual Anthropic SDK through QwenPaw's adapter and intercepts its HTTP transport. Across both direct regions, its 44 generation/streaming captures verify all five Flash effort values, the max default, stale off/budget overrides, and M3 behavior. For example, the captured Flash case with `extra_body={"thinking":{"type":"disabled"},"output_config":{"effort":"none"},"service_tier":"priority"}` produces `thinking={"type":"adaptive"}` and `output_config={"effort":"max"}` with no service tier. The separate `thinking={"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":1000}` case produces adaptive/max with no budget. An omitted/invalid Flash effort becomes max. M3's explicit enabled/budget setting becomes adaptive without a legacy budget, and its default request omits thinking so the Anthropic API default applies.

Catalog assertions verify Flash/M3 as the two ordinary direct defaults, Flash recommendations, the verified OpenCode route, hidden legacy discovery candidates, exact legacy metadata lookup, and preserved user overlays/custom discovery. Creator's additional four actual SDK streaming captures verify legal default payloads and current output capacity.

Observed local validation:

```text
python -m pytest tests/unit/providers -q
963 passed, 2 warnings

# Creator backend: output budgets, text protocols, model config,
# file-agent model client and MiniMax SDK defaults
88 passed

npm test -- src/components/creator/__tests__/ModelConfigModal.test.tsx
14 passed
npm run typecheck
passed
```

The follow-up runs the actual `.pre-commit-config.yaml` revisions, including add-trailing-comma 3.1.0 and Black 23.3.0, and commits their formatting corrections. All four changed files are AST-equivalent before/after formatting; the provider and Creator suites were rerun with the same passing totals above. Every repository-pinned hook passes on the complete PR diff, including Pylint and Prettier. The all-files run passes every hook except two reproducible Pylint E1120 reports at untouched base-file `src/qwenpaw/sandbox/runtime_boundary.py:107-108` (`ctypes.c_ulong()`), under local Python 3.12. That file is byte-identical to the base and is outside this patch. The repository's real-behavior proof evaluator passes this body for an external contributor without override labels; the new-head GitHub Real behavior proof job also passed. Catalog index regeneration and complete diff/body secret and whitespace checks also pass.

Captures used declared AgentScope 2.0.10 and resolved Anthropic 1.15.0, with HTTP intercepted before network I/O. No live or paid inference was performed. Upstream test execution remains subject to its maintainer approval gate.

References: [MiniMax model overview](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/guides/models-intro), [Anthropic-compatible API](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-chat-anthropic), [pricing](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/pricing/overview), [OpenCode live catalog](https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models), [OpenRouter live catalog](https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models), and [models.dev metadata](https://models.dev/api.json).

prs.title: fix(agents): recognize llama-server and DashScope URL audio rejections in audio-fallback classifier
prs.body:
## Description

Follow-up to #7015 (fixed by #7024). The modality-aware audio stripping works, but its reactive learning entry point (`_is_audio_fallback_error`) only recognizes DashScope's "incorrect modal" rejection. Two rejection shapes still fall through and kill the entire agent turn *after* `send_file_to_user` has already delivered the audio file to the user:

1. **DashScope URL-shape rejection** — the first failure mode documented in #7015: local audio serialized as raw base64 is rejected with HTTP 400 `"The provided URL does not appear to be valid"`. This wording never reaches the audio classifier, so no strip-and-retry happens, no `rejects_audio` capability is learned, and **every subsequent turn re-crashes** while the audio block remains in session history (reproduced: the user had to switch the active model to recover the conversation).
2. **llama.cpp `llama-server`** (self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a vision-only mmproj, e.g. Qwen-VL-family GGUFs) rejects `input_audio` with HTTP 500 `"audio input is not supported - hint: ..."`. Same outcome: turn dies, nothing learned.

Both shapes were reproduced in production on QwenPaw 2.2.0 (Windows 11, Python 3.12.13):

- provider `aliyun-tokenplan` / model `qwen3.8-max` → shape 1
- custom provider → local `llama-server` (b10715) serving a Qwen-VL GGUF with vision mmproj → shape 2

The fix reuses the existing strip → retry → learn machinery: both shapes now classify as audio-fallback errors, so the turn recovers and `rejects_audio` is learned for the model key (subsequent requests strip audio proactively while images keep working).

**Related Issue:** Relates to #7015

**Security Considerations:** None. The change only widens error-message classification for the existing audio strip-and-retry path; no new inputs are accepted and no credential/config handling is touched. The URL-shape match is gated on a 400-class status and, at the call site, on `_last_wire_request_had_audio()`, so malformed image/video URLs cannot be misclassified as audio rejections (addressing the concern raised in #7015 about matching the URL error broadly).

prs.title: fix(skills): preserve Chinese Windows ZIP filenames
prs.body:
## Description

Skill ZIP uploads made by Chinese Windows archivers can report success while extracting Chinese filenames as CP437 mojibake. A skill referring to `references/说明.txt` then cannot open its own reference. Decode member names before validation/extraction, honoring UTF-8 and CRC-validated Info-ZIP Unicode Path metadata and conservatively recovering likely DOS/Windows GBK names.

Keep original ZIP header metadata for member reads, validate all decoded paths before extraction, and retain `ZipFile.extractall()` behavior, including Windows filename sanitization. Hub-generated UTF-8 archives are unaffected; this change is scoped to the reported skill-upload path.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8270

**Security Considerations:** Decoded names are checked for traversal, absolute/drive-qualified paths and NUL bytes before any file is written. Symlink and uncompressed-size checks remain in place. Regression tests cover unsafe Unicode metadata and GBK paths.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] Affected local tests pass; repository-wide baseline failures are disclosed below
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed): no new user-facing option; encoding ambiguity is documented in the helper
- [x] Ready for review

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

Not applicable: no channel changes.

## Testing

Environment: Linux 6.8.0-138-generic x86_64, Python 3.11.15, source base `697aeb669f42f223d060772eb7a313eec78ebd20`, installed with `uv pip install -e ".[dev,test,full]"` in a separate environment.

The regression creates a real ZIP with GBK filename bytes in both local and central headers and UTF-8 bit 11 unset, then calls the actual skill extraction entry point. Coverage includes mixed UTF-8/GBK/CP437 entries, GBK trail byte `0x5c`, empty directories, valid and invalid Unicode Path metadata, Windows sanitization, traversal and symlink rejection.

A separate FastAPI `TestClient` reproduction exercised `POST /api/skills/upload?enable=false` through the real upload, scanning, and import pipeline, with only workspace lookup isolated. It ran the exact extraction function from the base revision and then the fixed function. This reproduces Windows ZIP filename bytes on Linux.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the regression expecting the real Chinese directory fails:

```text
pytest tests/unit/agents/skill_system/test_zip_filename_encoding.py::test_import_gbk_skill_preserves_referenced_files -q
1 failed
# actual directory: ╓╨╬─╝╝─▄
# expected directory: 中文技能
```

Actual HTTP upload comparison:

```text
BEFORE (exact extraction source at 697aeb66)
POST /api/skills/upload?enable=false: 200
Imported files: ['SKILL.md', 'references/╦╡├≈.txt']
Linked reference resolves: False

AFTER
POST /api/skills/upload?enable=false: 200
Imported files: ['SKILL.md', 'references/说明.txt']
Linked reference resolves: True
```

Final affected-suite validation:

```text
pytest tests/unit/agents/skill_system -q --tb=short
801 passed, 1 warning in 16.34s
```

## Repository-wide validation

Full `pre-commit run --all-files` passed on the final branch at `aab5b1a8`, including mypy, black, flake8, pylint, prettier and actionlint; the worktree remained clean. The same full gate also passed on the base plus the lint prerequisite.

The affected suites above pass. The repository-wide pytest gate is not completely green on the unchanged base plus the lint prerequisite; the baseline failures are documented below for review.

Plain `pytest` encounters the pre-existing duplicate module name between `tests/integration/test_backup.py` and `tests/unit/routers/test_backup.py`. Validation therefore followed the repository CI's separate unit / contract / integration tiers (integration excludes `manual_real`). Results on the base plus lint prerequisite:

- Unit: 17,259 passed, 24 skipped, 4 initially failed. All four pass when rerun after correcting host umask/locale and making the validation interpreter visible to bubblewrap. No repository source or tests were changed for these environment corrections.
- Contract: 412 passed, 1 skipped.
- Integration: 1,882 passed, 2 skipped, 3 xpassed, 9 initially failed. Seven failures came from a missing Playwright Chromium binary; after installing it, all 8 tests in the three affected browser files passed.
- Two integration assertions still fail independently on the baseline: `tests/integration/test_plugins_router.py::test_plugins_get_nonexistent` and `tests/integration/test_providers_router.py::test_providers_get_nonexistent`. Both expect HTTP 404/400 for GET requests to routes that support other methods and currently return HTTP 405. They do not exercise the code changed by this PR.

## Additional Notes

Flagless ZIP names are inherently ambiguous. GBK recovery is deliberately limited to DOS/Windows entries whose CP437 interpretation contains box-drawing characters and whose valid GBK interpretation contains CJK text; normal UTF-8 and accented CP437 names are preserved. Ambiguous archives should be exported as UTF-8 ZIPs.

A separate prerequisite commit explicitly initializes two Windows `ctypes.c_ulong` outputs to zero. This preserves their existing values and resolves baseline pylint E1120 errors at `runtime_boundary.py:107-108`, without disabling checks.

prs.title: feat(plugins): add clean unload and rollback-safe hot reload
prs.body:
## Description

Add a clean plugin unload path and rollback-safe hot reload so plugin install / update / uninstall no longer rebuilds every live workspace, and a failed update does not leave users on a half-applied new version.

This PR introduces a two-layer teardown ledger (`PluginInstance`) and a `PluginLifecycle` facade (`load` / `unload` / `reload` / `update_config`):

- Official `register_*` entries record real teardowns (HTTP, provider, control command, middleware, prompt section, channel, tools, hooks). Workspace contributions are projected and revoked by name via `WorkspaceProjector` (`start_one` / `stop_one` for channels). Uninstall no longer calls `_schedule_all_agents_reload`.
- Unload modes (`shutdown` / `unload` / `uninstall`) share one ledger. Author shutdown / uninstall hooks run before table rows are dropped. `shutdown` only stops hosted resources (`custody` / `effect`) and does not clear tables or disk.
- Reload probes new code into `plugin_<id>__probe` first; import failure does not tear down the old instance. Hosted resources that do not go quiescent abort the swap. Rollback restores the previous directory / modules and does not run legacy uninstall hooks. Boot recovers interrupted “updating” / “migrating” markers.
- `update_config` rebuilds contributions without reimporting; a half-successful `register()` is torn down before the old config is restored. Disable is `config.plugins[<id>].enabled = false` (reserved framework key).
- Boot dependency policy is local-only: missing deps mark the plugin `FAILED` without installing. Explicit install / update / `POST /plugins/{id}/repair-dependencies` still go through `DependencyGate` (imported host-package blacklist → require restart). Console repair / status UI is intentionally not wired.
- CloudPaw no longer monkeypatches `PluginLoader.unload_plugin`; agent cleanup is an `api.provision` teardown (uninstall only).
- `LifecycleDelegate` is the single predicate at the reserved branch points (`owns_commit` / `owns_dependency_env` / `notify_unload`). Name collisions fail loudly and name the occupant.

Out of scope (documented as deferred): `SourceWatcher`, dry-run / interval-intersection gate enhancements, and Console repair / last-unload UI.

**Security Considerations:** Dependency installation stays gated: boot never networks when deps are already satisfied; colliding with an already-imported host package (e.g. `httpx`) refuses the install and does not write site-packages. Unload / reload only revoke registrations owned by the plugin id; user `agent.json` / provisioned files are not deleted on `mode=unload`. Provision / directory swap are skipped when `owns_commit` is false.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [ ] Ready for review

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

- [ ] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh` (or `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`) and it passes
- [ ] **Contract test** exists in `tests/contract/channels/test_<channel>_contract.py` (REQUIRED)
- [ ] Contract test implements `create_instance()` with proper channel initialization
- [ ] All 19 contract verification points pass (see `tests/contract/channels/__init__.py`)
- [ ] **Optional**: Unit tests in `tests/unit/channels/test_<channel>.py` for complex internal logic

## Testing

1. Unit: `pytest tests/unit/plugins/ -q` (lifecycle, reload rollback, workspace revoke, config update, ledger teardowns).
2. Unload a loaded plugin via `DELETE /plugins/{id}` (or unload without delete) while a conversation is in progress — tools / commands / channels contributed by that plugin disappear by name; the workspace is not rebuilt; `agent.json` is unchanged on `mode=unload`.
3. Force-update a plugin whose new entry has a syntax error or whose `register()` raises — the previous version stays loaded; user-edited provision files stay on disk.
4. Kill the process mid-update (directory swap) and restart — boot restores the backup from the “updating” marker.
5. Boot offline with a plugin whose `requirements.txt` is missing — that plugin is `FAILED`; others still load. `POST /plugins/{id}/repair-dependencies` installs when the user explicitly asks.
6. `PATCH /plugins/{id}/enabled` with `{"enabled": false}` unloads the instance without renaming the plugin directory.

## Additional Notes

- `update_config` is a separate path and does not add a fourth unload mode.
- `enabled` is a reserved framework key and is stripped before `plugin.register()`.
- Repair HTTP is `POST /plugins/{id}/repair-dependencies` only; do not add a second endpoint. Console does not expose a repair button or last-unload report in this PR.
- `unregister_plugin` remains a leftover safety sweep; ledger teardowns are the primary path.
