prs.title: feat(modes): add Advisor Mode
prs.body: ## Description Adds **Advisor Mode**, a loop mode (picked per conversation from the chat input, like Goal and Mission) that pairs two models on one task: a stronger **advisor** model and the **worker** agent, which is running on a cheaper model. Several features: - **Opening plan.** On the first message of a conversation the advisor writes a strategic plan. QwenPaw appends it to the worker's context as a `consult_advisor` tool call with a fixed question and the plan as its result, so the worker reads the plan as an answer to a question it asked. Written once per conversation. - **Mid-run intervention.** QwenPaw watches tool results. On repeated failures (defaults: 3 in a row or 4 in the last 10 steps, at most 3 times per user turn, all configurable) it asks the advisor again. The advisor answers `CONTINUE` (the chat shows the verdict, nothing is added to the worker's context) or `ADJUST` followed by a short revised plan, which is appended the same way as a `consult_advisor_followup` call and result. - **On-demand consultation.** `consult_advisor` is a real tool in Advisor Mode. The worker can ask at a decision point (capped per conversation, default 32). Model setup: by default the advisor is the agent's primary model (`active_model`, the one picked in the chat header) and the worker is the sub-agent model (`subagent_model`, set under Agent model routing). Configuration: | Key | Default | In the template | | --- | --- | --- | | `advisor_model` / `worker_model` | `null` (primary model / sub-agent model) | Advisor and worker models (read-only here, set from the Advisor models panel) | | `advisor_thinking` | `off` | Advisor thinking | | `plan_enabled` | `true` | Opening plan | | `followup_enabled` | `true` | Mid-run auto intervention | | `intervention.consecutive_failures` | `3` | Failures in a row | | `intervention.window_failures` / `window_size` | `4` / `10` | Failures in the window / Window size (steps) | | `intervention.max_interventions` | `3` | Maximum interventions per run (one user turn) | | `intervention.cooldown_steps` | `0` | Cooldown (steps) | | `on_demand_enabled` | `true` | On-demand consultation | | `max_consults` | `32` | Maximum consultations per conversation | **Security Considerations:** None ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [x] Documentation - [ ] Refactoring ## Component(s) Affected - [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [x] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [x] Documentation (website) - [x] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy ## Checklist - [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes - [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks - [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass - [x] Documentation updated (if needed) - [x] Ready for review ## Testing 1. Agent → Configuration → Agent Loop Settings → **Advisor**: switch it on. The template shows every setting from the table above. 2. Start a new chat. In the chat input, open the Loop mode menu and pick **Advisor**. Advisor is listed with the built-in loops. 3. The **Advisor models** panel opens above the pill. Leave the defaults (primary model / sub-agent model) or pick other models, then send a task. 4. The `consult_advisor` plan card appears immediately and streams while the advisor writes. Later turns get no new plan. 5. The model pill in the chat header shows the pair (advisor → worker) and reopens the panel. 6. Give the worker a task whose tool calls keep failing, for example cloning a repository that does not exist and retrying the same command. The trigger fires at the third failed call in a row (`consecutive_failures`, default 3). It is evaluated before the worker's next model call, so when the worker fires several calls at once (four clones in the screenshot) the card follows the whole batch. The `consult_advisor_followup` card shows the advisor's verdict. `CONTINUE` is only shown in the chat and nothing reaches the worker. `ADJUST` comes with a revised plan that is appended to the worker's context, so its next step is taken with the advice in view. 7. `/advisor off`, `/new` or `/clear` leave the mode and drop the advisor's plan. With the **Advisor Mode** switch in the template off, `/advisor on` replies with where to enable it and the menu entry disappears. ## Evidence PawBench performance with and without the advisor. Advisor: Qwen 3.8 Max with thinking on. Run on an earlier build of this branch (v2.1.0b2). | Worker | Baseline | Advisor Mode | Δ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | QwenPaw 9B | 65.1 | 68.0 | +2.9 | | Qwen 3.8 27B (medium thinking) | 71.1 | 77.6 | +6.5 | ```bash pre-commit run --all-files # all hooks passed pytest tests/unit -n 6 # 10580 passed, 18 skipped cd console && npm run format && npm run test:run # Test Files 331 passed · Tests 3118 passed # format: no changes ```

prs.title: feat(deploy): add offline image variant with Office/PDF toolchain
prs.body:
## Description

Adds `deploy/Dockerfile.offline`, a variant of `deploy/Dockerfile` that bakes the
Office/PDF toolchain into the image, plus a short section in `scripts/README.md`
explaining how to build it.

The default image intentionally stays lean: the `docx`, `pptx`, `xlsx`, and `pdf`
skills resolve their prerequisites at task time (`apt-get`/`npm`/`pip`), which
fails in air-gapped or offline deployments and is slow for document-heavy
workloads. This variant preinstalls:

- **System:** `libreoffice-{writer,calc,impress,draw}`, `pandoc`, `poppler-utils`,
  `qpdf`, `tesseract-ocr` (+ `eng`, `chi-sim`, `chi-tra` traineddata)
- **npm (global):** `docx`, `pptxgenjs`, `pdf-lib`, `pdfjs-dist`, `react-icons`,
  `react`, `react-dom`, `sharp`, with `NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules`
- **Python (venv):** `pypdf`, `pdfplumber`, `reportlab`, `openpyxl`, `xlrd`,
  `pandas`, `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `markitdown[docx,pptx,xlsx,xls,pdf]`,
  `pdf2image`, `pytesseract`, `lxml`, `defusedxml`

The Python libraries are installed **before** the app so that the app's own pins
win in the final resolve (`markitdown`'s `magika` pulls `onnxruntime`, and the app
pins `onnxruntime<1.24`). The `uv` binary is therefore copied earlier in the
offline file than in the default one.

`scripts/docker_build.sh` already honours the `DOCKERFILE` env var, so no script
change was needed:

```bash
DOCKERFILE=deploy/Dockerfile.offline bash scripts/docker_build.sh qwenpaw:offline
```

Trade-off: the image grows by roughly 2 GB and duplicates the shared parts of
`deploy/Dockerfile`. The alternative — an opt-in build arg in the default
`Dockerfile` — was avoided so the default image and its build cache are
unaffected. If the duplication becomes a maintenance burden, collapsing to a
build arg is the natural follow-up.

**Related Issue:** N/A

**Security Considerations:** None. No new ports, credentials, or network
services; the added `tesseract`/`pandoc`/`libreoffice` packages are invoked
headless by the existing skills.

prs.title: fix(app): fire workspace_created hooks on agent reload (#8281)
prs.body:
## Description

In `MultiAgentManager.reload_agent()`, zero-downtime agent reloads construct a new `Workspace` instance and atomically replace the old instance, but previously never invoked `_fire_workspace_created_hooks()`.

As reported in #8281, runtime hooks registered via `register_runtime_hook()` in plugins rely on the `workspace_created` hook event (`rt_hook_ws_<plugin>_<name>`) to attach hooks to newly created workspaces. Because `_fire_workspace_created_hooks()` was only called during the initial `get_agent()` creation path, every runtime hook was silently lost on the first agent reload following plugin installation.

This PR adds `await self._fire_workspace_created_hooks({"agent_id": agent_id, "workspace_dir": str(agent_ref.workspace_dir)})` to `reload_agent()` immediately after the replacement workspace is swapped and the old instance is stopped.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8281

**Security Considerations:** None. Hooks are invoked through the existing `_fire_workspace_created_hooks()` classmethod with the same payload and error isolation as the initial creation path.

prs.title: fix(console): correct thinking slider fill and stabilize saving
prs.body:
## Description

Fix two connected UX problems in the thinking-strength control:

1. **Misleading fill:** the full rail is colored even at Low, because the rail has
   the gradient while the selected track is transparent.
2. **Flicker / rollback while saving:** every preference write dims and disables
   the whole panel. The panel also receives the last confirmed value rather than
   the existing preview, so its label can briefly revert to the previous strength.

### Complete fix

- Use the existing neutral `--app-fill-strong` rail and `--app-accent` selected
  track; keep Ant Design's own value-dependent track width.
- Remove the full-width budget gradient override and its unused custom property.
  Hide selected fill and thumb when the effective default is unresolved.
- Feed the same latest preview to the panel and trigger indicator. Ordinary
  strength saves no longer dim or disable the whole panel.
- Serialize writes so an older request cannot finish after and overwrite a newer
  selection. Older confirmations do not clear a newer preview, including a drag
  still in progress. A failed latest save restores the last confirmed value.
- Scope queued writes and responses to their originating chat. Reads wait for
  outstanding writes; switching chats invalidates queued work and old responses.
- Preserve the existing advanced decision-setting API and its edit lock. Cover
  both saved chats and new chats; decision updates retain the thinking state.

The complete PR changes **four existing frontend files**, including regression
tests. It adds no dependencies, business integration code, backend changes, public
API changes, or model/inference functionality.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8286

permissions, credential handling, or backend endpoints. Review fixtures contain

prs.title: fix(mcp): treat HTTP 422 on server/discover as legacy-protocol evidence
prs.body:
## Description

A handshake-era MCP server that mandates `initialize` as the first message
answers the unknown `server/discover` probe with **HTTP 422** and a
plain-text body (e.g. `Unexpected message, expect initialize request`). That
body is not a JSON-RPC envelope, so `_unwrap_jsonrpc_result` raises
`httpx.HTTPStatusError`, and `_is_legacy_protocol_evidence` only classified
`400/404/405` as fallback evidence — so the 422 propagated and the Driver
build failed:

```
Failed to build Driver 'dbx': MCP server/discover rejected with HTTP 422
503: MCP client 'dbx' is saved but not active yet (status=inactive)
```

The peer itself works fine over the legacy handshake (it answers a classic
`initialize` with 200 and `tools/list` with 25 tools); only the negotiation
gap prevented the fallback from triggering.

This adds `422` to the legacy-evidence status set, so `HttpAutoClient` falls
back to the legacy handshake as it already does for 400/404/405. Auth codes
(401/403) are classified separately, so this cannot mask a real
authorization problem.

**Related Issue:** Refs #8047

**Security Considerations:** None — it only widens the *protocol
negotiation* fallback on the `server/discover` probe; no auth path changes.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` locally and it passes
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest`) and they pass
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

- A DBX-style 422 (plain-text body) on `server/discover` now triggers the
  legacy fallback and the client connects as `is_stateful`.
- 422 is covered both bare and with the `Unexpected message, expect
  initialize request` body in `test_auto_falls_back_once`.
- Existing behaviour is preserved: 403 still stays a hard failure (not
  masked as fallback), and 400/404/405/401 cases are unchanged.

Regression proof: reverting the one-line source change makes the new tests
fail (`3 failed`), i.e. they genuinely pin this behaviour.

## Evidence

```bash
$ pytest tests/unit/drivers/handlers/test_mcp_dual_protocol.py -q
67 passed

# with the source change reverted:
$ pytest ...::test_auto_falls_back_on_plain_422 ...::test_auto_falls_back_once -q
```

prs.title: fix(chat): resolve deep links across agents
prs.body:
Previously, directly accessing `/chat/<id>` relied on the current Agent and the sidebar list, often resulting in a redirect to a blank session or a failure to load history. This fix ensures deep links correctly identify the associated Agent and open the target session.
- Added an API to resolve session ownership, prioritizing the actual Chat ID; runtime aliases are resolved based on uniqueness within the current Agent.
- Automatically switches to the correct Agent, retains the target session, activates SDK history, and supports archived sessions.
- Displays clear error messages and retry options for non-existent or ambiguous references, preventing load failures from being misinterpreted as empty sessions.

prs.title: fix(channels): hide injected context blocks at the display boundary
prs.body:
## Description

**Problem.** Two framework sources store control markers inside ordinary assistant text, and `MessageRenderer.message_to_parts()` forwards every `ContentType.TEXT` block unchanged, so channel users see them as the assistant's own words:

- `src/qwenpaw/tool_calls/_hint.py::make_offload_hint_msg()` builds `Msg(role="assistant", content=[TextBlock("<system-notification>…"), *result_blocks])` with no metadata marker. Its docstring says this flattening is deliberate, “so that provider formatters treat it as an ordinary assistant message”.
- Scroll context-compression / continuation notes carry `<system-info>…</system-info>` blocks.

The existing display flags cannot suppress either one: `show_thinking` / `show_tool_calls` / `show_tool_results` only gate structured block types.

**Fix.** Add `strip_injected_context()` next to `strip_headline()` and call it from the same `TEXT` branch. It follows the contract that `strip_headline()` already documents: display-only — the live context and the persisted row keep the original bytes.

Risk is kept minimal by four guards:

1. **Start only** — a block is removed only when it opens the text; mid-text mentions are untouched.
2. **Balanced only** — opening and closing tags must both be present; a dangling `<system-info>` is left alone.
3. **Quoted is safe** — a leading backtick means the marker is being quoted (`` `<system-info>` is … ``), so the text is returned unchanged.
4. **Fail-open** — if nothing can be removed, or stripping would empty the message, the original text is returned.

A trailing reasoning fragment is **not** addressed here; that is a separate boundary problem.

Fixes #8293.

## Evidence

- `pytest tests/unit/agents/context/test_serialize.py tests/unit/app/channels/test_renderer.py -q` → **96 passed** (6 new sanitizer tests + 1 renderer test).
- `pre-commit run --files <the four changed files>` → **all hooks Passed** (black, flake8, pylint, mypy, add-trailing-comma, check-docstring-first, trailing whitespace).
- Before/after on a real installation: a text block that starts with `<system-notification>…</system-notification>\nDone.` renders as `['Done.']`; a normal reply and the quoted-mention case render unchanged.
- Not covered by #7835: that PR guards a message carrying `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_BLOCK_HIDDEN_KEY`. The offload hint and the context note carry no metadata, so a message-level guard cannot see them — this is a text-level guard for a different source.

prs.title: fix(console): repair CJK emphasis boundaries in chat Markdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The chat message body renders Markdown through the vendor `Markdown` component, whose parser follows CommonMark's emphasis "flanking" rules. Those rules classify CJK sentence punctuation as Unicode punctuation, and CJK text is written without inter-word spaces. A closing `**` that sits immediately after CJK punctuation and immediately before CJK text is therefore judged "not a valid closer", and the raw markers leak into the bubble:

```
**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容保持不变。
```

The reader literally sees `**没有改动任何设置。**` instead of bold text. This is a common pattern in Chinese/Japanese/Korean replies, so it shows up frequently.

## Fix

Add `normalizeCjkEmphasis` in `console/src/utils/markdownCjk.ts`, which moves the trailing CJK punctuation run outside the delimiter (`**中文。**后` becomes `**中文**。后`), and apply it in `DeferredMarkdown` before the content reaches `<Markdown>`.

The repair is deliberately conservative and display-oriented:

- only `*`, `_`, `**`, `__`, `***`, `___` are considered;
- only `。！？；：，、…` plus full-width trailing closers (`”’」』】》〉）〕］`) are moved;
- only when the delimiter is immediately followed by Han / Hiragana / Katakana / Hangul;
- fenced, indented and inline code, escaped delimiters, CRLF endings and unrelated unfinished Markdown are preserved verbatim.

The helper is a pure, idempotent string transform, so applying it to a streaming (partial) value is safe — the result converges to the same text once the message completes.

## Evidence

- `node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/utils/markdownCjk.test.ts src/pages/Chat/HostBubbles.test.ts src/pages/Chat/HostBubbles.render.test.tsx` -> **30 passed** (15 new in `markdownCjk.test.ts`).
- `tsc -b --noEmit` -> clean.
- `prettier --check` on the three changed files -> clean; `eslint` -> clean.
- Direct checks:
  - `normalizeCjkEmphasis("**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容保持不变。")` -> `"**没有改动任何设置**。所有内容保持不变。"`
  - `normalizeCjkEmphasis("**重点**后接中文")` -> unchanged
  - fenced code block containing `**代码。**后` -> unchanged
  - `**内容。**latin` -> unchanged (follower must be CJK)

## Notes

- Targeted, display-oriented repair rather than a general Markdown parser; ASCII punctuation and non-CJK followers are out of scope by design.
- Related: CommonMark discussion `commonmark/commonmark-spec#650` on CJK-friendly emphasis.


---

> **Note:** this supersedes #8068, which the PR Spam Gate auto-closed on 2026-10-01 (author had >10 open PRs at the time). Same branch, same diff; GitHub refused to reopen the original, so this is a fresh PR.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): never write a sandbox ACE on a volume root
prs.body:
## Description

On Windows, sandbox ACLs are **inheritable** and are written on the
workspace, on every mount (including the session project directory, which
is mounted writable) and on every deny path. A volume root has no parent,
so writing one there re-propagates it to every existing child of the
volume. When the root DACL is missing (a NULL DACL) it gets replaced with
a sandbox-only DACL, and SYSTEM / Administrators / the user vanish from
the subtree — the drive becomes inaccessible even to an elevated
Administrator, and the sandbox-only ACE has to be removed by hand.

This closes every path that could create that state:

1. **A volume root is never a sandbox grant root** — `SandboxConfig`
   collects them (`volume_root_paths`) across `workspace_dir`, any mount
   (read-only mounts get an inheritable ACE too) and any `deny_paths`
   entry, and warns. `create_sandbox` then downgrades such a config to
   `SandboxMode.NONE` and logs a warning, so **the command still runs**
   while the volume stays usable. One check covers the AppContainer,
   elevated and unelevated backends.
2. **Never fill a NULL DACL** — `_set_path_ace` and `_add_traverse_ace`
   refuse instead of letting `SetEntriesInAclW` produce a DACL that holds
   only the sandbox SID.
3. **Never rewrite a volume root's DACL** — both DACL-reset fallbacks
   (`icacls /reset` in the elevated backend and
   `_reset_dacl_to_inherited` in the unelevated one) skip volume roots.
4. **A second guard in `_set_path_ace`** — it is the single point where
   sandbox ACEs are written (the AppContainer and elevated backends both
   delegate to it), so no caller can reintroduce the write.

The console warns before the user picks such a directory
(`ProjectSelectModal`), so the loss of the sandbox is not silent.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7943

**Security Considerations:** This tightens, rather than loosens, the
sandbox — no auth or config surface is added. Two judgement calls worth
flagging:

- **Fail-open on the volume root.** The sandbox is *skipped* rather than
  the session failing, because the reporter's expected behaviour is
  "command runs in the host / volume stays usable". That means a
  volume-root workspace runs **unsandboxed**; the backend logs a warning
  and the console asks the user first. If you would rather refuse
  outright (fail-closed), it is a two-line change — happy to switch.
- **The volume-root check is platform-independent**, so a POSIX
  `workspace_dir` of `/` also falls back. The ACL hazard is Windows-only,
  but "a volume root is not a usable workspace" holds everywhere. Happy
  to scope it to Windows if you prefer.

prs.title: fix(chat): truncate oversized tool outputs when serving chat history
prs.body:
## Description

Chat history responses can exceed 10 MB because file and screenshot tool outputs are persisted as **base64 inside `tool_result`** blocks. Serving them verbatim makes the console's fixed 30 s request timeout fail reliably on slow links: on a 5 Mbps link a single 13.3 MB response (`send_file_to_user` + `view_image` in a 6-message chat, 96 % of the payload base64) already takes ≥21 s in the ideal case and exceeds 30 s under loss — the fetch is aborted (`retries = 0`), the transcript never renders and no error toast is shown. See the issue for the full reproduction (rate-limited proxy shows the abort at exactly 30.3 s).

This PR caps oversized `tool_result` outputs **when serving chat history** (not at storage time and not for other consumers): each output is truncated to 64 KB with an explicit marker, so a 13.3 MB response drops to ~3.4 MB; combined with the upstream response-compression middleware (#7917, already in main) it becomes ~2 MB and transfers in ~3.3 s at 5 Mbps — comfortably inside the 30 s timeout.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8228

**Security Considerations:** None — no credentials or private data involved; this only bounds the size of what is served to the console.

prs.title: feat(harnesses): add USAGE event channel for backend token usage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Third-party (harness) backends have **no way to report token/context usage**, even though the capability flag for it already exists:

- `HarnessCapabilities.context_usage` is declared, but there is no event kind and no channel behind it — an adapter has literally nowhere to put usage numbers;
- so harness turns never produce the per-session usage snapshot that native turns produce, and the Console shows no token/context information for third-party agent runs (ACP-based agents do report usage, so the data exists upstream but is dropped).

This PR adds the missing channel. It is **additive and backward compatible**: adapters that cannot report usage simply do not emit the event, and no existing adapter behaviour changes (codex/qoder have no token data today).

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8324

**Security Considerations:** none — no new endpoint, no new data exposure; the usage numbers are staged into the existing per-session snapshot that the current turn-usage commit path already persists and emits.

## Description

1. `harnesses/events.py`
   - `HarnessEventKind.USAGE = "usage"`.
   - `HarnessUsage(input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, cached_tokens=None, context_tokens=None, context_limit=None)` — counters default to 0 so an adapter fills only what its provider exposes; optional fields stay `None` when unknown.
   - `HarnessEvent.usage: HarnessUsage | None = None` (explicit field rather than a `data["usage"]` convention: pydantic validation, discoverability, and `data` stays tool-argument semantics).
2. `harnesses/runtime.py`
   - `USAGE` events are consumed as **side-channel metadata**: they never emit text/tool envelopes and never abort the turn; staging failures are logged and swallowed.
   - `_usage_snapshot()` translates provider usage into the channel turn-usage shape (prompt/completion/total/cache/context), `_stage_usage()` feeds it to the shared per-turn path.
3. `token_usage/model_wrapper.py`
   - New public entry point `TokenRecordingModelWrapper.record_usage_for_session()` (harness turns do not run through the wrapped chat model, so they cannot use `_record_usage`), with the existing accumulation logic extracted into `_merge_usage()` — behaviour of the native path is unchanged.

Because the channel turn-usage commit path already reads this snapshot (`channels/base.py::_commit_turn_usage` → `turn_usage.resolve_turn_usage` → `pop_usage_for_session`), staged usage flows into the existing `turn_usage` SSE and `TURN_USAGE_META_KEY` persistence **without touching any channel**. `harnesses/`-external surface: one file.

prs.title: fix(harnesses): return readable 409 instead of 500 when login/logout is unavailable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Clicking **Connect** on a third-party provider whose runtime cannot log in — or whose optional dependency is not installed — returned **HTTP 500 with a server stack trace**:

- `POST /harnesses/{id}/login` calls `adapter.start_login(...)` unguarded. `QoderAdapter.start_login()` raises `HarnessOperationNotSupportedError`; `MissingDependencyAdapter.start_login()` raises `RuntimeError("Install qwenpaw[codex] to enable Codex.")`.
- `POST /harnesses/{id}/logout` already mapped `HarnessOperationNotSupportedError` to 409 but let the missing-dependency `RuntimeError` escape as 500.

Because `console/src/api/request.ts` only shows a **string** `detail` to the user, a 500 body gives the Console nothing actionable — the user just sees a failed request with no hint that they need to install `qwenpaw[codex]`.

After this PR both operations answer with **409 + a readable string message** (no traceback, no server paths), so the Console can display the provider's own explanation.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8323

**Security Considerations:** none — error details are reduced, not expanded (no traceback/stack exposure); no auth or credential path is touched.

## Description

- `login`: `HarnessOperationNotSupportedError` and `RuntimeError` → 409 with a readable string `detail`.
- `logout`: keeps the existing structured 409 shape (`{code: "logout_not_supported", message}`) and additionally maps `RuntimeError` → `{code: "logout_unavailable", message}`.
- Added `_operation_message()` so both handlers return a client-safe string with a fallback when the exception message is empty.
- Unknown provider still returns 404; no other route or status code changed. No new error class introduced.

409 (rather than 503) keeps consistency with the existing semantics of `coming_soon` and `logout_not_supported`, which the Console already handles.

prs.title: feat(console): drive third-party provider grid from /harnesses
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Console hardcodes the third-party backend list:

- `console/src/pages/Settings/Agents/components/AgentBackendFields.tsx` declares `type ProviderId = "codex" | "qoder"` plus a static `PROVIDERS` array;
- `providerOption()` returns `PROVIDERS.find(...) ?? PROVIDERS[0]`, so **any backend the runtime knows but the Console does not silently shows the Codex card and Codex copy**;
- the "Claude Code — coming soon" card is hardcoded in the grid.

The runtime already returns the full catalog from `GET /harnesses` (`id`, `name`, `available`, `coming_soon`, `installed`, `authenticated`, runtime info, capabilities — `claude` is already `coming_soon: true`).

Concrete user impact: a third-party backend registered through the plugin seam (e.g. a custom ACP harness) can be created through the API, but it is invisible in **Settings → Agents**, and its detail panel shows Codex strings — confusing for users and a blocker for every future backend. After this PR the grid is catalog-driven, so new backends appear automatically and `coming_soon` entries come from the server.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8321

**Security Considerations:** none — the change only reads an existing authenticated endpoint and renders it; no new endpoint, no new data exposure, no credential handling.

## Description

- Provider list is fetched when the backend panel opens (`harnessApi.list()`); the grid renders whatever the runtime reports, in catalog order.
- `codex` / `qoder` keep their dedicated name and copy; any other backend uses generic copy (`agent.backend.thirdParty*`) with the API-provided name (falling back to the id). The `?? PROVIDERS[0]` fallback is gone.
- `coming_soon: true` entries render as disabled cards, replacing the hardcoded Claude Code placeholder.
- Graceful degradation: the grid is seeded with `codex` + `qoder`; on request failure they stay and an inline `role="alert"` message is shown. A selected backend missing from the catalog still renders with correct (generic) copy.
- The "third-party" card selects the first non-`coming_soon` catalog entry instead of assuming `codex` exists.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #1453; fixes the CLI initialization failure shown in its attached transcript.

prs.title: fix(channels): retain consumers until shutdown cleanup finishes
prs.body:
## Description

A channel reload can discard a cancelled consumer while it is still awaiting asynchronous cleanup. `UnifiedQueueManager.stop_all()` waits five seconds and then clears `_queues`; after the replaced manager loses its owner, the task/future cycle can be collected and asyncio emits `Task was destroyed but it is pending!`.

Keep shutdown consumers in a module-level set before cancelling them, then release them and retrieve any exception when they actually finish. The existing five-second shutdown deadline and queue cleanup behavior are preserved. A manager-local collection would not suffice because it would be part of the same collectable cycle.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #3361

**Security Considerations:** No credentials, channel transport, permissions or message content handling changes. The fix keeps cancelled cleanup tasks alive until they complete.

prs.title: fix(observability): trace cancel reason and initiator in stop cascade
prs.body:
## 总结

Fixes #8252

跨 agent 会话被取消时，日志里只有一条裸的 `CancelledError`，**不记录取消原因和发起方**，运维无法区分"框架超时回收"和"用户主动停止"，也无法在级联取消中找到真正点火的那一跳。

（#8252 中"误报 interrupted by the user"的问题已由 #8183 修复，本 PR 补齐剩余的取消溯源缺口。）

## 改动

1. **`cancel_cleanup` 日志带上取消原因**（`hooks/error/error_hook.py`）

   ```
   改前: cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=…): CancelledError
   改后: cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=… reason=timeout): CancelledError
   ```

   原因无法确定时记 `reason=unknown`，绝不默认归因给用户。

2. **stop 级联逐跳传递发起方**（`agents/tools/agent_management.py`）：`chat_with_agent` / `spawn_subagent` 被取消后向目标会话发 stop 时，附带 `initiator=<调用方会话id>`。

3. **stop 端点落一条 INFO 审计日志**（`app/routers/console.py`）：

   ```
   [STOP API] chat stop: chat_id=… reason=timeout initiator=<上游会话> stopped=True tools_cancelled=1
   ```

   对 `chat_id` / `initiator` 做 CR/LF 消毒，防止伪造日志行。

4. **统一原因解析**（`tool_calls/_context.py`）：新增 `cancellation_reason()` 共享 helper，按 `CancelReason` 枚举校验 `Task.cancel(reason)` 附带的原因；`Runtime._cancellation_reason` 改为委托它（行为不变，消除重复白名单）。

5. **文档**：`chat_with_agent` docstring 明示级联停止语义（回应 issue 期望 #3），长任务指向 `submit_to_agent`。

## 收益

- **取消可溯源**（issue 期望 #1/#4）：grep 被取消会话 → 看到谁停的（initiator）、为什么（reason）→ 沿 initiator 逐跳上溯到真正超时的那一跳；`initiator=-` 即真人操作。无需再人工比对时间窗。
- **消除误归因**：级联受害者不再与超时源头混淆——reason 沿级联原样传播（叶子会话 269s 被停也记 timeout），只有 initiator 能区分；`reason=user` 的三种来源（真人停 / 级联继承 / 兜底默认）在日志上不再同形。
- **并发场景可判**：issue 的签名是"同一秒成批取消"（一秒内 4 条），时间戳邻近配对不可靠，initiator 把每条因果边显式写进日志。
- **完全向后兼容**：`initiator` 全链路可选（不传则请求与旧版逐字节一致）；纯日志 + 1 个 query 参数，无 schema、无取消路径行为变更。

## 测试

- 新增 16 个用例：reason 落日志（全枚举 / unknown / KeyboardInterrupt / 非取消错误不触发）、审计行内容与 CR/LF 消毒、无 initiator 兼容、级联转发 reason+initiator。
- 定点回归：runtime / hooks / tool_calls / routers / agent_management 相关单测全绿。
- 无 LLM 确定性复现（真实 Coordinator + 真实 chat_with_agent + mock HTTP）：修复前复现"同秒成对 cancel_cleanup 且无 reason"，修复后 reason + 逐跳 initiator 齐全。

prs.title: fix(agents): sanitize malformed file content parts lacking file_id or file_data (#8280)
prs.body:
## Description

When a conversation history contains a file reference whose backing data is missing (e.g. from an unavailable file or an incomplete message block), OpenAI-compatible providers reject the request with HTTP 400:

```text
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'file must have a file_id or file_data'}}
```

This blocks the entire session from continuing until the corrupted reference is evicted from context.

This PR adds a post-formatting sanitization step in `FileBlockSupportFormatter.format()` via `_sanitize_malformed_file_parts()` in `src/qwenpaw/agents/model_factory.py`. Any `{"type": "file"}` content part lacking both `file_id` and `file_data` (either top-level or inside a nested `file` dict) is safely replaced with a descriptive text placeholder (e.g. `[File 'report.pdf' unavailable — data lost from conversation history]`) prior to wire transmission, while logging a warning. Valid file parts with `file_id` or `file_data` remain intact.

prs.title: fix(task_tracker): bound the run completion callback and always clean up
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes the **run-cleanup half** of #8173: a chat run whose completion callback hangs or is cancelled never releases its entry in `TaskTracker._runs`, so the run stays `running` forever.

### Root cause

`TaskTracker._producer` clears its `_runs` entry and pushes the end-of-stream sentinel at the end of a `finally` block, *after* awaiting the `on_finished` completion callback. Two paths meant that cleanup never completed:

1. **The callback hangs.** `on_finished` is `ChatManager.mark_chat_finished`, which persists a completion marker under a lock shared with ~24 other manager methods. Lock contention or a stalled repo suspends the producer task *inside its own `finally`*. The task is then not done **and** the entry is still registered, so every status reader reports `running` — workspace reload is blocked and inbound messages are dropped with HTTP 409.
2. **The producer is cancelled mid-callback.** `CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so it escapes the `except Exception` guard and skips cleanup entirely, leaving subscriber streams without their sentinel.

### The fix

- Run the callback through `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(...))` bounded by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT`, so a hung callback is logged and given up on rather than holding the run open.
- Move the cleanup into a nested `finally` so it always runs.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8173

Deliberately *not* `Fixes` — see the scope note below.

### Scope — what this does **not** fix

This addresses the cleanup leak only. The other items from #8173 are **not** implemented here: the post-spawn connection health probe, the idle watchdog, `force` semantics on the reload/disable-enable paths, and in-channel hints for `/new` and `/stop` on backends that do not support them. Those are larger design questions and I would rather land the narrow fix first.

Note that the wedge is now **bounded** by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT` rather than eliminated: the run stays `running` while the callback runs, because `test_attach_or_start_reports_completion_before_becoming_idle` pins that ordering deliberately (it asserts `get_status == "running"` from inside the callback). Reordering the pop ahead of the callback would break that contract.

### What the new tests cover

New `tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py` (6 tests) covers a hung callback, a callback that raises, a callback that raises `TimeoutError`, a producer cancelled mid-callback, and `request_stop` against a slow callback. Waits are event-based rather than fixed sleeps.

Against unmodified source these fail on behavioural assertions (`run entry survived a hung completion callback`, etc.), not on import or attribute errors.

### Security Considerations

Not applicable — no change to channel auth, credentials, or config handling.

## Evidence

Verification is a real failure on unmodified source followed by the **same command** against the patched tree. Base is `5c56644a` (`main`), patch is `e2b7b8be`.

**1. Unmodified baseline — the new tests genuinely fail.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
=========================== short test summary info ============================
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_hung_completion_callback_does_not_block_new_messages
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_completion_callback_timeout_is_logged_not_raised
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_cancellation_during_callback_still_clears_the_run
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_request_stop_with_a_slow_callback_does_not_wedge_the_run
4 failed, 1 passed in 8.32s
```

**2. Same command with the patch — all green.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
.......................                                                  [100%]
23 passed in 0.49s
```

**3. Full `tests/unit/app` with the patch — no regression.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app
3118 passed, 1 skipped, 12 warnings in 58.77s
```

One caveat worth stating plainly: the baseline run pins the module source with `PYTHONPATH` pointing at a pristine checkout. The venv's editable install points at the patched worktree, so simply `cd`-ing to the unmodified tree would still have imported the patched code and produced a false green — that happened on the first attempt and the baseline above is from the corrected invocation.

Lint: `black`, `flake8` and `mypy` are clean. `pylint`, run with the full argument list from `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, scores **10.00/10 with zero findings on both the unmodified and the patched tree** — I have not pasted a terminal transcript for that one because I did not capture it to a file, and I would rather say so than manufacture the output.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks (no auto-fixes were needed)
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed) — `docs/pitfalls.md` records the `PYTHONPATH` trap that produces a false-green baseline
- [x] Ready for review

On the first box: I ran `black`, `flake8`, `mypy` and `pylint` individually against `.pre-commit-config.yaml`'s full argument list rather than the `pre-commit` wrapper. Flagging it rather than ticking it, since I did not invoke the wrapper itself.

## AI assistance

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude). The root-cause analysis was verified by running probes against both the unmodified and patched trees rather than taken from the issue description — in particular, the issue's claim that `has_active_tasks()` stays true does **not** hold on the cancellation path (the producer task has already completed there, so every status reader reports idle). The path that does produce the reported symptoms is the hung callback.

issues.title: [Feature]: Keep non-durable consolidation updates out of Core with a durability label and a user quote
issues.body:
### Summary

An opt-in `memory.consolidation_evidence_gate`: the consolidation model labels each `memory_update` durable or transient and quotes the user's own words for it, and only durable updates backed by a matching quote are written to Core; everything else is kept in Daily.

### Problem statement

`consolidate_turn` writes every non-empty `memory_update` to Core (subject only to the policy gate and the opt-in `dedup_on_write`), and Core is permanent, undecayed at recall and has the highest base importance (details in #11657). The model is asked for "new facts, preferences, decisions, or commitments worth remembering long-term", but nothing checks that an update is durable or that the user said it.

mov-xound-glitch's numbers in #11657 show what that does on a real install: 244 auto-extracted Core rows (of 269 in Core) in seven weeks, a fair share of them task state such as "a test email is still pending because of a provider error".

To measure it, I ran a small local eval: 65 made-up turns (three of them long ones built around the 4000-byte input cut): 35 that state a durable fact, 28 that don't, and two scored separately. Each was run three times through `consolidate_turn`. With today's prompt, more than half of the non-durable turns were written to Core, for example:

- transient state: "I'm at the store right now", "my build is failing right now", "I'm really tired today", "on vacation this week";
- the assistant's guesses or suggestions, stored as facts about the user: "Since you like jazz, …", "You should learn Rust";
- one-off requests and refusals: "Don't use bullet points in this one, I'm pasting it into a letter", "Not interested in that recipe";
- sarcasm, questions and tentative plans: "Oh yeah, I just love Mondays", "Do you think I should switch to vim?", "I might move to Lisbon next year, not sure yet".

### Proposed solution

Behind a new `memory.consolidation_evidence_gate` (default off), only when the plain consolidation prompt is used:

1. The consolidation prompt also asks for `durability` ("durable" if the update will still be true and useful weeks from now; "transient" for current state, today's plans, one-off requests or a single refusal) and `evidence`, the exact clause of the user's message that states the update. It tells the model not to store the assistant's claims, guesses or suggestions as facts about the user, and to write the update in the third person ("User …") in the language of the user's sentence.
2. The update goes to Core only if it is labelled durable and a quote passes three checks: it appears word for word in the part of the user's message the model was sent, ignoring case, punctuation and lines quoted with `>`; it has at least 2 words and 8 letters unless it is the whole message; and it shares a content word with the update, so a real quote is harder to attach to an unrelated update.
3. Anything else is stored in Daily, so it is kept for the history but not treated as a lasting fact.
4. The labels are read separately from `ConsolidationResult` and leniently, so an odd value never breaks parsing, and with the switch off the prompt, parsing and writes are unchanged.
5. Config load rejects the switch together with `memory.types.enabled` or `memory.consolidation_extract_facts`, because the typed prompt has no durability or evidence fields; per-fact labels for typed facts would be a follow-up.

The idea of a per-item `durability` field is mov-xound-glitch's, from #11657.

Results from the local eval (three runs per case; today's prompt is unchanged master from an earlier run of the same cases; one gated run was dropped after a provider timeout):

| | Today's prompt | With the gate |
|---|---|---|
| Durable-fact turns with a Core write | 105 of 105 (100%) | 103 of 105 (98%) |
| Non-durable turns written to Core | 47 of 84 (56%) | 2 of 83 (2%) |
| Replies that failed to parse | 1 | 0 |

Notes on the results:

- Only whether a Core write happened is scored, not whether it states the fact correctly.
- All of the improvement comes from the new prompt: the model labelled non-durable turns transient or returned no update, and the quote check did not hold back any non-durable turn.
- The quote check held back 3 replies the model had labelled durable, and all 3 were real facts: "Call me Sam" twice (the name case added after the comparison run, not in the table; a 3-letter name is never a shared content word) and a German turn once (the model wrote that update in English). In these cases it caught nothing that should have been kept out, so its value as a backstop is not measured here.
- The two leaks were sarcasm ("Oh yeah, I just love Mondays") and a durable-labelled "User has a sister who occasionally stays with them; currently her sister is visiting until Sunday, …" from "My sister is staying with us until Sunday, so plan dinners for three." The two missed facts were "Any tips for my sourdough?" and the German turn above.
- The gated prompt was revised twice after earlier runs on these same cases, so these are in-sample numbers from one model; a held-out set and other models are not tested.
- The cases are made up; the model was Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (IQ4_NL GGUF) through llama.cpp's OpenAI-compatible server at temperature 0.7.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Not a security boundary. Consolidation can't tell the user's own words from text a channel adds to the message: link previews (`[Link: …]`), Slack thread context (including the bot's own replies), Matrix thread roots and forwarded text all reach the quote check as if the user wrote them. A trustworthy version needs channels to pass the user's own text separately from the context they add. A turn-origin signal like the one in PR #10007 would only cover turns no person authored.
- Not per-fact gating for `consolidation_extract_facts` or typed memory.
- No change to the default behaviour.

### Alternatives considered

- A per-install target category (#11657). Simpler, but it moves durable facts out of Core along with the noise; the two can coexist, with the gate deciding per update and the category deciding where non-durable updates go.
- Schema-validated consolidation (#6998). Complementary: it makes the reply's shape reliable, and the durability and evidence fields would fit its schema.
- The existing `memory.dedup_on_write` (off by default). It catches near-identical text but not task state or assistant claims.

### Acceptance criteria

- The switch is off by default and, when off, consolidation behaves exactly as today.
- With the switch on, a non-empty `memory_update` reaches Core only when labelled durable and backed by a matching quote; otherwise it is stored in Daily.
- The switch is rejected at config load together with typed memory.
- Unit tests cover the quote rules and the routing.

### Architecture impact

`crates/zeroclaw-memory/src/consolidation.rs` (prompt, label parsing, routing) and `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs` (the switch and its validation). One new config key; no trait or storage change.

### Risk and rollback

Off by default; turning it off restores today's behaviour. Known limits if it is turned on:

- One matching quote clears the whole update, so a detail the assistant added can ride along with a real fact. In the eval, a request to set up a nightly backup was stored with the assistant's "2am" in all three runs, and "Yes, let's do that plan" was stored as a commitment in all three runs, twice with the assistant's "3-day split", although the prompt says agreeing with the assistant is not stating.
- One shared content word is enough to tie a quote to an update.
- Content words need 4 or more letters, so a short name ("Sam") or word ("cat") can never be the shared word, and the update is held back.
- An update written in a different language from the user's sentence often shares no content word with it and is then held back, even when the model was asked to keep the language.
- Updates held back are stored in Daily as plain text, and Daily entries are recalled into later prompts.
- Facts the user states about other people (for example a friend's allergy) are stored like any other fact.
- The content-word check and the stopword list work best for English and other space-separated languages.

### Expected routing

Needs maintainer design assessment

### Next decision surface

This issue: whether per-update durability with a quote check is a shape maintainers want, and how it should sequence with #11657, #6998 and #10007, under the persistent-memory tracker #8891. Related: #10755 and the closed RFC #9048.

I have this working locally behind the switch, with unit tests, an eval harness and the eval cases, and can open a PR if maintainers want this shape.

### Breaking change?

No

### Data hygiene checks

- [x] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [x] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

issues.body:
### Tracker kind

Implementation batch tracker

### Purpose

Coordinate Goal Mode implementation across the accepted V1 and V2 decisions, while keeping the future V3 work visible without pre-approving it.

#8303 and #9702 are the accepted policy authorities for V1 and V2. #9703 remains a future RFC path for asynchronous child supervision. This tracker can record V3 prerequisites and blocking work, but it does not authorize V3 implementation until #9703 is accepted.

This issue is also the execution home that #10330 identified for accepted #9702. It keeps the Goal Mode version ladder in one place so the project can answer "where is Goal Mode overall?" without scattering V1, V2, and V3 across separate implementation trackers.

### Scope and non-goals

In scope:

- Track V1 implementation and cleanup follow-through from accepted #8303.
- Track V2 durable continuation, paired Web admission, reconnect, and status/control follow-through from accepted #9702.
- Keep V3 prerequisites visible while #9703 remains unaccepted, especially background or concurrent child supervision, budget reservation, and durable child recovery.
- Name the identity, authorization, session, reconnect, browser-enrollment, and usage-accounting contracts that Goal Mode consumes.
- Link implementation PRs and child issues to the accepted decision they implement.
- Preserve version boundaries so V1 cleanup, V2 Web/continuation, and V3 async work do not collapse into one review unit.

Out of scope:

- Opening or deciding new RFC votes.
- Treating #9703 as implementation-authorized before it is accepted.
- Browser-owned task state, browser-owned policy caches, browser-owned usage ledgers, or a parallel Goal Mode identity/session store.
- Replacing the canonical task, usage, security, principal, or session authority with Goal Mode-specific state.
- Broad additional channel rollout beyond the accepted V1 and V2 surfaces.
- Relitigating accepted #8303 or #9702 decisions unless implementation exposes a real contradiction.

### Current implementation map

| Area | Decision state | Public home | Implementation status / next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Goal Mode V1 | Accepted | #8303 | Track the bounded foreground Matrix and existing ZeroCode session-control implementation, cleanup, and docs needed to finish the V1 baseline. |
| Goal Mode V2 | Accepted | #9702 | Define the first implementation slice for durable restart/reload continuation, approval-driven resumption, paired principal-bound Web admission, authenticated reconnect, and Web-visible status/control responses. |
| Goal Mode V3 | Not accepted | #9703 | Keep blocked until prerequisite task/background-delegation and execution-tree budget contracts are stable, then decide the RFC before implementation authorization. |
| Retired implementation split | Closed | #8681 | Historical stack only. Do not use this as the active Goal Mode implementation tracker. |
| Canonical principal and grants | Accepted / rollout | #7141 and #8289 | V2 Web admission should consume these surfaces for authenticated principal identity and authorization. |
| Runtime security pipeline | Accepted / planned ADR | #7142 and #6971 | Goal commands should enter the runtime-owned security and admission path rather than grow a goal-only policy gate. |
| Runtime sessions and continuation | In review / tracker | #9487 and #9600 | V2 restart, disconnect, reconnect, and ownership-transfer behavior should align with the runtime-session contract before landing. |
| WebSocket-independent lifetime and reconnect | Follow-up surfaces | #7759 and #9641 | Related reconnect and detached-turn evidence for Web-visible control behavior. |
| Browser enrollment frontdoor | Open PR | #10142 | Related enrollment/trust work that may provide the authenticated principal used by paired Web goal admission. |
| Accepted-RFC routing gap | Tracker | #10330 | Records that accepted #9702 needed an execution home; this issue should let #10330 remove that row. |

### Linked work

- #8303 - accepted Goal Mode V1.
- #9702 - accepted Goal Mode V2 durable continuation and paired Web controls.
- #9703 - Goal Mode V3 asynchronous child-supervision RFC.
- #10330 - accepted-RFC routing-gap tracker.
- #8681 - retired Goal Mode implementation split tracker.
- #7141 and #8289 - canonical principal and inbound-authentication rollout.
- #7142 and #6971 - runtime-owned security pipeline and security-posture architecture.
- #9487 and #9600 - runtime-owned session and continuation boundaries.
- #7759 and #9641 - reconnect and detached-turn follow-up surfaces.
- #10142 - secure transport and enrollment work that intersects with paired Web admission.

### Routing evidence and next decision

Reason to stay open:

Goal Mode now has multiple public decision surfaces. V1 and V2 are accepted, while V3 is still unaccepted and prerequisite-bound. A single implementation roadmap keeps the accepted work executable without letting the future V3 scope sneak into implementation through the back door.

Next decision/revisit:

Define the first V2 implementation slice and reconcile the V1 baseline. The first V2 slice should name which pairing/enrollment surface produces the authenticated principal, which session owner-transfer contract it consumes, which security/admission checks gate Web goal commands, and what V1 cleanup must land first.

Visible owner, assignee, milestone, linked tracker, or review cadence:

Use this issue as the public Goal Mode implementation roadmap. Refresh it when V1 implementation status changes, the first V2 PR opens, prerequisite session/security/identity boundaries settle, or #9703 changes state.

### Close criteria

Close when:

- V1 follow-through from #8303 is complete or moved to narrower child issues.
- V2 paired Web admission consumes the canonical principal/authorization path instead of a goal-only identity system.
- V2 durable restart, reload, disconnect, and reconnect continuation consume the runtime session/continuation contract.
- Web goal commands pass through server-side admission before ordinary model turns.
- V2 status/control behavior is implemented or split into linked child issues.
- V3 either has an accepted implementation path or is explicitly tracked elsewhere after #9703 resolves.
- Any remaining work is owned by concrete PRs, child issues, or a narrower tracker.

### Stale-exemption requested?

Yes - tracker itself is the active coordination surface

issues.title: RFC: Focus PR review on purpose, safety, and quality

labels.name: type:rfc
labels.description: Architectural proposal — RFC discussion issue

issues.body:
# RFC: Focus PR review on purpose, safety, and quality

## Problem

The current review skill loads about 2,500 lines of instructions and required documents before reading the PR itself.
It also handles labels, milestones, template checks, and queue bookkeeping alongside the code review.
This proposal aims to reduce context cost and improve review quality while preserving security and keeping contribution practical.

## Review design

A small coordinator automatically assigns subagents with fresh contexts to issue fit and code quality, security and integrations, and downstream behavior and CI.
Each receives the linked issue, relevant code at recorded revisions, and only the guidance needed for its perspective.
The coordinator verifies proposed blockers, removes duplicate or unsupported findings, and produces one draft.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Issue, PR revisions, and affected code"] --> B["Small review coordinator"]
    B --> C["Issue fit and code quality"]
    B --> D["Security and integrations"]
    B --> E["Downstream behavior and CI"]
    C --> F["Verify and combine findings"]
    D --> F
    E --> F
    F --> G["Draft for human review"]
```

## Blocking decisions

Block PRs that lack a linked issue or add behavior outside its agreed scope, while allowing ordinary implementation choices within that scope.
Apply repository standards to block concrete defects, security gaps, contract violations, or missing evidence needed to establish the changed behavior.
Keep preferences and unrelated cleanup non-blocking, and report a failure already on `master` separately when the PR neither causes nor worsens it.

## Integration approval

Every new external dependency, repository, or service integration needs explicit maintainer approval, including dependencies added indirectly through a lockfile or build step.
An explicit approval in the linked issue counts when it comes from a verified maintainer and covers the exact integration, source, purpose, and access proposed.
A generic PR approval, a popular package, or a passing security check does not satisfy this requirement.

## Persistent integration holds

When approval is missing, draft a prominent blocking finding that names the integration and the decision needed from a maintainer.
Once posted as a changes-requested review, the skill must not clear or supersede that hold automatically, even if the author removes the integration.
A maintainer must dismiss the hold deliberately, and that decision does not approve a later additional or different integration.

## Draft format

Show the human reviewer a draft before publication and publish only within their explicit authorization.
Use three plain-language sentences per finding to explain the problem, its consequence, and the required action.
Put concise evidence and broad repair steps in a collapsible section, giving the author or their coding assistant enough direction without writing the patch for them.

## Responsibilities and safeguards

Labels, milestones, PR-template checks, and queue bookkeeping belong to the final merge workflow, which will eventually invoke `pr-template-review`.
Until that skill exists, existing merge and manual procedures must cover those checks; a positive substantive review does not establish merge readiness.
Use live GitHub records as the source of truth, treat PR content and subagent findings as untrusted input, and never execute contributor code during review.

## Alternatives, risks, and validation

Simply shortening the entrypoint or adding reviewers that reload everything would preserve the context problem, while delegation without limits could increase cost.
Compare old and new behavior on missing or mismatched issues, hidden integrations, prior approval, persistent holds, prompt injection, downstream regressions, and unrelated failures on `master`, checking both missed defects and false blockers.
Bound the assignments, reuse captured evidence, and measure all agents' work, reporting context reduction separately from any verified token-cost savings.

## Adoption and rollback

The new gates and shifted review responsibilities require a decision under the [repository's RFC process](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/master/docs/book/src/contributing/rfcs.md) before the implementation PR can merge.
Skill instructions alone cannot enforce GitHub permissions, so the final merge check must still honor unresolved integration holds and required CI checks.
Keep the implementation PR in draft until the decision is recorded, and roll back by reverting the skill and protocol changes while deliberately reconciling any reviews already posted.

issues.title: [Bug]: long channel turns remain silent and whole-turn timeout blames the model
issues.body:
### Affected component
channel

### Severity
S1 - workflow blocked

### Current behavior
Messaging channels without editable drafts can remain silent through many slow but successful model/tool rounds. An observed task exhausted the scaled channel deadline (1200 seconds from a 300-second base and 100 tool iterations). The user-facing message said it timed out "while waiting for the model", although this was the whole-turn LLM+tools deadline. Operators cannot distinguish ongoing work from a stalled or forgotten request.

### Expected behavior
Provide an optional bounded, periodic channel liveness notice independent of model-generated narration and tool-detail notifications. Keep it owned by the turn, stop on completion/cancellation, do not let slow outbound delivery delay completion, and pass notices through existing outbound hook/leak policy. Notices must not claim success, expose tool arguments/reasoning, or spend model calls. Whole-turn deadline wording should identify the task deadline and warn that actions may already have completed before an operator retries.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Use a messaging channel without draft edits, with tool-detail messages disabled.
2. Execute multiple read-only operations while the provider takes 30-120 seconds per round.
3. Observe silence until the final answer or the scaled whole-turn timeout.
4. Inspect the timeout event: it reports the entire channel budget, not just an individual provider call.

### Impact
Long cyberops/administration tasks look stalled and encourage duplicate submissions. A misleading retry instruction can cause operators to repeat partially completed work.

### Logs / stack traces
```text
channel_message_timeout: LLM response timed out after 1200s (base=300s, max_tool_iterations=100)
```

### ZeroClaw version
0.8.6; orchestration inspected at master e8d2e5fc8.

### Rust version
rustc 1.98.0

### Operating system
Linux x86_64

### Regression?
Unknown

### Pre-flight checks
- [x] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

Related #11416 (Slack status capability) and #10168 (stall watchdog); this report is about channel-visible liveness and whole-turn timeout wording, not changing retry/cancellation thresholds. Related #11866 for preserving useful closeout after a loop guard.

prs.title: feat(gateway): move plugin webhook admission and dedup into a core ingress
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. **Depends on #11318** (plugin webhook golden frames and CI leg) and **Depends on #11339** (the reservation store move). The branch merges #11339 at `59875788c1`; both show in the diff until they land.
- **Restacked onto #11339 (maintainer decision on this PR):** #11339 lands first and moves the reservation store into `zeroclaw-api` with no behavior change. This PR now uses that store, `WebhookReservationStore`, instead of a store of its own, and keeps the ingress (route lookup, queue admission, the deadline) in `zeroclaw-infra`. On top of #11339 it makes the dedup behavior change described under **Behavior change** below.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Channel-plugin webhook dispatch was split between the gateway handler (route lookup, queue admission, the 10 s deadline) and the gateway's idempotency store (message dedup), both reached through in-process handles. A gateway in another process could reach neither. This moves all four into one core-owned service with a single entry point, so the next PR can expose it over RPC unchanged.
  - `zeroclaw-infra`: new `plugin_webhook` module. `PluginWebhookIngress` owns the route registry, per-route queue admission, the deadline counted from enqueue, and message dedup in #11339's `WebhookReservationStore`, with the same owner, in-flight, rollback and generation-fencing semantics as before. `dispatch(request, cancel)` returns a typed outcome; dropping or cancelling it cancels the worker's copy of the request.
  - `zeroclaw-api`: shared limits and path grammar, the route owner (`PluginWebhookOwner`), a validating `PluginWebhookRequest` (redacting `Debug`; header names limited to what `http`'s `HeaderName` accepts, values to what `HeaderValue::to_str` yields), and `PluginWebhookOutcome`. Routes now carry their owner.
  - `zeroclaw-gateway`: the `/plugin/{path}` handler is an HTTP adapter over `dispatch` with a pure outcome-to-response mapping. The idempotency store keeps only the `/webhook` and `/sop/*` replay path.
  - The gateway's `/webhook` and `/sop/*` replay store keeps #11339's `WebhookReservationStore` backing, with a store of its own for each gateway run.
- **Behavior change (dedup, on top of #11339):**
  - **Lifetime:** plugin webhook dedup lasts for the daemon generation instead of one gateway run. A gateway restart inside the generation keeps it; a reload or daemon restart still clears it.
  - **Budget:** plugin deliveries get a committed-key budget of their own (`gateway.idempotency_max_keys`), no longer shared with `/webhook` and `/sop/*`. A burst of generic keys can no longer push out plugin keys, or the reverse. The worst case is twice that many committed keys across the two stores.
  - **Key:** dedup keys include the owning plugin and channel alias, so two instances never collide and a path that changes owner starts clean. #11339's pinned unscoped key no longer applies.
  - Tests that pinned the old behavior in #11339 (per-run lifetime, shared budget, unscoped key) are replaced by `plugin_webhook_dedup_state_outlives_a_gateway_router`, `plugin_and_generic_webhook_keys_have_separate_budgets` and `dedup_key_separates_every_identity_component`. #11339's store tests stay in `zeroclaw-api`.
- **Follow-up from the review, not in this PR:** a per-owner share of the dedup budget, #11565.
- **Webhook paths stay out of failure logs (`fc5f3e95b9`, from Audacity88's review of #11322):** some vendors use an unguessable webhook path as their shared secret, and log records are persisted as written. The ingress's `plugin_webhook_route_closed`, `plugin_webhook_reply_dropped`, `plugin_webhook_unauthorized`, `plugin_webhook_invalid` and `plugin_webhook_unavailable` records and the gateway's `plugin_webhook_request_invalid` record no longer carry the path; the owner's plugin and channel alias still identify the route. `dispatch_logs_route_and_worker_failures_by_owner_without_the_path` and `plugin_webhook_bounds_record_keeps_a_secret_path_out` send requests to secret-shaped paths and assert that no record contains them. The gateway's `plugin_webhook_rate_limited` record still logs the path, as on master. #11320 merges the same commit, so #11322 carries it too.
- **Scope boundary:** No other HTTP-visible change: the PR 1 plugin webhook golden frames replay byte-identical. No WIT, config schema, `zeroclaw-plugins`, or `zeroclaw-channels` change. No RPC surface (next PR).
- **Blast radius:** plugin webhook ingress in the supervised and standalone gateway; the gateway's `/webhook` and `/sop/*` replay store (same behavior, #11339's implementation, its own budget); route publication in `zeroclaw-runtime/src/plugin_runtime.rs` (mechanical: routes gain an owner, and the grammar and queue depth come from shared definitions; no new functionality, so no holding-crate exception row is needed for it).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432. Related #11000.

### What this does, simply

When a chat platform calls a channel plugin's webhook, several things have to happen before the plugin sees the request: find which plugin owns the URL, check its queue has room, start a deadline, and make sure a message the platform retries is not delivered twice. That work was spread across the web gateway. This PR puts it in one place in the core, so a gateway running as its own process can later ask the core to do it.

One thing changes on purpose. The core remembers delivered message IDs for as long as the daemon runs its current configuration, not just while one gateway process lives, so restarting the gateway no longer forgets them; reloading the config still does. Plugin messages also get their own memory, so a flood of other webhooks cannot make the core forget them, and each plugin channel's IDs are kept apart. This only suppresses platform retries; it is not a security check, which stays with each plugin's signature verification.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the PR 1 golden frames replay the public HTTP contract byte-identical, and the root e2e test drives a real WASM guest through the ingress.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Check (plugins gateway ingress)` (gateway plugin webhook tests and golden frames), `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` (`plugin_channel_runtime_e2e` with the real guest, runtime plugin admission tests), `Test` (infra and api units, gateway default-feature tests), `Lint`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-api` alone does not compile on master (its manifest lacks tokio's `time` feature, which `channel.rs` uses); the api tests run through workspace feature unification, as in CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `98e1666b31`: this PR on master `a0f70b7925` with #11339 `59875788c1` merged; macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0)

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib
test result: ok. 292 passed ; test result: ok. 331 passed   (api includes #11339's store tests; infra includes plugin_webhook::*)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib
test result: ok. 636 passed ; test result: ok. 653 passed   (includes plugin_and_generic_webhook_keys_have_separate_budgets)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --test golden_frames plugin_webhook   (x2)
test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; fixtures unchanged
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --test golden_frames -- --include-ignored
test result: ok. 12 passed
$ cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e
test result: ok. 5 passed (includes a_repeated_message_id_is_delivered_once_through_the_core_ingress)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib plugin_runtime::
test result: ok. 17 passed
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets ; RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
Finished ; Finished, no warnings
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-gateway [--features zeroclaw-gateway/plugins-wasm] --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings ; cargo clippy --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --bin zeroclaw --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished, no warnings (all three)
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check ; bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh ; bash scripts/ci/plugin_backend_change_filter.test.sh ; docs quality gate on the changed docs
clean ; passed ; pass ; 0 errors
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutation checks, each caught by the new tests: a longer or shorter deadline, the wrong log level, key or alias, dropping `"` from the allowed header-name bytes, removing the header-name length bound, and one eviction assertion. A 256-byte sweep compares the header-name rule with `http::HeaderName` byte by byte.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Log path redaction (`fc5f3e95b9`, head `a63bcc6f89`):** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib plugin_webhook` (17 passed), `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib plugin_webhook` (15 passed), and clippy on `zeroclaw-api`, `zeroclaw-infra` and `zeroclaw-gateway` with and without `plugins-wasm` (no warnings). Mutation check: putting the path back into either record fails its test.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace clippy with `ci-all` is left to CI. The comment hygiene gate did not run locally for the redaction commit (this machine's ripgrep cannot load its pcre2 library); CI runs it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (plugin secrets stay in the guest; header values pass through as before). The new and moved failure records leave out the webhook path, which some vendors use as their shared secret.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The ingress re-validates every request with bounds that are supersets of what the HTTP layer admits, so nothing new reaches the guest.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for HTTP clients and plugins. Intended behavior changes, relative to #11339 (which keeps today's behavior):
  - Dedup lives for the daemon generation instead of one gateway run, so it survives gateway supervisor restarts; it still starts empty after a daemon reload or restart. In plain terms: restarting the gateway no longer lets a platform's retry of an already-delivered message through.
  - Dedup keys include the owning plugin and alias, so a path that changes owner starts clean.
  - Plugin dedup has its own capacity (from `gateway.idempotency_max_keys`) instead of sharing the `/webhook` and `/sop/*` store; the worst case is twice that many committed keys across both stores. In plain terms: heavy traffic on one kind of webhook no longer makes the other kind forget recent message IDs.
  - Dedup remains best effort: a key can still be displaced inside its TTL once the plugin store is full, and it is not replay protection (the plugin docs now say so).
  - Outcome logs (`plugin_webhook_unauthorized`, `plugin_webhook_invalid`, `plugin_webhook_unavailable`) now come from `zeroclaw_infra::plugin_webhook` with plugin and channel alias, and no longer the path. New WARN keys `plugin_webhook_route_closed` and `plugin_webhook_reply_dropped` replace two silent 503 paths. A request outside the ingress bounds gets 400 `invalid webhook` with `plugin_webhook_request_invalid`, also without the path (the HTTP listener's own header and URI limits normally refuse such a request first).
  - Rust API: `PluginWebhookRegistry::get` returns a `PluginWebhookRoute`; `GatewaySupervision::new` takes `Arc<PluginWebhookIngress>` in place of #11339's registry and per-run store, so #11339's `zeroclaw_gateway::plugin_webhook_reservations` and `IdempotencyStore::shared` are removed; `zeroclaw_gateway::IDEMPOTENCY_MAX_KEYS_DEFAULT` moved to `zeroclaw_infra` (no workspace users). Experimental crates.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. No persisted state, WIT, or config changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `plugins.enabled = false` or a build without `plugins-wasm` disables plugin webhook routes, as before.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `plugin_webhook_*` error keys from `zeroclaw_infra::plugin_webhook`; duplicate deliveries after a gateway restart would indicate dedup regressions; golden-frame drift in the plugin gateway CI leg.
