prs.title: feat(goal): add dormant configuration and command grammar [Goal V1 proposal 2/12]
prs.body:
## Summary

Goal V1 proposal 2/12. This is configuration and command grammar, not an executable Goal Mode prefix. No merge or deployment readiness is claimed.

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add transport-neutral Goal command parsing, including multiline resume responses and immediate-pause syntax, without exposing an unwired executable command.
  - Add default-disabled canonical Goal configuration and verifier-alias validation, rename, and deletion handling.
  - Preserve explicitly unlimited budget keys through full and incremental saves alongside ordinary built-in tool selections.
  - Return existing typed configuration error codes and exact field paths instead of internal enum names or pathless errors. Keep the existing English diagnostic payload and presentation-owned localization boundary.
  - Test actual gateway config-save responses, published state, and disk persistence for rejected invalid edits, saved-with-warning edits, and valid enabled settings.
- **Scope boundary:** Slice 02 adds configuration, grammar, persistence safeguards, diagnostics, and tests to slice 01's durable task/control-plane foundation. No Goal executor, provider call, transport admission, scheduler, or usage-ledger integration is added here. The gateway production save policy is unchanged; its new tests cover the consequences of more precise configuration error paths.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust task/config/command APIs, config introspection and serialization, alias references, full and dirty saves, and gateway error binding. An enable-only edit with a missing/dangling verifier can save with a warning; while that error exists, the unchanged first-error save policy reports only the Goal warning, so an unrelated edit to a field validated after Goal is saved without its own validation. The dashboard does not display these warnings. Direct invalid-verifier edits remain rejected. Execution admission must independently reject an invalid verifier in its owning later slice.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10341; Related #8303; Depends on #11878. Neither tracker nor RFC is closed by this PR.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11878

### What this does, simply

This defines how Goal commands and settings are represented, checked, and saved. It does not make Goal commands run. Zero budgets mean unlimited and survive saving. Enabling Goal through the editor without choosing budgets writes both zero defaults; this proposal treats that enablement as consent to unlimited operation, subject to maintainer acceptance. Maintainers may instead require an explicit budget choice before admission. Invalid settings get useful error codes and field locations. The configuration API can save an unrelated repair—or enablement that needs further verifier configuration—and return a warning. The dashboard currently hides successful-save warnings; this PR does not repair that existing limitation. Editing the verifier itself to an invalid value is rejected without changing saved or published state.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — compare the dashboard's configuration surface and error binding with the base.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, dashboard configuration over the ordinary paired gateway. No messaging channel or Goal execution.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a disposable configuration directory, a loopback-only gateway with pairing enabled, and the ordinary dashboard development server. Do not use an operator configuration or configure a paid provider. Keep both runs isolated. Use the same English locale and browser viewport on base and branch.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config and look for Goal under Agent. On this branch, open Goal, enter three spaces in its optional verifier Model field and click Save. Inspect the error and confirm that no whitespace model is written to the disposable config. Do not click Reload daemon or run a Goal. Separately, an Enable click saves immediately; do not follow it with the bottom Save button, because the existing dashboard's stale toggle/draft state can overwrite that write.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Goal settings are discoverable. The invalid model edit shows `required_field_empty`, `goal.verifier.model`, and `must not be empty when provided`; no invalid model is persisted. Enable-only writes retain both zero budget defaults. The API returns a missing-verifier warning (visible only in the PATCH response, e.g. browser developer tools), but the ordinary dashboard does not display successful-save warnings and its enable pill may remain visually disabled despite a successful write.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** At the comparison base `e8d2e5fc81`, there is no Goal settings section or these Goal-specific validation errors. The generic dashboard toggle and successful-save warning limitations are unchanged source, not fixes supplied by this PR.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Exact-head `8b0d412a45` Quality Gate completed successfully, including `CI Required Gate`, workspace tests, lint, Security, platform/feature checks, and three repeated runtime/channel runs. All checks are terminal: 48 succeeded and 10 conditional checks were expected skips. The workspace command covers default-feature, non-ignored configuration and runtime unit/integration tests; the plugin and opt-in jobs add selected feature coverage, not every possible feature combination.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39363405031
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Ignored/live tests, unrestricted feature combinations, and later-slice/full-stack behavior are not certified. The historical macOS failures and linker warning below remain recorded; their original causes were not established by the successful Linux run. Two deliberate descendant-process fixtures produced nextest process-leak warnings in the successful workspace job; this is not a warning-free result.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Final correction tests, lint, formatting, and hygiene ran against the exact tree committed as `8b0d412a4532fea4da49fad6094dd0946d9100cd`. A separate automated whole-diff review run also reran the 9 Goal configuration, 84 gateway, 320 API, and 26 control-plane tests at this exact commit; all passed. It repeated root-package Clippy, formatting, and both hygiene checks successfully. This is not a Core Team approval. The earlier broad runtime run remains failed.

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config goal::tests
test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1826 filtered out; finished in 0.06s

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway api_config::tests
test result: ok. 84 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 579 filtered out; finished in 4.29s

# All targets of the root zeroclaw package, not all workspace test targets:
cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 1m 46s

cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh
58 passed, 0 failed

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

Exact-head remote output:

```text
cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop
Summary [93.549s] 19348 tests run: 19348 passed (1 slow, 2 leaky), 41 skipped

# Parallel Runtime Test: all three runs of each crate completed, at 16 threads.
# Runtime, each run, in addition to two separately serialized passing tests:
test result: ok. 5797 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
# Channels, each run, in addition to one separately serialized passing test:
test result: ok. 2005 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

The workspace job individually passed all four tests that had failed locally: both legacy webhook-audit tests, config-owner release/reacquisition, and the OAuth callback loopback test. Its two `LEAK` warnings concern existing fixtures that deliberately leave short-lived descendants holding inherited stdout/stderr (`health_check_detects_direct_child_exit_with_inherited_stdout_open` and `spawned_daemon_exit_does_not_wait_for_inherited_stderr`); their source is unchanged from the base. The warnings are retained, not suppressed or represented as clean process hygiene.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39363405031/job/118434550030
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39363405031/job/118434686007

Earlier executed coverage on `6df4685278dcbefa112c78771c26033e8e6160b0` plus the diagnostic work-in-progress diff, before the final gateway-test additions: `cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` produced API **320 passed**, runtime **5791 passed, 4 failed, 8 ignored**. This is not an exact-`8b0d412a45` runtime result. Separate exact-`8b0d412a45` runs passed the API's **320** tests and `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test session_goal_control_plane_contract` (**26** tests). These counts do not imply the runtime gate passed.

The historical runtime failures concerned two webhook-audit timeouts, config-owner lock reacquisition, and an OAuth loopback connection reset. Their implementations and tests are unchanged from the pinned base; their precise historical causes and baseline reproduction remain unproven. Current-head CI passed those tests and the repeated runtime gate. A macOS large `__eh_frame`/compact-unwind linker warning also remains disclosed, without suppression or a claim that it is harmless.

Before the diagnostic correction, the integrated tree later committed as `6df4685` had commands **18 passed**, config **1832 passed, 1 failed**, and config integration **124 passed**. That config failure creates both `nul` and `NUL` on a case-insensitive filesystem; its source is unchanged from the base. The failed run is not counted as a pass. The final nine local Goal tests are filtered coverage; current-head Linux workspace CI now supplies the broader default-feature, non-ignored config coverage.

Dependency evidence: this exact head's Security job succeeded. The old full-stack dependency failure does not describe these current inputs. Six allowed unmaintained-crate warnings remain: anymap2, nostr-relay-pool, proc-macro-error, zbus_names, zvariant, and zvariant_derive. No dependency or security-policy change was made to suppress them.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39363405031/job/118434550119

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The actual dashboard against a paired, disposable loopback gateway: Goal settings rendered; Enable persisted `true` with both zero defaults; a whitespace-only model edit displayed a field-bound error and did not persist. Successful-save warnings were not displayed. The existing enable pill/draft inconsistency was also observed; its two owning dashboard files are unchanged from the base. No model, installed daemon, Matrix, ZeroCode, or operator-configuration action was performed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot — actual dashboard, English, 1280×720, including the field-specific error and surrounding form.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Tree `5b91d6607f1a2e181c7aa3b8550447ff6993822a`, commit `8b0d412a4532fea4da49fad6094dd0946d9100cd`, compared with base `e8d2e5fc81`. Real binary plus ordinary Vite dashboard, production config HTTP handlers. Automated API evidence is in `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_config.rs` tests `goal_patch_*`; typed diagnostic tests are in `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/goal.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Actual invalid-model Save result, with the ordinary dashboard form and field-specific error:

![Goal settings: whitespace-only model rejected at its exact field](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ecad307-c0d3-486d-9700-524379307bae)

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Browser Save showed `required_field_empty` at `goal.verifier.model`; disk retained the preceding valid fields without the whitespace model. Automated gateway tests separately prove a dangling-verifier edit returns 400 without changing disk, published config, or revision; enable-only and unrelated edits return saved-with-warning results; an unrelated edit with valid enabled Goal settings produces no Goal warning.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No live Goal execution: admission/execution is not wired by this prefix. CI skips were conditional: master-push debounce and benchmarks, unselected advisory Windows/targeted Windows Clippy jobs, unchanged relay/Nix/docs surfaces, and no crates.io version bump. Required selected Windows jobs and the aggregate gate passed. Historical full-stack results are not reused to certify later slices; no new all-feature, ignored/live, or full-stack run is claimed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No — this prefix adds no execution authority or filesystem scope.
- New external network calls? No — verifier aliases resolve against canonical typed configuration without contacting providers.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No — existing masking, encrypted storage, and environment handling remain authoritative.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No — fixtures are project-neutral.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes — the parser accepts user-controlled objectives and resume responses for later execution. This prefix does not construct a model prompt or execute those values; later admission/prompt enforcement is outside this slice.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Parsed user text is data, not trusted runtime control. This PR makes no claim that later model execution has been validated.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for Rust source consumers. `Config.goal` affects struct literals; `BuiltinCommandId::Goal` and `CommandExecution::GoalAdmission` are removed along with the dormant channel catalogue entry. The cumulative diff also contains slice 01 public task/control-plane and schema-13 storage changes. The config error envelope and code namespace are unchanged, but Goal errors now use more specific existing codes and field paths.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes — additive `goal.*` configuration and a dormant parser API; removal of the unwired generic `/goal` catalogue entry. No executable Goal CLI/channel handler is introduced.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No declared floor change.
- Exact upgrade steps: Omit `[goal]` for disabled defaults. An explicit section must contain both `default_token_limit` and `default_cost_limit_usd`; zero means unlimited. An editor enable-only save creates these zero defaults when `[goal]` is absent; this proposal treats that enablement as the operator's unlimited choice. Configure a resolvable verifier before any future Goal admission. Update downstream `Config` literals and references to the removed enum variants, and adapt to slice 01 task API changes. Back up task storage before upgrade; binary reversion alone does not downgrade schema 13.

Inherited task API migration: direct `TaskRecord` literals need `session_id`/`execution_epoch` (ordinary tasks use `None`/`0`); `GoalTaskRecord` literals need pending-call and accounting fields or its default. Registry implementations must use session/epoch-guarded create/replace, pause/resume, pending-operation, and terminal methods rather than generic Goal mutations. Objectives are immutable after creation; replacement requires a settled terminal predecessor. The predecessor's compatibility section documents the complete method/migration and recovery changes, including legacy Goals marked failed and the absence of a down-migration.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11878#compatibility-required

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Restore the prior binary/configuration and revert dependent proposal slices in reverse order before reverting this slice. Preserve task database backups; do not delete task or usage history or assume automatic schema downgrade.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `goal.enabled = false` is the default; this prefix contains no active Goal executor to disable.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** When required budget keys are absent, ordinary config loading salvages the invalid `[goal]` section to disabled defaults and records a degraded-section warning; strict deserialization, including `config migrate`, reports an error. Verifier validation at load warns so configuration remains repairable; config edits can return errors or warnings. Downstream Rust consumers can fail to compile until public API changes are accommodated.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A — no superseded PR is claimed.

---

## Open proposal gates

Compared with the previous description, this revision maps Goal validation errors to existing typed codes and exact field paths, adds gateway save-path tests, and expands the compatibility section. Current-head CI is successful. Historical provider, parallel-runtime, and strict no-default all-target failures/unexecuted legs remain recorded for full-stack candidate `628e84d9345cef20dce1c48e5a484b4c6138c16a`; they are not current failures of this prefix or proof about later slices. No clean full-stack validation result is claimed.

The predecessor is reviewable but unmerged. Required human reviews, later-slice/full-stack validation, the Core runtime exception or authoritative ownership decision, and rollout measurements remain open before merge or enablement. Successful exact-head CI and readiness for review do not grant those approvals. No merge, deployment, or live-room test has occurred.

prs.title: test(gateway): cover plugin webhook ingress in required CI
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The gateway's `/plugin/{path}` handler and its HTTP tests compile only under the gateway's `plugins-wasm` feature, so no required job ran them; only the advisory Windows job did. This adds a `plugins gateway ingress` leg to `check-plugin-backends` that runs them.
  - Adds five plugin webhook golden-frame scenarios (delivery, rejections, admission, rate limit, timeout) that start the real gateway listener with a test-owned route registry and scripted channel workers. They pin every public status and body, the `Allow` header, the rate-limit JSON, and what the worker receives: method, raw query, forwarded headers in order, and exact body bytes, including a non-UTF-8 body. Worker reports left over at the end of a scenario are recorded, so an extra delivery shows up as a fixture diff. They are required in the plugin leg, unlike the informational replay of the other golden scenarios in the Test job.
  - These fixtures are the parity baseline for the rest of the #11003 stack, which moves plugin webhook dispatch behind the core RPC without changing the HTTP contract.
- **Scope boundary:** No production code changes. No change to the other golden scenarios or their informational replay.
- **Blast radius:** CI only. `scripts/ci/plugin_backend_change_filter.sh` now also selects the job for the gateway's plugin webhook handler and tests, its router and manifest, the golden harness and fixtures, the shared webhook types in `zeroclaw-api`, and `crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/plugin_webhook*`, which the next PR in the stack creates. The golden harness helpers were refactored (`Gateway::launch`, `on_scenario_runtime`, `request_head`/`write_request`) without changing the bytes of existing scenarios.
- **Merge-order note:** #11165 and #11186 also edit the workflow gate registry in `.github/workflows/README.md`; preserve both entries if resolving overlapping changes. The harness calls `GatewayReloadControls::standalone()`, so #11186's `inproc` field does not require adding a field to a literal here. Replay the plugin goldens three times after any conflict resolution.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432.
- **Labels:** `ci`, `docs`, `scripts`, `release-gate`, `risk:medium`, `topic:plugins`, `size:XL`.

### What this does, simply

Channel plugins can receive webhooks through the gateway at `/plugin/{path}`, but the tests for that route never ran in required CI. This PR makes them run, and records exactly what a webhook sender and a channel plugin see today, so the follow-up PRs that move this path into the core can prove nothing changed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** gateway HTTP (`/plugin/{path}`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** a checkout of this branch.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`a0f70b7925`). **Depends on #11320** and **#11186** (`zeroclaw-rpc-client` and the gateway's core RPC seam). The branch merges #11320 at `d6ef5dc0af` (with #11319, #11339 and #11165 beneath it) and #11186 at its current head `84f31b29cb`; their commits show in the diff until they land. Review this PR's own commits: `d15729ebff` (the forwarder), `de5cd570ab` (the connector fix, see below), `5926ddde14` (docs), `c02e5c0bac` (the in-process seam tests get a TUI signing key, which #11186's current head requires before `initialize` succeeds) and `7702fe138c` (the forwarder's failure records keep the webhook path out).
- **#11186:** its current head merges master and resolves #10621 itself, so this branch now takes #11186's own resolution and the earlier merge's resolution is gone. The remaining conflicts were placement only: the `GatewayReloadControls` field order and the daemon's RPC drain tests follow #11186, and `golden_frames.rs` keeps #11318's launch refactor (a file #11186 does not change). Against #11186's head, `inproc.rs` differs only by the connector fix.
- **Fix for #11186 on top of the merge** (`fix(rpc): release the in-process connector's context when its generation retires`): the daemon hands the gateway a clone of the generation's `InprocConnector` through its reload controls, and the connector kept the generation's `RpcContext` (its sessions and their lifecycle leases) until the last clone dropped. With #10621, a reload waits for that state to drain before it releases process ownership, so `reload_waits_for_detached_write_before_releasing_process_ownership` failed 3 of 3 runs on the merge. Sealing admission now releases the context in the same critical section, `bind` leaves a sealed connector unbound, and a `connect` waiting for a bind gives up once the generation is sealed. Two new connector tests cover it, and the daemon test passes. It belongs in #11186: I asked for it there (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11186#issuecomment-5942108575; it cherry-picks cleanly onto `84f31b29cb`), and this branch drops it once #11186 has it.
- **Audacity88's review (both blockers):**
  - **Webhook paths stay out of failure logs.** Some vendors use an unguessable webhook path as their shared secret, and log records are persisted as written. `7702fe138c` drops the path from the five `plugin_webhook_core_*` records, which keep their error key and code. `core_failure_records_keep_a_secret_path_out` sends a secret-shaped path through each core failure and asserts no record contains it. The daemon-side part belongs to #11319 (`fc5f3e95b9`: the ingress's route-closed, reply-dropped and worker-answer records, plus the gateway's `plugin_webhook_request_invalid` record). It arrives here through #11320. The gateway's `plugin_webhook_rate_limited` record still logs the path, as on master.
  - **Removed-binding admission.** Merging #11320 at `d6ef5dc0af` (`853e49dfab`) brings its fail-closed fix `fcf4f6121c`: a route whose `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` binding a live config write removed is refused until reload retires it. #11320's `plugin_webhook_dispatch_refuses_a_published_route_once_its_binding_is_removed` proves that interval, and the forwarder answers that refusal 503 (`core_rpc_errors_map_to_503`). The two-process test still checks the state after reload.
- **#10621 and the standalone gateway:** a running daemon now owns its config state exclusively, so `zeroclaw gateway start` on the daemon's config dir exits with `config lifecycle is already owned`, on master too. Next to a daemon, the standalone gateway therefore runs on a config dir of its own and names the daemon's socket with `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET`. The gateway API guide documents this, and the two-process test runs that way.
- **Channel scoping from #11320:** the forwarder connects as the shared operator, which is `admin`, so `allowed_channels` does not narrow it. A channel instance or agent with `accept_injected_webhooks = false` still refuses its dispatches: that path answers 503, logged `plugin_webhook_core_refused`, while the connection stays up and other paths keep forwarding. The gateway API guide lists it.
- **What changed and why:**
  - The standalone `zeroclaw gateway` is the separate gateway process that exists today. Its `/plugin/{path}` route used an empty in-process route table and answered 404 for every path. It now forwards each request to the running daemon over the local RPC socket through `plugin-webhook/dispatch`, so channel-plugin webhooks work across the process boundary. The daemon-supervised gateway keeps calling the core ingress in process.
  - Forwarding: shared request validation, base64 body under a process-unique `request_id`, strict result decoding with the reply bound re-checked, the same `outcome_response` mapping as the in-process path, and a best-effort `plugin-webhook/cancel` when the HTTP request is dropped. The daemon decides 404; while it is unreachable every path answers 503.
  - Daemon identity: on Unix the gateway forwards only to a socket whose peer uid equals its own effective uid, checked before any frame is sent. On Windows, where pipe names share one namespace and the server cannot be verified yet, forwarding stays off and the route keeps answering 404.
  - `core_rpc`: one maintain loop serves the in-process and local dialers; the forwarder owns its own `CoreRpc`, separate from the extension other routes can reach.
  - `plugin-webhook/*` are refused on in-process RPC connections as well as WSS (the arm the transport match needs once #11186 is in).
  - A two-process test runs the real daemon and the real standalone gateway binaries.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to the supervised gateway's behavior, to vendor webhook handlers, WIT, or config. No gateway service identity (the standalone gateway authenticates by peer credentials; see Security). The standalone `zeroclaw-gw` binary is #11002.
- **Blast radius:** standalone `zeroclaw gateway` (start, restart, bare); gateway `core_rpc` seam from #11186; RPC transport refusal; CI plugin legs and path filters.
- **Changes to #11186's in-process seam (for its author):** after a lost connection the loop waits a backoff before redialing (it redialed immediately); logs only on state transitions with error keys `core_rpc_{lost,unreachable,refused}` (and `core_rpc_untrusted_peer` for the local dialer); a FORBIDDEN refusal logs at INFO; `CoreRpc` stores a `CoreLink` (Disconnected, Connected, Refused) with `client()` and `is_connected()` unchanged; new public `CoreLink`, `CoreRpc::link()`, and Unix-only `attach_local` and `daemon_endpoint`. Refusals still end the in-process loop. `GatewaySupervision::standalone(readiness, &config)` returns a `Result`, because it builds the live config authority master now requires.
- **Follow-ups from the review, not in this PR:** route `run_gateway` through `GatewaySupervision::standalone` or make it test-only, so an embedder does not get the old unrouted `/plugin/{path}` (#11568); a scoped service identity for the forwarder's connection, tracked in #11569 under #11002.
- **Merge-order note:** this PR carries the `TransportKind::Inproc` refusal arm and test that #11320's exhaustive match needs with #11186. If #11186 lands before #11320, move them into #11320. The arm must keep refusing `Inproc` with FORBIDDEN, never treat it like `Local`. #11289 replaces the free-text `AuthDenied::forbidden(message)` this arm uses, so if #11289 lands first the arm needs its `RpcDenialReason` (the variants are listed in #11320).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003 (acceptance: separate-process flow). Related #7432 (G4 transport; vendor migration stays under #8850). Related #11000. Related #11002. Depends on #11186.

### What this does, simply

You can run the web gateway on its own with `zeroclaw gateway`. Until now, webhooks meant for channel plugins did not work there, because the plugin routes live in the daemon. Now that gateway passes each plugin webhook to the daemon over the local socket and returns the daemon's answer, exactly as the built-in gateway would. If the daemon is down, senders get 503 so they retry, and nothing is forwarded to a socket owned by another user.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional (Unix).
- **Interface(s) exercised:** gateway HTTP (`/plugin/{path}`) plus the local RPC socket.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a config with an installed channel plugin that claims a webhook path and an enabled agent routing it, plus an empty second config dir for the gateway (for example `~/.zeroclaw-gateway`).
- **Steps to run:** `zeroclaw daemon --port 0`, then `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET="$HOME/.zeroclaw/data/daemon.sock" zeroclaw --config-dir "$HOME/.zeroclaw-gateway" gateway start -p 18080`, then `curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18080/plugin/<path> ...` with the plugin's signature header; stop the daemon and repeat.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the plugin's normal answer while the daemon runs; 503 `webhook unavailable` while it is down; the answer again after it restarts.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** 404 `webhook not found` from the standalone gateway for every path.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` runs `plugin_webhook_ipc_e2e` (real binaries) and `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e`; `Check (plugins gateway ingress)` runs the forwarder and handler tests and the golden frames; `Test` runs `core_rpc` and the runtime refusal tests; `Lint`; the filter and Windows-scope script tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows is not exercised (forwarding is off there by design); the `plugins cranelift runtime` leg's time against its 20-minute timeout needs measuring on hosted CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `c02e5c0bac`: this PR with #11320 `b5d9ebd577` and #11186 `84f31b29cb` merged, on master `a0f70b7925`; macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0)

```text
$ cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_webhook_ipc_e2e   (x3)
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed (38.8s, 38.2s, 39.7s)
$ cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e ; --test architecture
ok. 5 passed ; ok. 61 passed (includes plugin_webhook_boundary)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib
test result: ok. 650 passed ; test result: ok. 683 passed   (includes core_rpc::tests::inproc::*)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --test golden_frames plugin_webhook   (x2) ; --test golden_frames -- --include-ignored
ok. 5 passed (fixtures unchanged) ; ok. 12 passed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc:: ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib daemon::
FAILED. 798 passed; 1 failed ; FAILED. 104 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored   (configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock and a_live_config_write_reaches_the_daemon_pricing_refresher_without_a_reload, see below; reload_waits_for_detached_write_before_releasing_process_ownership passes)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-client ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib
ok. 14 passed ; ok. 31 passed ; ok. 295 passed, ok. 335 passed
$ cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- openrpc --check
openrpc: docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json is in sync
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets ; RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
Finished ; Finished, no warnings
$ cargo clippy (api, infra, gateway, rpc-client, rpc-proto; with and without zeroclaw-gateway/plugins-wasm; root bin and both e2e targets) --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished, no warnings
$ TMPDIR=/private/tmp ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh ; ZEROCLAW_PARALLEL_TEST_SCOPE=channels ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
runtime run 1/3: 5483 passed; 1 failed (peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget; the gate stops there) ; channels x3: ok. 1967 passed
$ comment hygiene, change filter, Windows scope, docs quality and docs links gates
all pass
```

The three failing runtime tests fail identically on untouched master `a0f70b7925` in this environment (#11320 lists the runs), and this stack does not touch them. `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` on macOS stops only on the pre-existing unused `std::sync::mpsc` import in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs` (no lint in any changed runtime file).
- **Known residual risk:** the deadline test asserts the gateway did not log its own `plugin_webhook_core_timeout`, which fires one second after the core deadline, so a very slow runner could time out on the gateway side first. It passed every run so far, including under saturated CPU. If it flakes in CI, assert the daemon-side worker timeout record instead of the gateway log's absence.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Before the restack onto today's master, the two-process suite passed 13 consecutive runs, 3 of them with every CPU saturated; after it, all 4 runs passed. Mutations caught by the new tests: the cancel guard never firing, the stop guard removed, Inproc allowed, Inproc retrying refusals, redialing immediately after a loss, and trusting any peer uid.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Refresh for Audacity88's review (head `7702fe138c`):** the same suite again: gateway lib 33 plugin webhook tests with the new one, golden frames (x2 plus all 12), `plugin_channel_runtime_e2e`, the two-process `plugin_webhook_ipc_e2e` (3 passed, x3), architecture (61), the OpenRPC check, workspace and no-default-features checks, and clippy on the touched crates and the root targets. The only failures are the pre-existing `configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock` and `a_live_config_write_reaches_the_daemon_pricing_refresher_without_a_reload`, and the macOS `std::sync::mpsc` clippy warning, as on the old master base. Mutation check: putting the path back into a core-failure record fails the new test.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The Windows cross-check could not run (the msvc target is not installed for the pinned toolchain); a macOS simulation that flipped the new `cfg(unix)`/`cfg(windows)` gates compiled clean with clippy `-D warnings`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: under the default policy (`security.trust_daemon_uid = true`) the standalone gateway authenticates by peer credentials as the shared operator, which holds every grant. Only the `/plugin/{path}` route uses that connection; it is separate from the core RPC extension other routes can reach.
- New external network calls? No (local socket only)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes: webhook headers, including vendor signature headers, now cross the local socket to the daemon. Mitigation: on Unix the gateway verifies the socket's peer uid equals its own before sending anything; on Windows forwarding is off until the pipe server can be verified.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new path: messages reach the same plugin channel listener as before.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: a publicly bound standalone gateway now exposes the daemon's plugin routes on that listener (same exposure as the supervised gateway on that address). The connection appears as a TUI client (`/api/tuis`) and keeps an `--ephemeral` daemon alive. A refused redial writes a daemon audit record, backed off from 30 seconds to 5 minutes. `zeroclaw gateway restart` first POSTs `/admin/shutdown` to the configured address, which stops a supervised gateway listening there (unchanged, now documented).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for the supervised gateway. Standalone gateway: `/plugin/{path}` changes from 404 for every path to forwarding (Unix); 503 for every path while the daemon is unreachable or the socket belongs to another user; 503 `plugin_webhook_core_unsupported` against an older daemon without the method. New error keys: `plugin_webhook_core_{unavailable,refused,unsupported,unexpected,timeout}`, `core_rpc_{lost,unreachable,refused,untrusted_peer}`, `plugin_webhook_forwarding_disabled` (Windows). Rust API: `GatewaySupervision::standalone(readiness, &config)`; `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` is an optional gateway dependency behind `plugins-wasm`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys. The standalone gateway resolves the daemon socket like other local clients (`ZEROCLAW_SOCKET` or `<data_dir>/daemon.sock`); next to a running daemon it runs on its own config dir, so it needs `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; the standalone gateway returns to answering 404 for plugin routes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** stop the daemon, or build without `plugins-wasm`; `security.trust_daemon_uid = false` without a `[users]` entry for the gateway's uid makes the daemon refuse the connection (webhooks then answer 503).
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `plugin_webhook_core_*` and `core_rpc_*` error keys in the gateway log; 503 bursts on `/plugin/*` from a standalone gateway; `RPC authorization denied` records for the gateway's connection in the daemon log.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (`a0f70b7925`). **Depends on #11319** (core ingress, which itself now builds on #11339) and **#11165** (`zeroclaw-rpc-proto`). The branch merges #11319 at `98e1666b31` plus #11319's log-path redaction `fc5f3e95b9` (merged on its own, so master does not come in with it), and #11165 at its current head `ec00bf0a12`; their commits show in the diff until they land, so review this PR's own commits, `7962184961` (the methods), `b5d9ebd577` (channel scoping), `fcf4f6121c` (the review's two non-blocking warnings), `4e9a208600` (channel rename and delete carry `allowed_channels` grants) and `d6ef5dc0af` (the removed-binding interval test). **Needs the holding-crate exception from #11317 approved first.**
- **#11165:** its current head merges master and resolves #10621 itself, so this branch now takes #11165's own resolution. The only conflict was the rewrapped catalog line in `schema.rs`, which takes #11165's wrapping; the proto crate, the OpenRPC document and the runtime RPC types match #11165 plus this PR's additions.
- **Channel scoping (maintainer decision on this PR):** `channels:execute` and `channels:read` reach only the channel instances a profile names, and config can close the path for a channel or an agent whatever the grants. Field names and defaults:
  - `[permission_profiles.<name>] allowed_channels = ["plugin.<alias>", ...]`: a channel selector like `allowed_agents`. Entries are `<type>.<alias>` names of configured instances, validated at load; `"*"` grants every instance; empty (the default) grants none. `admin`, including the same-uid shared operator, reaches all.
  - `[channels.plugin.<alias>] accept_injected_webhooks = true` (default): `false` refuses webhooks delivered through `plugin-webhook/dispatch` to that instance.
  - `[agents.<alias>] accept_injected_webhooks = true` (default): `false` refuses such a delivery to any channel the agent handles.
  - Checked at dispatch, not only when routes are listed: `PluginWebhookIngress::dispatch_admitted` runs the check on the owner the request would be queued to, before anything is queued or reserved, so a republished route cannot redirect an admitted request. A refusal is `FORBIDDEN` with an audit record. `plugin-webhook/routes` lists only granted channels.
  - The docs say what `channels = ["execute"]` and `["read"]` unlock (authentication guide and RPC socket guide), and that a route path can be a vendor's shared secret.
  - From the review's non-blocking warnings (`fcf4f6121c`): the refusal for an ungranted channel names no channel, while its audit record still does, and a route whose channel instance the live config no longer binds is refused (fail closed) until the next reload retires it. `d6ef5dc0af` proves that interval: a route admitted while its instance is bound is refused `FORBIDDEN` once a live config write removes the instance, while the route is still published, and its worker receives nothing (asked for in Audacity88's review of #11322).
  - Renaming or deleting a channel instance carries its `allowed_channels` grants along (`4e9a208600`): a rename rewrites them to the new name, a delete drops them, and the changed profiles are saved, so a grant never blocks the change.
- **What changed and why:** A gateway in another process needs to hand channel-plugin webhook requests to the core that owns the route table. Three daemon RPC methods over the core ingress:
  - `plugin-webhook/dispatch` (`channels:execute`): method, raw query, headers, and the body as standard base64 under a caller-chosen `request_id`; answers a typed outcome (`ack`, `reply` with `body`, `not_found`, `queue_full`, `unavailable`, `unauthorized`, `bad_request`, `invalid_response`, `timeout`, `cancelled`). Validated by the same shared constructor the HTTP adapter uses.
  - `plugin-webhook/cancel` (`channels:execute`): cancels an in-flight dispatch on the same connection; the dispatch response stays authoritative.
  - `plugin-webhook/routes` (`channels:read`): current route owners, for diagnostics.
  - Local IPC only: an exhaustive transport match refuses all three on WSS with FORBIDDEN and an audit record.
  - Dispatch runs in a task spawned from the dispatcher like `session/prompt`, so the serial read loop stays live for cancel and other requests. Each connection tracks in-flight dispatches for cancel and duplicate-id checks and holds at most 1024 until their responses are queued; the next gets `queue_full`. Connection close and daemon reload cancel in-flight work and send nothing; shutdown joins the tasks and never waits on a full writer queue.
  - The daemon registry hands the generation's ingress to the RPC context, and the daemon always builds one ingress.
- **Scope boundary:** No gateway change (the forwarder is the next PR). No new principal or credential. Runtime edits stay within the #11317 row: `src/rpc/{dispatch,context}.rs`, `src/daemon/{registry,mod}.rs`, and the denial message keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`. The new config field also updates `PluginChannelConfig` literals inside the test modules of `src/plugin_runtime.rs` and `src/tools/mod.rs` (mechanical, test-only). The grant selector and config fields live in `zeroclaw-api` and `zeroclaw-config`.
- **Blast radius:** runtime RPC dispatcher (new arms, per-connection state, shutdown join), daemon registry, `RpcContext` (all 14 literals), the OpenRPC document (regenerated), `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` (8 wire types, 3 `Method` variants), `zeroclaw-api` (route listing, the `allowed_channels` selector), `zeroclaw-infra` (route listing, `dispatch_admitted`), `zeroclaw-config` (three fields).
- **Follow-ups from the review, not in this PR:** one local-only gate shared with `file/upload/*`, with a per-method "local only" classification `xtask` can emit (#11566), and `schemars` bounds on the dispatch wire fields so the OpenRPC document states them (#11567).
- **Merge-order note:** #11186 adds `TransportKind::Inproc`. The transport match here is deliberately exhaustive, so whichever of this PR and #11186 lands second must add the `Inproc` arm (refused, with its test; #11322 carries both). #11289 replaces the free-text `AuthDenied::forbidden(message)` with `RpcDenialReason`: whichever of this PR and #11289 lands second needs variants for this PR's four refusals (for example `local_ipc_only`, `channel_not_granted`, `channel_refuses_injected_webhooks`, `agent_refuses_injected_webhooks`) and the updated audit assertions, which now read `reason` as a stable identifier.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11003. Related #7432. Related #11000. Related #11001. Depends on #11165.
- **Labels:** `ci`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `core`, `daemon`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `tests`, `scripts`, `size:XL`, `cli` (applied by the labelers)

### What this does, simply

The daemon already answers RPC calls from local clients such as zerocode. This PR teaches it three more calls so a separate web gateway can say "here is a webhook request for this plugin URL, what should I answer?" and get back the same result the in-process gateway gets today. Only local connections may use them, and only callers allowed to operate the specific channels they ask for. An operator can also switch the path off for one channel, or for one agent, in config, whatever access a caller has.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** local RPC socket.
- **Steps to run:** start a daemon with a configured channel plugin that claims a webhook path, then over `socat READLINE UNIX-CONNECT:<data_dir>/daemon.sock` send `initialize`, then `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"plugin-webhook/routes","params":{},"id":2}` and a `plugin-webhook/dispatch` for that path.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** routes lists the owner; dispatch answers `{"outcome":"ack"}` or the plugin's reply.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `METHOD_NOT_FOUND`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` (runtime `rpc::` and `daemon::` suites, proto tests), `Parallel Runtime Test` (runtime/channels interference), `Installer Drift` (OpenRPC `--check`), plugin legs for the ingress and gateway parity.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows named pipes are not exercised by a required job.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `b5d9ebd577`: this PR with #11319 `98e1666b31` and #11165 `ec00bf0a12` merged, on master `a0f70b7925`; macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0)

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::
test result: FAILED. 784 passed; 1 failed   (configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock, see below)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook   (x3)
test result: ok. 26 passed   (includes plugin_webhook_dispatch_reaches_only_granted_channels and plugin_webhook_dispatch_honors_channel_and_agent_refusal)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib daemon::
test result: FAILED. 101 passed; 1 failed; 1 ignored   (a_live_config_write_reaches_the_daemon_pricing_refresher_without_a_reload, see below)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib
ok. 295 passed, ok. 335 passed ; ok. 1760 passed   (channel selector, allowed_channels validation, accept_injected_webhooks defaults, dispatch_admitted)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto ; cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto --features schema-export
ok. 29 passed ; ok. 32 passed
$ cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- openrpc --check ; cargo test --locked -p xtask openrpc
openrpc: docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json is in sync ; ok
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features plugins-wasm --lib ; --test golden_frames plugin_webhook
ok. 653 passed ; ok. 5 passed (fixtures unchanged)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib plugin_runtime:: ; cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e ; --test architecture
ok. 17 passed ; ok. 5 passed ; ok. 57 passed
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets ; cargo check --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --tests ; RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
Finished ; Finished ; Finished, no warnings
$ cargo clippy (api, infra, config, gateway, rpc-proto; with and without zeroclaw-gateway/plugins-wasm; root bin and e2e) --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished, no warnings
$ TMPDIR=/private/tmp ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh ; ZEROCLAW_PARALLEL_TEST_SCOPE=channels ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
runtime run 1/3: 5466 passed; 1 failed (peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget; the gate stops there) ; channels x3: ok. 1967 passed
$ comment hygiene, change filter, docs quality and docs links gates
all pass
```

The three failing runtime tests fail identically on untouched master `a0f70b7925` in this environment (two runs each), and this PR does not touch them. `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` stops only on the pre-existing macOS `unused import std::sync::mpsc` in `service/mod.rs`; no lint in any changed runtime file.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutations caught by the new tests: releasing the permit before the send, shutdown not joining dispatch tasks, releasing the id after the send, allowing WSS, removing the send's race against connection cancel, and skipping the denial audit record.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Refresh for the #11322 review (head `d6ef5dc0af`):** the same suite again: `rpc::dispatch::tests::plugin_webhook` 27 passed (with the new test), and the only failures are the same three pre-existing runtime tests and the macOS `std::sync::mpsc` clippy warning described above. The new test fails if a missing binding is admitted.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --no-default-features --features agent-runtime` fails on six pre-existing dead-code helpers in `src/main.rs` whose only caller is gateway-gated; unrelated, reproduces on master.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: `Resource::Channels` gains its first RPC consumers, scoped to named channel instances through `allowed_channels`. `admin`, including the same-uid shared operator, reaches every route; any other profile reaches only the instances it names. `accept_injected_webhooks = false` on a channel instance or an agent refuses the path whatever the grants. Plugins still verify vendor signatures.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (headers pass through to the guest as they do over HTTP)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new path: dispatched messages enter the same plugin channel listener as HTTP webhooks.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: local IPC only (WSS refused with an audit record); grants checked at admission; the core enforces the shared request bounds, so a local caller bypassing the gateway's rate limit still cannot exceed them; 1024 in-flight dispatches per connection; no diagnostic detail in results.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (additive methods). Builds with plugins but without the gateway now build the ingress, so webhook-capable plugin channels validate and publish their route claims instead of activating poll-only. A worker that drops its reply after the caller cancelled now reports `cancelled` instead of `unavailable`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes, additive: `[permission_profiles.<name>] allowed_channels` (default empty, so a profile with `channels` grants but no selector reaches no channel; nothing consumed `channels` before this PR), and `accept_injected_webhooks` on `[channels.plugin.<alias>]` and `[agents.<alias>]` (default `true`).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; the methods disappear (`METHOD_NOT_FOUND`) and nothing persisted changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** remove `channels:execute` or the channel from a profile's `allowed_channels` to deny dispatch; `accept_injected_webhooks = false` on a channel instance or agent closes the path whatever the grants; `plugins.enabled = false` publishes no routes.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `RPC authorization denied` records for `plugin-webhook/*`, with reasons naming the channel or agent that refused; `queue_full` answers at the per-connection cap; WARN `plugin_webhook_dispatch_notification` for notification-form dispatches.

Phase 3: The Gateway. Separate the web surface from the agent core so the gateway is optional and can restart independently.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.9.0 gateway](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v090-gateway), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

Deliverables: agree the full core IPC contract first; finish the supported local IPC server; ship standalone zeroclaw-gw; migrate vendor webhook behavior into channel plugins; and have Tauri package and manage both processes.

Completion requires a core artifact without web assets or HTTP server code, a working IPC-connected gateway, core/channel operation when the gateway is absent, and demonstrated two-process desktop lifecycle. Existing OIDC, principal-isolation, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with this boundary. WATI is already retired. Feature acceptance and normal review/CI/release holds still apply.

prs.title: fix(providers): tell the model when a text-only follow-up has no new image
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Earlier user images keep their `[IMAGE:<path>]` markers in history so a deferred image stays available, and multimodal preparation re-sends them on every later turn looking exactly like fresh attachments. With the default `max_image_turns = 0`, a text-only follow-up such as "and this one?" then gets a confident description of a photo that was never sent (#11554).
  - A text-only user message that follows an earlier user image now carries a short model-facing note: "Note: no new image is attached to this message; any images above were sent earlier." The note is never added to image-bearing messages, earlier images are still sent (deferred access from #8151 keeps working), and conversations without images take the existing fast path untouched.
  - The note is added in one small pass after normalization (`note_text_only_followups`). Whether a message gets it depends only on that message and the ones before it, read from the request's input as it was before the age trim and the image cap, so the note never changes an earlier message from one request to the next and does not itself rewrite the provider prompt-cache prefix (the constraint from Audacity88's triage of #11554).
  - Some providers (the OpenAI-compatible and OpenAI Codex ones) prepare messages the runtime has already prepared, so a second pass must not change them: a message that already holds the note is left alone, and so is one an earlier pass reduced to the removed-image placeholder, the rejected-marker note, or the could-not-load note (each matched in the form its pass writes it: the placeholder and the could-not-load note only at the end of the message, the rejected-marker note anywhere, since it replaces the marker in place; so a user quoting the placeholder or could-not-load wording mid-sentence still gets the note). Image markers are counted with the same helper that selects the no-image fast path, so prose that uses marker syntax without a loadable reference (for example `[IMAGE:<path>]`) does not count as an earlier image. Tool-result carriers neither get the note nor count as earlier user images.
  - When provider-image quarantine or recovery (`omit_provider_image_ids`) removes every image from a captioned message, the provider view now keeps the caption followed by `[image removed from history]`, as it already did for image-only messages. Without this, a provider's second pass would add the new note to the very message the user sent an image with.
- **Scope boundary:** This fixes the behaviour #11554 reports (text-only follow-ups). Image-bearing messages are not labelled, so nothing marks a new image sent while earlier ones are still in history as new; that is outside the reported repro and is not addressed here. In the live check below, one local model still described a second photo sent straight after the first on its own, with no note anywhere in that request; this is one model and a short session, not evidence that the label is unneeded in general. A channel that stores a photo and its caption as separate consecutive user messages would see the note on the caption. The channel crate's own image placeholders (for example the one written when an inline image payload is collapsed from history, or "could not be read") are not recognised, so such a message after an earlier path-marker image also gets the note; the note then sits beside the channel's own placeholder, and for "could not be read" the two may read as contradictory. No change to `max_image_turns`, `max_images`, eviction, tool-result carriers, or stored history.
- **Blast radius:** The provider-visible text of text-only user messages that follow a user image, for every provider (shared multimodal preparation in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/multimodal.rs`), and the provider-only quarantine and recovery views of captioned messages whose images are all omitted. Each noted message gains about 20 tokens while the earlier image message stays in history, including after its image is evicted or age-trimmed; that keeps the note stable for the prompt cache. Text-only fallback requests strip media markers first and get no note. The runtime measures the prepared messages, so the note is counted in the context budget. Stored session history is unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11554. Related #8151, #11582.

### What this does, simply

When you send a photo in a chat and then keep talking, ZeroClaw keeps showing that photo to the model on every later message, so the model can still refer back to it. The model had no way to tell that the photo was old, so a follow-up like "and this one?" made it describe a brand-new photo that you never sent. Now, when your message has no image of its own and there was an image earlier, ZeroClaw adds a one-line note telling the model that nothing new is attached and the images above were sent earlier. The earlier photo is still there for the model to use.

### Possible follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The string checks for messages an earlier pass already prepared exist because some providers prepare the runtime's prepared messages a second time. Skipping that second preparation would make them unnecessary, but it is a cross-crate change.
- The image cap and the age trim leave a bare caption when they remove a captioned message's images; leaving the same placeholder there as quarantine now does would make the three paths consistent. It is not needed for this fix, because those trims always remove the oldest images first.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `signal` (with #11556); Telegram and Discord take the same path-marker route on master
- **Setup / preconditions:** a vision-capable model, default `[multimodal]` settings (`max_image_turns = 0`), a fresh session on Telegram or Discord. Signal image attachments need my open #11556, which is not on master yet.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Send one photo with a question.
  2. Send "and this one?" with no attachment.
  3. Send "what about this one?" with no attachment.
  4. Ask how many photos you have sent.
  5. Ask a question about the first photo.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** steps 2 and 3 are answered without describing a new photo; step 4 counts one; step 5 is answered from the first photo.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** as reported in #11554 (observed on Signal with master at 0.8.5 plus a Signal attachment branch for #7891): step 2 described "another photo of the same subject" with invented details, step 3 gave another invented description, and step 4 answered three. Step 5 was not part of the report.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` (format, clippy, and the workspace test run, which includes the `zeroclaw-providers` and `zeroclaw-runtime` tests that cover the new behaviour and the root `component` CLI test this PR updates).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI does not exercise model behaviour; the live check below covers that for one model.
- **Commands run and tail output:** in a throwaway container on this branch:
  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  exit 0
  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
  exit 0
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --locked --lib -- multimodal::
  test result: ok. 216 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1779 filtered out
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --locked --lib
  test result: FAILED. 1990 passed; 1 failed; 4 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --locked --test hailo_ollama
  test result: ok. 60 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw --locked --test component
  test result: FAILED. 262 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw --locked --test integration
  test result: ok. 142 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
  Comment hygiene gate passed.
  ```
  On the previous revision of this branch, which differed only by the `earlier_images_note_survives_the_age_trim_of_the_earlier_image` test and one doc comment in `multimodal.rs`:
  ```text
  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
  exit 0
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --lib
  test result: ok. 5798 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --locked --lib
  test result: FAILED. 2004 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  ```
  New tests:
  - `text_only_followup_after_an_image_is_told_no_new_image_is_attached` (the note is appended and the text, including leading indentation, is kept verbatim)
  - `text_before_the_first_image_gets_no_note`
  - `earlier_images_note_is_stable_across_requests` (later requests leave earlier messages byte-identical)
  - `earlier_images_note_survives_eviction_of_the_earlier_image` and `earlier_images_note_survives_the_age_trim_of_the_earlier_image` (the note is decided from the input, so it stays after the cap or the age limit removes the earlier image)
  - `preparing_prepared_messages_again_changes_nothing`, `a_failed_image_after_an_earlier_one_is_not_noted_on_a_second_pass`, `a_refused_marker_after_an_earlier_image_is_not_noted_on_a_second_pass`, and `a_message_whose_images_were_omitted_is_not_noted_on_a_second_pass` (prepare, then prepare the result again; the last one omits images in between)
  - `tool_result_carriers_neither_get_nor_trigger_the_note`
  - `quoting_the_could_not_load_wording_does_not_suppress_the_note`
  - `prose_that_only_contains_the_marker_prefix_is_not_an_earlier_image`

  The existing `image_cap_eviction_is_bounded_and_prefix_stable` still passes. I also removed each guard in turn (the existing-note check, each of the three already-prepared checks, the carrier skip, the input-based decision, and the caption placeholder on omit); each removal makes at least one of these tests fail. In `zeroclaw-runtime`, `enforce_retrims_against_the_prepared_population_for_retained_images` compared prepared and raw token estimates for a history with two text-only follow-ups after an image; it now compares against the prepared messages with only the image turn left raw, so it still isolates per-image pricing. In the root `component` suite, `interactive_agent_renders_image_recovery_and_next_text_turn` checked that the next turn's newest user message ends with "next text-only turn"; that message now also carries the note, so it checks that the message contains the text.

  The three failures are unrelated to this change. `openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` fails in full-suite runs in my environment and passes when run alone; its fixture has no images, and this change does not touch `openai.rs`. `tts::tests::edge_tts_removes_temp_output_when_read_fails` relies on `chmod 000` making a file unreadable, which does not hold in my container, which runs as root. `daemon_startup_feedback::daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions` fails at the same line when run alone on this branch and on unmodified master `e8d2e5fc8` in the same container.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** On Signal, with a local model served by llama.cpp through the OpenAI-compatible provider (which runs the second preparation pass), I ran the five steps above in a fresh session against a daemon built from v0.8.6 plus this branch's code change and my other PR branches (#11556 and #11660, open; #11637 and #11595, since merged to master). Steps 2 and 3 did not describe a new photo, step 4 counted one, and step 5 was answered from the first photo. An earlier revision of this change gave the same results. In a second session on the same build and setup, after `/clear` and with photos not used in any earlier test, I sent photo A with a question, then a different photo B with "and what is this one?", asked how many photos I had sent, asked about the first and then the second photo, and then sent a third photo C with "what about this one?". B was described on its own, without repeating or blending A, and C was described as the newest photo; the count was two; and the questions about the first and second photo were answered from A and B. Not verified: the "before" behaviour was not re-run on current master or v0.8.6; Telegram, Discord, and other models were not tested.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no rendered interface changes; the change is model-facing text in the provider request.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** unit and integration tests on this branch's head, except the `zeroclaw-runtime` clippy and library runs and the `zeroclaw-channels` library run, which are from the previous revision (see above); live check on Signal against v0.8.6 plus this branch's code change, as described above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A: the observable result is the model's reply in a private chat; the unit tests assert the exact note text and placement.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** text-only follow-ups after a photo: no invented photo; photo count: one; question about the first photo: answered from it; in a second session, a new photo after an earlier one was described on its own and the photo count was two.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace test suite was not run. The `zeroclaw-providers`, `zeroclaw-runtime`, and `zeroclaw-channels` library suites, the `zeroclaw-providers` `hailo_ollama` test, and the root `component` and `integration` suites were run; other workspace crates and integration suites were left to CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: the note and the removed-image placeholder are fixed constants; no user, channel, or file content is interpolated into them. User text can only suppress the note on its own message (for example by quoting the note), and cannot make the note appear without a real image marker in an earlier user message.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a text-only follow-up answered as if no earlier image existed would indicate the note is misleading the model; earlier images missing from the request would indicate a regression in deferred access (covered by the tests above).
