prs.title: feat(tools): add agy_cli coding-CLI tool for Antigravity CLI
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Google has moved terminal Gemini use from Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI (`agy`), and Gemini CLI has stopped serving most accounts (Google Developers Blog, June 2026). ZeroClaw can delegate coding tasks to Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, but not to `agy`.
  - Adds `agy_cli`, a peer of `codex_cli` / `claude_code` / `gemini_cli` / `opencode_cli`. It is built on the shared coding-CLI executor, so it inherits the same authorization, working-directory validation, timeout, output bounding and runtime-executor routing.
  - Headless `agy` exits 0 and reports `status: SUCCESS` even when it auto-denies a tool permission, so the exit code alone would report a blocked task as a success. `agy_cli` requests JSON output and decides success from it. A run succeeds only when the process exits 0, `status` is `SUCCESS`, and `denied_actions` is empty. Non-JSON or status-less output fails closed.
  - Tool-owned flags are attached (`--print=<prompt>`, `--model=<id>`, `--print-timeout=<n>s`) and placed after operator `extra_args`. A model-supplied prompt that starts with `-` cannot be parsed as a flag, and the tool's own settings take precedence over operator arguments.
- **Scope boundary:** `gemini_cli` is not changed or deprecated here. There is no `agy` model provider. The shared coding-CLI executor is unchanged apart from recognising the new tool name in the env-boundary helper. The sandbox and permission defaults of `agy` itself are left to the operator's agy settings.
- **Blast radius:** Opt-in only. The new `[agy_cli]` section defaults to `enabled = false`, and nothing changes for existing configs. Shared test fixtures changed in two places: the budget-test fake now returns agy-shaped JSON, which the other adapters pass through unchanged, and the runtime routing test now expects `agy_cli` to fail closed on its plain-text probe.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11075. Related #4879, whose closing comment suggested Antigravity CLI support as the follow-up. Related #10381 (merged): `agy_cli` builds its command through the shared `CodingCliCommand`/`CodingCliExecutor` path, so it inherits that PR's host-launcher resolution before the workspace working directory is applied.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw agents can hand a coding task to an external coding CLI. Google has replaced Gemini CLI with a new tool called Antigravity CLI (`agy`), so Gemini users had no supported way to do that. This PR adds an `agy_cli` tool that works like the existing Codex and Claude Code tools. It stays off until you turn it on in config.

The main difference from the other CLIs is how failure is detected. When `agy` runs without a terminal and wants to do something that needs permission, such as running a shell command, it refuses automatically but still exits successfully. `agy_cli` reads agy's JSON result, reports those refusals as a failure, and tells the user how to allow the action in agy's own settings.

ZeroClaw checks that the requested working directory is inside the workspace, but it does not sandbox what `agy` does once it is running. That is governed by agy's own permission settings. The docs section added in `tools/overview.md` states this plainly.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behaviour is covered by unit tests with fixtures copied from real agy 1.2.9 output. Manual testing needs an authenticated `agy` install, which most reviewers will not have.

### How I tested

- **Revision (2026-10-11):** one commit, which supersedes `76275ecf6`. It was authored and validated at `34d7aea0825a1e7cd7701135e4dc3f341271a56b` on master `0f8fb9d372a5cf850e87f9464c7f5c216a717fee`. **Rebase note (2026-10-11):** the then-current head `6239f29f26fcbe1e6b520016cb98b9eade20f329` was a base-only rebase of that commit onto master `d03325172eb6c64272f01042b60fd7f66d74c711` with GitHub's update-branch (`git range-diff` shows the commit identical; the local validation and review below were recorded on `34d7aea08`). **Rebase note (2026-10-14):** the then-current head `dc09ad4048d50e3960e9d8c44132a8fec3b4b1cd` was a base-only rebase of `6239f29f2` onto master `329e66f76` with GitHub's update-branch. Master had moved 32 commits and four files this PR touches changed upstream (`orchestrator/acp_server.rs`, `orchestrator/mod.rs`, `config/schema.rs`, `docs/book/src/tools/overview.md`); a trial merge was clean and the rebase applied without conflicts. `git range-diff` shows the commit unchanged apart from one context line in `docs/book/src/tools/overview.md` (the neighbouring heading was renamed upstream); the file set is unchanged (18 files). The local validation and review below were recorded on `34d7aea08`; required CI runs on the current head. **Rebase note (2026-10-17):** rebased again with GitHub's update-branch onto master `4e82ce46e` (32 commits, including the rustls/Wasmtime advisory fix #11755 that the earlier Security failure was waiting on). `git range-diff` shows the commit identical, with no content change; the new head is `91da937b6051c182654f7ba5d0cc240b722cece8`. A trial merge was clean; five files this PR changes were also touched on master (`zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs`, both `tools.ftl` files, `zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs`, `docs/book/src/developing/tool-inventory.md`) without conflict. What changed:
  - Inventory: `agy_cli` is registered in `BUILTIN_TOOLS` as a Host-tier tool, listed in the tier table and prose of `tool-inventory.md`, and enabled in the runtime maximal-config inventory test. This fixes the `matrix_safe_policy_names_only_inventoried_tools` failure that appeared after master's typed tool inventory landed, and Greptile's inventory finding.
  - i18n: the tool description, parameter descriptions and errors are Fluent `tool-agy-cli-*` keys in the canonical English catalogue, with the generated tools-crate mirror regenerated. This addresses Greptile's localization finding.
  - Hardening of `agy_cli`'s own contract: a bare `--` in `extra_args` is dropped from the agy argv and flagged by config validation, so it can no longer turn the tool-owned flags into positionals. An explicit JSON `null` for `response`, `denied_actions` or `error` no longer breaks parsing, so agy's real status and error are reported; success still requires `status == SUCCESS` and no denied actions. The `--print-timeout` margin scales with small timeouts instead of collapsing to `1s`. The attached form `--dangerously-skip-permissions=<value>` now triggers the risky-flag warning (agy only; Codex matching is unchanged). Stderr appended to errors is capped like stdout. `agy_cli` is added to the Integrations-group test.
  - Not changed: the shared coding-CLI workdir refactor, Codex helper naming, the model-visible remediation text, and tolerance for non-JSON banner lines.

- **Rebase note (2026-10-18):** rebased onto master `c473221313341a853e04122f93bb9bd26b5e6c47` (8 commits after `4e82ce46e`). GitHub's update-branch could not be used: master's #11221 (`8ed287bd4`) moved the coding-CLI tools behind per-tool Cargo features and conflicted in `zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs` and `zeroclaw-tools/src/coding_cli.rs`. I resolved it locally in an isolated worktree, starting from master's versions of both files and re-applying this PR's change on top. The new head is `400553d30eed7e316b68860003553e61700825c5` (previous head `91da937b6`). `agy_cli.rs` is byte-identical to the previous head; the previously approved behaviour is unchanged. What changed:
  - New `tool-agy-cli` feature, chained like its peers (`zeroclaw-config` -> `zeroclaw-tools` -> `zeroclaw-runtime` -> root) and added to the full-tool feature list.
  - `OptInTool::AgyCli` (`ALL` is now 13 entries) with section `agy_cli` and feature `tool-agy-cli`; the inventory entry now carries `compilation: OptIn(AgyCli)`.
  - `agy_cli` module, attribution and runtime registration are gated on the feature, with `warn_tool_compiled_out` otherwise; `any_coding_cli_tool_enabled` and the shared coding-CLI executor gates include it.
  - `collect_agy_cli_extra_arg_warnings` returns early when the tool is not compiled in (as the Codex collector does), so a build without `agy` reports only the compiled-out warning. Tests that need the feature are gated, and one new test covers the compiled-out case.
  - `tool-agy-cli` is added to the 13 generated feature lists (`Containerfile`, the Dockerfiles, `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`, `dist/aur/PKGBUILD`, `flake.nix`, `setup.bat`); `cargo run -p xtask --bin generate -- installers --check` reports every surface in sync.
  - The file set grows from 18 to 31 files: 13 additional files, namely the Cargo manifests, the packaging surfaces and `opt_in_tools.rs`.
  - Local validation (aarch64 Linux, rustc 1.97.1) on `0fee975c651b3302a16aafaab6bd30ac4df7492e`, which has the same patch-id as the published head and differs only by the base (two later master commits that touch none of this PR's files): `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `installers --check`; `zeroclaw-config` lib `agy_cli` 3 passed without the feature and 6 passed with `tool-agy-cli,tool-codex-cli`; `zeroclaw-tools` lib `agy_cli` 31 passed, environment-boundary 1, `coding_agent_budget_tests` 2, inventory docs-drift and source-scan 1 + 3; `zeroclaw-runtime` `registered_coding_cli_tools_use_configured_runtime_executor` 1 and `docker_without_workspace_mount_does_not_register_coding_cli_tools` 1 (with `--skip tunnel::tailscale`); `cargo clippy -D warnings` on `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-tools`; `git diff --check`; all exit 0. The numbers above supersede the `34d7aea08` figures below for the wiring; the `agy_cli.rs` unit-test evidence still applies.
  - Review: exact-SHA Gemini review via Agy (`gemini-3.8-flash-high`, complete diff bundle, no tools) returned READY with no findings on `0fee975c6`. An earlier candidate was rated NEEDS_WORK for missing feature gates on some config tests; that is fixed and re-reviewed. This is the only review lane for this revision.
  - CI: the two `Format` jobs fail on `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs`, added unformatted by master's #11837 (`c47322131`); `rustfmt --check` on that file at master reproduces it, and this PR does not touch it. Other required jobs were still running when this was written. Approval was given on earlier heads; since this revision changes the feature wiring, a fresh look at the gating is welcome.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required Rust CI (fmt, clippy, tests) covers the new tool, config section, and wiring.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI has no `agy` binary. The live behaviour against real agy was checked locally (below).
- **Validation at `34d7aea08` (aarch64 Linux, rustc 1.97.1):** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` 0; Fluent generator `--check` 0; `zeroclaw-tools` lib 43 passed; `zeroclaw-tools` inventory docs-drift/source-scan integration tests 1 + 3 passed; `zeroclaw-config` lib agy/section filters 26 passed; `zeroclaw-runtime` `coding_cli agy_cli` filters 17 passed; `zeroclaw-channels` inventory/matrix filters 2 passed; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on tools, runtime, channels and config 0; `git diff --check` 0.
- **Mutation checks:** reverting the explicit-`null` handling fails 3 of the new tests; reverting the bare-`--` filtering fails 1 test in `zeroclaw-tools` and 1 in `zeroclaw-config`. The tree was restored byte-identical afterwards.
- **Review:** exact-SHA Gemini review via Agy (`gemini-3.8-flash-high`, bundle of the complete `0f8fb9d37..34d7aea08` diff, no tools) returned READY with no findings, blockers or test gaps. This is the only review lane for this revision; a second review was not run.
- **CI:** on `34d7aea08`, all required Linux, lint, check, build and test jobs passed. `Platform Test (macOS)` and `Platform Test (Windows)` failed there with 13 failing tests, identical by name to master's scheduled platform run (`38021228494`); none is specific to this PR. CI on the rebased head `6239f29f2` is pending and is not carried over from the earlier head.
- **Live use (earlier revision, before the 2026-10-11 hardening):** the same patch ran in a local `release-fast` integration build (master `1d64833a9` + this PR + #11080) on aarch64 Linux since 2026-09-29; a live agent-driven `agy_cli` call returned the expected reply.
- **Historical local checks** (aarch64 Linux, rustc 1.97.1), from earlier heads with the same agy_cli patch: `411d9ec42` amends `0543611e8` only to name `agy_cli.extra_args` as the ZeroClaw-side remedy in the auto-denied-permission error, plus one assertion. `500590f3c` changes only `agy_cli.rs` relative to `5d4b5bc7e`.

```text
# at 411d9ec42 (differs from 0543611e8 only in agy_cli.rs error text + 1 assertion)
cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-tools -- --check                        -> exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings  -> exit 0
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- agy_cli
  test result: ok. 25 passed; 0 failed
git diff --check                                            -> exit 0

# at 500590f3c
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  -> exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings  -> exit 0
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- agy_cli coding_cli coding_agent cli_discovery attribution
  test result: ok. 41 passed; 0 failed
git diff --check                                            -> exit 0

# at 5d4b5bc7e (differs only in agy_cli.rs)
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime \
  -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings          -> exit 0
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- agy_cli codex_cli sections validation_warnings
  test result: ok. 68 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::tests::registered_coding_cli tools::tests::coding_cli
  test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::tests::docker_without_workspace_mount_does_not_register_coding_cli_tools
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- map_tool_kind matrix_safe
  test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I ran the real tool code (`AgyCliTool::execute`) against agy 1.2.9 with a throwaway, local-only `#[ignore]` test that is not part of this PR:
  - A plain prompt returned `success=true` with the expected text.
  - With `extra_args = ["--sandbox"]`, a prompt that needs a shell command returned `success=false` with the auto-denied `RunCommand` explanation. agy itself exited 0 with `status: SUCCESS`.
  - A prompt beginning with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` was treated as prompt text, returning `success=true` with the expected reply, not as a flag.
  - The scratch workspace was empty afterwards.

  Not verified: behaviour on macOS or Windows, and agy versions other than 1.2.9. The live run was at `5d4b5bc7e`; `500590f3c` only adds stderr to the non-`SUCCESS` status error and two unit tests.

  Operator misconfiguration: a bare `--` in `extra_args` made agy 1.2.9 reject the following tool-owned flags (`Error: unexpected argument "--output-format=json"`, exit 2) without running anything. As of `34d7aea08`, `agy_cli` drops bare `--` entries from the agy argv and config validation warns about them, so the flags stay flags; a trailing value-taking flag in `extra_args` (for example `--effort`) is still operator argv and is documented as such in the tools overview.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No user-visible interface state changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** A full-workspace `cargo test` was not run locally. The changed surfaces are covered by the focused tests above and required CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes**
- New external network calls? **Yes**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - Permissions and network: when enabled, `agy_cli` launches `agy`, which acts on files and calls Google's services under its own permission model, like the existing coding-CLI tools. The tool is disabled by default and gated by the same security policy, autonomy level and rate limiting as its peers, and the working directory is canonicalized and must stay inside the workspace. Operator `extra_args` that widen agy's permissions (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--add-dir`) produce a non-blocking config-validation warning that does not echo the values.
  - Prompt injection: agy's response is returned to the model as tool output, the same as for the other coding CLIs. Output is bounded by `max_output_bytes`.
  - Containment limit, stated in the docs: ZeroClaw validates only the starting directory. What `agy` touches after launch is governed by agy's own settings.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** New optional `[agy_cli]` config section, disabled by default. Existing configs are unaffected.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- Upgrade steps: none required. To use the tool, add `[agy_cli]` with `enabled = true` and have an authenticated `agy` on `PATH`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Medium risk and opt-in: `git revert <sha>`. The `[agy_cli] enabled = false` setting, which is the default, also disables it at runtime.

---
**Fix note (2026-10-20, head `02ad51ded`):** CI on the previous head (`400553d30`) failed `Test` on `schema::tests::codex_cli_policy_config_source_warnings_are_non_blocking_and_redacted`. Cause was mine: when I added the Agy config tests in `schema.rs` I dropped the `#[cfg(feature = "tool-codex-cli")]` gate on that existing Codex test, so it ran (and failed) in a default-features build. My earlier local runs filtered on `agy_cli`, so they did not exercise it. The gate is restored (the only gate differences from master are now the four new `tool-agy-cli` tests). Rebased onto master `24938afc6` (no overlap with this PR's files).

Validated locally on the pre-rebase head `3c171af0c` (same patch-id as `02ad51ded`; the rebase only picked up an unrelated `tunnel/tailscale.rs` commit): the full `zeroclaw-config` lib without a name filter (1783 tests default features, 1790 with all tool features), generated-file check, `zeroclaw-tools` agy tests, inventory tests, `zeroclaw-runtime` coding-CLI tests, clippy `-D warnings` on config+tools with all tool features, and `git diff --check`. I did not re-run these after the final one-commit rebase; CI is the check for `02ad51ded`.

Remaining non-code failures seen on the previous head: `Format` (master's own unformatted `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs`) and an arm64 `Source Image Build` runner `ResourceExhausted` error.

prs.title: ci(rust): bump routine toolchains to 1.99.1
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Upgrade routine GitHub Actions, release, platform, audit, and local CI toolchains to Rust 1.99.0.
  - Move generated Rust container builders to the 1.99 image tags and refresh registry digests from the canonical manifest, including Node and unchanged-tag Debian, distroless, and Alpine runtime base images.
  - Fix Rust 1.99 Clippy compatibility findings while preserving the declared workspace MSRV.
- **Scope boundary:** `Cargo.toml` remains unchanged at Rust 1.96.0. Historical changelog/audit entries and fixed-version release test fixtures remain historical or synthetic data rather than routine toolchain policy.
- **Blast radius:** CI, release builders, local CI containers, demo/relay image builds, and Windows test scope contracts use the newer routine compiler. No runtime behavior, configuration, API, permission, or security policy changes are intended.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9527

### What this does, simply

This keeps ZeroClaw's routine builds and checks on Rust 1.99.0, including pinned container builders that compile release images. The source compatibility floor remains Rust 1.96.0, so existing users are not required to upgrade their supported compiler. New compiler diagnostics are handled with behavior-preserving assertion changes and the `Atomic*::try_update` API, which has been stable since Rust 1.95; no new lint or deprecation allowances are added.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` - this is CI/toolchain configuration and compiler-lint maintenance with no user-facing workflow to exercise manually.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** No pending check is claimed as evidence. The local commands below cover the Rust 1.99 lint surface, the declared Rust 1.96 MSRV, affected atomic behavior, plugin egress behavior, architecture, Windows scope, and generated-installer surfaces.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local validation did not execute native macOS or Windows tests. Current-head platform and required CI runs provide that target-specific evidence once complete.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text

  bash scripts/ci/windows_test_scope.test.sh

  all generated installer/container surfaces: in sync
  ```

prs.title: feat(tools): add opt-in task-owned SSH transport reuse
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master.
- Propose an optional task-owned OpenSSH adapter: reuse one authenticated transport per resolved target/authentication route, including concurrent commands.
- Close transports on success, error, cancellation, broker death, and configurable idle expiration (default 1800 seconds). Active commands are not idle.
- Preserve configured aliases, SSH agent identities, host-key trust, stdin/stdout and remote exit codes. Refuse identity/trust/multiplexing overrides and unmanaged reconnect fallbacks.
- **Scope boundary:** Linux noninteractive SSH resource management only; no credential store, target authorization, firewall change or remote privilege change.
- **Blast radius:** default-off helper integration in task entry and shell environment; implementation lives in zeroclaw-tools and the optional adapter script.
- Related #11867. Draft pending maintainer ownership/configuration assessment, including any required bounded exception for the narrow transitional-runtime wiring. This PR does not grant itself an exception.

### What this does, simply

An agent issuing several SSH commands to one server should not repeatedly establish new connections or leave a shared master behind after its task. This adapter gives the task its own connection owner. A model does not have to remember a cleanup command, and a failed master does not silently create another TCP connection. Nothing is enabled in an existing installation until the operator explicitly configures the helper and managed PATH wrapper.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interfaces exercised:** shell commands inside the shared task runtime; no graphical UI changes.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Linux, Python 3.10+, OpenSSH, util-linux setpriv with pdeathsig; an authorized test host and existing SSH trust/agent. Follow `scripts/ssh/README.md`.
- **Steps to run:** `python3 scripts/ssh/test_ssh_task.py`; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib task_ssh`. Execute two commands to the same host, compare the master PID, then complete/cancel the owner; separately kill the helper and test a short idle interval.
- **Expected after:** one master for repeated/concurrent calls to an equivalent endpoint; every task-owned master closes at task end or broker death; idle expiration does not interrupt active commands.
- **Prior behavior:** independent shell calls establish independent SSH connections; unmanaged masters have no task-owned cleanup contract.

### How I tested

- `python scripts/ssh/test_ssh_task.py`: `Ran 6 tests ... OK`. Covers reuse, overlapping leases, 1800-second idle boundary, active commands, immediate cleanup, failed-connect caching, option rejection, and authentication-route isolation.
- Formatter and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Prototype integration on Linux with two authorized test hosts: four commands; repeated same-host command reused the master PID; remote `exit 7` returned 7; all masters exited after owner EOF. Repeated with forced broker death: all masters exited through Linux parent-death signaling. No private identities or infrastructure details are included here.
- Exact-head public-helper integration subsequently passed owner EOF cleanup, forced broker-death cleanup, same-host reuse, remote exit status preservation, and idle expiration with a short test interval (production default remains 1800 seconds). `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib task_ssh` also passed locally: `2 passed; 0 failed`, covering normal/error completion and cancellation. Rust owner tests are additionally covered by the successful exact-head CI Test job. This PR remains draft for maintainer ownership/configuration review.
- **CI checks relied on:** exact-head CI completed without failures, including Test, Lint, Format, Installer Drift and Repository Structure. These cover Rust lifecycle tests, compilation/lint, formatting and generated-catalog drift.
- **Known coverage gap:** none for the tested Linux deployment path. An authenticated daemon WebSocket smoke executed two distinct read-only shell SSH calls to the same authorized test host, observed the runtime SSH owner, received remote evidence and confirmed zero remaining task scopes after completion. No external notification was sent. Other deployment layouts/platforms are not claimed as manually tested.
- **Visual interface evidence:** exact plain-text Python result above; no graphical surface change.
- **Tested revision/evidence:** initial draft diff; prototype integration is explicitly not claimed as exact-head validation.
- **Skipped commands:** full workspace suite pending scoped checks and ownership review.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. Opt-in process/control sockets in a service-user-owned 0700 directory; no privilege elevation. The helper executable must be operator-controlled.
- New external network calls? No new endpoint authority; existing authorized SSH calls are multiplexed.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Existing OpenSSH configuration and agent remain authoritative; no private-key export or new vault.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. SSH failure feedback remains untrusted tool output and cannot grant execution or widen authorization.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes; default off. Once enabled, the managed wrapper intentionally supports bounded noninteractive SSH options and requires a task owner.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Initial opt-in `ZEROCLAW_SSH_TASK_HELPER` and `ZEROCLAW_SSH_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS`; runtime-owned task/state-directory environment. Maintainer feedback on the final configuration shape is requested.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Upgrade steps:** install the optional adapter and service-local wrapper, set the helper path/idle interval, retain existing SSH agent/trust, and restart. See the README for limitations.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback:** remove the helper setting and service-local PATH wrapper, restart, or revert the PR.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** unset `ZEROCLAW_SSH_TASK_HELPER`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** helper readiness/cleanup errors, managed SSH exit 255, unexpected master count or remaining task-owned masters.

prs.title: fix(agent): stop repeated calls before dispatch and retain closeout
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master.
- Refuse exact-repeat calls before dispatch after the existing detector threshold, including repeats within a parallel batch. Failed attempts now participate in the detector.
- Preserve advisory handling of equal outputs from different arguments: empty searches and silent commands alone must not terminate a valid investigation.
- Retain every completed tool outcome before closing the tool phase. Reuse the existing bounded tools-free summary path to distinguish verified work, failures and pending actions.
- **Scope boundary:** no retry-limit increase, new remediation authority, SSH implementation, or turn engine. The independent time-gated aggregate-output guard is unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** shared tool-loop preparation, result collection and graceful closeout. Disabled detection and ignored tools retain their opt-outs; error-at-cap callers retain a typed stop.
- Closes #11866.

### What this does, simply

When a tool keeps making the same failing request, the old code logs that it blocked the call but continues executing repeats. Eventually it aborts and discards the terminal tool round. This change stops another identical dispatch and lets the agent report the work it actually completed instead of returning only the circuit-breaker exception.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interfaces exercised:** shared runtime used by CLI, web and messaging channels; regression fixtures exercise the tool-loop seams without external services.
- **Setup / preconditions:** default loop detection; a repeatable tool exempt from ordinary deduplication; provider requests identical arguments repeatedly.
- **Steps to run:** run `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::turn` and `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib loop_detector`; exercise a mock provider returning repeated calls and a tool returning a connection failure.
- **Expected after:** the fourth identical dispatch is refused before execution at default thresholds, terminal outcomes remain available, and the tool phase ends with a tools-free closeout.
- **Prior behavior:** execution continues after a logged block, failed outcomes bypass the detector, and a later break drops the terminal round.

### How I tested

Review follow-up (f361da7ab): carry the preflight gate decision as a batch-local fact rather than reconstructing it from later detector state; drain already-queued SOP work through the existing authorized driver before closeout; render refusals through the existing Fluent key. Two full-loop regressions cover a hook-cancelled sibling before a refused repeat and a completed sibling that queues a SOP step.

- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --config skip_children=true` on changed Rust files: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Added regressions for preflight thresholds, disabled detection, parallel-batch suppression and hook abandonment, repeated failed outcomes, and retaining completed results.
- After recovering the build filesystem, `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::turn` passed: `380 passed; 0 failed`. Includes the provider-boundary regression asserting exactly one tools-free closeout with a visible stop reason. The separate detector suite passed: `28 passed; 0 failed`.
- **CI checks relied on:** new-head CI is pending. Local turn tests passed (380) and detector tests passed (28). The previous head had a dependency-download HTTP 502 before opt-in tests; this revision triggers a fresh run.
- **Known coverage gap:** new-head full CI and an actual channel closeout capture remain pending. Equal outputs from different arguments remain advisory, covered by the retained regression.
- **Visual interface evidence:** pending exact plain-text closeout evidence; no graphical layout change.
- **Tested revision/evidence:** f361da7ab; focused runtime suites and local formatter/whitespace checks. No real-channel closeout evidence claimed.
- **Skipped commands:** no local full workspace suite; focused runtime suites cover the changed loop boundaries while full upstream CI remains pending.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No new endpoint. Yes to one already-supported tools-free summary request on this closeout path, bounded by existing budget, timeout and cancellation checks.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Guard feedback is generated by the runtime; tool outputs remain untrusted evidence. The closeout instruction explicitly forbids retries and unverified success claims, and the summary request contains no tools.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for config and API consumers; deliberately stops repeated unsuccessful/blocked work earlier.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new setting; new localized guard/closeout text.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback:** revert this PR's commit and rebuild.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** existing loop detection enable/ignore settings; no new bypass.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** unexpectedly early loop closeout or missing tool outcomes; inspect loop-detector events and tool history.

prs.title: feat(channels): add configurable XMPP/Prosody channel with optional OMEMO
prs.body:
## Summary



- **Base branch:** `master`.

- Add a first-class, opt-in `channel-xmpp` adapter for direct XMPP conversations, including Prosody. Inbound messages and replies use the existing channel supervisor and agent runtime, rather than an HTTP bridge or a separate agent loop.

- Expose account JID, server, port, Direct TLS or mandatory STARTTLS, masked password, resource, limits, interpreter and optional OMEMO settings through the schema-driven WebUI. The channel page's **Allowed users** tab creates alias-scoped canonical authorization policies and edits allowed/blocked users without a second allowlist.

- Require verified TLS in both transport modes. Optional OMEMO requires manually pinned device fingerprints, persists identity/ratchet state per alias and never downgrades to plaintext.

- **Scope boundary:** direct one-to-one text; no MUC, attachments, MAM, carbons or OMEMO v2. No deployment-specific hosts, ports, accounts, credentials or server provisioning.

- **Blast radius:** additive configuration/attribution metadata, feature-gated channel registration/runtime wiring, and one WebUI tab scoped to XMPP aliases. Existing listeners and the shared agent loop are unchanged.



Closes #9814



### What this does, simply



Operators who already have an XMPP server can bind a ZeroClaw agent to an account and converse with it from authorized accounts. Server address and JID domain are independent: the former selects the TCP destination and the latter remains the TLS service identity. Both STARTTLS and Direct TLS are selectable, and changing protocol does not silently change the configured port.



The Rust adapter owns the normal `Channel` lifecycle and authorization. An embedded, isolated Python transport worker uses Slixmpp for XMPP and an optional slixmpp-omemo backend for legacy OMEMO. It does not call the gateway or run models/tools. Python dependencies must be installed explicitly; Cargo does not install them. Missing dependencies fail closed.



The optional **slixmpp-omemo backend is AGPL-3.0-only**. It is not vendored. This dependency/license tradeoff is explicit in the installation guide and requirements file; TLS-only operation needs only MIT-licensed Slixmpp.



## Testing (required)



### How you can test



- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.

- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`; messaging `channel=xmpp`.

- **Setup / preconditions:** build with `channel-xmpp`, install the documented Python requirements in a dedicated venv, and use disposable XMPP accounts with a trusted server certificate. For OMEMO, enable server PEP/pubsub and verify device fingerprints out of band.

- **Steps to run:** follow `docs/book/src/channels/xmpp.md`; create an XMPP alias in Config, enter the connection fields, authorize bare JIDs under Allowed users, bind the channel to an enabled agent, enable the listener and reload. Send a direct message from an authorized account and compare with an unauthorized account. Repeat with STARTTLS and Direct TLS. Enable OMEMO and verify that unencrypted/untrusted traffic is refused.

- **Expected on this branch (after):** the channel and settings are available; authorized text reaches the common agent runtime and replies use XMPP. Empty policy denies everyone. Encrypted mode refuses plaintext fallback.

- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no XMPP channel/configuration/transport is available.



### How I tested

Review follow-up (37275ff8c): the adapter now identifies its accepted one-to-one messages as direct chats, avoiding unintended reply-intent classification. Worker frames are explicitly UTF-8 bytes rather than ASCII escapes, keeping maximum-length Unicode bodies within the existing 512 KiB frame bound independently of process locale. The Playwright evidence script uses a literal loopback URL instead of an environment-supplied navigation target.

Focused validation for this revision: three Python bridge tests passed, including 64,000 non-BMP characters, worst-case escaped controls and successful decoding of the following frame; two Rust XMPP adapter tests passed, including direct-message classification after authorization/encryption checks. Rustfmt, Node syntax checking and `git diff --check` passed. New-head CI is pending; no additional live deployment or end-to-end server test is claimed for this follow-up.


OMEMO receive-trust regression (4384a374515f): the real-server integration test reproduces the failure with the previous bridge (cached DISTRUSTED device, then add its fingerprint and receive before any outbound message). The patched bridge passes this regression and inbound pin revocation. Direct TLS, mandatory STARTTLS, certificate rejection, persistent OMEMO identity, bidirectional encryption, plaintext rejection, and outbound trust revocation also pass.

```text
PASS newly pinned cached-distrusted device receives before first outbound
PASS removed pin blocks inbound before first outbound
PASS revoked trust blocks outbound without plaintext fallback
```




- Focused Linux Rust tests: configuration round trips, disabled partial configuration, password secrecy metadata, authorization before dispatch, required encryption, alias attribution and offline/unauthorized sends. Passed on the independent `master` base, including an isolated no-default-features channel build. Registry tests (2) and the channel-migration inventory regression (1) also passed.

- Real isolated Prosody 13 on loopback, disposable accounts and a temporary CA: both TLS modes, rejection of an untrusted certificate, authenticated OMEMO round trips, identity persistence after restart, rejection of plaintext in required-encryption mode, and revocation without downgrade all passed.

- Python helper unit tests: 2 passed. New guide Markdown lint: 0 errors. Frontend TypeScript and Vite production build passed on the independent source, and the final Chrome fixture run includes creating an initially empty authorization policy. Focused Clippy passed with `-D warnings`.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the clean generated dashboard contract (`cargo web check`) and Web Permission Tests passed on the initial code revision. The final head reruns the required suite and adds an isolated XMPP feature test lane. No claim is made that every final-head CI job has finished.

- **Known CI coverage gap:** the Python dependencies and real Prosody/OMEMO matrix are opt-in local tests. Native Windows worker execution and an actual model-provider conversation were not verified.

- **Commands run and tail output:**



```text

cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test xmpp

test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed

cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-xmpp xmpp --lib

test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed

cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-xmpp --lib -- -D warnings

Finished dev profile

python crates/zeroclaw-channels/tests/test_xmpp_bridge.py

Ran 2 tests ... OK

markdownlint-cli2 docs/book/src/channels/xmpp.md

Summary: 0 error(s)

```



- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Actual TLS/OMEMO transport against the isolated server. WebUI interactions use a privacy-safe local API fixture with the real page renderer; they are not a live production/gateway or model-provider test.

- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot.

- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `cf9df9215a40e5a0a447df072adf7602b2af9c2d`, `surface=web`, English locale, desktop 1440x1000 and mobile 390x844.

- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Verification notes, reproducible UI harness and screenshots](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/cf9df9215a40e5a0a447df072adf7602b2af9c2d/.pr-evidence/xmpp.md).

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** protocol saved independently of port; replacement password editor remained blank/masked; OMEMO and enabled controls wrote their schema fields; the page created a scoped `peer_groups.*.channel = "xmpp.<alias>"` policy and allowed-user edits wrote its `external_peers`. Only the authorization fields are edited by that scoped form. No page JavaScript errors or mobile page overflow in the fixture run.

- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full workspace/all-platform tests are left to repository CI; focused local checks cover the feature and real transport gap. A clean generated-contract check relies on CI because the local Windows generator cache contained missing build-script artifacts. The first CI run identified the migration inventory, expanded all-feature installer lists and one Clippy expression; all three are addressed in the final update.



## Security & Privacy Impact (required)



- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Enabling a listener launches the configured interpreter and creates private per-alias SQLite state. Interpreter/configuration remains an operator-controlled administrative capability.

- New external network calls? **Yes.** Only the configured XMPP endpoint and XMPP protocol discovery/pubsub operations; TLS certificates are verified and there is no plaintext transport or trust-all option.

- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** The account password uses the existing encrypted secret machinery and secret-aware editor, and crosses only private stdin to the worker, not argv/environment/logs. OMEMO keys remain in private per-alias state; confidential backup requirements are documented.

- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Only fictitious reserved-example identities and disposable loopback fixtures.

- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** XMPP text is a new untrusted input surface. Canonical peer policy is checked before dispatch to the shared agent runtime; existing tool/approval policies continue to apply. OMEMO protects transport to the bot, not plaintext subsequently sent to a configured model provider.



## Compatibility (required)



- Backward compatible? **Yes.** Additive schema; no configured listener is enabled by default.

- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** New `channels.xmpp.<alias>` settings and Cargo feature; no existing setting is renamed.

- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**

- **Upgrade steps:** no action for existing deployments. XMPP users opt into the build feature, install the documented Python dependencies, configure the alias and canonical authorization/agent binding, then enable it. OMEMO is separately optional and requires verified pins. The transport matrix is validated on Linux; native Windows execution is not claimed.



## Rollback



- **Fast rollback command/path:** disable the alias using its header toggle and reload; or revert this PR. Preserve the private OMEMO database if restoring the same account later.

- **Feature flags or config toggles:** omit `channel-xmpp`, set the alias `enabled=false`, or set `omemo_enabled=false` when intentionally choosing TLS-only chat.

- **Observable failure symptoms:** offline channel health, supervisor reconnect/backoff, generic bridge/TLS/authentication failures, or a send error without plaintext fallback. No stanza bodies, passwords or identity keys are logged for diagnosis.

prs.title: feat(config): control OpenRouter balance reporting in web settings
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add per-alias `credit_balance_enabled` in the OpenRouter Connection tab. Reporting requires explicit opt-in and defaults to disabled.
  - Keep the Management API Key in the same schema-driven form. Saved secrets show a constant `********` indicator; Change starts an empty password input rather than retrieving the stored key.
  - Gate credit requests on the current typed config. Disabling reporting retains both credentials and does not disable inference.
  - Honor the configured `model_provider.openrouter` proxy with the existing five-second timeout, and identify the selected provider alias on the balance card.
  - Add config/API persistence and privacy tests, a secret-field interaction test, documentation, and full-dashboard screenshots.
- **Scope boundary:** This is the settings follow-up to the balance endpoint/card. It does not add spend accounting, change model routing, or deploy a release. The shared secret renderer now consistently shows a fixed mask for all populated secret fields.
- **Blast radius:** OpenRouter config/introspection, authenticated credits selection, and the shared web secret renderer. Other Rust changes only update test literals for the added config field.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #11845. This stacked branch retains that PR's implementation until the prerequisite lands. The incremental settings change is commit [622a477b4](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/commit/622a477b4482d091039953a7cfab770fa7afc52e).

### What this does, simply

Operators can open Config → Model providers → OpenRouter → their alias → Connection, enter a separate Management API Key, and turn the balance card on or off. A previously saved key appears as eight asterisks, independent of its actual length. Changing it edits a new value; the browser never receives the saved credential. Turning reporting off keeps the key available for later use and leaves model inference working.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build the branch and its web assets; configure an OpenRouter alias used by an enabled agent. Use a disposable configuration and separate inference/Management API credentials for live verification.

- **Expected on this branch (after):** The key is masked after saving, the toggle persists, disabled reporting omits the card/returns 204 without a credits request, and both credentials remain configured. With reporting enabled and valid credentials, the existing balance card can appear.

prs.title: feat(dashboard): show OpenRouter credit balance
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds an optional, encrypted OpenRouter management API key, separate from the inference API key.
  - Adds an authenticated gateway endpoint that retrieves OpenRouter credit totals without exposing the management credential or upstream response to the browser, using the live configured proxy for `model_provider.openrouter` and the existing five-second timeout.
  - Shows an OpenRouter balance card in the web dashboard only when an enabled agent uses OpenRouter and the integration is configured and reachable.
  - Adds English and Portuguese UI strings and documents the optional configuration.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not change inference routing, model selection, billing, or other providers. It does not expose the management key to the dashboard.
- **Blast radius:** OpenRouter provider configuration, the authenticated web API, and the dashboard overview. Existing installations without `management_api_key` retain their current behavior and do not show the card.
- **Linked issue(s):** Supersedes #11231. Related #11204; this account-balance card does not repair per-request spend accounting.

### What this does, simply

OpenRouter users could configure inference but could not see their remaining credits in ZeroClaw. This change introduces a distinct management credential for the OpenRouter credits API, keeps that credential encrypted and server-side, and conditionally displays the returned credit balance on the dashboard. If OpenRouter is not actively configured, the management key is absent, or the request fails, the endpoint returns no content and the dashboard card stays hidden.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Configure an enabled OpenRouter agent, its inference API key, and a separate `management_api_key`; start the gateway and pair the dashboard.
- **Steps to run:** Open the overview. On a test installation, repeat with the management key missing or invalid and with the OpenRouter agent disabled.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Credit totals appear only for an active, configured, reachable integration. Missing/inactive/unavailable integrations return `204` and hide the card. Unauthenticated requests return `401`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** No account-credit endpoint or balance card.

### How I tested

Review follow-up (578386d4b): 11 focused credits tests passed on Linux with Rust 1.98.0. Nine new cases exercise the public handler through the HTTP route and real bearer pairing: missing/wrong auth, numeric totals and credential privacy, absent configuration, upstream HTTP failures, malformed/missing JSON, connection failure, service-scoped HTTP proxying, HTTPS CONNECT and invalid-proxy failure without direct fallback. The controlled upstream override is task-local and compiled only in tests; the production API URL remains fixed. Rustfmt and git diff --check passed. No new browser capture or live deployment is claimed for this follow-up; the UI code is unchanged.

Refreshed against master `8faf3a89f`. Repaired the four findings in the original review: deterministic `sort_by_key` and direct struct initialization in the credits tests. No lint-suppression attributes were added.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0

git diff --check upstream/master
# exit 0

npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
# added 226 packages; exit 0
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** new-head CI is pending. The earlier workspace Lint and Web Permission Tests results apply to 44e60879f only; fresh local evidence for 578386d4b is the 11-test HTTP/proxy suite above.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Strict local Windows Clippy was attempted, both with and without dependency linting. Files identical to master block it with Windows-only diagnostics: `resolved_launcher`, `resolved_shell`, the nested conditional in `windows_key_file.rs`, and `replace_parent` in `api_config.rs`. The Windows linker also emits a localized import-library notice. These platform limitations are disclosed, not suppressed or bundled as unrelated fixes. The original focused gateway credits tests passed: `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway openrouter_credits --lib` (2 passed, 0 failed). The credential-encryption test also passed: `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config openrouter_management_key_encrypts_and_decrypts --lib` (1 passed, 0 failed).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The running authenticated dashboard renders the balance card; reload retains authentication; authenticated credits return numeric totals; unauthenticated access returns `401`. We continue using the integration successfully in our own deployment.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real browser screenshots with financial text lines masked before writing the PNGs; no generated illustrations or isolated component mocks.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The renderer introduced in `0f965eee` is unchanged by this refresh and lint repair. Captures were taken on 2026-10-18 in visible Chrome at 1440 x 1000 and 390 x 844. The deployment reports gateway 0.8.6 and uses a compatibility adapter for its credits route. These historical screenshots prove the unchanged UI and deployed use; the new native handler evidence is the 11-test HTTP/proxy suite above. Details are in the provenance note.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**
  - [Desktop screenshot](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/44e60879fd57f6f9bf693528e481de6e878244e0/.pr-evidence/pr-11231-openrouter-balance-desktop.png)
  - [Mobile screenshot](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/44e60879fd57f6f9bf693528e481de6e878244e0/.pr-evidence/pr-11231-openrouter-balance-mobile.png)

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Opened the overview, verified the visible card, refreshed, and scrolled to it at mobile width. No JavaScript page errors or horizontal document overflow were observed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** A full local Linux workspace gate is not claimed; this workstation hits the baseline Windows diagnostics above. Required Linux CI remains the full gate. A new local web build is not claimed; the required web typecheck covers the refreshed schema and TypeScript contract.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **Yes**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The gateway makes a fixed-host HTTPS request to OpenRouter's credits API with a short timeout. The distinct management key uses the existing encrypted configuration path, is never returned to the browser, and upstream bodies are not logged. The endpoint is protected by the gateway bearer authentication and returns only normalized numeric totals.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Existing users need no action. To enable the optional card, add `management_api_key` to the relevant OpenRouter provider entry; omitting it preserves existing behavior.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Remove `management_api_key` to disable the integration; existing inference credentials are unaffected. Revert the balance feature if rollback is needed. No database migration is introduced.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #11231 by @CastelloBrancoTecnologia.
- Scope materially carried forward: The original optional encrypted management credential, authenticated credits endpoint, dashboard card, localization, documentation, and tests.

prs.title: fix(security): split POSIX commands at substitution and subshell boundaries
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The shell command scanner split segments only at `;`, newlines, `|`, `||`, and `&&`, and split words only at whitespace. The closing `)` of `$(...)`, `<(...)`, `>(...)`, or a subshell, and the closing backtick of `` `...` ``, stayed glued to the last inner word. `x=$(cmd 2>/dev/null)` therefore produced the redirect target `/dev/null)`. That is not the null device, so with the default forbidden `/dev` the shell tool refused it: `Path blocked by security policy: /dev/null)`. #11469's exact null-device matching is correct and unchanged; the bad token came from the tokenizer.
  - Under the POSIX dialect, `split_unquoted_segments` now treats command substitution, process substitution, backticks, and subshells as segment boundaries, tracked on a frame stack so nesting and substitution inside double quotes work. The inner command becomes its own segment, and the enclosing word keeps a `$()`-style placeholder.
  - Every character other than those delimiters still lands in exactly one segment (heredoc bodies aside), including for unbalanced input. An unterminated `$(` still flushes the command around it, and a stray `)` (for example a `case` pattern terminator) is a boundary. A misparse can over-split but cannot drop text from the scan.
  - `<<` inside `$((...))` is a shift, not a heredoc. Previously `echo $((8<<1))` opened a heredoc that hid the following lines from the scan, though bash runs them. A command substitution nested inside arithmetic is ordinary shell syntax again, so its heredocs are recognized.
  - A substitution closes only at the `)` bash treats as its closer. A `case` pattern terminator, a `)` inside `${...}`, or a `)` inside a `#` comment no longer ends `$(...)` early. Closing early would restore the enclosing quote state and hide the rest of the inner command inside one quoted argument. Comment text is not syntax until the newline, so an apostrophe in a comment no longer opens a quote that hides the next line (separators inside comments still split, conservatively). This addresses review feedback in 4935b7a82.
  - The strict allowlist keeps rejecting unquoted POSIX grouping parentheses, so `(git status)` is not newly accepted as `git status` as a side effect of the split. Escaped and quoted parentheses (`find . \( ... \)`, `grep -E '(a|b)'`) are still allowed.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change null-device classification (`is_null_device`, `is_safe_device_redirect_target`), the safe-redirect regexes, forbidden-path defaults, allowlists, or sandbox grants. `cmd.exe` and PowerShell splitting are unchanged. Not addressed here: `$(...)` inside an unquoted-delimiter heredoc body (bash runs it; the scanner still skips heredoc bodies by design), and `cmd.exe` parenthesized blocks.
- **Blast radius:** Every consumer of `split_unquoted_segments` under the POSIX dialect: the workspace path scan (`forbidden_path_argument*`) used by the shell, skill shell, and cron paths; `command_risk_level`; `is_command_allowed`; and `is_command_explicitly_allowed`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11469. Related #11823, Related #11824 (follow-ups for the scope this PR leaves out), Related #11825 (`zeroclaw-tools` test flake seen while validating).

### What this does, simply

Before running a shell command, ZeroClaw splits it into the individual commands it contains and checks each file path it mentions. That splitter didn't understand `$(...)`, backticks, or `(...)`, which are how shells run one command inside another. So in `x=$(ls 2>/dev/null)` it read the redirect target as `/dev/null)`, including the closing paren, and refused it as a forbidden path, even though #11469 made `/dev/null` always allowed. This was easy to hit, because `$(something 2>/dev/null)` is a very common shell idiom.

This PR teaches the splitter where those inner commands start and end. The inner command is checked on its own, so `2>/dev/null` inside it works again. As a side effect, commands hidden inside `$(...)` are now actually checked: a forbidden path inside `"$(...)"` is blocked, and `x=$(rm -rf ./build)` is rated high risk instead of low. Commands that the strict allowlist rejected before are still rejected.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** the `shell` tool, through any surface (`cli`, `tui`, or `web`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** Unix host, default `forbidden_paths` (includes `/dev`), `allowed_commands = ["*"]`, `block_high_risk_commands = false`
- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to run each of these with the shell tool: `x=$(echo a 2>/dev/null); echo "$x"`, then `(echo a 2>/dev/null)`, then ``echo "`echo a 2>/dev/null`"``
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Each command runs and prints `a`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Each is refused with `Path blocked by security policy: /dev/null)` (or ``/dev/null` `` for the backtick form).

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** CI Required Gate (format, lint, Linux workspace tests, MSRV, Windows/macOS compile checks). The change is in `zeroclaw-config` policy parsing, plus one runtime shell-tool test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None specific. The behavior change is gated to `ShellDialect::Posix`, and a new test pins `cmd.exe` splitting as unchanged.
- **Commands run and tail output:** On `4935b7a82` (base `cdefa0d0a`), with the CI toolchain `1.98.0`:

```sh
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
FMT_OK

$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 22s

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
test result: ok. 1799 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
test result: ok. 5777 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

# New end-to-end test against master's policy.rs (fix removed):
test tools::shell::tests::shell_allows_null_redirects_inside_posix_substitutions ... FAILED
x=$(echo zc-subst 2>/dev/null); echo "$x" must run, got: ToolResult { success: false, ..., error: Some("Path blocked by security policy: /dev/null)") }

# New policy tests against the unmodified tokenizer:
posix_segments_split_at_substitution_boundaries ... FAILED   left: ["x=$(echo a)"]
command_risk_level_sees_commands_inside_posix_substitutions ... FAILED   left: Low  right: High
forbidden_path_argument_allows_safe_devices_inside_posix_substitutions ... FAILED   left: Some("/dev/null)")
forbidden_path_argument_scans_inside_posix_substitutions ... FAILED   left: Some("/dev/nullx)")  right: Some("/dev/nullx")
```

- **Tests added or changed:**
  - `posix_segments_split_at_substitution_boundaries`: segment output for `$(...)`, `"$(...)"`, backticks, subshells, `<(...)`/`>(...)`, nesting, `$((...))`, unterminated and unbalanced input, quoted and escaped literals, and quotes inside a substitution.
  - `forbidden_path_argument_allows_safe_devices_inside_posix_substitutions`: 18 forms with `/dev/null` redirects inside substitutions, subshells, backticks, and process substitution, all allowed.
  - `forbidden_path_argument_scans_inside_posix_substitutions`: lookalikes (`/dev/nullx`, `/dev/null/../../etc/passwd`) and forbidden paths inside substitutions stay blocked and are reported without the closing `)`. prs.title: fix(tunnel): supervise and verify the tailscale gateway serve process
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The gateway's `tailscale serve|funnel --https=443` child was spawned in `TailscaleTunnel::start()` and never waited for. When it exited (port 443 still held by another foreground session, or a lost serve-config etag race with the `--tcp` forwarders started right after it), it stayed `<defunct>` for the life of the daemon. `health_check` still reported it alive because `tokio::process::Child::id()` stays `Some` until the child is polled to completion, and `start()` had already advertised a URL that nothing served.
  - The gateway serve process is now owned by the same watcher the TCP forwarders already use (`TcpForwarder` generalised to `ServeProcess`). An exit is reaped and logged with its stderr, stop or drop kills and reaps it, and `health_check` reflects the real state.
  - `start()` returns the URL only once `tailscale serve status --json` shows a new foreground session proxying `443` to `http://127.0.0.1:<local_port>`. Otherwise it fails with the process's stderr, and the gateway's existing `Err` path falls back to local-only.
  - `listener already exists for port N` (observed on Tailscale 1.104.1) is now retryable alongside the existing etag-conflict case, bounded to five attempts (about 2.5s of linear backoff). A previous generation's session being torn down across a reload is waited out; a holder that stays is reported, not spun on.
  - Serve stdout (an unread banner) is discarded instead of piped, so it can never fill a pipe and block the process.
- **Scope boundary:** No other tunnel provider, no change to the `Tunnel` trait or the gateway crate, no automatic respawn of an exited serve process, and no public exposure change (WSS/enrollment stay tailnet-only). Serve processes orphaned by a daemon that dies without running destructors (crash, SIGKILL) are **not** addressed here: they keep holding the port, and with this PR the next start reports that clearly instead of going defunct. A parent-death signal needs a dedicated spawner thread (Linux `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` is per forking thread, and tokio's `block_in_place` can retire such a thread), so it is left for a separate change.
- **Blast radius:** Tailscale tunnel users only. Behaviour change: if 443 cannot be published, `start()` now fails, so the gateway takes its existing "Tunnel failed to start, falling back to local-only" path and does not go on to publish WSS/enrollment via `publish_tcp_services`. Before, those were published next to a dead 443 proxy. Gateway startup may also wait up to about 2.5s (retries) or 5s (apply timeout) per serve process when tailscaled is slow or the port is held.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11530, Related #11531

### What this does, simply

With the Tailscale tunnel, ZeroClaw starts a `tailscale serve` process to put the gateway on the tailnet at `https://<node>`. If that process failed right away, for example because the port was still in use, ZeroClaw never noticed. The dead process lingered as a "defunct" entry in `ps`, health checks said all was well, and the startup output printed a URL that didn't work. This PR has ZeroClaw watch that process the same way it already watches the WSS/enrollment forwarders. It confirms that Tailscale is actually serving the gateway before printing the URL, waits briefly for a port that is still being released, cleans up the process if it exits, and logs why. It does not restart a process that dies later, and it does not yet clean up serve processes left behind by a daemon that crashed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw daemon` with `[tunnel] tunnel_provider = "tailscale"`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** Linux node logged into a tailnet (`tailscale up`), serve permitted for the operator (`tailscale set --operator=$USER`), `[tunnel] tunnel_provider = "tailscale"`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. In another terminal, hold the gateway port: `tailscale serve --https=443 8080` (leave it running).
  2. Start `zeroclaw daemon`.
  3. `ps -eo pid,stat,cmd | grep 'tailscale serve'`
  4. Stop the holder from step 1 and restart the daemon.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Step 2 prints `Tunnel failed to start: tailscale serve --https=443 <port> did not publish the gateway: exited (exit status: 1) after 5 attempt(s): ... listener already exists for port 443` and falls back to local-only. Step 3 shows no `<defunct>` entry. After step 4, `Tunnel active: https://<node>` and `tailscale serve status` shows the gateway proxy.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Step 2 prints `Tunnel active: https://<node>` even though nothing serves it, and step 3 shows `tailscale serve --https=443 <port> <defunct>` for as long as the daemon runs.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The CI `Clippy` job (`scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace`, Rust 1.98.0, `--features ci-all`, `-D warnings`) and the test jobs cover the changed Rust file. I ran the same clippy script locally on this head as well (below).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No CI job runs a real `tailscaled`. tailscaled's behaviour is pinned by the manual check below, and the tests use `sh` stand-ins for the process plus status JSON captured from a live 1.104.1 node.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
# clean (no diff)

$ RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.98.0 RUNNER_TEMP=$PWD/target/ci-tmp \
    bash scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace --summary-title "Lint diagnostics" --log-name cargo-clippy.log
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 3m 20s
# exit 0; 0 warning/error lines in cargo-clippy.log

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tunnel::
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::gateway_serve_exit_is_reaped_not_left_defunct ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::dropping_the_tunnel_kills_and_reaps_its_gateway_serve ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::gateway_sessions_match_only_an_https_proxy_to_the_local_port ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::held_port_is_retryable_but_other_failures_are_not ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::start_forwarder_waits_out_a_port_that_is_being_released ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::start_forwarder_reports_a_port_that_stays_held ... ok
test result: ok. 126 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5586 filtered out; finished in 0.33s
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Against a live Tailscale 1.104.1 tailscaled, on a scratch port (19999) so the running daemon's sessions were untouched: (1) a second foreground `tailscale serve --tcp` on a port held by another foreground session exits 1 immediately with `sending serve config: updating config: listener already exists for port 19999`, which is the string matched here; (2) after the holder is SIGKILLed, an immediate respawn gets the port (a new session appeared within 1s and held it until its timeout), which is why bounded retry is enough for a releasing holder; (3) a live `serve --https=443 42617` session is stored as `TCP["443"].HTTPS = true` plus `Web["<magicdns>:443"].Handlers["/"].Proxy = "http://127.0.0.1:42617"`, the shape the applied-check matches. **Not verified:** a full daemon start/reload cycle on this branch against real tailscaled (I didn't interrupt the running daemon), `funnel` mode against a live node, and non-Linux hosts.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`. No rendered interface changed; the only user-visible change is the existing tunnel start/fallback lines and log events.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** this branch's head; `cargo test` / `run_clippy.sh` on Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0 (clippy) and 1.99.0 (tests).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full `cargo test` for the workspace was not run locally; CI covers it, and the change is confined to `tunnel/tailscale.rs`, whose 126 module tests ran. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on local rustc 1.99.0 fails on lints new in 1.99 (`needless_borrows_for_generic_args` in `zeroclaw-providers`, deprecated `fetch_update` in `zeroclaw-tools` and `zeroclaw-runtime` rpc). Those are pre-existing and outside this diff, so I used CI's pinned 1.98.0 script instead, which is clean.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`. It adds local `tailscale serve status --json` calls to the local tailscaled during gateway startup, the same probe the forwarders already use.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`. Fixtures use the captured serve-status shape with placeholder node names and addresses.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`. No config, CLI or trait change. The one behaviour change, where an unpublishable 443 now fails `start()`, is described under Blast radius.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk PRs: `git revert <sha>` is the plan unless otherwise noted.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` (single commit, single file).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Setting `[tunnel] tunnel_provider = "none"` avoids the path entirely.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `Tunnel failed to start: tailscale ... did not publish the gateway` on startup; WARN events `tailscale did not publish the gateway` and `tailscale serve exited after publication` (attrs: `service`, `status`, `stderr`, `command`).

## Summary

### What this does, simply
The shipped REPL reads stdin directly and previously skipped the IUTF8 setup used by channel input. The guard makes multibyte backspace behavior consistent.

## Testing

Starting with `-iutf8`, one Backspace after 中 allowed `/help` to be recognized; `/quit` restored `-iutf8`. This is the author-reported result.
