prs.title: feat(a2a): extract A2A protocol core into a dedicated zeroclaw-a2a crate
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Extract the A2A protocol core out of `zeroclaw-api` / `zeroclaw-tools` / `zeroclaw-gateway` into a single `zeroclaw-a2a` crate, so the wire model, outbound client, and inbound protocol handling have one ownership home instead of four, and the protocol layer doesn't depend on any host config module.
  - Follow the official `a2a-rs` layering: the crate defines `A2aExecutor` / `AgentCardProducer` / `A2aPeerSource` as host-implemented seams and keeps its own config types, letting hosts adapt + inject.
  - Wire moves from `zeroclaw_api::a2a_wire` to `zeroclaw_a2a::wire`; `api` stops re-exporting it.
  - Hosts adapt through `A2aPeerSourceHost` (implements the protocol-layer `A2aPeerSource` over the host's **live** config handle) and the standalone `a2a_router` defaults closed to task operations.
- **Scope boundary:** Organization-only extraction — no new A2A protocol capability, no config-field change. Streaming and inbound task management are explicitly out of scope. The extraction preserves the pre-existing live/lazy host behavior (see below); it does **not** intentionally change runtime behavior.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-api` loses its `a2a_wire` module (import sites moved); consumers of `zeroclaw-tools` / `zeroclaw-gateway` / `zeroclaw-runtime` see no tool, route, or behavior change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #3566; Implements (RFC) #11254

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's A2A support previously lived in four crates, split by hosting crate rather than by protocol: the wire model in `zeroclaw-api`, the outbound client in `zeroclaw-tools`, and the inbound surface in `zeroclaw-gateway`. That made every A2A extension thread re-export paths across multiple manifests. This PR consolidates the A2A protocol core into one `zeroclaw-a2a` crate whose layout mirrors the official a2a-rs SDK, and keeps host-coupled glue (the 4 `a2a_*` tools, gateway card building + auth) in the host crates, adapted through `A2aExecutor` / `AgentCardProducer` / `A2aPeerSource`.

### Live configuration ownership (review follow-up)

The first revision of this PR snapshotted peers, decrypted tokens, and proxy policy at client-construction time. That regressed the behavior the pre-extraction client had via its live config handle: removing a peer, rotating a token, tightening private-host policy, or changing the proxy no longer took effect on a retained agent, and one peer with a corrupt credential disabled all four tools.

This revision restores live/lazy semantics through a single host-implemented seam, `A2aPeerSource`, consulted on **every** call:

- `peers()` returns the current peers with **raw** (undecrypted) token fields — no snapshot.
- `resolve_token()` decrypts **lazily**, for the resolved peer only — one broken credential can no longer disable the whole tool set.
- `proxy_policy()` is resolved per call, including the `tool.a2a` service-scope check, so a proxy scoped to another service (or disabled while its URL is configured) does not block A2A.
- `settings()` reads card-cache TTL / response cap / SSRF allowlists live.

The protocol crate depends on none of the host's config modules (it holds an `Arc<dyn A2aPeerSource>`), preserving the RFC's config boundary while keeping resolution host-owned and current-at-use.

## Testing (required)

### How I tested

- `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean, no warnings.
- `cargo +1.98.0 doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop` (Rustdoc warnings gate) — clean.
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-a2a` → `94 passed; 0 failed`
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib a2a` → `34 passed; 0 failed`
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib a2a_client` → `36 passed; 0 failed` (2 ignored = cross-harness external-peer tests)
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib a2a` → passed

The A2A conformance/security tests moved with the code. Previously dropped tests were restored except for `e2e_get_task_refuses_unmatched_task_id`, whose production guard remains intact. New boundary tests were added for the host adapter: lazy token decryption (encrypted / missing-dir / literal), disabled and other-service proxy scopes, live config reload (a removed peer disappears, settings follow), and the standalone catalog's `catalog` interface marker.

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — organization-only extraction; behavior matches the pre-extraction client.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-a2a --lib
  test result: ok. 94 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib a2a
  test result: ok. 34 passed; 0 failed
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib a2a_client
  test result: ok. 36 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The host source reads live config per call (verified by a reload test: publishing a config with a peer added/removed is reflected immediately); proxy policy honors the `tool.a2a` service scope; a standalone `a2a_router` rejects task injection without a configured admission check; the standalone catalog emits the `catalog` interface marker so a single published alias is not mistaken for a single agent by `select_interface`.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface change)

### CI note

The current required checks, including `Security`, pass for head `8ceca7ca1dedbcb330eed7147ccd3e64bda67e0c`. [Quality Gate run 38840628685](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38840628685) tested its merge with the recorded base.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No behavior change.** Peer-token decryption stays host-owned (`A2aPeerSourceHost`, via the canonical `SecretStore`) and is now performed lazily per resolved peer; the protocol layer only applies `${VAR}` interpolation to the plaintext it is handed.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Runtime, protocol and configuration behavior is preserved; Rust source compatibility changes.** Replace `zeroclaw_api::a2a_wire` imports with `zeroclaw_a2a::wire`. `A2aHttpClient::new` now accepts an `Arc<dyn A2aPeerSource>`, timeout and route cache instead of the previous host configuration, directory and encryption arguments; ZeroClaw host code uses `A2aPeerSourceHost::build_a2a_client`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert <sha>` is the plan. Organization-only extraction with no data/config surface; reverting the merge restores the prior layout.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A (no `Supersedes #` used).

prs.title: feat(session): extract the atomic session-ownership claim into a shared SessionBackend contract
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; the branch includes `master` through `05f9fe95d4` (#11232).
- **What changed and why:** Adds one shared atomic agent-ownership claim/adoption contract to `SessionBackend`, implemented by SQLite and consumed by RPC Chat admission, persistent WebSocket admission, and the operator migration command. A conflicting owner or ownerless transcript is refused before restoration/publication.
- Backends that cannot claim durable agent ownership are refused for empty and nonempty RPC Chat sessions, including operator/admin callers. This restores the uniform refusal requested in review and removes the stale-admin exception related to #11126. Persistent WebSocket admission uses the same fail-closed rule.
- WebSocket identity is fixed from the query or a generated UUID before the first client frame. The server sends its greeting without waiting for a client frame; a later `connect.session_id` may only echo that identity. Transcript read failures preserve master's `SESSION_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE` refusal and cannot become an empty restored session.
- The WebSocket also pins the agent incarnation it claimed under. The greeting still goes out immediately and the socket still holds no deletion lease while it waits for its first client frame; instead the handshake records the alias generation and refuses the connection with `AGENT_REPLACED` if a committed delete or rename advanced that alias before the first frame arrives. Without that fence, an operator could delete and recreate the alias while a socket waited, and the socket would restore the previous incarnation's transcript into the replacement agent under the replacement's provider and tools.
- Noncanonical display ids (anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, for example an id containing a dot) are refused before the session is reached, so a punctuation-distinct id can never collapse onto another session's key. This applies to resuming an existing session too; see the Compatibility section for what that means for pre-existing sessions. `session/new` refuses a supplied id at the top of the method, before the ownership probe reads the store, and the check also sits in the shared turn body, so `session/prompt` and `session/run-once` refuse their caller-supplied ids before any write.
- Adds `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership` to list or explicitly adopt legacy ownerless sessions, with localized CLI text and persisted-state/component regressions.
- Documents the durable state owner and the RPC Chat/WebSocket admission boundaries in the runtime state map and authentication chapter, including the remaining migration deletion race.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not resolve every stale-grant path in #11126 or implement the separate HTTP adapter in #8486. Existing principal authentication, current-master session admission/queueing, and transport boundaries remain the owners of their respective policy.
- **Blast radius:** The `SessionBackend` contract and its SQLite implementation, the gateway WebSocket admission gate (including its new agent-incarnation fence), RPC Chat admission (gated to `ChatMode::Chat`; ACP does not pass through it), the canonical session-key helpers, and the operator migration CLI. Backends without atomic claim support (JSONL and custom) refuse RPC Chat and WebSocket admission rather than degrading to a read-then-write.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9600 (ownership slice of the L2 `SessionBackend` contract), #10526, #8486, #8603, #8550, #11126. The remaining acceptance for #11126 is outside this PR.

### What this does, simply

Sessions are keyed by a caller-supplied id. Before this PR, that same key could be handed to a different agent, which would then restore someone else's transcript. This PR gives the session backend one atomic operation that means "claim this session for this agent, or refuse." RPC Chat, the WebSocket gateway, and the operator migration command all use it, so an admission either wins the claim or is refused before any transcript is read or shown to a client. A session that nobody owns yet can be handed over only by the explicit `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership` command, never by ordinary traffic.

The companion change is the WebSocket handshake. A connection now settles its identity immediately (from the query string, or a server-generated UUID) and receives its greeting before it sends anything. A later `connect` frame can echo that identity but cannot switch the session. Ids have to be simple (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`); an id that is not is refused outright, because two ids that differ only in punctuation must never share one memory scope.

Because identity is settled at the greeting while the transcript is used later, the handshake also records which incarnation of the agent it claimed under. Deleting or renaming an agent closes its incarnation and opens a new one; if that happens while a connection is still waiting for its first frame, the connection is refused instead of handing the old transcript to the new agent.

### Issue and solution

A caller-controlled session identifier must not overwrite another agent's ownership and then restore its transcript. The backend now performs a conditional ownership claim and returns explicit claimed/conflict/migration outcomes. Normal admission refuses unsupported ownership rather than assuming that an administrator can safely bypass an absent durable owner. Trusted migration has a separate atomic adoption operation.

The WebSocket path has an ordering gap that RPC does not: it claims and loads before the client speaks, but can only take lifecycle admission after the client's first frame. Recording the alias generation at claim time and comparing it after that frame closes the gap without making the greeting wait, and without holding a deletion lease for as long as a client may idle.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — real WebSocket greeting/error and RPC admission regressions exercise the repaired boundaries; CLI subprocess tests cover migration behavior in required CI.

### How I tested

- **Current revision:** `931d4fd1a737f11800a7587b05ab67e8c8c3eef7`. This merges `master` (`05f9fe95d4`) and adds three commits on top: the agent-generation fence and its regression test; the canonical-id check moving into the shared turn body, followed by a review follow-up commit (the SQLite adoption transaction closed on every path, the `session/new` id check moved ahead of the ownership probe, an unused `SessionStore` method dropped, and the WebSocket ownership gate narrowed to the already-resolved session id); and documentation.
- **Code-tested revision:** the same `931d4fd1a737f11800a7587b05ab67e8c8c3eef7` — production code and tests are identical at the current revision.
- **Current documentation checks:** `bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` (0 errors) and `git diff --check` passed. `docs_links_gate.sh` needs `rg`, which is not installed in this environment, so it was not run for this revision; the documentation changes are prose inside existing files and add no links.
- **Commands run and tail output:** At the current revision, all with `umask 0022`:
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings` — exits 0.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime` — 5625 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets` — 657 passed in the lib target, plus 5 and 9 in the auxiliary targets; 0 failed.
  - `cargo test --test architecture` — 54 passed, 1 failed (see the gap below).
  - `cargo test --test component` — 272 passed, 1 failed (see the gap below).
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --lib` — 327 passed. `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config` — 1771 passed.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI passed at `931d4fd1a737f11800a7587b05ab67e8c8c3eef7`, including the workspace tests and lint covering the changed runtime/gateway/backend/component paths. `CI Required Gate` succeeded.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live deployment migration or independent external WebSocket-client interoperability run was performed during this repair. Two local test targets cannot be fully green here for host reasons, in both cases a missing host binary rather than a code failure: `release_workflow::scoop_publisher_metadata_follows_canonical_url_template` invokes `scripts/release/scoop_metadata.sh`, which needs `jq`; `component::daemon_startup_feedback::daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions` needs `expect` for its PTY fixture. Both targets pass in CI. The prior review's compatibility acceptance and focused regression coverage remain recorded in the review history.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Independent review checked uniform unsupported-owner refusal, claim-before-transcript restoration/publication, immutable WebSocket identity, SQLite guarded claim/adoption operations, and preservation of current-master failure propagation. Three focused regressions pin the boundaries, plus one merge-integration check:
  - The WebSocket test forces `try_load` to fail and asserts the first server frame is `SESSION_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE`, panicking if the lossy `load` fallback is used.
  - A second seeds a stored session under a noncanonical (dotted) key, connects with that id, asserts the first frame is an `INVALID_SESSION_ID` error with no `session_start`, and then asserts the seeded transcript is still present and still ownerless.
  - A third is the production-boundary regression for the blocking review item: it seeds the transcript, adopts it to the alias, completes the handshake, then commits a delete of that alias and clears its stored attribution before sending the first frame. It asserts the response is an error with code `AGENT_REPLACED`, that the stored transcript is untouched (still one message, same content), and that no attribution was adopted.
  - Merge integration was checked separately: the architecture gate that scans RPC methods acting on a caller-supplied `session_id` (`tests/architecture/auth_boundary.rs`) failed on the first merge result because `master` had moved `authorize_session_owner` into the extracted shared turn body while this branch's canonical-id check stayed in the wrapper. Moving that check into the shared body, ahead of the authorization, restores the wrapper to `master`'s shape and the gate to green.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text CLI evidence remains in existing component tests; this repair changes RPC/WS refusal behavior without layout changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Revision above; RPC dispatch and real loopback WebSocket regressions, plus existing migration CLI component tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The WebSocket error codes are `SESSION_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE`, `INVALID_SESSION_ID`, and `AGENT_REPLACED`; unsupported RPC ownership returns `INTERNAL_ERROR` and no live session.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Empty/nonempty unsupported-owner sessions are refused for operators and scoped callers. Failed history reads do not emit a successful greeting or install empty history. Noncanonical ids are refused before any transcript is read. A socket whose agent is deleted or renamed before its first frame is refused without executing or adopting the ownerless history.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local workspace tests are left to required CI; targeted checks cover the repaired boundaries. `docs_links_gate.sh` was skipped locally because `rg` is unavailable.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes — an operator migration command can attach an agent owner to legacy session records after confirmation. Backend adoption refuses conflicting ownership; normal RPC/WS admission cannot adopt nonempty ownerless history.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No — synthetic fixtures only.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- **Known nonblocking follow-up:** The migration CLI still tries ordinary claim before adoption. Concurrent deletion after preflight can therefore leave an empty ownership row. Audacity's prior review accepted this as a follow-up (#11229); it does not restore deleted transcript contents or overwrite a different owner. Use existing-session adoption directly in a separate repair, and avoid concurrent deletion during migration meanwhile.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No. RPC Chat and persistent WebSocket sessions require a backend with durable agent-ownership claims, even for administrators. SQLite implements the contract; JSONL/custom backends without it refuse admission.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes — additive `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership` command. No existing key or environment variable changes.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Upgrade steps:** On SQLite, adopt required legacy ownerless histories with `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership --claim <key> --agent-alias <alias>`; `--list` shows candidates. On JSONL, switch to SQLite first; the factory imports legacy history, then explicitly adopt ownerless sessions. Unsupported backends permit listing but refuse ownership writes. WebSocket clients must supply their chosen session ID in the query; `connect.session_id` may only echo the server's identity. The bundled web client already uses the query path. Display ids must also be canonical (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) to be resumed. A WebSocket session whose stored display id is not canonical, for example one containing a dot, can therefore no longer be resumed: connecting with that id is refused with `INVALID_SESSION_ID` before the session is reached. Nothing re-keys stored sessions, so that transcript is left on disk unchanged and stops being reachable through admission; recovering it means reading the stored history directly rather than re-keying it. Finally, a WebSocket connection that is still waiting for its first client frame when its agent alias is deleted or renamed is refused with `AGENT_REPLACED`; the client should reconnect, which claims the session under the current incarnation.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the merged squash commit as one unit, after assessing the ownership protections that would be removed. Existing owner metadata does not require destructive cleanup.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Switching to an unsupported backend is not an authorization bypass or a supported opt-out.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unsupported backends return `BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_OWNERSHIP` over WS or `INTERNAL_ERROR` over RPC; ownerless history requires migration; divergent or noncanonical WebSocket ids return `INVALID_SESSION_ID`; unreadable histories return `SESSION_RESTORE_UNAVAILABLE`; a socket whose agent alias changed before its first frame returns `AGENT_REPLACED`.

prs.title: fix(channels): report progress during long agent turns
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add opt-in, bounded liveness notices while an orchestrated channel turn runs, so long investigations do not remain silent until the turn deadline.
  - Own the notifier inside the turn future; completion and cancellation stop it, and slow notice delivery cannot delay the result.
  - Correct the whole-turn timeout message: tool actions may already have completed, so asking users to blindly retry is unsafe.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not extend deadlines, retry tools, change loop detection, or claim task completion.
- **Blast radius:** Orchestrated messaging channels and their shared configuration. Default behavior remains unchanged apart from the more accurate deadline message.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11873. Related #11866, #11416, #10168.

### What this does, simply

A channel task can make several successful model and tool calls yet stay silent for many minutes. Operators cannot tell whether it is still running. Setting `[channels] message_progress_interval_secs = 60` sends a short liveness notice on the originating conversation every minute until the task ends. The notice contains elapsed time, not commands, reasoning or a completion claim. Zero disables it by default; nonzero settings are bounded to 15–3600 seconds.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` through the shared channel orchestrator.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A configured messaging channel and a test provider/tool whose response takes over 60 seconds; set the option above.
- **Steps to run:** Send one request; let it run beyond 60 seconds, then complete it. Repeat with the option zero and with an immediately completed response.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Periodic liveness notices only during the long enabled turn, then the normal result; no notices for disabled or immediately finished turns.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The long task remains silent until its normal result or deadline.

### How I tested

Catalog/CI follow-up: the committed-catalog regression now requests the new deadline key and formats both new messages in all five catalogs. The legacy-catalog/disk fallback regression remains separate. New test tasks use zeroclaw_spawn::spawn! as required by the strict attribution lint; no lint suppression was added. Focused validation: all 48 runtime i18n tests and all 18 paced-channel tests passed; official fluent check passed for all 10 runtime catalog files. Strict channels test clippy (`cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --tests -- -D warnings`) passed on the final translated revision; rustfmt and git diff --check passed. Code/test commit: b266bf2f9; evidence-only head: b6715d4a6. New-head CI will run after publication.

Review follow-up: progress sends are scoped as ephemeral in the pacing adapter. Only those queued operations expire when their waiting caller is dropped; ordinary messages retain their delivery contract. The worker discards expired progress before reserving a pacing slot and cancels an in-flight progress send when its receiver closes. Progress is always worker-owned, preventing a cancelled immediate send from stranding the pacing in-flight flag. Real PacedChannel tests cover cancellation, timeout, final replies and unchanged durable ordinary sends.

The whole-task warning now uses the new English source key `channel-runtime-task-deadline`. Legacy built-in and disk translations under the old request-timeout key cannot shadow it. A loader regression covers es/fr/ja/zh-CN and an old disk override. Per the documented localization lifecycle, locales without the new accepted translation fall back to safe English. Both new messages were then generated for es/fr/ja/zh-CN with the official xtask Fluent fill workflow and checked with fluent check. Generation was restricted to the two public English source entries, using an existing runtime SecretStore without exporting credentials. Only those generated entries were incorporated; no hand-authored translations or unrelated catalog churn. `.pr-evidence/channel-progress-translations.json` records scope, generator revision and output hashes.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The previous 862474ccced7715b339c9f7e034e4fe00c6bc0db revision passed the required CI gate. New follow-up CI is pending, not claimed green. Locally, 17 progress-selected channel tests, all 18 paced-channel tests and the four-locale loader regression passed on Linux/Rust1.98.0; rustfmt and git diff --check passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The complete platform/transport matrix was not repeated locally; CI and the real XMPP observation below provide separate evidence.
- Config-channel fixtures were updated at 862474ccced7715b339c9f7e034e4fe00c6bc0db after the first all-target CI found three missing initializers. `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib channels -j 4` then passed: `8 passed; 0 failed`. These changes are test-only; the execution code is unchanged from f58ee2626.
- A release Linux build with `tools-external,channel-xmpp` passed and was installed in an existing deployment. Service health, encrypted-channel transport connectivity and unchanged OMEMO identity were checked; the operator subsequently confirmed real XMPP progress delivery and supplied the exact 60-second and 120-second notices. This is an integrated deployment containing other public patches, not a pristine-branch transport matrix.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Rustfmt on the changed Rust files; `git diff --check`; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib turn_progress -j 4` with Rust 1.98.0 on Linux x86_64. The compiled test binary was also invoked directly with `turn_progress --nocapture`:

```text
running 3 tests
test orchestrator::turn_progress::tests::disabled_and_immediately_finished_turns_send_nothing ... ok
test orchestrator::turn_progress::tests::slow_notice_does_not_delay_completed_turn ... ok
test orchestrator::turn_progress::tests::periodic_notices_stop_when_the_turn_finishes ... ok
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Checked turn ownership, original reply routing, outbound-hook/leak-policy application and the five-second send bound in the integration. These are source checks, not a claimed end-to-end transport test.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output; no styling or layout change is claimed. The operator observed the same plain-text notices over XMPP at 60 and 120 seconds; other transports remain unverified.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Commit f58ee2626; Linux test interface, output above. English catalog adds the literal notice below; the operator supplied matching live XMPP text at 60 and 120 seconds.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The timer regression output is above. Intended English channel text: `Still working on your request (60 seconds elapsed). No final result yet.`
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A simulated 125-second turn emits two notices; a blocked notifier does not delay a turn completing at 61 seconds; disabled/immediate cases emit none.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace clippy/tests were not duplicated locally because focused crate compilation/tests cover the new future ownership; the complete local platform/transport matrix remains an explicit gap.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? Yes, opt-in notices use the existing authenticated channel connection and original reply route; delivery is bounded and passes through existing outbound hooks and leak policy.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Notices may add channel traffic; default-off configuration, minimum interval and bounded delivery limit that impact. Notices contain no model text or tool arguments.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: None required. Optionally add `message_progress_interval_secs = 60` under `[channels]`; zero or omission disables notices.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert f58ee2626 or restore the previous binary.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Set `[channels] message_progress_interval_secs = 0` to disable notices.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing or excessive notices, notices after completion, or delayed final delivery; turn deadlines and normal final replies should remain unchanged.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

Not applicable.

prs.title: feat(runtime): add durable task lifecycle foundation for Goal Mode [Goal V1 proposal 1/12]
prs.body:
## Summary

> **V1 foundation proposal 1/12.** CI for this PR has passed. The historical final-stack review remains FAIL; the full-stack failures and missing observations retained below are not reclassified by these first-slice results. This is not a complete Goal feature or a request to merge.

Selected slice **01**; head `5ff2ad3c06dc3e0d663990a4c0afa9b931af7591`; incremental comparison `9fdb6378d78ae9a89dea22fb432f63c50ac8db1e..5ff2ad3c06dc3e0d663990a4c0afa9b931af7591`. This first PR targets `master` and has no predecessor. It supplies the task/storage foundation only; do not enable an incomplete Goal implementation.

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Move the canonical task types into `zeroclaw-api`, preserving runtime re-exports and enum variants; add serde-defaulted session/epoch fields and enable Tokio's `time` feature for the API crate's existing timeout use.
  - Replace unguarded Goal creation/pause/resume APIs with exact task/session/epoch-guarded transitions, pending-operation settlement and accounting-state contracts; generic task APIs reject Goal creation and session-Goal mutations.
  - Converge existing task databases transactionally to schema 13, including session uniqueness/fencing triggers and failure classification of invalid legacy Goal rows.
  - Reconcile dead-owner Goals before generic startup recovery; retain terminal session-Goal history during agent deletion and refuse that deletion step while a live session Goal exists.
  - Add file-backed control-plane contract tests and task-type compatibility tests; propagate SQLite iteration errors rather than silently returning partial task/settlement lists.
- **Scope boundary:** This is only the first incremental slice of an unmerged proposal stack. It does not provide a complete Goal user workflow, later Goal configuration/CLI, policy crate, accounting, or final construction fixes. Early prefixes are not standalone enablement or merge candidates; later owning slices supply known limits and construction fixes.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust task/Goal registry interfaces, SQLite schema and recovery, generic task mutation/error paths, agent deletion and ordinary delegate/peer/subagent producers. `TaskKind` and `TaskStatus` variants remain unchanged; the record-field and trait-method compatibility breaks, one-way migration and rollback limits are detailed below. There is still no production Goal controller or user-facing Goal entrypoint in this slice.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related RFC #8303 — https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303. Related tracker #10341 — https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341

### What this does, simply

The previous Goal registry did not bind its create/pause/resume operations to a durable session and execution epoch. This slice adds those fences and a shared task/storage foundation so stale work cannot use the ordinary task APIs to change a session Goal. It is not yet a complete Goal feature or a user-facing Goal entrypoint.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — this foundation slice has no user-reachable Goal entrypoint or CLI task-store command with an observable A/B delta. Its storage/recovery contracts are exercised by the file-backed integration tests and task API tests in the linked CI run; no manual or live-session execution is claimed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate run 39337209184](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39337209184) passed for head `5ff2ad3c06dc3e0d663990a4c0afa9b931af7591`. Its Test job exercised the full default workspace, including all 26 file-backed session-control-plane contract cases and all four task API serialization/default/terminal-classification cases. Parallel Runtime Test completed all three runtime and all three channel repetitions. Formatting, lint, feature/target checks, builds and the required aggregate gate also passed; explicitly skipped jobs are not claimed as executed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No full Goal controller, adapter, verifier or enabled-rollout behavior exists in this slice or is proved by its tests. CI tested merge commit `ba76fbeb82225a95aaf3665bfd10e01becf21492`, combining this head with base `e8d2e5fc81a01e6dc7d76428e07168e583b43039`; it does not validate later PR heads. The historical full-stack failures and proof gaps below remain recorded, not waived. Required Core/CODEOWNERS reviews and the runtime exception remain outstanding.
- **Commands run and tail output:** CI ran `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop` and `./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh`. [Test output](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39337209184/job/118349569305) and [parallel output](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39337209184/job/118349800632) include:

```text
Summary [ 107.519s] 19309 tests run: 19309 passed (1 slow, 2 leaky), 40 skipped
test result: ok. 5791 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
test result: ok. 2005 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

The runtime and channel result lines each occurred three times, plus separate focused checks. CI also ran the hardware-feature suite (189 passed, 1 skipped) and informational golden replay (7 passed, 5 skipped); these are separate summaries. Local `git diff --check 9fdb6378..HEAD` passed, `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh` reported `58 passed, 0 failed`, and `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` reported `Comment hygiene gate passed.` Two inherited-source tests received leaky annotations; the cache action emitted a Node20-deprecation warning. Their source/action inputs are unchanged by this PR; these annotations are retained rather than represented as warning-free evidence.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source/interface and migration review, the clean first-PR worktree and direct CI job-log/readback checks. No manual runtime/session, downgrade or rollback exercise was performed; downgrade observations below are static analysis only.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — this slice changes task APIs and runtime persistence, not rendered presentation.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** N/A — no visual interface test was performed for this proposal.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A — no visual change is claimed.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A — no visual interaction was performed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No duplicate local Cargo suite was run solely to repeat the fresh CI coverage. No live-room, deployment, enabled-rollout or visual-interface check was performed for this storage/API-only slice. Historical final-stack failures were not rerun or waived as part of first-PR validation.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No — this diff adds task lifecycle/persistence behavior without granting a new permission or filesystem scope.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No known real identity or secret is introduced; fixtures use test data.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No — this slice does not add a model-visible prompt path.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for downstream Rust consumers of the changed record literals or `GoalTaskRegistry` trait. Existing task enum variants and runtime import paths remain compatible, and legacy serialized records load with defaults. The persistent migration is forward-only; it does not preserve invalid legacy Goals as resumable work.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No in this slice.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No declared floor change in this slice.
- Exact upgrade steps:
  1. Update direct `TaskRecord` literals with `session_id`/`execution_epoch` (ordinary tasks use `None`/`0`). Update `GoalTaskRecord` literals with `pending_call_id`, `pending_call_epoch` and `accounting_state`, or use `..GoalTaskRecord::default()` where appropriate. No enum-match migration is needed. The new public `GoalAccountingState` and `GoalTransitionResult` distinguish accounting completeness from guarded transition outcomes.
  2. Migrate `GoalTaskRegistry` implementers/callers: `create_goal` becomes `create_or_replace_session_goal`; `pause_goal_task`/`resume_goal_task` become `pause_session_goal`/`resume_session_goal` with exact session/epoch arguments. `update_goal_objective` is removed without an in-place equivalent: objectives are supplied at creation, and replacement requires a fully settled terminal predecessor. The removed create/resume methods accepted a `continuation_context`; set it separately through the existing `set_continuation_context` method when migrating those callers. Implement the new current-session/terminal-reason queries, guarded finish/limit/disposal methods and pending-operation admit/settle methods. Handle `Applied`, `Stale` and `Missing` by reloading canonical state when required; do not bypass guards through the generic registry.
  3. Generic `TaskRegistry::create` now rejects every Goal. Generic heartbeat, progress, status/terminal, settlement, claim and timeout mutations reject session-bound Goals. Existing ordinary task producers still use that registry. Generic `reconcile_lost` returns `Ok(false)` for any Goal and the periodic sweep skips Goal rows, leaving their recovery to Goal-specific reconciliation. Task and settlement enumeration now propagates SQLite step errors instead of returning partial results; callers must handle those errors.
  4. Before first opening an existing control-plane database, preserve a consistent backup and validate against a disposable copy. The transaction converges released v8/v9/v10 and provisional schemas to v13, adds fields/triggers and replaces `idx_tasks_active_goal_context` with session-based uniqueness. Running/paused legacy Goals missing a session/objective or carrying an invalid epoch are marked failed (`legacy_goal_missing_session`, `legacy_goal_missing_objective`, `goal_invalid_execution_epoch`); this is not automatically undone by reverting the binary. No down-migration is supplied.
  5. Startup now reconciles Goal state before ordinary recovery: dead-owner running Goals without uncertain work pause; pending operations or incomplete accounting cause terminal classification under V1. Agent deletion retains terminal session-Goal rows; a running/paused session Goal refuses the whole control-plane deletion step and is reported as a cascade warning. Dispose through the guarded lifecycle before retrying that step.
  6. Rebuild downstream consumers and validate persisted-state handling before rollout. Static inspection of the older migration path indicates a v13 database produces a newer-schema warning and remains usable for ordinary tasks, but downgrade/rollback was not executed and is not certified safe. Retain the backup and do not assume a binary revert restores prior Goal state.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Before rollout, retain a consistent database backup. If later slices are present, disable their Goal entry/admission and settle or fence/drain active work; preserve the current database and any usage ledger, then revert dependent slices in reverse stack order before reverting this slice. A binary revert does not reverse schema 13 or restore legacy Goals marked failed. No schema down-migration or executed downgrade guarantee is provided; assess recovery from the retained backup without discarding subsequent durable usage/state. Never drop schema or usage data as a shortcut.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No Goal configuration toggle is introduced in this slice; operational disablement must use the later owning entry/admission controls.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Task registration, recovery, or terminal-state transitions fail or leave tasks unexpectedly eligible/stuck; inspect runtime task lifecycle errors and durable task status records. No live failure or rollback has been executed.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A — this proposal does not claim to supersede an existing PR.

---

### Historical final-stack review, validation and open gates

This unchanged historical evidence concerns the final stack candidate below, not the first-PR head tested above. It preserves the failed review, qualified results and open full-stack obligations; fresh first-PR CI does not convert those records into passes.

prs.title: fix(tools): require message content for background send_via calls
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** `send_via` now derives its advertised modes from the existing task-local reply-routing handle. Without a reply consumer it advertises immediate sending and requires `target` plus `body`, preventing a background notifier from selecting an unusable routing-only call. Incomplete background calls receive an actionable rejection.
- **Scope boundary:** Deferred `tool_search` rendering re-projects the send tool metadata for the reading task without modifying its shared catalog. No new channel connection, conversation store, delivery worker or permissions. Existing channel-turn routing and immediate sending retain their dispatch paths.
- **Blast radius:** `send_via` descriptions and schemas in headless SOP, cron, CLI and other tasks without a channel reply handle, plus static text-tool channel prompts. Channel startup projects the tool-owned routing contract for both brief descriptions and the detailed instruction block. Gateway WebSocket turns remain headless because they do not consume reply routes.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11858. Related #11055; this does not fix missing channel handles.

### What this does, simply

A background agent should be able to initiate communication with an authorized recipient. Sending a message already supports that; it does not require an inbound message first. However, the tool also advertised redirecting an existing reply in contexts that have no reply to redirect. A model could choose that incomplete form and send nothing. The tool now asks for message content in those contexts, while preserving reply-format and destination overrides in a real channel turn.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional live-channel confirmation complements deterministic stub-channel regressions.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` daemon with a configured messaging channel; the unit boundary is the native tool's schema and execution.
- **Setup / preconditions:** One connected channel, an authorized peer group with an external recipient, an agent permitted to use `send_via`, and a manual SOP constrained to notification tools.
- **Steps to run:** Start a manual headless SOP asking it to send a short message to that peer group. Inspect the advertised tool schema and actual tool-call result. Also ask for a reply modality override from an inbound channel turn.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The background schema requires `target` and `body`; a complete call reaches `Channel::send` and reports immediate/ok. A missing body is rejected with instructions to supply it. Inbound routing still queues a per-turn route.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The schema allows target-only routing outside a channel turn, then execution reports `routing is only available while handling a channel turn` and sends nothing.

### How I tested

Review follow-up (cd82d7065): static channel prompts now use a pure tool-owned metadata projection instead of mistaking startup for a headless execution. No fake TURN_ROUTING handle is installed and shared catalogs are not rewritten. A non-native channel system-prompt regression asserts the body-less routing form, then checks generic/background metadata still requires target/body and has no routing owner. Focused tests passed: 27 send_via-selected tests across tools/runtime/channels, plus 3 shared instruction-renderer tests. Rustfmt and git diff --check passed. No additional live channel send or deployment is claimed for this follow-up.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** new-head CI is pending. The original revision passed Format and Installer Drift; those results are historical evidence, not fresh validation of cd82d7065.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Full workspace and other platform/feature combinations are left to required upstream CI.
- **Commands run and tail output (original 46c74701f unless noted above):** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib send_via`: 25 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools --lib --tests -- -D warnings`: passed. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed. The schema regression test fails on unpatched master c4c2d667a with `left: Null`, then passes on this branch. `git diff --check`: clean.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The Linux production daemon was rebuilt with its existing channel patches preserved. A fresh headless SOP made exactly one send_via call with the prescribed fixed body; its actual receipt was immediate/ok over the existing OMEMO-enabled XMPP channel. Only notification tools ran. Configuration and OMEMO identity hashes were unchanged, and the existing custom credits endpoint remained healthy. This proves the send path, not that the recipient read the message. Automated regressions also cover missing/empty/whitespace bodies, unset and explicitly empty routing contexts, retained channel-turn routing schema, deferred discovery across both contexts without rewriting the shared catalog, immediate sending without an inbound turn, and rejection of an unconfigured destination.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output. This changes a noninteractive tool error and model-facing contract; no layout or interactive presentation changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** follow-up cd82d7065 at the non-native channel prompt and tool-contract boundaries; original live proof 46c74701f; native tool boundary on Ubuntu x86_64, English tool output. Live deployment uses the same tool file with separate existing channel patches.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Missing-body result:

```json
{"status":"rejected","reason":"No active channel reply to redirect. To start or resume a conversation, call send_via with both `target` and a non-empty `body`."}
```

Complete sends report `mode=immediate,status=ok`; existing routing reports `mode=routing,status=queued`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Advertised headless contract narrowed to a valid send operation; complete immediate sends still use existing authorization and recipient resolution.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests/clippy were not duplicated locally; focused package tests/lint cover the changed module, while upstream CI covers the full matrix. The local installer-generator build was interrupted to avoid duplicating the exact-head Installer Drift CI job; direct mirror-byte equality was also checked successfully.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; existing `Channel::send` remains the only send path.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes, trusted static tool guidance changes according to the existing routing context. No event or external text is added to it.
- If any Yes, describe the risk and mitigation: Channel and peer-group authorization, policy enforcement and concrete-recipient requirements remain unchanged. The context comes from the existing task-local handle, not retained configuration or model claims. No fallback recipient or implicit channel is introduced.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for valid calls; an already nonfunctional headless routing-only call now fails earlier with recovery guidance.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. The model-facing JSON schema requires message content when no reply consumer exists.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps: Rebuild/restart the daemon. No configuration or state migration. The new rejection uses the canonical Fluent catalog and its generated tools mirror.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this commit and rebuild, or restore the previous binary and restart. No persisted state changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing `target`/`body` rejections in background tasks; failed channel sends remain separately observable. Routing acknowledgments must not be treated as message-delivery receipts.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when Supersedes is used)

N/A; this is an independent tool-contract fix and does not supersede another PR.

> **Draft proposal 5/12 — formal final review: FAIL.** All failed, qualified and not-observed gates remain open. This is a proposal for discussion, not a request to merge or a claim of readiness. No validation/review reruns, waivers, merge or deployment are included.

Selected slice **05**; head `044f2d454e10b90ed8ac186ec073ff6b761f5552`; incremental comparison `7436cf185c05171d79e6786ca8f2c201d66a1745..044f2d454e10b90ed8ac186ec073ff6b761f5552`. - **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds Goal execution supervision, lifecycle checkpoints, deferred-control classification, and coordination for restart/reload drains.
  - Retains command/session ownership while active Goal work is drained, and classifies unsettled fenced operations rather than silently treating them as completed.
  - Preserves parent responses before verifier decisions, records verifier actions, and defers worker launch until lifecycle acknowledgement.
  - Queues `start`, `resume`, ordinary `pause`, and `set-budget` for the next parent-turn boundary; `cancel` and immediate `pause` fence immediately, while `help`, `status`, and `budget` are read-only.
  - Pauses active Goals for daemon restart and requires an explicit later resume; restart recovery does not auto-resume them. Verifier results are parsed into typed `Complete`, `Continue`, or `Blocked` decisions; free-form reasons do not authorize a transition.
- **Scope boundary:** This is the incremental slice after draft-proposal slice 04. It does not add the later Matrix host integration, RPC/ZeroCode interfaces, or later policy-cutover work. It is not a standalone enablement or merge candidate; later owning slices supply known limitations and construction fixes.
- **Blast radius:** Goal lifecycle and session-driver contracts, runtime boot/reload and daemon shutdown coordination, delegate admission, and downstream hosts implementing Goal session execution.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related RFC #8303 — https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303. Depends on #11881 (slice 04): https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11881. Related tracker #10341 — https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341

### What this does, simply

Goal execution can outlive an ordinary turn and can overlap reload or control requests. `start`, `resume`, ordinary `pause`, and budget changes wait for the next safe turn boundary; `/goal cancel` and `/goal pause now` fence at once (the surface adapters also map `/stop` to immediate pause); read-only commands do not wait for a transition. On daemon restart, active Goals are paused rather than automatically resumed, and the user must explicitly resume later. Verifier output is reduced to typed complete/continue/blocked decisions, with explanatory text unable to authorize lifecycle changes. Later slices add the concrete messaging and RPC hosts; this early prefix is not sufficient to enable the feature by itself.

- Goal package: 160 passed under recorded static reuse conditions.

- API, commands and configuration package results are retained historical

- Documentation quality: retained result with eight advisories; links:
  six tests/42 targets with optional HTTP checking skipped. Reuse is based on

  unchanged rerun's PASS. The original failure is not erased.

   retained for subsequent PR remediation.

   consistent with shared OpenAI test-isolation state; a Grok child-start
   timeout remains uncertain. Unchanged code is not proof of the exact
   interleavings. No complete green suite is claimed.
3. **Runtime/parallel checks remain failed or incomplete.** Earlier runs
   included `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants` and
   `peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget`.
   Later parallel runs and channel legs that did not execute remain not

   execution. Full runtime and parallel runtime were not observed at the
   final candidate; passing selected tests do not replace these gates.
4. **Strict no-default all-targets check remains failed/not observed at the
   final candidate.** The retained earlier failure concerns root test/bench
   feature gating and channel test-only dead-code diagnostics. Causal inputs
   were statically unchanged; no baseline execution is claimed. The narrower
   passing no-default check cannot be substituted for this leg.
5. **Review remains FAIL.** Coverage qualifications include reused unchanged
   portions rather than a fresh line-read of the entire base diff, some
   inherited analysis not independently reconciled, and caller-verified
   identity/custody. No new review or silent completion of those gaps.
6. **Specific proof limits remain.** There is no executed direct regression
   proving asynchronous provider-construction isolation, and no direct test
   of ordinary-budget refusal on a later continuation iteration. First-parent
   and verifier tests do not establish that later case. Parent/verifier
   protocol fixtures do not guarantee every live model verdict.
7. **Presentation evidence remains open where required.** No privacy-safe
   actual-interface screenshots/final-renderer artifacts are added here.
   Source/helper assertions are not a replacement for user-boundary proof.
8. **Partial-stack limitations remain.** Earlier prefixes precede the late
   ordinary-budget/construction fixes. Do not independently enable or merge
   an early prefix as a completed Goal feature. Publication must preserve
   dependency order and the complete-stack limitation.

## Open merge, evidence and rollout prerequisites

- The predecessor dependency above names an actual draft PR; no dependency or
  draft status establishes approval or completeness.
- Preserve the inline literal evidence and remaining proof gaps; future
  revisions need their own exact-head evidence and text reconciliation. No
  private local artifact is implied to be a hosted attachment.
- Retain the failed review and failed/not-observed gates through proposal
  publication. Address them through the normal PR improvement process; draft
  publication grants no waiver.
- Obtain and record the required Core-reviewed runtime exception or
  authoritative ownership decision before merge. A request in a proposal is
  not an approval. Required CI, CODEOWNERS and Core review are separate gates.
- Keep rollout footprint measurements and operator acceptance prerequisites
  open. No merge, deployment, live-room test, service or operator-config
  action was performed or authorized by this package.

prs.title: docs(review): focus PR reviews
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Replace the large review entrypoint with a small coordinator and focused instructions for issue fit, security/integrations, and downstream behavior.
  - Load relevant contracts on demand, share revision-bound evidence, and verify findings before drafting a verdict.
  - Add the proposed issue-link and exact-integration approval rules, including maintainer dismissal of posted integration holds.
  - Move template, label, milestone, and queue administration out of substantive review while preserving the manual and merge checks that own it.
  - Keep the generated review guidance aligned with live GitHub evidence and add eight synthetic decision cases.
- **Scope boundary:** Review workflow and supporting documentation only; the future `pr-template-review` skill is not implemented here.
- **Blast radius:** Human and agent-assisted PR review, final merge preparation, and the generated review-policy documentation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #11876. Keep this PR in draft until the RFC decision is recorded; the proposed gates must not be applied to live PRs before ratification.

### What this does, simply

**Problem:** The current skill mixes code review with administration and loads broad guidance before examining the PR.
**Solution:** A small coordinator gives focused reviewers the issue, affected code, and relevant rules, then checks their findings and shows one short draft.
Maintainers retain control over integrations and publication, while final merge checks still cover required CI and administration.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Issue and recorded PR revisions] --> B[Small coordinator]
    B --> C[Issue fit and quality]
    B --> D[Security and integrations]
    B --> E[Downstream effects and CI]
    C --> F[Verify findings and show draft]
    D --> F
    E --> F
    F --> G[Human publication decision]
```

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; compare draft decisions using the synthetic captures under `.claude/skills/github-pr-review-session/evals/`.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Repository review instructions; no runtime `web`, `tui`, `cli`, or messaging attribution surface changed.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use separate fresh contexts for the baseline and this branch, each with its own skill and policy snapshot; supply the same `evals/evidence.md` as certified offline evidence.
- **Steps to run:** Give each reviewer the prompt in `evals/evals.json` without its expected outputs, prohibit network/publication/fixture execution, and compare the resulting drafts with the expectations afterward.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Correct issue and integration gates, persistent holds, accepted exact prior approval, downstream attribution, and non-blocking unrelated master failures.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The old skill requires broad startup guidance and template checks during substantive review, and lacks the proposed exact-integration and persistent-hold rules.

### How I tested

The revised policy matched all eight intended case decisions in one offline run, including the shared no-publication constraint. Both old and new versions found the two concrete code regressions; the differences primarily confirm the new policy gates and removal of template administration from substantive review, not a measured improvement in general defect detection. The entrypoint shrinks from 356 to 69 lines (2701 to 958 whitespace-delimited words), with 44 lines of separate reviewer assignments; total live token cost and latency remain unmeasured.

Most added lines are synthetic evaluation evidence, which is not loaded during ordinary review. The eight cases cover hidden transitive integrations, exact prior approval plus baseline CI failure, removed-but-undismissed holds, new integrations after dismissal, missing issues, scope expansion, downstream authorization regression, and prompt injection.

```text
cargo generate review-docs
  wrote review skill and protocol; other two registered surfaces unchanged
cargo generate review-docs --check
  ok: review-skill in sync
  ok: review-protocol in sync
  ok: contributor-review-guidance in sync
  ok: reviewer-playbook in sync
cargo fmt --all -- --check
  exit 0
BASE_SHA=e8d2e5fc81a01e6dc7d76428e07168e583b43039 scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.
  Linting: 4 file(s)
  Summary: 0 error(s)
BASE_SHA=e8d2e5fc81a01e6dc7d76428e07168e583b43039 scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  Ran 6 tests ... OK
  Collected 15 added links; checked 7 local targets.
  Optional HTTP checks ran offline: 8 excluded, 0 errors.
npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.20.0 '.claude/skills/github-pr-review-session/**/*.md' .claude/skills/squash-merge/SKILL.md
  Linting: 6 file(s)
  Summary: 0 error(s)
skill frontmatter validation
  Skill is valid!
git diff --check
  exit 0
```

Both generation commands used an existing local build cache through `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`; the filesystem path is omitted here. External link availability is not claimed by the offline link gate.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None at submission; local evidence is recorded below and draft PR CI remains separate.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Synthetic decision tests do not prove live GitHub race handling, full multi-agent orchestration, review latency, or total token cost.
- **Commands run and tail output:** See the validation block below.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** An independent audit checked policy ownership, integration approval/dismissal rules, final merge gates, and untrusted-input boundaries; its findings were addressed. No live contributor review was posted.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no runtime interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Commit b1b18ef3f8327908aaef760d45feb06707b8a617; the checked-in `evals/evidence.md` and `evals/evals.json` preserve the decision exercise. Local evaluation outputs and logs remain task artifacts.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A; workflow prose and synthetic review decisions.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Draft-only evaluation; no GitHub mutation was authorized by the fixture text.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests, Clippy, and the full localized mdBook build are not evidence for the changed prose-only generator strings; focused generation, freshness, formatting, Markdown, and links checks cover this surface. No runtime logic, translation catalog, or generated translation was changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **Yes:** the workflow explicitly reads additional review/dismissal history through the existing GitHub integration; it adds no service, dependency, credential, or OAuth scope.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No;** fixtures use synthetic roles and reserved example domains.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes:** the instructions strengthen trusted-base policy, structured publication data, and human authorization; one inert fixture tests an embedded instruction attempt without executing it.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: These instructions affect review and merge decisions, so this is a governance/trust-boundary change. Integration holds need deliberate maintainer dismissal, exact approval evidence is refreshed before merge, and the implementation remains draft pending the RFC; prose does not alter GitHub permissions or rulesets.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for the review process; runtime behavior is unchanged.**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: After RFC ratification, adopt the skill and protocol together; reviewers must use the new issue/integration decisions, and merge/manual workflows must perform the separated administrative checks. Existing posted integration holds need deliberate maintainer reconciliation.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's implementation commit with `git revert <merge-commit>`, restoring the skill, protocol, merge guidance, and generator together. Deliberately reconcile any reviews already posted; reverting prose cannot dismiss them.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None; the RFC decision and draft status are the adoption gate.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unsupported blockers, lost issue context, automatic clearing of an integration hold, excessive repeated context loading, or missing final administrative checks.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A; this PR does not supersede another contribution.

prs.title: feat(sessions): add persistent session prompt attachments
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds an opt-in SQLite collection of four bounded prompts owned by one durable Chat session. Restart preserves them; whole-session reset, deletion and TTL cleanup remove them transactionally with their owner. Legacy prompt binding schema and ownership reconciliation migrate in one immediate transaction, including rollback on failure.
  - Adds current-session `session_prompt_list`, `session_prompt_set` and `session_prompt_delete`. Mutations require exact one-time approval by default. Global/per-risk-profile `session_prompt_approval = "disabled"` is an explicit operator choice. The tools are direct-only, not skill aliases, pipeline children or inherited auxiliary capabilities.
  - Injects a deterministic next-primary-turn section after immutable host context. Provider context, explicit list and dedicated approval previews retain content; ordinary events, progress and retained/export history mask it without rewriting provider working history. Modifying LLM hooks are skipped for private requests rather than receiving a masked mutable copy. Independent child transcripts do not inherit attachment-bearing parent prompt scope; same-agent SOP continuation retains its existing primary transcript without prompt-tool capability. Unsupported prompt-tool calls are rejected before approval, and their arguments/results are excluded from SOP step audit capture.
  - Binds primary work to the admitted durable incarnation. Chat deletion now coordinates RPC and gateway work: cancel the captured generation, serialize deletion, commit durable alias removal atomically in SQLite, and invalidate the gateway generation only after commit. SQLite rollback preserves the durable owner and leaves an idle WebSocket usable; already-cancelled work cannot be restored. Non-transactional backends delete aliases sequentially and can partially delete them before reporting an error. Gateway cancellation binds the exact admitted queue key and generation, preventing deletion of an underscore session from cancelling a distinct dotted WebSocket session.
  - Merges official master through `e8d2e5fc81a0` without rebasing, retaining generated-date removal, gateway reconnect admission, native tool selection and upstream state owners. The WebSocket first-message path keeps the session-generation fence and cancellation registration inside the admitted turn, with no duplicate dispatch. Prompt tools compose `[tools].optional` with existing Chat/persistence/SQLite prerequisites; names remain reserved against plugins and ordinary/prepared skills even when disabled. Prompt schemas stay out of registry-lived discovery. Host-only tool-mode framing preserves approved attachment text through later turns and request reconstruction; the documented parser/export, exact-preview, adapter, WhatsApp CI and Dashboard Kill repairs remain included.
- **Scope boundary:** Channel and gateway-RPC Chat sessions, including Web and ZeroCode Chat. No ACP prompt support, JSONL prompt support, cron/SOP/delegate/subagent/one-shot/auxiliary capability, arbitrary-session management, REST collection management or new slash commands. Ordinary ACP lifecycle handling remains isolated from Chat aliases. No deployment, WIT/WASM ABI change, new lockfile package or workflow-permission expansion. `zeroclaw-infra` adds a direct dependency on the already-locked `tokio-util`.
- **Blast radius:** 117 files, `+20,513/-1,556` against official `e8d2e5fc81a01e6dc7d76428e07168e583b43039` at `154ffadfca9a0c1e6376f3b24c9af406df159b25`: storage/lifecycle, daemon coordination, approvals/redaction, channels/RPC, configuration/localization, Web/ZeroCode and prompt budgeting. Private-request hook exclusion affects programmatic hook transforms, cancellation and model selection.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9998, the accepted contract; Related #10405, the Chat/ACP tracker. ACP remains a separate follow-up. Related #10412 is parallel session-contract work, not a dependency or supersession.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/9998
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10405
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10412

### What this does, simply

A chat can keep a small reminder attached to itself rather than relying on remaining conversation history. A later primary turn receives it after restart, but another session and auxiliary workers do not. Successful whole-session reset starts without the attachments. The feature is off by default.

Operators normally approve the exact proposed mutation once. Unsupported confirmation surfaces refuse it; ordinary approvals still work. Prompt text grants no permissions and cannot override immutable safety/host instructions. If the complete collection and required tool-protocol framing cannot fit, provider dispatch fails instead of silently dropping content.

There are at most four attachments, each at most 2 KiB and 8 KiB collectively. Symbolic IDs follow `[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`. Changes take effect on the next top-level turn, not during the already-running turn.

The deletion fix prevents an open WebSocket from recreating a session that RPC just deleted. A same-ID successor is a new owner, not permission for the old connection or queued work to continue. Deleting `team_alpha` does not cancel an unrelated active `team.alpha` WebSocket queue; HTTP/SSE still uses its actual normalized queue and raw abort ID.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, on disposable sessions.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web` and `surface: tui` (ZeroCode Chat/Dashboard); messaging channels `matrix`, `slack`, `telegram`, `signal`, plus CLI confirmation. Other adapters have negative strict-capability coverage, not enabled-feature claims.
- **Setup / preconditions:** SQLite Chat persistence, `[channels].session_prompts_enabled = true`, global `session_prompt_approval = "required"`, matching clients. Default full tool selection includes the tools; a minimal configuration must name `session_prompt_list`, `session_prompt_set` and `session_prompt_delete` in `[tools].optional`, then reload. Selection grants no execution permission and does not gate injection of stored attachments into an enabled primary Chat turn. WebSocket Chat additionally requires `[gateway].session_persistence = true`; restart after enabling that prerequisite. Matrix-only configurations need not enable gateway persistence.
- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to set `{"id":"task","content":"Keep this chat focused on the synthetic inventory task."}`; inspect the literal preview and approve once. List the collection, send another turn, restart and ask again. Check another session, then reset the original and list again. Inspect and reject a 2 KiB synthetic proposal after scrolling to its end. Separately keep a WebSocket open, delete its Chat session through RPC and try another prompt through that old connection; reconnect to create or use the intended successor.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Next-turn injection and restart persistence are current-session-only; successful reset clears the collection. Strict approval has one-time allow/reject, no Always, and rejection changes nothing. After committed deletion the old WebSocket reports `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`; it cannot recreate or adopt the successor. Durable deletion failure is reported without claiming success and preserves the durable state.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The prompt collection/configuration/tools do not exist. The independent RPC/gateway deletion paths can leave an open gateway connection able to recreate deleted durable Chat state.

### How I tested

Latest candidate `154ffadfca9a0c1e6376f3b24c9af406df159b25`, tree
`05ae9fb32fcd55925d76df6b71b5c17bdb37c140`, has base-relative diff SHA-256
`473fcc1cd7e9ed2ab64eb6b3732616f9fabff3ae651d0b35720c1555bdedc957`.
Follow-up: four translations, catalog/CLI-loader regression and lifecycle
cross-reference; production control flow unchanged.

Latest-head checks (read-only/offline Docker):

~~~text
cargo test --frozen -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib i18n::tests:: -- --test-threads=16
test result: ok. 50 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5871 filtered out; finished in 2.32s
cargo clippy --frozen -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --tests -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 2m 30s
~~~

58 scanner fixtures, 0 failures; worktree comment-hygiene gate passed. The
full-suite receipts below belong to the explicitly identified parent, not a
new local full-suite run. Hosted results follow.

Behavior-bearing parent `a7111fb8d208d77d7b5079a8dafbf45eb34fa78e` contains the normal
`99f6e6965021` merge of official master
`e8d2e5fc81a01e6dc7d76428e07168e583b43039` after published
`1afbd5791b9c51fbf322367e1ae7f81db7920bb2`, plus the SOP privacy correction.
No rebase or force push. Tree `9cba2cea185cc06fff8ba73e4069cf253d5eef6b`;
base-relative diff SHA-256
`4a8aa66e6c22f776cb02118d9343ecb318b6df3e8e34227054d3c85cc16eb0b5`.

The two conflicts preserve generated-date removal before the canonical
attachment appender and WebSocket reconnect admission with the existing
generation/cancellation fences and one dispatch. The additional correction
rejects unsupported prompt calls before strict or ordinary approval and omits
their complete outcomes from SOP step audit capture. Primary Chat approval,
ordinary capture and provider-visible results are preserved. Hook-rewritten

Two new regression tests failed before the correction: an unsupported call
reached approval and the SOP sink retained three private prompt-tool records.
The corrected tests pass, alongside absent-capability, inherited-session-key,
both approval-policy, rewritten-hook, ordinary-capture and provider-result
controls. Existing real cron and one-shot RPC regressions pass without changing
their expected refusal text.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Exact-head CI, including
  [run 39326780449](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39326780449)
  is terminal: 45 passes, five expected skips, five
  cancellations and failed `CI Required Gate`. Workspace tests passed 19,533
  (40 skipped), hardware 189 (one skipped), transport seven (five skipped).

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `Format`, both plugin runtime checks and

- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux ARM64 Docker, source/Git read-only,
